and four thousand were gatekeepers; and four thousand praised the LORD with the instruments that I made for praising.
And David divided them into divisions, according to the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath and Merari.
Of the Gershonites: Ladan and Shimei.
The sons of Ladan: Jehiel the chief, and Zetham and Joel — three.
The sons of Shimei: Shelomith and Haziel and Haran — three. These were the heads of the ancestral houses of Ladan.
And the sons of Shimei: Jahath, Zina, and Jeush and Beriah. These were the sons of Shimei — four.
And Jahath was the chief, and Zizah the second; and Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons, so they were counted as one ancestral house, one muster.
The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel — four.

The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses. And Aaron was set apart, to be consecrated as most holy, he and his sons for ever — to burn incense as smoke before the LORD, to serve him and to bless in his name for ever.
And as for Moses the man of God, his sons were counted with the tribe of Levi.
The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.
The sons of Gershom: Shebuel the chief.
And the sons of Eliezer were: Rehabiah the chief. And Eliezer had no other sons; but the sons of Rehabiah were exceedingly numerous.
The sons of Izhar: Shelomith the chief.
The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the chief, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third and Jekameam the fourth.
The sons of Uzziel: Micah the chief and Isshiah the second.
The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish.
And Eleazar died, and he had no sons but only daughters; and the sons of Kish, their kinsmen, married them.
The sons of Mushi: Mahli and Eder and Jeremoth — three.

These were the sons of Levi by their ancestral houses, the heads of the ancestral houses as they were enrolled, listed by name, head by head, doing the work of the service of the house of the LORD, from twenty years old and upward.
For David had said, "The LORD the God of Israel has given rest to his people, and he has taken up his dwelling in Jerusalem for ever."
And so the Levites no longer need to carry the tabernacle or any of the articles for its service.
For by the last words of David, these were the number of the sons of Levi from twenty years old and upward.

For their duty was to be at the side of the sons of Aaron, for the service of the house of the LORD, over the courts and over the store-rooms and over the cleansing of every holy thing, and the work of the service of the house of God;

and for the bread of the row, and for the fine flour for a grain offering, and for the wafers of unleavened bread, and for what is baked on the griddle, and for the well-mixed dough, and for every measure of volume and length.
And to stand every morning to give thanks and praise the LORD, and likewise in the evening;

and for every offering up of burnt offerings to the LORD on the sabbaths, at the new moons and at the appointed times, in the required number, according to the ordinance laid on them, continually before the LORD.
And they kept the charge of the tent of meeting and the charge of the holy place and the charge of the sons of Aaron their kinsmen, for the service of the house of the LORD.

1 chronicles_24.t: And for the sons of Aaron, their divisions. The sons of Aaron: Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
And Nadab and Abihu died before their father, and they had no sons; so Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests.
And David divided them, with Zadok of the sons of Eleazar and Ahimelech of the sons of Ithamar, according to their appointed order of service.

And the sons of Eleazar were found to have more chief men than the sons of Ithamar, and so they divided them: for the sons of Eleazar, sixteen heads of ancestral houses; and for the sons of Ithamar, eight by their ancestral houses.
And they divided them by lot, one group alongside the other; for there were officials of the holy place and officials of God among the sons of Eleazar and among the sons of Ithamar.

And Shemaiah son of Nethanel the scribe, one of the Levites, recorded them before the king and the officials and Zadok the priest and Ahimelech son of Abiathar and the heads of the ancestral houses of the priests and of the Levites — one ancestral house drawn for Eleazar, and one drawn for Ithamar.
And the first lot fell to Jehoiarib, the second to Jedaiah,
the third to Harim, the fourth to Seorim,
the fifth to Malkijah, the sixth to Mijamin,
the seventh to Hakkoz, the eighth to Abijah,
the ninth to Jeshua, the tenth to Shecaniah,
the eleventh to Eliashib, the twelfth to Jakim,
the thirteenth to Huppah, the fourteenth to Jeshebeab,
the fifteenth to Bilgah, the sixteenth to Immer,
the seventeenth to Hezir, the eighteenth to Happizzez,
the nineteenth to Pethahiah, the twentieth to Jehezkel,
the twenty-first to Jakin, the twenty-second to Gamul,
the twenty-third to Delaiah, the twenty-fourth to Maaziah.

These were their appointed orders of service, to come into the house of the LORD according to the ordinance given them, by the hand of Aaron their ancestor, as the LORD the God of Israel had commanded him.
And for the rest of the sons of Levi: of the sons of Amram, Shubael; of the sons of Shubael, Jehdeiah.
Of Rehabiah: of the sons of Rehabiah, Isshiah the chief.
Of the Izharites: Shelomoth; of the sons of Shelomoth, Jahath.
And the sons of Hebron: Jeriah the chief, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, Jekameam the fourth.
The sons of Uzziel: Micah; of the sons of Micah, Shamir.
The brother of Micah: Isshiah; of the sons of Isshiah, Zechariah.
The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Jaaziah: Beno.
The sons of Merari: of Jaaziah, Beno; and Shoham and Zaccur and Ibri.
Of Mahli: Eleazar, and he had no sons.
Of Kish: the sons of Kish, Jerahmeel.
And the sons of Mushi: Mahli and Eder and Jerimoth. These were the sons of the Levites by their ancestral houses.

And they too cast lots, just as their kinsmen the sons of Aaron did, before David the king and Zadok and Ahimelech and the heads of the ancestral houses of the priests and of the Levites — the chief ancestral house treated no differently from the youngest brother's.

1 chronicles_25.t: And David and the commanders of the army set apart for the service the sons of Asaph and Heman and Jeduthun, who prophesied with lyres, harps and cymbals. And this was the number of the men who did this work in their service:
Of the sons of Asaph: Zaccur and Joseph and Nethaniah and Asarelah, the sons of Asaph, under the direction of Asaph, who prophesied under the direction of the king.

Of Jeduthun: the sons of Jeduthun — Gedaliah and Zeri and Jeshaiah, Hashabiah and Mattithiah, six — under the direction of their father Jeduthun, who prophesied with the lyre, in giving thanks and praising the LORD.
Of Heman: the sons of Heman — Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel and Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti and Romamti-ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, Mahazioth.
All these were sons of Heman the king's seer, in the words of God, to lift up a horn. And God gave Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.

All these were under the direction of their father in the song of the house of the LORD, with cymbals, harps and lyres, for the service of the house of God — under the direction of the king: Asaph and Jeduthun and Heman.
And their number, together with their kinsmen trained in song to the LORD, all who were skilled, was two hundred and eighty-eight.
And they cast lots for their duties, one alongside another, the small as well as the great, the trained alongside the pupil.
And the first lot fell for Asaph, to Joseph; the second, Gedaliah: he and his brothers and sons, twelve;
The third, Zaccur: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
The fourth, to Izri: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
The fifth, Nethaniah: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
The sixth, Bukkiah: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
The seventh, Jesharelah: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
The eighth, Jeshaiah: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
The ninth, Mattaniah: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
The tenth, Shimei: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
The eleventh, Azarel: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
The twelfth, to Hashabiah: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the thirteenth, Shubael: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the fourteenth, Mattithiah: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the fifteenth, to Jeremoth: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the sixteenth, to Hananiah: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the seventeenth, to Joshbekashah: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the eighteenth, to Hanani: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the nineteenth, to Mallothi: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the twentieth, to Eliathah: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the twenty-first, to Hothir: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the twenty-second, to Giddalti: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the twenty-third, to Mahazioth: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the twenty-fourth, to Romamti-ezer: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.

1 chronicles_26.t: For the divisions of the gatekeepers: of the Korahites, Meshelemiah son of Kore, one of the sons of Asaph.
And Meshelemiah had sons: Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth,
Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, Eliehoenai the seventh.
And Obed-edom had sons: Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third and Sakar the fourth, and Nethanel the fifth,
Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, Peullethai the eighth — for God had blessed him.
And to Shemaiah his son were born sons who ruled over their ancestral house, for they were mighty men of ability.
The sons of Shemaiah: Othni and Rephael and Obed, Elzabad; his kinsmen were men of ability, Elihu and Semakiah.
All these were of the sons of Obed-edom — they and their sons and their kinsmen, men of ability with the strength for the service — sixty-two belonging to Obed-edom.
And Meshelemiah had sons and kinsmen, men of ability — eighteen.
And Hosah, of the sons of Merari, had sons: Shimri the chief — for he was not the firstborn, but his father appointed him chief —
Hilkiah the second, Tebaliah the third, Zechariah the fourth. All the sons and kinsmen of Hosah were thirteen.
To these belonged the divisions of the gatekeepers, under their chief men, with duties matching those of their kinsmen, to serve in the house of the LORD.
And they cast lots, the small as well as the great, by their ancestral houses, gate by gate.
And the lot for the east fell to Shelemiah; and for Zechariah his son, a counsellor with insight, they cast lots, and his lot came out for the north.
To Obed-edom, the south; and to his sons, the storehouse.
To Shuppim and to Hosah, the west, beside the gate of Shalleketh on the ascending highway — guard post alongside guard post.
On the east, six Levites; on the north, four each day; on the south, four each day; and at the storehouse, two at a time.
At the Parbar on the west: four at the highway, two at the Parbar.
These were the divisions of the gatekeepers, of the sons of the Korahites and of the sons of Merari.
And of the Levites: Ahijah was over the storehouses of the house of God and over the storehouses of the holy things.
The sons of Ladan, the sons of the Gershonites belonging to Ladan, the heads of the ancestral houses belonging to Ladan the Gershonite: Jehieli.
The sons of Jehieli: Zetham and Joel his brother, who were over the storehouses of the house of the LORD.
Of the Amramites, of the Izharites, of the Hebronites, of the Uzzielites:
And Shebuel son of Gershom, son of Moses, was leader over the storehouses.
And his kinsmen, through Eliezer: Rehabiah his son, and Jeshaiah his son, and Joram his son, and Zikri his son, and Shelomith his son.

That Shelomoth and his kinsmen were over all the storehouses of the holy things that King David had consecrated, and that the heads of the ancestral houses, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and the commanders of the army had consecrated.
From the wars and from the plunder they had consecrated it, to keep the house of the LORD in repair.
And all that Samuel the seer had consecrated, and Saul son of Kish, and Abner son of Ner, and Joab son of Zeruiah — everything that anyone consecrated was under the hand of Shelomith and his kinsmen.
Of the Izharites: Kenaniah and his sons were assigned to the work outside, over Israel, as officers and as judges.

Of the Hebronites: Hashabiah and his kinsmen, men of ability, one thousand seven hundred, had the oversight of Israel on the western side of the Jordan, for all the work of the LORD and for the service of the king.

Of the Hebronites: Jeriah was the chief of the Hebronites, according to his generations, by ancestral houses. In the fortieth year of David's reign they were searched out, and mighty men of ability were found among them at Jazer of Gilead.

And his kinsmen, men of ability, were two thousand seven hundred, heads of ancestral houses; and King David appointed them over the Reubenites and the Gadites and the half-tribe of the Manassites, for every matter of God and every matter of the king.

1 chronicles_27.t: And the people of Israel by their number: the heads of the ancestral houses and the commanders of thousands and hundreds and their officers who served the king, in every matter of the divisions that came on duty and went off month by month, through all the months of the year — each division numbering twenty-four thousand.
Over the first division, for the first month, was Jashobeam son of Zabdiel; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
He was of the sons of Perez, the chief of all the commanders of the armies for the first month.
And over the division of the second month was Dodai the Ahohite, with his division; and Mikloth was the leader; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The commander of the third army, for the third month, was Benaiah son of Jehoiada the priest, as chief; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
This was the Benaiah who was the mighty man of the thirty and over the thirty; and in his division was Ammizabad his son.
The fourth, for the fourth month, was Asahel the brother of Joab, and Zebadiah his son after him; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The fifth, for the fifth month, was the leader Shamhuth the Izrahite; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The sixth, for the sixth month, was Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The seventh, for the seventh month, was Helez the Pelonite, of the sons of Ephraim; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The eighth, for the eighth month, was Sibbecai the Hushathite, of the Zerahites; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The ninth, for the ninth month, was Abiezer the Anathothite, of the Benjaminites; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The tenth, for the tenth month, was Maharai the Netophathite, of the Zerahites; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The eleventh, for the eleventh month, was Benaiah the Pirathonite, of the sons of Ephraim; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The twelfth, for the twelfth month, was Heldai the Netophathite, of the house of Othniel; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
And over the tribes of Israel: for the Reubenites, the leader was Eliezer son of Zikri; for the Simeonites, Shephatiah son of Maacah;
for Levi, Hashabiah son of Kemuel; for Aaron, Zadok;
for Judah, Elihu, one of David's brothers; for Issachar, Omri son of Michael;
for Zebulun, Ishmaiah son of Obadiah; for Naphtali, Jerimoth son of Azriel;
for the sons of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Azaziah; for the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joel son of Pedaiah;
for the half of Manasseh in Gilead, Iddo son of Zechariah; for Benjamin, Jaasiel son of Abner;
for Dan, Azarel son of Jeroham. These were the commanders of the tribes of Israel.
And David did not take the number of those twenty years old and under, because the LORD had said he would multiply Israel like the stars of the heavens.
Joab son of Zeruiah began to count and did not finish, and because of this wrath came upon Israel; and the number was never entered in the account of the days of King David.
And over the king's storehouses was Azmaveth son of Adiel; and over the storehouses in the open country, in the cities and in the villages and in the towers, was Jonathan son of Uzziah.
And over those doing the work of the field, for the labour of the ground, was Ezri son of Kelub.
And over the vineyards was Shimei the Ramathite; and over the produce of the vineyards for the wine stores was Zabdi the Shiphmite.
And over the olive trees and the sycamore figs that were in the Shephelah was Baal-hanan the Gederite; and over the stores of oil was Joash.
And over the cattle grazing in Sharon was Shirtai the Sharonite; and over the cattle in the valleys was Shaphat son of Adlai.
And over the camels was Obil the Ishmaelite; and over the she-asses was Jehdeiah the Meronothite.
And over the flocks was Jaziz the Hagrite. All these were the officials over the property that belonged to King David.
And Jonathan, David's uncle, was a counsellor; he was a man of understanding and a scribe. And Jehiel son of Hacmoni was with the king's sons.
And Ahithophel was a counsellor to the king; and Hushai the Arkite was the king's friend.
And after Ahithophel came Jehoiada son of Benaiah and Abiathar. And the commander of the king's army was Joab.

1 chronicles_28.t: And David assembled at Jerusalem all the officials of Israel: the leaders of the tribes and the commanders of the divisions who served the king, and the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, and the officials over all the property and livestock of the king and of his sons, together with the court officials and the mighty men and every mighty man of ability.

And King David rose to his feet and said, "Hear me, my brothers and my people. It was in my heart to build a house of rest for the ark of the covenant of the LORD, and for the footstool of our God's feet, and I made preparations to build."
"But God said to me, 'You shall not build a house for my name, for you are a man of war and you have shed blood.'"

"And the LORD the God of Israel chose me out of all my father's house to be king over Israel for ever; for he chose Judah as leader, and within the house of Judah, my father's house; and among my father's sons he took pleasure in me, to make me king over all Israel."
"And out of all my sons — for the LORD has given me many sons — he chose Solomon my son to sit on the throne of the kingdom of the LORD over Israel."
"And he said to me, 'Solomon your son, he shall build my house and my courts, for I have chosen him to be a son to me, and I will be a father to him.'"
"'And I will establish his kingdom for ever, if he holds firm to carry out my commandments and my judgements, as he does this day.'"

"And now, before the eyes of all Israel, the assembly of the LORD, and in the hearing of our God: keep and seek out all the commandments of the LORD your God, so that you may possess the good land and leave it as an inheritance to your sons after you for ever."

"And you, Solomon my son, know the God of your father and serve him with a whole heart and with a willing being; for the LORD searches all hearts and understands every inclination of the thoughts. If you seek him, he will let himself be found by you; and if you forsake him, he will reject you for ever."
"See now that the LORD has chosen you to build a house for the sanctuary. Be strong and act."
And David gave to Solomon his son the plan of the porch and of its buildings and its treasuries and its upper rooms and its inner rooms, and the house of the mercy seat;

and the plan of all that he had in mind by the spirit, for the courts of the house of the LORD and for all the surrounding rooms, for the storehouses of the house of God and for the storehouses of the holy things;
and for the divisions of the priests and the Levites, and for all the work of the service of the house of the LORD, and for all the articles of the service of the house of the LORD;
for the gold, by weight of gold, for the articles of each and every service; for all the silver articles, by weight, for the articles of each and every service;

and the weight for the gold lampstands and their gold lamps, by the weight of each and every lampstand and its lamps; and for the silver lampstands, by weight for each lampstand and its lamps, according to the service of each and every lampstand;
and the gold by weight for the tables of the row, for each and every table; and silver for the silver tables;
and the forks and the basins and the jugs, of pure gold; and for the gold bowls, by weight for each and every bowl; and for the silver bowls, by weight for each and every bowl;
and for the altar of incense, purged gold by weight; and for the plan of the chariot, the gold cherubim, spreading their wings and covering the ark of the covenant of the LORD.
"All this," said David, "is in writing from the hand of the LORD upon me; he gave me understanding of all the works of the plan."

And David said to Solomon his son, "Be strong and be courageous and act. Do not be afraid and do not be dismayed, for the LORD God, my God, is with you. He will not abandon you and he will not forsake you, until all the work of the service of the house of the LORD is finished."

"And here are the divisions of the priests and the Levites for all the service of the house of God; and with you in every work is every willing man skilled in every kind of service; and the officials and all the people are at your command."

1 chronicles_29.t: And King David said to all the assembly, "Solomon my son, the one whom God has chosen, is young and inexperienced, and the work is great; for the citadel is not for a man but for the LORD God."

"And with all my strength I have prepared for the house of my God: gold for the gold work, silver for the silver, bronze for the bronze, iron for the iron and wood for the wood; onyx stones and stones for setting, stones of antimony and of variegated work, and every precious stone, and alabaster in abundance."

"And further, because I take pleasure in the house of my God, I have a treasure of gold and silver of my own; I give it to the house of my God, over and above all that I have prepared for the holy house:"
"three thousand talents of gold, gold of Ophir, and seven thousand talents of purged silver, to overlay the walls of the buildings;"
"gold for the gold work and silver for the silver, and for all the work done by the hand of craftsmen. And who now is willing to consecrate himself today to the LORD?"
And the leaders of the ancestral houses and the leaders of the tribes of Israel and the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and the officials over the king's work, gave willingly;

and they gave for the service of the house of God five thousand talents of gold and ten thousand darics, and ten thousand talents of silver, and eighteen thousand talents of bronze, and a hundred thousand talents of iron.
And whoever had stones gave them to the treasury of the house of the LORD, under the hand of Jehiel the Gershonite.
And the people rejoiced over their willing giving, for with a whole heart they had given willingly to the LORD; and King David also rejoiced with great joy.
And David blessed the LORD before the eyes of all the assembly, and David said, "Blessed are you, LORD, God of Israel our father, from everlasting to everlasting."

"Yours, LORD, is the greatness and the might and the splendour and the endurance and the majesty; for all that is in the heavens and on the earth is yours. Yours, LORD, is the kingdom, and you are the one who lifts himself as head above all."
"And wealth and honour come from before you, and you rule over all; and in your hand are strength and might, and in your hand it lies to make great and to give strength to all."
"And now, our God, we give you thanks and praise your splendid name."
"And who am I, and who are my people, that we should have the strength to give willingly like this? For all things come from you, and from your own hand we have given to you."
"For we are sojourners before you, and resident aliens, as all our ancestors were; our days on the earth are like a shadow, and there is no hope."
"LORD our God, all this abundance that we have prepared to build you a house for your holy name — it is from your hand, and all of it is yours."

"And I know, my God, that you test the heart and take pleasure in uprightness. As for me, in the uprightness of my heart I have given all these things willingly; and now I have seen with joy that your people who are here give willingly to you."
"LORD, God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel our ancestors, keep this for ever as the inclination of the thoughts of your people's heart, and direct their heart to yourself."
"And to Solomon my son give a whole heart, to keep your commandments, your testimonies and your statutes, and to carry it all out, and to build the citadel for which I have made preparation."
And David said to all the assembly, "Bless the LORD your God." And all the assembly blessed the LORD the God of their ancestors; and they bowed low and bowed down to the LORD and to the king.

And they sacrificed sacrifices to the LORD, and offered up burnt offerings to the LORD on the day after that: a thousand bulls, a thousand rams, a thousand lambs, with their drink offerings, and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel.
And they ate and drank before the LORD on that day with great joy. And they made Solomon son of David king a second time, and anointed him to the LORD as leader, and Zadok as priest.
And Solomon sat on the throne of the LORD as king in place of David his father, and he succeeded; and all Israel listened to him.
And all the officials and the mighty men, and also all the sons of King David, pledged themselves under Solomon the king.
And the LORD made Solomon exceedingly great before the eyes of all Israel, and put upon him a royal majesty such as had not been on any king before him over Israel.
And David son of Jesse reigned over all Israel.
And the days that he reigned over Israel were forty years: in Hebron he reigned seven years, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three.
And he died at a good old age, full of days, wealth and honour; and Solomon his son reigned in his place.
And the matters of King David, the former and the latter, are written in the words of Samuel the seer and in the words of Nathan the prophet and in the words of Gad the seer,
together with all his reign and his might, and the times that passed over him and over Israel and over all the kingdoms of the lands.

1 kings_1.t: Now King David was old, advanced in days; and they covered him with clothes, but he could not get warm.

And his servants said to him, 'Let them seek out for my lord the king a young woman, a virgin, and let her stand before the king and be his nurse; and let her lie in your bosom, so that my lord the king may be warm.'
So they sought a beautiful young woman throughout all the territory of Israel, and they found Abishag the Shunammite, and brought her to the king.
And the young woman was exceedingly beautiful; she became the king's nurse and served him, but the king did not know her.
Now Adonijah son of Haggith was exalting himself, saying, 'I will be king.' And he acquired for himself a chariot and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him.
And his father had never rebuked him in his days, saying, 'Why have you done this?' He too was very handsome; and he was born after Absalom.
He conferred with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they gave their support to Adonijah.
But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei and Rei, and David's mighty men were not with Adonijah.

And Adonijah sacrificed sheep and cattle and fatlings near the stone of Zoheleth, which is beside En-rogel, and he invited all his brothers, the king's sons, and all the men of Judah, the king's servants.
But Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the mighty men and Solomon his brother he did not invite.
Then Nathan said to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon, 'Have you not heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has become king, and our lord David does not know?'
'And now come, let me give you counsel: save your own life and the life of your son Solomon.'

'Go in to King David and say to him, "Did you not, my lord the king, swear to your maidservant, saying, Solomon your son shall reign after me and he shall sit on my throne? Why then has Adonijah become king?"'
'And while you are still speaking there with the king, I myself will come in after you and confirm your words.'
So Bathsheba went in to the king, into the inner room; and the king was very old, and Abishag the Shunammite was serving the king.
And Bathsheba bowed low and bowed down to the king. And the king said, 'What do you want?'
And she said to him, 'My lord, you yourself swore by the LORD your God to your maidservant: "Solomon your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne."'
'And now, look, Adonijah has become king, and you, my lord the king, do not know it.'

'And he has sacrificed oxen and fatlings and sheep in abundance, and has invited all the king's sons, and Abiathar the priest and Joab the commander of the army; but Solomon your servant he has not invited.'
'And as for you, my lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are on you, to tell them who shall sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.'
'Otherwise it will come about, when my lord the king lies down with his fathers, that I and my son Solomon will be counted sinners.'
And while she was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet came in.
And they told the king, 'Here is Nathan the prophet.' And he came before the king and bowed down to the king with his face to the ground.
And Nathan said, 'My lord the king, have you said, "Adonijah shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne"?'

'For he has gone down today and sacrificed oxen and fatlings and sheep in abundance, and has invited all the king's sons, the commanders of the army and Abiathar the priest; and there they are, eating and drinking before him, and saying, "Long live King Adonijah!"'
'But me, your servant, and Zadok the priest, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and Solomon your servant, he has not invited.'
'If this thing has come about from my lord the king, then you have not made known to your servant who shall sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.'
Then King David answered and said, 'Summon Bathsheba for me.' And she came before the king and stood before the king.
And the king swore and said, 'As the LORD lives, who has ransomed my life from every trouble —'
'that just as I swore to you by the LORD, the God of Israel, saying, "Solomon your son shall reign after me and he shall sit on my throne in my place," so I will do this very day.'
And Bathsheba bowed low with her face to the ground and bowed down to the king, and said, 'May my lord King David live for ever!'
And King David said, 'Summon for me Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet and Benaiah son of Jehoiada.' And they came before the king.
And the king said to them, 'Take with you the servants of your lord, and set Solomon my son on the mule that is mine, and bring him down to Gihon.'
'And there Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet shall anoint him king over Israel; and you shall blow the ram's horn and say, "Long live King Solomon!"'
'And you shall come up after him, and he shall come in and sit on my throne; he shall reign in my place, for I have appointed him ruler over Israel and over Judah.'
And Benaiah son of Jehoiada answered the king and said, 'Amen! So may the LORD, the God of my lord the king, say.'
'Just as the LORD has been with my lord the king, so may he be with Solomon, and may he make his throne greater than the throne of my lord King David.'
So Zadok the priest went down, with Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and the Kerethites and the Pelethites; and they set Solomon on King David's mule and brought him to Gihon.
And Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tent and anointed Solomon; and they blew the ram's horn, and all the people said, 'Long live King Solomon!'
And all the people came up after him, playing on flutes and rejoicing with great joy, so that the ground was split open by their noise.
And Adonijah heard it, and all those invited who were with him, just as they had finished eating. And Joab heard the sound of the ram's horn and said, 'Why is the sound of the town in an uproar?'
While he was still speaking, Jonathan son of Abiathar the priest came in. And Adonijah said, 'Come, for you are a man of worth, and you bear good news.'
And Jonathan answered and said to Adonijah, 'Indeed — our lord King David has made Solomon king.'
'And the king has sent with him Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and the Kerethites and the Pelethites; and they have set him on the king's mule.'
'And Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet have anointed him king at Gihon, and they have come up from there rejoicing, and the town is in an uproar. That is the noise you have heard.'
'And Solomon has also taken his seat on the throne of the kingship.'

'And the king's servants have also come to bless our lord King David, saying, "May God make Solomon's name better than your name, and may he make his throne greater than your throne." And the king bowed down on the bed.'
'And the king also said this: "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who has this day given one to sit on my throne, and my own eyes seeing it."'
Then all those invited who were with Adonijah trembled, and they rose and went, each on his own way.
And Adonijah was afraid of Solomon; he rose and went and took hold of the horns of the altar.

And it was told to Solomon, 'Look, Adonijah fears King Solomon; and look, he has taken hold of the horns of the altar, saying, "Let King Solomon swear to me this day that he will not put his servant to death by the sword."'
And Solomon said, 'If he proves to be a man of worth, not one of his hairs shall fall to the ground; but if evil is found in him, he shall die.'
So King Solomon sent, and they brought him down from the altar; and he came and bowed down to King Solomon, and Solomon said to him, 'Go to your house.'

1 kings_2.t: Now the days of David drew near for him to die, and he commanded Solomon his son:
'I am going the way of all the earth. Be strong, and be a man.'

'And keep the charge of the LORD your God: to walk in his ways, to keep his statutes, his commandments, his judgements and his testimonies, according to what is written in the law of Moses, so that you may prosper in all you do and wherever you turn;'

'so that the LORD may establish his word that he spoke concerning me: "If your sons keep their way, to walk before me in faithfulness with all their heart and with all their soul, there shall not be cut off from you a man on the throne of Israel."'

'And you also know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me, what he did to the two commanders of the armies of Israel, Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether: he killed them, shedding the blood of war in a time of peace, and he put the blood of war on the belt that was on his loins and on the sandals that were on his feet.'
'Act according to your wisdom, and do not let his grey head go down to Sheol in peace.'
'But to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite show loyalty, and let them be among those who eat at your table; for so they came to me when I fled from before Absalom your brother.'

'And with you is Shimei son of Gera the Benjaminite from Bahurim. He cursed me with a grievous curse on the day I went to Mahanaim; but he came down to meet me at the Jordan, and I swore to him by the LORD, "I will not put you to death by the sword."'
'And now, do not leave him unpunished, for you are a wise man; you will know what to do to him, and you shall bring his grey head down in blood to Sheol.'
Then David lay down with his fathers, and he was buried in the city of David.
And the days that David reigned over Israel were forty years: in Hebron he reigned seven years, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years.
And Solomon sat on the throne of David his father, and his reign was firmly established.
Then Adonijah son of Haggith came to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon, and she said, 'Do you come in peace?' And he said, 'In peace.'
And he said, 'I have a word for you.' And she said, 'Speak.'
And he said, 'You know that the kingship was mine, and that all Israel set their faces on me to be king; but the kingship turned round and became my brother's, for it was his from the LORD.'
'And now I ask one petition of you; do not turn away my face.' And she said to him, 'Speak.'
And he said, 'Say to Solomon the king — for he will not turn away your face — that he give me Abishag the Shunammite as a wife.'
And Bathsheba said, 'Good. I myself will speak to the king concerning you.'

So Bathsheba came to King Solomon to speak to him concerning Adonijah. And the king rose to meet her and bowed down to her, and then sat on his throne; and he had a throne placed for the king's mother, and she sat at his right hand.
And she said, 'One small petition I ask of you; do not turn away my face.' And the king said to her, 'Ask, my mother, for I will not turn away your face.'
And she said, 'Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to Adonijah your brother as a wife.'

And King Solomon answered and said to his mother, 'And why are you asking Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? Ask the kingship for him too — for he is my brother, older than I — for him, and for Abiathar the priest, and for Joab son of Zeruiah!'
And King Solomon swore by the LORD, saying, 'So may God do to me and so may he add, if it is not at the cost of his own life that Adonijah has spoken this word.'
'And now, as the LORD lives, who established me and set me on the throne of David my father and who made me a house just as he promised — today Adonijah shall be put to death.'
And King Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he fell on him, and he died.

And to Abiathar the priest the king said, 'Go to Anathoth, to your own fields, for you are a man deserving death; but on this day I will not put you to death, because you carried the ark of the Lord GOD before David my father, and because you were afflicted in all that my father was afflicted.'
So Solomon drove out Abiathar from being a priest to the LORD, fulfilling the word of the LORD that he had spoken concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh.
And the report came to Joab — for Joab had turned aside after Adonijah, though after Absalom he had not turned aside — and Joab fled to the tent of the LORD and took hold of the horns of the altar.
And it was told to King Solomon that Joab had fled to the tent of the LORD, and that he was beside the altar. So Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, saying, 'Go, fall on him.'

And Benaiah came to the tent of the LORD and said to him, 'This is what the king says: come out.' And he said, 'No — here I will die.' And Benaiah brought the king back word: 'This is what Joab said, and this is how he answered me.'
And the king said to him, 'Do just as he has said: fall on him and bury him, and so remove from me and from my father's house the blood that Joab shed without cause.'

'And the LORD will return his blood on his own head, because he fell on two men more righteous and better than himself and killed them with the sword — and my father David did not know of it: Abner son of Ner, the commander of the army of Israel, and Amasa son of Jether, the commander of the army of Judah.'

'And their blood shall return on the head of Joab and on the head of his offspring for ever; but to David and to his offspring, to his house and to his throne, there shall be peace for ever from the LORD.'
So Benaiah son of Jehoiada went up and fell on him and put him to death; and he was buried in his own house in the wilderness.
And the king put Benaiah son of Jehoiada in his place over the army, and Zadok the priest the king put in the place of Abiathar.
And the king sent and summoned Shimei, and said to him, 'Build yourself a house in Jerusalem and dwell there, and do not go out from there anywhere at all.'
'And it shall be, on the day you go out and cross the wadi of Kidron, you shall surely know that you shall surely die; your blood shall be on your own head.'
And Shimei said to the king, 'The word is good. Just as my lord the king has spoken, so your servant will do.' And Shimei dwelt in Jerusalem many days.
And it happened at the end of three years that two of Shimei's servants fled to Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath; and they told Shimei, 'Look, your servants are in Gath.'
And Shimei rose and saddled his donkey and went to Gath, to Achish, to seek his servants; and Shimei went and brought his servants back from Gath.
And it was told to Solomon that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath and had returned.

And the king sent and summoned Shimei, and said to him, 'Did I not make you swear by the LORD and warn you, saying, "On the day you go out and go anywhere at all, you shall surely know that you shall surely die"? And you said to me, "The word is good; I have heard."'
'Why then have you not kept the oath of the LORD and the command that I commanded you?'
And the king said to Shimei, 'You know all the evil that your heart knows, which you did to David my father; and the LORD will return your evil on your own head.'
'But King Solomon shall be blessed, and the throne of David shall be established before the LORD for ever.'
And the king commanded Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he went out and fell on him, and he died. And the kingdom was established in Solomon's hand.

1 kings_3.t: And Solomon made a marriage alliance with Pharaoh king of Egypt; he took Pharaoh's daughter and brought her to the city of David, until he had finished building his own house and the house of the LORD and the wall of Jerusalem all around.
Only, the people were sacrificing at the high places, because a house had not been built for the name of the LORD until those days.
And Solomon loved the LORD, walking in the statutes of David his father — only, he was sacrificing and making offerings smoke at the high places.
And the king went to Gibeon to sacrifice there, for that was the great high place; a thousand burnt offerings Solomon offered up on that altar.
At Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream of the night, and God said, 'Ask what I shall give you.'

And Solomon said, 'You have shown great steadfast love to your servant David my father, according as he walked before you in faithfulness and in righteousness and in uprightness of heart with you; and you have kept for him this great steadfast love, and you have given him a son sitting on his throne, as at this day.'
'And now, LORD my God, you have made your servant king in place of David my father; and I am a young lad — I do not know how to go out or come in.'
'And your servant is in the midst of your people whom you have chosen, a numerous people that cannot be numbered or counted for multitude.'
'Give your servant a listening heart, to judge your people, to distinguish between good and evil; for who is able to judge this massive people of yours?'
And the thing was good in the eyes of the Lord, that Solomon had asked this.

And God said to him, 'Because you have asked this, and have not asked for yourself long life, and have not asked for yourself wealth, and have not asked for the life of your enemies, but have asked for yourself understanding to hear a case —'
'behold, I do according to your words. I give you a wise and understanding heart, so that there has been none like you before you, and after you none shall arise like you.'
'And also what you did not ask I give you — both wealth and honour — so that there shall not have been anyone like you among the kings all your days.'
'And if you will walk in my ways, keeping my statutes and my commandments, just as David your father walked, then I will lengthen your days.'

And Solomon awoke, and it had been a dream. And he came to Jerusalem and stood before the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and he offered up burnt offerings and made peace offerings, and made a feast for all his servants.
Then two women, prostitutes, came to the king and stood before him.
And the one woman said, 'Pardon me, my lord: I and this woman dwell in one house, and I gave birth while she was in the house.'
'And on the third day after I gave birth, this woman also gave birth; and we were together — there was no stranger with us in the house, only the two of us in the house.'
'And this woman's son died in the night, because she lay on him.'
'And she rose in the middle of the night and took my son from beside me while your maidservant was asleep, and laid him in her bosom; and her dead son she laid in my bosom.'
'And I rose in the morning to suckle my son, and he was dead. But when I looked at him carefully in the morning, he was not my son whom I had borne.'

And the other woman said, 'No — my son is the living one and your son is the dead one.' And this one was saying, 'No — your son is the dead one and my son is the living one.' And so they spoke before the king.
And the king said, 'This one says, "This is my son, the living one, and your son is the dead one," and this one says, "No — your son is the dead one and my son is the living one."'
And the king said, 'Bring me a sword.' And they brought the sword before the king.
And the king said, 'Cut the living child in two, and give half to the one and half to the other.'

And the woman whose son was the living one said to the king — for her compassion grew warm over her son — 'Pardon me, my lord: give her the living child; do not on any account kill him.' And the other was saying, 'It shall belong neither to me nor to you — cut!'
And the king answered and said, 'Give her the living child; do not on any account kill him. She is his mother.'
And all Israel heard the judgement that the king had judged, and they were in awe of the king; for they saw that the wisdom of God was within him to do justice.

1 kings_4.t: And King Solomon was king over all Israel.
And these were his officials: Azariah son of Zadok, the priest;
Elihoreph and Ahijah, sons of Shisha, scribes; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud, the recorder;
Benaiah son of Jehoiada over the army; Zadok and Abiathar, priests;
Azariah son of Nathan over the overseers; Zabud son of Nathan, a priest, the king's friend;
Ahishar over the household; and Adoniram son of Abda over the forced labour.
And Solomon had twelve overseers over all Israel, and they supplied the king and his household; each one had a month in the year to supply.
And these are their names: Ben-hur, in the hill country of Ephraim;
Ben-deker, in Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth-shemesh and Elon-beth-hanan;
Ben-hesed, in Arubboth; to him belonged Socoh and all the land of Hepher;
Ben-abinadab, all Naphath-dor; Taphath the daughter of Solomon became his wife;
Baana son of Ahilud: Taanach and Megiddo, and all Beth-shean which is beside Zarethan, below Jezreel, from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah, as far as beyond Jokmeam;

Ben-geber, in Ramoth-gilead; to him belonged the villages of Jair son of Manasseh which are in Gilead, and to him belonged the region of Argob which is in Bashan — sixty large cities with wall and bronze bar;
Ahinadab son of Iddo, at Mahanaim;
Ahimaaz, in Naphtali; he too took Basemath the daughter of Solomon as a wife;
Baana son of Hushai, in Asher and Bealoth;
Jehoshaphat son of Paruah, in Issachar;
Shimei son of Ela, in Benjamin;
Geber son of Uri, in the land of Gilead, the land of Sihon king of the Amorites and of Og king of Bashan; and there was one overseer who was in the land.
Judah and Israel were numerous, like the sand that is by the sea for multitude, eating and drinking and rejoicing.
And Solomon was ruling over all the kingdoms from the River to the land of the Philistines and as far as the border of Egypt; they brought tribute and served Solomon all the days of his life.
And Solomon's provision for one day was thirty cors of fine flour and sixty cors of flour,
ten fat cattle, twenty pasture-fed cattle and a hundred sheep, apart from deer, gazelle, roe-deer and fattened birds.
For he ruled over all the region beyond the River, from Tiphsah as far as Gaza, over all the kings beyond the River; and he had peace on all his sides round about.
And Judah and Israel dwelt in security, each under his own vine and under his own fig tree, from Dan as far as Beersheba, all the days of Solomon.
And Solomon had forty thousand stalls of horses for his chariotry, and twelve thousand horsemen.
And those overseers supplied King Solomon and everyone who came to the table of King Solomon, each in his own month; they let nothing be lacking.
And they brought the barley and the straw for the horses and the steeds to the place where it was needed, each according to his measure.
And God gave Solomon wisdom and understanding, very great, and breadth of heart, like the sand that is on the seashore.
And Solomon's wisdom was greater than the wisdom of all the people of the east and than all the wisdom of Egypt.
And he was wiser than all humankind — than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman and Kalkol and Darda, the sons of Mahol; and his name was known among all the nations round about.
And he spoke three thousand proverbs, and his songs were a thousand and five.
And he spoke about the trees, from the cedar that is in Lebanon to the hyssop that comes out of the wall; and he spoke about the animals and the birds and the creeping things and the fish.
And they came from all the peoples to hear the wisdom of Solomon, sent by all the kings of the earth who had heard of his wisdom.

1 kings_5.t: And Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants to Solomon, for he had heard that they had anointed him king in place of his father; for Hiram had always been a friend to David.
And Solomon sent to Hiram, saying:
'You know David my father, that he was not able to build a house for the name of the LORD his God because of the wars that surrounded him, until the LORD put them under the soles of my feet.'
'And now the LORD my God has given me rest on every side; there is no opponent and no evil occurrence.'

'And so I intend to build a house for the name of the LORD my God, just as the LORD said to David my father, "Your son, whom I will put in your place on your throne — he shall build the house for my name."'

'And now, command that cedars be cut for me from Lebanon; my servants will be with your servants, and I will give you the wages of your servants, according to all that you say. For you know that there is no one among us who knows how to cut timber like the Sidonians.'
And when Hiram heard the words of Solomon, he rejoiced exceedingly and said, 'Blessed be the LORD this day, who has given David a wise son over this great people.'
And Hiram sent to Solomon, saying, 'I have heard what you sent to me; I myself will do all your desire in cedar timber and cypress timber.'

'My servants will bring them down from Lebanon to the sea, and I will make them into rafts on the sea, to the place you send me word of; and I will break them up there, and you will carry them away. And you will do my desire by giving food for my household.'
So Hiram gave Solomon cedar timber and cypress timber, all his desire.
And Solomon gave Hiram twenty thousand cors of wheat as food for his household, and twenty cors of pressed oil. Thus Solomon gave to Hiram year by year.
And the LORD gave Solomon wisdom, just as he had promised him; and there was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and the two of them made a covenant.
And King Solomon raised forced labour out of all Israel; and the forced labour was thirty thousand men.
And he sent them to Lebanon, ten thousand a month in relays: a month they would be in Lebanon and two months at home. And Adoniram was over the forced labour.
And Solomon had seventy thousand burden-bearers and eighty thousand stone-cutters in the hill country,
apart from the chiefs of Solomon's overseers who were over the work — three thousand three hundred — who ruled over the people doing the work.
And the king commanded, and they quarried large stones, costly stones, to lay the foundation of the house with dressed stones.
And Solomon's builders and Hiram's builders and the Gebalites cut them to shape; and they prepared the timber and the stones to build the house.

1 kings_6.t: And in the four hundred and eightieth year after the coming out of the Israelites from the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon's reign over Israel, in the month of Ziv — that is the second month — he built the house for the LORD.
And the house that King Solomon built for the LORD was sixty cubits in length, twenty in breadth and thirty cubits in height.
And the porch, in front of the temple of the house, was twenty cubits in length, across the breadth of the house, and ten cubits in depth, in front of the house.
And he made for the house windows with recessed frames.
And he built against the wall of the house an extension all around — against the walls of the house all around, for the temple and for the innermost room; and he made side-chambers all around.

The lowest storey of the extension was five cubits in breadth, the middle six cubits, and the third seven cubits; for he made ledges for the house all around, on the outside, so that the beams would not take hold in the walls of the house.
And the house, when it was built, was built of whole stone from the quarry; and no hammer or axe or any iron tool was heard in the house while it was being built.
The entrance of the middle side-chamber was on the south side of the house; and by a stairway they went up to the middle storey, and from the middle to the third.
So he built the house and finished it; and he roofed the house with beams and planks of cedar.
And he built the extension against the whole house, five cubits in height, and he fastened it to the house with cedar timber.
And the word of the LORD came to Solomon, saying:

'As for this house that you are building: if you will walk in my statutes and observe my judgements and keep all my commandments, to walk in them, then I will establish with you my word that I spoke to David your father;'
'and I will dwell among the Israelites, and I will not abandon my people Israel.'
So Solomon built the house and finished it.

And he built the walls of the house on the inside with boards of cedar; from the floor of the house to the walls of the ceiling he overlaid them with wood on the inside; and he overlaid the floor of the house with boards of cypress.
And he built twenty cubits at the rear of the house with boards of cedar, from the floor to the walls; and he built it on the inside as an innermost room, as the holy of holies.
And the house — that is, the temple in front — was forty cubits.
And cedar was on the inside of the house — carved gourds and open flowers; the whole was cedar, and no stone was visible.
And he prepared an innermost room in the middle of the house, on the inside, to put there the ark of the covenant of the LORD.
And the innermost room was twenty cubits in length, twenty cubits in breadth and twenty cubits in height; and he overlaid it with refined gold, and he overlaid the altar with cedar.
And Solomon overlaid the house on the inside with refined gold; and he drew chains of gold across in front of the innermost room, and overlaid it with gold.
And he overlaid the whole house with gold, until all the house was finished; and the whole altar that belonged to the innermost room he overlaid with gold.
And in the innermost room he made two cherubim of olive wood, ten cubits in height.
And one wing of the cherub was five cubits and the second wing of the cherub five cubits — ten cubits from the tip of one wing to the tip of the other.
And the second cherub was ten cubits; the two cherubim had one measurement and one shape.
The height of the one cherub was ten cubits, and so was the second cherub.

And he put the cherubim in the middle of the inner house, and their wings were spread out: the wing of the one touched the one wall, and the wing of the second cherub touched the other wall, and their wings towards the middle of the house touched wing to wing.
And he overlaid the cherubim with gold.
And on all the walls of the house round about he carved engravings of cherubim and palm trees and open flowers, both within and without.
And the floor of the house he overlaid with gold, both within and without.
And for the entrance of the innermost room he made doors of olive wood; the pillar and the doorposts were five-sided.

And the two doors were of olive wood; and he carved on them carvings of cherubim and palm trees and open flowers, and overlaid them with gold; and he hammered the gold out over the cherubim and over the palm trees.
And so also he made for the entrance of the temple doorposts of olive wood, four-sided.
And two doors of cypress wood: the one door had two leaves that folded, and the second door two leaves that folded.
And he carved cherubim and palm trees and open flowers, and overlaid them with gold, fitted smoothly over the carved work.
And he built the inner court with three rows of dressed stone and a row of cedar beams.
In the fourth year the foundation of the house of the LORD was laid, in the month of Ziv.
And in the eleventh year, in the month of Bul — that is the eighth month — the house was complete in all its parts and according to all its specifications; and he built it in seven years.

1 kings_7.t: And Solomon built his own house for thirteen years, and he completed all his house.
And he built the House of the Forest of Lebanon: a hundred cubits in length, fifty cubits in breadth and thirty cubits in height, on four rows of cedar pillars, with cedar beams on the pillars.
And it was panelled with cedar above, over the side-chambers that were on the pillars: forty-five of them, fifteen to a row.
And there were window frames in three rows, and window opposite window, three times.
And all the openings and the doorposts were square in their framework; and at the front, window opposite window, three times.
And he made the Porch of the Pillars, fifty cubits in length and thirty cubits in breadth, with a porch in front of them, and pillars and a threshold in front of them.
And he made the Porch of the Throne, where he would give judgement — the Porch of Judgement — and it was panelled with cedar from floor to floor.
And his own house where he would dwell, in the other court, inward from the porch, was of the same workmanship. And he made a house like this porch for Pharaoh's daughter, whom Solomon had taken.
All these were costly stones, cut to the measurements of dressed stone, sawn with the saw within and without — from the foundation to the coping, and from the outside as far as the great court.
And the foundation was of costly stones, large stones — stones of ten cubits and stones of eight cubits.
And above were costly stones, cut to the measurements of dressed stone, and cedar.
And the great court all around had three rows of dressed stone and a row of cedar beams — and so also the inner court of the house of the LORD, and the porch of the house.
And King Solomon sent and brought Hiram from Tyre.

He was the son of a widow from the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a worker in bronze. He was filled with wisdom and skill and knowledge to do any work in bronze; and he came to King Solomon and did all his work.
And he cast the two pillars of bronze: eighteen cubits was the height of the one pillar, and a line of twelve cubits went round the second pillar.
And he made two capitals of cast bronze to set on the tops of the pillars: five cubits was the height of the one capital, and five cubits the height of the second capital.
There were networks, the work of a network, and festoons, the work of chains, for the capitals that were on the top of the pillars: seven for the one capital and seven for the second capital.
And he made the pillars, and two rows all around on the one network, to cover the capitals that were on top of the pomegranates; and so he did for the second capital.
And the capitals that were on the top of the pillars were a work of lilies, in the porch: four cubits.
And the capitals were on the two pillars, also above, close to the bulge that was beside the network; and the pomegranates were two hundred, in rows all around, on the second capital.
And he set up the pillars at the porch of the temple: he set up the right-hand pillar and called its name Jakin, and he set up the left-hand pillar and called its name Boaz.
And on the top of the pillars was a work of lilies. And the work of the pillars was complete.
And he made the sea of cast metal: ten cubits from lip to lip, circular all around; five cubits in height; and a measuring line of thirty cubits went round it all about.
And gourds were beneath its lip all around, encircling it — ten to a cubit — surrounding the sea all around; the gourds were in two rows, cast when it was cast.
It stood on twelve oxen: three facing north, three facing west, three facing south and three facing east; the sea was on top of them, and all their hindquarters were inward.
And its thickness was a handbreadth, and its lip was like the work of the lip of a cup, a lily blossom; it held two thousand baths.
And he made the ten stands of bronze: four cubits was the length of the one stand, four cubits its breadth, and three cubits its height.
And this was the work of the stand: they had rims, and there were rims between the crossbars.
And on the rims that were between the crossbars were lions, oxen and cherubim; and on the crossbars there was a base above; and beneath the lions and the oxen were garlands of hanging work.
And the one stand had four bronze wheels and bronze axles; and its four feet had supports. Beneath the washbasin were the cast supports, and beside each one were garlands.

And its opening, from inside the capital and upward, was a cubit; and its opening was round, the work of a base, a cubit and a half; and on its opening also were carvings; and their rims were square, not round.
And the four wheels were beneath the rims, and the axle-supports of the wheels were in the stand; and the height of the one wheel was a cubit and a half.
And the work of the wheels was like the work of a chariot wheel: their axle-supports, their rims, their spokes and their hubs — the whole was cast.
And four supports were at the four corners of each stand; the supports were of one piece with the stand.
And at the top of the stand there was a half-cubit in height, round all about; and on the top of the stand its axle-supports and its rims were of one piece with it.
And he engraved on the plates of its axle-supports and on its rims cherubim, lions and palm trees, according to the clear space of each, with garlands all around.
In this way he made the ten stands: one casting, one measurement, one shape for all of them.
And he made ten washbasins of bronze: each washbasin held forty baths, each washbasin was four cubits, and there was one washbasin on each of the ten stands.
And he set the stands, five on the right side of the house and five on the left side of the house; and the sea he set on the right side of the house, towards the east, opposite the south.
And Hiram made the washbasins and the shovels and the basins. So Hiram finished doing all the work that he did for King Solomon on the house of the LORD:
two pillars; the two bowls of the capitals that were on the top of the pillars; the two networks to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were on the top of the pillars;
and the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks — two rows of pomegranates for each network — to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were on the face of the pillars;
and the ten stands, and the ten washbasins on the stands;
and the one sea, and the twelve oxen under the sea;
and the pots and the shovels and the basins. And all these articles that Hiram made for King Solomon for the house of the LORD were of polished bronze.
In the plain of the Jordan the king cast them, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zarethan.
And Solomon left all the articles unweighed, because they were so very many; the weight of the bronze was not ascertained.
And Solomon made all the articles that were in the house of the LORD: the altar of gold; the table of gold on which was the bread of the presence;
and the lampstands of refined gold, five on the right and five on the left, before the innermost room; and the blossoms and the lamps and the tongs, of gold;

and the bowls and the snuffers and the basins and the pans and the firepans, of refined gold; and the sockets for the doors of the inner house, for the holy of holies, and for the doors of the house of the temple, of gold.

So all the work that King Solomon did on the house of the LORD was complete. And Solomon brought in the holy things of David his father — the silver and the gold and the articles — and put them in the treasuries of the house of the LORD.

1 kings_8.t: Then Solomon called together the elders of Israel, all the heads of the tribes, the leaders of the ancestral houses of the Israelites, to King Solomon in Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the city of David — that is Zion.
And every man of Israel assembled to King Solomon in the month of Ethanim, at the festival — that is the seventh month.
And all the elders of Israel came, and the priests lifted the ark.
And they brought up the ark of the LORD and the tent of meeting and all the holy articles that were in the tent; the priests and the Levites brought them up.
And King Solomon and all the congregation of Israel who had gathered to him were with him before the ark, sacrificing sheep and cattle that could not be counted or numbered for multitude.
And the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place, to the innermost room of the house, to the holy of holies, beneath the wings of the cherubim.
For the cherubim were spreading out their wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubim covered the ark and its poles from above.
And the poles were long, and the heads of the poles were visible from the holy place in front of the innermost room, but they were not visible outside; and they have been there until this day.
There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets of stone that Moses placed there at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the Israelites when they came out of the land of Egypt.
And when the priests came out from the holy place, the cloud filled the house of the LORD.
And the priests were not able to stand to serve because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD.
Then Solomon said: 'The LORD has said that he would dwell in thick darkness.'
'I have surely built you an exalted house, a place for you to dwell in for ever.'
And the king turned his face and blessed all the assembly of Israel, and all the assembly of Israel was standing.
And he said: 'Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who spoke with his mouth to David my father and with his hand has fulfilled it, saying:'

'Since the day I brought out my people Israel from Egypt, I did not choose a city out of all the tribes of Israel in which to build a house for my name to be there; but I chose David to be over my people Israel.'
'And it was in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.'
'And the LORD said to David my father, "Because it was in your heart to build a house for my name, you did well that it was in your heart."'
'"Only, you yourself shall not build the house; but your son who comes out from your loins — he shall build the house for my name."'

'And the LORD has established his word that he spoke; and I have arisen in place of David my father and have taken my seat on the throne of Israel, just as the LORD said, and I have built the house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.'
'And I have set there a place for the ark, where the covenant of the LORD is, which he made with our fathers when he brought them out of the land of Egypt.'
And Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD, in front of all the assembly of Israel, and spread out his palms towards the heavens.

And he said: 'LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like you in the heavens above or on the earth beneath, keeping the covenant and the steadfast love with your servants who walk before you with all their heart;'
'you who have kept for your servant David my father what you promised him — you spoke with your mouth and with your hand you have fulfilled it, as at this day.'

'And now, LORD, God of Israel, keep for your servant David my father what you promised him: "There shall not be cut off from you a man before me sitting on the throne of Israel" — only if your sons keep their way, to walk before me just as you have walked before me.'
'And now, God of Israel, let your word be established, which you spoke to your servant David my father.'
'But will God really dwell on the earth? Behold, the heavens and the heaven of heavens cannot contain you — how much less this house that I have built!'
'Yet turn to the prayer of your servant and to his supplication, LORD my God, to listen to the cry and to the prayer that your servant is praying before you today,'
'so that your eyes may be open towards this house night and day, towards the place of which you said, "My name shall be there," to listen to the prayer that your servant prays towards this place.'

'And listen to the supplication of your servant and of your people Israel, which they pray towards this place; and you yourself will hear in the place of your dwelling, in the heavens — and you will hear and forgive.'
'When a man sins against his neighbour and an oath is imposed on him to put him under oath, and he comes and swears before your altar in this house —'

'then hear in the heavens and act, and judge your servants: condemning the guilty by bringing his conduct on his own head, and declaring the righteous righteous by giving him according to his righteousness.'
'When your people Israel are defeated before an enemy because they sin against you, and they turn back to you and give thanks to your name and pray and seek favour before you in this house —'
'then hear in the heavens and forgive the sin of your people Israel, and bring them back to the ground that you gave to their fathers.'
'When the heavens are shut up and there is no rain because they sin against you, and they pray towards this place and give thanks to your name and turn back from their sin because you afflict them —'

'then hear in the heavens and forgive the sin of your servants and of your people Israel, when you teach them the good way in which they should walk; and give rain on your land that you gave to your people as an inheritance.'
'When there is famine in the land, when there is pestilence, blight, mildew, locust or grasshopper; when an enemy besieges them in the land of their towns — any plague, any sickness —'
'any prayer, any supplication that comes from any human being, from all your people Israel, each knowing the plague of his own heart and spreading out his palms towards this house —'

'then hear in the heavens, the place of your dwelling, and forgive and act, and give to each according to all his ways, since you know his heart — for you alone know the heart of all the children of humankind —'
'so that they may fear you all the days that they live on the face of the ground that you gave to our fathers.'
'And also the foreigner, who is not of your people Israel but comes from a distant land for the sake of your name —'
'for they will hear of your great name and your mighty hand and your outstretched arm — and he comes and prays towards this house —'

'then hear in the heavens, the place of your dwelling, and do according to all that the foreigner calls to you for — so that all the peoples of the earth may know your name, to fear you as your people Israel do, and to know that your name has been called over this house that I have built.'
'When your people go out to battle against their enemy by the way that you send them, and they pray to the LORD towards the city that you have chosen and the house that I have built for your name —'
'then hear in the heavens their prayer and their supplication, and maintain their cause.'

'When they sin against you — for there is no human being who does not sin — and you are angry with them and give them up before an enemy, and their captors take them captive to the land of the enemy, far or near,'

'and they take it to heart in the land where they have been taken captive, and they turn back and seek favour before you in the land of their captors, saying, "We have sinned and done wrong, we have acted wickedly" —'

'and they return to you with all their heart and with all their soul, in the land of their enemies who took them captive, and they pray to you towards their land that you gave to their fathers, the city that you have chosen and the house that I have built for your name —'
'then hear in the heavens, the place of your dwelling, their prayer and their supplication, and maintain their cause;'

'and forgive your people who have sinned against you, and all their transgressions by which they transgressed against you; and make them objects of compassion before their captors, so that they will have compassion on them.'
'for they are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out of Egypt, out of the midst of the iron furnace.'
'so that your eyes may be open to the supplication of your servant and to the supplication of your people Israel, to listen to them whenever they call to you.'

'For you yourself separated them for yourself as an inheritance from all the peoples of the earth, just as you spoke by the hand of Moses your servant when you brought our fathers out of Egypt, Lord GOD.'

And when Solomon had finished praying to the LORD all this prayer and supplication, he rose from before the altar of the LORD, from kneeling on his knees with his palms spread out towards the heavens.
And he stood and blessed all the assembly of Israel with a loud voice:
'Blessed be the LORD, who has given rest to his people Israel according to all that he promised; not one word has failed of all his good promise that he spoke by the hand of Moses his servant.'
'May the LORD our God be with us, just as he was with our fathers; may he not forsake us or abandon us,'
'to incline our heart to him, to walk in all his ways and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgements, which he commanded our fathers.'

'And may these words of mine, with which I have sought favour before the LORD, be near to the LORD our God day and night, to maintain the cause of his servant and the cause of his people Israel as each day requires;'
'so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the LORD is God; there is no other.'
'And let your heart be complete with the LORD our God, to walk in his statutes and to keep his commandments, as at this day.'
And the king and all Israel with him were offering sacrifice before the LORD.

And Solomon offered as the sacrifice of the peace offerings that he sacrificed to the LORD: twenty-two thousand cattle and a hundred and twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the Israelites dedicated the house of the LORD.

On that day the king consecrated the middle of the court that was before the house of the LORD, because he offered there the burnt offering and the grain offering and the fat of the peace offerings; for the bronze altar that was before the LORD was too small to hold the burnt offering, the grain offering and the fat of the peace offerings.
And Solomon observed the festival at that time, and all Israel with him — a great assembly, from Lebo-hamath to the wadi of Egypt — before the LORD our God, seven days and seven days: fourteen days.

On the eighth day he sent the people away, and they blessed the king; and they went to their tents joyful and glad of heart for all the good that the LORD had done for David his servant and for Israel his people.

1 kings_9.t: And when Solomon had finished building the house of the LORD and the king's house, and all that Solomon desired and delighted to do,
the LORD appeared to Solomon a second time, just as he had appeared to him at Gibeon.

And the LORD said to him: 'I have heard your prayer and your supplication that you made before me. I have consecrated this house that you have built, to put my name there for ever; and my eyes and my heart will be there all the days.'

'And as for you, if you will walk before me just as David your father walked, in integrity of heart and in uprightness, doing according to all that I have commanded you, and keeping my statutes and my judgements,'
'then I will establish the throne of your kingdom over Israel for ever, just as I promised concerning David your father: "There shall not be cut off from you a man on the throne of Israel."'
'But if you and your sons surely turn back from following me and do not keep my commandments and my statutes that I have set before you, and you go and serve other gods and bow down to them,'

'then I will cut off Israel from the face of the ground that I have given them; and the house that I have consecrated for my name I will cast out from before me, and Israel will become a byword and a taunt among all the peoples.'
'And this house will be most high; everyone who passes by it will be appalled and will hiss, and they will say, "Why has the LORD done thus to this land and to this house?"'

'And they will say, "Because they forsook the LORD their God, who brought their fathers out of the land of Egypt, and took hold of other gods and bowed down to them and served them — therefore the LORD has brought all this calamity upon them."'
And at the end of twenty years, in which Solomon had built the two houses — the house of the LORD and the king's house —
— Hiram king of Tyre having supported Solomon with cedar timber and cypress timber and with gold, according to all his desire — then King Solomon gave Hiram twenty cities in the land of Galilee.
And Hiram came out from Tyre to see the cities that Solomon had given him, and they were not pleasing in his eyes.
And he said, 'What are these cities that you have given me, my brother?' And they have been called the land of Cabul until this day.
And Hiram had sent the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold.
And this is the account of the forced labour that King Solomon raised, to build the house of the LORD and his own house and the Millo and the wall of Jerusalem, and Hazor and Megiddo and Gezer.
Pharaoh king of Egypt had gone up and captured Gezer and burned it with fire, and had killed the Canaanites dwelling in the city; and he had given it as a dowry to his daughter, Solomon's wife.
So Solomon rebuilt Gezer, and lower Beth-horon,
and Baalath, and Tadmor in the wilderness, in the land,

and all the storage cities that belonged to Solomon, the cities of the chariotry and the cities of the horsemen — and whatever Solomon desired to build in Jerusalem and in Lebanon and in all the land of his dominion.
All the people who remained of the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, who were not of the Israelites —
their descendants who were left after them in the land, whom the Israelites had not been able to devote to destruction — these Solomon raised as a forced labour force, until this day.
