Look, days are coming when I will cut off your arm and the arm of the house of your ancestor, so that there will not be an old man in your house.
And you will look on the distress of my dwelling, in all the good that he does to Israel; and there will not be an old man in your house, ever.
And a man of yours I will not cut off from my altar, only to make your eyes fail and to grieve your being; and all the increase of your house will die as men.
And this will be the sign for you, which will come upon your two sons, upon Hophni and Phinehas: on one day the two of them will die.
And I will raise up for myself a faithful priest; he will do according to what is in my heart and in my being, and I will build him a sure house, and he will walk before my anointed all the days.

And everyone who remains in your house will come to bow down to him for a payment of silver and a loaf of bread, and will say, 'Attach me, please, to one of the priestly offices, to eat a piece of bread.'

1 samuel_3.t: And the boy Samuel was serving the LORD before Eli. And the word of the LORD was rare in those days; vision was not widespread.
And on that day, when Eli was lying in his place — his eyes had begun to grow dim, so that he could not see —
and the lamp of God had not yet gone out, and Samuel was lying in the temple of the LORD, where the ark of God was —
the LORD called to Samuel; and he said, 'Here I am.'
And he ran to Eli and said, 'Here I am, for you called me.' And he said, 'I did not call. Go back, lie down.' And he went and lay down.
And the LORD called again, 'Samuel!' And Samuel rose and went to Eli and said, 'Here I am, for you called me.' And he said, 'I did not call, my son. Go back, lie down.'
Now Samuel did not yet know the LORD, and the word of the LORD had not yet been revealed to him.
And the LORD called Samuel again, a third time. And he rose and went to Eli and said, 'Here I am, for you called me.' And Eli understood that the LORD was calling the boy.
And Eli said to Samuel, 'Go, lie down; and if he calls to you, say, "Speak, LORD, for your servant is listening."' And Samuel went and lay down in his place.
And the LORD came and stood, and called as at the other times, 'Samuel! Samuel!' And Samuel said, 'Speak, for your servant is listening.'
And the LORD said to Samuel, 'Look, I am about to do a thing in Israel at which both ears of everyone who hears it will tingle.'
On that day I will carry out against Eli all that I have spoken concerning his house, from beginning to end.
And I have told him that I am about to judge his house for ever, for the iniquity that he knew: that his sons were bringing a curse upon themselves, and he did not rebuke them.
And therefore I have sworn to the house of Eli that the iniquity of the house of Eli shall not be atoned for by sacrifice or by offering, for ever.
And Samuel lay until the morning, and he opened the doors of the house of the LORD; and Samuel was afraid to tell the vision to Eli.
And Eli called Samuel and said, 'Samuel, my son.' And he said, 'Here I am.'
And he said, 'What is the word that he spoke to you? Do not hide it from me. So may God do to you, and more also, if you hide from me a single word of all that he spoke to you.'
And Samuel told him all the words and did not hide anything from him; and he said, 'He is the LORD; let him do what is good in his eyes.'
And Samuel grew up, and the LORD was with him, and he let none of his words fall to the ground.
And all Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, knew that Samuel was established as a prophet to the LORD.
And the LORD appeared again at Shiloh, for the LORD revealed himself to Samuel at Shiloh by the word of the LORD.

1 samuel_4.t: And the word of Samuel came to all Israel. And Israel went out to meet the Philistines in battle, and they encamped at Ebenezer, and the Philistines encamped at Aphek.
And the Philistines deployed to meet Israel, and the battle spread, and Israel was defeated before the Philistines; and they struck down about four thousand men in the battle line, in the field.

And the people came into the camp, and the elders of Israel said, 'Why has the LORD defeated us today before the Philistines? Let us bring to ourselves from Shiloh the ark of the covenant of the LORD, that it may come among us and deliver us from the hand of our enemies.'

And the people sent to Shiloh, and they carried from there the ark of the covenant of the LORD of hosts, who sits upon the cherubim; and there the two sons of Eli were with the ark of the covenant of God, Hophni and Phinehas.
And when the ark of the covenant of the LORD came into the camp, all Israel shouted a great shout, and the ground shook.
And the Philistines heard the sound of the shout and said, 'What is this sound of a great shout in the camp of the Hebrews?' And they knew that the ark of the LORD had come into the camp.
And the Philistines were afraid, for they said, 'A god has come into the camp.' And they said, 'Woe to us! Nothing like this has happened before.'
Woe to us! Who will deliver us from the hand of these mighty gods? These are the gods who struck Egypt with every plague in the wilderness.
Show yourselves strong and be men, O Philistines, lest you serve the Hebrews as they have served you. Be men, and fight!
And the Philistines fought, and Israel was defeated, and each fled to his tents; and the slaughter was very great, and there fell of Israel thirty thousand foot soldiers.
And the ark of God was taken, and the two sons of Eli died, Hophni and Phinehas.
And a man of Benjamin ran from the battle line and came to Shiloh that day, with his garments torn and earth on his head.
And when he came, Eli was sitting on his seat beside the road, watching, for his heart was trembling for the ark of God. And the man came to tell it in the city, and all the city cried out.
And Eli heard the sound of the outcry and said, 'What is this sound of uproar?' And the man hurried and came and told Eli.
Now Eli was ninety-eight years old, and his eyes were fixed, and he could not see.
And the man said to Eli, 'I am the one who has come from the battle line; I fled from the battle line today.' And he said, 'What has happened, my son?'

And the bearer of news answered, 'Israel has fled before the Philistines, and there has been a great slaughter among the people; and your two sons have died, Hophni and Phinehas; and the ark of God has been taken.'
And when he mentioned the ark of God, Eli fell backwards off his seat, beside the gate, and his neck was broken and he died; for the man was old and heavy. And he had judged Israel forty years.

And his daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, was pregnant, about to give birth; and she heard the report that the ark of God had been taken and that her father-in-law and her husband had died, and she crouched down and gave birth, for her pangs had come upon her.
And about the time of her death, those standing over her spoke: 'Do not be afraid, for you have borne a son.' And she did not answer, and she paid no attention.
And she called the boy Ichabod, saying, 'Glory has gone into exile from Israel' — because the ark of God had been taken, and because of her father-in-law and her husband.
And she said, 'Glory has gone into exile from Israel, for the ark of God has been taken.'

1 samuel_5.t: And the Philistines took the ark of God and brought it from Ebenezer to Ashdod.
And the Philistines took the ark of God, brought it into the house of Dagon and set it beside Dagon.
And the Ashdodites rose early the next day, and there was Dagon, fallen on his face to the ground before the ark of the LORD. And they took Dagon and returned him to his place.

And they rose early in the morning the next day, and there was Dagon, fallen on his face to the ground before the ark of the LORD; and the head of Dagon and the two palms of his hands were cut off, on the threshold — only Dagon was left of him.
Therefore the priests of Dagon and all who come into the house of Dagon do not tread on the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod, to this day.
And the hand of the LORD was heavy against the Ashdodites, and he devastated them; and he struck them with tumours — Ashdod and its territories.
And the men of Ashdod saw that it was so, and they said, 'The ark of the God of Israel shall not remain with us, for his hand is hard upon us and upon Dagon our god.'

And they sent and gathered all the rulers of the Philistines to them and said, 'What shall we do with the ark of the God of Israel?' And they said, 'Let the ark of the God of Israel be brought round to Gath.' And they brought the ark of the God of Israel round.
And after they had brought it round, the hand of the LORD was against the city — a very great panic; and he struck the men of the city, from small to great, and tumours broke out on them.
And they sent the ark of God to Ekron. And when the ark of God came to Ekron, the Ekronites cried out, saying, 'They have brought round to me the ark of the God of Israel, to kill me and my people!'

And they sent and gathered all the rulers of the Philistines and said, 'Send away the ark of the God of Israel, and let it return to its own place, and let it not kill me and my people.' For there was a panic of death in all the city; the hand of God was very heavy there.
And the men who did not die were struck with tumours; and the cry of the city went up to the heavens.

1 samuel_6.t: And the ark of the LORD was in the region of the Philistines seven months.
And the Philistines summoned the priests and the diviners and said, 'What shall we do with the ark of the LORD? Make known to us how we shall send it to its place.'

And they said, 'If you are sending away the ark of the God of Israel, do not send it away empty, but you shall surely send back to him a guilt offering. Then you will be healed, and it will be known to you why his hand does not turn aside from you.'

And they said, 'What is the guilt offering that we shall send back to him?' And they said, 'By the number of the rulers of the Philistines — five gold tumours and five gold mice; for one plague was on all of them and on your rulers.'

And you shall make images of your tumours and images of your mice that are ruining the land, and you shall give glory to the God of Israel; perhaps he will lighten his hand from upon you and from upon your gods and from upon your land.
And why will you harden your heart, as Egypt and Pharaoh hardened their heart? Was it not when he had dealt wantonly with them that they sent them away, and they went?
And now, take and make one new cart, and two nursing cows on which no yoke has ever come; harness the cows to the cart, and take their calves back home, away from them.

And you shall take the ark of the LORD and put it on the cart; and the articles of gold that you are sending back to him as a guilt offering you shall put in a box beside it. And you shall send it away, and let it go.

And you shall watch: if it goes up by the way of its own territory, to Beth-shemesh, then he has done us this great harm; and if not, then we shall know that it was not his hand that touched us — it was chance that happened to us.
And the men did so. They took two nursing cows and harnessed them to the cart, and shut their calves up at home.
And they put the ark of the LORD on the cart, with the box, the gold mice and the images of their tumours.

And the cows went straight on the road, on the road to Beth-shemesh; they kept to one highway, going and lowing, and they did not turn aside to the right or to the left. And the rulers of the Philistines went after them as far as the border of Beth-shemesh.
Now the people of Beth-shemesh were harvesting the wheat harvest in the valley; and they lifted up their eyes and saw the ark, and they rejoiced to see it.

And the cart came into the field of Joshua the Beth-shemeshite and stopped there; and a large stone was there. And they split up the wood of the cart, and offered the cows up as a burnt offering to the LORD.

And the Levites brought down the ark of the LORD and the box that was with it, in which were the articles of gold, and put them on the large stone. And the men of Beth-shemesh offered up burnt offerings and sacrificed sacrifices that day to the LORD.
And the five rulers of the Philistines saw it, and they returned to Ekron that day.
And these are the gold tumours that the Philistines sent back as a guilt offering to the LORD: for Ashdod one, for Gaza one, for Ashkelon one, for Gath one, for Ekron one.

And the gold mice were the number of all the cities of the Philistines belonging to the five rulers, from fortified city to village of the open country — and as far as Abel the great, on which they set down the ark of the LORD, to this day, in the field of Joshua the Beth-shemeshite.

And he struck down among the men of Beth-shemesh, because they had looked into the ark of the LORD; and he struck down among the people seventy men, fifty thousand men. And the people mourned, because the LORD had struck the people with a great blow.
And the men of Beth-shemesh said, 'Who is able to stand before the LORD, this holy God? And to whom shall he go up from us?'
And they sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kiriath-jearim, saying, 'The Philistines have brought back the ark of the LORD. Come down and take it up to yourselves.'

1 samuel_7.t: And the men of Kiriath-jearim came and took up the ark of the LORD and brought it to the house of Abinadab on the hill; and they consecrated Eleazar his son to keep the ark of the LORD.
And from the day the ark came to rest at Kiriath-jearim, the days grew many — they were twenty years; and all the house of Israel mourned after the LORD.

And Samuel said to all the house of Israel, 'If with all your heart you are turning back to the LORD, remove the foreign gods from among you, and the Ashtaroth, and direct your heart to the LORD and serve him alone; and he will deliver you from the hand of the Philistines.'
And the people of Israel removed the Baals and the Ashtaroth, and served the LORD alone.
And Samuel said, 'Gather all Israel to Mizpah, and I will pray for you to the LORD.'

And they gathered at Mizpah and drew water and poured it out before the LORD, and they fasted that day and said there, 'We have sinned against the LORD.' And Samuel judged the people of Israel at Mizpah.

And the Philistines heard that the people of Israel had gathered at Mizpah, and the rulers of the Philistines went up against Israel; and the people of Israel heard, and they were afraid of the Philistines.
And the people of Israel said to Samuel, 'Do not keep silent toward us, but cry out to the LORD our God, that he may deliver us from the hand of the Philistines.'
And Samuel took one nursing lamb and offered it up as a whole burnt offering to the LORD; and Samuel cried out to the LORD for Israel, and the LORD answered him.

And while Samuel was offering up the burnt offering, the Philistines drew near for battle against Israel; and the LORD thundered with a great sound that day against the Philistines and routed them, and they were defeated before Israel.
And the men of Israel went out from Mizpah and pursued the Philistines, and struck them down as far as below Beth-car.
And Samuel took a stone and set it between Mizpah and Shen, and called its name Ebenezer, and said, 'Until now the LORD has helped us.'
And the Philistines were brought low, and they did not come again into the territory of Israel; and the hand of the LORD was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.

And the cities that the Philistines had taken from Israel were returned to Israel, from Ekron as far as Gath; and Israel delivered their territory from the hand of the Philistines. And there was peace between Israel and the Amorites.
And Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.
And he would go year after year on a circuit to Bethel, Gilgal and Mizpah, and he judged Israel in all these places.
And his return was to Ramah, for his house was there, and there he judged Israel; and he built there an altar to the LORD.

1 samuel_8.t: And when Samuel was old, he made his sons judges over Israel.
And the name of his firstborn son was Joel, and the name of his second was Abijah; they were judges in Beersheba.
And his sons did not walk in his ways; they turned aside after unjust gain, took bribes, and turned justice aside.
And all the elders of Israel gathered together and came to Samuel at Ramah.
And they said to him, 'Look, you have grown old, and your sons have not walked in your ways. Now appoint for us a king to judge us, like all the nations.'
And the matter was displeasing in the eyes of Samuel when they said, 'Give us a king to judge us.' And Samuel prayed to the LORD.
And the LORD said to Samuel, 'Listen to the voice of the people in all that they say to you; for they have not rejected you, but they have rejected me from reigning over them.'
Just as they have done in all their deeds from the day I brought them up from Egypt until this day — forsaking me and serving other gods — so they are doing also to you.
And now, listen to their voice. Only, you shall solemnly warn them and tell them the right of the king who will reign over them.
And Samuel spoke all the words of the LORD to the people who were asking him for a king.

And he said, 'This will be the right of the king who will reign over you. He will take your sons and set them for himself in his chariotry and among his horsemen, and they will run before his chariot;
and to appoint for himself commanders of thousands and commanders of fifties, and to plough his ploughing and reap his reaping, and to make his weapons of war and the equipment of his chariotry.
And he will take your daughters for perfumers, cooks and bakers.
And he will take your fields, your vineyards and your best olive groves, and give them to his servants.
And he will take a tenth of your grain and your vineyards, and give it to his officials and his servants.
And he will take your male and female servants and your best young men and your donkeys, and use them for his work.
He will take a tenth of your flocks; and you yourselves will become his servants.
And you will cry out on that day because of your king whom you have chosen for yourselves; and the LORD will not answer you on that day.
But the people refused to listen to the voice of Samuel, and they said, 'No! There shall be a king over us,
and we also will be like all the nations; and our king will judge us and go out before us and fight our battles.'
And Samuel heard all the words of the people, and he repeated them in the hearing of the LORD.
And the LORD said to Samuel, 'Listen to their voice, and make a king reign over them.' And Samuel said to the men of Israel, 'Go, each to his own city.'

1 samuel_9.t: And there was a man from Benjamin, and his name was Kish son of Abiel son of Zeror son of Becorath son of Aphiah, a Benjaminite, a man of substance.
And he had a son whose name was Saul, a young man and handsome; and there was no man among the people of Israel better than he. From his shoulders up he was taller than all the people.
And the donkeys of Kish, Saul's father, were lost. And Kish said to Saul his son, 'Take one of the servants with you, and arise, go and seek the donkeys.'

And he passed through the hill country of Ephraim and through the land of Shalishah, and they did not find them. And they passed through the land of Shaalim, and there was nothing; and he passed through the land of the Benjaminites, and they did not find them.
They came into the land of Zuph, and Saul said to his servant who was with him, 'Come, let us turn back, or my father will stop worrying about the donkeys and be anxious for us.'
And he said to him, 'Look, there is a man of God in this city, and the man is honoured; all that he speaks certainly comes to pass. Let us go there; perhaps he will tell us the way we should go.'
And Saul said to his servant, 'But if we go, what shall we bring to the man? The bread is used up from our bags, and there is no gift to bring to the man of God. What is with us?'
And the servant answered Saul again, 'Look, I have in my hand a quarter of a shekel of silver; I will give it to the man of God, and he will tell us our way.'
(Formerly in Israel, this is what a man said when he went to consult God: 'Come, let us go to the seer' — for the prophet of today was formerly called the seer.)
And Saul said to his servant, 'Your word is good. Come, let us go.' And they went to the city where the man of God was.
As they were going up the ascent to the city, they found young women coming out to draw water; and they said to them, 'Is the seer here?'
And they answered them, 'He is; he is just ahead of you. Hurry now, for today he has come to the city, because there is a sacrifice today for the people at the high place.'

As soon as you come into the city you will find him, before he goes up to the high place to eat; for the people will not eat until he comes, because he blesses the sacrifice, and after that those who are invited eat. Go up now, for at this very time you will find him.
And they went up to the city. As they were coming into the midst of the city, Samuel was coming out to meet them, to go up to the high place.
Now the LORD had uncovered the ear of Samuel one day before Saul came, saying:

'About this time tomorrow I will send to you a man from the land of Benjamin, and you shall anoint him as leader over my people Israel; and he will deliver my people from the hand of the Philistines. For I have seen my people, for their cry has come to me.'
And Samuel saw Saul, and the LORD answered him: 'Here is the man of whom I spoke to you; this one shall rule over my people.'
And Saul approached Samuel in the middle of the gate and said, 'Tell me, please, where is the house of the seer?'
And Samuel answered Saul, 'I am the seer. Go up before me to the high place, and you shall eat with me today; and in the morning I will send you away, and I will tell you all that is in your heart.'

And as for the donkeys lost to you three days ago, do not set your heart on them, for they have been found. And to whom does all the desire of Israel belong? Is it not to you and to all your father's house?
And Saul answered, 'Am I not a Benjaminite, from the smallest of the tribes of Israel? And is my clan not the least of all the clans of the tribes of Benjamin? Why have you spoken to me in this way?'
And Samuel took Saul and his servant and brought them into the room, and gave them a place at the head of those who were invited; and they were about thirty men.
And Samuel said to the cook, 'Give the portion that I gave you, of which I said to you, "Put it beside you."'

And the cook lifted up the thigh and what was on it, and set it before Saul; and he said, 'Here is what was left — set it before you and eat; for it has been kept for you for the appointed time, as I said, "I have invited the people."' And Saul ate with Samuel that day.
And they went down from the high place to the city; and he spoke with Saul on the roof.
And they rose early; and as the dawn came up, Samuel called to Saul on the roof, 'Arise, and I will send you away.' And Saul arose, and the two of them went outside, he and Samuel.

As they were going down at the edge of the city, Samuel said to Saul, 'Tell the servant to pass on ahead of us' — and he passed on — 'and you, stand still just now, and I will make you hear the word of God.'

1 samuel_10.t: And Samuel took the flask of oil and poured it on his head and kissed him, and said, 'Has not the LORD anointed you over his inheritance as leader?'

When you go from me today, you will find two men near Rachel's tomb in the territory of Benjamin, at Zelzah; and they will say to you, "The donkeys that you went to seek have been found. And now your father has left off the matter of the donkeys and is anxious about you, saying, 'What shall I do about my son?'"

And you will pass on from there and beyond, and come to the great tree of Tabor; and three men will find you there, going up to God at Bethel — one carrying three kids, one carrying three round loaves of bread, and one carrying a skin of wine.
And they will greet you and give you two loaves of bread, and you will take them from their hand.

After that you will come to Gibeah of God, where the garrisons of the Philistines are; and as you come there to the city you will meet a company of prophets coming down from the high place, with a harp, a tambourine, a flute and a lyre before them, and they will be prophesying.
And the spirit of the LORD will rush upon you, and you will prophesy with them, and you will be turned into another man.
And when these signs come to you, do for yourself whatever your hand finds, for God is with you.

And you shall go down before me to Gilgal; and I will come down to you to offer up burnt offerings and to sacrifice sacrifices of peace offerings. Seven days you shall wait until I come to you, and I will make known to you what you shall do.
And when he turned his shoulder to go from Samuel, God turned another heart for him; and all these signs came that day.
And they came there to Gibeah, and there was a company of prophets to meet him; and the spirit of God rushed upon him, and he prophesied in their midst.
And when all who knew him from before saw that he was prophesying with prophets, the people said to one another, 'What is this that has happened to the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?'
And a man from there answered, 'And who is their father?' Therefore it became a proverb: 'Is Saul also among the prophets?'
And he finished prophesying and came to the high place.
And Saul's uncle said to him and to his servant, 'Where did you go?' And he said, 'To seek the donkeys. And when we saw that they were not there, we went to Samuel.'
And Saul's uncle said, 'Tell me, please, what Samuel said to you.'
And Saul said to his uncle, 'He told us plainly that the donkeys had been found.' But the matter of the kingship, of which Samuel had spoken, he did not tell him.
And Samuel called the people together to the LORD at Mizpah.

And he said to the people of Israel, 'Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: I brought Israel up from Egypt, and I delivered you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of all the kingdoms that were oppressing you.

And you today have rejected your God, who is your deliverer from all your calamities and your troubles; and you have said to him, "You shall set a king over us." And now, present yourselves before the LORD by your tribes and by your thousands.'
And Samuel brought near all the tribes of Israel, and the tribe of Benjamin was taken.
And he brought near the tribe of Benjamin by its clans, and the clan of the Matrite was taken; and Saul son of Kish was taken. And they sought him, and he was not found.
And they enquired again of the LORD, 'Has the man come here yet?' And the LORD said, 'He is hiding himself among the baggage.'
And they ran and took him from there, and he presented himself in the midst of the people; and he was taller than all the people from his shoulders up.
And Samuel said to all the people, 'Do you see the one whom the LORD has chosen? For there is none like him among all the people.' And all the people shouted and said, 'Long live the king!'
And Samuel spoke to the people the right of the kingship, and wrote it in the book and set it before the LORD. And Samuel sent all the people away, each to his house.
And Saul also went to his house at Gibeah; and the force whose heart God had touched went with him.
But sons of worthlessness said, 'How will this one deliver us?' And they despised him and brought him no gift. And he was like one who kept silent.

1 samuel_11.t: And Nahash the Ammonite went up and encamped against Jabesh-gilead; and all the men of Jabesh said to Nahash, 'Make a covenant with us, and we will serve you.'
And Nahash the Ammonite said to them, 'On this condition I will make it with you: by gouging out every right eye of yours; and I will make it a reproach on all Israel.'
And the elders of Jabesh said to him, 'Leave us seven days, and let us send messengers through all the territory of Israel; and if there is no one to deliver us, then we will come out to you.'
And the messengers came to Gibeah of Saul and spoke the words in the hearing of the people; and all the people lifted up their voice and wept.
And Saul was coming after the cattle from the field; and Saul said, 'What is the matter with the people, that they are weeping?' And they recounted to him the words of the men of Jabesh.
And the spirit of God rushed upon Saul when he heard these words, and his anger burned exceedingly.

And he took a pair of oxen and cut them in pieces, and sent them through all the territory of Israel by the hand of the messengers, saying, 'Whoever does not come out after Saul and after Samuel, so shall it be done to his oxen.' And the dread of the LORD fell on the people, and they came out as one man.
And he mustered them at Bezek; and the people of Israel were three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah thirty thousand.

And they said to the messengers who had come, 'Thus you shall say to the men of Jabesh-gilead: Tomorrow deliverance will be yours, when the sun is hot.' And the messengers came and told the men of Jabesh, and they were glad.
And the men of Jabesh said, 'Tomorrow we will come out to you, and you shall do to us whatever is good in your eyes.'

And the next day Saul set the people in three companies; and they came into the midst of the camp in the morning watch and struck down Ammon until the heat of the day. And those who were left were scattered, and no two of them were left together.
And the people said to Samuel, 'Who is the one who said, "Shall Saul reign over us?" Give up the men, and we will put them to death.'
And Saul said, 'No one shall be put to death on this day, for today the LORD has done deliverance in Israel.'
And Samuel said to the people, 'Come, let us go to Gilgal and renew the kingship there.'

And all the people went to Gilgal, and there they made Saul king before the LORD at Gilgal; and they sacrificed there sacrifices of peace offerings before the LORD, and Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced there exceedingly.

1 samuel_12.t: And Samuel said to all Israel, 'Look, I have listened to your voice in all that you said to me, and I have made a king reign over you.
And now the king is walking before you; and I am old and grey-haired, and my sons are with you. And I have walked before you from my youth until this day.

Here I am. Testify against me before the LORD and before his anointed: Whose ox have I taken, and whose donkey have I taken? Whom have I oppressed, and whom have I crushed? From whose hand have I taken a ransom, to hide my eyes with it? And I will restore it to you.'
And they said, 'You have not oppressed us, you have not crushed us, and you have not taken anything from the hand of anyone.'
And he said to them, 'The LORD is a witness against you, and his anointed is a witness this day, that you have found nothing in my hand.' And he said, 'He is a witness.'
And Samuel said to the people, 'It is the LORD, who appointed Moses and Aaron, and who brought your ancestors up from the land of Egypt.
And now, present yourselves, and let me enter into judgement with you before the LORD concerning all the righteous acts of the LORD that he did with you and with your ancestors.
When Jacob came to Egypt, your ancestors cried out to the LORD; and the LORD sent Moses and Aaron, and they brought your ancestors out of Egypt and settled them in this place.

And they forgot the LORD their God, and he sold them into the hand of Sisera, commander of the army of Hazor, and into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the king of Moab; and they fought against them.

And they cried out to the LORD and said, 'We have sinned, for we have forsaken the LORD and served the Baals and the Ashtaroth. And now deliver us from the hand of our enemies, and we will serve you.'
And the LORD sent Jerubbaal and Bedan and Jephthah and Samuel, and delivered you from the hand of your enemies round about; and you dwelt in security.
And you saw that Nahash king of the Ammonites was coming against you, and you said to me, 'No, but a king shall reign over us' — while the LORD your God was your king.
And now, here is the king whom you have chosen, whom you have asked for; and the LORD has set a king over you.
If you fear the LORD and serve him and listen to his voice, and do not rebel against the mouth of the LORD, then both you and the king who reigns over you will be after the LORD your God —
And if you do not listen to the voice of the LORD, and you rebel against the mouth of the LORD, then the hand of the LORD will be against you and against your ancestors.
Also now, stand and see this great thing that the LORD is about to do before your eyes.

Is it not the wheat harvest today? I will call to the LORD, and he will give thunder and rain; and know and see that your evil is great, which you have done in the eyes of the LORD by asking for yourselves a king.
And Samuel called to the LORD, and the LORD gave thunder and rain that day; and all the people feared the LORD and Samuel exceedingly.
And all the people said to Samuel, 'Pray for your servants to the LORD your God, and let us not die; for we have added to all our sins an evil, by asking for ourselves a king.'
And Samuel said to the people, 'Do not be afraid. You have done all this evil; nevertheless do not turn aside from following the LORD, but serve the LORD with all your heart.
And do not turn aside — for it would be after emptiness, which cannot benefit and cannot rescue, for they are emptiness.
For the LORD will not abandon his people, for the sake of his great name; for the LORD was pleased to make you a people for himself.
As for me also, far be it from me to sin against the LORD by ceasing to pray for you; and I will teach you the good and upright way.
Only fear the LORD and serve him in faithfulness with all your heart; for consider what great things he has done with you.
And if you still do evil, both you and your king will be swept away.

1 samuel_13.t: Saul was a year old when he became king, and he reigned two years over Israel.

And Saul chose for himself three thousand from Israel; two thousand were with Saul at Michmash and in the hill country of Bethel, and a thousand were with Jonathan at Gibeah of Benjamin. And the rest of the people he sent away, each to his tents.
And Jonathan struck the garrison of the Philistines that was at Geba, and the Philistines heard of it. And Saul blew the ram's horn throughout all the land, saying, 'Let the Hebrews hear!'
And all Israel heard it said, 'Saul has struck the garrison of the Philistines, and Israel has made itself odious among the Philistines.' And the people were summoned after Saul to Gilgal.

And the Philistines gathered to fight with Israel: thirty thousand chariots, six thousand horsemen, and a people like the sand on the seashore for multitude. And they came up and encamped at Michmash, east of Beth-aven.
And the men of Israel saw that they were in distress, for the people were hard pressed; and the people hid themselves in caves, in thickets, in rocks, in underground chambers and in cisterns.
And Hebrews crossed the Jordan to the land of Gad and Gilead; and Saul was still at Gilgal, and all the people trembled after him.
And he waited seven days, to the appointed time that Samuel had set; but Samuel did not come to Gilgal, and the people were scattering from him.
And Saul said, 'Bring near to me the burnt offering and the peace offerings.' And he offered up the burnt offering.
And as he finished offering up the burnt offering, Samuel was coming; and Saul went out to meet him, to bless him.

And Samuel said, 'What have you done?' And Saul said, 'Because I saw that the people were scattering from me, and you had not come at the appointed time of the days, and the Philistines were gathering at Michmash,
so I said, "Now the Philistines will come down against me at Gilgal, and I have not entreated the face of the LORD." And I forced myself, and offered up the burnt offering.'

And Samuel said to Saul, 'You have acted foolishly. You have not kept the commandment of the LORD your God, which he commanded you; for now the LORD would have established your kingdom over Israel for ever.

And now your kingdom will not stand. The LORD has sought for himself a man according to his own heart, and the LORD has appointed him as leader over his people, because you have not kept what the LORD commanded you.'
And Samuel arose and went up from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin. And Saul mustered the people who were found with him, about six hundred men.
And Saul and Jonathan his son and the people who were found with them were staying at Geba of Benjamin; and the Philistines encamped at Michmash.
And the raiding party went out from the camp of the Philistines in three companies: one company turned toward the road to Ophrah, to the land of Shual;
and one company turned toward the road to Beth-horon; and one company turned toward the road of the border that looks down over the Valley of Zeboim, toward the wilderness.
And a craftsman was not to be found in all the land of Israel, for the Philistines said, 'Lest the Hebrews make a sword or a spear.'
And all Israel would go down to the Philistines, each to sharpen his ploughshare, his mattock, his axe and his ploughshare.
And the charge was a pim for the ploughshares, the mattocks, the three-pronged fork and the axes, and to set the goad straight.
And so on the day of battle no sword or spear was found in the hand of any of the people who were with Saul and Jonathan; but it was found for Saul and for Jonathan his son.
And the garrison of the Philistines went out to the pass of Michmash.

1 samuel_14.t: And one day Jonathan son of Saul said to the young man who bore his armour, 'Come, let us cross over to the garrison of the Philistines on the other side over there.' But he did not tell his father.
And Saul was staying at the edge of Gibeah, under the pomegranate tree that is in Migron; and the people who were with him were about six hundred men.
And Ahijah son of Ahitub, the brother of Ichabod son of Phinehas son of Eli, the priest of the LORD at Shiloh, was bearing an ephod. And the people did not know that Jonathan had gone.

And between the passes by which Jonathan sought to cross over to the garrison of the Philistines, there was a rocky crag on one side and a rocky crag on the other; and the name of the one was Bozez and the name of the other Seneh.
The one crag stood as a pillar on the north, opposite Michmash, and the other on the south, opposite Geba.

And Jonathan said to the young man who bore his armour, 'Come, let us cross over to the garrison of these uncircumcised men. Perhaps the LORD will act for us, for there is no restraint on the LORD, to deliver by many or by few.'
And his armour-bearer said to him, 'Do all that is in your heart. Turn where you will; here I am with you, according to your heart.'
And Jonathan said, 'Look, we are crossing over to the men, and we will reveal ourselves to them.
If they say this to us, "Stand still until we reach you," then we will stand where we are, and we will not go up to them.
And if they say this, "Come up to us," then we will go up, for the LORD has given them into our hand; and this will be the sign for us.'
And the two of them revealed themselves to the garrison of the Philistines; and the Philistines said, 'Look, Hebrews are coming out of the holes where they have hidden themselves.'

And the men of the garrison answered Jonathan and his armour-bearer, 'Come up to us, and we will tell you something.' And Jonathan said to his armour-bearer, 'Come up after me, for the LORD has given them into the hand of Israel.'
And Jonathan went up on his hands and feet, with his armour-bearer after him; and they fell before Jonathan, and his armour-bearer was killing after him.
And the first slaughter that Jonathan and his armour-bearer struck was about twenty men, within about half a furrow of an acre of field.
And there was trembling in the camp, in the field, and among all the people; the garrison and the raiding party trembled too. And the earth quaked, and it became a trembling of God.
And the watchmen of Saul at Gibeah of Benjamin saw the multitude melting away and going this way and that.
And Saul said to the people who were with him, 'Muster now and see who has gone from us.' And they mustered, and Jonathan and his armour-bearer were not there.
And Saul said to Ahijah, 'Bring near the ark of God' — for the ark of God was on that day with the people of Israel.
And while Saul was speaking to the priest, the tumult in the camp of the Philistines went on growing and growing. And Saul said to the priest, 'Withdraw your hand.'
And Saul and all the people who were with him were called together, and they came to the battle; and each man's sword was against his neighbour — a very great panic.
And the Hebrews who had belonged to the Philistines as before, who had gone up with them into the camp round about — they too turned to be with Israel, who were with Saul and Jonathan.
And every man of Israel who had hidden himself in the hill country of Ephraim heard that the Philistines had fled, and they too pursued closely after them in the battle.
And the LORD delivered Israel that day, and the battle passed beyond Beth-aven.

And the men of Israel were hard pressed that day; for Saul had put the people under an oath, saying, 'Cursed be the man who eats food until the evening, until I have avenged myself on my enemies.' And none of the people tasted food.
And all the land came into the forest; and there was honey on the surface of the field.
And the people came into the forest, and there was a flow of honey; but no one put his hand to his mouth, for the people feared the oath.

But Jonathan had not heard when his father put the people under the oath; and he stretched out the end of the staff that was in his hand, dipped it in the honeycomb, and brought his hand back to his mouth, and his eyes brightened.
And a man from the people answered, 'Your father solemnly put the people under an oath, saying, "Cursed be the man who eats food today."' And the people were weary.
And Jonathan said, 'My father has troubled the land. See how my eyes have brightened because I tasted a little of this honey.
How much more, if the people had eaten freely today of the plunder of their enemies that they found! For as it is, the defeat among the Philistines has not been great.'
And they struck down the Philistines that day, from Michmash to Aijalon; and the people were very weary.
And the people rushed on the plunder and took sheep, cattle and calves, and slaughtered them on the ground; and the people ate with the blood.
And they told Saul, 'Look, the people are sinning against the LORD by eating with the blood.' And he said, 'You have acted treacherously. Roll a large stone to me today.'

And Saul said, 'Scatter among the people and say to them, "Bring near to me each his ox and each his sheep, and slaughter here and eat, and do not sin against the LORD by eating with the blood."' And all the people brought near, each his ox in his hand, that night, and slaughtered there.
And Saul built an altar to the LORD; this was the first altar he began to build to the LORD.

And Saul said, 'Let us go down after the Philistines by night and plunder among them until the light of the morning, and let us not leave a man among them.' And they said, 'Do all that is good in your eyes.' And the priest said, 'Let us draw near here to God.'
And Saul enquired of God, 'Shall I go down after the Philistines? Will you give them into the hand of Israel?' But he did not answer him that day.
And Saul said, 'Draw near here, all you chiefs of the people, and know and see how this sin has come about today.
For as the LORD lives, who delivers Israel, even if it is in Jonathan my son, he shall surely die.' And no one from all the people answered him.
And he said to all Israel, 'You shall be on one side, and I and Jonathan my son will be on the other.' And the people said to Saul, 'Do what is good in your eyes.'
And Saul said to the LORD, the God of Israel, 'Give Thummim.' And Jonathan and Saul were taken, and the people went out.
And Saul said, 'Cast between me and Jonathan my son.' And Jonathan was taken.
And Saul said to Jonathan, 'Tell me what you have done.' And Jonathan told him, 'I did indeed taste a little honey with the end of the staff that was in my hand. Here I am; I will die.'
And Saul said, 'So may God do, and more also — for you shall surely die, Jonathan.'

And the people said to Saul, 'Shall Jonathan die, who has done this great deliverance in Israel? Far be it! As the LORD lives, not one hair of his head shall fall to the ground, for he has acted with God this day.' And the people redeemed Jonathan, and he did not die.
And Saul went up from pursuing the Philistines, and the Philistines went to their own place.

And Saul took the kingship over Israel, and he waged war round about against all his enemies — against Moab, the Ammonites, Edom, the kings of Zobah and the Philistines; and wherever he turned, he routed them.
And he did valiantly and struck Amalek, and delivered Israel from the hand of those who plundered it.
And the sons of Saul were Jonathan, Ishvi and Malchi-shua; and the names of his two daughters were these: the name of the firstborn was Merab and the name of the younger Michal.
And the name of Saul's wife was Ahinoam daughter of Ahimaaz; and the name of the commander of his army was Abner son of Ner, Saul's uncle.
And Kish was Saul's father, and Ner the father of Abner was the son of Abiel.
And the war was severe against the Philistines all the days of Saul; and whenever Saul saw any mighty man or any man of strength, he gathered him to himself.

1 samuel_15.t: And Samuel said to Saul, 'It was I whom the LORD sent to anoint you as king over his people, over Israel. And now, listen to the voice of the words of the LORD.'
Thus says the LORD of hosts: 'I have taken account of what Amalek did to Israel, how it set itself against him on the way when he came up from Egypt.
Now go and strike Amalek, and devote to destruction all that it has; and do not spare it, but put to death man and woman, child and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and donkey.'
And Saul summoned the people and mustered them at Telaim: two hundred thousand foot soldiers, and ten thousand men of Judah.
And Saul came to the city of Amalek and lay in wait in the wadi.

And Saul said to the Kenites, 'Go, depart, go down from among the Amalekites, or I will sweep you away with them; for you showed loyalty to all the people of Israel when they came up from Egypt.' And the Kenites departed from among Amalek.
And Saul struck Amalek from Havilah as far as Shur, which is opposite Egypt.
And he took Agag king of Amalek alive; and all the people he devoted to destruction with the edge of the sword.

But Saul and the people spared Agag, and the best of the sheep and the cattle and the fatlings and the lambs, and all that was good; and they were not willing to devote them to destruction. But all the property that was despised and worthless — that they devoted to destruction.
And the word of the LORD came to Samuel:
'I regret that I made Saul king, for he has turned back from following me and has not carried out my words.' And Samuel was angry, and he cried out to the LORD all night.

And Samuel rose early to meet Saul in the morning; and it was told to Samuel, 'Saul came to Carmel, and there he was setting up a monument for himself; and he turned and passed on and went down to Gilgal.'
And Samuel came to Saul, and Saul said to him, 'Blessed are you to the LORD! I have carried out the word of the LORD.'
And Samuel said, 'And what is this sound of sheep in my ears, and the sound of cattle that I hear?'

And Saul said, 'They brought them from the Amalekites, because the people spared the best of the sheep and the cattle in order to sacrifice to the LORD your God; and the rest we devoted to destruction.'
And Samuel said to Saul, 'Stop, and let me tell you what the LORD said to me last night.' And he said to him, 'Speak.'
And Samuel said, 'Was it not when you were small in your own eyes that you became the head of the tribes of Israel? And the LORD anointed you as king over Israel.
And the LORD sent you on a journey and said, "Go and devote to destruction the sinners, Amalek, and wage war against them until they are finished."
And why did you not listen to the voice of the LORD? Why did you rush on the plunder and do the evil in the eyes of the LORD?'
And Saul said to Samuel, 'I did listen to the voice of the LORD, and I went on the journey on which the LORD sent me; and I brought Agag king of Amalek, and Amalek I devoted to destruction.
But the people took from the plunder sheep and cattle, the choicest of what was devoted to destruction, to sacrifice to the LORD your God at Gilgal.'
And Samuel said: Has the LORD delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices as in listening to the voice of the LORD? See, to listen is better than sacrifice, to pay attention than the fat of rams.
For rebellion is as the sin of divination, and presumption is as iniquity and idolatry. Because you have rejected the word of the LORD, he has rejected you from being king.
And Saul said to Samuel, 'I have sinned, for I transgressed the mouth of the LORD and your words; for I feared the people and listened to their voice.
And now, please forgive my sin, and return with me, that I may bow down to the LORD.'
And Samuel said to Saul, 'I will not return with you, for you have rejected the word of the LORD; and the LORD has rejected you from being king over Israel.'
And Samuel turned round to go, and Saul took hold of the skirt of his robe, and it tore.
And Samuel said to him, 'The LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel from you today, and has given it to your neighbour, who is better than you.
And also the Glory of Israel does not deal falsely and does not regret; for he is not a man, that he should regret.'
And he said, 'I have sinned. Now honour me, please, before the elders of my people and before Israel; and return with me, and I will bow down to the LORD your God.'
And Samuel turned back after Saul, and Saul bowed down to the LORD.
And Samuel said, 'Bring near to me Agag king of Amalek.' And Agag came to him cheerfully. And Agag said, 'Truly the bitterness of death has departed.'
And Samuel said, 'As your sword has made women childless, so shall your mother be childless among women.' And Samuel cut Agag to pieces before the LORD at Gilgal.
And Samuel went to Ramah, and Saul went up to his house at Gibeah of Saul.
And Samuel did not see Saul again until the day of his death, for Samuel mourned over Saul. And the LORD regretted that he had made Saul king over Israel.

1 samuel_16.t: And the LORD said to Samuel, 'How long will you mourn over Saul, when I have rejected him from reigning over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and go; I am sending you to Jesse the Bethlehemite, for I have seen among his sons a king for myself.'
And Samuel said, 'How can I go? Saul will hear of it and kill me.' And the LORD said, 'Take a heifer of the herd in your hand and say, "I have come to sacrifice to the LORD."'
And you shall invite Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will make known to you what you shall do; and you shall anoint for me the one whom I tell you.
And Samuel did what the LORD had said, and he came to Bethlehem. And the elders of the city trembled to meet him and said, 'Do you come in peace?'
And he said, 'In peace. I have come to sacrifice to the LORD. Consecrate yourselves and come with me to the sacrifice.' And he consecrated Jesse and his sons and invited them to the sacrifice.
And when they came, he saw Eliab and said, 'Surely the LORD's anointed is before him.'

And the LORD said to Samuel, 'Do not look at his appearance or at the height of his stature, for I have rejected him. For it is not what a human sees: a human sees by the eyes, but the LORD sees by the heart.'
And Jesse called Abinadab and made him pass before Samuel; and he said, 'Neither has the LORD chosen this one.'
And Jesse made Shammah pass by; and he said, 'Neither has the LORD chosen this one.'
And Jesse made seven of his sons pass before Samuel; and Samuel said to Jesse, 'The LORD has not chosen these.'

And Samuel said to Jesse, 'Are these all the young men?' And he said, 'The youngest still remains, and he is shepherding the flock.' And Samuel said to Jesse, 'Send and bring him, for we will not sit down until he comes here.'
And he sent and brought him. Now he was ruddy, with beautiful eyes and good to look at. And the LORD said, 'Arise, anoint him, for this is he.'
And Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the midst of his brothers; and the spirit of the LORD rushed upon David from that day onwards. And Samuel arose and went to Ramah.
And the spirit of the LORD departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the LORD terrified him.
And Saul's servants said to him, 'Look, an evil spirit of God is terrifying you.

Let our lord say the word — your servants are before you — let them seek a man who knows how to play on the lyre; and when an evil spirit of God is upon you, he will play with his hand, and it will be good for you.'
And Saul said to his servants, 'See for me a man who plays well, and bring him to me.'

And one of the young men answered, 'Look, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite who knows how to play — and a mighty man of valour, a man of war, discerning in speech, and a man of form; and the LORD is with him.'
And Saul sent messengers to Jesse and said, 'Send to me David your son, who is with the flock.'
And Jesse took a donkey loaded with bread, and a skin of wine, and one kid of the goats, and sent them by the hand of David his son to Saul.
And David came to Saul and stood before him; and Saul loved him greatly, and he became his armour-bearer.
And Saul sent to Jesse, saying, 'Let David stand before me, for he has found favour in my eyes.'
And whenever a spirit of God was upon Saul, David took the lyre and played with his hand; and there was relief for Saul, and it was good for him, and the evil spirit departed from him.

1 samuel_17.t: And the Philistines gathered their armies for battle, and they were gathered at Socoh which belongs to Judah; and they encamped between Socoh and Azekah, at Ephes-dammim.
And Saul and the men of Israel were gathered and encamped in the Valley of Elah, and they deployed for battle to meet the Philistines.
And the Philistines stood on the mountain on one side, and Israel stood on the mountain on the other side, with the valley between them.
And a champion came out from the camps of the Philistines; his name was Goliath, from Gath; his height was six cubits and a span.
And a bronze helmet was on his head, and he was clothed in scale body armour; and the weight of the body armour was five thousand shekels of bronze.
And bronze leg armour was on his legs, and a bronze javelin between his shoulders.
And the shaft of his spear was like a weaver's beam, and the blade of his spear was six hundred shekels of iron; and the bearer of the body shield walked before him.

And he stood and called out to the battle lines of Israel and said to them, 'Why do you come out to deploy for battle? Am I not the Philistine, and you the servants of Saul? Choose a man for yourselves, and let him come down to me.
If he is able to fight with me and strike me down, then we will become your slaves; and if I prevail over him and strike him down, then you will become our slaves, and you will serve us.'
And the Philistine said, 'I defy the battle lines of Israel this day. Give me a man, and let us fight together.'
And Saul and all Israel heard these words of the Philistine, and they were dismayed and greatly afraid.
Now David was the son of that Ephrathite man from Bethlehem of Judah, whose name was Jesse; and he had eight sons. And in the days of Saul the man was old, advanced in years.

And the three eldest sons of Jesse had gone after Saul to the battle. And the names of his three sons who had gone into the battle were Eliab the firstborn, Abinadab his second, and Shammah the third.
And David was the youngest; and the three eldest had gone after Saul.
And David went back and forth from Saul to shepherd his father's flock at Bethlehem.
And the Philistine drew near morning and evening, and took his stand for forty days.
And Jesse said to David his son, 'Take to your brothers this ephah of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread, and hurry them to the camp, to your brothers.
And these ten portions of cheese you shall bring to the commander of the thousand; and you shall enquire after your brothers' welfare, and bring back their pledge.'
Now Saul and they and every man of Israel were in the Valley of Elah, fighting with the Philistines.

And David rose early in the morning, left the flock with a keeper, took up the load and went, just as Jesse had commanded him. And he came to the camp as the army was going out to the battle line, and they shouted the war cry for the battle.
And Israel and the Philistines deployed, battle line facing battle line.
And David left the baggage in the care of the keeper of the baggage, and ran to the battle line; and he came and greeted his brothers.

And while he was speaking with them, the champion was coming up — Goliath the Philistine was his name, from Gath — from the battle lines of the Philistines; and he spoke the same words, and David heard.
And every man of Israel, when they saw the man, fled from before him and were greatly afraid.

And the men of Israel said, 'Have you seen this man who comes up? For he comes up to defy Israel. And the man who strikes him down — the king will make him rich with great riches, and will give him his daughter, and will make his father's house free in Israel.'

And David said to the men standing with him, 'What will be done for the man who strikes down this Philistine and removes reproach from Israel? For who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he has defied the battle lines of the living God?'
And the people answered him in the same way, 'So it will be done for the man who strikes him down.'

And Eliab his eldest brother heard when he spoke to the men, and Eliab's anger burned against David, and he said, 'Why have you come down? And with whom have you left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know your arrogance and the wickedness of your heart — you have come down to see the battle.'
And David said, 'What have I done now? Was it not just a word?'
And he turned away from him toward another, and spoke in the same way; and the people answered him as before.
And the words that David spoke were heard, and they were reported before Saul; and he sent for him.
And David said to Saul, 'Let no one's heart fall because of him. Your servant will go and fight with this Philistine.'
And Saul said to David, 'You are not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him, for you are a youth and he has been a man of war from his youth.'
And David said to Saul, 'Your servant was shepherding his father's flock, and a lion came, and a bear, and carried off a sheep from the flock.
And I went out after it and struck it and rescued the sheep from its mouth; and when it rose up against me, I took hold of its beard and struck it and killed it.
Your servant has struck down both the lion and the bear; and this uncircumcised Philistine will be like one of them, for he has defied the battle lines of the living God.'

And David said, 'The LORD, who rescued me from the hand of the lion and from the hand of the bear, he will rescue me from the hand of this Philistine.' And Saul said to David, 'Go, and may the LORD be with you.'
And Saul clothed David in his own garments, put a bronze helmet on his head, and clothed him in body armour.

And David girded his sword over his garments and tried to walk, for he had not tested them. And David said to Saul, 'I am not able to walk in these, for I have not tested them.' And David removed them from himself.

And he took his stick in his hand and chose for himself five smooth stones from the wadi, and put them in the shepherds' bag he had — in the pouch — and his sling was in his hand; and he drew near to the Philistine.
And the Philistine came, coming on and drawing near to David; and the man who bore the body shield was before him.
And the Philistine looked and saw David, and despised him, for he was a youth, and ruddy, with a handsome appearance.
And the Philistine said to David, 'Am I a dog, that you come against me with sticks?' And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.
And the Philistine said to David, 'Come to me, and I will give your flesh to the birds of the heavens and to the animals of the field.'

And David said to the Philistine, 'You come against me with sword and spear and javelin; and I come against you in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the battle lines of Israel, whom you have defied.

This day the LORD will deliver you up into my hand, and I will strike you down and remove your head from you; and I will give the corpses of the camp of the Philistines this day to the birds of the heavens and to the animals of the earth, so that all the earth may know that Israel has a God.
And all this assembly will know that the LORD does not save by sword or by spear, for the battle is the LORD's; and he will give you into our hand.'
And when the Philistine arose and came and drew near to meet David, David hurried and ran to the battle line to meet the Philistine.
And David put his hand into the bag and took a stone from there, and slung it and struck the Philistine on his forehead; and the stone sank into his forehead, and he fell on his face to the ground.
And David was stronger than the Philistine with the sling and with the stone, and he struck the Philistine down and killed him; and there was no sword in David's hand.

And David ran and stood over the Philistine, took his sword and drew it from its sheath, and killed him, and cut off his head with it. And when the Philistines saw that their mighty man was dead, they fled.

And the men of Israel and Judah arose and shouted the war cry, and pursued the Philistines as far as the entrance to Gath and as far as the gates of Ekron. And the slain of the Philistines fell on the road to Shaaraim, and as far as Gath and Ekron.
And the people of Israel returned from hotly pursuing the Philistines, and plundered their camps.
And David took the head of the Philistine and brought it to Jerusalem; and his weapons he put in his own tent.
And when Saul saw David going out to meet the Philistine, he said to Abner the commander of the army, 'Whose son is this youth, Abner?' And Abner said, 'As your being lives, O king, I do not know.'
And the king said, 'You ask whose son the young man is.'
And when David returned from striking down the Philistine, Abner took him and brought him before Saul, with the head of the Philistine in his hand.
And Saul said to him, 'Whose son are you, young man?' And David said, 'The son of your servant Jesse the Bethlehemite.'

1 samuel_18.t: And when he had finished speaking to Saul, the being of Jonathan was bound to the being of David; and Jonathan loved him as his own being.
And Saul took him that day and did not let him return to his father's house.
And Jonathan and David made a covenant, because he loved him as his own being.
And Jonathan stripped off the robe that was on him and gave it to David, with his garments, and even his sword, his bow and his belt.
And David went out wherever Saul sent him, and he prospered; and Saul set him over the men of war. And it was good in the eyes of all the people, and also in the eyes of Saul's servants.

And as they were coming, when David returned from striking down the Philistine, the women came out from all the cities of Israel with singing and dancing, to meet Saul the king, with tambourines, with joy, and with three-stringed instruments.
And the women who played sang out: Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his ten thousands.

And Saul burned with anger exceedingly, and this matter was displeasing in his eyes; and he said, 'They have ascribed ten thousands to David, and to me they have ascribed the thousands. What more is there for him but the kingship?'
And Saul kept his eye on David from that day onwards.
And the next day an evil spirit of God rushed upon Saul, and he prophesied inside the house; and David was playing with his hand as he did day by day, and the spear was in Saul's hand.
And Saul hurled the spear, saying, 'I will pin David to the wall!' And David turned aside from before him twice.
And Saul was afraid of David, for the LORD was with him and had turned aside from Saul.
And Saul removed him from his presence and made him a commander of a thousand; and he went out and came in before the people.
And David prospered in all his ways, and the LORD was with him.
And Saul saw that he was prospering exceedingly, and he was in dread of him.
And all Israel and Judah loved David, for he went out and came in before them.

And Saul said to David, 'Here is my elder daughter Merab; I will give her to you as a wife. Only be a man of valour for me, and fight the battles of the LORD.' For Saul said, 'Let my hand not be against him, but let the hand of the Philistines be against him.'
And David said to Saul, 'Who am I, and who are my kinsfolk, my father's clan in Israel, that I should be son-in-law to the king?'
And at the time when Merab, Saul's daughter, should have been given to David, she was given to Adriel the Meholathite as a wife.
And Michal, Saul's daughter, loved David; and they told Saul, and the matter was right in his eyes.

And Saul said, 'I will give her to him, and she will become a snare for him, and the hand of the Philistines will be against him.' And Saul said to David, 'By the second one you shall be my son-in-law today.'
And Saul commanded his servants, 'Speak to David in secret and say, "Look, the king delights in you, and all his servants love you. Now be son-in-law to the king."'
And Saul's servants spoke these words in David's hearing; and David said, 'Is it a trifling thing in your eyes to be son-in-law to the king, when I am a poor man and lightly esteemed?'
And Saul's servants told him, 'This is what David spoke.'

And Saul said, 'Thus you shall say to David: The king has no delight in a bride-price, but in a hundred foreskins of the Philistines, to avenge himself on the king's enemies.' And Saul planned to make David fall by the hand of the Philistines.
And his servants told David these words, and the matter was right in David's eyes, to be son-in-law to the king. And before the days were completed,

David arose and went, he and his men, and struck down two hundred men among the Philistines; and David brought their foreskins, and they gave them in full to the king, to be son-in-law to the king. And Saul gave him Michal his daughter as a wife.
And Saul saw and knew that the LORD was with David; and Michal, Saul's daughter, loved him.
And Saul was still more afraid of David; and Saul was David's enemy all his days.
And the commanders of the Philistines went out; and as often as they went out, David was more successful than all Saul's servants; and his name was greatly esteemed.

1 samuel_19.t: And Saul spoke to Jonathan his son and to all his servants about killing David; but Jonathan, Saul's son, delighted in David exceedingly.
And Jonathan told David, 'Saul my father is seeking to kill you. Now take care in the morning; stay in a hiding place and hide yourself.'
And I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where you are, and I will speak about you to my father; and whatever I see I will tell you.

And Jonathan spoke well of David to Saul his father, and said to him, 'Let the king not sin against his servant, against David, for he has not sinned against you, and his deeds have been very good for you.

And he put his life in his palm and struck down the Philistine, and the LORD made a great deliverance for all Israel. You saw it and rejoiced. And why will you sin against innocent blood, by killing David without cause?'
And Saul listened to the voice of Jonathan, and Saul swore, 'As the LORD lives, he shall not be put to death.'
And Jonathan called David and told him all these words; and Jonathan brought David to Saul, and he was in his presence as before.
And the war continued; and David went out and fought against the Philistines and struck them with a great defeat, and they fled from before him.
And an evil spirit of the LORD was upon Saul, and he was sitting in his house with his spear in his hand; and David was playing with his hand.
And Saul sought to pin David to the wall with the spear; but he slipped away from before Saul, and Saul struck the spear into the wall. And David fled and escaped that night.
And Saul sent messengers to David's house to watch him and to kill him in the morning. And Michal his wife told David, 'If you do not save your life tonight, tomorrow you will be put to death.'
And Michal let David down through the window, and he went and fled and escaped.
And Michal took the teraphim and put it on the bed, and put the quilt of goats' hair at its head, and covered it with the garment.
And Saul sent messengers to fetch David, and she said, 'He is sick.'
And Saul sent the messengers to see David, saying, 'Bring him up to me on the bed, to kill him.'
And the messengers came, and there was the teraphim on the bed, with the quilt of goats' hair at its head.
And Saul said to Michal, 'Why have you deceived me like this and let my enemy go, so that he escaped?' And Michal said to Saul, 'He said to me, "Let me go — why should I kill you?"'
And David fled and escaped, and came to Samuel at Ramah, and told him all that Saul had done to him. And he and Samuel went and stayed at Naioth.
And it was told to Saul, 'David is at Naioth in Ramah.'

And Saul sent messengers to fetch David; and they saw the company of the prophets prophesying, and Samuel standing as chief over them. And the spirit of God was upon Saul's messengers, and they also prophesied.
And they told Saul, and he sent other messengers, and they also prophesied. And Saul sent messengers again, a third time, and they also prophesied.
And he also went himself to Ramah, and came as far as the great cistern at Secu; and he asked, 'Where are Samuel and David?' And someone said, 'At Naioth in Ramah.'
And he went there, to Naioth in Ramah; and the spirit of God was upon him also, and he went on, going and prophesying, until he came to Naioth in Ramah.
And he also stripped off his clothes, and he also prophesied before Samuel; and he lay naked all that day and all night. Therefore they say, 'Is Saul also among the prophets?'

1 samuel_20.t: And David fled from Naioth in Ramah and came and said before Jonathan, 'What have I done? What is my iniquity, and what is my sin before your father, that he is seeking my life?'

And he said to him, 'Far be it! You will not die. Look, my father does not do anything great or anything small without uncovering my ear; and why should my father hide this thing from me? It is not so.'

And David swore again, 'Your father knows well that I have found favour in your eyes, and he has said, "Let Jonathan not know this, lest he be grieved." But as the LORD lives and as your being lives, there is only about a step between me and death.'
And Jonathan said to David, 'Whatever your being says, I will do for you.'
And David said to Jonathan, 'Look, tomorrow is the new moon, and I should certainly sit with the king to eat. But let me go, and I will hide myself in the field until the third evening.
If your father misses me at all, then say, "David asked leave of me urgently to run to Bethlehem his city, for the yearly sacrifice is there for all the clan."
If he says, "Good," then there is safety for your servant. But if he burns with anger, know that the harm has been determined by him.

And you shall do loyalty to your servant, for you have brought your servant into a covenant of the LORD with you. And if there is iniquity in me, kill me yourself; but why should you bring me to your father?'
And Jonathan said, 'Far be it from you! For if I ever know that the harm has been determined by my father to come upon you, would I not tell you?'
And David said to Jonathan, 'Who will tell me? Or what if your father answers you harshly?'
And Jonathan said to David, 'Come, let us go out to the field.' And the two of them went out to the field.

And Jonathan said to David, 'The LORD, God of Israel — when I have sounded out my father about this time tomorrow, or the third day, and there is good toward David, shall I not then send to you and uncover your ear?

So may the LORD do to Jonathan, and more also, if it seems good to my father to bring the harm upon you and I do not uncover your ear and send you away, so that you go in peace. And may the LORD be with you, as he has been with my father.
And while I am still alive, may you not fail to do the loyalty of the LORD with me, so that I do not die;
and may you not cut off your loyalty from my house for ever — not even when the LORD cuts off the enemies of David, every one, from the face of the ground.
And Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David: 'And may the LORD require it at the hand of David's enemies.'
And Jonathan made David swear again by his love for him, for he loved him with the love of his own being.
And Jonathan said to him, 'Tomorrow is the new moon, and you will be missed, for your seat will be empty.
And on the third day you shall go down quickly and come to the place where you hid yourself when the business was in hand, and stay beside the stone Ezel.
And I will shoot three arrows to the side of it, as though shooting at a target.

And I will send the lad: "Go, find the arrows." If I say plainly to the lad, "Look, the arrows are on this side of you" — then fetch it and come, for you are safe, and there is nothing, as the LORD lives.
But if I say this to the young man, "Look, the arrows are beyond you" — go, for the LORD has sent you away.
And as for the matter that we have spoken, I and you — the LORD is between me and you for ever.
And David hid himself in the field. And when the new moon came, the king sat down to the food to eat.
And the king sat on his seat as at other times, on the seat by the wall; and Jonathan arose, and Abner sat at Saul's side; and David's place was empty.
And Saul said nothing that day, for he thought, 'It is an accident; he is not clean — surely he is not clean.'
And on the next day, the second of the new moon, David's place was empty; and Saul said to Jonathan his son, 'Why has the son of Jesse not come to the food, either yesterday or today?'
And Jonathan answered Saul, 'David asked leave of me urgently for Bethlehem,

and he said, "Let me go, for we have a clan sacrifice in the city, and my brother himself has commanded me. And now, if I have found favour in your eyes, let me slip away and see my brothers." Therefore he has not come to the king's table.'

And Saul's anger burned against Jonathan, and he said to him, 'Son of a perverse and rebellious woman! Do I not know that you are choosing the son of Jesse — to your own shame and to the shame of your mother's nakedness?'
For all the days that the son of Jesse lives on the earth, you will not be established, you and your kingdom. And now, send and fetch him to me, for he is a son of death.'
And Jonathan answered Saul his father, 'Why should he be put to death? What has he done?'
And Saul hurled the spear at him to strike him; and Jonathan knew that it had been determined by his father to kill David.
And Jonathan arose from the table in the heat of anger, and he did not eat food on the second day of the new moon, for he was grieved concerning David, because his father had put him to shame.
And in the morning Jonathan went out to the field at the time appointed with David, and a small lad was with him.
And he said to his lad, 'Run, find the arrows that I am shooting.' The lad ran, and he shot the arrow to make it pass beyond him.
And the lad came to the place of the arrow that Jonathan had shot; and Jonathan called after the lad, 'Is not the arrow beyond you?'
And Jonathan called after the lad, 'Quickly, hurry, do not stand still!' And Jonathan's lad gathered up the arrows and came to his master.
And the lad knew nothing; only Jonathan and David knew the matter.
And Jonathan gave his weapons to the lad who was his, and said to him, 'Go, take them to the city.'

The lad went; and David arose from beside the south side, and fell on his face to the ground and bowed down three times. And they kissed one another and wept with one another, until David wept the more.

And Jonathan said to David, 'Go in peace, since we have both sworn, the two of us, by the name of the LORD, saying, "The LORD will be between me and you, and between my offspring and your offspring, for ever."' And he arose and went; and Jonathan came to the city.

1 samuel_21.t: And David came to Nob, to Ahimelech the priest; and Ahimelech trembled at meeting David and said to him, 'Why are you alone, and no man with you?'

And David said to Ahimelech the priest, 'The king has commanded me a matter, and he said to me, "Let no man know anything of the matter on which I am sending you and with which I have commanded you." And the young men I have directed to such and such a place.
And now, what is there under your hand? Give me five loaves, or whatever may be found.'
And the priest answered David, 'There is no common bread under my hand, but there is holy bread — if only the young men have kept themselves from a woman.'

And David answered the priest, 'Indeed, woman has been withheld from us as before, when I came out; and the vessels of the young men were holy — and this is a common journey; how much more, then, will it be holy today in the vessel.'

And the priest gave him what was holy, for there was no bread there except the bread of the Presence, which had been removed from before the LORD, to put hot bread in its place on the day it was taken away.
And a man of Saul's servants was there that day, detained before the LORD; and his name was Doeg the Edomite, the chief of the shepherds who belonged to Saul.
And David said to Ahimelech, 'And is there not here under your hand a spear or a sword? For I took neither my sword nor my weapons in my hand, because the king's matter was urgent.'

And the priest said, 'The sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you struck down in the valley of Elah — it is wrapped in a cloak behind the ephod. If you will take it for yourself, take it, for there is no other but it in this place.' And David said, 'There is none like it; give it to me.'
And David arose and fled that day from before Saul, and came to Achish king of Gath.

And the servants of Achish said to him, 'Is not this David, the king of the land? Is it not of this one that they sing in the dances, "Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his ten thousands"?'
And David took these words to heart, and he was exceedingly afraid of Achish king of Gath.
And he changed his behaviour in their sight and acted like a madman in their hands, and he made marks on the doors of the gate and let his spittle run down onto his beard.
And Achish said to his servants, 'Look, you see a man behaving like a madman. Why do you bring him to me?
Am I lacking madmen, that you have brought this one to behave like a madman at me? Shall this one come into my house?'
