1 samuel_22.t: And David went from there and escaped to the cave of Adullam; and his brothers and all his father's house heard of it, and they went down to him there.
And every man in distress, and every man who had a creditor, and every man bitter of being, gathered to him; and he became a commander over them, and there were with him about four hundred men.
And David went from there to Mizpeh of Moab, and he said to the king of Moab, 'Let my father and my mother go out and stay with you, until I know what God will do for me.'
And he left them with the king of Moab, and they stayed with him all the days that David was in the stronghold.
And Gad the prophet said to David, 'Do not stay in the stronghold. Go, and come to the land of Judah.' And David went and came to the forest of Hereth.

And Saul heard that David had been discovered, and the men who were with him; and Saul was sitting at Gibeah under the tamarisk on the height, with his spear in his hand, and all his servants standing about him.

And Saul said to his servants who were standing about him, 'Listen, Benjaminites. Will the son of Jesse also give all of you fields and vineyards? Will he appoint all of you commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds?

For all of you have conspired against me, and there is no one who uncovers my ear when my son makes a covenant with the son of Jesse; and none of you is grieved for me or uncovers my ear, that my son has raised up my servant against me to lie in ambush, as at this day.'
And Doeg the Edomite answered — he was standing with the servants of Saul — 'I saw the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech son of Ahitub;
and he enquired of the LORD for him, and gave him provisions, and gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.'
And the king sent to summon Ahimelech son of Ahitub the priest, and all his father's house, the priests who were at Nob; and all of them came to the king.
And Saul said, 'Listen, son of Ahitub.' And he said, 'Here I am, my lord.'

And Saul said to him, 'Why have you conspired against me, you and the son of Jesse, in giving him bread and a sword, and enquiring of God for him, so that he rises up against me to lie in ambush, as at this day?'
And Ahimelech answered the king, 'And who among all your servants is like David — faithful, and the king's son-in-law, and one who turns aside to your bodyguard, and honoured in your house?

Did I this day begin to enquire of God for him? Far be it from me! Let the king not lay anything against his servant, against all my father's house; for your servant knew nothing of all this, small or great.'
And the king said, 'You shall surely die, Ahimelech — you and all your father's house.'

And the king said to the runners who were standing about him, 'Turn and put to death the priests of the LORD, because their hand also is with David, and because they knew that he was fleeing and did not uncover my ear.' But the servants of the king were not willing to stretch out their hand to fall upon the priests of the LORD.

And the king said to Doeg, 'Turn, you, and fall upon the priests.' And Doeg the Edomite turned, and he himself fell upon the priests, and he put to death on that day eighty-five men who carried an ephod of linen.
And Nob, the city of the priests, he struck with the edge of the sword — man and woman, child and suckling, and ox and donkey and sheep — with the edge of the sword.
And one son of Ahimelech son of Ahitub escaped, and his name was Abiathar; and he fled after David.
And Abiathar told David that Saul had killed the priests of the LORD.
And David said to Abiathar, 'I knew on that day, because Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would surely tell Saul. I myself am responsible for every being of your father's house.
Stay with me; do not fear. For he who seeks my life seeks your life; you are in safekeeping with me.'

1 samuel_23.t: And they told David, 'The Philistines are fighting against Keilah, and they are plundering the threshing floors.'
And David enquired of the LORD, 'Shall I go and strike these Philistines?' And the LORD said to David, 'Go, and strike the Philistines, and deliver Keilah.'
And David's men said to him, 'We are afraid here in Judah; how much more if we go to Keilah, against the battle lines of the Philistines!'
And David enquired of the LORD again, and the LORD answered him, 'Arise, go down to Keilah, for I am giving the Philistines into your hand.'
And David and his men went to Keilah and fought against the Philistines, and drove away their livestock, and struck them with a great defeat; and David delivered the inhabitants of Keilah.
And when Abiathar son of Ahimelech fled to David at Keilah, an ephod came down in his hand.
And it was told to Saul that David had come to Keilah; and Saul said, 'God has handed him over into my hand, for he has shut himself in by coming into a city with doors and a bar.'
And Saul summoned all the people to battle, to go down to Keilah, to lay siege against David and against his men.
And David knew that Saul was devising harm against him, and he said to Abiathar the priest, 'Bring the ephod near.'
And David said, 'LORD, God of Israel, your servant has surely heard that Saul is seeking to come to Keilah, to destroy the city on my account.
Will the citizens of Keilah deliver me up into his hand? Will Saul come down, as your servant has heard? LORD, God of Israel, tell your servant.' And the LORD said, 'He will come down.'
And David said, 'Will the citizens of Keilah deliver me and my men into the hand of Saul?' And the LORD said, 'They will deliver you up.'

And David and his men arose, about six hundred men, and went out from Keilah and went about wherever they could go. And it was told to Saul that David had escaped from Keilah, and he gave up going out.
And David dwelt in the wilderness, in the strongholds; and he dwelt in the hill country, in the wilderness of Ziph. And Saul sought him all the days, but God did not give him into his hand.
And David saw that Saul had come out to seek his life; and David was in the wilderness of Ziph, at Horesh.
And Jonathan son of Saul arose and went to David at Horesh, and strengthened his hand in God.
And he said to him, 'Do not fear, for the hand of Saul my father will not find you; and you will reign over Israel, and I myself shall be second to you. And Saul my father also knows that it is so.'
And the two of them made a covenant before the LORD; and David remained at Horesh, and Jonathan went to his house.
And Ziphites went up to Saul at Gibeah, 'Is not David hiding himself with us, in the strongholds at Horesh, on the hill of Hakilah, which is to the south of Jeshimon?
And now, to all the desire of your being, O king, to come down — come down; and it is ours to deliver him up into the hand of the king.'
And Saul said, 'Blessed are you to the LORD, for you have had compassion on me.'
Go, make further preparation, and know and see the place where his foot is — who has seen him there — for someone has said to me that he is very crafty.

And see and know all the hiding places where he hides himself, and return to me with something certain; and I will go with you. And if he is in the land, I will search him out among all the thousands of Judah.'
And they arose and went to Ziph ahead of Saul. And David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, in the Arabah, to the south of Jeshimon.

And Saul and his men went to seek him; and they told David, and he went down to the rock and stayed in the wilderness of Maon. And Saul heard of it and pursued after David into the wilderness of Maon.

And Saul went on one side of the mountain, and David and his men on the other side of the mountain; and David was hurrying to get away from Saul, while Saul and his men were closing round David and his men to seize them.
And a messenger came to Saul, 'Hurry and come, for the Philistines have made a raid on the land.'
And Saul turned back from pursuing after David and went to meet the Philistines. Therefore they called that place Sela Hammahlekoth.
And David went up from there and dwelt in the strongholds of En Gedi.

1 samuel_24.t: And when Saul returned from following the Philistines, they told him, 'David is in the wilderness of En Gedi.'
And Saul took three thousand chosen men from all Israel and went to seek David and his men on the face of the rocks of the mountain goats.
And he came to the sheepfolds by the way, and there was a cave there; and Saul went in to cover his feet. And David and his men were sitting in the innermost parts of the cave.

And David's men said to him, 'This is the day of which the LORD said to you, "I am giving your enemy into your hand, and you shall do to him as it is good in your eyes."' And David arose and cut off the skirt of the robe that was Saul's, secretly.
And afterwards David's heart struck him, because he had cut off the skirt that was Saul's.

And he said to his men, 'Far be it from me, from the LORD, that I should do this thing to my lord, to the anointed of the LORD, to stretch out my hand against him; for he is the anointed of the LORD.'
And David reprimanded his men with words, and did not permit them to rise against Saul. And Saul rose from the cave and went on his way.
And David arose afterwards and went out from the cave, and called after Saul, 'My lord the king!' And Saul looked behind him, and David bowed his face to the ground and bowed down.
And David said to Saul, 'Why do you listen to the words of a man saying, "David is seeking your harm"?

This day your eyes have seen that the LORD gave you today into my hand in the cave; and someone said to kill you, but my eye had compassion on you. And I said, "I will not stretch out my hand against my lord, for he is the anointed of the LORD."

And my father, see — yes, see the skirt of your robe in my hand! For when I cut off the skirt of your robe I did not kill you. Know and see that there is no evil or transgression in my hand, and I have not sinned against you; yet you are lying in wait for my life, to take it.
May the LORD judge between me and you, and may the LORD avenge me on you; but my hand will not be against you.
As the proverb of the ancients says, 'From the wicked comes forth wickedness.' But my hand will not be against you.
After whom has the king of Israel come out? After whom are you pursuing? After a dead dog! After a single flea!
And the LORD will be judge, and he will judge between me and you; and may he see and conduct my case, and vindicate me from your hand.
And when David had finished speaking these words to Saul, Saul said, 'Is this your voice, my son David?' And Saul lifted up his voice and wept.
And he said to David, 'You are more righteous than I, for you have dealt out good to me, and I have dealt out evil to you.
And you have told this day what good you have done to me — that the LORD delivered me up into your hand and you did not kill me.
And if a man finds his enemy, will he send him away on a good journey? So may the LORD reward you with good in place of this day, for what you have done to me.
And now I know that you will surely reign, and the kingdom of Israel will be established in your hand.
And now, swear to me by the LORD that you will not cut off my offspring after me, and that you will not destroy my name from my father's house.'
And David swore to Saul; and Saul went to his house, and David and his men went up to the stronghold.

1 samuel_25.t: And Samuel died; and all Israel gathered and mourned for him, and they buried him at his house in Ramah. And David arose and went down to the wilderness of Paran.
And there was a man in Maon whose business was in Carmel; and the man was very great, and he had three thousand sheep and a thousand goats. And he was shearing his sheep in Carmel.
And the name of the man was Nabal, and the name of his wife Abigail. And the woman was good of insight and beautiful of form; but the man was hard and evil in his deeds — and he was a Calebite.
And David heard in the wilderness that Nabal was shearing his sheep.
And David sent ten young men, and David said to the young men, 'Go up to Carmel, and come to Nabal, and greet him in my name.
And you shall say, "Long life to you! Peace to you, and peace to your house, and peace to all that is yours.
And now I have heard that you have shearers. Your shepherds were with us; we did not humiliate them, and nothing of theirs was missing all the days they were in Carmel.
Ask your own young men, and they will tell you. And let the young men find favour in your eyes, for we have come on a good day. Give whatever your hand finds to your servants and to your son David."'
And David's young men came and spoke to Nabal all these words in David's name; and then they waited.
And Nabal answered David's servants, 'Who is David, and who is the son of Jesse? Today there are many servants breaking away, each from his master.
And shall I take my bread and my water and my meat that I have slaughtered for my shearers, and give it to men who I do not know where they are from?'
And David's young men turned round on their way, and returned and came and told him all these words.

And David said to his men, 'Gird on your swords, every man.' And every man girded on his sword, and David also girded on his sword. And about four hundred men went up after David, and two hundred remained with the baggage.
And one of the young men told Abigail, Nabal's wife, 'David sent messengers from the wilderness to bless our master, and he screamed at them.
But the men were very good to us, and we were not humiliated and nothing of ours went missing all the days we went about with them, when we were in the field.
They were a wall about us, both night and day, all the days we were with them, shepherding the flock.
And now, know and see what you will do, for harm has been determined against our master and against all his house; and he is a son of worthlessness, past speaking to.'

And Abigail made haste and took two hundred loaves and two skins of wine and five sheep prepared, five seahs of roasted grain, a hundred bunches of raisins and two hundred fig cakes, and put them on the donkeys.
And she said to her young men, 'Pass on ahead of me; I am coming after you.' But she did not tell her husband Nabal.
And as she was riding on the donkey, going down under the cover of the mountain, David and his men were coming down to meet her; and she met them.
And David had said, 'Surely it was in vain that I guarded all this man has in the wilderness, and nothing of all that is his went missing; and he has returned me evil in place of good.
So may God do to the enemies of David, and more also, if I leave until the morning, of all that is his, one who urinates against a wall.'
And Abigail saw David, and she made haste and came down from the donkey and fell before David on her face and bowed down to the ground.
And she fell at his feet and said, 'On me, my lord, on me be the iniquity! And let your slave woman speak in your ears, and hear the words of your slave woman.

Let my lord not set his heart on this man of worthlessness, on Nabal; for as his name is, so is he. Nabal is his name, and disgraceful folly is with him. But I, your slave woman, did not see my lord's young men whom you sent.

And now, my lord, as the LORD lives and as your being lives, since the LORD has restrained you from coming into bloodguilt and from delivering yourself by your own hand — now may your enemies, and those who seek harm against my lord, be like Nabal.
And now, this blessing that your maidservant has brought to my lord — let it be given to the young men who go about at my lord's feet.

Forgive the transgression of your slave woman, for the LORD will surely make for my lord an enduring house, because my lord is fighting the battles of the LORD; and evil will not be found in you all your days.

And though a man has arisen to pursue you and to seek your life, the being of my lord will be bound up in the bundle of the living with the LORD your God; but the being of your enemies he will sling out from the hollow of the sling.
And when the LORD does for my lord all the good that he has spoken concerning you, and appoints you as leader over Israel,

then this shall not be to you a staggering or a stumbling of heart for my lord — the pouring out of blood without cause, and my lord delivering himself. And when the LORD does good to my lord, remember your slave woman.'
And David said to Abigail, 'Blessed be the LORD, God of Israel, who sent you this day to meet me.
And blessed be your discernment, and blessed be you, who have restrained me this day from coming into bloodguilt and from delivering myself by my own hand.

But as the LORD, God of Israel, lives, who has restrained me from doing harm to you — if you had not made haste and come to meet me, then there would not have been left to Nabal until the light of the morning one who urinates against a wall.'
And David took from her hand what she had brought him, and said to her, 'Go up in peace to your house. See, I have listened to your voice and have granted your request.'

And Abigail came to Nabal, and he had a feast in his house like the feast of a king; and Nabal's heart was good within him, and he was very drunk. And she did not tell him anything, small or great, until the light of the morning.
And in the morning, when the wine had gone out from Nabal, his wife told him these things; and his heart died within him, and he became as a stone.
And about ten days later the LORD struck Nabal, and he died.

And David heard that Nabal was dead, and said, 'Blessed be the LORD, who has conducted the case of my disgrace from the hand of Nabal, and has kept back his servant from evil; and the LORD has returned the evil of Nabal on his own head.' And David sent and spoke with Abigail, to take her to himself as a wife.
And David's servants came to Abigail at Carmel and spoke to her, 'David has sent us to you, to take you to him as a wife.'
And she arose and bowed down, her face to the ground, and said, 'Here is your slave woman, a maidservant to wash the feet of my lord's servants.'
And Abigail made haste and arose and rode on the donkey, with five of her young women who went at her feet; and she went after David's messengers, and became his wife.
And David had taken Ahinoam from Jezreel; and both of them became his wives.
And Saul had given Michal his daughter, David's wife, to Palti son of Laish, who was from Gallim.

1 samuel_26.t: And the Ziphites came to Saul at Gibeah, 'Is not David hiding himself on the hill of Hakilah, facing Jeshimon?'
And Saul arose and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, and with him three thousand men, the chosen of Israel, to seek David in the wilderness of Ziph.
And Saul encamped on the hill of Hakilah, which faces Jeshimon, by the way. And David was dwelling in the wilderness, and he saw that Saul had come after him into the wilderness.
And David sent spies, and he knew for certain that Saul had come.

And David arose and came to the place where Saul had encamped; and David saw the place where Saul lay, and Abner son of Ner, the commander of his army. And Saul was lying in the encampment, and the people were encamped around him.
And David said to Ahimelech the Hittite and to Abishai son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, 'Who will go down with me to Saul, to the camp?' And Abishai said, 'I will go down with you.'
And David and Abishai came to the people by night; and Saul was lying asleep in the encampment, with his spear thrust into the ground at his head, and Abner and the people lying around him.
And Abishai said to David, 'God has delivered your enemy up into your hand this day. And now let me strike him with the spear into the ground once — I will not do it twice.'
And David said to Abishai, 'Do not destroy him; for who has stretched out his hand against the anointed of the LORD and been free of guilt?'
And David said, 'As the LORD lives, the LORD himself will strike him, or his day will come and he will die, or he will go down into battle and be swept away.
Far be it from me, before the LORD, to stretch out my hand against the anointed of the LORD. And now take the spear that is at his head, and the jug of water, and let us go.'

And David took the spear and the jug of water from Saul's head, and they went; and no one saw, and no one knew, and no one awoke, for all of them were sleeping, because a deep sleep from the LORD had fallen on them.
And David passed over to the other side and stood on the top of the hill, far off; a great space was between them.
And David called to the people and to Abner son of Ner, 'Will you not answer, Abner?' And Abner answered, 'Who are you who calls to the king?'
And David said to Abner, 'Are you not a man? And who is like you in Israel? Why then have you not kept watch over your lord the king? For one of the people came to destroy the king your lord.

This thing that you have done is not good. As the LORD lives, you are sons of death, because you have not kept watch over your lord, over the anointed of the LORD. And now see where the king's spear is, and the jug of water that was at his head!'
And Saul recognised David's voice and said, 'Is this your voice, my son David?' And David said, 'It is my voice, my lord the king.'
And he said, 'Why is this, that my lord is pursuing his servant? For what have I done, and what evil is in my hand?

And now let my lord the king hear the words of his servant. If the LORD has incited you against me, may he accept an offering; but if it is the sons of man, cursed are they before the LORD, for they have driven me out this day from having a share in the inheritance of the LORD, saying, "Go, serve other gods."
And now, let not my blood fall to the ground away from the presence of the LORD; for the king of Israel has come out to seek a single flea, as one pursues a partridge in the mountains.'
And Saul said, 'I have sinned. Return, my son David, for I will not do you harm again, because my life was precious in your eyes this day. I have acted foolishly and have gone very greatly astray.'
And David answered, 'Here is the king's spear! Let one of the young men come over and take it.
And the LORD will return to each man his righteousness and his faithfulness, for the LORD gave you today into my hand, but I was not willing to stretch out my hand against the anointed of the LORD.
And as your life was great in my eyes this day, so may my life be great in the eyes of the LORD, and may he deliver me from every trouble.
And Saul said to David, 'Blessed are you, my son David. You will surely do, and you will surely prevail.' And David went on his way, and Saul returned to his place.

1 samuel_27.t: And David said in his heart, 'Now I shall be swept away one day by the hand of Saul. There is nothing good for me but to escape to the land of the Philistines; then Saul will despair of seeking me again in all the territory of Israel, and I shall be delivered from his hand.'
And David arose and passed over, he and the six hundred men who were with him, to Achish son of Maoch, king of Gath.
And David dwelt with Achish at Gath, he and his men, each man with his household — David and his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail the Carmelite, Nabal's wife.
And it was told to Saul that David had fled to Gath, and he did not seek him again.

And David said to Achish, 'If I have found favour in your eyes, let them give me a place in one of the country towns, that I may dwell there. Why should your servant dwell in the royal city with you?'
And Achish gave him Ziklag on that day. Therefore Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah until this day.
And the number of the days that David dwelt in the region of the Philistines was a year and four months.

And David and his men went up and made raids against the Geshurites and the Girzites and the Amalekites; for they were the inhabitants of the land from of old, as you come to Shur and as far as the land of Egypt.
And David struck the land, and he did not let a man or a woman live; and he took sheep and cattle and donkeys and camels and clothing, and returned and came to Achish.
And Achish said, 'Against whom did you make a raid today?' And David said, 'Against the Negev of Judah, and against the Negev of the Jerahmeelites, and against the Negev of the Kenites.'

And David would not let a man or a woman live, to bring them to Gath, saying, 'Lest they should tell about us, "Thus David has done."' And such was his practice all the days that he dwelt in the region of the Philistines.
And Achish trusted David, saying, 'He has surely made himself odious among his own people, among Israel; and he will be my servant for ever.'

1 samuel_28.t: And in those days the Philistines gathered their forces for war, to fight against Israel. And Achish said to David, 'You surely know that you are to go out with me in the camp, you and your men.'
And David said to Achish, 'Therefore you shall know what your servant will do.' And Achish said to David, 'Therefore I will make you keeper of my head for all time.'
Now Samuel had died, and all Israel had mourned for him and buried him in Ramah, in his own city. And Saul had removed the mediums and the spiritists from the land.
And the Philistines gathered and came and encamped at Shunem; and Saul gathered all Israel, and they encamped at Gilboa.
And Saul saw the camp of the Philistines, and he was afraid, and his heart trembled exceedingly.
And Saul enquired of the LORD, and the LORD did not answer him — neither by dreams nor by the Urim nor by the prophets.
And Saul said to his servants, 'Seek me out a woman who is a medium, and I will go to her and enquire of her.' And his servants said to him, 'There is a woman who is a medium at En Dor.'

And Saul disguised himself and put on other garments, and he went, he and two men with him; and they came to the woman by night. And he said, 'Divine for me by the ghost, and bring up for me the one whom I shall name to you.'
And the woman said to him, 'You know what Saul has done, that he has cut off the mediums and the spiritists from the land. Why then are you setting a trap for my life, to put me to death?'
And Saul swore to her by the LORD, 'As the LORD lives, no punishment shall happen to you in this matter.'
And the woman said, 'Whom shall I bring up for you?' And he said, 'Bring up Samuel for me.'
And the woman saw Samuel, and she cried out with a loud voice; and the woman said to Saul, 'Why have you deceived me? And you are Saul!'
And the king said to her, 'Do not fear. What have you seen?' And the woman said to Saul, 'I have seen a divine being coming up from the earth.'
And he said to her, 'What is his form?' And she said, 'An old man is coming up, and he is wrapped in a robe.' And Saul knew that it was Samuel, and he bowed his face to the ground and bowed down.

And Samuel said to Saul, 'Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?' And Saul said, 'I am in great distress, and the Philistines are fighting against me, and God has turned aside from me and does not answer me any more, neither by the hand of the prophets nor by dreams. So I have called you, to make known to me what I should do.'
And Samuel said, 'And why do you ask me, when the LORD has turned aside from you and has become your enemy?
And the LORD has done to him as he spoke by my hand: the LORD has torn the kingdom from your hand and given it to your neighbour, to David.
Since you did not listen to the voice of the LORD, and did not execute the burning of his anger upon Amalek, therefore the LORD has done this thing to you this day.

And the LORD will give Israel also with you into the hand of the Philistines. And tomorrow you and your sons will be with me. The LORD will also give the camp of Israel into the hand of the Philistines.

And Saul hastened and fell full length to the ground, and he was exceedingly afraid because of Samuel's words. And there was no strength in him, for he had eaten no food all that day and all that night.

And the woman came to Saul and saw that he was greatly terrified, and she said to him, 'Your maidservant has listened to your voice, and I have taken my life in my hand and listened to your words that you spoke to me.
And now, listen, you also, to the voice of your maidservant, and let me set before you a piece of bread; and eat, so that there may be strength in you, for you will go on your way.'
And he refused and said, 'I will not eat.' But his servants urged him, and the woman also; and he listened to their voice, and rose from the ground and sat on the bed.
And the woman had a stall-fed calf in the house, and she hastened and slaughtered it; and she took flour and kneaded it and baked unleavened bread.
And she set it before Saul and before his servants, and they ate. And they arose and went away that night.

1 samuel_29.t: And the Philistines gathered all their forces at Aphek; and Israel were encamped at the spring which is in Jezreel.
And the rulers of the Philistines were passing along by hundreds and by thousands, and David and his men were passing along at the rear with Achish.

And the commanders of the Philistines said, 'What are these Hebrews?' And Achish said to the commanders of the Philistines, 'Is not this David, the servant of Saul king of Israel, who has been with me these days, or these years? And I have found nothing in him from the day he fell away until this day.'

And the commanders of the Philistines were angry with him, and the commanders of the Philistines said to him, 'Send the man back, and let him return to the place where you assigned him. Let him not go down with us into the battle, and let him not become an opponent to us in the battle. For how would this fellow make himself acceptable to his master? Would it not be with the heads of these men?'
Is not this David, of whom they sing in the dances, 'Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his ten thousands'?

And Achish called David and said to him, 'As the LORD lives, you are upright, and your going out and your coming in with me in the camp is good in my eyes, for I have not found evil in you from the day you came to me until this day. But in the eyes of the rulers you are not good.
And now, return and go in peace, and do nothing evil in the eyes of the rulers of the Philistines.'

And David said to Achish, 'But what have I done, and what have you found in your servant, from the day that I was before you until this day, that I should not go and fight against the enemies of my lord the king?'
And Achish answered David, 'I know that you are good in my eyes, like an angel of God; nevertheless the commanders of the Philistines have said, "He shall not go up with us into the battle."
And now, rise early in the morning, you and the servants of your master who came with you; rise early in the morning, and when it is light for you, go.'
And David rose early, he and his men, to go in the morning, to return to the land of the Philistines; and the Philistines went up to Jezreel.

1 samuel_30.t: And when David and his men came to Ziklag on the third day, the Amalekites had made a raid against the Negev and against Ziklag; and they had struck Ziklag and burned it with fire.
And they had taken captive the women who were in it, from small to great; they had not put anyone to death, but had driven them away and gone on their way.
And David and his men came to the city, and it was burned with fire; and their wives and their sons and their daughters had been taken captive.
And David and the people who were with him lifted up their voice and wept, until there was no strength in them to weep.
And David's two wives had been taken captive, Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.

And David was in great distress, for the people spoke of stoning him, because the being of all the people was bitter, each for his sons and for his daughters. But David strengthened himself in the LORD his God.
And David said to Abiathar the priest, son of Ahimelech, 'Bring the ephod near to me.' And Abiathar brought the ephod near to David.
And David enquired of the LORD, 'Shall I pursue this band? Shall I overtake it?' And he said to him, 'Pursue, for you will surely overtake and will surely rescue.'
And David went, he and the six hundred men who were with him, and they came to the wadi Besor; and those who were left behind remained.
And David pursued, he and four hundred men; and two hundred men remained, who were too exhausted to cross the wadi Besor.
And they found an Egyptian man in the open country and took him to David; and they gave him bread and he ate, and they gave him water to drink.
And they gave him a slice of fig cake and two bunches of raisins; and he ate, and his spirit returned to him, for he had eaten no food and drunk no water three days and three nights.

And David said to him, 'To whom do you belong, and where are you from?' And he said, 'I am an Egyptian lad, a slave to an Amalekite man; and my master abandoned me, because I fell sick three days ago.'
'We had made a raid on the Negev of the Kerethites, and on what belongs to Judah, and on the Negev of Caleb; and we burned Ziklag with fire.'

And David said to him, 'Will you take me down to this band?' And he said, 'Swear to me by God that you will not kill me and that you will not deliver me into the hand of my master, and I will take you down to this band.'

And he took him down, and they were spread out over the face of all the land, eating and drinking and celebrating, because of all the great plunder that they had taken from the land of the Philistines and from the land of Judah.
And David struck them down from the twilight until the evening of the next day; and not a man of them escaped, except four hundred young men who rode on the camels and fled.
And David rescued all that Amalek had taken; and his two wives David rescued.
And nothing of theirs was missing, from small to great, sons and daughters, and plunder, and everything they had taken for themselves; David brought back the whole of it.
And David took all the sheep and the cattle. They drove them ahead of the other livestock and said, 'This is David's plunder.'

And David came to the two hundred men who had been too exhausted to go after David, and whom they had left behind at the wadi Besor; and they went out to meet David and to meet the people who were with him. And David approached the people and greeted them.

And every evil and worthless man of those who had gone with David said, 'Because they did not go with me, we will not give them any of the plunder that we have recovered — except each man his wife and his children. Let them lead them away and go.'
And David said, 'You shall not do so, my brothers, with what the LORD has given us; and he has kept us, and has given the band that came against us into our hand.
And who will listen to you in this matter? For as the share of the one who goes down into the battle, so is the share of the one who remains with the baggage; they shall share alike.
And it was so from that day onward, and he made it a statute and an ordinance for Israel, until this day.
And David came to Ziklag and sent some of the plunder to the elders of Judah, to his neighbours: 'Here is a blessing for you, from the plunder of the enemies of the LORD.'
to those in Bethel, and to those in Ramoth of the Negev, and to those in Jattir,
and to those in Aroer, and to those in Siphmoth, and to those in Eshtemoa,
and to those in Racal, and to those in the cities of the Jerahmeelites, and to those in the cities of the Kenites,
and to those in Hormah, and to those in Bor Ashan, and to those in Athach,
and to those in Hebron, and to all the places where David had gone about, he and his men.

1 samuel_31.t: Now the Philistines were fighting against Israel; and the men of Israel fled from before the Philistines, and they fell slain on Mount Gilboa.
And the Philistines pursued closely after Saul and his sons; and the Philistines struck down Jonathan and Abinadab and Malchi-shua, the sons of Saul.
And the battle grew heavy against Saul, and the archers, men with the bow, found him; and he was in severe pain from the archers.

And Saul said to his armour-bearer, 'Draw your sword and pierce me through with it, lest these uncircumcised come and pierce me through and deal wantonly with me.' But his armour-bearer was not willing, for he was very afraid. So Saul took the sword and fell upon it.
And his armour-bearer saw that Saul was dead, and he also fell upon his sword and died with him.
So Saul died, and his three sons, and his armour-bearer, and also all his men, on that day together.

And the men of Israel who were on the other side of the valley, and those on the other side of the Jordan, saw that the men of Israel had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead; and they abandoned the cities and fled. And the Philistines came and dwelt in them.
And on the next day the Philistines came to strip the slain, and they found Saul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.
And they cut off his head and stripped off his armour, and they sent through the land of the Philistines all around, to bear the news to the house of their idols and to the people.
And they put his armour in the house of Ashtaroth, and they fixed his body to the wall of Beth Shan.
And the inhabitants of Jabesh Gilead heard concerning him what the Philistines had done to Saul.
And every man of valour arose and went all the night, and they took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Beth Shan; and they came to Jabesh and burned them there.
And they took their bones and buried them under the tamarisk at Jabesh, and they fasted seven days.

2 chronicles_1.t: And Solomon son of David strengthened his hold on his kingdom, and the LORD his God was with him and made him exceedingly great.
And Solomon spoke to all Israel — to the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, to the judges, and to every leader in all Israel, the heads of the ancestral houses —
and Solomon and all the assembly with him went to the high place at Gibeon; for the tent of meeting of God, which Moses the servant of the LORD had made in the wilderness, was there.
But the ark of God David had brought up from Kiriath-jearim to the place David had prepared for it, for he had pitched a tent for it in Jerusalem.
And the bronze altar that Bezalel son of Uri son of Hur had made was set before the tabernacle of the LORD; and Solomon and the assembly sought it out.
And Solomon went up there to the bronze altar before the LORD, which belonged to the tent of meeting, and offered up on it a thousand burnt offerings.
In that night God appeared to Solomon and said to him, "Ask what I shall give you."
And Solomon said to God, "You have shown great steadfast love to David my father, and have made me king in his place.
"Now, LORD God, let your word to David my father be established; for you have made me king over a people as numerous as the dust of the earth.
"Now give me wisdom and knowledge, that I may go out before this people and come in; for who can judge this great people of yours?"

And God said to Solomon, "Because this was in your heart, and you did not ask for wealth, riches and honour, nor for the life of those who hate you, and did not even ask for long life, but asked for yourself wisdom and knowledge to judge my people over whom I have made you king —
"the wisdom and the knowledge are given to you; and I will give you wealth and riches and honour such as no kings before you have had, and none after you will have."
Then Solomon came from the high place at Gibeon, from before the tent of meeting, to Jerusalem; and he reigned over Israel.
And Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen; he had one thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, and he stationed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.
And the king made silver and gold as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedars as common as the sycamores of the Shephelah, for abundance.
And Solomon's horses were exported from Egypt and from Que; the king's traders procured them from Que at a price.
And they imported from Egypt a chariot for six hundred shekels of silver and a horse for a hundred and fifty; and so, through them, for all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram.

2 chronicles_2.t: And Solomon resolved to build a house for the name of the LORD and a house for his kingship.
And Solomon counted out seventy thousand men as burden-bearers, eighty thousand as stonecutters in the hill country, and three thousand six hundred as overseers over them.
And Solomon sent to Huram king of Tyre, saying, "As you dealt with David my father and sent him cedars to build himself a house to live in —

"I am building a house for the name of the LORD my God, to set it apart as holy to him, to burn fragrant incense before him, and for the continual row of bread, and burnt offerings morning and evening, for the sabbaths and the new moons and the appointed times of the LORD our God — this is laid upon Israel for ever.
"And the house that I am building will be great, for our God is greater than all gods.
"And who has the strength to build him a house, when the heavens and the highest heavens cannot contain him? And who am I, that I should build him a house — except to burn incense before him?

"So now send me a skilled man to work in gold, silver, bronze and iron, and in purple, scarlet and violet, and who knows how to engrave engravings, to work with the skilled men who are with me in Judah and Jerusalem, whom David my father appointed.
"And send me cedar, fir and algum timber from Lebanon; for I know that your servants know how to cut the timber of Lebanon. And my servants will work with your servants,
"and prepare timber for me in abundance; for the house I am building is to be great and wonderful.

"And to the woodcutters, those who fell the timber, I give crushed wheat for your servants: twenty thousand cors, and twenty thousand cors of barley, and twenty thousand baths of wine, and twenty thousand baths of oil."
And Huram king of Tyre replied in a letter, which he sent to Solomon: "Because the LORD loves his people, he has made you king over them."

And Huram said, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who made the heavens and the earth, who has given King David a wise son, endowed with insight and understanding, who will build a house for the LORD and a house for his kingship.
"And now I have sent a skilled man, endowed with understanding — Huram-abi,

"the son of a woman of the daughters of Dan, his father a man of Tyre — skilled to work in gold and silver, in bronze and iron, in stone and wood, in purple, violet, fine linen and scarlet, and to engrave any engraving and devise any design assigned to him, together with your skilled men and the skilled men of my lord David your father.
"And now let my lord send to his servants the wheat and the barley, the oil and the wine of which he has spoken.
"And we will cut timber from Lebanon according to all your need, and bring it to you in rafts by sea to Joppa; and you will take it up to Jerusalem."

And Solomon counted all the resident aliens in the land of Israel, after the census by which David his father had counted them; and they were found to be a hundred and fifty-three thousand six hundred.
And he appointed from them seventy thousand as burden-bearers, eighty thousand as stonecutters in the hill country, and three thousand six hundred as overseers to keep the people at work.

2 chronicles_3.t: Then Solomon began to build the house of the LORD in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where he had appeared to David his father, at the place David had prepared, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
He began to build in the second month, on the second day, in the fourth year of his reign.
And these are the foundations Solomon laid for building the house of God: the length, in cubits by the former measure, sixty cubits; the breadth, twenty cubits.
And the porch in front, running along the breadth of the house, was twenty cubits; and the height, a hundred and twenty. And he overlaid it within with pure gold.
And the great house he panelled with fir wood and overlaid with fine gold, and set on it palms and chains.
And he adorned the house with precious stone for beauty; and the gold was gold of Parvaim.
And he overlaid the house — the beams, the thresholds, its walls and its doors — with gold, and engraved cherubim on the walls.
And he made the house of the holy of holies: its length, along the breadth of the house, twenty cubits, and its breadth twenty cubits. And he overlaid it with fine gold, six hundred talents' worth.
And the weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold; and the upper rooms he overlaid with gold.
And in the house of the holy of holies he made two cherubim, of cast work, and they overlaid them with gold.

And the wings of the cherubim: their span was twenty cubits. The wing of the one was five cubits, touching the wall of the house; and its other wing, five cubits, touching the wing of the other cherub.
And one wing of the second cherub, five cubits, touched the wall of the house; and its other wing, five cubits, clung to the wing of the other cherub.
The wings of these cherubim spread out twenty cubits; and they stood on their feet, with their faces toward the house.
And he made the veil of violet, purple, scarlet and fine linen, and worked cherubim on it.
And he made two pillars in front of the house, thirty-five cubits long; and the capital on the top of each was five cubits.
And he made chains in the inner sanctuary and put them on the tops of the pillars; and he made a hundred pomegranates and put them on the chains.
And he set up the pillars in front of the main hall, one on the right and one on the left; and he named the one on the right Jakin, and the one on the left Boaz.

2 chronicles_4.t: And he made a bronze altar, twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide and ten cubits high.
And he made the sea, of cast metal: ten cubits from rim to rim, circular all around; five cubits high; and a line of thirty cubits encircled it.
And the likeness of oxen was beneath it, all around, encircling it — ten to the cubit, going round the sea all around; the oxen were in two rows, cast in one piece with it.
It stood on twelve oxen: three facing north, three facing west, three facing south and three facing east; the sea rested on them, and all their hindquarters were inward.
Its thickness was a handbreadth, and its rim was made like the rim of a cup, like a lily blossom; it held three thousand baths.
And he made ten washbasins, and set five on the right and five on the left, for washing in them; what belonged to the burnt offering they rinsed in them. But the sea was for the priests to wash in.
And he made the ten gold lampstands according to their specification, and set them in the main hall, five on the right and five on the left.
And he made ten tables and placed them in the main hall, five on the right and five on the left. And he made a hundred gold basins.
And he made the court of the priests, and the great precinct, and doors for the precinct; and he overlaid their doors with bronze.
And he put the sea on the right side, toward the east, opposite the south.
And Huram made the pots, the shovels and the basins. And Huram finished the work that he did for King Solomon in the house of God:
two pillars, and the bowls and the capitals on the tops of the two pillars, and the two networks to cover the two bowls of the capitals on the tops of the pillars;
and the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks — two rows of pomegranates for each network — to cover the two bowls of the capitals in front of the pillars.
And he made the stands, and he made the washbasins on the stands;
the one sea, and the twelve oxen under it;
and the pots, the shovels, the forks and all their articles Huram-abi made for King Solomon, for the house of the LORD, of polished bronze.
In the plain of the Jordan the king cast them, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zeredah.
And Solomon made all these articles in great abundance, for the weight of the bronze was not ascertained.
And Solomon made all the articles that were in the house of God: the gold altar, and the tables with the bread of the Presence on them;
and the lampstands with their lamps, to burn as prescribed before the inner sanctuary, of refined gold;
and the flowers, the lamps and the tongs, of gold — the purest gold;

and the snuffers, the basins, the pans and the firepans, of refined gold. And as for the entrance of the house: its inner doors to the holy of holies, and the doors of the house of the main hall, were gold.

2 chronicles_5.t: So all the work that Solomon did for the house of the LORD was complete. And Solomon brought in the holy things of David his father — the silver, the gold and all the articles — and put them in the treasuries of the house of God.

Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel and all the chiefs of the tribes, the leaders of the ancestral houses of the Israelites, to Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the city of David, that is, Zion.
And every man of Israel assembled to the king at the festival, in the seventh month.
And all the elders of Israel came, and the Levites took up the ark.
And they brought up the ark and the tent of meeting and all the holy articles that were in the tent; the priests and the Levites brought them up.
And King Solomon and all the congregation of Israel who had gathered to him before the ark were sacrificing sheep and cattle that could not be counted or numbered for multitude.
And the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place, to the inner sanctuary of the house, to the holy of holies, beneath the wings of the cherubim.
And the cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubim covered the ark and its poles from above.
And the poles were long, and the ends of the poles were visible from the ark in front of the inner sanctuary, but they were not visible outside; and it has been there to this day.
There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets that Moses put there at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the Israelites when they came out of Egypt.
And when the priests came out from the holy place — for all the priests who were present had set themselves apart as holy, without keeping to their divisions —

and the Levites, the singers — all of them: Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun, with their sons and their brothers — clothed in fine linen, with cymbals, harps and lyres, stood east of the altar, and with them a hundred and twenty priests blowing trumpets —

and the trumpeters and the singers were as one, to make one voice heard in praise and thanks to the LORD; and when they lifted up the voice with trumpets and cymbals and instruments of song, praising the LORD — "For he is good, for his steadfast love is for ever" — the house was filled with a cloud, the house of the LORD,
and the priests were not able to stand and serve because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD filled the house of God.

2 chronicles_6.t: Then Solomon said: "The LORD has said that he would dwell in thick darkness.
"And I have built you a lofty house, a place for your dwelling for ever."
Then the king turned his face and blessed all the assembly of Israel, while all the assembly of Israel stood.
And he said, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who spoke with his mouth to David my father and with his hands has fulfilled it, saying,

"'Since the day I brought my people out of the land of Egypt, I have not chosen a city out of all the tribes of Israel in which to build a house for my name to be there, nor have I chosen a man to be ruler over my people Israel;
"'but I have chosen Jerusalem for my name to be there, and I have chosen David to be over my people Israel.'
"Now it was in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
"And the LORD said to David my father, 'Because it was in your heart to build a house for my name, you did well that it was in your heart;
"'only you shall not build the house; but your son, who comes from your loins, he shall build the house for my name.'

"And the LORD has established the word he spoke; and I have risen in place of David my father and sat on the throne of Israel, as the LORD spoke, and I have built the house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
"And I have put the ark there, where the covenant of the LORD is, which he made with the Israelites."
And he stood before the altar of the LORD, in front of all the assembly of Israel, and spread out his hands.

For Solomon had made a bronze platform and set it in the middle of the precinct, five cubits long, five cubits wide and three cubits high. And he stood on it, knelt on his knees in front of all the assembly of Israel, and spread out his hands toward the heavens.
And he said, "LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like you in the heavens or on the earth, keeping covenant and steadfast love with your servants who walk before you with all their heart;
"who have kept for your servant David my father what you spoke to him; you spoke with your mouth and with your hand have fulfilled it, as it is this day.

"And now, LORD, God of Israel, keep for your servant David my father what you spoke to him, saying, 'You shall never lack a man before me to sit on the throne of Israel — if only your sons keep their way, to walk in my law as you have walked before me.'
"And now, LORD, God of Israel, let your word be established, which you spoke to your servant David.
"For will God really dwell with humankind on the earth? Look — the heavens and the highest heavens cannot contain you; how much less this house that I have built!
"But turn to the prayer of your servant and to his supplication, LORD my God, to listen to the cry and to the prayer that your servant is praying before you,
"that your eyes may be open toward this house day and night, toward the place of which you said you would put your name there, to listen to the prayer that your servant prays toward this place.
"And listen to the supplications of your servant and of your people Israel, which they pray toward this place; and hear from the place of your dwelling, from the heavens — hear and forgive.
"If anyone sins against his neighbour and an oath is laid on him to put him under oath, and he comes and swears the oath before your altar in this house,
"then hear from the heavens and act, and judge your servants, repaying the guilty by putting his conduct on his own head, and vindicating the righteous by giving him according to his righteousness.
"And if your people Israel are defeated before an enemy because they sin against you, and they turn back and give thanks to your name and pray and make supplication before you in this house,
"then hear from the heavens and forgive the sin of your people Israel, and bring them back to the ground that you gave to them and to their ancestors.
"When the heavens are shut up and there is no rain because they sin against you, and they pray toward this place and give thanks to your name and turn from their sin because you afflict them,

"then hear in the heavens and forgive the sin of your servants and of your people Israel, for you will direct them to the good way in which they should walk; and give rain on your land, which you gave to your people as an inheritance.
"If there is famine in the land, if there is pestilence, blight or mildew, locust or grasshopper; if their enemies besiege them in the land of their own towns — any plague, any sickness —
"whatever prayer, whatever supplication comes from any person or from all your people Israel, each knowing his own plague and his own pain, and he spreads out his hands toward this house,
"then hear from the heavens, the place of your dwelling, and forgive; and give to each according to all his ways, whose heart you know — for you alone know the heart of the children of humankind —
"so that they may fear you and walk in your ways all the days they live on the face of the ground that you gave to our ancestors.

"And also as for the foreigner who is not of your people Israel, and who comes from a distant land for the sake of your great name and your mighty hand and your outstretched arm — when they come and pray toward this house —

"then hear from the heavens, from the place of your dwelling, and do according to all that the foreigner calls to you for; so that all the peoples of the earth may know your name and fear you as your people Israel do, and know that your name is called over this house that I have built.
"If your people go out to battle against their enemies by the way you send them, and they pray to you toward this city that you have chosen and the house that I have built for your name,
"then hear from the heavens their prayer and their supplication, and maintain their cause.
"If they sin against you — for there is no one who does not sin — and you are angry with them and give them up before an enemy, and their captors take them captive to a land far off or near,

"and they take it to heart in the land where they have been taken captive, and turn back and make supplication to you in the land of their captivity, saying, 'We have sinned, we have done wrong, we have acted wickedly';

"and they return to you with all their heart and with all their soul in the land of their captivity where they were taken, and pray toward their land that you gave to their ancestors, and the city you have chosen, and toward the house that I have built for your name;
"then hear from the heavens, from the place of your dwelling, their prayer and their supplications, and maintain their cause; and forgive your people who have sinned against you.
"Now, my God, let your eyes be open and your ears attentive to the prayer of this place.
"And now, arise, LORD God, to your resting place, you and the ark of your strength. Let your priests, LORD God, be clothed with salvation, and let your loyal ones rejoice in the good.
"LORD God, do not turn away the face of your anointed one; remember your steadfast love for David your servant."

2 chronicles_7.t: When Solomon finished praying, fire came down from the heavens and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices; and the glory of the LORD filled the house.
And the priests were not able to enter the house of the LORD, for the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD.

And all the Israelites were watching as the fire came down and the glory of the LORD was over the house; and they bowed with their faces to the ground on the pavement and prostrated themselves, giving thanks to the LORD: "For he is good, for his steadfast love is for ever."
And the king and all the people were offering sacrifices before the LORD.
And King Solomon sacrificed twenty-two thousand cattle and a hundred and twenty thousand sheep; and the king and all the people dedicated the house of God.

And the priests stood at their duties, and the Levites with the instruments of the song of the LORD that King David had made, to give thanks to the LORD — "for his steadfast love is for ever" — when David praised by their hand; and the priests blew trumpets before them, and all Israel stood.

And Solomon set apart as holy the middle of the court in front of the house of the LORD, for there he offered the burnt offerings and the fat of the peace offerings; because the bronze altar that Solomon had made could not hold the burnt offering, the grain offering and the fat.
And Solomon observed the festival at that time for seven days, and all Israel with him — a very great assembly, from Lebo-hamath to the wadi of Egypt.
And on the eighth day they held a solemn assembly, for they had observed the dedication of the altar for seven days and the festival for seven days.

And on the twenty-third day of the seventh month he sent the people away to their tents, joyful and glad of heart over the good that the LORD had done for David and for Solomon and for Israel his people.
So Solomon finished the house of the LORD and the king's house; and everything that came into Solomon's heart to do in the house of the LORD and in his own house he carried through successfully.
And the LORD appeared to Solomon in the night and said to him, "I have heard your prayer and have chosen this place for myself as a house of sacrifice.
"If I shut up the heavens so that there is no rain, or command the grasshopper to devour the land, or send pestilence among my people,
"and my people over whom my name is called humble themselves and pray and seek my face and turn from their evil ways, then I will hear from the heavens and forgive their sin and heal their land.
"Now my eyes will be open and my ears attentive to the prayer of this place.
"And now I have chosen and set apart as holy this house, for my name to be there for ever; and my eyes and my heart will be there all the days.
"And as for you, if you walk before me as David your father walked, and do according to all that I have commanded you, and keep my statutes and my judgements,
"then I will establish the throne of your kingdom, as I covenanted with David your father, saying, 'You shall never lack a man to rule in Israel.'
"But if you turn away and forsake my statutes and my commandments that I have set before you, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them,

"then I will pluck them up from my ground that I have given them; and this house that I have set apart as holy for my name I will cast away from before my face, and make it a byword and a taunt among all the peoples.
"And this house, which was so exalted — everyone passing by it will be appalled and will say, 'Why has the LORD done this to this land and to this house?'

"And they will say, 'Because they forsook the LORD, the God of their ancestors, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and took hold of other gods and bowed down to them and served them — therefore he has brought on them all this calamity.'"

2 chronicles_8.t: And at the end of twenty years, in which Solomon had built the house of the LORD and his own house,
the cities that Huram had given to Solomon — Solomon rebuilt them and settled the Israelites there.
And Solomon went to Hamath-zobah and prevailed over it.
And he built Tadmor in the wilderness, and all the storage cities that he built in Hamath.
And he built Upper Beth-horon and Lower Beth-horon, fortified cities with walls, doors and bars;

and Baalath, and all the storage cities that Solomon had, and all the chariot cities and the cities of the horsemen, and everything Solomon desired to build in Jerusalem and in Lebanon and in all the land of his dominion.
All the people who remained of the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, who were not of Israel —
some of their descendants who remained after them in the land, whom the Israelites had not destroyed — Solomon brought them up as forced labour, to this day.
But of the Israelites Solomon made none slaves for his work; they were the men of war, the commanders of his officers, and the commanders of his chariotry and his horsemen.
And these were the commanders of the overseers who belonged to King Solomon: two hundred and fifty, who ruled over the people.

And Solomon brought Pharaoh's daughter up from the city of David to the house he had built for her; for he said, "No wife of mine shall live in the house of David king of Israel, for the places to which the ark of the LORD has come are holy."
Then Solomon offered up burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of the LORD that he had built before the porch,

and according to the requirement of each day, to offer up according to the commandment of Moses: for the sabbaths, the new moons and the appointed times, three times a year — at the festival of unleavened bread, the festival of weeks and the festival of booths.

And he appointed, according to the ordinance of David his father, the divisions of the priests over their service, and the Levites over their duties, to praise and to serve before the priests, according to the requirement of each day; and the gatekeepers by their divisions for each gate — for such was the commandment of David the man of God.
And they did not turn aside from the king's commandment concerning the priests and the Levites in any matter, or concerning the treasuries.
So all Solomon's work was arranged, from the day of the foundation of the house of the LORD until its completion; the house of the LORD was finished.
Then Solomon went to Ezion-geber and to Eloth, on the seashore in the land of Edom.

And Huram sent him, by the hand of his servants, ships and crews who knew the sea; and they went with Solomon's servants to Ophir and took from there four hundred and fifty talents of gold, and brought it to King Solomon.

2 chronicles_9.t: And the queen of Sheba heard the report of Solomon, and came to test Solomon with hard questions at Jerusalem, with a very great retinue, and camels carrying spices and gold in abundance and precious stone. She came to Solomon and spoke with him about all that was in her heart.
And Solomon answered all her questions; nothing was hidden from Solomon that he did not tell her.
And the queen of Sheba saw the wisdom of Solomon, and the house that he had built,

and the food of his table, the seating of his servants, the attendance of his attendants and their clothing, his cupbearers and their clothing, and his ascent by which he went up to the house of the LORD — and there was no more breath in her.
And she said to the king, "The report I heard in my own land about your words and your wisdom was true.
"And I did not believe their words until I came and my own eyes saw; and behold, not half the greatness of your wisdom was told me. You have surpassed the report I heard.
"How blessed are your men, and how blessed these servants of yours who stand before you continually and hear your wisdom!

"May the LORD your God be blessed, who delighted in you to set you on his throne as king for the LORD your God; because your God loves Israel and would establish it for ever, he has made you king over them, to do judgement and righteousness."
And she gave the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold, spices in very great abundance, and precious stone; there has never been spice like that which the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
And the servants of Huram and the servants of Solomon, who brought gold from Ophir, also brought algum timber and precious stone.

And the king made the algum timber into walkways for the house of the LORD and for the king's house, and into lyres and harps for the singers; and none like them had been seen before in the land of Judah.
And King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba all she desired and asked for, besides what she had brought to the king. Then she turned and went to her own land, she and her servants.
And the weight of the gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold,
apart from what the travelling merchants and the traders brought in; and all the kings of Arabia and the governors of the land brought gold and silver to Solomon.
And King Solomon made two hundred large shields of beaten gold; six hundred shekels of beaten gold went on each large shield.
And three hundred shields of beaten gold; three hundred shekels of gold went on each shield. And the king put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
And the king made a great ivory throne and overlaid it with pure gold.
The throne had six steps and a gold footstool attached to it, and armrests on either side of the seat, with two lions standing beside the armrests;
and twelve lions standing there on the six steps, on either side. Nothing like it had been made for any kingdom.
And all King Solomon's drinking vessels were gold, and all the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were refined gold; silver was reckoned as nothing in the days of Solomon.
For the king had ships going to Tarshish with the servants of Huram; once in three years the ships of Tarshish would come in, carrying gold and silver, ivory, monkeys and apes.
And King Solomon became greater than all the kings of the earth in wealth and wisdom.
And all the kings of the earth sought the face of Solomon, to hear his wisdom that God had put in his heart.
And they brought, each his gift — articles of silver and articles of gold, garments, weaponry, spices, horses and mules — year by year.
And Solomon had four thousand stalls for horses and chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen; and he stationed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.
And he ruled over all the kings from the River to the land of the Philistines and to the border of Egypt.
And the king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedars as common as the sycamores of the Shephelah, for abundance.
And horses were brought out for Solomon from Egypt and from all the lands.

And the rest of the acts of Solomon, from first to last — are they not written in the words of Nathan the prophet, in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the visions of Iddo the seer concerning Jeroboam son of Nebat?
And Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel forty years.
And Solomon lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him in the city of David his father; and Rehoboam his son became king in his place.

2 chronicles_10.t: And Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king.
And when Jeroboam son of Nebat heard of it — he was in Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon — Jeroboam returned from Egypt.
So they sent and called him; and Jeroboam and all Israel came and spoke to Rehoboam, saying,
"Your father made our yoke hard. Now lighten the hard labour of your father and the heavy yoke he put on us, and we will serve you."
And he said to them, "Come back to me in three days." And the people went.
And King Rehoboam consulted the elders who had stood before Solomon his father while he was alive, saying, "How do you counsel me to answer this people?"
And they said to him, "If you will be good to this people and show them favour and speak kind words to them, they will be your servants always."
But he abandoned the counsel of the elders that they had given him, and consulted the young men who had grown up with him and stood before him.
And he said to them, "What do you counsel, that we may answer this people, who have said to me, 'Lighten the yoke your father put on us'?"

And the young men who had grown up with him said to him, "This is what you shall say to the people who said to you, 'Your father made our yoke heavy; now lighten it for us' — this is what you shall say to them: 'My little finger is thicker than my father's loins.
"'And now, my father loaded a heavy yoke on you; I will add to your yoke. My father disciplined you with whips; I will use scorpions.'"
And Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king had said: "Come back to me on the third day."
And the king answered them harshly; King Rehoboam abandoned the counsel of the elders,
and spoke to them according to the counsel of the young men, saying, "I will make your yoke heavy, and I will add to it. My father disciplined you with whips; I will use scorpions."
And the king did not listen to the people; for it was a turn of events from God, so that the LORD might establish the word he had spoken by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.

And when all Israel saw that the king had not listened to them, the people answered the king: "What portion have we in David? We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse! Each to your tents, Israel! Now see to your own house, David!" And all Israel went to their tents.
But as for the Israelites who lived in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned over them.
And King Rehoboam sent Hadoram, who was over the forced labour; and the Israelites stoned him to death. And King Rehoboam hastened to mount his chariot and flee to Jerusalem.
And Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David to this day.

2 chronicles_11.t: And Rehoboam came to Jerusalem and assembled the house of Judah and Benjamin — a hundred and eighty thousand chosen fighting men — to fight against Israel and restore the kingdom to Rehoboam.
And the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah the man of God, saying,
"Say to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all Israel in Judah and Benjamin:

"Thus says the LORD: 'You shall not go up and you shall not fight against your brothers. Return, each to his own house, for this thing has come about from me.'" And they obeyed the words of the LORD and turned back from going against Jeroboam.
And Rehoboam lived in Jerusalem, and built cities for fortification in Judah.
He built Bethlehem, Etam and Tekoa,
Beth-zur, Socoh and Adullam,
Gath, Mareshah and Ziph,
Adoraim, Lachish and Azekah,
Zorah, Aijalon and Hebron, which are in Judah and in Benjamin — fortified cities.
And he strengthened the fortifications and put commanders in them, with stores of food, oil and wine.
And in every single city he put large shields and spears, and made them exceedingly strong. And Judah and Benjamin were his.
And the priests and the Levites who were in all Israel took their stand with him from all their territory,
for the Levites left their pasture lands and their holdings and went to Judah and Jerusalem, because Jeroboam and his sons had rejected them from serving as priests to the LORD.
And he appointed for himself priests for the high places, for the goat-demons and for the calves that he had made.
And after them, from all the tribes of Israel, those who set their heart to seek the LORD, the God of Israel, came to Jerusalem to sacrifice to the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
And they strengthened the kingdom of Judah and made Rehoboam son of Solomon strong for three years, for they walked in the way of David and Solomon for three years.
And Rehoboam took as his wife Mahalath, daughter of Jerimoth son of David, and Abihail daughter of Eliab son of Jesse,
and she bore him sons: Jeush, Shemariah and Zaham.
And after her he took Maacah daughter of Absalom, and she bore him Abijah, Attai, Ziza and Shelomith.
And Rehoboam loved Maacah daughter of Absalom more than all his wives and concubines; for he had taken eighteen wives and sixty concubines, and fathered twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
And Rehoboam appointed Abijah son of Maacah as chief, as leader among his brothers, intending to make him king.

And he acted with understanding, and dispersed some of all his sons through all the lands of Judah and Benjamin, to all the fortified cities; and he gave them provisions in abundance, and sought a multitude of wives for them.

2 chronicles_12.t: And when the kingdom of Rehoboam was established and he had grown strong, he forsook the law of the LORD, and all Israel with him.
And in the fifth year of King Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem — for they had acted unfaithfully against the LORD —
with twelve hundred chariots and sixty thousand horsemen; and the people who came with him from Egypt were without number — Libyans, Sukkiim and Cushites.
And he captured the fortified cities of Judah and came as far as Jerusalem.

And Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and the leaders of Judah, who had gathered at Jerusalem because of Shishak, and said to them, "Thus says the LORD: 'You have abandoned me, and so I also have abandoned you into the hand of Shishak.'"
And the leaders of Israel and the king humbled themselves and said, "The LORD is righteous."

And when the LORD saw that they had humbled themselves, the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah: "They have humbled themselves; I will not destroy them. I will give them a measure of deliverance, and my rage will not be poured out on Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.
"But they will become his servants, so that they may know my service and the service of the kingdoms of the lands."

So Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem and took the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king's house — he took everything; and he took the gold shields that Solomon had made.
And King Rehoboam made bronze shields in their place, and entrusted them to the commanders of the runners who guarded the entrance of the king's house.
And whenever the king came to the house of the LORD, the runners came and carried them, and returned them to the guardroom of the runners.
And when he humbled himself, the anger of the LORD turned back from him, so as not to destroy him utterly; and in Judah too there were good things.

So King Rehoboam strengthened himself in Jerusalem and reigned; for Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city that the LORD had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel to put his name there. And his mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite.
And he did evil, for he did not set his heart to seek the LORD.

And the acts of Rehoboam, from first to last — are they not written in the words of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer, arranged by genealogy? And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually.
And Rehoboam lay down with his ancestors and was buried in the city of David; and Abijah his son became king in his place.

2 chronicles_13.t: In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam, Abijah became king over Judah.
He reigned three years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Micaiah daughter of Uriel of Gibeah. And there was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.
And Abijah joined battle with an army of mighty men of war, four hundred thousand chosen men; and Jeroboam drew up in battle against him with eight hundred thousand chosen men, mighty in strength.
And Abijah stood up on Mount Zemaraim, which is in the hill country of Ephraim, and said, "Hear me, Jeroboam and all Israel!
"Do you not know that the LORD, the God of Israel, gave kingship to David over Israel for ever — to him and to his sons, by a covenant of salt?
"But Jeroboam son of Nebat, the servant of Solomon son of David, arose and rebelled against his master.
"And empty men, worthless fellows, gathered to him and made themselves strong against Rehoboam son of Solomon; and Rehoboam was young and weak of heart, and did not stand strong before them.

"And now you say you will stand strong against the kingdom of the LORD, which is in the hand of the sons of David; and you are a great multitude, and with you are the golden calves that Jeroboam made you as gods.

"Have you not driven out the priests of the LORD, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and made yourselves priests like the peoples of the lands? Anyone who comes to fill his hand with a young bull and seven rams becomes a priest to what are not gods.
"But as for us, the LORD is our God, and we have not forsaken him; the priests who serve the LORD are the sons of Aaron, and the Levites are at their work.

"And they burn to the LORD burnt offerings morning by morning and evening by evening, and fragrant incense, and the row of bread on the pure table, and the golden lampstand and its lamps to burn every evening; for we keep the duty of the LORD our God, and you have forsaken him.

"And look — God is with us at our head, and his priests, with the trumpets of alarm to sound the alarm against you. Israelites, do not fight against the LORD, the God of your ancestors, for you will not succeed."
But Jeroboam had sent the ambush round to come at them from behind; so they were in front of Judah, and the ambush behind them.
And Judah turned, and behold, the battle was before them and behind. And they cried out to the LORD, and the priests blew the trumpets.
