And the men of Judah sounded the alarm; and when the men of Judah sounded the alarm, God defeated Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.
And the Israelites fled before Judah, and God gave them into their hand.
And Abijah and his people struck them a great blow; and there fell slain of Israel five hundred thousand chosen men.
And the Israelites were humbled at that time, and the people of Judah prevailed, because they leaned on the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
And Abijah pursued Jeroboam and captured cities from him: Bethel with its villages, Jeshanah with its villages, and Ephrain with its villages.
And Jeroboam did not recover his strength again in the days of Abijah; and the LORD struck him, and he died.
And Abijah grew strong, and took fourteen wives, and fathered twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.
And the rest of the acts of Abijah, and his ways and his words, are written in the record of the prophet Iddo.

2 chronicles_14.t: And Abijah lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him in the city of David; and Asa his son became king in his place. In his days the land was quiet for ten years.
And Asa did what was good and right in the eyes of the LORD his God.
And he removed the foreign altars and the high places, broke down the pillars and cut down the Asherim.
And he told Judah to seek the LORD, the God of their ancestors, and to keep the law and the commandment.
And he removed the high places and the incense altars from all the cities of Judah; and the kingdom was quiet under him.
And he built fortified cities in Judah, for the land was quiet; there was no war against him in those years, because the LORD had given him rest.

And he said to Judah, "Let us build these cities and surround them with wall and towers, gates and bars. The land is still ours, because we have sought the LORD our God; we sought him, and he has given us rest on every side." So they built and prospered.

And Asa had an army bearing large shield and spear, three hundred thousand from Judah; and from Benjamin, bearing shield and drawing the bow, two hundred and eighty thousand. All these were mighty men of valour.
And Zerah the Cushite came out against them with an army of a million and three hundred chariots, and came as far as Mareshah.
And Asa went out to meet him, and they drew up for battle in the valley of Zephathah at Mareshah.

And Asa called out to the LORD his God and said, "LORD, there is none like you to help, whether the mighty or the one with no strength. Help us, LORD our God, for on you we lean, and in your name we have come against this multitude. LORD, you are our God; let no man retain strength against you."
And the LORD defeated the Cushites before Asa and before Judah, and the Cushites fled.

And Asa and the people with him pursued them as far as Gerar; and the Cushites fell until none of them was left alive, for they were broken before the LORD and before his army. And they carried off very much booty.
And they struck all the cities around Gerar, for the dread of the LORD was on them; and they plundered all the cities, for there was much plunder in them.
And they also struck the herdsmen's tents, and carried off sheep in abundance and camels; and they returned to Jerusalem.

2 chronicles_15.t: And the spirit of God was upon Azariah son of Oded.

And he went out before Asa and said to him, "Hear me, Asa and all Judah and Benjamin: the LORD is with you while you are with him; and if you seek him, he will let himself be found by you; but if you forsake him, he will forsake you.
"And for many days Israel was without a true God, without a teaching priest and without law;
"but in its distress it turned back to the LORD, the God of Israel, and they sought him, and he let himself be found by them.
"And in those times there was no peace for anyone going out or coming in, for great disturbances lay on all the inhabitants of the lands.
"And they were crushed, nation against nation and city against city, for God troubled them with every kind of trouble.
"But you, be strong, and do not let your hands drop, for there is reward for your work."

When Asa heard these words and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage and removed the detestable things from all the land of Judah and Benjamin, and from the cities he had captured in the hill country of Ephraim; and he renewed the altar of the LORD that stood before the porch of the LORD.

And he gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and those living among them from Ephraim, Manasseh and Simeon; for they deserted to him from Israel in great numbers when they saw that the LORD his God was with him.
And they gathered at Jerusalem in the third month, in the fifteenth year of Asa's reign.
And on that day they sacrificed to the LORD, from the booty they had brought: seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep.
And they entered into the covenant, to seek the LORD, the God of their ancestors, with all their heart and with all their soul;
and everyone who would not seek the LORD, the God of Israel, was to be put to death, small or great, man or woman.
And they swore to the LORD with a loud voice, with shouting, with trumpets and with ram's horns.
And all Judah rejoiced over the oath, for they had sworn with all their heart and had sought him with all their will; and he let himself be found by them, and the LORD gave them rest on every side.

And Maacah, the mother of King Asa, he also removed from being queen mother, because she had made an abominable image for an Asherah; and Asa cut down her abominable image, crushed it and burned it in the wadi Kidron.
But the high places were not removed from Israel; yet the heart of Asa was undivided all his days.
And he brought into the house of God the holy things of his father and his own holy things: silver, gold and articles.
And there was no war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's reign.

2 chronicles_16.t: In the thirty-sixth year of Asa's reign, Baasha king of Israel came up against Judah and fortified Ramah, so as to allow no one to go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.
And Asa brought out silver and gold from the treasuries of the house of the LORD and the king's house, and sent to Ben-hadad king of Aram, who lived in Damascus, saying,

"Let there be a covenant between me and you, as between my father and your father. Here, I have sent you silver and gold. Go, break your covenant with Baasha king of Israel, so that he will withdraw from me."
And Ben-hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel; and they struck Ijon, Dan, Abel-maim and all the store cities of Naphtali.
And when Baasha heard of it, he stopped building Ramah and let his work cease.
And King Asa took all Judah, and they carried off the stones of Ramah and its timber that Baasha had built with; and with them he built Geba and Mizpah.

And at that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah and said to him, "Because you leaned on the king of Aram and did not lean on the LORD your God, the army of the king of Aram has escaped from your hand.
"Were not the Cushites and the Libyans a great army, with chariots and horsemen in exceedingly great abundance? Yet because you leaned on the LORD, he gave them into your hand.
"For the eyes of the LORD rove through all the earth, to show himself strong on behalf of those whose heart is undivided toward him. You have acted foolishly in this; from now on you will have wars."
And Asa was angry with the seer and put him in the house of the stocks, for he was in a rage with him over this. And Asa oppressed some of the people at that time.
And the acts of Asa, from first to last — they are written in the scroll of the kings of Judah and Israel.
And in the thirty-ninth year of his reign Asa became diseased in his feet; his disease was exceedingly severe. And even in his disease he did not seek the LORD, but the physicians.
And Asa lay down with his ancestors, and died in the forty-first year of his reign.

And they buried him in his own tomb that he had cut for himself in the city of David, and laid him on the bier that he had filled with spices and various kinds blended by the perfumer's art; and they made an exceedingly great fire for him.

2 chronicles_17.t: And Jehoshaphat his son became king in his place, and he strengthened himself against Israel.
And he stationed an army in all the fortified cities of Judah, and put garrisons in the land of Judah and in the cities of Ephraim that Asa his father had captured.
And the LORD was with Jehoshaphat, for he walked in the earlier ways of David his ancestor, and did not seek the Baals;
for he sought the God of his father, and walked in his commandments and not according to the deeds of Israel.
And the LORD established the kingdom in his hand; and all Judah brought tribute to Jehoshaphat, and he had wealth and honour in abundance.
And his heart was lifted up in the ways of the LORD; and again he removed the high places and the Asherim from Judah.
And in the third year of his reign he sent his officials — Ben-hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel and Micaiah — to teach in the cities of Judah;
and with them the Levites — Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah and Tob-adonijah, the Levites — and with them Elishama and Jehoram, the priests.
And they taught in Judah, and with them was the scroll of the law of the LORD; and they went round through all the cities of Judah and taught among the people.
And the dread of the LORD was on all the kingdoms of the lands around Judah, and they did not make war on Jehoshaphat.
And some of the Philistines brought Jehoshaphat tribute and silver as a load; the Arabs too brought him flocks — seven thousand seven hundred rams and seven thousand seven hundred male goats.
And Jehoshaphat went on growing exceedingly great; and he built fortresses and store cities in Judah.
And he had much property in the cities of Judah; and men of war, mighty men of valour, were in Jerusalem.
And these were their musters by their ancestral houses: of Judah, commanders of thousands — Adnah the commander, and with him three hundred thousand mighty men of valour;
next to him, Jehohanan the commander, and with him two hundred and eighty thousand;
next to him, Amasiah son of Zichri, who volunteered himself to the LORD, and with him two hundred thousand mighty men of valour;
and of Benjamin, a mighty man of valour, Eliada, and with him two hundred thousand equipped with bow and shield;
next to him, Jehozabad, and with him a hundred and eighty thousand equipped for war.
These were those who served the king, besides those the king had stationed in the fortified cities throughout all Judah.

2 chronicles_18.t: Now Jehoshaphat had wealth and honour in abundance; and he made a marriage alliance with Ahab.
And after some years he went down to Ahab at Samaria; and Ahab slaughtered sheep and cattle in abundance for him and for the people with him, and incited him to go up against Ramoth-gilead.

And Ahab king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, "Will you go with me to Ramoth-gilead?" And he said to him, "I am as you are, and my people as your people; and we will be with you in the battle."
And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "Consult the word of the LORD today."

So the king of Israel assembled the prophets, four hundred men, and said to them, "Shall we go to Ramoth-gilead for battle, or shall I desist?" And they said, "Go up, and God will give it into the hand of the king."
But Jehoshaphat said, "Is there not still a prophet of the LORD here, that we may enquire of him?"

And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "There is still one man through whom we may consult the LORD, but I hate him, because he does not prophesy good concerning me but evil all his days — Micaiah son of Imlah." And Jehoshaphat said, "Let not the king say so."
And the king of Israel called one court official and said, "Bring Micaiah son of Imlah quickly."

And the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting, each on his throne, dressed in their robes, at the threshing floor by the entrance of the gate of Samaria; and all the prophets were prophesying before them.
And Zedekiah son of Chenaanah made himself horns of iron and said, "Thus says the LORD: 'With these you shall gore Aram until they are finished.'"
And all the prophets prophesied the same, saying, "Go up to Ramoth-gilead and succeed, and the LORD will give it into the hand of the king."
And the messenger who had gone to call Micaiah said to him, "Look, the words of the prophets are with one mouth favourable to the king; let your word be like one of theirs, and speak favourably."
And Micaiah said, "As the LORD lives, what my God says, that I will speak."
And he came to the king, and the king said to him, "Micah, shall we go to Ramoth-gilead for battle, or shall I desist?" And he said, "Go up and succeed, and they will be given into your hand."
And the king said to him, "How many times must I make you swear to speak to me nothing but truth in the name of the LORD?"
And he said, "I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains, like sheep that have no shepherd. And the LORD said, 'These have no masters; let them return, each to his own house, in peace.'"
And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Did I not tell you that he does not prophesy good concerning me, but evil?"
And he said, "Therefore hear the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD sitting on his throne, and all the host of the heavens standing on his right hand and on his left.
"And the LORD said, 'Who will entice Ahab king of Israel, so that he goes up and falls at Ramoth-gilead?' And one said one thing and another said another.
"Then the spirit came out and stood before the LORD and said, 'I will entice him.' And the LORD said to him, 'By what means?'
"And it said, 'I will go out and become a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.' And he said, 'You will entice, and you will also prevail. Go out and do so.'
"And now look — the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouth of these prophets of yours; and the LORD has spoken calamity concerning you."
Then Zedekiah son of Chenaanah drew near and struck Micaiah on the cheek and said, "Which way did the spirit of the LORD pass from me to speak with you?"
And Micaiah said, "You will see on that day, when you go into an inner room to hide yourself."
And the king of Israel said, "Take Micaiah and return him to Amon the governor of the city, and to Joash the king's son,
"and say, 'Thus says the king: Put this man in the prison house and feed him meagre bread and meagre water, until I return in peace.'"
And Micaiah said, "If you do indeed return in peace, the LORD has not spoken by me." And he said, "Hear, you peoples, all of you!"
So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up against Ramoth-gilead.
And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I will disguise myself and go into the battle, but you wear your own robes." And the king of Israel disguised himself, and they went into the battle.
Now the king of Aram had commanded the commanders of his chariotry, "Do not fight with small or great, but with the king of Israel alone."

And when the commanders of the chariotry saw Jehoshaphat, they said, "He is the king of Israel," and surrounded him to fight. And Jehoshaphat cried out, and the LORD helped him, and God lured them away from him.
And when the commanders of the chariotry saw that he was not the king of Israel, they turned back from pursuing him.
And a man drew his bow at random and struck the king of Israel between the joints of the armour; and he said to the charioteer, "Turn your hand and take me out of the camp, for I am wounded."
And the battle grew fierce that day; and the king of Israel was propped up in his chariot facing Aram until the evening, and he died at the time of sunset.

2 chronicles_19.t: And Jehoshaphat king of Judah returned safely to his house in Jerusalem.

And Jehu son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him and said to King Jehoshaphat, "Should you help the wicked and love those who hate the LORD? Because of this, wrath is upon you from before the LORD.
"But good things have been found in you, for you have burned the Asherahs out of the land and have set your heart to seek God."
And Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem; and he went out again among the people, from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim, and turned them back to the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
And he appointed judges in the land, in all the fortified cities of Judah, city by city;
and he said to the judges, "Consider what you are doing, for you judge not for humankind but for the LORD; and he is with you in giving judgement.
"And now, let the dread of the LORD be upon you. Take care and act, for with the LORD our God there is no injustice, no partiality, and no taking of a bribe."

And in Jerusalem too Jehoshaphat appointed some of the Levites and the priests and some of the heads of the ancestral houses of Israel, for the judgement of the LORD and for disputes; and they returned to Jerusalem.
And he commanded them, "Thus you shall act, in the fear of the LORD, in faithfulness and with an undivided heart.

"And whatever dispute comes to you from your brothers who live in their cities — between one kind of bloodshed and another, between law and commandment, statutes and judgements — you shall warn them, so that they do not become guilty before the LORD and wrath come upon you and your brothers. Do this, and you will not become guilty.

"And Amariah the chief priest is over you for every matter of the LORD, and Zebadiah son of Ishmael, the leader of the house of Judah, for every matter of the king; and the Levites are officials before you. Be strong and act, and may the LORD be with the good."

2 chronicles_20.t: And after this the Moabites and the Ammonites, and with them some of the Ammonites, came against Jehoshaphat for battle.
And they came and told Jehoshaphat, "A great multitude is coming against you from beyond the sea, from Aram; and they are already at Hazazon-tamar" — that is, En-gedi.
And Jehoshaphat was afraid, and set his face to seek the LORD, and proclaimed a fast throughout all Judah.
And Judah gathered to seek from the LORD; from all the cities of Judah too they came to seek the LORD.
And Jehoshaphat stood in the assembly of Judah and Jerusalem, in the house of the LORD, before the new court,
and said, "LORD, God of our ancestors, are you not God in the heavens? You rule over all the kingdoms of the nations; in your hand are power and might, and none can stand against you.
"Did you not, our God, dispossess the inhabitants of this land before your people Israel, and give it to the offspring of Abraham your friend for ever?
"And they lived in it and built you a sanctuary in it for your name, saying,

"'If calamity comes upon us — sword, judgement, pestilence or famine — we will stand before this house and before you, for your name is in this house; and we will cry out to you from our distress, and you will hear and save.'
"And now look — the Ammonites and Moab and Mount Seir, whom you did not allow Israel to invade when they came from the land of Egypt, so that they turned aside from them and did not destroy them —
"and here they are repaying us, by coming to drive us out of your possession that you gave us to possess.
"Our God, will you not judge them? For we have no strength before this great multitude that is coming against us, and we do not know what to do — but our eyes are on you."
And all Judah was standing before the LORD — their little ones too, their wives and their children.
And upon Jahaziel son of Zechariah, son of Benaiah, son of Jeiel, son of Mattaniah, the Levite, of the descendants of Asaph, the spirit of the LORD came in the midst of the assembly.

And he said, "Pay attention, all Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, and King Jehoshaphat! Thus says the LORD to you: 'Do not fear and do not be dismayed before this great multitude, for the battle is not yours but God's.
"'Tomorrow go down against them. They will be coming up by the ascent of Ziz, and you will find them at the end of the wadi, facing the wilderness of Jeruel.

"'It is not for you to fight in this. Take your stand, stand still and see the salvation of the LORD with you, Judah and Jerusalem. Do not fear and do not be dismayed. Tomorrow go out before them, and the LORD will be with you.'"
And Jehoshaphat bowed low, face to the ground; and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fell before the LORD, to prostrate themselves to the LORD.
And the Levites, of the Kohathites and of the Korahites, stood up to praise the LORD, the God of Israel, with an exceedingly loud voice.

And they rose early in the morning and went out to the wilderness of Tekoa. As they went out, Jehoshaphat stood and said, "Hear me, Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem! Trust in the LORD your God and you will be established; trust in his prophets and you will succeed."

And he consulted with the people, and appointed singers to the LORD and those who praise in holy adornment, to go out before the armed men, saying: "Give thanks to the LORD, for his steadfast love is for ever."
And at the moment they began the shout and the praise, the LORD set ambushers against the Ammonites, Moab and Mount Seir who had come against Judah, and they were defeated.

And the Ammonites and Moab rose up against the inhabitants of Mount Seir, to devote them to destruction and to annihilate them; and when they had finished with the inhabitants of Seir, they helped destroy one another.
And Judah came to the watchtower of the wilderness and looked toward the multitude — and there they were, corpses fallen to the ground; and no one had escaped.

And Jehoshaphat and his people came to plunder their booty, and found among them in abundance both goods and corpses and precious articles; and they stripped off so much for themselves that they could carry no more. They were three days plundering the booty, for it was much.
And on the fourth day they assembled in the valley of Berachah, for there they blessed the LORD; that is why the name of that place has been called the valley of Berachah, to this day.
And every man of Judah and Jerusalem turned back, with Jehoshaphat at their head, to return to Jerusalem with joy; for the LORD had made them rejoice over their enemies.
And they came to Jerusalem with harps, lyres and trumpets, to the house of the LORD.
And the dread of God was on all the kingdoms of the lands when they heard that the LORD had fought against the enemies of Israel.
And the kingdom of Jehoshaphat was quiet, and his God gave him rest on every side.
So Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah. He was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.
And he walked in the way of Asa his father and did not turn aside from it, doing what was right in the eyes of the LORD.
Only the high places were not removed, and the people still had not set their heart on the God of their ancestors.
And the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, from first to last, are written in the words of Jehu son of Hanani, which was taken up into the scroll of the kings of Israel.
And after this, Jehoshaphat king of Judah made an alliance with Ahaziah king of Israel, who acted wickedly in what he did.
And he allied himself with him to build ships to go to Tarshish; and they built the ships at Ezion-geber.

And Eliezer son of Dodavahu of Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat, saying, "Because you have allied yourself with Ahaziah, the LORD has broken your works." And the ships were broken, and they could not go to Tarshish.

2 chronicles_21.t: And Jehoshaphat lay down with his ancestors and was buried with his ancestors in the city of David; and Jehoram his son became king in his place.
And he had brothers, the sons of Jehoshaphat: Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariahu, Michael and Shephatiah. All these were the sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel.
And their father gave them many gifts — silver, gold and precious things — with fortified cities in Judah; but the kingdom he gave to Jehoram, for he was the firstborn.
And Jehoram rose over his father's kingdom and strengthened himself, and killed all his brothers with the sword, and also some of the leaders of Israel.
Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, for a daughter of Ahab was his wife; and he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.
But the LORD was not willing to destroy the house of David, on account of the covenant he had made with David, and as he had said — to give him a lamp, and to his sons, for all time.
In his days Edom rebelled from under the hand of Judah, and they made a king over themselves.
And Jehoram crossed over with his commanders, and all the chariotry with him; and he arose by night and struck Edom, which had surrounded him, and the chariot commanders.
So Edom has been in rebellion against the hand of Judah to this day. And Libnah rebelled at that time from under his hand, because he had forsaken the LORD, the God of his ancestors.
He too made high places in the mountains of Judah, made the inhabitants of Jerusalem prostitute themselves, and led Judah astray.

And a letter came to him from Elijah the prophet, saying: "Thus says the LORD, the God of David your ancestor: 'Because you have not walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat your father, or in the ways of Asa king of Judah,

"'but have walked in the way of the kings of Israel, and have made Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem prostitute themselves as the house of Ahab did, and have also killed your brothers, your father's house, who were better than you —
"'the LORD is about to strike a great blow on your people, on your sons and your wives and all your property;
"'and you yourself will suffer great sicknesses, a disease of your bowels, until your bowels come out because of the disease, day after day.'"
And the LORD stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines and the Arabs who were beside the Cushites,

and they came up against Judah and broke into it, and carried off all the property found in the king's house, and also his sons and his wives; and no son was left to him except Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons.
And after all this, the LORD struck him in his bowels with an incurable disease.

And in the course of time, at the end of two years, his bowels came out because of his disease; and he died in agonising diseases. And his people made no fire for him like the fires for his ancestors.

He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem. And he departed with no one's regret; and they buried him in the city of David, but not in the graves of the kings.

2 chronicles_22.t: And the inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah his youngest son king in his place, for the raiding band that had come with the Arabs to the camp had killed all the elder ones. So Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah became king.
Ahaziah was forty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Athaliah, daughter of Omri.
He too walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother was his counsellor, to act wickedly.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, like the house of Ahab; for they were his counsellors after his father's death, to his destruction.
He also walked in their counsel, and went with Jehoram son of Ahab king of Israel to war against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-gilead; and the Arameans wounded Joram.

And he returned to be healed in Jezreel because of the wounds they had inflicted on him at Ramah when he fought Hazael king of Aram. And Azariah son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Jehoram son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he was ill.
And Ahaziah's downfall was from God, in his going to Joram. When he came, he went out with Jehoram to Jehu son of Nimshi, whom the LORD had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab.
And when Jehu was executing judgement on the house of Ahab, he found the officials of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah's brothers, who served Ahaziah, and he killed them.

And he searched for Ahaziah, and they captured him while he was hiding in Samaria; and they brought him to Jehu and put him to death, and they buried him — for they said, "He is the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart." And the house of Ahaziah had no one able to hold the kingship.
And when Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the royal offspring of the house of Judah.

But Jehoshabeath the king's daughter took Joash son of Ahaziah and stole him from among the king's sons who were being put to death, and put him and his nurse in the bedchamber. So Jehoshabeath, daughter of King Jehoram and wife of Jehoiada the priest — for she was Ahaziah's sister — hid him from Athaliah, and she did not kill him.
And he remained with them, hidden in the house of God, six years, while Athaliah reigned over the land.

2 chronicles_23.t: And in the seventh year Jehoiada took courage and took the commanders of hundreds — Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah and Elishaphat son of Zichri — into a covenant with him.
And they went round through Judah and gathered the Levites from all the cities of Judah, and the heads of the ancestral houses of Israel; and they came to Jerusalem.
And all the assembly made a covenant with the king in the house of God. And he said to them, "Look — the king's son shall reign, as the LORD has spoken concerning the sons of David.
"This is what you shall do: a third of you who come on duty on the sabbath, of the priests and the Levites, shall be gatekeepers at the thresholds;
"a third at the king's house, and a third at the Gate of the Foundation; and all the people in the courts of the house of the LORD.
"And let no one come into the house of the LORD except the priests and those of the Levites who serve — they may enter, for they are holy; and all the people shall keep the duty of the LORD.

"And the Levites shall surround the king on every side, each with his weapons in his hand; and whoever enters the house shall be put to death. And be with the king when he comes in and when he goes out."

And the Levites and all Judah did everything Jehoiada the priest had commanded; and each took his men, those coming on duty on the sabbath together with those going off duty, for Jehoiada the priest had not dismissed the divisions.
And Jehoiada the priest gave the commanders of hundreds the spears, the shields and the bucklers that had belonged to King David and were in the house of God.
And he stationed all the people, each with his weapon in his hand, from the right side of the house to the left side, by the altar and by the house, around the king.
Then they brought out the king's son and put the crown and the testimony on him, and made him king; and Jehoiada and his sons anointed him, and they said, "Long live the king!"
And Athaliah heard the sound of the people running and praising the king, and she came to the people at the house of the LORD.

And she looked, and there was the king standing at his pillar at the entrance, with the officials and the trumpets beside him, and all the people of the land rejoicing and blowing trumpets, and the singers with instruments of song leading the praise. And Athaliah tore her clothes and cried, "Treason! Treason!"

And Jehoiada the priest brought out the commanders of hundreds, the officers of the army, and said to them, "Bring her out between the ranks, and whoever follows her shall be put to death with the sword" — for the priest had said, "You shall not put her to death in the house of the LORD."
And they laid hands on her, and she came to the entrance of the Horse Gate of the king's house; and they put her to death there.
And Jehoiada made a covenant between himself and all the people and the king, that they should be a people belonging to the LORD.
And all the people came to the house of Baal and pulled it down; they broke its altars and its images, and they killed Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars.

And Jehoiada put the oversight of the house of the LORD into the hand of the priests, the Levites, whom David had apportioned over the house of the LORD, to offer up the burnt offerings of the LORD as is written in the law of Moses, with joy and with song, according to the directions of David.
And he stationed the gatekeepers at the gates of the house of the LORD, so that no one unclean in any way should enter.

And he took the commanders of hundreds, the nobles, the rulers among the people, and all the people of the land, and brought the king down from the house of the LORD; and they came through the Upper Gate to the king's house, and seated the king on the royal throne.
And all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet; and Athaliah they had put to death with the sword.

2 chronicles_24.t: Joash was seven years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Zibiah of Beersheba.
And Joash did what was right in the eyes of the LORD all the days of Jehoiada the priest.
And Jehoiada took two wives for him, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And after this it was in the heart of Joash to renew the house of the LORD.

And he gathered the priests and the Levites and said to them, "Go out to the cities of Judah and collect silver from all Israel to repair the house of your God, year by year; and act quickly in the matter." But the Levites did not act quickly.

And the king summoned Jehoiada the chief and said to him, "Why have you not required the Levites to bring in from Judah and Jerusalem the levy of Moses the servant of the LORD, and of the assembly of Israel, for the tent of the testimony?"
For Athaliah, that wicked woman — her sons had broken into the house of God, and had also used all the holy things of the house of the LORD for the Baals.
So the king gave orders, and they made a chest and put it at the gate of the house of the LORD, outside.
And they made a proclamation in Judah and Jerusalem to bring to the LORD the levy of Moses the servant of God, laid on Israel in the wilderness.
And all the officials and all the people rejoiced, and brought in and threw into the chest until it was full.

And whenever the chest was brought to the king's officers by the hand of the Levites, and they saw that the silver was much, the king's scribe and the officer of the chief priest would come and empty the chest, then take it and return it to its place. Thus they did day by day, and gathered silver in abundance.

And the king and Jehoiada gave it to those who did the work of the service of the house of the LORD, and they hired stonecutters and craftsmen to renew the house of the LORD, and also craftsmen in iron and bronze, to repair the house of the LORD.
And those who did the work worked, and the repair went forward under their hand; and they restored the house of God to its proper condition and made it strong.

And when they had finished, they brought the rest of the silver before the king and Jehoiada, and it was made into articles for the house of the LORD — articles of service and for offering up, pans, and articles of gold and silver. And they offered up burnt offerings in the house of the LORD continually, all the days of Jehoiada.
And Jehoiada grew old and was full of days, and died; he was a hundred and thirty years old at his death.
And they buried him in the city of David with the kings, for he had done good in Israel, and toward God and his house.
And after the death of Jehoiada, the officials of Judah came and bowed down to the king; and then the king listened to them.
And they abandoned the house of the LORD, the God of their ancestors, and served the Asherim and the idols; and wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem for this guilt of theirs.
And he sent prophets among them to bring them back to the LORD; and they warned them, but they would not listen.

And the spirit of God clothed Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest, and he stood above the people and said to them, "Thus says God: 'Why are you transgressing the commandments of the LORD, so that you cannot prosper? Because you have forsaken the LORD, he has forsaken you.'"
And they conspired against him, and stoned him with stones at the king's command, in the court of the house of the LORD.
And King Joash did not remember the loyalty that Jehoiada his father had shown him, and he killed his son. And as he was dying he said, "May the LORD see and require it."

And at the turn of the year the army of Aram came up against him; they came to Judah and Jerusalem and destroyed all the leaders of the people from among the people, and sent all their booty to the king of Damascus.

For the army of Aram came with a small number of men, and the LORD gave into their hand an army of exceedingly great size, because they had forsaken the LORD, the God of their ancestors; and on Joash they executed judgements.

And when they had gone from him — for they left him severely wounded — his own servants conspired against him because of the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest, and killed him on his bed, and he died. And they buried him in the city of David, but they did not bury him in the graves of the kings.
And these are those who conspired against him: Zabad son of Shimeath the Ammonite woman, and Jehozabad son of Shimrith the Moabite woman.

And as for his sons, and the many oracles against him, and the rebuilding of the house of God — they are written in the record of the scroll of the kings. And Amaziah his son became king in his place.

2 chronicles_25.t: Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Jehoaddan of Jerusalem.
And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, only not with an undivided heart.
And when the kingdom was firmly his, he killed his servants who had struck down the king his father.

But their children he did not put to death, for it is as written in the law, in the scroll of Moses, where the LORD commanded: "Fathers shall not die for children, and children shall not die for fathers, but each shall die for his own sin."

And Amaziah assembled Judah and organised them by ancestral houses, under commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, for all Judah and Benjamin; and he mustered them from twenty years old and upward, and found them to be three hundred thousand chosen men, fit for war, holding spear and large shield.
And he hired from Israel a hundred thousand mighty men of valour for a hundred talents of silver.
But a man of God came to him and said, "O king, do not let the army of Israel go with you, for the LORD is not with Israel — all the Ephraimites.
"But if you go — act, be strong for the battle — God will make you stumble before the enemy; for there is strength in God to help and to make stumble."
And Amaziah said to the man of God, "But what is to be done about the hundred talents I paid to the troop of Israel?" And the man of God said, "The LORD has more than this to give you."
So Amaziah dismissed the troop that had come to him from Ephraim, to go home; and their anger burned exceedingly against Judah, and they returned home in fierce anger.
And Amaziah took courage and led out his people, and went to the Valley of Salt, and struck down ten thousand of the people of Seir.
And the people of Judah took ten thousand alive, brought them to the top of the rock, and threw them down from the top of the rock; and all of them were split open.

And the men of the troop that Amaziah had turned back from going with him to the battle raided the cities of Judah, from Samaria as far as Beth-horon; and they struck down three thousand of them and took much plunder.
And after Amaziah came from defeating the Edomites, he brought the gods of the people of Seir and set them up for himself as gods, and bowed down before them and burned incense to them.
And the anger of the LORD burned against Amaziah, and he sent to him a prophet, who said to him, "Why have you sought the gods of a people who did not deliver their own people from your hand?"

And as he was speaking to him, the king said, "Have we made you a counsellor to the king? Stop! Why should you be struck down?" And the prophet stopped, and said, "I know that God has determined to destroy you, because you have done this and have not listened to my counsel."
And Amaziah king of Judah took counsel and sent to Joash son of Jehoahaz son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, "Come, let us face one another."

And Joash king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, "The thistle in Lebanon sent to the cedar in Lebanon, saying, 'Give your daughter to my son as a wife.' And a wild animal of Lebanon passed by and trampled the thistle.
"You have said, 'Look, I have struck down Edom,' and your heart has lifted you up to boasting. Now stay at home. Why should you provoke disaster and fall, you and Judah with you?"
But Amaziah did not listen, for it was from God, so as to give them into the enemy's hand, because they had sought the gods of Edom.
So Joash king of Israel went up, and they faced one another, he and Amaziah king of Judah, at Beth-shemesh, which belongs to Judah.
And Judah was defeated before Israel, and they fled, each to his tent.

And Joash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, son of Joash son of Jehoahaz, at Beth-shemesh; and he brought him to Jerusalem, and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Gate of Ephraim to the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits.
And he took all the gold and the silver, and all the articles found in the house of God with Obed-edom, and the treasures of the king's house, and hostages — and he returned to Samaria.
And Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived fifteen years after the death of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.
And the rest of the acts of Amaziah, from first to last — are they not written in the scroll of the kings of Judah and Israel?
And from the time that Amaziah turned aside from following the LORD, they conspired against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish; and they sent after him to Lachish and put him to death there.
And they carried him on horses and buried him with his ancestors in the city of Judah.

2 chronicles_26.t: And all the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
He rebuilt Elath and restored it to Judah, after the king lay down with his ancestors.
Uzziah was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Jecoliah of Jerusalem.
And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that Amaziah his father had done.
And he sought God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the seeing of God; and in the days when he sought the LORD, God made him prosper.
And he went out and fought against the Philistines, and broke down the wall of Gath, the wall of Jabneh and the wall of Ashdod; and he built cities in Ashdod and among the Philistines.
And God helped him against the Philistines and against the Arabs who lived in Gur-baal, and the Meunites.
And the Ammonites paid tribute to Uzziah, and his fame went as far as the entrance of Egypt, for he grew exceedingly strong.
And Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the Corner Gate, at the Valley Gate and at the Buttress, and fortified them.

And he built towers in the wilderness and dug many cisterns, for he had much livestock both in the Shephelah and on the plain; and he had farmers and vinedressers in the mountains and in the fertile land, for he loved the soil.

And Uzziah had an army fit for war, going out to battle by divisions, according to the number of their muster by the hand of Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the official, under the direction of Hananiah, one of the king's commanders.
The whole number of the heads of the ancestral houses, of mighty men of valour, was two thousand six hundred.
And under their command was an army of the host, three hundred and seven thousand five hundred, making war with powerful strength, to help the king against the enemy.
And Uzziah provided for them, for the whole army, shields, spears, helmets, body armour, bows and sling stones.

And he made in Jerusalem engines, devised by inventors, to be on the towers and on the corners, to shoot arrows and large stones. And his fame went out far, for he was wonderfully helped until he was strong.

But when he was strong, his heart grew haughty, to his own destruction; and he acted unfaithfully against the LORD his God, and went into the temple of the LORD to burn incense on the altar of incense.
And Azariah the priest went in after him, and with him eighty priests of the LORD, men of valour.

And they took their stand against King Uzziah and said to him, "It is not for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to the LORD, but for the priests, the sons of Aaron, who are set apart as holy to burn incense. Go out of the sanctuary, for you have acted unfaithfully; and it will bring you no honour from the LORD God."

And Uzziah was enraged, with a censer in his hand to burn incense; and while he was enraged with the priests, the leprosy broke out on his forehead before the priests in the house of the LORD, beside the altar of incense.

And Azariah the chief priest turned to him, and all the priests, and there he was, with leprosy on his forehead; and they hurried him out from there, and he himself also rushed to leave, because the LORD had struck him.

And King Uzziah had leprosy until the day of his death, and he lived in a separate house, having leprosy, for he was cut off from the house of the LORD; and Jotham his son was over the king's house, judging the people of the land.
And the rest of the acts of Uzziah, from first to last, Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet wrote.

And Uzziah lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him with his ancestors in the burial field that belonged to the kings, for they said, "He has leprosy." And Jotham his son became king in his place.

2 chronicles_27.t: Jotham was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Jerushah daughter of Zadok.
And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that Uzziah his father had done — only he did not go into the temple of the LORD. And the people still acted corruptly.
He built the Upper Gate of the house of the LORD, and he built extensively on the wall of the Ophel.
And he built cities in the hill country of Judah, and in the wooded areas he built fortresses and towers.

And he fought with the king of the Ammonites and prevailed over them; and the Ammonites gave him that year a hundred talents of silver, ten thousand cors of wheat and ten thousand of barley. This the Ammonites brought him in the second year and the third as well.
And Jotham grew strong, for he had ordered his ways before the LORD his God.
And the rest of the acts of Jotham, and all his wars and his ways, are written in the scroll of the kings of Israel and Judah.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.
And Jotham lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him in the city of David; and Ahaz his son became king in his place.

2 chronicles_28.t: Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem; and he did not do what was right in the eyes of the LORD, as David his ancestor had.
And he walked in the ways of the kings of Israel; and he also made molten images for the Baals.
And he burned incense in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, and burned his sons in the fire, according to the abominations of the nations whom the LORD had dispossessed before the Israelites.
And he sacrificed and burned incense at the high places, on the hills and under every green tree.

And the LORD his God gave him into the hand of the king of Aram, and they struck him and took a great number of captives from him and brought them to Damascus. He was also given into the hand of the king of Israel, who struck him a great blow.
And Pekah son of Remaliah killed a hundred and twenty thousand in Judah in one day, all of them men of valour, because they had forsaken the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
And Zichri, a warrior of Ephraim, killed Maaseiah the king's son, Azrikam the officer over the house, and Elkanah the second to the king.
And the Israelites took captive from their brothers two hundred thousand — women, sons and daughters — and they also took much booty from them, and brought the booty to Samaria.

And there was a prophet of the LORD there, Oded was his name; and he went out before the army that was coming to Samaria and said to them, "Look — because the LORD, the God of your ancestors, was angry with Judah, he gave them into your hand; and you have killed among them in a rage that has reached to the heavens.
"And now you say you will subdue the people of Judah and Jerusalem as male and female slaves for yourselves. Are there not, with you too, guilty acts against the LORD your God?
"And now hear me, and send back the captives you have taken from your brothers, for the burning of the LORD's anger is upon you."

And men from among the heads of the Ephraimites rose up — Azariah son of Jehohanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum and Amasa son of Hadlai — against those coming from the war,

and said to them, "You shall not bring the captives here; for you propose to bring on us guilt before the LORD, adding to our sins and our guilt. For our guilt is already great, and burning anger is upon Israel."
So the armed men left the captives and the plunder before the commanders and all the assembly.

And the men designated by name rose and took charge of the captives; and all who were naked among them they clothed from the plunder. They clothed them, gave them sandals, fed them, gave them drink and anointed them, and led all who stumbled on donkeys, and brought them to Jericho, the city of palms, to their brothers; and they returned to Samaria.
At that time King Ahaz sent to the kings of Assyria for help.
And again the Edomites had come and struck Judah and carried off captives.

And the Philistines had raided the cities of the Shephelah and the Negev of Judah, and had captured Beth-shemesh, Aijalon and Gederoth, and Socoh with its villages, Timnah with its villages and Gimzo with its villages; and they settled there.
For the LORD had humbled Judah because of Ahaz king of Israel, for he had let Judah run wild and had acted very unfaithfully against the LORD.
And Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria came against him and harassed him, and gave him no strength.
For Ahaz had stripped the house of the LORD and the house of the king and the officials, and had given it to the king of Assyria; but it was no help to him.
And at the time when he was harassed, he acted still more unfaithfully against the LORD — this same King Ahaz.

And he sacrificed to the gods of Damascus who had struck him, and said, "Because the gods of the kings of Aram are helping them, I will sacrifice to them so that they may help me." But they were the ruin of him and of all Israel.
And Ahaz gathered the articles of the house of God and cut them up, and shut the doors of the house of the LORD; and he made himself altars at every corner in Jerusalem.
And in every single city of Judah he made high places to burn incense to other gods, and he provoked the LORD, the God of his ancestors.
And the rest of his acts and all his ways, from first to last, are written in the scroll of the kings of Judah and Israel.
And Ahaz lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him in the city, in Jerusalem — for they did not bring him to the graves of the kings of Israel. And Hezekiah his son became king in his place.

2 chronicles_29.t: Hezekiah was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Abijah daughter of Zechariah.
And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that David his ancestor had done.
In the first year of his reign, in the first month, he opened the doors of the house of the LORD and repaired them.
And he brought in the priests and the Levites and gathered them in the square on the east,
and said to them, "Hear me, Levites! Now set yourselves apart as holy, and set apart as holy the house of the LORD, the God of your ancestors, and bring out the impurity from the holy place.

"For our ancestors acted unfaithfully and did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD our God, and forsook him; they turned their faces away from the tabernacle of the LORD and turned their backs on it.
"They also shut the doors of the porch and put out the lamps, and did not burn incense or offer up burnt offerings in the holy place to the God of Israel.
"And the wrath of the LORD was upon Judah and Jerusalem, and he made them an object of terror, of horror and of hissing, as you see with your own eyes.
"And look — our ancestors have fallen by the sword, and our sons and daughters and wives are in captivity because of this.
"Now it is in my heart to make a covenant with the LORD, the God of Israel, that the burning of his anger may turn back from us.
"My sons, do not be negligent now, for the LORD has chosen you to stand before him, to serve him, and to be his ministers and those who burn incense."

And the Levites arose: Mahath son of Amasai and Joel son of Azariah, of the Kohathites; of the Merarites, Kish son of Abdi and Azariah son of Jehallelel; of the Gershonites, Joah son of Zimmah and Eden son of Joah;
of the descendants of Elizaphan, Shimri and Jeuel; of the descendants of Asaph, Zechariah and Mattaniah;
of the descendants of Heman, Jehuel and Shimei; and of the descendants of Jeduthun, Shemaiah and Uzziel.
And they gathered their brothers and set themselves apart as holy, and came, according to the king's command by the words of the LORD, to cleanse the house of the LORD.

And the priests went inside the house of the LORD to cleanse it, and brought out all the uncleanness they found in the temple of the LORD into the court of the house of the LORD; and the Levites received it, to carry it out to the wadi Kidron, outside.

And they began on the first day of the first month to set apart as holy, and on the eighth day of the month they came to the porch of the LORD; they set apart as holy the house of the LORD for eight days, and on the sixteenth day of the first month they finished.
And they went in to Hezekiah the king and said, "We have cleansed all the house of the LORD — the altar of burnt offering and all its articles, and the table of the row of bread and all its articles.
"And all the articles that King Ahaz rejected in his reign, in his unfaithfulness, we have prepared and set apart as holy; and there they are, before the altar of the LORD."
And Hezekiah the king rose early and gathered the officials of the city, and went up to the house of the LORD.

And they brought seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs and seven male goats as a sin offering for the kingdom, for the sanctuary and for Judah; and he told the sons of Aaron, the priests, to offer them up on the altar of the LORD.

And they slaughtered the cattle, and the priests received the blood and dashed it against the altar; they slaughtered the rams and dashed the blood against the altar; they slaughtered the lambs and dashed the blood against the altar.
And they brought the goats of the sin offering near before the king and the assembly, and they laid their hands on them.

And the priests slaughtered them and purified from sin with their blood against the altar, to make atonement for all Israel; for the king had said that the burnt offering and the sin offering were for all Israel.

And he stationed the Levites in the house of the LORD with cymbals, harps and lyres, by the commandment of David and of Gad the king's seer and Nathan the prophet; for the commandment was by the hand of the LORD, through his prophets.
And the Levites stood with the instruments of David, and the priests with trumpets.

And Hezekiah gave the order to offer up the burnt offering on the altar; and when the burnt offering began, the song of the LORD began, with the trumpets and with the instruments of David king of Israel.
And all the assembly prostrated themselves, the singers sang and the trumpets sounded — all of it until the burnt offering was finished.
And when they had finished offering up, the king and all who were present with him bowed and prostrated themselves.
And Hezekiah the king and the officials told the Levites to praise the LORD with the words of David and of Asaph the seer; and they praised with joy, and bowed low and prostrated themselves.

And Hezekiah answered and said, "Now you have consecrated yourselves to the LORD. Draw near and bring sacrifices and thank offerings to the house of the LORD." And the assembly brought sacrifices and thank offerings, and all who were willing of heart brought burnt offerings.
And the number of the burnt offerings the assembly brought was seventy cattle, a hundred rams and two hundred lambs — all these for a burnt offering to the LORD.
And the holy offerings were six hundred cattle and three thousand sheep.

Only the priests were too few, and they were not able to skin all the burnt offerings; so their brothers the Levites helped them until the work was finished and until the priests had set themselves apart as holy — for the Levites were more upright of heart in setting themselves apart as holy than the priests.
And there were also burnt offerings in abundance, with the fat of the peace offerings and with the drink offerings for the burnt offering. So the service of the house of the LORD was set in order.
And Hezekiah rejoiced, and all the people with him, over what God had prepared for the people; for the thing had come about suddenly.

2 chronicles_30.t: And Hezekiah sent word to all Israel and Judah, and he also wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasseh, to come to the house of the LORD in Jerusalem to keep a passover to the LORD, the God of Israel.
And the king and his officials and all the assembly in Jerusalem had taken counsel to keep the passover in the second month.
For they had not been able to keep it at that time, because the priests had not set themselves apart as holy in sufficient numbers, and the people had not gathered at Jerusalem.
And the thing was right in the eyes of the king and in the eyes of all the assembly.

And they established a decree to send a proclamation through all Israel, from Beersheba to Dan, to come and keep a passover to the LORD, the God of Israel, in Jerusalem; for they had not kept it in great numbers as it is written.

And the couriers went with the letters from the hand of the king and his officials through all Israel and Judah, according to the king's command, saying: "Israelites, return to the LORD, the God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel, that he may return to the remnant of you that has escaped from the hand of the kings of Assyria.
"And do not be like your ancestors and your brothers, who acted unfaithfully against the LORD, the God of their ancestors, so that he made them an object of horror, as you see.

"Now do not stiffen your neck as your ancestors did. Give a hand to the LORD, and come to his sanctuary, which he has set apart as holy for ever, and serve the LORD your God, that the burning of his anger may turn back from you.

"For when you return to the LORD, your brothers and your children will find compassion before their captors, and will return to this land; for the LORD your God is gracious and compassionate, and will not turn his face away from you if you return to him."
And the couriers passed from city to city through the land of Ephraim and Manasseh and as far as Zebulun; but the people laughed at them and mocked them.
Nevertheless, men from Asher, Manasseh and Zebulun humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem.
In Judah too the hand of God was at work, to give them one heart to do the command of the king and the officials by the word of the LORD.
And a great many people gathered at Jerusalem to keep the festival of unleavened bread in the second month — an exceedingly great assembly.
And they arose and removed the altars that were in Jerusalem, and all the incense altars they removed and threw into the wadi Kidron.

And they slaughtered the passover lamb on the fourteenth of the second month; and the priests and the Levites were ashamed, and set themselves apart as holy, and brought burnt offerings to the house of the LORD.
And they stood at their post, according to their ordinance, according to the law of Moses the man of God; the priests dashed the blood, receiving it from the hand of the Levites.

For there were many in the assembly who had not set themselves apart as holy; so the Levites had charge of the slaughter of the passover lambs for everyone who was not clean, to set them apart as holy to the LORD.

For the greater part of the people — many from Ephraim and Manasseh, Issachar and Zebulun — had not cleansed themselves, but ate the passover otherwise than as it is written. For Hezekiah prayed for them, saying, "May the LORD, who is good, make atonement for
"everyone who has set his heart to seek God, the LORD, the God of his ancestors, even though not according to the cleansing required for the holy place."
And the LORD listened to Hezekiah and healed the people.

And the Israelites who were present in Jerusalem kept the festival of unleavened bread for seven days with great joy; and the Levites and the priests praised the LORD day by day, with loud instruments to the LORD.

And Hezekiah spoke encouragingly to all the Levites who showed good understanding toward the LORD. And they ate the appointed feast for seven days, sacrificing sacrifices of peace offerings and giving thanks to the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
And all the assembly took counsel to keep another seven days; and they kept seven days with joy.

For Hezekiah king of Judah contributed to the assembly a thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep, and the officials contributed a thousand bulls and ten thousand sheep; and priests set themselves apart as holy in great numbers.

And all the assembly of Judah rejoiced, with the priests and the Levites, and all the assembly that came from Israel, and the resident aliens who came from the land of Israel and those living in Judah.
And there was great joy in Jerusalem, for since the days of Solomon son of David king of Israel there had been nothing like this in Jerusalem.
And the priests and the Levites arose and blessed the people; and their voice was heard, and their prayer came to his holy dwelling, to the heavens.

2 chronicles_31.t: And when all this was finished, all Israel who were present went out to the cities of Judah and broke the pillars, cut down the Asherim and pulled down the high places and the altars, out of all Judah and Benjamin and in Ephraim and Manasseh, until they had finished. Then all the Israelites returned, each to his holding, to their cities.

And Hezekiah appointed the divisions of the priests and the Levites by their divisions, each according to his service, for the priests and for the Levites, for burnt offering and for peace offerings, to serve, to give thanks and to praise in the gates of the camps of the LORD.

And the king's portion from his own property was for the burnt offerings — for the morning and evening burnt offerings, and the burnt offerings for the sabbaths, the new moons and the appointed times — as is written in the law of the LORD.
And he told the people, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, to give the portion due to the priests and the Levites, so that they might hold firmly to the law of the LORD.

And as the word spread, the Israelites brought in abundance the firstfruits of grain, new wine, fresh oil and honey, and all the produce of the field; and they brought the tithe of everything in abundance.

And the Israelites and Judahites who lived in the cities of Judah — they too brought a tithe of herd and flock, and a tithe of the holy things set apart as holy to the LORD their God; and they made heap upon heap.
In the third month they began the heaps, and in the seventh month they finished.
And Hezekiah and the officials came and saw the heaps, and blessed the LORD and his people Israel.
And Hezekiah enquired of the priests and the Levites about the heaps.

And Azariah the chief priest, of the house of Zadok, said to him: "From the time the contribution began to be brought to the house of the LORD, we have eaten and been satisfied and had plenty left over; for the LORD has blessed his people, and what is left over is this abundance."
And Hezekiah gave orders to prepare chambers in the house of the LORD; and they prepared them.
And they brought in the contribution, the tithe and the holy things in faithfulness; and Conaniah the Levite was officer over them, with Shimei his brother second in command.

And Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath and Benaiah were officers under the direction of Conaniah and Shimei his brother, by the appointment of Hezekiah the king and Azariah the officer of the house of God.
And Kore son of Imnah the Levite, the gatekeeper on the east, was over the freewill offerings of God, to distribute the contribution of the LORD and the most holy things.
And under his direction were Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah and Shecaniah, in the cities of the priests, faithfully distributing to their brothers by divisions, to great and small alike,

besides the enrolment by genealogy of males from three years old and upward — everyone who entered the house of the LORD for the daily requirement, for their service in their duties by their divisions;
and the enrolment by genealogy of the priests by their ancestral houses, and of the Levites from twenty years old and upward, in their duties by their divisions;
and to enrol by genealogy all their little children, their wives, their sons and their daughters, for the whole assembly; for in their faithfulness they set themselves apart as holy.

And for the sons of Aaron, the priests, in the fields of the pasture lands of their cities, in every single city, there were men designated by name to distribute portions to every male among the priests and to everyone enrolled by genealogy among the Levites.
And Hezekiah did this in all Judah; and he did what was good and right and faithful before the LORD his God.
And in every work that he began in the service of the house of God, and in the law and in the commandment, to seek his God — he did it with all his heart, and he prospered.

2 chronicles_32.t: After these things and this faithfulness, Sennacherib king of Assyria came and entered Judah, encamped against the fortified cities, and intended to break into them for himself.
And Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come, and that he was set on war against Jerusalem.
And he took counsel with his officials and his warriors to stop up the waters of the springs outside the city; and they helped him.
And a great many people gathered and stopped up all the springs and the wadi that flowed through the land, saying, "Why should the kings of Assyria come and find plenty of water?"

And he took courage and rebuilt all the broken-down wall, raised towers on it, and built another wall outside it; and he strengthened the Millo of the city of David, and made weapons in abundance, and shields.
And he appointed commanders of war over the people, gathered them to himself in the square at the city gate, and spoke encouragingly to them:
"Be strong and be courageous. Do not fear and do not be dismayed before the king of Assyria or before all the multitude that is with him; for with us is one greater than with him.
"With him is an arm of flesh, but with us is the LORD our God, to help us and to fight our battles." And the people leaned on the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.
After this Sennacherib king of Assyria sent his servants to Jerusalem — he was at Lachish, with all his imperial might — to Hezekiah king of Judah and to all Judah who were in Jerusalem, saying:
"Thus says Sennacherib king of Assyria: 'On what are you relying, that you remain under siege in Jerusalem?
"'Is not Hezekiah misleading you, to give you over to die of hunger and thirst, saying, "The LORD our God will deliver us from the hand of the king of Assyria"?
"'Is it not this same Hezekiah who removed his high places and his altars, and said to Judah and Jerusalem, "Before one altar you shall bow down, and on it you shall burn incense"?
"'Do you not know what I and my ancestors have done to all the peoples of the lands? Were the gods of the nations of the lands able at all to deliver their land from my hand?
"'Who among all the gods of these nations that my ancestors devoted to destruction was able to deliver his people from my hand, that your God should be able to deliver you from my hand?

"'And now, do not let Hezekiah deceive you or mislead you like this, and do not believe him; for no god of any nation or kingdom has been able to deliver his people from my hand or from the hand of my ancestors — how much less will your gods deliver you from my hand!'"
And his servants spoke still more against the LORD God, and against Hezekiah his servant.

And he wrote letters to taunt the LORD, the God of Israel, and to speak against him, saying, "Like the gods of the nations of the lands who did not deliver their people from my hand, so the God of Hezekiah will not deliver his people from my hand."
And they called out with a loud voice in Judean to the people of Jerusalem who were on the wall, to frighten them and terrify them, so that they might capture the city.
And they spoke of the God of Jerusalem as of the gods of the peoples of the earth, the work of human hands.
And Hezekiah the king and Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet prayed about this and cried out to the heavens.

And the LORD sent an angel, who annihilated every mighty man of valour and every officer and commander in the camp of the king of Assyria. And he returned with shame of face to his own land; and when he entered the house of his god, some of his own offspring struck him down there with the sword.
And the LORD saved Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib king of Assyria and from the hand of everyone, and gave them rest on every side.
And many brought an offering to the LORD at Jerusalem, and precious gifts to Hezekiah king of Judah; and he was exalted in the eyes of all the nations from then on.
In those days Hezekiah was sick to the point of death, and he prayed to the LORD; and the LORD spoke to him and gave him a sign.
But Hezekiah did not repay according to the benefit done to him, for his heart grew haughty; and wrath came upon him, and upon Judah and Jerusalem.
But Hezekiah humbled himself for the haughtiness of his heart, he and the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and the wrath of the LORD did not come upon them in the days of Hezekiah.
And Hezekiah had exceedingly great wealth and honour; and he made himself treasuries for silver, gold, precious stone, spices, shields and all kinds of desirable articles,
and storehouses for the yield of grain, new wine and fresh oil, and stalls for all kinds of livestock, and pens for the flocks.
And he acquired cities for himself, and flocks and herds in abundance; for God had given him very much property.
And it was Hezekiah who stopped up the upper outlet of the waters of Gihon and directed them down to the west of the city of David. And Hezekiah prospered in all his work.

And so also in the matter of the envoys of the officials of Babylon, who were sent to him to enquire about the sign that had happened in the land — God left him, to test him, to know all that was in his heart.
And the rest of the acts of Hezekiah, and his acts of loyalty, are written in the vision of Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet, in the scroll of the kings of Judah and Israel.

And Hezekiah lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him on the ascent to the graves of the sons of David; and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem did him honour at his death. And Manasseh his son became king in his place.

2 chronicles_33.t: Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, according to the abominations of the nations that the LORD had dispossessed before the Israelites.
He rebuilt the high places that Hezekiah his father had pulled down; he set up altars to the Baals, made Asherahs, and bowed down to all the host of the heavens and served them.
And he built altars in the house of the LORD, of which the LORD had said, "In Jerusalem my name shall be for ever."
And he built altars to all the host of the heavens in the two courts of the house of the LORD.

And he made his sons pass through the fire in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, and practised soothsaying, divination and sorcery, and dealt with mediums and spiritists. He did much evil in the eyes of the LORD, to provoke him.

And he set the carved image of the idol that he had made in the house of God, of which God had said to David and to Solomon his son, "In this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will put my name for ever.

"And I will not again remove the foot of Israel from the ground that I appointed for your ancestors — if only they take care to do all that I have commanded them, according to all the law and the statutes and the judgements given by the hand of Moses."
And Manasseh misled Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that they did more evil than the nations the LORD had annihilated before the Israelites.
And the LORD spoke to Manasseh and to his people, but they paid no attention.
So the LORD brought upon them the commanders of the army of the king of Assyria, and they captured Manasseh with hooks, bound him with bronze fetters and brought him to Babylon.
And when he was in distress, he entreated the favour of the LORD his God, and humbled himself greatly before the God of his ancestors.
And he prayed to him, and he was entreated by him and heard his supplication, and brought him back to Jerusalem, to his kingdom. And Manasseh knew that the LORD — he is God.

And after this he built an outer wall for the city of David, west of Gihon in the wadi, running to the entrance at the Fish Gate; and he carried it round the Ophel and raised it very high. And he stationed commanders of the army in all the fortified cities in Judah.
And he removed the foreign gods and the idol from the house of the LORD, and all the altars he had built on the mountain of the house of the LORD and in Jerusalem, and threw them outside the city.
And he rebuilt the altar of the LORD and sacrificed on it sacrifices of peace offerings and thanksgiving; and he told Judah to serve the LORD, the God of Israel.
But the people still sacrificed at the high places — only to the LORD their God.
And the rest of the acts of Manasseh, and his prayer to his God, and the words of the seers who spoke to him in the name of the LORD, the God of Israel — they are in the acts of the kings of Israel.

And his prayer, and how God was entreated by him, and all his sin and his unfaithfulness, and the places where he built high places and set up the Asherim and the carved images before he humbled himself — they are written in the words of Hozai.
And Manasseh lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him in his own house; and Amon his son became king in his place.
Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, as Manasseh his father had done; and Amon sacrificed to all the carved images that Manasseh his father had made, and served them.
And he did not humble himself before the LORD as Manasseh his father had humbled himself; rather he, Amon, increased guilt.
And his servants conspired against him and killed him in his own house.
And the people of the land struck down all who had conspired against King Amon; and the people of the land made Josiah his son king in his place.

2 chronicles_34.t: Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem.
And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, and walked in the ways of David his ancestor, and did not turn aside to the right or the left.

And in the eighth year of his reign, while he was still a youth, he began to seek the God of David his ancestor; and in the twelfth year he began to cleanse Judah and Jerusalem of the high places, the Asherim, the carved images and the cast images.

And they pulled down before him the altars of the Baals, and he cut down the incense stands that stood above them; and the Asherim, the carved images and the cast images he broke in pieces and ground to dust, and scattered it on the graves of those who had sacrificed to them.
And he burned the bones of priests on their altars, and cleansed Judah and Jerusalem.
And in the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim and Simeon, as far as Naphtali, among their ruins all around —
— he pulled down the altars, crushed the Asherim and the carved images to dust, and cut down all the incense stands throughout the land of Israel; then he returned to Jerusalem.

And in the eighteenth year of his reign, to cleanse the land and the house, he sent Shaphan son of Azaliah, Maaseiah the governor of the city, and Joah son of Joahaz the recorder, to repair the house of the LORD his God.

They went to Hilkiah the high priest and gave him the money that had been brought to the house of God, which the Levites who kept the threshold had gathered from Manasseh and Ephraim and from all the remnant of Israel, and from all Judah and Benjamin; and they returned to Jerusalem.

And they put it into the hands of those doing the work, who were appointed over the house of the LORD; and those doing the work, who were working in the house of the LORD, spent it to mend and repair the house.
And they gave it to the craftsmen and the builders, to buy hewn stone and timber for the couplings, and to make beams for the buildings that the kings of Judah had let go to ruin.

And the men did the work faithfully; over them were appointed Jahath and Obadiah, Levites of the sons of Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam of the sons of the Kohathites, to oversee; and the Levites — every one of them skilled with instruments of song.
And they were over the burden-bearers and directed all who did work, service by service; and some of the Levites were scribes, officials and gatekeepers.
And when they were bringing out the money that had been brought to the house of the LORD, Hilkiah the priest found the scroll of the law of the LORD given by the hand of Moses.
And Hilkiah said to Shaphan the scribe, "I have found the scroll of the law in the house of the LORD." And Hilkiah gave the scroll to Shaphan.
And Shaphan brought the scroll to the king, and brought the king a further report, saying, "All that was entrusted to your servants — they are doing it.
"They have emptied out the money that was found in the house of the LORD and put it into the hands of those appointed and of those doing the work."
And Shaphan the scribe told the king, "Hilkiah the priest has given me a scroll." And Shaphan read aloud from it before the king.
