And when the king heard the words of the law, he tore his clothes.
And the king commanded Hilkiah, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Abdon son of Micah, Shaphan the scribe and Asaiah the king's servant,

"Go, seek the LORD on my behalf and on behalf of what remains in Israel and in Judah, concerning the words of the scroll that has been found; for great is the wrath of the LORD that has been poured out on us, because our ancestors did not keep the word of the LORD, to do all that is written in this scroll."

And Hilkiah, with those the king had appointed, went to Huldah the prophetess, wife of Shallum son of Tokhath son of Hasrah, keeper of the wardrobe; she was living in Jerusalem, in the Second Quarter. And they spoke to her to that effect.
And she said to them, "Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Say to the man who sent you to me,
"Thus says the LORD: I am bringing harm on this place and on its inhabitants — all the curses written in the scroll that they read before the king of Judah.
"Because they have forsaken me and burned offerings to other gods, provoking me to anger with all the works of their hands, my wrath will pour out on this place and will not be quenched."
"And to the king of Judah, who sent you to seek the LORD — this is what you shall say to him: Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, concerning the words you have heard:

"Because your heart was tender and you humbled yourself before God when you heard his words against this place and against its inhabitants — and you humbled yourself before me and tore your clothes and wept before me — I also have heard, declares the LORD.

"I will gather you to your ancestors, and you will be gathered to your graves in peace; and your eyes will not see all the distress that I am bringing on this place and on its inhabitants." And they brought word back to the king.
And the king sent and gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

And the king went up to the house of the LORD, with every man of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the priests and the Levites, and all the people from the greatest to the least; and he read in their hearing all the words of the scroll of the covenant that had been found in the house of the LORD.

And the king stood at his place and made the covenant before the LORD — to walk after the LORD and to keep his commandments, his testimonies and his statutes with all his heart and with all his soul, to carry out the words of the covenant written in this scroll.
And he made everyone present in Jerusalem and Benjamin take their stand in it; and the inhabitants of Jerusalem acted according to the covenant of God, the God of their ancestors.

And Josiah removed all the abominations from all the territories that belonged to the Israelites, and made everyone in Israel serve — serve the LORD their God. All his days they did not turn aside from following the LORD, the God of their ancestors.

2 chronicles_35.t: And Josiah kept a Passover to the LORD in Jerusalem; and they slaughtered the Passover lamb on the fourteenth day of the first month.
And he appointed the priests to their duties and encouraged them for the service of the house of the LORD.

And he said to the Levites who instructed all Israel, who were holy to the LORD, "Put the holy ark in the house that Solomon son of David king of Israel built. It is no longer a burden on your shoulders. Now serve the LORD your God and his people Israel,
"and prepare yourselves by your ancestral houses, according to your divisions, following the writing of David king of Israel and the document of Solomon his son.
"And stand in the holy place, grouped by the ancestral houses of your kinsmen, the lay people, with a division of a Levite ancestral house for each.
"Slaughter the Passover lamb, consecrate yourselves, and make preparation for your kinsmen, to do according to the word of the LORD given by the hand of Moses."

And Josiah contributed to the lay people flocks — lambs and young goats, all of them for the Passover offerings, for everyone present — thirty thousand in number, and three thousand cattle. These came from the king's own property.

And his officials made a freewill contribution for the people, for the priests and for the Levites. Hilkiah, Zechariah and Jehiel, the officers of the house of God, gave the priests two thousand six hundred for the Passover offerings, and three hundred cattle.

And Conaniah, Shemaiah and Nethanel his brothers, and Hashabiah, Jeiel and Jozabad, the leaders of the Levites, contributed for the Levites five thousand for the Passover offerings, and five hundred cattle.
And the service was arranged; the priests took their places and the Levites their divisions, according to the king's command.
And they slaughtered the Passover lambs, and the priests sprinkled the blood from their hand, while the Levites did the skinning.

And they set aside the burnt offerings, to give them to the groupings of the ancestral houses of the lay people, to present to the LORD as it is written in the scroll of Moses; and they did the same with the cattle.
And they cooked the Passover lamb over the fire, according to the rule; and the holy offerings they boiled in pots, cauldrons and pans, and brought them quickly to all the people.

And afterwards they prepared for themselves and for the priests, because the priests, the sons of Aaron, were offering up the burnt offerings and the fat pieces until nightfall; so the Levites prepared for themselves and for the priests, the sons of Aaron.

And the singers, the sons of Asaph, were at their post, according to the command of David, Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun the king's seer; and the gatekeepers were at each gate. They did not have to leave their service, because their kinsmen the Levites made preparation for them.
And all the service of the LORD was arranged that day, to keep the Passover and to offer up burnt offerings on the altar of the LORD, according to the command of King Josiah.
And the Israelites who were present kept the Passover at that time, and the Festival of Unleavened Bread for seven days.

And no Passover like it had been kept in Israel since the days of Samuel the prophet; none of the kings of Israel kept a Passover like the one Josiah kept, with the priests and the Levites and all Judah and Israel who were present and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
In the eighteenth year of Josiah's reign this Passover was kept.
After all this, when Josiah had put the house in order, Necho king of Egypt came up to fight at Carchemish on the Euphrates; and Josiah went out to meet him.

But he sent messengers to him, saying, "What is there between me and you, king of Judah? It is not you I am against today, but the house I am at war with; and God has told me to hurry. Stop, for your own sake, opposing the God who is with me, or he will destroy you."

But Josiah did not turn away from him; instead he disguised himself to fight him, and did not listen to the words of Necho, which came from the mouth of God, and he came to fight in the valley of Megiddo.
And the archers shot King Josiah; and the king said to his servants, "Take me away, for I am badly wounded."

And his servants took him out of the chariot and put him in his second chariot, and brought him to Jerusalem; and he died and was buried in the graves of his ancestors. And all Judah and Jerusalem mourned over Josiah.

And Jeremiah lamented over Josiah; and all the singers, men and women, have spoken of Josiah in their laments to this day. They made them a fixed practice in Israel, and they are written in the Laments.
And the rest of the acts of Josiah, and his acts of loyalty, in accordance with what is written in the law of the LORD,
and his acts, the earlier and the later — they are written in the scroll of the kings of Israel and Judah.

2 chronicles_36.t: And the people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah and made him king in place of his father in Jerusalem.
Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem.
And the king of Egypt deposed him in Jerusalem, and fined the land a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.
And the king of Egypt made Eliakim his brother king over Judah and Jerusalem, and changed his name to Jehoiakim; and Necho took Jehoahaz his brother and brought him to Egypt.
Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD his God.
Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against him and bound him with bronze fetters to take him to Babylon.
And some of the articles of the house of the LORD Nebuchadnezzar brought to Babylon and put in his palace in Babylon.

And the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim, and the abominations he committed, and what was found against him — they are written in the scroll of the kings of Israel and Judah. And Jehoiachin his son became king in his place.
Jehoiachin was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem. And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.

And at the turn of the year King Nebuchadnezzar sent and brought him to Babylon, along with the precious articles of the house of the LORD; and he made Zedekiah his kinsman king over Judah and Jerusalem.
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD his God. He did not humble himself before Jeremiah the prophet, who spoke from the mouth of the LORD.
He also rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear an oath by God; and he stiffened his neck and hardened his heart against turning back to the LORD, the God of Israel.

The leaders of the priests and the people also multiplied acts of unfaithfulness, following all the abominations of the nations; and they made unclean the house of the LORD that he had consecrated in Jerusalem.
And the LORD, the God of their ancestors, sent word to them again and again by the hand of his messengers — for he had compassion on his people and on his dwelling place.
But they kept deriding the messengers of God, despising his words and mocking his prophets, until the wrath of the LORD rose against his people, until there was no healing.

So he brought up against them the king of the Chaldeans, who killed their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary, and had no compassion on young man or virgin, the old or the infirm — he gave them all into his hand.
And all the articles of the house of God, great and small, and the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king and his officials — he brought everything to Babylon.
And they burned the house of God and pulled down the wall of Jerusalem; all its citadels they burned with fire, and all its precious articles were destroyed.
And he took into exile to Babylon those who had survived the sword, and they became servants to him and to his sons until the rise of the kingdom of Persia,
to fulfil the word of the LORD by the mouth of Jeremiah — until the land had accepted its sabbaths. All the days of its desolation it kept sabbath, to fulfil seventy years.

In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, so that the word of the LORD by the mouth of Jeremiah might be completed, the LORD stirred the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, and he sent a proclamation through all his kingdom, and also in writing, saying:

"Thus says Cyrus king of Persia: 'The LORD, the God of the heavens, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and he himself has charged me to build him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Whoever among you is from all his people — the LORD his God be with him, and let him go up.'"

2 kings_1.t: After the death of Ahab, Moab rebelled against Israel.

Ahaziah fell through the lattice in his upper room in Samaria and became ill. So he sent messengers and said to them, "Go, consult Baal-zebub the god of Ekron, whether I shall recover from this sickness."

But the angel of the LORD spoke to Elijah the Tishbite: "Arise, go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria, and say to them, 'Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to consult Baal-zebub the god of Ekron?'
"And therefore, thus says the LORD: 'The bed you have gone up on — you shall not come down from it, for you shall surely die.'" And Elijah went.
The messengers returned to him, and he said to them, "Why have you returned?"

They said to him, "A man came up to meet us and said to us, 'Go, return to the king who sent you and say to him: Thus says the LORD: Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are sending to consult Baal-zebub the god of Ekron? Therefore the bed you have gone up on — you shall not come down from it, for you shall surely die.'"
He said to them, "What was the appearance of the man who came up to meet you and spoke these words to you?"
They said to him, "A hairy man, with a leather belt girded on his loins." And he said, "That is Elijah the Tishbite."
Then he sent to him a commander of fifty with his fifty men; and he went up to him, and there he was, sitting on the top of the hill. And he said to him, "Man of God, the king has spoken: Come down!"
Elijah answered the commander of fifty, "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from the heavens and consume you and your fifty." And fire came down from the heavens and consumed him and his fifty.
Then he sent to him another commander of fifty with his fifty men; and he answered and said to him, "Man of God, thus says the king: Come down quickly!"
Elijah answered them, "If I am the man of God, let fire come down from the heavens and consume you and your fifty." And the fire of God came down from the heavens and consumed him and his fifty.

Then he sent a third commander of fifty with his fifty men. And the third commander of fifty went up and came and bowed down on his knees before Elijah and sought his favour, saying, "Man of God, let my life and the lives of these fifty servants of yours be precious in your eyes.
"See, fire came down from the heavens and consumed the two former commanders of fifty and their fifties. Now let my life be precious in your eyes."
Then the angel of the LORD said to Elijah, "Go down with him; do not be afraid of him." So he rose and went down with him to the king.

And he said to him, "Thus says the LORD: Because you sent messengers to consult Baal-zebub the god of Ekron — is it because there is no God in Israel whose word you might consult? — therefore the bed you have gone up on, you shall not come down from it, for you shall surely die."
So he died, according to the word of the LORD that Elijah had spoken. And Jehoram reigned in his place, in the second year of Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, for Ahaziah had no son.
And the rest of the acts of Ahaziah that he did — are they not written in the chronicle of the kings of Israel?

2 kings_2.t: When the LORD was about to take Elijah up to the heavens in a whirlwind, Elijah went from Gilgal, and Elisha with him.
And Elijah said to Elisha, "Stay here, for the LORD has sent me as far as Beth-el." But Elisha said, "As the LORD lives and as you yourself live, I will not leave you." So they went down to Beth-el.

And the sons of the prophets who were at Beth-el came out to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that today the LORD is taking your master from over your head?" And he said, "I know it too. Be silent."
And Elijah said to him, "Elisha, stay here, for the LORD has sent me to Jericho." But he said, "As the LORD lives and as you yourself live, I will not leave you." So they came to Jericho.

And the sons of the prophets who were at Jericho drew near to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that today the LORD is taking your master from over your head?" And he said, "I know it too. Be silent."
And Elijah said to him, "Stay here, for the LORD has sent me to the Jordan." But he said, "As the LORD lives and as you yourself live, I will not leave you." So the two of them went on.
And fifty men of the sons of the prophets went and stood opposite them, at a distance; and the two of them stood at the Jordan.
Then Elijah took his cloak, rolled it up, and struck the waters, and they were divided this way and that; and the two of them passed over on dry ground.
When they had passed over, Elijah said to Elisha, "Ask what I shall do for you before I am taken from you." And Elisha said, "Let a double share of your spirit be mine."
And he said, "You have asked a hard thing. If you see me taken from you, it shall be so for you; but if not, it shall not be."
And as they went on, walking and talking, there appeared a chariot of fire and horses of fire, and they separated the two of them; and Elijah went up in the whirlwind to the heavens.
And Elisha was watching, and he cried out, "My father, my father! The chariotry of Israel and its horsemen!" And he saw him no more. Then he took hold of his own clothes and tore them in two.
And he took up the cloak of Elijah that had fallen from him, and went back and stood on the bank of the Jordan.

And he took the cloak of Elijah that had fallen from him and struck the waters, and he said, "Where is the LORD, the God of Elijah?" And he too struck the waters, and they were divided this way and that, and Elisha passed over.
And the sons of the prophets who were at Jericho saw him opposite and said, "The spirit of Elijah has rested on Elisha." And they came to meet him and bowed down to the ground before him.

And they said to him, "See now, there are with your servants fifty able men. Let them go and search for your master, in case the spirit of the LORD has carried him off and cast him on one of the mountains or in one of the valleys." But he said, "Do not send them."
But they urged him until he was ashamed, and he said, "Send them." So they sent fifty men, and they searched three days and did not find him.
And they returned to him while he was staying at Jericho, and he said to them, "Did I not say to you, 'Do not go'?"
And the men of the city said to Elisha, "See now, the site of the city is good, as my lord sees; but the waters are bad, and the land is barren."
And he said, "Fetch me a new jar and put salt in it." So they brought it to him.
And he went out to the spring of the waters and threw the salt in, and he said, "Thus says the LORD: I have healed these waters. There shall no longer be from them death or barrenness."
And the waters have been healed to this day, according to the word of Elisha that he spoke.
And he went up from there to Beth-el; and as he was going up on the road, small boys came out of the city and jeered at him, saying, "Go up, baldhead! Go up, baldhead!"
And he turned round and saw them, and he cursed them in the name of the LORD. And two she-bears came out of the forest and tore in pieces forty-two of the boys.
And he went from there to Mount Carmel, and from there he returned to Samaria.

2 kings_3.t: Jehoram son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned twelve years.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, though not like his father and his mother; and he removed the pillar of the Baal that his father had made.
But he clung to the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin; he did not turn aside from them.
Now Mesha king of Moab was a sheep-breeder, and he used to render to the king of Israel a hundred thousand lambs and the wool of a hundred thousand rams.
And when Ahab died, the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.
So King Jehoram went out from Samaria on that day and mustered all Israel.

And he went and sent to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, saying, "The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you go with me against Moab to battle?" And he said, "I will go up. I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses."
And he said, "By which way shall we go up?" And he said, "By the way of the wilderness of Edom."
So the king of Israel went, with the king of Judah and the king of Edom; and they went round by a seven days' march, and there was no water for the army or for the animals following them.
And the king of Israel said, "Alas! The LORD has summoned these three kings only to give them into the hand of Moab."

But Jehoshaphat said, "Is there not here a prophet of the LORD, that we may consult the LORD through him?" And one of the servants of the king of Israel answered, "Elisha son of Shaphat is here, who poured water on the hands of Elijah."
And Jehoshaphat said, "The word of the LORD is with him." So the king of Israel went down to him, with Jehoshaphat and the king of Edom.

And Elisha said to the king of Israel, "What have I to do with you? Go to the prophets of your father and to the prophets of your mother." But the king of Israel said to him, "No — for the LORD has summoned these three kings only to give them into the hand of Moab."
And Elisha said, "As the LORD of hosts lives, before whom I stand — were it not that I show regard for Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would not look at you or see you."
"But now, fetch me a musician." And when the musician played, the hand of the LORD came upon him.
And he said, "Thus says the LORD: Make this wadi full of ditches."
"For thus says the LORD: You shall not see wind and you shall not see rain, yet that wadi will be filled with water, and you shall drink, you and your livestock and your animals."
"And this is a trifling thing in the eyes of the LORD; he will also give Moab into your hand."
"And you shall strike every fortified city and every choice city, fell every good tree, stop up all the springs of water, and spoil every good plot of land with stones."
And in the morning, at the time of the grain offering, water came from the direction of Edom, and the land was filled with water.
Now all Moab had heard that the kings had come up to fight against them, and they were called out, everyone old enough to gird on a belt and upward, and they took their stand at the border.
And they rose early in the morning, and the sun shone on the water; and Moab saw the water opposite them, red like blood.
And they said, "This is blood! The kings have utterly fought one another and struck each other down. And now, to the plunder, Moab!"
But when they came to the camp of Israel, Israel rose and struck the Moabites, and they fled before them; and they went on into the land, striking Moab down.

They tore down the cities, and on every good plot of land each man threw his stone until it was covered; they stopped up every spring of water and felled every good tree — until only its stones were left in Kir-hareseth. And the slingers surrounded it and struck it.
When the king of Moab saw that the battle was too strong for him, he took with him seven hundred men drawing the sword, to break through to the king of Edom; but they could not.

Then he took his firstborn son, who was to reign in his place, and offered him up as a burnt offering on the wall. And there was great wrath against Israel; and they withdrew from him and returned to their own land.

2 kings_4.t: Now a certain woman from among the wives of the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisha, "Your servant my husband is dead, and you yourself know that your servant feared the LORD; and the creditor has come to take my two children for himself as slaves."
And Elisha said to her, "What shall I do for you? Tell me, what do you have in the house?" And she said, "Your maidservant has nothing at all in the house except a jar of oil."
And he said, "Go, ask for yourself vessels from outside, from all your neighbours — empty vessels; do not gather few.
"Then go in and shut the door behind you and your sons, and pour into all these vessels; and set aside each one as it is filled."
So she went from him and shut the door behind her and her sons; they kept bringing the vessels to her, and she kept pouring.
And when the vessels were full, she said to her son, "Bring me another vessel." And he said to her, "There is no other vessel." And the oil stopped.
And she came and told the man of God, and he said, "Go, sell the oil and pay your debt; and you and your sons shall live on what is left."
One day Elisha passed on to Shunem, where there was a woman of standing, and she urged him to eat bread. And so, whenever he passed by, he would turn aside there to eat.
And she said to her husband, "I know that this is a holy man of God who passes by us continually.
"Let us make a small walled upper room, and put a bed, a table, a chair, and a lampstand there for him; and when he comes to us he can turn aside there."
One day he came there, and he turned aside to the upper room and lay down there.
And he said to Gehazi his servant, "Call this Shunammite." So he called her, and she stood before him.

And he said to him, "Say to her: You have taken all this care for us. What is to be done for you? Is there a word to be spoken for you to the king or to the commander of the army?" And she said, "I dwell among my own people."
And he said, "Then what is to be done for her?" And Gehazi said, "Indeed, she has no son, and her husband is old."
And he said, "Call her." So he called her, and she stood at the entrance.
And he said, "At this appointed time next year, you will be embracing a son." And she said, "No, my lord, man of God — do not lie to your maidservant."
And the woman conceived and bore a son at that appointed time the next year, as Elisha had spoken to her.
And the child grew; and one day he went out to his father, to the harvesters.
And he said to his father, "My head! My head!" And his father said to the servant, "Carry him to his mother."
And he carried him and brought him to his mother; and he sat on her knees until noon, and then he died.
And she went up and laid him on the bed of the man of God, shut the door behind him, and went out.
And she called to her husband and said, "Send me one of the servants and one of the donkeys, and let me run to the man of God and come back."
And he said, "Why are you going to him today? It is not new moon or sabbath." And she said, "It is well."
Then she saddled the donkey and said to her servant, "Lead on and go. Do not slow down for me in the riding unless I tell you."
So she went and came to the man of God at Mount Carmel. And when the man of God saw her at a distance, he said to Gehazi his servant, "There is that Shunammite!
"Now run to meet her and say to her: Is it well with you? Is it well with your husband? Is it well with the child?" And she said, "It is well."

And she came to the man of God at the mountain and took hold of his feet. Gehazi drew near to push her away, but the man of God said, "Let her alone, for she is bitter in herself; and the LORD has hidden it from me and has not told me."
And she said, "Did I ask my lord for a son? Did I not say, 'Do not mislead me'?"

And he said to Gehazi, "Gird your loins, take my staff in your hand, and go. If you meet anyone, do not greet him; and if anyone greets you, do not answer him. And lay my staff on the face of the boy."
And the mother of the boy said, "As the LORD lives and as you yourself live, I will not leave you." So he rose and followed her.
And Gehazi went on ahead of them and laid the staff on the face of the boy, but there was no sound and no response. So he went back to meet him and told him, "The boy has not awakened."
And Elisha came to the house, and there was the boy, dead, laid on his bed.
So he went in and shut the door behind the two of them, and he prayed to the LORD.
Then he went up and lay on the child, putting his mouth on his mouth, his eyes on his eyes, his palms on his palms; and he crouched over him, and the child's flesh grew warm.
Then he went back and walked in the house, once this way and once that; and he went up and crouched over him again. And the boy sneezed seven times, and the boy opened his eyes.
And he called Gehazi and said, "Call this Shunammite." So he called her, and she came to him. And he said, "Take up your son."
And she came and fell at his feet and bowed to the ground; then she took up her son and went out.

And Elisha returned to Gilgal while the famine was in the land, and the sons of the prophets were sitting before him. And he said to his servant, "Put on the large pot and boil stew for the sons of the prophets."

And one of them went out to the field to gather herbs, and he found a wild vine and gathered from it wild gourds, as much as his garment would hold; and he came and sliced them into the pot of stew, for they did not know what they were.
And they poured it out for the men to eat; and as they were eating of the stew, they cried out and said, "Death is in the pot, man of God!" And they could not eat it.
And he said, "Then fetch flour." And he threw it into the pot and said, "Pour it out for the people, and let them eat." And there was nothing bad in the pot.
And a man came from Baal-shalisha and brought to the man of God bread of the firstfruits — twenty barley loaves — and fresh grain in his sack. And he said, "Give it to the people, and let them eat."
And his attendant said, "How am I to set this before a hundred men?" And he said, "Give it to the people, and let them eat, for thus says the LORD: They shall eat and have some left over."
So he set it before them, and they ate and had some left over, according to the word of the LORD.

2 kings_5.t: Now Naaman, commander of the army of the king of Aram, was a great man before his master and held in high regard, for by him the LORD had given victory to Aram; and the man was a mighty man of valour — afflicted with leprosy.
Now the Arameans had gone out in raiding bands and had taken captive from the land of Israel a young girl, and she served the wife of Naaman.
And she said to her mistress, "If only my lord were before the prophet who is in Samaria! Then he would deliver him from his leprosy."
And he went and told his master, "Thus and thus spoke the girl who is from the land of Israel."
And the king of Aram said, "Go now, and let me send a letter to the king of Israel." So he went and took with him ten talents of silver, six thousand pieces of gold, and ten changes of clothes.
And he brought the letter to the king of Israel, which said, "Now when this letter comes to you — see, I have sent to you Naaman my servant, and you shall deliver him from his leprosy."

And when the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes and said, "Am I God, to put to death and to make alive, that this man sends to me to deliver a man from his leprosy? Only consider and see how he is seeking an occasion against me."

And when Elisha the man of God heard that the king of Israel had torn his clothes, he sent to the king, saying, "Why have you torn your clothes? Let him come to me, and let him know that there is a prophet in Israel."
So Naaman came with his horses and his chariot and stood at the entrance of Elisha's house.
And Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, "Go and wash seven times in the Jordan, and your flesh shall be restored to you, and you shall be clean."

But Naaman was angry and went away, and he said, "See, I said to myself, 'He will surely come out to me and stand and call on the name of the LORD his God, and wave his hand over the place, and deliver the one afflicted with leprosy.'
"Are not Amanah and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? Could I not wash in them and be clean?" And he turned and went off in a rage.

But his servants drew near and spoke to him, saying, "My father, if the prophet had told you to do some great thing, would you not have done it? How much more when he has said to you, 'Wash and be clean'?"
So he went down and dipped in the Jordan seven times, according to the word of the man of God; and his flesh was restored like the flesh of a young boy, and he was clean.

And he went back to the man of God, he and all his company, and he came and stood before him and said, "Now I know that there is no God in all the earth except in Israel. So now, accept a gift from your servant."
But he said, "As the LORD lives, before whom I stand, I will not accept." And he urged him to accept, but he refused.
And Naaman said, "If not, then let there be given to your servant two mule-loads of earth; for your servant will no longer offer a burnt offering or a sacrifice to other gods, but to the LORD.

"For this matter may the LORD forgive your servant: when my master goes into the house of Rimmon to bow down there, and he leans on my hand and I bow down in the house of Rimmon — when I bow down in the house of Rimmon, may the LORD forgive your servant in this matter."
And he said to him, "Go in peace." And he had gone from him some distance

But Gehazi, the servant of Elisha the man of God, said, "See, my master has spared this Naaman the Aramean by not accepting from his hand what he brought. As the LORD lives, I will run after him and accept something from him."
So Gehazi pursued Naaman. And when Naaman saw someone running after him, he got down from the chariot to meet him and said, "Is all well?"

And he said, "All is well. My master has sent me to say, 'Just now two young men have come to me from the hill country of Ephraim, from the sons of the prophets. Please give them a talent of silver and two changes of clothes.'"

And Naaman said, "Be willing — take two talents." And he urged him, and he bound up two talents of silver in two bags, with two changes of clothes, and gave them to two of his servants, and they carried them before Gehazi.
And when he came to the hill, he took them from their hand and deposited them in the house; and he sent the men away, and they went.
And he came in and stood before his master; and Elisha said to him, "Where have you come from, Gehazi?" And he said, "Your servant has not gone anywhere at all."

And he said to him, "Did not my heart go with you when the man turned from his chariot to meet you? Is this a time to accept silver, and to accept clothes and olive groves and vineyards and sheep and cattle and male and female servants?
"And the leprosy of Naaman shall cling to you and to your offspring for ever." And he went out from his presence, afflicted with leprosy, white as snow.

2 kings_6.t: Now the sons of the prophets said to Elisha, "See, the place where we dwell before you is too cramped for us.
"Let us go to the Jordan and take from there each one beam, and let us make ourselves a place there to dwell in." And he said, "Go."
And one of them said, "Be willing to go with your servants." And he said, "I will go."
So he went with them, and they came to the Jordan and cut down trees.
And as one was felling a beam, the iron fell into the water; and he cried out and said, "Alas, my lord! And it was borrowed."
And the man of God said, "Where did it fall?" And he showed him the place; and he cut off a piece of wood and threw it in, and made the iron float.
And he said, "Lift it out for yourself." So he reached out his hand and took it.
Now the king of Aram was at war with Israel, and he took counsel with his servants, saying, "At such and such a place shall be my encampment."
And the man of God sent to the king of Israel, saying, "Take care not to pass by this place, for the Arameans are coming down there."
And the king of Israel sent to the place of which the man of God had spoken and warned him; and he was on his guard there, more than once or twice.
And the heart of the king of Aram was enraged over this matter, and he called his servants and said to them, "Will you not tell me who among us is for the king of Israel?"
And one of his servants said, "No, my lord the king; for Elisha the prophet who is in Israel tells the king of Israel the words you speak in your bedchamber."
And he said, "Go and see where he is, that I may send and seize him." And he was told, "He is in Dothan."
So he sent horses and chariots there, and a massive force; and they came by night and surrounded the city.
And the attendant of the man of God rose early and went out; and there was a force surrounding the city, with horses and chariots. And his servant said to him, "Alas, my lord! What shall we do?"
And he said, "Do not be afraid, for those with us are more than those with them."
And Elisha prayed, "LORD, open his eyes, that he may see." And the LORD opened the eyes of the servant, and he saw; and there was the hill, full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.
And when they came down to him, Elisha prayed to the LORD and said, "Strike this nation with dazzlement." And he struck them with dazzlement, according to the word of Elisha.
And Elisha said to them, "This is not the way, and this is not the city. Follow me, and let me lead you to the man you are seeking." And he led them to Samaria.
And when they came to Samaria, Elisha said, "LORD, open the eyes of these men, that they may see." And the LORD opened their eyes, and they saw; and there they were, in the midst of Samaria.
And when the king of Israel saw them, he said to Elisha, "Shall I strike them down? Shall I strike them down, my father?"

And he said, "You shall not strike them down. Would you strike down those you had taken captive with your sword and your bow? Set bread and water before them, and let them eat and drink and go to their master."
So he prepared a great feast for them, and they ate and drank; then he sent them away, and they went to their master. And the raiding bands of Aram did not come again into the land of Israel.
And after this, Ben-hadad king of Aram gathered his whole army and went up and laid siege to Samaria.
And there was a great famine in Samaria, for they were besieging it, until a donkey's head sold for eighty pieces of silver and a quarter of a kab of dove's dung for five pieces of silver.
And as the king of Israel was passing by on the wall, a woman cried out to him, "Deliver me, my lord the king!"
And he said, "If the LORD does not deliver you, from where shall I deliver you? From the threshing floor or from the wine-press?"
And the king said to her, "What is the matter with you?" And she said, "This woman said to me, 'Give your son, and let us eat him today, and we will eat my son tomorrow.'
"So we boiled my son and ate him. And I said to her the next day, 'Give your son, and let us eat him' — but she had hidden her son."
And when the king heard the words of the woman, he tore his clothes — he was passing by on the wall — and the people saw, and there was sackcloth on his flesh underneath.
And he said, "So may God do to me and more also, if the head of Elisha son of Shaphat remains on him today!"

Now Elisha was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him. And the king sent a man ahead of him; but before the messenger came to him, Elisha said to the elders, "Do you see how this son of a murderer has sent to take off my head? Look — when the messenger comes, shut the door and press him back with the door. Is not the sound of his master's feet behind him?"
He was still speaking with them when the messenger came down to him. And he said, "See, this calamity is from the LORD. Why should I wait for the LORD any longer?"

2 kings_7.t: And Elisha said, "Hear the word of the LORD. Thus says the LORD: About this time tomorrow, a seah of fine flour for a shekel and two seahs of barley for a shekel, at the gate of Samaria."

And the officer on whose hand the king leaned answered the man of God, "Even if the LORD were making windows in the heavens, could this thing be?" And he said, "You are about to see it with your own eyes, but you shall not eat of it."
Now there were four men afflicted with leprosy at the entrance of the gate, and they said to one another, "Why are we sitting here until we die?

"If we say, 'We will go into the city,' the famine is in the city and we will die there; and if we sit here, we will die. So now, come, let us go over to the camp of Aram. If they let us live, we shall live; and if they put us to death, we shall die."
So they rose at twilight to go to the camp of Aram; and they came to the edge of the camp of Aram, and there was no one there.

For the Lord had made the camp of Aram hear a sound of chariots, a sound of horses, the sound of a great army; and they said to one another, "See, the king of Israel has hired against us the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Egypt to come against us!"
So they rose and fled at twilight and abandoned their tents, their horses, and their donkeys — the camp just as it was — and they fled for their lives.

And these men afflicted with leprosy came to the edge of the camp and went into one tent, and they ate and drank and carried off from there silver and gold and clothes, and went and hid them. Then they returned and went into another tent and carried off from there, and went and hid them.

Then they said to one another, "We are not doing right. This day is a day of good news, and we are keeping silent. If we wait until the light of morning, punishment will find us. Now come, let us go and tell the household of the king."

So they came and called to the gatekeeper of the city and told them, "We went into the camp of Aram, and there was no one there, and no sound of anyone — only the horses tied up and the donkeys tied up, and the tents just as they were."
And the gatekeepers called out, and it was told to the household of the king within.

And the king rose in the night and said to his servants, "Let me tell you what the Arameans have done to us. They know that we are hungry, so they have gone out from the camp to hide themselves in the open country, saying, 'When they come out of the city we will seize them alive, and we will get into the city.'"

And one of his servants answered, "Let them take five of the horses that are left in the city — they will fare like the whole multitude of Israel that is left in it, they will fare like the whole multitude of Israel that has perished — and let us send and see."
So they took two chariots with horses, and the king sent them after the camp of Aram, saying, "Go and see."

And they went after them as far as the Jordan, and there was the whole road full of clothes and equipment that the Arameans had thrown away in their haste. And the messengers returned and told the king.
And the people went out and plundered the camp of Aram; and a seah of fine flour sold for a shekel and two seahs of barley for a shekel, according to the word of the LORD.

Now the king had appointed the officer on whose hand he leaned to be over the gate; and the people trampled him in the gate, and he died, just as the man of God had spoken when the king came down to him.
And it was as the man of God had spoken to the king, saying, "Two seahs of barley for a shekel and a seah of fine flour for a shekel shall be about this time tomorrow at the gate of Samaria" —

and the officer answered the man of God, "Even if the LORD were making windows in the heavens, could such a thing be?" And he said, "You are about to see it with your own eyes, but you shall not eat of it."
And so it happened to him: the people trampled him in the gate, and he died.

2 kings_8.t: Now Elisha had spoken to the woman whose son he had restored to life, saying, "Arise and go, you and your household, and sojourn wherever you can; for the LORD has called for a famine, and it is coming upon the land for seven years."
And the woman rose and did according to the word of the man of God; and she went with her household and sojourned in the land of the Philistines seven years.
And at the end of seven years the woman returned from the land of the Philistines, and she went out to cry out to the king for her house and her field.
Now the king was speaking to Gehazi, the servant of the man of God, saying, "Recount to me all the great things that Elisha has done."

And just as he was recounting to the king how Elisha had restored the dead to life, the woman whose son he had restored to life came crying out to the king for her house and her field. And Gehazi said, "My lord the king, this is the woman, and this is her son, whom Elisha restored to life."

And the king asked the woman, and she recounted it to him. And the king assigned her a court official, saying, "Restore all that is hers, and all the produce of the field from the day she left the land until now."
And Elisha came to Damascus while Ben-hadad king of Aram was sick; and he was told, "The man of God has come here."
And the king said to Hazael, "Take a gift in your hand and go to meet the man of God, and consult the LORD through him, saying, 'Shall I recover from this sickness?'"

So Hazael went to meet him and took a gift in his hand, and every good thing of Damascus, forty camel-loads. And he came and stood before him and said, "Your son Ben-hadad king of Aram has sent me to you to ask, 'Shall I recover from this sickness?'"
And Elisha said to him, "Go, say to him, 'You shall surely recover.' But the LORD has shown me that he shall surely die."
And he set his face and held it fixed until he was ashamed; and the man of God wept.

And Hazael said, "Why is my lord weeping?" And he said, "Because I know the harm you will do to the Israelites: you will set their fortresses on fire, kill their young men with the sword, dash their children in pieces, and rip open their pregnant women."
And Hazael said, "But what is your servant, a dog, that he should do this great thing?" And Elisha said, "The LORD has shown me you as king over Aram."
And he went from Elisha and came to his master, who said to him, "What did Elisha say to you?" And he said, "He said to me, 'You shall surely recover.'"
And on the next day he took the coverlet, dipped it in water, and spread it over his face, and he died; and Hazael reigned in his place.
In the fifth year of Joram son of Ahab king of Israel, Jehoshaphat being king of Judah, Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah became king.
He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, for the daughter of Ahab was his wife; and he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.
But the LORD was not willing to destroy Judah, for the sake of David his servant, as he had promised him — to give him a lamp for his sons for all time.
In his days Edom rebelled from under the hand of Judah, and they set a king over themselves.
And Joram crossed over to Zair with all his chariots; and he rose by night and struck the Edomites who had surrounded him, and the commanders of the chariots — and the army fled to their tents.
So Edom has been in rebellion against the hand of Judah to this day. Then Libnah also rebelled at that time.
And the rest of the acts of Joram, and all that he did — are they not written in the chronicle of the kings of Judah?
And Joram lay down with his ancestors and was buried with his ancestors in the city of David; and Ahaziah his son reigned in his place.
In the twelfth year of Joram son of Ahab king of Israel, Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah became king.
Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem; and the name of his mother was Athaliah, the daughter of Omri king of Israel.
And he walked in the way of the house of Ahab, and he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, like the house of Ahab, for he was a son-in-law of the house of Ahab.
And he went with Joram son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-gilead, and the Arameans wounded Joram.

And King Joram returned to Jezreel to be healed of the wounds the Arameans had inflicted on him at Ramah when he fought against Hazael king of Aram. And Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Joram son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he was sick.

2 kings_9.t: Now Elisha the prophet called one of the sons of the prophets and said to him, "Gird your loins, take this flask of oil in your hand, and go to Ramoth-gilead.
"When you arrive there, look for Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi; go in, raise him up from among his brothers, and bring him into an inner room.
"Then take the flask of oil and pour it on his head and say, 'Thus says the LORD: I have anointed you as king over Israel.' Then open the door and flee, and do not wait."
So the young man went, the young man the prophet, to Ramoth-gilead.
And he came, and there were the commanders of the army, sitting; and he said, "I have a word for you, commander." And Jehu said, "For which of us all?" And he said, "For you, commander."
And he rose and went into the house, and he poured the oil on his head and said to him, "Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: I have anointed you as king over the people of the LORD, over Israel.
"And you shall strike down the house of Ahab your master; and I will avenge the blood of my servants the prophets, and the blood of all the servants of the LORD, at the hand of Jezebel.
"The whole house of Ahab shall perish; and I will cut off from Ahab every male, bond and free alike, in Israel.
"And I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah."
"And the dogs shall devour Jezebel in the territory of Jezreel, and there shall be no one to bury her." And he opened the door and fled.
And Jehu went out to the servants of his master, and one said to him, "Is all well? Why did this madman come to you?" And he said to them, "You know the man and his kind of talk."
And they said, "That is false! Tell us." And he said, "Thus and thus he said to me: 'Thus says the LORD: I have anointed you as king over Israel.'"
And they hurried and each took his garment and put it under him on the bare steps; and they blew the ram's horn and said, "Jehu is king!"
So Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi conspired against Joram. Now Joram had been holding Ramoth-gilead, he and all Israel, against Hazael king of Aram;

but King Jehoram had returned to Jezreel to be healed of the wounds the Arameans had inflicted on him when he fought against Hazael king of Aram. And Jehu said, "If this is your mind, let no fugitive go out from the city to go and tell it in Jezreel."
So Jehu mounted his chariot and went to Jezreel, for Joram was lying there; and Ahaziah king of Judah had gone down to see Joram.

Now the watchman was standing on the tower in Jezreel, and he saw the throng of Jehu as he came, and he said, "I see a throng." And Jehoram said, "Take a horseman and send him to meet them, and let him say, 'Is it peace?'"

So the rider of the horse went to meet him and said, "Thus says the king: Is it peace?" And Jehu said, "What have you to do with peace? Turn round behind me." And the watchman reported, "The messenger reached them and has not turned back."
So he sent a second rider of a horse, and he came to them and said, "Thus says the king: Peace?" And Jehu said, "What have you to do with peace? Turn round behind me."
And the watchman reported, "He reached them and has not turned back. And the driving is like the driving of Jehu son of Nimshi, for he drives with madness."

And Jehoram said, "Harness!" And they harnessed his chariot. And Jehoram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah went out, each in his chariot, and they went out to meet Jehu and found him in the plot of land of Naboth the Jezreelite.
And when Jehoram saw Jehu he said, "Is it peace, Jehu?" And he said, "What peace, so long as the prostitutions of Jezebel your mother and her many sorceries continue?"
And Jehoram turned his hands and fled, and he said to Ahaziah, "Treachery, Ahaziah!"
And Jehu drew the bow with his full strength and struck Jehoram between his shoulders, and the arrow came out at his heart; and he sank down in his chariot.

And he said to Bidkar his officer, "Pick him up and throw him into the plot of the field of Naboth the Jezreelite; for remember, you and I were riding side by side behind Ahab his father when the LORD lifted up this oracle against him:

"'Surely I saw yesterday the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons — declares the LORD — and I will repay you on this plot of land — declares the LORD.' Now then, pick him up and throw him onto the plot of land, according to the word of the LORD."

And when Ahaziah king of Judah saw it, he fled by the way of Beth-haggan; and Jehu pursued him and said, "Strike him down too, in the chariot!" — at the ascent of Gur, which is near Ibleam. And he fled to Megiddo and died there.
And his servants carried him by chariot to Jerusalem, and they buried him in his grave with his ancestors in the city of David.
Now in the eleventh year of Joram son of Ahab, Ahaziah had become king over Judah.
And Jehu came to Jezreel; and when Jezebel heard of it, she painted her eyes and dressed her head, and she looked down through the window.
And as Jehu came into the gate, she said, "Is it peace, Zimri, murderer of his master?"
And he lifted his face to the window and said, "Who is with me? Who?" And two or three court officials looked down at him.
And he said, "Throw her down!" And they threw her down; and some of her blood spattered on the wall and on the horses, and he trampled her.
Then he went in and ate and drank, and he said, "Attend to this accursed woman and bury her, for she is a king's daughter."
And they went to bury her, and they found nothing of her except the skull, the feet, and the palms of the hands.

And they returned and told him; and he said, "This is the word of the LORD that he spoke through his servant Elijah the Tishbite: 'In the territory of Jezreel the dogs shall devour the flesh of Jezebel;
"'and the corpse of Jezebel shall be like dung on the face of the field, in the territory of Jezreel, so that no one shall say, "This is Jezebel."'"

2 kings_10.t: Now Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. And Jehu wrote letters and sent them to Samaria, to the officials of Jezreel, the elders, and to the guardians of Ahab's sons, saying,
"Now when this letter comes to you — and with you are your master's sons, and with you are the chariots and the horses and a fortified city and the weaponry —
"choose the best and most upright of your master's sons, set him on his father's throne, and fight for the house of your master."
But they were exceedingly afraid, and they said, "See, the two kings did not stand before him — how then shall we stand?"

So the one who was over the palace, and the one over the city, and the elders and the guardians sent to Jehu, saying, "We are your servants, and all that you say to us we will do. We will not make anyone king. Do what is good in your eyes."

Then he wrote them a second letter, saying, "If you are for me, and you are listening to my voice, take the heads of the men, your master's sons, and come to me about this time tomorrow, to Jezreel." Now the king's sons, seventy men, were with the great men of the city, who were bringing them up.
And when the letter came to them, they took the king's sons and slaughtered seventy men; and they put their heads in baskets and sent them to him at Jezreel.
And the messenger came and told him, "They have brought the heads of the king's sons." And he said, "Make them two heaps at the entrance of the gate until morning."
And in the morning he went out and stood and said to all the people, "You are innocent. See, I conspired against my master and killed him — but who struck down all these?"
"Know then that nothing of the word of the LORD shall fall to the ground, which the LORD spoke concerning the house of Ahab; and the LORD has done what he spoke through his servant Elijah."
And Jehu struck down all who remained of the house of Ahab in Jezreel, and all his great men, his close friends, and his priests, until he left him no survivor.
Then he rose and went and came to Samaria. He was at Beth-eked of the Shepherds on the way,

and Jehu found the brothers of Ahaziah king of Judah, and he said, "Who are you?" And they said, "We are the brothers of Ahaziah, and we have come down to greet the sons of the king and the sons of the queen mother."
And he said, "Seize them alive." And they seized them alive and slaughtered them at the pit of Beth-eked — forty-two men — and he spared not one of them.

And he went from there and found Jehonadab son of Rechab coming to meet him, and he greeted him and said to him, "Is your heart right, as my heart is with your heart?" And Jehonadab said, "It is, it is." "Then give me your hand." And he gave his hand, and Jehu took him up into the chariot with him.
And he said, "Come with me and see my zeal for the LORD." So they made him ride in his chariot.
And he came to Samaria and struck down all who remained of Ahab in Samaria, until he had destroyed him, according to the word of the LORD that he had spoken to Elijah.
Then Jehu gathered all the people and said to them, "Ahab served the Baal a little; Jehu will serve him much.

"Now summon to me all the prophets of the Baal, all who serve him, and all his priests. Let no one be missing, for I have a great sacrifice to the Baal. Whoever is missing shall not live." But Jehu acted with guile, in order to destroy those who serve the Baal.
And Jehu said, "Set apart an assembly for the Baal." And they proclaimed it.

And Jehu sent throughout all Israel, and all who serve the Baal came; not one was left who did not come. And they came into the house of the Baal, and the house of the Baal was filled from end to end.
And he said to the one who was over the wardrobe, "Bring out clothing for all who serve the Baal." And he brought out the clothing for them.

And Jehu came into the house of the Baal, with Jehonadab son of Rechab; and he said to those who serve the Baal, "Search and see that there is none here with you of the servants of the LORD — only those who serve the Baal, they alone."

And they came in to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. Now Jehu had stationed eighty men outside for himself, and had said, "The man who lets any escape of the men I am bringing into your hands — his life for his life."

And when he had finished offering the burnt offering, Jehu said to the runners and the officers, "Go in, strike them down; let no one come out." And they struck them with the edge of the sword; and the runners and the officers threw them out, and they went into the city of the house of the Baal.
And they brought out the pillars of the house of the Baal and burned them.
And they pulled down the pillar of the Baal, and they pulled down the house of the Baal and made it into latrines, to this day.
So Jehu destroyed the Baal from Israel.
But from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, Jehu did not turn aside — the calves of gold that were at Beth-el and at Dan.

And the LORD said to Jehu, "Because you have done well in doing what is right in my eyes, and have done to the house of Ahab according to all that was in my heart, your sons to the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel."
But Jehu did not take care to walk in the law of the LORD, the God of Israel, with all his heart; he did not turn aside from the sins of Jeroboam, who caused Israel to sin.
In those days the LORD began to cut off parts of Israel, and Hazael struck them down throughout all the territory of Israel,
from the Jordan eastward: all the land of Gilead, the Gadites, the Reubenites, and the Manassites, from Aroer, which is by the wadi Arnon, and Gilead and Bashan.
And the rest of the acts of Jehu, and all that he did, and all his might — are they not written in the chronicle of the kings of Israel?
And Jehu lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him in Samaria; and Jehoahaz his son reigned in his place.
And the days that Jehu reigned over Israel were twenty-eight years, in Samaria.

2 kings_11.t: Now when Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, saw that her son was dead, she rose and destroyed all the royal offspring.

But Jehosheba, daughter of King Joram, sister of Ahaziah, took Joash son of Ahaziah and stole him from among the king's sons who were being put to death — him and his nurse — into the bedchamber; and they hid him from Athaliah, and he was not put to death.
And he was with her in the house of the LORD, hidden, six years, while Athaliah reigned over the land.

But in the seventh year Jehoiada sent and took the commanders of hundreds of the Carites and of the runners, and brought them to himself into the house of the LORD; and he made a covenant with them and put them under oath in the house of the LORD, and he showed them the king's son.
And he commanded them, "This is what you shall do: a third of you, those coming on duty on the sabbath, shall keep the watch of the house of the king;
"and a third at the gate of Sur, and a third at the gate behind the runners; and you shall keep the watch of the house by turns.
"And the two divisions among you, all those going off duty on the sabbath, shall keep the watch of the house of the LORD for the king.
"And you shall surround the king all around, each with his weapons in his hand; and anyone who comes into the ranks shall be put to death. And be with the king when he goes out and when he comes in."

And the commanders of hundreds did according to all that Jehoiada the priest commanded; and each took his men, those coming on duty on the sabbath together with those going off duty on the sabbath, and they came to Jehoiada the priest.
And the priest gave the commanders of hundreds the spear and the shields that had belonged to King David, which were in the house of the LORD.
And the runners stood, each with his weapons in his hand, from the south side of the house to the north side of the house, by the altar and by the house, all around the king.
Then he brought out the king's son and put the crown on him, and the testimony; and they made him king and anointed him, and they clapped their hands and said, "Long live the king!"
And when Athaliah heard the sound of the runners and of the people, she came to the people at the house of the LORD.

And she looked, and there was the king standing by the pillar according to the custom, with the commanders and the trumpeters beside the king, and all the people of the land rejoicing and blowing the trumpets. And Athaliah tore her clothes and cried out, "Conspiracy! Conspiracy!"

And Jehoiada the priest commanded the commanders of hundreds, the officers of the force, and said to them, "Bring her out between the ranks, and whoever comes after her, put to death with the sword" — for the priest had said, "Let her not be put to death in the house of the LORD."
So they laid hands on her, and she went by the way of the horses' entrance to the house of the king; and she was put to death there.
And Jehoiada made the covenant between the LORD and the king and the people, that they should be a people for the LORD; and between the king and the people.

And all the people of the land came to the house of the Baal and pulled it down; they broke his altars and his images thoroughly, and they killed Mattan the priest of the Baal before the altars. And the priest appointed overseers over the house of the LORD.

And he took the commanders of hundreds, the Carites, the runners, and all the people of the land, and they brought the king down from the house of the LORD; and they came by the way of the gate of the runners to the house of the king, and he sat on the throne of the kings.
And all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city had rest; and they had put Athaliah to death with the sword at the house of the king.
Jehoash was seven years old when he became king.

2 kings_12.t: In the seventh year of Jehu, Jehoash became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. And the name of his mother was Zibiah, from Beer-sheba.
And Jehoash did what was right in the eyes of the LORD all his days, in which Jehoiada the priest instructed him.
Only the high places were not removed; the people still sacrificed and made offerings of smoke at the high places.

And Jehoash said to the priests, "All the money of the holy gifts that is brought into the house of the LORD — the census money, the money assessed for persons at his valuation, and all the money that comes into a man's heart to bring into the house of the LORD —
"let the priests take it for themselves, each from his acquaintance; and they shall repair the damage of the house, wherever damage is found."
But in the twenty-third year of King Jehoash, the priests had still not repaired the damage of the house.

So King Jehoash summoned Jehoiada the priest and the priests, and he said to them, "Why are you not repairing the damage of the house? Now then, take no more money from your acquaintances, but hand it over for the damage of the house."
And the priests agreed neither to take money from the people nor to repair the damage of the house.

Then Jehoiada the priest took a chest and bored a hole in its lid, and he set it beside the altar, on the right as one comes into the house of the LORD; and the priests who kept the threshold put in it all the money that was brought into the house of the LORD.
And whenever they saw that there was much money in the chest, the king's scribe and the high priest came up and bagged it and counted the money that was found in the house of the LORD.

And they put the money that had been weighed out into the hands of those doing the work, who were appointed over the house of the LORD; and they paid it out to the carpenters and the builders who were working on the house of the LORD,
and to the masons and the stonecutters, and to buy timber and hewn stone to repair the damage of the house of the LORD, and for everything that was laid out on the house to repair it.
But no silver bowls, snuffers, basins, trumpets, or any articles of gold or silver were made for the house of the LORD from the money that was brought into the house of the LORD;
for they gave it to those doing the work, and with it they repaired the house of the LORD.
And they did not settle accounts with the men into whose hands they put the money to pay those doing the work, for they were dealing in good faith.
Money of a guilt offering and money of sin offerings was not brought into the house of the LORD; it belonged to the priests.
Then Hazael king of Aram went up and fought against Gath and captured it; and Hazael set his face to go up against Jerusalem.

So Jehoash king of Judah took all the holy things that Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah his ancestors, the kings of Judah, had consecrated, and his own holy things, and all the gold found in the treasuries of the house of the LORD and of the house of the king, and he sent them to Hazael king of Aram; and he withdrew from Jerusalem.
And the rest of the acts of Joash, and all that he did — are they not written in the chronicle of the kings of Judah?
And his servants rose and formed a conspiracy, and they struck down Joash at Beth-millo, on the road that goes down to Silla.

It was Jozacar son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer, his servants, who struck him down, and he died; and they buried him with his ancestors in the city of David. And Amaziah his son reigned in his place.

2 kings_13.t: In the twenty-third year of Joash son of Ahaziah king of Judah, Jehoahaz son of Jehu became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned seventeen years.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and he walked after the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin; he did not turn aside from them.
And the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he gave them into the hand of Hazael king of Aram and into the hand of Ben-hadad son of Hazael, all their days.
But Jehoahaz entreated the favour of the LORD, and the LORD listened to him, for he saw the oppression of Israel, how the king of Aram oppressed them.
And the LORD gave Israel a deliverer, and they went out from under the hand of Aram; and the Israelites dwelt in their tents as they had before.
Nevertheless they did not turn aside from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, who caused Israel to sin; in them they walked. And the Asherah also remained standing in Samaria.
For he had left Jehoahaz no army except fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand foot soldiers; for the king of Aram had destroyed them and made them like the dust to be trampled.
And the rest of the acts of Jehoahaz, and all that he did, and his might — are they not written in the chronicle of the kings of Israel?
And Jehoahaz lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him in Samaria; and Joash his son reigned in his place.
In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoash son of Jehoahaz became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned sixteen years.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD; he did not turn aside from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin — in them he walked.
And the rest of the acts of Joash, and all that he did, and his might, with which he fought against Amaziah king of Judah — are they not written in the chronicle of the kings of Israel?
And Joash lay down with his ancestors, and Jeroboam sat on his throne; and Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.

Now Elisha had fallen sick with the sickness of which he would die; and Joash king of Israel went down to him and wept over his face and said, "My father, my father! The chariotry of Israel and its horsemen!"
And Elisha said to him, "Take a bow and arrows." So he took a bow and arrows for himself.
And he said to the king of Israel, "Set your hand on the bow." And he set his hand on it; and Elisha put his hands on the king's hands.

And he said, "Open the window eastward." And he opened it. And Elisha said, "Shoot." And he shot. And he said, "An arrow of victory for the LORD, and an arrow of victory over Aram! And you shall strike Aram at Aphek until you have made an end of them."
And he said, "Take the arrows." And he took them. And he said to the king of Israel, "Strike the ground." And he struck three times and stopped.

And the man of God was angry with him and said, "You should have struck five or six times! Then you would have struck Aram until you had made an end of them; but now you shall strike Aram three times."
And Elisha died, and they buried him. Now marauding bands of Moab used to come into the land at the turn of the year.

And once, as they were burying a man, they suddenly saw a raiding band, and they threw the man into the grave of Elisha; and when the man touched the bones of Elisha, he came to life and stood on his feet.
Now Hazael king of Aram had oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.

But the LORD showed them favour and had compassion on them and turned to them, because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; and he was not willing to destroy them, and he has not cast them out from his presence until now.
And Hazael king of Aram died, and Ben-hadad his son reigned in his place.

And Jehoash son of Jehoahaz took back from the hand of Ben-hadad son of Hazael the cities that he had taken from the hand of Jehoahaz his father in battle. Three times Joash struck him down, and he restored the cities of Israel.

2 kings_14.t: In the second year of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel, Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah became king.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem; and the name of his mother was Jehoaddan, from Jerusalem.
And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, though not like David his ancestor. He did according to all that Joash his father had done.
Only the high places were not removed; the people still sacrificed and made offerings of smoke at the high places.
And when the kingdom was secure in his hand, he struck down his servants who had struck down the king his father.

But the sons of those who struck him down he did not put to death, according to what is written in the book of the law of Moses, which the LORD commanded: "Fathers shall not be put to death for sons, and sons shall not be put to death for fathers; but each shall be put to death for his own sin."
He struck down ten thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt and seized Sela in the battle, and he named it Joktheel, which it is called to this day.
Then Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash son of Jehoahaz son of Jehu king of Israel, saying, "Come, let us look one another in the face."

And Jehoash king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, "The thornbush in the Lebanon sent to the cedar in the Lebanon, saying, 'Give your daughter to my son as a wife.' But a wild animal in the Lebanon passed by and trampled the thornbush.
"You have indeed struck Edom, and your heart has lifted you up. Take the honour and stay at home! Why should you provoke harm and fall, you and Judah with you?"
But Amaziah did not listen. So Jehoash king of Israel went up, and they looked one another in the face, he and Amaziah king of Judah, at Beth-shemesh, which belongs to Judah.
And Judah was defeated before Israel, and they fled, each to his tents.

And Jehoash king of Israel seized Amaziah king of Judah, son of Jehoash son of Ahaziah, at Beth-shemesh; and he came to Jerusalem and made a breach in the wall of Jerusalem, from the gate of Ephraim to the corner gate — four hundred cubits.
And he took all the gold and silver and all the articles found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the house of the king, and hostages as well; and he returned to Samaria.
And the rest of the acts of Jehoash, which he did, and his might, and how he fought against Amaziah king of Judah — are they not written in the chronicle of the kings of Israel?
And Jehoash lay down with his ancestors and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel; and Jeroboam his son reigned in his place.
And Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived fifteen years after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.
And the rest of the acts of Amaziah — are they not written in the chronicle of the kings of Judah?
And they formed a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish; but they sent after him to Lachish and put him to death there.
And they carried him back on horses, and he was buried in Jerusalem with his ancestors in the city of David.
And all the people of Judah took Azariah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
He rebuilt Elath and restored it to Judah, after the king lay down with his ancestors.
In the fifteenth year of Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah, Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel became king in Samaria, and he reigned forty-one years.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD; he did not turn aside from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.

He restored the border of Israel from Lebo-hamath to the sea of the Arabah, according to the word of the LORD, the God of Israel, which he spoke through his servant Jonah son of Amittai the prophet, who was from Gath-hepher.
For the LORD saw the affliction of Israel, very bitter, with none left, bond or free, and no helper for Israel.
And the LORD had not said that he would wipe out the name of Israel from under the heavens; so he delivered them by the hand of Jeroboam son of Joash.

And the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, and all that he did, and his might, how he fought and how he recovered Damascus and Hamath, which had belonged to Judah, for Israel — are they not written in the chronicle of the kings of Israel?
And Jeroboam lay down with his ancestors, with the kings of Israel; and Zechariah his son reigned in his place.

2 kings_15.t: In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah king of Judah became king.
He was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem; and the name of his mother was Jecoliah, from Jerusalem.
And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that Amaziah his father had done.
Only the high places were not removed; the people still sacrificed and made offerings of smoke at the high places.

And the LORD struck the king, and he was afflicted with leprosy until the day of his death; and he dwelt in a house of separateness. And Jotham the king's son was over the palace, judging the people of the land.
And the rest of the acts of Azariah, and all that he did — are they not written in the chronicle of the kings of Judah?
And Azariah lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him with his ancestors in the city of David; and Jotham his son reigned in his place.
In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah king of Judah, Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned six months.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, as his ancestors had done; he did not turn aside from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.
And Shallum son of Jabesh conspired against him and struck him down before the people and killed him, and he reigned in his place.
And the rest of the acts of Zechariah — see, they are written in the chronicle of the kings of Israel.
That was the word of the LORD that he had spoken to Jehu: "Your sons to the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel." And so it was.
Shallum son of Jabesh became king in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah, and he reigned a full month in Samaria.
Then Menahem son of Gadi went up from Tirzah and came to Samaria and struck down Shallum son of Jabesh in Samaria, and killed him; and he reigned in his place.
And the rest of the acts of Shallum, and the conspiracy he formed — see, they are written in the chronicle of the kings of Israel.
Then Menahem struck Tiphsah and all who were in it and its territories, from Tirzah — because it did not open to him, he struck it; and all its pregnant women he ripped open.
In the thirty-ninth year of Azariah king of Judah, Menahem son of Gadi became king over Israel, and he reigned ten years in Samaria.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD; he did not turn aside from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, all his days.
Pul king of Assyria came against the land, and Menahem gave Pul a thousand talents of silver, that his hands might be with him to strengthen the kingdom in his hand.

And Menahem exacted the silver from Israel, from all the wealthy men, to give to the king of Assyria — fifty shekels of silver for each man. And the king of Assyria turned back and did not remain there in the land.
And the rest of the acts of Menahem, and all that he did — are they not written in the chronicle of the kings of Israel?
And Menahem lay down with his ancestors; and Pekahiah his son reigned in his place.
In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekahiah son of Menahem became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned two years.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD; he did not turn aside from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.

And Pekah son of Remaliah, his officer, conspired against him and struck him down in Samaria, in the fortress of the house of the king, along with Argob and Arieh; and fifty men of the Gileadites were with him. And he killed him and reigned in his place.
And the rest of the acts of Pekahiah, and all that he did — see, they are written in the chronicle of the kings of Israel.
In the fifty-second year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekah son of Remaliah became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned twenty years.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD; he did not turn aside from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.

In the days of Pekah king of Israel, Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria came and took Ijon, Abel-beth-maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali; and he took them into exile to Assyria.
