And David said to him, "Do not be afraid, for I will certainly show you loyalty for the sake of Jonathan your father, and I will restore to you all the land of Saul your father, and you shall eat bread at my table continually."
And he bowed down and said, "What is your servant, that you have turned to a dead dog such as I am?"
Then the king summoned Ziba, Saul's servant, and said to him, "All that belonged to Saul and to all his house I have given to your master's son.

"And you shall work the ground for him — you and your sons and your servants — and bring in the produce, and it shall be food for your master's son, and he shall eat it. But Mephibosheth your master's son shall eat bread at my table continually." Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.
And Ziba said to the king, "According to all that my lord the king commands his servant, so your servant will do." And Mephibosheth ate at David's table like one of the king's sons.
And Mephibosheth had a young son whose name was Mica. And all who lived in the house of Ziba were servants to Mephibosheth.
So Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, for he ate continually at the king's table. And he was lame in both his feet.

2 samuel_10.t: After this the king of the Ammonites died, and Hanun his son reigned in his place.

And David said, "I will show loyalty to Hanun son of Nahash, as his father showed loyalty to me." So David sent by the hand of his servants to comfort him for his father. And the servants of David came to the land of the Ammonites.

But the leaders of the Ammonites said to Hanun their lord, "Do you think David is honouring your father, that he has sent you comforters? Has David not sent his servants to you in order to explore the city and spy on it and overthrow it?"
So Hanun took the servants of David, shaved off half their beards, cut off their robes in the middle as far as their buttocks, and sent them away.
When they told David, he sent to meet them, for the men were deeply humiliated. And the king said, "Remain at Jericho until your beards grow back, and then return."

When the Ammonites saw that they had made themselves odious to David, the Ammonites sent and hired the Arameans of Beth-rehob and the Arameans of Zobah, twenty thousand foot soldiers, and the king of Maacah with a thousand men, and the men of Tob, twelve thousand men.
When David heard of it, he sent Joab and all the army, the mighty men.
The Ammonites went out and drew up for battle at the entrance of the gate, while the Arameans of Zobah and Rehob and the men of Tob and Maacah were by themselves in the open country.
When Joab saw that the front of the battle was against him both before and behind, he chose from all the picked men of Israel and drew them up to meet the Arameans.
And the rest of the people he put under the hand of Abishai his brother, and he drew them up to meet the Ammonites.
And he said, "If the Arameans are too strong for me, then you shall be my deliverance; and if the Ammonites are too strong for you, then I will come to deliver you.
"Be strong, and let us show ourselves strong for our people and for the cities of our God. And the LORD will do what is good in his eyes."
So Joab drew near, with the people who were with him, for the battle against the Arameans, and they fled before him.
And when the Ammonites saw that the Arameans had fled, they fled before Abishai and went into the city. And Joab returned from the Ammonites and came to Jerusalem.
When the Arameans saw that they had been defeated before Israel, they gathered themselves together.
And Hadadezer sent and brought out the Arameans who were beyond the River, and they came to Helam, with Shobach the commander of Hadadezer's army at their head.
When it was told to David, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan and came to Helam. And the Arameans drew up to meet David, and they fought with him.
And the Arameans fled before Israel, and David killed seven hundred of their charioteers and forty thousand horsemen; and he struck down Shobach the commander of their army, and he died there.

And when all the kings who were servants of Hadadezer saw that they had been defeated before Israel, they made peace with Israel and served them. And the Arameans were afraid to help the Ammonites any more.

2 samuel_11.t: At the turn of the year, at the time when the messengers go out, David sent Joab and his servants with him and all Israel, and they ravaged the Ammonites and besieged Rabbah. But David stayed in Jerusalem.
At evening David rose from his bed and walked about on the roof of the king's house, and from the roof he saw a woman bathing. And the woman was very beautiful.
And David sent and enquired about the woman, and someone said, "Is this not Bathsheba daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?"
And David sent messengers and took her, and she came to him, and he lay with her — and she had been consecrating herself from her uncleanness — and she returned to her house.
And the woman conceived, and she sent and told David, "I am pregnant."
And David sent to Joab, "Send me Uriah the Hittite." And Joab sent Uriah to David.
And Uriah came to him, and David asked after the welfare of Joab, the welfare of the people and the welfare of the war.
And David said to Uriah, "Go down to your house and wash your feet." And Uriah went out from the king's house, and a gift from the king went out after him.
But Uriah lay down at the entrance of the king's house with all the servants of his lord, and he did not go down to his house.
And they told David, "Uriah did not go down to his house." And David said to Uriah, "Have you not come from a journey? Why have you not gone down to your house?"

And Uriah said to David, "The ark and Israel and Judah are dwelling in booths, and my lord Joab and the servants of my lord are camping in the open field. And am I to go to my house to eat and to drink and to lie with my wife? By your life and by the life of your being, I will not do this thing."
And David said to Uriah, "Stay here today also, and tomorrow I will send you off." So Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day and the next.

And David summoned him, and he ate and drank before him, and David made him drunk. And in the evening he went out to lie down on his bed with the servants of his lord, and he did not go down to his house.
In the morning David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it by the hand of Uriah.
And he wrote in the letter, "Set Uriah at the front of the fiercest fighting, and draw back from behind him, so that he is struck down and dies."
And when Joab was besieging the city, he put Uriah at the place where he knew there were valiant men.
And the men of the city came out and fought with Joab, and some of the people, some of the servants of David, fell; and Uriah the Hittite also died.
And Joab sent and told David all the matters of the battle.
And he instructed the messenger, "When you have finished telling the king all the matters of the battle,
"then, if the king's anger rises and he says to you, 'Why did you go so near the city to fight? Did you not know that they would shoot from the wall?

"'Who struck down Abimelech son of Jerubbesheth? Did not a woman throw an upper millstone on him from the wall, so that he died at Thebez? Why did you go so near the wall?' — then you shall say, 'Your servant Uriah the Hittite is also dead.'"
And the messenger went, and came and told David all that Joab had sent him with.
And the messenger said to David, "The men prevailed against us and came out to us into the open field, and we drove them back as far as the entrance of the gate.
"And the archers shot at your servants from the wall, and some of the king's servants died. And your servant Uriah the Hittite is also dead."

And David said to the messenger, "Say this to Joab: 'Do not let this thing be evil in your eyes, for the sword devours now one and now another. Press your battle against the city and tear it down.' And encourage him."
And the wife of Uriah heard that Uriah her husband was dead, and she mourned over her husband.
And when the mourning was over, David sent and brought her to his house, and she became his wife and bore him a son. But the thing that David had done was evil in the eyes of the LORD.

2 samuel_12.t: And the LORD sent Nathan to David. And he came to him and said to him, "There were two men in one city, one rich and one poor.
"The rich man had very many flocks and herds.

"But the poor man had nothing at all except one little ewe lamb that he had bought. He kept it alive, and it grew up with him and with his children: it would eat from his morsel and drink from his cup and lie in his bosom, and it was to him like a daughter.

"And a traveller came to the rich man, and he was unwilling to take from his own flock or his own herd to prepare for the wayfarer who had come to him; so he took the poor man's ewe lamb and prepared it for the man who had come to him."
Then David's anger burned greatly against the man, and he said to Nathan, "As the LORD lives, the man who did this deserves to die!
"And he shall restore the ewe lamb fourfold, because he did this thing and because he had no pity."
And Nathan said to David, "You are the man! Thus says the LORD, God of Israel: I anointed you as king over Israel, and I delivered you from the hand of Saul,

"and I gave you your master's house, and your master's wives into your bosom, and I gave you the house of Israel and Judah. And if that were too little, I would add to you this much and this much again.

"Why have you despised the word of the LORD, to do what is evil in my eyes? Uriah the Hittite you struck down with the sword, and his wife you took for yourself as a wife, and him you killed with the sword of the Ammonites.
"And now the sword will never depart from your house, because you despised me and took the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be your wife.

"Thus says the LORD: I am raising up evil against you out of your own house, and I will take your wives before your eyes and give them to your neighbour, and he will lie with your wives in the sight of this sun.
"For you acted in secret, but I will do this thing before all Israel and before the sun."
And David said to Nathan, "I have sinned against the LORD." And Nathan said to David, "The LORD also has taken away your sin; you will not die.
"Nevertheless, because by this thing you have utterly scorned the enemies of the LORD, the son born to you shall also surely die."
And Nathan went to his house. And the LORD struck the child that the wife of Uriah had borne to David, and it became sick.
And David sought God for the boy. David fasted a fast, and he went in and spent the night lying on the ground.
And the elders of his house stood over him to raise him from the ground, but he was not willing, and he would not eat food with them.

On the seventh day the child died. And the servants of David were afraid to tell him that the child was dead, for they said, "While the child was alive we spoke to him and he would not listen to us; how then can we say to him, 'The child is dead'? He may do himself harm."
But David saw that his servants were whispering to one another, and David understood that the child was dead. And David said to his servants, "Is the child dead?" And they said, "He is dead."

Then David rose from the ground, washed, anointed himself and changed his garments, and he went into the house of the LORD and bowed down. Then he went to his own house and asked, and they set food before him and he ate.
And his servants said to him, "What is this thing you have done? While the child was alive you fasted and wept for him; and when the child died you got up and ate food."
And he said, "While the child was still alive I fasted and wept, for I said, 'Who knows? The LORD may show me favour and the child may live.'
"But now he is dead. Why should I fast? Can I bring him back again? I am going to him, but he will not return to me."
And David comforted Bathsheba his wife, and he went in to her and lay with her. And she bore a son, and she called his name Solomon. And the LORD loved him,
and he sent word by the hand of Nathan the prophet, and he called his name Jedidiah, for the LORD's sake.
Meanwhile Joab fought against Rabbah of the Ammonites and captured the royal city.
And Joab sent messengers to David and said, "I have fought against Rabbah; I have also captured the city of waters.
"And now gather the rest of the people and encamp against the city and capture it, lest I capture the city myself and my name be called over it."
So David gathered all the people and went to Rabbah, and he fought against it and captured it.

And he took the crown of their king from his head — its weight was a talent of gold, and there was a precious stone in it — and it was set on David's head. And he brought out the plunder of the city, a very great quantity.

And the people who were in it he brought out and set to labour with the saws and the iron picks and the iron axes, and he made them work at the brick kilns. And so he did to all the cities of the Ammonites. Then David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.

2 samuel_13.t: After this: Absalom son of David had a beautiful sister whose name was Tamar, and Amnon son of David loved her.
And Amnon was so distressed over Tamar his sister that he made himself ill, for she was a virgin; and it seemed impossible in Amnon's eyes to do anything to her.
Now Amnon had a friend whose name was Jonadab son of Shimeah, David's brother; and Jonadab was a very shrewd man.
And he said to him, "Why are you so wasted, son of the king, morning after morning? Will you not tell me?" And Amnon said to him, "Tamar, the sister of Absalom my brother — I love her."

And Jonadab said to him, "Lie down on your bed and make yourself ill. And when your father comes to see you, say to him, 'Let Tamar my sister come and give me food to eat; let her prepare the food before my eyes, so that I may see it and eat from her hand.'"
So Amnon lay down and made himself ill. And the king came to see him, and Amnon said to the king, "Let Tamar my sister come and make two cakes before my eyes, so that I may eat from her hand."
And David sent word to Tamar at the house, saying, "Go to the house of Amnon your brother and make the food for him."
And Tamar went to the house of Amnon her brother, and he was lying down. And she took the dough and kneaded it and made the cakes before his eyes, and she cooked the cakes.
And she took the pan and turned them out before him, but he refused to eat. And Amnon said, "Send everyone out from me!" And everyone went out from him.
And Amnon said to Tamar, "Bring the food into the inner room, so that I may eat from your hand." And Tamar took the cakes she had made and brought them to Amnon her brother, into the inner room.
And she brought them near to him to eat, and he took hold of her and said to her, "Come, lie with me, my sister."
And she said to him, "No, my brother! Do not violate me, for such a thing is not done in Israel. Do not do this outrage.
"And I — where could I carry my reproach? And you would be like one of the fools in Israel. And now speak to the king, for he will not withhold me from you."
But he was not willing to listen to her voice, and he was stronger than she was, and he violated her and lay with her.
Then Amnon hated her with a very great hatred, for the hatred with which he hated her was greater than the love with which he had loved her. And Amnon said to her, "Get up, go."
And she said to him, "No! This great evil of sending me away is worse than the other that you did to me." But he was not willing to listen to her.
And he summoned the young man who served him and said, "Send this one away from me, outside, and bolt the door after her."
And she was wearing a long tunic, for so the virgin daughters of the king wore robes. And his servant brought her outside and bolted the door after her.
And Tamar put ashes on her head, and she tore the long tunic that was on her, and she put her hand on her head and went away, crying out as she went.

And Absalom her brother said to her, "Has Amnon your brother been with you? Now, my sister, be silent. He is your brother. Do not set your heart on this matter." And Tamar remained, desolate, in the house of Absalom her brother.
And King David heard all these things, and he was very angry.
And Absalom did not speak with Amnon, either bad or good, for Absalom hated Amnon because he had violated Tamar his sister.
Two full years later, Absalom had shearers at Baal-hazor, which is near Ephraim, and Absalom invited all the sons of the king.
And Absalom came to the king and said, "Your servant has shearers. Let the king and his servants go with your servant."
And the king said to Absalom, "No, my son. Let us not all go, or we shall be a burden on you." And he pressed him, but he was not willing to go, and he blessed him.
And Absalom said, "If not, then let Amnon my brother go with us." And the king said to him, "Why should he go with you?"
But Absalom pressed him, and he sent Amnon with him, and all the sons of the king.

And Absalom commanded his young men, "See now, when Amnon's heart is merry with wine and I say to you, 'Strike Amnon,' then put him to death. Do not be afraid. Have I not myself commanded you? Be strong and be valiant."
And Absalom's young men did to Amnon just as Absalom had commanded. Then all the sons of the king rose, and each mounted his mule, and they fled.
And while they were still on the road, the report came to David: "Absalom has struck down all the sons of the king, and not one of them is left."
And the king rose and tore his garments and lay on the ground, and all his servants stood by with their garments torn.

But Jonadab son of Shimeah, David's brother, said, "Let not my lord say that they have put to death all the young men, the sons of the king; for Amnon alone is dead. For it has been determined by Absalom's own word from the day he violated Tamar his sister.
"And now let not my lord the king take to heart the report that all the sons of the king are dead — for Amnon alone is dead."
And Absalom fled. And the young man on watch lifted his eyes and looked, and there were many people coming along the road behind him, from the side of the mountain.
And Jonadab said to the king, "The sons of the king have come. It has happened just as your servant said."
And when he had finished speaking, the sons of the king came, and they lifted up their voice and wept. And the king also, and all his servants, wept very bitterly.
And Absalom fled and went to Talmai son of Ammihud, king of Geshur. And David mourned for his son every day.
And Absalom fled and went to Geshur, and he was there three years.
And King David ceased from going out against Absalom, for he was comforted concerning Amnon, that he was dead.

2 samuel_14.t: And Joab son of Zeruiah knew that the king's heart was toward Absalom.

And Joab sent to Tekoa and brought from there a wise woman, and he said to her, "Play the mourner. Put on mourning garments, do not anoint yourself with oil, and be like a woman who has been mourning many days for a dead man.
"And you shall go to the king and speak to him in this way." And Joab put the words in her mouth.
And the woman of Tekoa spoke to the king, and she fell on her face to the ground and bowed down, and she said, "Help, O king!"
And the king said to her, "What is your trouble?" And she said, "Truly I am a widow, and my husband is dead.
"And your maidservant had two sons, and the two of them struggled together in the field, and there was no one to part them; and the one struck the other and killed him.

"And now the whole clan has risen against your maidservant, and they say, 'Give up the one who struck down his brother, and we will put him to death for the life of his brother whom he killed, and we will destroy the heir also' — and so they would quench my coal that is left, leaving my husband neither name nor remnant on the face of the ground."
And the king said to the woman, "Go to your house, and I will give orders concerning you."
And the woman of Tekoa said to the king, "On me, my lord the king, be the iniquity, and on my father's house; and let the king and his throne be innocent."
And the king said, "Whoever speaks to you, bring him to me, and he will not touch you again."

And she said, "Let the king remember the LORD your God, that the avenger of blood may not multiply destruction, and that they may not destroy my son." And he said, "As the LORD lives, not one hair of your son shall fall to the ground."
And the woman said, "Let your maidservant speak a word to my lord the king." And he said, "Speak."
And the woman said, "Then why have you planned such a thing against the people of God? For in speaking this word the king convicts himself, in that the king does not bring back his own banished one.

"For we shall surely die, and we are like water spilt on the ground, which cannot be gathered up. And God does not take away a life, but he devises plans so that the banished one may not remain banished from him.

"And now, that I have come to speak this word to the king my lord is because the people made me afraid. And your maidservant said, 'Let me speak to the king; perhaps the king will do what his servant asks.
"'For the king will hear, and deliver his servant from the hand of the man who would destroy both me and my son together from the inheritance of God.'
"And your maidservant said, 'Let the word of my lord the king bring rest, for my lord the king is like the angel of God, to discern good and bad.' And may the LORD your God be with you."
And the king answered and said to the woman, "Do not hide from me the thing I am about to ask you." And the woman said, "Let my lord the king speak."

And the king said, "Is the hand of Joab with you in all this?" And the woman answered, "As your being lives, my lord the king, there is no turning to right or left from anything my lord the king has said. It was your servant Joab who commanded me, and he put all these words in the mouth of your maidservant.
"It was to change the face of the matter that your servant Joab did this thing. And my lord is wise, with the wisdom of the angel of God, to know all that is in the land."
And the king said to Joab, "See now, I have done this thing. Go, bring back the young man Absalom."

And Joab fell on his face to the ground and bowed down and blessed the king, and Joab said, "Today your servant knows that I have found favour in your eyes, my lord the king, in that the king has done what his servant asked."
So Joab rose and went to Geshur and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.
But the king said, "Let him turn to his own house; he shall not see my face." So Absalom turned to his own house, and he did not see the face of the king.
Now in all Israel there was no man so handsome as Absalom, so greatly to be praised: from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.

And when he shaved his head — for it was at the end of every year that he would shave it, because it was heavy on him, and so he shaved it — he would weigh the hair of his head: two hundred shekels by the king's weight.
And three sons were born to Absalom, and one daughter, whose name was Tamar. She was a beautiful woman.
And Absalom lived in Jerusalem two full years, and he did not see the face of the king.
And Absalom sent to Joab, to send him to the king, but Joab was not willing to come to him. And he sent again a second time, but he was not willing to come.
So he said to his servants, "See, Joab's field is next to mine, and he has barley there. Go and set it on fire." And Absalom's servants set the field on fire.
Then Joab rose and came to Absalom at his house and said to him, "Why have your servants set my field on fire?"

And Absalom said to Joab, "I sent to you, saying, 'Come here, so that I may send you to the king to say: Why have I come from Geshur? It would be better for me to be still there.' Now let me see the face of the king; and if there is iniquity in me, let him put me to death."
So Joab came to the king and told him. And he summoned Absalom, and he came to the king and bowed down to him on his face to the ground before the king; and the king kissed Absalom.

2 samuel_15.t: After this Absalom acquired for himself a chariot and horses, and fifty men to run before him.

And Absalom would rise early and stand beside the road to the gate. And whenever anyone had a dispute to bring before the king for judgement, Absalom would call to him and say, "What city are you from?" And he would say, "Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel."
And Absalom would say to him, "See, your case is good and right, but there is no one appointed by the king to hear you."
And Absalom would say, "If only I were made a judge in the land! Then everyone who had a case or a claim could come to me, and I would give him justice."
And whenever anyone drew near to bow down to him, he would put out his hand, take hold of him and kiss him.
And Absalom did this to all Israel who came to the king for judgement. And Absalom stole the heart of the men of Israel.
And at the end of forty years Absalom said to the king, "Let me go and pay my vow that I vowed to the LORD in Hebron.
"For your servant vowed a vow while I was living at Geshur in Aram, saying, 'If the LORD will surely bring me back to Jerusalem, then I will serve the LORD.'"
And the king said to him, "Go in peace." So he rose and went to Hebron.
But Absalom sent scouts through all the tribes of Israel, saying, "When you hear the sound of the horn, then say, 'Absalom has become king in Hebron.'"
And two hundred men went with Absalom from Jerusalem. They had been invited and went in their innocence, and they knew nothing at all.

And Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David's counsellor, from his city, from Giloh, while he was offering the sacrifices. And the conspiracy grew strong, and the people with Absalom kept increasing.
And a messenger came to David and said, "The heart of the men of Israel has gone after Absalom."

And David said to all his servants who were with him in Jerusalem, "Rise and let us flee, for there will be no escape for us from Absalom. Hurry and go, lest he move quickly and overtake us and bring disaster down upon us and strike the city with the edge of the sword."
And the king's servants said to the king, "Whatever my lord the king chooses — your servants are here."
And the king went out, with all his household following on foot; and the king left ten women, concubines, to keep the house.
And the king went out, with all the people following on foot, and they halted at the last house.

And all his servants were passing by at his side, and all the Kerethites and all the Pelethites; and all the Gittites, six hundred men who had come in his train from Gath, were passing on before the king.
And the king said to Ittai the Gittite, "Why should you also go with us? Go back and stay with the king, for you are a foreigner and also an exile from your own place.
"You came only yesterday; and today should I make you wander about with us, when I am going wherever I go? Go back, and take your brothers back with you. Loyalty and faithfulness be with you."
And Ittai answered the king, "As the LORD lives and as my lord the king lives, in whatever place my lord the king is — whether for death or for life — there your servant will be."
And David said to Ittai, "Go on, pass over." So Ittai the Gittite passed on, and all his men and all the little ones with him.
And all the land wept aloud as all the people passed by; and the king crossed the Wadi Kidron, and all the people passed on toward the way of the wilderness.

And there was Zadok also, and all the Levites with him, carrying the ark of the covenant of God; and they set down the ark of God, and Abiathar went up, until all the people had finished passing out of the city.
And the king said to Zadok, "Take the ark of God back to the city. If I find favour in the eyes of the LORD, he will bring me back and let me see it and its dwelling place.
"And if he says, 'I have no delight in you' — here I am; let him do to me as seems good in his eyes."
And the king said to Zadok the priest, "Are you not a seer? Return to the city in peace, with Ahimaaz your son and Jonathan son of Abiathar, your two sons.
"See, I will wait at the desert plains of the wilderness until word comes from you to tell me."
So Zadok and Abiathar took the ark of God back to Jerusalem, and they remained there.
And David went up the ascent of the olive trees, weeping as he went, his head covered and walking barefoot. And all the people with him covered their heads, and they went up, weeping as they went.
And David was told, "Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom." And David said, "Turn the counsel of Ahithophel to foolishness, LORD."
And when David came to the summit, where he would bow down to God, Hushai the Arkite came to meet him, his tunic torn and earth on his head.
And David said to him, "If you go over with me, you will be a burden to me.

"But if you return to the city and say to Absalom, 'I am your servant, O king; I was your father's servant in time past, and now I am your servant' — then you will frustrate the counsel of Ahithophel for me.
"And are not Zadok and Abiathar the priests there with you? Every word you hear from the king's house you shall tell to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.
"Their two sons are there with them, Ahimaaz for Zadok and Jonathan for Abiathar, and by their hand you shall send me every word that you hear."
So Hushai, David's friend, came to the city; and Absalom was entering Jerusalem.

2 samuel_16.t: When David had passed on a little beyond the summit, there was Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth to meet him, with a pair of saddled donkeys, and on them two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred bunches of raisins, a hundred summer fruits and a skin of wine.

And the king said to Ziba, "What are these of yours for?" And Ziba said, "The donkeys are for the king's household to ride, the bread and the summer fruit are for the young men to eat, and the wine is for the weary in the wilderness to drink."
And the king said, "And where is your master's son?" And Ziba said to the king, "He is staying in Jerusalem, for he said, 'Today the house of Israel will restore to me the kingdom of my father.'"
And the king said to Ziba, "All that belonged to Mephibosheth is yours." And Ziba said, "I bow down. May I find favour in your eyes, my lord the king."
And King David came as far as Bahurim, and there a man was coming out from the clan of the house of Saul whose name was Shimei son of Gera; he came out cursing as he came.
And he threw stones at David and at all the servants of King David — and all the people and all the mighty men were on his right and on his left.
And this is what Shimei said as he cursed: "Get out, get out, man of blood, worthless man!

"The LORD has brought back upon you all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose place you have reigned; and the LORD has given the kingship into the hand of Absalom your son. And here you are, caught in your own calamity, for you are a man of blood."
And Abishai son of Zeruiah said to the king, "Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Let me go over and take off his head."
And the king said, "What have I to do with you, sons of Zeruiah? Let him curse; for the LORD has said to him, 'Curse David.' And who shall say, 'Why have you done so?'"

And David said to Abishai and to all his servants, "My own son, who came out from my own body, is seeking my life; how much more now this Benjaminite! Leave him alone and let him curse, for the LORD has spoken to him.
"Perhaps the LORD will look upon my eye, and the LORD will repay me with good in place of his cursing this day."
And David and his men went on along the road, while Shimei went along the side of the mountain opposite him, cursing as he went; and he threw stones opposite him and flung dust.
And the king came, and all the people with him, exhausted; and he refreshed himself there.
And Absalom and all the people, the men of Israel, came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him.
And when Hushai the Arkite, David's friend, came to Absalom, Hushai said to Absalom, "Long live the king! Long live the king!"
And Absalom said to Hushai, "Is this your loyalty to your friend? Why did you not go with your friend?"
And Hushai said to Absalom, "No; the one whom the LORD and this people and all the men of Israel have chosen — his I will be, and with him I will remain.
"And a second thing: whom should I serve? Should it not be his son? As I served in your father's presence, so I will be in yours."
And Absalom said to Ahithophel, "Give your counsel: what shall we do?"

And Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Go in to your father's concubines, whom he left to keep the house; and all Israel will hear that you have made yourself odious to your father, and the hands of all who are with you will be strengthened."
So they pitched a tent for Absalom on the roof, and Absalom went in to his father's concubines before the eyes of all Israel.
Now the counsel of Ahithophel that he gave in those days was as when a man enquires of the word of God: so was all the counsel of Ahithophel, both to David and to Absalom.

2 samuel_17.t: And Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Let me choose twelve thousand men, and let me set out and pursue David tonight.
"And I will come upon him while he is weary and his hands are slack, and I will terrify him, and all the people with him will flee; and I will strike down the king alone.
"And I will bring all the people back to you. When all return — it is only the one man you are seeking — all the people will be at peace."
And the word seemed right to Absalom and to all the elders of Israel.
But Absalom said, "Call Hushai the Arkite also, and let us hear what he too has to say."
And Hushai came to Absalom, and Absalom said to him, "This is what Ahithophel has spoken. Shall we do as he says? If not, you speak."
And Hushai said to Absalom, "The counsel Ahithophel has given is not good this time."

And Hushai said, "You know your father and his men — that they are mighty men, and they are enraged, like a bear robbed of her cubs in the open country. And your father is a man of war, and he will not spend the night with the people.

"See, by now he is hidden in one of the ravines or in some other place; and when some of them fall at the first onset, whoever hears of it will say, 'There has been a slaughter among the people who follow Absalom.'
"And even the valiant man, whose heart is like the heart of a lion, will utterly melt; for all Israel knows that your father is a mighty man, and that those with him are valiant men.
"But I counsel that all Israel be gathered to you, from Dan to Beersheba, as numerous as the sand by the sea, and that you yourself go into the battle.
"And we will come upon him in whatever place he is found, and we will settle on him as the dew falls on the ground; and not one of him or of all the men with him will be left.
"And if he withdraws into a city, then all Israel will bring ropes to that city, and we will drag it down to the wadi until not even a pebble is found there."

And Absalom and all the men of Israel said, "The counsel of Hushai the Arkite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel." For the LORD had ordained to frustrate the good counsel of Ahithophel, in order that the LORD might bring disaster upon Absalom.
And Hushai said to Zadok and Abiathar the priests, "This and this Ahithophel counselled Absalom and the elders of Israel, and this and this I have counselled.
"And now send quickly and tell David, 'Do not spend the night at the desert plains of the wilderness, but be sure to cross over, or the king will be swallowed up, and all the people with him.'"
Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz were staying at En-rogel, and a maidservant would go and tell them, and they would go and tell King David; for they could not risk being seen entering the city.
But a young man saw them and told Absalom. So the two of them went quickly and came to the house of a man in Bahurim, who had a well in his courtyard, and they went down into it.
And the woman took a covering and spread it over the mouth of the well and spread out grain on it; and nothing was known.

And Absalom's servants came to the woman at the house and said, "Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?" And the woman said to them, "They have crossed the brook of water." And they searched and did not find them, and they returned to Jerusalem.
And after they had gone, the two came up out of the well and went and told King David. They said to David, "Rise and cross the water quickly, for this is what Ahithophel has counselled against you."
So David rose, with all the people who were with him, and they crossed the Jordan. By the light of morning not one was missing who had not crossed the Jordan.

And when Ahithophel saw that his counsel had not been carried out, he saddled his donkey and rose and went to his house, to his city, and gave orders concerning his household, and hanged himself; and he died and was buried in the tomb of his father.
And David had come to Mahanaim, while Absalom crossed the Jordan, he and all the men of Israel with him.
And Absalom had appointed Amasa over the army in place of Joab. Amasa was the son of a man named Jether the Israelite, who had gone in to Abigail daughter of Nahash, sister of Zeruiah, Joab's mother.
And Israel and Absalom encamped in the land of Gilead.
And when David came to Mahanaim, Shobi son of Nahash from Rabbah of the Ammonites, and Machir son of Ammiel from Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim
brought bedding, basins and earthenware vessels, and wheat, barley, flour and roasted grain, and beans, lentils and roasted grain,
and honey, curds, sheep and cheese from the herd. They brought these to David and to the people with him, to eat; for they said, "The people are hungry and weary and thirsty in the wilderness."

2 samuel_18.t: And David mustered the people who were with him and set over them commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds.

And David sent out the people, a third under Joab, a third under Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, and a third under Ittai the Gittite. And the king said to the people, "I will certainly go out with you myself."

But the people said, "You shall not go out. For if we flee, they will not care about us; and if half of us die, they will not care about us. But you are worth ten thousand of us. So it is better that you be ready to help us from the city."
And the king said to them, "Whatever seems good to you I will do." And the king stood beside the gate, and all the people went out by hundreds and by thousands.

And the king commanded Joab and Abishai and Ittai, "Deal gently for my sake with the young man, with Absalom." And all the people heard when the king gave all the commanders this command concerning Absalom.
And the people went out into the open country to meet Israel, and the battle was in the forest of Ephraim.
And the people of Israel were defeated there before the servants of David, and the slaughter there was great on that day: twenty thousand.
And the battle there spread over the face of all the land, and the forest consumed more of the people that day than the sword consumed.

And Absalom happened to meet the servants of David. Absalom was riding on his mule, and the mule went under the thick branches of the great oak, and his head caught fast in the oak, and he was left hanging between the heavens and the earth, and the mule that was under him passed on.
And one man saw it and told Joab, "I saw Absalom hanging in the oak."
And Joab said to the man who told him, "You saw him! Why then did you not strike him to the ground there? I would have been bound to give you ten pieces of silver and a belt."

And the man said to Joab, "Even if I were weighing out a thousand pieces of silver in my hands, I would not put out my hand against the son of the king; for in our hearing the king commanded you and Abishai and Ittai, saying, 'Whoever you are, protect the young man Absalom.'
"Or if I had dealt falsely at the cost of my own life — and nothing is hidden from the king — then you yourself would have stood aloof."
And Joab said, "I will not waste time with you like this." And he took three spears in his hand and thrust them into the heart of Absalom, while he was still alive in the heart of the oak.
And ten young men, Joab's armour-bearers, surrounded him and struck Absalom and killed him.
And Joab blew the horn, and the people turned back from pursuing Israel, for Joab restrained the people.
And they took Absalom and threw him into the great pit in the forest, and they raised over him a very great heap of stones. And all Israel fled, each to his tents.

Now Absalom, in his lifetime, had taken and set up for himself the pillar that is in the King's Valley, for he said, "I have no son to keep my name in remembrance." And he called the pillar by his own name, and it is called Absalom's Monument to this day.
And Ahimaaz son of Zadok said, "Let me run and carry the news to the king, that the LORD has vindicated him from the hand of his enemies."
And Joab said to him, "You are not the man to carry news this day. You may carry news on another day, but this day you shall not carry news, because the king's son is dead."
And Joab said to the Cushite, "Go, tell the king what you have seen." And the Cushite bowed down to Joab and ran.
And Ahimaaz son of Zadok said again to Joab, "Come what may, let me also run after the Cushite." And Joab said, "Why would you run, my son, when you have no news that will bring you a reward?"
"Come what may, I will run." And he said to him, "Run." So Ahimaaz ran by the way of the plain and outran the Cushite.
Now David was sitting between the two gates. And the watchman went up to the roof of the gate, on the wall, and lifted up his eyes and looked, and there was a man running alone.
And the watchman called out and told the king. And the king said, "If he is alone, there is news in his mouth." And he came on, drawing steadily nearer.
And the watchman saw another man running, and the watchman called to the gatekeeper, "There is another man running alone." And the king said, "This one also is bearing news."
And the watchman said, "I see that the running of the first is like the running of Ahimaaz son of Zadok." And the king said, "He is a good man, and he comes with good news."

And Ahimaaz called out and said to the king, "All is well!" And he bowed down to the king with his face to the ground and said, "Blessed be the LORD your God, who has delivered up the men who lifted their hand against my lord the king."
And the king said, "Is it well with the young man, with Absalom?" And Ahimaaz said, "I saw a great commotion when the king's servant Joab sent your servant, but I do not know what it was."
And the king said, "Turn aside and stand here." And he turned aside and stood.
And there the Cushite came, and the Cushite said, "Let my lord the king receive the news: the LORD has vindicated you this day from the hand of all who rose up against you."

And the king said to the Cushite, "Is it well with the young man, with Absalom?" And the Cushite said, "May the enemies of my lord the king, and all who have risen against you for harm, be like the young man."

And the king was shaken, and he went up to the upper room over the gate and wept. And this is what he said as he went: "My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! If only I had died, I in your place! Absalom, my son, my son!"

2 samuel_19.t: And it was told to Joab, "The king is weeping and mourning over Absalom."
And the victory that day was turned to mourning for all the people, for the people heard on that day that the king was grieved over his son.
And the people stole into the city that day, as people steal in who are ashamed when they flee in battle.
And the king covered his face, and the king cried out with a loud voice, "My son Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!"

And Joab came to the king in the house and said, "You have put to shame today the faces of all your servants, who this day saved your life, and the lives of your sons and your daughters, and the lives of your wives and the lives of your concubines,

"by loving those who hate you and hating those who love you. For you have made plain today that commanders and servants mean nothing to you; for I know today that if Absalom were alive and all of us today were dead, then it would be right in your eyes.

"And now rise, go out and speak to the heart of your servants. For I swear by the LORD that if you do not go out, not a man will stay with you tonight; and this will be worse for you than all the harm that has come upon you from your youth until now."
So the king rose and sat in the gate. And they told all the people, "The king is sitting in the gate." And all the people came before the king. Now Israel had fled, each to his tents.

And all the people were quarrelling throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, "The king delivered us from the hand of our enemies, and he rescued us from the hand of the Philistines; and now he has fled from the land because of Absalom.
"And Absalom, whom we anointed over us, has died in the battle. So why are you silent about bringing back the king?"

And King David sent to Zadok and Abiathar the priests, saying, "Speak to the elders of Judah: 'Why should you be the last to bring the king back to his house?' " — and the word of all Israel had come to the king, to his house.
"You are my brothers, my bone and my flesh. Why then should you be the last to bring back the king?"
"And to Amasa you shall say, 'Are you not my bone and my flesh? So may God do to me and so may he add, if you are not commander of the army before me from now on, in place of Joab.'"
And he turned the heart of all the men of Judah as one man, and they sent word to the king, "Return, you and all your servants."
So the king returned and came to the Jordan; and Judah came to Gilgal to go to meet the king and bring the king over the Jordan.
And Shimei son of Gera, the Benjaminite from Bahurim, hurried down with the men of Judah to meet King David.
And a thousand men of Benjamin were with him; and Ziba, the servant of the house of Saul, with his fifteen sons and his twenty servants. And they rushed down to the Jordan before the king.
And the ferry crossed over to bring over the king's household and to do what was good in his eyes. And Shimei son of Gera fell down before the king as he was crossing the Jordan,

and he said to the king, "Let my lord not reckon guilt to me, and do not remember what your servant did perversely on the day my lord the king went out from Jerusalem — do not let the king take it to heart.
"For your servant knows that I have sinned; and I have come today, the first of all the house of Joseph, to come down to meet my lord the king."
But Abishai son of Zeruiah said, "Shall Shimei not be put to death for this, because he cursed the LORD's anointed?"

And David said, "What have I to do with you, sons of Zeruiah, that you should become an opponent to me today? Shall anyone be put to death in Israel today? Do I not know that today I am king over Israel?"
And the king said to Shimei, "You shall not die." And the king swore it to him.

And Mephibosheth son of Saul came down to meet the king. He had not cared for his feet nor trimmed his moustache nor washed his clothes, from the day the king left until the day he came back in peace.
And when he came to Jerusalem to meet the king, the king said to him, "Why did you not go with me, Mephibosheth?"
And he said, "My lord the king, my servant deceived me. For your servant said, 'Let me saddle the donkey for myself, that I may ride on it and go with the king' — for your servant is lame.
"And he has slandered your servant to my lord the king. But my lord the king is like the angel of God; so do what is good in your eyes.

"For all my father's house were nothing but men doomed to death before my lord the king; yet you set your servant among those who eat at your table. What claim have I still, to cry out further to the king?"
And the king said to him, "Why speak any more of your affairs? I have said it: you and Ziba shall divide the land."
And Mephibosheth said to the king, "Let him take it all, now that my lord the king has come home in peace."
And Barzillai the Gileadite had come down from Rogelim, and he crossed the Jordan with the king to see him off at the Jordan.
Now Barzillai was very old, eighty years of age, and he had supplied the king while he stayed at Mahanaim, for he was a very great man.
And the king said to Barzillai, "Cross over with me, and I will provide for you at my side in Jerusalem."
And Barzillai said to the king, "How many are the days of the years of my life, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem?

"I am eighty years old today. Can I discern between good and bad? Can your servant taste what I eat or what I drink? Can I still hear the voice of singing men and singing women? Why then should your servant be a further burden to my lord the king?
"Your servant would go only a little way over the Jordan with the king. Why should the king reward me with such a reward?

"Let your servant go back and die in his own city, near the grave of my father and my mother. But here is your servant Kimham: let him cross over with my lord the king, and do for him what is good in your eyes."
And the king said, "Kimham shall cross over with me, and I will do for him what is good in your eyes; and whatever you choose of me I will do for you."
And all the people crossed the Jordan, and the king crossed over. And the king kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and Barzillai returned to his own place.
And the king crossed over to Gilgal, and Kimham crossed over with him. And all the people of Judah brought the king over, and half the people of Israel also.

And all the men of Israel came to the king and said to the king, "Why have our brothers the men of Judah stolen you away, and brought the king and his household over the Jordan, and all David's men with him?"

And all the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, "Because the king is a near relative of ours. And why should this anger you? Have we eaten anything at the king's expense, or has anything been taken for us?"

And the men of Israel answered the men of Judah, "We have ten shares in the king, and in David we have more than you. Why then have you treated us with contempt? Was not our word first, to bring back our king?" And the word of the men of Judah was harsher than the word of the men of Israel.

2 samuel_20.t: Now there a worthless man happened to be, whose name was Sheba son of Bichri, a Benjaminite. And he blew the horn and said, "We have no portion in David, and no inheritance in the son of Jesse. Each to his tents, O Israel!"
So all the men of Israel went up from following David and followed Sheba son of Bichri; but the men of Judah clung to their king from the Jordan to Jerusalem.

And David came to his house at Jerusalem, and the king took the ten women, concubines, whom he had left to keep the house, and put them in a house of confinement. He provided for them, but he did not go in to them. And they were shut up until the day of their death, in living widowhood.
And the king said to Amasa, "Summon the men of Judah to me within three days, and you yourself be here."
And Amasa went to summon Judah, but he delayed beyond the appointed time that had been set for him.
And David said to Abishai, "Now Sheba son of Bichri will do us more harm than Absalom did. Take your master's servants and pursue him, or he will find fortified cities for himself and escape us."
So Joab's men went out after him, with the Kerethites and the Pelethites and all the mighty men; and they went out from Jerusalem to pursue Sheba son of Bichri.

They were by the great stone that is in Gibeon when Amasa came before them. Joab was wearing his robe as his clothing, and over it a belt with a sword fastened at his waist in its sheath; and as he stepped forward, it fell out.
And Joab said to Amasa, "Is it well with you, my brother?" And Joab's right hand took hold of Amasa's beard to kiss him.

And Amasa did not take heed of the sword that was in Joab's hand, and Joab struck him with it in the belly and poured out his bowels on the ground; he did not strike him twice, and he died. And Joab and Abishai his brother pursued Sheba son of Bichri.
And a man stood over him, one of Joab's young men, and said, "Whoever favours Joab, and whoever is for David — follow Joab!"

And Amasa lay wallowing in his blood in the middle of the highway. And when the man saw that all the people were stopping, he moved Amasa from the highway into the field and threw a garment over him, since he saw that everyone who came upon him stopped.
When he had been removed from the highway, every man passed on after Joab to pursue Sheba son of Bichri.
And Sheba passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel and Beth-maacah and all the Berites; and they assembled and followed him too.

And they came and besieged him in Abel of Beth-maacah, and they threw up a siege mound against the city, and it stood against the rampart. And all the people with Joab were battering the wall to bring it down.
Then a wise woman called out from the city, "Listen! Listen! Say to Joab, 'Come near here, that I may speak with you.'"
And he came near to her, and the woman said, "Are you Joab?" And he said, "I am." And she said to him, "Listen to the words of your maidservant." And he said, "I am listening."
And she said, "In former times they used to say, 'Let them ask at Abel', and so the matter was settled.
"I am one of the peaceable and faithful of Israel. You are seeking to put to death a city that is a mother in Israel. Why will you swallow up the inheritance of the LORD?"
And Joab answered, "Far be it, far be it from me, that I should swallow up or destroy!

"That is not the matter. But a man from the hill country of Ephraim, whose name is Sheba son of Bichri, has lifted his hand against the king, against David. Give him up alone, and I will withdraw from the city." And the woman said to Joab, "His head will be thrown to you over the wall."

And the woman went to all the people in her wisdom, and they cut off the head of Sheba son of Bichri and threw it out to Joab. And he blew the horn, and they dispersed from the city, each to his tents. And Joab returned to Jerusalem, to the king.
Now Joab was over all the army of Israel; Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Kerethites and over the Pelethites;
Adoram was over the forced labour; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the recorder;
Sheva was secretary; Zadok and Abiathar were priests;
and Ira the Jairite also was priest to David.

2 samuel_21.t: And there was a famine in the days of David for three years, year after year, and David sought the face of the LORD. And the LORD said, "It is because of Saul and because of the house of blood, because he put the Gibeonites to death."

And the king summoned the Gibeonites and spoke to them — now the Gibeonites were not of the Israelites but of the remnant of the Amorites, and the Israelites had sworn an oath to them, and Saul had sought to strike them down in his zeal for the Israelites and Judah —
and David said to the Gibeonites, "What shall I do for you? And with what shall I make atonement, so that you may bless the inheritance of the LORD?"

And the Gibeonites said to him, "It is not a matter of silver and gold between us and Saul and his house, and it is not for us to put any man to death in Israel." And he said, "Whatever you say I will do for you."
And they said to the king, "The man who made an end of us and who planned against us that we should be destroyed from standing in all the territory of Israel —
"let seven men of his sons be given to us, and we will impale them before the LORD at Gibeah of Saul, the LORD's chosen." And the king said, "I will give them."
But the king spared Mephibosheth son of Jonathan son of Saul, because of the oath of the LORD that was between them, between David and Jonathan son of Saul.

And the king took the two sons of Rizpah daughter of Aiah, whom she had borne to Saul — Armoni and Mephibosheth — and the five sons of Michal daughter of Saul, whom she had borne to Adriel son of Barzillai the Meholathite,

and he gave them into the hand of the Gibeonites, and they impaled them on the mountain before the LORD. And the seven of them fell together; they were put to death in the days of harvest, in the first days, at the beginning of the barley harvest.

And Rizpah daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and spread it out for herself on the rock, from the beginning of harvest until water was poured out on them from the heavens. And she did not allow the birds of the heavens to rest on them by day, nor the beasts of the field by night.
And it was told to David what Rizpah daughter of Aiah, Saul's concubine, had done.

And David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the citizens of Jabesh Gilead, who had stolen them from the open square of Beth-shan, where the Philistines had hung them up on the day the Philistines struck down Saul at Gilboa.
And he brought up from there the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son, and they gathered the bones of those who had been impaled.

And they buried the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son in the land of Benjamin at Zela, in the tomb of Kish his father; and they did all that the king commanded. And after that God was entreated for the land.
And there was war again between the Philistines and Israel, and David went down with his servants and they fought the Philistines; and David grew weary.
And Ishbi-benob, who was among the descendants of the giant — the weight of his spear was three hundred shekels of bronze, and he was girded with a new sword — said he would strike David down.

But Abishai son of Zeruiah came to his help and struck the Philistine down and killed him. Then the men of David swore to him, "You shall not go out with us to battle any more, and you shall not quench the lamp of Israel."
After this there was war again at Gob with the Philistines. Then Sibbecai the Hushathite struck down Saph, who was among those born of the Raphah.
And there was war again at Gob with the Philistines, and Elhanan son of Jaare-oregim the Bethlehemite struck down Goliath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver's beam.

And there was war again at Gath, and there was a man of great stature, and the fingers of his hands and the toes of his feet were six and six, twenty-four in number; and he also was born to the Raphah.
And he taunted Israel, and Jonathan son of Shimei, David's brother, struck him down.
These four were born to the Raphah in Gath, and they fell by the hand of David and by the hand of his servants.

2 samuel_22.t: And David spoke to the LORD the words of this song on the day the LORD delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.
And he said: The LORD is my rock and my stronghold, and my deliverer, mine;
My God, my rock, in whom I take refuge, my shield and the horn of my salvation, my fastness and my place of escape, my saviour — from violence you save me.
The one to be praised — I call upon the LORD, and from my enemies I am saved.
For the breakers of death surrounded me, the torrents of worthlessness overwhelmed me;
the cords of Sheol surrounded me, the snares of death confronted me.
In my distress I called upon the LORD, and to my God I called; and he heard my voice from his temple, and my cry for help was in his ears.
Then the earth shook and quaked, the foundations of the heavens trembled and shook, because he was angry.
Smoke went up from his nostrils, and fire from his mouth consumed; coals burned from him.
And he stretched out the heavens and came down, and thick darkness was under his feet.
And he rode on a cherub and flew, and he appeared on the wings of the wind.
And he set darkness around him as shelters, a sieve of waters, dark clouds of the skies.
From the brightness before him coals of fire blazed.
The LORD thundered from heaven, and the Most High gave his voice.
And he sent out arrows and scattered them, lightning, and routed them.
And the channels of the sea appeared, the foundations of the world were uncovered, at the rebuke of the LORD, at the blast of the breath of his nostrils.
He reached down from on high, he took me, he drew me out of many waters.
He rescued me from my strong enemy, from those who hate me, for they were too strong for me.
They confronted me in the day of my calamity, but the LORD was a support to me.
And he brought me out to a broad place; he rescued me, for he delighted in me.
The LORD dealt with me according to my righteousness; according to the purity of my hands he repaid me.
For I have kept the ways of the LORD, and have not acted wickedly away from my God.
For all his judgements are before me, and from his statutes I do not turn aside.
And I was blameless toward him, and I kept myself from my iniquity.
And the LORD repaid me according to my righteousness, according to my purity before his eyes.
With the loyal you show yourself loyal, with the blameless warrior you show yourself blameless;
with the pure you show yourself pure, and with the crooked you show yourself twisted.
And an afflicted people you save, but your eyes are on the haughty — you bring them low.
For you are my lamp, LORD, and the LORD lightens my darkness.
For by you I can charge a raiding band, by my God I can leap a wall.
As for God — his way is blameless, the speech of the LORD is refined; he is a shield to all who take refuge in him.
For who is God apart from the LORD, and who is a Rock apart from our God?
God is my strong refuge, and he set my way free, blameless.
making my feet like the does', and on my high places he makes me stand.
training my hands for battle, so that my arms bend a bow of bronze.
And you gave me the shield of your salvation, and your answering makes me great.
You enlarge my step beneath me, and my ankles do not slip.
I pursued my enemies and destroyed them, and I did not turn back until they were finished.
And I finished them and shattered them, and they did not rise; they fell under my feet.
And you girded me with strength for battle; you made those who rose against me bow down beneath me.
And my enemies — you gave me their neck; those who hate me — I destroyed them.
They looked, and there was no deliverer; to the LORD, and he did not answer them.
And I beat them fine as the dust of the earth; like the mud of the streets I crushed them and stamped them out.
And you rescued me from the strifes of my people; you kept me as head of nations — a people I did not know serves me.
Foreigners cringe before me; at the hearing of the ear they obey me.
Foreigners wither, and they come girded out of their strongholds.
The LORD lives, and blessed be my Rock, and exalted be the God of the Rock of my salvation —
the God who gives me vengeance and brings peoples down beneath me,
and who brings me out from my enemies. And from those who rise against me you lift me up; from the man of violence you rescue me.
Therefore I will give you thanks, LORD, among the nations, and to your name I will make music —
a tower of salvation for his king, and showing steadfast love to his anointed, to David and to his offspring for ever.

2 samuel_23.t: And these are the last words of David: The declaration of David son of Jesse, and the declaration of the man raised on high, the anointed of the God of Jacob, and the pleasant one of the songs of Israel.
The spirit of the LORD has spoken by me, and his word is on my tongue.
The God of Israel said, to me the Rock of Israel spoke: One who rules over humankind, righteous, ruling in the fear of God —
and like the light of morning when the sun rises, a morning without clouds; through brightness after rain grass springs from the earth.
For is not my house so with God? For he has made with me a perpetual covenant, ordered in every part and kept. For all my salvation and every desire — will he not make it grow?
But the worthless — like thorns chased away are they all, for they cannot be taken by hand;
and the man who touches them arms himself with iron and the shaft of a spear; and with fire they are utterly burned where they lie.
These are the names of the mighty men who belonged to David: Josheb-basshebeth a Tahchemonite, chief of the three; he was Adino the Eznite, against eight hundred slain at one time.
And after him was Eleazar son of Dodo son of Ahohi, one of the three mighty men with David when they defied the Philistines who were gathered there for battle; and the men of Israel had withdrawn.

He rose and struck the Philistines until his hand was weary and his hand clung to the sword. And the LORD brought about a great deliverance that day, and the people returned after him only to strip the slain.
And after him was Shammah son of Agee the Hararite. The Philistines were gathered into a band, and there was a plot of field full of lentils, and the people fled before the Philistines.
But he took his stand in the middle of the plot and defended it, and struck the Philistines. And the LORD brought about a great deliverance.
And three of the thirty chiefs went down and came at harvest time to David, to the cave of Adullam; and a company of Philistines was encamped in the valley of Rephaim.
And David was then in the stronghold, and a Philistine garrison was then at Bethlehem.
And David craved and said, "Who will give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem, which is at the gate?"

And the three mighty men broke through the camp of the Philistines and drew water from the well of Bethlehem, which was at the gate, and carried it and brought it to David. But he was not willing to drink it, and he poured it out to the LORD.
And he said, "Far be it from me, LORD, that I should do this! Is it not the blood of the men who went at the risk of their lives?" And he would not drink it. These things the three mighty men did.
And Abishai the brother of Joab, son of Zeruiah — he was chief of the three, and he wielded his spear against three hundred slain; and he had a name among the three.
Was he not the most honoured of the three? He became their commander, but he did not attain to the three.
And Benaiah son of Jehoiada was the son of a valiant man, great in deeds, from Kabzeel. He struck down the two ariels of Moab; and he went down and struck down a lion inside a pit on a snowy day.

And he struck down an Egyptian, an imposing man; the Egyptian had a spear in his hand, but Benaiah went down to him with a staff, seized the spear from the Egyptian's hand and killed him with his own spear.
These things Benaiah son of Jehoiada did, and he had a name among the three mighty men.
He was honoured above the thirty, but he did not attain to the three. And David set him over his bodyguard.
Asahel the brother of Joab was among the thirty; Elhanan son of Dodo of Bethlehem;
Shammah the Harodite, Elika the Harodite;
Helez the Paltite, Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite;
Abiezer the Anathothite, Mebunnai the Hushathite;
Zalmon the Ahohite, Maharai the Netophathite;
Heleb son of Baanah the Netophathite, Ittai son of Ribai from Gibeah of the Benjaminites;
Benaiah the Pirathonite, Hiddai from the wadis of Gaash;
Abi-albon the Arbathite, Azmaveth the Barhumite;
Eliahba the Shaalbonite, the sons of Jashen, Jonathan,
Shammah the Hararite, Ahiam son of Sharar the Ararite;
Eliphelet son of Ahasbai son of the Maacathite, Eliam son of Ahithophel the Gilonite;
Hezrai the Carmelite, Paarai the Arbite;
Igal son of Nathan from Zobah, Bani the Gadite;
Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Beerothite, the armour-bearer of Joab son of Zeruiah;
Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,
Uriah the Hittite — thirty-seven in all.

2 samuel_24.t: And the anger of the LORD burned against Israel again, and he incited David against them, saying, "Go, count Israel and Judah."
And the king said to Joab the commander of the army who was with him, "Go through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, and enrol the people, so that I may know the number of the people."

And Joab said to the king, "May the LORD your God add to the people a hundred times as many as they are, while the eyes of my lord the king see it. But why does my lord the king delight in this thing?"
But the word of the king prevailed over Joab and over the commanders of the army, and Joab and the commanders of the army went out from before the king to enrol the people, Israel.
And they crossed the Jordan and encamped at Aroer, south of the city that is in the middle of the wadi of Gad, and went on to Jazer.
And they came to Gilead, and to the land of Tahtim-hodshi; and they came to Dan-jaan and round to Sidon.
And they came to the fortress of Tyre and all the cities of the Hivites and the Canaanites; and they went out to the Negev of Judah, to Beersheba.
And they went about through all the land, and at the end of nine months and twenty days they came to Jerusalem.
And Joab gave the number of the muster of the people to the king. Israel numbered eight hundred thousand valiant men who drew the sword, and the men of Judah five hundred thousand men.

And David's heart struck him after he had counted the people. And David said to the LORD, "I have sinned greatly in what I have done. And now, LORD, take away the iniquity of your servant, for I have acted very foolishly."
And David rose in the morning, and the word of the LORD came to Gad the prophet, David's seer, saying,
"Go and speak to David: Thus says the LORD: Three things I am laying upon you. Choose one of them for yourself, and I will do it to you."

And Gad came to David and told him and said to him, "Shall seven years of famine come upon you in your land? Or three months of fleeing before your foes while they pursue you? Or three days of pestilence in your land? Now consider and see what answer I am to bring back to the one who sent me."
And David said to Gad, "I am in great distress. Let us fall into the hand of the LORD, for his compassions are many; but into the hand of human beings let me not fall."
And the LORD sent a pestilence on Israel from the morning until the appointed time, and of the people from Dan to Beersheba seventy thousand men died.

And the angel stretched out his hand toward Jerusalem to destroy it, but the LORD relented concerning the harm and said to the angel who was destroying among the people, "Enough! Now let your hand drop." And the angel of the LORD was by the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

And David said to the LORD when he saw the angel who was striking the people, "I have sinned and I have done wrong; but these sheep — what have they done? Let your hand be against me and against my father's house."
And Gad came to David that day and said to him, "Go up, raise an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite."
And David went up according to the word of Gad, just as the LORD had commanded.
And Araunah looked down and saw the king and his servants coming over toward him, and Araunah went out and bowed down to the king with his face to the ground.

And Araunah said, "Why has my lord the king come to his servant?" And David said, "To buy the threshing floor from you, to build an altar to the LORD, so that the plague may be held back from the people."
And Araunah said to David, "Let my lord the king take and offer up what seems good to him. Here are the oxen for the burnt offering, and the threshing sledges and the oxen's gear for the wood."
"All this Araunah gives to the king, O king." And Araunah said to the king, "May the LORD your God accept you favourably."

But the king said to Araunah, "No — I will certainly buy it from you for a price. I will not offer up to the LORD my God burnt offerings that cost me nothing." And David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
And David built there an altar to the LORD and offered up burnt offerings and peace offerings. And the LORD was entreated for the land, and the plague was held back from Israel.

amos_1.t: The words of Amos, who was among the sheep-breeders of Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.
And he said: The LORD roars from Zion, and from Jerusalem he utters his voice; the pastures of the shepherds dry up, and the top of Carmel withers.
Thus says the LORD: For three transgressions of Damascus, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they threshed Gilead with threshing sledges of iron.
And I will send fire into the house of Hazael, and it will consume the fortresses of Ben Hadad.

And I will break the bar of Damascus, and I will cut off the inhabitant from the Valley of Aven, and the holder of a sceptre from Beth Eden, and the people of Aram will go into exile to Kir, says the LORD.
Thus says the LORD: For three transgressions of Gaza, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they carried into exile a complete exile, to deliver them up to Edom.
And I will send fire into the wall of Gaza, and it will consume her fortresses.
And I will cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod, and the holder of a sceptre from Ashkelon, and I will turn my hand against Ekron, and the remnant of the Philistines will perish, says Lord GOD.
Thus says the LORD: For three transgressions of Tyre, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they delivered up a complete exile to Edom and did not remember the covenant of brothers.
And I will send fire into the wall of Tyre, and it will consume her fortresses.

Thus says the LORD: For three transgressions of Edom, and for four, I will not turn it back, because he pursued his brother with the sword and ruined his compassion, and his anger tore for ever, and he kept his fury perpetually.
And I will send fire into Teman, and it will consume the fortresses of Bozrah.
Thus says the LORD: For three transgressions of the people of Ammon, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead so as to enlarge their territory.
And I will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah, and it will consume her fortresses, with a shout of alarm on the day of battle, with a storm on the day of the whirlwind.
And their king will go into exile, he and his officials together, says the LORD.

amos_2.t: Thus says the LORD: For three transgressions of Moab, and for four, I will not turn it back, because he burned the bones of the king of Edom into lime.
And I will send fire into Moab, and it will consume the fortresses of Kerioth, and Moab will die in an uproar, with a shout of alarm, with the sound of a horn.
And I will cut off the judge from her midst, and I will kill all her officials with him, says the LORD.

Thus says the LORD: For three transgressions of Judah, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they rejected the law of the LORD and did not keep his statutes, and their lies led them astray, the lies their fathers walked after.
And I will send fire into Judah, and it will consume the fortresses of Jerusalem.
Thus says the LORD: For three transgressions of Israel, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they sold the righteous for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals.
They trample the head of the poor into the dust of the earth and turn aside the way of the humble; a man and his father go to the same young woman, so profaning my holy name.
They stretch out beside every altar on garments taken in pledge, and in the house of their gods they drink the wine of those who have been fined.
And I myself destroyed the Amorite before them, whose height was like the height of the cedars and who was strong as the oaks; and I destroyed his fruit above and his roots beneath.
And I myself brought you up from the land of Egypt and led you in the wilderness forty years, to take possession of the land of the Amorite.
And I raised up some of your sons as prophets and some of your young men as nazirites. Is this not so, people of Israel? declares the LORD.
But you made the nazirites drink wine, and you commanded the prophets, saying, "You shall not prophesy."
Look, I am about to press you in your place, as a cart full of cut grain presses.
Escape will be lost to the swift, and the strong will not hold his power firm, and the mighty will not save his own being.
The one who handles the bow will not stand, and the swift of foot will not save himself, and the rider of the horse will not save his own being.
And the one strong of heart among the warriors will flee naked on that day, declares the LORD.

amos_3.t: Hear this word that the LORD has spoken against you, people of Israel, against the whole clan that I brought up from the land of Egypt:
You only have I known of all the clans of the earth; therefore I will visit upon you all your iniquities.
Do two walk together unless they have agreed to meet?
Does a lion roar in the forest when it has no prey? Does a young lion utter his voice from his den unless he has caught something?
Does a bird fall into a trap on the ground when there is no snare set for it? Does a trap spring up from the ground and catch nothing at all?
If a horn is blown in a city, do the people not tremble? If calamity comes on a city, has the LORD not done it?
For Lord GOD does not do a thing unless he has revealed his secret counsel to his servants the prophets.
A lion has roared — who will not fear? Lord GOD has spoken — who will not prophesy?

Proclaim to the fortresses in Ashdod and to the fortresses in the land of Egypt, and say: "Gather on the mountains of Samaria and see the great disturbances within her, and the acts of oppression in her midst."
"They do not know how to do what is straight," declares the LORD — those who store up violence and devastation in their fortresses.
Therefore thus says Lord GOD: An adversary — and all around the land! He will bring your strength down from you, and your fortresses will be plundered.

Thus says the LORD: As a shepherd rescues from the mouth of the lion two shin-bones or a piece of an ear, so will the people of Israel be rescued — those who sit in Samaria with the corner of a bed and the silk of a couch.
Hear, and warn the house of Jacob, declares Lord GOD, the God of hosts.
For on the day I visit the transgressions of Israel upon him, I will also visit upon the altars of Bethel; the horns of the altar will be cut off and fall to the ground.
And I will strike the winter house along with the summer house; the houses of ivory will perish, and many houses will come to an end, declares the LORD.

amos_4.t: Hear this word, you cows of Bashan on the mountain of Samaria, who oppress the poor and crush the needy, who say to their masters, "Bring, and let us drink!"
Lord GOD has sworn by his holiness: Look, days are coming upon you when you will be carried off with hooks, and your posterity with fish-hooks.
And you will go out through the breaches, each one straight ahead, and you will be flung out to Harmon, declares the LORD.
Come to Bethel — and transgress! To Gilgal — and transgress all the more! Bring your sacrifices in the morning, your tithes on the third day.
Burn as smoke a thanksgiving offering from what is leavened, and proclaim freewill offerings — make them heard! For this is what you love, people of Israel, declares Lord GOD.
And I myself gave you cleanness of teeth in all your cities and lack of bread in all your places, and yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD.
