And I myself withheld the rain from you while there were still three months to the harvest. I sent rain on one city and on another city I sent no rain; one plot of ground was rained on, and the plot on which it did not rain dried up.
Two or three cities staggered to one city to drink water, and they were not satisfied, and yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD.
I struck you with blight and with mildew. The locust ate the multitude of your gardens and your vineyards, your fig trees and your olive trees, and yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD.

I sent pestilence among you in the manner of Egypt. I killed your young men with the sword, along with the capture of your horses, and I made the stench of your camp rise into your nostrils, and yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD.
I overthrew among you as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you were like a brand snatched from the burning, and yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD.
Therefore this is what I will do to you, Israel. Because I will do this to you, prepare to meet your God, Israel!

For here is the one who forms the mountains and creates the wind, and tells humankind what his thought is, who turns the dawn to darkness and treads on the high places of the earth — the LORD, God of hosts, is his name.

amos_5.t: Hear this word that I am raising over you — a lamentation, house of Israel:
She has fallen, she will not rise again, the virgin Israel. She lies abandoned on her own ground; there is no one to raise her up.
For thus says Lord GOD: The city that marches out a thousand will have a hundred left, and the one that marches out a hundred will have ten left, for the house of Israel.
For thus says the LORD to the house of Israel: Seek me and live.
But do not seek Bethel, and do not go to Gilgal, and do not cross over to Beersheba, for Gilgal will surely go into exile, and Bethel will come to nothing.
Seek the LORD and live, lest he break out like fire on the house of Joseph and consume it, with no one to extinguish it for Bethel.
You who turn justice into wormwood and thrust righteousness down to the ground!
The maker of Kimah and Kesil, who turns deep darkness into morning and darkens day into night, who summons the waters of the sea and pours them out on the face of the earth — the LORD is his name;
who flashes devastation on the strong, and devastation comes upon the fortress.
They hate the one who reproves in the gate, and they abhor the one who speaks blamelessly.

Therefore, because you trample on the poor and take a portion of grain from him, you have built houses of hewn stone but you will not live in them; you have planted vineyards of delight but you will not drink their wine.
For I know that your transgressions are many and your sins are numerous — you who oppose the righteous, who take a bribe, and who turn aside the needy in the gate.
Therefore the prudent will keep silent at that time, for it is an evil time.
Seek good and not evil, so that you may live, and so it may be that the LORD, God of hosts, will be with you just as you have said.
Hate evil and love good, and establish justice in the gate. Perhaps the LORD, God of hosts, will show favour to the remnant of Joseph.

Therefore thus says the LORD, God of hosts, the Lord: In all the open squares there will be wailing, and in all the streets they will say, "Alas! Alas!" They will summon the farmer to mourning, and wailing to those who know how to lament.
And in all the vineyards there will be wailing, for I will pass through your midst, says the LORD.
Woe to those who long for the day of the LORD! Why would you want it — the day of the LORD? It is darkness and not light.
As when a man flees from a lion and a bear meets him, or he goes into the house and leans his hand on the wall and a serpent bites him.
Is not the day of the LORD darkness and not light, gloom with no brightness in it?
I hate, I reject your festivals, and I take no delight in your solemn assemblies.
Even if you offer me burnt offerings and your grain offerings, I will not accept them, and I will not look upon the peace offering of your fatlings.
Take away from me the noise of your songs; I will not listen to the music of your harps.
But let justice roll on like the waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing wadi.
Did you bring me sacrifices and grain offering in the wilderness for forty years, house of Israel?
And you will carry Sikkuth your king and Kiyyun your images, the star of your gods, which you made for yourselves.
And I will send you into exile beyond Damascus, says the LORD — God of hosts is his name.

amos_6.t: Woe to those at ease in Zion and those who trust in the mountain of Samaria, the notables of the foremost of the nations, to whom the house of Israel comes!
Cross over to Calneh and see; go from there to Hamath Rabbah, and go down to Gath of the Philistines. Are they better than these kingdoms? Is their territory greater than yours?
You who push away the day of evil and bring near a seat of violence,
who lie on beds of ivory and sprawl on their couches, who eat lambs from the flock and calves from the midst of the stall;
who improvise to the mouth of the harp and, like David, have devised instruments of song for themselves;
who drink wine from bowls and anoint themselves with the finest oils, but are not sickened over the ruin of Joseph.
Therefore now they will go into exile at the head of the exiles, and the revelry of the sprawlers will come to an end.
Lord GOD has sworn by his own being — declares the LORD, God of hosts: I loathe the pride of Jacob and I hate his fortresses, and I will deliver up the city and all that fills it.
And it will be that if ten men remain in one house, they will die.

And a man's kinsman will lift him up, and the one who burns him, to bring the bones out of the house. And he will say to the one in the innermost part of the house, "Is anyone still with you?" And he will say, "No one." And he will say, "Hush! For the name of the LORD is not to be brought to remembrance."
For look, the LORD is giving the command, and the great house will be struck to fragments and the small house to rubble.
Do horses run on the rock? Does anyone plough there with oxen? Yet you have turned justice into poison and the fruit of righteousness into wormwood.
You who rejoice over Lo Debar, who say, "Was it not by our own strength that we took Karnaim for ourselves?"
For look, I am raising up a nation against you, house of Israel — declares the LORD, God of hosts — and they will oppress you from Lebo Hamath to the wadi of the Arabah.

amos_7.t: This is what Lord GOD showed me: he was forming locusts at the beginning of the coming up of the late growth — and there was a late growth after the king's mowings.
And when it had finished eating the vegetation of the land, I said: "Lord GOD, forgive, please! How will Jacob stand? For he is small."
The LORD relented concerning this: "It will not be," said the LORD.
This is what Lord GOD showed me: Lord GOD was calling for a contention by fire, and it consumed the great deep and consumed the portion of land.
And I said: "Lord GOD, cease, please! How will Jacob stand? For he is small."
The LORD relented concerning this: "This also will not be," said Lord GOD.
This is what he showed me: the Lord was standing on a wall made by a plumb line, with a plumb line in his hand.
And the LORD said to me, "What are you seeing, Amos?" And I said, "A plumb line." And the Lord said, "Look, I am setting a plumb line in the midst of my people Israel. I will not pass by them again."
And the high places of Isaac will be made desolate, and the sanctuaries of Israel will be laid waste, and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.
And Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, "Amos has conspired against you in the midst of the house of Israel. The land is not able to endure all his words."
"For this is what Amos has said: 'By the sword Jeroboam will die, and Israel will surely go into exile from its ground.'"
And Amaziah said to Amos, "Seer, go, flee to the land of Judah, and eat bread there, and prophesy there."
"And do not prophesy at Bethel again, for it is a king's sanctuary and a royal house."
And Amos answered and said to Amaziah: "I am no prophet, and I am no prophet's son; for I am a herdsman and a tender of sycamore figs.
"And the LORD took me from following the flock, and the LORD said to me, 'Go, prophesy to my people Israel.'
"And now hear the word of the LORD: You say, 'Do not prophesy against Israel, and do not preach against the house of Isaac.'"

Therefore thus says the LORD: Your wife will be a prostitute in the city, and your sons and your daughters will fall by the sword, and your ground will be divided by the measuring-line, and you yourself will die on unclean ground, and Israel will surely go into exile from its ground.

amos_8.t: This is what Lord GOD showed me: a basket of summer fruit.
And he said, "What are you seeing, Amos?" And I said, "A basket of summer fruit." And the LORD said to me, "The end has come upon my people Israel. I will not pass by them again."
And the songs of the temple will become wailing on that day, declares Lord GOD. Many the corpses! In every place they have been thrown out. Hush!
Hear this, you who trample on the needy and put an end to the afflicted of the land,
saying, "When will the new moon pass, so that we may sell grain, and the sabbath, so that we may open the wheat?" — making the ephah small and the shekel great, and falsifying balances of deceit,
to buy the poor for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals, and to sell the refuse of the wheat.
The LORD has sworn by the pride of Jacob: "I will never forget any of their deeds."
Shall the land not tremble over this, and everyone who dwells in it mourn? All of it will rise like the Nile, and be tossed and sink like the River of Egypt.
And it will be on that day, declares Lord GOD, that I will make the sun go down at noon and darken the earth in broad daylight.

And I will turn your festivals into mourning and all your songs into lamentation; I will bring sackcloth up on every set of loins and baldness on every head, and I will make it like the mourning for an only son, and its end like a bitter day.
Look, days are coming, declares Lord GOD, when I will send a famine in the land — not a famine for bread and not a thirst for water, but for hearing the words of the LORD.
And they will stagger from sea to sea, and from the north to the east; they will rove about seeking the word of the LORD, and they will not find it.
On that day the beautiful virgins and the young men will faint from thirst.
Those who swear by the guilt of Samaria and say, "As your god lives, Dan!" and, "As the way of Beersheba lives!" — they will fall and not rise again.

amos_9.t: I saw the Lord standing on the altar, and he said: "Strike the capital, so that the thresholds shake, and break them off on the head of all of them; and their posterity I will kill with the sword. No one who flees among them will get away, and no escapee among them will escape."
If they dig into Sheol, from there my hand will take them; and if they go up to the heavens, from there I will bring them down.

And if they hide themselves on the top of Carmel, from there I will search them out and take them; and if they conceal themselves from before my eyes at the bottom of the sea, from there I will command the serpent, and it will bite them.
And if they go into captivity before their enemies, from there I will command the sword, and it will kill them. And I will set my eye on them for evil and not for good.
And Lord GOD of hosts, who touches the earth and it melts, and all who dwell in it mourn, and all of it rises like the Nile and sinks like the River of Egypt;
who builds his stairs in the heavens and has founded his vault upon the earth, who summons the waters of the sea and pours them out on the face of the earth — the LORD is his name.
Are you not like the Cushites to me, people of Israel? declares the LORD. Did I not bring up Israel from the land of Egypt, and the Philistines from Caphtor, and Aram from Kir?
Look, the eyes of Lord GOD are on the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from the face of the ground — except that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob, declares the LORD.
For look, I am giving the command, and I will shake the house of Israel among all the nations as grain is shaken in a sieve, and not a pebble will fall to the ground.
By the sword all the sinners of my people will die — those who say, "The calamity will not draw near or come upon us."
On that day I will raise up the falling booth of David; I will wall up their breaches, and his ruins I will raise up, and I will rebuild her as in the days of old,
so that they may take possession of the remnant of Edom and all the nations over whom my name is called, declares the LORD, who does this.

Look, days are coming, declares the LORD, when the ploughman will overtake the reaper and the treader of grapes the sower of seed; the mountains will drip sweet wine, and all the hills will flow with it.

And I will restore the fortunes of my people Israel; they will rebuild desolated cities and live in them, they will plant vineyards and drink their wine, and they will make gardens and eat their fruit.
And I will plant them on their own ground, and they will never again be plucked up from the ground that I have given them, says the LORD your God.

daniel_1.t: In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it.

And the Lord gave Jehoiakim king of Judah into his hand, along with some of the articles of the house of God; and he brought them to the land of Shinar, to the house of his god, and he brought the articles into the treasury of his god.
And the king told Ashpenaz, the chief of his officials, to bring some of the sons of Israel, some of the royal offspring and some of the nobles —

young men in whom there was no blemish, good in appearance, having insight in all wisdom, knowing knowledge and understanding what they learned, and having the ability to stand in the king's palace — and to teach them the writing and the tongue of the Chaldeans.

And the king assigned them a daily portion from the king's delicacies and from the wine he drank, and that they should be brought up for three years, and at the end of them they were to stand before the king.
Among them, from the sons of Judah, were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah.
And the chief of the officials assigned them names: to Daniel, Belteshazzar; to Hananiah, Shadrach; to Mishael, Meshach; and to Azariah, Abed-nego.
But Daniel set it on his heart that he would not defile himself with the king's delicacies or with the wine he drank, and he asked the chief of the officials that he might not defile himself.
And God gave Daniel favour and compassion in the sight of the chief of the officials.

But the chief of the officials said to Daniel, 'I fear my lord the king, who has assigned your food and your drink. Why should he see your faces looking worse than those of the young men of your own age, and then you would make my head forfeit to the king?'
Then Daniel said to the guardian whom the chief of the officials had assigned over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah,
'Test your servants for ten days: let them give us vegetables to eat and water to drink.'
'Then let our appearance be seen before you, and the appearance of the young men who are eating the king's delicacies, and deal with your servants according to what you see.'
And he listened to them in this matter and tested them for ten days.
And at the end of ten days their appearance was better and they were fatter of flesh than all the young men who were eating the king's delicacies.
So the guardian kept taking away their delicacies and the wine they were to drink, and gave them vegetables.
And to these four young men God gave knowledge and insight in all writing and wisdom; and Daniel understood every vision and dream.
And at the end of the days that the king had set for bringing them, the chief of the officials brought them before Nebuchadnezzar.
And the king spoke with them, and among all of them none was found like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah; so they stood before the king.
And in every matter of wisdom and understanding that the king asked of them, he found them ten times better than all the soothsayer-priests and conjurers in his whole kingdom.
And Daniel remained until the first year of Cyrus the king.

daniel_2.t: In the second year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuchadnezzar dreamed dreams; his spirit was troubled and his sleep left him.
So the king gave orders to summon the soothsayer-priests, the conjurers, the sorcerers and the Chaldeans, to tell the king his dreams. And they came and stood before the king.
And the king said to them, 'I have dreamed a dream, and my spirit is troubled to know the dream.'
And the Chaldeans spoke to the king in Aramaic: 'King, live for ever! Tell the dream to your servants, and we will declare the interpretation.'

The king answered and said to the Chaldeans, 'The word from me is firm. If you do not make known to me the dream and its interpretation, you will be made into limbs and your houses will be made a refuse heap.'
'But if you declare the dream and its interpretation, you will receive from me gifts and a reward and great honour. So declare to me the dream and its interpretation.'
They answered a second time and said, 'Let the king tell the dream to his servants, and we will declare the interpretation.'
The king answered and said, 'I know for certain that you are gaining time, because you have seen that the word from me is firm —'

'that if you do not make known to me the dream, there is one law for you. You have agreed together to speak a lying and corrupt word before me until the time changes. So tell me the dream, and I shall know that you can declare its interpretation to me.'

The Chaldeans answered before the king and said, 'There is no person on earth who can declare the king's matter, because no king, however great and powerful, has asked such a thing of any magician or conjurer or Chaldean.'
'And the matter the king is asking is difficult, and there is no one else who can declare it before the king except the gods, whose dwelling is not with flesh.'
Because of this the king was angry and exceedingly furious, and he gave orders to destroy all the wise men of Babylon.
So the law went out, and the wise men were about to be killed; and they sought Daniel and his companions, to kill them.
Then Daniel answered with counsel and discretion to Arioch, the chief of the king's executioners, who had gone out to kill the wise men of Babylon.
He answered and said to Arioch the king's captain, 'Why is the law from the king so harsh?' Then Arioch made the matter known to Daniel.
So Daniel went in and asked the king to give him time, and he would declare the interpretation to the king.
Then Daniel went to his house and made the matter known to Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah, his companions,
and told them to ask compassion from before the God of the heavens concerning this secret, so that Daniel and his companions would not be destroyed with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
Then the secret was revealed to Daniel in a vision of the night, and Daniel blessed the God of the heavens.
Daniel answered and said: 'Let the name of God be blessed from age to age, for wisdom and power are his.'
'And he changes the times and the appointed times; he removes kings and sets up kings; he gives wisdom to the wise and understanding to those who know discernment.'
'He reveals the deep things and the hidden things; he knows what is in the darkness, and the light dwells with him.'
'To you, God of my fathers, I give thanks and praise, for you have given me wisdom and power; and now you have made known to me what we asked of you — you have made known to us the king's matter.'

Because of this Daniel went in to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon. He went and said to him, 'Do not destroy the wise men of Babylon. Bring me in before the king, and I will declare the interpretation to the king.'
Then Arioch hurriedly brought Daniel in before the king and said to him, 'I have found a man from the sons of the exile of Judah who will make known the interpretation to the king.'
The king answered and said to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, 'Are you able to make known to me the dream I have seen, and its interpretation?'
Daniel answered before the king and said, 'The secret the king is asking — wise men, conjurers, magicians and astrologers are not able to declare it to the king.'

'Nevertheless there is a God in the heavens who reveals secrets, and he has made known to King Nebuchadnezzar what will be at the end of the days. Your dream and the visions of your head upon your bed are these:'
'As for you, King, your thoughts came up on your bed about what will be after this, and the revealer of secrets has made known to you what will be.'

'And as for me, this secret has not been revealed to me because of wisdom in me greater than in all the living, but so that the interpretation should be made known to the king and that you should know the thoughts of your heart.'
'You, King, were looking, and behold: a single great image. That image was great and its splendour extraordinary; it stood before you, and its appearance was terrible.'
'That image: its head was of fine gold, its breast and arms of silver, its belly and loins of bronze,'
'its legs of iron, its feet partly of iron and partly of clay.'
'You were looking until a stone was cut out, not by hands, and it struck the image on its feet of iron and clay and shattered them.'

'Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver and the gold were shattered together and became like chaff from the summer threshing floors, and the wind carried them away, and no place was found for them. And the stone that struck the image became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.'
'This is the dream, and we will tell its interpretation before the king.'
'You, King, are the king of kings, to whom the God of the heavens has given the kingdom, the power, the strength and the honour;'
'and wherever the sons of humankind dwell, he has given the animals of the field and the birds of the heavens into your hand and made you ruler over them all. You are the head of gold.'
'And after you another kingdom will arise, inferior to you; and a third kingdom, of bronze, which will rule over the whole earth.'
'And a fourth kingdom will be strong as iron; for iron shatters and crushes everything, and like iron that breaks in pieces, it will shatter and crush all these.'

'And that you saw the feet and toes partly of a potter's clay and partly of iron — it will be a divided kingdom; and some of the firmness of iron will be in it, because you saw the iron mixed with the clay of mud.'
'And as the toes of the feet were partly iron and partly clay, so the kingdom will be partly strong and partly breakable.'
'And that you saw the iron mixed with the clay of mud — they will be mixing with the offspring of humankind, but they will not cling to one another, just as iron does not mix with clay.'

'And in the days of those kings the God of the heavens will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, and the kingdom will not be left to another people. It will shatter and put an end to all these kingdoms, and it will stand for ever.'

'Because you saw that a stone was cut out of the mountain, not by hands, and that it shattered the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver and the gold — the great God has made known to the king what will be after this. The dream is certain and its interpretation trustworthy.'
Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face and paid homage to Daniel, and gave orders to offer an offering and soothing offerings to him.
The king answered Daniel and said, 'In truth your God is the God of gods and the lord of kings and a revealer of secrets, since you have been able to reveal this secret.'
Then the king made Daniel great and gave him many great gifts, and made him ruler over the whole province of Babylon and chief of the prefects over all the wise men of Babylon.
And Daniel made a request of the king, and he appointed Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego over the administration of the province of Babylon; and Daniel was in the king's gate.

daniel_3.t: King Nebuchadnezzar made an image of gold; its height was sixty cubits and its width six cubits. He set it up on the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon.

And King Nebuchadnezzar sent to gather the satraps, the prefects, the governors, the counsellors, the ministers, the judges, the magistrates and all the authorities of the provinces, to come to the dedication of the image that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.

Then the satraps, the prefects, the governors, the counsellors, the ministers, the judges, the magistrates and all the authorities of the provinces were gathered for the dedication of the image that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up, and they stood before the image that Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
And the herald proclaimed with power: 'To you it is commanded, peoples, nations and languages:'

'At the time when you hear the sound of the horn, the flute, the zither, the trigon, the harp, the pipe and all kinds of music, you shall fall down and pay homage to the image of gold that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.'
'And whoever does not fall down and pay homage will at that moment be thrown into the midst of the burning fiery furnace.'

Therefore, at that time, as soon as all the peoples heard the sound of the horn, the flute, the zither, the trigon, the harp and all kinds of music, all the peoples, nations and languages fell down and paid homage to the image of gold that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
Therefore, at that time, certain Chaldean men came forward and denounced the Jews.
They answered and said to King Nebuchadnezzar, 'King, live for ever!'

'You, King, made a decree that every person who hears the sound of the horn, the flute, the zither, the trigon, the harp, the pipe and all kinds of music shall fall down and pay homage to the image of gold;'
'and whoever does not fall down and pay homage will be thrown into the midst of the burning fiery furnace.'

'There are Jewish men whom you have appointed over the administration of the province of Babylon: Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego. These men have paid no attention to you, King. They do not serve your god, and they do not pay homage to the image of gold you have set up.'
Then Nebuchadnezzar, in rage and anger, gave orders to bring Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego. So these men were brought before the king.
Nebuchadnezzar answered and said to them, 'Is it true, Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego, that you do not serve my gods and do not pay homage to the image of gold I have set up?'

'Now, if you are ready, at the time when you hear the sound of the horn, the flute, the zither, the trigon, the harp, the pipe and all kinds of music, fall down and pay homage to the image I have made. But if you do not pay homage, at that moment you will be thrown into the midst of the burning fiery furnace — and who is the god who will deliver you from my hands?'
Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego answered and said to the king, 'Nebuchadnezzar, we have no need to send you back a word about this matter.'
'If it is so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace and from your hand, King, he will deliver.'
'But if not, let it be known to you, King, that we do not serve your god, and we will not pay homage to the image of gold you have set up.'

Then Nebuchadnezzar was filled with anger, and the image of his face was changed towards Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego. He gave orders to heat the furnace seven times more than it was proper to heat it.
And he ordered mighty men of power who were in his army to bind Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego and throw them into the burning fiery furnace.
Then these men were bound in their mantles, their trousers, their caps and their other clothes, and were thrown into the midst of the burning fiery furnace.
Because the king's word was harsh and the furnace exceedingly heated, the flame of the fire killed the men who took up Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego.
And these three men — Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego — fell bound into the midst of the burning fiery furnace.

Then King Nebuchadnezzar was alarmed and rose in haste. He answered and said to his counsellors, 'Did we not throw three men, bound, into the midst of the fire?' They answered and said to the king, 'It is certain, King.'
He answered and said, 'Look — I see four men, loosed, walking in the midst of the fire, and there is no hurt on them; and the appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods.'

Then Nebuchadnezzar approached the door of the burning fiery furnace and said, 'Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego, servants of the Most High God, come out and come here!' So Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego came out from the midst of the fire.

And the satraps, the prefects, the governors and the king's counsellors gathered and saw these men: the fire had had no power over their bodies, the hair of their heads was not singed, their mantles were not changed, and the smell of fire had not touched them.

Nebuchadnezzar answered and said, 'Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego, who sent his angel and delivered his servants who trusted in him. They violated the king's word and gave up their bodies, so as not to serve or pay homage to any god except their own God.'

'And from me a decree is made: any people, nation or language that speaks anything amiss against the God of Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego will be made into limbs, and his house will be made a refuse heap; for there is no other god able to rescue like this.'
Then the king made Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego prosper in the province of Babylon.

daniel_4.t: King Nebuchadnezzar, to all the peoples, nations and languages who dwell in all the earth: may your peace increase.
It has seemed good to me to declare the signs and the wonders that the Most High God has done with me.
How great are his signs, and how strong his wonders! His kingdom is a perpetual kingdom, and his dominion is from generation to generation.
I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at ease in my house and flourishing in my palace.
I saw a dream, and it made me afraid; imaginings on my bed and the visions of my head alarmed me.
So from me a decree was made to bring in before me all the wise men of Babylon, that they should make known to me the interpretation of the dream.
Then the magicians, the conjurers, the Chaldeans and the astrologers came in, and I told the dream before them; but they did not make known to me its interpretation.
And at last Daniel came in before me — whose name is Belteshazzar, after the name of my god, and in whom is a spirit of holy gods — and I told the dream before him:
'Belteshazzar, chief of the magicians, because I know that a spirit of holy gods is in you and no secret is too hard for you — tell me the visions of my dream that I saw, and its interpretation.'
'And the visions of my head upon my bed were these: I was looking, and behold, a tree in the midst of the earth, and its height was great.'
'The tree grew great and strong; its height reached to the heavens, and it was visible to the end of all the earth.'

'Its foliage was beautiful and its fruit plentiful, and there was food for all in it. Under it the animals of the field found shade, in its branches the birds of the heavens nested, and from it all flesh was fed.'
'I was looking in the visions of my head upon my bed, and behold, a watcher, a holy one, was coming down from the heavens.'
'He proclaimed with power and said: Cut down the tree and cut off its branches; strip off its foliage and scatter its fruit. Let the animals flee from under it, and the birds from its branches.'

'Nevertheless leave the stump of its roots in the ground, with a fetter of iron and bronze, in the grass of the field; and let it be wet with the dew of the heavens, and let its portion be with the animals in the grass of the earth.'
'Let his heart be changed from a human's, and let the heart of an animal be given to him; and let seven times pass over him.'

'The command is by the decree of the watchers, and the affair by the word of the holy ones — so that the living may know that the Most High has mastery over the kingdom of humankind, and gives it to whomever he pleases, and sets over it the lowliest of humankind.'

'This is the dream I saw, I, King Nebuchadnezzar. And you, Belteshazzar, tell its interpretation, because all the wise men of my kingdom are not able to make the interpretation known to me; but you are able, because a spirit of holy gods is in you.'

Then Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, was appalled for a moment, and his thoughts alarmed him. The king answered and said, 'Belteshazzar, do not let the dream and its interpretation alarm you.' Belteshazzar answered and said, 'My lord, let the dream be for those who hate you, and its interpretation for your adversaries.'
'The tree you saw, which grew great and strong, whose height reached to the heavens and which was visible to all the earth,'
'whose foliage was beautiful and its fruit plentiful, and in which there was food for all; under which the animals of the field dwelt, and in whose branches the birds of the heavens dwelt —'
'it is you, King, who have grown great and strong. Your greatness has grown and reached to the heavens, and your dominion to the end of the earth.'

'And that the king saw a watcher, a holy one, coming down from the heavens and saying, Cut down the tree and destroy it — nevertheless leave the stump of its roots in the ground, with a fetter of iron and bronze, in the grass of the field, and let it be wet with the dew of the heavens, and let its portion be with the animals of the field, until seven times pass over it —'
'this is the interpretation, King, and it is the decree of the Most High that has come upon my lord the king:'

'You will be chased away from humankind, and your dwelling will be with the animals of the field; you will be fed grass like oxen and made wet with the dew of the heavens. Seven times will pass over you, until you know that the Most High has mastery over the kingdom of humankind and gives it to whomever he pleases.'
'And that they said to leave the stump of the roots of the tree: your kingdom will remain yours, from the time you know that the heavens have mastery.'

'Therefore, King, let my advice be acceptable to you: break off your sin by doing righteousness, and your iniquities by showing mercy to the poor; perhaps there may be a prolonging of your prosperity.'
All of it came upon King Nebuchadnezzar.
At the end of twelve months he was walking about on the roof of the royal palace of Babylon.
The king answered and said, 'Is this not Babylon the great, which I myself have built as a royal house by the strength of my power and for the honour of my majesty?'
The word was still in the king's mouth when a voice fell from the heavens: 'To you it is said, King Nebuchadnezzar: the kingdom has passed away from you,'

'and you are about to be chased away from humankind, and your dwelling will be with the animals of the field; you will be fed grass like oxen, and seven times will pass over you, until you know that the Most High has mastery over the kingdom of humankind and gives it to whomever he pleases.'

At that moment the word was fulfilled upon Nebuchadnezzar. He was chased away from humankind and ate grass like oxen; his body was wet with the dew of the heavens, until his hair grew long like eagles' feathers and his nails like birds' claws.

And at the end of the days I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted my eyes to the heavens, and my understanding returned to me. I blessed the Most High; I praised and glorified the one who lives for ever, whose dominion is a perpetual dominion and whose kingdom is from generation to generation.

And all the inhabitants of the earth are reckoned as nothing; he does according to his pleasure with the army of the heavens and the inhabitants of the earth, and there is none who can strike his hand or say to him, 'What have you done?'

At that time my understanding returned to me, and for the honour of my kingdom my majesty and my splendour returned to me. My counsellors and my nobles sought me out, I was established over my kingdom, and surpassing greatness was added to me.
Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and exalt and glorify the King of the heavens, all of whose deeds are truth and whose ways are justice; and those who walk in pride he is able to bring low.

daniel_5.t: King Belshazzar made a great feast for a thousand of his nobles, and before the thousand he was drinking wine.

Belshazzar, under the influence of the wine, gave orders to bring the vessels of gold and silver that Nebuchadnezzar his father had brought out of the temple in Jerusalem, so that the king and his nobles, his wives and his concubines might drink from them.
Then they brought the vessels of gold that had been brought out of the temple, the house of God, in Jerusalem; and the king and his nobles, his wives and his concubines drank from them.
They drank the wine and praised the gods of gold and silver, bronze, iron, wood and stone.
At that moment the fingers of a human hand came out and wrote opposite the lampstand on the plaster of the wall of the king's palace; and the king saw the palm of the hand that was writing.
Then the king's brightness changed, his thoughts alarmed him, the joints of his loins were loosened, and his knees knocked one against the other.

The king called out with power to bring in the conjurers, the Chaldeans and the astrologers. The king answered and said to the wise men of Babylon, 'Any person who reads this writing and declares its interpretation to me will be clothed with purple, a necklace of gold will be on his neck, and he will rule as third in the kingdom.'
Then all the king's wise men went in, but they were not able to read the writing or to make its interpretation known to the king.
Then King Belshazzar was exceedingly alarmed, his brightness was changing upon him, and his nobles were dumbfounded.

The queen, because of the words of the king and his nobles, came into the banqueting house. The queen answered and said, 'King, live for ever! Do not let your thoughts alarm you, and do not let your brightness be changed.'

'There is a man in your kingdom in whom is a spirit of holy gods; and in the days of your father, illumination and insight and wisdom like the wisdom of gods were found in him. King Nebuchadnezzar your father made him chief of the magicians, conjurers, Chaldeans and astrologers — your father the king —'

'because an extraordinary spirit, and understanding and insight — interpreting dreams, declaring riddles and loosening knots — were found in him, in Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar. Now let Daniel be summoned, and he will declare the interpretation.'
Then Daniel was brought in before the king. The king answered and said to Daniel, 'Are you that Daniel, one of the sons of the exile of Judah, whom the king my father brought from Judah?'
'And I have heard concerning you that a spirit of gods is in you, and that illumination and insight and extraordinary wisdom have been found in you.'

'And now the wise men and the conjurers have been brought in before me to read this writing and make its interpretation known to me, but they were not able to declare the interpretation of the matter.'

'And I have heard concerning you that you are able to interpret interpretations and to loosen knots. Now if you are able to read the writing and make its interpretation known to me, you will be clothed with purple, a necklace of gold will be on your neck, and you will rule as third in the kingdom.'

Then Daniel answered and said before the king, 'Let your gifts be for yourself, and give your rewards to another. Nevertheless I will read the writing to the king and make the interpretation known to him.'
'You, King: the Most High God gave the kingdom and the greatness and the honour and the majesty to Nebuchadnezzar your father.'

'And because of the greatness he gave him, all the peoples, nations and languages trembled and feared before him. Whom he pleased he killed, and whom he pleased he let live; whom he pleased he lifted up, and whom he pleased he brought low.'
'And when his heart rose up and his spirit grew strong to act presumptuously, he was deposed from the throne of his kingdom and the honour was removed from him.'

'He was chased away from the sons of humankind, his heart was made like the animals', and his dwelling was with the wild donkeys. They fed him grass like oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of the heavens, until he knew that the Most High God has mastery over the kingdom of humankind and appoints over it whomever he pleases.'
'And you, his son Belshazzar, have not brought your heart low, though you knew all this.'

'And you have lifted yourself up against the lord of the heavens. They have brought the vessels of his house before you, and you and your nobles, your wives and your concubines have been drinking wine from them; and you have praised the gods of silver and gold, bronze, iron, wood and stone, which do not see or hear or know. But the God in whose hand is your breath, and to whom all your ways belong, you have not glorified.'
'Then from before him the palm of the hand was sent out, and this writing was inscribed.'
'And this is the writing that was inscribed: MENE MENE TEQEL AND PHARSIN.'
'This is the interpretation of the matter: MENE — God has numbered your kingdom and finished it.'
'TEQEL — you have been weighed in the scales and found lacking.'
'PERES — your kingdom has been broken in two and given to the Medes and the Persians.'
Then Belshazzar gave orders, and they clothed Daniel with purple, and a necklace of gold was put on his neck; and they made proclamation concerning him that he should rule as third in the kingdom.
In that night Belshazzar the Chaldean king was killed.
And Darius the Mede received the kingdom, being about sixty-two years old.

daniel_6.t: It seemed good to Darius to appoint over the kingdom a hundred and twenty satraps, who were to be throughout the whole kingdom;
and above them three overseers, of whom Daniel was one, to whom these satraps were to give the report, so that the king should suffer no injury.
Then this Daniel distinguished himself above the overseers and the satraps, because an extraordinary spirit was in him, and the king planned to appoint him over the whole kingdom.

Then the overseers and the satraps sought to find an occasion against Daniel in the affairs of the kingdom, but they were not able to find any occasion or corruption, because he was trustworthy, and no negligence or corruption was found in him.
Then these men said, 'We will find no occasion against this Daniel unless we find it against him in the law of his God.'
Then these overseers and satraps came in a crowd to the king and said to him, 'Darius the king, live for ever!'

'All the overseers of the kingdom, the prefects and the satraps, the counsellors and the governors, have taken counsel together to establish a royal statute and to make stringent a prohibition: that anyone who asks a petition of any god or person for thirty days, except of you, King, will be thrown into the den of lions.'
'Now, King, establish the prohibition and sign the writing, which is not to be changed, according to the law of the Medes and the Persians, which does not pass away.'
Because of this King Darius signed the writing and the prohibition.

And Daniel, when he knew that the writing was signed, went into his house — where windows were open for him in his upper room facing Jerusalem — and three times a day he knelt on his knees and prayed and gave praise before his God, just as he had been doing before this.
Then these men came in a crowd and found Daniel asking and imploring favour before his God.

Then they approached and said before the king, concerning the king's prohibition, 'Did you not sign a prohibition that any person who asks of any god or person for thirty days, except of you, King, will be thrown into the den of lions?' The king answered and said, 'The word is certain, according to the law of the Medes and the Persians, which does not pass away.'

Then they answered and said before the king, 'Daniel, one of the sons of the exile of Judah, has paid no attention to you, King, nor to the prohibition you signed; and three times a day he asks his petition.'
Then the king, when he heard the word, was exceedingly displeased at it; he set his mind on Daniel to deliver him, and until the going down of the sun he was striving to rescue him.
Then these men came in a crowd to the king and said to him, 'Know, King, that the law of the Medes and the Persians is that no prohibition or statute the king establishes may be changed.'
Then the king gave orders, and they brought Daniel and threw him into the den of lions. The king answered and said to Daniel, 'Your God, whom you serve continually — may he deliver you.'
And a stone was brought and set over the mouth of the den, and the king sealed it with his signet ring and with the signet rings of his nobles, so that nothing should be changed concerning Daniel.
Then the king went to his palace and passed the night fasting; no diversions were brought in before him, and his sleep fled from him.
Then the king rose at dawn, at first light, and went in haste to the den of lions.

And as he approached the den, to Daniel, he cried out with a pained voice. The king answered and said to Daniel, 'Daniel, servant of the living God, your God whom you serve continually — has he been able to deliver you from the lions?'
Then Daniel spoke with the king: 'King, live for ever!'
'My God sent his angel and closed the mouth of the lions, and they did not harm me, because innocence was found in me before him; and before you also, King, I have done no hurtful act.'
Then the king was exceedingly glad, and gave orders to take Daniel up from the den. And Daniel was taken up from the den, and no hurt was found on him, because he had trusted in his God.

And the king gave orders, and they brought those men who had denounced Daniel and threw them into the den of lions — them, their sons and their wives. And they had not reached the bottom of the den before the lions had power over them and shattered all their bones.
Then Darius the king wrote to all the peoples, nations and languages who dwell in all the earth: may your peace increase.

'From me a decree is made, that in all the dominion of my kingdom people are to tremble and fear before the God of Daniel; for he is the living God and endures for ever, his kingdom is one that will not be destroyed, and his dominion is to the end.'
'He delivers and rescues, and does signs and wonders in the heavens and on the earth — he who has delivered Daniel from the hand of the lions.'
And this Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian.

daniel_7.t: In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon, Daniel saw a dream and visions of his head upon his bed. Then he wrote the dream down; he told the sum of the matters.
Daniel answered and said: 'I was looking in my vision in the night, and behold, the four winds of the heavens were stirring up the great sea.'
'And four great beasts were coming up from the sea, each different from the others.'

'The first was like a lion, and it had eagle's wings. I was looking until its wings were plucked off, and it was lifted up from the earth and made to stand on two feet like a human being; and a human heart was given to it.'
'And behold, another beast, a second, like a bear. It was raised up on one side, and three ribs were in its mouth between its teeth; and they said to it, Arise, devour much flesh.'
'After this I was looking, and behold, another, like a leopard, with four wings of a bird on its back; and the beast had four heads, and dominion was given to it.'

'After this I was looking in the visions of the night, and behold, a fourth beast, fearful and terrible and exceedingly strong. It had great teeth of iron; it was devouring and shattering and trampling the rest with its feet. And it was different from all the beasts before it, and it had ten horns.'

'I was considering the horns, and behold, another horn, a small one, came up among them, and three of the former horns were uprooted from before it. And behold, in this horn there were eyes like the eyes of a human being, and a mouth speaking great things.'

'I was looking until thrones were placed, and the Ancient of Days took his seat. His clothing was white like snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool; his throne was flames of fire, its wheels burning fire.'
'A river of fire was flowing and coming out from before him. A thousand thousands were ministering to him, and a myriad of myriads were standing before him. The court sat, and books were opened.'
'I was looking then, because of the sound of the great words that the horn was speaking. I was looking until the beast was killed and its body destroyed and given over to the burning of fire.'
'And as for the rest of the beasts, their dominion was removed; but a prolonging of life was given to them until a time and a season.'
'I was looking in the visions of the night, and behold, with the clouds of the heavens one like a son of man was coming; and he came to the Ancient of Days, and he was presented before him.'

'And to him were given dominion and honour and a kingdom, and all the peoples, nations and languages will serve him. His dominion is a perpetual dominion that will not pass away, and his kingdom one that will not be destroyed.'
'As for me, Daniel, my spirit was distressed within its sheath, and the visions of my head alarmed me.'
'I approached one of those standing there and asked him the truth about all this. And he told me, and made known to me the interpretation of the matters:'
'These great beasts, which are four, are four kings who will arise from the earth.'
'But the saints of the Most High will receive the kingdom and will take possession of the kingdom for ever, and for ever and ever.'

'Then I desired to make certain concerning the fourth beast, which was different from all the others — exceedingly terrible, its teeth of iron and its claws of bronze, devouring, shattering, and trampling the rest with its feet —'

'and concerning the ten horns that were on its head, and the other one that came up, before which three fell — that horn which had eyes, and a mouth speaking great things, and whose appearance was greater than its companions'.'
'I was looking, and that horn was making war with the saints and prevailing against them,'
'until the Ancient of Days came, and judgement was given in favour of the saints of the Most High; and the appointed time arrived, and the saints took possession of the kingdom.'
'He said: The fourth beast is a fourth kingdom that will be on the earth, different from all the kingdoms; and it will devour all the earth and tread it down and shatter it.'
'And the ten horns: from that kingdom ten kings will arise, and another will arise after them. He will be different from the former ones, and he will bring low three kings.'

'And he will speak words against the Most High, and he will wear out the saints of the Most High, and he will think to change appointed times and law; and they will be given into his hand for a time and times and half a time.'
'And the court will sit, and his dominion will be removed, to be annihilated and destroyed until the end.'

'And the kingdom and the dominion and the greatness of the kingdoms under all the heavens were given to a people, the saints of the Most High. His kingdom is a perpetual kingdom, and all the empires will serve and obey him.'
'Here is the end of the matter.' As for me, Daniel, my thoughts alarmed me exceedingly and my brightness was changed upon me; but I kept the matter in my heart.

daniel_8.t: In the third year of the reign of Belshazzar the king, a vision appeared to me, Daniel, after the one that had appeared to me at the beginning.
And I saw in the vision — and it happened, when I saw, that I was in Susa the citadel, which is in the province of Elam — and I saw in the vision, and I was by the canal of Ulai.
And I lifted up my eyes and saw, and behold, a single ram standing before the canal, and it had two horns. The two horns were high, but one was higher than the other, and the higher one came up last.

I saw the ram thrusting westward and northward and southward, and no living creatures could stand before it, and there was none who could deliver from its hand. It did as it pleased and magnified itself.
And I was observing, and behold, a he-goat coming from the west over the face of the whole earth, and it was not touching the earth; and the he-goat had a conspicuous horn between its eyes.
And it came to the ram, the one with the two horns, which I had seen standing before the canal, and it ran at it in the rage of its strength.

And I saw it reach the ram; it was enraged at it and struck the ram and broke its two horns, and there was no strength in the ram to stand before it. It threw it to the ground and trampled it, and there was none who could deliver the ram from its hand.
And the he-goat magnified itself exceedingly; but when it became mighty, the great horn was broken, and four conspicuous horns came up in its place, towards the four winds of the heavens.
And out of one of them came a single horn, small at first, and it became exceedingly great towards the south and towards the east and towards the beautiful land.
And it became great as far as the host of the heavens, and it made some of the host and some of the stars fall to the ground, and trampled them.
And it magnified itself as far as the Prince of the host; from him the perpetual offering was removed, and the place of his sanctuary was thrown down.
And an army will be set over the perpetual offering in transgression, and it will throw truth to the ground; and it will act and succeed.

And I heard one holy one speaking, and one holy one said to the certain one who was speaking, 'Until when does the vision hold — the perpetual offering, and the transgression that desolates, the giving over of both the sanctuary and the host to trampling?'
And he said to me, 'Until evening and morning — two thousand three hundred; then the sanctuary will be restored.'
And it happened, when I, Daniel, saw the vision and sought understanding, that behold, one like the appearance of a man was standing before me.
And I heard a human voice between the banks of the Ulai, and it called and said, 'Gabriel, explain the vision to this one.'
And he came beside where I was standing; and when he came I was terrified and fell on my face. And he said to me, 'Understand, son of humankind, that the vision is for the time of the end.'
And while he was speaking with me I was dazed, face down on the ground. And he touched me and made me stand where I had been standing.
And he said, 'I am about to make known to you what will be at the end of the indignation; for it is for the appointed time of the end.'
'The ram you saw, the one with the two horns, is the kings of Media and Persia.'
'And the hairy he-goat is the king of Greece, and the great horn between its eyes is the first king.'
'And as for the broken horn and the four that arose in its place: four kingdoms will arise from that nation, but not with its power.'
'And at the end of their reign, when the rebels have reached their full measure, a king strong of face and understanding intrigues will arise.'
'And his power will be mighty, but not by his own power; and he will destroy wonderfully, and he will succeed and act, and he will destroy the mighty and a people of holy ones.'

'And through his insight deceit will succeed in his hand; in his heart he will magnify himself, and in prosperity he will destroy many. He will stand against a prince of princes, and by no hand he will be broken.'
'And the vision of the evening and the morning that has been told is truth. But you, keep the vision secret, for it is for many days.'
And I, Daniel, was overcome and was sick for days; then I arose and did the king's work. And I was appalled at what I had seen, and there was none who could give understanding.

daniel_9.t: In the first year of Darius son of Ahasuerus, of the offspring of Media, who had been made king over the kingdom of the Chaldeans —

in the first year of his reign, I, Daniel, observed in the books the number of the years that the word of the LORD had come to Jeremiah the prophet, to complete for the ruins of Jerusalem seventy years.
And I set my face to the Lord God, to seek him in prayer and supplications, with fasting and sackcloth and ashes.

And I prayed to the LORD my God and confessed, and said: 'I beg you, Lord, the great and awesome God, who keeps the covenant and the steadfast love with those who love him and keep his commandments —'
'we have sinned and committed iniquity, we have acted wickedly and rebelled, and we have turned aside from your commandments and from your judgements.'
'And we have not listened to your servants the prophets, who spoke in your name to our kings, our leaders and our ancestors, and to all the people of the land.'

'To you, Lord, belongs the righteousness, and to us the shame of faces, as at this day — to the people of Judah, to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to all Israel, near and far, in all the lands where you have banished them, in the unfaithfulness by which they acted unfaithfully against you.'
'LORD, to us belongs the shame of faces — to our kings, to our leaders and to our ancestors — because we have sinned against you.'
'To the Lord our God belong compassion and forgiveness, for we have rebelled against him,'
'and we have not listened to the voice of the LORD our God, to walk in his laws, which he set before us by the hand of his servants the prophets.'

'And all Israel have transgressed your law and turned aside, not listening to your voice. So the curse and the oath written in the law of Moses the servant of God has been poured out upon us, because we have sinned against him.'

'And he has carried out his word that he spoke against us and against our judges who judged us, by bringing upon us a great calamity, such as has not been done under all the heavens as it has been done in Jerusalem.'

'Just as it is written in the law of Moses, all this calamity has come upon us; and we have not entreated the face of the LORD our God by turning from our iniquity and by giving attention to your faithfulness.'
'And the LORD kept watch over the calamity and brought it upon us; for the LORD our God is righteous in all the deeds he has done, and we have not listened to his voice.'
'And now, Lord our God, who brought your people out of the land of Egypt with a strong hand and made a name for yourself as at this day: we have sinned, we have acted wickedly.'

'Lord, according to all your righteousnesses, let your anger and your rage turn back from your city Jerusalem, your holy mountain; for because of our sins and the iniquities of our ancestors, Jerusalem and your people have become a reproach to all who are around us.'
'And now, listen, our God, to the prayer of your servant and to his supplications, and make your face shine upon your desolate sanctuary, for the Lord's sake.'

'Incline your ear, my God, and listen; open your eyes and see our desolations and the city over which your name has been called. For it is not on our righteousnesses that we lay our supplications before you, but on your great compassion.'
'Lord, hear! Lord, forgive! Lord, be attentive and act — do not delay — for your own sake, my God; for your name has been called over your city and over your people.'
And while I was still speaking and praying and confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel, and laying my supplication before the LORD my God concerning the holy mountain of my God —
and while I was still speaking in the prayer, the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, came to me when I was worn out and spent, about the time of the evening offering.
And he gave understanding and spoke with me, and said, 'Daniel, I have now come out to give you insight and understanding.'
'At the beginning of your supplications a word went out, and I have come to declare it, for you are precious. So understand the word and understand the vision.'

'Seventy weeks have been decreed upon your people and upon your holy city, to put an end to the transgression, to complete sin, to atone for iniquity, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal up vision and prophet, and to anoint a holy place of holy places.'

'And you shall know and understand: from the going out of a word to restore and rebuild Jerusalem until an anointed one, a prince, is seven weeks; and for sixty-two weeks it shall be restored and rebuilt, with open place and moat, and in the distress of the times.'

'And after the sixty-two weeks an anointed one will be cut off and will have nothing. And the people of the prince who is coming will destroy the city and the sanctuary; and its end will come in the flood, and until the end there is war — desolations are determined.'

'And he will make a covenant strong for the many for one week; and in the middle of the week he will cause sacrifice and offering to cease. And on a wing of detestable things will come one who desolates — and until a complete destruction, what is determined will be poured out on the desolator.'

daniel_10.t: In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia, a word was revealed to Daniel, whose name was called Belteshazzar. The word was truth, and a great war. And he understood the word, and understanding came to him in the vision.
In those days I, Daniel, was mourning for three sevens of days.
I ate no desirable food; meat and wine did not come into my mouth, and I did not anoint myself at all, until three sevens of days were completed.
And on the twenty-fourth day of the first month I was on the bank of the great river, that is, the Tigris.
And I lifted up my eyes and saw, and behold, a single man clothed in linen, his loins girded with the gold of Uphaz.

His body was like beryl, his face like the appearance of lightning, his eyes like torches of fire; his arms and his feet like the appearance of burnished bronze, and the sound of his words like the sound of a multitude.
And I, Daniel, alone saw the vision; the men who were with me did not see the vision. But a great terror fell on them and they fled into hiding.
And I was left alone, and I saw this great vision; no strength remained in me, my vigour was turned to ruin in me, and I retained no strength.
And I heard the sound of his words; and as I heard the sound of his words, I was dazed, face down, my face to the ground.
And behold, a hand touched me and set me trembling on my knees and the palms of my hands.

And he said to me, 'Daniel, greatly precious man, understand the words I am speaking to you, and stand where you are standing, for I have now been sent to you.' And when he spoke this word with me, I stood up trembling.

And he said to me, 'Do not fear, Daniel, for from the first day that you set your heart to understand and to humble yourself before your God, your words were heard; and I have come because of your words.'
'But the prince of the kingdom of Persia stood against me twenty-one days; and behold, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me, and I was left there beside the kings of Persia.'
'And I have come to make you understand what will happen to your people at the end of the days; for the vision is still for those days.'
And while he was speaking with me according to these words, I set my face to the ground and was dumb.

And behold, one like the likeness of the sons of humankind touched my lips; and I opened my mouth and spoke, and said to the one standing before me, 'My lord, because of the vision my pangs have turned upon me, and I have retained no strength.'
'And how is this servant of my lord able to speak with this my lord? As for me, from now on no strength remains in me, and no breath is left in me.'
And again he touched me, one like the appearance of a human being, and strengthened me.
And he said, 'Do not fear, greatly precious man; peace to you. Be strong, and be strong.' And as he spoke with me I was strengthened, and I said, 'Let my lord speak, for you have strengthened me.'
And he said, 'Do you know why I have come to you? And now I will return to fight with the prince of Persia; and as I go out, behold, the prince of Greece is coming.'
'But I will tell you what is inscribed in a writing of truth. And there is none who stands strong with me against these except Michael your prince.'

daniel_11.t: 'And as for me, in the first year of Darius the Mede, I took my stand to strengthen and protect him.'

'And now I will tell you the truth. Behold, three more kings are about to arise for Persia, and the fourth will gain great wealth, more than all of them; and by his strength, through his wealth, he will stir up everyone against the kingdom of Greece.'
'And a mighty king will arise; he will rule with great dominion and do as he pleases.'

'And as soon as he has arisen, his kingdom will be broken up and divided to the four winds of the heavens — not to his posterity, and not according to the dominion with which he ruled; for his kingdom will be plucked up, and given to others besides these.'
'And the king of the south will become strong, and one of his commanders; but that one will become stronger than he and will exercise dominion — his dominion will be a great dominion.'

'And at the end of years they will make an alliance: the daughter of the king of the south will come to the king of the north to make an agreement. But she will not retain the power of the arm, and he will not stand, nor his arm; and she will be given up — she and those who brought her, and the one who fathered her, and the one who strengthened her in those times.'
'And one from the shoot of her roots will arise in his place; he will come against the army and enter the stronghold of the king of the north, and he will act against them and prevail.'
'And also their gods, with their molten images and their precious vessels of silver and gold, he will carry into captivity to Egypt; and for years he will stand away from the king of the north.'
'And he will come into the kingdom of the king of the south, and then return to his own land.'
'And his sons will wage war and gather a multitude of great armies; and one will surely come and overflow and pass over, and then return and wage war as far as his stronghold.'

'And the king of the south will be enraged; he will go out and fight with him, with the king of the north. And that one will raise up a great multitude, but the multitude will be given into his hand.'
'And the multitude will be carried off, and his heart will be lifted up; he will make tens of thousands fall, but he will not prevail.'
'And the king of the north will return and raise up a multitude greater than the first; and at the end of the times, after years, he will surely come with a large army and much equipment.'
'And in those times many will arise against the king of the south; and the sons of the violent ones among your people will exalt themselves to fulfil the vision, but they will stumble.'

'And the king of the north will come and throw up a siege mound and capture a fortified city; and the forces of the south will not stand, nor his chosen troops, and there will be no strength to stand.'
'And the one who comes against him will do as he pleases, and there will be none standing before him; and he will stand in the land of beauty, with complete destruction in his hand.'

'And he will set his face to come with the power of his whole kingdom, and terms of agreement with him; and he will act. And he will give him the daughter of women, to destroy her; but she will not stand, and she will not be his.'
'And he will set his face to the coastlands and capture many. But a commander will put an end to the scorn he offers; without his scorn, he will turn it back on him.'
'And he will turn his face to the strongholds of his own land; and he will stumble and fall, and not be found.'
'And there will arise in his place one who sends an oppressor through the splendour of a kingdom; and in a few days he will be broken, but not in anger and not in battle.'
'And there will arise in his place a despicable one, on whom the honour of royalty has not been conferred; and he will come in a time of quiet and take hold of royalty by intrigues.'
'And the forces of the flood will be swept away from before him and broken; and also a prince of a covenant.'
'And from the time an alliance is made with him he will act deceitfully; and he will rise and become mighty with a small nation.'

'In a time of quiet he will come into the fertile places of the province, and do what his fathers and his fathers' fathers did not do: he will scatter plunder and booty and property among them, and against strongholds he will lay his plans — but only for a time.'

'And he will stir up his strength and his heart against the king of the south with a large army; and the king of the south will make ready for battle with an exceedingly large and mighty army. But he will not stand, for plans will be laid against him.'
'And those who eat his delicacies will break him; his army will be swept away, and many slain will fall.'
'And as for the two kings, their heart is bent on evil, and at one table they will speak falsehood. But it will not succeed, for the end is still for the appointed time.'
'And he will return to his own land with great property, and his heart will be against the covenant of holiness. He will act, and return to his own land.'
'At the appointed time he will return and come into the south; but it will not be as the former time or as the latter.'

'And ships of Kittim will come against him, and he will be disheartened. He will turn back and direct his indignation against the covenant of holiness, and he will act; and he will turn back and give attention to those who forsake the covenant of holiness.'
'And forces from him will arise; they will profane the sanctuary, the stronghold, abolish the perpetual offering, and set up the detestable thing that desolates.'
'And those who act wickedly against the covenant he will pollute with flattering words; but a people who know their God will display strength and act.'
'And those who have insight among the people will give understanding to the many; but they will stumble by sword and by flame, by captivity and by plunder, for days.'
'And when they stumble they will be helped with a little help; and many will join themselves to them with intrigues.'
'And some of those who have insight will stumble, so as to refine among them and to purge and to make white, until the time of the end; for it is still for the appointed time.'

'And the king will do as he pleases; he will exalt himself and magnify himself above every god, and against the God of gods he will speak extraordinary things. And he will succeed until the indignation is completed, for what is decreed will be done.'
'And he will pay no attention to the gods of his fathers, nor to the one desired by women, nor to any god; for above all he will magnify himself.'
'But to a god of strongholds, in its place, he will give honour; and to a god whom his fathers did not know he will give honour with gold and silver and costly stone and precious things.'

'And he will act against the fortresses of strongholds with a foreign god; whoever acknowledges him he will increase in honour, and he will make them rule over the many, and he will divide land for a price.'

'And at the time of the end the king of the south will wage war with him; and the king of the north will storm against him with chariotry and horsemen and many ships, and he will come into lands and overflow and pass through.'
'And he will come into the land of beauty, and many will stumble; but these will escape from his hand: Edom and Moab and the first of the people of Ammon.'
'And he will stretch out his hand against lands, and the land of Egypt will not escape.'
'And he will rule over the treasures of gold and silver and over all the precious things of Egypt; and Libyans and Cushites will be in his train.'
'But reports from the east and from the north will dismay him, and he will go out in great rage to destroy and to devote many to destruction.'
'And he will pitch the tents of his palace between the seas and the mountain of the beauty of holiness; and he will come to his end, and there will be no helper for him.'

daniel_12.t: 'And at that time Michael, the great prince who stands over the sons of your people, will arise. And there will be a time of distress such as has not happened since a nation came to be until that time; and at that time your people will escape — everyone who is found written in the scroll.'
'And many of those who sleep in the ground of dust will awake — these to everlasting life, and these to reproaches, to everlasting abhorrence.'
'And those who have insight will shine like the shining of the vault, and those who turn the many to righteousness like the stars, for ever and ever.'
'And you, Daniel, keep the words secret and seal up the scroll until the time of the end. Many will rove about, and knowledge will increase.'
And I, Daniel, looked, and behold, two others were standing, one on this bank of the River and one on that bank of the River.
And one said to the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the River, 'Until when is the end of the wonders?'

And I heard the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the River; and he raised his right hand and his left to the heavens and swore by the one who lives for ever: that it is for a time, times and a half; and when the shattering of the hand of the people of holiness is finished, all these things will be finished.
And I heard, but I did not understand; and I said, 'My lord, what will be the latter part of these things?'
And he said, 'Go, Daniel, for the things are kept secret and sealed up until the time of the end.'
'Many will purge themselves and make themselves white and be refined; and the wicked will act wickedly, and none of the wicked will understand — but those who have insight will understand.'
'And from the time the perpetual offering is abolished, and the setting up of the detestable thing that desolates, will be a thousand two hundred and ninety days.'
'How blessed is the one who waits and reaches a thousand three hundred and thirty-five days!'
'And you, go to the end; and you will rest, and you will arise to your allotted portion at the end of the days.'

deuteronomy_1.t: These are the words that Moses spoke to all Israel across the Jordan, in the wilderness, in the desert plain opposite Suph, between Paran and Tophel and Laban and Hazeroth and Di Zahab.
It is eleven days from Horeb by the way of Mount Seir to Kadesh Barnea.
In the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, Moses spoke to the Israelites according to all that the LORD had commanded him for them.
This was after he had struck down Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth, at Edrei.
Across the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses undertook to make this law plain, saying:
The LORD our God spoke to us at Horeb: "You have stayed long enough at this mountain.

Turn and set out and go to the hill country of the Amorites and to all their neighbours — in the desert plain, the hill country, the Shephelah, the Negev, and along the seacoast — the land of the Canaanites, and Lebanon, as far as the great river, the river Euphrates.

See, I have set the land before you. Go in and take possession of the land that the LORD swore to your ancestors — to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob — to give to them and to their offspring after them.
At that time I said to you, "I am not able to bear you by myself.
The LORD your God has multiplied you, and today you are as many as the stars of the heavens.
May the LORD, the God of your ancestors, add to you a thousand times as many as you are, and may he bless you as he has promised you.
How can I bear your load and your burden and your disputes by myself?
Choose for yourselves men who are wise and understanding and experienced, from your tribes, and I will appoint them as your heads.
And you answered me and said, "What you have said is a good thing to do."

So I took the heads of your tribes, men who were wise and experienced, and appointed them as heads over you — leaders of thousands, leaders of hundreds, leaders of fifties and leaders of tens, and officials for your tribes.
And at that time I commanded your judges: "Hear the cases between your brothers and judge rightly between a man and his brother, and between a man and the sojourner with him.

You shall not show partiality in judgement. You shall hear the small and the great alike. You shall not be afraid of anyone, for the judgement belongs to God. And any matter that is too hard for you, bring to me, and I will hear it."
And at that time I commanded you all the things you were to do.

Then we set out from Horeb and went through all that great and awesome wilderness which you saw, by the way of the hill country of the Amorites, just as the LORD our God had commanded us, and we came to Kadesh Barnea.
And I said to you, "You have come to the hill country of the Amorites, which the LORD our God is giving us.
See, the LORD your God has set the land before you. Go up and take possession of it, just as the LORD, the God of your ancestors, has said to you. Do not be afraid and do not be dismayed."
Then all of you came to me and said, "Let us send men ahead of us to search out the land for us and bring us back word about the way by which we should go up and the cities we should come to."
The plan seemed good to me, and I took twelve men from among you, one man for each tribe.
They turned and went up into the hill country and came to the Wadi Eshcol, and they spied it out.
They took some of the fruit of the land in their hands and brought it down to us, and they brought word back to us and said, "The land that the LORD our God is giving us is good."
But you were not willing to go up, and you rebelled against the command of the LORD your God.
And you murmured in your tents and said, "It is because the LORD hated us that he brought us out of the land of Egypt, to hand us over to the Amorites and destroy us.

Where are we going up to? Our brothers have made our hearts melt, saying, 'The people are greater and taller than we are; the cities are great and fortified up to the heavens; and we even saw the sons of the Anakim there.'"
And I said to you, "Do not be terrified and do not be afraid of them.
The LORD your God, who goes before you, he himself will fight for you, just as he did for you in Egypt before your eyes,
and in the wilderness, where you saw that the LORD your God carried you as a man carries his son, all the way that you went until you came to this place."
Yet in this matter you did not trust the LORD your God,
who went before you on the way to seek out a place for you to camp — in the fire by night, to show you the way you should go, and in the cloud by day.
