And the LORD heard the sound of your words, and he was angry and swore an oath:
"Not one of these men, this evil generation, shall see the good land that I swore to give to your ancestors —
"except Caleb son of Jephunneh. He shall see it, and to him and to his sons I will give the land on which he has trodden, because he followed the LORD fully.
The LORD was angry with me too, because of you, and said, 'You also shall not go in there.'
Joshua son of Nun, who stands before you, he shall go in there. Strengthen him, for he is the one who will give Israel possession of it.

And your little ones, of whom you said they would become plunder, and your children, who today do not know good from evil — they shall go in there. To them I will give it, and they shall take possession of it.
But as for you, turn and set out toward the wilderness, by the way of the Sea of Reeds."

Then you answered and said to me, "We have sinned against the LORD. We ourselves will go up and fight, just as the LORD our God commanded us." And every man of you strapped on his weapons of war, and you thought it an easy thing to go up into the hill country.
But the LORD said to me, "Say to them: Do not go up and do not fight, for I am not in your midst, or you will be struck down before your enemies."
So I spoke to you, and you did not listen. You rebelled against the command of the LORD, and you acted presumptuously and went up into the hill country.
And the Amorites who lived in that hill country came out to meet you and pursued you as bees do, and they beat you down in Seir as far as Hormah.
And you returned and wept before the LORD, but the LORD did not listen to your voice and did not give ear to you.
And you stayed at Kadesh many days — as many days as you stayed.

deuteronomy_2.t: Then we turned and set out toward the wilderness by the way of the Sea of Reeds, just as the LORD had spoken to me, and we went around the hill country of Seir for many days.
And the LORD said to me:
"You have gone around this hill country long enough. Turn northward.
And command the people: 'You are about to pass through the territory of your brothers, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir, and they will be afraid of you. So be very careful.
Do not provoke them, for I will not give you any of their land, not so much as a footstep's worth, because I have given the hill country of Seir to Esau as a possession.
You shall buy food from them with silver, and eat; and you shall buy water from them with silver, and drink.

For the LORD your God has blessed you in all the work of your hands. He has known your going through this great wilderness. These forty years the LORD your God has been with you; you have lacked nothing.

So we passed on, away from our brothers the descendants of Esau who live in Seir, away from the road of the desert plain, from Elath and from Ezion Geber. Then we turned and passed along the way of the wilderness of Moab.

And the LORD said to me, "Do not harass Moab and do not provoke them to battle, for I will not give you any of their land as a possession, because I have given Ar to the descendants of Lot as a possession.
The Emim formerly lived there — a people great and numerous and tall, like the Anakim.
They too were reckoned as Rephaim, like the Anakim, and the Moabites call them Emim.

And in Seir the Horites formerly lived, and the descendants of Esau dispossessed them and destroyed them before them and settled in their place — just as Israel did to the land of its possession, which the LORD gave them.
'Now arise and cross the Wadi Zered.' So we crossed the Wadi Zered.

And the time we travelled from Kadesh Barnea until we crossed the Wadi Zered was thirty-eight years, until the whole generation, the men of war, had died out from the midst of the camp, just as the LORD had sworn to them.
And the hand of the LORD was also against them, to rout them from the midst of the camp until they were finished.
And when all the men of war had finished dying out from among the people,
the LORD spoke to me:
"Today you are passing through the territory of Moab, that is, Ar.

And you will come near, opposite the Ammonites. Do not harass them and do not provoke them, for I will not give you any of the land of the Ammonites as a possession, because I have given it to the descendants of Lot as a possession.
That too was reckoned a land of Rephaim. Rephaim formerly lived there, and the Ammonites call them Zamzummim.
a people great and numerous and tall, like the Anakim. But the LORD destroyed them before them, and they dispossessed them and settled in their place —
just as he did for the descendants of Esau who live in Seir, when he destroyed the Horites before them, and they dispossessed them and have lived in their place to this day.
And as for the Avvim, who lived in villages as far as Gaza — the Caphtorim, who came out from Caphtor, destroyed them and settled in their place.
'Arise, set out and cross the Wadi Arnon. See, I have given into your hand Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land. Begin to take possession, and provoke him to battle.
This day I begin to put the dread and fear of you on the face of the peoples under all the heavens. They will hear the report of you, and they will tremble and be in anguish because of you.'
Then I sent messengers from the wilderness of Kedemoth to Sihon king of Heshbon with words of peace:
'Let me pass through your land. I will keep to the road; I will not turn aside to the right or to the left.
Sell me food for silver, and I will eat; give me water for silver, and I will drink. Only let me pass through on foot —
just as the descendants of Esau who live in Seir did for me, and the Moabites who live in Ar — until I cross the Jordan into the land that the LORD our God is giving us.'

But Sihon king of Heshbon was not willing to let us pass through his land, for the LORD your God had hardened his spirit and made his heart obstinate, in order to give him into your hand, as he has this day.
And the LORD said to me, "See, I have begun to give Sihon and his land over to you. Begin to take possession, so as to possess his land."
Then Sihon came out to meet us, he and all his people, to do battle at Jahaz.
And the LORD our God gave him over to us, and we struck him down, and his sons, and all his people.
And at that time we captured all his cities, and we devoted to destruction every city — the men, the women and the little ones. We left no survivor.
Only the livestock we took as plunder for ourselves, along with the spoil of the cities we had captured.
From Aroer, which is on the edge of the Wadi Arnon, and the city that is in the wadi, as far as Gilead, there was no town too high for us. The LORD our God gave everything over to us.
Only to the land of the Ammonites you did not go near — all along the side of the Wadi Jabbok, and the cities of the hill country, and wherever the LORD our God had commanded.

deuteronomy_3.t: Then we turned and went up by the way of Bashan, and Og king of Bashan came out to meet us, he and all his people, to do battle at Edrei.

And the LORD said to me, "Do not fear him, for I have given him into your hand, and all his people and his land, and you shall do to him just as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon."
So the LORD our God gave into our hand also Og king of Bashan and all his people, and we struck him down until no survivor was left to him.
And at that time we captured all his cities. There was no town that we did not take from them — sixty cities, the whole region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
All these were fortified cities with a high wall, double gates and a bar, besides a great many unwalled towns.
And we devoted them to destruction, just as we had done to Sihon king of Heshbon — devoting to destruction every city, the men, the women and the little ones.
But all the livestock and the spoil of the cities we took as plunder for ourselves.
So at that time we took the land from the hand of the two kings of the Amorites who were across the Jordan, from the Wadi Arnon as far as Mount Hermon —
(the Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir)
— all the cities of the plateau, and all Gilead, and all Bashan, as far as Salecah and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

For only Og king of Bashan was left of the remnant of the Rephaim. His bed was a bed of iron — is it not in Rabbah of the Ammonites? Nine cubits was its length and four cubits its breadth, by the ordinary cubit.
And this land we took possession of at that time. From Aroer, which is by the Wadi Arnon, and half the hill country of Gilead with its cities, I gave to the Reubenites and the Gadites.
And the rest of Gilead and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, I gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh — all the region of Argob, all that part of Bashan; it is called the land of Rephaim.
Jair son of Manasseh took all the region of Argob, as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and he called them, that is Bashan, by his own name: Havvoth Jair, to this day.
And to Makir I gave Gilead.

And to the Reubenites and the Gadites I gave the territory from Gilead as far as the Wadi Arnon, the middle of the wadi being the boundary, and as far as the Jabbok, the wadi that is the border of the Ammonites;
and the Arabah, with the Jordan as its boundary, from Kinnereth as far as the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, under the slopes of Pisgah on the east.

And at that time I commanded you: "The LORD your God has given you this land to take possession of it. You shall cross over equipped for battle, ahead of your brothers the Israelites — all of you who are men of valour.
Only your wives and your little ones and your livestock — I know that you have much livestock — shall remain in your cities that I have given you,

until the LORD gives rest to your brothers as he has to you, and they also take possession of the land that the LORD your God is giving them across the Jordan. Then each of you shall return to his possession, which I have given you."
And at that time I commanded Joshua: "Your own eyes have seen all that the LORD your God did to these two kings. So the LORD will do to all the kingdoms into which you are crossing over.
You shall not fear them, for the LORD your God, he himself is the one who fights for you."
And at that time I pleaded with the LORD:
"Lord GOD, you have begun to show your servant your greatness and your strong hand. For what god is there in the heavens or on the earth who can do according to your works and your mighty deeds?
Please let me cross over and see the good land that is across the Jordan, this good hill country, and Lebanon."
But the LORD was furious with me on your account and would not listen to me. And the LORD said to me, "Enough from you. Do not speak to me again about this matter.
Go up to the top of Pisgah and lift up your eyes west and north and south and east, and see it with your own eyes, for you shall not cross this Jordan.
But commission Joshua and encourage him and strengthen him, for he shall cross over ahead of this people, and he shall give them possession of the land that you will see."
And we stayed in the valley opposite Beth Peor.

deuteronomy_4.t: And now, Israel, listen to the statutes and the ordinances that I am teaching you to do, so that you may live and go in and take possession of the land that the LORD, the God of your ancestors, is giving you.
You shall not add to the word that I am commanding you, and you shall not take away from it, so that you may keep the commandments of the LORD your God, which I am commanding you.
Your own eyes saw what the LORD did at Baal Peor, for every man who followed Baal Peor — the LORD your God destroyed him from among you.
But you who clung to the LORD your God are all alive today.
See, I have taught you statutes and ordinances, just as the LORD my God commanded me, that you should do them in the land you are entering to take possession of it.

You shall keep them and do them, for that is your wisdom and your understanding in the eyes of the peoples, who will hear all these statutes and say, "Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people."
For what great nation is there that has a god near to it as the LORD our God is to us whenever we call on him?
And what great nation is there that has statutes and ordinances as righteous as all this law that I am setting before you today?

Only take heed to yourself and guard yourself carefully, so that you do not forget the things your eyes have seen, and so that they do not depart from your heart all the days of your life. And you shall make them known to your children and your children's children —

the day when you stood before the LORD your God at Horeb, when the LORD said to me, "Assemble the people to me, and I will let them hear my words, so that they may learn to fear me all the days they live on the ground, and may teach them to their children."
And you came near and stood at the foot of the mountain, and the mountain was burning with fire up to the heart of the heavens — darkness, cloud and thick darkness.
And the LORD spoke to you from the midst of the fire. You heard the sound of words, but you saw no form — only a voice.
And he declared to you his covenant, which he commanded you to do: the ten words. And he wrote them on two tablets of stone.
And me the LORD commanded at that time to teach you statutes and ordinances, for you to do them in the land into which you are crossing over to take possession of it.
So take great heed to yourselves — for you saw no form on the day the LORD spoke to you at Horeb from the midst of the fire —
lest you act corruptly and make for yourselves a carved image, a form of any figure — a likeness of male or female,
a likeness of any animal that is on the earth, a likeness of any winged bird that flies in the heavens,
a likeness of anything that creeps on the ground, a likeness of any fish that is in the waters beneath the earth.

and lest you lift up your eyes to the heavens and see the sun and the moon and the stars, all the host of the heavens, and be drawn away and bow down to them and serve them — things that the LORD your God has allotted to all the peoples under all the heavens.
But you the LORD took, and he brought you out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be for him a people of inheritance, as you are this day.
And the LORD was angry with me on account of your words, and he swore that I should not cross the Jordan and should not enter the good land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.
For I am to die in this land; I am not crossing the Jordan. But you are crossing over, and you shall take possession of this good land.

Take heed to yourselves, lest you forget the covenant of the LORD your God that he made with you, and make for yourselves a carved image, a form of anything, which the LORD your God has forbidden you.
For the LORD your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God.

When you have fathered children and children's children and have grown old in the land, and you act corruptly and make a carved image, a form of anything, and do what is evil in the eyes of the LORD your God, provoking him to anger —

I call the heavens and the earth as witnesses against you today, that you shall quickly and utterly perish from the land into which you are crossing the Jordan to take possession of it. You shall not prolong your days upon it, for you shall be utterly destroyed.
And the LORD will scatter you among the peoples, and you will be left few in number among the nations to which the LORD will drive you.
And there you will serve gods that are the work of human hands, wood and stone, which do not see or hear or eat or smell.
But from there you will seek the LORD your God, and you will find him, if you search for him with all your heart and with all your soul.
In your distress, when all these things have come upon you, in the latter days, you will return to the LORD your God and listen to his voice.
For the LORD your God is a compassionate God. He will not abandon you or destroy you, and he will not forget the covenant with your ancestors that he swore to them.

For ask now about the former days that were before you, from the day when God created humankind on the earth, and from one end of the heavens to the other: has anything like this great thing ever happened, or has anything like it been heard?
Has any people heard the voice of God speaking from the midst of the fire, as you have heard, and lived?

Or has any god attempted to come and take for himself a nation from the midst of another nation, by trials, by signs and wonders, by battle and a strong hand and an outstretched arm and great terrors, according to all that the LORD your God did for you in Egypt before your eyes?
You yourself were shown these things, so that you would know that the LORD, he is God; there is no other besides him.
From the heavens he made you hear his voice, to discipline you; and on the earth he showed you his great fire, and you heard his words from the midst of the fire.
And because he loved your ancestors, he chose their offspring after them, and he brought you out by his own presence, by his great power, from Egypt,
to dispossess before you nations greater and mightier than you, to bring you in and give you their land as an inheritance, as it is this day.
So know today, and take it to heart, that the LORD, he is God in the heavens above and on the earth beneath; there is no other.

And you shall keep his statutes and his commandments, which I am commanding you today, so that it may go well with you and with your children after you, and so that you may prolong your days upon the ground that the LORD your God is giving you for all time.
Then Moses set apart three cities across the Jordan, toward the sunrise,
so that a killer might flee there who kills his neighbour without intent, not having hated him previously; he shall flee to one of these cities and live —
Bezer in the wilderness, in the land of the plateau, for the Reubenites; Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites; and Golan in Bashan for the Manassites.
And this is the law that Moses set before the Israelites.
These are the testimonies, the statutes and the ordinances that Moses spoke to the Israelites when they came out of Egypt,
across the Jordan, in the valley opposite Beth Peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, whom Moses and the Israelites struck down when they came out of Egypt.
And they took possession of his land and the land of Og king of Bashan, the two kings of the Amorites who were across the Jordan, toward the sunrise,
from Aroer, which is on the edge of the Wadi Arnon, as far as Mount Siyon (that is, Hermon),
and all the Arabah across the Jordan on the east, as far as the Sea of the Arabah, under the slopes of Pisgah.

deuteronomy_5.t: And Moses summoned all Israel and said to them: "Hear, Israel, the statutes and the ordinances that I am speaking in your ears today. Learn them and keep them, and do them.
The LORD our God made a covenant with us at Horeb.
It was not with our ancestors that the LORD made this covenant, but with us — with us, these here today, all of us alive.
Face to face the LORD spoke with you at the mountain, out of the midst of the fire.
I was standing between the LORD and you at that time, to declare to you the word of the LORD — for you were afraid because of the fire and did not go up the mountain. He said:
"I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of a house of slaves.
"You shall have no other gods before my face.
"You shall not make for yourself a carved image of any form that is in the heavens above, or on the earth beneath, or in the waters beneath the earth.

"You shall not bow down to them and you shall not serve them; for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of fathers upon sons, upon the third generation and upon the fourth, of those who hate me,
"and showing steadfast love to thousands, to those who love me and keep my commandments.
"You shall not take up the name of the LORD your God for emptiness, for the LORD will not leave unpunished the one who takes up his name for emptiness.
"Keep the sabbath day, to set it apart as holy, just as the LORD your God commanded you.
"Six days you shall labour and do all your work,

"but the seventh day is a sabbath to the LORD your God. You shall not do any work — you, or your son or your daughter, or your male servant or your female servant, or your ox or your donkey or any of your livestock, or your sojourner who is within your gates — so that your male servant and your female servant may rest as you do.

"And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God brought you out from there by a strong hand and an outstretched arm. Therefore the LORD your God commanded you to keep the sabbath day.
"Honour your father and your mother, just as the LORD your God commanded you, so that your days may be long and so that it may go well with you upon the ground that the LORD your God is giving you.
"You shall not murder.
"You shall not commit adultery.
"You shall not steal.
"You shall not give empty testimony against your neighbour.

"You shall not covet your neighbour's wife. And you shall not desire your neighbour's house, or his field, or his male servant or his female servant, his ox or his donkey, or anything that is your neighbour's."

These words the LORD spoke to your whole assembly at the mountain, out of the midst of the fire, the cloud and the thick darkness, with a great voice — and he added no more. And he wrote them on two tablets of stone and gave them to me.
And when you heard the voice out of the midst of the darkness, while the mountain was burning with fire, you came near to me — all the heads of your tribes and your elders —

and you said, "See, the LORD our God has shown us his glory and his greatness, and we have heard his voice out of the midst of the fire. Today we have seen that God speaks with a human being and that person lives.
And now, why should we die? For this great fire will consume us. If we go on hearing the voice of the LORD our God any longer, we shall die.
For who of all flesh has heard the voice of the living God speaking out of the midst of the fire, as we have, and lived?
You go near and hear all that the LORD our God says, and you shall speak to us all that the LORD our God speaks to you, and we will listen and do it."

And the LORD heard the sound of your words when you spoke to me, and the LORD said to me, "I have heard the sound of the words of this people, which they spoke to you. They have done well in all that they have spoken.
If only this heart of theirs might remain theirs, to fear me and to keep all my commandments all the days, so that it might go well with them and with their children forever!
Go, say to them: 'Return to your tents.'

But as for you, stand here with me, and I will speak to you the whole commandment and the statutes and the ordinances that you shall teach them, and they shall do them in the land that I am giving them to take possession of it."
So you shall be careful to do just as the LORD your God has commanded you. You shall not turn aside to the right or to the left.
In all the way that the LORD your God has commanded you, you shall walk, so that you may live and it may go well with you, and you may prolong your days in the land that you will take possession of.

deuteronomy_6.t: And this is the commandment — the statutes and the ordinances — that the LORD your God commanded to be taught to you, for you to do in the land into which you are crossing over to take possession of it,

so that you may fear the LORD your God by keeping all his statutes and his commandments that I am commanding you — you and your son and your son's son — all the days of your life, and so that your days may be long.

So hear, Israel, and be careful to do them, so that it may go well with you and so that you may increase greatly, just as the LORD, the God of your ancestors, has promised you — a land flowing with milk and honey.
Hear, Israel: the LORD our God, the LORD is one.
And you shall love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength.
And these words that I am commanding you today shall be upon your heart.
And you shall repeat them to your children, and you shall speak of them when you sit in your house and when you walk on the road, when you lie down and when you rise up.
And you shall bind them as a sign on your hand, and they shall be as marks between your eyes.
And you shall write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates.
And when the LORD your God brings you into the land that he swore to your ancestors, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, to give you — great and good cities that you did not build,
and houses full of every good thing that you did not fill, and hewn cisterns that you did not hew, vineyards and olive trees that you did not plant — and you shall eat and be satisfied;
then take heed to yourself, lest you forget the LORD, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of a house of slaves.
You shall fear the LORD your God, and him you shall serve, and by his name you shall swear.
You shall not go after other gods, from among the gods of the peoples who are around you —
for the LORD your God in your midst is a jealous God — lest the anger of the LORD your God burn against you and he destroy you from the face of the ground.
You shall not put the LORD your God to the test, as you tested him at Massah.
You shall diligently keep the commandments of the LORD your God, and his testimonies and his statutes that he has commanded you.
And you shall do what is right and good in the eyes of the LORD, so that it may go well with you, and you shall go in and take possession of the good land that the LORD swore to your ancestors,
driving out all your enemies from before you, just as the LORD has spoken.
When your son asks you in time to come, "What are the testimonies and the statutes and the ordinances that the LORD our God commanded you?" —
then you shall say to your son, "We were slaves to Pharaoh in Egypt, and the LORD brought us out of Egypt with a strong hand.
And the LORD gave signs and wonders, great and grievous, against Egypt, against Pharaoh and against all his household, before our eyes.
And us he brought out from there, in order to bring us in and give us the land that he swore to our ancestors.
And the LORD commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear the LORD our God, for our good all our days, to keep us alive, as he has this day.
And it will be righteousness for us if we are careful to do all this commandment before the LORD our God, just as he commanded us.

deuteronomy_7.t: When the LORD your God brings you into the land you are entering to take possession of it, and clears away many nations before you — the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, seven nations greater and mightier than you —
and the LORD your God gives them over to you and you strike them down, then you shall utterly devote them to destruction. You shall not make a covenant with them and you shall not show them favour.
And you shall not intermarry with them. You shall not give your daughter to his son, and you shall not take his daughter for your son,
for he would turn your son away from following me, and they would serve other gods, and the anger of the LORD would burn against you, and he would destroy you quickly.
But this is what you shall do to them: you shall break down their altars, shatter their pillars, cut down their Asherim, and burn their images with fire.
For you are a people holy to the LORD your God. The LORD your God chose you to be for him a people of treasured possession out of all the peoples on the face of the ground.
It was not because you were more numerous than all the peoples that the LORD set his love on you and chose you — for you were the fewest of all the peoples —

but because of the LORD's love for you and because he kept the oath that he swore to your ancestors, the LORD brought you out with a strong hand and redeemed you from a house of slaves, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.
And you shall know that the LORD your God, he is God, the faithful God, who keeps the covenant and the steadfast love with those who love him and keep his commandments, to a thousand generations,
and repaying to his face the one who hates him, to destroy him. He will not delay with the one who hates him; to his face he will repay him.
And you shall keep the commandment, the statutes and the ordinances that I am commanding you today, to do them.

And it shall be, in consequence of your hearing these ordinances and keeping and doing them, that the LORD your God will keep for you the covenant and the steadfast love that he swore to your ancestors.

And he will love you and bless you and multiply you, and he will bless the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground — your grain, your new wine and your fresh oil, the offspring of your cattle and the young of your flock — upon the ground that he swore to your ancestors to give you.
You shall be blessed above all the peoples. There shall not be among you a sterile male or a barren female, nor among your livestock.
And the LORD will remove every sickness from you, and none of the grievous diseases of Egypt that you knew will he put on you; he will set them on all who hate you.
And you shall consume all the peoples whom the LORD your God gives over to you. Your eye shall not look with pity on them, and you shall not serve their gods, for that would be a snare to you.
If you say in your heart, "These nations are greater than I am; how can I dispossess them?" —
you shall not be afraid of them. You shall surely remember what the LORD your God did to Pharaoh and to all Egypt —

the great trials that your eyes saw, and the signs and the wonders, and the strong hand and the outstretched arm by which the LORD your God brought you out. So the LORD your God will do to all the peoples of whom you are afraid.
And the LORD your God will also send the hornet among them, until those who remain and those who hide themselves from you perish.
You shall not be terrified of them, for the LORD your God is in your midst, a great and awesome God.
And the LORD your God will clear away these nations before you little by little. You will not be able to finish them off quickly, lest the wild animals increase against you.
And the LORD your God will give them over to you and throw them into great confusion, until they are destroyed.
And he will give their kings into your hand, and you shall destroy their name from under the heavens. No one shall stand before you until you have destroyed them.
The images of their gods you shall burn with fire. You shall not covet the silver and gold on them and take it for yourself, lest you be ensnared by it, for it is an abomination to the LORD your God.
And you shall not bring an abomination into your house, or you will become devoted to destruction like it. You shall utterly detest it and utterly abhor it, for it is devoted to destruction.

deuteronomy_8.t: All the commandment that I am commanding you today you shall be careful to do, so that you may live and increase and go in and take possession of the land that the LORD swore to your ancestors.

And you shall remember all the way that the LORD your God led you these forty years in the wilderness, in order to humble you, to test you, to know what was in your heart — whether you would keep his commandments or not.

And he humbled you and let you hunger, and he fed you the manna, which you did not know and your ancestors did not know, in order to make you know that a human being does not live on bread alone, but a human being lives on every word that comes from the mouth of the LORD.
Your clothing did not wear out on you, and your foot did not swell, these forty years.
And you shall know in your heart that just as a man disciplines his son, so the LORD your God disciplines you.
And you shall keep the commandments of the LORD your God, walking in his ways and fearing him.
For the LORD your God is bringing you into a good land — a land of streams of water, of springs and deeps flowing out in the valley and in the hill country,
a land of wheat and barley, of vine and fig and pomegranate, a land of the oil-olive and of honey,
a land in which you will eat bread without scarcity, in which you will lack nothing; a land whose stones are iron, and from whose hills you will dig copper.
And you shall eat and be satisfied, and you shall bless the LORD your God for the good land that he has given you.
Take heed to yourself, lest you forget the LORD your God by failing to keep his commandments, his ordinances and his statutes, which I am commanding you today —
lest you eat and be satisfied, and build good houses and live in them,
and your herd and your flock increase, and silver and gold increase for you, and all that you have increases,
and your heart is lifted up, and you forget the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of a house of slaves,
who led you through the great and awesome wilderness — fiery serpent and scorpion and thirsty ground where there was no water — who brought water out for you from the flinty rock,
who fed you manna in the wilderness, which your ancestors did not know, in order to humble you and to test you, to do you good in your latter end —
and you say in your heart, "My own strength and the might of my hand have made this wealth for me."
But you shall remember the LORD your God, that it is he who gives you strength to make wealth, in order to confirm his covenant that he swore to your ancestors, as he has this day.
And if you utterly forget the LORD your God and go after other gods and serve them and bow down to them, I testify against you today that you shall utterly perish.
Like the nations that the LORD is destroying before you, so you shall perish, in consequence of your not listening to the voice of the LORD your God.

deuteronomy_9.t: Hear, Israel: today you are crossing the Jordan to go in and dispossess nations greater and mightier than you, cities great and fortified up to the heavens,
a people great and tall, the descendants of the Anakim, whom you know and of whom you have heard it said, "Who can stand before the descendants of Anak?"

And you shall know today that the LORD your God, he himself is the one who crosses over before you, a consuming fire. He will destroy them and subdue them before you, and you shall dispossess them and destroy them quickly, just as the LORD has spoken to you.

Do not say in your heart, when the LORD your God drives them out before you, "It is because of my righteousness that the LORD has brought me in to take possession of this land." It is because of the wickedness of these nations that the LORD is dispossessing them before you.

It is not because of your righteousness or the uprightness of your heart that you are going in to take possession of their land, but because of the wickedness of these nations the LORD your God is dispossessing them before you, and in order to confirm the word that the LORD swore to your ancestors, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob.
And you shall know that it is not because of your righteousness that the LORD your God is giving you this good land to take possession of it, for you are a stiff-necked people.

Remember, do not forget, how you provoked the LORD your God to anger in the wilderness. From the day you came out of the land of Egypt until you came to this place, you have been rebellious against the LORD.
And at Horeb you provoked the LORD to anger, and the LORD was angry with you enough to destroy you.

When I went up the mountain to receive the tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant that the LORD made with you, I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water.

And the LORD gave me the two tablets of stone, written by the finger of God, and on them was written all that the LORD spoke with you on the mountain out of the midst of the fire, on the day of the assembly.
And at the end of forty days and forty nights, the LORD gave me the two tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant.

And the LORD said to me, "Arise, go down quickly from here, for your people whom you brought out of Egypt have acted corruptly. They have turned aside quickly from the way that I commanded them; they have made for themselves a molten image."
And the LORD said to me: "I have seen this people, and behold, they are a stiff-necked people.
Let me alone, and I will destroy them and wipe out their name from under the heavens, and I will make you into a nation mightier and greater than they are."
So I turned and went down from the mountain, and the mountain was burning with fire, and the two tablets of the covenant were on my two hands.
And I saw that you had sinned against the LORD your God. You had made for yourselves a calf of cast metal. You had turned aside quickly from the way that the LORD had commanded you.
And I seized the two tablets and threw them from my two hands, and I broke them before your eyes.

And I fell down before the LORD as at the first, forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water, because of all your sin that you had sinned, in doing what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, provoking him to anger.
For I was afraid because of the anger and the rage with which the LORD was angry against you, enough to destroy you. And the LORD listened to me that time also.
And the LORD was very angry with Aaron, enough to destroy him; and I prayed for Aaron also at that time.

And your sin, which you had made — the calf — I took and burned with fire, and I crushed it, grinding it thoroughly until it was as fine as dust, and I threw its dust into the wadi that comes down from the mountain.
And at Taberah and at Massah and at Kibroth Hattaavah you provoked the LORD to anger.

And when the LORD sent you from Kadesh Barnea, saying, "Go up and take possession of the land that I have given you," you rebelled against the command of the LORD your God, and you did not trust him and did not listen to his voice.
You have been rebellious against the LORD from the day I knew you.
So I fell down before the LORD the forty days and the forty nights that I fell down, for the LORD had said he would destroy you.
And I prayed to the LORD and said, "Lord GOD, do not destroy your people and your inheritance, whom you redeemed by your greatness, whom you brought out of Egypt with a strong hand.
Remember your servants Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Do not turn toward the stubbornness of this people, or its wickedness, or its sin,

lest the land from which you brought us out should say, 'Because the LORD was not able to bring them into the land that he spoke of to them, and because of his hatred of them, he brought them out to put them to death in the wilderness.'
And they are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out by your great strength and by your outstretched arm."

deuteronomy_10.t: At that time the LORD said to me, "Cut for yourself two tablets of stone like the first, and come up to me on the mountain, and make yourself an ark of wood.
And I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke, and you shall put them in the ark."
So I made an ark of acacia wood and cut two tablets of stone like the first, and I went up the mountain with the two tablets in my hand.

And he wrote on the tablets, like the first writing, the ten words that the LORD had spoken to you on the mountain out of the midst of the fire on the day of the assembly; and the LORD gave them to me.
And I turned and came down from the mountain, and I put the tablets in the ark that I had made, and there they have been, just as the LORD commanded me.
(The Israelites set out from Beeroth Bene Jaakan to Moserah. There Aaron died and there he was buried, and Eleazar his son served as priest in his place.
From there they set out to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land of streams of water.
At that time the LORD set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of the covenant of the LORD, to stand before the LORD to serve him, and to bless in his name, to this day.
Therefore Levi has no portion or inheritance with his brothers. The LORD is his inheritance, just as the LORD your God said to him.)
And I stayed on the mountain as at the former time, forty days and forty nights, and the LORD listened to me that time also; the LORD was not willing to destroy you.
And the LORD said to me, "Arise, set out on the journey ahead of the people, so that they may go in and take possession of the land that I swore to their ancestors to give them."

And now, Israel, what does the LORD your God ask of you but to fear the LORD your God, to walk in all his ways and to love him, and to serve the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul,
to keep the commandments of the LORD and his statutes, which I am commanding you today, for your good?
See, to the LORD your God belong the heavens and the heavens of the heavens, the earth and all that is in it.
Yet it was on your ancestors that the LORD set his love, to love them, and he chose their offspring after them — you — out of all the peoples, as it is this day.
And you shall circumcise the foreskin of your heart, and you shall not stiffen your neck again.
For the LORD your God, he is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great, the mighty and the awesome God, who does not show partiality and does not take a bribe,
who executes justice for the fatherless and the widow, and who loves the sojourner, giving him bread and clothing.
And you shall love the sojourner, for you were sojourners in the land of Egypt.
You shall fear the LORD your God; him you shall serve, and to him you shall cling, and by his name you shall swear.
He is your praise and he is your God, who has done for you these great and awesome things that your eyes have seen.
With seventy persons your ancestors went down to Egypt, and now the LORD your God has made you as many as the stars of the heavens.

deuteronomy_11.t: And you shall love the LORD your God and keep his charge, his statutes, his ordinances and his commandments, all the days.
And know today — for I am not speaking with your children, who have not known and have not seen the discipline of the LORD your God, his greatness, his strong hand and his outstretched arm,
and his signs and his deeds that he did in the midst of Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to all his land,
and what he did to the army of Egypt, to its horses and its chariotry, when he made the waters of the Sea of Reeds flow over them as they pursued you, and the LORD destroyed them, to this day;
and what he did to you in the wilderness until you came to this place;

and what he did to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab son of Reuben, when the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and their households and their tents and every living thing that was at their feet, in the midst of all Israel —
for your own eyes have seen all the great work of the LORD that he did.
And you shall keep all the commandment that I am commanding you today, so that you may be strong and go in and take possession of the land into which you are crossing over to take possession of it,
and so that you may prolong your days upon the ground that the LORD swore to your ancestors to give to them and to their offspring, a land flowing with milk and honey.
For the land you are entering to take possession of it is not like the land of Egypt, from which you came out, where you would sow your seed and water it by hand, like a vegetable garden.
But the land into which you are crossing over to take possession of it is a land of mountains and valleys, drinking water from the rain of the heavens,
a land that the LORD your God cares for. The eyes of the LORD your God are continually upon it, from the beginning of the year to the end of the year.
And if you diligently listen to my commandments that I am commanding you today, to love the LORD your God and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul,
then I will give the rain of your land in its season, the early rain and the later rain, and you shall gather your grain, your new wine and your fresh oil.
And I will give grass in your field for your livestock, and you shall eat and be satisfied.
Take heed to yourselves, lest your heart be enticed and you turn aside and serve other gods and bow down to them,

and the anger of the LORD burn against you, and he shut up the heavens so that there is no rain and the ground does not give its produce, and you perish quickly from the good land that the LORD is giving you.
And you shall put these words of mine upon your heart and upon your soul, and you shall bind them as a sign on your hand, and they shall be as marks between your eyes.
And you shall teach them to your children, speaking of them when you sit in your house and when you walk on the road, when you lie down and when you rise up.
And you shall write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates,
so that your days and the days of your children may be many upon the ground that the LORD swore to your ancestors to give them, like the days of the heavens above the earth.
For if you diligently keep all this commandment that I am commanding you to do — to love the LORD your God, to walk in all his ways and to cling to him —
then the LORD will dispossess all these nations before you, and you shall dispossess nations greater and mightier than you.
Every place on which the sole of your foot treads shall be yours. From the wilderness and Lebanon, from the River, the river Euphrates, to the western sea shall be your territory.
No one shall stand before you. The LORD your God will put the dread and fear of you on the face of all the land on which you tread, just as he has said to you.
See, I am setting before you today a blessing and a curse:
the blessing, if you listen to the commandments of the LORD your God that I am commanding you today;
and the curse, if you do not listen to the commandments of the LORD your God, but turn aside from the way that I am commanding you today, to go after other gods that you have not known.
And when the LORD your God brings you into the land you are entering to take possession of it, you shall set the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.
Are they not across the Jordan, beyond the road toward the sunset, in the land of the Canaanites who live in the Arabah, opposite Gilgal, beside the oaks of Moreh?
For you are crossing the Jordan to go in and take possession of the land that the LORD your God is giving you, and you shall take possession of it and live in it.
And you shall be careful to do all the statutes and the ordinances that I am setting before you today.

deuteronomy_12.t: These are the statutes and the ordinances that you shall be careful to do in the land that the LORD, the God of your ancestors, has given you to take possession of it, all the days that you live upon the ground.
You shall utterly destroy all the places where the nations whom you are dispossessing served their gods — on the high mountains and on the hills and under every green tree.
And you shall break down their altars and shatter their pillars, and burn their Asherim with fire, and cut down the images of their gods, and you shall destroy their name from that place.
You shall not do so to the LORD your God.
But to the place that the LORD your God will choose out of all your tribes, to put his name there — to his dwelling you shall resort, and there you shall come.

And you shall bring there your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes and the contribution of your hand, your vows and your freewill offerings, and the firstborn of your herd and of your flock.
And you shall eat there before the LORD your God, and you shall rejoice in every undertaking of your hand, you and your households, in which the LORD your God has blessed you.
You shall not do according to all that we are doing here today, each man doing whatever is right in his own eyes.
For you have not yet come to the resting place and to the inheritance that the LORD your God is giving you.

And you shall cross the Jordan and live in the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, and he will give you rest from all your enemies round about, and you shall live in security.

And to the place that the LORD your God will choose to cause his name to dwell there — there you shall bring all that I am commanding you: your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes and the contribution of your hand, and all the choicest of your vows that you vow to the LORD.

And you shall rejoice before the LORD your God — you and your sons and your daughters, your male servants and your female servants, and the Levite who is within your gates, for he has no portion or inheritance with you.
Take heed to yourself, lest you offer up your burnt offerings in any place that you see.
But in the place that the LORD will choose in one of your tribes, there you shall offer up your burnt offerings, and there you shall do all that I am commanding you.

Only, according to all the desire of your being you may slaughter and eat meat, according to the blessing of the LORD your God that he has given you, within all your gates. The unclean and the clean alike may eat it, as they eat the gazelle and the deer.
Only the blood you shall not eat; you shall pour it out on the ground like water.

You may not eat within your gates the tithe of your grain or your new wine or your fresh oil, or the firstborn of your herd or your flock, or any of your vows that you vow, or your freewill offerings, or the contribution of your hand.

But before the LORD your God you shall eat it, in the place that the LORD your God will choose — you and your son and your daughter, your male servant and your female servant, and the Levite who is within your gates — and you shall rejoice before the LORD your God in every undertaking of your hand.
Take heed to yourself, lest you neglect the Levite all your days upon your ground.
When the LORD your God enlarges your territory, as he promised you, and you say, "Let me eat meat," because you have an appetite for meat, you may eat meat according to all the desire of your being.

If the place that the LORD your God will choose to put his name there is too far from you, then you shall slaughter from your herd and from your flock that the LORD has given you, just as I have commanded you, and you shall eat within your gates according to all the desire of your being.
Surely, just as the gazelle and the deer are eaten, so you shall eat it; the unclean and the clean alike may eat it.
Only be firm in not eating the blood, for the blood is the life, and you shall not eat the life with the meat.
You shall not eat it; you shall pour it out on the ground like water.
You shall not eat it, so that it may go well with you and with your children after you, when you do what is right in the eyes of the LORD.
Only your holy things that you have, and your vows, you shall take and go to the place that the LORD will choose.

And you shall offer your burnt offerings, the flesh and the blood, on the altar of the LORD your God; and the blood of your sacrifices shall be poured out on the altar of the LORD your God, and the flesh you shall eat.

Be careful to hear all these words that I am commanding you, so that it may go well with you and with your children after you forever, when you do what is good and right in the eyes of the LORD your God.
When the LORD your God cuts off before you the nations whom you are going in to dispossess, and you dispossess them and live in their land,

take heed to yourself, lest you be ensnared into following them after they have been destroyed before you, and lest you enquire after their gods, saying, "How did these nations serve their gods? I too will do the same."

You shall not do so to the LORD your God, for every abomination of the LORD, which he hates, they have done for their gods — for they even burn their sons and their daughters in the fire for their gods.
Every word that I am commanding you, that you shall be careful to do. You shall not add to it and you shall not take away from it.

deuteronomy_13.t: If a prophet or a dreamer of dreams arises in your midst and gives you a sign or a wonder,
and the sign or the wonder comes to pass, of which he spoke to you, saying, "Let us go after other gods, whom you have not known, and let us serve them,"

you shall not listen to the words of that prophet or that dreamer of dreams, for the LORD your God is testing you, to know whether you love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
You shall walk after the LORD your God, and him you shall fear, and his commandments you shall keep, and to his voice you shall listen, and him you shall serve, and to him you shall cling.

And that prophet or that dreamer of dreams shall be put to death, for he has spoken rebellion against the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt and redeemed you from a house of slaves, seeking to thrust you aside from the way in which the LORD your God commanded you to walk. So you shall burn out the evil from your midst.

If your brother, the son of your mother, or your son or your daughter, or the wife of your bosom, or your friend who is as your own being, entices you in secret, saying, "Let us go and serve other gods," which you have not known, neither you nor your ancestors —
from among the gods of the peoples who are around you, near you or far from you, from one end of the earth to the other —
you shall not yield to him and you shall not listen to him; your eye shall not look with pity on him, and you shall not spare him or cover for him.
For you shall surely kill him. Your hand shall be against him first, to put him to death, and afterward the hand of all the people.
And you shall stone him with stones so that he dies, for he sought to thrust you aside from the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of a house of slaves.
And all Israel shall hear and fear, and they shall never again do such an evil thing as this in your midst.
If you hear it said of one of your cities that the LORD your God is giving you to live in,
"Worthless men have gone out from your midst and have thrust aside the inhabitants of their city, saying, 'Let us go and serve other gods,' whom you have not known,"
then you shall investigate and search and enquire thoroughly. And if it is true, if the thing is established that this abomination has been done in your midst,
you shall utterly strike the inhabitants of that city with the edge of the sword, devoting it to destruction, and all that is in it, and its livestock, with the edge of the sword.

And all its plunder you shall gather into the middle of its open square, and you shall burn the city and all its plunder with fire, as a whole offering to the LORD your God. And it shall be a mound forever; it shall never be rebuilt.

And nothing of what is devoted to destruction shall cling to your hand, so that the LORD may turn from the burning of his anger and give you compassion, and have compassion on you and multiply you, just as he swore to your ancestors,
when you listen to the voice of the LORD your God, keeping all his commandments that I am commanding you today, doing what is right in the eyes of the LORD your God.

deuteronomy_14.t: You are children to the LORD your God. You shall not cut yourselves, and you shall not make yourselves bald between your eyes for the dead.
For you are a people holy to the LORD your God, and the LORD has chosen you to be for him a people of treasured possession out of all the peoples on the face of the ground.
You shall not eat any abomination.
These are the animals that you may eat: the ox, the sheep and the goat,
the deer, the gazelle and the roebuck, the wild goat, the ibex, the antelope and the mountain sheep.
And every animal that has a divided hoof, cleft right through into two hooves, and chews the cud among the animals — that you may eat.

Nevertheless, of those that chew the cud and of those that have a divided, cloven hoof, you shall not eat these: the camel, the hare and the rock hyrax, for they chew the cud but do not have a divided hoof — they are unclean for you.
And the pig, for it has a divided hoof but does not chew the cud — it is unclean for you. You shall not eat their meat, and you shall not touch their carcasses.
These you may eat, of all that is in the water: everything that has fins and scales you may eat.
And everything that does not have fins and scales you shall not eat; it is unclean for you.
Every clean bird you may eat.
And these are the ones of which you shall not eat: the eagle, the bearded vulture, the black vulture,
and the red kite, the falcon, and the kite of every kind,
and every raven of every kind,
and the ostrich, the owl, the gull, the hawk of every kind,
the little owl, the great owl, the white owl,
and the desert owl, the carrion vulture, the cormorant,
and the stork, the heron of every kind, the hoopoe and the bat.
And every winged swarming creature is unclean for you; they shall not be eaten.
Every clean winged creature you may eat.

You shall not eat any carcass. You may give it to the sojourner who is within your gates, and he may eat it, or you may sell it to a foreigner; for you are a people holy to the LORD your God. You shall not boil a kid in its mother's milk.
You shall surely tithe all the produce of your seed that comes out of the field, year by year.

And you shall eat before the LORD your God, in the place that he will choose to cause his name to dwell there, the tithe of your grain, your new wine and your fresh oil, and the firstborn of your herd and of your flock, so that you may learn to fear the LORD your God all the days.

And if the way is too long for you, so that you are not able to carry it, because the place that the LORD your God will choose to put his name there is too far from you — for the LORD your God will bless you —
then you shall exchange it for silver, and bind up the silver in your hand, and go to the place that the LORD your God will choose.

And you shall spend the silver on whatever your appetite desires — on cattle, on flock, on wine, on strong drink, on whatever your appetite asks of you — and you shall eat there before the LORD your God and rejoice, you and your household.
And the Levite who is within your gates — you shall not neglect him, for he has no portion or inheritance with you.
At the end of three years you shall bring out all the tithe of your produce in that year, and you shall deposit it within your gates.

And the Levite shall come — for he has no portion or inheritance with you — and the sojourner, the fatherless and the widow who are within your gates, and they shall eat and be satisfied, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hand that you do.

deuteronomy_15.t: At the end of seven years you shall make a release.

And this is the manner of the release: every creditor shall release the loan of his hand that he has lent to his neighbour. He shall not press his neighbour or his brother, for a release has been proclaimed for the LORD.
You may press the foreigner, but whatever of yours is with your brother your hand shall release.
Nevertheless, there shall be no needy person among you, for the LORD will surely bless you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance to take possession of it —
only if you diligently listen to the voice of the LORD your God, to be careful to do all this commandment that I am commanding you today.
For the LORD your God has blessed you, as he promised you, and you shall lend to many nations but you shall not borrow; and you shall rule over many nations, but over you they shall not rule.

If there is among you a needy person, one of your brothers, in any of your gates in your land that the LORD your God is giving you, you shall not harden your heart and you shall not shut your hand against your needy brother.
For you shall surely open your hand to him, and you shall surely lend him enough for his lack, whatever he lacks.

Take heed to yourself, lest there be a worthless thought in your heart, saying, "The seventh year, the year of release, has drawn near," and your eye be evil toward your needy brother and you give him nothing, and he cry out against you to the LORD, and it be sin on you.

You shall surely give to him, and your heart shall not be grieved when you give to him, for on account of this thing the LORD your God will bless you in all your work and in every undertaking of your hand.
For the needy will not cease from the midst of the land. Therefore I am commanding you: You shall surely open your hand to your brother, to your poor and to your needy in your land.
If your brother, a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman, is sold to you, he shall serve you six years, and in the seventh year you shall send him out free from you.
And when you send him out free from you, you shall not send him out empty-handed.
You shall surely furnish him from your flock, from your threshing floor and from your winepress. As the LORD your God has blessed you, so you shall give to him.
And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed you. Therefore I am commanding you this thing today.
And if he says to you, "I will not go out from you," because he loves you and your household, because it is good for him with you,
then you shall take the awl and put it through his ear into the door, and he shall be your slave forever. And to your maidservant also you shall do the same.
It shall not seem hard to you when you send him out free from you, for he has served you six years at double the wage of a hired worker; and the LORD your God will bless you in all that you do.

Every firstborn male that is born in your herd and in your flock you shall set apart as holy to the LORD your God. You shall not work with the firstborn of your ox, and you shall not shear the firstborn of your flock.
Before the LORD your God you shall eat it, year by year, in the place that the LORD will choose, you and your household.
And if there is a blemish in it — lame or blind, any serious blemish — you shall not sacrifice it to the LORD your God.
Within your gates you shall eat it, the unclean and the clean alike, as they eat the gazelle and the deer.
Only its blood you shall not eat; you shall pour it out on the ground like water.

deuteronomy_16.t: Keep the month of Abib and make the passover to the LORD your God, for in the month of Abib the LORD your God brought you out of Egypt by night.
And you shall sacrifice the passover to the LORD your God, from the flock and from the herd, in the place that the LORD will choose to cause his name to dwell there.

You shall not eat leavened bread with it. Seven days you shall eat with it unleavened bread, the bread of affliction — for in haste you came out of the land of Egypt — so that you may remember the day of your coming out of the land of Egypt all the days of your life.
And no leaven shall be seen with you in all your territory for seven days, and none of the meat that you sacrifice in the evening on the first day shall remain overnight until morning.
You may not sacrifice the passover in any of your gates that the LORD your God is giving you,

but at the place that the LORD your God will choose to cause his name to dwell there, there you shall sacrifice the passover in the evening, as the sun goes down, at the appointed time of your coming out of Egypt.
And you shall cook it and eat it in the place that the LORD your God will choose, and in the morning you shall turn and go to your tents.
Six days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there shall be a solemn assembly to the LORD your God. You shall do no work.
Seven weeks you shall count for yourself; from the time the sickle first goes into the standing grain you shall begin to count seven weeks.
And you shall keep a festival of weeks to the LORD your God, with the tribute of a freewill offering of your hand that you give, according as the LORD your God blesses you.

And you shall rejoice before the LORD your God — you and your son and your daughter, your male servant and your female servant, and the Levite who is within your gates, and the sojourner, the fatherless and the widow who are in your midst — in the place that the LORD your God will choose to cause his name to dwell there.
And you shall remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and you shall be careful to do these statutes.
You shall keep the festival of booths for yourself seven days, when you gather in from your threshing floor and from your winepress.

And you shall rejoice in your festival — you and your son and your daughter, your male servant and your female servant, and the Levite, the sojourner, the fatherless and the widow who are within your gates.

Seven days you shall keep the festival to the LORD your God in the place that the LORD will choose, for the LORD your God will bless you in all your produce and in all the work of your hands, and you shall be altogether joyful.

Three times in the year every male of yours shall appear before the face of the LORD your God in the place that he will choose: at the festival of unleavened bread, at the festival of weeks, and at the festival of booths. And he shall not appear before the face of the LORD empty-handed.
Each man according to the gift of his hand, according to the blessing of the LORD your God that he has given you.
You shall appoint judges and officials for yourself in all your gates that the LORD your God is giving you, according to your tribes, and they shall judge the people with righteous judgement.
You shall not pervert judgement. You shall not show partiality. And you shall not take a bribe, for the bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and twists the words of the righteous.
Righteousness, righteousness you shall pursue, so that you may live and take possession of the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
You shall not plant for yourself an Asherah of any wood beside the altar of the LORD your God that you shall make for yourself.
And you shall not set up for yourself a pillar, which the LORD your God hates.

deuteronomy_17.t: You shall not sacrifice to the LORD your God an ox or a sheep in which there is a blemish, any serious defect, for that is an abomination to the LORD your God.
If there is found in your midst, in any of your gates that the LORD your God is giving you, a man or a woman who does what is evil in the eyes of the LORD your God, transgressing his covenant,
and has gone and served other gods and bowed down to them — to the sun or the moon or all the host of the heavens, which I have not commanded —
and it is told to you and you hear it, then you shall investigate thoroughly. And if it is true, if the thing is established that this abomination has been done in Israel,
then you shall bring out to your gates that man or that woman who has done this evil thing — the man or the woman — and you shall stone them with stones, and they shall die.
On the testimony of two witnesses or three witnesses the one who is to die shall be put to death. He shall not be put to death on the testimony of one witness.
The hand of the witnesses shall be against him first, to put him to death, and afterward the hand of all the people. So you shall burn out the evil from your midst.

If a matter is too difficult for you to judge — between blood and blood, between case and case, between wound and wound, matters of dispute within your gates — then you shall arise and go up to the place that the LORD your God will choose.
And you shall come to the priests, the Levites, and to the judge who is in office in those days, and you shall enquire, and they shall declare to you the word of the verdict.
And you shall act according to the word that they declare to you from that place which the LORD will choose, and you shall be careful to do according to all that they instruct you.

According to the law that they give you, and according to the verdict that they pronounce to you, you shall act. You shall not turn aside from the word that they declare to you, to the right or to the left.

And the man who acts presumptuously, refusing to listen to the priest who stands to serve there before the LORD your God, or to the judge — that man shall die. So you shall burn out the evil from Israel.
And all the people shall hear and fear, and they shall not act presumptuously again.
When you come into the land that the LORD your God is giving you, and you take possession of it and live in it, and you say, "Let me set a king over me, like all the nations that are around me,"

you shall surely set over yourself a king whom the LORD your God will choose. From among your brothers you shall set a king over yourself. You may not put over yourself a foreign man, who is not your brother.
Only he shall not multiply horses for himself, and he shall not make the people return to Egypt in order to multiply horses — for the LORD has said to you, "You shall never return that way again."
And he shall not multiply wives for himself, so that his heart may not turn aside; and silver and gold he shall not multiply for himself excessively.
And when he sits on the throne of his kingdom, he shall write for himself a copy of this law on a scroll, from that which is before the priests, the Levites.
And it shall be with him, and he shall read in it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear the LORD his God, to keep all the words of this law and these statutes, to do them,

so that his heart may not be lifted up above his brothers, and so that he may not turn aside from the commandment, to the right or to the left; and so that he may prolong his days over his kingdom, he and his sons, in the midst of Israel.

deuteronomy_18.t: The priests, the Levites—the whole tribe of Levi—shall have no share or inheritance along with Israel. They are to eat the food offerings of the LORD and his inheritance.
He shall have no inheritance among his kinsmen; the LORD himself is his inheritance, just as he said to him.
This shall be the priests' due from the people, from those who offer a sacrifice, whether ox or sheep: he is to give the priest the foreleg, the two cheeks, and the stomach.
You are to give him the first of your grain, your new wine, and your fresh oil, and the first fleece of your flock.
For the LORD your God has chosen him out of all your tribes to stand and serve in the name of the LORD, he and his sons, for all time.
If a Levite comes from any of your towns anywhere in Israel where he has been living as a sojourner, and comes with all his desire to the place the LORD chooses,
then he may serve in the name of the LORD his God like all his fellow Levites who stand there before the LORD.
They shall eat share for share, besides what comes from the sale of his patrimony.
When you come into the land the LORD your God is giving you, you must not learn to act according to the abominations of those nations.
There must not be found among you anyone who makes his son or his daughter pass through the fire, anyone who practises divination, a soothsayer, an augurer, a sorcerer,
anyone who casts spells, anyone who consults a medium or a spiritist, or who enquires of the dead.
For everyone who does these things is an abomination to the LORD, and it is because of these abominations that the LORD your God is dispossessing them before you.
You shall be blameless with the LORD your God.
For these nations that you are dispossessing listen to soothsayers and diviners; but as for you, the LORD your God has not allowed you this.
The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among you, from your kinsmen; to him you shall listen.

just as you asked of the LORD your God at Horeb on the day of the assembly, when you said, 'Let me not hear the voice of the LORD my God again, and let me not see this great fire any more, so that I do not die.'
And the LORD said to me, 'They are right in what they have said.'
'I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their kinsmen, and I will put my words in his mouth, and he shall speak to them everything I command him.'
'And whoever does not listen to my words that he speaks in my name, I myself will require it of him.'
'But the prophet who presumes to speak a word in my name that I have not commanded him to speak, or who speaks in the name of other gods—that prophet shall die.'
'And if you say in your heart, "How are we to know the word that the LORD has not spoken?"'

'When a prophet speaks in the name of the LORD and the thing does not happen and does not come about, that is a word the LORD has not spoken. The prophet spoke it presumptuously. You need not be afraid of him.'

deuteronomy_19.t: When the LORD your God cuts off the nations whose land the LORD your God is giving you, and you dispossess them and settle in their cities and their houses,
you shall set apart three cities for yourself in the middle of your land, which the LORD your God is giving you to take possession of it.
You shall prepare the road for yourself and divide into three parts the territory of the land the LORD your God is giving you to inherit, so that any killer may flee there.
This is the case of the killer who may flee there and live: whoever strikes his neighbour without intending it, not having hated him beforehand.

Or whoever goes into the forest with his neighbour to cut wood, and his hand swings the axe to fell the tree, and the iron head slips off the handle and strikes his neighbour so that he dies—he shall flee to one of these cities and live.

Otherwise the avenger of blood might pursue the killer while his heart is hot, and overtake him because the road is long, and strike him dead—though he does not deserve a sentence of death, since he had not hated him beforehand.
That is why I am commanding you: set apart three cities for yourself.
And if the LORD your God enlarges your territory, as he swore to your fathers, and gives you all the land he said he would give to your fathers—
if you keep all this commandment, doing it as I command you today, loving the LORD your God and walking in his ways all your days—then you shall add three more cities for yourself to these three.
so that innocent blood is not shed in the middle of your land, which the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, and bloodguilt come upon you.
But if a man hates his neighbour and lies in wait for him and rises against him and strikes him dead, and then flees to one of these cities,
then the elders of his city shall send and take him from there and hand him over to the avenger of blood, and he shall die.
Your eye shall not pity him. You shall purge the blood of the innocent from Israel, and it will go well with you.
You shall not move back your neighbour's boundary marker, which those before you set, in the inheritance you receive in the land the LORD your God is giving you to take possession of it.
A single witness shall not stand against a man for any iniquity or any sin, in any sin he commits. A matter shall be established on the testimony of two witnesses or of three witnesses.
If a malicious witness stands against a man, to testify against him falsely,
then the two men who have the dispute shall stand before the LORD, before the priests and the judges who are in office in those days.
The judges shall investigate thoroughly, and if the witness proves to be a false witness, having testified falsely against his brother,
then you shall do to him just as he schemed to do to his brother. So you shall purge the evil from among you.
And the rest shall hear and be afraid, and they will never again do such an evil thing as this among you.
Your eye shall not pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

deuteronomy_20.t: When you go out to war against your enemies and see horses and chariots, an army greater than yours, you shall not be afraid of them, for the LORD your God is with you, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.
When you are drawing near to the battle, the priest shall come forward and speak to the people.
He shall say to them: 'Hear, Israel! Today you are drawing near to battle against your enemies. Do not let your heart be faint. Do not be afraid, do not panic, do not be in dread before them.
For the LORD your God is the one who goes with you, to fight for you against your enemies and to give you victory.'

Then the officers shall speak to the people: 'Is there a man who has built a new house and has not dedicated it? Let him go and return to his house, in case he dies in the battle and another man dedicates it.
Is there a man who has planted a vineyard and has not yet begun to use its fruit? Let him go and return to his house, in case he dies in the battle and another man begins to use it.
Is there a man who has betrothed a woman and has not yet taken her? Let him go and return to his house, in case he dies in the battle and another man takes her.

The officers shall speak to the people again and say: 'Is there a man who is afraid and soft of heart? Let him go and return to his house, so that he does not melt his brothers' hearts as his own is melted.'
When the officers have finished speaking to the people, they shall appoint commanders of the forces at the head of the people.
When you draw near to a city to fight against it, you shall call out to it an offer of peace.
If it answers you with peace and opens to you, then all the people found in it shall become forced labour for you and shall serve you.
But if it does not make peace with you and makes war against you, then you shall besiege it.
And the LORD your God will give it into your hand, and you shall put every male in it to the edge of the sword.

Only the women, the little ones, the livestock, and everything in the city—all its spoil—you shall plunder for yourself, and you shall consume the spoil of your enemies, which the LORD your God has given you.
This is what you shall do to all the cities that are very far from you, which do not belong to the cities of these nations.
But in the cities of these peoples, which the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, you shall not let anything that breathes remain alive.
For you shall utterly devote them to destruction—the Hittite and the Amorite, the Canaanite and the Perizzite, the Hivite and the Jebusite—as the LORD your God has commanded you,
so that they do not teach you to act according to all the abominations they have done for their gods, and so cause you to sin against the LORD your God.

When you besiege a city for many days, fighting against it in order to capture it, you shall not destroy its trees by wielding an axe against them; you may eat from them, but you shall not cut them down—for is the tree of the field a man, that it should come under siege from you?
Only a tree that you know is not a food tree may you destroy and cut down, and you may build siege works against the city that is making war against you, until it falls.

deuteronomy_21.t: If someone slain is found in the land the LORD your God is giving you to take possession of it, lying in the open country, and it is not known who struck him,
then your elders and your judges shall go out and measure the distance to the cities around the slain one.
