And the city nearest to the slain one—the elders of that city shall take a heifer from the herd that has never been worked and has never pulled in a yoke,
and the elders of that city shall bring the heifer down to an ever-flowing wadi that is not tilled or sown, and there in the wadi they shall break the heifer's neck.

Then the priests, the sons of Levi, shall come forward, for the LORD your God has chosen them to serve him and to bless in the name of the LORD, and every dispute and every case of affliction is settled by their word.
And all the elders of that city, those nearest to the slain one, shall wash their hands over the heifer whose neck was broken in the wadi,
and they shall declare: 'Our hands did not shed this blood, and our eyes did not see it.
Make atonement for your people Israel, whom you ransomed, LORD, and do not lay innocent blood on your people Israel.' And the blood will be atoned for them.
So you shall purge the innocent blood from among you, because you will have done what is right in the eyes of the LORD.
When you go out to war against your enemies, and the LORD your God gives them into your hand and you take them captive,
and you see among the captives a woman beautiful in form, and you desire her, and you take her for yourself as a wife,
then you shall bring her into your house, and she shall shave her head and trim her nails,

and she shall take off the clothing of her captivity and live in your house and weep for her father and her mother for a full month. After that you may go in to her and be her husband, and she shall become your wife.
And if you take no delight in her, you shall let her go wherever she wishes. You must not sell her for money; you must not treat her as a slave, because you have violated her.
If a man has two wives, one loved and the other hated, and both bear him sons—the loved one and the hated one—and the firstborn son is the hated one's,
then on the day he divides his inheritance among his sons, he may not treat the son of the loved wife as firstborn in preference to the son of the hated wife, who is the firstborn.

Rather he shall acknowledge the firstborn, the son of the hated wife, by giving him a double portion of all that he possesses; for he is the first of his strength, and the right of the birthright belongs to him.
If a man has a stubborn and rebellious son who does not listen to the voice of his father or the voice of his mother, and though they discipline him he still does not listen to them,
then his father and his mother shall seize him and bring him out to the elders of his city, to the gate of his town,
and they shall say to the elders of his city: 'This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious. He does not listen to our voice. He is a glutton and a drunkard.'
Then all the men of his city shall stone him with stones so that he dies. So you shall purge the evil from among you, and all Israel shall hear and be afraid.
And if a man has committed a sin carrying a sentence of death, and he is put to death, and you hang him on a tree,

his corpse shall not remain overnight on the tree. You shall certainly bury him that same day, for a hanged man is a curse of God; and you shall not defile your land, which the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.

deuteronomy_22.t: You shall not see your brother's ox or his sheep straying and ignore it; you shall certainly return them to your brother.

And if your brother is not near you, or you do not know who he is, then you shall bring it into your house, and it shall stay with you until your brother comes looking for it, and then you shall return it to him.
You shall do the same for his donkey, the same for his garment, the same for anything your brother loses and you find. You may not ignore it.
You shall not see your brother's donkey or his ox fallen on the road and ignore it; you shall certainly help him raise it up.
A man's gear shall not be worn by a woman, and a man shall not put on a woman's garment, for everyone who does these things is an abomination to the LORD your God.

If you come upon a bird's nest along the road, in any tree or on the ground, with chicks or eggs in it and the mother lying on the chicks or on the eggs, you shall not take the mother together with the young.
You shall certainly let the mother go, and you may take the young for yourself, so that it may go well with you and you may live long.
When you build a new house, you shall make a parapet for your roof, so that you do not bring bloodguilt on your house if anyone falls from it.
You shall not sow your vineyard with two kinds of seed, or the whole yield will become forfeit as holy—both the seed you sow and the produce of the vineyard.
You shall not plough with an ox and a donkey together.
You shall not wear mixed fabric—wool and linen together.
You shall make tassels for yourself on the four corners of the covering with which you cover yourself.
If a man takes a wife and goes in to her and then hates her,
and brings charges against her and puts out a bad name about her, saying, 'I took this woman, and when I came near to her I did not find in her the tokens of virginity,'
then the young woman's father and her mother shall take the tokens of the young woman's virginity and bring them out to the elders of the city at the gate.
And the young woman's father shall say to the elders: 'I gave my daughter to this man as a wife, and he hated her.

And now he has brought charges, saying, "I did not find the tokens of virginity in your daughter." But here are the tokens of my daughter's virginity.' And they shall spread the garment before the elders of the city.
And the elders of that city shall take the man and punish him.

They shall fine him a hundred pieces of silver and give them to the young woman's father, because he put out a bad name about a virgin of Israel. And she shall remain his wife; he may not send her away as long as he lives.
But if the charge was true, and the tokens of virginity were not found for the young woman,

then they shall bring the young woman out to the entrance of her father's house, and the men of her city shall stone her with stones so that she dies, because she has done an outrage in Israel by acting the prostitute in her father's house. So you shall purge the evil from among you.
If a man is found lying with a woman married to a husband, then both of them shall die—the man who lay with the woman, and the woman. So you shall purge the evil from Israel.
If there is a young woman, a virgin betrothed to a man, and another man finds her in the city and lies with her,

then you shall bring both of them out to the gate of that city and stone them with stones so that they die—the young woman because she did not cry out in the city, and the man because he violated his neighbour's wife. So you shall purge the evil from among you.
But if the man finds the betrothed young woman out in the open country, and the man seizes her and lies with her, then only the man who lay with her shall die.
But to the young woman you shall do nothing; the young woman has committed no sin deserving death, for this case is like the case of a man who rises against his neighbour and murders him.
For he found her out in the open country; the betrothed young woman cried out, and there was no one to save her.
If a man finds a young woman, a virgin who is not betrothed, and seizes her and lies with her, and they are discovered,
then the man who lay with her shall give the young woman's father fifty pieces of silver, and she shall become his wife, because he violated her. He may not send her away as long as he lives.
A man shall not take his father's wife, and he shall not uncover his father's skirt.

deuteronomy_23.t: No man whose testicles are crushed or whose penis is cut off shall enter the assembly of the LORD.
One of illegitimate birth shall not enter the assembly of the LORD; even to the tenth generation none of his descendants shall enter the assembly of the LORD.
No Ammonite or Moabite shall enter the assembly of the LORD; even to the tenth generation none of their descendants shall enter the assembly of the LORD, for ever.
because they did not meet you with food and water on the way when you came out of Egypt, and because he hired Balaam son of Beor from Pethor in Aram-naharaim against you, to curse you.
But the LORD your God was not willing to listen to Balaam, and the LORD your God turned the curse into a blessing for you, because the LORD your God loved you.
You shall not seek their welfare or their good all your days, for ever.
You shall not abhor an Edomite, for he is your brother. You shall not abhor an Egyptian, for you were a sojourner in his land.
The children born to them in the third generation may enter the assembly of the LORD.
When you go out as a camp against your enemies, you shall keep yourself from every evil thing.
If there is among you a man who is not clean because of a nocturnal emission, he shall go outside the camp; he shall not come inside the camp.
Toward evening he shall wash with water, and when the sun goes down he may come back inside the camp.
You shall have a place outside the camp, and you shall go out there.
You shall have a peg with your equipment, and when you sit down outside you shall dig with it, then turn back and cover your excrement.

For the LORD your God walks about in the middle of your camp, to deliver you and to give your enemies over to you; so your camp shall be holy, that he may not see anything indecent among you and turn away from following you.
You shall not hand over to his master a slave who has escaped to you from his master.
He shall live with you, among you, in whatever place he chooses within one of your towns, wherever seems good to him. You shall not maltreat him.
There shall be no cult prostitute among the daughters of Israel, and no cult prostitute among the sons of Israel.
You shall not bring the fee of a prostitute or the price of a dog into the house of the LORD your God in payment of any vow, for both of them are an abomination to the LORD your God.
You shall not charge your brother interest—interest on money, interest on food, interest on anything that is lent at interest.

You may charge interest to a foreigner, but you shall not charge interest to your brother, so that the LORD your God may bless you in every undertaking of your hand in the land you are entering to take possession of it.
When you vow a vow to the LORD your God, you shall not delay in paying it, for the LORD your God will certainly require it of you, and you will incur sin.
But if you refrain from vowing, you will not incur sin.
You shall keep and do what your lips have uttered, just as you have vowed to the LORD your God as a freewill offering, which you spoke with your own mouth.
When you go into your neighbour's vineyard, you may eat as many grapes as you want, your fill, but you shall not put any into your basket.
When you go into your neighbour's standing grain, you may pluck the ears with your hand, but you shall not put a sickle to your neighbour's standing grain.

deuteronomy_24.t: When a man takes a wife and marries her, and then she does not find favour in his eyes because he has found something indecent in her, and he writes her a certificate of divorce, puts it in her hand, and sends her away from his house,
and she leaves his house and goes and becomes another man's wife,
and the second man hates her and writes her a certificate of divorce, puts it in her hand, and sends her away from his house; or if the second man who took her as his wife dies—

then her first husband, who sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife after she has been made unclean; for that is an abomination before the LORD, and you shall not bring sin upon the land the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.
When a man takes a new wife, he shall not go out with the army, and no obligation shall be laid on him for any purpose. He shall be free at home for one year, and shall gladden the wife he has taken.
No one shall take a hand-mill or an upper millstone in pledge, for that is taking a life in pledge.
If a man is found stealing a person from among his brothers, the people of Israel, and treats him as a slave and sells him, then that thief shall die. So you shall purge the evil from among you.

Take care in a case of the skin disease leprosy, to be very careful and to act according to everything the priests, the Levites, instruct you; you shall be careful to do just as I have commanded them.
Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam on the way when you came out of Egypt.
When you make your neighbour a loan of any kind, you shall not go into his house to take his pledge.
You shall stand outside, and the man you are lending to shall bring the pledge out to you.
And if he is a poor man, you shall not sleep in his pledge.
You shall certainly return the pledge to him when the sun goes down, so that he may sleep in his garment and bless you; and it will be righteousness for you before the LORD your God.
You shall not oppress a hired labourer who is poor and needy, whether one of your brothers or one of the sojourners in your land, in your towns.
You shall give him his wages on the same day, before the sun goes down on them, for he is poor and sets his life on them; otherwise he will call out against you to the LORD, and you will incur sin.
Fathers shall not be put to death for their sons, and sons shall not be put to death for their fathers; each shall be put to death for his own sin.
You shall not pervert the justice due to a sojourner or a fatherless one, and you shall not take a widow's garment in pledge.
Remember that you were a slave in Egypt and the LORD your God redeemed you from there; that is why I am commanding you to do this.

When you reap your harvest in your field and forget a sheaf in the field, you shall not go back to get it. It shall belong to the sojourner, the fatherless and the widow, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
When you beat your olive tree, you shall not go over the boughs a second time. It shall belong to the sojourner, the fatherless and the widow.
When you gather the grapes of your vineyard, you shall not glean it afterwards. It shall belong to the sojourner, the fatherless and the widow.
Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt; that is why I am commanding you to do this.

deuteronomy_25.t: If there is a dispute between men and they come to court and the judges try them, they shall acquit the one in the right and condemn the one in the wrong.
And if the guilty one deserves a beating, the judge shall have him lie down and be beaten in his presence, with the number of strokes matching his offence.
Forty strokes he may give him, no more; if he goes beyond that and gives him a heavy beating on top of them, your brother will be degraded before your eyes.
You shall not muzzle an ox while it is threshing.

If brothers live together and one of them dies and has no son, the dead man's wife shall not marry outside the family, to a stranger. Her husband's brother shall go in to her and take her as his wife and do the duty of a husband's brother for her.
And the firstborn she bears shall carry on the name of the dead brother, so that his name is not wiped out from Israel.

But if the man does not want to take his brother's widow, then his brother's widow shall go up to the gate, to the elders, and say: 'My husband's brother refuses to raise up a name for his brother in Israel; he is not willing to do the duty of a husband's brother for me.'
Then the elders of his city shall summon him and speak to him. And if he stands his ground and says, 'I do not want to take her,'

then his brother's widow shall come up to him before the eyes of the elders, pull his sandal off his foot, and spit in his face; and she shall declare: 'This is what is done to the man who will not build up his brother's house.'
And his household shall be called in Israel 'The house of the one whose sandal was pulled off.'

If men are fighting together, a man and his brother, and the wife of one of them comes near to rescue her husband from the hand of the man striking him, and reaches out her hand and seizes his genitals,
then you shall cut off her hand; your eye shall not pity her.
You shall not have in your bag two kinds of weight, a large and a small.
You shall not have in your house two kinds of measure, a large and a small.
You shall have a full and honest weight, and a full and honest measure, so that your days may be long on the land the LORD your God is giving you.
For everyone who does these things is an abomination to the LORD your God—everyone who acts unjustly.
Remember what Amalek did to you on the way when you came out of Egypt,
how he met you on the way and cut off your rear, all the stragglers behind you, when you were exhausted and weary; and he did not fear God.

And when the LORD your God gives you rest from all your enemies round about, in the land the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance to take possession of it, you shall wipe out the remembrance of Amalek from under the heavens. You shall not forget.

deuteronomy_26.t: When you come into the land the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, and you take possession of it and settle in it,

then you shall take some of the first of all the fruit of the ground that you bring in from your land, which the LORD your God is giving you, and put it in a basket, and go to the place the LORD your God chooses to make his name dwell there.
And you shall come to the priest who is in office in those days and say to him: 'I declare today to the LORD your God that I have come into the land the LORD swore to our fathers to give us.'
And the priest shall take the basket from your hand and set it down before the altar of the LORD your God.
And you shall declare before the LORD your God: 'A wandering Aramean was my father. He went down to Egypt and sojourned there, few in number, and there he became a nation great, mighty and numerous.
And the Egyptians did us harm, afflicted us, and laid hard labour on us.
And we cried out to the LORD, the God of our fathers, and the LORD heard our voice and saw our affliction, our toil and our oppression.
And the LORD brought us out of Egypt with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, with great terror, with signs and with wonders.
And he brought us to this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.
And now I have brought the first of the fruit of the ground that you have given me, LORD.' Then you shall set it down before the LORD your God and bow down before the LORD your God.
And you shall rejoice in all the good that the LORD your God has given you and your household—you, the Levite, and the sojourner who is among you.

When you have finished setting aside the whole tithe of your produce in the third year, the year of the tithe, you shall give it to the Levite, the sojourner, the fatherless and the widow, and they shall eat in your towns and be satisfied.

And you shall say before the LORD your God: 'I have cleared the holy portion out of my house, and I have given it to the Levite, the sojourner, the fatherless and the widow, according to all the commandment you commanded me. I have not transgressed any of your commandments and I have not forgotten them.

I have not eaten any of it in mourning, I have not cleared any of it out while unclean, and I have not given any of it to the dead. I have obeyed the voice of the LORD my God; I have done everything you commanded me.
Look down from your holy habitation, from heaven, and bless your people Israel and the ground you have given us, as you swore to our fathers—a land flowing with milk and honey.'
This day the LORD your God commands you to do these statutes and ordinances. You shall keep them and do them with all your heart and with all your soul.
Today you have declared the LORD to be your God, and that you will walk in his ways and keep his statutes, his commandments and his ordinances, and listen to his voice.
And today the LORD has declared you to be his own treasured people, as he said to you, and that you will keep all his commandments,
and to set you high above all the nations he has made, for praise and fame and honour, and that you should be a people holy to the LORD your God, as he has spoken.

deuteronomy_27.t: Then Moses and the elders of Israel commanded the people: 'Keep the whole commandment that I am commanding you today.
On the day you cross the Jordan into the land the LORD your God is giving you, you shall set up large stones for yourself and coat them with lime.

And you shall write on them all the words of this law when you have crossed over, so that you may come into the land the LORD your God is giving you, a land flowing with milk and honey, as the LORD the God of your fathers has spoken to you.
When you have crossed the Jordan, you shall set up these stones, as I am commanding you today, on Mount Ebal, and coat them with lime.
And you shall build there an altar to the LORD your God, an altar of stones; you shall not use an iron tool on them.
You shall build the altar of the LORD your God of whole stones, and offer up burnt offerings on it to the LORD your God.
And you shall sacrifice peace offerings and eat there and rejoice before the LORD your God.
And you shall write all the words of this law on the stones, making them very plain.
Then Moses and the priests, the Levites, spoke to all Israel: 'Be silent and hear, Israel! This day you have become a people belonging to the LORD your God.
You shall obey the voice of the LORD your God and do his commandments and his statutes, which I am commanding you today.'
And on that day Moses commanded the people:
'These shall stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people when you have crossed the Jordan: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph and Benjamin.
And these shall stand for the curse on Mount Ebal: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan and Naphtali.
And the Levites shall declare to every man of Israel in a loud voice:
'Cursed be the man who makes a carved image or a cast image, an abomination to the LORD, the work of a craftsman's hands, and sets it up in secret.' And all the people shall answer, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who dishonours his father and his mother.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who moves back his neighbour's boundary marker.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who leads a blind man astray on the road.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who perverts the justice due to a sojourner, a fatherless one or a widow.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who lies with his father's wife, for he has uncovered his father's skirt.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who lies with any animal.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who lies with his sister, the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who lies with his mother-in-law.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who strikes down his neighbour in secret.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who takes a bribe to strike down a person, shedding innocent blood.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who does not uphold the words of this law by doing them.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'

deuteronomy_28.t: And if you truly obey the voice of the LORD your God, being careful to do all his commandments which I am commanding you today, then the LORD your God will set you high above all the nations of the earth.
And all these blessings shall come upon you and overtake you, if you obey the voice of the LORD your God.
Blessed shall you be in the city, and blessed shall you be in the open country.
Blessed shall be the fruit of your womb, the fruit of your ground and the fruit of your livestock, the offspring of your cattle and the young of your flock.
Blessed shall be your basket and your kneading trough.
Blessed shall you be when you come in, and blessed shall you be when you go out.
The LORD will make your enemies who rise against you be defeated before you: by one road they shall come out against you, and by seven roads they shall flee before you.
The LORD will command the blessing to be with you in your barns and in every undertaking of your hand, and he will bless you in the land the LORD your God is giving you.
The LORD will establish you for himself as a holy people, as he swore to you, if you keep the commandments of the LORD your God and walk in his ways.
And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the LORD is called over you, and they will be afraid of you.
And the LORD will make you abound in good things—in the fruit of your womb, the fruit of your livestock and the fruit of your ground—on the land the LORD swore to your fathers to give you.

The LORD will open for you his good storehouse, the heavens, to give your land its rain in its season and to bless all the work of your hand; and you shall lend to many nations, and you shall not borrow.

And the LORD will make you the head and not the tail; you shall be only on top and never underneath, if you obey the commandments of the LORD your God which I am commanding you today, to keep and to do them,
and if you do not turn aside from any of the words I am commanding you today, to the right or to the left, to go after other gods and serve them.

But if you do not obey the voice of the LORD your God, being careful to do all his commandments and his statutes which I am commanding you today, then all these curses shall come upon you and overtake you.
Cursed shall you be in the city, and cursed shall you be in the open country.
Cursed shall be your basket and your kneading trough.
Cursed shall be the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground, the offspring of your cattle and the young of your flock.
Cursed shall you be when you come in, and cursed shall you be when you go out.

The LORD will send upon you the curse, the panic and the rebuke, in every undertaking of your hand that you do, until you are destroyed and perish quickly, because of the evil of your deeds, in that you have forsaken me.
The LORD will make the pestilence cling to you until he has made an end of you from off the land you are entering to take possession of it.
The LORD will strike you with wasting disease, fever, inflammation and burning heat, and with the sword, with blight and with mildew; and they shall pursue you until you perish.
And the heavens over your head shall be bronze, and the ground under you iron.
The LORD will turn the rain of your land into dust and powder; it shall come down on you from the heavens until you are destroyed.

The LORD will make you be defeated before your enemies: by one road you shall go out against them, and by seven roads you shall flee before them. And you shall become a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
And your corpse shall become food for every bird of the heavens and for the animals of the earth, and there will be no one to frighten them off.
The LORD will strike you with the boils of Egypt, with tumours, with scab and with itch, from which you will not be able to be healed.
The LORD will strike you with madness, with blindness and with bewilderment of heart.
And you shall grope about at noon as a blind man gropes in the dark, and you shall not make your ways succeed. You shall be nothing but oppressed and robbed all your days, with no one to save you.
You shall betroth a woman, and another man will lie with her. You shall build a house, and you will not live in it. You shall plant a vineyard, and you will not begin to use its fruit.

Your ox will be slaughtered before your eyes, and you will not eat any of it. Your donkey will be seized from in front of you, and it will not be returned to you. Your flock will be given to your enemies, and you will have no one to save you.
Your sons and your daughters will be given to another people, while your eyes look on and fail with longing for them all day long, and your hand will be powerless.
A people you have not known shall eat the fruit of your ground and all the produce of your toil, and you shall be nothing but oppressed and crushed all your days.
And you shall be driven mad by the sight of what your eyes see.
The LORD will strike you with malignant boils on the knees and on the legs, from which you will not be able to be healed, from the sole of your foot to the crown of your head.
The LORD will lead you, and your king whom you set over you, to a nation you have not known, neither you nor your fathers, and there you shall serve other gods—wood and stone.
And you shall become an object of horror, a byword and a taunt among all the peoples where the LORD drives you.
You shall carry much seed out to the field and gather little in, for the locust will consume it.
You shall plant vineyards and tend them, but you shall not drink the wine or gather it in, for the worm will eat it.
You shall have olive trees throughout your territory, but you shall not anoint yourself with oil, for your olives will drop off.
You shall father sons and daughters, but they will not be yours, for they will go into captivity.
All your trees and the fruit of your ground the whirring locust will take possession of.
The sojourner who is among you shall rise above you higher and higher, and you shall go down lower and lower.
He shall lend to you, and you shall not lend to him. He shall become the head, and you shall become the tail.

And all these curses shall come upon you and pursue you and overtake you until you are destroyed, because you did not obey the voice of the LORD your God, to keep his commandments and his statutes which he commanded you.
And they shall be on you as a sign and a wonder, and on your offspring, for ever.
Because you did not serve the LORD your God with joy and gladness of heart out of the abundance of everything,

you shall serve your enemies, whom the LORD will send against you, in hunger and thirst, in nakedness and in lack of everything; and he will put a yoke of iron on your neck until he has destroyed you.
The LORD will raise up against you a nation from far away, from the end of the earth, swooping like an eagle; a nation whose language you will not understand,
a nation fierce of face, which will show no regard for the old and no favour to the young.

And it shall eat the fruit of your livestock and the fruit of your ground until you are destroyed, leaving you no grain, new wine or fresh oil, no offspring of your cattle or young of your flock, until it has made you perish.

And it shall besiege you in all your towns until your high, fortified walls come down, the ones you are trusting in, throughout all your land; it shall besiege you in all your towns throughout all the land the LORD your God has given you.
And you shall eat the fruit of your womb, the flesh of your sons and your daughters whom the LORD your God has given you, in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy will press you.
The man among you who is gentle and very refined—his eye will be grudging toward his brother, toward the wife of his bosom, and toward the rest of his children whom he has left,

so that he will not give any of them any of the flesh of his children whom he is eating, because nothing at all is left to him, in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy will press you in all your towns.

The gentle and refined woman among you, who would not venture to set the sole of her foot on the ground because she was so refined and gentle—her eye will be grudging toward the husband of her bosom, toward her son and toward her daughter,

and toward the afterbirth that comes out from between her feet, and toward the children she bears; for she will eat them in secret, in the lack of everything, in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy will press you in your towns.
If you are not careful to do all the words of this law which are written in this book, to fear this glorious and awesome name, the LORD your God,
then the LORD will make your plagues extraordinary, and the plagues of your offspring—great and lasting plagues, harmful and lasting sicknesses.
And he will bring back on you all the diseases of Egypt which you dreaded, and they will cling to you.
Also every sickness and every plague not written in the book of this law—the LORD will bring them up on you until you are destroyed.
And you shall be left few in number, where you had been as numerous as the stars of the heavens, because you did not obey the voice of the LORD your God.

And just as the LORD rejoiced over you to do you good and to multiply you, so the LORD will rejoice over you to make you perish and to destroy you; and you shall be torn away from the land you are entering to take possession of it.
And the LORD will scatter you among all the peoples, from one end of the earth to the other, and there you shall serve other gods whom neither you nor your fathers have known—wood and stone.
And among those nations you shall find no rest, and there will be no resting place for the sole of your foot; and there the LORD will give you a trembling heart, failing eyes and a despairing spirit.
And your life shall hang in doubt before you; you shall be in dread night and day, and you shall have no confidence in your life.

In the morning you shall say, 'If only it were evening!' and in the evening you shall say, 'If only it were morning!'—because of the dread in your heart which you will dread, and the sight of your eyes which you will see.

And the LORD will bring you back to Egypt in ships, by the way of which I said to you, 'You shall never see it again'; and there you shall offer yourselves for sale to your enemies as male and female slaves, and there will be no buyer.

deuteronomy_29.t: These are the words of the covenant which the LORD commanded Moses to make with the people of Israel in the land of Moab, besides the covenant he made with them at Horeb.
And Moses summoned all Israel and said to them: 'You have seen all that the LORD did before your eyes in the land of Egypt, to Pharaoh, to all his officials and to all his land—
the great trials your eyes saw, those great signs and wonders.
But to this day the LORD has not given you a heart to understand, or eyes to see, or ears to hear.
And I led you forty years in the wilderness; your clothes did not wear out on you, and your sandals did not wear out on your feet.
You ate no bread, and you drank no wine or strong drink, so that you might know that I am the LORD your God.
And you came to this place, and Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out to meet us in battle, and we struck them down.
And we took their land and gave it as an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
So keep the words of this covenant and do them, so that you may prosper in all that you do.
Today you are all standing before the LORD your God: your heads, your tribes, your elders and your officers, every man of Israel,
your little ones, your wives, and the sojourner in your camp, from the one who cuts your wood to the one who draws your water—
so that you may enter into the covenant of the LORD your God and into his oath, which the LORD your God is making with you today,
so as to establish you today as his people, and that he may be your God, just as he spoke to you and just as he swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob.
And it is not with you alone that I am making this covenant and this oath,
but with whoever is here with us, standing today before the LORD our God, and with whoever is not here with us today.
For you know how we lived in the land of Egypt and how we passed through the midst of the nations you passed through,
and you saw their detestable things and their idols—wood and stone, silver and gold—which they had with them.

Beware lest there be among you a man or a woman, a clan or a tribe, whose heart is turning away today from the LORD our God to go and serve the gods of those nations—lest there be among you a root bearing poison and wormwood,

and when he hears the words of this oath, he blesses himself in his heart, saying, 'I shall be safe, though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart'—so sweeping away the watered land along with the thirsty.

The LORD will not be willing to forgive him; the anger of the LORD and his jealousy will smoke against that man, and every oath written in this book will settle on him, and the LORD will wipe out his name from under the heavens.
And the LORD will single him out for harm from all the tribes of Israel, according to all the oaths of the covenant written in this book of the law.

And the generation to come—your children who rise up after you—and the foreigner who comes from a distant land will say, when they see the plagues of that land and the diseases with which the LORD has made it sick,

'Its whole land is sulphur and salt, a burnt waste; it is not sown, it does not sprout, and no vegetation comes up in it, like the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which the LORD overthrew in his anger and his rage'—
and all the nations will say, 'Why has the LORD done this to this land? What is this great heat of anger?'
And they will say: 'Because they forsook the covenant of the LORD, the God of their fathers, which he made with them when he brought them out of the land of Egypt,
and they went and served other gods and bowed down to them—gods they had not known, whom he had not allotted to them.
So the anger of the LORD burned against that land, bringing on it every curse written in this book.
And the LORD uprooted them from their ground in anger, rage and great wrath, and cast them into another land, as it is this day.'
The hidden things belong to the LORD our God, but the revealed things belong to us and to our children for ever, that we may do all the words of this law.

deuteronomy_30.t: And when all these things come upon you, the blessing and the curse which I have set before you, and you call them to mind among all the nations where the LORD your God has driven you,
and you return to the LORD your God and obey his voice, according to all that I am commanding you today, you and your children, with all your heart and with all your soul,
then the LORD your God will restore your fortunes and have compassion on you, and he will gather you again from all the peoples where the LORD your God has scattered you.
Even if your banished ones are at the end of the heavens, from there the LORD your God will gather you, and from there he will take you.
And the LORD your God will bring you into the land your fathers possessed, and you shall possess it; and he will do you good and make you more numerous than your fathers.
And the LORD your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your offspring, to love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul, so that you may live.
And the LORD your God will put all these oaths on your enemies and on those who hate you, who persecuted you.
And you shall return and obey the voice of the LORD, and do all his commandments which I am commanding you today.

And the LORD your God will make you abound in good things in every work of your hand—in the fruit of your womb, the fruit of your livestock and the fruit of your ground; for the LORD will again rejoice over you for good, just as he rejoiced over your fathers,

if you obey the voice of the LORD your God, keeping his commandments and his statutes written in this book of the law, and if you return to the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
For this commandment which I am commanding you today is not too hard for you, and it is not far off.
It is not in the heavens, so that you should say, 'Who will go up to the heavens for us and get it for us and make us hear it, so that we may do it?'
Nor is it beyond the sea, so that you should say, 'Who will cross the sea for us and get it for us and make us hear it, so that we may do it?'
No, the word is very near to you—in your mouth and in your heart—for you to do it.
See, I have set before you today life and good, death and evil—

which I am commanding you today, to love the LORD your God, to walk in his ways and to keep his commandments, his statutes and his ordinances; and you shall live and increase, and the LORD your God will bless you in the land you are entering to take possession of it.
But if your heart turns away and you do not listen, and you are drawn aside to bow down to other gods and serve them,
I declare to you today that you shall certainly perish; you shall not live long on the land you are crossing the Jordan to enter and possess.
I call the heavens and the earth as witnesses against you today: I have set before you life and death, the blessing and the curse. So choose life, that you may live, you and your offspring,

by loving the LORD your God, by obeying his voice and by clinging to him; for he is your life and the length of your days, so that you may dwell on the land the LORD swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, to give them.

deuteronomy_31.t: Then Moses went and spoke these words to all Israel.
He said to them, "I am a hundred and twenty years old today. I am no longer able to go out and come in, and the LORD has said to me, 'You shall not cross this Jordan.'

The LORD your God himself is crossing over before you. He will destroy these nations from before you, and you will dispossess them. Joshua is the one crossing over before you, just as the LORD has spoken.
And the LORD will do to them just as he did to Sihon and Og, the kings of the Amorites, and to their land, when he destroyed them.
And the LORD will deliver them up before you, and you are to do to them according to all the commandment that I have commanded you.
Be strong and bold. Do not fear and do not be terrified before them, for the LORD your God himself is the one going with you; he will not abandon you and will not forsake you.

Then Moses summoned Joshua and said to him in the sight of all Israel, "Be strong and bold, for you will go with this people into the land that the LORD swore to their ancestors to give them, and you will give it to them as an inheritance.
And the LORD himself is the one going before you. He will be with you; he will not abandon you and will not forsake you. Do not fear and do not be dismayed.
And Moses wrote down this law and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi, who carry the ark of the covenant of the LORD, and to all the elders of Israel.
And Moses commanded them, "At the end of seven years, at the appointed time of the year of remission, at the Festival of Booths,
when all Israel comes to appear before the LORD your God in the place that he will choose, you are to read this law aloud before all Israel, in their hearing.

Assemble the people — the men, the women, the little ones, and the sojourner who is in your gates — so that they may hear and so that they may learn, and fear the LORD your God and take care to do all the words of this law,
and their children who have not known it will hear and learn to fear the LORD your God all the days that you live on the ground that you are crossing the Jordan to enter and take possession of.

And the LORD said to Moses, "Your days have drawn near for you to die. Summon Joshua, and present yourselves at the tent of meeting, so that I may commission him." So Moses went, with Joshua, and they presented themselves at the tent of meeting.
And the LORD appeared at the tent in a pillar of cloud, and the pillar of cloud stood over the entrance of the tent.

And the LORD said to Moses, "You are about to lie down with your ancestors, and this people will rise and act the prostitute after the foreign gods of the land it is entering, and it will forsake me and break my covenant that I made with it.

And my anger will burn against it on that day, and I will forsake them and hide my face from them, and it will be devoured; many calamities and troubles will come upon it. And on that day it will say, 'Is it not because my God is not in my midst that these calamities have come upon me?'
And I will certainly hide my face on that day, because of all the evil that it has done, for it has turned to other gods.
"Now then, write down this song for yourselves and teach it to the sons of Israel; put it in their mouth, so that this song may be a witness for me against the sons of Israel.

For I will bring it to the ground that I swore to its ancestors, flowing with milk and honey, and it will eat and be satisfied and grow fat; then it will turn to other gods and serve them, and they will spurn me, and it will break my covenant.

And when many calamities and troubles come upon it, this song will testify before it as a witness, for it will not be forgotten from the mouth of its offspring; for I know the intention that it is forming today, before I bring it into the land that I swore.
So Moses wrote down this song that day and taught it to the sons of Israel.
And he commissioned Joshua son of Nun and said, "Be strong and bold, for you will bring the sons of Israel into the land that I swore to them, and I myself will be with you."
And when Moses had finished writing down the words of this law in a book, to the very end,
Moses commanded the Levites who carry the ark of the covenant of the LORD,
"Take this book of the law and put it beside the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God, and it will be there as a witness against you.
For I know your rebellion and your stiff neck. Even now, while I am still alive with you today, you have been rebellious against the LORD — how much more after my death!
Assemble to me all the elders of your tribes and your officials, so that I may speak these words in their hearing and call the heavens and the earth as witnesses against them.

For I know that after my death you will certainly act corruptly and turn aside from the way that I have commanded you; and the evil will come upon you in the latter days, because you will do what is evil in the eyes of the LORD, provoking him to anger by the work of your hands.
And Moses spoke the words of this song in the hearing of all the assembly of Israel, to the very end.

deuteronomy_32.t: Give ear, heavens, and let me speak; let the earth hear the sayings of my mouth.
May my teaching drop like the rain, my speech distil like the dew, like showers on the grass and abundant showers on the vegetation.
For I proclaim the name of the LORD; ascribe greatness to our God!
The Rock—his work is perfect, for all his ways are justice; a God of faithfulness and without injustice, righteous and upright is he.
They have acted corruptly toward him; they are not his children—the blemish is theirs— a perverse and crooked generation.
Is this how you repay the LORD, foolish people, and not wise? Is he not your father, who created you, who made you and established you?
Remember the days of old, consider the years of generation after generation; ask your father and he will tell you, your elders and they will say to you.
When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance, when he separated humankind, he fixed the boundaries of the peoples according to the number of the sons of God.
For the LORD's share is his people; Jacob is the measured portion of his inheritance.
He found him in a wilderness land, in a howling waste of desolation; he surrounded him, he cared for him, he guarded him like the pupil of his eye.
Like an eagle that stirs up its nest and hovers over its young, he spread his wings, he took him, he carried him on his pinion.
The LORD alone guided him, and there was no foreign god with him.
He made him ride on the heights of the land, and he ate the produce of the field; he made him suck honey out of a rock, and oil out of flinty rock.
Curds of the herd and milk of the flock, with the fat of lambs, and rams of Bashan, and goats, with the choicest of the wheat; and you drank the blood of the grape as wine.
And Jeshurun grew fat and kicked— you grew fat, you grew thick, you were gorged— and he abandoned the God who made him, and treated with contempt the Rock of his salvation.
They made him jealous with strange gods; with abominations they provoked him to anger.
They sacrificed to demons, not to God— gods they had not known, new ones that had lately come, whom your fathers had not dreaded.
You neglected the Rock who fathered you, and you forgot the God who gave you birth.
And the LORD saw and spurned them, because of the provocation of his sons and his daughters.
And he said: I will hide my face from them, I will see what their end will be; for they are a generation of perversity, children in whom there is no faithfulness.
They made me jealous with what is no god, they provoked me to anger with their vanities; so I will make them jealous with what is no people, with a foolish nation I will provoke them to anger.
For a fire has been kindled in my anger, and it burns down to the lowest Sheol; it consumes the earth and its produce, and sets ablaze the foundations of the mountains.
I will heap calamities on them; I will spend my arrows on them.
Wasted with hunger, devoured by burning plague and bitter destruction; and I will send against them the tooth of beasts, with the venom of things that crawl in the dust.
Outside, the sword will bereave; inside, terror— young man and virgin alike, the nursing child with the grey-haired man.
I said, I will cut them to pieces, I will make the memory of them cease from humankind—
were it not that I feared the provocation of the enemy, that their adversaries would misread it, that they would say, Our own hand is raised high; it was not the LORD who did all this.
For they are a nation lost to counsel, and there is no understanding in them.
If only they were wise, they would comprehend this; they would understand their end.
How could one pursue a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight, unless their Rock had sold them and the LORD had handed them over?
For their rock is not like our Rock— and our enemies themselves are the judges of it.
For their vine is from the vine of Sodom and from the terraces of Gomorrah; their grapes are poisonous grapes, their clusters are bitter.
Their wine is the venom of serpents and the cruel poison of cobras.
Is this not stored up with me, sealed up in my storehouses?
Vengeance is mine, and recompense, for the time when their foot slips; for the day of their disaster is near, and what is prepared for them comes quickly.
For the LORD will judge his people and have compassion on his servants, when he sees that their strength is gone, and no one remains, bond or free.
And he will say: Where are their gods, the rock in which they took refuge,
who ate the fat of their sacrifices and drank the wine of their drink offering? Let them rise up and help you; let them be a shelter over you!
See now that I, I am he, and there is no god beside me. I put to death and I make alive; I have wounded and I heal, and there is no one who delivers from my hand.
For I lift my hand to the heavens and say: As I live for ever,
when I sharpen my flashing sword and my hand takes hold on judgement, I will return vengeance to my foes and repay those who hate me.
I will make my arrows drunk with blood, and my sword shall devour flesh— with the blood of the slain and the captives, from the heads of the long-haired leaders of the enemy.
Rejoice, you nations, with his people, for he will avenge the blood of his servants; he will bring vengeance back on his foes and make atonement for his land and his people.
And Moses came and spoke all the words of this song in the hearing of the people, he and Hoshea son of Nun.
And when Moses had finished speaking all these words to all Israel,
he said to them: 'Set your heart on all the words I am testifying against you today, which you shall command your children to be careful to do—all the words of this law.
For it is not an empty word for you; it is your life, and by this word you shall live long on the land you are crossing the Jordan to take possession of it.'
And on that very day the LORD spoke to Moses:
'Go up this mountain of the Abarim, Mount Nebo, which is in the land of Moab opposite Jericho, and see the land of Canaan which I am giving to the people of Israel as a holding.
And die on the mountain you are going up, and be gathered to your kin, as Aaron your brother died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his kin,
because you acted unfaithfully against me among the people of Israel at the waters of Meribath-kadesh in the wilderness of Zin, because you did not treat me as holy among the people of Israel.
For you shall see the land from a distance, but you shall not go there, into the land I am giving to the people of Israel.'

deuteronomy_33.t: This is the blessing with which Moses, the man of God, blessed the sons of Israel before his death.
He said: The LORD came from Sinai and dawned on them from Seir; he shone forth from Mount Paran and came from among ten thousands of holy ones, from his right hand, fire of law for them.
Indeed he loves peoples; all his holy ones are in your hand, and they followed at your feet; he receives of your words.
Moses commanded us a law, a possession for the assembly of Jacob.
And the LORD became king in Jeshurun when the heads of the people gathered, the tribes of Israel together.
Let Reuben live and not die, though his men be few.
And this for Judah; he said: Hear, O LORD, the voice of Judah, and bring him to his people. With his own hands he contended for himself; be a help against his foes.
Of Levi he said: Your Thummim and your Urim belong to your loyal one, whom you tested at Massah, with whom you contended at the waters of Meribah;
who said of his father and mother, I have not regarded him, who did not recognise his brothers or acknowledge his children; for they kept your speech and observed your covenant.
They will teach your judgements to Jacob and your law to Israel; they will set incense before you and the whole offering on your altar.
Bless, O LORD, his substance, and accept the work of his hands. Shatter the loins of those who rise against him, and of those who hate him, that they rise no more.
Of Benjamin he said: The beloved of the LORD dwells in safety beside him; he shelters him all day long, and he dwells between his shoulders.
Of Joseph he said: Blessed by the LORD is his land, with the choice gift of the heavens, with dew, and with the deep that lies beneath,
with the choice gift of what the sun brings forth, and the choice gift of what the months yield,
with the finest of the ancient mountains, and the choice gift of the everlasting hills,
with the choice gift of the earth and its fullness, and the favour of the one who dwelt in the bush. May it come on the head of Joseph, on the crown of the one set apart from his brothers.

His firstborn bull — majesty is his, and his horns are the horns of a wild ox; with them he will gore the peoples, all of them, to the ends of the earth. These are the ten thousands of Ephraim; these are the thousands of Manasseh.
Of Zebulun he said: Rejoice, O Zebulun, in your going out, and Issachar, in your tents.
They will summon peoples to the mountain; there they will offer sacrifices of righteousness. For they will draw on the abundance of the seas and the hidden treasures of the sand.
Of Gad he said: Blessed is the one who enlarges Gad. He dwells like a lion and tears the arm, and the crown of the head as well.
He chose the best for himself, for there a commander's portion was reserved; and he came at the head of the people. He executed the righteousness of the LORD and his judgements with Israel.
Of Dan he said: Dan is a lion's cub that leaps out from Bashan.
Of Naphtali he said: Naphtali is satisfied with favour and full of the blessing of the LORD; take possession of the west and the south.
Of Asher he said: Most blessed of sons is Asher; let him be the favoured of his brothers and dip his foot in oil.
Iron and bronze are your bolts, and as your days, so your strength.
There is none like God, O Jeshurun, who rides the heavens to your help, and in his majesty the skies.
The God of old is a dwelling, and underneath are the everlasting arms; he drove out the enemy before you and said, Destroy.
So Israel dwelt in safety, alone, the fountain of Jacob, in a land of grain and new wine; and his heavens drop dew.

How blessed you are, O Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by the LORD, the shield of your help and the sword of your eminence? Your enemies will cringe before you, and you will tread on their high places.

deuteronomy_34.t: Then Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, the top of Pisgah, opposite Jericho; and the LORD showed him all the land — Gilead as far as Dan,
all Naphtali, the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, all the land of Judah as far as the western sea,
the Negev, and the district — the valley of Jericho, the city of palm trees — as far as Zoar.

And the LORD said to him: This is the land I swore to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, saying, To your offspring I will give it. I have let you see it with your own eyes, but you shall not cross over there.
So Moses the servant of the LORD died there in the land of Moab, at the mouth of the LORD.
And he buried him in the valley in the land of Moab, opposite Beth-peor; and no one knows his burial place to this day.
Moses was a hundred and twenty years old when he died; his eye was not dim, and his vigour had not fled.
The sons of Israel wept for Moses in the plains of Moab for thirty days, and the days of weeping in mourning for Moses were completed.
And Joshua son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom, because Moses had laid his hands on him; and the sons of Israel listened to him and did just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
And there has not arisen a prophet since in Israel like Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face,
for all the signs and wonders which the LORD sent him to do in the land of Egypt, to Pharaoh and all his servants and all his land,
and for all the mighty hand and all the great terror which Moses displayed before the eyes of all Israel.

ecclesiastes_1.t: The words of Qoheleth, son of David, king in Jerusalem.
Vanity of vanities, said Qoheleth, vanity of vanities; everything is vanity.
What profit has a person from all the toil at which he toils under the sun?
A generation goes and a generation comes, but the earth stands for ever.
The sun rises and the sun sets, and hurries back to the place where it rises.
Going to the south and circling to the north, round and round goes the wind, and on its circuits the wind returns.
All the rivers go to the sea, and the sea is not full; to the place where the rivers go, there they return to go again.
All words are wearisome; no one can express it. The eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.
What has been is what will be, and what has been done is what will be done, and there is nothing new under the sun.
Is there a thing of which one says, "Look, this is new"? It has already been, in the ages that were before us.
There is no remembrance of former things, and of the things to come there will be no remembrance either among those who come after.
I, Qoheleth, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
And I gave my heart to seek out and to search by wisdom all that has been done under the heavens. It is a grievous task that God has given to the children of humankind to be busied with.
I have seen all the works that have been done under the sun, and see: everything is vanity and a chasing of wind.
What is bent cannot be made straight, and what is lacking cannot be counted.
I spoke with my heart, saying: "See, I have made great and increased wisdom beyond all who were before me over Jerusalem, and my heart has seen much wisdom and knowledge."
And I gave my heart to knowing wisdom, and to knowing madness and folly. I knew that this too is a striving after wind.
For in much wisdom is much vexation, and whoever increases knowledge increases pain.

ecclesiastes_2.t: I said in my heart, "Come now, let me test you with pleasure; look on what is good." And see: that too was vanity.
Of laughter I said, "It is madness," and of pleasure, "What does this accomplish?"

I searched in my heart how to gratify my flesh with wine — my heart still guiding me with wisdom — and how to take hold of folly, until I might see what is good for the children of humankind to do under the heavens for the number of the days of their lives.
I made my works great: I built houses for myself; I planted vineyards for myself.
I made myself gardens and parks, and planted in them trees of every kind of fruit.
I made myself pools of water, to water from them a forest of growing trees.
I acquired male and female slaves, and I had slaves born in my house; I also had livestock, herds and flocks in abundance, more than all who were before me in Jerusalem.
I gathered myself silver and gold as well, and the treasure of kings and provinces. I got myself male and female singers, and the delights of the children of humankind — many concubines.
So I became great and increased beyond all who were before me in Jerusalem; and my wisdom stood by me.
And whatever my eyes asked for I did not withhold from them; I did not keep my heart from any pleasure, for my heart was glad in all my toil, and this was my portion from all my toil.
Then I turned to all my works that my hands had done, and to the toil that I had toiled to do, and see: everything was vanity and a chasing of wind, and there was no profit under the sun.
Then I turned to consider wisdom and madness and folly; for what can the one who comes after the king do, beyond what has already been done?
And I saw that wisdom has profit over folly, as light has profit over darkness.
The wise one has his eyes in his head, but the dullard walks in darkness. And yet I knew that one and the same thing happens to them all.
And I said in my heart, "What happens to the dullard will happen to me too. Why then have I been so exceedingly wise?" And I said in my heart that this too is vanity.

For there is no lasting remembrance of the wise one any more than of the dullard, since in the days to come everything will already have been forgotten. And how the wise one dies, just like the dullard!
So I hated life, because the work that is done under the sun was grievous to me; for everything is vanity and a chasing of wind.
And I hated all my toil that I had toiled at under the sun, because I must leave it to the person who comes after me.
And who knows whether he will be wise or a fool? Yet he will have power over all my toil, at which I have toiled and worked with wisdom under the sun. This too is vanity.
So I turned to make my heart despair over all the toil at which I had toiled under the sun.
For there is a person whose toil is with wisdom, knowledge, and skill, and he must give it as a portion to someone who has not toiled at it. This too is vanity, and a great evil.
For what does a person get from all his toil and from the striving of his heart at which he toils under the sun?
For all his days are pains, and his task is vexation; even at night his heart does not rest. This too is vanity.
There is nothing better for a person than that he should eat and drink and find good in his toil. This too I saw: that it is from the hand of God.
For who can eat, and who can enjoy, apart from him?

For to the person who is good before him he gives wisdom and knowledge and joy, but to the sinner he gives the task of gathering and heaping up, only to hand it to one who is good before God. This too is vanity and a chasing of wind.

ecclesiastes_3.t: For everything there is an appointed time, and a time for every matter under the heavens:
a time to give birth and a time to die, a time to plant and a time to uproot what is planted;
a time to kill and a time to heal, a time to break down and a time to build;
a time to weep and a time to laugh, a time to mourn and a time to dance;
a time to throw stones away and a time to gather stones, a time to embrace and a time to keep far from embracing;
a time to seek and a time to give up as lost, a time to keep and a time to throw away;
a time to tear and a time to sew, a time to be silent and a time to speak;
a time to love and a time to hate, a time of war and a time of peace.
What profit has the worker from that at which he toils?
I have seen the task that God has given to the children of humankind to be busied with.
He has made everything beautiful in its time; he has also put eternity into their heart, yet so that no one can find out the work that God has done from beginning to end.
I know that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice and to do good while they live.
And also that everyone should eat and drink and see good in all his toil — that is a gift of God.
I know that all that God does will last for ever; nothing can be added to it, and nothing taken from it; and God has done it so that they should fear before him.
What is has already been, and what is to be has already been; and God seeks out what has been driven away.
And again I have seen under the sun: in the place of judgement, wickedness was there, and in the place of righteousness, wickedness was there.
I said in my heart: "God will judge the righteous and the wicked, for there is a time for every matter, and for every deed, there."
I said in my heart concerning the children of humankind that God is testing them, so that they may see that they are, in themselves, animals.

For what happens to the children of humankind and what happens to the animals — the same thing happens to them. As one dies, so dies the other; they all have the same breath, and humankind has no advantage over the animals, for everything is vanity.
Everything goes to one place. Everything came from the dust, and everything returns to the dust.
Who knows whether the spirit of the children of humankind goes upward, and whether the spirit of the animals goes downward to the earth?
And I saw that there is nothing better than that a person should rejoice in his works, for that is his portion; for who will bring him to see what will be after him?

ecclesiastes_4.t: And I turned again and saw all the oppressions that are done under the sun. And see: the tears of the oppressed, and they have no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors, power — and they have no comforter.
And I called the dead who have already died more fortunate than the living who are still alive;
and better than both is the one who has not yet been, who has not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.
And I considered all toil and all skill in work, and saw that it comes from a person's envy of his neighbour. This too is vanity and a chasing of wind.
The dullard folds his hands and eats his own flesh.
Better a handful with quietness than two hands full of toil and a chasing of wind.
And I turned again and saw vanity under the sun:

There is one alone, without a second; he has neither son nor brother, and there is no end to all his toil; nor is his eye satisfied with wealth. "And for whom am I toiling and depriving myself of good?" This too is vanity, and a grievous task.
Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their toil.
For if they fall, one will raise his companion; but woe to the one who falls and has no second to raise him.
Also, if two lie down together, they have warmth; but how can one alone be warm?
And though someone may overpower one who is alone, two will withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly torn apart.
Better a poor but wise youth than an old king who is a dullard, who no longer knows how to take warning.
For out of prison he came out to reign, though in his own kingdom he had been born poor.
I saw all the living who walk about under the sun siding with the second youth who rises up in his place.
There is no end to all the people, to all who were before them; yet those who come after will not rejoice in him. For this too is vanity and a striving after wind.

ecclesiastes_5.t: Guard your step when you go to the house of God; draw near to listen rather than to offer the sacrifice of dullards, for they do not know that they are doing evil.
Do not be hasty with your mouth, and do not let your heart hurry to bring out a word before God; for God is in the heavens and you are on the earth. Therefore let your words be few.
For a dream comes with much business, and a dullard's voice with many words.
When you vow a vow to God, do not delay to pay it, for he has no pleasure in dullards. What you vow, pay.
Better that you do not vow than that you vow and do not pay.
Do not let your mouth make your flesh sin, and do not say before the messenger, "It was a mistake." Why should God be angry at your voice and destroy the work of your hands?
For in many dreams and vanities there are many words; rather, fear God.

If you see the oppression of the poor and the robbery of justice and righteousness in a province, do not be astonished at the matter; for one official watches over another, and there are higher ones over them.
And the profit of a land is in everything — even a king is served by a cultivated field.
Whoever loves silver will not be satisfied with silver, nor whoever loves abundance with income. This too is vanity.
When goods increase, those who consume them increase; and what profit is there for the owner except the sight of his eyes?
Sweet is the sleep of the labourer, whether he eats little or much; but the plenty of the rich will not let him sleep.
There is a grievous evil I have seen under the sun: wealth hoarded by its owner to his own harm.
And that wealth was lost in a bad venture, and he fathered a son, and there was nothing in his hand.
As he came out from his mother's womb, so he will return, naked, to go as he came; and he will carry nothing away from his toil that he may take in his hand.
And this too is a grievous evil: exactly as he came, so he will go; and what profit has he for toiling for the wind?
All his days, too, he eats in darkness, with much vexation, sickness and anger.

Here is what I have seen to be good, and beautiful: to eat and to drink and to see good in all one's toil at which one toils under the sun for the number of the days of life that God has given — for that is one's portion.
Also everyone to whom God has given wealth and riches, and has given power to eat from it and to receive his portion and rejoice in his toil — this is a gift of God.
For he will not much remember the days of his life, because God keeps him occupied with the joy of his heart.

ecclesiastes_6.t: There is an evil I have seen under the sun, and it lies heavy on humankind:

A person to whom God gives wealth and riches and honour, so that he lacks nothing his appetite desires, yet God does not give him power to eat from it, for a stranger eats it — this is vanity, and a grievous affliction.

If a man fathers a hundred children and lives many years, so that the days of his years are many, but he is not satisfied with good, and he has no burial as well — I say: better than he is the stillborn child.
For it came in vanity, and in darkness it goes, and in darkness its name is covered.
It has not even seen the sun or known anything. It has more rest than the other.
And though he lived a thousand years twice over and saw no good — do not all go to one place?
All a person's toil is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is never filled.
For what advantage has the wise over the dullard? And what advantage has the poor who knows how to conduct himself among the living?
Better the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the appetite. This too is vanity and a chasing of wind.
Whatever has come to be, its name has already been given, and it is known what humankind is; and no one can contend with one stronger than he.
For there are many words that only increase vanity. What advantage has a person from them?
For who knows what is good for a person in life, through the number of the days of his vain life, which he spends like a shadow? For who can tell a person what will be after him under the sun?

ecclesiastes_7.t: Better a name than good oil, and the day of death than the day of one's birth.
Better to go to a house of mourning than to go to a house of feasting, for that is the end of everyone, and the living will take it to heart.
Better vexation than laughter, for by a sad face the heart is made good.
The heart of the wise is in a house of mourning, but the heart of dullards is in a house of gladness.
Better to listen to the rebuke of the wise than to be one who listens to the song of dullards.
For like the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the dullard. This too is vanity.
For oppression makes a wise person foolish, and a bribe destroys the heart.
Better the end of a matter than its beginning; better one patient in spirit than one proud in spirit.
Do not be hasty in your spirit to become angry, for anger settles in the bosom of dullards.
Do not say, "Why were the former days better than these?" for it is not out of wisdom that you ask about this.
Wisdom is good together with an inheritance, and an advantage to those who see the sun.
For wisdom is a shelter, and money is a shelter, but the profit of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of the one who has it.
Consider the work of God: who can straighten what he has bent?
In a day of good, be in good; and in a day of adversity, consider: God has made the one alongside the other, so that no one may find out anything about what comes after.
All this I have seen in the days of my vanity: there is a righteous person perishing in his righteousness, and there is a wicked person prolonging his life in his evil.
Do not be righteous overmuch, and do not make yourself wise to excess. Why should you destroy yourself?
Do not be wicked overmuch, and do not be a fool. Why should you die before your time?
It is good that you should take hold of the one and not withdraw your hand from the other; for whoever fears God will come out with both.
Wisdom gives strength to the wise more than ten rulers who are in a city.
For there is no righteous person on the earth who does good and never sins.
Also, do not give your heart to everything people say, lest you hear your servant cursing you.
For your heart knows many times over that you too have cursed others.
All this I have tested by wisdom. I said, "Let me be wise" — but it was far from me.
Far off is whatever has been, and deep, deep — who can find it out?
I turned, I and my heart, to know and to search and to seek wisdom and a reckoning, and to know that wickedness is stupidity and that folly is madness.
And I found more bitter than death the woman who is a snare, whose heart is a net and whose hands are fetters. Whoever is good before God escapes her, but a sinner is captured by her.
"See, this I have found," said Qoheleth, "adding one to one to find a reckoning —
what I have gone on seeking and have not found: one man among a thousand I have found, but a woman among all these I have not found.
Only see this that I have found: that God made humankind upright, but they have sought out many schemes."

ecclesiastes_8.t: Who is like the wise? And who knows the interpretation of a matter? A person's wisdom makes his face shine, and the hardness of his face is changed.
Keep the king's command, and do so because of the oath of God.
Do not be hasty to go from his presence. Do not persist in an evil matter, for he does whatever he desires.
Inasmuch as a king's word is supreme, who can say to him, "What are you doing?"
Whoever keeps a command will know no evil thing, and a wise heart will know a time and a custom.
For there is a time and a custom for every matter, for human trouble lies heavy on a person.
For no one knows what will be, for who can tell him how it will be?
No one has mastery over the wind, to restrain the wind, and no one has mastery over the day of death, and there is no discharge in the battle, and wickedness will not rescue those who own it.
All this I have seen, giving my heart to every deed that is done under the sun, a time when one person domineers over another to his harm.
And so I have seen the wicked buried, and they came; they used to go from the holy place, and they were forgotten in the city where they had done so. This too is vanity.
Because sentence on an evil deed is not carried out quickly, therefore the heart of the children of humankind is fully set on doing evil.
Though a sinner does evil a hundred times and prolongs his days, yet I also know that it will be well with those who fear God, who fear before him.
But it will not be well with the wicked, and he will not prolong his days, which are like a shadow, because he does not fear before God.

There is a vanity that is done on the earth: that there are righteous people to whom it happens according to the deeds of the wicked, and wicked people to whom it happens according to the deeds of the righteous. I said that this too is vanity.

So I commended gladness, because there is nothing better for a person under the sun than to eat and to drink and to be glad; and this will accompany him in his toil through the days of life that God has given him under the sun.
When I gave my heart to know wisdom and to see the task that is done on the earth — for neither by day nor by night does one see sleep with one's eyes —

then I saw all the work of God, that no one can find out the work that is done under the sun. However much a person toils in seeking, he does not find out; and even if the wise one claims to know, he cannot find out.

ecclesiastes_9.t: For all this I gave to my heart, to make all this clear: that the righteous and the wise and their deeds are in the hand of God. Whether it is love or hatred, no one knows; everything lies before them.

Everything comes alike to all: one and the same thing happens to the righteous and to the wicked, to the good, and to the clean and to the unclean, to the one who sacrifices and to the one who does not sacrifice; as it is with the good, so with the sinner; as with the one who swears an oath, so with the one who fears an oath.

This is an evil in all that is done under the sun: that the same thing happens to all; and also the heart of the children of humankind is full of evil, and madness is in their heart while they live, and after that — to the dead.
For whoever is joined to all the living has hope; for a living dog is better than the dead lion.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing at all, and they have no further reward, for their memory is forgotten.
Their love, their hatred and their envy have already perished, and they have no portion for ever in all that is done under the sun.
Go, eat your bread with gladness, and drink your wine with a glad heart, for God has already accepted what you do.
Let your garments always be white, and let oil never be lacking on your head.

Enjoy life with a wife whom you love, all the days of your vain life that he has given you under the sun, all the days of your vanity; for that is your portion in life and in the toil at which you toil under the sun.
Whatever your hand finds to do, do with your strength, for there is no work or reckoning or knowledge or wisdom in Sheol, where you are going.

I turned and saw under the sun that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the mighty, nor bread to the wise, nor wealth to the discerning, nor favour to the knowledgeable; for time and chance happen to them all.
