And a large mixed company also went up with them, and flocks and herds, very heavy livestock.

They baked the dough that they had brought out from Egypt into unleavened cakes, for it was not leavened, because they had been driven out from Egypt and were not able to delay; and they had not made provisions for themselves.
And the dwelling of the people of Israel, which they dwelt in Egypt, was four hundred and thirty years.
At the end of four hundred and thirty years, on this very day, all the hosts of the LORD went out from the land of Egypt.
It was a night of vigil for the LORD, to bring them out from the land of Egypt. This is that night for the LORD — a vigil for all the people of Israel throughout their generations.
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron, "This is the statute of the Passover. No son of a foreigner shall eat of it.
But every slave of a man, bought with silver — you shall circumcise him, and then he shall eat of it.
A resident alien and a hired worker shall not eat of it.
In one house it shall be eaten. You shall not bring any of the flesh out of the house to the outside, and you shall not break a bone in it.
All the congregation of Israel shall do it.

And when a sojourner sojourns with you and would keep a Passover to the LORD, let every male of his be circumcised, and then let him draw near to keep it, and he shall be like a native of the land. But no uncircumcised man shall eat of it.
One law shall be for the native and for the sojourner who sojourns among you.
All the people of Israel did just as the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron; so they did.
And on this very day the LORD brought the people of Israel out from the land of Egypt by their hosts.

exodus_13.t: The LORD spoke to Moses:
Set apart as holy to me every firstborn. Whatever opens the womb first among the Israelites, among people and among livestock, is mine.

Moses said to the people, "Remember this day, on which you came out of Egypt, out of a house of slaves, for by the strength of his hand the LORD brought you out from here. Nothing leavened is to be eaten."
Today you are going out, in the month of Abib.

When the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanites and Hittites and Amorites and Hivites and Jebusites, which he swore to your fathers to give you, a land flowing with milk and honey, you are to keep this service in this month.
For seven days you are to eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there is a festival to the LORD.
Unleavened bread is to be eaten for the seven days. No leavened bread is to be seen with you, and no leaven is to be seen with you anywhere in your territory.
On that day you are to tell your son, "It is because of what the LORD did for me when I came out of Egypt."
It is to be a sign for you on your hand and a reminder between your eyes, so that the law of the LORD may be in your mouth, for with a strong hand the LORD brought you out of Egypt.
You are to keep this statute at its appointed time, year after year.
When the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanites, as he swore to you and to your fathers, and gives it to you,
then you are to hand over to the LORD everything that first opens the womb. Every firstborn of the offspring of an animal that belongs to you — the males belong to the LORD.
Every firstborn donkey you are to redeem with a sheep, and if you do not redeem it, you are to break its neck. Every firstborn human among your sons you are to redeem.
When your son asks you in time to come, "What is this?" you are to say to him, "With the strength of his hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt, out of a house of slaves."

When Pharaoh made it hard to let us go, the LORD killed every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of humans to the firstborn of animals. That is why I sacrifice to the LORD every male that first opens the womb, and why I redeem every firstborn of my sons.
It is to be a sign on your hand and marks between your eyes, for with the strength of his hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt.

When Pharaoh let the people go, God did not lead them by the way of the land of the Philistines, though it was near, for God said, "The people might have a change of heart when they see battle and go back to Egypt."
So God took the people around by the way of the wilderness of the Sea of Reeds. The Israelites went up out of the land of Egypt arrayed for battle.
Moses took the bones of Joseph with him, because Joseph had made the Israelites swear a solemn oath: "God will surely take notice of you, and you are to carry my bones up from here with you."
They set out from Succoth and camped at Etham, at the edge of the wilderness.
The LORD went before them by day in a pillar of cloud to lead them on the way, and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light, so that they could travel by day and by night.
The pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night did not depart from before the people.

exodus_14.t: The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Tell the Israelites to turn back and camp in front of Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, in front of Baal-zephon. You are to camp opposite it, by the sea."
Pharaoh will say of the Israelites, "They are wandering about in confusion in the land. The wilderness has closed in on them."
"I will harden Pharaoh's heart, and he will pursue them, and I will gain honour through Pharaoh and through all his army, and the Egyptians will know that I am the LORD." And they did so.

When the king of Egypt was told that the people had fled, the heart of Pharaoh and of his servants was turned against the people, and they said, "What is this we have done, letting Israel go from serving us?"
So he harnessed his chariot and took his people with him.
He took six hundred chosen chariots and all the other chariotry of Egypt, with officers over all of them.
The LORD hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he pursued the Israelites, while the Israelites were going out with a high hand.
The Egyptians pursued them and overtook them camped by the sea — all the horses of Pharaoh's chariotry, his horsemen and his army — at Pi-hahiroth, in front of Baal-zephon.
As Pharaoh drew near, the Israelites lifted their eyes, and there were the Egyptians, marching after them. They were terrified, and the Israelites cried out to the LORD.
They said to Moses, "Was it because there were no graves in Egypt that you took us away to die in the wilderness? What is this you have done to us, bringing us out of Egypt?"
"Is this not what we said to you in Egypt: 'Leave us alone, and let us serve the Egyptians'? For it is better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in the wilderness."
Moses said to the people, "Do not be afraid. Stand firm and see the deliverance of the LORD, which he will work for you today. The Egyptians you see today you will never see again."
The LORD will fight for you, and you have only to keep silent.
The LORD said to Moses, "Why are you crying out to me? Tell the Israelites to set out."
"And you, raise your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea and divide it, so that the Israelites may go into the middle of the sea on dry ground."
"And I, I am about to harden the heart of the Egyptians, so that they will go in after them. I will gain honour through Pharaoh and through all his army, his chariotry and his horsemen."
"And the Egyptians will know that I am the LORD, when I gain honour through Pharaoh, his chariotry and his horsemen."
The angel of God, who had been going before the camp of Israel, moved and went behind them; and the pillar of cloud moved from in front of them and stood behind them.
It came between the camp of Egypt and the camp of Israel. There was the cloud and the darkness, and it lit up the night, and neither came near the other all night.
Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and the LORD drove the sea back with a strong east wind all night and made the sea into dry land, and the waters were divided.
The Israelites went into the middle of the sea on dry ground, and the waters were a wall for them on their right and on their left.
The Egyptians pursued and went in after them — all Pharaoh's horses, his chariotry and his horsemen — into the middle of the sea.
In the morning watch the LORD looked down on the camp of Egypt through the pillar of fire and cloud, and he threw the camp of Egypt into confusion.
He turned aside the wheels of their chariots and made them drive with difficulty. The Egyptians said, "Let me flee from Israel, for the LORD is fighting for them against Egypt."
The LORD said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand over the sea, so that the waters may return over the Egyptians, over their chariotry and their horsemen."

Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and at the turn of morning the sea returned to its normal flow. The Egyptians were fleeing straight into it, and the LORD shook the Egyptians off into the middle of the sea.
The waters returned and covered the chariotry and the horsemen, the whole army of Pharaoh that had gone into the sea after them. Not one of them remained.
But the Israelites had walked on dry ground in the middle of the sea, and the waters were a wall for them on their right and on their left.
So on that day the LORD delivered Israel from the hand of Egypt, and Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the shore of the sea.
Israel saw the great hand that the LORD had wielded against Egypt, and the people feared the LORD, and they believed in the LORD and in Moses his servant.

exodus_15.t: Then Moses and the Israelites sang this song to the LORD, and they said: Let me sing to the LORD, for he is highly exalted; horse and its rider he has thrown into the sea.
My strength and my song is the LORD, and he has become my deliverance. This is my God, and I will glorify him, my father's God, and I will exalt him.
The LORD is a man of war; the LORD is his name.
Pharaoh's chariots and his army he cast into the sea, and the choicest of his officers were sunk in the Sea of Reeds.
The deeps cover them; they went down into the depths like a stone.
Your right hand, LORD, is glorious in power; your right hand, LORD, shatters the enemy.
In the greatness of your majesty you tear down those who rise against you; you send out your burning anger, and it consumes them like stubble.
By the breath of your nostrils the waters were piled up; the streams stood up like a heap; the deeps congealed in the heart of the sea.
The enemy said, "I will pursue, I will overtake, I will divide the plunder; my appetite will have its fill of them. I will draw my sword; my hand will dispossess them."
You blew with your breath, and the sea covered them; they sank like lead in the mighty waters.
Who is like you among the gods, LORD? Who is like you — glorious in holiness, fearsome in praises, doing wonder?
You stretched out your right hand, and the earth swallowed them.
In your steadfast love you led the people whom you redeemed; you guided them in your strength to your holy abode.
The peoples have heard, and they tremble; writhing has seized the inhabitants of Philistia.
Then the chiefs of Edom were terrified; trembling seizes the leaders of Moab; all the inhabitants of Canaan have melted away.
Terror and dread fall upon them; by the greatness of your arm they are still as a stone, until your people pass over, LORD, until the people pass over whom you purchased.
You will bring them and plant them on the mountain of your inheritance, the place for your dwelling that you made, LORD, the sanctuary, my Lord, that your hands established.
The LORD will reign forever and ever.

For Pharaoh's horses went into the sea with his chariotry and his horsemen, and the LORD brought the waters of the sea back over them, while the Israelites walked on dry ground in the middle of the sea.
Miriam the prophetess, Aaron's sister, took the tambourine in her hand, and all the women went out after her with tambourines and dancing.
Miriam sang in response to them: Sing to the LORD, for he is highly exalted; horse and its rider he has thrown into the sea.
Moses led Israel out from the Sea of Reeds, and they went out into the wilderness of Shur. They travelled three days in the wilderness and found no water.
They came to Marah, but they could not drink the water at Marah, because it was bitter. That is why its name was called Marah.
The people grumbled against Moses, saying, "What are we to drink?"
He cried out to the LORD, and the LORD showed him a tree. He threw it into the water, and the water became sweet. There he made a statute and an ordinance for them, and there he tested them.

He said, "If you will listen carefully to the voice of the LORD your God, and do what is right in his eyes, and give ear to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, then I will not put on you any of the sicknesses I put on the Egyptians; for I am the LORD who heals you."
They came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there by the water.

exodus_16.t: They set out from Elim, and the whole congregation of the Israelites came to the wilderness of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after they came out of the land of Egypt.
The whole congregation of the Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness.

The Israelites said to them, "If only we had died by the hand of the LORD in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the pot of meat and ate bread to the full! You have brought us out into this wilderness to put this whole assembly to death by hunger."

The LORD said to Moses, "I am about to rain down bread from the heavens for you. The people are to go out and gather each day's portion on its day, so that I may test them, whether they will walk in my law or not."
"On the sixth day they are to prepare what they bring in, and it will be double what they gather day by day."
Moses and Aaron said to all the Israelites, "At evening you will know that it was the LORD who brought you out of the land of Egypt,
"and in the morning you will see the glory of the LORD, because he has heard your grumblings against the LORD. And what are we, that you grumble against us?"

Moses said, "When the LORD gives you meat to eat at evening, and bread in the morning to be full, it is because the LORD has heard your grumblings that you are grumbling against him. And what are we? Your grumblings are not against us but against the LORD."
Moses said to Aaron, "Say to the whole congregation of the Israelites, 'Draw near before the LORD, for he has heard your grumblings.'"
As Aaron was speaking to the whole congregation of the Israelites, they turned toward the wilderness, and there the glory of the LORD appeared in the cloud.
The LORD spoke to Moses:

"I have heard the grumblings of the Israelites. Speak to them and say, 'At twilight you will eat meat, and in the morning you will have your fill of bread. And you will know that I am the LORD your God.'"
That evening the quail came up and covered the camp, and in the morning there was a layer of dew around the camp.
When the layer of dew lifted, there on the surface of the wilderness was something fine and flaking, fine as frost on the ground.
When the Israelites saw it, they said to one another, "What is it?" — for they did not know what it was. Moses said to them, "It is the bread that the LORD has given you to eat."
"This is what the LORD has commanded: Gather from it, each according to what he can eat — an omer per head, by the number of persons in your household. Each of you is to take for those in his tent."
The Israelites did so, and they gathered, some much and some little.
When they measured it by the omer, the one who gathered much had nothing over, and the one who gathered little had no lack. Each had gathered according to what he could eat.
Moses said to them, "No one is to leave any of it over until morning."
But they did not listen to Moses. Some of them left part of it over until morning, and it bred worms and stank, and Moses was angry with them.
They gathered it morning by morning, each according to what he could eat, and when the sun grew hot it melted.
On the sixth day they gathered double the bread, two omers each, and all the leaders of the congregation came and told Moses.

He said to them, "This is what the LORD said: Tomorrow is a sabbath observance, a sabbath of holiness to the LORD. Bake what you will bake and boil what you will boil, and all that is left over set aside for yourselves, to be kept until morning."
They set it aside until morning, as Moses had commanded, and it did not stink, and there were no maggots in it.
Moses said, "Eat it today, for today is a sabbath to the LORD. Today you will not find it in the field."
"Six days you are to gather it, but on the seventh day, the sabbath, there will be none."
On the seventh day some of the people went out to gather, and they found none.
The LORD said to Moses, "How long will you refuse to keep my commandments and my laws?"
"See that the LORD has given you the sabbath. That is why on the sixth day he gives you bread for two days. Each of you stay where you are; let no one go out from his place on the seventh day."
So the people rested on the seventh day.
The house of Israel called its name manna. It was like coriander seed, white, and its taste was like a wafer made with honey.

Moses said, "This is what the LORD has commanded: A full omer of it is to be kept for your generations, so that they may see the bread I fed you in the wilderness when I brought you out of the land of Egypt."
Moses said to Aaron, "Take one jar, put a full omer of manna in it, and set it before the LORD, to be kept for your generations."
As the LORD had commanded Moses, Aaron set it before the testimony, to be kept.
The Israelites ate the manna forty years, until they came to an inhabited land; they ate the manna until they came to the border of the land of Canaan.
Now an omer is a tenth of an ephah.

exodus_17.t: The whole congregation of the Israelites set out from the wilderness of Sin by stages, at the command of the LORD, and camped at Rephidim; and there was no water for the people to drink.
The people quarrelled with Moses and said, "Give us water to drink." Moses said to them, "Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you test the LORD?"

But the people were thirsty there for water, and the people grumbled against Moses and said, "Why is this? You have brought us up from Egypt to put me and my children and my livestock to death by thirst."
Moses cried out to the LORD, "What am I to do for this people? A little more and they will stone me."
The LORD said to Moses, "Go on ahead of the people and take some of the elders of Israel with you. Take in your hand the staff with which you struck the River, and go."
"I will be standing there before you on the rock at Horeb. You are to strike the rock, and water will come out of it, and the people will drink." Moses did so before the eyes of the elders of Israel.
He called the name of the place Massah and Meribah, because of the quarrelling of the Israelites and because they tested the LORD, saying, "Is the LORD among us or not?"
Then Amalek came and made war on Israel at Rephidim.
Moses said to Joshua, "Choose men for us and go out and fight against Amalek. Tomorrow I will be standing on the top of the hill with the staff of God in my hand."
Joshua did as Moses had told him, and fought against Amalek, while Moses, Aaron and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
Whenever Moses lifted up his hand, Israel prevailed; and whenever he let his hand rest, Amalek prevailed.

But the hands of Moses were heavy, so they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it, while Aaron and Hur supported his hands, one on one side and one on the other. So his hands were steady until the sun went down.
So Joshua defeated Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.
The LORD said to Moses, "Write this as a reminder in the book and put it in the ears of Joshua: I will utterly wipe out the remembrance of Amalek from under the heavens."
Moses built an altar and called its name "The LORD is my banner."
He said, "For a hand is on the throne of the LORD: the LORD has war against Amalek from generation to generation."

exodus_18.t: Jethro, the priest of Midian, Moses' father-in-law, heard all that God had done for Moses and for Israel his people — that the LORD had brought Israel out of Egypt.
Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, had taken Zipporah, Moses' wife, after he had sent her away,
and her two sons. The name of the one was Gershom, for he had said, "I have become a sojourner in a foreign land";
and the name of the other was Eliezer, "for the God of my father was my help, and he delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh."
Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, came with his sons and his wife to Moses in the wilderness, where he was camped at the mountain of God.
He sent word to Moses, "I, your father-in-law Jethro, am coming to you, with your wife and her two sons with her."
Moses went out to meet his father-in-law, bowed down and kissed him. They asked after each other's welfare, and they went into the tent.
Moses recounted to his father-in-law all that the LORD had done to Pharaoh and to Egypt for Israel's sake, all the hardship that had come upon them on the way, and how the LORD had delivered them.
Jethro rejoiced over all the good that the LORD had done for Israel, whom he had delivered from the hand of Egypt.
Jethro said, "Blessed be the LORD, who has delivered you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of Pharaoh, who has delivered the people from under the hand of Egypt."
"Now I know that the LORD is greater than all the gods — for in the very matter in which they acted presumptuously against them."
Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, took a burnt offering and sacrifices for God, and Aaron came with all the elders of Israel to eat bread with Moses' father-in-law before God.
The next day Moses sat to judge the people, and the people stood before Moses from morning until evening.

When Moses' father-in-law saw all that he was doing for the people, he said, "What is this that you are doing for the people? Why do you sit alone, with all the people standing before you from morning until evening?"
Moses said to his father-in-law, "Because the people come to me to consult God."
"When they have a matter, it comes to me, and I judge between a man and his neighbour, and I make known the statutes of God and his laws."
Moses' father-in-law said to him, "What you are doing is not good."
"You will certainly wear yourself out, both you and this people who are with you, for the task is too heavy for you. You are not able to do it alone."
"Now listen to my voice. Let me advise you, and may God be with you. You be for the people before God, and bring their matters to God."
"You are to warn them about the statutes and the laws, and make known to them the way in which they are to walk and the work they are to do."

"And you are to look out from all the people men of ability, who fear God, men of truth, who hate unjust gain, and appoint them over the people as officials of thousands, officials of hundreds, officials of fifties and officials of tens."
"They are to judge the people at all times. Every great matter they will bring to you, and every small matter they will judge themselves. Lighten your own load, and they will bear it with you."
"If you do this, and God commands you, then you will be able to endure, and all this people also will go to its place in peace."
Moses listened to the voice of his father-in-law and did all that he had said.
Moses chose men of ability from all Israel and appointed them heads over the people: officials of thousands, officials of hundreds, officials of fifties and officials of tens.
They judged the people at all times. The hard matter they would bring to Moses, and every small matter they judged themselves.
Then Moses sent his father-in-law on his way, and he went to his own land.

exodus_19.t: In the third month after the Israelites came out of the land of Egypt, on that very day, they came to the wilderness of Sinai.
They set out from Rephidim and came to the wilderness of Sinai, and camped in the wilderness. Israel camped there in front of the mountain.
Moses went up to God, and the LORD called to him from the mountain: "This is what you are to say to the house of Jacob and tell the Israelites:
"You yourselves have seen what I did to Egypt, and how I carried you on eagles' wings and brought you to myself.
"Now then, if you will listen carefully to my voice and keep my covenant, you will be my treasured possession out of all the peoples — for all the earth is mine —
"and you yourselves will be for me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation." These are the words that you are to speak to the Israelites.
Moses came and summoned the elders of the people, and set before them all these words that the LORD had commanded him.
All the people answered together and said, "All that the LORD has spoken we will do." And Moses brought back the words of the people to the LORD.

The LORD said to Moses, "I am about to come to you in the thickness of the cloud, so that the people may hear when I speak with you and may also trust in you forever." And Moses told the words of the people to the LORD.
The LORD said to Moses, "Go to the people and set them apart as holy today and tomorrow, and have them wash their clothes.
"Let them be ready for the third day, for on the third day the LORD will come down before the eyes of all the people on Mount Sinai.
"You are to set a boundary for the people all around, saying, 'Take care not to go up on the mountain or touch its edge. Anyone who touches the mountain is to be put to death.'
"'No hand is to touch him: he is to be stoned or shot through. Whether animal or human, it is not to live. When the ram's horn sounds long, they may go up on the mountain.'
Moses went down from the mountain to the people, set them apart as holy, and they washed their clothes.
He said to the people, "Be ready for three days. Do not draw near to a woman."
On the third day, when morning came, there were thunders and lightnings and a heavy cloud on the mountain, and a very loud sound of a ram's horn, and all the people in the camp trembled.
Moses brought the people out of the camp to meet God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
Mount Sinai was smoking, all of it, because the LORD had come down on it in fire, and its smoke went up like the smoke of a furnace, and all the mountain trembled violently.
The sound of the ram's horn grew louder and louder. Moses would speak, and God would answer him with a voice.
The LORD came down on Mount Sinai, to the top of the mountain, and the LORD summoned Moses to the top of the mountain, and Moses went up.
The LORD said to Moses, "Go down and warn the people, so that they do not break through to the LORD to see, and many of them fall."
"And also the priests who draw near to the LORD are to set themselves apart as holy, or the LORD will break out against them."
Moses said to the LORD, "The people are not able to go up Mount Sinai, for you yourself warned us, saying, 'Set a boundary for the mountain and set it apart as holy.'"
The LORD said to him, "Go down, and come up, you and Aaron with you. But the priests and the people are not to break through to come up to the LORD, or he will break out against them."
So Moses went down to the people and spoke to them.

exodus_20.t: And God spoke all these words:
"I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of a house of slaves.
"You shall have no other gods before me.
"You shall not make for yourself a carved image, or any form of what is in the heavens above, or on the earth beneath, or in the waters under the earth.

"You shall not bow down to them and you shall not serve them; for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of fathers upon sons, upon the third generation and upon the fourth, of those who hate me,
"and showing steadfast love to thousands, to those who love me and keep my commandments.
"You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain, for the LORD will not leave unpunished the one who takes his name in vain.
"Remember the sabbath day, to set it apart as holy.
"Six days you shall labour and do all your work,

"but the seventh day is a sabbath to the LORD your God. You shall not do any work — you, or your son or your daughter, your male servant or your female servant, or your livestock, or the sojourner who is within your gates.
"For in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, the sea and all that is in them, and rested on the seventh day. Therefore the LORD blessed the sabbath day and set it apart as holy.
"Honour your father and your mother, so that your days may be long upon the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
"You shall not murder.
"You shall not commit adultery.
"You shall not steal.
"You shall not testify against your neighbour as a false witness.
"You shall not covet your neighbour's house. You shall not covet your neighbour's wife, or his male servant, or his female servant, or his ox, or his donkey, or anything that is your neighbour's."
All the people were seeing the thunders and the torches and the sound of the ram's horn and the mountain smoking. The people saw, and they trembled, and they stood at a distance.
They said to Moses, "You speak with us, and we will listen; but do not let God speak with us, or we will die."
Moses said to the people, "Do not be afraid, for God has come in order to test you, and so that the fear of him may be before you, that you may not sin."
The people stood at a distance, and Moses drew near to the thick darkness where God was.
The LORD said to Moses, "This is what you are to say to the Israelites: You yourselves have seen that I spoke with you from the heavens.
"You shall not make alongside me gods of silver, and gods of gold you shall not make for yourselves.

"An altar of earth you are to make for me, and on it you are to sacrifice your burnt offerings and your peace offerings, your sheep and your cattle. In every place where I cause my name to be remembered, I will come to you and bless you.
"And if you make me an altar of stones, you are not to build them of hewn stone, for if you wield your tool upon it you have profaned it.
"And you shall not go up by steps to my altar, so that your nakedness may not be uncovered on it."

exodus_21.t: These are the rulings that you are to set before them.
When you buy a Hebrew slave, he is to serve six years, and in the seventh he is to go out free, paying nothing.
If he comes in by himself, he goes out by himself. If he is a married man, his wife goes out with him.
If his master gives him a wife and she bears him sons or daughters, the woman and her children belong to her master, and he goes out by himself.
But if the slave declares, "I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free,"
then his master is to bring him to God, and bring him to the door or the doorpost, and his master is to pierce his ear with an awl; and he will serve him forever.
When a man sells his daughter as a female slave, she does not go out as the male slaves go out.
If she is displeasing to her master, who designated her for himself, he must let her be redeemed. He has no right to sell her to a foreign people, since he has broken faith with her.
If he designates her for his son, he is to treat her according to the custom for daughters.
If he takes another woman for himself, he must not reduce her food, her clothing, or her conjugal right.
If he does not do these three things for her, she goes out free of charge; no money is paid.
Whoever strikes a person and that person dies is to be put to death.
But if he did not lie in wait, and God let it come about by his hand, then I will appoint a place for you where he may flee.
But when a man acts deliberately against his neighbour, to kill him by cunning, you are to take him from my altar to die.
Whoever strikes his father or his mother is to be put to death.
Whoever steals a person and sells him, or is found still holding him, is to be put to death.
Whoever reviles his father or his mother is to be put to death.
When men quarrel and one strikes the other with a stone or a fist, and he does not die but is confined to bed,
if he gets up and walks about outside with his staff, the one who struck him is clear of guilt; he must only pay for his lost time and see that he is fully healed.
When a man strikes his slave or his female slave with the rod and the slave dies under his hand, it is to be avenged.
But if the slave survives a day or two, it is not to be avenged, for he is his money.

When men are fighting and they strike a pregnant woman so that she gives birth prematurely, and there is no harm, he is certainly to be fined, as the woman's husband imposes on him, and he is to pay as the judges determine.
But if there is harm, you are to give life for life —
eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
burn for burn, wound for wound, bruise for bruise.
When a man strikes the eye of his slave or the eye of his female slave and destroys it, he is to set the slave free in place of the eye.
And if he knocks out the tooth of his slave or the tooth of his female slave, he is to set the slave free in place of the tooth.
When an ox gores a man or a woman to death, the ox is to be stoned and its meat is not to be eaten, but the owner of the ox is not liable.
But if the ox had been prone to gore in the past, and its owner had been warned and did not keep it in, and it kills a man or a woman, the ox is to be stoned and its owner too is to be put to death.
If a ransom is imposed on him, he is to pay the redemption price for his life, according to all that is imposed on him.
Whether it gores a son or a daughter, this same ruling applies to him.
If the ox gores a slave or a female slave, the owner is to give thirty shekels of silver to the slave's master, and the ox is to be stoned.
When a man opens a pit, or digs a pit and does not cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it,
the owner of the pit is to make compensation; he is to pay silver to the animal's owner, and the dead animal is his.
When one man's ox injures his neighbour's ox so that it dies, they are to sell the live ox and divide the proceeds, and they are to divide the dead animal too.
But if it was known that the ox had been prone to gore in the past and its owner did not keep it in, he must certainly make compensation, ox for ox, and the dead animal is his.

exodus_22.t: When a man steals an ox or a sheep and slaughters it or sells it, he is to repay five head of cattle for the ox and four sheep for the sheep.
If a thief is caught breaking in and is struck so that he dies, there is no bloodguilt in his case.
If the sun has risen on him, there is bloodguilt. The thief must certainly make restitution; if he has nothing, he is to be sold for his theft.
If the stolen animal is found alive in his possession — ox, donkey, or sheep — he is to make twofold restitution.

When a man grazes a field or a vineyard, and turns his livestock loose so that they graze in another man's field, he is to make compensation from the best of his own field and the best of his own vineyard.
When a fire breaks out and catches in thornbushes, and a stack of sheaves or the standing grain or the field is consumed, the one who started the fire must certainly make compensation.
When a man gives his neighbour silver or goods for safekeeping, and it is stolen from that man's house — if the thief is found, the thief is to make twofold restitution.
If the thief is not found, the owner of the house is to be brought before God, to determine whether he has laid a hand on his neighbour's property.

In every case of misappropriation — concerning an ox, a donkey, a sheep, a garment, or any lost thing about which someone says, "This is it" — the case of both parties is to come before God; the one whom God condemns is to make twofold restitution to his neighbour.
When a man gives his neighbour a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any animal for safekeeping, and it dies or is injured or is carried off, with no one seeing it,
an oath before the LORD is to stand between the two of them, that he has not laid a hand on his neighbour's property; the owner is to accept it, and no compensation is made.
But if it was stolen from him, he is to make restitution to its owner.
If it was torn by a predator, he is to bring it as evidence; he does not make restitution for the torn animal.
When a man borrows an animal from his neighbour and it is injured or dies, its owner not being present, he must certainly make restitution.
If its owner was present, he does not make restitution. If it was hired, the loss is covered by the hire.
When a man seduces a virgin who is not betrothed and lies with her, he must pay the bride-price for her, to be his wife.
If her father flatly refuses to give her to him, the man is to weigh out silver equal to the bride-price for virgins.
You are not to let a sorceress live.
Anyone who lies with an animal is to be put to death.
Whoever sacrifices to the gods is to be devoted to destruction — to none but the LORD alone.
You are not to mistreat a sojourner or oppress him, for you were sojourners in the land of Egypt.
You are not to afflict any widow or fatherless child.
If you do afflict him, then when he cries out to me, I will certainly hear his cry.
My anger will burn, and I will kill you with the sword, and your wives will become widows and your children fatherless.
If you lend silver to my people, to the poor among you, you are not to be a creditor to him; you are not to charge him interest.
If you take your neighbour's cloak as a pledge, you are to return it to him before sunset,
for it is his only covering; it is the cloak for his skin. In what else would he sleep? And when he cries out to me, I will hear, for I am gracious.
You are not to revile God, and you are not to curse a leader among your people.
You are not to hold back the fullness of your harvest or the outflow of your press. The firstborn of your sons you are to give to me.
You are to do the same with your oxen and your sheep: seven days it stays with its mother, and on the eighth day you are to give it to me.
You are to be people set apart as holy to me. You are not to eat flesh torn in the field; you are to throw it to the dogs.

exodus_23.t: You are not to spread a false report. Do not join hands with a wicked man to be a malicious witness.
You are not to follow the many in doing wrong, and you are not to testify in a lawsuit so as to side with the many and pervert justice.
You are not to show partiality to a poor man in his lawsuit.
When you come upon your enemy's ox or his donkey straying, you are certainly to bring it back to him.
When you see the donkey of one who hates you lying down under its load, and you would hold back from helping him with it, you are certainly to help him with it.
You are not to deny justice to your needy in his lawsuit.
Keep far from a false charge. Do not kill the innocent and the righteous, for I will not acquit the guilty.
You are not to take a bribe, for a bribe blinds those who see clearly and twists the words of the righteous.
You are not to oppress a sojourner. You yourselves know the life of a sojourner, for you were sojourners in the land of Egypt.
For six years you are to sow your land and gather in its produce.

But in the seventh year you are to let it rest and leave it fallow, so that the needy of your people may eat, and the wild animals may eat what they leave. Do the same with your vineyard and your olive grove.
Six days you are to do your work, and on the seventh day you are to cease, so that your ox and your donkey may rest, and the son of your female slave and the sojourner may be refreshed.
Be watchful in all that I have said to you. You are not to invoke the name of other gods; it is not to be heard from your mouth.
Three times a year you are to hold a festival to me.

You are to keep the Festival of Unleavened Bread: for seven days you are to eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of Abib, for in it you came out of Egypt. And no one is to appear before me empty-handed.
And the Festival of Harvest, the firstfruits of your labour that you sow in the field; and the Festival of Ingathering at the close of the year, when you gather in your labour from the field.
Three times a year every male among you is to appear before the Lord GOD.
You are not to offer the blood of my sacrifice along with anything leavened, and the fat of my festival offering is not to remain overnight until morning.
The choicest of the firstfruits of your ground you are to bring to the house of the LORD your God. You are not to boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
I am sending an angel ahead of you to guard you on the way and to bring you to the place I have prepared.
Be watchful before him and listen to his voice. Do not defy him, for he will not pardon your transgression, for my name is within him.
But if you truly listen to his voice and do all that I say, I will be an enemy to your enemies and a foe to your foes.
For my angel will go ahead of you and bring you to the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, and I will annihilate them.
You are not to bow down to their gods or be drawn into serving them, and you are not to do as they do. You are to tear them down completely and shatter their pillars to pieces.
You are to serve the LORD your God, and he will bless your bread and your water, and I will remove sickness from among you.
None will miscarry or be barren in your land. I will fill out the number of your days.
I will send my terror ahead of you, and I will throw into confusion every people you come among, and I will make all your enemies turn their backs to you.
I will send hornets ahead of you, and they will drive out the Hivites, the Canaanites, and the Hittites from before you.
I will not drive them out from before you in a single year, or the land would become desolate and the wild animals would multiply against you.
Little by little I will drive them out from before you, until you have become fruitful and taken possession of the land.

I will fix your border from the Sea of Reeds to the Sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness to the River; for I will give the inhabitants of the land into your hand, and you will drive them out from before you.
You are not to make a covenant with them or with their gods.
They are not to dwell in your land, or they will make you sin against me; for you would serve their gods, and it would become a snare to you.

exodus_24.t: To Moses he said, "Come up to the LORD — you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel — and bow down at a distance."
Moses alone is to draw near to the LORD; the others are not to draw near, and the people are not to come up with him.
Moses came and recounted to the people all the words of the LORD and all the rulings. And all the people answered with one voice and said, "Everything the LORD has spoken we will do."
Moses wrote down all the words of the LORD. He rose early in the morning and built an altar at the foot of the mountain, with twelve pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel.
He sent the young men of the sons of Israel, and they offered up burnt offerings and sacrificed young bulls as peace offerings to the LORD.
Moses took half of the blood and put it in bowls, and half of the blood he dashed against the altar.
He took the Book of the Covenant and read it aloud to the people. And they said, "Everything the LORD has spoken we will do, and we will obey."
Moses took the blood and dashed it on the people and said, "This is the blood of the covenant that the LORD has made with you on the basis of all these words."
Then Moses went up, with Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel.
And they saw the God of Israel, and under his feet was something like a pavement of sapphire, like the very substance of the heavens in its clarity.
Yet he did not stretch out his hand against the nobles of the sons of Israel; they beheld God, and they ate and drank.
The LORD said to Moses, "Come up to me on the mountain and stay there, and I will give you the tablets of stone, with the law and the commandment that I have written, to teach them."
So Moses arose, with Joshua his attendant, and Moses went up the mountain of God.
To the elders he said, "Stay here for us until we come back to you. Aaron and Hur are with you; whoever has a dispute may go to them."
Moses went up the mountain, and the cloud covered the mountain.
The glory of the LORD settled on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it for six days. On the seventh day he called to Moses from within the cloud.
The appearance of the glory of the LORD was like a consuming fire on the mountaintop, in the sight of the sons of Israel.
Moses entered the midst of the cloud and went up the mountain. And Moses was on the mountain forty days and forty nights.

exodus_25.t: The LORD spoke to Moses:
Speak to the sons of Israel, that they take up a contribution for me. From everyone whose heart moves him you are to take my contribution.
This is the contribution you are to take from them: gold, silver, and bronze;
violet, purple, and scarlet; fine linen and goat hair;
ram skins dyed red, fine leather, and acacia wood;
oil for the light; spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense;
onyx stones and stones for setting, for the ephod and the breastpiece.
They are to make a sanctuary for me, and I will dwell among them.
You are to make it according to all that I show you: the pattern of the tabernacle and the pattern of all its articles.
They are to make an ark of acacia wood, two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high.
Overlay it with pure gold, inside and out, and make a gold moulding around it.
Cast four gold rings for it and put them on its four feet, two rings on one side and two rings on the other side.
Make poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
Put the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, to carry the ark by them.
The poles are to remain in the rings of the ark; they are not to be removed from it.
Put into the ark the testimony that I will give you.
Make a mercy seat of pure gold, two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
Make two cherubim of gold, of hammered work, at the two ends of the mercy seat.
Make one cherub at one end and one cherub at the other end; make the cherubim of one piece with the mercy seat, at its two ends.
The cherubim are to spread their wings upward, overshadowing the mercy seat with their wings, their faces toward one another; the faces of the cherubim are to be toward the mercy seat.
Put the mercy seat on top of the ark, and into the ark put the testimony that I will give you.
There I will meet with you and speak with you from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubim that are over the ark of the testimony — everything that I command you for the sons of Israel.
Make a table of acacia wood, two cubits long, a cubit wide, and a cubit and a half high.
Overlay it with pure gold and make a gold moulding around it.
Make a rim a handbreadth wide around it, and make a gold moulding for the rim all around.
Make four gold rings for it and put the rings at the four corners, at its four legs.
The rings are to be close to the rim, as holders for the poles to carry the table.
Make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold, and the table is to be carried by them.
Make its dishes and its pans, and its jars and its bowls for pouring out; make them of pure gold.
And you are to put the bread of the Presence on the table before me continually.
Make a lampstand of pure gold. The lampstand is to be made of hammered work — its base and its shaft, its cups, its bulbs, and its blossoms are to be of one piece with it.
Six branches are to go out from its sides, three branches of the lampstand from one side and three branches from the other.

There are to be three cups shaped like almond blossoms on the one branch, with bulb and blossom, and three cups shaped like almond blossoms on the next branch, with bulb and blossom — so for the six branches going out from the lampstand.
On the lampstand itself there are to be four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with its bulbs and its blossoms.
A bulb is to be under the first pair of branches from it, a bulb under the second pair, and a bulb under the third pair — for the six branches going out from the lampstand.
Their bulbs and their branches are to be of one piece with it; the whole of it one hammered work of pure gold.
Make its seven lamps, and set up its lamps so that they light the space in front of it.
Its tongs and its firepans are to be of pure gold.
It is to be made of a talent of pure gold, with all these articles.
See that you make them by the pattern that you are being shown on the mountain.

exodus_26.t: Make the tabernacle of ten curtains of fine twisted linen, with violet, purple, and scarlet; make them with cherubim, the work of a designer.
Each curtain is to be twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide; all the curtains are to be of one measure.
Five of the curtains are to be joined to one another, and the other five curtains joined to one another.
Make loops of violet on the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and do the same on the edge of the outermost curtain in the second set.
Make fifty loops on the one curtain and fifty loops at the end of the curtain in the second set, the loops opposite one another.
Make fifty gold clasps and join the curtains to one another with the clasps, so that the tabernacle becomes one whole.
Make curtains of goat hair for a tent over the tabernacle; make eleven of them.
Each curtain is to be thirty cubits long and four cubits wide; the eleven curtains are to be of one measure.
Join five of the curtains together by themselves and six of the curtains by themselves, and fold the sixth curtain double at the front of the tent.
Make fifty loops on the edge of the outermost curtain in the one set, and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain of the second set.
Make fifty bronze clasps, put the clasps into the loops, and join the tent, so that it becomes one whole.
As for the surplus that overhangs in the curtains of the tent, the half curtain left over is to hang over the back of the tabernacle.
The cubit on one side and the cubit on the other, left over in the length of the tent curtains, are to hang over the sides of the tabernacle on either side, to cover it.
Make a covering for the tent of ram skins dyed red, and a covering of fine leather over that.
Make the frames for the tabernacle of acacia wood, standing upright.
Each frame is to be ten cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
Each frame is to have two tenons, joined to one another; do the same for all the frames of the tabernacle.
Make the frames for the tabernacle: twenty frames for the south side.
Make forty silver bases under the twenty frames: two bases under one frame for its two tenons, and two bases under the next frame for its two tenons.
And for the second side of the tabernacle, the north side, twenty frames,
with their forty silver bases: two bases under one frame and two bases under the next.
For the rear of the tabernacle, on the west, make six frames.
Make two frames for the corners of the tabernacle at the rear.
They are to be doubled at the bottom and joined complete at the top into a single ring; so it is to be for both of them, at the two corners.
So there are to be eight frames, with their silver bases, sixteen bases: two bases under one frame and two bases under the next.
Make bars of acacia wood: five for the frames of the one side of the tabernacle,
five bars for the frames of the second side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the frames of the side of the tabernacle at the rear, on the west.
The middle bar, halfway up the frames, is to pass through from end to end.
Overlay the frames with gold, make their rings of gold as holders for the bars, and overlay the bars with gold.
Set up the tabernacle according to the plan you have been shown on the mountain.
Make a veil of violet, purple, and scarlet, and of fine twisted linen; it is to be made by a designer, with cherubim.
Hang it on four pillars of acacia overlaid with gold, with hooks of gold, on four silver bases.
Hang the veil under the clasps, and bring the ark of the testimony there, inside the veil; the veil is to separate for you the holy place from the holy of holies.
Put the mercy seat on the ark of the testimony in the holy of holies.
Set the table outside the veil, and the lampstand opposite the table on the south side of the tabernacle; put the table on the north side.
Make a screen for the entrance of the tent, of violet, purple, and scarlet, and of fine twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer.
Make five pillars of acacia for the screen and overlay them with gold, with hooks of gold; and cast five bronze bases for them.

exodus_27.t: Make the altar of acacia wood, five cubits long and five cubits wide — the altar is to be square — and three cubits high.
Make its horns on its four corners; the horns are to be of one piece with it, and overlay it with bronze.
Make its pots for removing the ashes, and its shovels, basins, forks, and firepans; make all its articles of bronze.
Make a grating for it, a network of bronze, and make four bronze rings on the network at its four ends.
Put it under the ledge of the altar, below, so that the network reaches halfway up the altar.
Make poles for the altar, poles of acacia wood, and overlay them with bronze.
Its poles are to be put into the rings, and the poles are to be on the two sides of the altar when it is carried.
Make it hollow, of boards; as he showed you on the mountain, so they are to do.
Make the courtyard of the tabernacle. On the south side there are to be hangings for the courtyard of fine twisted linen, a hundred cubits long on that side.
Its pillars are to be twenty and their bases twenty, of bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands are to be of silver.
So too along the north side: hangings a hundred cubits long, with its twenty pillars and their twenty bronze bases, the hooks of the pillars and their bands of silver.
The breadth of the courtyard on the west side is to have hangings of fifty cubits, with ten pillars and ten bases.
The breadth of the courtyard on the east side is to be fifty cubits.
Fifteen cubits of hangings are to be on the one side, with three pillars and three bases.
And on the second side, fifteen cubits of hangings, with three pillars and three bases.
For the gate of the courtyard there is to be a screen of twenty cubits, of violet, purple, and scarlet, and of fine twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer, with four pillars and four bases.
All the pillars around the courtyard are to be furnished with silver bands, their hooks of silver and their bases of bronze.
The courtyard is to be a hundred cubits long and fifty wide, five cubits high, of fine twisted linen, with bases of bronze.
All the articles of the tabernacle for all its service, and all its tent pegs and all the tent pegs of the courtyard, are to be of bronze.
You yourself are to command the sons of Israel to bring you pure beaten olive oil for the light, to keep a lamp set up continually.

In the tent of meeting, outside the veil that stands before the testimony, Aaron and his sons are to tend it from evening until morning before the LORD. It is a perpetual statute for their generations, on behalf of the sons of Israel.

exodus_28.t: Bring your brother Aaron near to yourself, and his sons with him, from among the Israelites, to serve me as priest — Aaron, and Aaron's sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
You shall make holy garments for your brother Aaron, for glory and for beauty.
You shall speak to all who are skilled, whom I have filled with a spirit of skill, and they shall make Aaron's garments, to consecrate him so that he may serve me as priest.

These are the garments they shall make: a breastpiece, an ephod, a robe, a checkered tunic, a turban, and a sash. They shall make holy garments for your brother Aaron and for his sons, so that he may serve me as priest.
They shall take the gold, the violet, the purple, the scarlet, and the fine linen.
They shall make the ephod of gold, violet, purple, scarlet, and fine twisted linen, the work of a designer.
It shall have two shoulder-pieces joined to it, at its two ends, and so it shall be joined together.
The band of its ephod, which is on it, shall be of the same workmanship, of one piece with it: gold, violet, purple, scarlet, and fine twisted linen.
You shall take two onyx stones and engrave on them the names of the sons of Israel:
six of their names on the one stone and the names of the remaining six on the second stone, in order of their birth.
With the work of a craftsman in stone, like the engravings of a seal, you shall engrave the two stones with the names of the sons of Israel; you shall make them enclosed in gold settings.
You shall put the two stones on the shoulder-pieces of the ephod as stones of remembrance for the Israelites. Aaron shall bear their names before the LORD on his two shoulders, for remembrance.
You shall make settings of gold,
and two chains of pure gold, made like cords, the work of braiding, and you shall attach the braided chains to the settings.
You shall make a breastpiece of judgement, the work of a designer; you shall make it like the work of the ephod, of gold, violet, purple, scarlet, and fine twisted linen.
It shall be square and doubled over, a span long and a span wide.
You shall set in it a setting of stones, four rows of stones. The first row: ruby, topaz, and emerald.
The second row: turquoise, sapphire, and diamond.
The third row: jacinth, agate, and amethyst.
The fourth row: beryl, onyx, and jasper. They shall be enclosed in gold in their settings.
The stones shall correspond to the names of the sons of Israel, twelve according to their names; engraved like a seal, each with its own name, for the twelve tribes.
You shall make on the breastpiece chains of twisted work, braided, of pure gold.
You shall make two gold rings on the breastpiece and put the two rings on the two ends of the breastpiece.
You shall put the two gold braids through the two rings at the ends of the breastpiece.
The two ends of the two braids you shall attach to the two settings, and attach them to the shoulder-pieces of the ephod, at its front.
You shall make two gold rings and put them on the two ends of the breastpiece, on its inner edge, the one facing the ephod.
You shall make two gold rings and put them on the two shoulder-pieces of the ephod, low down at the front, close to its seam, above the band of the ephod.
They shall bind the breastpiece by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a violet cord, so that it rests on the band of the ephod and the breastpiece does not come loose from the ephod.
Aaron shall bear the names of the sons of Israel on the breastpiece of judgement over his heart when he enters the holy place, as a continual remembrance before the LORD.

You shall put the Urim and the Thummim into the breastpiece of judgement, and they shall be over Aaron's heart when he comes before the LORD. So Aaron shall bear the judgement of the Israelites over his heart before the LORD continually.
You shall make the robe of the ephod entirely of violet.
The opening for the head shall be in the middle of it, with a woven edge all around the opening, like the opening of a corselet, so that it is not torn.
On its hem you shall make pomegranates of violet, purple, and scarlet, all around the hem, with gold bells between them all around:
a gold bell and a pomegranate, a gold bell and a pomegranate, all around the hem of the robe.
Aaron shall wear it when he serves, and its sound shall be heard when he enters the holy place before the LORD and when he goes out, so that he does not die.
You shall make a plate of pure gold and engrave on it, like the engraving of a seal: Holy to the LORD.
You shall fasten it with a violet cord, and it shall be on the turban; it shall be on the front of the turban.

It shall be on Aaron's forehead, and Aaron shall bear the iniquity attaching to the holy things that the Israelites consecrate, for all their holy gifts. It shall be on his forehead continually, so that they may find acceptance before the LORD.
You shall weave the tunic of fine linen in checker-work, make a turban of fine linen, and make a sash, the work of an embroiderer.
For Aaron's sons you shall make tunics, and you shall make sashes for them, and you shall make headdresses for them, for glory and for beauty.
You shall clothe your brother Aaron and his sons with him, and anoint them and ordain them and consecrate them, and they shall serve me as priests.
Make linen undergarments for them to cover their naked flesh; they shall reach from the hips to the thighs.

They shall be on Aaron and on his sons when they enter the tent of meeting or when they draw near to the altar to serve in the holy place, so that they do not incur iniquity and die. This is a perpetual statute for him and for his offspring after him.

exodus_29.t: This is what you shall do to them to consecrate them, so that they may serve me as priests: take one young bull and two rams without blemish;
and unleavened bread, unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers smeared with oil; you shall make them of fine wheat flour.
You shall put them in one basket and bring them near in the basket, along with the bull and the two rams.
You shall bring Aaron and his sons near to the entrance of the tent of meeting and wash them with water.
You shall take the garments and clothe Aaron with the tunic, the robe of the ephod, the ephod, and the breastpiece, and gird him with the band of the ephod.
You shall put the turban on his head and put the holy crown on the turban.
You shall take the anointing oil, pour it on his head, and anoint him.
You shall bring his sons near and clothe them with tunics.
You shall gird them with sashes, Aaron and his sons, and bind headdresses on them, and the priesthood shall be theirs as a perpetual statute. And you shall ordain Aaron and his sons.
You shall bring the bull near before the tent of meeting, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the head of the bull.
You shall slaughter the bull before the LORD, at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
You shall take some of the blood of the bull and put it on the horns of the altar with your finger, and pour out all the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
You shall take all the fat that covers the entrails, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys and the fat on them, and burn them as smoke on the altar.
But the flesh of the bull, its hide, and its offal you shall burn with fire outside the camp. It is a sin offering.
You shall take the one ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the head of the ram.
You shall slaughter the ram, take its blood, and dash it against the altar all around.
You shall cut the ram into its pieces, wash its entrails and its legs, and put them with its pieces and its head.
You shall burn the whole ram as smoke on the altar. It is a burnt offering to the LORD, a soothing odour, a food offering to the LORD.
You shall take the second ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the head of the ram.

You shall slaughter the ram, take some of its blood, and put it on the lobe of Aaron's ear and on the lobes of the right ears of his sons, on the thumbs of their right hands and on the big toes of their right feet; and you shall dash the blood against the altar all around.

You shall take some of the blood that is on the altar and some of the anointing oil and spatter it on Aaron and his garments, and on his sons and their garments with him; and he shall be holy, he and his garments, and his sons and their garments with him.
From the ram you shall take the fat, the fat tail, the fat that covers the entrails, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys with the fat on them, and the right thigh — for it is a ram of ordination.
And one round loaf of bread, one cake of oil-bread, and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread that is before the LORD.
You shall put all of it on the palms of Aaron and on the palms of his sons, and wave them as a wave offering before the LORD.
Then you shall take them from their hands and burn them as smoke on the altar, on top of the burnt offering, as a soothing odour before the LORD. It is a food offering to the LORD.
You shall take the breast of the ram of ordination that belongs to Aaron and wave it as a wave offering before the LORD, and it shall be your portion.

You shall consecrate the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution, which were waved and raised, from the ram of ordination, from what belongs to Aaron and from what belongs to his sons.

It shall belong to Aaron and his sons as a perpetual prescribed portion from the Israelites, for it is a contribution; it shall be a contribution from the Israelites out of their peace-offering sacrifices, their contribution to the LORD.
The holy garments that belong to Aaron shall pass to his sons after him, to be anointed in them and ordained in them.
The priest who succeeds him from among his sons shall wear them seven days, when he comes into the tent of meeting to serve in the holy place.
You shall take the ram of ordination and boil its flesh in a holy place.
Aaron and his sons shall eat the flesh of the ram and the bread that is in the basket, at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
They shall eat those things by which atonement was made, to ordain them and consecrate them; and no outsider shall eat them, for they are holy.
If any of the flesh of the ordination or of the bread is left over until morning, you shall burn what is left over with fire. It shall not be eaten, for it is holy.
You shall do this for Aaron and his sons, according to all that I have commanded you. Seven days you shall ordain them.
Each day you shall offer a bull as a sin offering for atonement, and you shall purify the altar by making atonement for it, and you shall anoint it to consecrate it.
Seven days you shall make atonement for the altar and consecrate it, and the altar shall be most holy; whatever touches the altar shall become holy.
This is what you shall offer on the altar: two year-old lambs each day, continually.
You shall offer the one lamb in the morning and the second lamb at twilight.
And with the one lamb, a tenth of fine flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of beaten oil, and a drink offering of a quarter of a hin of wine.
You shall offer the second lamb at twilight, with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning, as a soothing odour, a food offering to the LORD.
This shall be a continual burnt offering throughout your generations, at the entrance of the tent of meeting before the LORD, where I will meet with you to speak to you there.
There I will meet with the Israelites, and the place shall be consecrated by my glory.
I will consecrate the tent of meeting and the altar, and I will consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve me as priests.
I will dwell among the Israelites, and I will be their God.
And they shall know that I am the LORD their God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt so that I might dwell among them. I am the LORD their God.

exodus_30.t: You shall make an altar for burning incense; you shall make it of acacia wood.
It shall be a cubit long and a cubit wide, square, and two cubits high; its horns shall be of one piece with it.
You shall overlay it with pure gold, its top and its sides all around and its horns, and make a gold moulding around it.
You shall make two gold rings for it below its moulding, on its two sides; make them on its two flanks, to be holders for the poles by which it is carried.
You shall make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
You shall put it in front of the veil that is over the ark of the testimony, in front of the mercy seat that is over the testimony, where I will meet with you.
Aaron shall burn fragrant incense on it as smoke; every morning, when he tends the lamps, he shall burn it.
And when Aaron sets up the lamps at twilight, he shall burn it — a continual incense before the LORD throughout your generations.
You shall not offer on it any strange incense, or a burnt offering, or a grain offering, and you shall not pour out a drink offering on it.

Once a year Aaron shall make atonement on its horns; with the blood of the sin offering of atonement he shall make atonement on it once a year, throughout your generations. It is most holy to the LORD.
The LORD spoke to Moses:

When you take a census of the Israelites by their enrolment, each shall give a ransom for his life to the LORD when they are enrolled, so that there may be no plague among them when they are enrolled.
This is what everyone who passes over to those enrolled shall give: half a shekel by the sanctuary shekel — the shekel is twenty gerahs — half a shekel as a contribution to the LORD.
Everyone who passes over to those enrolled, from twenty years old and upward, shall give the contribution to the LORD.
The rich shall not give more and the poor shall not give less than half a shekel, when you give the contribution to the LORD to make atonement for your lives.

You shall take the atonement money from the Israelites and give it for the service of the tent of meeting, and it shall be a remembrance for the Israelites before the LORD, to make atonement for your lives.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
You shall make a bronze washbasin with a bronze stand for washing, and put it between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water in it.
Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and their feet from it.
When they come into the tent of meeting they shall wash with water, so that they do not die; or when they draw near to the altar to serve, to burn a food offering to the LORD as smoke,
they shall wash their hands and their feet, so that they do not die. This shall be a perpetual decree for them, for him and for his offspring throughout their generations.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
Take for yourself the finest spices: five hundred of flowing myrrh, half as much of fragrant cinnamon, two hundred and fifty, and two hundred and fifty of fragrant cane;
and five hundred of cassia, by the sanctuary shekel, and a hin of olive oil.
You shall make it a holy anointing oil, a compounded perfume, the work of a perfumer; it shall be a holy anointing oil.
With it you shall anoint the tent of meeting and the ark of the testimony,
the table and all its articles, the lampstand and its articles, the altar of incense,
the altar of burnt offering and all its articles, and the washbasin with its stand.
You shall consecrate them, and they shall be most holy; whatever touches them shall become holy.
You shall anoint Aaron and his sons and consecrate them, to serve me as priests.
And you shall say to the Israelites: This shall be a holy anointing oil to me throughout your generations.
It shall not be poured on anyone's body, and you shall not make any like it in the same proportions. It is holy; it shall be holy to you.
Anyone who compounds any like it, or who puts any of it on an outsider, shall be cut off from his kin.
The LORD said to Moses: Take for yourself spices — stacte, onycha, and galbanum — spices with pure frankincense; there shall be an equal part of each.
You shall make it into an incense, a compound, the work of a perfumer, salted, pure, and holy.
You shall beat some of it very fine and put some of it before the testimony in the tent of meeting, where I will meet with you. It shall be most holy to you.
As for the incense you make, you shall not make any for yourselves in the same proportions. It shall be holy to you, belonging to the LORD.
Anyone who makes any like it, to smell it, shall be cut off from his kin.

exodus_31.t: See, I have called by name Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
And I have filled him with the Spirit of God, with skill, understanding, and knowledge in every kind of work,
to devise designs, to work in gold, silver, and bronze,
in cutting stones for setting, and in carving wood, to work in every kind of craft.
And I have appointed with him Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan; and in the heart of everyone who is skilled I have put skill, so that they may make all that I have commanded you:
the tent of meeting, the ark for the testimony, the mercy seat that is on it, and all the articles of the tent,
the table and its articles, the pure lampstand and all its articles, the altar of incense,
the altar of burnt offering and all its articles, the washbasin and its stand,
the woven garments, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons for serving as priests,
the anointing oil, and the fragrant incense for the holy place. They shall do according to all that I have commanded you.
Say to the Israelites: Above all, you shall keep my sabbaths, for it is a sign between me and you throughout your generations, so that you may know that I am the LORD who consecrates you.
You shall keep the sabbath, for it is holy to you. Whoever profanes it shall surely be put to death; anyone who does work on it, that person shall be cut off from among his kin.
Six days work shall be done, but the seventh day is a sabbath of solemn rest, holy to the LORD. Anyone who does work on the sabbath day shall surely be put to death.
The Israelites shall keep the sabbath, observing the sabbath throughout their generations as a perpetual covenant.
It is a sign forever between me and the Israelites, for in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, and on the seventh day he ceased and took breath.
When he had finished speaking with Moses on Mount Sinai, he gave him the two tablets of the testimony, tablets of stone written by the finger of God.

exodus_32.t: When the people saw that Moses delayed in coming down from the mountain, the people gathered against Aaron and said to him, "Get up, make us gods who will go before us; for this Moses, the man who brought us up from the land of Egypt — we do not know what has become of him."
Aaron said to them, "Tear off the gold rings that are in the ears of your wives, your sons, and your daughters, and bring them to me."
So all the people tore off the gold rings that were in their ears and brought them to Aaron.
He took it from their hands, formed it with a graving tool, and made it into a cast-metal calf. And they said, "These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt."
When Aaron saw this, he built an altar before it, and Aaron called out and said, "Tomorrow shall be a festival to the LORD."
They rose early the next day and offered up burnt offerings and brought near peace offerings, and the people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.
The LORD said to Moses, "Go down, for your people, whom you brought up from the land of Egypt, have acted corruptly.

They have turned aside quickly from the way that I commanded them. They have made themselves a cast-metal calf and have bowed down to it and sacrificed to it and said, 'These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.'
The LORD said to Moses, "I have seen this people, and they are a stiff-necked people.
Now leave me alone, so that my anger may burn against them and I may make an end of them; and I will make you into a great nation."
But Moses entreated the face of the LORD his God and said, "Why, LORD, does your anger burn against your people, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt with great power and with a strong hand?

Why should the Egyptians say, 'It was with evil intent that he brought them out, to kill them in the mountains and make an end of them from the face of the earth'? Turn from your burning anger and relent concerning the harm to your people.

Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, your servants, to whom you swore by yourself and said, 'I will multiply your offspring like the stars of the heavens, and all this land that I have spoken of I will give to your offspring, and they shall possess it forever.'"
And the LORD relented concerning the harm that he had said he would do to his people.
Then Moses turned and went down from the mountain with the two tablets of the testimony in his hand, tablets written on both sides; they were written on the one side and on the other.
The tablets were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, engraved on the tablets.
When Joshua heard the sound of the people as they shouted, he said to Moses, "There is a sound of war in the camp."
But he said, "It is not the sound of singing for victory, and it is not the sound of singing for defeat; it is the sound of singing that I hear."
As he drew near the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, Moses' anger burned, and he threw the tablets from his hands and shattered them at the foot of the mountain.
He took the calf they had made, burned it with fire, ground it to powder, scattered it on the water, and made the Israelites drink it.
Moses said to Aaron, "What did this people do to you, that you have brought a great sin upon them?"
Aaron said, "Do not let my lord's anger burn. You yourself know the people, that they are set on evil.
"They said to me, 'Make us gods who will go before us; for this Moses, the man who brought us up from the land of Egypt — we do not know what has become of him.'
"So I said to them, 'Whoever has gold, tear it off.' They gave it to me, and I threw it into the fire, and out came this calf."
Moses saw that the people were running wild, for Aaron had let them run wild, to the derision of their adversaries.
Then Moses stood at the gate of the camp and said, "Who is for the LORD? To me!" And all the sons of Levi gathered to him.

He said to them, "Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Each of you put your sword on your thigh; go back and forth from gate to gate in the camp, and kill — each of you your brother, your companion, and your kin."
The sons of Levi did as Moses had said, and about three thousand of the people fell that day.
And Moses said, "Today you have filled your hand for the LORD, for each was against his own son and his own brother, and so to bring a blessing upon yourselves today."
The next day Moses said to the people, "You yourselves have sinned a great sin. And now I will go up to the LORD; perhaps I may make atonement for your sin."
So Moses returned to the LORD and said, "Ah, this people has sinned a great sin: they have made themselves gods of gold.
"And now, if you will forgive their sin — ; but if not, please wipe me out of your book that you have written."
The LORD said to Moses, "Whoever has sinned against me, that one I will wipe out of my book.
"Now go, lead the people to the place of which I have spoken to you. My angel will go before you. But on the day when I visit, I will visit their sin upon them."
And the LORD struck the people because they had made the calf, the one Aaron made.

exodus_33.t: The LORD said to Moses, "Go up from here, you and the people whom you brought up from the land of Egypt, to the land that I swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, saying, 'To your offspring I will give it.'
I will send an angel before you, and I will drive out the Canaanites, the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites,
to a land flowing with milk and honey. But I will not go up among you, for you are a stiff-necked people, lest I make an end of you on the way."
