When the people heard this bad word, they mourned, and no one put on his ornaments.

For the LORD had said to Moses, "Say to the Israelites, 'You are a stiff-necked people. If I were to go up among you for one moment, I would make an end of you. Now take off your ornaments, and I will decide what to do with you.'"
So the Israelites stripped themselves of their ornaments from Mount Horeb onward.

Moses used to take the tent and pitch it for himself outside the camp, far away from the camp, and he called it the tent of meeting. Everyone who sought the LORD would go out to the tent of meeting, which was outside the camp.
Whenever Moses went out to the tent, all the people would rise and stand, each at the entrance of his own tent, and watch Moses until he had entered the tent.
Whenever Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and stand at the entrance of the tent, and he would speak with Moses.
When all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance of the tent, all the people would rise and bow down, each at the entrance of his own tent.
And the LORD would speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his companion. Then Moses would return to the camp, but his servant Joshua son of Nun, a young man, would not leave the tent.

Moses said to the LORD, "See, you are saying to me, 'Bring up this people,' and you have not made known to me whom you will send with me. Yet you yourself have said, 'I know you by name, and you have also found favour in my eyes.'
Now, if I have found favour in your eyes, please make your ways known to me, that I may know you and so find favour in your eyes. And consider that this nation is your people."
And he said, "My presence will go with you, and I will give you rest."
And Moses said to him, "If your presence is not going, do not bring us up from here.

For how shall it be known that I have found favour in your eyes, I and your people, unless you go with us? So we shall be distinguished, I and your people, from every people on the face of the earth."
The LORD said to Moses, "I will also do this thing that you have spoken, for you have found favour in my eyes and I know you by name."
And Moses said, "Please show me your glory."

And he said, "I myself will cause all my goodness to pass before you, and I will proclaim the name of the LORD before you. I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion.
And he said, "You cannot see my face, for no human being can see me and live."
And the LORD said, "Here is a place beside me, and you shall stand on the rock.
And when my glory passes by, I will put you in the cleft of the rock and cover you with my palm until I have passed by.
Then I will remove my palm, and you shall see my back; but my face shall not be seen.

exodus_34.t: The LORD said to Moses, "Cut two tablets of stone for yourself like the first ones, and I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you shattered.
Be ready by morning, and in the morning come up to Mount Sinai and station yourself for me there on the top of the mountain.
No one shall come up with you, and let no one be seen anywhere on the mountain; nor shall the flocks or herds graze in front of that mountain.
So Moses cut two tablets of stone like the first ones, and rose early in the morning and went up Mount Sinai, as the LORD had commanded him, and he took the two tablets of stone in his hand.
The LORD came down in the cloud and stood with him there, and proclaimed the name of the LORD.
The LORD passed by before him and proclaimed: "The LORD, the LORD, a God compassionate and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness,

keeping steadfast love for thousands, bearing iniquity and transgression and sin, yet by no means clearing the guilty — visiting the iniquity of fathers upon sons and upon sons of sons, to the third and the fourth generation."
Moses quickly bowed low to the ground and bowed down.
And he said, "If I have found favour in your eyes, my Lord, let my Lord go in our midst — for it is a stiff-necked people — and forgive our iniquity and our sin, and take us as your possession."

And he said, "I am making a covenant. Before all your people I will do wonders that have not been created in all the earth or among any of the nations, and all the people among whom you live shall see the work of the LORD, for what I am about to do with you is fearful.
Observe what I am commanding you today. I am about to drive out before you the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
Take heed, lest you make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land into which you are going, and it become a snare among you.
Rather, you shall pull down their altars, break their pillars, and cut down their Asherahs.
For you shall not bow down to another god, for the LORD — Jealous is his name — is a jealous God.
Lest you make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, and when they prostitute themselves after their gods and sacrifice to their gods, someone invites you and you eat of his sacrifice;
and you take some of his daughters for your sons, and his daughters prostitute themselves after their gods and make your sons prostitute themselves after their gods.
You shall not make cast-metal gods for yourself.

You shall keep the festival of unleavened bread: seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of Abib, for in the month of Abib you came out of Egypt.
Every firstborn of a womb is mine, and all your livestock that bears a male, the firstborn of ox and sheep.

The firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem with a sheep; and if you do not redeem it, you shall break its neck. Every firstborn of your sons you shall redeem, and no one shall appear before me empty-handed.
Six days you shall labour, but on the seventh day you shall cease; at ploughing time and at harvest you shall cease.
You shall keep the festival of weeks, the firstfruits of the wheat harvest, and the festival of ingathering at the turn of the year.
Three times in the year all your males shall appear before the Lord GOD, the God of Israel.
For I will dispossess nations before you and enlarge your border, and no one shall covet your land when you go up to appear before the LORD your God three times in the year.
You shall not slaughter the blood of my sacrifice with anything leavened, and the sacrifice of the passover festival shall not be left over until morning.
The first of the firstfruits of your ground you shall bring to the house of the LORD your God. You shall not boil a kid in its mother's milk.
The LORD said to Moses, "Write these words for yourself, for according to these words I have made a covenant with you and with Israel."
He was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights; he ate no bread and drank no water. And he wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the ten words.

When Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the two tablets of the testimony in his hand — when he came down from the mountain — Moses did not know that the skin of his face shone because he had been speaking with him.
When Aaron and all the Israelites saw Moses, the skin of his face was shining, and they were afraid to come near him.
But Moses called to them, and Aaron and all the leaders of the congregation returned to him, and Moses spoke to them.
Afterward all the Israelites drew near, and he commanded them all that the LORD had spoken with him on Mount Sinai.
When Moses had finished speaking with them, he put a face covering over his face.
Whenever Moses went in before the LORD to speak with him, he would remove the face covering until he came out; and he would come out and tell the Israelites what he had been commanded.
And the Israelites would see the face of Moses, that the skin of Moses' face shone; and Moses would put the face covering back over his face until he went in to speak with him.

exodus_35.t: Moses assembled the whole congregation of the Israelites and said to them, "These are the words that the LORD has commanded, to do them.
For six days work is to be done, but the seventh day shall be for you a holy thing, a sabbath of solemn rest to the LORD. Anyone who does work on it shall be put to death.
You shall not kindle a fire in any of your dwellings on the sabbath day.
Moses said to the whole congregation of the Israelites, "This is the word that the LORD has commanded:
Take from among yourselves a contribution for the LORD. Everyone whose heart is willing is to bring it, the LORD's contribution: gold, silver, and bronze;
violet, purple, and scarlet; fine linen and goat hair;
ram skins dyed red, fine leather, and acacia wood;
oil for the light; spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense;
and onyx stones and stones for setting, for the ephod and for the breastpiece.
And let every skilled person among you come and make everything that the LORD has commanded:
the tabernacle, its tent and its covering, its clasps and its frames, its bars, its pillars and its bases;
the ark and its poles, the mercy seat, and the screening veil;
the table and its poles and all its articles, and the bread of the Presence;
the lampstand for the light and its articles and its lamps, and the oil for the light;
the altar of incense and its poles; the anointing oil and the fragrant incense; and the screen for the entrance of the tabernacle;
the altar of the burnt offering with its bronze grating, its poles and all its articles; the washbasin and its stand;
the hangings of the courtyard, its pillars and its bases, and the screen for the gate of the courtyard;
the tent pegs of the tabernacle and the tent pegs of the courtyard, and their cords;
the woven garments for serving in the holy place, the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments of his sons for serving as priests."
Then the whole congregation of the Israelites went out from before Moses.

And they came, everyone whose heart moved him and everyone whose spirit made him willing, and brought the LORD's contribution for the work of the tent of meeting and for all its service and for the holy garments.

The men came with the women; everyone whose heart was willing brought brooches and rings and signet rings and ornaments, every kind of gold article — every man who waved a wave-offering of gold to the LORD.
And everyone who had violet, purple or scarlet, fine linen or goat hair, ram skins dyed red or fine leather, brought them.
Everyone who offered a contribution of silver or bronze brought the LORD's contribution; and everyone who had acacia wood for any part of the work brought it.
And every skilled woman spun with her hands and brought what she had spun: the violet and the purple, the scarlet and the fine linen.
And all the women whose heart moved them with skill spun the goat hair.
And the leaders brought the onyx stones and the stones for setting, for the ephod and for the breastpiece,
and the spice and the oil for the light, for the anointing oil, and for the fragrant incense.

Every man and woman whose heart made them willing to bring anything for all the work that the LORD had commanded to be done through Moses — the Israelites brought it as a freewill offering to the LORD.
Then Moses said to the Israelites, "See, the LORD has called by name Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
He has filled him with the Spirit of God, with skill, understanding, and knowledge in every kind of work,
to devise designs, to work in gold, silver, and bronze,
in cutting stones for setting, and in carving wood, to work in every kind of designed craft.
And he has put it in his heart to teach, both him and Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan.

He has filled them with skill of heart to do all the work of a craftsman, a designer, an embroiderer in violet and purple and scarlet and fine linen, and a weaver — workers in every craft and devisers of designs.

exodus_36.t: So Bezalel and Oholiab are to work, and every skilled man in whom the LORD has put skill and understanding to know how to do all the work of the service of the holy place, according to everything the LORD has commanded."
Then Moses called Bezalel and Oholiab and every skilled man in whose heart the LORD had put skill, everyone whose heart moved him to draw near to the work and do it.

They received from Moses all the contribution that the Israelites had brought for the work of the service of the holy place, to do it. And the people still kept bringing him freewill offerings morning after morning.
So all the skilled men who were doing all the work of the holy place came, each one from the work he was doing,
and said to Moses, "The people are bringing much more than enough for the service of the work that the LORD commanded to be done."
So Moses gave an order, and they sent a proclamation through the camp: "Let no man or woman do any more work for the contribution of the holy place." And the people were restrained from bringing.
For what they had was enough for all the work, to do it, and more than enough.
And all the skilled men among those doing the work made the tabernacle: ten curtains of fine twisted linen and violet and purple and scarlet, with cherubim, the work of a designer — he made them.
The length of each curtain was twenty-eight cubits and the breadth four cubits; all the curtains had one measure.
He joined five of the curtains to one another, and the other five curtains he joined to one another.
He made loops of violet on the edge of the outermost curtain of the first set, and did the same on the edge of the outermost curtain of the second set.
He made fifty loops on the one curtain and fifty loops on the end of the curtain in the second set, the loops opposite one another.
And he made fifty clasps of gold and joined the curtains to one another with the clasps, and the tabernacle became one.
He made curtains of goat hair for a tent over the tabernacle; he made eleven of them.
The length of each curtain was thirty cubits and the breadth four cubits; all eleven curtains had one measure.
He joined five of the curtains together by themselves and six of the curtains by themselves.
He made fifty loops on the edge of the outermost curtain of the one set, and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain of the second set.
He made fifty clasps of bronze to join the tent together, so that it would be one.
He made a covering for the tent of ram skins dyed red, and a covering of fine leather over that.
He made the frames for the tabernacle of acacia wood, standing upright.
The length of each frame was ten cubits and the breadth of each frame a cubit and a half.
Each frame had two tenons, joined to one another; he did this for all the frames of the tabernacle.
He made the frames for the tabernacle: twenty frames for the south side.
And he made forty silver bases to go under the twenty frames: two bases under each frame for its two tenons.
And for the second side of the tabernacle, the north side, he made twenty frames,
and their forty silver bases, two bases under each frame.
And for the rear of the tabernacle, on the west, he made six frames.
And he made two frames for the corners of the tabernacle at the rear.
They were doubled from below and complete together at the top, into the one ring; he did this for both of them, for the two corners.
So there were eight frames with their silver bases, sixteen bases, two bases under each frame.
He made bars of acacia wood, five for the frames of the one side of the tabernacle,
five bars for the frames of the second side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the frames of the tabernacle at the rear, on the west.
He made the middle bar to run through the middle of the frames from end to end.
He overlaid the frames with gold and made their rings of gold as holders for the bars, and he overlaid the bars with gold.
He made the veil of violet, purple and scarlet and fine twisted linen; he made it the work of a designer, with cherubim.
He made four pillars of acacia for it and overlaid them with gold, with gold hooks, and cast four silver bases for them.
And he made a screen for the entrance of the tent of violet, purple and scarlet and fine twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer,
and its five pillars with their hooks. He overlaid their tops and their bands with gold, and their five bases were bronze.

exodus_37.t: Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood, two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high.
He overlaid it with pure gold inside and out, and made a gold moulding around it.
He cast four gold rings for it, on its four feet — two rings on one side and two rings on the other side.
He made poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
He put the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, to carry the ark.
He made a mercy seat of pure gold, two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
He made two cherubim of gold; he made them of hammered work, at the two ends of the mercy seat.
One cherub was at one end and one cherub at the other end; he made the cherubim of one piece with the mercy seat, at its two ends.
The cherubim spread out their wings upward, covering the mercy seat with their wings, their faces toward each other; the faces of the cherubim were toward the mercy seat.
He made the table of acacia wood, two cubits long, a cubit wide, and a cubit and a half high.
He overlaid it with pure gold and made a gold moulding around it.
He made a rim of a handbreadth around it, and made a gold moulding for its rim all around.
He cast four gold rings for it and put the rings on the four corners at its four legs.
The rings were close to the rim, as holders for the poles to carry the table.
He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold, to carry the table.
He made the articles that were on the table — its dishes and pans and bowls, and the jars used for pouring — of pure gold.
He made the lampstand of pure gold. He made the lampstand of hammered work — its base and its shaft; its cups, its bulbs and its blossoms were of one piece with it.
Six branches went out from its sides, three branches of the lampstand from one side and three branches of the lampstand from the other side.

There were three cups shaped like almond blossoms on the one branch, with a bulb and a blossom, and three cups shaped like almond blossoms on the next branch, with a bulb and a blossom — so for the six branches going out from the lampstand.
On the lampstand itself were four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with their bulbs and their blossoms.
A bulb was under the first pair of branches from it, a bulb under the second pair, and a bulb under the third pair — for the six branches going out from it.
Their bulbs and their branches were of one piece with it; all of it was one piece of hammered work of pure gold.
He made its seven lamps, and its tongs and firepans, of pure gold.
He made it, and all its articles, of a talent of pure gold.
He made the altar of incense of acacia wood, a cubit long and a cubit wide — square — and two cubits high; its horns were of one piece with it.
He overlaid it with pure gold — its top, its sides all around, and its horns — and made a gold moulding around it.
He made two gold rings for it below its moulding, on its two sides, on both its flanks, as holders for the poles to carry it with.
He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
And he made the holy anointing oil and the pure fragrant incense, the work of a perfumer.

exodus_38.t: He made the altar of the burnt offering of acacia wood, five cubits long and five cubits wide — square — and three cubits high.
He made its horns on its four corners; the horns were of one piece with it, and he overlaid it with bronze.
He made all the articles of the altar — the pots, the shovels, the basins, the forks and the firepans; he made all its articles of bronze.
He made a grating for the altar, a bronze network, under its ledge below, reaching halfway up.
He cast four rings at the four ends of the bronze grating, as holders for the poles.
He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with bronze.
He put the poles into the rings on the sides of the altar, to carry it with. He made it hollow, of boards.
He made the washbasin of bronze and its stand of bronze, from the mirrors of the serving women who served at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
He made the courtyard. For the south side, the hangings of the courtyard were of fine twisted linen, a hundred cubits long;
their twenty pillars and their twenty bases were of bronze, and the hooks of the pillars and their bands were of silver.
For the north side, a hundred cubits; their twenty pillars and their twenty bases were of bronze, and the hooks of the pillars and their bands were of silver.
For the west side, hangings of fifty cubits, with ten pillars and ten bases; the hooks of the pillars and their bands were of silver.
And for the east side, fifty cubits.
There were hangings of fifteen cubits for the one side, with three pillars and three bases;
and for the second side, on either side of the gate of the courtyard, hangings of fifteen cubits, with three pillars and three bases.
All the hangings around the courtyard were of fine twisted linen.
The bases for the pillars were of bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands were of silver, and their tops were overlaid with silver; all the pillars of the courtyard were banded with silver.

The screen for the gate of the courtyard was the work of an embroiderer, of violet, purple and scarlet and fine twisted linen; it was twenty cubits long, and its height, measured across the fabric, was five cubits, matching the hangings of the courtyard.
Their four pillars and their four bases were of bronze; their hooks were of silver, and the overlay of their tops and their bands were of silver.
And all the tent pegs for the tabernacle and for the courtyard all around were of bronze.
These are the accounts of the tabernacle, the tabernacle of the testimony, which were drawn up at Moses' command: the service of the Levites, under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
And Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made everything that the LORD had commanded Moses.
With him was Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, a craftsman and designer and embroiderer in violet, purple and scarlet and fine linen.
All the gold used for the work, in all the work of the holy place — the gold of the wave-offering — was twenty-nine talents and seven hundred and thirty shekels by the sanctuary shekel.
The silver from those of the congregation who were enrolled was a hundred talents and 1,775 shekels by the sanctuary shekel:
a beka a head — that is, half a shekel by the sanctuary shekel — for everyone who passed over to those enrolled, from twenty years old and upward: 603,550 men.
The hundred talents of silver were for casting the bases of the holy place and the bases of the veil — a hundred bases for the hundred talents, a talent to a base.
And from the 1,775 shekels he made hooks for the pillars, overlaid their tops, and banded them.
The bronze of the wave-offering was seventy talents and 2,400 shekels.
With it he made the bases for the entrance of the tent of meeting, the bronze altar and its bronze grating, and all the articles of the altar,
the bases of the courtyard all around and the bases of the gate of the courtyard, and all the tent pegs of the tabernacle and all the tent pegs of the courtyard all around.

exodus_39.t: From the violet and the purple and the scarlet they made woven garments for serving in the holy place, and they made the holy garments for Aaron, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He made the ephod of gold, violet, purple and scarlet, and fine twisted linen.
They hammered out sheets of gold and he cut them into threads, to work in among the violet and the purple and the scarlet and the fine linen, the work of a designer.
They made joined shoulder-pieces for it, joined at its two ends.
The band of its ephod, which was on it, was of one piece with it, of the same workmanship: gold, violet, purple and scarlet, and fine twisted linen — just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They prepared the onyx stones, set in gold settings, engraved like a seal, with the names of the sons of Israel.
He put them on the shoulder-pieces of the ephod as stones of remembrance for the Israelites, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He made the breastpiece, the work of a designer, like the work of the ephod: gold, violet, purple and scarlet, and fine twisted linen.
It was square; they made the breastpiece doubled over, a span long and a span wide, doubled over.
They set in it four rows of stones. The first row was ruby, topaz and emerald;
the second row was turquoise, sapphire and diamond;
the third row was jacinth, agate and amethyst;
and the fourth row was beryl, onyx and jasper; they were enclosed in gold settings in their mountings.
The stones were according to the names of the sons of Israel — twelve of them, with their names, engraved like a seal, each with its own name, for the twelve tribes.
They made on the breastpiece chains of twisted work, braided, of pure gold.
They made two gold settings and two gold rings, and they put the two rings on the two ends of the breastpiece.
They put the two gold braids on the two rings at the ends of the breastpiece.
The two ends of the two braids they attached to the two settings, and they attached those to the shoulder-pieces of the ephod, at its front.
They made two gold rings and put them on the two ends of the breastpiece, on the edge facing the ephod, on the inside.
They made two gold rings and put them on the two shoulder-pieces of the ephod, low down at the front, close to its seam, above the band of the ephod.

They bound the breastpiece by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a cord of violet, so that it would sit on the band of the ephod and the breastpiece would not come loose from the ephod, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He made the robe of the ephod, the work of a weaver, entirely of violet.
The opening of the robe was in the middle of it, like the opening of a corselet, with a binding around the opening so that it would not tear.
On the hem of the robe they made pomegranates of violet, purple and scarlet, twisted.
They made bells of pure gold and put the bells among the pomegranates on the hem of the robe all around, among the pomegranates —
a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, all around the hem of the robe, for serving — just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They made the tunics of fine linen, the work of a weaver, for Aaron and his sons,
the turban of fine linen, the head-wraps of the headdresses of fine linen, and the linen undergarments of fine twisted linen,
and the sash of fine twisted linen and violet and purple and scarlet, the work of an embroiderer — just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They made the plate of the holy crown of pure gold and inscribed on it, like the engraving of a seal: Holy to the LORD.
They fastened a cord of violet to it, to set it on the turban above, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
So all the labour of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting was finished. The Israelites did everything the LORD had commanded Moses; so they did.
Then they brought the tabernacle to Moses: the tent and all its articles, its clasps, its frames, its bars, its pillars and its bases;
the covering of ram skins dyed red, the covering of fine leather, and the screening veil;
the ark of the testimony with its poles, and the mercy seat;
the table with all its articles, and the bread of the Presence;
the pure lampstand with its lamps, the lamps set in their row, and all its articles, and the oil for the light;
the golden altar, the anointing oil, the fragrant incense, and the screen for the entrance of the tent;
the bronze altar with its bronze grating, its poles and all its articles; the washbasin and its stand;

the hangings of the courtyard with its pillars and its bases, the screen for the gate of the courtyard, its cords and its tent pegs, and all the articles for the service of the tabernacle, for the tent of meeting;
the woven garments for serving in the holy place, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons for serving as priests.
According to everything the LORD had commanded Moses, so the Israelites did all the labour.
And Moses saw all the work, and there it was: they had done it just as the LORD had commanded; so they had done. And Moses blessed them.

exodus_40.t: And the LORD spoke to Moses:
"On the first day of the first month you are to set up the tabernacle of the tent of meeting.
Put the ark of the testimony there, and screen the ark with the veil.
Bring in the table and set out its arrangement; bring in the lampstand and set up its lamps.
Put the golden altar for incense in front of the ark of the testimony, and set up the screen for the entrance of the tabernacle.
Put the altar of the burnt offering in front of the entrance to the tabernacle of the tent of meeting.
Put the washbasin between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water in it.
Set up the courtyard all around, and put up the screen for the gate of the courtyard.
Take the anointing oil and anoint the tabernacle and everything in it; consecrate it, with all its articles, and it will be holy.
Anoint the altar of the burnt offering and all its articles; consecrate the altar, and the altar will be most holy.
Anoint the washbasin and its stand, and consecrate it.
Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent of meeting and wash them with water.
Clothe Aaron with the holy garments, anoint him and consecrate him, and he will serve me as priest.
Bring his sons and clothe them with tunics.
Anoint them as you anointed their father, and they will serve me as priests. Their anointing will be for them a perpetual priesthood throughout their generations."
And Moses did everything the LORD commanded him; so he did.
And in the first month of the second year, on the first day of the month, the tabernacle was set up.
Moses set up the tabernacle: he laid its bases, set up its frames, put in its bars, and raised its pillars.
He spread the tent over the tabernacle and put the covering of the tent over it above, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He took the testimony and put it into the ark, set the poles on the ark, and put the mercy seat on the ark above.
He brought the ark into the tabernacle, set up the screening veil, and screened the ark of the testimony, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He put the table in the tent of meeting, on the north side of the tabernacle, outside the veil.
He set out on it an arrangement of bread before the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He put the lampstand in the tent of meeting opposite the table, on the south side of the tabernacle.
He set up the lamps before the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He put the golden altar in the tent of meeting in front of the veil,
and he sent up fragrant incense on it in smoke, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He put up the screen for the entrance of the tabernacle.
He set the altar of the burnt offering at the entrance of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting, and offered up on it the burnt offering and the grain offering, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He put the washbasin between the tent of meeting and the altar and put water in it for washing.
Moses and Aaron and his sons washed their hands and their feet from it.
Whenever they went into the tent of meeting and whenever they drew near to the altar, they washed, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He set up the courtyard around the tabernacle and the altar, and put up the screen for the gate of the courtyard. So Moses finished the work.
Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
And Moses was not able to enter the tent of meeting, because the cloud had settled on it and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
Whenever the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle, the Israelites would set out on all their journeys.
But if the cloud was not taken up, they would not set out until the day it was taken up.
For the cloud of the LORD was over the tabernacle by day, and fire was in it by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel, throughout all their journeys.

ezekiel_1.t: In the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth of the month, while I was among the exiles by the river Kebar, the heavens were opened and I saw visions of God.
On the fifth of the month — it was the fifth year of the exile of king Jehoiachin —
the word of the LORD came indeed to Ezekiel son of Buzi the priest, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Kebar; and the hand of the LORD was upon him there.

And I looked, and there was a storm wind coming from the north, a great cloud and flashing fire, with brightness around it; and from its midst something like glowing metal, from the midst of the fire.
And from its midst came a likeness of four living creatures. And this was their appearance: they had a likeness of a human.
Each one had four faces, and each one of them had four wings.
And their legs were straight, and the sole of their feet was like the sole of a calf's foot, and they gleamed like the gleam of burnished bronze.
And human hands were under their wings on their four sides; and the four of them had their faces and their wings.
Their wings touched one another. They did not turn when they moved; each moved straight toward the side its face was turned to.

And the likeness of their faces was this: the face of a human; and the face of a lion on the right, for the four of them; and the face of an ox on the left, for the four of them; and the face of an eagle, for the four of them.
And their faces and their wings were spread apart above; each had two wings touching those of another, and two covering its body.
And each moved toward the side its face was turned to. Wherever the spirit was to go, they went; they did not turn when they moved.

And as for the likeness of the living creatures: their appearance was like burning coals of fire, like the appearance of torches. It was moving about among the living creatures; and the fire had brightness, and out of the fire went lightning.
And the living creatures darted back and forth, like the appearance of a flash of lightning.
And I saw the living creatures, and there was one wheel on the ground beside the living creatures, for each of its four faces.

The appearance of the wheels and their construction was like the gleam of beryl, and the four of them had one likeness; and their appearance and their construction was as though a wheel were within a wheel.
They moved on their four sides when they moved; they did not turn when they moved.
And their rims — they were tall, and they were fearsome; and their rims were full of eyes all around, for the four of them.
And when the living creatures moved, the wheels moved beside them; and when the living creatures were lifted up from the ground, the wheels were lifted up.
Wherever the spirit was to go, they went — there the spirit was to go — and the wheels were lifted up alongside them, for the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.

When they moved, the wheels moved; and when they stood still, the wheels stood still; and when they were lifted up from the ground, the wheels were lifted up alongside them, for the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.
And over the heads of the living creature was a likeness of a vault, like the gleam of awesome ice, spread out over their heads above.
And under the vault their wings were straight, each toward the next; each had two covering it, and each had two covering it — their bodies.

And I heard the sound of their wings, like the sound of many waters, like the sound of the Almighty, when they moved — a sound of tumult, like the sound of an army. When they stood still, they let their wings drop.
And there came a sound from above the vault that was over their heads. When they stood still, they let their wings drop.

And above the vault that was over their heads was something like the appearance of a sapphire stone, a likeness of a throne; and on the likeness of the throne was a likeness like the appearance of a human upon it, above.

And I saw something like glowing metal, like the appearance of fire enclosing it all around, from the appearance of his loins upward; and from the appearance of his loins downward I saw something like the appearance of fire, and he had brightness all around.

Like the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud on a day of rain, so was the appearance of the brightness all around. That was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD. And I saw it, and I fell on my face, and I heard a voice speaking.

ezekiel_2.t: And he said to me, "Mortal, stand on your feet, and I will speak with you."
And a spirit came into me as he spoke to me, and it set me on my feet; and I heard the one speaking to me.
And he said to me, "Mortal, I am sending you to the people of Israel, to rebellious nations who have rebelled against me. They and their fathers have transgressed against me to this very day.
And the children are stern of face and hard of heart. I am sending you to them, and you shall say to them, 'This is what Lord GOD says.'
And they — whether they listen or whether they refrain, for they are a house of rebellion — will know that a prophet has been among them.

And you, mortal — do not fear them, and do not fear their words, though nettles and thorns are with you and you are living among scorpions. Do not fear their words, and do not be dismayed at their faces, for they are a house of rebellion.
And you shall speak my words to them, whether they listen or whether they refrain, for they are rebellion.
And you, mortal, hear what I am speaking to you. Do not be rebellion like the house of rebellion. Open your mouth and eat what I am giving you."
And I looked, and there was a hand stretched out to me, and in it was a scroll of a document.
And he spread it out before me, and it was written on the front and on the back; and written on it were lamentations and moaning and wailing.

ezekiel_3.t: And he said to me, "Mortal, eat what you find. Eat this scroll, and go, speak to the house of Israel."
And I opened my mouth, and he made me eat this scroll.
And he said to me, "Mortal, feed your belly and fill your inward parts with this scroll that I am giving you." And I ate it, and in my mouth it was as sweet as honey.
And he said to me, "Mortal, go, come to the house of Israel, and you shall speak my words to them.
For you are not being sent to a people of obscure speech and difficult language, but to the house of Israel —
not to many peoples of obscure speech and difficult language, whose words you would not understand. Surely, if I had sent you to them, they would listen to you.
But the house of Israel will not be willing to listen to you, for they are not willing to listen to me; for the whole house of Israel are hard of forehead and stern of heart.
Look, I have made your face hard to match their faces, and your forehead hard to match their forehead.
Like shamir, harder than flint, I have made your forehead. Do not fear them and do not be dismayed at their faces, for they are a house of rebellion."
And he said to me, "Mortal, all my words that I will speak to you — take them into your heart, and hear them with your ears.
And go, come to the exiles, to the children of your people, and speak to them and say to them, 'This is what Lord GOD says' — whether they listen or whether they refrain."
And a spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me the sound of a great rumbling: "Blessed be the glory of the LORD from his place!"
And the sound of the wings of the living creatures brushing against one another, and the sound of the wheels alongside them, and the sound of a great rumbling.
And a spirit lifted me up and took me away, and I went in bitterness, in the rage of my spirit; and the hand of the LORD was strong upon me.
And I came to the exiles at Tel Abib, who were living by the river Kebar, and I sat where they were living; and I sat there seven days, appalled among them.
And at the end of seven days the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel. You shall hear a word from my mouth and warn them from me.

When I say to the wicked, 'You shall surely die,' and you have not warned him and have not spoken to warn the wicked from his wicked way, to keep him alive — that wicked one shall die in his iniquity, and I will require his blood from your hand.
But you, if you have warned the wicked and he has not turned from his wickedness and from his wicked way — he shall die in his iniquity, and you have delivered your own life.

And when a righteous one turns from his righteousness and does injustice, and I put an obstacle before him — he shall die. Because you did not warn him, he shall die in his sin, and the righteous acts he did shall not be remembered; and I will require his blood from your hand.
But you, if you have warned him, the righteous one, so that the righteous one does not sin, and he has not sinned — he shall surely live, because he was warned; and you have delivered your own life."
And the hand of the LORD was upon me there, and he said to me, "Arise, go out to the plain, and there I will speak with you."
And I arose and went out to the plain, and there the glory of the LORD was standing, like the glory that I had seen by the river Kebar; and I fell on my face.
And a spirit came into me and set me on my feet, and he spoke with me and said to me, "Go, shut yourself up inside your house.
And you, mortal — look, they will put ropes on you and bind you with them, and you will not go out among them.
And I will make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth, and you will be mute, and you will not be a man who reproves them, for they are a house of rebellion.

And when I speak with you I will open your mouth, and you shall say to them, 'This is what Lord GOD says.' Let the one who hears, hear; and the one who refrains, let him refrain — for they are a house of rebellion."

ezekiel_4.t: "And you, mortal, take a brick and set it before you, and inscribe a city on it — Jerusalem.
And lay a siege against it, and build a siege-wall against it, and throw up a ramp against it, and set camps against it, and place battering-rams against it all around.

And you, take an iron griddle and set it as an iron wall between you and the city; set your face against it, and it shall be under siege, and you shall besiege it. It is a sign for the house of Israel.
And you, lie on your left side and put the iniquity of the house of Israel on it. For the number of days that you lie on it, you shall bear their iniquity.
And I myself have assigned to you the years of their iniquity as a number of days: three hundred and ninety days. And you shall bear the iniquity of the house of Israel.

And when you have completed these, you shall lie a second time on your right side and bear the iniquity of the house of Judah: forty days. A day for a year, a day for a year, I have assigned it to you.
And you shall set your face toward the siege of Jerusalem, with your arm bared, and prophesy against it.
And look, I will put ropes on you, and you shall not turn from one side to your other side until you have completed the days of your siege.

And you, take wheat and barley and beans and lentils and millet and spelt, and put them in one vessel, and make them into bread for yourself. For the number of days that you are lying on your side — three hundred and ninety days — you shall eat it.
And your food that you eat shall be by weight, twenty shekels a day; from time to time you shall eat it.
And water by measure you shall drink, a sixth of a hin; from time to time you shall drink.
And you shall eat it as a barley cake, and you shall bake it over balls of human excrement, before their eyes."
And the LORD said, "Thus the people of Israel shall eat their bread unclean, among the nations where I will banish them."

And I said, "Alas, Lord GOD! Look, I have never been made unclean; from my youth until now I have not eaten an animal that died of itself or one torn by beasts, and no foul flesh has come into my mouth."
And he said to me, "See, I give you cattle dung in place of human dung, and you shall prepare your bread over it."
And he said to me, "Mortal, look, I am about to break the staff of bread in Jerusalem, and they shall eat bread by weight and in anxiety, and drink water by measure and in horror,
so that they may lack bread and water, and be appalled, each with his brother, and waste away in their iniquity."

ezekiel_5.t: "And you, mortal, take a sharp sword — take it as a barber's razor — and pass it over your head and over your beard. Then take scales for weighing and divide the hair.

A third you shall burn in the fire in the middle of the city when the days of the siege are completed. And you shall take a third and strike it with the sword all around the city; and a third you shall scatter to the wind, and I will draw a sword after them.
And you shall take a few of them, a small number, and bind them into the skirts of your robe.
And of these again you shall take some, and throw them into the middle of the fire, and burn them in the fire. From it a fire will go out to all the house of Israel."
This is what Lord GOD says: "This is Jerusalem. In the middle of the nations I have set her, with lands around her.

And she has rebelled against my judgements more wickedly than the nations, and against my statutes more than the lands that are around her; for they have rejected my judgements, and as for my statutes, they have not walked in them.

Therefore this is what Lord GOD says: "Because your tumult is more than that of the nations around you — you have not walked in my statutes and you have not done my judgements, and you have not even acted according to the judgements of the nations around you —
therefore this is what Lord GOD says: Look, I am against you — I myself — and I will perform acts of judgement in the middle of you before the eyes of the nations.
And I will do in you what I have not done, and the like of which I will never do again, because of all your abominations.
Therefore fathers shall eat sons in the middle of you, and sons shall eat their fathers; and I will perform acts of judgement in you, and I will scatter all your remnant to every wind.

Therefore, as I live — declares Lord GOD — surely, because you have made my sanctuary unclean with all your detestable things and with all your abominations, I too will cut you back, and my eye will not spare, and I too will show no pity.

A third of you shall die by pestilence and come to an end by famine in the middle of you; a third shall fall by the sword around you; and a third I will scatter to every wind, and I will draw a sword after them.
And my anger will be spent, and I will give my rage rest upon them, and I will be relieved; and they will know that I, the LORD, have spoken in my jealousy, when I have completed my rage upon them.
And I will make you a ruin and a reproach among the nations that are around you, before the eyes of everyone who passes by.

And it shall be a reproach and a taunt, a warning and a horror to the nations that are around you, when I perform acts of judgement on you in anger and in rage and with rebukes of rage. I, the LORD, have spoken.
When I shoot the evil arrows of famine at them, which will be for destruction, which I will shoot to destroy you — and I will increase famine upon you and break your staff of bread —
and I will send famine and wild beasts upon you, and they will bereave you; and pestilence and blood will pass through you, and I will bring a sword upon you. I, the LORD, have spoken."

ezekiel_6.t: And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, set your face toward the mountains of Israel, and prophesy against them,

and say: Mountains of Israel, hear the word of Lord GOD. This is what Lord GOD says to the mountains and to the hills, to the ravines and to the valleys: Look, I myself am bringing a sword upon you, and I will destroy your high places.
And your altars shall be made desolate and your incense altars shattered; and I will make your slain fall before your idols.
And I will put the corpses of the people of Israel before their idols, and I will scatter your bones around your altars.

In all your dwelling places the cities shall be laid waste and the high places made desolate, so that your altars may be laid waste and held guilty, and your idols shattered and brought to an end, and your incense altars cut down, and your works wiped out.
And the slain shall fall in the middle of you, and you will know that I am the LORD.
But I will leave some over: some of you will escape the sword among the nations, when you are scattered among the lands.

And your escapees will remember me among the nations where they have been taken captive — how I was broken by their whoring heart that turned aside from me, and by their eyes that whored after their idols — and they will loathe themselves to their own faces for the evils they did, for all their abominations.
And they will know that I am the LORD: it was not for nothing that I spoke of doing this evil to them."

This is what Lord GOD says: Strike with your hand and stamp with your foot and say, "Alas!" — over all the evil abominations of the house of Israel, who will fall by the sword, by famine and by pestilence.
The one far off shall die by pestilence, the one near shall fall by the sword, and the one left over and preserved shall die by famine; and I will complete my rage upon them.

And you will know that I am the LORD, when their slain are among their idols, around their altars, on every high hill, on all the mountain tops, and under every green tree and under every leafy terebinth — the place where they gave a soothing odour to all their idols.
And I will stretch out my hand over them and make the land a desolation and a waste, from the wilderness to Diblah, in all their dwelling places; and they will know that I am the LORD."

ezekiel_7.t: And the word of the LORD came to me:
"And you, mortal — this is what Lord GOD says to the land of Israel: An end! The end has come upon the four corners of the land.
Now the end is upon you, and I will send my anger against you, and I will judge you according to your ways, and I will requite upon you all your abominations.
And my eye will not spare you, and I will not show pity; for I will requite your ways upon you, and your abominations shall be in the middle of you. And you will know that I am the LORD.
This is what Lord GOD says: An evil! A single evil! Look, it is coming.
An end has come! The end has come! It has woken up against you. Look, it is coming.
Doom has come upon you, inhabitant of the land. The time has come, the day is near — confusion, and not a shout on the mountains.
Now, soon, I will pour out my rage upon you and complete my anger against you, and I will judge you according to your ways, and I will requite upon you all your abominations.

And my eye will not spare, and I will not show pity. According to your ways I will requite upon you, and your abominations shall be in the middle of you. And you will know that I, the LORD, am the one striking.
Look, the day! Look, it is coming. Doom has gone out. The rod has blossomed; arrogance has budded.
Violence has risen into a rod of wickedness. Nothing of them, nothing of their multitude, nothing of their tumult; and there is no distinction among them.
The time has come, the day has arrived. Let the buyer not rejoice and the seller not mourn, for burning anger is against all her multitude.

For the seller will not return to what was sold, even while they are still alive; for the vision concerning all her multitude will not turn back, and no one will strengthen himself in his iniquity, in his life.
They have blown the trumpet and made everything ready, but there is no one going to the battle, for my burning anger is against all her multitude.
The sword is outside, and pestilence and famine inside. Whoever is in the open country will die by the sword, and whoever is in the city — famine and pestilence will consume him.
And their escapees will escape and be on the mountains, like the doves of the valleys, all of them moaning, each in his iniquity.
All hands will drop, and all knees will run with water.
And they will gird on sackcloth, and shuddering will cover them; on every face, shame; on all their heads, baldness.

They will throw their silver into the streets, and their gold will become an impurity. Their silver and their gold will not be able to deliver them on the day of the LORD's fury; they will not satisfy their appetite or fill their inward parts, for it has been the stumbling block of their iniquity.
And the beauty of its ornament — he turned it into pride, and in it they made the images of their abominations, their detestable things. Therefore I have made it an impurity to them.
And I will give it into the hand of strangers as spoil, and to the wicked of the earth as plunder, and they will profane it.
And I will turn my face away from them, and they will profane my treasured place; and robbers will come into it and profane it.
Make the chain! For the land is full of the judgement of blood, and the city is full of violence.
And I will bring the worst of the nations, and they will take possession of their houses; and I will put an end to the pride of the strong, and their sanctuaries will be profaned.
Anguish has come. They will seek peace, and there is none.
Disaster upon disaster will come, and report upon report. And they will seek a vision from a prophet, and law will perish from the priest, and counsel from the elders.

The king will mourn, and the prince will clothe himself in desolation, and the hands of the people of the land will be terrified. I will deal with them according to their way, and by their own judgements I will judge them; and they will know that I am the LORD."

ezekiel_8.t: In the sixth year, in the sixth month, on the fifth of the month, I was sitting in my house and the elders of Judah were sitting before me; and there the hand of Lord GOD fell upon me.

And I looked, and there was a likeness like the appearance of fire: from the appearance of his loins downward, fire; and from his loins upward, something like the appearance of brightness, like glowing metal.

And he stretched out the form of a hand and took me by a lock of my hair; and a spirit lifted me between the earth and the heavens and brought me to Jerusalem in visions of God, to the entrance of the inner gate that faces north, where the seat of the idol of jealousy stood, the one that provokes to jealousy.
And there was the glory of the God of Israel, like the appearance that I had seen on the plain.
And he said to me, "Mortal, lift up your eyes now toward the north." And I lifted up my eyes toward the north, and there, north of the altar gate, was this idol of jealousy, at the entrance.

And he said to me, "Mortal, do you see what they are doing — the great abominations that the house of Israel are doing here, to drive me far from my sanctuary? And you will see still greater abominations."
And he brought me to the entrance of the court; and I looked, and there was a hole in the wall.
And he said to me, "Mortal, dig now through the wall." And I dug through the wall, and there was an opening.
And he said to me, "Go in and see the wicked abominations that they are doing here."
And I went in and looked, and there was every form of creeping thing and detestable animal, and all the idols of the house of Israel, carved on the wall all around, all around.

And seventy men of the elders of the house of Israel, with Jaazaniah son of Shaphan standing among them, were standing before them, each with his censer in his hand; and the fragrance of the cloud of incense was going up.

And he said to me, "Have you seen, mortal, what the elders of the house of Israel are doing in the dark, each in the rooms of his carved image? For they are saying, 'The LORD does not see us; the LORD has forsaken the land.'"
And he said to me, "You will yet again see great abominations that they are doing."
And he brought me to the entrance of the gate of the house of the LORD that faces north; and there the women were sitting, weeping for the Tammuz.
And he said to me, "Have you seen, mortal? You will yet again see abominations greater than these."

And he brought me to the inner court of the house of the LORD; and there, at the entrance of the temple of the LORD, between the porch and the altar, were about twenty-five men, their backs to the temple of the LORD and their faces eastward; and they were bowing down eastward to the sun.

And he said to me, "Have you seen, mortal? Is it too slight a thing for the house of Judah to do the abominations that they have done here, that they have filled the land with violence and have turned back to provoke me to anger? And look, they are putting the branch to their nose.
And I too will act in rage. My eye will not spare, and I will not show pity; and though they call out in my ears with a great voice, I will not hear them."

ezekiel_9.t: And he called out in my ears with a great voice: "The punishments of the city have drawn near, and each with his weapon of destruction in his hand!"

And there were six men coming from the direction of the upper gate that faces north, each with his weapon of shattering in his hand; and one man among them was clothed in linen, with a scribe's writing case at his waist. And they came and stood beside the bronze altar.

And the glory of the God of Israel had gone up from over the cherub on which it had been, to the threshold of the house. And he called to the man clothed in linen, who had the scribe's writing case at his waist;

and the LORD said to him, "Pass through the middle of the city, through the middle of Jerusalem, and put a taw on the foreheads of the people who sigh and groan over all the abominations that are done in the middle of it."
And to the others he said in my hearing, "Pass through the city after him and strike. Let your eye not spare, and do not show pity.

Old man, young man and virgin, little ones and women — kill them to destruction. But do not come near any man on whom the taw is. And begin from my sanctuary." And they began with the old men who were before the house.
And he said to them, "Make the house unclean, and fill the courts with the slain. Go out!" And they went out and struck in the city.
And while they were striking, and I was left, I fell on my face and cried out and said, "Alas, Lord GOD! Are you destroying all the remnant of Israel in pouring out your rage on Jerusalem?"

And he said to me, "The iniquity of the house of Israel and Judah is very, very great; the land is filled with blood and the city is full of perversity. For they have said, 'The LORD has forsaken the land, and the LORD does not see.'
And I too — my eye will not spare, and I will not show pity. I have requited their conduct on their own head."
And there was the man clothed in linen, who had the writing case at his waist, bringing back a word: "I have done according to all that you commanded me."

ezekiel_10.t: And I looked, and there, toward the vault that was over the head of the cherubim, was something like a sapphire stone; like the appearance of the likeness of a throne, it appeared above them.

And he said to the man clothed in linen, "Go in between the whirling wheels, under the cherub, and fill your cupped hands with coals of fire from between the cherubim, and scatter them over the city." And he went in before my eyes.
And the cherubim were standing on the south side of the house when the man went in; and the cloud filled the inner court.
And the glory of the LORD rose from over the cherub, to the threshold of the house; and the house was filled with the cloud, and the court was full of the brightness of the glory of the LORD.
And the sound of the wings of the cherubim was heard as far as the outer court, like the sound of God Almighty when he speaks.
And when he commanded the man clothed in linen, "Take fire from between the whirling wheels, from between the cherubim," he went in and stood beside the wheel.

And the cherub stretched out his hand from between the cherubim to the fire that was between the cherubim, lifted some, and put it into the cupped hands of the one clothed in linen; and he took it and went out.
And there appeared on the cherubim the form of a human hand under their wings.
And I looked, and there were four wheels beside the cherubim — one wheel beside one cherub, and one wheel beside one cherub; and the appearance of the wheels was like the gleam of beryl.
And as for their appearance: the four of them had one likeness, as though a wheel were within a wheel.
When they moved, they moved toward their four sides; they did not turn when they moved. For wherever the head turned, they went after it; they did not turn when they moved.
And all their body and their backs and their hands and their wings, and the wheels, were full of eyes all around — the four of them, their wheels.
As for the wheels — in my hearing they were called "the whirling wheel".
And each one had four faces: the face of the first was the face of the cherub, the face of the second the face of a human, the third the face of a lion, and the fourth the face of an eagle.
And the cherubim rose. That was the living creature that I had seen by the river Kebar.
And when the cherubim moved, the wheels moved beside them; and when the cherubim lifted their wings to rise from the ground, the wheels also did not turn from beside them.
When they stood still, the wheels stood still; and when they rose, the wheels rose with them; for the spirit of the living creature was in them.
And the glory of the LORD went out from over the threshold of the house and stood over the cherubim.

And the cherubim lifted their wings and rose from the ground before my eyes as they went out, and the wheels alongside them. And it stood at the entrance of the eastern gate of the house of the LORD, and the glory of the God of Israel was above them.
That was the living creature that I had seen under the God of Israel by the river Kebar; and I knew that they were cherubim.
Each had four faces — four — and each four wings; and the likeness of human hands was under their wings.
And as for the likeness of their faces: they were the faces that I had seen by the river Kebar — their appearance, and themselves. Each moved toward the side its face was turned to.

ezekiel_11.t: And a spirit lifted me up and brought me to the eastern gate of the house of the LORD, which faces east; and there at the entrance of the gate were twenty-five men, and I saw among them Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah, leaders of the people.
And he said to me, "Mortal, these are the men who plan wickedness and who give evil counsel in this city,
who say, 'It is not near — the building of houses! This city is the pot and we are the meat.'
Therefore prophesy against them; prophesy, mortal."
And the spirit of the LORD fell upon me and said to me, "Say: This is what the LORD says: So you have said, house of Israel; and the risings of your spirit — I myself know them.
You have multiplied your slain in this city and filled its streets with the slain."
Therefore this is what Lord GOD says: Your slain whom you have put in the middle of it — they are the meat, and it is the pot; but you he will bring out from the middle of it.
A sword you have feared, and a sword I will bring upon you — declares Lord GOD.
And I will bring you out from the middle of it and give you into the hand of strangers, and I will perform acts of judgement on you.
By the sword you shall fall. On the border of Israel I will judge you, and you will know that I am the LORD.
It will not be a pot for you, and you will not be the meat in the middle of it. At the border of Israel I will judge you,
and you will know that I am the LORD — you who have not walked in my statutes and have not done my judgements, but have acted according to the judgements of the nations that are around you."
And while I was prophesying, Pelatiah son of Benaiah died. And I fell on my face and cried out with a great voice and said, "Alas, Lord GOD! Are you making a complete end of the remnant of Israel?"
And the word of the LORD came to me:

"Mortal, your brothers, your brothers — the men who hold your right of redemption — and all the house of Israel, all of it, to whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem have said, 'Keep far from the LORD; to us this land has been given as a possession' —

therefore say: This is what Lord GOD says: Though I have removed them far off among the nations, and though I have scattered them among the lands, yet I have become for them a sanctuary for a little while in the lands where they have gone.
Therefore say: This is what Lord GOD says: And I will gather you from the peoples and assemble you from the lands where you have been scattered, and I will give you the land of Israel.
And they will come there and remove all its detestable things and all its abominations from it.
And I will give them one heart, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove the heart of stone from their flesh and give them a heart of flesh,
so that they may walk in my statutes and keep my judgements and do them. And they will be my people, and I will be their God.
But as for those whose heart goes after the heart of their detestable things and their abominations, I have requited their conduct on their own head — declares Lord GOD."
And the cherubim lifted their wings, with the wheels alongside them; and the glory of the God of Israel was above them.
And the glory of the LORD went up from over the middle of the city and stood on the mountain that is east of the city.
And a spirit lifted me up and brought me to Chaldea, to the exiles, in the vision, by the spirit of God; and the vision that I had seen went up from me.
And I spoke to the exiles all the words of the LORD that he had shown me.

ezekiel_12.t: And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, you are living in the middle of the house of rebellion, who have eyes to see and do not see, ears to hear and do not hear; for they are a house of rebellion.

And you, mortal, prepare an exile's baggage for yourself, and go into exile by day before their eyes; you shall go into exile from your place to another place before their eyes. Perhaps they will see — for they are a house of rebellion.
And you shall bring out your baggage like an exile's baggage, by day, before their eyes; and you yourself shall go out in the evening before their eyes, like those who go out into exile.
Before their eyes dig through the wall for yourself, and bring your baggage out through it.
Before their eyes lift it on your shoulder; in the dark bring it out. You shall cover your face and not see the land, for I have made you a sign for the house of Israel."

And I did so, as I was commanded. My baggage I brought out like an exile's baggage, by day; and in the evening I dug through the wall with my hand; in the dark I brought it out, and lifted it on my shoulder, before their eyes.
And in the morning the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, has not the house of Israel, the house of rebellion, said to you, 'What are you doing?'
Say to them: This is what Lord GOD says: The prince — this oracle — in Jerusalem, and all the house of Israel who are among them.
Say: I am your sign. As I have done, so it will be done to them: into exile, into captivity they will go.

And the prince who is among them shall lift his baggage onto his shoulder in the dark and go out; they will dig through the wall to bring it out through it. He shall cover his face because he himself will not see the land with his eye.
And I will spread my net over him, and he will be caught in my hunting net; and I will bring him to Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans — and he will not see it, and there he will die.
And all who are around him, his help and all his troops, I will scatter to every wind, and I will draw a sword after them.
And they will know that I am the LORD, when I scatter them among the nations and disperse them among the lands.

But I will leave over from them a few men, from the sword, from famine and from pestilence, so that they may recount all their abominations among the nations where they have gone; and they will know that I am the LORD."
And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, eat your bread with quaking, and drink your water with trembling and with anxiety.

And say to the people of the land: This is what Lord GOD says concerning the inhabitants of Jerusalem, concerning the land of Israel: They shall eat their bread with anxiety and drink their water with horror, so that her land may be stripped of its fullness, because of the violence of all who dwell in it.
And the inhabited cities shall be laid waste, and the land shall become a desolation; and you will know that I am the LORD."
And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, what is this proverb you have concerning the land of Israel: 'The days grow long, and every vision perishes'?

Therefore say to them: This is what Lord GOD says: I will put an end to this proverb, and they shall not use it as a proverb in Israel any more. But say this to them instead: The days have drawn near, and the matter of every vision.
For there will be no more any worthless vision or flattering divination in the middle of the house of Israel.
For I, the LORD, will speak. What I speak as a word will be done; it will not be postponed any more. For in your days, house of rebellion, I will speak a word and do it — declares Lord GOD."
And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, look, the house of Israel are saying, 'The vision that he is seeing is for many days off; he is prophesying of distant times.'
Therefore say to them: This is what Lord GOD says: None of my words will be postponed any more. What I speak as a word will be done — declares Lord GOD."

ezekiel_13.t: And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, prophesy against the prophets of Israel who are prophesying, and say to those who prophesy out of their own heart: Hear the word of the LORD!
This is what Lord GOD says: Woe to the foolish prophets, who walk after their own spirit and have seen nothing!
Like foxes among ruins your prophets have been, Israel.
You have not gone up into the breaches, nor built a wall around the house of Israel, to stand in the battle on the day of the LORD.
They have seen worthlessness and lying divination — those who say, 'Declares the LORD,' when the LORD has not sent them; and they have waited for a word to be fulfilled.
Have you not seen a worthless vision and spoken a lying divination, when you say, 'Declares the LORD,' and I have not spoken?
Therefore this is what Lord GOD says: Because you have spoken worthlessness and seen falsehood, therefore look, I am against you — declares Lord GOD.

And my hand will be against the prophets who see worthlessness and divine falsehood. They will not be in the council of my people, they will not be written in the register of the house of Israel, and they will not come into the land of Israel; and you will know that I am Lord GOD.
Because, yes because, they have led my people astray, saying 'Peace!' when there is no peace — and one builds a flimsy partition and, look, they plaster it with whitewash —
say to those who plaster with whitewash that it will fall. There will be an overflowing rain; and you, hailstones, will fall; and a tempest wind will break through.
And look, the wall has fallen. Will it not be said to you, "Where is the plastering that you plastered?"
Therefore this is what Lord GOD says: I will make a tempest wind break out in my rage, and an overflowing rain will come in my anger, and hailstones in rage, for a complete end.

And I will tear down the wall that you plastered with whitewash and bring it down to the ground, and its foundation will be laid bare; and it will fall, and you will come to an end in the middle of it; and you will know that I am the LORD.
And I will complete my rage on the wall and on those who plastered it with whitewash; and I will say to you: The wall is no more, and those who plastered it are no more —
the prophets of Israel who prophesied concerning Jerusalem and saw for her a vision of peace, when there was no peace — declares Lord GOD.
And you, mortal, set your face against the daughters of your people who prophesy out of their own heart, and prophesy against them.

And say: This is what Lord GOD says: Woe to the women who sew magic bands on all the joints of the hands and make veils for the head of every stature, to hunt lives! Will you hunt the lives of my people and keep your own lives alive?

And you have profaned me among my people for handfuls of barley and for fragments of bread, putting to death lives that should not die and keeping alive lives that should not live, by your lying to my people, who listen to falsehood.

Therefore this is what Lord GOD says: Look, I am against your bands with which you are hunting the lives there like birds, and I will tear them off your arms; and I will set free the lives, the lives that you are hunting like birds.
And I will tear off your veils and deliver my people from your hand, and they will no longer be prey in your hand; and you will know that I am the LORD.

Because you have disheartened the righteous with falsehood, when I myself had not caused him pain, and have strengthened the hands of the wicked so that he does not turn back from his evil way and be kept alive —
therefore you will not see worthlessness and will not practise divination any more; and I will deliver my people from your hand, and you will know that I am the LORD."

ezekiel_14.t: And men from the elders of Israel came to me, and they sat down before me.
And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, these men have brought their idols up into their heart and have set the stumbling block of their iniquity before their faces. Shall I really let myself be consulted by them?

Therefore speak with them and say to them: This is what Lord GOD says: Anyone at all of the house of Israel who brings his idols up into his heart and sets the stumbling block of his iniquity before his face, and then comes to the prophet — I, the LORD, will let myself answer him, as he comes, according to the multitude of his idols,
so as to seize the house of Israel by their heart, because all of them have become estranged from me through their idols.
Therefore say to the house of Israel: This is what Lord GOD says: Turn back, and turn away from your idols; and turn your faces away from all your abominations.

For anyone at all of the house of Israel, or of the sojourner who sojourns in Israel, who separates himself from following me and brings his idols up into his heart and sets the stumbling block of his iniquity before his face, and then comes to the prophet to consult me through him — I, the LORD, will let myself answer him myself.
And I will set my face against that man and make him a sign and a byword, and I will cut him off from the middle of my people; and you will know that I am the LORD.
And the prophet, if he is deceived and speaks a word — I, the LORD, have deceived that prophet; and I will stretch out my hand against him and destroy him from the middle of my people Israel.
And they will bear their iniquity: as the iniquity of the enquirer, so will be the iniquity of the prophet,

so that the house of Israel may no longer wander from following me and no longer make themselves unclean with all their transgressions. And they will be my people, and I will be their God — declares Lord GOD."
And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, if a land sins against me by acting unfaithfully, and I stretch out my hand against it and break its staff of bread and send famine on it and cut off from it humankind and animals —
and these three men were in the middle of it — Noah, Danel and Job — they by their righteousness would deliver their own lives, declares Lord GOD.
If I make wild beasts pass through the land and they leave it bereaved, and it becomes a desolation with no one passing through because of the beasts —
these three men in the middle of it — as I live, declares Lord GOD, they would deliver neither sons nor daughters. They alone would be delivered, and the land would be a desolation.
Or if I bring a sword upon that land and say, 'Sword, pass through the land,' and I cut off from it humankind and animals —
and these three men in the middle of it — as I live, declares Lord GOD, they would not deliver sons or daughters, for they alone would be delivered.
Or if I send pestilence against that land and pour out my rage on it in blood, to cut off from it humankind and animals —
and Noah, Danel and Job were in the middle of it — as I live, declares Lord GOD, they would deliver neither son nor daughter. They by their righteousness would deliver their own lives.
For this is what Lord GOD says: How much more when I send my four evil judgements — sword and famine and wild beasts and pestilence — against Jerusalem, to cut off from it humankind and animals!

And look, there will be left in it an escaped remnant, those being brought out — sons and daughters. Look, they are coming out to you, and you will see their conduct and their practices; and you will be comforted concerning the evil that I have brought upon Jerusalem, all that I have brought upon it.
And they will comfort you when you see their conduct and their practices; and you will know that it is not without cause that I have done all that I have done in it — declares Lord GOD."

ezekiel_15.t: And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, what is the wood of the vine more than any other wood — the vine branch that is among the trees of the forest?
Is wood taken from it to make anything at all? Do people take from it a peg to hang any vessel on?
Look, it is given to the fire for fuel; the fire consumes its two ends and its middle is charred. Is it fit for anything?
Look, when it was whole it could not be made into anything. How much less, now that fire has consumed it and it is charred, can it still be made into anything!
Therefore this is what Lord GOD says: Like the wood of the vine among the trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire for fuel, so I have given the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
And I will set my face against them. They have come out from the fire, and the fire will consume them; and you will know that I am the LORD, when I set my face against them.
And I will make the land a desolation, because they have acted unfaithfully — declares Lord GOD."

ezekiel_16.t: And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, make Jerusalem know her abominations,
and say: This is what Lord GOD says to Jerusalem: Your origins and your birth were from the land of the Canaanite; your father was the Amorite and your mother a Hittite.

And as for your birth: on the day you were born your umbilical cord was not cut, and you were not washed with water to make you clean; you were not rubbed with salt at all, and you were not wrapped at all.
No eye looked on you with compassion, to do any one of these things for you, to have pity on you; and you were thrown out onto the open field, in loathing of your life, on the day you were born.
