And you say, 'The way of the Lord is not right.' I will judge each of you according to his ways, house of Israel."
In the twelfth year of our exile, in the tenth month, on the fifth of the month, the escapee came to me from Jerusalem and said, "The city has been struck."

And the hand of the LORD had been upon me in the evening, before the escapee came, and he had opened my mouth before the man came to me in the morning; and my mouth was opened, and I was no longer mute.
And the word of the LORD came to me:

"Mortal, the inhabitants of these waste places in the land of Israel are saying: 'Abraham was one, and he took possession of the land; and we are many — the land has been given to us as a possession.'
Therefore say to them: This is what Lord GOD says: You eat with the blood, you lift your eyes to your idols, and you shed blood — and shall you possess the land?
You have relied on your sword; you have done abomination; and each of you has made his neighbour's wife unclean — and shall you possess the land?

This is what you shall say to them: This is what Lord GOD says: As I live, surely those who are in the waste places will fall by the sword; the one who is out in the open field I will give to the beasts to be devoured; and those who are in the strongholds and in the caves will die of pestilence.
And I will make the land a desolation and a waste, and the pride of her strength will cease; and the mountains of Israel will be desolate, with no one passing through.
And they will know that I am the LORD, when I make the land a desolation and a waste, because of all their abominations that they have done.

"And you, mortal — the children of your people who talk about you beside the walls and in the doorways of the houses, one speaking with another, each with his brother: 'Come now and hear what the word is that comes out from the LORD!' —

and they come to you as a crowd comes, and my people sit before you and hear your words, but they do not do them. For with their mouths they make a show of desire, but their heart goes after their unjust gain.
And look, you are to them like a love-song, beautiful of voice and well played; and they hear your words but do not do them.
And when it comes — look, it is coming — then they will know that a prophet has been among them."

ezekiel_34.t: And the word of the LORD came to me:

"Mortal, prophesy against the shepherds of Israel. Prophesy, and say to them, to the shepherds: This is what Lord GOD says: Woe to the shepherds of Israel who have been shepherding themselves! Should the shepherds not shepherd the flock?
You eat the fat and clothe yourselves with the wool; you slaughter the fattened sheep; you do not shepherd the flock.

The weak you have not strengthened, the sick you have not healed, the broken you have not bound up, the strayed you have not brought back, the lost you have not sought; and with force you have ruled them, and with harshness.
And they were scattered for lack of a shepherd, and became food for every beast of the field; and they were scattered.
My flock wander on all the mountains and on every high hill; over all the face of the earth my flock have been scattered, with no one searching and no one seeking.
Therefore, shepherds, hear the word of the LORD:

As I live — declares Lord GOD — surely, because my flock has become prey and my flock has become food for every beast of the field, for lack of a shepherd, and my shepherds did not search for my flock, and the shepherds shepherded themselves and did not shepherd my flock —
therefore, shepherds, hear the word of the LORD:

This is what Lord GOD says: Look, I am against the shepherds, and I will require my flock from their hand and make them cease from shepherding a flock; and the shepherds will no longer shepherd themselves. And I will deliver my flock from their mouth, and they will not be food for them.
For this is what Lord GOD says: Look, I myself will search for my flock and seek them out.

As a shepherd seeks out his flock on the day he is among his scattered sheep, so I will seek out my flock; and I will deliver them from all the places where they were scattered on a day of cloud and thick darkness.

And I will bring them out from the peoples and gather them from the lands and bring them to their own land; and I will shepherd them on the mountains of Israel, in the ravines and in all the habitable places of the land.

In good pasture I will shepherd them, and on the mountain heights of Israel will be their pastureland. There they will lie down in good pastureland, and on rich pasture they will graze, on the mountains of Israel.
I myself will shepherd my flock, and I myself will make them lie down — declares Lord GOD.
The lost I will seek, the strayed I will bring back, the broken I will bind up, the sick I will make strong; and the fat and the strong I will destroy. I will shepherd them with justice.
And as for you, my flock — this is what Lord GOD says: Look, I am judging between one sheep and another, between the rams and the male goats.

Is it too little for you that you graze the good pasture, that you must trample the rest of your pasture with your feet? And that you drink the clear water, that you must foul the rest with your feet?
And my flock — must they graze what your feet have trampled and drink what your feet have fouled?
Therefore this is what Lord GOD says to them: Look, I myself will judge between a fat sheep and a lean sheep.
Because you push with side and shoulder and thrust at all the weak with your horns, until you have scattered them abroad —
I will save my flock, and they will no longer be prey; and I will judge between one sheep and another.
And I will raise up over them one shepherd, and he will shepherd them — my servant David. He will shepherd them, and he will be their shepherd.
And I, the LORD, will be their God, and my servant David a prince among them. I, the LORD, have spoken.
And I will make with them a covenant of peace and put an end to wild beasts in the land; and they will dwell in the wilderness in safety and sleep in the forests.
And I will make them and the places around my hill a blessing, and I will send down the rain in its season; they will be rains of blessing.

And the tree of the field will give its fruit, and the land will give its produce; and they will be on their own land in safety. And they will know that I am the LORD, when I break the bars of their yoke and deliver them from the hand of those who made them labour.
And they will no longer be spoil for the nations, and the beasts of the land will not devour them; and they will dwell in safety, with no one making them afraid.
And I will establish for them a planting of renown; and they will no longer be swept away by famine in the land, and they will no longer bear the insult of the nations.
And they will know that I, the LORD their God, am with them, and that they are my people, the house of Israel — declares Lord GOD.
And you are my flock, the flock of my pasture. You are human beings; I am your God — declares Lord GOD."

ezekiel_35.t: And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, set your face against Mount Seir and prophesy against it,
and say to it: This is what Lord GOD says: Look, I am against you, Mount Seir, and I will stretch out my hand against you and make you a desolation and a waste.
Your cities I will make a ruin, and you will be a desolation; and you will know that I am the LORD.
Because you had a perpetual enmity and delivered the people of Israel over to the sword at the time of their disaster, at the time of final punishment —
therefore, as I live — declares Lord GOD — I will appoint you to blood, and blood will pursue you. Surely you have not hated blood, and blood will pursue you.
And I will make Mount Seir an utter desolation, and I will cut off from it anyone who comes or goes.
And I will fill its mountains with its slain; your hills and your valleys and all your ravines — those slain by the sword will fall in them.
I will make you perpetual desolations, and your cities will not be inhabited again; and you will know that I am the LORD.
Because you said, 'The two nations and the two lands will be mine, and we will take possession of them' — and the LORD was there —

therefore, as I live — declares Lord GOD — I will act according to your anger and according to your jealousy, which you showed out of your hatred of them; and I will make myself known among them when I judge you.
And you will know that I, the LORD, have heard all the insults you spoke against the mountains of Israel: 'They are desolate; they have been given to us to devour.'
And you magnified yourselves against me with your mouth and multiplied your words against me. I have heard.
This is what Lord GOD says: When all the earth rejoices, I will make you a desolation.

As you rejoiced over the inheritance of the house of Israel because it was desolate, so I will do to you. You will be a desolation, Mount Seir, and all Edom, all of it; and they will know that I am the LORD."

ezekiel_36.t: "And you, mortal, prophesy to the mountains of Israel and say: Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the LORD.
This is what Lord GOD says: Because the enemy has said over you, 'Aha! The ancient heights have become our possession' —

therefore prophesy and say: This is what Lord GOD says: Because, yes because, they have made you desolate and crushed you from every side, so that you became a possession for the rest of the nations, and you were taken up on people's lips and in their gossip —

therefore, mountains of Israel, hear the word of Lord GOD. This is what Lord GOD says to the mountains and to the hills, to the ravines and to the valleys, and to the desolate waste places and to the forsaken cities that have become spoil and mockery to the rest of the nations all around —

therefore this is what Lord GOD says: Surely in the fire of my jealousy I have spoken against the rest of the nations and against all Edom, who made my land their own possession with whole-hearted joy and with scorn of self, so that its pastureland might be plundered.

Therefore prophesy concerning the land of Israel and say to the mountains and to the hills, to the ravines and to the valleys: This is what Lord GOD says: Look, in my jealousy and in my rage I have spoken, because you have borne the insult of the nations.
Therefore this is what Lord GOD says: I raise my hand in an oath: surely the nations that are around you — they will bear their own insult.
And you, mountains of Israel, will put out your branches and bear your fruit for my people Israel, for they are soon to come.
For look, I am for you, and I will turn toward you; and you will be tilled and sown.
And I will multiply humankind upon you — all the house of Israel, all of it; and the cities will be inhabited and the waste places rebuilt.

And I will multiply upon you humankind and animals, and they will increase and be fruitful; and I will make you inhabited as in your former state, and do better for you than at your beginnings. And you will know that I am the LORD.
And I will cause humankind to walk upon you — my people Israel; and they will take possession of you, and you will be their inheritance; and you will no longer bereave them of children.
This is what Lord GOD says: Because they say to you, 'You are a devourer of people, and you have bereaved your nations of children' —
therefore you will no longer devour people and will no longer bereave your nations of children — declares Lord GOD.
And I will no longer make you hear the insult of the nations, and you will no longer bear the reproach of the peoples; and you will no longer cause your nations to stumble — declares Lord GOD."
And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, the house of Israel were dwelling on their own land, and they made it unclean by their conduct and by their practices. Like the uncleanness of menstrual impurity was their conduct before me.
And I poured out my rage upon them for the blood they had poured out on the land, and because they had made it unclean with their idols.
And I scattered them among the nations, and they were dispersed among the lands; according to their conduct and according to their practices I judged them.
And they came to the nations where they went, and they profaned my holy name, when it was said of them, 'These are the people of the LORD, and they have come out of his land.'
But I had pity on my holy name, which the house of Israel had profaned among the nations where they had gone.

Therefore say to the house of Israel: This is what Lord GOD says: It is not for your sake that I am acting, house of Israel, but for my holy name, which you have profaned among the nations where you have gone.

And I will set apart as holy my great name, which has been profaned among the nations, which you profaned in their midst; and the nations will know that I am the LORD — declares Lord GOD — when I show myself holy among you before their eyes.
And I will take you from the nations and gather you from all the lands and bring you to your own land.
And I will sprinkle clean water on you, and you will be clean; from all your uncleannesses and from all your idols I will cleanse you.
And I will give you a new heart, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh.
And my spirit I will put within you, and I will bring it about that you walk in my statutes and keep my judgements and do them.
And you will dwell in the land that I gave to your fathers; and you will be my people, and I myself will be your God.
And I will save you from all your uncleannesses; and I will summon the grain and multiply it, and I will not bring famine upon you.
And I will multiply the fruit of the tree and the produce of the field, so that you will no longer receive the reproach of famine among the nations.
And you will remember your evil ways and your deeds that were not good, and you will loathe yourselves to your own faces because of your iniquities and because of your abominations.
It is not for your sake that I am acting — declares Lord GOD — let that be known to you. Be ashamed and humiliated because of your ways, house of Israel!"
This is what Lord GOD says: On the day I cleanse you from all your iniquities, I will cause the cities to be inhabited, and the waste places will be rebuilt.
And the desolated land will be tilled, instead of lying a desolation before the eyes of everyone who passes by.
And they will say, 'This land that was desolated has become like the garden of Eden; and the cities that were wasted and desolated and broken down are fortified and inhabited.'
And the nations that are left around you will know that I, the LORD, have rebuilt what was broken down and planted what was desolated. I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will do it.
This is what Lord GOD says: This also I will let myself be sought for by the house of Israel, to do for them: I will multiply their people like a flock.
Like a flock of holy offerings, like the flock of Jerusalem at her appointed feasts, so the wasted cities will be full of flocks of people; and they will know that I am the LORD."

ezekiel_37.t: The hand of the LORD was upon me, and he brought me out by the spirit of the LORD and set me down in the middle of the valley; and it was full of bones.
And he made me pass among them, all around, all around; and there they were, very many on the surface of the valley, and very dry.
And he said to me, "Mortal, will these bones live?" And I said, "Lord GOD, you know."
And he said to me, "Prophesy to these bones and say to them: Dry bones, hear the word of the LORD!
This is what Lord GOD says to these bones: Look, I am bringing breath into you, and you will live.
And I will put sinews on you and bring up flesh over you and cover you with skin, and I will put breath in you, and you will live; and you will know that I am the LORD."
And I prophesied as I was commanded; and there was a sound as I prophesied, and there was a rattling; and the bones drew near, bone to its bone.
And I looked, and there were sinews on them, and flesh came up, and skin covered them over from above; but there was no breath in them.

And he said to me, "Prophesy to the breath; prophesy, mortal, and say to the breath: This is what Lord GOD says: From the four winds come, breath, and blow on these killed ones, so that they may live."
And I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived and stood on their feet — a very, very great army.
And he said to me, "Mortal, these bones are all the house of Israel. Look, they are saying, 'Our bones have dried up and our hope has perished; we are cut off completely.'
Therefore prophesy and say to them: This is what Lord GOD says: Look, I am about to open your graves and bring you up from your graves, my people; and I will bring you to the land of Israel.
And you will know that I am the LORD, when I open your graves and bring you up from your graves, my people.
And I will put my spirit in you, and you will live; and I will set you down on your own land. And you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken and have done it — declares the LORD."
And the word of the LORD came to me:

"And you, mortal, take one stick and write on it, 'For Judah and for the people of Israel, his associates'; and take another stick and write on it, 'For Joseph — the stick of Ephraim — and all the house of Israel, his associates.'
And bring them near, one to the other, into a single stick; and they will become one in your hand.
And when the children of your people say to you, 'Will you not tell us what these mean for you?' —

speak to them: This is what Lord GOD says: Look, I am about to take the stick of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim, and the tribes of Israel his associates, and I will put them with it — with the stick of Judah — and make them a single stick; and they will be one in my hand.
And the sticks on which you write will be in your hand before their eyes.

And speak to them: This is what Lord GOD says: Look, I am about to take the people of Israel from among the nations where they have gone, and I will gather them from all around and bring them to their own land.

And I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel; and one king will be king over all of them. They will no longer be two nations, and will no longer be divided into two kingdoms.

And they will no longer make themselves unclean with their idols and their detestable things and all their transgressions; and I will save them from all their dwelling places in which they have sinned, and I will cleanse them. And they will be my people, and I myself will be their God.
And my servant David will be king over them, and they will all have one shepherd; and they will walk in my judgements and keep my statutes and do them.

And they will dwell on the land that I gave to my servant Jacob, in which your fathers dwelt. And they will dwell on it — they and their children and their children's children — for ever; and David my servant will be their prince for ever.
And I will make with them a covenant of peace; it will be a perpetual covenant with them. And I will establish them and multiply them, and I will put my sanctuary in their midst for ever.
And my dwelling place will be over them; and I will be their God, and they will be my people.
And the nations will know that I, the LORD, am the one who sets Israel apart as holy, when my sanctuary is in their midst for ever."

ezekiel_38.t: And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, set your face toward Gog, of the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, and prophesy against him,
and say: This is what Lord GOD says: Look, I am against you, Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.

And I will turn you around and put hooks in your jaws, and bring you out — you and all your army, horses and horsemen, all of them magnificently clothed, a great company with body shield and shield, all of them wielding swords —
Persia, Cush and Put with them, all of them with shield and helmet;
Gomer and all its troops, Beth-togarmah from the remotest parts of the north, and all its troops — many peoples with you.
Be prepared and prepare yourself, you and all your company that have assembled to you; and you will be their guard.

After many days you will be mustered; at the end of the years you will come into a land restored from the sword, gathered from many peoples, on the mountains of Israel, which had been a continual desolation. And its people have been brought out from the peoples, and they are all dwelling in safety.
And you will go up; like a storm you will come; like a cloud covering the land you will be — you and all your troops, and many peoples with you.
This is what Lord GOD says: And it will be on that day that thoughts will come up in your heart, and you will plan an evil plan.
And you will say: I will go up against a land of unwalled villages; I will come against those at peace, dwelling in safety — all of them dwelling with no wall, and they have no bars and no gates —

to plunder plunder and take spoil as spoil; to turn your hand against inhabited waste places and against a people gathered from the nations, who have acquired livestock and possessions, who dwell at the centre of the earth.

Sheba and Dedan and the traders of Tarshish and all its young lions will say to you: Have you come to plunder plunder? Have you assembled your company to take spoil as spoil — to carry away silver and gold, to take livestock and possessions, to plunder great plunder?
Therefore prophesy, mortal, and say to Gog: This is what Lord GOD says: On that day, when my people Israel are dwelling in safety, will you not know it?
And you will come from your place, from the remotest parts of the north, you and many peoples with you, all of them riding horses — a great company and a mighty army.

And you will go up against my people Israel like a cloud covering the land. At the end of the days it will happen, and I will bring you against my land, so that the nations may know me, when I show myself holy through you before their eyes, Gog.
This is what Lord GOD says: Are you the one of whom I spoke in former days through my servants the prophets of Israel, who prophesied in those days, for years, that I would bring you against them?
And it will be on that day, on the day Gog comes against the land of Israel — declares Lord GOD — that my rage will rise in my anger.
And in my jealousy, in the fire of my wrath, I have spoken: surely on that day there will be a great earthquake on the land of Israel.

And the fish of the sea and the birds of the heavens and the beasts of the field and every creeping thing that creeps on the ground, and every human being on the face of the ground, will shake before me. And the mountains will be thrown down and the cliffs will fall, and every wall will fall to the ground.
And I will summon a sword against him on all my mountains — declares Lord GOD; each man's sword will be against his brother.

And I will enter into judgement with him by pestilence and by blood; and an overflowing rain and hailstones, fire and sulphur, I will rain down on him and on his troops and on the many peoples that are with him.
And I will show myself great and show myself holy and make myself known before the eyes of many nations; and they will know that I am the LORD."

ezekiel_39.t: "And you, mortal, prophesy against Gog and say: This is what Lord GOD says: Look, I am against you, Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.
And I will turn you around and lead you on, and bring you up from the remotest parts of the north, and bring you against the mountains of Israel.
And I will strike your bow out of your left hand and make your arrows fall from your right hand.
On the mountains of Israel you will fall — you and all your troops and the peoples that are with you. To birds of prey of every kind and to the beasts of the field I will give you for food.
On the open field you will fall, for I have spoken — declares Lord GOD.
And I will send fire on Magog and on those who dwell in safety in the coastlands; and they will know that I am the LORD.
And my holy name I will make known in the midst of my people Israel, and I will not let my holy name be profaned any more; and the nations will know that I am the LORD, holy in Israel.
Look, it is coming, and it will happen — declares Lord GOD. That is the day of which I have spoken.
And the inhabitants of the cities of Israel will go out and kindle and burn weapons — shield and body shield, bow and arrows, hand-staff and spear; and they will make fire with them for seven years.

And they will not carry wood from the field or cut it from the forests, for they will make fire with the weapons; and they will plunder those who plundered them and take spoil from those who took spoil from them — declares Lord GOD.

And on that day I will give Gog a place there, a burial site in Israel: the Valley of the Travellers, east of the sea. And it will block the way of those who travel; and they will bury Gog and all his multitude there, and they will call it the Valley of Hamon-gog.
And the house of Israel will bury them for seven months, so as to cleanse the land.
And all the people of the land will bury them, and it will bring them renown, on the day I show myself glorious — declares Lord GOD.

And they will set apart men on continual duty, passing through the land, burying those who travel — the ones left on the face of the land — to cleanse it. At the end of seven months they will make a search.
And those who pass through will pass through the land; and when one sees a human bone, he will build a marker beside it, until the buriers have buried it in the Valley of Hamon-gog.
And the name of a city there is also Hamonah. And they will cleanse the land.

"And you, mortal — this is what Lord GOD says: Say to the birds of every wing and to every beast of the field: Assemble and come; gather from all around to my sacrifice, which I am sacrificing for you — a great sacrifice on the mountains of Israel — and you will eat flesh and drink blood.
The flesh of warriors you will eat, and the blood of the princes of the earth you will drink — rams, lambs and goats, bulls, all of them fatlings of Bashan.
And you will eat fat to satiety and drink blood to drunkenness, from my sacrifice that I have sacrificed for you.
And you will be satisfied at my table with horse and charioteer, warrior and every man of war — declares Lord GOD.
And I will set my glory among the nations; and all the nations will see the judgement I have executed and the hand I have laid on them.
And the house of Israel will know that I am the LORD their God, from that day onwards.

And the nations will know that the house of Israel went into exile for their iniquity, because they acted unfaithfully against me; and I hid my face from them and gave them into the hand of their adversaries, and they all fell by the sword.
According to their uncleanness and according to their transgressions I dealt with them, and I hid my face from them.
Therefore this is what Lord GOD says: Now I will turn back the captivity of Jacob and have compassion on all the house of Israel; and I will be jealous for my holy name.
And they will bear their disgrace and all the unfaithfulness by which they acted unfaithfully against me, when they dwell on their own land in safety with no one disturbing them.
when I bring them back from the peoples and gather them from the lands of their enemies, and show myself holy through them before the eyes of many nations.
And they will know that I am the LORD their God, in that I sent them into exile among the nations and then gathered them to their own land; and I will leave none of them there any more.
And I will not hide my face from them any more, because I have poured out my spirit on the house of Israel — declares Lord GOD."

ezekiel_40.t: In the twenty-fifth year of our exile, at the beginning of the year, on the tenth of the month, in the fourteenth year after the city was struck — on that very day the hand of the LORD was upon me, and he brought me there.
In visions of God he brought me to the land of Israel and set me down on a very high mountain; and on it, to the south, was something like the structure of a city.
And he brought me there, and there was a man whose appearance was like the appearance of bronze, with a cord of linen in his hand and a measuring reed; and he was standing in the gate.

And the man spoke to me: "Mortal, see with your eyes and hear with your ears and set your heart on all that I am about to show you, for you have been brought here in order to be shown it. Tell all that you see to the house of Israel."

And there was a wall on the outside of the house, all around, all around. And in the man's hand was the measuring reed, six cubits — by the long cubit, a cubit and a handbreadth. And he measured the breadth of the structure: one reed; and the height: one reed.
And he went to the gate that faces east and went up its steps, and he measured the threshold of the gate: one reed deep; and the other threshold: one reed deep.
And each guard chamber: one reed long and one reed wide; and between the guard chambers, five cubits. And the threshold of the gate, beside the porch of the gate on the inside: one reed.
And he measured the porch of the gate on the inside: one reed.
And he measured the porch of the gate: eight cubits; and its jambs: two cubits. And the porch of the gate was on the inside.
And the guard chambers of the east gate: three on one side and three on the other — one measurement for the three of them; and one measurement for the jambs on either side.
And he measured the width of the gate's entrance: ten cubits; the width of the gateway: thirteen cubits.
And a barrier in front of the guard chambers: one cubit; and one cubit a barrier on the other side. And each guard chamber: six cubits on one side and six cubits on the other.
And he measured the gate from the roof of one guard chamber to the roof of the other: a width of twenty-five cubits, entrance opposite entrance.
And he made the jambs sixty cubits; and to the jamb was the court, the gate all around, all around.
And from the front of the outer gate's entrance to the front of the porch of the inner gate: fifty cubits.

And recessed windows opened onto the guard chambers and their jambs, inward to the gate, all around, all around; and so also onto the porches. And there were windows all around, all around, inward; and on the jambs, palm trees.
And he brought me into the outer court; and there were rooms, and a pavement made for the court all around, all around — thirty rooms on the pavement.
And the pavement was at the side of the gates, matching the length of the gates — the lower pavement.
And he measured the distance from the front of the lower gate to the front of the inner court, on the outside: a hundred cubits — on the east and on the north.
And the gate of the outer court that faces north — he measured its length and its width.
And its guard chambers: three on one side and three on the other; and its jambs and its porches were according to the measurement of the first gate — fifty cubits long, and twenty-five cubits wide.
And its windows and its porches and its palm trees were according to the measurement of the gate that faces east; and one goes up to it by seven steps, and its porches were in front of them.
And a gate to the inner court was opposite the gate on the north and on the east; and he measured from gate to gate: a hundred cubits.
And he led me toward the south, and there was a gate facing south; and he measured its jambs and its porches according to these measurements.
And it had windows, and its porches had windows all around, all around, like these windows: fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
And its stairway was seven steps, and its porches were in front of them; and it had palm trees, one on one side and one on the other, on its jambs.
And the inner court had a gate facing south; and he measured from gate to gate on the south: a hundred cubits.
And he brought me into the inner court by the south gate; and he measured the south gate according to these measurements.

And its guard chambers and its jambs and its porches were according to these measurements; and it had windows, and its porches had windows all around, all around — fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
And porches all around, all around: twenty-five cubits long and five cubits wide.
And its porches faced the outer court, and palm trees were on its jambs; and its ascent was eight steps.
And he brought me into the inner court toward the east; and he measured the gate according to these measurements.

And its guard chambers and its jambs and its porches were according to these measurements; and it had windows, and its porches had windows all around, all around — fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
And its porches faced the outer court, with palm trees on its jambs on either side; and its ascent was eight steps.
And he brought me to the north gate, and he measured according to these measurements —
its guard chambers, its jambs and its porches; and it had windows all around, all around — fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
And its jambs faced the outer court, with palm trees on its jambs on either side; and its ascent was eight steps.
And there was a room, with its entrance at the jambs of the gateways; there they rinse the burnt offering.
And in the porch of the gate: two tables on one side and two tables on the other, on which to slaughter the burnt offering, the sin offering and the guilt offering.
And at the outer side, as one goes up to the entrance of the north gate: two tables; and at the other side, belonging to the porch of the gate: two tables.
Four tables on one side and four tables on the other, at the side of the gate — eight tables, on which they slaughter.

And four tables for the burnt offering, of hewn stone: a cubit and a half long, a cubit and a half wide and one cubit high; on them they set down the equipment with which they slaughter the burnt offering and the sacrifice.
And hooks, one handbreadth long, were fixed inside, all around, all around; and on the tables was the flesh of the offering.
And outside the inner gate were rooms for the singers, in the inner court, at the side of the north gate, and they faced south; one was at the side of the east gate, facing north.
And he spoke to me: "This room facing south is for the priests who keep the charge of the house;
and the room facing north is for the priests who keep the charge of the altar. They are the sons of Zadok, who among the sons of Levi draw near to the LORD to serve him."
And he measured the court: a hundred cubits long and a hundred cubits wide, a square; and the altar was in front of the house.

And he brought me to the porch of the house, and he measured the jambs of the porch: five cubits on one side and five cubits on the other; and the width of the doorway: three cubits on one side and three cubits on the other.
The porch was twenty cubits long and eleven cubits wide; and one goes up to it by steps. And there were columns at the jambs, one on one side and one on the other.

ezekiel_41.t: And he brought me to the great hall, and he measured the jambs: six cubits wide on one side and six cubits wide on the other — the width of the tent.
And the width of the entrance: ten cubits; and the sides of the entrance: five cubits on one side and five cubits on the other. And he measured its length: forty cubits, and its width: twenty cubits.
And he went inside and measured the jamb of the entrance: two cubits; the entrance itself: six cubits; and the width of the entrance: seven cubits.
And he measured its length: twenty cubits, and its width: twenty cubits, at the front of the great hall. And he said to me, "This is the holy of holies."
And he measured the wall of the house: six cubits; and the width of each side chamber: four cubits, all around, all around the house, all around.

And the side chambers, side chamber upon side chamber: three and thirty times. And they went into the wall belonging to the house, for the side chambers, all around, all around, so as to be held fast — and they were not held fast in the wall of the house itself.

And it broadened and wound upward, upward, to the side chambers, for the house's surrounding structure went upward, upward, all around, all around the house; and so the house grew wider as it rose. And so one goes up from the lowest storey to the highest by way of the middle one.
And I saw that the house had a raised base all around, all around; the foundations of the side chambers were a full reed — six long cubits.
The thickness of the outer wall of the side chambers: five cubits. And what was left free was the open space of the side chambers belonging to the house.
And between the rooms: a width of twenty cubits around the house, all around, all around.
And the entrance of the side chambers opened onto the open space: one entrance on the north and one entrance on the south. And the width of the open place: five cubits all around, all around.

And the structure at the front of the separate place, on the side toward the west: seventy cubits wide; and the wall of the structure: five cubits thick all around, all around; and its length: ninety cubits.
And he measured the house: a hundred cubits long; and the separate place and the building and its walls: a hundred cubits long.
And the width of the front of the house and of the separate place, on the east: a hundred cubits.

And he measured the length of the structure at the front of the separate place that was behind it, and its galleries on either side: a hundred cubits. And the inner great hall, and the porches of the court,

the thresholds and the recessed windows and the galleries all around, for the three of them — opposite the threshold, wood panelling all around, all around; and the floor up to the windows; and the windows were covered over.
over the entrance and as far as the inner house, and outside, and on the whole wall all around, all around, inside and outside: measured spaces.
And it was made with cherubim and palm trees, a palm tree between one cherub and the next; and each cherub had two faces:
a human face toward the palm tree on one side, and a young lion's face toward the palm tree on the other. It was made so for the whole house all around, all around.
From the floor up to above the entrance the cherubim and the palm trees were made; and the wall of the great hall.
The great hall: a squared doorpost; and the front of the holy place — the appearance of one was like the appearance of the other.
The altar was of wood, three cubits high and two cubits long; and it had its corners; and its length and its sides were of wood. And he spoke to me: "This is the table that is before the LORD."
And the great hall and the holy place each had two doors.
And the doors had two leaves apiece, two turning leaves — two for the one door and two leaves for the other.
And on them, on the doors of the great hall, were made cherubim and palm trees, just as they were made for the walls; and there was a canopy of wood at the front of the porch, on the outside.
And recessed windows and palm trees on either side, on the sides of the porch; and the side chambers of the house, and the canopies.

ezekiel_42.t: And he brought me out to the outer court, by the way toward the north; and he brought me to the room that faced the separate place and faced the structure, toward the north.
At the front of the hundred-cubit length was the north entrance; and the width was fifty cubits.
Opposite the twenty cubits belonging to the inner court, and opposite the pavement belonging to the outer court, was gallery facing gallery, in three storeys.
And in front of the rooms was a walk ten cubits wide toward the inner part, a way of one cubit; and their entrances faced north.
And the upper rooms were shortened, because the galleries took space from them, more than from the lower and the middle ones of the structure.
For they were in three storeys, and they had no columns like the columns of the courts; therefore the upper storey was set back, more than the lower and the middle ones, from the ground up.
And the wall outside, alongside the rooms, on the side of the outer court in front of the rooms — its length was fifty cubits.
For the length of the rooms belonging to the outer court was fifty cubits; and at the front of the great hall, a hundred cubits.
And below these rooms was the entry from the east, as one comes to them from the outer court.
In the thickness of the court's wall, on the east, facing the separate place and facing the structure: rooms.
And a way ran in front of them, like the appearance of the rooms on the north — as their length, so their width; and all their exits, and according to their plans and their entrances.
And like the entrances of the rooms on the south: an entrance at the head of a way, a way in front of the matching wall, on the east as one comes to them.

And he said to me, "The rooms on the north and the rooms on the south that face the separate place — they are the holy rooms, where the priests who draw near to the LORD shall eat the holiest of the holy things. There they shall set down the holiest of the holy things: the grain offering, the sin offering and the guilt offering — for the place is holy.

When the priests go in, they shall not go out from the holy place into the outer court; and there they shall set down the garments in which they serve, for they are holy. And they shall put on other garments, and they shall draw near to what belongs to the people."
And he finished the measurements of the inner house, and he brought me out by the gate that faces east, and measured it all around, all around.
He measured the east side with the measuring reed: five hundred reeds by the measuring reed, all around.
He measured the north side: five hundred reeds by the measuring reed, all around.
The south side he measured: five hundred reeds by the measuring reed.
He turned to the west side and measured five hundred reeds by the measuring reed.
He measured it on its four sides. It had a wall all around, all around: five hundred long and five hundred wide, to separate between the holy and the common.

ezekiel_43.t: And he led me to the gate, the gate that faces east.
And there was the glory of the God of Israel, coming from the east; and his voice was like the sound of many waters, and the earth shone with his glory.

And it was like the appearance of the vision that I saw, like the vision that I saw when I came to destroy the city; and the visions were like the vision that I saw by the river Kebar. And I fell on my face.
And the glory of the LORD came into the house by way of the gate that faces east.
And a spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner court; and there, the glory of the LORD filled the house.
And I heard someone speaking to me from the house; and a man was standing beside me.

And he said to me: "Mortal, the place of my throne and the place of the soles of my feet, where I will dwell among the people of Israel for ever. And the house of Israel will not make my holy name unclean again — they and their kings — by their whoring and by the corpses of their kings at their high places,

when they put their threshold against my threshold and their doorpost beside my doorpost, with only the wall between me and them; and they made my holy name unclean by the abominations they committed. And I made an end of them in my anger.
Now let them put their whoring and the corpses of their kings far away from me, and I will dwell among them for ever.
You, mortal, describe the house to the house of Israel, and let them be ashamed of their iniquities; and let them measure the pattern.

And if they are ashamed of all that they have done, make known to them the design of the house and its arrangement, its exits and its entrances, and all its designs, and all its statutes, and all its designs, and all its laws; and write it down before their eyes, so that they may keep all its design and all its statutes and do them.
This is the law of the house: on the top of the mountain, all its territory all around, all around, is a holy of holies. This is the law of the house.

And these are the measurements of the altar in cubits — the cubit being a cubit and a handbreadth: the gutter, a cubit deep; and a cubit wide; and its rim on its edge all around, one span. And this is the base of the altar.
And from the gutter at the ground to the lower ledge: two cubits, with a setback of one cubit. And from the small ledge to the great ledge: four cubits, with a setback of one cubit.
And the altar hearth: four cubits; and from the hearth upward, the four horns.
And the altar hearth: twelve cubits long by twelve wide, square, on its four sides.
And the ledge: fourteen cubits long by fourteen wide, on its four sides; and the rim around it, half a cubit; and its gutter, a cubit all around. And its steps face east.
And he said to me: "Mortal, this is what Lord GOD says: These are the statutes of the altar on the day it is made, to offer up a burnt offering on it and to dash blood on it.
And you shall give to the priests, the Levites who are of the offspring of Zadok, who draw near to me — declares Lord GOD — to serve me, a bull, a young one of the herd, for a sin offering.
And you shall take some of its blood and put it on its four horns, on the four corners of the ledge and on the rim all around; and so purify it from sin and make atonement for it.
And you shall take the bull of the sin offering, and it shall be burnt in the appointed place of the house, outside the sanctuary.
And on the second day you shall bring near a male goat of the goats, unblemished, for a sin offering; and they shall purify the altar from sin as they purified it from sin with the bull.
When you finish purifying it from sin, you shall bring near a bull, a young one of the herd, unblemished, and a ram from the flock, unblemished.
And you shall bring them near before the LORD; and the priests shall throw salt on them and offer them up as a burnt offering to the LORD.
Seven days you shall offer a male goat as a sin offering each day; and a bull, a young one of the herd, and a ram from the flock, unblemished, they shall offer.
Seven days they shall make atonement for the altar and cleanse it; and so they shall install it.
And they shall complete the days. And on the eighth day and onwards the priests shall offer on the altar your burnt offerings and your peace sacrifices; and I will accept you — declares Lord GOD."

ezekiel_44.t: And he brought me back by way of the outer gate of the sanctuary, the one facing east; and it was shut.
And the LORD said to me: "This gate shall be shut. It shall not be opened, and no one shall go in by it, for the LORD the God of Israel has gone in by it; and it shall be shut.
As for the prince — a prince, he may sit in it to eat bread before the LORD. He shall come in by way of the porch of the gate, and go out by the same way."
And he brought me by way of the north gate to the front of the house; and I looked, and there — the glory of the LORD had filled the house of the LORD. And I fell on my face.

And the LORD said to me: "Mortal, set your heart and see with your eyes and hear with your ears all that I am speaking to you concerning all the statutes of the house of the LORD and all its laws. And set your heart to the entrance of the house, with all the exits of the sanctuary.
And you shall say to rebellion, to the house of Israel: This is what Lord GOD says: Enough of all your abominations, house of Israel!

when you brought in foreigners, uncircumcised of heart and uncircumcised of flesh, to be in my sanctuary, to profane it — my house — while you brought near my food, the fat and the blood; and they broke my covenant, on top of all your abominations.
And you did not keep the charge of my holy things; instead you appointed keepers of my charge in my sanctuary for yourselves.
This is what Lord GOD says: No foreigner, uncircumcised of heart and uncircumcised of flesh, shall come into my sanctuary — none of the foreigners who are among the people of Israel.
But the Levites who went far from me when Israel went astray, who strayed from me after their idols — they shall bear their iniquity.

And they shall be servants in my sanctuary, overseers at the gates of the house and serving the house. They shall slaughter the burnt offering and the sacrifice for the people, and they shall stand before them to serve them.

Because they served them before their idols and became for the house of Israel a stumbling block of iniquity — therefore I have raised my hand in an oath against them, declares Lord GOD, and they shall bear their iniquity.

And they shall not draw near to me to serve me as priests, nor draw near to any of my holy things, to the holiest of the holy things; and they shall bear their disgrace and the abominations they have done.
And I will make them keepers of the charge of the house, for all its service and for all that is done in it.

But the priests, the Levites, the sons of Zadok, who kept the charge of my sanctuary when the people of Israel went astray from me — they shall draw near to me to serve me, and they shall stand before me to bring near to me fat and blood, declares Lord GOD.
They shall come into my sanctuary, and they shall draw near to my table to serve me; and they shall keep my charge.
And when they come into the gates of the inner court, they shall wear linen garments; and no wool shall come upon them when they serve at the gates of the inner court and inside.
Linen head-dresses shall be on their heads, and linen undergarments on their loins. They shall not gird themselves with anything that makes them sweat.

And when they go out to the outer court — to the outer court, to the people — they shall take off the garments in which they serve and set them down in the holy rooms; and they shall put on other garments, so as not to consecrate the people with their garments.
And they shall not shave their heads, and they shall not let their hair go loose; they shall surely trim their heads.
And no priest shall drink wine when they come into the inner court.
And they shall not take a widow or a divorced woman for themselves as wives, but virgins from the offspring of the house of Israel; and a widow who is the widow of a priest they may take.
And they shall instruct my people in the difference between the holy and the common, and shall make known to them the difference between the unclean and the clean.
And in a dispute they shall stand to give judgement; by my judgements they shall judge it. And my laws and my statutes they shall keep at all my appointed times, and my sabbaths they shall keep holy.
And he shall not go near a dead person, and so become unclean; only for a father or a mother, a son or a daughter, a brother or an unmarried sister may they make themselves unclean.
And after his cleansing they shall count seven days for him.
And on the day he goes into the holy place, into the inner court, to serve in the holy place, he shall bring near his sin offering — declares Lord GOD.
And this shall be their inheritance: I am their inheritance. And you shall give them no holding in Israel: I am their holding.
The grain offering, the sin offering and the guilt offering — they shall eat them; and every devoted thing in Israel shall be theirs.

And the best of all the first fruits of everything, and every contribution of everything, from all your contributions, shall belong to the priests. And the best of your dough you shall give to the priest, to cause a blessing to rest on your house.
The priests shall not eat any carcass or torn animal, whether bird or beast.

ezekiel_45.t: And when you allot the land as an inheritance, you shall offer up a contribution to the LORD, a holy portion from the land: twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand wide. It is holy in all its territory all around.
Of this there shall be for the holy place five hundred by five hundred, square all around; and fifty cubits of pasture land for it all around.
And from this measured area you shall measure a length of twenty-five thousand and a width of ten thousand; and in it shall be the sanctuary, a holy of holies.

It is a holy portion from the land; it shall be for the priests who serve the sanctuary, who draw near to serve the LORD; and it shall be for them a place for houses, and a holy place for the sanctuary.
And twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand wide shall belong to the Levites who serve the house, as their holding: twenty rooms.
And as the holding of the city you shall give five thousand wide and twenty-five thousand long, alongside the holy contribution. It shall belong to all the house of Israel.

And to the prince: on either side of the holy contribution and of the holding of the city, in front of the holy contribution and in front of the holding of the city, from the west side westward and from the east side eastward; and its length corresponding to one of the tribal portions, from the western border to the eastern border.
As for the land, it shall be his as a holding in Israel; and my princes shall no longer oppress my people, and they shall give the land to the house of Israel by their tribes.
This is what Lord GOD says: Enough of you, princes of Israel! Put away violence and destruction, and do justice and righteousness. Lift your evictions off my people — declares Lord GOD.
You shall have balances of righteousness, an ephah of righteousness and a bath of righteousness.
The ephah and the bath shall be of one measure, so that the bath holds a tenth of a homer, and the ephah a tenth of a homer; the homer shall be the standard for both.
And the shekel shall be twenty gerahs. Twenty shekels, twenty-five shekels and fifteen shekels shall be your mina.
This is the contribution that you shall offer up: a sixth of an ephah from each homer of wheat; and a sixth of an ephah from each homer of barley.
And the prescribed portion of oil, measured by the bath: a tenth of a bath from each cor — ten baths make a homer, for ten baths make a homer.

And one sheep from the flock, one from every two hundred, from the well-watered land of Israel — for a grain offering, a burnt offering and peace sacrifices, to make atonement for them, declares Lord GOD.
All the people of the land shall be bound to this contribution to the prince in Israel.

And it shall fall to the prince to provide the burnt offerings, the grain offering and the drink offering at the festivals, at the new moons and on the sabbaths, at all the appointed times of the house of Israel. He shall provide the sin offering, the grain offering, the burnt offering and the peace sacrifices, to make atonement for the house of Israel.
This is what Lord GOD says: In the first month, on the first of the month, you shall take a bull, a young one of the herd, unblemished, and purify the sanctuary from sin.

And the priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering and put it on the doorpost of the house, on the four corners of the ledge of the altar, and on the doorpost of the gate of the inner court.
And so you shall do on the seventh of the month, for anyone who errs and for the simple; and so make atonement for the house.
In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, you shall have the Passover, a festival of seven days; unleavened bread shall be eaten.
And on that day the prince shall provide, for himself and for all the people of the land, a bull as a sin offering.

And for the seven days of the festival he shall provide a burnt offering to the LORD: seven bulls and seven rams, unblemished, each day for the seven days; and a sin offering, a male goat of the goats, each day.
And a grain offering: an ephah for each bull and an ephah for each ram he shall provide; and oil, a hin to the ephah.
In the seventh month, on the fifteenth day of the month, at the festival, he shall provide the same for the seven days: the same sin offering, burnt offering, grain offering and oil.

ezekiel_46.t: This is what Lord GOD says: The gate of the inner court that faces east shall be shut the six working days; and on the sabbath day it shall be opened, and on the day of the new moon it shall be opened.

And the prince shall come by way of the porch of the gate from outside and stand at the doorpost of the gate; and the priests shall offer his burnt offering and his peace sacrifices. And he shall bow down at the threshold of the gate and go out; and the gate shall not be shut until the evening.
And the people of the land shall bow down at the entrance of that gate on the sabbaths and on the new moons, before the LORD.
And the burnt offering that the prince shall bring near to the LORD on the sabbath day: six lambs, unblemished, and a ram, unblemished.
And a grain offering: an ephah for the ram; and for the lambs, a grain offering as much as he chooses to give; and oil, a hin to the ephah.
And on the day of the new moon: a bull, a young one of the herd, unblemished; and six lambs and a ram — they shall be unblemished.
And an ephah for the bull and an ephah for the ram he shall provide as a grain offering; and for the lambs, as much as his hand can afford; and oil, a hin to the ephah.
And when the prince comes in, he shall come by way of the porch of the gate, and go out by the same way.

And when the people of the land come before the LORD at the appointed times: whoever comes in by the north gate to bow down shall go out by the south gate, and whoever comes in by the south gate shall go out by the north gate. No one shall return by the gate he came in by; he shall go out opposite it.
And the prince shall be among them: when they come in, he comes in; and when they go out, they go out together.

And at the festivals and at the appointed times the grain offering shall be an ephah for the bull and an ephah for the ram, and for the lambs as much as he chooses to give; and oil, a hin to the ephah.

And when the prince provides a freewill offering — a burnt offering or peace sacrifices, a freewill offering to the LORD — the gate that faces east shall be opened for him, and he shall offer his burnt offering and his peace sacrifices as he does on the sabbath day; and he shall go out, and the gate shall be shut after he has gone out.
And a lamb, a year old, unblemished, you shall provide as a burnt offering each day to the LORD; morning by morning you shall provide it.

And a grain offering you shall provide with it, morning by morning: a sixth of an ephah, and a third of a hin of oil, to moisten the fine flour — a grain offering to the LORD, a perpetual statute, continually.
They shall provide the lamb, the grain offering and the oil, morning by morning: a continual burnt offering.
This is what Lord GOD says: If the prince gives a gift to any of his sons, it is his inheritance; it shall belong to his sons — it is their holding by inheritance.
And if he gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his servants, it shall be his until the year of liberty, and then it returns to the prince. His inheritance is his sons'; it shall be theirs.

And the prince shall not take from the inheritance of the people, oppressing them out of their holding. From his own holding he shall give his sons an inheritance, so that my people shall not be scattered, each from his holding.
And he brought me by the entrance at the side of the gate, to the holy rooms for the priests, which face north; and there was a place there, in the far corners to the west.

And he said to me, "This is the place where the priests shall boil the guilt offering and the sin offering, and where they shall bake the grain offering, so as not to carry them out into the outer court and consecrate the people."
And he brought me out to the outer court and led me past the four corners of the court; and there was a court in each corner of the court, a court in each corner of the court.
In the four corners of the court were enclosed courts, forty cubits long and thirty wide: one measurement for all four of them, set in the corners.
And a row of masonry ran around inside them, around all four; and cooking hearths were made under the rows all around.
And he said to me, "These are the kitchens, where those who serve the house shall boil the people's sacrifice."

ezekiel_47.t: And he brought me back to the entrance of the house; and there were waters going out from under the threshold of the house eastward, for the front of the house faces east. And the waters were going down from under the south side of the house, south of the altar.
And he brought me out by way of the north gate and led me round by the way outside, to the outer gate, by the way that faces east; and there were waters trickling from the south side.
When the man went out eastward with a measuring line in his hand, he measured off a thousand cubits and made me pass through the waters: ankle-deep water.
And he measured off a thousand and made me pass through the waters: knee-deep water. And he measured off a thousand and made me pass through: waist-deep water.
And he measured off a thousand — a river that I could not pass through, for the waters had risen: water deep enough to swim in, a river that could not be crossed.
And he said to me, "Do you see, mortal?" And he led me and brought me back to the bank of the river.
When I returned, there at the bank of the river were very many trees, on one side and on the other.
And he said to me: "These waters are going out to the eastern region and will go down to the Arabah and come to the sea; when they are brought out into the sea, the waters will be healed.

And every living creature that swarms, wherever the two rivers go, shall live; and there shall be very many fish, for these waters have come there and they shall be healed. And everything shall live wherever the river goes.
And fishermen shall stand beside it; from En-gedi to En-eglaim there shall be a place for spreading nets. Their fish shall be of many kinds, like the fish of the Great Sea, very many.
Its swamps and its marshes shall not be healed; they are given over to salt.

And by the river, on its bank on either side, shall grow every tree for food. Its foliage shall not wither and its fruit shall not fail; month by month it shall bear early fruit, because its waters come out from the sanctuary. And its fruit shall be for food, and its foliage for healing.
This is what Lord GOD says: This is the boundary by which you shall give the land as an inheritance to the twelve tribes of Israel: Joseph, two portions.
And you shall divide it as an inheritance, each alike with his brother, the land I raised my hand in an oath to give to your fathers; and this land shall fall to you as an inheritance.
And this is the boundary of the land. On the north side: from the Great Sea by the road of Hethlon, to Lebo-zedad,
Hamath, Berothah, Sibraim, which is between the territory of Damascus and the territory of Hamath; Hazer-hattikon, which is on the border of Hauran.
And the boundary shall run from the sea: Hazar-enan, the border of Damascus, and north northward, and the territory of Hamath. This is the north side.
And the east side: between Hauran and Damascus and Gilead and the land of Israel — the Jordan; from the border to the eastern sea you shall measure. This is the east side.
And the south side, southward: from Tamar to the waters of Meribath-kadesh, the Wadi, to the Great Sea. This is the south side, southward.
And the west side: the Great Sea, from the border to opposite Lebo-hamath. This is the west side.
And you shall divide this land among yourselves, according to the tribes of Israel.

And you shall allot it as an inheritance for yourselves and for the sojourners who sojourn among you, who have fathered children among you. And they shall be to you as the native-born among the people of Israel; with you they shall have an inheritance allotted among the tribes of Israel.
And in whatever tribe the sojourner sojourns, there you shall give him his inheritance — declares Lord GOD.

ezekiel_48.t: And these are the names of the tribes. From the northern end, beside the road of Hethlon, to Lebo-hamath, Hazar-enan, the border of Damascus northward, beside Hamath — and the east side and the west side shall be his: Dan, one portion.
And beside the border of Dan, from the east side to the west side: Asher, one portion.
And beside the border of Asher, from the east side and to the west side: Naphtali, one portion.
And beside the border of Naphtali, from the east side to the west side: Manasseh, one portion.
And beside the border of Manasseh, from the east side to the west side: Ephraim, one portion.
And beside the border of Ephraim, from the east side and to the west side: Reuben, one portion.
And beside the border of Reuben, from the east side to the west side: Judah, one portion.

And beside the border of Judah, from the east side to the west side, shall be the contribution that you shall offer up: twenty-five thousand wide, and in length like one of the tribal portions, from the east side to the west side; and the sanctuary shall be in the midst of it.
The contribution that you shall offer up to the LORD: twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand wide.

And to these shall the holy contribution belong, to the priests: on the north, twenty-five thousand; on the west, a width of ten thousand; on the east, a width of ten thousand; and on the south, a length of twenty-five thousand. And the sanctuary of the LORD shall be in the midst of it.
It is for the priests, the consecrated ones from the sons of Zadok, who kept my charge, who did not go astray when the people of Israel went astray, as the Levites went astray.
And it shall be for them a contribution from the contribution of the land, a holy of holies, beside the border of the Levites.
And the Levites, alongside the border of the priests: twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand wide. The whole length, twenty-five thousand; and the width, ten thousand.
And they shall not sell any of it, and none shall exchange it, nor shall the choicest of the land be transferred; for it is holy to the LORD.
And the five thousand that remain in the width, alongside the twenty-five thousand, is common land for the city, for dwelling and for pasture land; and the city shall be in the midst of it.

And these are its measurements: the north side, four thousand five hundred; the south side, four thousand five hundred; the east side, four thousand five hundred; and the west side, four thousand five hundred.
And the city shall have pasture land: two hundred and fifty on the north, two hundred and fifty on the south, two hundred and fifty on the east, and two hundred and fifty on the west.

And what remains in the length, alongside the holy contribution — ten thousand to the east and ten thousand to the west; and it shall lie alongside the holy contribution — its produce shall be food for those who work the city.
And those who work the city shall work it, drawn from all the tribes of Israel.
The whole contribution: twenty-five thousand by twenty-five thousand, a square. You shall offer up the holy contribution together with the holding of the city.

And what remains shall be for the prince, on either side of the holy contribution and of the holding of the city, in front of the twenty-five thousand of the contribution as far as the eastern border; and westward, in front of the twenty-five thousand as far as the western border, alongside the tribal portions — for the prince. And the holy contribution and the sanctuary of the house shall be in the midst of it.
And the holding of the Levites and the holding of the city lie in the midst of what belongs to the prince: between the border of Judah and the border of Benjamin, it shall be the prince's.
And the rest of the tribes: from the east side to the west side, Benjamin, one portion.
And beside the border of Benjamin, from the east side to the west side: Simeon, one portion.
And beside the border of Simeon, from the east side to the west side: Issachar, one portion.
And beside the border of Issachar, from the east side to the west side: Zebulun, one portion.
And beside the border of Zebulun, from the east side to the west side: Gad, one portion.
And beside the border of Gad, on the south side southward: the border shall run from Tamar to the waters of Meribath-kadesh, the Wadi, to the Great Sea.
This is the land that you shall allot as an inheritance to the tribes of Israel; and these are their portions — declares Lord GOD.
And these are the exits of the city. On the north side, four thousand five hundred by measure —
and the gates of the city shall be named for the tribes of Israel: three gates on the north — the gate of Reuben, one; the gate of Judah, one; the gate of Levi, one.
And on the east side, four thousand five hundred, and three gates: the gate of Joseph, one; the gate of Benjamin, one; the gate of Dan, one.
And the south side, four thousand five hundred by measure, and three gates: the gate of Simeon, one; the gate of Issachar, one; the gate of Zebulun, one.
The west side, four thousand five hundred; their gates, three: the gate of Gad, one; the gate of Asher, one; the gate of Naphtali, one.
The circuit: eighteen thousand. And the name of the city from that day: The LORD Is There.

ezra_1.t: In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, so that the word of the LORD from the mouth of Jeremiah might be completed, the LORD stirred the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, and he sent a proclamation through all his kingdom, and also in writing, saying:
"Thus says Cyrus king of Persia: 'The LORD, the God of the heavens, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and he himself has charged me to build him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah.

"'Whoever among you is from all his people — may his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build the house of the LORD, the God of Israel. He is the God who is in Jerusalem.

"'And everyone who remains, from any of the places where he is living as a foreigner — let the people of his place support him with silver and gold, with property and cattle, along with the freewill offering for the house of God which is in Jerusalem.'"

Then the heads of the ancestral houses of Judah and Benjamin arose, and the priests and the Levites — everyone whose spirit God had stirred — to go up and build the house of the LORD which is in Jerusalem.
And all those around them strengthened their hands with vessels of silver, with gold, with property and cattle and precious things, besides all that was freely offered.
And King Cyrus brought out the articles of the house of the LORD which Nebuchadnezzar had carried off from Jerusalem and put in the house of his gods.
Cyrus king of Persia brought them out by the hand of Mithredath the treasurer, and counted them out to Sheshbazzar the leader of Judah.
And this was their number: thirty dishes of gold; a thousand dishes of silver; twenty-nine knives;
thirty bowls of gold; four hundred and ten bowls of silver of a second sort; a thousand other articles.
All the articles of gold and silver were five thousand four hundred. Sheshbazzar brought all of it up when the exiles were brought up from Babylon to Jerusalem.

ezra_2.t: These are the people of the province who came up out of the captivity of the exile, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried into exile to Babylon, and who returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his own city —
those who came with Zerubbabel: Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Rehum, Baanah. The number of the men of the people of Israel:
the descendants of Parosh, two thousand one hundred and seventy-two;
the descendants of Shephatiah, three hundred and seventy-two;
the descendants of Arah, seven hundred and seventy-five;
the descendants of Pahath-moab, of the line of Jeshua and Joab, two thousand eight hundred and twelve;
the descendants of Elam, one thousand two hundred and fifty-four;
the descendants of Zattu, nine hundred and forty-five;
the descendants of Zaccai, seven hundred and sixty;
the descendants of Bani, six hundred and forty-two;
the descendants of Bebai, six hundred and twenty-three;
the descendants of Azgad, one thousand two hundred and twenty-two;
the descendants of Adonikam, six hundred and sixty-six;
the descendants of Bigvai, two thousand and fifty-six;
the descendants of Adin, four hundred and fifty-four;
the descendants of Ater, of the line of Hezekiah, ninety-eight;
the descendants of Bezai, three hundred and twenty-three;
the descendants of Jorah, a hundred and twelve;
the descendants of Hashum, two hundred and twenty-three;
the descendants of Gibbar, ninety-five;
the people of Bethlehem, a hundred and twenty-three;
the men of Netophah, fifty-six;
the men of Anathoth, a hundred and twenty-eight;
the people of Azmaveth, forty-two;
the people of Kiriath-arim, Kephirah and Beeroth, seven hundred and forty-three;
the people of Ramah and Geba, six hundred and twenty-one;
the men of Michmas, a hundred and twenty-two;
the men of Bethel and Ai, two hundred and twenty-three;
the people of Nebo, fifty-two;
the people of Magbish, a hundred and fifty-six;
the descendants of the other Elam, one thousand two hundred and fifty-four;
the descendants of Harim, three hundred and twenty;
the people of Lod, Hadid and Ono, seven hundred and twenty-five;
the people of Jericho, three hundred and forty-five;
the people of Senaah, three thousand six hundred and thirty.
The priests: the descendants of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua, nine hundred and seventy-three;
the descendants of Immer, one thousand and fifty-two;
the descendants of Pashhur, one thousand two hundred and forty-seven;
the descendants of Harim, one thousand and seventeen.
The Levites: the descendants of Jeshua and Kadmiel, of the line of Hodaviah, seventy-four.
The singers: the descendants of Asaph, a hundred and twenty-eight.
The descendants of the gatekeepers: the descendants of Shallum, Ater, Talmon, Akkub, Hatita and Shobai — a hundred and thirty-nine in all.
The temple servants: the descendants of Ziha, Hasupha, Tabbaoth,
Keros, Siaha, Padon,
Lebanah, Hagabah, Akkub,
Hagab, Shalmai, Hanan,
Giddel, Gahar, Reaiah,
Rezin, Nekoda, Gazzam,
Uzza, Paseah, Besai,
Asnah, Meunim, Nephussim,
Bakbuk, Hakupha, Harhur,
Bazluth, Mehida, Harsha,
Barkos, Sisera, Temah,
Neziah and Hatipha.
The descendants of Solomon's servants: the descendants of Sotai, Hassophereth, Peruda,
Jaalah, Darkon, Giddel,
Shephatiah, Hattil, Pochereth-hazzebaim and Ami.
All the temple servants and the descendants of Solomon's servants: three hundred and ninety-two.
And these are those who came up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addan and Immer, but could not declare their ancestral house or their descent, whether they were from Israel:
the descendants of Delaiah, Tobiah and Nekoda: six hundred and fifty-two.
And from the descendants of the priests: the descendants of Habaiah, of Hakkoz, and of Barzillai — who had taken a wife from the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by their name.
These searched for their register among those enrolled by genealogy, and it was not found; so they were excluded from the priesthood as defiled.
And the Tirshatha told them that they should not eat of the most holy things until a priest should stand with Urim and Thummim.
The whole assembly together: forty-two thousand three hundred and sixty,
besides their male and female servants — these were seven thousand three hundred and thirty-seven; and they had two hundred male and female singers.
Their horses were seven hundred and thirty-six; their mules, two hundred and forty-five;
their camels, four hundred and thirty-five; their donkeys, six thousand seven hundred and twenty.
And some of the heads of the ancestral houses, when they came to the house of the LORD which is in Jerusalem, made freewill offerings for the house of God, to erect it on its site.
According to their ability they gave to the treasury of the work sixty-one thousand darics of gold, five thousand minas of silver, and a hundred priestly tunics.
And the priests and the Levites, and some of the people, and the singers and the gatekeepers and the temple servants, settled in their cities; and all Israel in their cities.

ezra_3.t: When the seventh month arrived, and the Israelites were in the cities, the people gathered as one man to Jerusalem.

Then Jeshua son of Jozadak arose, with his brothers the priests, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel with his brothers, and they built the altar of the God of Israel, to offer up burnt offerings on it, as is written in the law of Moses, the man of God.
And they set the altar on its foundations, for terror was on them because of the peoples of the lands; and they offered up burnt offerings on it to the LORD, burnt offerings morning and evening.
And they kept the festival of booths, as is written, and the daily burnt offerings by number, according to the ordinance for each day, on its own day;

and after this the continual burnt offering, and the offerings for the new moons and for all the appointed times of the LORD that are set apart as holy, and for everyone who made a freewill offering to the LORD.
From the first day of the seventh month they began to offer up burnt offerings to the LORD; but the temple of the LORD had not been founded.

And they gave silver to the masons and the craftsmen, and food and drink and oil to the Sidonians and the Tyrians, to bring cedar timber from Lebanon to the sea at Joppa, according to the permission granted them by Cyrus king of Persia.

In the second year of their coming to the house of God at Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak made a beginning, with the rest of their brothers the priests and the Levites and all who had come from the captivity to Jerusalem; and they appointed the Levites, from twenty years old and upward, to oversee the work of the house of the LORD.

And Jeshua stood with his sons and his brothers, and Kadmiel with his sons, the sons of Judah, together, to oversee those doing the work in the house of God; also the sons of Henadad, with their sons and their brothers, the Levites.

And when the builders laid the foundation of the temple of the LORD, they appointed the priests, robed, with trumpets, and the Levites the sons of Asaph with cymbals, to praise the LORD according to the directions of David king of Israel.

And they sang responsively, praising and giving thanks to the LORD: "For he is good, for his steadfast love is upon Israel for ever." And all the people shouted a great shout, praising the LORD, because the foundation of the house of the LORD had been laid.

And many of the priests and the Levites and the heads of the ancestral houses, the old men who had seen the first house — when this house was founded before their eyes — wept with a loud voice; and many lifted up their voice with a shout of joy and gladness.
And the people could not tell the sound of the shout of gladness from the sound of the people's weeping; for the people shouted a great shout, and the sound was heard far off.

ezra_4.t: And the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard that the returned exiles were building a temple to the LORD, the God of Israel.

And they approached Zerubbabel and the heads of the ancestral houses and said to them, "Let us build with you, for like you we seek your God, and we have been sacrificing to him since the days of Esarhaddon king of Assyria, who brought us up here."
