Husham died, and Hadad son of Bedad reigned in his place; he defeated Midian in the region of Moab. The name of his city was Avith.
Hadad died, and Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his place.
Samlah died, and Shaul of Rehoboth on the River reigned in his place.
Shaul died, and Baal-hanan son of Achbor reigned in his place.
Baal-hanan son of Achbor died, and Hadar reigned in his place. The name of his city was Pau, and the name of his wife was Mehetabel the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Me-zahab.
These are the names of Esau's chiefs, by their clans and their places, by name: chief Timna, chief Alvah, chief Jetheth,
chief Oholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,
chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar,
chief Magdiel, chief Iram. These are the chiefs of Edom, by their dwelling places in the land of their possession. That is Esau, the father of Edom.

genesis_37.t: Jacob settled in the land where his father had lived as an alien, in the land of Canaan.

These are the generations of Jacob. Joseph, seventeen years old, was shepherding the flock with his brothers — he was still a youth — with the sons of Bilhah and the sons of Zilpah, his father's wives. And Joseph brought a bad report of them to their father.
Israel loved Joseph more than all his other sons, because he was a son of his old age; and he made him a long tunic.
When his brothers saw that their father loved him more than all his brothers, they hated him, and they could not speak peaceably to him.
Joseph dreamed a dream and told it to his brothers, and they hated him all the more.
He said to them, 'Hear, please, this dream that I have dreamed.'
'Look — we were binding sheaves in the middle of the field, and my sheaf rose and stood upright, and your sheaves gathered round and bowed down to my sheaf.'
His brothers said to him, 'Are you really to reign over us? Are you really to rule over us?' And they hated him all the more, for his dreams and for his words.
Then he dreamed another dream and recounted it to his brothers. He said, 'Look, I have dreamed another dream: the sun and the moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me.'

He recounted it to his father and to his brothers, and his father rebuked him and said, 'What is this dream you have dreamed? Are we really to come — I and your mother and your brothers — to bow down to you to the ground?'
His brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept the matter.
His brothers went to pasture their father's flock at Shechem.
Israel said to Joseph, 'Are not your brothers pasturing at Shechem? Come, and I will send you to them.' He said to him, 'Here I am.'
He said to him, 'Go, please, and see whether it is well with your brothers and well with the flock, and bring me back word.' So he sent him from the valley of Hebron, and he came to Shechem.
A man found him wandering in the open country, and the man asked him, 'What are you seeking?'
He said, 'I am seeking my brothers. Please tell me where they are pasturing.'
The man said, 'They have moved on from here; I heard them say, "Let us go to Dothan."' So Joseph went after his brothers and found them at Dothan.
They saw him from a distance, and before he came near to them they plotted against him, to put him to death.
They said to one another, 'Look, here comes this master of dreams.'
'Come now, let us kill him and throw him into one of the pits, and we will say, "A wild animal has eaten him." Then we shall see what becomes of his dreams.'
But Reuben heard, and he rescued him from their hand, and said, 'Let us not take his life.'
Reuben said to them, 'Do not shed blood. Throw him into this pit in the wilderness, but do not lay a hand on him' — so that he might rescue him from their hand and bring him back to his father.
When Joseph came to his brothers, they stripped Joseph of his tunic, the long tunic that was on him,
and they took him and threw him into the pit. The pit was empty; there was no water in it.
Then they sat down to eat bread. They looked up and saw a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead, their camels carrying gum, balm and ladanum, on their way to take them down to Egypt.
Judah said to his brothers, 'What profit is there if we kill our brother and conceal his blood?
'Come, let us sell him to the Ishmaelites, and let our hand not be against him; for he is our brother, our own flesh.' And his brothers listened to him.
Then Midianite men, traders, passed by; and they drew Joseph up out of the pit and sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver. And they brought Joseph to Egypt.
When Reuben came back to the pit and saw that Joseph was not in the pit, he tore his clothes.
He went back to his brothers and said, 'The boy is gone! And I — where am I to go?'
They took Joseph's tunic, slaughtered a male goat, and dipped the tunic in the blood.
They sent the long tunic and brought it to their father and said, 'We found this. Recognise it, please: is it your son's tunic or not?'
He recognised it and said, 'It is my son's tunic. A wild animal has eaten him. Joseph has surely been torn to pieces.'
Jacob tore his clothes, put sackcloth on his loins, and mourned over his son many days.
All his sons and all his daughters arose to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted, and he said, 'I will go down to my son, mourning, to Sheol.' And his father wept for him.
Meanwhile the Medanites sold him in Egypt to Potiphar, an official of Pharaoh, the commander of the guard.

genesis_38.t: At that time Judah went down from his brothers and turned aside to an Adullamite man whose name was Hirah.
There Judah saw the daughter of a Canaanite man whose name was Shua; he took her and went in to her.
She conceived and bore a son, and he called his name Er.
She conceived again and bore a son, and she called his name Onan.
She bore yet another son and called his name Shelah; and he was at Kezib when she bore him.
Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn, and her name was Tamar.
But Er, Judah's firstborn, was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD put him to death.
Then Judah said to Onan, 'Go in to your brother's wife and do the brother-in-law's duty for her, and raise up offspring for your brother.'
But Onan knew that the offspring would not be his; so whenever he went in to his brother's wife, he spilled on the ground, so as not to give offspring to his brother.
What he did was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and he put him to death also.

Then Judah said to Tamar his daughter-in-law, 'Remain a widow in your father's house until Shelah my son grows up' — for he thought, 'He may die too, like his brothers.' So Tamar went and lived in her father's house.
After a long time the daughter of Shua, Judah's wife, died. When Judah was comforted, he went up to his sheepshearers at Timnah, he and his friend Hirah the Adullamite.
Tamar was told, 'Look, your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep.'

So she took off the clothes of her widowhood, covered herself with a veil and wrapped herself up, and sat at the entrance of Enaim, which is on the road to Timnah — for she had seen that Shelah had grown up and she had not been given to him for a wife.
When Judah saw her, he took her for a prostitute, because she had covered her face.
He turned aside to her by the road and said, 'Come now, let me go in to you' — for he did not know that she was his daughter-in-law. She said, 'What will you give me, that you may come in to me?'
He said, 'I will send you a young goat from the flock.' She said, 'Only if you give a pledge until you send it.'
He said, 'What pledge shall I give you?' She said, 'Your seal and your cord and your staff that is in your hand.' So he gave them to her, went in to her, and she conceived by him.
Then she got up and went away; she took off her veil and put on the clothes of her widowhood.
Judah sent the young goat by the hand of his friend the Adullamite, to take the pledge back from the woman's hand; but he did not find her.
He asked the men of her place, 'Where is the shrine prostitute, the one who was at Enaim by the road?' They said, 'There has been no shrine prostitute in this place.'
So he returned to Judah and said, 'I did not find her; and the men of the place said too, "There has been no shrine prostitute in this place."'
Judah said, 'Let her keep them for herself, or we shall become a laughing-stock. Look, I sent this young goat, and you did not find her.'
About three months later Judah was told, 'Tamar your daughter-in-law has acted as a prostitute, and moreover she is pregnant by prostitution.' And Judah said, 'Bring her out, and let her be burned.'

As she was being brought out, she sent word to her father-in-law: 'By the man to whom these belong I am pregnant.' And she said, 'Recognise, please: whose are these — the seal, the cord and the staff?'
Judah recognised them and said, 'She is more in the right than I am, because I did not give her to Shelah my son.' And he did not know her again.
When the time came for her to give birth, there were twins in her womb.
And as she gave birth, one put out a hand; the midwife took a scarlet thread and tied it on his hand, saying, 'This one came out first.'
But as he withdrew his hand, his brother came out; and she said, 'How you have broken out! A breach upon you!' So his name was called Perez.
Afterward his brother came out, the one with the scarlet thread on his hand, and his name was called Zerah.

genesis_39.t: Now Joseph had been brought down to Egypt, and Potiphar, an official of Pharaoh, the commander of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him from the hand of the Ishmaelites who had brought him down there.
The LORD was with Joseph, and he became a successful man; and he was in the house of his Egyptian master.
His master saw that the LORD was with him, and that the LORD made everything he did succeed in his hand.
So Joseph found favour in his eyes and served him; he appointed him over his household and gave into his hand all that he had.

From the time he appointed him over his household and over all that he had, the LORD blessed the Egyptian's house on account of Joseph; and the blessing of the LORD was on all that he had, in the house and in the field.
So he left everything he had in Joseph's hand, and with Joseph there he gave no thought to anything except the food he ate. Now Joseph was handsome in form and handsome in appearance.
After these things his master's wife lifted up her eyes to Joseph, and she said, 'Lie with me.'
But he refused, and said to his master's wife, 'Look, my master gives no thought, with me here, to what is in the house, and all that he has he has given into my hand.
'He is not greater in this house than I am, and he has withheld nothing from me except you, since you are his wife. How then could I do this great evil, and sin against God?'
And though she spoke to Joseph day after day, he did not listen to her, to lie beside her or to be with her.
One such day he came into the house to do his work, and none of the men of the house were there in the house.
She seized him by his clothing and said, 'Lie with me.' But he left his clothing in her hand and fled, and went outside.
When she saw that he had left his clothing in her hand and had fled outside,
she called out to the men of her household and said to them, 'See — he has brought us a Hebrew man to mock us. He came to me to lie with me, and I called out with a loud voice.
'And when he heard me raise my voice and call out, he left his clothing beside me and fled, and went outside.'
She kept his clothing beside her until his master came home.
Then she spoke to him in these words: 'The Hebrew servant whom you brought to us came to me to mock me.
'And when I raised my voice and called out, he left his clothing beside me and fled outside.'
When his master heard the words his wife spoke to him — 'This is what your servant did to me' — his anger burned.
So Joseph's master took him and put him in the house of the prison, the place where the king's prisoners were confined; and he was there in the house of the prison.
But the LORD was with Joseph and extended steadfast love to him, and gave him favour in the eyes of the commander of the house of the prison.
The commander of the house of the prison gave into Joseph's hand all the prisoners who were in the prison, and whatever was done there, he was the one who did it.
The commander of the house of the prison did not look into anything at all that was in Joseph's hand, because the LORD was with him; and whatever he did, the LORD made it succeed.

genesis_40.t: Some time after this, the cupbearer of the king of Egypt and the baker offended their master, the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh was angry with his two officials, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker.
He put them in custody in the house of the commander of the guard, in the prison, the place where Joseph was confined.
The commander of the guard assigned Joseph to them, and he attended them. They were in custody for some time.
Both of them dreamed a dream on the same night, each his own dream, each dream with its own meaning — the cupbearer and the baker of the king of Egypt, who were confined in the prison.
When Joseph came to them in the morning, he saw that they were downcast.
He asked Pharaoh's officials who were with him in custody in his master's house, "Why do you look so troubled today?"
They said to him, "We have each dreamed a dream, and there is no one to interpret it." Joseph said to them, "Do interpretations not belong to God? Tell me, please."
So the chief cupbearer told Joseph his dream. He said to him, "In my dream there was a vine in front of me,
and on the vine were three branches. As it budded, its blossom came out, and its clusters ripened into grapes.
Pharaoh's cup was in my hand, and I took the grapes and squeezed them into Pharaoh's cup, and I placed the cup in Pharaoh's hand.
Joseph said to him, "This is its interpretation: the three branches are three days."
In three days Pharaoh will lift up your head and restore you to your post, and you will put Pharaoh's cup in his hand as you used to do, when you were his cupbearer.
But remember me when it goes well for you, and please show me loyalty: mention me to Pharaoh, and get me out of this house.
For I was truly stolen away from the land of the Hebrews, and here too I have done nothing for them to have put me in the pit.
When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was favourable, he said to Joseph, "I too had a dream: three baskets of ḥori were on my head,
and in the top basket there was every kind of baked food for Pharaoh, and the birds were eating it out of the basket on my head."
Joseph answered, "This is its interpretation: the three baskets are three days."
In three days Pharaoh will lift up your head — off you — and hang you on a tree, and the birds will eat your flesh off you.
On the third day, Pharaoh's birthday, he made a feast for all his servants, and he lifted up the head of the chief cupbearer and the head of the chief baker among his servants.
He restored the chief cupbearer to his cupbearing, and he placed the cup in Pharaoh's hand.
But the chief baker he hanged, just as Joseph had interpreted to them.
But the chief cupbearer did not remember Joseph. He forgot him.

genesis_41.t: At the end of two full years, Pharaoh had a dream: he was standing by the Nile,
and out of the Nile came up seven cows, handsome and fat, and they grazed in the reed grass.
Then seven other cows came up after them out of the Nile, ugly and gaunt, and they stood beside the other cows on the bank of the Nile.
And the ugly, gaunt cows ate the seven handsome, fat cows. Then Pharaoh woke up.
He fell asleep and dreamed a second time: seven ears of grain were coming up on one stalk, plump and good.
Then seven ears of grain, thin and scorched by the east wind, sprang up after them.
And the thin ears swallowed the seven plump, full ears. Then Pharaoh woke up, and it had been a dream.
In the morning his spirit was troubled, so he sent and summoned all the ḥarṭummim of Egypt and all its wise men. Pharaoh told them his dream, but no one could interpret it for Pharaoh.
Then the chief cupbearer spoke to Pharaoh: "Today I bring my sins to remembrance.
Pharaoh was angry with his servants and put me in custody in the house of the commander of the guard, me and the chief baker.
We each dreamed a dream on the same night, he and I, and each dream had its own meaning.
A young Hebrew was there with us, a slave of the commander of the guard. We told him, and he interpreted our dreams for us, each according to his own dream.
And just as he interpreted for us, so it happened: I was restored to my post, and he was hanged.
So Pharaoh sent and summoned Joseph, and they rushed him out of the pit. He shaved, changed his clothes, and came in to Pharaoh.
Pharaoh said to Joseph, "I have dreamed a dream, and there is no one to interpret it. And I have heard it said of you that you hear a dream and interpret it."
Joseph answered Pharaoh, "It is not in me. God will answer for Pharaoh's welfare."
So Pharaoh said to Joseph, "In my dream, there I was, standing on the bank of the Nile,
and out of the Nile came up seven cows, fat and well-formed, and they grazed in the reed grass.
Then seven other cows came up after them, weak and very ill-formed and lean — I have never seen any so bad in all the land of Egypt.
And the lean, ugly cows ate the seven fat cows that came first.
They went inside them, but it could not be told that they had gone inside them: they looked as bad as they had at the start. Then I woke up.
Then I saw in my dream: seven ears of grain were coming up on one stalk, full and good.
Then seven ears of grain, ṣenumot — thin, scorched by the east wind — sprang up after them.
And the thin ears swallowed the seven good ears. I told this to the ḥarṭummim, but no one could tell me what it meant."
Joseph said to Pharaoh, "Pharaoh's dream is one and the same. God has told Pharaoh what he is about to do.
The seven good cows are seven years, and the seven good ears are seven years. It is one dream.
And the seven lean, ugly cows that came up after them are seven years, and so are the seven empty ears scorched by the east wind: they will be seven years of famine.
This is what I said to Pharaoh: God has shown Pharaoh what he is about to do.
Seven years are coming of great plenty throughout the land of Egypt.
Then seven years of famine will arise after them, and all the plenty in the land of Egypt will be forgotten, and the famine will consume the land.
The plenty will not be remembered in the land because of the famine that follows, for it will be very severe.
As for the dream being repeated to Pharaoh twice: it is because the matter is fixed by God, and God is hurrying to do it.
Now then, let Pharaoh look out a man who is discerning and wise, and set him over the land of Egypt.
Let Pharaoh act: let him appoint officers over the land and take a fifth of the produce of the land of Egypt during the seven years of plenty.
Let them gather all the food of these good years that are coming, and store up grain under Pharaoh's authority as food in the cities, and let them keep it.
The food will be a reserve for the land through the seven years of famine that will come upon the land of Egypt, so that the land will not be cut off by the famine.
The proposal seemed good to Pharaoh and to all his servants.
Pharaoh said to his servants, "Can we find another like this, a man in whom is the spirit of God?"
Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Since God has made all this known to you, there is no one as discerning and wise as you.
You shall be over my house, and by your mouth all my people shall order themselves; only in the throne will I be greater than you."
And Pharaoh said to Joseph, "See, I have set you over all the land of Egypt."
Pharaoh took his signet ring off his hand and put it on Joseph's hand, clothed him in garments of fine linen, and put the gold chain around his neck.
He had him ride in his second chariot, and they called out before him, "Abrek!" So he set him over all the land of Egypt.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph, "I am Pharaoh, and without your word no one shall lift hand or foot in all the land of Egypt."
Pharaoh named Joseph Zaphenath-paneah, and gave him Asenath, the daughter of Poti-phera, priest of On, as a wife. And Joseph went out over the land of Egypt.
Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. Joseph went out from Pharaoh's presence and travelled through all the land of Egypt.
In the seven years of plenty the land produced by handfuls.
He gathered all the food of the seven years that came upon the land of Egypt and stored the food in the cities; the food from the fields around each city he stored inside it.
Joseph stored up grain like the sand of the sea, so much that he stopped measuring it, for it was beyond measure.
Two sons were born to Joseph before the year of famine came, whom Asenath the daughter of Poti-phera, priest of On, bore to him.
Joseph named the firstborn Manasseh, "for God has made me forget all my trouble and all my father's house."
And the second he named Ephraim, "for God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction."
Then the seven years of plenty in the land of Egypt came to an end.
And the seven years of famine began to come, just as Joseph had said. There was famine in all the lands, but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.
When all the land of Egypt grew hungry, the people cried out to Pharaoh for bread. And Pharaoh said to all Egypt, "Go to Joseph; whatever he says to you, do."
The famine was over the whole face of the land, and Joseph opened all the storehouses and sold grain to Egypt, and the famine grew severe in the land of Egypt.
And all the earth came to Egypt to buy grain from Joseph, for the famine was severe over all the earth.

genesis_42.t: When Jacob saw that there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons, "Why do you keep looking at one another?"
He said, "I have heard that there is grain in Egypt. Go down there and buy grain for us, so that we may live and not die."
So ten of Joseph's brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt.
But Jacob did not send Benjamin, Joseph's brother, with his brothers, for he said, "Something might happen to him."
So the sons of Israel came to buy grain among the others who were coming, for the famine was in the land of Canaan.
Now Joseph was the ruler over the land; he was the one who sold grain to all the people of the land. Joseph's brothers came and bowed down to him with their faces to the ground.

Joseph saw his brothers and recognised them, but he made himself a stranger to them and spoke harshly with them. He said to them, "Where have you come from?" They said, "From the land of Canaan, to buy food."
Joseph recognised his brothers, but they did not recognise him.
Then Joseph remembered the dreams he had dreamed about them, and he said to them, "You are spies. You have come to see the nakedness of the land."
They said to him, "No, my lord. Your servants have come to buy food."
"We are all the sons of one man. We are honest men. Your servants have never been spies."
But he said to them, "No. You have come to see the nakedness of the land."
They said, "Your servants are twelve brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan. The youngest is with our father today, and one is no more."
Joseph said to them, "It is just as I said to you: you are spies."
"By this you will be tested: by the life of Pharaoh, you shall not leave this place unless your youngest brother comes here."

"Send one of your number to fetch your brother, and the rest of you be held prisoner, so that your words may be tested, whether the truth is with you. And if not, then by the life of Pharaoh, you are spies."
And he put them all in custody for three days.
On the third day Joseph said to them, "Do this and live. I fear God."
"If you are honest men, let one of your brothers be held in the place of your custody, while the rest of you go and take grain for the hunger of your households,
"and bring your youngest brother to me. Then your words will be confirmed and you will not die." And they did so.
They said to one another, "We are truly guilty concerning our brother. We saw his distress when he pleaded with us, and we did not listen. That is why this distress has come upon us."
Reuben answered them, "Did I not say to you, 'Do not sin against the boy'? But you would not listen. And now his blood is being required."
They did not know that Joseph was listening, for there was an interpreter between them.
He turned away from them and wept. Then he came back to them and spoke to them, and he took Simeon from among them and bound him before their eyes.
Then Joseph gave orders to fill their containers with grain, to return each man's silver into his sack, and to give them provisions for the journey. And so it was done for them.
They loaded their grain onto their donkeys and set off from there.
At the lodging place one of them opened his sack to give his donkey fodder, and he saw his silver — there it was, in the mouth of his bag.
He said to his brothers, "My silver has been returned — here it is in my bag!" Their hearts sank, and they turned to one another trembling and said, "What is this that God has done to us?"
They came to Jacob their father in the land of Canaan and told him everything that had happened to them:
"The man who is lord of the land spoke harshly with us and treated us as men spying out the land.
"We said to him, 'We are honest men; we have never been spies.
"'We are twelve brothers, sons of our father. One is no more, and the youngest is with our father today in the land of Canaan.'
"And the man who is lord of the land said to us, 'By this I shall know that you are honest men: leave one of your brothers with me, take grain for the hunger of your households, and go.
"'And bring your youngest brother to me, and I shall know that you are not spies but honest men. Then I will give you back your brother, and you may trade in the land.'"
Then, as they were emptying their sacks, there was each man's bundle of silver in his sack. When they and their father saw the bundles of silver, they were afraid.
Jacob their father said to them, "You have bereaved me of my children. Joseph is no more, and Simeon is no more, and now you would take Benjamin. All these things have come upon me."
Then Reuben said to his father, "You may put my two sons to death if I do not bring him back to you. Put him in my hand, and I will return him to you."
But he said, "My son shall not go down with you, for his brother is dead and he alone is left. If harm befalls him on the journey you are taking, you will bring my grey head down in sorrow to Sheol."

genesis_43.t: The famine was severe in the land.
When they had finished eating the grain they had brought from Egypt, their father said to them, "Go back and buy us a little food."
But Judah said to him, "The man warned us solemnly: 'You shall not see my face unless your brother is with you.'
"If you will send our brother with us, we will go down and buy food for you.
"But if you will not send him, we will not go down, for the man said to us, 'You shall not see my face unless your brother is with you.'"
Israel said, "Why did you do me this harm, telling the man that you had another brother?"

They said, "The man questioned us closely about ourselves and our family: 'Is your father still alive? Do you have a brother?' And we answered him according to these words. How could we have known that he would say, 'Bring your brother down'?"
Then Judah said to Israel his father, "Send the boy with me, and we will get up and go, so that we may live and not die — we, and you, and our little ones.
"I myself will stand surety for him; from my hand you may require him. If I do not bring him back to you and set him before you, then I will bear the guilt before you all my days.
"For if we had not delayed, by now we could have gone back twice over."

Then Israel their father said to them, "If it must be so, then do this: take some of the best products of the land in your containers and carry down a gift to the man — a little balm and a little honey, gum and myrrh, pistachios and almonds.
"Take double the silver with you, and carry back the silver that was returned in the mouth of your sacks; perhaps it was an oversight.
"Take your brother too, and get up and go back to the man.
"And may God Almighty grant you compassion before the man, so that he releases to you your other brother, and Benjamin. And as for me, if I am bereaved, I am bereaved."
So the men took this gift, and they took double the silver with them, and Benjamin. They set out, went down to Egypt, and stood before Joseph.
When Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to the steward of his house, "Bring the men into the house, slaughter an animal and prepare it, for the men are to eat with me at noon."
The man did as Joseph said, and brought the men into Joseph's house.

The men were afraid because they had been brought into Joseph's house, and they said, "It is because of the silver that was returned in our sacks the first time that we are being brought in — so that he may fall upon us and overpower us and take us as slaves, and our donkeys with us."
So they approached the steward of Joseph's house and spoke to him at the entrance of the house.
They said, "Please, my lord, we did indeed come down the first time to buy food.
"And when we came to the lodging place and opened our sacks, there was each man's silver in the mouth of his sack, our silver in its full weight. We have brought it back with us.
"And we have brought down other silver with us to buy food. We do not know who put our silver in our sacks."
He said, "Peace to you; do not be afraid. Your God, the God of your father, has given you treasure in your sacks. Your silver came to me." And he brought Simeon out to them.
The man brought the men into Joseph's house, gave them water to wash their feet, and gave fodder to their donkeys.
They got the gift ready for Joseph's arrival at noon, for they had heard that they would eat a meal there.
When Joseph came into the house, they brought him the gift they had with them into the house, and bowed down to him to the ground.
He asked after their welfare and said, "Is your aged father well, the one you spoke of? Is he still alive?"
They said, "Your servant our father is well; he is still alive." And they bowed low and bowed down.
Then he lifted his eyes and saw Benjamin his brother, his mother's son, and he said, "Is this your youngest brother, the one you spoke to me about?" And he said, "God be gracious to you, my son."
Joseph hurried out, for his compassion for his brother had grown warm and he needed to weep. He went into an inner room and wept there.
Then he washed his face and came out. He restrained himself and said, "Serve the meal."
They served him by himself, and them by themselves, and the Egyptians who ate with him by themselves; for the Egyptians could not eat with the Hebrews, since that is an abomination to Egypt.
They were seated before him, the firstborn according to his birthright and the youngest according to his youth, and the men looked at one another in astonishment.
Portions were carried to them from his table, and Benjamin's portion was five times greater than any of theirs. And they drank and became drunk with him.

genesis_44.t: Then Joseph commanded the steward of his house, "Fill the men's sacks with as much food as they can carry, and put each man's silver in the mouth of his sack.
"And put my cup, the silver cup, in the mouth of the youngest one's sack, along with the silver for his grain." And he did as Joseph had said.
At first light the men were sent off, they and their donkeys.

They had gone out of the city and were not yet far off when Joseph said to the steward of his house, "Get up, pursue the men, and when you overtake them say to them, 'Why have you repaid evil for good?
"'Is this not the cup my lord drinks from, and by which he practises divination? You have done evil in what you have done.'"
He overtook them and spoke these words to them.
They said to him, "Why does my lord speak words like these? Far be it from your servants to do such a thing!
"Look, the silver we found in the mouth of our sacks we brought back to you from the land of Canaan. How then would we steal silver or gold from your master's house?
"Whichever of your servants it is found with, let him die — and the rest of us will be slaves to my lord."
He said, "Now let it be as you say: the one it is found with shall be my slave, and the rest of you shall be innocent."
Each of them quickly lowered his sack to the ground, and each opened his sack.
He searched, beginning with the eldest and finishing with the youngest. And the cup was found in Benjamin's sack.
They tore their garments, and each man loaded his donkey, and they went back to the city.
Judah and his brothers came to Joseph's house, and he was still there, and they fell to the ground before him.
Joseph said to them, "What is this deed you have done? Did you not know that a man like me practises divination?"

Judah said, "What shall we say to my lord? What shall we speak? How can we justify ourselves? God has found out the guilt of your servants. Here we are, slaves to my lord — we ourselves, and the one in whose hand the cup was found."
But he said, "Far be it from me to do that. The man in whose hand the cup was found shall be my slave; and as for you, go up in peace to your father."
Then Judah drew near to him and said, "Please, my lord, let your servant speak a word in my lord's ears, and do not let your anger burn against your servant, for you are like Pharaoh himself.
"My lord asked his servants, 'Have you a father or a brother?'
"And we said to my lord, 'We have an aged father and a young child of his old age. His brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother, and his father loves him.'
"And you said to your servants, 'Bring him down to me, that I may set my eyes on him.'
"And we said to my lord, 'The boy cannot leave his father; if he leaves his father, his father will die.'
"And you said to your servants, 'If your youngest brother does not come down with you, you shall not see my face again.'
"And when we went up to your servant my father, we told him the words of my lord.
"And our father said, 'Go back and buy us a little food.'
"And we said, 'We cannot go down. If our youngest brother is with us, then we will go down, for we cannot see the man's face unless our youngest brother is with us.'
"And your servant my father said to us, 'You know that my wife bore me two sons.
"'And one went out from me, and I said, "He has surely been torn to pieces" — and I have not seen him since.
"'And if you take this one also from me and harm befalls him, you will bring my grey head down in calamity to Sheol.'
"So now, when I come to your servant my father and the boy is not with us — and his own life is bound up with the boy's life —
"then when he sees that the boy is not there, he will die, and your servants will have brought the grey head of your servant our father down in sorrow to Sheol.
"For your servant went surety for the boy with my father, saying, 'If I do not bring him back to you, I will bear the guilt before my father all my days.'
"Now therefore, let your servant remain in place of the boy as a slave to my lord, and let the boy go up with his brothers.
"For how can I go up to my father if the boy is not with me? Let me not see the evil that would come upon my father."

genesis_45.t: Then Joseph could no longer restrain himself before all those standing by him, and he cried out, "Send everyone out from me!" So no one stood with him when Joseph made himself known to his brothers.
He wept aloud, and the Egyptians heard, and the house of Pharaoh heard.
Joseph said to his brothers, "I am Joseph. Is my father still alive?" But his brothers could not answer him, for they were terrified before him.
Then Joseph said to his brothers, "Come near to me." And they came near. And he said, "I am Joseph your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.
"And now, do not be grieved, and do not be angry with yourselves that you sold me here, for God sent me before you to preserve life.
"For the famine has been in the land these two years, and there are five more years in which there will be neither ploughing nor harvest.
"And God sent me before you to establish a remnant for you on the earth and to keep you alive for a great deliverance.
"So it was not you who sent me here, but God. He has made me a father to Pharaoh, lord of all his house, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.
"Hurry, go up to my father and say to him, 'Thus says your son Joseph: God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me; do not delay.
"'You shall dwell in the land of Goshen and be near me — you and your sons and your grandsons, your flocks and your herds and all that you have.
"'And I will provide for you there, for there are five more years of famine, so that you are not impoverished, you and your household and all that you have.'
"And look, your own eyes can see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my mouth speaking to you.
"Tell my father of all my honour in Egypt and of everything you have seen, and hurry and bring my father down here."
Then he fell on the neck of Benjamin his brother and wept, and Benjamin wept on his neck.
He kissed all his brothers and wept over them, and after that his brothers talked with him.
The report was heard in Pharaoh's house: "Joseph's brothers have come." And it pleased Pharaoh and his servants.
Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Say to your brothers, 'Do this: load your animals and go on to the land of Canaan,
"'and take your father and your households and come to me. I will give you the best of the land of Egypt, and you shall eat the fat of the land.'
"And you are commanded: 'Do this — take carts from the land of Egypt for your little ones and your wives, and bring your father, and come.
"'And do not be concerned about your possessions, for the best of all the land of Egypt is yours.'"
The sons of Israel did so. Joseph gave them carts at Pharaoh's command and gave them provisions for the journey.
To each of them he gave changes of garments, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of garments.
And to his father he sent the like: ten donkeys carrying the good things of Egypt, and ten she-donkeys carrying grain and bread and food for his father for the journey.
So he sent his brothers off, and as they went he said to them, "Do not quarrel on the way."
So they went up from Egypt and came to the land of Canaan, to Jacob their father.
They told him, "Joseph is still alive, and he is ruler over all the land of Egypt." But his heart went numb, for he did not believe them.
But when they told him all the words of Joseph that he had spoken to them, and when he saw the carts that Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of Jacob their father revived.
And Israel said, "Enough. Joseph my son is still alive. I will go and see him before I die."

genesis_46.t: So Israel set out with all that he had. He came to Beersheba and offered sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac.
And God spoke to Israel in visions of the night: "Jacob, Jacob." And he said, "Here I am."
He said, "I am God, the God of your father. Do not be afraid to go down to Egypt, for I will make you into a great nation there.
"I myself will go down with you to Egypt, and I myself will surely bring you up again. And Joseph will set his hand on your eyes."
Then Jacob set out from Beersheba, and the sons of Israel carried Jacob their father, their little ones and their wives, in the carts that Pharaoh had sent to carry him.
They took their livestock and the possessions they had acquired in the land of Canaan, and they came to Egypt, Jacob and all his offspring with him:
his sons and his grandsons with him, his daughters and his granddaughters — all his offspring he brought with him to Egypt.
These are the names of the sons of Israel who came to Egypt, Jacob and his sons: Reuben, Jacob's firstborn;
The sons of Reuben: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
The sons of Simeon: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jakin, Zohar, and Shaul the son of the Canaanite woman.
The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
The sons of Judah: Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah (but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan). And the sons of Perez were Hezron and Hamul.
The sons of Issachar: Tola, Puvah, Iob, and Shimron.
The sons of Zebulun: Sered, Elon, and Jahleel.
These are the sons of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob in Paddan-aram, together with Dinah his daughter. All the persons of his sons and daughters were thirty-three.
The sons of Gad: Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli.
The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah, with Serah their sister. And the sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel.
These are the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to Leah his daughter; she bore these to Jacob — sixteen persons.
The sons of Rachel, Jacob's wife: Joseph and Benjamin.
And to Joseph in the land of Egypt were born Manasseh and Ephraim, whom Asenath the daughter of Poti-phera, priest of On, bore to him.
The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim, and Ard.
These are the sons of Rachel who were born to Jacob — fourteen persons in all.
The sons of Dan: Hushim.
The sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
These are the sons of Bilhah, whom Laban gave to Rachel his daughter; she bore these to Jacob — seven persons in all.
All the persons belonging to Jacob who came to Egypt, his own direct descendants, apart from the wives of Jacob's sons, were sixty-six in all.
And the sons of Joseph, who were born to him in Egypt, were two persons. All the persons of the house of Jacob who came to Egypt were seventy.
He sent Judah ahead of him to Joseph, to give directions before him to Goshen. And they came to the land of Goshen.
Joseph harnessed his chariot and went up to Goshen to meet Israel his father. He presented himself to him, fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a long while.
Israel said to Joseph, "Now let me die, since I have seen your face and you are still alive."
Joseph said to his brothers and to his father's household, "I will go up and tell Pharaoh, and say to him, 'My brothers and my father's household, who were in the land of Canaan, have come to me.
"'The men are shepherds; they have always been keepers of livestock. They have brought their flocks and their herds and all that they have.'
"And when Pharaoh summons you and asks, 'What is your occupation?'

"you shall say, 'Your servants have been keepers of livestock from our youth until now, both we and our fathers' — so that you may settle in the land of Goshen, for every shepherd is an abomination to the Egyptians."

genesis_47.t: Then Joseph came and told Pharaoh, "My father and my brothers, with their flocks and herds and all that they have, have come from the land of Canaan, and they are now in the land of Goshen."
And from among his brothers he took five men and presented them before Pharaoh.
Pharaoh said to his brothers, "What is your occupation?" They said to Pharaoh, "Your servants are shepherds, both we and our fathers."

They said to Pharaoh, "We have come to sojourn in the land, for there is no pasture for your servants' flocks; the famine is severe in the land of Canaan. Now therefore, please let your servants settle in the land of Goshen."
Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Your father and your brothers have come to you.

"The land of Egypt is before you; settle your father and your brothers in the best of the land. Let them dwell in the land of Goshen. And if you know of capable men among them, put them in charge of my own livestock."
Then Joseph brought Jacob his father in and presented him before Pharaoh, and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
Pharaoh said to Jacob, "How many are the days of the years of your life?"

Jacob said to Pharaoh, "The days of the years of my sojournings are a hundred and thirty years. Few and hard have been the days of the years of my life, and they have not reached the days of the years of the lives of my fathers in the days of their sojournings."
Then Jacob blessed Pharaoh and went out from Pharaoh's presence.
So Joseph settled his father and his brothers and gave them a holding in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.
And Joseph provided his father and his brothers and all his father's household with food, according to the number of their little ones.
Now there was no food in all the land, for the famine was very severe, and the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan languished because of the famine.
Joseph gathered up all the silver that was to be found in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan, in payment for the grain they were buying, and he brought the silver into Pharaoh's house.
When the silver of the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan was spent, all Egypt came to Joseph and said, "Give us food! Why should we die before your eyes? For the silver is gone."
Joseph said, "Give me your livestock, and I will give you food in exchange for your livestock, since the silver is gone."

So they brought their livestock to Joseph, and Joseph gave them food in exchange for the horses, the flocks, the herds, and the donkeys. He sustained them with food that year in exchange for all their livestock.

When that year was ended, they came to him in the second year and said to him, "We will not hide it from my lord: the silver is spent, and the herds of cattle belong to my lord. Nothing is left before my lord but our bodies and our ground.

"Why should we die before your eyes, we and our ground alike? Buy us and our ground for food, and we with our ground will be slaves to Pharaoh. Give us seed, that we may live and not die, and that the ground may not become desolate."
So Joseph bought all the ground of Egypt for Pharaoh, for every Egyptian sold his field, because the famine was severe upon them. And the land became Pharaoh's.
And as for the people, he moved them into the cities, from one end of the territory of Egypt to the other.
Only the ground of the priests he did not buy, for the priests had an allowance from Pharaoh and lived on the allowance Pharaoh gave them; therefore they did not sell their ground.
Then Joseph said to the people, "Look, I have bought you today, and your ground, for Pharaoh. Here is seed for you; sow the ground.
"And at the harvests you shall give a fifth to Pharaoh, and four parts shall be yours, for seed for the field, for your own food, for those in your households, and for your little ones to eat."
They said, "You have kept us alive. May we find favour in the eyes of my lord, and we will be slaves to Pharaoh."
And Joseph made it a statute concerning the ground of Egypt, in force to this day: a fifth to Pharaoh. Only the ground of the priests alone did not become Pharaoh's.
So Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen. They acquired holdings there, and were fruitful and multiplied greatly.
Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years, and the days of Jacob, the years of his life, were a hundred and forty-seven years.

When the time drew near for Israel to die, he called for his son Joseph and said to him, "If I have found favour in your eyes, put your hand under my thigh and deal with me in loyalty and faithfulness: do not bury me in Egypt.
"When I lie down with my fathers, carry me out of Egypt and bury me in their burial place." And he said, "I will do as you say."
And he said, "Swear to me." So he swore to him. And Israel bowed down at the head of the bed.

genesis_48.t: Some time after this, Joseph was told, "Your father is ill." So he took his two sons with him, Manasseh and Ephraim.
Jacob was told, "Your son Joseph has come to you." And Israel gathered his strength and sat up on the bed.
Jacob said to Joseph, "God Almighty appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan and blessed me,
"and he said to me, 'I am about to make you fruitful and multiply you, and I will make you into a company of peoples, and I will give this land to your offspring after you as a perpetual holding.'
"And now your two sons who were born to you in the land of Egypt before I came to you in Egypt are mine. Ephraim and Manasseh shall be mine, like Reuben and Simeon.
"But the offspring born to you after them shall be yours; they shall be called by the name of their brothers in their inheritance.

"As for me, when I came from Paddan, Rachel died beside me in the land of Canaan, on the way, while there was still some distance to go to Ephrath; and I buried her there on the way to Ephrath, that is Bethlehem."
When Israel saw Joseph's sons, he said, "Who are these?"
Joseph said to his father, "They are my sons, whom God has given me here." And he said, "Bring them to me, please, and I will bless them."
Now Israel's eyes were dim with age; he could not see. So Joseph brought them near to him, and he kissed them and embraced them.
Israel said to Joseph, "I never expected to see your face, and look — God has shown me your offspring too."
Then Joseph took them out from between his knees and bowed down with his face to the ground.
Joseph took the two of them, Ephraim in his right hand toward Israel's left, and Manasseh in his left hand toward Israel's right, and brought them near to him.
But Israel stretched out his right hand and laid it on the head of Ephraim, who was the younger, and his left hand on the head of Manasseh, crossing his hands; for Manasseh was the firstborn.
And he blessed Joseph and said: "The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, the God who has been my shepherd from my beginning until this day,

"the angel who redeems me from all harm — may he bless the boys. Let my name be called upon them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac, and let them teem into a multitude in the midst of the earth."
When Joseph saw that his father was laying his right hand on Ephraim's head, it displeased him, and he took hold of his father's hand to move it from Ephraim's head to Manasseh's head.
Joseph said to his father, "Not so, my father; this one is the firstborn. Put your right hand on his head."

But his father refused and said, "I know, my son, I know. He too shall become a people, and he too shall be great; but his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his offspring shall become a multitude of nations."
So he blessed them that day, saying, "By you Israel will pronounce blessing, saying, 'May God make you like Ephraim and like Manasseh.'" And he set Ephraim before Manasseh.
Then Israel said to Joseph, "I am about to die, but God will be with you and will bring you back to the land of your fathers.
"And to you I give one ridge of land more than to your brothers, which I took from the hand of the Amorites with my sword and my bow."

genesis_49.t: Then Jacob called his sons and said, "Gather round, and let me tell you what will happen to you in the days to come.
Assemble and hear, sons of Jacob; listen to Israel your father.
Reuben, you are my firstborn, my strength and the first of my vigour, surpassing in dignity, surpassing in power.
Reckless as water, you shall not excel, for you went up onto your father's bed; then you defiled it — he went up onto my couch.
Simeon and Levi are brothers; their swords are weapons of violence.
Let me not enter their council; let me not join their assembly — for in their anger they killed a man, and at their pleasure they hamstrung an ox.
Cursed be their anger, for it is fierce, and their wrath, for it is cruel. I will divide them in Jacob and scatter them in Israel.
Judah, your brothers shall praise you; your hand shall be on the neck of your enemies; your father's sons shall bow down to you.
Judah is a lion's cub; from the prey, my son, you have gone up. He crouched, he lay down like a lion, like a lioness — who dares rouse him?
The staff shall not depart from Judah, nor the ruler's rod from between his feet, until tribute comes to him, and to him shall be the obedience of peoples.
He ties his donkey to the vine, his donkey's colt to the choice vine; he washes his garments in wine, his robe in the blood of grapes.
His eyes are dark from wine, his teeth white from milk.
Zebulun shall dwell at the shore of the seas; he shall be a haven for ships, and his flank shall reach toward Sidon.
Issachar is a strong-boned donkey, lying down between the sheepfolds.
He saw that a resting place was good and that the land was pleasant; so he bent his shoulder to the burden and became a labouring serf.
Dan shall judge his people as one of the tribes of Israel.
Let Dan be a serpent on the road, a viper on the path, that bites the horse's heels so that its rider falls backward.
I wait for your deliverance, the LORD.
Gad — a raiding band shall raid him, but he shall raid at their heel.
Asher's bread shall be rich, and he shall provide a king's delicacies.
Naphtali is a doe let loose, that gives beautiful sayings.
Joseph is a fruitful bough, a fruitful bough by a spring; its branches run over a wall.
The archers dealt bitterly with him; they shot at him and harassed him.
But his bow remained firm, and his arms were made supple by the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob, from there, the Shepherd, the Stone of Israel,
from the God of your father, who will help you, and with the Almighty, who will bless you: blessings of the heavens above, blessings of the deep that lies beneath, blessings of breasts and womb.

The blessings of your father have prevailed over the blessings of my forebears, to the bounty of the ancient hills. May they rest on the head of Joseph, on the crown of the head of the nazir among his brothers.
Benjamin is a ravening wolf: in the morning he devours the prey, and at evening he divides the spoil.
All these are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is what their father said to them as he blessed them; he blessed each one with the blessing suited to him.
Then he charged them and said to them, "I am about to be gathered to my people. Bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite,
in the cave in the field of Machpelah, facing Mamre, in the land of Canaan — the field Abraham bought from Ephron the Hittite as a burial holding.
There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife; there they buried Isaac and Rebekah his wife; and there I buried Leah.
The field and the cave that is in it were purchased from the sons of Heth.
When Jacob had finished charging his sons, he drew his feet up into the bed, and he breathed his last and was gathered to his people.

genesis_50.t: Then Joseph fell on his father's face and wept over him and kissed him.
Joseph commanded his servants, the physicians, to embalm his father, and the physicians embalmed Israel.
Forty days were required for it, for that is the full time for embalming; and the Egyptians wept for him seventy days.
When the days of weeping for him had passed, Joseph spoke to the household of Pharaoh: "If I have found favour in your eyes, please speak in the ears of Pharaoh and say,

"'My father made me swear, saying, "I am about to die. In the grave I dug for myself in the land of Canaan, there you shall bury me." Now therefore let me go up and bury my father, and I will return.'"
Pharaoh said, "Go up and bury your father, as he made you swear."
So Joseph went up to bury his father, and with him went all the servants of Pharaoh, the elders of his household, and all the elders of the land of Egypt,
along with all Joseph's household, his brothers, and his father's household. Only their little ones and their flocks and herds they left behind in the land of Goshen.
Chariots and horsemen also went up with him, and it was a very great company.
They came to the threshing floor of Atad, which is across the Jordan, and there they made a great and very solemn lamentation; and he observed seven days of mourning for his father.

When the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, saw the mourning at the threshing floor of Atad, they said, "This is a solemn mourning for Egypt." Therefore it was named Abel-mizraim, which is across the Jordan.
So his sons did for him just as he had commanded them.
His sons carried him to the land of Canaan and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, the field Abraham had bought as a burial holding from Ephron the Hittite, facing Mamre.
Then Joseph returned to Egypt, he and his brothers and all who had gone up with him to bury his father, after he had buried his father.
When Joseph's brothers saw that their father was dead, they said, "What if Joseph bears a grudge against us and pays us back in full for all the harm we did him?"
So they sent a message to Joseph: "Your father gave a command before his death:

"'Say this to Joseph: Please forgive the transgression of your brothers and their sin, for they dealt you evil. And now forgive the transgression of the servants of the God of your father.'" And Joseph wept when they spoke to him.
Then his brothers also came and fell down before him and said, "Here we are, your slaves."
But Joseph said to them, "Do not be afraid. Am I in the place of God?"
"As for you, you devised evil against me, but God devised it for good, in order to bring about what has happened this day, to keep alive a numerous people.
"So now, do not be afraid. I myself will provide for you and your little ones." And he comforted them and spoke to their heart.
So Joseph dwelt in Egypt, he and his father's household, and Joseph lived a hundred and ten years.
Joseph saw Ephraim's children to the third generation; the sons of Machir the son of Manasseh were also born on Joseph's knees.
Then Joseph said to his brothers, "I am about to die, but God will surely attend to you and bring you up out of this land to the land he swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob."
And Joseph made the sons of Israel swear, saying, "God will surely attend to you, and you shall carry up my bones from here."
So Joseph died, a hundred and ten years old. They embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.

habakkuk_1.t: The oracle which Habakkuk the prophet saw.
How long, LORD, have I cried for help and you do not hear? I cry out to you, "Violence!" and you do not save.
Why do you make me see wickedness, and look on mischief? Devastation and violence are before me; there is strife, and contention rises up.
Therefore law grows numb, and justice never goes forth. For the wicked surrounds the righteous; therefore justice goes forth perverted.
Look among the nations and see, and be astounded, be astonished! For a work is being done in your days that you would not believe if it were told.
For look, I am raising up the Chaldeans, that bitter and impetuous nation, who march across the breadths of the earth to take possession of dwellings not their own.
Terrifying and dreadful it is; from itself its own justice and its own dignity go forth.
Its horses are swifter than leopards, keener than the wolves of the evening; its warhorses paw the ground. Its horsemen come from afar; they fly like an eagle hastening to devour.
All of it comes for violence; the set of their faces is eastward; it gathers captives like the sand.
It derides kings, and rulers are a laughing matter to it. It laughs at every fortress; it heaps up earth and captures it.
Then it sweeps on like a wind and passes over — and he becomes guilty, this one whose strength is his god.
Are you not from of old, LORD my God, my Holy One? We shall not die. LORD, you have appointed it for judgement; and Rock, you have established it for reproof.
You are too pure of eyes to see evil, and you are not able to look on mischief. Why then do you look on the treacherous, and keep silent when the wicked swallows one more righteous than he is?
And you make humankind like the fish of the sea, like creeping things that have no ruler over them.
All of it he brings up with a hook; he drags it away in his net and gathers it in his dragnet. Therefore he rejoices and is glad.
Therefore he sacrifices to his net and makes offerings smoke to his dragnet, for by them his portion is fat and his food rich.
Shall he therefore keep emptying his net, and go on killing nations without pity?

habakkuk_2.t: I will stand at my post and station myself on the rampart, and I will watch to see what he will say to me, and what I shall answer concerning my complaint.
And the LORD answered me and said: Write the vision down, and make it plain on the tablets, so that the one who reads it may run.
For the vision is still for the appointed time; it pants toward the end and does not lie. If it delays, wait for it, for it will surely come; it will not be late.
Look — his being is puffed up; it is not upright within him. But the righteous will live by his faithfulness.

And moreover, wine is treacherous; an arrogant man — and he does not rest; who has made his throat wide as Sheol, and like death he is never satisfied. He gathers to himself all the nations and assembles to himself all the peoples.
Shall not all of these lift up a saying against him, and a mocking song of riddles about him, and say: "Woe to him who multiplies what is not his — how long? — and loads himself with pledges!"
Will your creditors not suddenly rise, and those who make you tremble awake? And you will become plunder for them.
Because you have plundered many nations, all the rest of the peoples will plunder you — because of human blood and violence done to the land, to the town and all who dwell in it.
Woe to him who gains an evil gain for his house, to set his nest on high, to be delivered from the hand of harm!
You have planned shame for your house, cutting off many peoples, and sinning against your own being.
For a stone will cry out from the wall, and a rafter from the woodwork will answer it.
Woe to him who builds a city with blood, and founds a town with injustice!
Is it not — look! — from the LORD of hosts that peoples labour only for fire, and nations weary themselves for nothing?
For the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD, as the waters cover the sea.
Woe to him who makes his neighbour drink — you who pour out your rage and make them drunk as well — so as to look on their nakedness!
You are sated with shame rather than glory. Drink, you also, and be uncircumcised! The cup of the LORD's right hand will come round to you, and disgrace upon your glory.
For the violence done to Lebanon will cover you, and the devastation of the animals will terrify them — because of human blood and violence done to the land, to the town and all who dwell in it.

What profit is a carved image, that its maker has carved it — a molten image, a teacher of falsehood — that the one who formed it trusts in what he himself formed, making worthless idols that cannot speak?
Woe to him who says to the wood, "Wake up!" — "Awake!" to a silent stone. Can it teach? Look, it is overlaid with gold and silver, and there is no breath at all within it.
But the LORD is in his holy temple. Hush before him, all the earth!

habakkuk_3.t: A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, on shigionoth.
LORD, I have heard the report of you, and I was afraid. LORD, your work — in the midst of the years revive it; in the midst of the years make it known. In wrath remember to have compassion.
God comes from Teman, and the Holy One from Mount Paran. Selah. His splendour has covered the heavens, and his praise has filled the earth.
And the brightness is like the light; rays come from his hand; and there is the hiding place of his strength.
Before him goes pestilence, and a flame goes out at his feet.
He stood and shook the earth; he looked and made the nations start. The ancient mountains were shattered; the everlasting hills bowed down. The everlasting ways are his.
In trouble I saw the tents of Cushan; the curtains of the land of Midian tremble.
Was the LORD angry with the rivers? Was your anger against the rivers, or your fury against the sea, that you ride on your horses, your chariots of salvation?
Your bow is stripped utterly bare; oaths of arrows — a word. Selah. With rivers you split the earth.
The mountains saw you and writhed. A downpour of water passed over. The deep gave its voice; it lifted its hands on high.
Sun and moon — it stood still in its lofty abode at the light of your arrows as they went, at the brightness of the flash of your spear.
In indignation you marched through the earth; in anger you trampled down nations.
You went out for the salvation of your people, for the salvation of your anointed. You shattered the head from the house of the wicked, laying it bare from foundation to neck. Selah.
You pierced with his own arrows the head of his warriors, who storm out to scatter me. Their exultation was like devouring the afflicted in secret.
You trod on the sea with your horses, the heaping of many waters.

I heard, and my belly trembled; at the sound my lips quivered. Rottenness entered my bones, and I trembled where I stood — that I must wait quietly for the day of distress, for the coming up against the people who attack us.

Though the fig tree does not blossom, and there is no produce on the vines; though the yield of the olive fails, and the fields produce no food; though the flock is cut off from the fold, and there is no cattle in the stalls —
yet I will exult in the LORD; I will rejoice in the God of my salvation.
GOD the Lord is my strength. He makes my feet like the feet of does, and he makes me tread on my high places. To the choirmaster, with my stringed instruments.

haggai_1.t: In the second year of Darius the king, in the sixth month, on the first day of the month, the word of the LORD came by the hand of Haggai the prophet to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest:
Thus says the LORD of hosts: This people say, 'The time has not come, the time for the house of the LORD to be built.'
Then the word of the LORD came by the hand of Haggai the prophet:
Is it a time for you yourselves to live in your panelled houses, while this house lies desolate?
And now, thus says the LORD of hosts: Set your heart on your ways.

You have sown much and brought in little; you eat, and are not satisfied; you drink, and are not filled; you clothe yourselves, and no one is warm; and the one who earns wages earns wages into a bag with holes in it.
Thus says the LORD of hosts: Set your heart on your ways.
Go up to the hill country, bring wood, and build the house; and I will take pleasure in it and be honoured, says the LORD.

You looked for much, and it came to little; and when you brought it home, I blew it away. Why? declares the LORD of hosts. Because of my house, which lies desolate, while each of you runs to his own house.
Therefore over you the heavens have withheld their dew, and the land has withheld its produce.

And I summoned a drought on the land and on the mountains, on the grain, the new wine and the fresh oil, on what the ground brings forth, on humankind and on the livestock, and on all the toil of your hands.

Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, and Joshua son of Jehozadak the high priest, and all the remnant of the people, listened to the voice of the LORD their God and to the words of Haggai the prophet, as the LORD their God had sent him; and the people feared before the LORD.
Then Haggai, the messenger of the LORD, spoke to the people with the LORD's message: I am with you, declares the LORD.

And the LORD stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and the spirit of Joshua son of Jehozadak the high priest, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people; and they came and did work on the house of the LORD of hosts their God,
on the twenty-fourth day of the month, in the sixth month, in the second year of Darius the king.

haggai_2.t: In the seventh month, on the twenty-first day of the month, the word of the LORD came by the hand of Haggai the prophet:
Say now to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak the high priest, and to the remnant of the people:
Who is left among you who saw this house in its former glory? And how do you see it now? Is it not as nothing in your eyes?

And now, be strong, Zerubbabel, declares the LORD; be strong, Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest; be strong, all you people of the land, declares the LORD; and work. For I am with you, declares the LORD of hosts.
The word that I cut with you when you came out of Egypt — and my spirit stands in your midst. Do not be afraid.
For thus says the LORD of hosts: Once more, in a little while, I am going to shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land.
And I will shake all the nations, and the treasures of all the nations will come, and I will fill this house with glory, says the LORD of hosts.
The silver is mine and the gold is mine, declares the LORD of hosts.
The latter glory of this house will be greater than the former, says the LORD of hosts; and in this place I will give peace, declares the LORD of hosts.
On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to Haggai the prophet:
Thus says the LORD of hosts: Ask the priests about the law:
Suppose a man carries holy flesh in the skirt of his garment, and with his skirt touches bread, or cooked food, or wine, or oil, or any food: does it become holy? And the priests answered, No.
Then Haggai said: If someone unclean by a corpse touches any of these, does it become unclean? And the priests answered, It becomes unclean.
Then Haggai answered: So is this people, and so is this nation before me, declares the LORD; and so is every work of their hands; and what they offer there is unclean.
And now, set your heart, from this day onward: before stone was laid on stone in the temple of the LORD —
from what you were then: someone came to a heap of twenty measures, and there were ten; someone came to the wine vat to draw off fifty, and there were twenty.
I struck you with blight and mildew and hail — all the work of your hands — and you did not turn to me, declares the LORD.
Set your heart, from this day onward: from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, from the day the temple of the LORD was founded — set your heart.
Is the seed still in the granary? Even the vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate and the olive tree have not borne fruit. From this day on I will bless.
And the word of the LORD came a second time to Haggai, on the twenty-fourth day of the month:
Say to Zerubbabel, governor of Judah: I am going to shake the heavens and the earth,

and I will overthrow the throne of kingdoms and destroy the strength of the kingdoms of the nations; and I will overthrow chariotry and its riders, and horses and their riders will go down, each by the sword of his brother.

On that day, declares the LORD of hosts, I will take you, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, my servant, declares the LORD; and I will make you like a signet ring, for I have chosen you, declares the LORD of hosts.

hosea_1.t: The word of the LORD that came to Hosea son of Beeri, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel.

The beginning of the LORD's speaking through Hosea. The LORD said to Hosea, "Go, take for yourself a wife of prostitution and children of prostitution, for the land is utterly prostituting itself away from the LORD."
So he went and took Gomer daughter of Diblaim, and she conceived and bore him a son.
And the LORD said to him, "Call his name Jezreel, for in a little while I will visit the bloodshed of Jezreel on the house of Jehu, and I will put an end to the kingdom of the house of Israel.
On that day I will break the bow of Israel in the valley of Jezreel."
She conceived again and bore a daughter. And he said to him, "Call her name Lo-ruhamah, for I will no longer have compassion on the house of Israel, that I should forgive them at all.
But on the house of Judah I will have compassion, and I will save them by the LORD their God; I will not save them by bow or sword or battle, by horses or horsemen."
When she had weaned Lo-ruhamah, she conceived and bore a son.
And he said, "Call his name Lo-ammi, for you are not my people, and I will not be your God."

Yet the number of the people of Israel will be like the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured and cannot be counted. And in the place where it was said to them, "You are not my people," it will be said to them, "Children of the living God."
And the people of Judah and the people of Israel will be gathered together, and they will appoint for themselves one head, and they will go up from the land; for great will be the day of Jezreel.

hosea_2.t: Say to your brothers, "Ammi," and to your sisters, "Ruhamah."
Bring a case against your mother, bring a case, for she is not my wife and I am not her husband — and let her put away her prostitutions from her face and her adulteries from between her breasts,
lest I strip her naked and set her out as on the day she was born, and make her like the wilderness, and set her like a parched land, and kill her with thirst.
And on her children I will not have compassion, for they are children of prostitution.

For their mother has prostituted herself; she who conceived them has acted shamefully. For she said, "Let me go after my lovers, who give me my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, my oil and my drink."
Therefore I am about to hedge up your way with thorns, and I will wall up her wall, so that she will not find her paths.
She will pursue her lovers and not overtake them; she will seek them and not find them. And she will say, "Let me go and return to my first husband, for it was better for me then than now."
She did not know that it was I who gave her the grain and the new wine and the fresh oil, and that I lavished silver on her, and gold, which they made into the Baal.
Therefore I will take back my grain in its time and my new wine in its appointed time, and I will snatch away my wool and my flax, which were to cover her nakedness.
And now I will uncover her lewdness before the eyes of her lovers, and no one will deliver her from my hand.
And I will put an end to all her rejoicing: her festival, her new moon, her sabbath, and all her appointed feasts.
And I will lay waste her vine and her fig tree, of which she said, "These are my fee, which my lovers gave me." I will turn them into a thicket, and the wild animals of the field will devour them.

And I will visit on her the days of the Baals, when she made offerings smoke to them and adorned herself with her ring and her jewellery and went after her lovers — and me she forgot. Declaration of the LORD.
Therefore I am about to allure her; I will lead her into the wilderness and speak to her heart.
And from there I will give her her vineyards, and the valley of Achor as a door of hope. And she will answer there as in the days of her youth, as on the day she came up from the land of Egypt.
And on that day — declaration of the LORD — you will call me "My husband," and you will no longer call me "My baal."
And I will remove the names of the Baals from her mouth, and they will no longer be invoked by name.

And on that day I will cut a covenant for them with the wild animals of the field, the birds of the heavens, and the creeping things of the ground; and bow and sword and battle I will break from the land, and I will make them lie down in security.
And I will betroth you to myself for ever; I will betroth you to myself in righteousness and in justice, in steadfast love and in compassion.
And I will betroth you to myself in faithfulness, and you will know the LORD.
And on that day I will answer — declaration of the LORD — I will answer the heavens, and they will answer the earth,
and the earth will answer the grain and the new wine and the fresh oil, and they will answer Jezreel.
And I will sow her for myself in the land, and I will have compassion on Lo-ruhamah, and I will say to Lo-ammi, "You are my people," and he will say, "My God."

hosea_3.t: And the LORD said to me, "Go again, love a woman who is loved by a companion and commits adultery — as the LORD loves the people of Israel, though they turn to other gods and love cakes of raisins."
So I bought her for myself for fifteen pieces of silver and a homer of barley and a lethech of barley.
And I said to her, "Many days you are to remain for me; you are not to prostitute yourself and not to belong to a man — and I also will be toward you."
For many days the people of Israel will remain without king or prince, without sacrifice or pillar, without ephod or teraphim.
Afterwards the people of Israel will return and seek the LORD their God and David their king, and they will come in dread to the LORD and to his goodness at the end of the days.

hosea_4.t: Hear the word of the LORD, people of Israel, for the LORD has a case against the inhabitants of the land: there is no faithfulness and no steadfast love and no knowledge of God in the land.
Cursing, deceiving, murdering, stealing, committing adultery — they have broken out, and bloodshed touches bloodshed.
Therefore the land mourns, and all who dwell in it wither, along with the wild animals of the field and the birds of the heavens; and even the fish of the sea are swept away.
Yet let no one bring a case, and let no one reprove, for your people are like those who contend with a priest.
You will stumble by day, and a prophet will stumble with you by night; and I will destroy your mother.

My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I reject you from serving me as a priest; and because you have forgotten the law of your God, I also will forget your children.
The more they increased, the more they sinned against me; I will exchange their glory for shame.
They feed on the sin offering of my people, and to their iniquity they lift up their appetite.
And it will be: as the people, so the priest. I will visit his ways on him and repay him his deeds.
They will eat and not be satisfied; they will prostitute themselves and not increase, for they have abandoned the LORD, to keep —
Prostitution and wine and new wine take away the heart.
My people enquire of a piece of wood, and their stick tells them, for a spirit of prostitution has led them astray, and they have prostituted themselves out from under their God.

On the tops of the mountains they sacrifice, and on the hills they make offerings smoke, under oak and poplar and terebinth, because their shade is good. Therefore your daughters prostitute themselves and your brides commit adultery.

I will not visit judgement on your daughters when they prostitute themselves, nor on your brides when they commit adultery, for the men themselves go apart with the prostitutes and sacrifice with the shrine prostitutes. And a people that does not understand comes to ruin.
Though you prostitute yourself, Israel, let Judah not become guilty. Do not go to Gilgal, do not go up to Beth-aven, and do not swear, "As the LORD lives."
For Israel is stubborn like a stubborn heifer. Will the LORD now pasture them like a lamb in an open meadow?
Ephraim is joined to idols. Let him alone.
Their drink is gone; they have utterly prostituted themselves. Her shields dearly love shame.
A wind has wrapped her in its wings, and they will be ashamed because of their sacrifices.

hosea_5.t: Hear this, priests; pay attention, house of Israel; give ear, house of the king, for the sentence falls on you: you have been a trap at Mizpah and a net spread over Tabor.
And in slaughtering, rebels have gone deep; and I am a discipline to all of them.
