From the edge of the earth we have heard songs: 'Glory to the righteous one!' And I said: I waste away, I waste away! Alas for me! The treacherous act treacherously; with treachery the treacherous act treacherously.
Dread and pit and snare are upon you, inhabitant of the earth!

And whoever flees from the sound of the dread will fall into the pit, and whoever comes up from the midst of the pit will be caught in the snare; for the windows on high are opened, and the foundations of the earth shake.
The earth is utterly broken; the earth is torn apart; the earth is violently shaken.
The earth staggers wildly like a drunkard; it sways like a shelter; its transgression is heavy upon it, and it falls and will not rise again.
And it will be in that day that the LORD will visit the host of the height on high, and the kings of the earth on the earth.
And they will be gathered together, prisoners gathered to a pit, and shut up in a prison; and after many days they will be punished.
And the moon will be abashed and the sun ashamed; for the LORD of hosts reigns on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, and before his elders — glory.

isaiah_25.t: LORD, you are my God; I will exalt you, I will give thanks to your name, for you have done a wonder — plans from long ago, in perfect faithfulness.
For you have made a city into a heap, a fortified town into a ruin; the fortress of strangers is no longer a city; it will never be rebuilt.
Therefore a strong people will honour you; the town of ruthless nations will fear you.

For you have been a refuge for the weak, a refuge for the needy in his distress, a shelter from the rainstorm, a shade from the heat; for the breath of the ruthless is like a rainstorm against a wall.
Like heat in a dry land you subdue the uproar of strangers; as heat is subdued by the shade of a cloud, so the song of the ruthless is quietened.
And on this mountain the LORD of hosts will make for all the peoples a feast of rich food, a feast of old wines, rich food full of marrow, old wines distilled.
And on this mountain he will swallow up the covering that covers all the peoples, and the veil that is woven over all the nations.
He will swallow up death for ever; and the Lord GOD will wipe the tears from every face, and the reproach of his people he will remove from all the earth — for the LORD has spoken.
And it will be said in that day: Look — this is our God; we waited for him, and he delivered us. This is the LORD; we waited for him. Let us be glad and rejoice in his deliverance.
For the hand of the LORD will rest on this mountain; and Moab will be trampled down where it stands, as straw is trampled down in a dung pit.
And he will spread out his hands in the midst of it as a swimmer spreads them out to swim; and the LORD will bring low his haughtiness together with the trickery of his hands.
And the high fortification of your walls he will lay low; he will bring it low, he will bring it down to the ground, to the dust.

isaiah_26.t: In that day this song will be sung in the land of Judah: We have a strong city; he sets deliverance as walls and rampart.
Open the gates, that a righteous nation may enter, one that keeps faith.
The firm of mind you keep in peace, perfect peace, because he trusts in you.
Trust in the LORD for ever, for in the LORD, the LORD, is an everlasting Rock.
For he has laid low those who dwell on high, the town set on high; he brings it low, he brings it low to the ground, he brings it down to the dust.
A foot will trample it — the feet of the poor, the footsteps of the weak.
The path of the righteous is level; upright one, you make level the track of the righteous.
Also in the path of your judgements, LORD, we have waited for you; your name and your remembrance are what the whole being desires.
My whole being has desired you in the night; yes, my spirit within me seeks you at dawn. For when your judgements are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness.
If the wicked is shown favour, he does not learn righteousness; in a land of uprightness he acts unjustly, and does not see the majesty of the LORD.
LORD, your hand is raised, and they do not see it. Let them see and be ashamed of your zeal for your people; let the fire meant for your adversaries consume them.
LORD, you will establish peace for us; for even all our works you have done for us.
LORD our God, lords other than you have ruled over us; by you alone do we make mention of your name.
The dead will not live; the departed spirits will not rise. Therefore you have visited and destroyed them, and made all remembrance of them perish.
You have added to the nation, LORD; you have added to the nation, you have gained glory; you have extended all the boundaries of the land.
LORD, in distress they sought you; they poured out a whispered prayer when your chastening was on them.
As a pregnant woman drawing near to give birth writhes and cries out in her labour pains, so were we before you, LORD.
We were pregnant, we writhed — it was as if we gave birth to wind. We have accomplished no deliverance in the earth, and the inhabitants of the world have not fallen.
Your dead will live; my corpses will rise. Awake and shout for joy, you who dwell in the dust! For your dew is a dew of lights, and the earth will give birth to the departed spirits.
Go, my people, enter your rooms and shut your door behind you; hide for a little moment until the indignation passes by.

For look — the LORD is going out from his place to visit the iniquity of the inhabitants of the earth upon them; and the earth will disclose the blood shed on her and will no longer cover over her slain.

isaiah_27.t: In that day the LORD will visit, with his fierce and great and mighty sword, Leviathan the fleeing serpent, and Leviathan the twisting serpent; and he will slay the sea monster that is in the sea.
In that day: A delightful vineyard — sing of it!
I, the LORD, am its keeper; every moment I water it. So that no one may injure it, night and day I guard it.
I have no rage. If only there were thorns and briars against me in battle! I would march against them, I would burn them altogether.
Or else let him take hold of my protection; let him make peace with me; let him make peace with me.
In the days to come Jacob will take root; Israel will blossom and bud, and they will fill the face of the world with fruit.
Has he struck him as he struck the one who struck him? Or has he been slain as those he slew were slain?
By banishing, by sending her away, you contended with her; he drove her out with his fierce wind on the day of the east wind.

Therefore by this the iniquity of Jacob will be atoned for, and this is the whole fruit of the removing of his sin: when he makes all the stones of the altar like pulverised chalkstones, no asherahs or incense altars will stand.
For the fortified city stands alone, a habitation deserted and forsaken like the wilderness. There a calf will graze, and there it will lie down and strip its branches bare.

When its branches dry up they are broken off; women come and set light to them. For it is not a people of understanding; therefore the one who made it will not have compassion on it, and the one who formed it will not show it favour.
And it will be in that day that the LORD will beat out the grain from the flowing stream of the River to the Wadi of Egypt; and you will be gathered one by one, Israelites.

And it will be in that day that a great ram's horn will be blown; and those lost in the land of Assyria will come, and the outcasts in the land of Egypt; and they will bow down to the LORD on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.

isaiah_28.t: Woe — the proud crown of the drunkards of Ephraim, and the withering flower of its glorious beauty, which is on the head of the fertile valley, of those struck down with wine!
Look — the Lord has one mighty and strong; like a storm of hail, a tempest of destruction, like a storm of mighty overflowing waters, he will thrust it down to the ground with his hand.
It will be trampled underfoot — the proud crown of the drunkards of Ephraim.

And the withering flower of its glorious beauty, which is on the head of the fertile valley, will be like an early fig before summer: whoever sees it, as soon as he sees it, swallows it while it is still in his hand.
In that day the LORD of hosts will become a crown of beauty and a diadem of splendour for the remnant of his people,
and a spirit of justice for the one who sits in judgement, and might for those who turn back the battle at the gate.

And these too reel with wine and stagger with strong drink: priest and prophet reel with strong drink, they are confused by wine, they stagger from strong drink; they reel in vision, they totter in giving judgement.
For all the tables are full of vomit and filth, with no room left.
Whom will he teach knowledge? And to whom will he explain the message? Those just weaned from milk, just taken from the breast?
For it is 'command upon command, command upon command, line upon line, line upon line, a little here, a little there.'
For with stammering lips and a foreign tongue he will speak to this people —
he who said to them: This is the resting place — give rest to the weary; and this is the place of repose. But they were not willing to listen.

And the word of the LORD will be to them 'command upon command, command upon command, line upon line, line upon line, a little here, a little there' — so that they may go and stumble backward and be broken, and be ensnared and captured.
Therefore hear the word of the LORD, you mockers, rulers of this people who are in Jerusalem.

Because you have said: We have cut a covenant with death, and with Sheol we have made an agreement. The overflowing scourge, when it passes through, will not reach us, for we have made falsehood our refuge and hidden ourselves in deception.
Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Look — I am laying in Zion a stone, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation. The one who trusts will not be in haste.
And I will make justice the measuring-line and righteousness the plummet; and hail will sweep away the refuge of falsehood, and waters will overflow the hiding place.
And your covenant with death will be annulled, and your agreement with Sheol will not stand. When the overflowing scourge passes through, you will become a trampling ground for it.
As often as it passes through it will take you; for morning by morning it will pass through, by day and by night. And it will be sheer terror to understand the message.
For the bed is too short to stretch out on, and the blanket too narrow to wrap oneself in.
For the LORD will rise as at Mount Perazim; he will rage as in the valley at Gibeon, to do his deed — strange is his deed — and to work his work — alien is his work.
And now, do not mock, or your fetters will be made strong; for I have heard of a complete destruction, one decreed, from the Lord GOD of hosts against all the land.
Give ear and hear my voice; pay attention and hear my speech.
Does the ploughman plough all day to sow? Does he keep loosening and harrowing his ground?
Does he not, when he has levelled its surface, scatter black cumin and sprinkle cumin, and set wheat in rows and barley in its place and spelt at its border?
And he instructs him in the right way; his God teaches him.
For black cumin is not threshed with a threshing sledge, nor is a cart wheel rolled over cumin; but black cumin is beaten out with a staff, and cumin with a rod.
Grain for bread is crushed; but he does not go on threshing it for ever. He drives the wheel of his cart and his horses over it, but he does not crush it to powder.
This too comes from the LORD of hosts: he has made his counsel wonderful, he has made sound wisdom great.

isaiah_29.t: Woe — Ariel, Ariel, the town where David encamped! Add year to year; let the festivals go round.
And I will bring distress on Ariel, and there will be mourning and lamentation; and she will be to me like an Ariel.
And I will encamp against you all round, and lay siege against you with siege-works, and raise fortifications against you.

And you will be brought low; from the ground you will speak, and from the dust your speech will be humbled. And your voice will be like a ghost's from the ground, and from the dust your speech will whisper.
And the multitude of your strangers will be like fine dust, and the multitude of the ruthless like passing chaff; and it will happen in an instant, suddenly.
From the LORD of hosts she will be visited, with thunder and earthquake and a great noise, storm and tempest and the flame of a devouring fire.
And the multitude of all the nations who wage war against Ariel will be like a dream, a vision of the night — all who wage war against her and her stronghold, and those who bring distress on her.

And it will be as when a hungry man dreams that he is eating, and he awakes and his being is empty; and as when a thirsty man dreams that he is drinking, and he awakes and there he is, faint, his throat still longing: so will be the multitude of all the nations who wage war against Mount Zion.
Linger and be astounded! Blind yourselves and be blind! They are drunk, but not with wine; they stagger, but not with strong drink.
For the LORD has poured out on you a spirit of deep sleep; he has shut your eyes — the prophets — and covered your heads — the seers.
And the whole vision has become for you like the words of a sealed scroll, which people hand to one who can read, saying: Read this, please. And he says: I cannot, for it is sealed.
And the scroll is given to one who cannot read, saying: Read this, please. And he says: I cannot read.
And the Lord said: Because this people draws near with its mouth and honours me with its lips, while its heart is far from me, and their fear of me has become a commandment of men, learned by rote —
therefore, look — I will again deal wonderfully with this people, wonder upon wonder; and the wisdom of its wise men will perish, and the understanding of its discerning men will hide itself.
Woe to those who go deep to hide a plan from the LORD, whose deeds are in a dark place, and who say: Who sees us? Who knows us?

How you turn things upside down! Shall the potter be reckoned as the clay, that a thing made should say of its maker: He did not make me, and a thing formed say of the one who formed it: He has no understanding?
Is it not yet a very little while until Lebanon turns into an orchard, and the orchard is reckoned as a forest?
And in that day the deaf will hear the words of a scroll, and out of gloom and out of darkness the eyes of the blind will see.
And the humble will have joy upon joy in the LORD, and the neediest of humankind will be glad in the Holy One of Israel.
For the ruthless will come to an end and the mocker be finished, and all who lie in wait to do wrong will be cut off —
those who make a person out to be guilty by a word, and lay a trap for the one who arbitrates in the gate, and turn the righteous aside with an empty case.
Therefore thus says the LORD to the house of Jacob, he who ransomed Abraham: Jacob will not now be ashamed, and his face will not now grow pale.
For when he sees his children, the work of my hands, in his midst, they will regard my name as holy; they will regard as holy the Holy One of Jacob, and will hold the God of Israel in awe.
And those who go astray in spirit will come to understanding, and murmurers will learn instruction.

isaiah_30.t: Woe to stubborn children — declares the LORD — who carry out a plan, but not from me, and pour out a libation, but not of my spirit, so as to add sin to sin;
who set out to go down to Egypt but have not consulted my mouth, to take refuge in the refuge of Pharaoh and to seek shelter in the shadow of Egypt.
And the refuge of Pharaoh will become your shame, and the shelter in the shadow of Egypt your ignominy.
For his officials have been in Zoan, and his messengers have reached Hanes.
All are put to shame over a people who bring them no profit, no help and no profit, but shame and reproach.

The oracle concerning the animals of the Negeb. Through a land of trouble and distress, of lioness and lion, viper and flying serpent, they carry their wealth on the shoulders of donkeys and their treasures on the humps of camels, to a people who bring no profit.
And Egypt — its help is futility and emptiness. Therefore I have called her Rahab Who Sits Still.
Now go, write it on a tablet before them, and inscribe it on a scroll, that it may be for a later day, for ever, to eternity.
For they are a people of rebellion, lying children, children who have not been willing to hear the law of the LORD;
who say to the seers: Do not see; and to the visionaries: Do not give us visions of what is right. Speak smooth things to us; give us visions of illusion.
Turn aside from the way; turn away from the path; make the Holy One of Israel cease from before us!
Therefore thus says the Holy One of Israel: Because you have rejected this word and have trusted in oppression and crookedness and leaned on them,
therefore this iniquity will be to you like a breach about to fall, a bulge in a high wall, whose collapse comes suddenly, in an instant.
And it will be broken like a potter's jar, smashed without pity, so that among its fragments not a sherd will be found to carry fire from a hearth or to scoop water from a cistern.
For thus says the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel: In returning and rest you will be delivered; in quietness and in trust will be your might. But you were not willing.
And you said: No — we will flee on horses! Therefore you will flee. And: We will ride on swift ones! Therefore your pursuers will be swift.
A thousand will flee at the threat of one; at the threat of five you will flee, until you are left like a flagstaff on a mountain top and like a standard on a hill.
And therefore the LORD waits to show you favour, and therefore he rises up to have compassion on you; for the LORD is a God of justice. How blessed are all who wait for him!
For a people will dwell in Zion, in Jerusalem. You will weep no more. He will surely show you favour at the sound of your crying out; when he hears it, he will answer you.
And the Lord will give you the bread of distress and the water of oppression; but your Teacher will no longer hide himself, and your eyes will see your Teacher.
And your ears will hear a word behind you, saying: This is the way; walk in it — whenever you turn to the right or to the left.
And you will make unclean the plating of your silver images and the sheathing of your molten image of gold. You will throw them away like a menstrual rag; you will say to it: Filth!
And he will give rain for the seed with which you sow the ground, and bread, the produce of the ground, will be rich and fat; in that day your livestock will graze in a broad pasture.
And the cattle and the donkeys that work the ground will eat salted fodder, winnowed with shovel and pitchfork.
And on every high mountain and on every lifted hill there will be streams, watercourses of water, on the day of great slaughter, when the towers fall.

And the light of the moon will be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun will be sevenfold, like the light of seven days, on the day the LORD binds up the fracture of his people and heals the wound of his blow.
Look — the name of the LORD comes from afar, his anger burning, and in thick rising smoke; his lips are full of indignation, and his tongue is like a devouring fire.
And his breath is like an overflowing torrent that reaches up to the neck, to sift the nations in a sieve of destruction, and a bridle that leads astray is on the jaws of the peoples.
You will have a song as on a night when a festival is consecrated, and gladness of heart as when one walks to the flute to go to the mountain of the LORD, to the Rock of Israel.
And the LORD will make the grandeur of his voice heard, and will show his arm descending in raging anger and the flame of a devouring fire, in driving storm and rainstorm and hailstones.
For at the voice of the LORD Assyria will be shattered; he will strike with the rod.
And every stroke of the appointed staff that the LORD lays on it will be to the sound of tambourines and lyres; and with brandishing battles he will fight against them.

For a place of burning has long been arranged; it too has been prepared for the king. He has made it deep and wide; its pyre is fire and much wood. The breath of the LORD, like a torrent of sulphur, sets it ablaze.

isaiah_31.t: Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help and lean on horses, and trust in chariotry because it is many and in horsemen because they are exceedingly numerous; but they do not look to the Holy One of Israel and do not seek the LORD.
But he too is wise, and he has brought disaster; and he has not turned aside his words. He will rise against the house of evildoers and against the help of those who do wrong.

And Egypt is human and not God, and their horses are flesh and not spirit. And the LORD will stretch out his hand, and the helper will stumble and the helped will fall, and together all of them will come to an end.

For thus the LORD said to me: As a lion growls, a young lion over its prey, when a whole band of shepherds is called out against it — at their voice it is not dismayed, and at their tumult it does not cringe — so the LORD of hosts will come down to wage war on Mount Zion and on its hill.
Like birds hovering, so the LORD of hosts will shield Jerusalem; shielding and rescuing, passing over and bringing to safety.
Return to him from whom you have so deeply turned away, Israelites!
For in that day everyone will reject his idols of silver and his idols of gold, which your own hands have made for you as sin.
And Assyria will fall by a sword that is not a man's, and a sword that is not humankind's will devour it; and it will flee before the sword, and its young men will be put to forced labour.
And its rock will pass away in terror, and its commanders will be dismayed at a standard — declares the LORD, whose fire is in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem.

isaiah_32.t: Look — a king will reign for righteousness, and officials will rule for justice.
And each will be like a hiding place from the wind and a shelter from the rainstorm, like streams of water in a dry land, like the shadow of a great rock in a weary land.
And the eyes of those who see will not be closed, and the ears of those who hear will pay attention.
And the heart of the rash will come to understand knowledge, and the tongue of stammerers will speak readily and clearly.
A fool will no longer be called noble, and a scoundrel will not be called eminent.
For a fool speaks folly, and his heart does wrong: practising godlessness, and speaking error about the LORD, leaving the being of the hungry empty, and depriving the thirsty of drink.
And a scoundrel — his weapons are evil; he plans wicked schemes, to ruin the poor with sayings of falsehood even when the needy speaks what is just.
But a noble plans noble things, and on noble things he stands.
Carefree women, rise up, hear my voice! Confident daughters, give ear to my speech!
In little more than a year you will be agitated, you confident ones; for the grape harvest will fail, the gathering will not come.
Tremble, you carefree ones! Be agitated, you confident ones! Strip off and make yourselves bare, and gird sackcloth on your loins!
Beating your breasts for the fields of delight, for the fruitful vine —
on the ground of my people, where briars and thorns come up; yes, on all the houses of gaiety in the jubilant town.
For the palace will be forsaken, the tumult of the city abandoned; the hill and the watchtower will become bare places for ever, a delight of wild donkeys, a pasture of flocks —
until a spirit is poured out on us from on high, and the wilderness becomes an orchard, and the orchard is reckoned a forest.
And justice will dwell in the wilderness, and righteousness will remain in the orchard.
And the work of righteousness will be peace, and the labour of righteousness, quietness and security for ever.
And my people will dwell in a habitation of peace, in dwelling places of security, in undisturbed resting places.
And it will hail when the forest comes down, and the city will be brought utterly low.
How blessed are you who sow beside every water, who let the ox and the donkey range free!

isaiah_33.t: Woe, destroyer, and you yourself not destroyed; traitor, and no one has dealt treacherously with you! When you have finished destroying, you will be destroyed; when you have done with dealing treacherously, they will deal treacherously with you.
LORD, show us favour; for you we have waited. Be their arm every morning, and our deliverance in a time of distress.
At the sound of tumult peoples flee; at your rising, nations scatter.
And your plunder will be gathered as the locust gathers; as locusts rush, so they will rush upon it.
The LORD is exalted, for he dwells on high; he fills Zion with justice and righteousness.
And he will be the trustworthiness of your times, a wealth of deliverance, wisdom and knowledge; the fear of the LORD — that is his treasure.
Look — their valiant ones cry out in the streets; the messengers of peace weep bitterly.
The highways are desolate; the traveller on the road has ceased. A covenant has been broken, cities rejected; no human being has been valued.
The land dries up and languishes; Lebanon is shamed and withers; Sharon has become like the desert plain, and Bashan and Carmel shake off their leaves.
Now I will arise, says the LORD; now I will exalt myself; now I will lift myself up.
You conceive dry grass; you give birth to stubble. Your own breath is a fire that will consume you.
And peoples will be burnings of lime, thorns cut down and kindled in the fire.
Hear, you who are far off, what I have done; and know, you who are near, my might.
Sinners in Zion are in dread; trembling has seized the godless: Who among us can live with a devouring fire? Who among us can live with everlasting hearths?

The one who walks in righteousness and speaks uprightly, who rejects the gain of extortion, who shakes his hands free from taking hold of a bribe, who stops his ear against hearing of bloodshed and shuts his eyes against looking on evil —
he will dwell on the heights; the strongholds of the rocks will be his refuge; his bread will be given him, his water sure.
Your eyes will behold a king in his beauty; they will see a land stretching far away.
Your heart will muse on the terror: Where is the one who counted? Where is the one who weighed? Where is the one who counted the towers?
You will not see the barbarous people, a people whose speech is too obscure to hear, stammering of tongue, without understanding.

Look on Zion, the town of our appointed times! Your eyes will see Jerusalem, an undisturbed habitation, a tent that will not be struck, whose tent pegs will never be pulled out, and none of whose ropes will be torn apart.
But there the majestic LORD will be for us a place of rivers, of broad canals, where no rowing ship will go and no majestic vessel will pass.
For the LORD is our judge; the LORD is our lawgiver; the LORD is our king — he will deliver us.
Your ropes hang loose; they do not hold the base of the mast firm; they have not spread out the sail. Then abundant booty of plunder will be divided; the lame will take spoil.
And no inhabitant will say: I am sick. The people who dwell in her will be forgiven their iniquity.

isaiah_34.t: Draw near, nations, to hear; and peoples, pay attention! Let the earth hear, and all that fills it, the world and all that comes from it.
For the LORD has wrath against all the nations and rage against all their host; he has devoted them to destruction, given them over to slaughter.
And their slain will be thrown out, and the stench of their corpses will go up, and the mountains will melt with their blood.

And all the host of the heavens will rot away, and the heavens will be rolled up like a scroll; and all their host will wither as the leaves wither from a vine, and like withered fruit from a fig tree.
For my sword has drunk its fill in the heavens. Look — it will come down on Edom, and on the people I have devoted to destruction, for judgement.

The LORD has a sword; it is full of blood, it is gorged with fat — with the blood of lambs and goats, with the fat of the kidneys of rams. For the LORD has a sacrifice in Bozrah, and a great slaughter in the land of Edom.
And wild oxen will go down with them, and young bulls with the mighty bulls; and their land will drink its fill of blood, and their dust will be gorged with fat.
For the LORD has a day of vengeance, a year of retribution for the cause of Zion.
And her torrents will be turned into pitch, and her dust into sulphur; and her land will become burning pitch.
Night and day it will not be quenched; its smoke will go up for ever. From generation to generation it will lie desolate; for ever and ever no one will pass through it.
And the desert owl and the hedgehog will possess it, and the great owl and the raven will dwell in it. And he will stretch over it a measuring-line of emptiness and the plumb-stones of emptiness.
As for her nobles, there is no kingship there to proclaim, and all her princes will be nothing.
And thorns will grow up in her fortresses, nettles and thornbushes in her fortifications; and she will become a habitation of jackals, grass for the daughters of the ostrich.
And desert creatures will meet with hyenas, and the goat-demon will call to its companion. Surely there Lilith will settle and find for herself a resting place.
There the owl will nest and lay, and hatch and gather her brood in her shadow. Surely there the kites will be gathered, each with her companion.
Seek from the scroll of the LORD and read: not one of these will be missing; none will lack her companion. For his mouth has commanded, and his spirit has gathered them.
And he himself has cast the lot for them, and his hand has divided it out to them by the measuring-line. For ever they will possess it; from generation to generation they will dwell in it.

isaiah_35.t: The wilderness and the dry region will rejoice, and the desert plain will be glad and bud like a crocus.

It will bud abundantly and be glad — yes, with gladness and shouting for joy! The glory of Lebanon will be given to it, the magnificence of Carmel and Sharon. They will see the glory of the LORD, the splendour of our God.
Strengthen the slack hands, and make firm the stumbling knees.
Say to those who are hasty of heart: Be strong, do not be afraid! Look — your God: vengeance will come, the requital of God; he himself will come and deliver you.
Then the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf will be unstopped.
Then the lame will leap like a deer, and the tongue of the mute will shout for joy; for waters will burst forth in the wilderness, and torrents in the desert plain.
And the parched ground will become a pool, and the thirsty ground springs of water; in the habitation of jackals, where they lay down, there will be grass for reeds and papyrus.

And there will be a highway there, and a way, and it will be called the Way of Holiness. The unclean will not pass along it; it is for them alone — whoever walks the way, even fools, will not go astray.
No lion will be there, and no ravening beast will go up on it; none will be found there. And the redeemed will walk there.
And the ransomed of the LORD will return and come to Zion with a shout of joy, and everlasting joy will be on their head. Gladness and joy will overtake them, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.

isaiah_36.t: In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the fortified cities of Judah and seized them.

And the king of Assyria sent the chief commander from Lachish to Jerusalem, to King Hezekiah, with a massive army; and he took his stand at the conduit of the upper pool, on the highway to the Launderer's Field.
And there went out to him Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the house, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder.
And the chief commander said to them: Say to Hezekiah: Thus says the great king, the king of Assyria: What is this trust of yours that you trust in?
I say that a word of the lips is plan and strength enough for war! Now, in whom do you trust, that you have rebelled against me?
Look — you trust in the staff of this crushed reed, in Egypt, which will go into a man's palm and pierce it if he leans on it. So is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust in him.
And if you say to me: We trust in the LORD our God — is he not the one whose high places and altars Hezekiah has removed, saying to Judah and to Jerusalem: Before this altar you shall bow down?
And now, make a wager with my master the king of Assyria: let me give you two thousand horses, if you are able to put riders on them!
And how will you turn back one governor among the least of my master's servants, when you have been relying on Egypt for chariotry and horsemen?
And now, is it apart from the LORD that I have come up against this land to destroy it? The LORD said to me: Go up against this land and destroy it.

And Eliakim and Shebna and Joah said to the chief commander: Speak to your servants in Aramaic, please, for we understand it; and do not speak to us in Judean in the hearing of the people on the city wall.

And the chief commander said: Has my master sent me to speak these words to your master and to you, and not to the men sitting on the city wall, who are to eat their own excrement and drink the water of their own feet along with you?
And the chief commander stood and called out with a loud voice in Judean: Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!
Thus says the king: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, for he will not be able to rescue you.
And do not let Hezekiah make you trust in the LORD, saying: The LORD will surely rescue us; this city will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.

Do not listen to Hezekiah. For thus says the king of Assyria: Make peace with me and come out to me, and each of you will eat from his own vine and his own fig tree, and each will drink the water of his own cistern,
until I come and take you to a land like your own land, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards.
Do not let Hezekiah mislead you, saying: The LORD will deliver us. Have the gods of the nations rescued, any of them, their own land from the hand of the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? And have they rescued Samaria from my hand?
Who among all the gods of these lands has delivered his land from my hand, that the LORD should rescue Jerusalem from my hand?
And they kept silent and did not answer him a word, for the king's command was: Do not answer him.

And Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the house, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder, came to Hezekiah with their garments torn, and told him the words of the chief commander.

isaiah_37.t: And when King Hezekiah heard it, he tore his garments and covered himself with sackcloth and went into the house of the LORD.
And he sent Eliakim, who was over the house, and Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet.
And they said to him: Thus says Hezekiah: This day is a day of distress and rebuke and insult; for children have come to the birth, and there is no strength to bring them out.

Perhaps the LORD your God will hear the words of the chief commander, whom his master the king of Assyria has sent to taunt the living God, and will rebuke the words that the LORD your God has heard. So lift up a prayer for the remnant that is left.
And the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.

And Isaiah said to them: This is what you shall say to your master: Thus says the LORD: Do not be afraid because of the words you have heard, with which the attendants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me.
Look — I am putting a spirit in him, and he will hear a report and return to his own land; and I will make him fall by the sword in his own land.
And the chief commander returned and found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah, for he had heard that he had left Lachish.
And he heard concerning Tirhakah king of Cush: He has come out to do battle with you. And when he heard it, he sent messengers to Hezekiah:
This is what you shall say to Hezekiah king of Judah: Do not let your God, in whom you are trusting, deceive you, saying: Jerusalem will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.
Look — you yourself have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands, devoting them to destruction. And will you be rescued?
Did the gods of the nations rescue them — the nations my fathers destroyed: Gozan and Haran and Rezeph, and the people of Eden who were in Telassar?
Where is the king of Hamath and the king of Arpad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena and Ivvah?
And Hezekiah took the letters from the hand of the messengers and read them; and he went up to the house of the LORD and spread them out before the LORD.
And Hezekiah prayed to the LORD:
LORD of hosts, God of Israel, enthroned upon the cherubim: you alone are the God of all the kingdoms of the earth; you have made the heavens and the earth.
Incline your ear, LORD, and hear! Open your eyes, LORD, and see! And hear all the words of Sennacherib, which he has sent to taunt the living God.
It is true, LORD, that the kings of Assyria have laid waste all the lands and their land,
and have put their gods into the fire — for they were not gods but the work of human hands, wood and stone — and so they destroyed them.
And now, LORD our God, deliver us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you alone are the LORD.
And Isaiah son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah: Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Because you have prayed to me concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria —
this is the word that the LORD has spoken concerning him: She despises you, she mocks you — the virgin daughter of Zion; behind your back she shakes her head — the daughter of Jerusalem.
Whom have you taunted and blasphemed? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your eyes on high? Against the Holy One of Israel!

By the hand of your servants you have taunted the Lord, and have said: With the abundance of my chariotry I have gone up to the heights of the mountains, to the remotest parts of Lebanon; and I will cut down its tallest cedars, its choicest pines, and come to its farthest height, its densest forest.
I myself have dug wells and drunk water, and with the sole of my feet I will dry up all the canals of Egypt.
Have you not heard? Long ago I did it; from days of antiquity I planned it; now I have brought it to pass, so that you should turn fortified cities into ruined heaps.
And their inhabitants were powerless; they were dismayed and ashamed. They were the vegetation of the field, the green of growing things, grass on the roofs, blasted before it is grown.
And your sitting down and your going out and your coming in I know, and your raging against me.
Because of your raging against me, and because your arrogance has come up into my ears, I will put my hook in your nose and my bridle on your lips, and I will turn you back by the way you came.
And this will be the sign for you: this year you will eat what grows of itself, and in the second year what springs from that; and in the third year sow and reap, plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
And the escaped of the house of Judah that remains will again take root downward and bear fruit upward.
For from Jerusalem a remnant will go out, and the escaped from Mount Zion. The zeal of the LORD of hosts will do this.

Therefore thus says the LORD concerning the king of Assyria: He will not come into this city, and will not shoot an arrow there; he will not confront it with a shield, and will not throw up a siege mound against it.
By the way he came he will return, and into this city he will not come — declares the LORD.
And I will shield this city, to deliver it, for my own sake and for the sake of David my servant.
And the angel of the LORD went out and struck down in the camp of Assyria a hundred and eighty-five thousand; and when they rose early in the morning, there they all were — dead corpses.
And Sennacherib king of Assyria set out and went and returned, and stayed in Nineveh.

And while he was bowing down in the house of Nisroch his god, Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons struck him down with the sword; and they escaped to the land of Ararat. And Esarhaddon his son reigned in his place.

isaiah_38.t: In those days Hezekiah became sick to the point of death. And Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet came to him and said: Thus says the LORD: Put your household in order, for you are about to die and will not live.
And Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD.
And he said: Please, LORD, remember how I have walked before you in faithfulness and with a whole heart, and have done what is good in your eyes. And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
And the word of the LORD came to Isaiah:
Go and say to Hezekiah: Thus says the LORD, the God of David your father: I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears. Look — I am adding fifteen years to your days.
And I will rescue you and this city from the hand of the king of Assyria; and I will shield this city.
And this will be the sign for you from the LORD, that the LORD will do this thing that he has spoken:
Look — I am turning back the shadow of the steps, which has gone down on the steps of Ahaz with the sun, backward ten steps. And the sun went back ten steps on the steps by which it had gone down.
A writing of Hezekiah king of Judah, when he had been sick and had recovered from his sickness.
I said: In the noontide of my days I must go into the gates of Sheol; I am deprived of the remainder of my years.
I said: I shall not see the LORD, the LORD in the land of the living; I shall not look on humankind any more with the inhabitants of the world that ceases.
My dwelling is pulled up and carried off from me like a shepherd's tent. I have rolled up my life like a weaver; he cuts me off from the loom. From day to night you make an end of me.
I have quieted myself until morning; like a lion, so he breaks all my bones. From day to night you make an end of me.
Like a swift or a crane, so I chirp; I moan like a dove. My eyes are worn out looking to the heights. Lord, I am oppressed — stand surety for me!
What can I say? He has spoken to me, and he himself has done it. I shall walk slowly all my years because of the bitterness of my whole being.
Lord, by these things people live, and in all of them is the life of my spirit. So restore me to health and keep me alive.
Look — it was for my welfare that I was bitterly embittered; but you have held my life back from the pit of destruction, for you have thrown all my sins behind your back.
For Sheol does not give you thanks; death does not praise you; those who go down to the pit do not hope for your faithfulness.
The living, the living — he gives you thanks, as I do this day. A father makes your faithfulness known to his children.
The LORD is at hand to deliver me; and we will play my songs on stringed instruments all the days of our lives, at the house of the LORD.
And Isaiah had said: Let them take a cake of figs and rub it on the boil, and he will live.
And Hezekiah had said: What is the sign that I shall go up to the house of the LORD?

isaiah_39.t: At that time Merodach-baladan son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah, for he had heard that he had been sick and had recovered.

And Hezekiah was pleased with them, and showed them his treasure house — the silver and the gold, the spices and the fine oil, his whole armoury, and everything found in his storehouses. There was nothing in his house or in all his realm that Hezekiah did not show them.
And Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah and said: What did these men say, and where have they come to you from? And Hezekiah said: They have come to me from a distant land, from Babylon.
And he said: What did they see in your house? And Hezekiah said: They saw everything that is in my house. There was nothing in my storehouses that I did not show them.
And Isaiah said to Hezekiah: Hear the word of the LORD of hosts!
Look — days are coming when everything in your house, and what your fathers have stored up until this day, will be carried off to Babylon. Nothing will remain, says the LORD.
And some of your own sons who come from you, whom you will father, will be taken; and they will be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.
And Hezekiah said to Isaiah: The word of the LORD that you have spoken is good. For, he said, there will be peace and security in my days.

isaiah_40.t: Comfort, comfort my people, says your God.
Speak to the heart of Jerusalem and proclaim to her that her hard service is completed, that her iniquity is pardoned, that she has received from the hand of the LORD double for all her sins.
A voice calling: In the wilderness clear the way of the LORD; make straight in the desert plain a highway for our God.
Every valley will be lifted up, and every mountain and hill brought low; the steep place will become level ground, and the rough places a plain.
And the glory of the LORD will be revealed, and all flesh together will see it; for the mouth of the LORD has spoken.
A voice saying: Proclaim! And he said: What shall I proclaim? All flesh is grass, and all its beauty is like the flower of the field.
The grass dries up, the flower withers, for the wind of the LORD blows on it. Truly the people is grass.
The grass dries up, the flower withers, but the word of our God will stand for ever.
Go up on a high mountain, bearer of good news to Zion; lift up your voice with strength, bearer of good news to Jerusalem! Lift it up, do not be afraid; say to the cities of Judah: Look — your God!
Look — the Lord GOD comes with strength, and his arm rules for him. Look — his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.
Like a shepherd he will shepherd his flock; in his arm he will gather the lambs and carry them in his bosom; he will gently lead the nursing ewes.

Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and marked off the heavens with a span, and held the dust of the earth in a measure, and weighed the mountains in a balance and the hills in scales?
Who has directed the spirit of the LORD, or as his counsellor has instructed him?
With whom did he take counsel, and who gave him understanding and taught him the path of justice, and taught him knowledge and made known to him the way of understanding?
Look — the nations are like a drop from a bucket, and are reckoned like the dust on the scales. Look — he lifts the coastlands like fine dust.
And Lebanon is not enough for the fire, and its animals not enough for a burnt offering.
All the nations are as nothing before him; they are reckoned by him as less than nothingness and emptiness.
To whom then will you liken God? And what likeness will you set beside him?
The image — a craftsman casts it, a refiner overlays it with gold and casts silver chains for it.
The one too poor for such an offering chooses wood that will not rot; he seeks out a skilled craftsman to set up an image that will not totter.
Do you not know? Do you not hear? Has it not been told you from the beginning? Have you not understood since the earth was founded?
It is he who sits above the circle of the earth, and its inhabitants are like grasshoppers; who stretches out the heavens like a thin curtain and spreads them like a tent to dwell in;
who brings rulers to nothing and makes the judges of the earth like emptiness.
Scarcely are they planted, scarcely are they sown, scarcely has their stock taken root in the ground, when he blows on them and they dry up, and a tempest carries them off like stubble.
To whom then will you liken me, that I should be his equal? says the Holy One.

Lift up your eyes on high and see: who created these? He who brings out their host by number, calling them all by name; by the greatness of his might and the strength of his power, not one is missing.
Why do you say, Jacob, and declare, Israel: My way is hidden from the LORD, and my cause passes away from my God?
Do you not know? Have you not heard? The LORD is the everlasting God, the creator of the ends of the earth. He does not grow faint and does not grow weary; his understanding cannot be searched out.
He gives strength to the faint, and to those with no vigour he increases might.
Youths grow faint and weary, and young men stumble and fall;
but those who wait for the LORD will renew their strength; they will rise on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary; they will walk and not grow faint.

isaiah_41.t: Be silent before me, coastlands, and let the peoples renew their strength. Let them draw near, then let them speak; let us come near together for judgement.
Who stirred up one from the east — whom he calls in righteousness to his foot? He gives up nations before him and subdues kings; he makes them like dust by his sword, like driven stubble by his bow.
He pursues them; he passes on unharmed, by a path his feet have not travelled.
Who has done it and accomplished it, calling the generations from the beginning? I, the LORD, am first, and with the last ones — I am he.
The coastlands have seen and are afraid; the ends of the earth tremble; they have drawn near and come.
Each helps his neighbour, and to his brother he says: Be strong!
And the craftsman encouraged the refiner, the one who smooths with the hammer him who strikes the anvil, saying of the soldering: It is good. And he fastened it with nails so it would not totter.
But you, Israel, my servant, Jacob, whom I have chosen, the offspring of Abraham my friend —
you whom I took hold of from the ends of the earth and called from its farthest parts, and I said to you: You are my servant; I have chosen you and have not rejected you.
Do not be afraid, for I am with you; do not be dismayed, for I am your God. I have strengthened you, I have also helped you, I have also upheld you with the right hand of my righteousness.
See, all who are angry with you will be ashamed and disgraced; those who contend with you will be as nothing and will perish.
You will seek them and not find them, those who strive with you. Those who make war on you will be as nothing, as nothingness.
For I am the LORD your God, who takes hold of your right hand, who says to you: Do not be afraid; I myself will help you.
Do not be afraid, worm Jacob, men of Israel! I myself will help you, declares the LORD, and your redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.
See, I have made you a threshing-sledge, sharp, new, and full of teeth. You will thresh mountains and crush them, and make hills like chaff.
You will winnow them, and a wind will carry them away, and a tempest will scatter them. And you will be glad in the LORD; in the Holy One of Israel you will boast.
The poor and the needy are seeking water, and there is none; their tongue is parched with thirst. I, the LORD, will answer them; I, the God of Israel, will not forsake them.
I will open rivers on the bare heights, and fountains in the midst of the valleys. I will make the wilderness a pool of water, and the dry region springs of water.
I will put in the wilderness the cedar, the acacia, the myrtle and the olive tree. I will set in the desert plain the juniper, the plane and the cypress together.
so that they may see and know, and take it to heart and understand together, that the hand of the LORD has done this, and the Holy One of Israel has created it.
Bring near your case, says the LORD; bring forward your arguments, says the King of Jacob.
Let them bring them near and tell us what will happen. The former things — what were they? Tell us, and let us take it to heart and know their outcome; or make us hear the things that are coming.
Tell us the things that are coming afterwards, and we will know that you are gods. Yes — do good or do harm, so that we may be dismayed and see it together.
See, you are nothing, and your work is worthless. An abomination is the one who chooses you.
I have stirred up one from the north, and he has come; from the rising of the sun he will call on my name. And he will trample officials like mud, as a potter tramples clay.
Who told it from the beginning, that we might know, and beforehand, that we might say: He is right? No — there was none who told; none who proclaimed; none who heard a saying from you.
I was first to say to Zion: See, here they are! and to Jerusalem I gave a bearer of good news.
And I look, and there is no one; among these there is no counsellor, that I might ask them and they answer.
See, all of them — deception; their deeds are nothingness; wind and emptiness are their cast images.

isaiah_42.t: See, my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen one, in whom my being delights. I have put my spirit on him; he will bring forth judgement to the nations.
He will not cry out and will not lift up his voice, and will not make it heard in the street.
A crushed reed he will not break, and a dim wick he will not snuff out; in faithfulness he will bring forth judgement.
He will not grow dim and will not be crushed until he establishes judgement on the earth; and for his law the coastlands hope.

Thus says the God, the LORD, who created the heavens and stretched them out, who spread out the earth and what it brings forth, who gives breath to the people on it and spirit to those who walk on it:
I, the LORD, have called you in righteousness, and I will take hold of your hand; and I will watch over you and make you a covenant for the people, a light of the nations,
to open blind eyes, to bring the prisoner out from the prison, and from the house of imprisonment those who dwell in darkness.
I am the LORD — that is my name; and my glory I will not give to another, nor my praise to images.
The former things — see, they have come; and new things I now tell. Before they spring up I make you hear them.
Sing to the LORD a new song, his praise from the end of the earth — you who go down to the sea and all that fills it, the coastlands and those who dwell in them.
Let the wilderness and its cities lift up their voice, and the villages where Kedar dwells. Let the inhabitants of Sela shout for joy; let them cry aloud from the top of the mountains.
Let them give glory to the LORD, and declare his praise in the coastlands.
The LORD will go forth like a warrior; like a man of war he will stir up his zeal. He will raise a war-cry, yes, a battle shout; against his enemies he will prevail.
I have been silent from of old; I have kept still, I have restrained myself. Like a woman giving birth I groan; I gasp and pant at once.
I will lay waste mountains and hills and dry up all their vegetation. I will turn rivers into dry ground and dry up the pools.

And I will lead the blind by a way they have not known; in paths they have not known I will guide them. I will turn the darkness before them into light, and the rough places into level ground. These are the things I will do, and I will not abandon them.
They are turned back and utterly disgraced, those who trust in the image, those who say to a molten image: You are our gods.
You deaf, listen! And you blind, look, and see!
Who is blind but my servant, and deaf like my messenger whom I send? Who is blind like my dedicated one, and blind like the servant of the LORD?
You have seen many things, but you do not keep them; your ears are open, but he does not listen.
The LORD was pleased, for the sake of his righteousness, to make his law great and glorious.

But this is a people despoiled and plundered; all of them are trapped in holes and hidden away in houses of imprisonment. They have become spoil, and there is no rescuer; plunder, and no one says: Bring it back.
Who among you will give ear to this, will pay attention and listen for the time to come?
Who gave Jacob up to plunder, and Israel to despoilers? Was it not the LORD, against whom we have sinned? They were not willing to walk in his ways, and they did not listen to his law.
So he poured out on him the heat of his anger and the fierceness of battle. It set him ablaze all round, and he did not know it; it burned in him, and he did not take it to heart.

isaiah_43.t: And now, thus says the LORD, who created you, Jacob, and who formed you, Israel: Do not be afraid, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by your name — you are mine.
When you pass through the waters, I am with you; and through the rivers, they will not overwhelm you. When you walk through fire you will not be scorched, and the flame will not burn you.
For I am the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, your deliverer. I have given Egypt as your ransom price, Cush and Seba in place of you.
Because you are precious in my eyes, you are honoured, and I myself love you; and I give humankind in place of you, and peoples in place of your being.
Do not be afraid, for I am with you. From the east I will bring your offspring, and from the west I will gather you.
I will say to the north: Give them up! and to the south: Do not hold them back! Bring my sons from far off, and my daughters from the end of the earth —
everyone who is called by my name, whom I created for my glory, whom I formed, whom I also made.
Bring out a people that is blind, though it has eyes, and deaf, though they have ears.

All the nations have assembled together, and the peoples have gathered. Who among them declares this, and makes us hear the former things? Let them bring their witnesses and be justified; and let them hear and say: It is true.

You are my witnesses, declares the LORD, and my servant whom I have chosen, so that you may know and believe me and understand that I am he. Before me no god was formed, and after me there will be none.
I, I am the LORD, and apart from me there is no deliverer.
I declared and delivered and proclaimed, and there was no strange god among you; and you are my witnesses, declares the LORD, and I am God.
Also, from this day on, I am he, and there is no one who rescues from my hand. I act, and who can reverse it?
Thus says the LORD, your redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: For your sake I have sent to Babylon and brought them all down as fugitives, and the Chaldeans in the ships of their shout of joy.
I am the LORD, your Holy One, the creator of Israel, your King.
Thus says the LORD, who makes a way in the sea and a path in mighty waters;
who brings out chariot and horse, army and mighty one together. They lie down and do not rise; they are extinguished, quenched like a wick.
Do not remember the former things, and do not consider the ancient things.
See, I am doing a new thing; now it springs up — do you not perceive it? I will indeed make a way in the wilderness, rivers in the wasteland.
The animals of the field will honour me, jackals and daughters of the ostrich, because I have put water in the wilderness, rivers in the wasteland, to give drink to my people, my chosen one.
The people I formed for myself will recount my praise.
But you have not called on me, Jacob, for you have grown weary of me, Israel.
You have not brought me the sheep of your burnt offerings, and with your sacrifices you have not honoured me. I have not burdened you with offerings, and I have not made you weary with frankincense.
You have not bought me sweet cane with money, and with the fat of your sacrifices you have not satisfied me. Rather, you have burdened me with your sins; you have made me weary with your iniquities.
I, I am he who wipes out your transgressions for my own sake, and your sins I will not remember.
Remind me; let us enter into judgement together. Make your own case, so that you may be justified.
Your first ancestor sinned, and your spokesmen transgressed against me.
So I profaned the officials of the sanctuary, and gave Jacob over to be devoted to destruction, and Israel to reviling.

isaiah_44.t: And now listen, Jacob my servant, and Israel, whom I have chosen.
Thus says the LORD, who made you and formed you from the belly, who will help you: Do not be afraid, Jacob my servant, and Jeshurun, whom I have chosen.
For I will pour water on the thirsty ground and streams on the dry ground. I will pour my spirit on your offspring and my blessing on your descendants.
And they will spring up among the grass, like poplars by watercourses of water.
This one will say: I belong to the LORD; and this one will call himself by the name of Jacob; and this one will write on his hand: Belonging to the LORD, and will take the name of Israel.
Thus says the LORD, the King of Israel, and its redeemer, the LORD of hosts: I am first and I am last, and apart from me there is no god.

And who is like me? Let him proclaim it, let him declare it and set it in order before me, since I established an ancient people; and the things coming, and the things that will come — let them declare them.
Do not dread and do not be afraid. Did I not make you hear it long ago and declare it? And you are my witnesses. Is there a god apart from me? There is no Rock — I know none.
Those who form an image are all of them emptiness, and the things they treasure confer no profit; and their own witnesses see nothing and know nothing, so that they may be ashamed.
Who has formed a god or cast an image that confers no profit?
See, all his companions will be ashamed, and the craftsmen — they are only human. Let them all gather together and stand; let them dread, let them be ashamed together.

The craftsman in iron takes a tool, and works it on the coals and forms it with hammers, and works it with the arm of his strength. He grows hungry, and there is no strength; he has drunk no water, and he grows weary.

The craftsman in wood stretches out a measuring-line; he outlines it with a marker; he works it with scraping tools and outlines it with a compass. And he makes it like the form of a man, like the splendour of humankind, to dwell in a house.
cutting down cedars for himself — he took a cypress and an oak and let it grow strong for himself among the trees of the forest. He plants a cedar, and the rain makes it grow.

And it becomes something for a person to burn: he takes some of it and warms himself; he also kindles a fire and bakes bread; he also makes a god and bows down; he makes it an image and prostrates himself to it.
Half of it he burns in the fire; over half of it he eats meat; he roasts a roast and is satisfied. He also warms himself and says: Aha! I am warm; I have seen the fire.
And the remainder of it he makes into a god, into his image; he prostrates himself to it and bows down and prays to it and says: Rescue me, for you are my god.
They do not know and do not understand, for their eyes are smeared shut so they cannot see, their hearts so they cannot have insight.

And no one brings it back to his heart, and there is no knowledge and no understanding, to say: Half of it I burned in the fire, and I also baked bread on its coals; I roast meat and eat. And shall I make the remainder of it into an abomination? Shall I prostrate myself to a block of wood?
He feeds on ashes; a deceived heart has turned him aside, and he will not rescue his own being, and will not say: Is there not a lie in my right hand?
Remember these things, Jacob, and Israel, for you are my servant. I formed you; you are a servant of mine. Israel, you will not be forgotten by me.
I have wiped out your transgressions like a dark cloud, and your sins like a cloud. Return to me, for I have redeemed you.

Shout for joy, heavens, for the LORD has acted! Shout in triumph, depths of the earth! Break forth in a shout of joy, mountains, forest and every tree in it! For the LORD has redeemed Jacob, and in Israel he will get glory for himself.
Thus says the LORD, your redeemer, and the one who formed you from the belly: I am the LORD, who makes everything, who stretches out the heavens alone, who spreads out the earth — by myself.
who frustrates the signs of empty talkers and makes diviners look foolish, who turns the wise back and makes their knowledge foolish;

who establishes the word of his servant and performs the counsel of his messengers; who says of Jerusalem: It will be inhabited, and of the cities of Judah: They will be rebuilt, and its waste places I will raise up;
who says to the deep: Be dried up, and I will make your rivers dry;
who says of Cyrus: My shepherd, and he will perform all my desire; and who says of Jerusalem: Let it be rebuilt, and of the temple: Let its foundation be laid.

isaiah_45.t: Thus says the LORD to his anointed one, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have taken hold of, to subdue nations before him and to loosen the belts of kings, to open doors before him and gates that will not be shut:
I myself will go before you and make the rough places smooth. I will break doors of bronze and cut through bars of iron.
And I will give you treasures of darkness and hidden hoards of secret places, so that you may know that I am the LORD, who calls you by your name — the God of Israel.
For the sake of my servant Jacob and Israel my chosen one, I called you by your name; I gave you a title, though you do not know me.
I am the LORD, and there is no other; besides me there is no god. I gird you, though you do not know me,
so that they may know, from the rising of the sun and from its setting, that there is nothing apart from me. I am the LORD, and there is no other;
who forms light and creates darkness, who makes well-being and creates calamity. I am the LORD, who does all these things.

Drip down, heavens, from above, and let the clouds flow with righteousness. Let the earth open, and let deliverance bear fruit, and let it make righteousness sprout with it. I, the LORD, have created it.
Woe to the one who contends with the one who formed him — a potsherd among the potsherds of the ground! Does the clay say to the one who forms it: What are you making? Or: Your work has no hands?
Woe to the one who says to a father: What are you fathering? and to a woman: What are you in labour with?
Thus says the LORD, the Holy One of Israel and the one who formed it: Ask me about the things that are coming! Concerning my children and the work of my hands, would you command me?
I myself made the earth and created humankind on it. I — my own hands stretched out the heavens, and I commanded all their host.
I myself have stirred him up in righteousness, and all his ways I will make smooth. He will build my city and let my exiles go, not for a price and not for a bribe, says the LORD of hosts.

Thus says the LORD: The produce of Egypt and the traffic of Cush and the Sabeans, men of stature — they will pass over to you and will be yours; they will walk behind you; in fetters they will pass over; and to you they will bow down, to you they will pray: Only among you is God, and there is no other; there are no gods.
Truly you are a God who hides himself, God of Israel, deliverer.
They are ashamed and disgraced, all of them; they walk in ignominy together — the makers of effigies.
Israel has been delivered by the LORD with an everlasting deliverance. You will not be ashamed and will not be disgraced for ever and ever.

For thus says the LORD, the creator of the heavens — he is God — the one who formed the earth and made it; he established it; he did not create it an emptiness; he formed it to be dwelt in: I am the LORD, and there is no other.
I did not speak in secret, in a place of a land of darkness. I did not say to the offspring of Jacob: Seek me in emptiness. I, the LORD, speak righteousness, declaring what is upright.
Gather together and come; draw near together, fugitives of the nations! They know nothing — those who carry the wood of their image and pray to a god that cannot deliver.

Declare and bring it near; yes, let them take counsel together. Who made this heard from of old, who declared it long ago? Was it not I, the LORD? And there is no god apart from me — a righteous God and a deliverer; there is none besides me.
Turn to me and be delivered, all the ends of the earth; for I am God, and there is no other.
By myself I have sworn; righteousness has gone out from my mouth, a word that will not return: that to me every knee will bend, and every tongue will swear.
Only in the LORD, it will be said of me, are righteousness and power. To him they will come, and all who are angry with him will be ashamed.
In the LORD all the offspring of Israel will be justified and will boast.

isaiah_46.t: Bel has bent down; Nebo is stooping low. Their figures are loaded on the animals, on the cattle. The things you carried in procession are loaded up, a load for a weary beast.
They have stooped low, they have bent down together; they could not bring the load to safety, and they themselves have gone into captivity.
Listen to me, house of Jacob and all the remnant of the house of Israel, who have been carried since the belly, borne since the womb.
And to your old age I am he, and to your grey hair I will carry you. I myself made you, and I myself will bear you; and I will carry you and bring you to safety.
To whom will you liken me and make me equal, and compare me, that we should be alike?
Those who pour out gold from a bag and weigh silver on the scales — they hire a refiner, and he makes it a god; they prostrate themselves; they also bow down.

They lift it on a shoulder; they carry it and set it down in its place, and it stands; from its place it does not move. Even if one cries out to it, it does not answer; it does not deliver him from his distress.
Remember this and take courage; bring it back to heart, you transgressors.
Remember the former things from of old: that I am God and there is no other, God, and there is nothing like me;
declaring the end from the beginning, and from long ago the things that have not been done; saying: My plan will stand, and all my desire I will do —
calling a bird of prey from the east, from a distant land the man of my plan. I have spoken; I will also bring it about. I have formed it; I will also do it.
Listen to me, you stubborn of heart, far from righteousness:
I have brought near my righteousness; it is not far off, and my deliverance will not delay. I will give deliverance in Zion, to Israel my splendour.

isaiah_47.t: Go down and sit in the dust, virgin daughter of Babylon. Sit on the ground — there is no throne, daughter of the Chaldeans. For you will no longer be called tender and delicate.
Take a hand-mill and grind flour. Uncover your veil; strip off your skirt; bare your leg; wade through rivers.
Let your nakedness be uncovered; let your reproach also be seen. I will take vengeance, and I will spare no one.
Our redeemer — the LORD of hosts is his name, the Holy One of Israel.
Sit silently and go into the darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans; for you will no longer be called queen of kingdoms.
I was angry with my people; I profaned my inheritance and gave them into your hand. You showed them no compassion; on the old you laid your yoke very heavily.
And you said: For ever I will be a queen — so you did not set these things on your heart; you did not remember how it would end.
And now hear this, voluptuous one, who sits in security, who says in her heart: I, and besides me there is no other. I will not sit as a widow and will not know childlessness.

And both of these will come to you in a moment, in one day: childlessness and widowhood. In their full measure they will come upon you, for all the abundance of your sorceries, for all the great might of your spells.
And you trusted in your wickedness. You said: No one sees me. Your wisdom and your knowledge have led you astray; and you said in your heart: I, and besides me there is no other.

And calamity will come upon you that you will not know how to charm away, and disaster will fall on you that you will not be able to avert; and ruin will come upon you suddenly, which you will not know.
Stand now with your spells and with the abundance of your sorceries, in which you have laboured from your youth. Perhaps you will be able to profit; perhaps you will inspire awe.

You have become weary with the abundance of your counsels. Let them stand up and deliver you — those who divide the heavens, who gaze at the stars, who at the new moons make known what will come upon you.
See, they have become like stubble; fire has burned them. They will not rescue their own being from the hand of the flame. There will be no coal to warm them, no fire to sit before.
So they have become for you — those for whom you have laboured, your traders from your youth. Each has wandered off his own way; there is no one to deliver you.

isaiah_48.t: Hear this, house of Jacob, you who are called by the name of Israel and who came out from the waters of Judah, who swear by the name of the LORD and invoke the God of Israel — but not in truth and not in righteousness.
For they call themselves after the holy city and lean on the God of Israel — the LORD of hosts is his name.
The former things I declared long ago; they went out from my mouth, and I proclaimed them. Suddenly I acted, and they came about.
Because I knew that you are stubborn, and your neck a sinew of iron, and your forehead bronze,
so I declared it to you long ago; before it came about I proclaimed it to you, lest you should say: My figure did them, and my image and my cast image commanded them.
You have heard; look at all of it! And you — will you not declare it? From now on I make you hear new things, hidden things you have not known.
They are created now and not long ago, and before this day you had not heard of them, lest you should say: See, I knew them.
You had neither heard nor known, nor from long ago was your ear opened; for I knew you would deal treacherously indeed, and that you were called a transgressor from the belly.
For the sake of my name I will hold back my anger, and for my praise I will restrain myself towards you, so as not to cut you off.
See, I have refined you, but not as silver; I have tested you in the furnace of affliction.
For my own sake, for my own sake I will act — for how should my name be profaned? And my glory I will not give to another.
Listen to me, Jacob, and Israel, my called one: I am he; I am first, yes, I am last.
My own hand founded the earth, and my right hand spanned the heavens. I call to them; they stand together.
Gather together, all of you, and listen! Who among them declared these things? The LORD loves him; he will do his desire on Babylon, and his arm will be on the Chaldeans.
I, I have spoken; yes, I have summoned him. I have brought him, and he will make his way succeed.
Draw near to me; hear this! From the beginning I have not spoken in secret; from the time it came about, I was there. And now the Lord GOD has sent me — and his spirit.
Thus says the LORD, your redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: I am the LORD your God, who teaches you to profit, who leads you in the way you should go.
If only you had paid attention to my commandments! Then your peace would have been like the river, and your righteousness like the waves of the sea.
And your offspring would have been like the sand, and the descendants of your body like its grains. His name would not be cut off and would not be destroyed from before me.
Go out from Babylon; flee from the Chaldeans! With a sound of joyful shouting declare this; proclaim it; send it out to the end of the earth. Say: The LORD has redeemed his servant Jacob.
And they were not thirsty when he led them through the waste places; he made water flow for them from a rock; he split a rock, and the waters gushed out.
There is no peace, says the LORD, for the wicked.

isaiah_49.t: Listen to me, coastlands, and pay attention, you peoples far off! The LORD called me from the belly; from the inward parts of my mother he named my name.
And he made my mouth like a sharp sword; in the shadow of his hand he hid me. And he made me a polished arrow; in his quiver he concealed me.
And he said to me: You are my servant, Israel, in whom I will get glory for myself.
And I myself said: For nothing I have laboured; for emptiness and futility I have spent my strength. Yet my cause is with the LORD, and my recompense with my God.

And now the LORD says — who formed me from the belly to be his servant, to bring Jacob back to him, and that Israel might be gathered to him; and I am honoured in the eyes of the LORD, and my God has been my power —

and he said: It is too slight a thing for you to be my servant, to raise up the tribes of Jacob and to bring back the preserved of Israel. I will make you a light of the nations, to be my deliverance to the end of the earth.

Thus says the LORD, the redeemer of Israel, its Holy One, to the one deeply despised, to the one abhorred by a nation, to a servant of rulers: Kings will see and stand up, princes — and they will bow down, because of the LORD, who is faithful, the Holy One of Israel, and he has chosen you.

Thus says the LORD: In a time of favour I answered you, and in a day of deliverance I helped you. I will watch over you and make you a covenant for the people, to raise up the land, to apportion the desolate inheritances,
saying to the prisoners: Come out! to those in darkness: Show yourselves! Along the roads they will graze, and on all the bare heights will be their pasture.
They will not hunger and will not thirst, and burning heat and sun will not strike them; for the one who has compassion on them will guide them, and by springs of water he will gently lead them.
And I will make all my mountains a road, and my highways will be raised up.
See, these come from far off, and see, these from the north and from the west, and these from the land of Sinim.
Shout for joy, heavens, and be glad, earth! Break forth in a shout of joy, mountains! For the LORD has comforted his people and has compassion on his poor.
And Zion said: The LORD has forsaken me, and the Lord has forgotten me.
Does a woman forget her nursing child, or stop having compassion on the child of her womb? Even these may forget, but I myself will not forget you.
See, on the palms of my hands I have inscribed you; your walls are before me continually.
Your children have hastened back; those who tore you down and made you desolate go out from you.
Lift up your eyes all around and see: all of them have gathered together; they have come to you. As I live, declares the LORD, you will put them all on like an ornament and tie them on like a bride.
For your waste places and your desolate places and the land of your destruction — now you will be too cramped for your inhabitants, and those who swallowed you up will be far off.
The children of your bereavement will yet say in your ears: The place is too cramped for me; make room for me, that I may live here.
And you will say in your heart: Who fathered these for me? I was bereaved and barren, gone into exile and thrust away — and these, who brought them up? See, I was left alone; these — where were they?

Thus says the Lord GOD: See, I will lift up my hand to the nations and raise my standard to the peoples; and they will bring your sons in their arms, and your daughters will be carried on their shoulders.

And kings will be your foster-fathers, and their princesses your nursing-mothers. With faces to the ground they will bow down to you and lick up the dust of your feet. And you will know that I am the LORD, and those who wait for me will not be ashamed.
