Can booty be taken from a warrior, or the captives of a righteous one escape?

For thus says the LORD: Even the captives of a warrior will be taken, and the booty of a ruthless one will escape; and I myself will contend with the one who contends with you, and I myself will deliver your children.

And I will make those who maltreat you eat their own flesh, and they will be drunk on their own blood as on sweet wine. And all flesh will know that I, the LORD, am your deliverer and your redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.

isaiah_50.t: Thus says the LORD: Where is this document of your mother's divorce, by which I sent her away? Or which of my creditors is it to whom I sold you? See, for your iniquities you were sold, and for your transgressions your mother was sent away.

Why did I come and there was no one? I called, and there was no one who answered. Is my hand really too short to ransom? Or is there no strength in me to rescue? See, by my rebuke I dry up the sea; I make rivers a wilderness. Their fish stink for lack of water and die of thirst.
I clothe the heavens with darkness and make sackcloth their covering.
The Lord GOD has given me a tongue of disciples, to know how to sustain the weary with a word. He awakens me morning by morning; he awakens my ear to hear like disciples.
The Lord GOD has opened my ear, and I myself was not rebellious; I did not turn back.
I gave my back to those who struck it, and my cheeks to those who pulled out the beard. I did not hide my face from insults and spitting.
And the Lord GOD helps me; therefore I have not been humiliated. Therefore I have set my face like flint, and I know that I will not be put to shame.
The one who justifies me is near. Who will contend with me? Let us stand together. Who has a case against me? Let him draw near to me.
See, the Lord GOD helps me. Who is he who will condemn me? See, all of them will wear out like a garment; a moth will eat them.
Who among you fears the LORD, listening to the voice of his servant, who has walked in darkness and has no brightness? Let him trust in the name of the LORD and lean on his God.
See, all of you who kindle a fire, who gird on firebrands: walk by the light of your fire and by the firebrands you have kindled. This has come to you from my hand: you will lie down in pain.

isaiah_51.t: Listen to me, you who pursue righteousness, you who seek the LORD: look to the rock from which you were hewn, and to the quarry of the pit from which you were dug out.
Look to Abraham your father, and to Sarah who gave birth to you; for he was but one when I called him, and I blessed him and multiplied him.

For the LORD has comforted Zion; he has comforted all her waste places and made her wilderness like Eden and her desert plain like the garden of the LORD. Rejoicing and joy will be found in her, thanksgiving and the sound of music.
Pay attention to me, my people, and give ear to me, my nation; for law will go out from me, and I will set my judgement as a light of peoples.
My righteousness is near; my deliverance has gone out, and my arms will judge peoples. For me the coastlands will wait, and for my arm they will hope.

Lift up your eyes to the heavens and look at the earth beneath; for the heavens will be dispersed like smoke, and the earth will wear out like a garment, and its inhabitants will die like gnats. But my deliverance will be for ever, and my righteousness will not be broken.
Listen to me, you who know righteousness, a people with my law in their heart: do not fear the reproach of humankind, and do not be dismayed by their reviling.
For a moth will eat them like a garment, and a clothes-moth will eat them like wool. But my righteousness will be for ever, and my deliverance to generation after generation.
Awake, awake, put on power, arm of the LORD! Awake as in the days of old, the generations of long ago. Was it not you who cut Rahab in pieces, who pierced the sea monster?
Was it not you who dried up the sea, the waters of the great deep, who made the depths of the sea a way for the redeemed to pass over?
And the ransomed of the LORD will return and come to Zion with a shout of joy, and everlasting joy will be on their head. Gladness and joy will overtake them, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.
I, I am he who comforts you. Who are you, that you are afraid of a mortal who dies, and of a child of humankind who is made grass?

And you have forgotten the LORD your maker, who stretched out the heavens and founded the earth, and you dread continually, all day long, before the rage of the oppressor, when he has made ready to destroy. And where is the rage of the oppressor?
The one bowed down hastens to be set free; he will not die and go down to the pit, and his bread will not run out.
And I am the LORD your God, who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar — the LORD of hosts is his name.
And I have put my words in your mouth and covered you with the shadow of my hand, to plant the heavens and to found the earth, and to say to Zion: You are my people.
Rouse yourself, rouse yourself, arise, Jerusalem, you who have drunk from the hand of the LORD the cup of his rage; the bowl, the cup of staggering, you have drunk and drained.
There is no one to lead her of all the children she has borne, and no one to take hold of her hand of all the children she has brought up.
These two things have happened to you — who will show sympathy to you? — the devastation and the destruction, the famine and the sword. How shall I comfort you?
Your children have become faint; they have lain down at the head of every street like an antelope in a net, full of the rage of the LORD, the rebuke of your God.
Therefore hear this, poor one, and drunken, but not with wine:
Thus says your Lord, the LORD, your God, who contends for his people: See, I have taken from your hand the cup of staggering; the bowl, the cup of my rage — you will not drink it again.
And I will put it into the hand of those who torment you, who said to your being: Lie down, that we may walk over you. And you made your back like the ground, like the street for those who pass over.

isaiah_52.t: Awake, awake, put on your power, Zion! Put on the garments of your splendour, Jerusalem, holy city; for the uncircumcised and the unclean will never again come into you.
Shake yourself free from the dust! Arise, be seated, Jerusalem! Loosen the fetters from your neck, captive daughter of Zion!
For thus says the LORD: You were sold for nothing, and not with money will you be redeemed.
For thus says the Lord GOD: To Egypt my people went down at the first, to sojourn there; and Assyria oppressed it for nothing.
And now, what is there for me here — declares the LORD — for my people has been taken for nothing? Its rulers wail — declares the LORD — and continually, all day long, my name is reviled.
Therefore my people will know my name; therefore, in that day — that I am he who speaks: here I am.
How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of the one who bears news, who proclaims peace, who bears good news, who proclaims deliverance, who says to Zion: Your God reigns!
The voice of your watchmen — they lift up their voice; together they shout for joy; for eye to eye they will see when the LORD returns to Zion.
Break forth, shout for joy together, waste places of Jerusalem! For the LORD has comforted his people; he has redeemed Jerusalem.
The LORD has bared his holy arm before the eyes of all the nations; and all the ends of the earth will see the deliverance of our God.
Depart, depart, go out from there! Touch nothing unclean! Go out from her midst; purify yourselves, you who carry the articles of the LORD!
For you will not go out in haste, and you will not go in flight; for the LORD is going before you, and the God of Israel is your rearguard.
See, my servant will prosper; he will be high and lifted up and exalted exceedingly.
Just as many were appalled at you — so disfigured was his appearance, beyond that of a man, and his form beyond that of the children of humankind —
so he will sprinkle many nations; kings will shut their mouths because of him. For what had not been recounted to them they will see, and what they had not heard they will understand.

isaiah_53.t: Who has believed our report, and the arm of the LORD — to whom has it been revealed?
And he grew up before him like a shoot, like a root out of dry ground. He had no form and no magnificence, that we should look at him; and no appearance, that we should desire him.
He was despised and rejected by others, a man of pains and acquainted with sickness; and like one from whom people hide the face he was despised, and we did not value him.
Truly he bore our sicknesses and carried our pains; and we ourselves considered him stricken, struck by God and afflicted.
And he was pierced for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities. The chastening that brought us peace was on him, and by his wound we were healed.
All of us like sheep have gone astray; each has turned to his own way. And the LORD made the iniquity of us all fall upon him.
He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, and he did not open his mouth. Like a sheep that is brought to the slaughter, and like a ewe that is silent before her shearers, he did not open his mouth.

By oppression and judgement he was taken away; and as for his generation — who gives it a thought? For he was cut off from the land of the living; because of the transgression of my people he was stricken.
And they assigned his grave with the wicked, and with a rich man in his death, though he had done no violence and there was no deceit in his mouth.
And the LORD desired to crush him; he made him sick. If his being makes a guilt offering, he will see offspring, he will prolong days; and the desire of the LORD will prosper in his hand.
From the labour of his being he will see; he will be satisfied. By his knowledge the righteous one, my servant, will justify the many, and he himself will carry their iniquities.

Therefore I will allot him a portion among the many, and with the mighty he will apportion plunder, because he poured out his being to death and was numbered with transgressors; and he himself bore the sin of many and makes intercession for the transgressors.

isaiah_54.t: Shout for joy, barren one who has not given birth! Break forth in a shout of joy and cry aloud, you who have not been in labour! For the children of the desolate one are more than the children of the married one, says the LORD.
Enlarge the place of your tent, and let them stretch out the curtains of your dwellings; do not hold back. Lengthen your tent cords and drive your tent pegs firm.
For you will spread out to the right and to the left, and your offspring will take possession of nations and will resettle desolated cities.

Do not be afraid, for you will not be put to shame; and do not be disgraced, for you will not be humiliated. For you will forget the shame of your youth, and the reproach of your widowhood you will not remember again.
For your husband is your maker — the LORD of hosts is his name — and your redeemer is the Holy One of Israel; the God of all the earth he is called.
For like a wife abandoned and grieved in spirit the LORD has called you, and like a wife of one's youth when she is rejected, says your God.
For a small moment I abandoned you, and with great compassion I will gather you.
In a flood of wrath I hid my face for a moment from you; but with everlasting steadfast love I will have compassion on you, says your redeemer, the LORD.
For this is like the waters of Noah to me: as I swore that the waters of Noah would not pass over the earth again, so I have sworn not to be angry with you and not to rebuke you.

For the mountains may be removed and the hills may shake, but my steadfast love will not be removed from you, and my covenant of peace will not shake, says the one who has compassion on you, the LORD.
Poor one, storm-tossed, not comforted: see, I am setting your stones in antimony and will lay your foundations with sapphires.
And I will make your battlements of ruby, and your gates of stones of beryl, and all your border of precious stones.
And all your children will be taught by the LORD, and great will be the peace of your children.
In righteousness you will be established. Be far from oppression, for you will not be afraid, and from terror, for it will not come near you.
See, if anyone quarrels, it is not from me; whoever quarrels with you will fall because of you.
See, I myself created the craftsman who blows on a fire of charcoal and brings out a weapon for its work; and I myself created the destroyer to ruin.

No weapon formed against you will succeed, and every tongue that rises against you in judgement you will condemn. This is the inheritance of the servants of the LORD, and their righteousness is from me, declares the LORD.

isaiah_55.t: Ah, every thirsty one, come to the waters! And the one who has no money — come, buy grain and eat! Come, buy grain without money and without price — wine and milk!
Why do you weigh out money for what is not bread, and your toil for what does not satisfy? Listen, listen to me and eat what is good, and let your being take delight in rich food.
Incline your ear and come to me; listen, and let your being live. And I will make with you an everlasting covenant, the faithful steadfast loves of David.
See, I made him a witness to peoples, a leader and a commander of peoples.
See, a nation you do not know you will call, and a nation that has not known you will run to you, because of the LORD your God and for the Holy One of Israel, for he has glorified you.
Seek the LORD while he lets himself be found; call on him while he is near.
Let the wicked forsake his way, and the man of wrongdoing his thoughts; and let him return to the LORD, and he will have compassion on him, and to our God, for he will abundantly forgive.
For my thoughts are not your thoughts, and your ways are not my ways, declares the LORD.
For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so my ways are higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts.
For as the rain and the snow come down from the heavens and do not return there until they have watered the earth and made it bring forth and sprout, giving seed to the sower and bread to the eater —
so will my word be that goes out from my mouth: it will not return to me empty, but will do what I have desired and prosper in what I sent it for.
For in joy you will go out, and in peace you will be led. The mountains and the hills will break forth before you in a shout of joy, and all the trees of the field will clap their hands.
In place of the thornbush a cypress will grow up, and in place of the nettle a myrtle will grow up. And it will be for the LORD a name, an everlasting sign that will not be cut off.

isaiah_56.t: Thus says the LORD: Keep justice and do righteousness; for my deliverance is near to come, and my righteousness to be revealed.
How blessed is the mortal who does this, and the child of humankind who takes hold of it: keeping the sabbath from profaning it, and keeping his hand from doing any evil.
And let not the foreigner who has joined himself to the LORD say: The LORD will surely separate me from his people. And let not the eunuch say: See, I am a dry tree.
For thus says the LORD to the eunuchs who keep my sabbaths and choose what I desire and take hold of my covenant:
I will give them in my house and within my walls a monument and a name, better than sons and daughters. An everlasting name I will give him that will not be cut off.

And the foreigners who join themselves to the LORD to serve him and to love the name of the LORD, to become his servants — every one who keeps the sabbath from profaning it and who takes hold of my covenant —

I will bring them to my holy mountain and make them rejoice in my house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and their sacrifices will be accepted on my altar; for my house will be called a house of prayer for all the peoples.
Declares the Lord GOD, who gathers the banished of Israel: I will gather still more to him, besides those of his already gathered.
All you animals of the field, come to devour — all you animals in the forest!
Its watchmen are blind, all of them; they know nothing. All of them are dumb dogs; they cannot bark — dreaming, lying down, loving to slumber.

And the dogs are greedy of being; they do not know satiety. And they are shepherds who do not know how to understand. All of them have turned to their own way, each to his own unjust gain, to the last of them.
Come, let me fetch wine, and let us drink our fill of strong drink! And tomorrow will be like this day — great, exceedingly abundant.

isaiah_57.t: The righteous one has perished, and there is no one who takes it to heart; and men of loyalty are taken away, with no one understanding that the righteous one is taken away from before the evil.
Peace will come; they will rest on their beds — each one who walks in his uprightness.
And you, draw near here, children of a soothsayer, offspring of an adulterer and of a prostitute!
At whom are you making fun? At whom do you open your mouth wide and stick out your tongue? Are you not children of transgression, offspring of deception?
you who inflame yourselves among the great trees, under every luxuriant tree, who slaughter the children in the wadis, under the clefts of the rocks.

Among the smooth stones of the wadi is your portion; they, they are your allotted portion. Even to them you have poured out a drink offering, you have offered up a grain offering. Shall I relent over these?
On a high and lofty mountain you have set your bed; there too you went up to offer sacrifice.

And behind the door and the doorpost you have set up your memorial. For away from me you have uncovered yourself and gone up; you have made your bed wide and made a bargain for yourself with them. You have loved their bed; you have gazed on nakedness.
And you journeyed to the king with oil and increased your perfumes. And you sent your envoys far off and brought yourself low as far as Sheol.
With the length of your journey you became weary; you did not say: It is hopeless. You found renewal of strength; therefore you did not become weak.
And of whom were you in dread and afraid, that you should lie and not remember me, not take it to heart? Is it not that I have been silent, even from long ago, and so you do not fear me?
I myself will declare your righteousness — and your deeds; and they will not benefit you.

When you cry out, let your collection of idols rescue you! But a wind will carry them all away; a vapour will take them. But the one who takes refuge in me will inherit the land and will possess my holy mountain.
And it will be said: Build up, build up! Clear the way! Lift the obstacle from the way of my people!

For thus says the high and lofty one, who dwells for ever, and whose name is holy: I dwell in a high and holy place, and with the contrite and lowly of spirit, to restore the spirit of the lowly and to restore the heart of the contrite.
For I will not contend for ever and will not be angry for all time; for the spirit would grow faint before me, and the breaths that I myself have made.
For the iniquity of his unjust gain I was angry, and I struck him, hiding myself, and was angry; and he went on, turning away, in the way of his own heart.
I have seen his ways, and I will heal him; and I will lead him and restore comforts to him and to his mourners.
creating the fruit of the lips: Peace, peace to the far off and to the near, says the LORD, and I will heal him.
But the wicked are like the tossing sea, for it cannot be quiet, and its waters toss up mire and mud.
There is no peace, says my God, for the wicked.

isaiah_58.t: Call out full-throated; do not hold back! Like the trumpet raise your voice, and declare to my people their transgression, and to the house of Jacob their sins.

And me they seek day by day, and they desire the knowledge of my ways, like a nation that has done righteousness and has not forsaken the judgement of its God. They ask me for righteous judgements; they desire the approach of God.
Why have we fasted, and you have not seen? We have humbled our being, and you do not notice. See, on the day of your fasting you pursue your own desire, and you drive hard all your labourers.
See, you fast for strife and contention and to strike with a wicked fist. You do not fast as you do this day if you want your voice heard on high.

Is a fast like this the one I choose, a day for a person to humble his being? Is it to bow his head like a bulrush and to spread sackcloth and ashes as a bed? Is this what you call a fast and a day of acceptance to the LORD?
Is not this the fast I choose: to loosen the bonds of wickedness, to unfasten the bindings of the yoke-bar, and to let the crushed go free, and that you tear apart every yoke-bar?
Is it not to break your bread for the hungry, and to bring the homeless poor into your house; when you see the naked, to cover him, and not to hide yourself from your own flesh?
Then your light will break forth like the dawn, and your healing will spring up quickly; and your righteousness will go before you; the glory of the LORD will be your rearguard.
Then you will call and the LORD will answer; you will cry for help and he will say: Here I am. If you remove the yoke-bar from among you, the pointing finger and the speaking of wrongdoing,
and you offer your very being to the hungry and satisfy the being of the afflicted, then your light will rise in the darkness, and your gloom will be like noon.
And the LORD will lead you continually and satisfy your being in arid regions and strengthen your bones. And you will be like a watered garden and like a spring of waters whose waters do not fail.

And some of you will rebuild the ancient waste places; you will raise up the foundations of generation after generation. And you will be called the repairer of the breach, the restorer of paths to dwell in.

If you turn back your foot from the sabbath, from doing your own desires on my holy day, and call the sabbath a delight, the holy day of the LORD honourable, and honour it by not going your own ways, not pursuing your desire or speaking idle words —
then you will take delight in the LORD, and I will make you ride on the heights of the land and feed you the inheritance of Jacob your father; for the mouth of the LORD has spoken.

isaiah_59.t: See, the hand of the LORD is not too short to deliver, and his ear is not too dull to hear.
But your iniquities have been separating between you and your God, and your sins have hidden his face from you, so that he does not hear.
For your hands are defiled with blood and your fingers with iniquity; your lips have spoken deception; your tongue mutters injustice.
There is no one who calls in righteousness, and no one who goes to judgement in trustworthiness. They trust in emptiness and speak worthlessness; they conceive mischief and bring forth wrongdoing.
They have hatched viper's eggs and weave spider's webs. Whoever eats any of their eggs will die, and the crushed egg hatches a snake.
Their webs will not become clothing, and no one will cover himself with what they make. What they make is the product of wrongdoing, and a deed of violence is in their hands.
Their feet run to evil, and they hasten to shed innocent blood. Their thoughts are thoughts of wrongdoing; devastation and destruction are on their highways.
A way of peace they do not know, and there is no justice on their tracks. Their paths they have made crooked for themselves; no one who treads on them knows peace.
Therefore justice is far from us, and righteousness does not reach us. We wait for the light, and see — darkness; for brightness, and we walk in gloom.
We grope for the wall like the blind, and like those with no eyes we grope. We stumble at noon as in the twilight; among the vigorous we are like the dead.
We all growl like bears, and like doves we moan and moan. We wait for justice, and there is none; for deliverance — it is far from us.
For our transgressions are many before you, and our sins have testified against us; for our transgressions are with us, and our iniquities — we know them.
Transgressing and denying the LORD, and turning back from following our God; speaking oppression and rebellion, conceiving and uttering from the heart words of deception.
And justice has been driven back, and righteousness stands far off; for truth has stumbled in the public square, and uprightness cannot enter.
And truth has become lacking, and the one who turns aside from evil is plundered. And the LORD saw, and it was evil in his eyes that there was no justice.
And he saw that there was no one, and he was appalled that there was no one to intervene. And his own arm brought him deliverance, and his own righteousness — it sustained him.
And he put on righteousness like body armour, and a helmet of deliverance on his head. And he put on garments of vengeance as clothing and wrapped himself in zeal like a robe.
According to their deeds, so he will repay: rage to his adversaries, requital to his enemies; to the coastlands he will repay requital.
And they will fear the name of the LORD from the west, and his glory from the rising of the sun; for he will come like a rushing stream that the wind of the LORD drives.
And a redeemer will come to Zion, and to those in Jacob who turn from transgression, declares the LORD.

And I — this is my covenant with them, says the LORD: my spirit that is on you, and my words that I have put in your mouth, will not depart from your mouth or from the mouth of your offspring or from the mouth of your offspring's offspring, says the LORD, from now and for ever.

isaiah_60.t: Arise, shine, for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD has dawned upon you.
For see, the darkness will cover the earth, and thick darkness the peoples; but upon you the LORD will dawn, and his glory will appear over you.
And nations will come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your dawn.
Lift up your eyes all around and see: all of them have gathered together; they have come to you. Your sons will come from far off, and your daughters will be carried on the hip.
Then you will see and be radiant, and your heart will throb and swell; for the abundance of the sea will be turned over to you, the wealth of nations will come to you.
A multitude of camels will cover you, the young camels of Midian and Ephah; all of them will come from Sheba. They will carry gold and frankincense and will bear news of the praises of the LORD.
Every flock of Kedar will be gathered to you; the rams of Nebaioth will serve you. They will go up on my altar and be accepted, and I will beautify my splendid house.
Who are these that fly like a cloud, and like doves to their cotes?

For the coastlands will wait for me, and the ships of Tarshish first of all, to bring your children from far off, their silver and their gold with them, for the name of the LORD your God and for the Holy One of Israel, for he has glorified you.
And foreigners will rebuild your walls, and their kings will serve you; for in my wrath I struck you, and in my favour I have had compassion on you.
And your gates will stand open continually; day and night they will not be shut, to bring to you the wealth of nations, with their kings led in.
For the nation and the kingdom that will not serve you will perish, and those nations will be utterly desolate.
The glory of Lebanon will come to you — the juniper, the plane and the cypress together — to beautify the place of my sanctuary; and I will glorify the place of my feet.

And the children of those who afflicted you will come to you bowing down, and all who despised you will bow down at the soles of your feet. And they will call you the City of the LORD, Zion of the Holy One of Israel.
In place of your being forsaken and hated, with no one passing through, I will make you an everlasting majesty, a joy of generation after generation.
And you will suck the milk of nations and suck the breast of kings; and you will know that I, the LORD, am your deliverer, and your redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.

In place of the bronze I will bring gold, and in place of the iron I will bring silver, and in place of the wood, bronze, and in place of the stones, iron. And I will make peace your overseer and righteousness your taskmaster.
Violence will no longer be heard in your land, nor devastation and destruction within your territories; and you will call your walls Deliverance and your gates Praise.
The sun will no longer be your light by day, and the moon will not shine on you for brightness; but the LORD will be for you an everlasting light, and your God your splendour.
Your sun will no longer go down, and your moon will not withdraw; for the LORD will be for you an everlasting light, and the days of your mourning will be complete.
And your people — all of them righteous — will possess the land for ever: the shoot of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may glorify myself.
The small one will become a thousand, and the little one a mighty nation. I am the LORD; in its time I will hasten it.

isaiah_61.t: The spirit of the Lord GOD is on me, because the LORD has anointed me to bear good news to the humble. He has sent me to bind up the broken-hearted, to proclaim liberty to captives and release to prisoners,
to proclaim the year of the LORD's favour and the day of our God's vengeance, to comfort all mourners,

to appoint for the mourners of Zion, to give them a turban in place of ashes, oil of rejoicing in place of mourning, a mantle of praise in place of a faint spirit; and they will be called the great trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he may glorify himself.
And they will rebuild the ancient waste places; they will raise up the former desolate places and renew the ruined cities, desolate for generation after generation.
And strangers will stand and shepherd your flocks, and foreigners will be your farmers and your vinedressers.
And you will be called the priests of the LORD; ministers of our God will be said of you. You will consume the wealth of nations, and in their glory you will boast.
In place of your shame — a double portion; and instead of ignominy they will shout for joy over their share. Therefore in their land they will possess double; everlasting joy will be theirs.
For I, the LORD, love justice; I hate robbery with injustice. And I will give their recompense in faithfulness and make an everlasting covenant with them.
And their offspring will be known among the nations, and their descendants in the midst of the peoples. All who see them will recognise them, that they are the offspring the LORD has blessed.

I will greatly rejoice in the LORD; my being will be glad in my God; for he has clothed me with garments of deliverance, has covered me with a robe of righteousness, like a bridegroom who wears his turban as a priest does, and like a bride who adorns herself with her ornaments.
For as the ground brings forth its growth, and as a garden makes what is sown in it grow, so the Lord GOD will make righteousness and praise grow before all the nations.

isaiah_62.t: For Zion's sake I will not be silent, and for Jerusalem's sake I will not remain quiet, until her righteousness goes forth like brightness and her deliverance burns like a torch.
And nations will see your righteousness, and all kings your glory; and you will be called by a new name that the mouth of the LORD will designate.
And you will be a crown of splendour in the hand of the LORD, and a royal headdress in the palm of your God.

It will no longer be said of you: Forsaken, and of your land it will no longer be said: Desolation. For you will be called My-Delight-Is-In-Her, and your land Married; for the LORD delights in you, and your land will be married.
For as a young man marries a virgin, your sons will marry you; and with the joy of a bridegroom over a bride, your God will rejoice over you.
On your walls, Jerusalem, I have appointed guards; all day and all night, continually, they will not be silent. You who bring the LORD to remembrance, take no rest!
And give him no rest until he establishes Jerusalem and makes her a praise in the earth.
The LORD has sworn by his right hand and by the arm of his power: I will never again give your grain as food to your enemies, and foreigners will not drink your new wine for which you have laboured.
For those who gather it will eat it and praise the LORD, and those who collect it will drink it in my holy courts.
Pass through, pass through the gates! Clear the way of the people! Build up, build up the highway; clear it of stones! Raise a standard over the peoples!
See, the LORD has proclaimed to the end of the earth: Say to the daughter of Zion: See, your deliverance is coming! See, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.
And they will be called the holy people, the redeemed of the LORD; and you will be called Sought-Out, a city not forsaken.

isaiah_63.t: Who is this coming from Edom, in garments stained red, from Bozrah? This one, magnificent in his clothing, marching in the greatness of his strength? It is I, speaking in righteousness, mighty to deliver.
Why is your clothing red, and your garments like one who treads in a winepress?

I have trodden the winepress alone, and from the peoples there was no one with me. And I trod them in my anger and trampled them in my rage, and their lifeblood spattered on my garments, and all my clothes I have stained.
For a day of vengeance was in my heart, and the year of my redemption had come.
And I looked, and there was no helper, and I was appalled that there was no sustainer. And my own arm brought me deliverance, and my rage — it sustained me.
And I trod down peoples in my anger and made them drunk in my rage, and I brought down their lifeblood to the ground.

I will bring to remembrance the steadfast loves of the LORD, the praises of the LORD, according to all that the LORD has dealt out to us, and the great goodness to the house of Israel that he has dealt out to them according to his compassion and the greatness of his steadfast loves.
And he said: Surely they are my people, children who will not deal falsely. And he became their deliverer.
In all their distress he was distressed, and the angel of his presence delivered them. In his love and in his mercy he redeemed them, and he lifted them and carried them all the days of old.
But they rebelled and grieved his holy spirit; and he turned himself into an enemy to them; he himself fought against them.
And he remembered the days of old, Moses and his people: Where is the one who brought them up from the sea with the shepherds of his flock? Where is the one who put his holy spirit in their midst,
who made the arm of his splendour go at the right hand of Moses, who split the waters before them, to make himself an everlasting name,
who made them walk through the deeps — like a horse in the wilderness, they did not stumble.
Like livestock that goes down into the valley, the spirit of the LORD gave them rest. So you led your people, to make yourself a name of splendour.
Look down from the heavens and see, from your holy and splendid abode! Where are your zeal and your mighty deeds, the stirring of your inward parts and your compassion? They are held back from me.
For you are our father, though Abraham does not know us and Israel does not acknowledge us. You, LORD, are our father; our redeemer from of old is your name.
Why, LORD, do you make us wander from your ways and harden our heart so that we do not fear you? Return, for the sake of your servants, the tribes of your inheritance!
For a little while your holy people possessed it; our adversaries have trodden down your sanctuary.
We have become like those you have never ruled over, like those on whom your name has never been called.

isaiah_64.t: If only you would tear open the heavens and come down — the mountains would shake before you!
As fire kindles brushwood, as fire makes water boil, to make your name known to your adversaries, so that nations would quake before you!
When you did awesome deeds we were not looking for, you came down; the mountains shook before you.
And from of old no one has heard, no one has given ear; no eye has seen a God besides you who acts for the one who waits for him.
You meet the one who rejoices and does righteousness, who remembers you in your ways. See, you were angry, and we sinned — in our sins for a long time — and shall we be delivered?
And we have all become like the unclean, and all our righteous acts like a menstrual garment. And we have all withered like a leaf, and our iniquities carry us off like the wind.
And there is no one who calls on your name, who rouses himself to take hold of you; for you have hidden your face from us and melted us away by the hand of our iniquity.
And now, LORD, you are our father. We are the clay, and you are the one who formed us, and all of us are the work of your hand.
Do not be angry, LORD, beyond measure, and do not remember iniquity for ever. See, look now — all of us are your people!
Your holy cities have become a wilderness; Zion has become a wilderness, Jerusalem a desolation.
Our holy and splendid house, where our fathers praised you, has been burned with fire; and all our pleasant things have become a ruin.
Over these will you restrain yourself, LORD? Will you be silent and afflict us beyond measure?

isaiah_65.t: I let myself be sought by those who did not ask; I let myself be found by those who did not seek me. I said: Here I am, here I am! to a nation not called by my name.
I spread out my hands all day long to a rebellious people who walk in the way that is not good, after their own thoughts —
the people who provoke me to anger to my face continually, sacrificing in the gardens and burning incense on the bricks,
who sit among the graves and spend the night in secret places, who eat the flesh of the pig, with broth of unclean meat in their vessels —
who say: Keep to yourself; do not come near me, for I am holier than you! These are smoke in my nose, a fire burning all day long.
See, it is written before me: I will not be silent, but I will repay; and I will repay into their bosom —
your iniquities and the iniquities of your fathers together, says the LORD, who burned incense on the mountains and taunted me on the hills. And I will measure their former work into their bosom.
Thus says the LORD: As the new wine is found in the cluster and one says: Do not destroy it, for a blessing is in it — so I will act for the sake of my servants, so as not to destroy them all.
And I will bring out offspring from Jacob, and from Judah a possessor of my mountains; and my chosen ones will take possession of it, and my servants will dwell there.
And Sharon will become a pasture for sheep, and the valley of Achor a resting place for cattle, for my people who have sought me.
But you who forsake the LORD, who forget my holy mountain, who spread a table for Fortune and fill bowls of mixed wine for Destiny —

I will appoint you for the sword, and all of you will bow down to the slaughter; because I called and you did not answer, I spoke and you did not listen, and you did what was evil in my eyes and chose what I did not desire.
Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: See, my servants will eat, but you will be hungry; see, my servants will drink, but you will be thirsty; see, my servants will rejoice, but you will be ashamed;
see, my servants will shout for joy from gladness of heart, but you will cry out from pain of heart and wail from brokenness of spirit.
and you will leave your name as a curse for my chosen ones. And the Lord GOD will put you to death, and he will call his servants by another name,

so that the one who blesses himself in the land will bless himself by the God of Amen, and the one who swears in the land will swear by the God of Amen; for the former troubles will be forgotten and hidden from my eyes.
For see, I am creating new heavens and a new earth; and the former things will not be remembered or come to mind.
But rejoice and be glad for ever in what I am creating; for see, I am creating Jerusalem a joy and her people a gladness.
And I will be glad in Jerusalem and rejoice in my people; and the sound of weeping will no longer be heard in her, nor the sound of a cry of distress.

There will no longer be there an infant of days, or an old one who does not complete his days; for the young man will die a hundred years old, and the one who fails to reach a hundred years will be cursed.
And they will build houses and dwell in them, and plant vineyards and eat their fruit.

They will not build and another dwell; they will not plant and another eat. For like the days of a tree will be the days of my people, and my chosen ones will enjoy to the full the work of their hands.
They will not labour for emptiness and will not bring forth children for sudden terror; for they are the offspring of those blessed by the LORD, and their descendants with them.
And it will be that before they call, I myself will answer; while they are still speaking, I myself will hear.

Wolf and lamb will graze as one, and the lion will eat straw like the ox, and as for the snake — dust will be its food. They will do no harm and will not destroy in all my holy mountain, says the LORD.

isaiah_66.t: Thus says the LORD: The heavens are my throne, and the earth my footstool. Where is this house that you would build for me, and where is this place of my rest?
And all these my hand made, and all these came to be, declares the LORD. And to this one I will look: to the poor and stricken in spirit and the one who trembles at my word.

The one who slaughters the ox is like one who strikes down a person; the one who sacrifices the lamb is like one who breaks a dog's neck; the one who offers up a grain offering is like one who offers the blood of a pig; the one who offers frankincense as a memorial is like one who blesses wrongdoing. They too have chosen their own ways, and their being has delighted in their detestable things.

I too will choose their punishments and bring their fears upon them; because I called and no one answered, I spoke and they did not listen, and they did what was evil in my eyes and chose what I did not desire.

Hear the word of the LORD, you who tremble at his word: Your brothers who hate you, who exclude you for my name's sake, have said: Let the LORD be honoured, that we may look on your joy! But they will be ashamed.
A sound of uproar from the city! A sound from the temple! The sound of the LORD repaying requital to his enemies!
Before she was in labour she gave birth; before the pain came to her she delivered a male child.

Who has heard the like of this? Who has seen the like of these? Can a land be brought forth in one day? Or can a nation be born in a single moment? For Zion was in labour and also gave birth to her children.
Shall I bring to the birth and not deliver? says the LORD. Or am I the one who delivers, and shall I close the womb? says your God.
Rejoice with Jerusalem and be glad in her, all who love her! Rejoice with her a rejoicing, all who mourn over her!
so that you may suck and be satisfied from the breast of her consolations, so that you may drain and take delight from the breast of her glory.
For thus says the LORD: See, I am extending peace to her like a river, and the wealth of nations like an overflowing torrent; and you will suck, be carried on the hip and be dandled on the knees.
Like a person whose mother comforts him, so I myself will comfort you; and in Jerusalem you will be comforted.
And you will see, and your heart will rejoice, and your bones will sprout like grass; and the hand of the LORD will be made known to his servants, and his indignation against his enemies.
For see, the LORD will come in fire, and his chariots like the storm-wind, to render his anger in rage and his rebuke in flames of fire.
For by fire the LORD will enter into judgement, and by his sword, with all flesh; and those slain by the LORD will be many.

Those who consecrate themselves and cleanse themselves for the gardens, following one in the middle, eating the flesh of the pig and the detestable thing and the mouse — they will come to an end together, declares the LORD.
And I know their deeds and their thoughts; the time is coming to gather all the nations and tongues; and they will come and see my glory.

And I will perform a sign among them and send survivors from them to the nations — Tarshish, Pul and Lud, who draw the bow, Tubal and Javan, the distant coastlands that have not heard my report and have not seen my glory — and they will declare my glory among the nations.

And they will bring all your brothers from all the nations as an offering to the LORD — on horses and in chariots and in wagons and on mules and on camels — to my holy mountain, Jerusalem, says the LORD, just as the Israelites bring the grain offering in a clean vessel to the house of the LORD.
And I will also take some of them for the priests, for the Levites, says the LORD.
For just as the new heavens and the new earth that I am making endure before me, declares the LORD, so your offspring and your name will endure.
And it will be that from new moon to new moon and from sabbath to sabbath, all flesh will come to bow down before me, says the LORD.

And they will go out and look on the corpses of the people who transgressed against me; for their worm will not die and their fire will not be extinguished, and they will be an abhorrence to all flesh.

judges_1.t: After the death of Joshua the Israelites enquired of the LORD, "Who shall go up for us against the Canaanites first, to fight against them?"
The LORD said, "Judah shall go up. See, I have given the land into his hand."
Judah said to Simeon his brother, "Come up with me into my allotted territory, and let us fight against the Canaanites, and I too will go with you into yours." So Simeon went with him.
Judah went up, and the LORD gave the Canaanites and the Perizzites into their hand, and they struck down ten thousand men at Bezek.
They found Adoni-bezek at Bezek and fought against him, and they struck down the Canaanites and the Perizzites.
Adoni-bezek fled, but they pursued him and caught him, and they cut off his thumbs and his big toes.
Adoni-bezek said, "Seventy kings with their thumbs and big toes cut off used to gather scraps under my table. As I have done, so God has repaid me." They brought him to Jerusalem, and he died there.
The men of Judah fought against Jerusalem and captured it, and they struck it with the edge of the sword and set the city on fire.
Afterwards the men of Judah went down to fight against the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, the Negev, and the Shephelah.
Judah went against the Canaanites who lived in Hebron (the name of Hebron was formerly Kiriath-arba), and they struck down Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.
From there he went against the inhabitants of Debir (the name of Debir was formerly Kiriath-sepher).
Caleb said, "Whoever strikes Kiriath-sepher and captures it, to him I will give Achsah my daughter as a wife."
Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, captured it, and Caleb gave him Achsah his daughter as a wife.
When she came to him, she urged him to ask her father for a field. She dismounted from her donkey, and Caleb said to her, "What do you want?"
She said to him, "Give me a blessing. Since you have given me the land of the Negev, give me also springs of water." So Caleb gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.

The descendants of the Kenite, Moses' father-in-law, went up from the city of palms with the men of Judah to the wilderness of Judah, which lies in the Negev of Arad; and they went and settled with the people.
Judah went with Simeon his brother, and they struck the Canaanites who lived in Zephath and devoted it to destruction; and the city was named Hormah.
Judah captured Gaza with its territory, Ashkelon with its territory, and Ekron with its territory.
The LORD was with Judah, and he took possession of the hill country, but he could not dispossess the inhabitants of the valley, because they had chariots of iron.
They gave Hebron to Caleb, as Moses had said, and he dispossessed from there the three sons of Anak.
The Benjaminites did not dispossess the Jebusites who lived in Jerusalem; so the Jebusites have lived with the Benjaminites in Jerusalem to this day.
The house of Joseph also went up, against Beth-el, and the LORD was with them.
The house of Joseph sent spies to Beth-el (the name of the city was formerly Luz).
The watchers saw a man coming out of the city and said to him, "Show us the way into the city, and we will deal loyally with you."
He showed them the way into the city, and they struck the city with the edge of the sword, but they let the man and all his family go.
The man went to the land of the Hittites and built a city and named it Luz; that is its name to this day.

Manasseh did not dispossess Beth-shean and its villages, or Taanach and its villages, or the inhabitants of Dor and its villages, or the inhabitants of Ibleam and its villages, or the inhabitants of Megiddo and its villages; the Canaanites were determined to remain in this land.
When Israel grew strong, it put the Canaanites to forced labour, but it did not actually dispossess them.
Ephraim did not dispossess the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, and the Canaanites lived among them in Gezer.
Zebulun did not dispossess the inhabitants of Kitron or the inhabitants of Nahalol, and the Canaanites lived among them and became forced labour.
Asher did not dispossess the inhabitants of Acco or the inhabitants of Sidon, or Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, or Rehob.
So the Asherites lived among the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land, because they did not dispossess them.

Naphtali did not dispossess the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh or the inhabitants of Beth-anath, and they lived among the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land; but the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath became forced labour for them.
The Amorites pressed the Danites back into the hill country, for they did not allow them to come down to the valley.
The Amorites were determined to remain in Mount Heres, in Aijalon, and in Shaalbim; but the hand of the house of Joseph lay heavy on them, and they became forced labour.
The border of the Amorites ran from the ascent of Akrabbim, from Sela upward.

judges_2.t: The angel of the LORD went up from Gilgal to Bokim and said, "I brought you up from Egypt and brought you into the land I swore to your ancestors, and I said, 'I will never break my covenant with you.
"'And you shall not make a covenant with the inhabitants of this land; you shall pull down their altars.' But you have not listened to my voice. What is this you have done?"
"So I also say, I will not drive them out from before you; they shall become adversaries at your side, and their gods shall become a snare to you."
When the angel of the LORD had spoken these words to all the Israelites, the people lifted up their voice and wept.
So they named that place Bokim, and they sacrificed there to the LORD.
When Joshua sent the people away, the Israelites went, each to his own inheritance, to take possession of the land.
The people served the LORD all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders who outlived Joshua, who had seen all the great work of the LORD that he had done for Israel.
Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died at the age of a hundred and ten.
They buried him in the territory of his inheritance, at Timnath-heres in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
That whole generation also was gathered to their ancestors, and another generation arose after them who did not know the LORD, or the work he had done for Israel.
The Israelites did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and they served the Baals.

They forsook the LORD, the God of their ancestors, who had brought them out of the land of Egypt, and went after other gods from among the gods of the peoples around them, and they bowed down to them and provoked the LORD to anger.
They forsook the LORD and served the Baal and the Ashtaroth.

The anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he gave them into the hand of plunderers who plundered them, and he sold them into the hand of their enemies all around, so that they could no longer stand before their enemies.
Wherever they went out, the hand of the LORD was against them for harm, just as the LORD had said and just as the LORD had sworn to them; and they were greatly distressed.
Then the LORD raised up judges, who delivered them from the hand of those who plundered them.

Yet they did not listen to their judges either, for they prostituted themselves after other gods and bowed down to them. They turned aside quickly from the way their ancestors had walked in obeying the commandments of the LORD; they did not do as they had done.

Whenever the LORD raised up judges for them, the LORD was with the judge and delivered them from the hand of their enemies all the days of that judge; for the LORD was moved to compassion by their groaning under those who oppressed and crushed them.

But when the judge died, they would turn back and act more corruptly than their ancestors, going after other gods to serve them and bow down to them. They did not give up any of their practices or their stubborn way.
So the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he said, "Because this nation has transgressed my covenant, which I commanded their ancestors, and has not listened to my voice,
"I also will no longer dispossess before them any of the nations that Joshua left when he died."
so as to test Israel by them, whether they will keep the way of the LORD and walk in it as their ancestors did, or not.
So the LORD left these nations, not dispossessing them quickly, and he had not given them into the hand of Joshua.

judges_3.t: These are the nations the LORD left, to test Israel by them — all those who had not known any of the wars of Canaan;
only so that the generations of the Israelites might know war, to teach it to them — only those who had not known it before.
the five lords of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites who lived in the Lebanon mountains, from Mount Baal-hermon as far as Lebo-hamath.
They were there to test Israel by them, to know whether they would obey the commandments of the LORD that he had commanded their ancestors through Moses.
The Israelites lived among the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
They took their daughters as wives for themselves, gave their own daughters to their sons, and served their gods.
The Israelites did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD; they forgot the LORD their God and served the Baals and the Asherahs.
The anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram-naharaim, and the Israelites served Cushan-rishathaim eight years.
Then the Israelites cried out to the LORD, and the LORD raised up a deliverer for the Israelites who delivered them: Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother.
The spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he judged Israel and went out to war; and the LORD gave Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram into his hand, and his hand prevailed over Cushan-rishathaim.
And the land had rest for forty years; then Othniel son of Kenaz died.
The Israelites again did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD strengthened Eglon king of Moab against Israel, because they did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.
He gathered the Ammonites and Amalek to himself, and went and struck Israel, and they took possession of the city of palms.
The Israelites served Eglon king of Moab eighteen years.

Then the Israelites cried out to the LORD, and the LORD raised up for them a deliverer, Ehud son of Gera, the Benjaminite, a man impeded in his right hand. The Israelites sent tribute by his hand to Eglon king of Moab.
Ehud made himself a sword with two edges, a gomed in length, and he strapped it under his clothes on his right thigh.
He presented the tribute to Eglon king of Moab. Now Eglon was a very fat man.
When he had finished presenting the tribute, he sent away the people who had carried it.
But he himself turned back at the images near Gilgal and said, "I have a secret word for you, O king." And the king said, "Silence!" And all who stood by him went out from his presence.
Ehud came to him while he was sitting alone in his cool roof chamber. Ehud said, "I have a word of God for you." And he rose from his seat.
Ehud reached with his left hand, took the sword from his right thigh, and thrust it into his belly.
The hilt went in after the blade, and the fat closed over the blade, for he did not draw the sword out of his belly; and the dung came out.
Then Ehud went out to the porch, and he shut the doors of the roof chamber behind him and locked them.
When he had gone out, the king's servants came and looked, and there were the doors of the roof chamber, locked. They said, "He must be covering his feet in the cool chamber."
They waited until they were ashamed, and still he did not open the doors of the roof chamber. So they took the key and opened them, and there was their lord fallen to the ground, dead.
Ehud escaped while they delayed. He passed by the images and escaped to Seirah.
When he arrived, he blew the ram's horn in the hill country of Ephraim, and the Israelites went down with him from the hill country, with him at their head.

He said to them, "Follow me, for the LORD has given your enemies, Moab, into your hand." So they went down after him and captured the fords of the Jordan toward Moab, and they did not let anyone cross over.
At that time they struck down about ten thousand men of Moab, every stout one and every able man; and not one escaped.
So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel, and the land had rest for eighty years.
After him came Shamgar son of Anath, who struck down six hundred Philistines with an ox goad; and he also delivered Israel.

judges_4.t: The Israelites again did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, now that Ehud was dead.
So the LORD sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor. The commander of his army was Sisera, who lived in Harosheth-hagoyim.
Then the Israelites cried out to the LORD, for he had nine hundred chariots of iron, and he had oppressed the Israelites harshly for twenty years.
Now Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, was judging Israel at that time.
She used to sit under the Palm of Deborah between Ramah and Beth-el in the hill country of Ephraim, and the Israelites went up to her for judgement.

She sent and summoned Barak son of Abinoam from Kedesh-naphtali and said to him, "Has not the LORD, the God of Israel, commanded you: Go, march to Mount Tabor, and take with you ten thousand men from Naphtali and from Zebulun?"
"And I will draw Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army, with his chariots and his troops, to you at the wadi Kishon, and I will give him into your hand."
Barak said to her, "If you will go with me, I will go; but if you will not go with me, I will not go."

She said, "I will certainly go with you; but the honour will not be yours on the way you are going, for the LORD will sell Sisera into the hand of a woman." Then Deborah rose and went with Barak to Kedesh.
Barak called Zebulun and Naphtali up to Kedesh, and ten thousand men went up behind him; and Deborah went up with him.
Now Heber the Kenite had separated from the Kenites, from the descendants of Hobab, Moses' father-in-law, and had pitched his tent as far away as the great tree in Zaanannim, which is near Kedesh.
They told Sisera that Barak son of Abinoam had gone up to Mount Tabor.
So Sisera called out all his chariots, nine hundred chariots of iron, and all the troops with him, from Harosheth-hagoyim to the wadi Kishon.

Deborah said to Barak, "Get up, for this is the day on which the LORD has given Sisera into your hand. Has not the LORD gone out before you?" So Barak went down from Mount Tabor with ten thousand men after him.
And the LORD routed Sisera and all his chariots and all his army with the edge of the sword before Barak; and Sisera got down from his chariot and fled on foot.
Barak pursued the chariots and the army as far as Harosheth-hagoyim, and the whole army of Sisera fell by the edge of the sword; not one was left.
Sisera fled on foot to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, for there was peace between Jabin king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite.
Jael went out to meet Sisera and said to him, "Turn aside, my lord, turn aside to me; do not be afraid." So he turned aside to her, into the tent, and she covered him with a rug.
He said to her, "Please give me a little water to drink, for I am thirsty." So she opened a skin of milk, gave him a drink, and covered him again.
He said to her, "Stand at the entrance of the tent, and if anyone comes and asks you, 'Is there a man here?' say, 'No one.'"

But Jael, Heber's wife, took a tent peg and took the hammer in her hand, and she came to him quietly and drove the peg through his temple, and it went down into the ground; and he was fast asleep and exhausted, and he died.

Just then Barak came, pursuing Sisera, and Jael went out to meet him and said to him, "Come, and I will show you the man you are seeking." He came to her, and there was Sisera, fallen dead, with the peg in his temple.
So on that day God subdued Jabin king of Canaan before the Israelites.
The hand of the Israelites pressed harder and harder against Jabin king of Canaan, until they cut off Jabin king of Canaan.

judges_5.t: On that day Deborah sang, and Barak son of Abinoam, saying:
When the leaders took the lead in Israel, when the people offered themselves freely — bless the LORD!
Hear, O kings! Give ear, O rulers! I, to the LORD, I — I will sing, I will make music to the LORD, the God of Israel.
LORD, when you went out from Seir, when you marched from the country of Edom, the earth shook, the heavens also dripped, the clouds also dripped water.
The mountains flowed down before the LORD — this Sinai — before the LORD, the God of Israel.
In the days of Shamgar son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the caravans ceased, and travellers on the paths went by twisting roads.
The villagers ceased in Israel, they ceased, until I arose, Deborah, until I arose, a mother in Israel.
New gods were chosen; then — war at the gates. Was shield or spear to be seen among forty thousand in Israel?
My heart goes out to the commanders of Israel, who offered themselves freely among the people — bless the LORD!
You who ride tawny she-asses, you who sit on rich carpets, and you who walk the road — tell it out!

From the sound of those who parcel out the flocks among the watering places, there they recount the righteous acts of the LORD, the righteous acts of his villagers in Israel. Then the people of the LORD went down to the gates.
Awake, awake, Deborah! Awake, awake, break into song! Arise, Barak, and take your captives captive, son of Abinoam!
Then the survivors came down to the nobles; the people of the LORD came down to me as warriors.
From Ephraim, their root in Amalek; after you, Benjamin, among your peoples; from Machir the commanders went down, and from Zebulun those who wield the muster-officer's staff.
My princes in Issachar were with Deborah; and Issachar, so Barak — into the valley he was sent at his heels. Among the divisions of Reuben there were great resolves of heart.
Why did you sit among the sheepfolds, listening to the whistling for the flocks? Among the divisions of Reuben there were great searchings of heart.
Gilead stayed beyond the Jordan; and Dan — why did he linger by the ships? Asher remained at the seashore and settled by his landings.
Zebulun is a people that scorned its own life to the point of death, and Naphtali too, on the heights of the open country.
Kings came and fought; then the kings of Canaan fought at Taanach, by the waters of Megiddo. They took no plunder of silver.
From heaven they fought; the stars from their courses fought against Sisera.
The wadi Kishon swept them away, that ancient wadi, the wadi Kishon. March on, my soul, in strength!
Then the hooves of the horses hammered from the galloping, the galloping of his stallions.
"Curse Meroz," says the angel of the LORD, "utterly curse her inhabitants, for they did not come to the help of the LORD, to the help of the LORD among the mighty."
Most blessed of women be Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite; of women in the tent, most blessed.
He asked for water; she gave milk. In a lordly bowl she brought him curds.
She stretched out her hand to the tent peg, her right hand to the workmen's hammer; she struck Sisera, she shattered his head, she smashed and pierced his temple.
Between her feet he sank, he fell, he lay; between her feet he sank, he fell; where he sank, there he fell, destroyed.
Through the window she looked out and wailed, the mother of Sisera, through the lattice: "Why is his chariot so long in coming? Why do the hoofbeats of his chariots delay?"
The wisest of her noble ladies answer her — indeed, she returns her own sayings to herself:

"Are they not finding and dividing the spoil? — a womb, two wombs for the head of each man; spoil of dyed cloths for Sisera, spoil of dyed cloths, embroidered, a dyed cloth, two embroidered cloths, for the necks of the spoil."
So may all your enemies perish, LORD; and may those who love him be like the sun going out in its strength. And the land had rest for forty years.

judges_6.t: The Israelites did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD gave them into the hand of Midian for seven years.
The hand of Midian prevailed over Israel, and because of Midian the Israelites made for themselves the dens that are in the mountains, and the caves and the strongholds.
Whenever Israel sowed, Midian would come up, and Amalek and the people of the east, and they would come up against them.
They would encamp against them and destroy the produce of the land as far as Gaza, and they would leave no sustenance in Israel, and no sheep or ox or donkey.
For they and their livestock would come up, with their tents, and they would come in like locusts for multitude — they and their camels beyond counting — and they came into the land to destroy it.
So Israel was brought very low because of Midian, and the Israelites cried out to the LORD.
When the Israelites cried out to the LORD on account of Midian,
the LORD sent a prophet to the Israelites, and he said to them, "Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: I brought you up from Egypt and brought you out from a house of slaves.
"I delivered you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of all who oppressed you; I drove them out from before you and gave you their land.
"And I said to you, 'I am the LORD your God; you shall not fear the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you are dwelling.' But you have not listened to my voice."
The angel of the LORD came and sat under the oak in Ophrah, which belonged to Joash the Abiezrite; and Gideon his son was beating out wheat in the winepress, to hide it from Midian.
The angel of the LORD appeared to him and said to him, "The LORD is with you, mighty man of valour."

Gideon said to him, "Pardon me, my lord — but if the LORD is with us, why has all this come upon us? And where are all his wonders that our ancestors told us of, saying, 'Did not the LORD bring us up from Egypt?' But now the LORD has abandoned us and given us into the grip of Midian."
The LORD turned to him and said, "Go in this strength of yours, and you shall deliver Israel from the grip of Midian. Have I not sent you?"
He said to him, "Pardon me, my Lord — with what shall I deliver Israel? See, my clan is the weakest in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father's house."
The LORD said to him, "I will be with you, and you shall strike down Midian as one man."
He said to him, "If I have found favour in your eyes, then give me a sign that it is you who are speaking with me.
"Please do not depart from here until I come back to you and bring out my gift and set it before you." And he said, "I will stay until you return."
Gideon went and prepared a young goat, and an ephah of flour as unleavened bread. He put the meat in a basket and the broth in a pot, and brought them out to him under the oak and presented them.
The angel of God said to him, "Take the meat and the unleavened bread and set them on this rock, and pour out the broth." And he did so.

The angel of the LORD stretched out the end of the staff in his hand and touched the meat and the unleavened bread, and fire went up from the rock and consumed the meat and the unleavened bread. And the angel of the LORD vanished from his sight.
Then Gideon saw that it was the angel of the LORD, and Gideon said, "Alas, Lord GOD! For I have seen the angel of the LORD face to face."
But the LORD said to him, "Peace to you. Do not fear; you shall not die."
So Gideon built an altar there to the LORD and called it 'The LORD is peace'. To this day it is still in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
That night the LORD said to him, "Take your father's bull, the second bull, seven years old, and tear down the altar of the Baal that belongs to your father, and cut down the Asherah beside it.

"And you shall build an altar to the LORD your God on the top of this stronghold, in an ordered arrangement; and you shall take the second bull and offer it up as a burnt offering with the wood of the Asherah you cut down."
So Gideon took ten men from his servants and did as the LORD had told him; but because he was too afraid of his father's household and the men of the city to do it by day, he did it by night.
When the men of the city rose early in the morning, there was the altar of the Baal torn down, and the Asherah beside it cut down, and the second bull offered up on the altar that had been built.
They said to one another, "Who has done this thing?" And when they investigated and searched, they said, "Gideon son of Joash has done this thing."
The men of the city said to Joash, "Bring out your son, and let him die, for he has torn down the altar of the Baal and cut down the Asherah beside it."

But Joash said to all who stood against him, "Will you contend for the Baal? Or will you deliver him? Whoever contends for him shall be put to death by morning. If he is a god, let him contend for himself, because someone has torn down his altar."
So on that day he called him Jerubbaal, saying, "Let the Baal contend against him, because he has torn down his altar."
Now all Midian and Amalek and the people of the east gathered together, crossed over, and encamped in the valley of Jezreel.
And the spirit of the LORD clothed Gideon, and he blew the ram's horn, and Abiezer was called out after him.
He sent messengers throughout all Manasseh, and they too were called out after him; and he sent messengers to Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, and they went up to meet them.
Then Gideon said to God, "If you are going to deliver Israel by my hand, as you have said —

"see, I am setting the fleece of wool on the threshing floor. If there is dew on the fleece alone and all the ground is dry, then I shall know that you will deliver Israel by my hand, as you have said."
And it was so. He rose early the next day and squeezed the fleece, and wrung dew from the fleece — a bowlful of water.

Then Gideon said to God, "Do not let your anger burn against me; let me speak just this once. Let me test just once more with the fleece: let the fleece alone be dry, and let there be dew on all the ground."
And God did so that night: the fleece alone was dry, and there was dew on all the ground.

judges_7.t: Jerubbaal — that is, Gideon — rose early, and all the people with him, and they encamped at En-harod; and the camp of Midian was north of him, by the hill of Moreh, in the valley.
The LORD said to Gideon, "The people with you are too many for me to give Midian into their hand, lest Israel glorify itself over me, saying, 'My own hand has delivered me.'
"Now proclaim in the hearing of the people: Whoever is afraid and trembling, let him turn back and leave Mount Gilead." And twenty-two thousand of the people turned back, and ten thousand remained.

The LORD said to Gideon, "There are still too many people. Bring them down to the water, and I will refine them for you there. Whoever I say to you, 'This one shall go with you' — he shall go with you; and everyone I say to you, 'This one shall not go with you' — he shall not go."

So he brought the people down to the water, and the LORD said to Gideon, "Everyone who laps the water with his tongue, as a dog laps, set apart by himself; and everyone who bows down on his knees to drink."
The number of those who lapped, with their hand to their mouth, was three hundred men; all the rest of the people bowed down on their knees to drink water.
The LORD said to Gideon, "By the three hundred men who lapped I will deliver you, and I will give Midian into your hand; and let all the rest of the people go, each to his own place."

So they took the people's provisions in their hand, and their ram's horns; and he sent every man of Israel away, each to his tents, and kept hold of the three hundred men. The camp of Midian was below him, in the valley.
That night the LORD said to him, "Get up, go down into the camp, for I have given it into your hand.
"But if you are afraid to go down, go down with Purah your servant to the camp,

"and you shall hear what they say; afterwards your hands will be strengthened, and you shall go down into the camp." So he went down with Purah his servant to the edge of the armed men who were in the camp.
Midian and Amalek and all the people of the east lay in the valley like locusts for multitude; their camels were beyond counting, like the sand on the seashore for multitude.

Gideon came, and there was a man recounting a dream to his neighbour. He said, "I have dreamed a dream: a round loaf of barley bread was tumbling into the camp of Midian, and it came to the tent and struck it so that it fell, and turned it upside down, and the tent fell flat."
His neighbour answered, "This is nothing but the sword of Gideon son of Joash, a man of Israel. God has given Midian and all the camp into his hand."

When Gideon heard the recounting of the dream and its interpretation, he bowed down. Then he returned to the camp of Israel and said, "Get up, for the LORD has given the camp of Midian into your hand."
He divided the three hundred men into three companies and put ram's horns into the hand of all of them, and empty jars with torches inside the jars.
He said to them, "Watch me, and do the same. When I come to the edge of the camp, then as I do, so you shall do.
"When I blow the ram's horn, I and all who are with me, then you also shall blow the ram's horns all around the whole camp, and you shall say, 'For the LORD and for Gideon!'"

Gideon came, and the hundred men with him, to the edge of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch, just after the watch had been posted; and they blew the ram's horns and smashed the jars in their hand.

The three companies blew the ram's horns and broke the jars; they held the torches in their left hand and the ram's horns in their right hand to blow, and they called out, "A sword for the LORD and for Gideon!"
They stood, each in his place, all around the camp; and the whole camp ran, and they cried out and fled.

The three hundred blew the ram's horns, and the LORD set every man's sword against his neighbour throughout all the camp; and the camp fled as far as Beth-shittah toward Zererah, as far as the border of Abel-meholah, by Tabbath.
The men of Israel were called out from Naphtali, from Asher, and from all Manasseh, and they pursued Midian.

Gideon sent messengers throughout all the hill country of Ephraim, saying, "Come down to meet Midian, and capture the waters ahead of them as far as Beth-barah, and the Jordan." So every man of Ephraim was called out, and they captured the waters as far as Beth-barah, and the Jordan.

They captured the two commanders of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb; they killed Oreb at the rock of Oreb, and Zeeb they killed at the winepress of Zeeb. Then they pursued Midian, and they brought the head of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon from across the Jordan.

judges_8.t: The men of Ephraim said to him, "What is this you have done to us, not calling us when you went to fight against Midian?" And they quarrelled with him bitterly.
He said to them, "What have I now done compared with you? Are not Ephraim's gleanings better than Abiezer's vintage?
"Into your hand God has given the commanders of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb. And what have I been able to do compared with you?" Then their spirit toward him relaxed when he said this.
Gideon came to the Jordan and crossed over, he and the three hundred men with him — exhausted, and still pursuing.
He said to the men of Succoth, "Please give loaves of bread to the people who follow me, for they are exhausted, and I am pursuing Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian."
But the officials of Succoth said, "Is the hand of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your grasp, that we should give bread to your army?"
Gideon said, "Very well — when the LORD gives Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, I will thresh your flesh with the thorns of the wilderness and with briers."
He went up from there to Penuel and spoke to them in the same way, and the men of Penuel answered him just as the men of Succoth had answered.
So he said also to the men of Penuel, "When I return in peace, I will tear down this tower."

Now Zebah and Zalmunna were at Karkor with their armies, about fifteen thousand, all who remained of the whole army of the people of the east; and those who had fallen were a hundred and twenty thousand men who drew the sword.
Gideon went up by the route of those who dwell in tents, east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and struck the camp while the camp was off its guard.
Zebah and Zalmunna fled, and he pursued them and captured the two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna, and routed the whole army.
Gideon son of Joash returned from the battle by the ascent of Heres.
He captured a young man from the men of Succoth and questioned him, and the young man wrote down for him the officials of Succoth and its elders, seventy-seven men.

Then he came to the men of Succoth and said, "Here are Zebah and Zalmunna, about whom you taunted me, saying, 'Is the hand of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your grasp, that we should give bread to your weary men?'"
So he took the elders of the city, and the thorns of the wilderness and the briers, and with them he taught the men of Succoth a lesson.
He tore down the tower of Penuel and killed the men of the city.
Then he said to Zebah and Zalmunna, "Where are the men you killed at Tabor?" They said, "As you are, so were they — each one like the form of a king's sons."
He said, "They were my brothers, the sons of my mother. As the LORD lives, if you had let them live, I would not kill you."
Then he said to Jether his firstborn, "Get up, kill them." But the young man did not draw his sword, for he was afraid, because he was still only a boy.

Then Zebah and Zalmunna said, "Rise yourself and fall upon us, for as the man is, so is his strength." So Gideon rose and killed Zebah and Zalmunna, and he took the crescents that were on their camels' necks.
Then the men of Israel said to Gideon, "Rule over us — you, and your son, and your son's son — for you have delivered us from the hand of Midian."
