But Gideon said to them, "I will not rule over you, and my son will not rule over you. The LORD will rule over you."
Then Gideon said to them, "Let me make one request of you: each of you give me the earring from his plunder." (For they had earrings of gold, because they were Ishmaelites.)
They said, "We will gladly give them." And they spread out a garment, and each man threw there the earring from his plunder.

The weight of the gold earrings he asked for was a thousand seven hundred shekels of gold, apart from the crescents, the pendants, and the purple garments that were on the kings of Midian, and apart from the necklaces on their camels' necks.
Gideon made it into an ephod and set it up in his city, in Ophrah; and all Israel prostituted themselves after it there, and it became a snare to Gideon and to his household.
So Midian was subdued before the Israelites and did not lift up its head again; and the land had rest for forty years in the days of Gideon.
Jerubbaal son of Joash went and lived in his own house.
Gideon had seventy sons who came from his own body, for he had many wives.
And his concubine who was in Shechem also bore him a son, and he gave him the name Abimelech.
Gideon son of Joash died at a good old age and was buried in the tomb of Joash his father, in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
As soon as Gideon was dead, the Israelites turned back and prostituted themselves after the Baals, and they made Baal-berith their god.
The Israelites did not remember the LORD their God, who had delivered them from the hand of all their enemies all around.
And they did not deal loyally with the house of Jerubbaal, that is Gideon, in return for all the good he had done for Israel.

judges_9.t: Abimelech son of Jerubbaal went to Shechem, to his mother's brothers, and spoke to them and to all the clan of his mother's father's house, saying,
"Ask all the lords of Shechem: 'Which is better for you, that seventy men, all the sons of Jerubbaal, rule over you, or that one man rule over you?' And remember that I am your own bone and flesh."
His mother's brothers spoke about him in the hearing of all the lords of Shechem, all these words; and their heart turned after Abimelech, for they said, "He is our brother."
They gave him seventy pieces of silver from the house of Baal-berith, and with them Abimelech hired worthless and reckless men, and they followed him.
He came to his father's house at Ophrah and killed his brothers, the sons of Jerubbaal, seventy men, on one stone. But Jotham, the youngest son of Jerubbaal, was left, for he had hidden himself.
Then all the lords of Shechem and all Beth-millo gathered, and they went and made Abimelech king, by the great tree of the pillar in Shechem.
When they told Jotham, he went and stood on the top of Mount Gerizim, lifted up his voice, and called out. He said to them, "Listen to me, lords of Shechem, and may God listen to you."
"Once the trees went out to anoint a king over them; and they said to the olive tree, 'Reign over us.'
"But the olive tree said to them, 'Shall I give up my fatness, by which gods and men are honoured, and go to sway over the trees?'
"Then the trees said to the fig tree, 'Come, you reign over us.'
"But the fig tree said to them, 'Shall I give up my sweetness and my good fruit, and go to sway over the trees?'
"Then the trees said to the vine, 'Come, you reign over us.'
"But the vine said to them, 'Shall I give up my new wine, which gladdens gods and men, and go to sway over the trees?'
"Then all the trees said to the bramble, 'Come, you reign over us.'

"And the bramble said to the trees, 'If in faithfulness you are anointing me king over you, come and take refuge in my shade; but if not, let fire go out from the bramble and consume the cedars of Lebanon.'
"Now then, if you have acted in faithfulness and integrity in making Abimelech king, and if you have dealt well with Jerubbaal and his house, and if you have done to him as his hands deserved —
"— for my father fought for you and threw his life away in front of him, and he delivered you from the hand of Midian;

"and you have risen up against my father's house this day and killed his sons, seventy men, on one stone, and made Abimelech, the son of his female slave, king over the lords of Shechem, because he is your brother —
"if you have acted in faithfulness and integrity with Jerubbaal and his house this day, then rejoice in Abimelech, and let him also rejoice in you.
"But if not, let fire go out from Abimelech and consume the lords of Shechem and Beth-millo, and let fire go out from the lords of Shechem and from Beth-millo and consume Abimelech."
Then Jotham fled and ran away and went to Beer, and he lived there because of Abimelech his brother.
Abimelech ruled over Israel for three years.
Then God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the lords of Shechem, and the lords of Shechem dealt treacherously with Abimelech,

so that the violence done to the seventy sons of Jerubbaal might come home, and their blood be laid on Abimelech their brother, who killed them, and on the lords of Shechem, who strengthened his hands to kill his brothers.
The lords of Shechem set men in ambush against him on the mountaintops, and they robbed everyone who passed by them on the road; and Abimelech was told.
Then Gaal son of Ebed came with his brothers, and they passed through Shechem, and the lords of Shechem put their trust in him.
They went out into the field, gathered the grapes of their vineyards and trod them, and held a festival; and they went into the house of their god, ate and drank, and cursed Abimelech.

And Gaal son of Ebed said, "Who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem, that we should serve him? Is he not the son of Jerubbaal, with Zebul as his deputy? Serve the men of Hamor, the father of Shechem! Why should we serve him?"
"If only this people were in my hand, I would remove Abimelech!" And he said of Abimelech, "Increase your army and come out!"
When Zebul the official of the city heard the words of Gaal son of Ebed, his anger burned.
He sent messengers to Abimelech secretly, saying, "See, Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers are coming to Shechem, and they are turning the city against you.
"Now then, get up by night, you and the people with you, and lie in wait in the field.
"In the morning, when the sun rises, get up early and make a raid on the city; and when he and the people with him come out against you, do to him as your hand finds occasion."
So Abimelech and all the people with him got up by night, and they lay in wait against Shechem in four companies.
Gaal son of Ebed went out and stood at the entrance of the city gate, and Abimelech and the people with him rose from the ambush.
When Gaal saw the people he said to Zebul, "Look, people are coming down from the mountaintops." But Zebul said to him, "It is the shadow of the mountains you are seeing, like men."
Gaal spoke again and said, "Look, people are coming down from the navel of the land, and one company is coming from the direction of the Soothsayers' Tree."
Then Zebul said to him, "Where is your mouth now, you who said, 'Who is Abimelech, that we should serve him?' Is this not the people you despised? Go out now and fight against him."
So Gaal went out at the head of the lords of Shechem and fought against Abimelech.
Abimelech pursued him, and he fled before him, and many fell fatally wounded as far as the entrance of the gate.
Abimelech stayed at Arumah, and Zebul drove out Gaal and his brothers so that they could not stay in Shechem.
The next day the people went out into the field, and Abimelech was told.
So he took his people, divided them into three companies, and lay in wait in the field; and when he saw the people coming out of the city, he rose up against them and struck them down.
Abimelech and the companies with him made a raid and took their stand at the entrance of the city gate, while the two companies raided all who were in the field and struck them down.
Abimelech fought against the city all that day; he captured the city, killed the people in it, pulled the city down, and sowed it with salt.
When all the lords of the tower of Shechem heard, they went into the stronghold of the house of El-berith.
Abimelech was told that all the lords of the tower of Shechem had gathered together.

So Abimelech went up Mount Zalmon, he and all the people with him. Abimelech took an axe in his hand, cut off a branch from the trees, lifted it and put it on his shoulder, and said to the people with him, "What you have seen me do, hurry and do the same."

So all the people also cut branches, each his own, and followed Abimelech and put them against the stronghold, and set the stronghold on fire over them; and all the people of the tower of Shechem died too, about a thousand men and women.
Then Abimelech went to Thebez, encamped against Thebez, and captured it.
But there was a strong tower in the middle of the city, and all the men and the women and all the lords of the city fled there; they shut the door behind them and went up onto the roof of the tower.
Abimelech came to the tower and fought against it, and he drew near to the entrance of the tower to burn it with fire.
But one woman threw an upper millstone down on Abimelech's head and crushed his skull.

He called quickly to the young man who carried his armour and said to him, "Draw your sword and kill me, so that they will not say of me, 'A woman killed him.'" So his young man ran him through, and he died.
When the men of Israel saw that Abimelech was dead, they went, each to his own place.
So God repaid the evil of Abimelech that he had done to his father, in killing his seventy brothers;
and all the evil of the men of Shechem God repaid on their head; and the curse of Jotham son of Jerubbaal came upon them.

judges_10.t: After Abimelech there arose to deliver Israel Tola son of Puah son of Dodo, a man of Issachar, who lived in Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim.
He judged Israel twenty-three years; then he died and was buried in Shamir.
After him arose Jair the Gileadite, and he judged Israel twenty-two years.
He had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkeys, and they had thirty towns; they are called Havvoth-jair to this day, and they are in the land of Gilead.
Jair died and was buried in Kamon.

The Israelites again did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD: they served the Baals and the Ashtaroth, and the gods of Aram, the gods of Sidon, the gods of Moab, the gods of the Ammonites, and the gods of the Philistines; they forsook the LORD and did not serve him.
The anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of the Philistines and into the hand of the Ammonites.
They shattered and crushed the Israelites that year — for eighteen years — all the Israelites beyond the Jordan in the land of the Amorites, which is in Gilead.
The Ammonites also crossed the Jordan to fight against Judah, against Benjamin, and against the house of Ephraim, and Israel was greatly distressed.
Then the Israelites cried out to the LORD, saying, "We have sinned against you, for we have forsaken our God and served the Baals."
The LORD said to the Israelites, "Was it not from Egypt, from the Amorites, from the Ammonites, and from the Philistines,
"and when the Sidonians, Amalek, and Maon oppressed you, and you cried out to me, that I delivered you from their hand?
"But you have forsaken me and served other gods. Therefore I will not deliver you again.
"Go and cry out to the gods you have chosen; let them deliver you in the time of your distress."
The Israelites said to the LORD, "We have sinned. Do to us whatever is good in your eyes; only deliver us this day."
So they removed the foreign gods from their midst and served the LORD; and he could no longer bear the trouble of Israel.
The Ammonites were called out and encamped in Gilead, and the Israelites gathered and encamped at Mizpah.
And the people, the leaders of Gilead, said to one another, "Who is the man who will begin the fight against the Ammonites? He shall become chief over all the inhabitants of Gilead."

judges_11.t: Now Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty man of valour, and he was the son of a prostitute; and Gilead fathered Jephthah.
Gilead's wife bore him sons, and when the wife's sons grew up they drove Jephthah out and said to him, "You shall not inherit in our father's house, for you are the son of another woman."
So Jephthah fled from his brothers and lived in the land of Tob; and worthless men gathered around Jephthah and went out with him.
Some time later the Ammonites fought against Israel.
When the Ammonites fought against Israel, the elders of Gilead went to fetch Jephthah from the land of Tob.
They said to Jephthah, "Come and be our commander, and let us fight against the Ammonites."
But Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, "Was it not you who hated me and drove me out of my father's house? Why have you come to me now, when you are in distress?"
The elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, "That is exactly why we have returned to you now: come with us and fight against the Ammonites, and you shall be our chief over all the inhabitants of Gilead."
Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, "If you bring me back to fight against the Ammonites and the LORD gives them over to me, then I will be your chief."
The elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, "The LORD will be the one who hears between us, if we do not do as you have said."
So Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people set him over them as chief and commander; and Jephthah spoke all his words before the LORD at Mizpah.
Then Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the Ammonites, saying, "What is there between me and you, that you have come against me to fight in my land?"

The king of the Ammonites said to Jephthah's messengers, "Because Israel took my land when it came up from Egypt, from the Arnon as far as the Jabbok and as far as the Jordan. Now restore it peaceably."
Jephthah again sent messengers to the king of the Ammonites,
and said to him, "Thus says Jephthah: Israel did not take the land of Moab or the land of the Ammonites.
"For when they came up from Egypt, Israel went through the wilderness as far as the Sea of Reeds and came to Kadesh.

"And Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, 'Please let us pass through your land.' But the king of Edom would not listen. It sent also to the king of Moab, and he was not willing; so Israel stayed at Kadesh.

"Then it went through the wilderness and went around the land of Edom and the land of Moab, and came to the east of the land of Moab; and they encamped beyond the Arnon and did not enter the territory of Moab, for the Arnon was Moab's border.
"Then Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, king of Heshbon, and Israel said to him, 'Please let us pass through your land to our place.'
"But Sihon did not trust Israel to pass through his territory; Sihon gathered all his people, encamped at Jahaz, and fought against Israel.
"And the LORD, the God of Israel, gave Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they struck them down; and Israel took possession of all the land of the Amorites who inhabited that land.
"They took possession of all the territory of the Amorites, from the Arnon as far as the Jabbok, and from the wilderness as far as the Jordan.
"Now then, the LORD, the God of Israel, has dispossessed the Amorites from before his people Israel — and would you take possession of it?
"Is it not so: what Chemosh your god gives you to possess, that you possess; and all that the LORD our God has dispossessed before us, that we possess?
"And now, are you any better than Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever quarrel with Israel, or ever wage war against them?
"While Israel lived in Heshbon and its villages, in Aroer and its villages, and in all the cities along the banks of the Arnon — three hundred years — why did you not recover them in that time?
"I have not sinned against you, but you are doing me wrong by waging war against me. May the LORD, the Judge, judge this day between the Israelites and the Ammonites."
But the king of the Ammonites did not listen to the words of Jephthah that he sent to him.
Then the spirit of the LORD came upon Jephthah, and he passed through Gilead and Manasseh; he passed through Mizpeh of Gilead, and from Mizpeh of Gilead he passed on to the Ammonites.
And Jephthah made a vow to the LORD and said, "If you will indeed give the Ammonites into my hand,
"then whatever comes out — whatever comes out of the doors of my house to meet me when I return in peace from the Ammonites — shall be the LORD's, and I will offer it up as a burnt offering."
So Jephthah crossed over to the Ammonites to fight against them, and the LORD gave them into his hand.
He struck them from Aroer as far as Minnith — twenty cities — and as far as Abel-keramim, a very great defeat; and the Ammonites were subdued before the Israelites.
Then Jephthah came to Mizpah, to his house — and there was his daughter coming out to meet him with tambourines and dancing. She was an only child; he had no son or daughter besides her.
When he saw her he tore his clothes and said, "Alas, my daughter! You have brought me very low; you are among those who bring me trouble. I have opened my mouth to the LORD, and I cannot turn back."

She said to him, "My father, you have opened your mouth to the LORD. Do to me according to what has come out of your mouth, since the LORD has done vengeance for you on your enemies, on the Ammonites."
And she said to her father, "Let this be done for me: leave me alone for two months, and let me go down on the mountains and weep over my virginity, I and my companions."
He said, "Go." And he sent her away for two months; and she went with her companions and wept over her virginity on the mountains.
At the end of two months she returned to her father, and he did to her according to his vow that he had vowed; and she had not known a man. And it became a custom in Israel,
that year by year the daughters of Israel go to commemorate the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite, four days in the year.

judges_12.t: The men of Ephraim were called out and crossed over to Zaphon, and they said to Jephthah, "Why did you cross over to fight against the Ammonites and not summon us to go with you? We will burn your house down over you!"
Jephthah said to them, "I was a man in great strife, I and my people, with the Ammonites; and I summoned you, and you did not deliver me from their hand.

"When I saw that you would not deliver me, I took my life in my hand and crossed over against the Ammonites, and the LORD gave them into my hand. So why have you come up against me this day to fight against me?"

So Jephthah gathered all the men of Gilead and fought against Ephraim, and the men of Gilead struck Ephraim down, because they had said, "You are fugitives of Ephraim, you Gileadites, in the midst of Ephraim, in the midst of Manasseh."

And Gilead captured the fords of the Jordan against Ephraim; and whenever a fugitive of Ephraim said, "Let me cross over," the men of Gilead would say to him, "Are you an Ephraimite?" and he would say, "No."

they would say to him, "Say shibboleth," and he would say "sibboleth," for he could not manage to pronounce it rightly; and they would seize him and slaughter him at the fords of the Jordan. Forty-two thousand of Ephraim fell at that time.
Jephthah judged Israel six years; then Jephthah the Gileadite died and was buried in one of the cities of Gilead.
After him Ibzan of Bethlehem judged Israel.
He had thirty sons; he sent thirty daughters outside and brought in thirty daughters for his sons from outside. And he judged Israel seven years.
Ibzan died and was buried in Bethlehem.
After him Elon the Zebulunite judged Israel, and he judged Israel ten years.
Elon the Zebulunite died and was buried in Aijalon in the land of Zebulun.
After him Abdon son of Hillel the Pirathonite judged Israel.
He had forty sons and thirty grandsons who rode on seventy donkeys, and he judged Israel eight years.
Abdon son of Hillel the Pirathonite died and was buried at Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, in the hill country of the Amalekites.

judges_13.t: The Israelites again did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD gave them into the hand of the Philistines for forty years.
There was a man from Zorah, of the clan of the Danites, whose name was Manoah; and his wife was barren and had borne no children.
The angel of the LORD appeared to the woman and said to her, "You are barren and have borne no children; but you shall conceive and bear a son.
"Now take care: do not drink wine or strong drink, and do not eat anything unclean.

"For you shall conceive and bear a son; and no razor shall come on his head, for the boy shall be a Nazirite of God from the womb. And he shall begin to deliver Israel from the hand of the Philistines."

The woman came and said to her husband, "A man of God came to me, and his appearance was like the appearance of the angel of God, very fearsome. I did not ask him where he was from, and he did not tell me his name.

"And he said to me, 'You shall conceive and bear a son. Now do not drink wine or strong drink, and do not eat any uncleanness, for the boy shall be a Nazirite of God from the womb until the day of his death.'"
Then Manoah prayed to the LORD and said, "Pardon me, my Lord — let the man of God whom you sent come to us again, and teach us what we are to do for the boy who is to be born."
God listened to the voice of Manoah, and the angel of God came again to the woman while she was sitting in the field; and Manoah her husband was not with her.
The woman hurried and ran and told her husband, saying to him, "The man has appeared to me — the one who came to me the other day."
Manoah got up and followed his wife, and he came to the man and said to him, "Are you the man who spoke to the woman?" And he said, "I am."
Manoah said, "Now when your words come true, what is to be the rule for the boy, and what is he to do?"
The angel of the LORD said to Manoah, "Of all that I said to the woman she shall take care.
"She shall not eat anything that comes from the vine of the wine, she shall not drink wine or strong drink, and she shall not eat any uncleanness. All that I commanded her she shall keep."
Manoah said to the angel of the LORD, "Let us detain you, and prepare a young goat for you."

The angel of the LORD said to Manoah, "If you detain me, I will not eat your food; and if you prepare a burnt offering, offer it up to the LORD." For Manoah did not know that he was the angel of the LORD.
Manoah said to the angel of the LORD, "What is your name, so that when your word comes true we may honour you?"
The angel of the LORD said to him, "Why do you ask for my name? It is beyond understanding."
So Manoah took the young goat and the grain offering and offered it up on the rock to the LORD; and he did an extraordinary thing while Manoah and his wife looked on.
When the flame went up from the altar toward the heavens, the angel of the LORD went up in the flame of the altar, while Manoah and his wife looked on; and they fell on their faces to the ground.
The angel of the LORD did not appear again to Manoah or to his wife. Then Manoah knew that he was the angel of the LORD.
And Manoah said to his wife, "We shall surely die, for we have seen God."

But his wife said to him, "If the LORD had wanted to kill us, he would not have accepted a burnt offering and a grain offering from our hand, and he would not have shown us all these things, and at this time he would not have let us hear such things as these."
The woman bore a son and named him Samson; and the boy grew, and the LORD blessed him.
And the spirit of the LORD began to stir him in Mahaneh-dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.

judges_14.t: Samson went down to Timnah, and there he saw a woman, one of the daughters of the Philistines.
He went up and told his father and mother, "I have seen a woman in Timnah, one of the daughters of the Philistines. Now get her for me as a wife."

But his father and mother said to him, "Is there no woman among the daughters of your kin, or among all my people, that you go to take a wife from the uncircumcised Philistines?" And Samson said to his father, "Get her for me, for she is right in my eyes."
His father and mother did not know that this was from the LORD, for he was seeking an occasion against the Philistines; and at that time the Philistines were ruling over Israel.
Samson went down to Timnah with his father and mother, and they came as far as the vineyards of Timnah; and there was a young lion roaring toward him.
And the spirit of the LORD rushed upon him, and he tore the lion apart as one tears apart a young goat, with nothing in his hand; and he did not tell his father or his mother what he had done.
Then he went down and spoke to the woman, and she was right in the eyes of Samson.
After some days he returned to take her, and he turned aside to see the carcass of the lion; and there was a swarm of bees in the body of the lion, and honey.

He scraped it out into his hands and went on, eating as he went; and he came to his father and mother and gave them some, and they ate. But he did not tell them that he had scraped the honey out of the body of the lion.
His father went down to the woman, and Samson made a feast there, for that is what the young men used to do.
When they saw him, they took thirty companions, and they were with him.

Samson said to them, "Let me put a riddle to you. If you can indeed tell me the answer within the seven days of the feast and find it out, then I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothes.
"But if you cannot tell me, then you shall give me thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothes." And they said to him, "Ask your riddle; let us hear it."
And he said to them: "Out of the eater came something to eat, and out of the strong came something sweet." And for three days they could not tell the riddle.
On the seventh day they said to Samson's wife, "Entice your husband to tell us the riddle, or we will burn you and your father's house with fire. Did you invite us here to impoverish us?"

Samson's wife wept over him and said, "You only hate me; you do not love me. You have put a riddle to my own people, and you have not told me the answer." And he said to her, "I have not told my father or my mother — and shall I tell you?"
She wept over him the seven days that their feast lasted; and on the seventh day he told her, because she pressed him hard. And she told the riddle to her own people.

And the men of the city said to him on the seventh day, before the sun went down: "What is sweeter than honey, and what is stronger than a lion?" And he said to them: "If you had not ploughed with my heifer, you would not have found out my riddle."

And the spirit of the LORD rushed upon him, and he went down to Ashkelon and struck down thirty men of them and took what they had, and gave the changes of clothes to those who had told the riddle. And his anger burned, and he went up to his father's house.
And Samson's wife was given to his companion, the one who had been his best friend.

judges_15.t: After some days, in the days of the wheat harvest, Samson visited his wife with a young goat, and he said, "Let me go in to my wife, into the chamber." But her father would not let him go in.
Her father said, "I was sure you utterly hated her, so I gave her to your companion. Is not her younger sister better than she? Let her be yours instead."
Samson said to them, "This time I shall be blameless toward the Philistines when I do them harm."
So Samson went and caught three hundred foxes, and he took torches and turned them tail to tail and put a torch between each pair of tails, in the middle.
He set fire to the torches and let them go into the standing grain of the Philistines, and burned up the stacked sheaves and the standing grain and the olive groves.

The Philistines said, "Who has done this?" And they said, "Samson, the son-in-law of the Timnite, because he took his wife and gave her to his companion." So the Philistines went up and burned her and her father with fire.
Samson said to them, "If this is how you act, then I will surely avenge myself on you, and after that I will stop."
And he struck them down, leg and thigh, a great slaughter; then he went down and stayed in the cleft of the rock of Etam.
The Philistines went up and encamped in Judah, and they spread out at Lehi.
The men of Judah said, "Why have you come up against us?" And they said, "We have come up to bind Samson, to do to him as he did to us."

Then three thousand men from Judah went down to the cleft of the rock of Etam and said to Samson, "Do you not know that the Philistines are ruling over us? What is this you have done to us?" And he said to them, "As they did to me, so I have done to them."
They said to him, "We have come down to bind you and give you into the hand of the Philistines." And Samson said to them, "Swear to me that you yourselves will not fall upon me."
They said to him, "No — we will only bind you and give you into their hand; we will certainly not kill you." So they bound him with two new ropes and brought him up from the rock.

As he came to Lehi, the Philistines shouted at meeting him; and the spirit of the LORD rushed upon him, and the ropes on his arms became like flax that has been burned with fire, and his bonds dropped off his hands.
He found a fresh jawbone of a donkey, and he reached out his hand and took it, and with it he struck down a thousand men.
And Samson said: "With the jawbone of the donkey, a heap, two heaps — with the jawbone of the donkey I have struck down a thousand men."
When he had finished speaking, he threw the jawbone from his hand, and he called that place Ramath-lehi.

He was very thirsty, and he called out to the LORD and said, "You yourself have given this great victory by the hand of your servant. And now shall I die of thirst and fall into the hand of the uncircumcised?"
So God split open the hollow at Lehi, and water came out of it, and he drank; his spirit returned and he revived. Therefore he called its name En-hakkore, which is at Lehi to this day.
And he judged Israel twenty years, in the days of the Philistines.

judges_16.t: Samson went to Gaza, and he saw there a prostitute, and he went in to her.

The Gazites were told, "Samson has come here." So they surrounded the place and lay in wait for him all night at the city gate; they kept silent all night, saying, "At the light of morning we will kill him."

But Samson lay down only until midnight, and at midnight he rose and took hold of the doors of the city gate and the two doorposts, pulled them up with the bar, put them on his shoulders, and carried them to the top of the mountain that faces Hebron.
After this he loved a woman in the valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah.

The lords of the Philistines went up to her and said to her, "Entice him and find out where his great strength lies, and by what we may prevail over him, so that we may bind him and humble him; and each of us will give you eleven hundred pieces of silver."
So Delilah said to Samson, "Tell me where your great strength lies, and by what you may be bound and humbled."
Samson said to her, "If they bind me with seven fresh cords that have not been dried, then I shall become weak and be like anyone else."
So the lords of the Philistines brought her seven fresh cords that had not been dried, and she bound him with them.

Now the ambusher was sitting in the inner chamber for her. And she said to him, "The Philistines are upon you, Samson!" But he tore the cords apart as a thread of tow is torn apart when it touches fire; and the secret of his strength was not known.
Then Delilah said to Samson, "You have deceived me and spoken lies to me. Now tell me by what you may be bound."
He said to her, "If they indeed bind me with new ropes with which no work has been done, then I shall become weak and be like anyone else."

So Delilah took new ropes and bound him with them, and she said to him, "The Philistines are upon you, Samson!" — and the ambusher was sitting in the inner chamber. But he tore them off his arms like a thread.
Then Delilah said to Samson, "Until now you have deceived me and spoken lies to me. Tell me by what you may be bound." And he said to her, "If you weave the seven plaits of my head with the web."
And she thrust with the pin, and said to him, "The Philistines are upon you, Samson!" But he awoke from his sleep and pulled out the pin of the loom and the web.
She said to him, "How can you say 'I love you' when your heart is not with me? Three times now you have deceived me, and you have not told me where your great strength lies."
And because she pressed him with her words day after day and urged him, he was worn to death.

So he told her all his heart and said to her, "No razor has come on my head, for I have been a Nazirite of God from my mother's womb. If I were shaved, my strength would depart from me, and I should become weak and be like anyone else."

When Delilah saw that he had told her all his heart, she sent and summoned the lords of the Philistines, saying, "Come up this time, for he has told me all his heart." So the lords of the Philistines came up to her and brought the silver in their hand.
She made him sleep on her knees, and she summoned the man and shaved off the seven plaits of his head; and she began to humble him, and his strength departed from him.

And she said, "The Philistines are upon you, Samson!" He awoke from his sleep and said, "I will go out as at other times and shake myself free." But he did not know that the LORD had departed from him.
The Philistines seized him and gouged out his eyes, and they brought him down to Gaza and bound him with bronze fetters; and he ground grain in the prison house.
But the hair of his head began to grow back after it had been shaved.
Now the lords of the Philistines gathered to sacrifice a great sacrifice to Dagon their god, and to rejoice; and they said, "Our god has given Samson our enemy into our hand."
And when the people saw him they praised their god, for they said, "Our god has given into our hand our enemy, the one who laid waste our land and multiplied our slain."

And when their heart was merry, they said, "Summon Samson, and let him make sport for us." So they summoned Samson from the prison house, and he made sport before them; and they set him between the pillars.
And Samson said to the young man who was holding his hand, "Let go of me, and let me feel the pillars on which the house rests, so that I may lean on them."
Now the house was full of men and women, and all the lords of the Philistines were there; and on the roof were about three thousand men and women looking on while Samson made sport.
Then Samson called out to the LORD and said, "Lord GOD, remember me and strengthen me, only this once, O God, that I may avenge myself with one act of vengeance for my two eyes on the Philistines."
Then Samson grasped the two middle pillars on which the house rested, and he braced himself against them, one with his right hand and one with his left.

And Samson said, "Let me die with the Philistines." Then he pushed with strength, and the house fell on the lords and on all the people in it. And the dead whom he killed in his death were more than those he had killed in his life.
Then his brothers and all his father's house went down and carried him up, and they buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the tomb of Manoah his father. And he had judged Israel twenty years.

judges_17.t: There was a man from the hill country of Ephraim whose name was Micayehu.

He said to his mother, "The eleven hundred pieces of silver that were taken from you, about which you uttered a curse and spoke it in my hearing — the silver is with me; I took it." And his mother said, "Blessed be my son by the LORD."

So he returned the eleven hundred pieces of silver to his mother, and his mother said, "I do consecrate the silver to the LORD from my hand, for my son, to make a carved image and a cast image. Now I will return it to you."

So he returned the silver to his mother, and his mother took two hundred pieces of silver and gave it to the silversmith, and he made it into a carved image and a cast image; and it was in the house of Micayehu.
Now the man Micah had a house of God; he made an ephod and teraphim, and he ordained one of his sons, who became his priest.
In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did what was right in his own eyes.
Now there was a young man from Bethlehem of Judah, of the clan of Judah; he was a Levite, and he was sojourning there.
The man left the city, Bethlehem of Judah, to sojourn wherever he might find a place; and he came to the hill country of Ephraim, to the house of Micah, as he went on his way.
Micah said to him, "Where do you come from?" And he said to him, "I am a Levite from Bethlehem of Judah, and I am going to sojourn wherever I may find a place."
Micah said to him, "Stay with me and be a father and a priest to me, and I will give you ten pieces of silver a year, and an outfit of clothes, and your keep." So the Levite went in.
The Levite was willing to dwell with the man, and the young man became to him like one of his sons.
Micah ordained the Levite, and the young man became his priest; and he was in the house of Micah.
Then Micah said, "Now I know that the LORD will do good to me, for the Levite has become my priest."

judges_18.t: In those days there was no king in Israel. And in those days the tribe of the Danites was seeking an inheritance for itself to dwell in, for until that day nothing had fallen to it as an inheritance among the tribes of Israel.

So the Danites sent from their clan five men from their whole number, men of valour, from Zorah and Eshtaol, to spy out the land and explore it; and they said to them, "Go, explore the land." They came to the hill country of Ephraim, to the house of Micah, and spent the night there.

While they were near the house of Micah, they recognised the voice of the young man, the Levite; so they turned aside there and said to him, "Who brought you here? What are you doing in this place? And what have you here?"
He said to them, "Micah has done such and such for me; he has hired me, and I have become his priest."
And they said to him, "Enquire of God, that we may know whether the journey we are on will succeed."
And the priest said to them, "Go in peace. The way you are going is before the LORD."

So the five men went on and came to Laish, and they saw the people in it dwelling in security, after the manner of the Sidonians, quiet and secure; and there was no ruler in the land putting anyone to shame in anything; and they were far from the Sidonians and had no dealings with anyone.
They came back to their brothers at Zorah and Eshtaol, and their brothers said to them, "What do you report?"
And they said, "Get up, let us go up against them, for we have seen the land, and it is very good. And you are doing nothing! Do not hesitate to go in and take possession of the land.
"When you go, you will come to a people that is secure, and the land is broad on both sides, for God has given it into your hand — a place where nothing on earth is lacking."
So six hundred men of the clan of the Danites, girded with weapons of war, set out from there, from Zorah and Eshtaol.
They went up and encamped at Kiriath-jearim in Judah. Therefore that place is called Mahaneh-dan to this day; it is west of Kiriath-jearim.
From there they passed through the hill country of Ephraim and came to the house of Micah.

Then the five men who had gone to spy out the land of Laish said to their brothers, "Do you know that in these houses there is an ephod, teraphim, a carved image, and a cast image? Now consider what you will do."
So they turned aside there and came to the house of the young man, the Levite — the house of Micah — and greeted him.
Meanwhile the six hundred men of the Danites, girded with their weapons of war, were standing at the entrance of the gate.

And the five men who had gone to spy out the land went up, came in there, and took the carved image, the ephod, the teraphim, and the cast image — while the priest stood at the entrance of the gate with the six hundred men girded with weapons of war.
These men came into the house of Micah and took the carved image, the ephod, the teraphim, and the cast image; and the priest said to them, "What are you doing?"

And they said to him, "Keep quiet. Put your hand over your mouth and come with us, and be a father and a priest to us. Is it better for you to be priest to the house of one man, or to be priest to a tribe and a clan in Israel?"
The priest's heart was glad, and he took the ephod, the teraphim, and the carved image, and went along in the midst of the people.
So they turned and went on, and they put the little ones, the livestock, and the goods in front of them.
When they had gone some distance from the house of Micah, the men who were in the houses near the house of Micah were called out, and they overtook the Danites.
They called out to the Danites, who turned their faces round and said to Micah, "What is the matter with you, that you have been called out?"
And he said, "You have taken my gods that I made, and the priest, and you have gone. What is left to me? How can you say to me, 'What is the matter with you?'"
And the Danites said to him, "Do not let your voice be heard among us, or bitter-tempered men will fall upon you and you will lose your life and the lives of your household."
So the Danites went on their way; and when Micah saw that they were too strong for him, he turned and went back to his house.
And they took what Micah had made, and the priest who was his, and came upon Laish, upon a people quiet and secure, and struck them with the edge of the sword; and they burned the city with fire.
And there was no deliverer, for it was far from Sidon and they had no dealings with anyone; and it lay in the valley that belongs to Beth-rehob. They rebuilt the city and lived in it.
They named the city Dan, after the name of Dan their ancestor, who was born to Israel; but the name of the city was formerly Laish.
And the Danites set up the carved image for themselves; and Jonathan son of Gershom son of Manasseh, he and his sons, were priests to the tribe of the Danites until the day the land went into exile.
So they set up for themselves the carved image of Micah, which he had made, all the days that the house of God was at Shiloh.

judges_19.t: In those days, when there was no king in Israel, there was a man, a Levite, sojourning in the remotest parts of the hill country of Ephraim; and he took for himself a concubine from Bethlehem of Judah.
And his concubine prostituted herself against him, and she left him for her father's house at Bethlehem of Judah, and she was there some days — four months.

Then her husband rose and went after her, to speak to her heart and bring her back; his servant was with him, and a pair of donkeys. And she brought him into her father's house; and the young woman's father saw him and was glad to meet him.
His father-in-law, the young woman's father, kept hold of him, and he stayed with him three days; they ate and drank and spent the night there.
On the fourth day they rose early in the morning, and he got up to go; and the young woman's father said to his son-in-law, "Sustain your heart with a morsel of bread, and afterwards you shall go."
So the two of them sat and ate and drank together; and the young woman's father said to the man, "Please be willing to stay the night, and let your heart be glad."
The man rose to go, but his father-in-law urged him, and he turned back and spent the night there.
He rose early in the morning on the fifth day to go, and the young woman's father said, "Please sustain your heart, and wait until the day declines." And the two of them ate.

The man rose to go, he and his concubine and his servant; and his father-in-law, the young woman's father, said to him, "See now, the day is sinking toward evening. Please stay the night. See, the day is declining. Stay here and let your heart be glad; and tomorrow you can rise early for your journey and go home."
But the man was not willing to stay the night. He rose and went, and came opposite Jebus (that is, Jerusalem), and with him were a pair of saddled donkeys, and his concubine was with him.
When they were near Jebus and the day was far gone, the servant said to his master, "Come, let us turn aside to this city of the Jebusites and spend the night in it."
But his master said to him, "We will not turn aside to a foreign city that is not of the Israelites; we will pass on as far as Gibeah."
And he said to his servant, "Come, let us draw near to one of these places, and spend the night in Gibeah or in Ramah."
So they passed on and went, and the sun set on them beside Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin.
They turned aside there to go in and spend the night in Gibeah; and he went in and sat down in the open square of the city, and there was no one who took them into a house to spend the night.
And there was an old man coming from his work in the field in the evening; the man was from the hill country of Ephraim and was sojourning in Gibeah, and the men of the place were Benjaminites.
He lifted up his eyes and saw the traveller in the open square of the city, and the old man said, "Where are you going, and where do you come from?"

And he said to him, "We are passing from Bethlehem of Judah to the remotest parts of the hill country of Ephraim. I am from there; I went to Bethlehem of Judah, and I am going to the house of the LORD. And there is no one who takes me into a house.
"There is both straw and fodder for our donkeys, and there is bread and wine for me and for your maidservant and for the young man who is with your servants. We lack nothing."
And the old man said, "Peace to you. Only let all your need be on me; only do not spend the night in the open square."
So he brought him into his house and gave the donkeys fodder; and they washed their feet and ate and drank.

While they were making their hearts glad, the men of the city, worthless men, surrounded the house, beating violently on the door; and they said to the man, the master of the house, the old man, "Bring out the man who came into your house, that we may know him."
The man, the master of the house, went out to them and said to them, "No, my brothers, do not do evil. Since this man has come into my house, do not do this outrage."
"Here are my daughter, a virgin, and his concubine. Let me bring them out; afflict them and do to them what is good in your eyes; but to this man do not do this outrageous thing."

But the men were not willing to listen to him. So the man took hold of his concubine and brought her outside to them; and they knew her and abused her all night until morning, and they let her go as the dawn came up.
And the woman came at daybreak and fell at the entrance of the man's house where her master was, and lay there until it was light.

Her master rose in the morning and opened the doors of the house and went out to go on his way; and there was the woman, his concubine, fallen at the entrance of the house, with her hands on the threshold.
And he said to her, "Get up, let us go." But there was no answer. So he took her onto the donkey, and the man rose and went to his place.
And he came to his house, took the knife, took hold of his concubine, and cut her in pieces, limb by limb, into twelve pieces; and he sent her throughout all the territory of Israel.
And everyone who saw it said, "Such a thing has not happened and has not been seen from the day the Israelites came up from the land of Egypt to this day. Consider it, take counsel, and speak."

judges_20.t: Then all the Israelites went out, and the congregation assembled as one man, from Dan to Beer-sheba, and the land of Gilead, to the LORD at Mizpah.
And the chiefs of all the people, all the tribes of Israel, presented themselves in the assembly of the people of God: four hundred thousand men on foot, drawing the sword.
And the Benjaminites heard that the Israelites had gone up to Mizpah. And the Israelites said, "Tell us: how did this evil happen?"
And the man, the Levite, the husband of the murdered woman, answered, "I came to Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin, I and my concubine, to spend the night.
"And the lords of Gibeah rose up against me and surrounded the house against me by night. They intended to kill me, and they abused my concubine, and she died.
"So I took hold of my concubine, cut her in pieces, and sent her throughout all the land of Israel's inheritance, because they had done depravity and outrage in Israel.
"Here you all are, Israelites. Give your word and counsel here."
And all the people rose as one man, saying, "Not one of us will go to his tent, and not one of us will turn aside to his house."
"Now this is what we will do to Gibeah: we will go against it by lot.

"We will take ten men out of every hundred from all the tribes of Israel, a hundred out of every thousand, and a thousand out of every ten thousand, to fetch provisions for the people, so that when they come to Geba of Benjamin they may deal with it according to all the outrage it has done in Israel."
So every man of Israel gathered against the city as one man, united.
And the tribes of Israel sent men throughout all the tribes of Benjamin, saying, "What is this evil that has happened among you?

"Now give up the men, the worthless men who are in Gibeah, that we may put them to death and burn evil out of Israel." But the Benjaminites were not willing to listen to the voice of their brothers the Israelites.
And the Benjaminites gathered from their cities to Gibeah, to go out to battle against the Israelites.
The Benjaminites were mustered that day from the cities: twenty-six thousand men drawing the sword, apart from the inhabitants of Gibeah, who were mustered at seven hundred chosen men.
Out of all this people were seven hundred chosen men impeded in the right hand; every one of them could sling a stone at a hair and not miss.
And the men of Israel were mustered, apart from Benjamin: four hundred thousand men drawing the sword; every one of them a man of war.
They rose and went up to Beth-el and enquired of God; and the Israelites said, "Who shall go up for us first to the battle against the Benjaminites?" And the LORD said, "Judah first."
The Israelites rose in the morning and encamped against Gibeah.
The men of Israel went out to battle against Benjamin, and the men of Israel deployed for battle against them at Gibeah.
The Benjaminites came out from Gibeah, and on that day they struck down twenty-two thousand men of Israel to the ground.
But the people, the men of Israel, took courage and again deployed for battle in the place where they had deployed on the first day.

And the Israelites went up and wept before the LORD until evening, and they enquired of the LORD, saying, "Shall I again draw near to battle against the Benjaminites, my brother?" And the LORD said, "Go up against him."
So the Israelites drew near to the Benjaminites on the second day.
And Benjamin came out to meet them from Gibeah on the second day, and again they struck down eighteen thousand men of the Israelites to the ground; all these were drawers of the sword.

Then all the Israelites and all the people went up and came to Beth-el, and they wept and sat there before the LORD, and they fasted that day until evening; and they offered up burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD.
And the Israelites enquired of the LORD — for the ark of the covenant of God was there in those days,

and Phinehas son of Eleazar son of Aaron was ministering before it in those days — saying, "Shall I again go out to battle against the Benjaminites, my brother, or shall I stop?" And the LORD said, "Go up, for tomorrow I will give him into your hand."
So Israel set men in ambush around Gibeah.
And the Israelites went up against the Benjaminites on the third day and deployed against Gibeah as at other times.

The Benjaminites came out to meet the people and were drawn away from the city, and they began to strike down some of the people, fatally wounded, as at other times, on the highways — one of which goes up to Beth-el and one to Gibeah — and in the open country: about thirty men of Israel.
And the Benjaminites said, "They are defeated before us as at first." But the Israelites said, "Let us flee and draw them away from the city to the highways."
And every man of Israel rose from his place and deployed at Baal-tamar, while the ambush of Israel burst forth from its place, from the open ground of Geba.
And ten thousand chosen men out of all Israel came against Gibeah, and the battle was heavy; and they did not know that calamity was upon them.
And the LORD defeated Benjamin before Israel, and on that day the Israelites struck down twenty-five thousand one hundred men of Benjamin; all these were drawing the sword.
And the Benjaminites saw that they were defeated; for the men of Israel had given ground to Benjamin, because they trusted in the ambush they had set against Gibeah.
And the men in ambush hurried and made a raid against Gibeah; the ambush deployed and struck all the city with the edge of the sword.
Now the appointed signal between the men of Israel and the men in ambush was that they should make a great cloud of smoke rise from the city.

And the men of Israel turned in the battle. Benjamin had begun to strike down about thirty of the men of Israel, fatally wounded, for they said, "Surely he is utterly defeated before us, as in the first battle."
But the rising began to go up from the city, a pillar of smoke; and Benjamin turned round, and there was the whole city going up toward the heavens.
And the men of Israel turned, and the men of Benjamin were terrified, for they saw that calamity had touched them.
And they turned before the men of Israel toward the way of the wilderness, but the battle overtook them; and those who came from the cities were destroying them in their midst.
They surrounded Benjamin, pursued him, and trod him down at his resting place, as far as opposite Gibeah, toward the east.
And eighteen thousand men of Benjamin fell — all of them men of valour.

And they turned and fled toward the wilderness, to the rock of Rimmon; and on the highways they gleaned five thousand of them, and pursued closely after them as far as Gidom, and struck down two thousand more.
So all who fell of Benjamin that day were twenty-five thousand men drawing the sword; all of them men of valour.
But six hundred men turned and fled toward the wilderness, to the rock of Rimmon, and they stayed at the rock of Rimmon four months.

And the men of Israel turned back against the Benjaminites and struck them with the edge of the sword — from the city, everything sound, to the animals, to all that was found; and all the cities they found they set on fire.

judges_21.t: Now the men of Israel had sworn at Mizpah, "Not one of us shall give his daughter to Benjamin as a wife."
And the people came to Beth-el and sat there before God until evening, and they lifted up their voice and wept bitterly.
And they said, "Why, LORD, God of Israel, has this happened in Israel, that today one tribe should be missing from Israel?"
The next day the people rose early and built an altar there and offered up burnt offerings and peace offerings.

And the Israelites said, "Who among all the tribes of Israel did not go up in the assembly to the LORD?" — for a great oath had been sworn concerning whoever did not go up to the LORD at Mizpah, saying, "He shall surely be put to death."
And the Israelites were moved to compassion for Benjamin their brother, and they said, "Today one tribe has been cut off from Israel.
"What shall we do for wives for those who remain? For we have sworn by the LORD not to give them any of our daughters as wives."
And they said, "Which one of the tribes of Israel did not go up to the LORD at Mizpah?" And it turned out that no one from Jabesh-gilead had come to the camp, to the assembly.
For when the people were mustered, no one was there from the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead.
So the congregation sent there twelve thousand men of valour and commanded them, "Go and strike the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead with the edge of the sword — the women and the little ones as well.
"And this is what you shall do: every male, and every woman who has known lying with a male, you shall devote to destruction."

And they found among the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead four hundred young women, virgins who had not known a man by lying with a male; and they brought them to the camp at Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan.
Then the whole congregation sent and spoke to the Benjaminites who were at the rock of Rimmon, and proclaimed peace to them.
And Benjamin returned at that time, and they gave them the women they had kept alive from the women of Jabesh-gilead; but there were not enough for them.
And the people were moved to compassion for Benjamin, because the LORD had made a breach in the tribes of Israel.
And the elders of the congregation said, "What shall we do for wives for those who remain? For the women have been destroyed out of Benjamin."
And they said, "There must be an inheritance for the survivors of Benjamin, so that a tribe may not be wiped out from Israel."
"But we ourselves cannot give them wives from our daughters, for the Israelites have sworn, "Cursed be anyone who gives a wife to Benjamin."
And they said, "See, there is a festival of the LORD at Shiloh year by year, which is north of Beth-el, east of the highway that goes up from Beth-el to Shechem, and south of Lebonah."
And they commanded the Benjaminites, "Go and lie in wait in the vineyards,

"and watch; and when the daughters of Shiloh come out to dance in the dances, then come out from the vineyards and seize for yourselves, each man his wife, from the daughters of Shiloh; and go to the land of Benjamin.

"And when their fathers or their brothers come to complain to us, we will say to them, 'Show us favour concerning them, for we did not take each man his wife in the battle; and you did not give them to them, otherwise you would now be guilty.'"

And the Benjaminites did so; they carried off wives according to their number from the dancers whom they had seized, and they went and returned to their inheritance, and rebuilt the cities and lived in them.
And the Israelites dispersed from there at that time, each to his tribe and to his clan; and they went out from there, each to his inheritance.
In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did what was right in his own eyes.

jeremiah_1.t: The words of Jeremiah son of Hilkiah, one of the priests at Anathoth in the land of Benjamin.
The word of the LORD came to him in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign,
and it came in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the end of the eleventh year of Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah, until Jerusalem went into exile in the fifth month.
The word of the LORD came to me:
Before I formed you in the belly I knew you, and before you came out of the womb I set you apart as holy; I appointed you a prophet to the nations.
But I said, "Ah, Lord GOD! I do not know how to speak, for I am a youth."
But the LORD said to me: "Do not say, 'I am a youth.' For you shall go to everyone I send you to, and you shall speak everything I command you."
"Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to rescue you," declares the LORD.
Then the LORD stretched out his hand and touched my mouth, and the LORD said to me, "See, I have put my words in your mouth."
"See, I appoint you today over the nations and over the kingdoms, to uproot and to pull down, to destroy and to overthrow, to build and to plant."
The word of the LORD came to me: "What do you see, Jeremiah?" And I said, "I see a branch of an almond tree."
And the LORD said to me, "You have seen well, for I am watching over my word to carry it out."
The word of the LORD came to me a second time: "What do you see?" And I said, "I see a pot at the boil, and it is tilted away from the north."
And the LORD said to me: "From the north disaster will be let loose on all the inhabitants of the land."

"For I am about to summon all the clans of the kingdoms of the north," declares the LORD, "and they will come, and each will set his throne at the entrance of the gates of Jerusalem, against all its walls round about, and against all the cities of Judah."
"And I will pronounce my judgements against them for all their evil, in that they have forsaken me, burned offerings as smoke to other gods, and bowed down to the works of their own hands."
"But you — gird your loins, get up, and say to them everything I command you. Do not be dismayed before them, or I will dismay you before them."

"And I — see, I have made you today a fortified city, a pillar of iron, and walls of bronze against the whole land: against the kings of Judah, its officials, its priests, and the people of the land."
"They will fight against you, but they will not prevail over you, for I am with you," declares the LORD, "to rescue you."

jeremiah_2.t: The word of the LORD came to me:

Go and proclaim in the hearing of Jerusalem: This is what the LORD says: I remember to your credit the loyalty of your youth, the love of your betrothal, how you walked after me in the wilderness, in a land not sown.
Israel was holy to the LORD, the first of his harvest. All who devoured her were held guilty; disaster came upon them, declares the LORD.
Hear the word of the LORD, house of Jacob, and all you clans of the house of Israel.
This is what the LORD says: What wrong did your ancestors find in me, that they went far from me, and walked after worthlessness and became worthless?

They did not say, "Where is the LORD, who brought us up from the land of Egypt, who led us through the wilderness, through a land of desert plain and pit, through a land of drought and deep darkness, through a land no one passes through and no human being lives in?"
I brought you into a fruitful land, to eat its fruit and its good things; but you came and made my land unclean, and you made my inheritance an abomination.
The priests did not say, "Where is the LORD?" Those who handle the law did not know me; the shepherds rebelled against me, the prophets prophesied by Baal and walked after things that do not profit.
Therefore I will contend with you again, declares the LORD, and with your children's children I will contend.
Cross over to the coasts of Kittim and see; send to Kedar and look closely; see whether there has ever been anything like this.
Has any nation exchanged its gods, though they are not gods at all? But my people have exchanged their glory for what does not profit.
Be appalled at this, you heavens; shudder, be utterly desolate, declares the LORD.
For my people have done two evils: they have forsaken me, the spring of living water, to dig out cisterns for themselves — broken cisterns that cannot hold water.
Is Israel a slave? Was he born a slave in the house? Why then has he become plunder?
Over him young lions have roared; they have raised their voice. They have made his land a waste; his cities are burned, with no one living in them.
The people of Memphis and Tahpanhes too have grazed your scalp bare.
Have you not brought this on yourself, by forsaking the LORD your God at the time he was leading you in the way?
And now, what is the road to Egypt to you, to drink the water of the Shihor? And what is the road to Assyria to you, to drink the water of the River?

Your own evil will discipline you, and your turnings away will rebuke you. Know, then, and see how evil and bitter it is that you have forsaken the LORD your God, and that the dread of me is not upon you, declares Lord GOD of hosts.
Long ago I broke your yoke, I tore off your bonds, and you said, "I will not transgress." But on every high hill and under every green tree you sprawled as a prostitute.
I myself planted you a choice vine, wholly a faithful seed. How then have you turned against me into the degenerate shoots of an alien vine?
Though you wash with natron and use a great deal of soap, your iniquity is stained before me, declares Lord GOD.
How can you say, "I have not made myself unclean; I have not walked after the Baals"? Look at your way in the valley, know what you have done — a swift young camel criss-crossing her ways,
a wild donkey used to the wilderness, sniffing the wind in the craving of her appetite — her heat, who can turn it back? None who seek her need weary themselves; in her month they will find her.
Keep your foot from going unshod, and your throat from thirst. But you said, "It is hopeless. No — I have loved strangers, and after them I will go."
As a thief is shamed when he is caught, so the house of Israel has been put to shame — they, their kings, their officials, their priests and their prophets,

who say to a tree, "You are my father," and to a stone, "You gave birth to us." For they have turned their backs to me and not their faces; yet at the time of their calamity they say, "Arise and save us!"
And where are the gods you made for yourself? Let them arise, if they can save you at the time of your calamity — for your gods are as many as your cities, Judah.
Why do you contend against me? All of you have rebelled against me, declares the LORD.
In vain I struck your children; they accepted no correction. Your own sword devoured your prophets like a destroying lion.
You of this generation, consider the word of the LORD! Have I been a wilderness to Israel, or a land of thick darkness? Why have my people said, "We roam free; we will not come to you again"?
Does a virgin forget her ornaments, or a bride her sashes? Yet my people have forgotten me days without number.
How well you set your course to seek love! And so you have even taught your ways to wicked women.
On your skirts, too, is found the blood of the lives of the innocent poor. You did not find them breaking in — yet it is on account of all these things.
And you said, "Surely I am innocent; his anger has turned away from me." I am about to enter into judgement with you because you say, "I have not sinned."
Why do you go about so lightly, changing your way? You will be shamed by Egypt too, just as you were shamed by Assyria.
From this one too you will go out, your hands on your head; for the LORD has rejected those you trust in, and you will not prosper by them.

jeremiah_3.t: If a man sends his wife away and she leaves him and becomes another man's, will he return to her again? Would not that land be utterly polluted? And you have played the whore with many lovers — and would you return to me? declares the LORD.

Lift your eyes to the bare heights and look: where have you not been lain with? You sat waiting for them by the roads like an Arab in the wilderness. You polluted the land with your whoring and your evil.
So the showers were withheld, and the spring rain did not come; yet you had a whore's forehead — you refused to be ashamed.
Have you not just now called to me, "My father, you are the companion of my youth"?
"Will he keep his anger for ever? Will he hold on to it to the end?" See — this is how you have spoken, and you have done evil things, and you have got your way.
The LORD said to me in the days of King Josiah: Have you seen what Turning-away Israel did? She went up on every high hill and under every green tree, and played the whore there.
And I said, after she had done all this, "She will return to me" — but she did not return. And her treacherous sister Judah saw it.

And I saw that for all the reasons that Turning-away Israel had committed adultery I had sent her away and given her a document of divorce; yet her treacherous sister Judah was not afraid, but went and played the whore herself as well.
And so, through the lightness of her whoring, the land was polluted, and she committed adultery with stone and with wood.
And even after all this, her treacherous sister Judah did not return to me with all her heart, but in falsehood, declares the LORD.
And the LORD said to me: Turning-away Israel has shown herself more in the right than treacherous Judah.

Go and proclaim these words toward the north, and say: Turn back, Turning-away Israel, declares the LORD. I will not make my face fall upon you, for I am loyal, declares the LORD. I will not keep anger for ever.

Only acknowledge your iniquity, that you have rebelled against the LORD your God, and scattered your ways among the strangers under every green tree, and have not listened to my voice, declares the LORD.
Turn back, turning-away sons, declares the LORD, for I am master over you; and I will take you, one from a city and two from a clan, and bring you to Zion.
And I will give you shepherds after my own heart, and they will shepherd you with knowledge and insight.

And in those days, when you have multiplied and become fruitful in the land, declares the LORD, they will no longer say, "The ark of the covenant of the LORD." It will not come to mind; they will not remember it, they will not miss it, and it will not be made again.

At that time they will call Jerusalem "The Throne of the LORD," and all the nations will be gathered to it, to the name of the LORD, to Jerusalem; and they will no longer walk after the stubbornness of their evil heart.
In those days the house of Judah will walk with the house of Israel, and together they will come from the land of the north to the land I gave your ancestors as an inheritance.

And I myself said: How I would set you among the sons and give you a desirable land, the most beautiful inheritance of the nations! And I said: You will call me "My father," and you will not turn away from following me.
Nevertheless, as a wife deals treacherously with her husband, so you have dealt treacherously with me, house of Israel, declares the LORD.
A sound is heard on the bare heights, the weeping and pleading of the people of Israel, because they have perverted their way, they have forgotten the LORD their God.
Turn back, turning-away sons; I will heal your turnings away. "Here we are, we have come to you, for you are the LORD our God."
Truly, the hills are a falsehood, the tumult on the mountains. Truly, in the LORD our God is the salvation of Israel.
And the Shame has consumed the toil of our ancestors from our youth — their flocks and their herds, their sons and their daughters.

Let us lie down in our shame, and let our disgrace cover us; for we have sinned against the LORD our God, we and our ancestors, from our youth until this day; and we have not listened to the voice of the LORD our God.

jeremiah_4.t: If you will turn back, Israel, declares the LORD, turn back to me; and if you will remove your detestable things from before me, then you will not waver.
and you will swear, "As the LORD lives," in faithfulness, in justice and in righteousness; then the nations will bless themselves by him, and in him they will boast.
For this is what the LORD says to the people of Judah and to Jerusalem: Break up your unbroken ground, and do not sow among thorns.

Circumcise yourselves to the LORD, and remove the foreskins of your heart, people of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, or my wrath will go out like fire and burn with no one to quench it, because of the evil of your deeds.
Declare it in Judah, proclaim it in Jerusalem, and say: Blow the ram's horn through the land! Call out at full voice and say: Gather together, and let us go into the fortified cities!
Raise a standard toward Zion! Take refuge, do not stand still! For I am bringing disaster from the north, and a great shattering.
A lion has gone up from his thicket; a destroyer of nations has set out. He has gone out from his place to make your land a waste. Your cities will fall in ruins, with no one living in them.
For this, put on sackcloth; mourn and wail, for the burning of the LORD's anger has not turned back from us.
And on that day, declares the LORD, the heart of the king will fail, and the heart of the officials; the priests will be appalled, and the prophets astounded.
And I said: Ah, Lord GOD! Truly you have utterly deceived this people and Jerusalem, saying, "You shall have peace" — and a sword reaches to the throat.
At that time it will be said to this people and to Jerusalem: A scorching wind off the bare heights in the wilderness comes toward the daughter of my people — not to winnow and not to cleanse.
A wind too full for that will come at my bidding. Now I too will pronounce my judgements against them.
See — he comes up like clouds, and his chariots like the storm-wind; his horses are swifter than eagles. Woe to us, for we are devastated!
Wash your heart clean of evil, Jerusalem, so that you may be saved. How long will your wicked thoughts lodge within you?
For a voice declares from Dan, proclaiming trouble from the hill country of Ephraim.
Make it known to the nations! See — proclaim it concerning Jerusalem: Besiegers are coming from a distant land, and they raise their voice against the cities of Judah.
Like those who guard a field they surround her, for she has rebelled against me, declares the LORD.
Your way and your deeds have brought this upon you. This is your evil — how bitter it is, how it has reached your very heart.

My inward parts, my inward parts! I must wait! The walls of my heart! My heart is in turmoil within me; I cannot keep silent, for you have heard the sound of the ram's horn, my very self, the shout of battle.
Shattering upon shattering is proclaimed, for the whole land is devastated. Suddenly my tents are devastated, in a moment my curtains.
How long must I see the standard, and hear the sound of the ram's horn?
For my people are foolish; they do not know me. They are senseless children, with no understanding. They are skilled at doing evil, and they do not know how to do good.
I looked at the earth, and there it was — formless and empty; and to the heavens, and their light was gone.
I looked at the mountains, and they were quaking, and all the hills were shaking to and fro.
I looked, and there was no human being, and all the birds of the heavens had fled.
I looked, and the fruitful land was a wilderness, and all its cities were pulled down before the LORD, before the burning of his anger.
For this is what the LORD says: The whole land will be a desolation, yet I will not make a full end.
For this the land will mourn, and the heavens above will grow dark; because I have spoken, I have purposed, and I have not relented and will not turn back from it.
At the sound of horseman and bowman every city takes flight. They have gone into the thickets, they have climbed among the rocks. Every city is abandoned, and no one lives in them.

And you, devastated one, what are you doing, dressing in scarlet, decking yourself with ornaments of gold, tearing your eyes wide with eye-paint? In vain you make yourself beautiful. Your lovers have rejected you; they seek your life.

For I have heard a sound like a woman in labour, anguish like a woman bearing her first child, the sound of the daughter of Zion gasping for breath, spreading out her hands: "Woe to me now, for I faint before murderers!"

jeremiah_5.t: Rove about in the streets of Jerusalem; look now, and know, and search her open squares: if you can find a man, if there is one who does justice and seeks faithfulness — then I will forgive her.
And though they say, "As the LORD lives," they swear falsely.

LORD, are your eyes not on faithfulness? You struck them, but they did not writhe; you brought them to an end, but they refused to accept correction. They made their faces harder than rock; they refused to turn back.
And I said: These are only the poor; they have acted foolishly, for they do not know the way of the LORD, the ordinance of their God.
Let me go to the great and speak with them, for they know the way of the LORD, the ordinance of their God. But they too had broken the yoke, they had torn off the bonds.

Therefore a lion from the forest will strike them, a wolf of the desert plains will devastate them, a leopard is watching over their cities. Everyone who goes out from them will be torn to pieces, for their rebellions are many, their turnings away are numerous.
Why should I forgive you for this? Your children have forsaken me and sworn by what are not gods. I satisfied them, and they committed adultery, and they troop to a whore's house.
They were well-fed, lusting horses; each one neighs for his neighbour's wife.
Shall I not call them to account for these things, declares the LORD; and on a nation such as this shall I not avenge myself?
Go up among her vine rows and destroy, but do not make a full end. Strip away her tendrils, for they are not the LORD's.
For the house of Israel and the house of Judah have dealt utterly treacherously with me, declares the LORD.
They have denied the LORD and said, "He is nothing! Disaster will not come upon us, and we will not see sword or famine."
The prophets will become wind, and the word is not in them. So let it be done to them.
Therefore this is what the LORD, the God of hosts, says: Because you have spoken this word, I am about to make my words in your mouth a fire and this people wood, and it will consume them.

I am about to bring upon you a nation from far off, house of Israel, declares the LORD — an enduring nation, a nation from long ago, a nation whose language you do not know, and you will not understand what it says.
Their quiver is like an open grave; all of them are warriors.

It will devour your harvest and your food; they will devour your sons and your daughters; it will devour your flocks and your herds; it will devour your vines and your fig trees. With the sword it will shatter your fortified cities in which you are trusting.
Yet even in those days, declares the LORD, I will not make a full end of you.

And when you say, "For what has the LORD our God done all this to us?", you shall say to them: Just as you forsook me and served foreign gods in your own land, so you shall serve strangers in a land not your own.
Declare this in the house of Jacob, and proclaim it in Judah:
Hear this now, foolish people, without a heart: they have eyes and do not see, they have ears and do not hear.

Do you not fear me, declares the LORD, or tremble before me — who set the sand as a boundary for the sea, a perpetual statute it cannot pass over? They toss themselves, but cannot prevail; its waves roar, but they cannot pass over it.
But this people has a stubborn and rebellious heart; they have turned aside and gone.
They have not said in their heart, "Let us fear the LORD our God, who gives the rain — the autumn rain and the spring rain — in its season, who keeps for us the appointed weeks of harvest."
Your iniquities have turned these things aside, and your sins have withheld the good from you.
For wicked men are found among my people; he lies in wait, as fowlers crouch; they have set a trap that destroys — it is men they catch.
Like a cage full of birds, so are their houses full of deceit. That is how they have become great and grown rich.

They have grown fat, they have grown sleek; they overflow with deeds of evil. They do not plead a cause — the cause of the fatherless — so that it might prosper; and the justice of the needy they have not judged.
Shall I not call them to account for these things, declares the LORD; and on a nation such as this shall I not avenge myself?
