Nevertheless the hand of Ahikam son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah, so that he was not given into the hand of the people to be put to death.

jeremiah_27.t: In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
This is what the LORD said to me: Make for yourself bonds and yoke-bars, and put them on your neck.

And send word to the king of Edom, the king of Moab, the king of the Ammonites, the king of Tyre and the king of Sidon, by the hand of the messengers who have come to Jerusalem to Zedekiah king of Judah.
And command them to say to their masters: This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: This is what you shall say to your masters:
I myself made the earth, humankind and the animals that are on the face of the earth, by my great power and my outstretched arm; and I give it to whomever seems right in my eyes.
And now I myself have given all these lands into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, my servant; and I have also given him the animals of the field to serve him.
And all the nations will serve him, and his son and his son's son, until the time of his own land comes, and many nations and great kings make him serve.

And the nation or kingdom that will not serve him — Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon — and will not put its neck into the yoke of the king of Babylon: with sword and famine and pestilence I will call that nation to account, declares the LORD, until I have finished them by his hand.
And as for you, do not listen to your prophets, your diviners, your dreams, your soothsayers or your sorcerers, who say to you: You shall not serve the king of Babylon.
For they are prophesying falsehood to you, so as to remove you far from your soil; and I will drive you out and you will perish.
But the nation that brings its neck into the yoke of the king of Babylon and serves him, I will let remain on its own soil, declares the LORD; it will work it and dwell in it.
And to Zedekiah king of Judah I spoke according to all these words: Bring your necks into the yoke of the king of Babylon, serve him and his people, and live.
Why should you die, you and your people, by sword, famine and pestilence, as the LORD has spoken concerning the nation that will not serve the king of Babylon?
And do not listen to the words of the prophets who say to you: You shall not serve the king of Babylon — for they are prophesying falsehood to you.
For I did not send them, declares the LORD, and they are prophesying in my name to falsehood, so that I drive you out and you perish, you and the prophets who prophesy to you.

And to the priests and to all this people I spoke: This is what the LORD says: Do not listen to the words of your prophets who prophesy to you, saying: The articles of the house of the LORD are about to be brought back from Babylon now, quickly — for they are prophesying falsehood to you.
Do not listen to them. Serve the king of Babylon, and live. Why should this city become a ruin?

And if they are prophets, and if the word of the LORD is with them, let them now entreat the LORD of hosts, so that the articles remaining in the house of the LORD and the house of the king of Judah and in Jerusalem may not go to Babylon.
For this is what the LORD of hosts says concerning the pillars, the sea, the stands and the rest of the articles that remain in this city,
which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon did not take when he took Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon, along with all the nobles of Judah and Jerusalem.
For this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says concerning the articles that remain in the house of the LORD and the house of the king of Judah and Jerusalem:
They will be taken to Babylon, and there they will remain until the day I attend to them, declares the LORD, and bring them up and bring them back to this place.

jeremiah_28.t: And in that year, in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the fourth year, in the fifth month, Hananiah son of Azzur the prophet, who was from Gibeon, said to me in the house of the LORD, before the eyes of the priests and all the people:
This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon.
Within two years' time I am bringing back to this place all the articles of the house of the LORD that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took from this place and brought to Babylon.
And Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and all the exiles of Judah who went to Babylon I am bringing back to this place, declares the LORD; for I will break the yoke of the king of Babylon.
And Jeremiah the prophet said to Hananiah the prophet, before the eyes of the priests and before the eyes of all the people standing in the house of the LORD —

and Jeremiah the prophet said: Amen! May the LORD do so; may the LORD carry out your words that you have prophesied, to bring back the articles of the house of the LORD and all the exiles from Babylon to this place.
Nevertheless, hear now this word that I am about to speak in your ears and in the ears of all the people:
The prophets who were before me and before you, from of old, prophesied against many lands and great kingdoms, of war and disaster and pestilence.
As for the prophet who prophesies peace — when the word of that prophet comes to pass, then the prophet will be known, the one the LORD has truly sent.
And Hananiah the prophet took the yoke-bar from the neck of Jeremiah the prophet and broke it.

And Hananiah said before the eyes of all the people: This is what the LORD says: So will I break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon within two years' time from off the neck of all the nations. And Jeremiah the prophet went his way.
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, after Hananiah the prophet had broken the yoke-bar from the neck of Jeremiah the prophet:
Go and say to Hananiah: This is what the LORD says: Yoke-bars of wood you have broken, but you will make in their place yoke-bars of iron.

For this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: A yoke of iron I have put on the neck of all these nations, to serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon; and they will serve him. And I have also given him the animals of the field.
And Jeremiah the prophet said to Hananiah the prophet: Listen now, Hananiah: the LORD did not send you, and you have made this people rely on falsehood.
Therefore this is what the LORD says: I am about to cast you out from the face of the ground. This year you are to die, for you have spoken rebellion against the LORD.
And Hananiah the prophet died in that year, in the seventh month.

jeremiah_29.t: And these are the words of the letter that Jeremiah the prophet sent from Jerusalem to the rest of the elders of the exile, and to the priests and the prophets and all the people whom Nebuchadnezzar had taken into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon,
after Jeconiah the king and the queen mother and the court officials, the officials of Judah and Jerusalem, and the craftsmen and the smiths had gone out from Jerusalem —
by the hand of Eleasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah, whom Zedekiah king of Judah sent to Babylon, to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. It said:
This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says to all the exiles whom I have sent into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon:
Build houses and live in them; plant gardens and eat their produce.
Take wives and father sons and daughters; take wives for your sons and give your daughters to husbands, so that they may bear sons and daughters; and multiply there and do not diminish.
And seek the welfare of the city where I have sent you into exile, and pray for it to the LORD; for in its welfare you will have welfare.
For this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Do not let your prophets who are among you, or your diviners, deceive you; and do not listen to your dreams that you are dreaming.
For they are prophesying falsehood to you in my name. I did not send them, declares the LORD.
For this is what the LORD says: When seventy years are completed for Babylon, I will attend to you and carry out for you my good word, to bring you back to this place.
For I myself know the plans I am planning for you, declares the LORD — plans of well-being and not of harm, to give you a future and a hope.
And you will call on me and come and pray to me, and I will listen to you.
And you will seek me and find me, when you seek me with all your heart.

And I will let myself be found by you, declares the LORD, and I will restore your fortunes and gather you from all the nations and from all the places where I have banished you, declares the LORD; and I will bring you back to the place from which I sent you into exile.
But you have said: The LORD has raised up prophets for us in Babylon.
For this is what the LORD says concerning the king who sits on the throne of David and concerning all the people who dwell in this city — your brothers who did not go out with you into exile —
this is what the LORD of hosts says: I am about to send against them sword, famine and pestilence; and I will make them like rotten figs that cannot be eaten because they are so bad.

And I will pursue them with sword, famine and pestilence; and I will make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth — a curse and a waste and a hissing and a reproach among all the nations where I have banished them,
because they did not listen to my words, declares the LORD, which I sent to them by my servants the prophets, rising early and sending them; and you did not listen, declares the LORD.
And you, hear the word of the LORD, all you exiles whom I have sent from Jerusalem to Babylon.

This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says concerning Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, who are prophesying falsehood to you in my name: I am about to give them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will strike them down before your eyes.
And from them a curse will be taken up by all the exiles of Judah who are in Babylon: May the LORD make you like Zedekiah and like Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire —

because they did folly in Israel and committed adultery with their neighbours' wives, and spoke a word in my name, falsehood, which I did not command them. And I am the one who knows, and a witness, declares the LORD.
And to Shemaiah the Nehelamite you shall say:

This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Because you have sent letters in your own name to all the people in Jerusalem, and to Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest and to all the priests, saying:

The LORD has made you priest in place of Jehoiada the priest, to be officers in the house of the LORD over every man who is mad and prophesies, and you shall put him in the stocks and the iron collar.
And now, why have you not rebuked Jeremiah the Anathothite, who is prophesying to you?
For on that account he has sent to us in Babylon, saying: It will be a long time. Build houses and live in them; plant gardens and eat their produce.
And Zephaniah the priest read this letter in the hearing of Jeremiah the prophet.
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:
Send to all the exiles: This is what the LORD says concerning Shemaiah the Nehelamite: Because Shemaiah has prophesied to you, and I did not send him, and he has made you rely on falsehood —

therefore this is what the LORD says: I am about to call Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his offspring to account. He will have no one dwelling among this people, and he will not look on the good that I am doing for my people, declares the LORD; for he has spoken rebellion against the LORD.

jeremiah_30.t: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Write for yourself in a book all the words I have spoken to you.

For days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will restore the fortunes of my people Israel and Judah, says the LORD; and I will bring them back to the land I gave to their ancestors, and they will take possession of it.
And these are the words that the LORD spoke concerning Israel and concerning Judah.
For this is what the LORD says: A sound of trembling we have heard — dread, and there is no peace.
Ask now and see: does a male give birth? Why then have I seen every man with his hands on his loins like a woman in labour, and every face turned pale?
Woe! For that day is great; there is none like it. It is a time of distress for Jacob, yet out of it he will be saved.
And on that day, declares the LORD of hosts, I will break his yoke from off your neck, and I will tear apart your bonds; and strangers will no longer make him serve.
And they will serve the LORD their God and David their king, whom I will raise up for them.

And you, do not fear, my servant Jacob, declares the LORD, and do not be dismayed, Israel; for I am about to save you from far off, and your offspring from the land of their captivity. Jacob will return and be undisturbed and at ease, with no one to frighten him.

For I am with you, declares the LORD, to save you; for I will make a full end of all the nations among whom I scattered you, but of you I will not make a full end. I will discipline you in due measure, and I will certainly not leave you unpunished.
For this is what the LORD says: Your shattering is incurable; your wound is severe.
There is no one to plead your cause; for a sore there are no medicines of healing for you.

All your lovers have forgotten you; they do not care for you. For with the blow of an enemy I have struck you, the correction of a cruel one, because of the greatness of your iniquity; your sins are numerous.
Why do you cry out over your shattering? Your pain is incurable. Because of the greatness of your iniquity, your sins being numerous, I have done these things to you.
Therefore all who devour you will be devoured, and all your foes, every one of them, will go into captivity; those who plunder you will become plunder, and all who despoil you I will make spoil.
For I will bring up new flesh over you, and from your wounds I will heal you, declares the LORD, because they have called you an outcast: "It is Zion; no one cares for her."

This is what the LORD says: I am about to restore the fortunes of the tents of Jacob, and on his dwellings I will have compassion; a city will be rebuilt on its mound, and a fortress will stand in its proper place.
And from them will go out thanksgiving and the sound of merrymakers; I will multiply them and they will not diminish, I will make them honoured and they will not be insignificant.
And his children will be as they were long ago, and his congregation will be established before me; and I will call to account all who oppress him.

And his noble one will be one of his own, and his ruler will come out from his midst; I will bring him near, and he will draw near to me. For who is this who has pledged his heart to draw near to me? declares the LORD.
And you will be a people to me, and I will be God to you.
See — the storm of the LORD! Wrath has gone out, a storm sweeping on; it will whirl on the head of the wicked.
The burning of the LORD's anger will not turn back until he has done and carried out the purposes of his heart. At the end of the days you will understand it.

jeremiah_31.t: At that time, declares the LORD, I will be God to all the clans of Israel, and they will be a people to me.
This is what the LORD says: A people, the survivors of the sword, found favour in the wilderness when Israel went to find rest.
From far off the LORD appeared to me: With an everlasting love I have loved you; therefore I have prolonged steadfast love toward you.
Again I will build you, and you will be rebuilt, virgin of Israel. Again you will adorn yourself with your tambourines and go out in the dance of the merrymakers.
Again you will plant vineyards on the hills of Samaria; the planters will plant and enjoy the fruit.
For there will be a day when watchmen call out in the hill country of Ephraim: Arise, and let us go up to Zion, to the LORD our God!
For this is what the LORD says: Cry out with gladness for Jacob, and shout for joy at the head of the nations! Proclaim, praise, and say: Save your people, LORD, the remnant of Israel!

I am about to bring them from the land of the north, and I will gather them from the remotest parts of the earth — among them the blind and the lame, the pregnant woman and the one in labour together; a great company will return here.

With weeping they will come, and with pleas for mercy I will bring them; I will lead them to torrents of water, on a straight way where they will not stumble. For I have become a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn.
Hear the word of the LORD, you nations, and declare it in the coastlands far off; and say: The one who scattered Israel will gather him, and keep him as a shepherd keeps his flock.
For the LORD has ransomed Jacob and redeemed him from the hand of one stronger than he.

And they will come and cry out for joy on the height of Zion, and be radiant over the goodness of the LORD — over grain and new wine and fresh oil, and over the young of the flock and the herd. Their life will be like a watered garden, and they will never languish again.
Then a virgin will rejoice in the dance, and young men and old together; and I will turn their mourning into joy, and comfort them and make them glad after their sorrow.
And I will satisfy the appetite of the priests with fatness, and my people will be satisfied with my goodness, declares the LORD.
This is what the LORD says: A voice is heard in Ramah, a wailing, bitter weeping — Rachel weeping for her children, refusing to be comforted for her children, because he is no more.
This is what the LORD says: Restrain your voice from weeping and your eyes from tears; for there is a reward for your work, declares the LORD, and they will return from the land of the enemy.
And there is hope for your future, declares the LORD, and children will return to their own territory.
I have surely heard Ephraim bemoaning himself: You disciplined me, and I was disciplined, like an untrained calf. Turn me back and I will turn back, for you are the LORD my God.
For after I turned away I relented, and after I was made to know I struck my thigh. I was ashamed, and I was also humiliated, because I bore the reproach of my youth.

Is Ephraim a dear son to me, a child of delight? For as often as I speak against him, I still surely remember him. Therefore my inward parts are in tumult for him; I will surely have compassion on him, declares the LORD.
Set up signposts for yourself, place guideposts for yourself; set your heart on the highway, the way you went. Return, virgin of Israel, return to these cities of yours!
How long will you waver, turning-away daughter? For the LORD has created a new thing in the land: a female will encompass a man.

This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Again they will say this word in the land of Judah and in its cities, when I restore their fortunes: May the LORD bless you, abode of righteousness, holy mountain!
And Judah and all its cities together will dwell in it — farmers and those who journey with the flock.
For I will satisfy the weary throat, and every faint person I will fill.
At this I awoke and looked, and my sleep had been pleasant to me.
Days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of humankind and the seed of animals.
And just as I watched over them to uproot and to pull down and to overthrow and to destroy and to do harm, so I will watch over them to build and to plant, declares the LORD.
In those days they will no longer say: The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge.
But each will die for his own iniquity; every human being who eats the sour grapes, his own teeth will be set on edge.
Days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will cut a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah —

not like the covenant I cut with their ancestors on the day I took hold of their hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt — my covenant that they themselves broke, though I was a husband to them, declares the LORD.

For this is the covenant I will cut with the house of Israel after those days, declares the LORD: I will put my law within them, and on their heart I will write it; and I will be God to them, and they will be a people to me.

And they will no longer teach one another, each his neighbour and each his brother, saying: Know the LORD! For all of them will know me, from the least of them to the greatest, declares the LORD; for I will forgive their iniquity, and their sin I will remember no more.

This is what the LORD says, who gives the sun for light by day, the fixed orders of the moon and the stars for light by night, who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar — the LORD of hosts is his name:
If these fixed orders depart from before me, declares the LORD, then the offspring of Israel too will cease from being a nation before me for all time.

This is what the LORD says: If the heavens above can be measured and the foundations of the earth below explored, then I too will reject all the offspring of Israel for all that they have done, declares the LORD.
Days are coming, declares the LORD, when the city will be rebuilt for the LORD, from the Tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate.
And the measuring line will go out farther, straight ahead, to the hill of Gareb, and then turn toward Goah.

And the whole valley of the corpses and of the fatty ash, and all the terraced fields as far as the Wadi Kidron, as far as the corner of the Horse Gate eastward, will be holy to the LORD. It will not be uprooted or overthrown again, for ever.

jeremiah_32.t: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD in the tenth year of Zedekiah king of Judah — that was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar.
At that time the army of the king of Babylon was besieging Jerusalem, and Jeremiah the prophet was shut up in the courtyard of the guard, which was in the house of the king of Judah,

where Zedekiah king of Judah had shut him up, saying: Why are you prophesying, saying: This is what the LORD says: I am about to give this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it;

and Zedekiah king of Judah will not escape from the hand of the Chaldeans, for he will surely be given into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will speak with him mouth to mouth and see him eye to eye;
and he will take Zedekiah to Babylon, and there he will remain until I attend to him, declares the LORD. Though you fight the Chaldeans, you will not succeed.
And Jeremiah said: The word of the LORD came to me:
Hanamel son of Shallum your uncle is coming to you, saying: Buy my field that is at Anathoth for yourself, for the right of redemption is yours, to buy it.

And Hanamel my cousin came to me, according to the word of the LORD, to the courtyard of the guard, and said to me: Buy my field that is at Anathoth, in the land of Benjamin, for the right of possession is yours and the redemption is yours; buy it for yourself. And I knew that this was the word of the LORD.
So I bought the field from Hanamel my cousin, the one at Anathoth, and weighed out the silver for him — seventeen shekels of silver.
And I wrote in the document and sealed it and had witnesses attest it, and I weighed the silver on scales.
And I took the document of purchase — the sealed one, containing the terms and conditions, and the open one —

and I gave the document of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah son of Mahseiah, before the eyes of Hanamel my cousin and before the eyes of the witnesses who had signed the document of purchase, before the eyes of all the Judeans sitting in the courtyard of the guard.
And I commanded Baruch before their eyes:

This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Take these documents — this document of purchase, both the sealed one and this open document — and put them in an earthenware vessel, so that they may last many days.
For this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Houses and fields and vineyards will again be bought in this land.
And I prayed to the LORD, after I had given the document of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah:
Ah, Lord GOD! You made the heavens and the earth by your great power and your outstretched arm; nothing is too difficult for you —
who shows steadfast love to thousands and repays the iniquity of the ancestors into the bosom of their children after them, the great and mighty God — the LORD of hosts is his name,
great in counsel and mighty in deed, whose eyes are open to all the ways of the children of humankind, to give to each according to his ways and according to the fruit of his deeds;
who performed signs and wonders in the land of Egypt, until this day, and in Israel and among humankind, and made a name for yourself, as it is this day;
and you brought your people Israel out of the land of Egypt with signs and wonders and a strong hand and an outstretched arm and great terror;
and you gave them this land, which you had sworn to their ancestors to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey;

and they came and took possession of it, but they did not listen to your voice and did not walk in your law; all that you commanded them to do they did not do, and you have made all this disaster happen to them.

See, the siege mounds have reached the city to capture it, and the city has been given into the hand of the Chaldeans who are fighting against it, because of sword and famine and pestilence; and what you spoke has happened, and here you are, seeing it.
And you yourself said to me, Lord GOD: Buy the field for yourself with silver and have witnesses attest it — and the city has been given into the hand of the Chaldeans.
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:
See, I am the LORD, the God of all flesh. Is anything too difficult for me?
Therefore this is what the LORD says: I am about to give this city into the hand of the Chaldeans and into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will capture it.

And the Chaldeans who are fighting against this city will come and set this city on fire and burn it, with the houses on whose roofs they burned offerings as smoke to Baal and poured out drink offerings to other gods, so as to provoke me to anger.

For the people of Israel and the people of Judah have done only what is evil in my eyes from their youth; the people of Israel have done nothing but provoke me to anger with the work of their hands, declares the LORD.
For this city has been to me a provocation of my anger and my wrath from the day they built it until this day, so that I should remove it from before my face,

because of all the evil of the people of Israel and the people of Judah that they did to provoke me to anger — they, their kings, their officials, their priests and their prophets, and the people of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
They turned their backs to me and not their faces; and though I taught them, rising early and teaching, they were not listening, so as to accept correction.
And they put their detestable things in the house that is called by my name, to make it unclean.

And they built the high places of Baal in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, to make their sons and their daughters pass over to Molech — which I did not command them, and it never came into my mind to do this abomination, so as to cause Judah to sin.

And now, therefore, this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says concerning this city of which you are saying: It has been given into the hand of the king of Babylon by sword and famine and pestilence:
I am about to gather them from all the lands where I have banished them in my anger and my wrath and great rage; and I will bring them back to this place and let them dwell in security.
And they will be a people to me, and I will be God to them.
And I will give them one heart and one way, to fear me all their days, for good to them and to their children after them.
And I will cut for them a perpetual covenant, that I will not turn back from following them, to do them good; and I will put the fear of me in their heart, so that they will not turn aside from me.
And I will rejoice over them, to do them good; and I will plant them in this land in faithfulness, with all my heart and with all my being.
For this is what the LORD says: Just as I have brought upon this people all this great disaster, so I am bringing upon them all the good that I am speaking concerning them.
And fields will be bought in this land, of which you are saying: It is a desolation, without human being or animal; it has been given into the hand of the Chaldeans.

Fields will be bought with silver, and documents written and sealed and witnessed, in the land of Benjamin and around Jerusalem, in the cities of Judah and the cities of the hill country and the cities of the Shephelah and the cities of the Negev; for I will restore their fortunes, declares the LORD.

jeremiah_33.t: And the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah a second time, while he was still shut up in the courtyard of the guard:
This is what the LORD says, who made it, the LORD who formed it to establish it — the LORD is his name:
Call to me and I will answer you, and I will tell you great and inaccessible things that you do not know.

For this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says concerning the houses of this city and the houses of the kings of Judah, which have been pulled down to make a defence against the siege mounds and the sword:

they are coming to fight the Chaldeans and to fill them with the corpses of humankind, whom I struck down in my anger and my wrath, and from whom I have hidden my face from this city because of all their evil:
I am about to bring up new flesh and healing for it, and I will heal them; and I will reveal to them an abundance of well-being and faithfulness.
And I will restore the fortunes of Judah and the fortunes of Israel, and I will rebuild them as at the first.
And I will cleanse them from all their iniquity by which they sinned against me, and I will forgive all their iniquities by which they sinned against me and rebelled against me.

And it will be to me a name of joy, a praise and a splendour, to all the nations of the earth who hear of all the good I am doing for them; and they will be in awe and tremble because of all the good and all the well-being I am doing for it.

This is what the LORD says: Again there will be heard in this place, of which you are saying: It is desolate, without human being or animal — in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem that are made desolate, without human being or inhabitant or animal —

the sound of joy and the sound of gladness, the sound of the bridegroom and the sound of the bride, the sound of those who say: Give thanks to the LORD of hosts, for the LORD is good, for his steadfast love is for ever! — bringing a thank offering to the house of the LORD. For I will restore the fortunes of the land as at the first, says the LORD.

This is what the LORD of hosts says: Again there will be in this place, which is desolate, without human being or even animal, and in all its cities, a pasture of shepherds making their flocks lie down.

In the cities of the hill country, the cities of the Shephelah and the cities of the Negev, in the land of Benjamin, around Jerusalem and in the cities of Judah, the flocks will again pass under the hands of one who counts them, says the LORD.
Days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will carry out the good word I have spoken to the house of Israel and concerning the house of Judah.
In those days and at that time I will cause a Branch of righteousness to sprout for David, and he will do justice and righteousness in the land.
In those days Judah will be saved and Jerusalem will dwell in security. And this is what she will be called: The LORD Our Righteousness.
For this is what the LORD says: There will never be cut off for David a man sitting on the throne of the house of Israel;
and for the priests, the Levites, there will never be cut off a man from before me, offering up a burnt offering and burning a grain offering as smoke and making a sacrifice, all the days.
And the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:
This is what the LORD says: If you could break my covenant with the day and my covenant with the night, so that day and night did not come at their appointed time,
then also my covenant with David my servant could be broken, so that he had no son reigning on his throne, and my covenant with the Levites, the priests, my ministers.
As the host of the heavens cannot be counted and the sand of the sea cannot be measured, so I will increase the offspring of David my servant and the Levites who minister to me.
And the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:
Have you not seen what this people have said: The two clans that the LORD chose — he has rejected them? So they spurn my people, so that they are no longer a nation in their sight.
This is what the LORD says: If I have not established my covenant with day and night, the fixed orders of heaven and earth,

then also I will reject the offspring of Jacob and David my servant, so as not to take from his offspring rulers over the offspring of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. For I will restore their fortunes and have compassion on them.

jeremiah_34.t: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, while Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his army and all the kingdoms of the earth under the rule of his hand and all the peoples were fighting against Jerusalem and against all its cities:

This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Go and say to Zedekiah king of Judah, and say to him: This is what the LORD says: I am about to give this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will burn it with fire.

And you will not escape from his hand, for you will surely be captured and given into his hand; your eyes will see the eyes of the king of Babylon, and his mouth will speak with your mouth, and you will go to Babylon.
Only hear the word of the LORD, Zedekiah king of Judah: This is what the LORD says concerning you: You will not die by the sword.

You will die in peace; and as with the burnings for your ancestors, the former kings who were before you, so they will burn spices for you, and they will lament for you: Alas, lord! For I myself have spoken the word, declares the LORD.
And Jeremiah the prophet spoke all these words to Zedekiah king of Judah in Jerusalem,

while the army of the king of Babylon was fighting against Jerusalem and against all the cities of Judah that were left — against Lachish and Azekah; for these were the fortified cities that remained among the cities of Judah.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD after King Zedekiah had cut a covenant with all the people in Jerusalem, to proclaim liberty to them:
that each should let his male slave and his female slave go free, the Hebrew man and the Hebrew woman — so that no one should make a slave of a Judean, his own brother.

And all the officials and all the people who had entered into the covenant obeyed, that each should let his male slave and his female slave go free, so as not to make slaves of them again; and they obeyed and let them go.
But afterwards they turned back and took back the male slaves and the female slaves whom they had let go free, and subdued them again as male slaves and female slaves.
And the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I myself cut a covenant with your ancestors on the day I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of a house of slaves, saying:

At the end of seven years each of you shall let go his brother, the Hebrew who sells himself to you and serves you six years; you shall let him go free from you. But your ancestors did not listen to me and did not incline their ear.
And you yourselves turned back today and did what is right in my eyes, by proclaiming liberty each to his neighbour; and you cut a covenant before me in the house that is called by my name.

But you turned back and profaned my name, and each took back his male slave and his female slave, whom you had let go free at their own desire, and you subdued them to be male slaves and female slaves for you.

Therefore this is what the LORD says: You have not listened to me, to proclaim liberty each to his brother and each to his neighbour. So I am proclaiming liberty for you, declares the LORD — to the sword, to the pestilence and to the famine; and I will make you a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
And the men who transgressed my covenant, who did not carry out the words of the covenant they cut before me — the calf they cut in two and passed between its pieces — I will make them
the officials of Judah and the officials of Jerusalem, the court officials and the priests and all the people of the land, who passed between the pieces of the calf —
I will give them into the hand of their enemies and into the hand of those who seek their life; and their corpses will become food for the birds of the heavens and the animals of the earth.

And Zedekiah king of Judah and his officials I will give into the hand of their enemies and into the hand of those who seek their life, and into the hand of the army of the king of Babylon that has withdrawn from you.

I am about to give command, declares the LORD, and I will bring them back to this city; and they will fight against it and capture it and burn it with fire. And the cities of Judah I will make a waste, with no inhabitant.

jeremiah_35.t: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:
Go to the house of the Rechabites and speak with them, and bring them to the house of the LORD, into one of the rooms, and give them wine to drink.
So I took Jaazaniah son of Jeremiah son of Habazziniah, and his brothers and all his sons, and the whole house of the Rechabites,

and I brought them to the house of the LORD, to the room of the sons of Hanan son of Igdaliah, the man of God, which was beside the room of the officials, above the room of Maaseiah son of Shallum, the keeper of the threshold.
And I set before the sons of the house of the Rechabites bowls full of wine, and cups; and I said to them: Drink wine.
And they said: We do not drink wine, for Jonadab son of Rechab our ancestor commanded us: You shall not drink wine, you or your children, for ever.

And you shall not build a house, and you shall not sow seed, and you shall not plant a vineyard, or own one; for you shall dwell in tents all your days, so that you may live many days on the face of the soil where you are sojourning.
And we have listened to the voice of Jonadab son of Rechab our ancestor, in all that he commanded us — not to drink wine all our days, we, our wives, our sons and our daughters,
and not to build houses for us to live in; and we have no vineyard or field or seed.
And we have dwelt in tents, and we have obeyed and done according to all that Jonadab our ancestor commanded us.
But when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against the land, we said: Come, let us go to Jerusalem, because of the army of the Chaldeans and the army of Aram. And so we have dwelt in Jerusalem.
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:

This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Go and say to the people of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem: Will you not accept correction, and listen to my words? declares the LORD.

The words of Jonadab son of Rechab, who commanded his sons not to drink wine, have been carried out; they have not drunk to this day, for they have obeyed their father's commandment. But I myself have spoken to you, rising early and speaking, and you have not listened to me.

And I sent to you all my servants the prophets, rising early and sending them, saying: Turn back now, each from his evil way, and make your deeds good, and do not walk after other gods to serve them; and dwell on the soil I gave to you and to your ancestors. But you did not incline your ear and did not listen to me.
For the sons of Jonadab son of Rechab have carried out their father's commandment that he commanded them, but this people has not listened to me.

Therefore this is what the LORD, the God of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am about to bring on Judah and on all the inhabitants of Jerusalem all the disaster I have spoken against them; because I spoke to them and they did not listen, and I called to them and they did not answer.

And to the house of the Rechabites Jeremiah said: This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Because you have listened to the commandment of Jonadab your father and kept all his commandments and done according to all that he commanded you,
therefore this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: There will never be cut off for Jonadab son of Rechab a man standing before me, all the days.

jeremiah_36.t: In the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
Take a scroll for yourself and write on it all the words I have spoken to you concerning Israel and Judah and all the nations, from the day I spoke to you, from the days of Josiah, until this day.
Perhaps the house of Judah will hear all the harm I am planning to do to them, so that they may turn back, each from his evil way, and I will forgive their iniquity and their sin.
So Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah, and Baruch wrote on a scroll, from the mouth of Jeremiah, all the words of the LORD that he had spoken to him.
And Jeremiah commanded Baruch: I am shut up; I am not able to go to the house of the LORD.

So you go and read from the scroll that you have written from my mouth — the words of the LORD — in the hearing of the people, in the house of the LORD on a fast day; and read them also in the hearing of all Judah who come from their cities.
Perhaps their supplication will fall before the LORD, and they will turn back, each from his evil way; for great is the anger and the wrath that the LORD has spoken against this people.
And Baruch son of Neriah did according to all that Jeremiah the prophet commanded him, reading from the scroll the words of the LORD in the house of the LORD.

And in the fifth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, in the ninth month, they proclaimed a fast before the LORD — all the people in Jerusalem and all the people who came from the cities of Judah to Jerusalem.

And Baruch read the words of Jeremiah from the scroll, in the house of the LORD, in the room of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper court, at the entrance of the New Gate of the house of the LORD, in the hearing of all the people.
And Micaiah son of Gemariah son of Shaphan heard all the words of the LORD from the scroll.

And he went down to the house of the king, to the room of the scribe; and there all the officials were sitting: Elishama the scribe, Delaiah son of Shemaiah, Elnathan son of Achbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah, and all the officials.
And Micaiah told them all the words he had heard when Baruch read from the scroll in the hearing of the people.

And all the officials sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah son of Shelemiah son of Cushi to Baruch, saying: The scroll from which you read in the hearing of the people — take it in your hand and come. And Baruch son of Neriah took the scroll in his hand and came to them.
And they said to him: Sit now and read it in our hearing. And Baruch read it in their hearing.
And when they heard all the words, they were in dread, looking at one another, and they said to Baruch: We must surely tell the king all these words.
And they asked Baruch: Tell us, how did you write all these words from his mouth?
And Baruch said to them: From his mouth he proclaimed all these words to me, and I wrote them on the scroll with ink.
And the officials said to Baruch: Go, hide yourself, you and Jeremiah, and let no one know where you are.
And they went to the king, into the court, having deposited the scroll in the room of Elishama the scribe; and they told all the words in the hearing of the king.
And the king sent Jehudi to fetch the scroll, and he fetched it from the room of Elishama the scribe; and Jehudi read it in the hearing of the king and of all the officials standing beside the king.
And the king was sitting in the winter house, in the ninth month, with the fire-pot burning before him.

And whenever Jehudi had read three or four columns, he would tear it off with the scribe's knife and throw it into the fire in the fire-pot, until the whole scroll was consumed on the fire in the fire-pot.
And they were not afraid and did not tear their clothes — the king and all his servants who heard all these words.
And even Elnathan and Delaiah and Gemariah had entreated the king not to burn the scroll, but he did not listen to them.
And the king commanded Jerahmeel the king's son, and Seraiah son of Azriel, and Shelemiah son of Abdeel, to seize Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet; but the LORD hid them.
And the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, after the king had burned the scroll and the words that Baruch had written from the mouth of Jeremiah:
Take another scroll for yourself, and write on it all the former words that were on the former scroll, which Jehoiakim king of Judah burned.

And concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah you shall say: This is what the LORD says: You yourself burned this scroll, saying: Why have you written on it that the king of Babylon will surely come and destroy this land and make human being and animal cease from it?

Therefore this is what the LORD says concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah: He will have no one sitting on the throne of David; and his corpse will be thrown out to the heat by day and the frost by night.

And I will call him and his offspring and his servants to account for their iniquity; and I will bring on them and on the inhabitants of Jerusalem and on the people of Judah all the disaster I have spoken against them, but they did not listen.

And Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch son of Neriah the scribe, and he wrote on it from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the document that Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire; and many words like them were added to them besides.

jeremiah_37.t: And Zedekiah son of Josiah reigned as king in place of Coniah son of Jehoiakim, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made king in the land of Judah.
But he did not listen — he and his servants and the people of the land — to the words of the LORD that he spoke by the hand of Jeremiah the prophet.
And King Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest to Jeremiah the prophet, saying: Pray for us now to the LORD our God.
Now Jeremiah was coming and going among the people, and they had not put him in the prison house.
Now the army of Pharaoh had come out from Egypt, and the Chaldeans who were besieging Jerusalem heard the report of them and withdrew from Jerusalem.
And the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet:

This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: This is what you shall say to the king of Judah, who is sending you to me to consult me: The army of Pharaoh that was coming out to help you is about to return to its own land, Egypt.
And the Chaldeans will return and fight against this city, capture it and burn it with fire.
This is what the LORD says: Do not deceive yourselves, saying: The Chaldeans will surely go away from us — for they will not go.

For even if you struck down the whole army of the Chaldeans who are fighting against you, and only men pierced through were left among them, each in his tent, they would rise up and burn this city with fire.
And when the army of the Chaldeans had withdrawn from Jerusalem because of the army of Pharaoh,
Jeremiah went out from Jerusalem to go to the land of Benjamin, to take possession of a portion there among the people.

And he was at the Gate of Benjamin, and there was a captain of the guard whose name was Irijah son of Shelemiah son of Hananiah; and he arrested Jeremiah the prophet, saying: You are deserting to the Chaldeans!
And Jeremiah said: A falsehood! I am not deserting to the Chaldeans. But he did not listen to him, and Irijah seized Jeremiah and brought him to the officials.
And the officials were angry at Jeremiah and struck him, and they put him in the house of fetters, the house of Jonathan the scribe, for they had made it into the prison house.
For Jeremiah went into the house of the cistern and into the cells, and Jeremiah remained there many days.

And King Zedekiah sent and took him, and the king asked him in his house, in secret: Is there a word from the LORD? And Jeremiah said: There is. And he said: You will be given into the hand of the king of Babylon.
And Jeremiah said to King Zedekiah: How have I sinned against you and against your servants and against this people, that you have put me in the prison house?
And where are your prophets who prophesied to you, saying: The king of Babylon will not come against you or against this land?
And now, hear me, my lord the king: Let my supplication fall before you, and do not send me back to the house of Jonathan the scribe, or I will die there.

And King Zedekiah commanded, and they placed Jeremiah in the courtyard of the guard; and a round loaf of bread was given him daily from the bakers' street, until all the bread in the city was gone. And Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard.

jeremiah_38.t: And Shephatiah son of Mattan, Gedaliah son of Pashhur, Jucal son of Shelemiah and Pashhur son of Malchiah heard the words that Jeremiah was speaking to all the people:

This is what the LORD says: Whoever remains in this city will die by sword, famine and pestilence; but whoever goes out to the Chaldeans will live, and his life will be his as plunder, and he will live.
This is what the LORD says: This city will surely be given into the hand of the army of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it.

And the officials said to the king: Let this man be put to death, for in this way he is weakening the hands of the fighting men who remain in this city and the hands of all the people, by speaking such words to them; for this man is not seeking the welfare of this people, but harm.
And King Zedekiah said: See, he is in your hand; for the king can do nothing against you.

And they took Jeremiah and threw him into the cistern of Malchiah the king's son, which was in the courtyard of the guard, and they let Jeremiah down with ropes. And in the cistern there was no water, only mud; and Jeremiah sank in the mud.
And Ebed-melech the Cushite, a court official who was in the house of the king, heard that they had put Jeremiah into the cistern; and the king was sitting in the Gate of Benjamin.
And Ebed-melech went out from the house of the king and spoke to the king:

My lord the king, these men have done evil in all that they have done to Jeremiah the prophet, whom they have thrown into the cistern; and he will die where he is because of the famine, for there is no more bread in the city.
And the king commanded Ebed-melech the Cushite: Take thirty men from here with you, and bring Jeremiah the prophet up from the cistern before he dies.

And Ebed-melech took the men with him and went to the house of the king, to a place under the storehouse, and took from there worn-out clothes and worn-out rags, and let them down to Jeremiah into the cistern with ropes.
And Ebed-melech the Cushite said to Jeremiah: Put the worn-out clothes and rags under your armpits, under the ropes. And Jeremiah did so.
And they drew Jeremiah out with the ropes and brought him up from the cistern; and Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard.
And King Zedekiah sent and brought Jeremiah the prophet to him, to the third entrance in the house of the LORD; and the king said to Jeremiah: I am asking you something; do not hide anything from me.
And Jeremiah said to Zedekiah: If I tell you, will you not surely put me to death? And if I give you counsel, you will not listen to me.
And King Zedekiah swore to Jeremiah in secret: As the LORD lives, who made this life for us, I will not put you to death, and I will not give you into the hand of these men who are seeking your life.

And Jeremiah said to Zedekiah: This is what the LORD, the God of hosts, the God of Israel, says: If you will indeed go out to the commanders of the king of Babylon, then your life will be spared, and this city will not be burned with fire; and you will live, you and your household.

But if you do not go out to the commanders of the king of Babylon, then this city will be given into the hand of the Chaldeans, and they will burn it with fire; and you yourself will not escape from their hand.
And King Zedekiah said to Jeremiah: I dread the Judeans who have deserted to the Chaldeans, in case they give me into their hand and they deal wantonly with me.
And Jeremiah said: They will not give you over. Listen to the voice of the LORD, to what I am speaking to you, and it will go well for you, and your life will be spared.
But if you refuse to go out, this is what the LORD has shown me:

And see, all the women who are left in the house of the king of Judah are being brought out to the commanders of the king of Babylon, and they are saying: They misled you and prevailed over you, those you trusted; your feet are sunk in the mire, and they have turned back.

And all your wives and your children they will bring out to the Chaldeans; and you yourself will not escape from their hand, for by the hand of the king of Babylon you will be captured, and this city will be burned with fire.
And Zedekiah said to Jeremiah: Let no one know of these words, and you will not die.

And if the officials hear that I have spoken with you, and they come to you and say: Tell us what you said to the king; do not hide it from us, and we will not put you to death — and what did the king say to you? —
then you shall say to them: I was letting my supplication fall before the king, that he not send me back to the house of Jonathan to die there.

And all the officials came to Jeremiah and asked him, and he told them according to all these words that the king had commanded; and they kept silent toward him, for the matter had not been overheard.
And Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard until the day Jerusalem was captured. And when Jerusalem was captured —

jeremiah_39.t: In the ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his army came to Jerusalem and laid siege to it.
In the eleventh year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, on the ninth day of the month, the city was broken into.

And all the officials of the king of Babylon came and sat in the Middle Gate: Nergal-sharezer, Samgar-nebu, Sarsekim the Rab-saris, Nergal-sharezer the Rab-mag, and all the rest of the officials of the king of Babylon.

And when Zedekiah king of Judah and all the fighting men saw them, they fled and went out from the city by night, by way of the king's garden, through the gate between the two walls; and he went out by way of the Arabah.

And the army of the Chaldeans pursued them and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho; and they took him and brought him up to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, and he passed sentence on him.
And the king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah at Riblah before his eyes; and all the nobles of Judah the king of Babylon slaughtered.
And he blinded the eyes of Zedekiah, and bound him in bronze fetters to take him to Babylon.
And the Chaldeans burned the house of the king and the house of the people with fire, and pulled down the walls of Jerusalem.

And the rest of the people who remained in the city, and the deserters who had gone over to him, and the rest of the people who remained, Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards took into exile to Babylon.
But some of the poor people, who had nothing, Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards left in the land of Judah; and he gave them vineyards and fields on that day.
And Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon gave command concerning Jeremiah, by the hand of Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards:
Take him and set your eyes on him, and do him no harm at all; but do with him just as he tells you.
So Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards sent, and Nebushazban the Rab-saris, and Nergal-sharezer the Rab-mag, and all the chiefs of the king of Babylon;
and they sent and took Jeremiah from the courtyard of the guard, and gave him over to Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, to take him home; and he remained among the people.
Now the word of the LORD had come to Jeremiah while he was shut up in the courtyard of the guard:

Go and say to Ebed-melech the Cushite: This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am about to bring my words against this city for harm and not for good; and they will happen before your eyes on that day.
But I will deliver you on that day, declares the LORD, and you will not be given into the hand of the men you are afraid of.
For I will surely rescue you, and you will not fall by the sword; and your life will be yours as plunder, because you trusted in me, declares the LORD.

jeremiah_40.t: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD after Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards had set him free from Ramah, when he took him — and he was bound in chains among all the exiles of Jerusalem and Judah who were being taken into exile to Babylon.
And the chief of the bodyguards took Jeremiah and said to him: The LORD your God spoke this harm against this place,
and the LORD has brought it and done just as he said; for you sinned against the LORD and did not listen to his voice, and so this thing has happened to you.

And now, see, I have set you free today from the chains that were on your hand. If it seems good in your eyes to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will set my eye on you; but if it seems wrong in your eyes to come with me to Babylon, do not. See, the whole land is before you: go wherever it seems good and right in your eyes to go.

And while he was still not turning back — Return to Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has appointed over the cities of Judah, and dwell with him among the people; or go wherever it seems right in your eyes to go. And the chief of the bodyguards gave him a food allowance and a present, and let him go.
So Jeremiah went to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, to Mizpah, and dwelt with him among the people who remained in the land.

And all the commanders of the armies who were in the open country, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam over the land, and had put in his charge men and women and little ones, and some of the poor of the land, from those who had not been taken into exile to Babylon.

And they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan the sons of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah son of the Maacathite — they and their men.
And Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan swore to them and to their men: Do not be afraid to serve the Chaldeans. Dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well for you.

And as for me, I am dwelling at Mizpah to stand before the Chaldeans who come to us; and you, gather wine and summer fruit and oil, and put them in your vessels, and dwell in your cities that you have taken hold of.

And also all the Judeans who were in Moab and among the Ammonites and in Edom, and in all the lands, heard that the king of Babylon had given a remnant to Judah, and had appointed over them Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan.
And all the Judeans returned from all the places where they had been driven, and came to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah at Mizpah; and they gathered wine and summer fruit in great abundance.
And Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies who were in the open country came to Gedaliah at Mizpah,
and said to him: Do you know for certain that Baalis king of the Ammonites has sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to strike you down and take your life? But Gedaliah son of Ahikam did not believe them.

And Johanan son of Kareah said to Gedaliah in secret at Mizpah: Let me go and strike down Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and no one will know. Why should he strike you down and take your life, so that all the Judeans who have gathered to you are scattered and the remnant of Judah perishes?
And Gedaliah son of Ahikam said to Johanan son of Kareah: You shall not do this thing, for you are speaking falsehood about Ishmael.

jeremiah_41.t: And in the seventh month Ishmael son of Nethaniah son of Elishama, of the royal offspring and one of the chiefs of the king, came with ten men to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah; and they were eating bread there together at Mizpah.

And Ishmael son of Nethaniah arose, and the ten men who were with him, and they struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan with the sword; and he killed the man whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.
And all the Judeans who were with Gedaliah at Mizpah, and the Chaldeans who were found there, the fighting men, Ishmael struck down.
And on the second day after the killing of Gedaliah, when no one yet knew,

men came from Shechem, from Shiloh and from Samaria — eighty men, their beards shaven and their clothes torn and having gashed themselves — with a grain offering and frankincense in their hand, to bring to the house of the LORD.
And Ishmael son of Nethaniah went out from Mizpah to meet them, weeping as he went; and when he met them he said to them: Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam.
And when they came into the midst of the city, Ishmael son of Nethaniah slaughtered them into the midst of the cistern — he and the men who were with him.

But ten men were found among them, and they said to Ishmael: Do not kill us, for we have hidden stores in the field — wheat and barley and oil and honey. And he refrained and did not kill them among their brothers.

And the cistern into which Ishmael threw all the corpses of the men he had struck down alongside Gedaliah — it was the one King Asa had made because of Baasha king of Israel; Ishmael son of Nethaniah filled it with the slain.

And Ishmael took captive all the rest of the people who were at Mizpah — the daughters of the king and all the people who remained at Mizpah, whom Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards had committed to Gedaliah son of Ahikam. Ishmael son of Nethaniah took them captive and set out to cross over to the Ammonites.
And Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies who were with him heard all the evil that Ishmael son of Nethaniah had done.
And they took all the men and went to do battle with Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and they found him at the great waters in Gibeon.
And when all the people who were with Ishmael saw Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies who were with him, they were glad.
And all the people whom Ishmael had taken captive from Mizpah turned round; they turned back and went to Johanan son of Kareah.
And Ishmael son of Nethaniah escaped with eight men from Johanan, and went to the Ammonites.

And Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies who were with him took all the rest of the people whom he had brought back from Ishmael son of Nethaniah, from Mizpah — after he had struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam — men, the fighting men, and women and little ones and court officials, whom he had brought back from Gibeon.
And they went and stayed at Geruth Kimham, which is beside Bethlehem, intending to go on into Egypt,
because of the Chaldeans; for they were afraid of them, because Ishmael son of Nethaniah had struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.

jeremiah_42.t: And all the commanders of the armies approached, with Johanan son of Kareah and Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people, from the least to the greatest,
and said to Jeremiah the prophet: Let our supplication fall before you, and pray for us to the LORD your God, for all this remnant; for we are left a few out of many, as your eyes see us.
And let the LORD your God declare to us the way we should go and the thing we should do.

And Jeremiah the prophet said to them: I have heard. I am about to pray to the LORD your God according to your words; and every word that the LORD answers you I will tell you — I will not withhold a word from you.
And they said to Jeremiah: May the LORD be a true and faithful witness against us, if we do not act according to every word with which the LORD your God sends you to us.
Whether good or bad, we will listen to the voice of the LORD our God, to whom we are sending you; so that it may go well for us, because we will listen to the voice of the LORD our God.
And at the end of ten days the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah.
And he summoned Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies who were with him, and all the people, from the least to the greatest,
and said to them: This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says — the one to whom you sent me to make your supplication fall before him:
If you will indeed remain in this land, then I will build you and not tear you down, and I will plant you and not uproot you; for I relent concerning the harm I have done to you.
Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon, of whom you are afraid; do not be afraid of him, declares the LORD, for I am with you, to save you and to deliver you from his hand.
And I will grant you compassion, and he will have compassion on you and restore you to your own soil.
But if you say: We will not remain in this land — so as not to listen to the voice of the LORD your God —
saying: No, we will go to the land of Egypt, where we will not see warfare or hear the sound of the ram's horn or hunger for bread; and there we will dwell —
and now, therefore, hear the word of the LORD, remnant of Judah: This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: If you indeed set your faces to go to Egypt, and go to sojourn there,
then the sword you are afraid of will overtake you there, in the land of Egypt; and the famine you are anxious about will pursue closely after you there in Egypt, and there you will die.
And all the men who set their faces to go to Egypt to sojourn there will die by sword, famine and pestilence; and they will have no survivor or escapee from the disaster I am bringing on them.

For this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Just as my anger and my wrath were poured out on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so my wrath will be poured out on you when you go to Egypt; and you will become an execration and a horror and a curse and a reproach, and you will not see this place again.
The LORD has spoken concerning you, remnant of Judah: Do not go to Egypt. Know for certain that I have warned you today.

For you have gone astray at the cost of your lives; for you yourselves sent me to the LORD your God, saying: Pray for us to the LORD our God, and according to all that the LORD our God says, so tell us, and we will do it.
And I have told you today, but you have not listened to the voice of the LORD your God, or to anything with which he sent me to you.
And now, know for certain that you will die by sword, famine and pestilence in the place where you desire to go and sojourn.

jeremiah_43.t: And when Jeremiah had finished speaking to all the people all the words of the LORD their God, with which the LORD their God had sent him to them — all these words —

Azariah son of Hoshaiah and Johanan son of Kareah and all the arrogant men said to Jeremiah: You are speaking falsehood! The LORD our God did not send you to say: You shall not go to Egypt to sojourn there.
For Baruch son of Neriah is inciting you against us, so as to give us into the hand of the Chaldeans, to put us to death and to take us into exile to Babylon.
And Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies and all the people did not listen to the voice of the LORD, to remain in the land of Judah.
And Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies took all the remnant of Judah, who had come back from all the nations where they had been driven, to sojourn in the land of Judah:

the men and the women and the little ones and the daughters of the king, and every person whom Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, and Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah.
And they went to the land of Egypt, for they did not listen to the voice of the LORD; and they came to Tahpanhes.
And the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes:
Take large stones in your hand and hide them in the mortar, in the brick terrace at the entrance of Pharaoh's house in Tahpanhes, before the eyes of Judean men,

and say to them: This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am about to send and fetch Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, my servant, and I will set his throne above these stones that I have hidden; and he will spread his canopy over them.
And he will come and strike the land of Egypt: those who are for death, to death; those who are for captivity, to captivity; those who are for the sword, to the sword.

And I will kindle fire in the houses of the gods of Egypt, and he will burn them and take them captive; and he will pick the land of Egypt clean as a shepherd picks his garment clean, and he will go out from there in peace.
And he will shatter the pillars of Beth-shemesh, which is in the land of Egypt; and the houses of the gods of Egypt he will burn with fire.

jeremiah_44.t: The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the Judeans who were dwelling in the land of Egypt — at Migdol, at Tahpanhes, at Memphis and in the land of Pathros:

This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: You yourselves have seen all the disaster I brought on Jerusalem and on all the cities of Judah; and today they are a ruin, with no inhabitant in them,
because of the evil they did, to provoke me to anger, by going to burn offerings as smoke and to serve other gods whom they did not know — they, you, and your ancestors.
And I sent to you all my servants the prophets, rising early and sending them, saying: Do not do this abominable thing, which I hate.
But they did not listen and did not incline their ear, to turn back from their evil and stop burning offerings as smoke to other gods.
And my wrath and my anger poured out and burned in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem, and they became a ruin and a desolation, as they are this day.

And now, this is what the LORD, the God of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Why are you doing great harm to your own lives, cutting off from among you man and woman, child and infant, from the midst of Judah, so as to leave yourselves no remnant —

provoking me to anger with the works of your hands, by burning offerings as smoke to other gods in the land of Egypt, where you have come to sojourn — so as to cut yourselves off and to become a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth?

Have you forgotten the evils of your ancestors and the evils of the kings of Judah and the evils of his wives, and your own evils and the evils of your wives, which they did in the land of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?
They have not been humbled to this day; they have not feared, and they have not walked in my law and my statutes that I set before you and before your ancestors.
Therefore this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am setting my face against you for harm, and to cut off all Judah.

And I will take away the remnant of Judah, who set their faces to go to the land of Egypt to sojourn there; and they will all meet their end in the land of Egypt. They will fall by the sword, by famine they will meet their end, from the least to the greatest; by sword and famine they will die, and they will become an execration, a horror, a curse and a reproach.
And I will call to account those who dwell in the land of Egypt, just as I called Jerusalem to account — by sword, by famine and by pestilence.

And there will be no escapee or survivor for the remnant of Judah who went to sojourn there in the land of Egypt, to return to the land of Judah, to which they long to return and dwell; for they will not return, except as fugitives.

And all the men who knew that their wives were burning offerings as smoke to other gods, and all the women who were standing by, a great company, and all the people who were dwelling in the land of Egypt, in Pathros, answered Jeremiah:
As for the word you have spoken to us in the name of the LORD — we are not going to listen to you.

For we will surely do everything that has gone out of our own mouth: to burn offerings as smoke to the queen of the heavens and to pour out drink offerings to her, as we did, we and our ancestors, our kings and our officials, in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. And we had our fill of bread and were well, and we saw no disaster.
But since we ceased to burn offerings as smoke to the queen of the heavens and to pour out drink offerings to her, we have lacked everything, and by sword and famine we have met our end.

And when we were burning offerings as smoke to the queen of the heavens and pouring out drink offerings to her — was it without our husbands that we made cakes for her, shaped in her image, and poured out drink offerings to her?
And Jeremiah said to all the people — to the men and to the women and to all the people who had answered him — saying:

Was it not the offerings of smoke that you burned in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem — you and your ancestors, your kings and your officials and the people of the land — that the LORD remembered, and that came into his mind?

And the LORD could no longer endure it, because of the evil of your deeds, because of the abominations you did; and your land has become a ruin and a waste and a curse, with no inhabitant, as it is this day.

Because you burned offerings as smoke, and because you sinned against the LORD and did not listen to the voice of the LORD, and did not walk in his law and his statutes and his testimonies — therefore this disaster has come upon you, as it is this day.
And Jeremiah said to all the people and to all the women: Hear the word of the LORD, all Judah who are in the land of Egypt.

This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: You and your wives — you have spoken with your mouths and fulfilled it with your hands, saying: We will surely perform our vows that we have vowed, to burn offerings as smoke to the queen of the heavens and to pour out drink offerings to her. Then surely carry out your vows; surely perform your vows!

Therefore hear the word of the LORD, all Judah who dwell in the land of Egypt: I have sworn by my great name, says the LORD: My name will no longer be named in the mouth of any man of Judah, saying: As Lord GOD lives! — in all the land of Egypt.
I am watching over them for harm and not for good; and every man of Judah who is in the land of Egypt will meet his end by sword and famine, until they are finished.

And escapees of the sword will return from the land of Egypt to the land of Judah, few in number; and all the remnant of Judah who went to the land of Egypt to sojourn there will know whose word stands — mine or theirs.
And this will be the sign for you, declares the LORD, that I am about to call you to account in this place, so that you may know that my words will surely stand against you for harm:

This is what the LORD says: I am about to give Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies and into the hand of those who seek his life, just as I gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, his enemy who sought his life.

jeremiah_45.t: The word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch son of Neriah, when he wrote these words on a scroll from the mouth of Jeremiah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:
This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says concerning you, Baruch:
You said: Woe to me now, for the LORD has added sorrow to my pain! I am weary with my groaning, and I have found no rest.
This is what you shall say to him: This is what the LORD says: What I have built I am tearing down, and what I have planted I am uprooting — and that is the whole land.

And you — are you seeking great things for yourself? Do not seek them. For I am about to bring disaster on all flesh, declares the LORD; but I will give you your life as plunder, in all the places where you go.

jeremiah_46.t: The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the nations.

Concerning Egypt, against the army of Pharaoh Necho king of Egypt, which was by the river Euphrates at Carchemish, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck down in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:
Set the buckler and shield in order, and draw near for battle!
Harness the horses, and mount, you horsemen! Take your stand in helmets; polish the spears, put on the armour!
Why have I seen it? They are terrified, turning back; their warriors are crushed. They have fled in headlong flight and have not turned round — terror all around! declares the LORD.
Let not the swift flee, and let not the warrior escape! Northward, beside the river Euphrates, they have stumbled and fallen.
Who is this that rises like the Nile, whose waters surge like the rivers?
Egypt rises like the Nile, and its waters surge like the rivers. And it said: I will rise, I will cover the earth; I will destroy the city and those who live in it.
Go up, you horses; drive madly, you chariots! Let the warriors go forth — Cush and Put, who wield the shield, and the Ludites, who wield and bend the bow.

And that day belongs to Lord GOD of hosts, a day of vengeance, to avenge himself on his foes. The sword will devour and be satisfied, and take its fill of their blood; for Lord GOD of hosts has a sacrifice in the land of the north, by the river Euphrates.
Go up to Gilead and take balm, virgin daughter of Egypt! In vain you have multiplied remedies; there is no healing for you.
The nations have heard your shame, and your outcry has filled the earth; for warrior has stumbled against warrior — both of them have fallen together.
The word that the LORD spoke to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the coming of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to strike the land of Egypt:
Declare it in Egypt, and proclaim it in Migdol; proclaim it in Memphis and in Tahpanhes! Say: Take your stand and prepare yourself, for the sword has devoured all around you.
Why have your mighty ones been swept away? They did not stand, for the LORD pushed them down.
He has made many stumble; indeed, each has fallen against his neighbour. And they said: Arise, let us return to our own people and to the land of our birth, because of the sword of the oppressor.
They have called out there: Pharaoh king of Egypt is a noise; he has let the appointed time pass by.
As I live, declares the King, whose name is the LORD of hosts — surely, like Tabor among the mountains and like Carmel by the sea, he will come.
Make yourself baggage for exile, you who dwell there, daughter of Egypt! For Memphis will become a waste, laid desolate, with no inhabitant.
