Egypt is a beautiful heifer; a gadfly from the north is coming, coming.

Her hired soldiers in her midst are like fattened calves; for they too have turned and fled together; they have not stood their ground. For the day of their doom has come upon them, the time of their punishment.
Her sound goes like a serpent's; for they come with an army, and with axes they come against her, like woodcutters.
They have cut down her forest, declares the LORD, though it cannot be searched out; for they are more numerous than locusts, beyond number.
The daughter of Egypt is put to shame; she is given into the hand of the people of the north.
The LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am about to call to account Amon of Thebes, and Pharaoh, and Egypt, and her gods and her kings — Pharaoh and those who trust in him.

And I will give them into the hand of those who seek their life, into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and into the hand of his servants. But afterwards it will be inhabited as in days of old, declares the LORD.

And you, do not fear, my servant Jacob, and do not be dismayed, Israel; for I am about to save you from far off, and your offspring from the land of their captivity. Jacob will return and be undisturbed and at ease, with no one to frighten him.

You, do not fear, my servant Jacob, declares the LORD, for I am with you; for I will make a full end of all the nations where I have driven you, but of you I will not make a full end. I will discipline you in due measure, and I will certainly not leave you unpunished.

jeremiah_47.t: The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the Philistines, before Pharaoh struck Gaza.

This is what the LORD says: Waters are rising from the north, and they will become an overflowing torrent; they will overflow the land and all that fills it, the city and those who live in it. The people will cry out, and every inhabitant of the land will wail
at the sound of the stamping of the hooves of his stallions, at the rattling of his chariotry, the din of his wheels. Fathers have not turned back for their children, because their hands hang slack —

because of the day that is coming to devastate all the Philistines, to cut off from Tyre and Sidon every surviving helper. For the LORD is devastating the Philistines, the remnant of the coastland of Caphtor.
Baldness has come upon Gaza; Ashkelon is silenced. O remnant of their valley, how long will you cut yourself?
Alas, sword of the LORD! How long until you are quiet? Gather yourself into your sheath; rest, and be still.
How can it be quiet, when the LORD has given it a command? Against Ashkelon and against the seacoast — there he has appointed it.

jeremiah_48.t: Concerning Moab. This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Woe to Nebo, for it is devastated! Kiriathaim is put to shame and captured; the stronghold is put to shame and shattered.
The praise of Moab is no more. In Heshbon they have planned calamity against her: Come, let us cut her off from being a nation! You too, Madmen, will be silenced; the sword will go after you.
A sound of crying from Horonaim: devastation and great ruin!
Moab is broken; her little ones have made their crying heard.
For the ascent of Luhith — with weeping they go up weeping; for on the descent of Horonaim they have heard the anguish of the cry of ruin.
Flee! Save your lives, and be like a bush in the wilderness!
Because you trusted in your works and in your treasures, you too will be captured; and Chemosh will go out into exile, with his priests and his officials together.
A devastator will come to every city, and no city will escape; the valley will perish and the plain be destroyed, as the LORD has said.
Give a ṣiṣ to Moab, for she will surely go out in flight; her cities will become a waste, with no one living in them.
Cursed is the one who does the work of the LORD slackly, and cursed is the one who withholds his sword from blood!
Moab has been at ease from his youth, settled on his lees; he has not been poured from vessel to vessel, and he has not gone into exile. So his taste has stayed in him, and his aroma has not changed.
Therefore, days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will send to him men who tip, and they will tip him; they will empty his vessels and smash their jars.
And Moab will be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel, their trust.
How can you say: We are warriors, men of strength for battle?
Moab is devastated; her cities have been stormed, and the choicest of his young men have gone down to the slaughter, declares the King, whose name is the LORD of hosts.
The doom of Moab is near at hand, and his calamity comes on fast.
Grieve for him, all you who are around him, and all who know his name! Say: How the staff of strength is broken, the rod of splendour!
Come down from honour and sit in thirst, you who dwell there, daughter of Dibon! For the devastator of Moab has come up against you; he has ruined your strongholds.
Stand by the road and watch, you who dwell in Aroer! Ask the man who flees and the woman who escapes; say: What has happened?
Moab is put to shame, for it is shattered. Wail and cry out! Declare at the Arnon that Moab is devastated.
And judgement has come to the land of the plain: to Holon, to Jahzah, and against Mephaath,
against Dibon, against Nebo, against Beth-diblathaim,
against Kiriathaim, against Beth-gamul, against Beth-meon,
against Kerioth, against Bozrah, and against all the cities of the land of Moab, far and near.
The horn of Moab is cut off, and his arm is broken, declares the LORD.
Make him drunk, for he magnified himself against the LORD; and Moab will sprawl in his vomit, and he too will become a laughing-stock.
And was not Israel a laughing-stock to you? Was he caught among thieves, that every time you spoke of him you shook your head?
Abandon the cities and live in the rock, you inhabitants of Moab! Be like a dove that nests at the sides of the mouth of a ravine.
We have heard of the pride of Moab — he is very proud — his haughtiness, his pride and his arrogance, and the loftiness of his heart.
I myself know his insolence, declares the LORD, and it is not right; his empty boasts have accomplished nothing right.
Therefore I will wail over Moab; for all Moab I will cry out; for the people of Kir-heres one groans.

More than the weeping of Jazer I will weep for you, vine of Sibmah! Your tendrils crossed the sea; they reached as far as the sea of Jazer. On your summer fruit and on your vintage a devastator has fallen.
Joy and rejoicing are taken away from the garden-land and from the land of Moab; I have made the wine cease from the winepresses. No one will tread with the shout; the shout will be no shout.
From the cry of Heshbon as far as Elealeh, as far as Jahaz, they have raised their voice; from Zoar as far as Horonaim, Eglath-shelishiyah. For the waters of Nimrim too will become wastes.
And I will put an end for Moab, declares the LORD, to the one who offers up at a high place and the one who burns offerings to his gods.
Therefore my heart groans for Moab like flutes, and my heart groans like flutes for the people of Kir-heres; therefore the wealth he acquired has perished.
For every head is shaved bald and every beard is clipped; on all hands are gashes, and sackcloth on the loins.
On all the roofs of Moab and in her open squares there is wailing everywhere; for I have shattered Moab like a vessel no one delights in, declares the LORD.
How it is shattered! They wail! How Moab has turned his back in shame! Moab has become a laughing-stock and an object of terror to all around him.
For this is what the LORD says: One will swoop like the eagle and spread his wings against Moab.
Kerioth is captured, and the strongholds are seized; and the heart of Moab's warriors on that day will be like the heart of a woman in labour.
And Moab will be destroyed from being a people, because he magnified himself against the LORD.
Terror and pit and snare are upon you, you who dwell in Moab, declares the LORD.

Whoever flees from the terror will fall into the pit, and whoever climbs up out of the pit will be caught in the snare; for I will bring upon her, upon Moab, the year of their punishment, declares the LORD.

In the shadow of Heshbon those who flee have halted, without strength; for a fire has gone out from Heshbon and a flame from the midst of Sihon, and it has devoured the forehead of Moab and the crown of the head of the sons of uproar.
Woe to you, Moab! The people of Chemosh has perished; for your sons have been taken captive and your daughters taken captive.
But I will restore the fortunes of Moab in the latter days, declares the LORD. Thus far is the judgement of Moab.

jeremiah_49.t: Concerning the sons of Ammon. This is what the LORD says: Has Israel no sons? Has he no heir? Why then has Milcom dispossessed Gad, and his people settled in its cities?

Therefore, days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will sound the shout of battle against Rabbah of the sons of Ammon; and it will become a mound of desolation, and her daughter-towns will be set on fire. And Israel will dispossess those who dispossessed him, says the LORD.

Wail, Heshbon, for Ai is devastated! Cry out, daughters of Rabbah! Gird yourselves with sackcloth, mourn, and run to and fro among the walls; for Milcom will go into exile, with his priests and his officials together.
Why do you boast in your valleys — your valley flowing away, you turning-away daughter, who trusts in her treasures and says: Who will come against me?
I am about to bring terror upon you, declares Lord GOD of hosts, from all who are around you; and you will be driven out, each one straight ahead, with no one to gather the fugitive.
But afterwards I will restore the fortunes of the sons of Ammon, declares the LORD.
Concerning Edom. This is what the LORD of hosts says: Is there no longer wisdom in Teman? Has counsel perished from the discerning? Has their wisdom gone rotten?
Flee, turn back, go deep down to dwell, you who live in Dedan! For I have brought the doom of Esau upon him, the time when I called him to account.
If grape-gatherers came to you, would they not leave gleanings? If thieves came by night, they would destroy only as much as they wanted.
For I myself have stripped Esau bare; I have uncovered his hiding-places, and he cannot hide himself. His offspring is devastated, and his brothers and his neighbours, and he is no more.
Leave your fatherless children; I myself will keep them alive. And let your widows trust in me.

For this is what the LORD says: Those whose sentence was not to drink the cup will certainly drink it — and are you the one who will be utterly exempt from punishment? You will not be exempt, for you will certainly drink.
For by myself I swear, declares the LORD, that Bozrah will become a waste, a reproach, a desolation and a curse; and all her cities will become everlasting ruins.
I have heard a report from the LORD, and an envoy has been sent among the nations: Gather yourselves and come against her, and rise up for battle!
For I have made you small among the nations, despised among humankind.

The horror you inspire has deceived you, the presumption of your heart — you who dwell in the clefts of the rock, who hold the height of the hill. Though you make your nest as high as the eagle's, from there I will bring you down, declares the LORD.
And Edom will become a horror. Everyone who passes by her will be appalled and will hiss at all her wounds.
Like the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbours, says the LORD, no one will dwell there, and no human being will settle in her.

Like a lion he will come up from the thicket of the Jordan to the ever-flowing pasture; for in a moment I will drive him away from her, and I will appoint over her whoever is chosen. For who is like me, and who will summon me, and who is the shepherd who can stand before me?

Therefore hear the counsel of the LORD that he has counselled against Edom, and the purposes he has purposed against the inhabitants of Teman: surely the little ones of the flock will be dragged away; surely their pasture will be made desolate over them.
At the sound of their fall the earth quakes; the outcry — its sound is heard at the Sea of Reeds.
Like the eagle he will go up and swoop, and spread his wings over Bozrah; and the heart of Edom's warriors on that day will be like the heart of a woman in labour.
Concerning Damascus. Hamath and Arpad are put to shame, for they have heard a bad report; they melt away. In the sea there is anxiety; it cannot be quiet.
Damascus has grown slack; she has turned to flee, and panic has seized her. Distress and pains have taken hold of her, like a woman giving birth.
How is the city of praise not abandoned, the town of my joy?
Therefore her young men will fall in her open squares, and all the men of war will be silenced on that day, declares the LORD of hosts.
And I will kindle a fire in the wall of Damascus, and it will devour the fortresses of Ben-hadad.
Concerning Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck. This is what the LORD says: Arise, go up against Kedar, and devastate the sons of the east!
Their tents and their flocks will be taken; their tent-curtains and all their equipment and their camels they will carry off for themselves; and they will call out over them: Terror all around!
Flee, take flight far away, go deep down to dwell, you who live in Hazor, declares the LORD! For Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has counselled counsel against you and purposed a purpose against you.
Arise, go up against a nation at ease, dwelling in security, declares the LORD, with no gates and no bars; they dwell alone.

Their camels will become spoil, and the abundance of their livestock plunder; and I will scatter to every wind those who have their temples clipped, and from every side I will bring their doom, declares the LORD.
And Hazor will become a lair of jackals, a desolation for ever; no one will dwell there, and no human being will settle in her.
The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning Elam, at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah:
This is what the LORD of hosts says: I am about to break the bow of Elam, the chief of their strength.
And I will bring against Elam four winds from the four ends of the heavens, and I will scatter them to all these winds; and there will be no nation where the outcasts of Elam do not come.

And I will shatter Elam before their enemies and before those who seek their life; and I will bring calamity upon them, the burning of my anger, declares the LORD. And I will send the sword after them until I have made an end of them.
And I will set my throne in Elam, and I will destroy from there king and officials, declares the LORD.
And it will be, in the latter days, that I will restore the fortunes of Elam, declares the LORD.

jeremiah_50.t: The word that the LORD spoke concerning Babylon, concerning the land of the Chaldeans, through Jeremiah the prophet.

Declare it among the nations and proclaim it; lift up a standard; proclaim it, do not conceal it! Say: Babylon is captured; Bel is put to shame, Marduk is shattered; her images are put to shame, her idols are shattered.
For a nation has come up against her from the north; it will make her land a waste, and there will be no inhabitant in her. From human being to animal, they have taken flight, they have gone.
In those days and at that time, declares the LORD, the sons of Israel will come, they and the sons of Judah together; they will go, going and weeping, and they will seek the LORD their God.
They will ask the way to Zion, with their faces set that way: Come, let us join ourselves to the LORD in an everlasting covenant that will not be forgotten.
My people have become lost sheep; their shepherds have made them wander; on the mountains they have turned them away. From mountain to hill they have gone; they have forgotten their resting-place.
All who found them devoured them, and their adversaries said: We are not guilty — because they sinned against the LORD, the habitation of righteousness, and the hope of their fathers, the LORD.
Take flight from the midst of Babylon, and go out from the land of the Chaldeans; and be like he-goats leading the flock.

For I am about to rouse and bring up against Babylon an assembly of great nations from the land of the north; they will draw up against her — from there she will be captured. His arrows are like a skilled warrior's; he does not come back empty.
And Chaldea will become plunder; all who plunder her will be satisfied, declares the LORD.
Because you rejoice, because you exult, you plunderers of my inheritance; because you skip about like a threshing heifer and neigh like stallions —
your mother is utterly put to shame; she who bore you is abashed. Look — the last of the nations: a wilderness, a parched land and a desert plain.
Because of the rage of the LORD she will not be inhabited, but will be wholly desolate. Everyone who passes by Babylon will be appalled and will hiss over all her wounds.
Draw up against Babylon all around, all you who bend the bow! Shoot at her, spare no arrow, for she has sinned against the LORD.

Shout against her all around! She has given her hand in surrender; her towers have fallen, her walls are torn down. For this is the vengeance of the LORD: take vengeance on her; as she has done, do to her.
Cut off the sower from Babylon, and the one who wields the sickle in the time of harvest. Because of the sword of the oppressor, each will turn to his own people, and each will flee to his own land.
Israel is a scattered sheep that lions have driven away. The first devoured him — the king of Assyria; and this last one has gnawed his bones — Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.
Therefore this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am about to call the king of Babylon and his land to account, as I called the king of Assyria to account.
And I will bring Israel back to his pasture, and he will graze on Carmel and Bashan; and on the hill country of Ephraim and in Gilead his appetite will be satisfied.

In those days and at that time, declares the LORD, the iniquity of Israel will be sought and there will be none, and the sins of Judah, and they will not be found; for I will forgive those whom I leave as a remnant.
Against the land of Merathaim — go up against her, and against the inhabitants of Pekod! Slay and utterly destroy them, declares the LORD, and do according to all that I have commanded you.
A sound of battle is in the land, and a great ruin.
How the hammer of all the earth is cut down and broken! How Babylon has become a horror among the nations!
I set a snare for you, and you were caught, Babylon, and you did not know it. You were found and seized, because you engaged in strife with the LORD.
The LORD has opened his armoury and brought out the weapons of his indignation; for Lord GOD of hosts has a work to do in the land of the Chaldeans.
Come against her from the farthest end; open her granaries; pile her up like heaps of grain and destroy her utterly; let her have no remnant.
Slay all her young bulls; let them go down to the slaughter! Woe to them, for their day has come, the time of their punishment.
A sound of fugitives and escapees from the land of Babylon, to declare in Zion the vengeance of the LORD our God, the vengeance of his temple!

Summon archers against Babylon, all who bend the bow! Encamp against her all around; let no one escape from her. Repay her according to her deed; according to all she has done, do to her. For she has been presumptuous against the LORD, against the Holy One of Israel.
Therefore her young men will fall in her open squares, and all her men of war will be silenced on that day, declares the LORD.
I am against you, Arrogance, declares Lord GOD of hosts, for your day has come, the time when I call you to account.
And Arrogance will stumble and fall, with no one to raise him up; and I will kindle a fire in his cities, and it will devour everything around him.
This is what the LORD of hosts says: The sons of Israel are oppressed, and the sons of Judah with them; all their captors have kept hold of them; they have refused to let them go.
Their Redeemer is strong; the LORD of hosts is his name. He will surely conduct their case, so as to give rest to the earth and to disquiet the inhabitants of Babylon.
A sword against the Chaldeans, declares the LORD, and against the inhabitants of Babylon, and against her officials and her wise men!
A sword against the empty talkers, and they will become fools! A sword against her warriors, and they will be shattered!
A sword against his horses and his chariotry, and against all the mixed people who are in her midst, and they will become women! A sword against her treasuries, and they will be plundered!
A drought against her waters, and they will dry up! For it is a land of carved images, and over their dread things they act like madmen.
Therefore desert creatures will live there with hyenas, and ostriches will live in her. She will never again be inhabited, nor settled from generation to generation.
Like the overthrow by God of Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbours, declares the LORD, no one will dwell there, and no human being will settle in her.
A people is coming from the north, and a great nation and many kings will be roused from the remotest parts of the earth.
Bow and javelin they take hold of; cruel they are, and they show no mercy. Their sound roars like the sea, and on horses they ride, drawn up as a man for battle against you, daughter of Babylon.
The king of Babylon has heard the report of them, and his hands hang limp. Distress has taken hold of him, anguish like a woman giving birth.

Like a lion he will come up from the thicket of the Jordan to the ever-flowing pasture; for in a moment I will drive them away from her, and I will appoint over her whoever is chosen. For who is like me, and who will summon me, and who is the shepherd who can stand before me?

Therefore hear the counsel of the LORD that he has counselled against Babylon, and the purposes he has purposed against the land of the Chaldeans: surely the little ones of the flock will be dragged away; surely the pasture will be made desolate over them.
At the sound of the cry Babylon is captured! — the earth quakes, and an outcry is heard among the nations.

jeremiah_51.t: This is what the LORD says: I am about to rouse against Babylon and against the inhabitants of Leb-qamai a destroying wind.
And I will send to Babylon winnowers, and they will winnow her and empty out her land; for they will be against her from all around on the day of calamity.
Let no archer bend his bow, and let no one rise up in his armour! And do not spare her young men; utterly destroy all her army.
The slain will fall in the land of the Chaldeans, and those run through in her streets.
For Israel and Judah are not widowed of their God, of the LORD of hosts — though their land is full of guilt before the Holy One of Israel.
Flee from the midst of Babylon; let each save his own life! Do not be destroyed for her iniquity; for this is a time of vengeance for the LORD — he is repaying her what she deserves.
Babylon was a golden cup in the hand of the LORD, making all the earth drunk. The nations drank of her wine; therefore the nations act like madmen.
Suddenly Babylon has fallen and is broken. Wail over her! Take balm for her pain; perhaps she may be healed.
We tried to heal Babylon, but she was not healed. Leave her, and let us each go to his own land; for her judgement has reached to the heavens and has been lifted up to the clouds.
The LORD has brought forth our vindication. Come, let us recount in Zion the work of the LORD our God!

Sharpen the arrows; fill the quivers! The LORD has roused the spirit of the kings of Media, for his purpose against Babylon is to destroy her; for this is the vengeance of the LORD, the vengeance of his temple.

Against the walls of Babylon lift up a standard! Strengthen the watch; station watchmen; prepare the ambushes! For the LORD has both purposed and done what he spoke concerning the inhabitants of Babylon.
You who dwell by many waters, rich in treasures: your end has come, the measure of your cutting off.
The LORD of hosts has sworn by himself: Surely I will fill you with men like the locust, and they will raise the shout over you.
He made the earth by his power, established the world by his wisdom, and by his understanding stretched out the heavens.

At the sound of his giving forth, there is a tumult of waters in the heavens; and he makes clouds rise from the end of the earth. He makes lightnings for the rain and brings out the wind from his storehouses.
Every human is stupid, without knowledge; every metalsmith is put to shame by his idol, for his molten image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them.
They are vapour, a work of mockery; at the time of their punishment they will perish.
Not like these is the portion of Jacob, for he is the one who formed everything; and the tribe of his inheritance — the LORD of hosts is his name.
You are my war-club, my weapons of war; with you I smash nations, and with you I destroy kingdoms.
with you I smash horse and rider, and with you I smash chariot and driver;
with you I smash man and woman, and with you I smash old and young, and with you I smash young man and virgin;
with you I smash shepherd and flock, and with you I smash farmer and team, and with you I smash governors and officials.
And I will repay Babylon and all the inhabitants of Chaldea for all the evil they did in Zion before your eyes, declares the LORD.
I am against you, destroying mountain, declares the LORD, you who destroy all the earth! I will stretch out my hand against you and roll you down from the rocks, and make you a burnt mountain.
And they will not take from you a stone for a corner or a stone for foundations, for you will be everlasting wastes, declares the LORD.

Lift up a standard in the land; blow a horn among the nations! Consecrate nations against her; summon against her the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni and Ashkenaz. Appoint a marshal against her; bring up horses like the bristling locust.
Consecrate nations against her: the kings of Media, their governors and all their officials, and every land under their dominion.
The land quakes and writhes, for the purposes of the LORD against Babylon stand: to make the land of Babylon a waste, with no inhabitant.
The warriors of Babylon have ceased fighting; they sit in the strongholds. Their strength has dried up; they have become women. Her dwellings are set on fire; her bars are broken.
Runner runs to meet runner, and messenger to meet messenger, to tell the king of Babylon that his city is captured from end to end,
and that the fords are seized, the reed-marshes burned with fire, and the men of war are terrified.

For this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: The daughter of Babylon is like a threshing floor at the time it is trodden. Yet a little while, and the time of harvest will come for her.

Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has devoured me; he has thrown me into confusion; he has set me down an empty vessel. He has swallowed me like the sea-monster; he has filled his belly from my delicacies; he has rinsed me out.
The violence done to me and to my flesh be upon Babylon — she who dwells in Zion will say. And my blood be upon the inhabitants of Chaldea — Jerusalem will say.
Therefore this is what the LORD says: I am about to conduct your case, and I will take vengeance for you; I will dry up her sea and make her spring dry.
And Babylon will become heaps of stones, a lair of jackals, a horror and a hissing, with no inhabitant.
Together they roar like young lions; they growl like lions' cubs.
When they are heated I will set out their drinking-feast, and I will make them drunk, so that they exult; and they will sleep an everlasting sleep and not wake, declares the LORD.
I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams with he-goats.
How Sheshach is captured, and the praise of all the earth seized! How Babylon has become a horror among the nations!
The sea has gone up over Babylon; she is covered by the tumult of its waves.
Her cities have become a waste, a parched land and a desert plain, a land where no one dwells and no human being passes through.
And I will call Bel to account in Babylon, and I will bring out of his mouth what he has swallowed; and the nations will no longer stream to him. The wall of Babylon has fallen too.
Come out from her midst, my people, and let each save his own life from the burning of the LORD's anger!

And do not let your heart grow faint, and do not fear at the report that is heard in the land; for the report will come in one year, and after it the report in the next year, and violence in the land, and ruler against ruler.
Therefore, days are coming when I will call to account the carved images of Babylon; all her land will be put to shame, and all her slain will fall in her midst.
And heaven and earth and all that is in them will shout for joy over Babylon; for from the north the destroyers will come against her, declares the LORD.
Babylon too must fall for the slain of Israel, just as for Babylon the slain of all the earth have fallen.
You who have escaped the sword, go; do not stand still! Remember the LORD from far off, and let Jerusalem come to mind.
We are put to shame, for we have heard reproach; disgrace has covered our faces, for strangers have come into the holy places of the house of the LORD.
Therefore, days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will call to account her carved images; and in all her land the fatally wounded will groan.
Though Babylon should climb up to the heavens, and though she should fortify her stronghold on high, from me destroyers will come against her, declares the LORD.
A sound of crying from Babylon, and great ruin from the land of the Chaldeans!
For the LORD is devastating Babylon and silencing in her the great voice; and their waves roar like many waters; the uproar of their voice is given out.
For a devastator has come against her, against Babylon, and her warriors are captured; their bows are broken; for the LORD is a God of recompense — he will surely repay.

And I will make her officials and her wise men, her governors and her officers and her warriors drunk; and they will sleep an everlasting sleep and not wake, declares the King, whose name is the LORD of hosts.

This is what the LORD of hosts says: The broad walls of Babylon will be utterly demolished, and her high gates will be burned with fire; peoples labour for nothing, and nations for fire — and they grow weary.
The word that Jeremiah the prophet commanded Seraiah son of Neriah son of Mahseiah, when he went with Zedekiah king of Judah to Babylon in the fourth year of his reign. Seraiah was quartermaster.
And Jeremiah wrote all the calamity that would come upon Babylon in a single scroll — all these words that are written concerning Babylon.
And Jeremiah said to Seraiah: When you come to Babylon, see that you read aloud all these words,
and say: LORD, you yourself have spoken concerning this place, to cut it off, so that there will be no inhabitant in it, from human being to animal, but it will be everlasting desolations.
And when you have finished reading this scroll aloud, tie a stone to it and throw it into the middle of the Euphrates,
and say: So Babylon will sink and not rise, because of the calamity that I am bringing upon her — and they will grow weary. Thus far are the words of Jeremiah.

jeremiah_52.t: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah, from Libnah.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as Jehoiakim had done.
For it came about because of the anger of the LORD against Jerusalem and Judah, until he cast them out from his presence. And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

In the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came, he and all his army, against Jerusalem; and they encamped against it and built a siege-wall around it.
And the city was under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
In the fourth month, on the ninth of the month, the famine was severe in the city, and there was no food for the people of the land.

And the city was broken into; and all the men of war fled and went out from the city by night, by way of the gate between the two walls, which was by the king's garden — and the Chaldeans were around the city — and they went by way of the Arabah.
And the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho; and all his army was scattered from him.
And they seized the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath; and he passed sentence on him.
And the king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes; and he also slaughtered all the officials of Judah at Riblah.
And he blinded the eyes of Zedekiah and bound him in bronze fetters; and the king of Babylon brought him to Babylon and put him in the prison-house until the day of his death.

And in the fifth month, on the tenth of the month — that was the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon — Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards, who stood before the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
And he burned the house of the LORD and the house of the king and all the houses of Jerusalem; every great house he burned with fire.
And all the walls of Jerusalem all around were broken down by the whole army of the Chaldeans who were with the chief of the bodyguards.

And some of the poorest of the people, and the rest of the people who remained in the city, and the deserters who had gone over to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the artisans, Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards took into exile.
And Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards left behind some of the poorest of the land, to be vinedressers and ploughmen.

And the bronze pillars that belonged to the house of the LORD, and the stands, and the bronze sea that was in the house of the LORD, the Chaldeans broke in pieces; and they carried all their bronze to Babylon.
And they took away the pots and the shovels and the snuffers and the basins and the pans, and all the bronze vessels used in the service.

And the bowls and the fire-pans and the basins and the pots and the lampstands and the pans and the libation-bowls — what was of gold as gold, and what was of silver as silver — the chief of the bodyguards took away.
The two pillars, the one sea, and the twelve bronze bulls that were under the stands, which King Solomon had made for the house of the LORD — the bronze of all these vessels was beyond weighing.
As for the pillars: the height of one pillar was eighteen cubits, and a line of twelve cubits went round it; its thickness was four fingers, and it was hollow.

And a bronze capital was upon it; the height of the one capital was five cubits, with a network and pomegranates on the capital all around, all of bronze. The second pillar had the same, and pomegranates.
And the pomegranates were ninety-six to a side; all the pomegranates on the network all around were one hundred.
And the chief of the bodyguards took Seraiah the chief priest and Zephaniah the second priest and the three keepers of the threshold.

And from the city he took one court official who was an officer over the men of war, and seven men from those who saw the king's face, who were found in the city, and the scribe of the commander of the army, who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land who were found inside the city.
And Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
And the king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah went into exile from its land.
This is the people whom Nebuchadnezzar took into exile: in the seventh year, three thousand and twenty-three Judeans;
in the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, from Jerusalem, eight hundred and thirty-two persons;
in the twenty-third year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards took into exile seven hundred and forty-five Judean persons. All the persons were four thousand six hundred.

And in the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fifth of the month, Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year he became king, lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah and brought him out of the prison-house.
And he spoke kindly with him and set his seat above the seat of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
And he changed his prison clothes, and he ate at his table continually all the days of his life.
And as for his allowance, a continual allowance was given him by the king of Babylon, a day's portion each day, until the day of his death, all the days of his life.

job_1.t: There was a man in the land of Uz whose name was Job. That man was blameless and upright, one who feared God and turned aside from evil.
Seven sons and three daughters were born to him.

His livestock was seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen and five hundred female donkeys, and a very large household of servants; and that man was greater than all the people of the east.
His sons used to go and hold a feast, each in his own house on his day, and they would send and invite their three sisters to eat and drink with them.

And when the days of the feast had gone round, Job would send and set them apart as holy, rising early in the morning and offering up burnt offerings according to the number of them all; for Job said, "Perhaps my sons have sinned and cursed God in their heart." This is what Job did continually.
Now the day came when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan also came among them.
The LORD said to Satan, "Where have you come from?" And Satan answered the LORD, "From roving about on the earth and from walking up and down on it."
And the LORD said to Satan, "Have you considered my servant Job? For there is none like him on the earth — a man blameless and upright, who fears God and turns aside from evil."
And Satan answered the LORD, "Is it for nothing that Job fears God?
Have you not yourself put a hedge around him and around his house and around all that is his, on every side? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his livestock has spread out in the land.
But stretch out your hand now and touch all that is his — see if he will not curse you to your face!"
And the LORD said to Satan, "All that is his is in your hand; only against him do not stretch out your hand." So Satan went out from the presence of the LORD.
Now the day came when his sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their eldest brother.
And a messenger came to Job and said, "The oxen were ploughing and the female donkeys grazing beside them,
and Sabeans fell on them and took them, and they struck down the servants with the edge of the sword; and I alone have escaped, only I, to tell you."

This one was still speaking when another came and said, "The fire of God fell from the heavens and burned up the sheep and the servants and consumed them; and I alone have escaped, only I, to tell you."

This one was still speaking when another came and said, "Chaldeans formed three companies, made a raid on the camels and took them, and they struck down the servants with the edge of the sword; and I alone have escaped, only I, to tell you."
While this one was still speaking, another came and said, "Your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their eldest brother,
and a great wind came from across the wilderness and struck the four corners of the house, and it fell on the young people and they died; and I alone have escaped, only I, to tell you."
Then Job arose and tore his robe and shaved his head, and he fell to the ground and bowed down.
And he said, "Naked I came from my mother's womb, and naked I shall return there. The LORD gave and the LORD has taken; may the name of the LORD be blessed."
In all this Job did not sin, and he did not charge God with unseemliness.

job_2.t: Now the day came when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan also came among them to present himself before the LORD.
And the LORD said to Satan, "Where have you come from?" And Satan answered the LORD, "From roving about on the earth and from walking up and down on it."

And the LORD said to Satan, "Have you considered my servant Job? For there is none like him on the earth — a man blameless and upright, who fears God and turns aside from evil. And still he holds fast to his integrity, though you incited me against him to ruin him without cause."
And Satan answered the LORD, "Skin for skin! All that a man has he will give for his life.
But stretch out your hand now and touch his bone and his flesh — see if he will not curse you to your face!"
And the LORD said to Satan, "He is in your hand; only preserve his life."
So Satan went out from the presence of the LORD and struck Job with malignant boils, from the sole of his foot to his scalp.
And he took a potsherd to scrape himself with, and he sat among the ashes.
And his wife said to him, "Are you still holding fast to your integrity? Curse God and die."
But he said to her, "You speak as one of the foolish women speaks. Shall we accept the good from God and not accept the evil?" In all this Job did not sin with his lips.

Now the three friends of Job heard of all this evil that had come upon him, and each came from his own place — Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite — and they met together by appointment to come and show him sympathy and comfort him.
When they lifted up their eyes from a distance they did not recognise him, and they lifted up their voice and wept; and each tore his robe, and they sprinkled dust on their heads toward the heavens.
And they sat with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that his pain was very great.

job_3.t: After this Job opened his mouth and cursed his day.
And Job answered and said:
Let the day perish on which I was born, and the night that said, "A man has been conceived."
That day — let it be darkness; let God above not seek it out, and let no daylight shine upon it.
Let darkness and deep darkness reclaim it; let a cloud settle over it; let the blackness of the day terrify it.
That night — let gloom seize it; let it not rejoice among the days of the year; let it not come into the number of the months.
That night — let it be barren; let no cry of joy come into it.
Let those who curse the day damn it, those ready to rouse Leviathan.
Let the stars of its twilight grow dark; let it hope for light and find none, and let it not look on the eyelids of dawn —
because it did not shut the doors of my mother's womb or hide trouble from my eyes.
Why did I not die at birth, come out from the belly and expire?
Why did knees receive me, and why were there breasts for me to suck?
For now I would be lying down and at peace; I would have slept, and then there would be rest for me,
with kings and counsellors of the earth who rebuilt ruins for themselves,
or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver.
Or I would not have been, like a hidden miscarriage, like infants who never saw light.
There the wicked cease from turmoil, and there the weary of strength are at rest.
Together the prisoners are at ease; they do not hear the voice of a taskmaster.
Small and great are there, and a slave is free from his master.
Why is light given to the sufferer, and life to the bitter in spirit —
who long for death and it does not come, and dig for it more than for hidden treasure;
those who rejoice to exultation, who are glad when they find the grave.
to a man whose way is hidden, and whom God has hedged in.
For my groaning comes before my bread, and my roarings pour out like water.
For the fear I feared has come upon me, and what I dreaded has come to me.
I am not at ease and I am not at peace and I am not at rest, and turmoil has come.

job_4.t: And Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
If one ventures a word to you, will you be impatient? Yet who can hold back from speaking?
See, you have instructed many, and you have strengthened slack hands.
Your words have raised up the stumbling, and you have made firm the bending knees.
But now it comes to you and you are impatient; it touches you and you are dismayed.
Is not your fear of God your confidence, and your hope the integrity of your ways?
Remember, now: who that was innocent ever perished? And where were the upright destroyed?
As I have seen it: those who plough iniquity and sow trouble reap the same.
By the breath of God they perish, and by the blast of his anger they come to an end.
The roaring of the lion, the voice of the fierce lion, and the teeth of the young lions are broken.
The old lion perishes for lack of prey, and the whelps of the lioness are scattered.
Now a word was brought to me by stealth, and my ear caught a whisper of it.
In disquieting thoughts from visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on people,
fear met me, and trembling, and it made all my bones tremble.
And a spirit passed over my face; it made the hair of my flesh stand up.
It stood still, but I did not recognise its appearance; a form was before my eyes. There was silence, and I heard a voice:
"Can a mortal be righteous before God? Can a man be clean before his Maker?"
See, he does not trust his servants, and he charges his angels with error;
how much more those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, who are crushed before a moth!
Between morning and evening they are shattered; with no one giving it a thought, they perish for ever.
Is not their tent-cord pulled up within them? They die, and not in wisdom.

job_5.t: Call now — is there anyone who will answer you? And to which of the holy ones will you turn?
For vexation kills the fool, and jealousy slays the simple.
I myself have seen a fool taking root, and suddenly I pronounced his dwelling cursed.
His children are far from safety; they are crushed in the gate, and there is no one to deliver them.
Whose harvest the hungry eat, taking it even from among thorns, and a snare pants after their wealth.
For hardship does not come out of the dust, and trouble does not spring up from the ground;
for a human is born to trouble, as the sparks fly upward.
But as for me, I would seek God, and to God I would lay my case.
who does great things beyond searching out, wonders beyond number;
who gives rain on the face of the earth and sends water on the face of the fields;
to set the lowly on high, so that mourners are lifted to safety.
who frustrates the plans of the shrewd, so that their hands achieve no success.
who catches the wise in their own shrewdness, and the counsel of the twisted is hurried away.
By day they meet darkness, and they grope at noon as in the night.
But he saves the needy from the sword of their mouth, and from the hand of the strong.
So there is hope for the poor, and injustice shuts its mouth.
See, how blessed is the mortal whom God reproves! So do not reject the discipline of the Almighty,
for he causes pain and he binds up; he shatters, and his own hands heal.
In six troubles he will deliver you, and in seven no harm will touch you.
In famine he will ransom you from death, and in war from the power of the sword.
You will be hidden from the whip of the tongue, and you will not fear destruction when it comes.
At destruction and at hunger you will laugh, and you need not fear the wild animals of the earth.
For your covenant will be with the stones of the field, and the wild animals of the field will be at peace with you.
And you will know that your tent is at peace, and you will inspect your fold and find nothing missing.
And you will know that your offspring are many, and your descendants like the grass of the earth.
You will come to the grave in full vigour, as a shock of grain goes up in its season.
See, this we have searched out; so it is. Hear it, and know it for yourself.

job_6.t: And Job answered and said:
If only my vexation were truly weighed, and my calamity laid with it in the balances!
For it would be heavier than the sand of the seas; that is why my words have been rash.
For the arrows of the Almighty are in me; my spirit drinks their poison; the terrors of God are arrayed against me.
Does the wild donkey bray over grass, or the ox low over its fodder?
Is tasteless food eaten without salt? Is there any taste in the white of an egg?
I refuse to touch them; they are like sickness in my food.
Who will grant that my petition come, and that God give me my hope?
That God would be willing to crush me, that he would loose his hand and cut me off!
And this would still be my comfort — I would exult in unsparing anguish — that I have not concealed the sayings of the Holy One.
What is my strength, that I should wait? And what is my end, that I should prolong my life?
Is my strength the strength of stones? Is my flesh bronze?
Is there no help within me, and has sound wisdom been driven from me?
To the despairing, kindness is owed from his friend, even if he forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
My brothers have been as treacherous as a wadi, like the channel of wadis that pass away —
dark with ice, with the snow hiding itself in them;
At the time they grow warm, they fall silent; in the heat they are dried up from their place.
The paths of their course wind about; they go up into the waste and perish.
The caravans of Tema looked; the travelling companies of Sheba hoped for them.
They were ashamed because they had been confident; they came there and were disappointed.
For now you have become like that to me; you see a terror and you are afraid.
Is it because I said, "Give me something," or "From your wealth pay a bribe for me,"
or "Rescue me from the hand of an adversary, and ransom me from the hand of the ruthless"?
Teach me, and I will be silent; make me understand where I have erred.
How painful are honest sayings! But what does your reproof prove?
Do you plan to reprove mere words, and treat the sayings of a despairing man as wind?
You would even cast lots over an orphan, and bargain over your friend.
And now be willing: turn and look at me; I would not lie to your faces.
Turn back, please; let there be no injustice. Turn back again — my righteousness is still in the matter.
Is there injustice on my tongue? Can my palate not discern what is ruinous?

job_7.t: Is there not hard service for a mortal on earth, and are not his days like a hired labourer's days?
like a slave panting for shade, like a hired labourer waiting for his wages —
so I have been allotted months of emptiness, and nights of trouble have been apportioned to me.
When I lie down I say, "When shall I rise?" But the evening drags on, and I have my fill of tossing until twilight.
My flesh is clothed with maggots and caked with dirt; my skin closes up and then breaks out afresh.
My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle, and they come to an end without hope.
Remember that my life is a breath; my eye will not return to see good.
The eye that sees me will not behold me; your eyes will be on me, and I shall be gone.
A cloud is spent and gone; so the one who goes down to Sheol does not come up.
He does not return again to his house, and his place does not recognise him again.
So I will not restrain my mouth; I will speak in the distress of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my being.
Am I the sea, or a sea monster, that you set a watch over me?
When I say, "My couch will comfort me, my bed will carry away my complaint,"
then you dismay me with dreams and terrify me with visions,
so that I would choose strangling, death rather than these bones of mine.
I have had enough — I shall not live for ever. Let me alone, for my days are a breath.
What is a mortal, that you make so much of him, and that you set your heart on him,
and visit him every morning and test him every moment?
How long will you not look away from me, or let me alone long enough to swallow my spittle?
If I have sinned, what do I do to you, watcher of humankind? Why have you set me as your target, so that I have become a burden to myself?
And why do you not lift away my transgression and make my iniquity pass? For now I shall lie down in the dust, and you will seek me, and I shall be gone.

job_8.t: And Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
How long will you say such things, and let the sayings of your mouth be a mighty wind?
Does God pervert justice, or does the Almighty pervert righteousness?
If your children sinned against him, he gave them over into the hand of their transgression.
If you yourself will seek God and plead for favour from the Almighty,
if you are pure and upright, surely now he will rouse himself for you and restore your righteous abode.
And though your beginning was small, your latter end will grow very great.
For ask the former generation, and give attention to what their fathers searched out.
For we are of yesterday and know nothing; our days on earth are a shadow.
Will they not teach you and tell you, and bring forth words from their heart?
Does papyrus grow tall without a marsh? Does reed-grass grow without water?
While it is still green and not cut, it withers before any other plant.
Such are the paths of all who forget God, and the hope of the godless perishes,
whose confidence is fragile, and whose trust is a spider's house.
He leans on his house, and it does not stand; he takes hold of it, and it does not endure.
He is a well-watered plant in the sun, and his shoot spreads over his garden.
His roots are interwoven over a heap of rocks; he finds a place among the stones.
If he is swallowed up from his place, then it denies him: "I have never seen you."
See, that is the joy of his way, and from the dust others spring up.
See, God does not reject a blameless man, and does not take hold of the hand of evildoers.
until he fills your mouth with laughter, and your lips with a shout of joy.
Those who hate you will be clothed with shame, and the tent of the wicked will be no more.

job_9.t: And Job answered and said:
Truly I know that it is so; but how can a mortal be righteous before God?
If one desired to contend with him, he could not answer him once in a thousand times.
Wise of heart and mighty in strength — who has hardened himself against him and come out unharmed?
who removes mountains and they do not know it, who overturns them in his anger;
who shakes the earth from its place, and its pillars shudder;
who speaks to the sun and it does not rise, and who seals up the stars;
who alone stretches out the heavens and treads on the high places of the Sea;
who makes the Bear, Orion and the Pleiades, and the chambers of the south;
who does great things beyond searching out, and wonders beyond number.
See, he passes by me and I do not see him; he moves on and I do not perceive him.
See, he snatches away — who can turn him back? Who will say to him, "What are you doing?"
God does not turn back his anger; beneath him the helpers of Rahab lay prostrate.
How much less can I answer him, or choose my words to argue with him!
Though I were in the right, I could not answer him; I would have to plead for favour with my judge.
If I called and he answered me, I would not believe that he was listening to my voice —
he who crushes me with a tempest and multiplies my wounds without cause.
He does not let me get my breath back, but fills me to surfeit with bitterness.
If it is a matter of strength — he is the mighty one! And if of justice — who will summon him?
Though I were in the right, my own mouth would condemn me; blameless as I am, it would declare me perverse.
I am blameless — I do not care for myself. I reject my life.
It is all one; therefore I say: he brings the blameless and the wicked alike to an end.
When a scourge kills suddenly, he mocks at the despair of the innocent.
The earth is given into the hand of the wicked; he covers the faces of its judges. If it is not he, then who is it?
And my days are swifter than a runner; they flee away, they have seen no good.
They have passed on like ships of reed, like an eagle swooping on its food.
If I say, "I will forget my complaint, I will change my expression and be cheerful,"
then I dread all my pains; I know that you will not hold me innocent.
I shall be counted guilty; why then should I labour in vain?
If I washed myself in snow water and cleansed my hands with lye,
then you would plunge me into the pit, and my own clothes would abhor me.
For he is not a man like me, that I could answer him, that we could come together to trial.
There is no arbiter between us who might lay his hand on us both.
Let him remove his rod from me, and let his terror not dismay me.
Then I would speak and not fear him, for that is not how I am in myself.

job_10.t: I loathe my life; I will give free rein to my complaint; I will speak in the bitterness of my being.
I will say to God: Do not condemn me; make known to me why you contend with me.
Is it good to you that you should oppress, that you should reject the labour of your hands and shine upon the counsel of the wicked?
Do you have eyes of flesh? Do you see as a mortal sees?
Are your days like the days of a mortal, or your years like a man's days,
that you seek out my iniquity and search for my sin,
though you know that I am not guilty, and there is no one to deliver from your hand?
Your hands shaped me and made me, every part of me — and now you swallow me up.
Remember that you made me like clay — and will you return me to dust?
Did you not pour me out like milk and curdle me like cheese?
You clothed me with skin and flesh, and knitted me together with bones and sinews.
Life and steadfast love you have shown me, and your care has kept my spirit.
Yet these things you hid in your heart; I know that this was your purpose.
If I sinned, you would be watching me, and you would not acquit me of my iniquity.
If I am guilty — woe to me! And if I am in the right, I still cannot lift my head, sated with shame and looking on my affliction.
And if it rises up, you hunt me like a lion, and you turn back and show yourself marvellous against me.
You renew your witnesses against me and increase your vexation with me; relief troops and an army come at me.
And why did you bring me out from the womb? I would have expired, and no eye would have seen me.
I would have been as though I had never been, carried from the womb to the grave.
Are not my days few? Then stop, and turn away from me, that I may be cheerful a little,
before I go, never to return, to the land of darkness and deep darkness,
a land of gloom like darkness, of deep darkness and no order, where the light itself is like darkness.

job_11.t: And Zophar the Naamathite answered and said:
Shall a flood of words go unanswered? And shall a man of many words be acquitted?
Shall your empty talk silence men? Shall you mock with no one to shame you?
For you have said, "My teaching is pure, and I am clean in your eyes."
But if only God would speak and open his lips against you!
and tell you the secrets of wisdom, for sound wisdom has two sides — and know that God is overlooking part of your iniquity.
Can you find out the deep things of God? Can you find out the limit of the Almighty?
It is higher than the heavens — what can you do? Deeper than Sheol — what can you know?
Its measure is longer than the earth and broader than the sea.
If he passes by and shuts a man up and calls an assembly, who can turn him back?
For he knows men of falsehood; when he sees iniquity, will he not consider it?
A hollow man will get understanding when a wild donkey's colt is born a human.
If you yourself set your heart right and spread out your palms to him,
if iniquity is in your hand, put it far away, and do not let injustice dwell in your tents,
then you will lift up your face without blemish, and you will be firmly established and not afraid.
For you will forget your trouble; you will remember it like waters gone by.
Your life will rise brighter than noon; though it grow dark, it will be like morning.
And you will be secure, for there is hope; you will look about you and lie down in safety.
And you will lie down with no one to make you afraid, and many will seek your favour.
But the eyes of the wicked will fail; escape will perish from them, and their hope is the last gasp of life.

job_12.t: And Job answered and said:
Truly you are the people, and wisdom will die with you!
I also have a mind like yours; I do not fall short of you. And who does not know such things as these?
I am a laughingstock to my friend — one who called on God and was answered — a laughingstock: the righteous, the blameless man.
Contempt for misfortune, in the thought of one at ease; a shove for those whose foot is slipping.
The tents of destroyers are at peace, and those who provoke God are secure — whoever carries his god in his hand.
But ask the animals, and let them teach you, and the birds of the heavens, and let them tell you;
or speak to the earth, and let it teach you, and let the fish of the sea recount it to you.
Who among all these does not know that the hand of the LORD has done this?
in whose hand is the life of every living thing, and the breath of all human flesh.
Does not the ear test words, as the palate tastes its food?
With the aged is wisdom, and in length of days, understanding.
With him are wisdom and might; to him belong counsel and understanding.
See, he tears down and it is not rebuilt; he shuts a man in and there is no opening.
See, he holds back the waters and they dry up; he sends them out and they overturn the earth.
With him are strength and sound wisdom; both the deceived and the deceiver are his.
He leads counsellors away stripped, and makes fools of judges.
He loosens the bond of kings and binds a loincloth on their loins.
He leads priests away stripped, and overthrows the long-established.
He removes the speech of the trusted, and takes away the discernment of elders.
He pours contempt on nobles and loosens the belt of the mighty.
He uncovers deep things out of darkness and brings deep darkness out to the light.
He makes nations great and destroys them; he spreads nations out and leads them away.
He removes the understanding of the leaders of the people of the earth, and makes them wander in a trackless waste.
They grope in darkness with no light, and he makes them stagger like a drunkard.

job_13.t: See, my eye has seen all this; my ear has heard it and understood.
What you know, I also know; I do not fall short of you.
But I would speak to the Almighty, and I desire to argue my case with God.
But you are plasterers of lies; you are all worthless physicians.
If only you would be altogether silent! That would be wisdom in you.
Hear now my argument, and attend to the contentions of my lips.
Will you speak unrighteousness for God, and speak deceit on his behalf?
Will you show partiality to him? Will you argue the case for God?
Would it go well if he examined you? Or will you deceive him as one deceives a mortal?
He will surely rebuke you if in secret you show partiality.
Will not his majesty terrify you, and his dread fall upon you?
Your maxims are proverbs of ashes; your defences are defences of clay.
Be silent and leave me alone, and let me speak, and let come upon me what may.
Why do I take my flesh in my teeth and put my life in my own hand?
See, he will kill me; in him I will hope — yet I will argue my ways to his face.
This also will be my deliverance, that no godless man can come before him.
Listen carefully to my speech, and let my declaration be in your ears.
See now, I have set out my case; I know that I am in the right.
Who is there that will contend with me? For then I would be silent and expire.
Only two things do not do to me; then I will not hide from your face.
Take your hand far away from me, and let your dread not terrify me.
Then call, and I will answer; or let me speak, and answer me.
How many are my iniquities and sins? Make known to me my transgression and my sin.
Why do you hide your face and consider me your enemy?
Will you terrify a driven leaf and pursue dry chaff?
For you write bitter things against me and make me inherit the iniquities of my youth.
You put my feet in the stocks and watch all my paths; you score a mark around the soles of my feet.
And a man wears out like something rotten, like a garment eaten by a moth.

job_14.t: A human, born of a woman, is short of days and full of turmoil.
Like a flower he comes out and withers; he flees like a shadow and does not stand.
Yet on such a one you open your eye, and you bring me into judgement with you.
Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? No one.
Since his days are determined, and the number of his months is with you, and you have appointed his limits which he cannot pass —
look away from him and let him rest, until like a hired labourer he can enjoy his day.
For there is hope for a tree: if it is cut down, it will sprout again, and its shoot will not fail.
Though its root grows old in the ground and its stump dies in the dust,
at the scent of water it will bud and put out branches like a new plant.
But a man dies and is laid low; a human expires — and where is he?
Waters disappear from the sea, and a river dries up and is parched;
so a man lies down and does not rise; till the heavens are no more they will not awake, nor be roused out of their sleep.
If only you would hide me in Sheol, conceal me until your anger turns back, set me a term and remember me!
If a man dies, will he live again? All the days of my hard service I would wait, until my relief should come.
You would call and I would answer you; you would long for the work of your hands.
For then you would count my steps, but you would not keep watch over my sin.
My transgression would be sealed up in a bag, and you would plaster over my iniquity.
But a falling mountain crumbles away, and a rock is moved from its place;
waters wear away stones; their torrents wash away the dust of the earth — and so you destroy the hope of a mortal.
You overpower him for ever and he goes; you change his face and send him away.
His sons are honoured, and he does not know it; they are brought low, and he does not perceive it.
Only his own flesh feels pain for him, and his own being mourns for him.

job_15.t: And Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
Does a wise man answer with windy knowledge and fill his belly with the east wind?
arguing with talk that does no good, with words by which no one profits?
You yourself annul the fear of God and diminish devotion before God.
For your iniquity instructs your mouth, and you choose the tongue of the crafty.
Your own mouth condemns you, and not I; your own lips testify against you.
Were you the first human born? Were you brought forth before the hills?
Do you listen in the council of God and keep wisdom to yourself?
What do you know that we do not know? What do you understand that is not with us?
Both the grey-haired and the aged are among us, older in days than your father.
Are the consolations of God too little for you, and a word spoken gently with you?
Why does your heart carry you away, and why do your eyes flash,
that you turn your spirit against God and bring out such words from your mouth?
What is a mortal, that he should be pure, or one born of a woman, that he should be in the right?
See, he does not trust his holy ones, and the heavens are not pure in his eyes;
how much less one abhorrent and corrupt, a man who drinks unrighteousness like water!
I will declare to you — listen to me — and what I have seen I will recount:
what wise men have told and have not hidden, received from their fathers,
to whom alone the land was given, and among whom no stranger passed:
All the days of the wicked man he writhes in pain, and the number of years stored up for the ruthless.
The sound of terrors is in his ears; in time of peace the destroyer comes upon him.
He does not believe he will return from darkness, and he is marked out for the sword.
He wanders about for bread — where is it? He knows that a day of darkness is ready at his hand.
Anxiety and distress terrify him; they overpower him like a king ready for battle.
For he stretched out his hand against God and behaved proudly against the Almighty;
he runs at him with a stiff neck, behind the thick bosses of his shields.
For he has covered his face with his fat and made rolls of fat upon his loins.
And he settled in ruined cities, in houses where no one lives, which are destined to become heaps of stones.
He will not be rich; his wealth will not endure; nor will his possessions spread over the earth.
He will not escape from darkness; a flame will wither his shoot, and he will depart by the breath of God's mouth.
Let him not trust in emptiness — he is deceived; for emptiness will be his recompense.
It will be paid in full before his day, and his palm branch will not stay green.
He will shake off his unripe grapes like a vine, and cast off his blossom like an olive tree.
For the company of the godless is barren, and fire consumes the tents of bribery.
They conceive trouble and give birth to iniquity, and their belly prepares deceit.

job_16.t: And Job answered and said:
I have heard many things like these; miserable comforters are you all.
Is there an end to windy words? What provokes you that you keep answering?
I also could speak as you do, if you were in my place; I could string words together against you and shake my head at you.
But I would strengthen you with my mouth, and the condolence of my lips would hold back your pain.
If I speak, my pain is not held back; and if I stop, what leaves me?
But now he has worn me out; you have devastated all my company.
You have shrivelled me up — and it has become a witness; my leanness has risen up against me and testifies to my face.
His anger has torn me and assailed me; he has gnashed his teeth at me; my adversary sharpens his eyes against me.
They have opened wide their mouths at me; in scorn they have struck my cheeks; together they mass themselves against me.
God delivers me up to the unjust and casts me into the hands of the wicked.
I was at ease, and he shattered me; he seized me by the neck and dashed me to pieces; he set me up as his target.
His archers surround me; he splits my kidneys open and does not spare; he pours out my gall on the ground.
He breaks through me, breach upon breach; he runs at me like a warrior.
I have sewed sackcloth over my skin and buried my horn in the dust.
My face is red from weeping, and on my eyelids is deep darkness,
though there is no violence in my hands and my prayer is pure.
Earth, do not cover my blood, and let my outcry have no resting place!
Even now, see — my witness is in the heavens, and the one who vouches for me is on high.
My friends scorn me; my eye weeps to God.
that he might argue the case of a man with God, as a man argues for his companion.
For a few numbered years will come, and then I shall go the way from which I do not return.

job_17.t: My spirit is broken, my days are snuffed out; the graves are ready for me.
Surely mockers are around me, and my eye must dwell on their provocation.
Lay down a pledge for me with yourself! Who else will strike hands with me?
For you have closed their heart to understanding; therefore you will not let them triumph.
One who denounces his friends for plunder — the eyes of his children will fail.
He has made me a byword among peoples, and I am one spat in the face.
My eye has grown dim from vexation, and all my limbs are like a shadow.
Upright men are appalled at this, and the innocent rouses himself against the godless.
And the righteous holds to his way, and the clean of hands grows stronger.
But all of you — turn back and come again! I shall not find a wise man among you.
My days have passed; my plans are torn apart — the desires of my heart.
They turn night into day: 'Light is near,' they say, in the face of darkness.
If I hope for Sheol as my house, if I have spread my bed in the darkness,
to the pit I have said, "You are my father," and to the maggot, "My mother and my sister" —
where then is my hope? And my hope — who will see it?
Will it go down to the bars of Sheol? Shall we descend together into the dust?

job_18.t: And Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
How long until you make an end of words? Understand, and afterwards we will speak.
Why are we counted as cattle, reckoned stupid in your eyes?
You who tear yourself in your anger — shall the earth be abandoned for your sake, and a rock be moved from its place?
Yes, the light of the wicked is put out, and the flame of his fire does not shine.
The light grows dark in his tent, and the lamp above him is put out.
The steps of his vigour are hemmed in, and his own counsel throws him down.
For his own feet send him into a net, and he walks about on a mesh.
A trap seizes him by the heel; a snare takes hold of him.
A rope is hidden for him in the ground, and a trap for him on the path.
All around, sudden terrors terrify him and chase him at his heels.
His strength is hunger-worn, and disaster is ready for his stumbling.
It consumes the parts of his skin; the firstborn of death consumes his limbs.
His trust is torn from his tent, and he is marched off to the king of terrors.
In his tent dwells what is not his; sulphur is scattered over his habitation.
Below, his roots dry up, and above, his branch withers.
His memory perishes from the earth, and he has no name in the open street.
They drive him from light into darkness and chase him out of the world.
He has no offspring and no posterity among his people, and no survivor where he sojourned.
At his day those in the west are appalled, and those in the east are seized with horror.
Surely such are the dwellings of the unrighteous, and this is the place of one who does not know God.

job_19.t: And Job answered and said:
How long will you torment me and crush me with words?
These ten times you have insulted me; you are not ashamed to wrong me.
And even if it is true that I have erred, my error remains with me.
If you truly magnify yourselves against me and use my disgrace to argue against me,
know then that God has wronged me and has closed his net around me.
See, I cry out "Violence!" and am not answered; I cry for help, and there is no justice.
He has walled up my way so that I cannot pass, and on my paths he puts darkness.
He has stripped my honour from me and taken the crown from my head.
He tears me down on every side, and I am gone; he has uprooted my hope like a tree.
He has kindled his anger against me and counted me among his foes.
Together his troops come; they cast up their siege-road against me and encamp around my tent.
He has put my brothers far from me, and my acquaintances are wholly estranged from me.
My kindred have failed me, and those who knew me have forgotten me.
The guests of my house and my slave women count me a stranger; I have become a foreigner in their eyes.
I call my servant and he does not answer; with my own mouth I must beg him.
My breath is loathsome to my wife, and I am repulsive to my own brothers.
Even young boys despise me; when I rise up, they speak against me.
All the men of my circle abhor me, and those I loved have turned against me.
My bone clings to my skin and my flesh, and I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.
Have pity on me, have pity on me, you my friends, for the hand of God has touched me.
Why do you pursue me as God does, and are never satisfied with my flesh?
If only my words were written down! If only they were inscribed in a scroll!
with an iron stylus and lead, engraved in the rock for ever!
And I myself know that my redeemer lives, and at the last he will stand upon the earth.
And after my skin has been thus destroyed, yet from my flesh I shall see God,
whom I myself shall see for myself, and my own eyes shall see, and not another's. My inmost self is consumed within me.
If you say, "How shall we pursue him, since the root of the matter is found in him" —
be afraid for yourselves of the sword, for wrath brings the punishment of the sword, so that you may know that there is a judgement.

job_20.t: And Zophar the Naamathite answered and said:
Therefore my disquieting thoughts make me answer, because of the agitation within me.
I hear a correction that insults me, and a spirit out of my understanding answers me.
Do you know this, from of old, from when humankind was set upon the earth,
that the exulting of the wicked is brief, and the gladness of the godless lasts only a moment?
Though his loftiness rises to the heavens and his head reaches the clouds,
like his own dung he perishes for ever; those who saw him will say, "Where is he?"
Like a dream he flies away and is not found; he is chased away like a vision of the night.
The eye that caught sight of him does so no more, and his place beholds him no longer.
His children will seek the favour of the poor, and his own hands will give back his wealth.
His bones were full of youthful vigour, but it will lie down with him in the dust.
Though evil is sweet in his mouth and he hides it under his tongue,
though he spares it and will not let it go, and holds it back in his palate,
his food is turned in his inward parts; it becomes the venom of cobras within him.
He swallows wealth and vomits it up; God drives it out of his belly.
He sucks the poison of cobras; the tongue of a viper kills him.
He will not look on the streams, the rivers and wadis of honey and curds.
He gives back his gain and does not swallow it; according to the wealth of his trading he will not rejoice.
For he crushed and abandoned the poor; he seized a house he did not build.
For he knew no quiet within him; he will not escape with what he desired.
Nothing was left of his devouring; therefore his prosperity will not endure.
At the height of his sufficiency he will be in distress; every hand of the wretched will come against him.
Let it come, to fill his belly: God will send against him the burning of his anger and rain it on him as his food.
He will flee from an iron weapon; a bow of bronze will pierce him through.
He draws it out and it comes from his back, the glittering point from his gall; terrors come upon him.
Total darkness is laid up for his treasures; a fire not fanned will consume him; it will go badly for any survivor in his tent.
The heavens will reveal his iniquity, and the earth will rise up against him.
The produce of his house will be carried off, poured away on the day of his anger.
This is the portion of a wicked man from God, the inheritance decreed for him by God.

job_21.t: And Job answered and said:
Listen carefully to my speech, and let this be your consolation to me.
Bear with me, and I will speak; and after I have spoken, mock on.
Is my complaint against a human? And if it were, why should my spirit not be impatient?
Turn to me and be appalled, and lay your hand over your mouth.
When I remember, I am dismayed, and shuddering seizes my flesh.
Why do the wicked live on, grow old, and also grow mighty in strength?
Their offspring is established before them, with them, and their descendants before their eyes.
Their houses are at peace, without fear, and the rod of God is not upon them.
