His bull breeds and does not fail; his cow calves and does not miscarry.
They send out their little ones like a flock, and their children skip about.
They raise the tambourine and lyre and rejoice at the sound of the pipe.
They finish their days in prosperity, and in a moment they go down to Sheol.
And they say to God, "Depart from us; we have no desire for the knowledge of your ways."
"What is the Almighty, that we should serve him? What do we gain if we entreat him?"
See, their prosperity is not in their own hand; the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
How often is the lamp of the wicked put out? How often does their calamity come upon them, and God apportion pains in his anger?
Are they like straw before the wind, like chaff that a whirlwind has carried off?
"God stores up a man's iniquity for his children" — let him repay the man himself, and let him know it!
Let his own eyes see his destruction, and let him drink of the rage of the Almighty.
For what pleasure has he in his household after him, when the number of his months is cut off?
Shall anyone teach God knowledge, seeing that he judges those on high?
One man dies in the full strength of his prime, wholly at ease and quiet.
His body is well nourished, and the marrow of his bones is moist.
And another dies with a bitter spirit, never having tasted anything good.
Together they lie down in the dust, and the maggot covers them.
See, I know your thoughts, and the schemes by which you wrong me.
For you say, "Where is the house of the noble, and where the tent, the dwellings of the wicked?"
Have you not asked those who travel the roads? Do you not recognise their evidence —
that the evil man is spared on the day of calamity, that they are rescued on the day of wrath?
Who declares his way to his face? And who repays him for what he has done?
And he is borne to the graves, and a watch is kept over his tomb.
The clods of the wadi are sweet to him; all humanity follows after him, and before him there were countless others.
How then will you comfort me with emptiness? Of your answers there remains only treachery.

job_22.t: And Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
Can a man be of use to God? Surely a wise man is of use only to himself.
Is it any pleasure to the Almighty that you are in the right? Is it any gain to him that you make your ways blameless?
Is it for your reverence that he reproves you and brings you to trial?
Is not your evil great? Is there no end to your iniquities?
For you have taken pledges from your brothers without cause and stripped the clothes off the naked.
You have given the weary no water to drink, and withheld bread from the hungry.
But the man with a strong arm owned the land, and the favoured man dwelt in it.
You have sent widows away empty-handed, and the arms of the fatherless were crushed.
Therefore snares are all around you, and sudden dread terrifies you,
or darkness, so that you cannot see, and a flood of waters covers you.
Is not God in the height of the heavens? See the topmost stars, how high they are!
And you say, "What does God know? Can he judge through thick darkness?"
"Clouds are his hiding place and he does not see; he walks about on the vault of the heavens."
Will you keep to the ancient path that men of iniquity have trodden,
who were snatched away before their time, whose foundation a river washed away?
who said to God, "Depart from us!" and, "What can the Almighty do to us?"
Yet he filled their houses with good things — and the counsel of the wicked is far from me!
The righteous see it and rejoice, and the innocent mocks them:
"Surely our adversary is destroyed, and fire has consumed what was left of them."
Come to terms with him now and be at peace; by this good will come to you.
Accept law from his mouth, and put his sayings in your heart.
If you return to the Almighty you will be restored; you will put injustice far from your tent.
and lay your gold in the dust, the gold of Ophir among the rocks of the wadis,
and the Almighty will be your gold, and precious silver to you.
For then you will take delight in the Almighty and lift up your face to God.
You will pray to him and he will hear you, and you will pay your vows.
You will pronounce a decision and it will stand for you, and light will shine on your ways.
When men are brought low, you will say, "Lift them up!" and he saves the downcast.
He will deliver even the one who is not innocent, and he will be delivered by the purity of your hands.

job_23.t: Even today my complaint is bitter rebellion; his hand is heavy upon my groaning.
If only I knew where I might find him, that I might come to his dwelling place!
I would set out my case before him and fill my mouth with arguments.
I would know the words he would answer me and understand what he would say to me.
Would he contend with me in the greatness of his power? No — surely he would give heed to me.
There an upright man could reason with him, and I would be delivered for ever from my judge.
See, I go eastward and he is not there, and westward, and I do not perceive him;
on the north when he works, I do not see him; he turns to the south, and I do not see him.
For he knows the way I take; when he has tested me, I shall come out like gold.
My foot has held to his step; I have kept his way and not turned aside.
I have not departed from the commandment of his lips; I have treasured the sayings of his mouth more than my daily bread.
But he is unchanging, and who can turn him back? What he desires, he does.
For he performs what is decreed for me, and many such things are with him.
Therefore I am terrified before him; when I consider, I am in dread of him.
God has made my heart faint, and the Almighty has terrified me;
for I was not silenced before the darkness, nor because thick gloom covers my face.

job_24.t: Why are set times not laid up by the Almighty, and why do those who know him not see his days?
Men move boundary markers; they seize a flock and pasture it.
They drive away the donkey of the fatherless; they take the widow's ox in pledge.
They thrust the needy off the road; the poor of the earth all hide themselves.
Like wild donkeys in the wilderness they go out to their work, scavenging for food; the desert plain yields them food for their children.
In the field they reap what is not theirs, and they glean the vineyard of the wicked.
Naked they spend the night, without clothing, with no covering in the cold.
They are drenched by the mountain rains, and for lack of shelter they embrace the rock.
They tear the fatherless child from the breast, and take a pledge from the poor.
Naked they go about, without clothing; hungry, they carry the sheaves.
Among the olive rows they press out oil; they tread the winepresses and go thirsty.
From the city men groan, and the throat of the wounded cries for help; yet God charges no one with wrong.
They are among those who rebel against the light; they do not recognise its ways or dwell in its paths.
At daybreak the murderer rises; he kills the poor and the needy, and in the night he is like a thief.
The eye of the adulterer watches for twilight, saying, "No eye will see me," and he puts a covering over his face.
In the darkness he digs through houses; by day they shut themselves in; they do not know the light.
For morning is deep darkness to them all alike; for each is acquainted with the terrors of deep darkness.
Swift is he on the face of the waters; their portion in the land is cursed; no one turns toward their vineyards.
Drought and heat snatch away the snow waters; so Sheol snatches those who have sinned.
The womb forgets him; the maggot feeds sweetly on him; he is remembered no more, and injustice is broken like a tree.
He preys on the barren woman who bears no child, and does no good to the widow.
Yet God drags off the mighty by his power; he rises up, and no one is sure of his life.
God gives him security, and he leans on it; yet his eyes are on their ways.
They are exalted a little, and then are gone; they are brought low and gathered in like all others, and like the head of an ear of grain they wither.
And if it is not so, who will prove me a liar and reduce my speech to nothing?

job_25.t: And Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
Dominion and dread are with him; he makes peace in his heights.
Is there any number to his troops? On whom does his light not rise?
How then can a mortal be in the right before God? How can one born of a woman be pure?
See, even the moon is not bright, and the stars are not pure in his eyes;
how much less a mortal, who is a maggot, and a son of humankind, who is a worm!

job_26.t: How you have helped the powerless! How you have saved the arm that has no strength!
How you have counselled one without wisdom, and made sound wisdom known in abundance!
To whom have you uttered words, and whose breath has gone out from you?
The shades writhe beneath the waters, with those who dwell in them.
Sheol is naked before him, and Abaddon has no covering.
He stretches out the north over emptiness; he hangs the earth on nothing.
He binds up the waters in his clouds, and the cloud is not split open under their weight.
He covers the face of his throne; he spreads his cloud over it.
He has drawn a circle as a boundary on the face of the waters, at the frontier of light and darkness.
The pillars of the heavens shake and are astonished at his rebuke.
By his power he stilled the sea, and by his understanding he shattered Rahab.
By his wind the heavens were made fair; his hand pierced the fleeing serpent.
See, these are but the outskirts of his ways, and what a whisper of a word we hear of him! But the thunder of his might — who can understand?

job_27.t: And Job again took up his discourse and said:
As God lives, who has taken away my right, and the Almighty, who has made me bitter —
as long as my breath is in me and the spirit of God is in my nostrils,
my lips will not speak injustice, and my tongue will not utter deceit.
Far be it from me to declare you in the right! Until I expire I will not put away my integrity.
I have kept hold of my righteousness and will not let it go; my heart does not reproach me for any of my days.
May my enemy be like the wicked, and the one who rises against me like the unrighteous.
For what is the hope of the godless when he is cut off, when God takes away his life?
Will God hear his cry when distress comes upon him?
Will he take delight in the Almighty? Will he call on God at all times?
I will teach you about the hand of God; what is with the Almighty I will not conceal.
See, all of you have seen it yourselves; why then do you talk such empty nonsense?
This is the portion of a wicked man from God, and the inheritance the ruthless receive from the Almighty:
If his children increase, it is for the sword, and his descendants will not have bread enough.
His survivors will be buried by the plague, and their widows will not weep.
Though he heaps up silver like dust and piles up clothing like clay,
he prepares it, and the righteous will wear it, and the innocent will divide the silver.
He has built his house like a moth's, and like the shelter a watchman makes.
He lies down rich, but will not do so again; he opens his eyes, and it is all gone.
Terrors overtake him like a flood; by night a storm-wind steals him away.
The east wind lifts him up and he is gone; it whirls him away from his place.
It hurls itself at him without pity; he flees headlong from its power.
Men clap their hands at him and hiss him out of his place.

job_28.t: Surely there is a mine for silver, and a place for gold that they purge.
Iron is taken from the earth, and copper is smelted from stone.
Man puts an end to darkness and searches out to the farthest limit the ore in gloom and deep darkness.
He breaks open a shaft far from where anyone lives, places forgotten by the foot; they dangle far from human beings and swing.
The earth — from it comes food, yet beneath it, it is turned over as by fire.
Its stones are the place of lapis lazuli, and it holds dust of gold.
It is a path no bird of prey knows, and the falcon's eye has not caught sight of it.
The proud beasts have not trodden it; the lion has not passed over it.
He puts his hand to the flint; he overturns mountains at the root.
In the rocks he cuts out channels, and his eye sees every precious thing.
He dams the streams from trickling, and brings what is hidden out to light.
But wisdom — where shall it be found? And where is the place of understanding?
No human knows its price, and it is not found in the land of the living.
The deep says, "It is not in me," and the sea says, "It is not with me."
Fine gold cannot be given for it, nor silver weighed out as its price.
It cannot be paid for with the gold of Ophir, with precious onyx or lapis lazuli.
Gold and glass cannot equal it, nor can a vessel of fine gold be given in exchange for it.
Coral and crystal are not worth mentioning, and the price of wisdom is beyond pearls.
The topaz of Cush cannot equal it; it cannot be paid for with pure gold.
And wisdom — where does it come from? And where is the place of understanding?
It is concealed from the eyes of every living thing and hidden from the birds of the heavens.
Abaddon and Death say, "With our ears we have heard a rumour of it."
God understands the way to it, and he knows its place.
For he looks to the ends of the earth and sees everything under the heavens,
when he gave the wind its weight and measured out the waters by measure;
when he made a decree for the rain and a way for the thunderbolt,
then he saw it and declared it; he established it and searched it out.
And he said to humankind: "See, the fear of the Lord — that is wisdom, and to turn from evil is understanding."

job_29.t: And Job again took up his discourse and said:
If only I were as in the months of long ago, as in the days when God watched over me,
when his lamp shone over my head, and by his light I walked through darkness;
as I was in the days of my prime, when the friendship of God was over my tent,
when the Almighty was still with me and my young men were around me;
when my steps were bathed in curds, and the rock poured out streams of oil beside me;
when I went out to the gate of the town and took my seat in the public square;
the young men saw me and withdrew, and the aged rose and stood;
princes restrained their words and laid a hand over their mouth;
the voice of nobles was hushed, and their tongue stuck to the roof of their mouth;
for the ear that heard called me blessed, and the eye that saw bore witness for me;
For I rescued the poor who cried for help, and the fatherless who had no helper.
The blessing of the perishing came upon me, and I made the widow's heart sing for joy.
I put on righteousness and it clothed me; my justice was like a robe and a turban.
I was eyes to the blind and feet to the lame.
I was a father to the needy, and I investigated the case of one I did not know.
I broke the jaws of the unrighteous and made him drop the prey from his teeth.
And I said, "I shall die in my nest, and multiply my days like the sand."
My root is open to the water, and dew lies all night on my branch.
My honour stays fresh with me, and my bow is renewed in my hand.
To me men listened and waited, and were silent for my counsel.
After my word they did not speak again, and my speech dropped upon them.
They waited for me as for the rain, and opened their mouths wide as for the spring rain.
I smiled on them when they had no confidence, and they did not let the light of my face fall.
I chose their way and sat as chief; I dwelt like a king among his troops, like one who comforts mourners.

job_30.t: But now they laugh at me — men younger than I in days, whose fathers I would have refused to set with the dogs of my flock.
What use to me was the strength of their hands? All vigour had perished from them.
Gaunt with want and hunger, they gnaw the dry ground, by night a waste and desolation;
who pluck saltwort among the bushes, and whose food is the root of the broom plant.
They are driven out from among men; people shout after them as after a thief.
They live in the gullies of the wadis, in holes in the ground and among rocks.
Among the bushes they bray; under the nettles they huddle together.
Sons of fools, sons of no name, they were whipped out of the land.
And now I have become their taunt-song; I am a byword to them.
They abhor me and keep their distance; they do not withhold spittle from my face.
Because God has loosened my bowstring and afflicted me, they have cast off restraint before me.
On my right hand a rabble rises; they drive my feet away and cast up their siege-roads of disaster against me.
They have broken up my path; they profit from my ruin; no one holds them back.
They come on as through a wide breach; amid the crash they roll themselves forward.
Terrors are turned upon me; my dignity is driven off like the wind, and my prosperity has passed away like a cloud.
And now my life is poured out within me; days of affliction have seized me.
By night my bones are pierced within me, and my gnawing pains do not rest.
With great force my clothing is disfigured; it binds me like the collar of my tunic.
He has thrown me into the mud, and I have become like dust and ashes.
I cry for help to you, and you do not answer me; I stand, and you only stare at me.
You have turned cruel toward me; with the might of your hand you assail me.
You lift me up to the wind and make me ride it, and you toss me about in the storm.
For I know you will bring me back to death, to the house appointed for all the living.
Surely no one stretches out a hand against a ruined man, or is there no cry for help in his disaster?
Did I not weep for the one whose day was hard? Was I not grieved for the needy?
Yet when I waited for good, evil came; and when I hoped for light, darkness came.
My inward parts boil and are never still; days of affliction have come to meet me.
I go about blackened, but not by the sun; I stand up in the assembly and cry for help.
I have become a brother to jackals and a companion to ostriches.
My skin has turned black on me, and my bones burn with fever.
My lyre has turned to mourning, and my flute to the sound of weeping.

job_31.t: I made a covenant with my eyes; how then should I gaze at a virgin?
And what is the portion from God above, the inheritance from the Almighty on high?
Is it not calamity for the unrighteous, and disaster for those who do iniquity?
Does he not see my ways and count all my steps?
If I have walked with falsehood and my foot has hurried after deceit —
let him weigh me in honest balances, and let God know my integrity!
If my step has turned aside from the way, and my heart has gone after my eyes, and any stain has stuck to my hands —
let me sow and another eat, and let my crops be rooted up!
If my heart has been enticed by a woman, and I have lain in wait at my neighbour's door —
let my wife grind for another, and let others kneel over her!
For that would be depravity, an iniquity for the judges to punish;
for it is a fire that devours down to Abaddon and would root up all my increase.
If I have rejected the cause of my male servant or my slave woman when they brought a complaint against me —
then what shall I do when God rises up? When he calls to account, what shall I answer him?
Did not the one who made me in the belly make him, and did not the same one form us in the womb?
If I have withheld from the poor what they desired, or made the eyes of a widow fail,
or eaten my morsel alone while the fatherless ate none of it —
for from my youth I reared him as a father would, and from my mother's womb I guided her —
if I have seen anyone perishing for lack of clothing, or a needy man with no covering,
if his loins have not blessed me, warmed with the fleece of my lambs —
if I have raised my hand against the fatherless because I saw I had support in the gate —
let my shoulder fall from its socket, and my arm be broken off at the joint!
For the calamity of God was a terror to me, and before his majesty I could do nothing.
If I have made gold my confidence and called fine gold my security —
if I rejoiced because my wealth was great and because my hand had found so much —
if I looked at the sun when it shone, or the moon moving in splendour,
and my heart was secretly enticed, and my hand kissed my mouth in homage —
that too would be an iniquity for the judges, for I would have denied God above.
If I rejoiced at the ruin of one who hated me or exulted when calamity found him —
and I did not let my mouth sin by asking for his life with a curse —
if the men of my tent have not said, "Who can be found that his meat has not filled?" —
no sojourner spent the night in the street; I opened my doors to the traveller —
If I have covered my transgressions as humans do, hiding my iniquity in my bosom,
because I feared the great crowd and the contempt of the clans dismayed me, so that I kept silent and did not go out of doors —
If only I had someone to hear me! Here is my signature — let the Almighty answer me! — and let my accuser write out his indictment.
Surely I would carry it on my shoulder; I would bind it on me like a crown.
I would tell him the number of my steps; like a prince I would approach him.
If my land has cried out against me, and its furrows have wept together,
if I have eaten its produce without payment and snuffed out the life of its owners —
let thorns come up instead of wheat, and foul weeds instead of barley! The words of Job are finished.

job_32.t: So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
Then the anger of Elihu son of Barakel the Buzite, of the clan of Ram, burned. His anger burned against Job because he justified himself rather than God.
And his anger burned against his three friends, because they had found no answer and yet had condemned Job.
Now Elihu had waited to speak to Job, because they were older than he in days.
When Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of the three men, his anger burned.
And Elihu son of Barakel the Buzite answered and said: I am young in days and you are aged; so I held back, afraid to tell you what I know.
I said, "Let days speak, and many years make wisdom known."
But there is a spirit in a mortal, and the breath of the Almighty gives them understanding.
It is not the many who are wise, nor the aged who understand justice.
Therefore I say, listen to me; I too will tell what I know.
See, I waited for your words; I gave ear to your reasonings while you searched out what to say.
I gave you my full attention, and see, there was no one to refute Job, not one of you answering his sayings.
Beware of saying, "We have found wisdom; let God rout him, not a man" —
He has not marshalled his words against me, and I will not answer him with your sayings.
They are dismayed; they answer no more; words have failed them.
And shall I wait, because they do not speak, because they stand there and answer no more?
I will answer, I too, for my part; I too will tell what I know.
For I am full of words; the spirit within me constrains me.
See, my belly is like wine that has no vent; like new wineskins, it is ready to burst.
Let me speak and find relief; let me open my lips and answer.
Let me show partiality to no one, and flatter no human being;
for I do not know how to flatter; my Maker would soon carry me off.

job_33.t: But now, Job, hear my speech, and give ear to all my words.
See now, I have opened my mouth; my tongue speaks in my palate.
My sayings come from an upright heart, and my lips speak knowledge sincerely.
The spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
Answer me if you can; set your case in order before me and take your stand.
See, before God I am as you are; I too was pinched off from clay.
See, no dread of me will terrify you, and no pressure of mine will weigh on you.
Surely you have spoken in my hearing, and I have heard the sound of your words:
"I am pure, without transgression; I am clean, and there is no iniquity in me.
See, he finds occasions against me; he considers me his enemy.
He puts my feet in the stocks; he watches all my paths."
See, in this you are not in the right — I will answer you — for God is greater than a mortal.
Why have you contended against him, saying that he answers none of a man's words?
For God speaks in one way, and in a second, though no one perceives it.
In a dream, a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls on people, in slumber on the bed,
then he opens the ear of people and seals their warning,
to turn a human aside from his deed and to hide pride from a man;
he keeps his life back from the pit, and his life from passing away by the weapon.
Or he is chastened with pain on his bed, with unceasing strife in his bones;
so that his life loathes bread, and he loathes the food he once craved.
His flesh wastes away out of sight, and his bones, once unseen, stick out.
His life draws near to the pit, and his life to the bringers of death.
If there is at his side an angel, a mediator, one out of a thousand, to declare to a man what is right for him,
then he shows him favour and says, "Spare him from going down to the pit; I have found a ransom" —
his flesh grows fresher than a boy's; he returns to the days of his youth.
He prays to God, and God accepts him; he sees his face with a shout of joy, and God restores to the mortal his righteousness.
He sings before others and says, "I have sinned and perverted what was right, and it was not repaid to me as it deserved."
He has ransomed my life from going down to the pit, and my life shall look on the light.
See, God does all these things twice, three times, with a man,
to bring his life back from the pit, to be lighted with the light of the living.
Pay attention, Job; listen to me; be silent, and I will speak.
If you have anything to say, answer me; speak, for I would gladly declare you in the right.
If not, listen to me; be silent, and I will teach you wisdom.

job_34.t: And Elihu answered and said:
Hear my words, you wise men, and give ear to me, you who know;
for the ear tests words as the palate tastes food.
Let us choose what is just for ourselves; let us know among ourselves what is good.
For Job has said, "I am in the right, and God has taken away my right."
"Concerning my right, am I to lie? My wound is incurable, though I am without transgression."
What man is like Job, who drinks up mockery like water,
who keeps company with doers of iniquity and walks with wicked men?
For he has said, "It profits a man nothing to take delight in God."
Therefore, men of understanding, hear me: far be it from God to do wickedness, and from the Almighty to do wrong!
For he repays a person according to his work, and makes each man's way find him out.
Yes, truly, God does not act wickedly, and the Almighty does not pervert justice.
Who gave him charge over the earth? And who appointed him over the whole world?
If he set his heart upon a man and gathered to himself his spirit and his breath,
all flesh would expire together, and humankind would return to dust.
If you have understanding, hear this; give ear to the sound of my words.
Shall one who hates justice govern? And will you condemn the Righteous and Mighty One?
Does one say to a king, "You worthless one," or to nobles, "You wicked ones"?
who shows no partiality to princes and does not regard the rich above the poor, for they are all the work of his hands.
In a moment they die, at midnight; a people is shaken and passes away, and the mighty are removed by no human hand.
For his eyes are on the ways of a man, and he sees all his steps.
There is no darkness and no deep darkness where the doers of iniquity can hide.
For he need set no time for a man to go before God for judgement.
He shatters the mighty without inquiry and sets others in their place.
Therefore he takes note of their deeds; he overturns them in the night, and they are crushed.
He strikes them down as wicked men in a place where people can see,
because they turned aside from following him and paid no regard to any of his ways,
so that they brought to him the outcry of the poor, and he heard the outcry of the afflicted.
When he is quiet, who can condemn? When he hides his face, who can behold him? — and this over a nation and over an individual alike,
so that a godless man should not reign, nor be a snare to the people.
For has anyone said to God, "I have borne my punishment; I will offend no more;
teach me what I do not see; if I have done wrong, I will not do it again"?
Should he repay on your terms, because you refuse them? You must choose, not I; so say what you know.
Men of understanding will say to me, and any wise man who hears me:
"Job speaks without knowledge, and his words are without insight."
Would that Job were tested to the utmost, for answering like men of iniquity!
For he adds transgression to his sin; he claps his hands among us and multiplies his sayings against God.

job_35.t: Do you think this is justice? You have said, "My righteousness is greater than God's."
For you say, "What use is it to you? What do I gain more than if I had sinned?"
I will answer you with words, and your friends along with you.
Look at the heavens and see; behold the clouds, which are higher than you.
If you have sinned, what do you do to him? If your transgressions are many, what do you do to him?
If you are in the right, what do you give him, or what does he receive from your hand?
Your wickedness affects only a man like yourself, and your righteousness only a fellow human being.
Under a multitude of oppressions people cry out; they cry for help against the arm of the great.
But no one says, "Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night,
who teaches us more than the animals of the earth and makes us wiser than the birds of the heavens?"
There they cry out, and he does not answer, because of the pride of evil men.
Surely God does not hear an empty cry, and the Almighty does not regard it.
How much less when you say you do not see him — the case is before him, and you must wait for him!
And now, because his anger has not punished, and he has not taken much notice of transgression,
Job opens his mouth to no purpose; without knowledge he multiplies words.

job_36.t: And Elihu went on and said:
Bear with me a little and I will show you, for there is still something to say on God's behalf.
I will bring my knowledge from afar and ascribe righteousness to my Maker.
For truly my words are not falsehood; one perfect in knowledge is with you.
See, God is mighty and does not despise any; he is mighty in strength of understanding.
He does not keep the wicked alive, but he gives justice to the afflicted.
He does not withdraw his eyes from the righteous, but with kings on the throne he seats them for ever, and they are exalted.
And if they are bound in fetters, caught in cords of affliction,
then he declares to them what they have done, and their transgressions, that they behaved proudly.
He opens their ear to correction and commands them to turn back from iniquity.
If they listen and serve him, they will complete their days in prosperity and their years in pleasantness.
But if they do not listen, they pass away by the weapon and expire without knowledge.
The godless in heart cherish anger; they do not cry for help when he binds them.
They die young, and their life ends among the shrine prostitutes.
He rescues the afflicted by their affliction and opens their ear by oppression.
He also lured you out of distress into a broad place where there was no constraint, and your table was set with rich food.
But you are full of the case of the wicked; judgement and justice have taken hold of you.
Beware lest wrath entice you into scoffing, and let no great ransom turn you aside.
Will your wealth avail to keep you from distress, or all your efforts of strength?
Do not long for the night, when peoples are cut off in their place.
Take heed; do not turn to iniquity, for you have chosen this rather than affliction.
See, God is exalted in his power; who is a teacher like him?
Who has prescribed his way for him? And who has said, "You have done wrong"?
Remember to magnify his work, of which people have sung.
All humankind has looked on it; a mortal beholds it from afar.
See, God is exalted beyond our knowing; the number of his years is beyond searching out.
For he draws up the drops of water; they distil as rain from his mist,
which the clouds pour down; they drip abundantly on humankind.
Can anyone understand the spreading of the clouds, the crashings of his pavilion?
See, he spreads his lightning about him and covers the depths of the sea.
For by these he judges peoples and gives food in abundance.
He covers his hands with lightning and commands it to strike the mark.
His thunder tells of him; even the cattle sense what is coming.

job_37.t: At this also my heart trembles and leaps from its place.
Listen carefully to the raging of his voice and the rumbling that goes out from his mouth.
Under all the heavens he lets it loose, and his lightning to the corners of the earth.
After it a voice roars; he thunders with his majestic voice, and he does not hold the lightnings back when his voice is heard.
God thunders wondrously with his voice; he does great things beyond our knowing.
For to the snow he says, "Fall on the earth"; and so to the shower of rain, and to the showers of his mighty rain.
He seals up the hand of every human, so that all whom he has made may know his work.
The wild animals go into their lairs and stay in their dens.
From its chamber comes the whirlwind, and cold from the scattering winds.
By the breath of God ice is given, and the broad waters are frozen fast.
He also loads the thick cloud with moisture and scatters his lightning-cloud abroad.
And it turns round and round by his guidance, to do all that he commands on the face of the inhabited world.
Whether for correction, or for his earth, or for steadfast love, he makes it find its mark.
Give ear to this, Job; stand still and consider the wonders of God.
Do you know how God lays his charge upon them and makes the lightning of his cloud shine out?
Do you know how the clouds are balanced, the wondrous works of him who is perfect in knowledge?
you whose garments are hot when the earth lies still under the south wind?
Can you beat out the skies with him, hard as a mirror of cast metal?
Teach us what we should say to him; we cannot marshal our case because of darkness.
Shall he be told that I want to speak? Did ever a man ask to be swallowed up?
And now people cannot look at the light when it is brilliant in the skies, after a wind has passed and swept them clear.
Out of the north comes golden splendour; about God is awesome majesty.
The Almighty — we cannot find him out; he is exalted in power, and justice and abundant righteousness he does not violate.
Therefore people fear him; he regards none who are wise in their own eyes.

job_38.t: Then the LORD answered Job out of the tempest and said:
Who is this that darkens counsel by words without knowledge?
Gird up your loins like a man; I will question you, and you shall inform me.
Where were you when I laid the earth's foundation? Tell me, if you have understanding.
Who fixed its measurements — surely you know! — or who stretched the measuring line over it?
On what were its bases sunk, or who laid its cornerstone,
when the morning stars sang together and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
And who shut in the sea with doors when it burst forth from the womb,
when I made the cloud its clothing and thick darkness its swaddling band,
and I fixed my limit for it and set bars and doors,
and said, "This far you shall come and no further, and here shall your proud waves be stayed"?
Have you in your lifetime commanded the morning, or caused the dawn to know its place,
to take hold of the corners of the earth and shake the wicked out of it?
The earth is changed like clay under a seal, and its features stand out like a garment.
The wicked are deprived of their light, and the uplifted arm is broken.
Have you gone to the springs of the sea or walked in the recesses of the deep?
Have the gates of death been revealed to you? Have you seen the gates of deep darkness?
Have you comprehended the breadth of the earth? Tell me, if you know it all.
Where is the way to the dwelling of light, and where is the place of darkness,
that you should take it to its own territory and know the paths to its house?
You know, for you were born then, and the number of your days is great!
Have you entered the storehouses of snow, or seen the storehouses of hail,
which I have kept back for the time of distress, for the day of battle and war?
Where is the way by which light is distributed, or the east wind scattered over the earth?
Who has cut a channel for the torrent and a way for the thunderbolt,
to bring rain on a land where no one lives, on a wilderness with no human in it,
to satisfy the waste and desolate ground and make the fresh grass sprout?
Has the rain a father? Who fathered the drops of dew?
From whose womb did the ice come? And the frost of heaven — who gave it birth?
The waters become hard as stone, and the surface of the deep is frozen fast.
Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades or loosen the cords of Orion?
Can you bring out the constellations in their season, or guide the Bear with her young?
Do you know the statutes of the heavens? Can you establish their rule over the earth?
Can you lift up your voice to the clouds, so that a flood of water covers you?
Can you send out lightnings, and they go and say to you, "Here we are"?
Who put wisdom in the hidden parts, or gave understanding to the mind?
Who can number the clouds by wisdom, and who can tip the waterskins of heaven,
when the dust hardens into a mass and the clods stick fast together?
Can you hunt prey for the lioness and satisfy the appetite of the young lions,
when they crouch in their dens or lie in wait in the thicket?
Who provides food for the raven when its young cry to God for help and wander about for lack of food?

job_39.t: Do you know the time when the mountain goats of the rock give birth? Do you watch over the labour of the does?
Can you count the months they complete, and do you know the time when they give birth,
when they crouch and deliver their young, and their labour pains are past?
Their young grow strong and grow up in the open; they go out and do not return to them.
Who let the wild donkey go free, and who loosed the bonds of the wild ass,
whose home I made the desert plain, and its dwellings the salt land?
It laughs at the tumult of the town; it does not hear the driver's shouts.
It ranges the mountains as its pasture and searches after every green thing.
Is the wild ox willing to serve you? Will it spend the night at your feeding trough?
Can you bind the wild ox to the furrow with a rope? Will it harrow the valleys behind you?
Will you trust it because its strength is great, and leave your labour to it?
Will you trust it to bring back your grain and gather it to your threshing floor?
The ostrich's wing flaps joyously — but is it the pinion and plumage of a stork?
For it leaves its eggs on the ground and lets them warm in the dust,
and it forgets that a foot may crush them and a wild animal trample them.
It treats its young harshly, as if they were not its own; its labour is in vain, and it has no fear,
for God has made it forget wisdom and given it no share in understanding.
Yet when it rouses itself to run, it laughs at the horse and its rider.
Do you give the horse his strength? Do you clothe his neck with a mane?
Do you make him leap like a locust? The majesty of his snorting is terrifying.
He paws in the valley and rejoices in his strength; he goes out to meet the weapons.
He laughs at fear and is not dismayed; he does not turn back from the sword.
Upon him the quiver rattles, the flashing spear and the javelin.
With quivering and rage he swallows the ground; he will not stand still at the sound of the horn.
At every blast of the horn he says, "Aha!" He smells the battle from afar, the thunder of the commanders and the war-cry.
Is it by your understanding that the falcon soars, spreading its wings toward the south?
Is it at your command that the eagle mounts up and sets its nest on high?
It dwells on the rock and lodges there, on the tooth of the rock, a stronghold.
From there it spies out its food; its eyes look far off.
Its young ones lap up blood; and where the slain are, there it is.

job_40.t: And the LORD answered Job and said:
Shall a faultfinder contend with the Almighty? Let him who accuses God answer for it.
And Job answered the LORD and said:
See, I am of small account. What shall I answer you? I lay my hand on my mouth.
Once I have spoken, and I will not answer; twice, and I will say no more.
Then the LORD answered Job out of the tempest and said:
Gird up your loins like a man; I will question you, and you shall inform me.
Will you even annul my justice? Will you condemn me so that you may be in the right?
Have you an arm like God's? Can you thunder with a voice like his?
Deck yourself now with majesty and dignity; clothe yourself with glory and honour.
Pour out the overflowings of your anger; look on every proud one and bring him low.
Look on every proud one and humble him, and tread down the wicked where they stand.
Hide them in the dust together; shut up their faces in the hidden place.
Then I also will acknowledge you, that your own right hand can save you.
See now Behemoth, which I made along with you; he eats grass like an ox.
See now, his strength is in his loins, and his power in the muscles of his belly.
He stiffens his tail like a cedar; the sinews of his thighs are knit together.
His bones are tubes of bronze; his limbs like bars of iron.
He is the first of God's works; only his Maker can bring a sword near him.
For the mountains bring him their produce, and all the wild animals play there.
Under the lotus plants he lies down, in the covert of the reeds and the marsh.
The lotus plants cover him with their shade; the poplars of the wadi surround him.
If the river rages, he is not alarmed; he is confident though the Jordan bursts against his mouth.
Can anyone capture him while he watches, or pierce his nose with a snare?

job_41.t: Can you draw out Leviathan with a fish-hook, or press down his tongue with a cord?
Can you put a cord through his nose or pierce his jaw with a hook?
Will he plead with you at length? Will he speak soft words to you?
Will he cut a covenant with you, that you should take him as a slave for ever?
Will you play with him as with a bird, or put him on a leash for your girls?
Will trading partners bargain over him? Will they divide him up among merchants?
Can you fill his hide with harpoons or his head with fish-spears?
Lay your hand on him; remember the battle — you will not do it again!
See, any hope of him proves false; is one not cast down at the mere sight of him?
No one is fierce enough to rouse him. Who then is able to stand before me?
Who has ever confronted me, that I should repay him? Whatever is under all the heavens is mine.
I will not keep silence about his limbs, his mighty strength, or his graceful frame.
Who has stripped off his outer covering? Who can come within his double coat of mail?
Who can open the doors of his face? Around his teeth is terror.
His back is rows of shields, shut up with a tight seal.
One is so near to another that no air can come between them.
Each clings to the next; they grip one another and cannot be parted.
His snorting flashes out light, and his eyes are like the eyelids of dawn.
From his mouth go flaming torches; sparks of fire leap out.
From his nostrils goes out smoke, as from a boiling pot over burning rushes.
His breath kindles coals, and a flame goes out from his mouth.
Strength lodges in his neck, and dismay dances before him.
The folds of his flesh cling together, firmly cast upon him and immovable.
His heart is hard as stone, hard as the lower millstone.
At his rising the mighty are afraid; at the crashing they lose their senses.
The sword that reaches him does not hold, nor the spear, the dart, or the javelin.
He counts iron as straw, bronze as rotten wood.
The arrow does not make him flee; sling-stones turn to chaff against him.
A club is counted as chaff, and he laughs at the rattling of a javelin.
Beneath him are sharp potsherds; he spreads a threshing sledge over the mud.
He makes the deep boil like a pot; he makes the sea like a boiling ointment-pot.
Behind him he leaves a shining wake; one would think the deep had turned grey-haired.
There is nothing on earth like him, a creature made without fear.
He looks down on everything that is high; he is king over all the sons of pride.

job_42.t: I know that you can do all things, and that no purpose of yours can be blocked.
'Who is this that hides counsel without knowledge?' So I spoke of what I did not understand, things too wonderful for me, which I did not know.
'Hear now, and I will speak; I will question you, and you inform me.'
I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye has seen you.
Therefore I reject, and I am consoled, upon dust and ashes.

After the LORD had spoken these words to Job, the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite: My anger burns against you and your two friends, because you have not spoken of me what is right, as my servant Job has.

Now take seven bulls and seven rams, go to my servant Job, and offer a burnt offering for yourselves, and my servant Job will pray for you; for I will accept his prayer and not deal with you as your folly deserves — because you have not spoken of me what is right, as my servant Job has.
So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the LORD had told them; and the LORD accepted Job.
And the LORD restored Job's fortunes when he prayed for his friends, and the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.

And all his brothers and sisters and everyone who had known him before came to him and ate bread with him in his house; they shook their heads over him and comforted him for all the trouble that the LORD had brought upon him. And each one gave him a piece of money and a gold ring.
And the LORD blessed the latter end of Job's life more than his beginning; he had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand yoke of oxen and a thousand female donkeys.
And he had seven sons and three daughters.
He named the first Jemimah, the second Keziah, and the third Keren-happuch.
And in all the land no women were found as beautiful as Job's daughters; and their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.
And Job lived a hundred and forty years after this, and saw his children and his children's children, four generations.
And Job died, old and full of days.

joel_1.t: The word of the LORD that came to Joel son of Pethuel.
Hear this, you elders; listen, all you who live in the land. Has this happened in your days, or in the days of your ancestors?
Tell it to your children, and your children to their children, and their children to another generation.
What the shearing locust left, the swarming locust ate; what the swarming locust left, the licking locust ate; what the licking locust left, the consuming locust ate.
Wake up, you drunkards, and weep; wail, all you who drink wine, over the sweet wine, for it is cut off from your mouth.
For a nation has come up against my land, mighty and beyond counting. Its teeth are a lion's teeth, and it has the fangs of a lioness.
It has laid my vine waste and splintered my fig tree. It has stripped it utterly bare and thrown it down; its branches have turned white.
Wail like a virgin girded with sackcloth over the husband of her youth.
The grain offering and the drink offering are cut off from the house of the LORD. The priests mourn, those who serve the LORD.
The field is devastated, the ground mourns, for the grain is devastated, the new wine has dried up, the fresh oil withers.
Be ashamed, you farmers; wail, you vinedressers, over the wheat and over the barley, for the harvest of the field has perished.
The vine has dried up and the fig tree withers; pomegranate, palm and apple too — all the trees of the field have dried up. For joy has dried up from human beings.

Gird yourselves and lament, you priests; wail, you who serve at the altar. Come, spend the night in sackcloth, you who serve my God, for grain offering and drink offering are withheld from the house of your God.
Set apart a fast as holy, call a solemn assembly, gather the elders and all who live in the land to the house of the LORD your God, and cry out to the LORD.
Alas for the day! For the day of the LORD is near, and it comes like devastation from the Almighty.
Has not food been cut off before our eyes, and joy and rejoicing from the house of our God?
The seeds have shrivelled under their clods; the storehouses lie desolate, the granaries are torn down, for the grain has dried up.
How the livestock groans! The herds of cattle wander in confusion, for they have no pasture; the flocks of sheep suffer too.
To you, O LORD, I call, for fire has consumed the pastures of the wilderness, and a flame has set ablaze all the trees of the field.
The animals of the field also pant for you, for the channels of water have dried up, and fire has consumed the pastures of the wilderness.

joel_2.t: Blow a ram's horn in Zion, sound the alarm on my holy mountain. Let all who live in the land tremble, for the day of the LORD is coming — it is near:

a day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and thick darkness. Like dawn spread over the mountains, a people numerous and mighty; nothing like it has ever been, and after it there will be nothing like it again for the years of generation upon generation.
Before it fire consumes, and behind it a flame sets ablaze. The land before it is like the garden of Eden, and behind it a wilderness of desolation; and nothing escapes it.
Its appearance is like the appearance of horses, and like horsemen, so they run.
Like the sound of chariots they leap on the mountain tops, like the sound of a flame of fire consuming stubble, like a mighty people drawn up for battle.
Before it peoples writhe in anguish; all faces gather a glow.
Like warriors they run, like men of war they scale a wall. Each goes his own way, and they do not swerve from their paths.
They do not press one another; each goes on his own track. They burst through the weapons and are not stopped.
They rush upon the city, they run along the wall, they climb into the houses, they come in through the windows like a thief.
Before it the earth trembles, the heavens shake. Sun and moon grow dark, and the stars withdraw their brightness.

And the LORD has given his voice before his army, for his camp is very great, for mighty is the one who carries out his word. For the day of the LORD is great and very awesome — and who can endure it?
"Yet even now," declares the LORD, "return to me with all your heart, with fasting and weeping and wailing."
"Tear your heart and not your garments, and return to the LORD your God, for he is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love, and he relents over harm."
Who knows? He may turn and relent, and leave a blessing behind him — a grain offering and a drink offering for the LORD your God.
Blow a ram's horn in Zion, set apart a fast as holy, call a solemn assembly.
Gather the people, set the assembly apart as holy, assemble the elders, gather the children and the nursing infants. Let the bridegroom come out from his room, and the bride from her chamber.

Between the porch and the altar let the priests weep, those who serve the LORD, and let them say: "Spare your people, LORD, and do not give your inheritance over to reproach, for nations to rule over them. Why should it be said among the peoples, 'Where is their God?'"
Then the LORD became jealous for his land, and had compassion on his people.

And the LORD answered and said to his people: "I am sending you the grain and the new wine and the fresh oil, and you will be satisfied with it; and I will no longer make you a reproach among the nations.

And I will remove the northerner far from you, and drive it into a land dry and desolate, its face toward the eastern sea and its rear toward the western sea. Its stench will go up, its foul smell will go up, for it has done great things.
Do not fear, O ground; be glad and rejoice, for the LORD has done great things.
Do not fear, you animals of the field, for the pastures of the wilderness have turned green; the tree has borne its fruit, the fig tree and the vine have given their full yield.

And you people of Zion, be glad and rejoice in the LORD your God, for he has given you the early rain for your vindication; and he has sent down for you rain, early rain and spring rain, in the first month.
The threshing floors will be full of grain, and the vats will overflow with new wine and fresh oil.
"And I will repay you for the years that the swarming locust ate, the licking locust and the consuming locust and the shearing locust, my great army that I sent among you.
"You will eat your fill and be satisfied, and you will praise the name of the LORD your God, who has dealt with you wondrously; and my people will never be ashamed.
"And you will know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the LORD your God, and there is no other; and my people will never be ashamed."
"And afterwards it will be that I will pour out my spirit on all flesh, and your sons and your daughters will prophesy; your old men will dream dreams, your young men will see visions.
"And also on the male servants and the female servants, in those days I will pour out my spirit.
"And I will set wonders in the heavens and on the earth: blood and fire and columns of smoke.
"The sun will be turned to darkness, and the moon to blood, before the coming of the day of the LORD, the great and awesome day.

"And everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will escape; for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be those who escape, just as the LORD has said, and among the survivors whom the LORD is calling."

joel_3.t: "For look — in those days and at that time, when I restore the fortunes of Judah and Jerusalem,

I will gather all the nations and bring them down to the valley of Jehoshaphat, and I will enter into judgement with them there over my people and my inheritance Israel, whom they scattered among the nations — and they divided up my land.
For my people they cast lots; they traded a boy for a prostitute, and sold a girl for wine — and drank it.

"And what are you to me, Tyre and Sidon and all the regions of Philistia? Are you repaying me a recompense? If you are making recompense against me, swiftly, speedily I will return your recompense on your own head —
you who took my silver and my gold, and carried my fine treasures into your temples;
and the people of Judah and the people of Jerusalem you sold to the Greeks, to remove them far from their own territory.
"I am rousing them from the place where you sold them, and I will return your recompense on your head.
And I will sell your sons and your daughters into the hand of the people of Judah, and they will sell them to the Sabeans, to a distant nation" — for the LORD has spoken.
Proclaim this among the nations: Set apart a war as holy! Rouse the warriors! Let all the men of war draw near and come up!
Beat your plowshares into swords and your pruning knives into spears. Let the weak one say, "I am a warrior."
Hurry and come, all you nations from round about, and gather there. Bring down your warriors, LORD!
"Let the nations be roused and come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat, for there I will sit to judge all the nations from round about.
Send out the sickle, for the harvest is ripe. Come, tread, for the winepress is full, the vats overflow, for their evil is great."
Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision! For the day of the LORD is near in the valley of decision.
Sun and moon have grown dark, and the stars have withdrawn their brightness.
And the LORD will roar from Zion, and from Jerusalem he will give his voice, and the heavens and the earth will shake. But the LORD is a refuge for his people and a stronghold for the Israelites.
"And you will know that I am the LORD your God, dwelling in Zion, my holy mountain. And Jerusalem will be a holy place, and strangers will not pass through it again."

"And on that day the mountains will drip sweet wine, the hills will flow with milk, and all the ravines of Judah will flow with water. A spring will go out from the house of the LORD and water the Wadi of the Acacias.
Egypt will become a desolation, and Edom a wilderness of desolation, because of the violence done to the people of Judah, in whose land they shed innocent blood.
But Judah will remain for ever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.
"And I will hold their blood innocent — that which I did not hold innocent." And the LORD is dwelling in Zion.

jonah_1.t: The word of the LORD came to Jonah son of Amittai:
'Get up, go to Nineveh, the great city, and call out against it, for their evil has come up before me.'

But Jonah got up to flee to Tarshish, away from the presence of the LORD. He went down to Joppa and found a ship bound for Tarshish, and he paid its fare and went down into it to go with them to Tarshish, away from the presence of the LORD.
But the LORD hurled a great wind at the sea, and there was a great storm on the sea, and the ship thought it would break up.

The sailors were afraid, and each cried out to his own god, and they hurled the gear that was in the ship into the sea to lighten it for themselves. But Jonah had gone down into the innermost parts of the vessel, and had lain down, and had fallen fast asleep.
The chief helmsman came to him and said, 'What is this with you, sleeper? Get up, call on your god! Perhaps the god will give us a thought, and we will not perish.'
They said to one another, 'Come, let us cast lots, so we may know on whose account this evil has come upon us.' So they cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.
They said to him, 'Tell us, please, on whose account this evil has come upon us. What is your occupation? Where do you come from? What is your land? What people are you from?'
He said to them, 'I am a Hebrew, and I fear the LORD, the God of the heavens, who made the sea and the dry ground.'
Then the men were seized with a great fear, and they said to him, 'What is this you have done?' For the men knew that he was fleeing from the presence of the LORD, because he had told them.
They said to him, 'What shall we do to you, so that the sea will be calm for us?' For the sea was growing more and more stormy.
He said to them, 'Pick me up and hurl me into the sea, and the sea will be calm for you. For I know that this great storm is upon you on my account.'
But the men rowed hard to bring the ship back to the dry ground, and they could not, for the sea was growing more and more stormy against them.
So they called out to the LORD: 'Please, LORD, do not let us perish for this man's life, and do not put innocent blood on us. For you, LORD, have done as you pleased.'
Then they picked up Jonah and hurled him into the sea, and the sea stopped its raging.
Then the men feared the LORD with a great fear, and they offered a sacrifice to the LORD and made vows.
And the LORD appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the inward parts of the fish three days and three nights.

jonah_2.t: Then Jonah prayed to the LORD his God from the inward parts of the fish.
He said: I called from my distress to the LORD, and he answered me; from the belly of Sheol I cried for help, you heard my voice.
You cast me into the deep, into the heart of the seas, and the current surrounded me; all your breakers and your waves passed over me.
And I said, 'I have been driven away from before your eyes; yet I will look again toward your holy temple.'
The waters encompassed me up to the throat; the deep surrounded me; reeds were wound about my head.
I went down to the roots of the mountains; the earth's bars closed behind me for ever; but you brought up my life from the pit, LORD my God.
When my life was fainting away within me, I remembered the LORD; and my prayer came to you, to your holy temple.
Those who cling to worthless vanities forsake the steadfast love that could be theirs.
But I, with a voice of thanksgiving, will sacrifice to you; what I have vowed I will fulfil. Deliverance belongs to the LORD.
Then the LORD spoke to the fish, and it vomited Jonah out onto the dry ground.

jonah_3.t: The word of the LORD came to Jonah a second time:
'Get up, go to Nineveh, the great city, and call out to it the proclamation that I am speaking to you.'
So Jonah got up and went to Nineveh, according to the word of the LORD. Now Nineveh was an exceedingly great city, a journey of three days across.
Jonah began to go into the city, a journey of one day, and he proclaimed: 'Forty days more, and Nineveh is overthrown!'
And the people of Nineveh believed in God. They proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth, from their greatest to their smallest.
The word reached the king of Nineveh, and he got up from his throne, took off his cloak, covered himself with sackcloth and sat in the ashes.

And he had it proclaimed in Nineveh: 'By decree of the king and his great ones: no people or livestock, no cattle or flocks are to taste anything; they are not to graze, and they are not to drink water.
Let them cover themselves with sackcloth — people and livestock — and let them call out to God with force, and let each turn back from his evil way and from the violence that is in his hands.
Who knows? God may turn and relent, and turn back from his burning anger, so that we will not perish.'
And God saw their deeds — that they had turned back from their evil way — and God relented concerning the evil that he had said he would do to them, and he did not do it.

jonah_4.t: But to Jonah this was a great evil, and he burned with anger.

And he prayed to the LORD: 'Please, LORD — was this not my word while I was still on my own ground? That is why I fled to Tarshish at the first: I knew that you are a gracious and compassionate God, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love, and one who relents concerning evil.'
'And now, LORD, take my life from me, please, for my death is better than my life.'
And the LORD said, 'Is it right for you to burn with anger?'
Then Jonah went out of the city and sat down east of the city. He made himself a booth there and sat under it in the shade, until he could see what would happen in the city.
And the LORD God appointed a plant, and it came up over Jonah to be a shade over his head, to deliver him from his evil. And Jonah rejoiced over the plant with a great joy.
But God appointed a worm at daybreak the next day, and it attacked the plant, and it withered.
And when the sun rose, God appointed a hot east wind, and the sun struck Jonah's head, and he became faint. He asked that he might die, and he said, 'My death is better than my life.'
And God said to Jonah, 'Is it right for you to burn with anger over the plant?' And he said, 'It is right for me to burn with anger — enough to die.'
And the LORD said, 'You had pity on the plant, for which you did not toil and which you did not make grow — which came in a night and perished in a night.
And should I not have pity on Nineveh, the great city, in which there are more than a hundred and twenty thousand people who do not know their right hand from their left — and much livestock?'

joshua_1.t: After the death of Moses the servant of the LORD, the LORD said to Joshua son of Nun, Moses' attendant,
"Moses my servant is dead. Now arise, cross this Jordan, you and all this people, into the land that I am giving to them, to the Israelites.
"Every place on which the sole of your foot treads I have given to you, just as I spoke to Moses.

"From the wilderness and this Lebanon as far as the great river, the river Euphrates — all the land of the Hittites — and as far as the Great Sea toward the setting of the sun shall be your territory.
"No one shall stand before you all the days of your life. Just as I was with Moses, I will be with you; I will not abandon you and I will not forsake you.
"Be strong and be bold, for you will give this people the land as their inheritance, the land I swore to their ancestors to give them.

"Only be strong and very bold, taking care to act according to all the law that Moses my servant commanded you. Do not turn aside from it to the right or to the left, so that you may act wisely wherever you go.

"This book of the law shall not depart from your mouth, and you shall meditate on it day and night, so that you may take care to act according to all that is written in it; for then you will make your ways succeed, and then you will act wisely.
"Have I not commanded you? Be strong and be bold. Do not be terrified and do not be dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go."
And Joshua commanded the officers of the people,

"Pass through the midst of the camp and command the people, 'Prepare provisions for yourselves, for in three days you are to cross this Jordan, to go in and take possession of the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess.'"
And to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh Joshua said,
"Remember the word that Moses the servant of the LORD commanded you: 'The LORD your God is giving you rest, and he will give you this land.'

"Your wives, your little ones and your livestock shall remain in the land that Moses gave you beyond the Jordan; but you shall cross over armed for battle ahead of your brothers, all the mighty men of valour, and you shall help them,

"until the LORD gives rest to your brothers as he has to you, and they also take possession of the land that the LORD your God is giving them. Then you shall return to the land of your possession and take possession of it, the land that Moses the servant of the LORD gave you beyond the Jordan toward the rising of the sun."
And they answered Joshua, "All that you have commanded us we will do, and wherever you send us we will go.
"Just as we listened to Moses in everything, so we will listen to you. Only may the LORD your God be with you, as he was with Moses.
"Anyone who rebels against your command and does not listen to your words, to all that you command him, shall be put to death. Only be strong and be bold."

joshua_2.t: And Joshua son of Nun secretly sent two men as spies from Shittim, saying, "Go, look over the land, and Jericho." And they went and came to the house of a prostitute whose name was Rahab, and they lay down there.
And the king of Jericho was told, "Men have come here tonight from the Israelites to spy out the land."
And the king of Jericho sent to Rahab, saying, "Bring out the men who came to you, who came to your house, for they have come to spy out the whole land."
But the woman had taken the two men and hidden them, and she said, "Yes, the men came to me, but I did not know where they were from.
"And when the gate was about to be shut, at dark, the men went out. I do not know where the men went. Pursue them quickly, for you will overtake them."
But she had taken them up to the roof and hidden them among the stalks of flax that she had laid out on the roof.
And the men pursued them by the road of the Jordan, to the fords; and the gate was shut as soon as the pursuers had gone out after them.
And before they lay down, she went up to them on the roof,
and she said to the men, "I know that the LORD has given you the land, and that dread of you has fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land have melted away before you.

"For we have heard how the LORD dried up the waters of the Sea of Reeds before you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, to Sihon and to Og, whom you devoted to destruction.
"We heard, and our heart melted, and no courage was left in anyone because of you; for the LORD your God — he is God in the heavens above and on the earth beneath.
"And now swear to me by the LORD, since I have shown loyalty to you, that you also will show loyalty to my father's house; and give me a sign of faithfulness,
"and let my father and my mother, my brothers and my sisters and all who belong to them live, and deliver our lives from death."
And the men said to her, "Our life for yours, to the death — if you do not tell this business of ours! And when the LORD gives us the land, we will show you loyalty and faithfulness."
Then she let them down by a rope through the window, for her house was in the outer wall, and she was living in the city wall itself.
And she said to them, "Go to the hill country, lest the pursuers meet you; hide yourselves there three days until the pursuers return, and afterward go on your way."
And the men said to her, "We shall be free from this oath of yours that you have made us swear,

"When we come into the land, you shall bind this cord of scarlet thread in the window by which you let us down; and you shall gather to yourself into the house your father and your mother, your brothers and all your father's household.

"And anyone who goes out of the doors of your house into the street — his blood shall be on his own head, and we shall be free; and anyone who is with you in the house — his blood shall be on our head, if a hand is laid on him.
"And if you tell this business of ours, then we shall be free from your oath that you have made us swear."
And she said, "According to your words, so be it." And she sent them off and they went; and she bound the scarlet cord in the window.
And they went and came to the hill country and stayed there three days until the pursuers returned. And the pursuers searched all along the way and did not find them.
Then the two men returned, came down from the hill country, crossed over and came to Joshua son of Nun, and they recounted to him all that had happened to them.
And they said to Joshua, "The LORD has given all the land into our hand; and all the inhabitants of the land have melted away before us."

joshua_3.t: And Joshua rose early in the morning, and they set out from Shittim and came to the Jordan, he and all the Israelites; and they stayed there before they crossed over.
At the end of three days the officers passed through the midst of the camp,
and they commanded the people, "When you see the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God, and the priests, the Levites, carrying it, then set out from your place and go after it.
"Only let there be a distance between you and it, about two thousand cubits by measure. Do not come near it, so that you may know the way you are to go, for you have not passed this way before."
And Joshua said to the people, "Consecrate yourselves, for tomorrow the LORD will do wonders in your midst."
And Joshua said to the priests, "Lift up the ark of the covenant and cross over ahead of the people." And they lifted up the ark of the covenant and went ahead of the people.
And the LORD said to Joshua, "This day I will begin to make you great in the eyes of all Israel, so that they may know that just as I was with Moses I will be with you.
"And you shall command the priests who carry the ark of the covenant, 'When you come to the edge of the waters of the Jordan, you shall stand still in the Jordan.'"
And Joshua said to the Israelites, "Draw near here and hear the words of the LORD your God."

And Joshua said, "By this you shall know that a living God is in your midst, and that he will surely dispossess before you the Canaanites and the Hittites and the Hivites and the Perizzites and the Girgashites and the Amorites and the Jebusites:
"the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth is about to cross over ahead of you into the Jordan.
"And now take for yourselves twelve men from the tribes of Israel, one man from each tribe.

"And when the soles of the feet of the priests who carry the ark of the LORD, the Lord of all the earth, rest in the waters of the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan shall be cut off — the waters coming down from above — and they shall stand as one heap."
And when the people set out from their tents to cross the Jordan, with the priests carrying the ark of the covenant ahead of the people,

and as those carrying the ark came to the Jordan, and the feet of the priests carrying the ark were dipped in the edge of the waters — now the Jordan overflows all its banks throughout the days of harvest —

the waters coming down from above stood still; they rose up as one heap very far off, at Adam, the city beside Zarethan; and those going down to the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, were wholly cut off. And the people crossed over opposite Jericho.

And the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the LORD stood firm on the dry land in the middle of the Jordan, while all Israel crossed over on the dry land, until the whole nation had finished crossing the Jordan.

joshua_4.t: And when the whole nation had finished crossing the Jordan, the LORD said to Joshua,
"Take for yourselves twelve men from the people, one man from each tribe,

"and command them, 'Take up for yourselves from here, from the middle of the Jordan, from the place where the priests' feet stood firm, twelve stones; carry them over with you and set them down at the lodging place where you stay tonight.'"
And Joshua called the twelve men whom he had appointed from the Israelites, one man from each tribe.

And Joshua said to them, "Cross over ahead of the ark of the LORD your God into the middle of the Jordan, and each of you lift one stone onto his shoulder, according to the number of the tribes of the Israelites,
"so that this may be a sign in your midst. When your children ask in time to come, 'What do these stones mean to you?'

"then you shall say to them, 'Because the waters of the Jordan were cut off before the ark of the covenant of the LORD; when it crossed the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan were cut off.' And these stones shall be a memorial to the Israelites for ever."

And the Israelites did so, just as Joshua commanded: they took up twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan, just as the LORD had said to Joshua, according to the number of the tribes of the Israelites; and they carried them over with them to the lodging place and set them down there.
And Joshua set up twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan, at the place where the feet of the priests who carried the ark of the covenant had stood; and they have been there to this day.

And the priests carrying the ark stood in the middle of the Jordan until everything was finished that the LORD had commanded Joshua to speak to the people, according to all that Moses had commanded Joshua. And the people hurried and crossed over.
And when all the people had finished crossing over, the ark of the LORD crossed over, with the priests, before the people.
And the Reubenites and the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh crossed over armed for battle ahead of the Israelites, just as Moses had spoken to them —
about forty thousand armed for war crossed over before the LORD for battle, to the plains of Jericho.
On that day the LORD made Joshua great in the eyes of all Israel, and they feared him just as they had feared Moses all the days of his life.
And the LORD said to Joshua,
"Command the priests who carry the ark of the testimony to come up from the Jordan."
And Joshua commanded the priests, "Come up from the Jordan."

And when the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the LORD came up from the middle of the Jordan, and the soles of the priests' feet were drawn up onto the dry ground, the waters of the Jordan returned to their place and went as before over all its banks.
And the people came up from the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month, and they encamped at Gilgal, on the eastern edge of Jericho.
And those twelve stones that they had taken from the Jordan Joshua set up at Gilgal.
And he said to the Israelites, "When your children ask their fathers in time to come, 'What are these stones?'
"then you shall make it known to your children, saying, 'On dry ground Israel crossed this Jordan,'

"for the LORD your God dried up the waters of the Jordan before you until you had crossed over, just as the LORD your God did to the Sea of Reeds, which he dried up before us until we had crossed over,
"so that all the peoples of the earth may know the hand of the LORD, that it is mighty, and so that you may fear the LORD your God all your days."

joshua_5.t: And when all the kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan to the west, and all the kings of the Canaanites who were by the sea, heard that the LORD had dried up the waters of the Jordan before the Israelites until they had crossed over, their heart melted, and there was no courage left in them because of the Israelites.
At that time the LORD said to Joshua, "Make for yourself flint knives, and circumcise the Israelites again, a second time."
So Joshua made flint knives and circumcised the Israelites at the Hill of the Foreskins.
And this is the reason Joshua circumcised them: all the people who came out of Egypt, the males, all the men of war, had died in the wilderness on the way, after they came out of Egypt.
For all the people who came out had been circumcised, but all the people born in the wilderness on the way, after they came out of Egypt, had not been circumcised.

For forty years the Israelites walked in the wilderness, until the whole nation, the men of war who came out of Egypt, was finished — those who had not listened to the voice of the LORD, to whom the LORD swore that he would not let them see the land that the LORD swore to their ancestors to give us, a land flowing with milk and honey.
And their children he raised up in their place; these Joshua circumcised, for they were uncircumcised, because they had not been circumcised on the way.
And when the whole nation had finished being circumcised, they stayed where they were in the camp until they were healed.
And the LORD said to Joshua, "Today I have rolled away the reproach of Egypt from you." And the name of that place was called Gilgal, to this day.
And the Israelites encamped at Gilgal, and they kept the passover on the fourteenth day of the month, in the evening, on the plains of Jericho.
And on the day after the passover they ate of the produce of the land — unleavened bread and roasted grain — on that very day.
And the manna ceased on the day after, when they ate of the produce of the land; the Israelites had manna no longer, and they ate of the yield of the land of Canaan that year.

And when Joshua was at Jericho, he lifted up his eyes and looked, and there was a man standing opposite him with his sword drawn in his hand. And Joshua went to him and said to him, "Are you for us or for our foes?"
And he said, "No; I am the commander of the army of the LORD. Now I have come." And Joshua fell on his face to the ground and bowed down, and said to him, "What is my lord saying to his servant?"
And the commander of the army of the LORD said to Joshua, "Take off your sandal from your foot, for the place on which you are standing is holy." And Joshua did so.

joshua_6.t: Now Jericho was shut fast because of the Israelites; no one went out and no one came in.
And the LORD said to Joshua, "See, I have given Jericho into your hand, and its king and the mighty men of valour.
"You shall go around the city, all the men of war, encircling the city once. So you shall do for six days.
