"And seven priests shall carry seven trumpets of rams' horns before the ark. And on the seventh day you shall go around the city seven times, and the priests shall blow the trumpets.

"And when they blow a long blast on the horn of the ram, when you hear the sound of the trumpet, all the people shall shout a great shout; and the wall of the city shall fall down where it stands, and the people shall go up, each straight ahead."
And Joshua son of Nun called the priests and said to them, "Take up the ark of the covenant, and let seven priests carry seven trumpets of rams' horns before the ark of the LORD."
And he said to the people, "Pass on and go around the city, and let the armed men pass on before the ark of the LORD."

And when Joshua had said this to the people, the seven priests carrying the seven trumpets of rams' horns before the LORD passed on and blew the trumpets, and the ark of the covenant of the LORD went after them.
And the armed men went before the priests who blew the trumpets, and the rearguard went after the ark, blowing the trumpets as they went.
And Joshua commanded the people, "You shall not shout, you shall not let your voice be heard, and no word shall go out of your mouth, until the day I say to you, 'Shout!' Then you shall shout."
So he had the ark of the LORD go around the city, encircling it once; and they came to the camp and stayed in the camp.
And Joshua rose early in the morning, and the priests took up the ark of the LORD.

And the seven priests carrying the seven trumpets of rams' horns before the ark of the LORD went on continually, blowing the trumpets; and the armed men went before them, and the rearguard went after the ark of the LORD, blowing the trumpets as they went.
And they went around the city once on the second day, and returned to the camp. So they did for six days.
And on the seventh day they rose early, at the break of dawn, and went around the city in the same manner seven times. Only on that day did they go around the city seven times.
And at the seventh time, when the priests blew the trumpets, Joshua said to the people, "Shout! For the LORD has given you the city.

"And the city shall be devoted to destruction, it and all that is in it, to the LORD. Only Rahab the prostitute shall live, she and all who are with her in the house, because she hid the messengers whom we sent.

"But as for you, keep away from what is devoted to destruction, lest you devote yourselves to destruction by taking from what is devoted to destruction, and so make the camp of Israel devoted to destruction and bring trouble on it.
"And all the silver and gold and the articles of bronze and iron are holy to the LORD; they shall go into the treasury of the LORD."

And the people shouted, and they blew the trumpets. And when the people heard the sound of the trumpet, the people shouted a great shout, and the wall fell down where it stood, and the people went up into the city, each straight ahead, and they captured the city.
And they devoted to destruction all that was in the city, men and women, young and old, and ox and sheep and donkey, with the edge of the sword.
And to the two men who had spied out the land Joshua said, "Go into the house of the prostitute and bring out from there the woman and all who belong to her, just as you swore to her."

And the young men who had spied out went in and brought out Rahab and her father and her mother and her brothers and all who belonged to her — all her clans they brought out — and they put them outside the camp of Israel.
And they burned the city with fire, and all that was in it. Only the silver and the gold and the articles of bronze and iron they put into the treasury of the house of the LORD.

And Rahab the prostitute, and her father's household and all who belonged to her, Joshua let live; and she has dwelt in the midst of Israel to this day, because she hid the messengers whom Joshua sent to spy out Jericho.

And Joshua administered an oath at that time, saying, "Cursed before the LORD be the man who rises up and rebuilds this city, Jericho. At the cost of his firstborn he shall lay its foundation, and at the cost of his youngest he shall set up its gates."
And the LORD was with Joshua, and the report of him was in all the land.

joshua_7.t: But the Israelites acted unfaithfully in the matter of what was devoted to destruction: Achan son of Carmi son of Zabdi son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took some of what was devoted to destruction. And the anger of the LORD burned against the Israelites.
And Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which is beside Beth-aven, east of Bethel, and said to them, "Go up and spy out the land." So the men went up and spied out Ai.

And they returned to Joshua and said to him, "Let not all the people go up; let about two thousand or about three thousand men go up and strike Ai. Do not make all the people toil there, for they are few."
So about three thousand men of the people went up there, and they fled before the men of Ai.

And the men of Ai struck down about thirty-six of them, and pursued them from before the gate as far as Shebarim, and struck them down on the descent. And the heart of the people melted and became as water.
And Joshua tore his garments and fell on his face to the ground before the ark of the LORD until evening, he and the elders of Israel; and they put dust on their heads.

And Joshua said, "Alas, Lord GOD! Why have you brought this people right over the Jordan, to give us into the hand of the Amorites, to destroy us? If only we had been content to stay beyond the Jordan!
"Pardon me, Lord! What shall I say, now that Israel has turned its back before its enemies?
"And the Canaanites and all the inhabitants of the land will hear of it and surround us and cut off our name from the earth. And what will you do for your great name?"
And the LORD said to Joshua, "Get up! Why are you lying on your face?

"Israel has sinned. They have transgressed my covenant that I commanded them; they have taken some of what is devoted to destruction; they have stolen; they have deceived; and they have put it among their own belongings.

"And the Israelites are not able to stand before their enemies; they turn their backs before their enemies, because they have become devoted to destruction. I will not be with you any more unless you destroy what is devoted to destruction from your midst.

"Arise, consecrate the people, and say, 'Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow. For thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: There is something devoted to destruction in your midst, Israel. You will not be able to stand before your enemies until you remove what is devoted to destruction from your midst.'

"And you shall be brought near in the morning by your tribes. And the tribe that the LORD takes shall come near by families, and the family that the LORD takes shall come near by households, and the household that the LORD takes shall come near man by man.

"And the one taken with what is devoted to destruction shall be burned with fire, he and all that belongs to him, because he has transgressed the covenant of the LORD and because he has done an outrage in Israel."
And Joshua rose early in the morning and brought Israel near by its tribes, and the tribe of Judah was taken.
And he brought near the family of Judah, and he took the family of the Zerahites; and he brought near the family of the Zerahites man by man, and Zabdi was taken.
And he brought near his household man by man, and Achan son of Carmi son of Zabdi son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was taken.
And Joshua said to Achan, "My son, give glory to the LORD the God of Israel, and make confession to him; and tell me what you have done. Do not hide it from me."
And Achan answered Joshua, "Truly I have sinned against the LORD, the God of Israel, and this is what I did.

"I saw among the spoil one fine cloak of Shinar, two hundred shekels of silver, and one wedge of gold weighing fifty shekels; and I coveted them and took them. There they are, hidden in the ground inside my tent, with the silver under it."
And Joshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent; and there it was, hidden in his tent, with the silver under it.
And they took them from inside the tent and brought them to Joshua and to all the Israelites, and they poured them out before the LORD.

And Joshua took Achan son of Zerah, and the silver and the cloak and the wedge of gold, and his sons and his daughters and his ox and his donkey and his flock and his tent and all that belonged to him — and all Israel with him — and they brought them up to the Valley of Achor.
And Joshua said, "Why have you brought trouble on us? The LORD will bring trouble on you this day." And all Israel stoned him with stones; and they burned them with fire and stoned them with stones.

And they raised over him a great heap of stones, which is there to this day. And the LORD turned from the burning of his anger. That is why the name of that place was called the Valley of Achor, to this day.

joshua_8.t: And the LORD said to Joshua, "Do not fear and do not be dismayed. Take with you all the people of war, and arise, go up to Ai. See, I have given into your hand the king of Ai and his people and his city and his land.
"And you shall do to Ai and to its king just as you did to Jericho and to its king. Only its spoil and its livestock you may plunder for yourselves. Set an ambush for the city, behind it."
So Joshua arose, and all the people of war, to go up to Ai. And Joshua chose thirty thousand men, mighty men of valour, and sent them out by night.
And he commanded them, "See, you are to lie in ambush for the city, behind the city. Do not go very far from the city, and all of you be ready.
"And I and all the people with me will draw near to the city; and when they come out to meet us as at the first, we shall flee before them.
"And they will come out after us until we have drawn them away from the city, for they will say, 'They are fleeing before us as at the first.' So we shall flee before them.
"Then you shall rise from the ambush and take possession of the city, and the LORD your God will give it into your hand.
"And when you have captured the city, you shall set the city on fire. According to the word of the LORD you shall do it. See, I have commanded you."
And Joshua sent them out, and they went to the place of ambush and stayed between Bethel and Ai, to the west of Ai. And Joshua stayed that night among the people.
And Joshua rose early in the morning and mustered the people; and he went up, he and the elders of Israel, ahead of the people to Ai.
And all the people of war who were with him went up and drew near and came before the city, and they encamped north of Ai, with the valley between them and Ai.
And he took about five thousand men and set them as an ambush between Bethel and Ai, to the west of the city.
And the people set the whole camp that was north of the city, with its rear guard west of the city. And Joshua went that night into the middle of the valley.

And when the king of Ai saw it, they hurried and rose early, and the men of the city went out to meet Israel for battle — he and all his people — at the appointed place before the Arabah. And he did not know that there was an ambush against him behind the city.
And Joshua and all Israel let themselves be beaten before them, and they fled by the way of the wilderness.
And all the people who were in Ai were called together to pursue them, and they pursued Joshua and were drawn away from the city.
And not a man was left in Ai and Bethel who did not go out after Israel; and they left the city open and pursued Israel.
And the LORD said to Joshua, "Stretch out the javelin that is in your hand toward Ai, for I will give it into your hand." And Joshua stretched out the javelin that was in his hand toward the city.
And the men in ambush rose quickly from their place and ran when he stretched out his hand; and they came into the city and captured it, and they hurried and set the city on fire.

And the men of Ai turned behind them and looked, and the smoke of the city had gone up to the heavens; and they had no strength to flee this way or that. And the people who were fleeing to the wilderness turned back against the pursuers.
And Joshua and all Israel saw that the men in ambush had captured the city and that the smoke of the city had gone up; and they turned back and struck the men of Ai.

And the others came out of the city to meet them, so that they were caught by Israel in the middle, some on one side and some on the other; and they struck them down until no survivor or fugitive was left to them.
And the king of Ai they captured alive and brought him to Joshua.

And when Israel had finished killing all the inhabitants of Ai in the open country, in the wilderness where they had pursued them, and all of them had fallen by the edge of the sword until they were finished, all Israel returned to Ai and struck it with the edge of the sword.
And all who fell that day, men and women, were twelve thousand — all the people of Ai.
And Joshua did not draw back his hand, which he had stretched out with the javelin, until he had devoted to destruction all the inhabitants of Ai.
Only the livestock and the spoil of that city Israel plundered for themselves, according to the word of the LORD that he had commanded Joshua.
And Joshua burned Ai and made it a perpetual mound, a desolation, to this day.

And the king of Ai he hanged on the tree until evening; and at sunset Joshua commanded, and they took his corpse down from the tree and threw it at the entrance of the gate of the city, and raised over it a great heap of stones, which is there to this day.
Then Joshua built an altar to the LORD, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal,

just as Moses the servant of the LORD commanded the Israelites, as it is written in the book of the law of Moses: an altar of whole stones on which no one has wielded iron. And they offered up on it burnt offerings to the LORD and sacrificed peace offerings.
And he wrote there on the stones a copy of the law of Moses, which he had written before the Israelites.

And all Israel — its elders and officers and its judges — stood on either side of the ark, before the priests, the Levites, who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD, the resident alien as the native-born; half of them in front of Mount Gerizim and half of them in front of Mount Ebal, just as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded, to bless the people Israel first of all.
And afterward he read aloud all the words of the law, the blessing and the curse, according to all that is written in the book of the law.
There was not a word of all that Moses commanded that Joshua did not read aloud before all the assembly of Israel, and the women and the little ones and the resident aliens who walked in their midst.

joshua_9.t: And when all the kings who were beyond the Jordan — in the hill country, in the Shephelah and along all the coast of the Great Sea toward Lebanon: the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites — heard of it,
they gathered together, all as one, to fight against Joshua and Israel, with one accord.
But the inhabitants of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and to Ai,
and they too acted with cunning: they went and provisioned themselves, and took worn-out sacks for their donkeys, and worn-out wineskins, split and mended,
and worn-out, patched sandals on their feet and worn-out garments on themselves; and all the bread of their provisions was dry and crumbling.
And they went to Joshua, to the camp at Gilgal, and said to him and to the men of Israel, "We have come from a distant land. Now make a covenant with us."
And the men of Israel said to the Hivites, "Perhaps you are dwelling among us; and how can we make a covenant with you?"
And they said to Joshua, "We are your servants." And Joshua said to them, "Who are you, and where do you come from?"
And they said to him, "From a very distant land your servants have come, because of the name of the LORD your God; for we have heard the report of him, and all that he did in Egypt,
"and all that he did to the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, to Sihon king of Heshbon and to Og king of Bashan, who was at Ashtaroth.
"And our elders and all the inhabitants of our land said to us, 'Take provisions in your hand for the journey and go to meet them, and say to them: We are your servants; now make a covenant with us.'
"This bread of ours we took warm as our provisions from our homes on the day we came out to go to you; and now it is dry and crumbling.
"And these wineskins that we filled were new, and now they have split. And these garments of ours and our sandals have worn out from the very great length of the journey."
And the men took some of their provisions, but they did not enquire of the mouth of the LORD.
And Joshua made peace with them and made a covenant with them, to let them live; and the leaders of the congregation swore an oath to them.
And at the end of three days, after they had made a covenant with them, they heard that they were near neighbours and were dwelling among them.
And the Israelites set out and came to their cities on the third day; and their cities were Gibeon, Kephirah, Beeroth and Kiriath-jearim.
And the Israelites did not strike them, because the leaders of the congregation had sworn to them by the LORD, the God of Israel. And the whole congregation grumbled against the leaders.
But all the leaders said to the whole congregation, "We have sworn to them by the LORD, the God of Israel; and now we cannot touch them.
"This is what we will do to them: let them live, so that there be no wrath upon us because of the oath that we swore to them."
And the leaders said to them, "Let them live." And they became cutters of wood and drawers of water for the whole congregation, just as the leaders had spoken to them.
And Joshua summoned them and spoke to them, "Why did you deceive us, saying, 'We are very far from you,' when you are dwelling among us?
"And now you are cursed, and none of you shall ever cease to be slaves — cutters of wood and drawers of water for the house of my God."

And they answered Joshua, "Because it was plainly told to your servants that the LORD your God had commanded Moses his servant to give you all the land and to destroy all the inhabitants of the land before you. So we feared greatly for our lives because of you, and we did this thing.
"And now we are in your hand. Do to us as it seems good and right in your eyes."
And he did so to them: he delivered them from the hand of the Israelites, and they did not kill them.
And on that day Joshua made them cutters of wood and drawers of water for the congregation and for the altar of the LORD, to this day, at the place that he would choose.

joshua_10.t: And when Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had captured Ai and devoted it to destruction — as he had done to Jericho and to its king, so he had done to Ai and to its king — and that the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were among them,
they feared greatly, because Gibeon was a great city, like one of the royal cities, and because it was greater than Ai, and all its men were mighty.
So Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem sent to Hoham king of Hebron, to Piram king of Jarmuth, to Japhia king of Lachish and to Debir king of Eglon, saying,
"Come up to me and help me, and let us strike Gibeon, for it has made peace with Joshua and with the Israelites."

So the five kings of the Amorites — the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish and the king of Eglon — gathered and went up, they and all their armies, and encamped against Gibeon and fought against it.

And the men of Gibeon sent to Joshua, to the camp at Gilgal, saying, "Do not let your hands drop from your servants. Come up to us quickly and save us and help us, for all the kings of the Amorites who dwell in the hill country have gathered against us."
So Joshua went up from Gilgal, he and all the people of war with him, and all the mighty men of valour.
And the LORD said to Joshua, "Do not fear them, for I have given them into your hand. Not a man of them shall stand before you."
And Joshua came upon them suddenly, having gone up from Gilgal all night.

And the LORD routed them before Israel, and he struck them with a great defeat at Gibeon and pursued them by the way of the ascent of Beth-horon, and struck them as far as Azekah and as far as Makkedah.

And as they fled before Israel — they were at the descent of Beth-horon — the LORD threw down great stones on them from the heavens as far as Azekah, and they died. More died from the hailstones than those whom the Israelites killed with the sword.
Then Joshua spoke to the LORD, on the day the LORD gave the Amorites over before the Israelites, and he said in the sight of Israel: "Sun, at Gibeon be still, and moon, in the Valley of Aijalon."

And the sun was still, and the moon stood, until the nation took vengeance on its enemies. Is this not written in the Scroll of Jashar? And the sun stood in the middle of the heavens and did not hasten to set for about a whole day.
And there has been no day like that one, before it or after it, when the LORD listened to the voice of a man; for the LORD was fighting for Israel.
And Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to the camp at Gilgal.
And those five kings fled and hid themselves in the cave at Makkedah.
And Joshua was told, "The five kings have been found, hidden in the cave at Makkedah."
And Joshua said, "Roll great stones against the mouth of the cave, and appoint men over it to guard them.
"But you, do not stand still. Pursue your enemies and cut off their rear. Do not let them enter their cities, for the LORD your God has given them into your hand."
And when Joshua and the Israelites had finished striking them with a very great defeat until they were finished, and the survivors who survived of them had gone into the fortified cities,
all the people returned to the camp, to Joshua at Makkedah, in peace. No one sharpened his tongue against any of the Israelites.
And Joshua said, "Open the mouth of the cave and bring out to me those five kings from the cave."
And they did so, and brought out to him those five kings from the cave: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish and the king of Eglon.

And when they brought out those kings to Joshua, Joshua summoned all the men of Israel and said to the commanders of the men of war who had gone with him, "Come near, put your feet on the necks of these kings." And they came near and put their feet on their necks.
And Joshua said to them, "Do not fear and do not be dismayed. Be strong and be bold, for thus the LORD will do to all your enemies whom you are fighting."
And afterward Joshua struck them and put them to death and hanged them on five trees; and they hung on the trees until evening.

And at sunset Joshua commanded, and they took them down from the trees and threw them into the cave where they had hidden themselves, and put great stones over the mouth of the cave, which are there to this very day.

And Joshua captured Makkedah on that day and struck it with the edge of the sword, and its king; he devoted them to destruction, and every person who was in it — he left no survivor. And he did to the king of Makkedah just as he had done to the king of Jericho.
And Joshua passed on, and all Israel with him, from Makkedah to Libnah, and fought against Libnah.

And the LORD gave it also into the hand of Israel, with its king; and he struck it with the edge of the sword, and every person who was in it — he left no survivor in it. And he did to its king just as he had done to the king of Jericho.
And Joshua passed on, and all Israel with him, from Libnah to Lachish, and encamped against it and fought against it.

And the LORD gave Lachish into the hand of Israel, and he captured it on the second day and struck it with the edge of the sword, and every person who was in it, according to all that he had done to Libnah.
Then Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish, and Joshua struck him and his people until he had left him no survivor.
And Joshua passed on, and all Israel with him, from Lachish to Eglon, and they encamped against it and fought against it.
And they captured it on that day and struck it with the edge of the sword, and every person who was in it he devoted to destruction on that day, according to all that he had done to Lachish.
And Joshua went up, and all Israel with him, from Eglon to Hebron, and they fought against it.

And they captured it and struck it with the edge of the sword, and its king and all its cities and every person who was in it — he left no survivor, according to all that he had done to Eglon; and he devoted it to destruction, and every person who was in it.
And Joshua turned back, and all Israel with him, to Debir, and fought against it.

And he captured it and its king and all its cities, and they struck them with the edge of the sword and devoted to destruction every person who was in it — he left no survivor. Just as he had done to Hebron, so he did to Debir and to its king, and just as he had done to Libnah and to its king.

And Joshua struck all the land — the hill country, the Negev, the Shephelah and the slopes — and all their kings. He left no survivor, and every breathing thing he devoted to destruction, just as the LORD the God of Israel had commanded.
And Joshua struck them from Kadesh-barnea as far as Gaza, and all the land of Goshen, as far as Gibeon.
And all these kings and their land Joshua captured at one time, because the LORD the God of Israel was fighting for Israel.
And Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to the camp at Gilgal.

joshua_11.t: And when Jabin king of Hazor heard of it, he sent to Jobab king of Madon and to the king of Shimron and to the king of Acshaph,
and to the kings who were in the north, in the hill country, in the Arabah south of Kinnereth, in the Shephelah and on the heights of Dor to the west,
to the Canaanites in the east and in the west, and the Amorites and the Hittites and the Perizzites and the Jebusites in the hill country, and the Hivites under Hermon in the land of Mizpah.
And they came out, they and all their armies with them, a people as numerous as the sand on the seashore, with very many horses and chariots.
And all these kings met together, and they came and encamped together at the waters of Merom to fight against Israel.
And the LORD said to Joshua, "Do not fear them, for tomorrow about this time I am giving all of them over, slain, before Israel. You shall hamstring their horses and burn their chariots with fire."
And Joshua came upon them, and all the people of war with him, at the waters of Merom suddenly, and they fell upon them.

And the LORD gave them into the hand of Israel, and they struck them and pursued them as far as Greater Sidon and as far as Misrephoth-maim and as far as the Valley of Mizpeh eastward; and they struck them until he had left them no survivor.
And Joshua did to them just as the LORD had said to him: he hamstrung their horses and burned their chariots with fire.
And Joshua turned back at that time and captured Hazor, and struck its king with the sword; for Hazor was formerly the head of all these kingdoms.
And they struck every person who was in it with the edge of the sword, devoting them to destruction; not a breathing thing was left. And Hazor he burned with fire.

And all the cities of these kings, and all their kings, Joshua captured, and he struck them with the edge of the sword, devoting them to destruction, just as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded.
Only, all the cities that stood on their mounds Israel did not burn — except Hazor alone, which Joshua burned.

And all the spoil of these cities and the livestock the Israelites plundered for themselves; only every human being they struck with the edge of the sword until they had destroyed them — they left not a breathing thing.
Just as the LORD had commanded Moses his servant, so Moses commanded Joshua, and so Joshua did. He left nothing undone of all that the LORD had commanded Moses.
And Joshua took all this land: the hill country and all the Negev and all the land of Goshen and the Shephelah and the Arabah, and the hill country of Israel and its Shephelah,
from Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir, as far as Baal-gad in the Valley of Lebanon under Mount Hermon. And all their kings he captured and struck and put to death.
For many days Joshua made war with all these kings.
There was not a city that made peace with the Israelites, except the Hivites, the inhabitants of Gibeon; all of them they took in battle.

For it was from the LORD to harden their heart to meet Israel in battle, so that they might be devoted to destruction and receive no favour, but that they might be destroyed, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

And Joshua came at that time and cut off the Anakim from the hill country — from Hebron, from Debir, from Anab, from all the hill country of Judah and from all the hill country of Israel; with their cities Joshua devoted them to destruction.
No Anakim were left in the land of the Israelites; only in Gaza, in Gath and in Ashdod did they remain.

So Joshua took all the land, according to all that the LORD had spoken to Moses; and Joshua gave it as an inheritance to Israel according to their divisions, by their tribes. And the land had rest from war.

joshua_12.t: And these are the kings of the land whom the Israelites struck, and whose land they took possession of beyond the Jordan toward the rising of the sun, from the Wadi Arnon as far as Mount Hermon, and all the Arabah eastward:

Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon and ruled from Aroer on the edge of the Wadi Arnon, and the middle of the wadi, and half of Gilead, as far as the Wadi Jabbok, the border of the Ammonites;
and the Arabah as far as the Sea of Kinnereth eastward, and as far as the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, eastward, the way to Beth-jeshimoth; and from the south, under the slopes of Pisgah;
and the territory of Og king of Bashan, one of the remnant of the Rephaim, who dwelt at Ashtaroth and at Edrei,
and ruling over Mount Hermon and over Salecah and over all Bashan as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and half of Gilead, the border of Sihon king of Heshbon.
Moses the servant of the LORD and the Israelites struck them; and Moses the servant of the LORD gave it as a possession to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

And these are the kings of the land whom Joshua and the Israelites struck beyond the Jordan westward, from Baal-gad in the Valley of Lebanon as far as Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir; and Joshua gave it to the tribes of Israel as a possession, according to their divisions:
in the hill country, in the Shephelah, in the Arabah, on the slopes, in the wilderness and in the Negev: the Hittites, the Amorites and the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites.
the king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai, which is beside Bethel, one;
the king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one;
the king of Jarmuth, one; the king of Lachish, one;
the king of Eglon, one; the king of Gezer, one;
the king of Debir, one; the king of Geder, one;
the king of Hormah, one; the king of Arad, one;
the king of Libnah, one; the king of Adullam, one;
the king of Makkedah, one; the king of Bethel, one;
the king of Tappuah, one; the king of Hepher, one;
the king of Aphek, one; the king of Lasharon, one;
the king of Madon, one; the king of Hazor, one;
the king of Shimron-meron, one; the king of Acshaph, one;
the king of Taanach, one; the king of Megiddo, one;
the king of Kedesh, one; the king of Jokneam in Carmel, one;
the king of Dor, of the heights of Dor, one; the king of Goyim in Gilgal, one;
the king of Tirzah, one. All the kings were thirty-one.

joshua_13.t: Now Joshua was old, advanced in years; and the LORD said to him, "You are old, advanced in years, and very much of the land remains to be taken possession of.
"This is the land that remains: all the regions of the Philistines and all the Geshurites,

"from the Shihor, which is before Egypt, as far as the border of Ekron to the north — it is reckoned as Canaanite: the five rulers of the Philistines, of Gaza, of Ashdod, of Ashkelon, of Gath and of Ekron; and the Avvim,
"from the south: all the land of the Canaanites, and Mearah which belongs to the Sidonians, as far as Aphek, as far as the border of the Amorites;
"and the land of the Gebalites, and all Lebanon toward the rising of the sun, from Baal-gad under Mount Hermon as far as Lebo-hamath.

"All the inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon as far as Misrephoth-maim, all the Sidonians — I myself will dispossess them before the Israelites. Only allot it to Israel as an inheritance, just as I commanded you.
"And now apportion this land as an inheritance to the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh."
With it the Reubenites and the Gadites had received their inheritance, which Moses gave them beyond the Jordan eastward, just as Moses the servant of the LORD gave them:
from Aroer on the edge of the Wadi Arnon, and the city in the middle of the wadi, and all the plain of Medeba as far as Dibon,
and all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, as far as the border of the Ammonites;
and Gilead, and the territory of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and all Mount Hermon, and all Bashan as far as Salecah;
all the kingdom of Og in Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth and in Edrei — he was left of the remnant of the Rephaim. And Moses struck them and dispossessed them.
But the Israelites did not dispossess the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and Geshur and Maacath have dwelt in the midst of Israel to this day.
Only to the tribe of Levi he gave no inheritance: the food offerings of the LORD, the God of Israel — that is its inheritance, just as he spoke to it.
And Moses gave to the tribe of the Reubenites, by their clans;
and their territory was from Aroer on the edge of the Wadi Arnon, and the city in the middle of the wadi, and all the plain by Medeba;
Heshbon and all its cities that are in the plain: Dibon, Bamoth-baal and Beth-baal-meon,
and Jahaz, Kedemoth and Mephaath,
and Kiriathaim, Sibmah and Zereth-shahar on the hill of the valley,
and Beth-peor, the slopes of Pisgah and Beth-jeshimoth,

and all the cities of the plain, and all the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, whom Moses struck, with the leaders of Midian — Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur and Reba, the princes of Sihon, who dwelt in the land.
And Balaam son of Beor, the diviner, the Israelites killed with the sword among their slain.
And the border of the Reubenites was the Jordan and its territory. This was the inheritance of the Reubenites by their clans, the cities and their villages.
And Moses gave to the tribe of Gad, to the Gadites, by their clans;
and their territory was Jazer and all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the Ammonites, as far as Aroer which faces Rabbah;
and from Heshbon as far as Ramath-mizpeh and Betonim, and from Mahanaim as far as the territory of Lo-debar;

and in the valley: Beth-haram, Beth-nimrah, Succoth and Zaphon, the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon, the Jordan and its territory, as far as the end of the Sea of Kinnereth, beyond the Jordan eastward.
This was the inheritance of the Gadites by their clans, the cities and their villages.
And Moses gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh; and it belonged to the half-tribe of the Manassites by their clans.
And their territory was from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the villages of Jair that are in Bashan, sixty cities;
and half of Gilead, and Ashtaroth and Edrei, the cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan, belonged to the descendants of Machir son of Manasseh, to half of the descendants of Machir by their clans.
These are the inheritances that Moses apportioned in the plains of Moab, beyond the Jordan of Jericho, eastward.
And to the tribe of Levi Moses gave no inheritance: the LORD, the God of Israel — he is their inheritance, just as he spoke to them.

joshua_14.t: And these are the inheritances that the Israelites received in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun and the heads of the ancestral houses of the tribes of the Israelites apportioned to them,
by the lot of their inheritance, just as the LORD commanded by the hand of Moses, for the nine tribes and the half-tribe.
For Moses had given the inheritance of the two and a half tribes beyond the Jordan; but to the Levites he gave no inheritance among them.

For the descendants of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim; and they gave no portion to the Levites in the land, except cities to live in, with their pasture lands for their livestock and their property.
Just as the LORD commanded Moses, so the Israelites did, and they apportioned the land.

And the Judahites approached Joshua at Gilgal, and Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him, "You know the word that the LORD spoke to Moses the man of God concerning me and concerning you at Kadesh-barnea.
"I was forty years old when Moses the servant of the LORD sent me from Kadesh-barnea to spy out the land, and I brought him back word just as it was in my heart.
"But my brothers who went up with me melted the heart of the people, while I followed the LORD my God fully.
"And Moses swore on that day, 'Surely the land on which your foot has trodden shall be an inheritance for you and for your children for ever, because you have followed the LORD my God fully.'
"And now the LORD has kept me alive, just as he spoke, these forty-five years since the LORD spoke this word to Moses, while Israel walked in the wilderness. And now I am today eighty-five years old.
"I am still as strong today as on the day Moses sent me; as my strength was then, so is my strength now, for war and for going out and for coming in.

"And now give me this hill country of which the LORD spoke on that day; for you yourself heard on that day that the Anakim were there and cities great and fortified. Perhaps the LORD will be with me, and I shall dispossess them, just as the LORD spoke."
And Joshua blessed him, and he gave Hebron to Caleb son of Jephunneh as an inheritance.
Therefore Hebron became the inheritance of Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite to this day, because he followed the LORD, the God of Israel, fully.
And the name of Hebron formerly was Kiriath-arba — Arba was the greatest man among the Anakim. And the land had rest from war.

joshua_15.t: And the lot for the tribe of the Judahites, by their clans, ran toward the border of Edom, the Wilderness of Zin, southward, from the far end of the south.
And their southern border was from the end of the Salt Sea, from the bay that faces southward;
and it goes out south of the Ascent of Akrabbim and passes on to Zin, and goes up south of Kadesh-barnea, passes on to Hezron, goes up to Addar and turns to Karka,
and passes on to Azmon and goes out at the Wadi of Egypt; and the border ends at the sea. This shall be your southern border.
And the eastern border is the Salt Sea as far as the end of the Jordan. And the border on the northern side is from the bay of the sea at the end of the Jordan;
and the border goes up to Beth-hoglah and passes north of Beth-arabah; and the border goes up to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben;

and the border goes up to Debir from the Valley of Achor, and northward it turns toward Gilgal, which is opposite the Ascent of Adummim, south of the wadi; and the border passes on to the waters of En-shemesh, and ends at En-rogel;

and the border goes up the Valley of Ben-hinnom to the southern slope of the Jebusites — that is Jerusalem; and the border goes up to the top of the mountain that faces the Valley of Hinnom on the west, at the northern end of the Valley of Rephaim;
and the border bends from the top of the mountain to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah, and goes out to the cities of Mount Ephron; and the border bends to Baalah — that is Kiriath-jearim;
and the border turns from Baalah westward to Mount Seir and passes on to the northern slope of Mount Jearim — that is Kesalon — and goes down to Beth-shemesh and passes on to Timnah;
and the border goes out to the northern slope of Ekron, bends to Shikkeron, passes on to Mount Baalah and goes out at Jabneel; and the border ends at the sea.
And the western border is the Great Sea and its coast. This is the border of the Judahites round about, by their clans.
And to Caleb son of Jephunneh he gave a portion among the Judahites, according to the mouth of the LORD to Joshua: Kiriath-arba — Arba was the father of Anak — that is Hebron.
And Caleb dispossessed from there the three sons of Anak: Sheshai, Ahiman and Talmai, those born of Anak.
And he went up from there against the inhabitants of Debir; and the name of Debir formerly was Kiriath-sepher.
And Caleb said, "Whoever strikes Kiriath-sepher and captures it, I will give him Achsah my daughter as a wife."
And Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's brother, captured it; and he gave him Achsah his daughter as a wife.
And when she came, she incited him to ask a field from her father. And she alighted from the donkey, and Caleb said to her, "What is your trouble?"
And she said, "Give me a blessing; since you have given me the land of the Negev, give me also springs of water." And he gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the Judahites by their clans.
And the cities at the far end of the tribe of the Judahites, toward the border of Edom in the south, were Kabzeel, Eder and Jagur,
Kinah, Dimonah and Adadah,
Kedesh, Hazor and Ithnan,
Ziph, Telem and Bealoth,
Hazor-hadattah and Kerioth-hezron — that is Hazor —
Amam, Shema and Moladah,
Hazar-gaddah, Heshmon and Beth-pelet,
Hazar-shual, Beersheba and Biziothiah,
Baalah, Iim and Ezem,
Eltolad, Kesil and Hormah,
Ziklag, Madmannah and Sansannah,
Lebaoth, Shilhim, Ain and Rimmon: all the cities, twenty-nine, with their villages.
In the Shephelah: Eshtaol, Zorah and Ashnah,
Zanoah and En-gannim, Tappuah and Enam,
Jarmuth and Adullam, Socoh and Azekah,
Shaaraim, Adithaim, Gederah and Gederothaim: fourteen cities, with their villages.
Zenan, Hadashah and Migdal-gad,
Dilean, Mizpeh and Joktheel,
Lachish, Bozkath and Eglon,
Cabbon, Lahmas and Kitlish,
Gederoth, Beth-dagon, Naamah and Makkedah: sixteen cities, with their villages.
Libnah, Ether and Ashan,
Iphtah, Ashnah and Nezib,
Keilah, Aczib and Mareshah: nine cities, with their villages.
Ekron, with its daughter-towns and its villages;
from Ekron westward, all that lies beside Ashdod, with their villages;
Ashdod, its daughter-towns and its villages; Gaza, its daughter-towns and its villages, as far as the Wadi of Egypt, and the Great Sea and its coast.
And in the hill country: Shamir, Jattir and Socoh,
Dannah and Kiriath-sannah — that is Debir —
Anab, Eshtemoh and Anim,
Goshen, Holon and Giloh: eleven cities, with their villages.
Arab, Rumah and Eshan,
Janum, Beth-tappuah and Aphekah,
Humtah, Kiriath-arba — that is Hebron — and Zior: nine cities, with their villages.
Maon, Carmel, Ziph and Juttah,
Jezreel, Jokdeam and Zanoah,
Kain, Gibeah and Timnah: ten cities, with their villages.
Halhul, Beth-zur and Gedor,
Maarath, Beth-anoth and Eltekon: six cities, with their villages.
Kiriath-baal — that is Kiriath-jearim — and Rabbah: two cities, with their villages.
In the wilderness: Beth-arabah, Middin and Secacah,
Nibshan, the City of Salt and En-gedi: six cities, with their villages.
But the Jebusites, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the Judahites were not able to dispossess; and the Jebusites have dwelt with the Judahites in Jerusalem to this day.

joshua_16.t: And the lot for the descendants of Joseph went out from the Jordan of Jericho, to the waters of Jericho on the east, the wilderness going up from Jericho into the hill country to Bethel.
And it goes out from Bethel to Luz and passes on to the border of the Archites, to Ataroth,
and goes down westward to the border of the Japhletites, as far as the border of Lower Beth-horon and as far as Gezer; and it ends at the sea.
And the descendants of Joseph — Manasseh and Ephraim — received their inheritance.
And the territory of the Ephraimites by their clans was this: the border of their inheritance on the east was Ataroth-addar as far as Upper Beth-horon;
and the border goes out westward — Micmethath is on the north — and the border turns eastward to Taanath-shiloh and passes by it on the east to Janoah,
and goes down from Janoah to Ataroth and Naarah, touches Jericho and goes out at the Jordan.
From Tappuah the border goes westward to the Wadi Kanah, and ends at the sea. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the Ephraimites by their clans;
and the cities set apart for the Ephraimites within the inheritance of the Manassites, all the cities with their villages.
But they did not dispossess the Canaanites who dwelt in Gezer; and the Canaanites have dwelt in the midst of Ephraim to this day, and have become a slave gang doing forced labour.

joshua_17.t: And the lot fell to the tribe of Manasseh, for he was Joseph's firstborn — to Machir, Manasseh's firstborn, the father of Gilead, because he was a man of war; and Gilead and Bashan belonged to him.

And it belonged to the rest of the Manassites by their clans: to the descendants of Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher and Shemida. These were the male descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, by their clans.
And Zelophehad son of Hepher son of Gilead son of Machir son of Manasseh had no sons, but only daughters; and these are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah.

And they came near before Eleazar the priest and before Joshua son of Nun and before the leaders, saying, "The LORD commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brothers." And he gave them, according to the mouth of the LORD, an inheritance among their father's brothers.
And ten portions fell to Manasseh, besides the land of Gilead and Bashan, which is beyond the Jordan;
for the daughters of Manasseh received an inheritance among his sons; and the land of Gilead belonged to the rest of the Manassites.
And the border of Manasseh was from Asher to Micmethath, which faces Shechem; and the border goes to the south, to the inhabitants of En-tappuah.
The land of Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, but Tappuah itself, on the border of Manasseh, belonged to the Ephraimites.

And the border goes down to the Wadi Kanah, south of the wadi. These cities belonged to Ephraim among the cities of Manasseh; and the border of Manasseh was on the north of the wadi, and it ended at the sea.
Southward it belonged to Ephraim and northward to Manasseh, and the sea was its border; on the north they touch Asher, and on the east Issachar.

And in Issachar and in Asher there belonged to Manasseh: Beth-shean and its daughter-towns, Ibleam and its daughter-towns, the inhabitants of Dor and its daughter-towns, the inhabitants of En-dor and its daughter-towns, the inhabitants of Taanach and its daughter-towns, and the inhabitants of Megiddo and its daughter-towns — the three of Napheth.
But the Manassites were not able to take possession of these cities, and the Canaanites were determined to dwell in this land.
And when the Israelites became strong, they put the Canaanites to forced labour; but they did not utterly dispossess them.
And the descendants of Joseph spoke with Joshua, saying, "Why have you given me one lot and one portion as an inheritance, when I am a numerous people, seeing that until now the LORD has blessed me?"

And Joshua said to them, "If you are a numerous people, go up to the forest and clear ground for yourself there, in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim, since the hill country of Ephraim is too narrow for you."

And the descendants of Joseph said, "The hill country will not be enough for us, and the Canaanites who dwell in the land of the valley all have iron chariots — those in Beth-shean and its daughter-towns and those in the Valley of Jezreel."
And Joshua said to the house of Joseph, to Ephraim and to Manasseh, "You are a numerous people and you have great strength; you shall not have one lot only,

"for the hill country shall be yours. Though it is forest, you shall clear it, and its farthest parts shall be yours; for you shall dispossess the Canaanites, though they have iron chariots, though they are strong."

joshua_18.t: And the whole congregation of the Israelites assembled at Shiloh, and they set up the tent of meeting there; and the land was subdued before them.
And there remained among the Israelites seven tribes that had not received their inheritance by division.
And Joshua said to the Israelites, "How long will you hold back from going in to take possession of the land that the LORD the God of your ancestors has given you?
"Provide for yourselves three men for each tribe, and I will send them out; and they shall go and walk through the land and describe it in writing according to their inheritance, and come to me.
"And they shall divide it among themselves into seven portions. Judah shall remain on its territory in the south, and the house of Joseph shall remain on their territory in the north.
"And you shall describe the land in writing in seven portions and bring it to me here, and I will cast the lot for you here before the LORD our God.

"For the Levites have no portion among you, because the priesthood of the LORD is their inheritance; and Gad and Reuben and the half-tribe of Manasseh have received their inheritance beyond the Jordan eastward, which Moses the servant of the LORD gave them."

And the men arose and went; and Joshua commanded those who went to describe the land in writing, "Go and walk through the land, describe it in writing and return to me, and here I will cast the lot for you before the LORD in Shiloh."
And the men went and passed through the land and described it in writing by cities, in seven portions, on a scroll; and they came to Joshua, to the camp at Shiloh.
And Joshua cast the lot for them in Shiloh before the LORD; and there Joshua apportioned the land to the Israelites according to their divisions.
And the lot of the tribe of the Benjaminites came up by their clans, and the territory of their lot went out between the Judahites and the descendants of Joseph.
And their border on the northern side was from the Jordan; and the border goes up to the northern slope of Jericho and goes up in the hill country westward, and ends at the wilderness of Beth-aven.
And from there the border passes on to Luz, to the southern slope of Luz — that is Bethel; and the border goes down to Ataroth-addar, on the mountain south of Lower Beth-horon.

And the border bends and turns on the western side southward, from the mountain that faces Beth-horon on the south; and it ends at Kiriath-baal — that is Kiriath-jearim, a city of the Judahites. This is the western side.
And the southern side is from the end of Kiriath-jearim; and the border goes out westward and goes out to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah.

And the border goes down to the end of the mountain that faces the Valley of Ben-hinnom, which is in the Valley of Rephaim to the north; and it goes down the Valley of Hinnom to the southern slope of the Jebusites, and goes down to En-rogel.
And it bends from the north, goes out to En-shemesh and goes out to Geliloth, which is opposite the Ascent of Adummim; and it goes down to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben,
and passes on to the slope opposite the Arabah northward, and goes down to the Arabah;
and the border passes on to the northern slope of Beth-hoglah; and the border ends at the northern bay of the Salt Sea, at the southern end of the Jordan. This is the southern border.
And the Jordan borders it on the eastern side. This is the inheritance of the Benjaminites, by its borders round about, by their clans.
And the cities of the tribe of the Benjaminites by their clans were Jericho, Beth-hoglah and Emek-keziz,
Beth-arabah, Zemaraim and Bethel,
Avvim, Parah and Ophrah,
Kephar-ammoni, Ophni and Geba: twelve cities, with their villages.
Gibeon, Ramah and Beeroth,
Mizpeh, Kephirah and Mozah,
Rekem, Irpeel and Taralah,
and Zela, Haeleph and the Jebusite city — that is Jerusalem — Gibeah and Kiriath: fourteen cities, with their villages. This is the inheritance of the Benjaminites by their clans.

joshua_19.t: And the second lot came out for Simeon, for the tribe of the Simeonites by their clans; and their inheritance was within the inheritance of the Judahites.
And they had as their inheritance: Beersheba, Sheba and Moladah,
Hazar-shual, Balah and Ezem,
Eltolad, Bethul and Hormah,
Ziklag, Beth-marcaboth and Hazar-susah,
Beth-lebaoth and Sharuhen: thirteen cities, with their villages.
Ain, Rimmon, Ether and Ashan: four cities, with their villages;
and all the villages around these cities as far as Baalath-beer, Ramah of the Negev. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the Simeonites by their clans.

The inheritance of the Simeonites came out of the portion of the Judahites, because the portion of the Judahites was too great for them; and the Simeonites received their inheritance within their inheritance.
And the third lot came up for the Zebulunites by their clans; and the border of their inheritance reached as far as Sarid.
And their border goes up westward to Maralah, touches Dabbesheth, and touches the wadi that faces Jokneam;
and it turns back from Sarid eastward, toward the rising of the sun, to the border of Kisloth-tabor, goes out to Daberath and goes up to Japhia;
and from there it passes on eastward, toward the sunrise, to Gath-hepher, to Eth-kazin, and goes out to Rimmon, which bends round to Neah;
and the border turns about it on the north to Hannathon; and it ends at the Valley of Iphtah-el;
and Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah and Bethlehem: twelve cities, with their villages.
This is the inheritance of the Zebulunites by their clans: these cities, with their villages.
For Issachar the fourth lot came out, for the Issacharites by their clans;
and their border was to Jezreel, Kesulloth and Shunem,
Hapharaim, Shion and Anaharath,
Rabbith, Kishion and Ebez,
Remeth, En-gannim, En-haddah and Beth-pazzez.
And the border touches Tabor, Shahazumah and Beth-shemesh, and their border ends at the Jordan: sixteen cities, with their villages.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the Issacharites by their clans: the cities, with their villages.
And the fifth lot came out for the tribe of the Asherites by their clans;
and their border was Helkath, Hali, Beten and Acshaph,
and Allammelech, Amad and Mishal; and it touches Carmel on the west and Shihor-libnath,
and it turns back toward the rising of the sun to Beth-dagon and touches Zebulun and the Valley of Iphtah-el northward, Beth-emek and Neiel, and goes out to Cabul on the north,
and Ebron, Rehob, Hammon and Kanah, as far as Greater Sidon.
And the border turns back to Ramah and to the fortified city of Tyre; and the border turns back to Hosah, and it ends at the sea, in the region of Aczib;
and Ummah, Aphek and Rehob: twenty-two cities, with their villages.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the Asherites by their clans: these cities, with their villages.
For the Naphtalites the sixth lot came out, for the Naphtalites by their clans;
and their border was from Heleph, from the great tree at Zaanannim, and Adami-nekeb and Jabneel, as far as Lakkum; and it ended at the Jordan.
And the border turns back westward to Aznoth-tabor, and goes out from there to Hukkok; it touches Zebulun on the south, Asher on the west, and Judah at the Jordan toward the rising of the sun.
And the fortified cities were Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath and Kinnereth,
Adamah, Ramah and Hazor,
Kedesh, Edrei and En-hazor,
and Yiron, Migdal-el, Horem, Beth-anath and Beth-shemesh: nineteen cities, with their villages.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the Naphtalites by their clans: the cities, with their villages.
For the tribe of the Danites by their clans the seventh lot came out.
And the territory of their inheritance was Zorah, Eshtaol and Ir-shemesh,
Shaalabbin, Aijalon and Ithlah,
Elon, Timnah and Ekron,
Eltekeh, Gibbethon and Baalath,
Jehud, Bene-berak and Gath-rimmon,
and the waters of the Jarkon and the Rakkon, with the territory opposite Joppa.

And the territory of the Danites went out from them; so the Danites went up and fought against Leshem and captured it, struck it with the edge of the sword, took possession of it and dwelt in it; and they called Leshem Dan, after the name of Dan their ancestor.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the Danites by their clans: these cities, with their villages.
And they finished dividing the land for possession by its borders; and the Israelites gave an inheritance to Joshua son of Nun among them.
According to the mouth of the LORD they gave him the city he asked for, Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim; and he built the city and dwelt in it.

These are the inheritances that Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun and the heads of the ancestral houses of the tribes of the Israelites apportioned by lot at Shiloh, before the LORD, at the entrance of the tent of meeting. And they finished dividing the land.

joshua_20.t: And the LORD spoke to Joshua,
"Speak to the Israelites: 'Assign for yourselves the cities of refuge of which I spoke to you by the hand of Moses,
'that a killer who strikes a person down inadvertently, without knowledge, may flee there; and they shall be for you a refuge from the avenger of blood.

'And he shall flee to one of these cities and stand at the entrance of the gate of the city and state his case in the hearing of the elders of that city; and they shall take him into the city to themselves and give him a place, and he shall dwell with them.
'And if the avenger of blood pursues him, they shall not deliver the killer into his hand, because he struck his neighbour without knowledge and had not hated him previously.

'And he shall dwell in that city until he stands before the congregation for judgement, until the death of the high priest who is in office in those days. Then the killer may return and come to his own city and his own house, to the city from which he fled.'"
And they set apart Kedesh in Galilee in the hill country of Naphtali, Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and Kiriath-arba — that is Hebron — in the hill country of Judah.

And beyond the Jordan of Jericho, eastward, they assigned Bezer in the wilderness, in the plain, from the tribe of Reuben; Ramoth in Gilead from the tribe of Gad; and Golan in Bashan from the tribe of Manasseh.

These were the appointed cities for all the Israelites and for the resident alien living among them, that anyone who strikes a person down inadvertently might flee there and not die by the hand of the avenger of blood until he stood before the congregation.

joshua_21.t: And the heads of the ancestral houses of the Levites approached Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun and the heads of the ancestral houses of the tribes of the Israelites;
and they spoke to them at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, saying, "The LORD commanded by the hand of Moses to give us cities to live in, with their pasture lands for our livestock."
And the Israelites gave to the Levites out of their inheritance, according to the mouth of the LORD, these cities with their pasture lands.

And the lot came out for the clans of the Kohathites; and the descendants of Aaron the priest, from among the Levites, received by lot from the tribe of Judah, from the tribe of the Simeonites and from the tribe of Benjamin thirteen cities.
And the rest of the descendants of Kohath received by lot ten cities from the clans of the tribe of Ephraim, from the tribe of Dan and from the half-tribe of Manasseh.

And the descendants of Gershon received by lot thirteen cities from the clans of the tribe of Issachar, from the tribe of Asher, from the tribe of Naphtali and from the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.
The descendants of Merari, by their clans, received twelve cities from the tribe of Reuben, from the tribe of Gad and from the tribe of Zebulun.
And the Israelites gave these cities with their pasture lands to the Levites by lot, just as the LORD had commanded by the hand of Moses.
And they gave from the tribe of the Judahites and from the tribe of the Simeonites these cities, which are named here.
And it went to the descendants of Aaron, of the clans of the Kohathites, of the descendants of Levi, for the first lot was theirs.
And they gave them Kiriath-arba — Arba was the father of Anak — that is Hebron, in the hill country of Judah, with its pasture lands around it.
But the fields of the city and its villages they gave to Caleb son of Jephunneh as his holding.
And to the descendants of Aaron the priest they gave the city of refuge for the killer, Hebron, with its pasture lands; and Libnah with its pasture lands,
Jattir with its pasture lands, Eshtemoa with its pasture lands,
Holon with its pasture lands, Debir with its pasture lands,
Ain with its pasture lands, Juttah with its pasture lands and Beth-shemesh with its pasture lands: nine cities from these two tribes.
And from the tribe of Benjamin: Gibeon with its pasture lands, Geba with its pasture lands,
Anathoth with its pasture lands and Almon with its pasture lands: four cities.
All the cities of the descendants of Aaron, the priests, were thirteen cities with their pasture lands.
And to the clans of the descendants of Kohath, the Levites who remained of the descendants of Kohath — the cities of their lot were from the tribe of Ephraim.
And they gave them the city of refuge for the killer, Shechem, with its pasture lands, in the hill country of Ephraim; and Gezer with its pasture lands,
Kibzaim with its pasture lands and Beth-horon with its pasture lands: four cities.
And from the tribe of Dan: Eltekeh with its pasture lands, Gibbethon with its pasture lands,
Aijalon with its pasture lands and Gath-rimmon with its pasture lands: four cities.
And from the half-tribe of Manasseh: Taanach with its pasture lands and Gath-rimmon with its pasture lands: two cities.
All the cities were ten, with their pasture lands, for the clans of the descendants of Kohath who remained.

And to the descendants of Gershon, of the clans of the Levites: from the half-tribe of Manasseh, the city of refuge for the killer, Golan in Bashan, with its pasture lands; and Beeshterah with its pasture lands: two cities.
And from the tribe of Issachar: Kishion with its pasture lands, Daberath with its pasture lands,
Jarmuth with its pasture lands and En-gannim with its pasture lands: four cities.
And from the tribe of Asher: Mishal with its pasture lands, Abdon with its pasture lands,
Helkath with its pasture lands and Rehob with its pasture lands: four cities.
And from the tribe of Naphtali: the city of refuge for the killer, Kedesh in Galilee, with its pasture lands; Hammoth-dor with its pasture lands and Kartan with its pasture lands: three cities.
All the cities of the Gershonites, by their clans, were thirteen cities with their pasture lands.
And to the clans of the descendants of Merari, the Levites who remained: from the tribe of Zebulun, Jokneam with its pasture lands, Kartah with its pasture lands,
Dimnah with its pasture lands and Nahalal with its pasture lands: four cities.
And from the tribe of Reuben: Bezer with its pasture lands, Jahaz with its pasture lands,
Kedemoth with its pasture lands and Mephaath with its pasture lands: four cities.
And from the tribe of Gad: the city of refuge for the killer, Ramoth in Gilead, with its pasture lands; and Mahanaim with its pasture lands,
Heshbon with its pasture lands and Jazer with its pasture lands: four cities in all.
All the cities of the descendants of Merari, by their clans, who remained of the clans of the Levites — their lot was twelve cities.
All the cities of the Levites within the holding of the Israelites were forty-eight cities with their pasture lands.
Each of these cities had its pasture lands around it; so it was for all these cities.
And the LORD gave to Israel all the land that he had sworn to give to their ancestors; and they took possession of it and dwelt in it.
And the LORD gave them rest round about, according to all that he had sworn to their ancestors; and not one of all their enemies stood before them. All their enemies the LORD gave into their hand.
Not a word failed of all the good word that the LORD had spoken to the house of Israel; all of it came to pass.

joshua_22.t: Then Joshua summoned the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh
and said to them, "You have kept all that Moses the servant of the LORD commanded you, and you have listened to my voice in all that I commanded you.
"You have not forsaken your brothers these many days, to this day, and you have kept the charge of the commandment of the LORD your God.

"And now the LORD your God has given rest to your brothers, just as he spoke to them. So turn and go to your tents, to the land of your holding, which Moses the servant of the LORD gave you beyond the Jordan.

"Only take great care to do the commandment and the law that Moses the servant of the LORD commanded you: to love the LORD your God, to walk in all his ways, to keep his commandments, to cling to him, and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul."
And Joshua blessed them and sent them away, and they went to their tents.

Now to the half-tribe of Manasseh Moses had given a portion in Bashan, and to its other half Joshua gave a portion with their brothers beyond the Jordan westward. And when Joshua sent them away to their tents, he blessed them

and said to them, "Return to your tents with great riches and with very much livestock, with silver, gold, bronze and iron, and with very many garments. Divide the spoil of your enemies with your brothers."

And the Reubenites and the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh returned and went from the Israelites, from Shiloh in the land of Canaan, to go to the land of Gilead, to the land of their holding, in which they had taken possession according to the mouth of the LORD by the hand of Moses.
And they came to Geliloth of the Jordan, in the land of Canaan, and the Reubenites and the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh built an altar there at the Jordan, a great altar to look at.

And the Israelites heard it said, "The Reubenites and the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh have built the altar opposite the land of Canaan, at Geliloth of the Jordan, on the side belonging to the Israelites."
And when the Israelites heard, the whole congregation of the Israelites assembled at Shiloh to go up against them for war.
And the Israelites sent to the Reubenites, to the Gadites and to the half-tribe of Manasseh, to the land of Gilead, Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest,
and ten leaders with him, one leader for each ancestral house, for all the tribes of Israel; and each of them was head of his ancestral house among the thousands of Israel.
And they came to the Reubenites, to the Gadites and to the half-tribe of Manasseh, to the land of Gilead, and spoke with them, saying,

"Thus says the whole congregation of the LORD: What is this unfaithfulness that you have committed against the God of Israel, turning back today from following the LORD, by building for yourselves an altar, rebelling today against the LORD?
"Was the iniquity of Peor too little for us — from which we have not cleansed ourselves to this day, and because of which the plague came upon the congregation of the LORD —
"that you should turn away today from following the LORD? And it will be: you rebel today against the LORD, and tomorrow he will be angry with the whole congregation of Israel.

"And surely, if the land of your holding is unclean, cross over to the land of the LORD's holding, where the tabernacle of the LORD dwells, and take a holding among us. But do not rebel against the LORD, and do not rebel against us, by building for yourselves an altar besides the altar of the LORD our God.

"Did not Achan son of Zerah commit unfaithfulness in the matter of what was devoted to destruction, and wrath came upon the whole congregation of Israel? And he was one man — did he not perish for his iniquity?"
And the Reubenites and the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh answered and spoke with the heads of the thousands of Israel:
"God, God, the LORD! God, God, the LORD! He knows, and let Israel itself know: if it was in rebellion or in unfaithfulness against the LORD — do not save us this day!

"— to build for ourselves an altar to turn back from following the LORD; or if to offer up on it a burnt offering and a grain offering, or if to make on it sacrifices of peace offerings — may the LORD himself require it!
"But truly, we did this out of anxiety over a matter, saying, 'In time to come your children will say to our children, What have you to do with the LORD, the God of Israel?
"'For the LORD has set a border between us and you, Reubenites and Gadites — the Jordan. You have no portion in the LORD.' And so your children would make our children cease from fearing the LORD.
"And we said, 'Let us act for ourselves by building the altar — not for burnt offering and not for sacrifice,

"'but that it may be a witness between us and you and between our generations after us, that we may perform the service of the LORD before him with our burnt offerings and our sacrifices and our peace offerings; so that your children will not say to our children in time to come, You have no portion in the LORD.'

"And we said, 'When they say this to us and to our generations in time to come, we shall say: See the copy of the altar of the LORD that our ancestors made — not for burnt offering and not for sacrifice, but it is a witness between us and you.'

"Far be it from us to rebel against the LORD and to turn back today from following the LORD by building an altar for burnt offering, for grain offering or for sacrifice, besides the altar of the LORD our God that is before his tabernacle."

And when Phinehas the priest and the leaders of the congregation and the heads of the thousands of Israel who were with him heard the words that the Reubenites and the Gadites and the Manassites spoke, it seemed good to them.

And Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest said to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the Manassites, "Today we know that the LORD is in our midst, because you have not committed this unfaithfulness against the LORD. Now you have delivered the Israelites from the hand of the LORD."
And Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest and the leaders returned from the Reubenites and the Gadites, from the land of Gilead to the land of Canaan, to the Israelites, and brought them back word.

And the word seemed good to the Israelites, and the Israelites blessed God; and they did not speak of going up against them for war, to destroy the land in which the Reubenites and the Gadites were dwelling.
And the Reubenites and the Gadites named the altar — for it is a witness between us that the LORD is God.

joshua_23.t: And it was, after many days, after the LORD had given rest to Israel from all their enemies round about, and Joshua was old and advanced in years,
Joshua summoned all Israel — its elders, its heads, its judges and its officers — and said to them, "I am old, advanced in years.
"And you, you have seen all that the LORD your God has done to all these nations before you; for the LORD your God, he is the one fighting for you.
"See, I have allotted to you these remaining nations as an inheritance for your tribes, from the Jordan; and all the nations that I cut off, and the Great Sea, toward the setting of the sun.
"And the LORD your God, he will thrust them out from before you and dispossess them from before you, and you shall take possession of their land, just as the LORD your God spoke to you.
"And you shall be very strong, to take care to do all that is written in the book of the law of Moses, so as not to turn aside from it to the right or to the left,

"so as not to go in among these nations, these that remain with you. And the name of their gods you shall not invoke, and you shall not cause anyone to swear by them, and you shall not serve them, and you shall not bow down to them.
"But to the LORD your God you shall cling, as you have done to this day.
"And the LORD has dispossessed from before you nations great and mighty; and as for you, no one has stood before you to this day.
"One man of you puts a thousand to flight, for the LORD your God, he is the one fighting for you, just as he spoke to you.
"And you shall take great heed to yourselves, to love the LORD your God.
"For if you ever turn back and cling to the remnant of these nations, these that remain with you, and intermarry with them and go in among them and they among you,

"know certainly that the LORD your God will not continue to dispossess these nations from before you; and they shall become for you a trap and a snare, a scourge in your sides and pricks in your eyes, until you perish from upon this good ground that the LORD your God has given you.

"And here I am, going today in the way of all the earth. And you know with all your heart and with all your soul that not one word has fallen of all the good words that the LORD your God spoke concerning you. All of them have come to you; not one word of them has fallen.

"And it shall be, just as every good word has come upon you that the LORD your God spoke to you, so the LORD will bring upon you every bad word, until he has destroyed you from upon this good ground that the LORD your God has given you,

"when you transgress the covenant of the LORD your God that he commanded you, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them. Then the anger of the LORD will burn against you, and you will perish quickly from upon the good land that he has given you."

joshua_24.t: And Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel to Shechem, and summoned the elders of Israel, its heads, its judges and its officers; and they presented themselves before God.

And Joshua said to all the people, "Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: 'Beyond the River your ancestors dwelt from of old — Terah the father of Abraham and the father of Nahor — and they served other gods.
'And I took your ancestor Abraham from beyond the River and led him through all the land of Canaan, and I multiplied his offspring and gave him Isaac.
'And I gave to Isaac Jacob and Esau; and to Esau I gave Mount Seir to take possession of it; and Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt.
'And I sent Moses and Aaron, and I struck Egypt according to what I did in its midst; and afterwards I brought you out.
'And I brought your ancestors out from Egypt, and you came to the sea; and Egypt pursued after your ancestors with chariotry and with horsemen to the Sea of Reeds.

'And they cried out to the LORD, and he put gloom between you and the Egyptians, and he brought the sea over them and covered them. And your eyes saw what I did in Egypt. And you dwelt in the wilderness many days.

'And I brought you to the land of the Amorite who dwelt beyond the Jordan, and they fought with you; and I gave them into your hand, and you took possession of their land, and I destroyed them from before you.
'And Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, arose and fought against Israel; and he sent and summoned Balaam son of Beor to curse you.
'And I was not willing to listen to Balaam, and he blessed you again and again; and I delivered you from his hand.

'And you crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho; and the lords of Jericho fought against you — the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Girgashite, the Hivite and the Jebusite — and I gave them into your hand.
'And I sent the hornet before you, and it drove them out from before you — the two kings of the Amorite — not by your sword and not by your bow.
'And I gave you a land for which you did not labour, and cities which you did not build, and you dwelt in them; vineyards and olive trees which you did not plant, you are eating.'"
"And now, fear the LORD and serve him in blamelessness and in faithfulness; and remove the gods that your ancestors served beyond the River and in Egypt, and serve the LORD.

"And if it seems bad to you to serve the LORD, choose for yourselves today whom you will serve — whether the gods that your ancestors served beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorite in whose land you are dwelling. But as for me and my household, we will serve the LORD."
And the people answered, "Far be it from us to forsake the LORD to serve other gods!

"For the LORD our God, he is the one who brought us and our ancestors up from the land of Egypt, from a house of slaves, and who did these great signs before our eyes and kept us on all the way that we went and among all the peoples through whose midst we passed.
"And the LORD drove out all the peoples, and the Amorite who dwelt in the land, from before us. We also will serve the LORD, for he is our God."
And Joshua said to the people, "You are not able to serve the LORD, for he is a holy God; he is a jealous God. He will not forgive your transgression and your sins.
"If you forsake the LORD and serve gods of foreignness, then he will turn and do you harm and make an end of you, after he has done you good."
And the people said to Joshua, "No — the LORD we will serve."
And Joshua said to the people, "You are witnesses against yourselves that you yourselves have chosen the LORD, to serve him." And they said, "Witnesses."
"And now, remove the gods of foreignness that are in your midst, and turn your heart to the LORD, the God of Israel."
And the people said to Joshua, "The LORD our God we will serve, and to his voice we will listen."
And Joshua cut a covenant for the people that day, and set for it a statute and an ordinance at Shechem.
And Joshua wrote these words in the book of the law of God; and he took a great stone and set it up there under the oak that was at the sanctuary of the LORD.

And Joshua said to all the people, "See, this stone shall be a witness against us, for it has heard all the sayings of the LORD that he spoke with us; and it shall be a witness against you, lest you deny your God."
And Joshua sent the people away, each to his inheritance.
And it was after these things that Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died, at a hundred and ten years old.
And they buried him in the territory of his inheritance, at Timnath-serah, which is in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
And Israel served the LORD all the days of Joshua and all the days of the elders who outlived Joshua and who knew all the work of the LORD that he had done for Israel.

And the bones of Joseph, which the Israelites had brought up from Egypt, they buried at Shechem, in the portion of the field that Jacob bought from the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for a hundred pieces of money; and they became an inheritance for the descendants of Joseph.
And Eleazar son of Aaron died, and they buried him at Gibeah of Phinehas his son, which had been given to him in the hill country of Ephraim.

lamentations_1.t: How she sits alone, the city that was great with people! She has become like a widow — she who was great among the nations, a princess among the provinces, now put to forced labour.
