Bitterly she weeps in the night, and her tears are on her cheek. She has no comforter among all her lovers; all her friends have dealt treacherously with her; they have become her enemies.
Judah has gone into exile out of affliction and much servitude. She dwells among the nations and has found no resting place. All her pursuers have overtaken her in the narrow places.
The roads of Zion are mourning, for none come to the appointed feast. All her gates are desolate; her priests groan; her virgins grieve, and she herself is in bitterness.
Her adversaries have become the head; her enemies are at ease, for the LORD has brought her grief for the multitude of her transgressions. Her children have gone into captivity before the adversary.
And all her splendour has gone from the daughter of Zion. Her princes have become like deer that find no pasture; they have gone without strength before a pursuer.

Jerusalem remembers, in the days of her affliction and her homelessness, all the precious things that were hers from days of old, when her people fell into the hand of an adversary and she had no helper. The adversaries saw her; they laughed at her downfall.
Jerusalem has sinned grievously; therefore she has become an impurity. All who honoured her despise her, for they have seen her nakedness; she herself groans and turns her face away.
Her uncleanness is on her skirts; she gave no thought to her end. She has come down astonishingly; she has no comforter. "See, LORD, my affliction, for the enemy has magnified himself."
The adversary has spread out his hand over all her precious things, for she has seen nations enter her sanctuary — those whom you commanded should not come into your assembly.
All her people are groaning, seeking bread. They have given their precious things for food, to keep themselves alive. "See, LORD, and look, for I have become despised."

Is it nothing to you, all you who pass along the road? Look and see whether there is any pain like my pain, which was dealt out to me, with which the LORD brought me grief on the day of his burning anger.
From on high he sent fire into my bones, and it overcame them. He spread a net for my feet; he turned me back; he made me desolate, faint all day long.

The yoke of my transgressions has been bound on by his hand; they are woven together, they have come up on my neck; he has made my strength fail. The Lord has given me into the hands of those I cannot withstand.
The Lord has cast aside all my mighty ones in my midst. He has summoned an assembly against me, to break my young men. The Lord has trodden the winepress of the virgin daughter of Judah.
For these things I weep; my eye, my eye runs down with water, for a comforter is far from me, one who would restore my life. My children are desolate, for the enemy has prevailed.
Zion spreads out her hands; she has no comforter. The LORD has commanded concerning Jacob that those around him should be his adversaries. Jerusalem has become an impure thing among them.
The LORD is righteous, for I have rebelled against his word. Listen, please, all you peoples, and see my pain: my virgins and my young men have gone into captivity.
I called to my lovers; they deceived me. My priests and my elders perished in the city while they sought food for themselves, to keep themselves alive.
See, LORD, for I am in distress; my inward parts are in turmoil. My heart is overturned within me, for I have been utterly rebellious. Outside, the sword bereaves; in the house, it is like death.
They have heard that I am groaning; I have no comforter. All my enemies have heard of my distress; they rejoice, for you have done it. Bring the day you proclaimed, and let them become like me.
Let all their wickedness come before you, and deal with them as severely as you have dealt with me for all my transgressions; for my groanings are many and my heart is faint.

lamentations_2.t: How the Lord has covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger! He has thrown down from heaven to earth the splendour of Israel, and has not remembered his footstool in the day of his anger.

The Lord has swallowed up without sparing all the settlements of Jacob. In his wrath he has torn down the fortifications of the daughter of Judah; he has brought them to the ground; he has profaned the kingdom and its princes.
In burning anger he has cut off every horn of Israel; he has drawn back his right hand from before the enemy, and he has burned in Jacob like a flaming fire consuming all around.

He has bent his bow like an enemy; his right hand is set like an adversary's, and he has killed all that was delightful to the eye. In the tent of the daughter of Zion he has poured out his rage like fire.

The Lord has become like an enemy; he has swallowed up Israel. He has swallowed up all her palaces and ruined his fortifications, and he has multiplied mourning and lamentation in the daughter of Judah.

He has broken down his booth like a garden; he has ruined his appointed place. The LORD has caused appointed feast and sabbath to be forgotten in Zion, and in the indignation of his anger he has spurned king and priest.

The Lord has rejected his altar; he has repudiated his sanctuary. He has delivered the walls of her palaces into the hand of an enemy. They have raised a shout in the house of the LORD as on the day of an appointed feast.

The LORD planned to destroy the wall of the daughter of Zion. He stretched out a measuring-line; he did not draw back his hand from swallowing up; he made rampart and wall mourn; together they have languished.
Her gates have sunk into the ground; he has destroyed and broken her bars. Her king and her princes are among the nations; there is no law; her prophets too have found no vision from the LORD.
The elders of the daughter of Zion sit on the ground in silence. They have thrown dust on their heads; they have put on sackcloth. The virgins of Jerusalem have bowed their heads to the ground.

My eyes have failed with tears; my inward parts are in turmoil. My liver is poured out on the ground for the brokenness of the daughter of my people, because child and infant faint in the open squares of the town.
To their mothers they say, "Where is grain and wine?" as they faint away like the fatally wounded in the open squares of the city, as their life pours out into their mothers' bosom.

What can I say for you? To what can I liken you, daughter of Jerusalem? What can I compare you to, that I may comfort you, virgin daughter of Zion? For your brokenness is as great as the sea; who can heal you?
Your prophets have seen for you worthlessness and sham; they have not laid bare your iniquity, so as to restore your fortunes; but they have seen for you oracles of worthlessness and enticement.
All who pass along the road clap their hands at you; they hiss and shake their heads at the daughter of Jerusalem: "Is this the city of which they said, 'Perfect in beauty, a joy to all the earth'?"
All your enemies open their mouth wide at you; they hiss and gnash their teeth; they say, "We have swallowed her up! Surely this is the day we waited for; we have found it, we have seen it."

The LORD has done what he purposed; he has fulfilled his speech, which he commanded from days of old. He has torn down without sparing; he has made the enemy rejoice over you; he has lifted up the horn of your adversaries.
Their heart cries out to the Lord. Wall of the daughter of Zion, let tears run down like a river, day and night! Give yourself no rest; let the pupil of your eye not be still.

Arise, cry out in the night, at the beginning of the night-watches! Pour out your heart like water before the presence of the Lord. Lift up your hands to him for the life of your children, who faint from hunger at the head of every street.
See, LORD, and look! To whom have you dealt so severely? Shall women eat their own offspring, the children they have reared? Shall priest and prophet be killed in the sanctuary of the Lord?
Young and old lie on the ground in the streets; my virgins and my young men have fallen by the sword. You have killed in the day of your anger; you have slaughtered; you have not spared.
You have summoned, as on a feast day, my terrors from every side, and on the day of the LORD's anger there was no escapee or survivor. Those I had borne and reared, my enemy has made an end of them.

lamentations_3.t: I am the man who has seen affliction under the rod of his fury.
He has driven me and made me walk in darkness and not in light.
Surely against me he turns his hand again and again, all day long.
He has made my flesh and my skin waste away; he has broken my bones.
He has built siegeworks against me and surrounded me with poison and hardship.
In dark places he has made me dwell, like those long dead.
He has walled me in so that I cannot get out; he has made my bronze fetters heavy.
Even when I cry out and call for help, he shuts out my prayer.
He has walled up my ways with hewn stone; he has made my paths crooked.
He is to me a bear lying in wait, a lion in hiding.
He has turned my ways aside and torn me in pieces; he has left me desolate.
He has bent his bow and set me up as a target for the arrow.
He has brought into my kidneys the sons of his quiver.
I have become a laughingstock to all my people, their taunt song all day long.
He has filled me with bitterness; he has made me drink wormwood.
He has broken my teeth on gravel; he has pressed me down into ashes.
My life is shut out from peace; I have forgotten what good is.
And I said, "My endurance has perished, and my expectation from the LORD."
Remember my affliction and my homelessness, the wormwood and the poison.
My being remembers it well, and it is bowed down within me.
This I call to mind; therefore I will wait.
The steadfast love of the LORD — surely we are not consumed, for his compassion does not come to an end.
They are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.
"The LORD is my portion," I have said; "therefore I will wait for him."
The LORD is good to those who wait for him, to anyone who seeks him.
It is good that one should wait quietly for the deliverance of the LORD.
It is good for a man to bear a yoke in his youth.
Let him sit alone in silence, for he has laid it upon him.
Let him put his mouth in the dust; perhaps there is hope.
Let him give his cheek to the one who strikes him; let him have his fill of reproach.
For the Lord will not reject for ever.
For though he has brought grief, he will have compassion according to the greatness of his steadfast love.
For he does not afflict from his heart, nor does he grieve the children of a man.
To crush under one's feet all the prisoners of the land,
to turn aside a man's justice before the presence of the Most High,
to subvert a person in his lawsuit — does the Lord not see it?
Who is this who speaks and it comes to be, unless the Lord has commanded it?
Is it not from the mouth of the Most High that both troubles and good come?
Why should any living person complain, a man, about the punishment of his sins?
Let us examine our ways and search them out, and let us return to the LORD.
Let us lift up our heart along with our hands to God in the heavens.
We ourselves have transgressed and rebelled; you have not forgiven.
You have covered yourself with anger and pursued us; you have killed and have not spared.
You have covered yourself with a cloud, so that no prayer can pass through.
You have made us scourings and refuse in the midst of the peoples.
All our enemies open their mouth wide at us.
Terror and a pit have come upon us, devastation and brokenness.
My eye runs down with streams of water for the brokenness of the daughter of my people.
My eye pours itself out and will not cease, for there is no stopping,
until the LORD looks down and sees from heaven.
My eye brings grief to me because of all the daughters of my city.
My enemies have hunted me like a bird, without cause.
They have cut off my life in the pit and cast a stone down on me.
Waters flowed over my head; I said, "I am cut off."
I called on your name, LORD, from the depths of the pit.
You heard my voice: "Do not hide your ear from my plea for relief, from my cry for help."
You drew near on the day I called on you; you said, "Do not fear."
You have taken up my cause, Lord; you have redeemed my life.
You have seen the wrong done to me, LORD; judge my case.
You have seen all their vengeance, all their plans against me.
You have heard their reproach, LORD, all their plans against me,
the lips of those who rise against me, and their muttering against me all day long.
Look at their sitting and their rising: I am their mocking song.
You will repay them a recompense, LORD, according to the work of their hands.
You will give them hardness of heart; let your curse be upon them.
You will pursue them in anger and destroy them from under the heavens of the LORD.

lamentations_4.t: How the gold is dimmed, the fine gold changed! The holy stones lie scattered at the head of every street.
The precious children of Zion, once weighed against pure gold — how they are reckoned as jars of earthenware, the work of a potter's hands!
Even jackals offer the breast and suckle their young; but the daughter of my people has become cruel, like ostriches in the wilderness.
The tongue of the infant cleaves to its palate for thirst; children ask for bread, and no one breaks it for them.
Those who ate delicacies lie desolate in the streets; those brought up in crimson embrace ash heaps.
The punishment of the daughter of my people is greater than that of Sodom, which was overthrown in a moment, with no hands wrung over her.
Her nobles were brighter than snow, more dazzling than milk; their bodies were more ruddy than corals; their form was sapphire.
Their appearance is darker than soot; they are not recognised in the streets. Their skin has shrivelled on their bones; it has become dry as wood.
Better were those slain by the sword than those slain by hunger, who wasted away, pierced through, for lack of the produce of the field.
The hands of compassionate women have boiled their own children; they became their food in the brokenness of the daughter of my people.
The LORD has spent his rage; he has poured out his burning anger, and he has kindled a fire in Zion that has consumed her foundations.
The kings of the earth did not believe, nor did any inhabitant of the world, that adversary and enemy would enter the gates of Jerusalem.
It was because of the sins of her prophets and the iniquities of her priests, who shed in her midst the blood of the righteous.
They wandered blind in the streets, defiled with blood, so that no one could touch their garments.
"Away! Unclean!" people called to them; "Away, away, do not touch!" So they fled and wandered; people said among the nations, "They shall not stay here any longer."
The presence of the LORD has scattered them; he will look on them no more. They showed no regard for the priests; they showed no favour to the elders.
Our eyes still failed, looking for help that was a vapour. In our watchtower we watched for a nation that could not save.
They hunted our steps, so that we could not walk in our open squares. Our end drew near; our days were completed; for our end had come.
Our pursuers were swifter than the eagles of heaven; they hunted us down on the mountains; in the wilderness they lay in wait for us.
The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of the LORD, was captured in their pits — he of whom we said, "In his shadow we shall live among the nations."
Exult and rejoice, daughter of Edom, who dwell in the land of Uz! To you also the cup will pass; you will become drunk and strip yourself naked.
Your iniquity is finished, daughter of Zion; he will not exile you again. He will punish your iniquity, daughter of Edom; he will lay bare your sins.

lamentations_5.t: Remember, LORD, what has happened to us; look, and see our reproach.
Our inheritance has been turned over to strangers, our houses to foreigners.
We have become orphans, without a father; our mothers are like widows.
We have drunk our own water for money; our own wood comes at a price.
We are pursued at our very neck; we are weary, and we are given no rest.
We have given a hand to Egypt, and to Assyria, to have our fill of bread.
Our ancestors sinned, and they are no more; and we have borne their iniquities.
Slaves rule over us; there is no one to tear us free from their hand.
We bring in our bread at the risk of our life, because of the sword of the wilderness.
Our skin is hot as an oven, because of the scorching heat of hunger.
Women in Zion they have violated, virgins in the cities of Judah.
Princes were hung up by their hands; the faces of elders were not honoured.
Young men carry the millstone; and boys stagger under loads of wood.
The elders have ceased from the gate, the young men from their music.
The joy of our heart has ceased; our dancing has turned to mourning.
The crown has fallen from our head! Woe now to us, for we have sinned.
Because of this our heart is faint; because of these things our eyes have grown dim.
For Mount Zion lies desolate; foxes prowl over it.
You, LORD, are enthroned for ever; your throne endures to generation after generation.
Why do you forget us for ever, abandon us for so long a time?
Turn us back to yourself, LORD, and we shall return; renew our days as they were of old.
Unless you have utterly rejected us, and are angry with us beyond measure.

leviticus_1.t: The LORD called to Moses and spoke to him from the tent of meeting:
Speak to the people of Israel and say to them: When any one of you presents an offering to the LORD, you shall present your offering from the livestock, from the herd or from the flock.
If his offering is a burnt offering from the herd, he shall present an unblemished male. He shall present it at the entrance of the tent of meeting, for acceptance before the LORD.
He shall press his hand on the head of the burnt offering, and it will be accepted for him, to make atonement for him.
He shall slaughter the young bull before the LORD, and Aaron's sons the priests shall present the blood and dash the blood against the altar all around, at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
He shall skin the burnt offering and cut it into its pieces.
The sons of Aaron the priest shall put fire on the altar and arrange wood on the fire.
Aaron's sons the priests shall arrange the pieces, the head and the suet, on the wood that is on the fire on the altar.
Its entrails and its legs he shall wash with water, and the priest shall turn all of it to smoke on the altar: a burnt offering, a food offering, a soothing odour to the LORD.
If his offering for a burnt offering is from the flock, from the sheep or from the goats, he shall present an unblemished male.
He shall slaughter it on the north side of the altar before the LORD, and Aaron's sons the priests shall dash its blood against the altar all around.
He shall cut it into its pieces, with its head and its suet, and the priest shall arrange them on the wood that is on the fire on the altar.
The entrails and the legs he shall wash with water, and the priest shall present all of it and turn it to smoke on the altar. It is a burnt offering, a food offering, a soothing odour to the LORD.
If his offering to the LORD is a burnt offering from birds, he shall present his offering from turtle-doves or from young pigeons.
The priest shall present it at the altar, pinch off its head and turn it to smoke on the altar, and its blood shall be drained out against the wall of the altar.
He shall remove its craw with its feathers and throw it beside the altar on the east side, at the place of the fatty ashes.

He shall tear it apart by its wings without separating it, and the priest shall turn it to smoke on the altar, on the wood that is on the fire. It is a burnt offering, a food offering, a soothing odour to the LORD.

leviticus_2.t: When a person presents a grain offering to the LORD, his offering shall be fine flour. He shall pour oil on it and put frankincense on it.

He shall bring it to Aaron's sons the priests, and the priest shall scoop out from it a full handful of its fine flour and its oil, with all its frankincense, and turn its memorial portion to smoke on the altar: a food offering, a soothing odour to the LORD.
The remainder of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons — most holy, from the food offerings of the LORD.
When you present a grain offering baked in an oven, it shall be fine flour: unleavened loaves mixed with oil, or unleavened wafers smeared with oil.
If your offering is a grain offering on a griddle, it shall be fine flour mixed with oil, unleavened.
Crumble it into pieces and pour oil on it. It is a grain offering.
If your offering is a grain offering made in a pan, it shall be made of fine flour with oil.
You shall bring to the LORD the grain offering made from these things. It shall be presented to the priest, and he shall bring it to the altar.
The priest shall lift out from the grain offering its memorial portion and turn it to smoke on the altar: a food offering, a soothing odour to the LORD.
The remainder of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons — most holy, from the food offerings of the LORD.
No grain offering that you present to the LORD shall be made with leaven, for you shall not turn any leaven or any honey to smoke as a food offering to the LORD.
You shall present them to the LORD as an offering of first produce, but they shall not go up on the altar as a soothing odour.
You shall salt every grain offering of yours with salt. You shall not let the salt of the covenant of your God be missing from your grain offering; with all your offerings you shall present salt.
If you present a grain offering of first fruits to the LORD, you shall present fresh ears roasted in fire, groats of fresh grain, as the grain offering of your first fruits.
You shall put oil on it and place frankincense on it. It is a grain offering.
The priest shall turn its memorial portion to smoke — some of its groats and some of its oil, with all its frankincense: a food offering to the LORD.

leviticus_3.t: If his offering is a sacrifice of peace offering, and he presents it from the herd, whether male or female, he shall present it unblemished before the LORD.
He shall press his hand on the head of his offering and slaughter it at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and Aaron's sons the priests shall dash the blood against the altar all around.
From the sacrifice of peace offering he shall present a food offering to the LORD: the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat that is on the entrails,
and the two kidneys and the fat that is on them, at the loins, and the lobe on the liver, which he shall remove with the kidneys.
Aaron's sons shall turn it to smoke on the altar, on the burnt offering that is on the wood on the fire: a food offering, a soothing odour to the LORD.
If his offering for a sacrifice of peace offering to the LORD is from the flock, he shall present it unblemished, male or female.
If he presents a sheep as his offering, he shall present it before the LORD.
He shall press his hand on the head of his offering and slaughter it in front of the tent of meeting, and Aaron's sons shall dash its blood against the altar all around.

From the sacrifice of peace offering he shall present a food offering to the LORD: its fat, the whole fat tail, which he shall remove close to the backbone; and the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat that is on the entrails,
and the two kidneys and the fat that is on them, at the loins, and the lobe on the liver, which he shall remove with the kidneys.
The priest shall turn it to smoke on the altar: food of a food offering to the LORD.
If his offering is a goat, he shall present it before the LORD.
He shall press his hand on its head and slaughter it in front of the tent of meeting, and Aaron's sons shall dash its blood against the altar all around.
From it he shall present his offering, a food offering to the LORD: the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat that is on the entrails,
and the two kidneys and the fat that is on them, at the loins, and the lobe on the liver, which he shall remove with the kidneys.
The priest shall turn them to smoke on the altar: food of a food offering, a soothing odour. All fat belongs to the LORD.
This is a perpetual statute throughout your generations, in all your dwelling places: you shall eat no fat and no blood.

leviticus_4.t: The LORD spoke to Moses:
Speak to the people of Israel: When a person sins inadvertently against any of the commandments of the LORD about things that are not to be done, and does any one of them —
If it is the anointed priest who sins, bringing guilt on the people, then for the sin he has committed he shall present to the LORD an unblemished young bull as a sin offering.
He shall bring the bull to the entrance of the tent of meeting before the LORD, press his hand on the head of the bull, and slaughter the bull before the LORD.
The anointed priest shall take some of the bull's blood and bring it into the tent of meeting.
The priest shall dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle some of the blood seven times before the LORD, towards the face of the veil of the holy place.

The priest shall put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of fragrant incense that is before the LORD in the tent of meeting, and all the rest of the bull's blood he shall pour out at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
He shall lift out from it all the fat of the bull of the sin offering: the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat that is on the entrails,
and the two kidneys and the fat that is on them, at the loins, and the lobe on the liver, which he shall remove with the kidneys,
just as it is lifted out from the ox of the sacrifice of peace offering; and the priest shall turn them to smoke on the altar of burnt offering.
But the hide of the bull and all its flesh, with its head and its legs, its entrails and its dung —
he shall carry all the rest of the bull outside the camp to a clean place, where the fatty ashes are poured out, and burn it on wood in fire. It shall be burned where the fatty ashes are poured out.
If the whole congregation of Israel goes astray and the matter is hidden from the eyes of the assembly, and they do one of the things the LORD has commanded not to be done, and they become guilty —
and the sin they committed in the matter becomes known, then the assembly shall present a young bull as a sin offering and bring it in front of the tent of meeting.
The elders of the congregation shall press their hands on the head of the bull before the LORD, and the bull shall be slaughtered before the LORD.
The anointed priest shall bring some of the bull's blood into the tent of meeting.
The priest shall dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the LORD, towards the face of the veil.

He shall put some of the blood on the horns of the altar that is before the LORD in the tent of meeting, and all the rest of the blood he shall pour out at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
He shall lift out all its fat from it and turn it to smoke on the altar.
He shall do with this bull just as he did with the bull of the sin offering; so he shall do with it. The priest shall make atonement for them, and they shall be forgiven.
He shall carry the bull outside the camp and burn it as he burned the first bull. It is the sin offering of the assembly.
When a leader sins and inadvertently does one of the things the LORD his God has commanded not to be done, and becomes guilty —
or the sin he has committed is made known to him, then he shall bring as his offering an unblemished male goat.
He shall press his hand on the head of the goat and slaughter it in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered before the LORD. It is a sin offering.

The priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour out the rest of its blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering.
All its fat he shall turn to smoke on the altar, like the fat of the sacrifice of peace offering. So the priest shall make atonement for him from his sin, and he shall be forgiven.
If one of the ordinary people sins inadvertently by doing one of the things the LORD has commanded not to be done, and becomes guilty —
or the sin he has committed is made known to him, then he shall bring as his offering an unblemished female goat, for the sin he has committed.
He shall press his hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter the sin offering in the place of the burnt offering.
The priest shall take some of its blood with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour out all the rest of its blood at the base of the altar.

All its fat he shall remove, just as the fat is removed from the sacrifice of peace offering, and the priest shall turn it to smoke on the altar as a soothing odour to the LORD. So the priest shall make atonement for him, and he shall be forgiven.
If he brings a lamb as his offering for a sin offering, he shall bring an unblemished female.
He shall press his hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter it as a sin offering in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered.
The priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour out all the rest of its blood at the base of the altar.

All its fat he shall remove, just as the fat of the sheep is removed from the sacrifice of peace offering, and the priest shall turn them to smoke on the altar, on the food offerings of the LORD. So the priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he has committed, and he shall be forgiven.

leviticus_5.t: When a person sins in this way: he hears a public adjuration and he was a witness, whether he saw or came to know of it, and he does not report it, then he shall bear his iniquity.

Or if a person touches anything unclean — the carcass of an unclean wild animal, or of unclean livestock, or of an unclean swarming creature — and it is hidden from him, he is unclean and becomes guilty.
Or if he touches a human uncleanness, any uncleanness by which a person becomes unclean, and it is hidden from him, and then he comes to know of it, he becomes guilty.

Or if a person swears, speaking rashly with his lips to do harm or to do good — whatever people speak rashly in an oath — and it is hidden from him, and then he comes to know of it, he becomes guilty in one of these matters.
When he becomes guilty in one of these matters, he shall confess the sin he has committed.

He shall bring his guilt offering to the LORD for the sin he has committed: a female from the flock, a ewe lamb or a female goat, as a sin offering. So the priest shall make atonement for him from his sin.
If he cannot afford a sheep, he shall bring to the LORD as his guilt offering for the sin he has committed two turtle-doves or two young pigeons, one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering.
He shall bring them to the priest, who shall present first the one for the sin offering. He shall pinch off its head at the front of its neck but not sever it.
He shall sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering against the wall of the altar, and the rest of the blood shall be drained out at the base of the altar. It is a sin offering.
The second he shall offer as a burnt offering according to the ordinance. So the priest shall make atonement for him from the sin he has committed, and he shall be forgiven.

If he cannot afford two turtle-doves or two young pigeons, he shall bring as his offering for the sin he has committed a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a sin offering. He shall not put oil on it or place frankincense on it, for it is a sin offering.
He shall bring it to the priest, and the priest shall scoop from it a full handful as its memorial portion and turn it to smoke on the altar, on the food offerings of the LORD. It is a sin offering.
So the priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he has committed in any one of these matters, and he shall be forgiven. The rest shall belong to the priest, like the grain offering.

When a person acts unfaithfully and sins inadvertently against the holy things of the LORD, he shall bring to the LORD as his guilt offering an unblemished ram from the flock, at the valuation in silver shekels, by the sanctuary shekel.

He shall repay what he took wrongly from the holy thing, add a fifth to it, and give it to the priest. The priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering, and he shall be forgiven.
If a person sins by doing one of the things the LORD has commanded not to be done, and did not know it, he becomes guilty and shall bear his iniquity.

He shall bring to the priest an unblemished ram from the flock at the valuation, as a guilt offering. The priest shall make atonement for him for the inadvertence in which he went astray without knowing it, and he shall be forgiven.
It is a guilt offering. He is certainly guilty before the LORD.

leviticus_6.t: The LORD spoke to Moses:

When a person sins and acts unfaithfully against the LORD by deceiving a fellow Israelite about a deposit, or a pledge placed in his hand, or something taken by robbery, or by extorting from a fellow Israelite,
or if he has found lost property and lied about it and sworn falsely — in any one of all the things people do and so sin —
then when he sins and becomes guilty, he shall return what he took by robbery, or what he obtained by extortion, or the deposit entrusted to him, or the lost property he found,
or anything about which he swore falsely. He shall repay it in full and add a fifth to it, and give it to its owner on the day he is found guilty.
He shall bring to the LORD his guilt offering: an unblemished ram from the flock, at the valuation, as a guilt offering, to the priest.
The priest shall make atonement for him before the LORD, and he shall be forgiven for any one of the things a person may do and so become guilty.
The LORD spoke to Moses:

Command Aaron and his sons: This is the law for the burnt offering. The burnt offering shall stay on the hearth on the altar all night until morning, and the fire of the altar shall be kept burning on it.

The priest shall put on his linen garment and linen undergarments over his body, and lift up the fatty ashes to which the fire has consumed the burnt offering on the altar, and put them beside the altar.
Then he shall take off his garments, put on other garments, and carry the fatty ashes outside the camp to a clean place.

The fire on the altar shall be kept burning on it; it shall not go out. Morning by morning the priest shall kindle wood on it, arrange the burnt offering on it, and turn to smoke on it the fats of the peace offerings.
A fire shall be kept burning continually on the altar; it shall not go out.
This is the law for the grain offering. Aaron's sons shall present it before the LORD, in front of the altar.

He shall lift out from it with his handful some of the fine flour of the grain offering and some of its oil, and all the frankincense that is on the grain offering, and turn it to smoke on the altar: a soothing odour, its memorial portion, to the LORD.
Aaron and his sons shall eat the remainder of it. It shall be eaten unleavened, in a holy place; they shall eat it in the courtyard of the tent of meeting.
It shall not be baked with leaven. I have given it as their share from my food offerings. It is most holy, like the sin offering and like the guilt offering.
Every male among Aaron's sons shall eat it — a perpetual due throughout your generations from the food offerings of the LORD. Whatever touches them shall become holy.
The LORD spoke to Moses:

This is the offering that Aaron and his sons shall present to the LORD on the day he is anointed: a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a regular grain offering, half of it in the morning and half of it in the evening.
It shall be made on a griddle with oil; you shall bring it well mixed. You shall present it baked in pieces, a grain offering of crumbs, a soothing odour to the LORD.
The anointed priest who succeeds him from among his sons shall make it. It is a perpetual due to the LORD; it shall be turned entirely to smoke as a whole offering.
Every grain offering of a priest shall be a whole offering; it shall not be eaten.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
Speak to Aaron and his sons: This is the law for the sin offering. The sin offering shall be slaughtered before the LORD in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered. It is most holy.
The priest who offers it as a sin offering shall eat it. It shall be eaten in a holy place, in the courtyard of the tent of meeting.
Whatever touches its flesh shall become holy; and if any of its blood is sprinkled on a garment, you shall wash what it was sprinkled on in a holy place.
An earthenware vessel in which it was boiled shall be broken; and if it was boiled in a bronze vessel, that shall be scoured and rinsed with water.
Every male among the priests shall eat it. It is most holy.
But any sin offering some of whose blood is brought into the tent of meeting to make atonement in the holy place shall not be eaten; it shall be burned in the fire.

leviticus_7.t: This is the law for the guilt offering. It is most holy.
The guilt offering shall be slaughtered in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, and its blood shall be dashed against the altar all around.
All its fat he shall present from it: the fat tail and the fat that covers the entrails,
and the two kidneys and the fat that is on them, at the loins, and the lobe on the liver, which he shall remove with the kidneys.
The priest shall turn them to smoke on the altar as a food offering to the LORD. It is a guilt offering.
Every male among the priests shall eat it. It shall be eaten in a holy place. It is most holy.
The guilt offering is like the sin offering: one law applies to both. It shall belong to the priest who makes atonement with it.
The priest who presents anyone's burnt offering shall have the hide of the burnt offering he presented; it shall belong to him.
Every grain offering baked in an oven, and everything made in a pan or on a griddle, shall belong to the priest who presents it.
Every grain offering mixed with oil, or dry, shall belong to all Aaron's sons alike, each like his brother.
This is the law for the sacrifice of peace offering that a person presents to the LORD.

If he presents it for thanksgiving, then with the sacrifice of thanksgiving he shall present unleavened loaves mixed with oil, unleavened wafers smeared with oil, and loaves of well-mixed fine flour mixed with oil.
With loaves of leavened bread he shall present his offering, along with his thanksgiving sacrifice of peace offering.
From each kind of offering he shall present one as a contribution to the LORD; it shall belong to the priest who dashes the blood of the peace offerings.
The meat of his thanksgiving sacrifice of peace offering shall be eaten on the day it is offered; he shall leave none of it until morning.
If the sacrifice of his offering is a vow or a freewill offering, it shall be eaten on the day he presents his sacrifice, and what remains of it may be eaten the next day.
What remains of the meat of the sacrifice on the third day shall be burned in the fire.

If any of the meat of his sacrifice of peace offering is eaten at all on the third day, it shall not be accepted. It shall not be credited to the one who presented it; it shall be tainted, and the person who eats of it shall bear his iniquity.
Meat that touches anything unclean shall not be eaten; it shall be burned in the fire. As for the meat, anyone who is clean may eat it.
But the person who eats meat from the sacrifice of peace offering that belongs to the LORD while his uncleanness is on him shall be cut off from his kin.

If a person touches anything unclean — a human uncleanness, unclean livestock, or any unclean detestable creature — and then eats meat from the sacrifice of peace offering that belongs to the LORD, that person shall be cut off from his kin.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
Speak to the people of Israel: You shall eat no fat of ox or sheep or goat.
The fat of a carcass and the fat of an animal torn by beasts may be put to any use, but you shall certainly not eat it.
Anyone who eats the fat of an animal from which a food offering is presented to the LORD shall be cut off from his kin.
You shall eat no blood in any of your dwelling places, whether of bird or of livestock.
Any person who eats blood of any kind shall be cut off from his kin.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
Speak to the people of Israel: Whoever presents his sacrifice of peace offering to the LORD shall bring his offering to the LORD from that sacrifice of peace offering.
With his own hands he shall bring the food offerings of the LORD: he shall bring the fat with the breast, the breast to be waved as a wave offering before the LORD.
The priest shall turn the fat to smoke on the altar, and the breast shall belong to Aaron and his sons.
You shall give the right thigh to the priest as a contribution from your sacrifices of peace offerings.
The one among Aaron's sons who presents the blood of the peace offerings and the fat shall have the right thigh as his portion.

For I have taken from the people of Israel, from their sacrifices of peace offerings, the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution, and I have given them to Aaron the priest and his sons as a perpetual due from the people of Israel.
This is the anointing portion of Aaron and of his sons from the food offerings of the LORD, from the day they were presented to serve as priests to the LORD,
which the LORD commanded to be given to them by the people of Israel on the day he anointed them — a perpetual statute throughout their generations.
This is the law for the burnt offering, the grain offering, the sin offering, the guilt offering, the ordination offering, and the sacrifice of peace offering,
which the LORD commanded Moses on Mount Sinai, on the day he commanded the people of Israel to present their offerings to the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai.

leviticus_8.t: The LORD spoke to Moses:
Take Aaron and his sons with him, the garments, the anointing oil, the bull of the sin offering, the two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread,
and assemble the whole congregation at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
Moses did just as the LORD commanded him, and the congregation assembled at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
Moses said to the congregation: This is what the LORD has commanded to be done.
Moses brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water.
He put the tunic on him, girded him with the sash, clothed him with the robe, put the ephod on him, girded him with the waistband of the ephod, and bound it on him with it.
He placed the breastpiece on him and put the Urim and the Thummim into the breastpiece.
He placed the turban on his head and set on the turban, at the front, the gold plate, the holy crown, just as the LORD commanded Moses.
Moses took the anointing oil, anointed the tabernacle and everything in it, and set them apart as holy.
He sprinkled some of it on the altar seven times, and anointed the altar and all its articles, and the washbasin and its stand, to set them apart as holy.
He poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron's head and anointed him, to set him apart as holy.
Moses brought Aaron's sons forward, clothed them with tunics, girded them with sashes, and bound headdresses on them, just as the LORD commanded Moses.
He brought forward the bull of the sin offering, and Aaron and his sons pressed their hands on the head of the bull of the sin offering.

It was slaughtered, and Moses took the blood and with his finger put it on the horns of the altar all around, and purified the altar from sin. He poured the blood at the base of the altar and set it apart as holy, to make atonement for it.
He took all the fat that was on the entrails, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys and their fat, and Moses turned them to smoke on the altar.
The bull, with its hide, its flesh and its dung, he burned in the fire outside the camp, just as the LORD commanded Moses.
He brought forward the ram of the burnt offering, and Aaron and his sons pressed their hands on the head of the ram.
It was slaughtered, and Moses dashed the blood against the altar all around.
He cut the ram into its pieces, and Moses turned the head, the pieces and the suet to smoke.

He washed the entrails and the legs with water, and Moses turned the whole ram to smoke on the altar. It was a burnt offering, a soothing odour; it was a food offering to the LORD, just as the LORD commanded Moses.
He brought forward the second ram, the ram of the ordination offering, and Aaron and his sons pressed their hands on the head of the ram.
It was slaughtered, and Moses took some of its blood and put it on the lobe of Aaron's right ear, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.

He brought Aaron's sons forward, and Moses put some of the blood on the lobes of their right ears, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. Then Moses dashed the blood against the altar all around.
He took the fat, the fat tail, all the fat that was on the entrails, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys with their fat, and the right thigh.
From the basket of unleavened bread that was before the LORD he took one unleavened loaf, one loaf of oiled bread and one wafer, and placed them on the fat portions and on the right thigh.
He put all of it on the palms of Aaron and on the palms of his sons, and waved them as a wave offering before the LORD.
Then Moses took them from their palms and turned them to smoke on the altar, on the burnt offering. They were an ordination offering, a soothing odour; it was a food offering to the LORD.
Moses took the breast and waved it as a wave offering before the LORD. From the ram of the ordination offering it was Moses' portion, just as the LORD commanded Moses.

Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood that was on the altar and sprinkled it on Aaron and his garments, and on his sons and his sons' garments with him. So he set apart as holy Aaron and his garments, and his sons and his sons' garments with him.

Moses said to Aaron and his sons: Boil the meat at the entrance of the tent of meeting and eat it there, with the bread that is in the basket of the ordination offering, as I commanded: Aaron and his sons shall eat it.
What remains of the meat and the bread you shall burn in the fire.
You shall not go out from the entrance of the tent of meeting for seven days, until the day your days of ordination are completed; for seven days he shall ordain you.
As has been done this day, the LORD has commanded to be done, to make atonement for you.
You shall stay at the entrance of the tent of meeting day and night for seven days and keep the charge of the LORD, so that you do not die; for so I have been commanded.
Aaron and his sons did everything the LORD commanded through Moses.

leviticus_9.t: On the eighth day Moses summoned Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel.
He said to Aaron: Take for yourself a young bull calf for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering, both unblemished, and present them before the LORD.
And to the people of Israel you shall say: Take a male goat for a sin offering, and a calf and a lamb, both a year old and unblemished, for a burnt offering,
and an ox and a ram for peace offerings, to sacrifice before the LORD, and a grain offering mixed with oil; for today the LORD is appearing to you.
They took what Moses had commanded to the front of the tent of meeting, and the whole congregation drew near and stood before the LORD.
Moses said: This is what the LORD has commanded you to do, so that the glory of the LORD may appear to you.

Moses said to Aaron: Draw near to the altar, offer your sin offering and your burnt offering, and make atonement for yourself and for the people; then offer the people's offering and make atonement for them, just as the LORD commanded.
Aaron drew near to the altar and slaughtered the calf of the sin offering that was for himself.
Aaron's sons brought the blood to him, and he dipped his finger in the blood and put it on the horns of the altar; and he poured the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
The fat, the kidneys and the lobe of the liver from the sin offering he turned to smoke on the altar, just as the LORD commanded Moses.
The flesh and the hide he burned in the fire outside the camp.
He slaughtered the burnt offering, and Aaron's sons handed him the blood, and he dashed it against the altar all around.
They handed him the burnt offering in its pieces, and the head, and he turned them to smoke on the altar.
He washed the entrails and the legs and turned them to smoke on the burnt offering on the altar.
Then he presented the people's offering. He took the goat of the sin offering that was for the people, slaughtered it, and offered it as a sin offering like the first one.
He presented the burnt offering and offered it according to the ordinance.
He presented the grain offering, filled his palm from it, and turned it to smoke on the altar, in addition to the morning burnt offering.
He slaughtered the ox and the ram, the people's sacrifice of peace offering, and Aaron's sons handed him the blood, and he dashed it against the altar all around.
As for the fat portions from the ox and from the ram: the fat tail, the covering fat, the kidneys and the lobe of the liver —
they placed the fat portions on the breasts, and he turned the fat portions to smoke on the altar.
Aaron waved the breasts and the right thigh as a wave offering before the LORD, just as Moses commanded.
Aaron lifted his hands towards the people and blessed them. Then he came down from making the sin offering, the burnt offering and the peace offerings.
Moses and Aaron went into the tent of meeting. When they came out they blessed the people, and the glory of the LORD appeared to all the people.
Fire went out from before the LORD and consumed the burnt offering and the fat portions on the altar. All the people saw it, and they shouted and fell on their faces.

leviticus_10.t: Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, each took his censer, put fire in them, placed incense on it, and presented before the LORD unauthorised fire, which he had not commanded them.
Fire went out from before the LORD and consumed them, and they died before the LORD.
Moses said to Aaron: This is what the LORD spoke: 'Among those near me I will show myself holy, and before all the people I will be honoured.' And Aaron was silent.
Moses summoned Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Uzziel, Aaron's uncle, and said to them: Come forward, carry your kinsmen away from the front of the holy place, outside the camp.
They came forward and carried them in their tunics outside the camp, just as Moses had said.

Moses said to Aaron and to Eleazar and Ithamar his sons: Do not let your heads go loose and do not tear your garments, so that you do not die and he does not become angry with the whole congregation. But your kinsmen, all the house of Israel, may weep for the burning that the LORD has burned.
You shall not go out from the entrance of the tent of meeting, or you will die, for the LORD's anointing oil is on you. And they did as Moses said.
The LORD spoke to Aaron:
You and your sons with you shall not drink wine or strong drink when you come into the tent of meeting, so that you do not die. This is a perpetual statute throughout your generations,
so that you may separate between the holy and the common, and between the unclean and the clean,
and teach the people of Israel all the statutes that the LORD has spoken to them through Moses.

Moses spoke to Aaron and to Eleazar and Ithamar, his remaining sons: Take the grain offering that is left from the food offerings of the LORD and eat it unleavened beside the altar, for it is most holy.
You shall eat it in a holy place, for it is your due and your sons' due from the food offerings of the LORD; for so I have been commanded.

The breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution you shall eat in a clean place, you and your sons and your daughters with you; for they are given as your due and your sons' due from the sacrifices of peace offerings of the people of Israel.

They shall bring the thigh of the contribution and the breast of the wave offering with the food offerings of the fat portions, to be waved as a wave offering before the LORD. It shall belong to you and to your sons with you as a perpetual due, just as the LORD commanded.
Moses searched and searched for the goat of the sin offering, and there it was — burned. He was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron's remaining sons, and said:
Why did you not eat the sin offering in the holy place? For it is most holy, and he gave it to you to bear the iniquity of the congregation, to make atonement for them before the LORD.
Look, its blood was not brought inside the holy place. You should certainly have eaten it in the holy place, as I commanded.

Aaron said to Moses: Look, today they presented their sin offering and their burnt offering before the LORD, and such things as these have befallen me. Had I eaten a sin offering today, would it have been good in the eyes of the LORD?
Moses heard this, and it was good in his eyes.

leviticus_11.t: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron:
Speak to the people of Israel: These are the creatures you may eat from among all the animals on the land.
Any animal that has a divided hoof, cleft right through, and chews the cud, you may eat.
But of those that chew the cud or have a divided hoof, you shall not eat these: the camel, for it chews the cud but does not have a divided hoof — it is unclean for you;
and the rock hyrax, for it chews the cud but does not have a divided hoof — it is unclean for you;
and the hare, for it chews the cud but does not have a divided hoof — it is unclean for you;
and the pig, for it has a divided hoof, cleft right through, but does not chew the cud — it is unclean for you.
You shall not eat their meat, and you shall not touch their carcasses. They are unclean for you.
Of all that is in the waters you may eat these: anything with fins and scales in the waters, in the seas and in the wadis, you may eat.
But everything in the seas and the wadis that has no fins and scales, among all the swarming creatures of the waters and all the living creatures in the waters, is detestable to you.
They shall be detestable to you: you shall not eat their flesh, and you shall treat their carcasses as detestable.
Anything in the waters that has no fins and scales is detestable to you.
And these you shall treat as detestable among the birds; they shall not be eaten, for they are detestable: the eagle, the bearded vulture, the black vulture,
the kite, the falcon of every kind,
every kind of raven,
the ostrich, the screech owl, the gull, the hawk of every kind,
the little owl, the cormorant, the great owl,
the white owl, the desert owl, the carrion vulture,
the stork, the heron of every kind, the hoopoe, and the bat.
Every winged swarming creature that goes on four legs is detestable to you.
But of all the winged swarming creatures that go on four legs, you may eat these: those that have jointed legs above their feet, for hopping with them on the ground.
Of these you may eat: the locust of every kind, the bald locust of every kind, the cricket of every kind, and the grasshopper of every kind.
But every other winged swarming creature that has four feet is detestable to you.
By these you become unclean: whoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening,
and whoever carries any of their carcasses shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening.
Every animal that has a divided hoof but is not cleft right through, or does not chew the cud, is unclean for you. Whoever touches them shall be unclean.
Everything that goes on its paws, among all the creatures that go on four feet, is unclean for you. Whoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening,
and whoever carries their carcasses shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening. They are unclean for you.
These are unclean for you among the swarming creatures that swarm on the ground: the choled, the mouse, the tsav of every kind,
the gecko, the monitor lizard, the lizard, the skink, and the chameleon.
These are unclean for you among all the swarming creatures. Whoever touches them when they are dead shall be unclean until evening.

Anything on which one of them falls when dead shall be unclean: any wooden vessel, garment, hide or sacking, any vessel with which work is done. It shall be put into water and be unclean until evening, and then it shall be clean.
If one of them falls into any earthenware vessel, everything in it shall be unclean, and you shall break the vessel.
Any food that may be eaten on which such water has come shall be unclean, and any drink that may be drunk from any such vessel shall be unclean.
Anything on which part of their carcass falls shall be unclean. An oven or a stove shall be broken down; they are unclean, and they shall remain unclean for you.
But a spring or a cistern, a gathering of water, shall remain clean; yet whoever touches their carcass in it shall be unclean.
If part of their carcass falls on any seed for sowing that is to be sown, it remains clean.
But if water has been put on the seed and part of their carcass falls on it, it is unclean for you.
If an animal that you may eat dies, whoever touches its carcass shall be unclean until evening.
Whoever eats of its carcass shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening, and whoever carries its carcass shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening.
Every swarming creature that swarms on the ground is detestable; it shall not be eaten.

Anything that goes on its belly, anything that goes on four feet, and anything with many feet, among all the swarming creatures that swarm on the ground — you shall not eat them, for they are detestable.
Do not make yourselves detestable by any swarming creature that swarms, and do not make yourselves unclean by them, and so become unclean through them.
For I am the LORD your God. You shall set yourselves apart as holy and be holy, for I am holy. You shall not make yourselves unclean by any swarming creature that creeps on the ground.
For I am the LORD who brought you up from the land of Egypt to be your God. You shall be holy, for I am holy.
This is the law concerning livestock and birds and every living creature that moves in the waters and every creature that swarms on the ground,
to separate between the unclean and the clean, and between the creature that may be eaten and the creature that may not be eaten.

leviticus_12.t: Speak to the people of Israel: When a woman conceives and bears a male, she shall be unclean for seven days, as in the days of her menstrual impurity.
On the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised.
Then for thirty-three days she shall remain in the blood of her cleansing. She shall not touch any holy thing and shall not enter the sanctuary until the days of her cleansing are completed.
If she bears a female, she shall be unclean for two weeks, as in her menstrual impurity; and for sixty-six days she shall remain upon the blood of her cleansing.

When the days of her cleansing are completed, whether for a son or for a daughter, she shall bring a year-old lamb for a burnt offering and a young pigeon or a turtle-dove for a sin offering, to the entrance of the tent of meeting, to the priest.

The priest shall present it before the LORD and make atonement for her, and she shall be clean from the flow of her blood. This is the law for the woman who gives birth, whether to a male or to a female.

If she cannot afford a sheep, she shall take two turtle-doves or two young pigeons, one for a burnt offering and one for a sin offering. The priest shall make atonement for her, and she shall be clean.

leviticus_13.t: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron:

When a person has on the skin of his body a swelling, a rash or a bright spot, and it becomes on the skin of his body an affliction of leprosy, he shall be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons the priests.

The priest shall examine the affliction on the skin of the body. If the hair in the affliction has turned white and the affliction appears deeper than the skin of the body, it is an affliction of leprosy; the priest shall examine him and pronounce him unclean.

But if it is a white bright spot on the skin of his body, and it does not appear deeper than the skin, and its hair has not turned white, the priest shall shut the afflicted person away for seven days.
The priest shall examine him on the seventh day. If the affliction has stayed as it was in his sight and has not spread in the skin, the priest shall shut him away for a second seven days.

The priest shall examine him again on the seventh day. If the affliction has faded and has not spread in the skin, the priest shall pronounce him clean. It is a rash; he shall wash his garments and be clean.
But if the rash spreads further in the skin after he has shown himself to the priest for his cleansing, he shall show himself to the priest a second time.
The priest shall examine him, and if the rash has spread in the skin, the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is leprosy.
When an affliction of leprosy is on a person, he shall be brought to the priest.
The priest shall examine him. If there is a white swelling in the skin that has turned the hair white, and there is a raw spot of living flesh in the swelling,
it is a long-standing leprosy in the skin of his body, and the priest shall pronounce him unclean. He shall not shut him away, for he is unclean.
But if the leprosy breaks out all over the skin, and covers all the skin of the afflicted person from head to foot, as far as the priest can see,
then the priest shall examine him, and if the leprosy has covered his whole body, he shall pronounce the afflicted person clean. All of it has turned white; he is clean.
But on the day living flesh appears on him he shall be unclean.
The priest shall examine the living flesh and pronounce him unclean. The living flesh is unclean; it is leprosy.
Or if the living flesh changes back and turns white, he shall come to the priest.
The priest shall examine him, and if the affliction has turned white, the priest shall pronounce the afflicted person clean. He is clean.
When there is a boil on someone's skin and it heals,
and in the place of the boil there is a white swelling or a reddish-white bright spot, he shall show himself to the priest.

The priest shall examine it, and if it appears lower than the skin and its hair has turned white, the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is an affliction of leprosy that has broken out in the boil.
But if the priest examines it and there is no white hair in it, and it is not lower than the skin, and it is faded, the priest shall shut him away for seven days.
If it spreads further in the skin, the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is an affliction.
But if the bright spot stays in its place and has not spread, it is the scar of the boil, and the priest shall pronounce him clean.
Or when there is a burn from fire on someone's skin, and the raw spot of the burn becomes a reddish-white or white bright spot,

then the priest shall examine it. If the hair has turned white in the bright spot and it appears deeper than the skin, it is leprosy that has broken out in the burn. The priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is an affliction of leprosy.
But if the priest examines it and there is no white hair in the bright spot, and it is not lower than the skin, and it is faded, the priest shall shut him away for seven days.
The priest shall examine him on the seventh day. If it has spread further in the skin, the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is an affliction of leprosy.
But if the bright spot stays in its place and has not spread in the skin, and it is faded, it is the swelling of the burn, and the priest shall pronounce him clean, for it is the scar of the burn.
When a man or a woman has an affliction on the head or in the beard,

then the priest shall examine the affliction. If it appears deeper than the skin and there is thin yellow hair in it, the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is a scall; it is leprosy of the head or the beard.

But when the priest examines the affliction of the scall and it does not appear deeper than the skin, and there is no black hair in it, the priest shall shut the person with the scall away for seven days.
The priest shall examine the affliction on the seventh day. If the scall has not spread, there is no yellow hair in it, and it does not appear deeper than the skin,
he shall shave himself, but shall not shave the scall; and the priest shall shut the scall away for a second seven days.

The priest shall examine the scall on the seventh day. If it has not spread in the skin and does not appear deeper than the skin, the priest shall pronounce him clean; he shall wash his garments and be clean.
But if the scall spreads further in the skin after his cleansing,
then the priest shall examine him, and if the scall has spread in the skin, the priest need not look for the yellow hair. He is unclean.
But if in his sight the scall has stayed as it was and black hair has grown in it, the scall has healed. He is clean, and the priest shall pronounce him clean.
When a man or a woman has bright spots on the skin of the body, white bright spots,
then the priest shall examine them. If the bright spots on the skin of the body are a faded white, it is a harmless rash that has broken out on the skin. The person is clean.
When a man's head loses its hair, he is bald; he is clean.
If his head loses its hair at the front, towards his face, he is bald at the forehead; he is clean.
But if there is a reddish-white affliction on the bald patch or the bald forehead, it is leprosy breaking out on his bald patch or his bald forehead.
The priest shall examine him. If the swelling of the affliction on his bald patch or bald forehead is reddish-white, like the appearance of leprosy of the skin of the body,
he is a man with leprosy; he is unclean. The priest shall certainly pronounce him unclean; his affliction is on his head.
The person with leprosy, on whom the affliction is, shall have his garments torn and his head let loose; he shall cover his upper lip and call out, Unclean! Unclean!
As long as the affliction is on him he shall be unclean. He is unclean. He shall live alone; his dwelling shall be outside the camp.
When there is an affliction of leprosy on a garment, whether a woollen garment or a linen garment,
or in the warp or the weft of linen or wool, or in a hide or anything made of hide,
and the affliction is greenish or reddish in the garment, the hide, the warp, the weft, or anything made of hide, it is an affliction of leprosy and shall be shown to the priest.
The priest shall examine the affliction and shut it away for seven days.

He shall examine the affliction on the seventh day. If it has spread in the garment, the warp, the weft or the hide, in whatever the hide is made into for use, the affliction is a persistent leprosy. It is unclean.
He shall burn the garment, or the warp or weft of wool or linen, or any article of hide in which the affliction is, for it is a persistent leprosy. It shall be burned in the fire.
But if the priest examines it and the affliction has not spread in the garment, the warp, the weft or anything made of hide,
then the priest shall give orders, and they shall wash the thing that has the affliction in it, and he shall shut it away for a second seven days.

The priest shall examine it after the affliction has been washed, and if the affliction has not changed its appearance and has not spread, it is unclean. You shall burn it in the fire. It is a pitting, on its back or on its front.
But if the priest examines it and the affliction has faded after it was washed, he shall tear it out of the garment, the hide, the warp or the weft.
If it appears again in the garment, the warp, the weft or anything made of hide, it is breaking out. You shall burn in the fire the thing that has the affliction in it.
The garment, warp, weft or any article of hide that you wash, from which the affliction departs, shall be washed a second time and be clean.
This is the law for an affliction of leprosy in a woollen or linen garment, in the warp or the weft, or in any article of hide, to pronounce it clean or unclean.

leviticus_14.t: The LORD spoke to Moses:
This shall be the law for the person with leprosy on the day of his cleansing: he shall be brought to the priest,
and the priest shall go outside the camp and examine him. If the affliction of leprosy has healed in the person who had leprosy,
then the priest shall give orders, and two live clean birds, cedar wood, scarlet and hyssop shall be taken for the person being cleansed.
The priest shall give orders, and one of the birds shall be slaughtered into an earthenware vessel over living water.
He shall take the live bird, with the cedar wood, the scarlet and the hyssop, and dip them and the live bird in the blood of the bird that was slaughtered over the living water.
He shall sprinkle it seven times on the person being cleansed from the leprosy, pronounce him clean, and let the live bird go over the open field.

The person being cleansed shall wash his garments, shave off all his hair, and bathe in water, and he shall be clean. After that he may come into the camp, but he shall stay outside his tent for seven days.

On the seventh day he shall shave off all his hair — his head, his beard and his eyebrows; all his hair he shall shave off. He shall wash his garments and bathe his body in water, and he shall be clean.
On the eighth day he shall take two unblemished male lambs, one unblemished year-old ewe lamb, three tenths of fine flour as a grain offering mixed with oil, and one log of oil.
The priest who pronounces him clean shall station the person being cleansed, together with these offerings, before the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
The priest shall take one of the lambs and present it as a guilt offering, with the log of oil, and wave them as a wave offering before the LORD.
He shall slaughter the lamb in the holy place, where the sin offering and the burnt offering are slaughtered; for like the sin offering, the guilt offering belongs to the priest. It is most holy.

The priest shall take some of the blood of the guilt offering and put it on the lobe of the right ear of the person being cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand and on the big toe of his right foot.
The priest shall take some of the log of oil and pour it into his own left palm.
The priest shall dip his right finger in the oil that is on his left palm and sprinkle some of the oil with his finger seven times before the LORD.

From the rest of the oil on his palm the priest shall put some on the lobe of the right ear of the person being cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand and on the big toe of his right foot, on top of the blood of the guilt offering.
What is left of the oil on the priest's palm he shall put on the head of the person being cleansed. So the priest shall make atonement for him before the LORD.
The priest shall offer the sin offering and make atonement for the person being cleansed from his uncleanness. Afterwards he shall slaughter the burnt offering.
The priest shall offer up the burnt offering and the grain offering on the altar. So the priest shall make atonement for him, and he shall be clean.

But if he is poor and cannot afford this, he shall take one lamb as a guilt offering to be waved, to make atonement for him, one tenth of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, and a log of oil,
and two turtle-doves or two young pigeons, whichever he can afford; one shall be a sin offering and the other a burnt offering.
He shall bring them on the eighth day for his cleansing to the priest, at the entrance of the tent of meeting, before the LORD.
The priest shall take the lamb of the guilt offering and the log of oil and wave them as a wave offering before the LORD.

He shall slaughter the lamb of the guilt offering, and the priest shall take some of the blood of the guilt offering and put it on the lobe of the right ear of the person being cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand and on the big toe of his right foot.
The priest shall pour some of the oil into his own left palm.
The priest shall sprinkle with his right finger some of the oil on his left palm, seven times before the LORD.

The priest shall put some of the oil on his palm on the lobe of the right ear of the person being cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand and on the big toe of his right foot, on the place where the blood of the guilt offering was put.
What is left of the oil on the priest's palm he shall put on the head of the person being cleansed, to make atonement for him before the LORD.
He shall offer one of the turtle-doves or young pigeons, whichever he can afford,
whatever he can afford: one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, with the grain offering. So the priest shall make atonement for the person being cleansed before the LORD.
This is the law for a person who has an affliction of leprosy and cannot afford the usual offerings for his cleansing.
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron:
When you come into the land of Canaan, which I am giving you as a possession, and I put an affliction of leprosy in a house in the land you possess,
then the owner of the house shall come and tell the priest: Something like an affliction has appeared to me in the house.

The priest shall give orders that the house be cleared before he comes to examine the affliction, so that everything in the house does not become unclean; after that the priest shall come to examine the house.
He shall examine the affliction. If the affliction in the walls of the house consists of greenish or reddish hollows that appear lower than the wall,
then the priest shall go out of the house to its entrance and shut the house away for seven days.
The priest shall return on the seventh day and examine it. If the affliction has spread in the walls of the house,
then the priest shall give orders, and they shall tear out the stones that have the affliction in them and throw them outside the city, to an unclean place.
He shall have the house scraped inside all around, and they shall pour out the plaster dust they have scraped off outside the city, to an unclean place.
They shall take other stones and put them in place of the first stones, and he shall take other plaster and plaster the house.
But if the affliction returns and breaks out in the house after the stones have been torn out, the house scraped and plastered,
then the priest shall come and examine it, and if the affliction has spread in the house, it is a persistent leprosy in the house. It is unclean.
He shall pull down the house — its stones, its timbers and all its plaster — and carry them outside the city, to an unclean place.
Whoever goes into the house during the days it is shut up shall be unclean until evening.
Whoever lies down in the house shall wash his garments, and whoever eats in the house shall wash his garments.
But if the priest comes and examines it and the affliction has not spread in the house after the house was plastered, the priest shall pronounce the house clean, for the affliction has healed.
To purify the house from sin he shall take two birds, cedar wood, scarlet and hyssop.
He shall slaughter one of the birds into an earthenware vessel over living water.
He shall take the cedar wood, the hyssop, the scarlet and the live bird, dip them in the blood of the slaughtered bird and in the living water, and sprinkle the house seven times.
So he shall purify the house from sin with the blood of the bird, the living water, the live bird, the cedar wood, the hyssop and the scarlet.
He shall let the live bird go outside the city, over the open field, and make atonement for the house, and it shall be clean.
This is the law for every affliction of leprosy, for the scall,
for the leprosy of a garment and of a house,
for the swelling, the rash and the bright spot,
to give a ruling on the day something is unclean and on the day it is clean. This is the law for leprosy.

leviticus_15.t: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron:
Speak to the people of Israel and say to them: When any man has a discharge from his body, his discharge is unclean.
This is how his discharge makes him unclean: whether his body runs with the discharge or is blocked by it, he is unclean.
Any bed the man with the discharge lies on becomes unclean, and anything he sits on becomes unclean.
Anyone who touches his bed must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Whoever sits on anything the man with the discharge has sat on must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Whoever touches the body of the man with the discharge must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
If the man with the discharge spits on someone who is clean, that person must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Any saddle the man with the discharge rides on becomes unclean.
Anyone who touches anything that was under him will be unclean until evening, and anyone who carries such things must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Anyone whom the man with the discharge touches without having rinsed his hands in water must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
A clay vessel the man with the discharge touches must be broken, and any wooden vessel must be rinsed in water.
When the man with the discharge becomes clean of his discharge, he is to count off seven days for his cleansing, wash his clothes, and bathe his body in fresh running water; then he will be clean.
On the eighth day he is to take two turtle-doves or two young pigeons, come before the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and give them to the priest.
The priest is to offer them, one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering, and so make atonement for him before the LORD for his discharge.
When a man has an emission of semen, he must bathe his whole body in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Any garment or leather on which there is semen must be washed in water, and it will be unclean until evening.
When a man lies with a woman and there is an emission of semen, both of them must bathe in water, and they will be unclean until evening.
When a woman has a discharge, and the discharge from her body is blood, she will be in her menstrual impurity for seven days, and anyone who touches her will be unclean until evening.
Anything she lies on during her menstrual impurity becomes unclean, and anything she sits on becomes unclean.
Anyone who touches her bed must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Anyone who touches anything she has sat on must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
