If it is on the bed or on whatever she was sitting on, whoever touches it will be unclean until evening.
If a man does lie with her and her menstrual impurity comes upon him, he will be unclean for seven days, and any bed he lies on becomes unclean.

When a woman has a flow of blood for many days outside the time of her menstrual impurity, or when the flow continues beyond it, then for as long as her unclean discharge lasts she will be as she is in the days of her menstrual impurity: she is unclean.
Any bed she lies on throughout her discharge will be for her like the bed of her menstrual impurity, and anything she sits on will be unclean, like the uncleanness of her menstrual impurity.
Anyone who touches them will be unclean; he must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
When she becomes clean of her discharge, she is to count off seven days, and after that she will be clean.
On the eighth day she is to take two turtle-doves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
The priest is to offer one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering, and so make atonement for her before the LORD for her unclean discharge.
You are to keep the people of Israel separate from their uncleanness, so that they do not die in it by defiling my tabernacle, which is among them.
This is the law concerning the man with a discharge, and the man who has an emission of semen and is made unclean by it;
and concerning the woman who is ailing in her menstrual impurity, and anyone with a discharge, male or female, and a man who lies with an unclean woman.

leviticus_16.t: The LORD spoke to Moses after the death of Aaron's two sons, when they drew near before the LORD and died.

The LORD said to Moses: Tell Aaron your brother that he is not to come at just any time into the holy place inside the veil, before the mercy seat that is on the ark, or he will die; for I appear in the cloud over the mercy seat.
This is how Aaron is to come into the holy place: with a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.

He is to wear a holy linen tunic, with linen undergarments on his body; he is to be girded with a linen sash and wound with a linen turban. These are holy garments; he must bathe his body in water and then put them on.
From the congregation of the people of Israel he is to take two male goats for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering.
Aaron is to present the bull of the sin offering that is his own and make atonement for himself and for his household.
He is to take the two goats and set them before the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
Aaron is to cast lots over the two goats: one lot for the LORD and one lot for Azazel.
Aaron is to present the goat on which the lot for the LORD fell, and offer it as a sin offering.
But the goat on which the lot for Azazel fell is to be set alive before the LORD, to make atonement over it, and then to be sent away to Azazel into the wilderness.
Aaron is to present the bull of the sin offering that is his own and make atonement for himself and for his household, and he is to slaughter the bull of the sin offering that is his own.
He is to take a censer full of burning coals from the altar before the LORD, and two handfuls of finely ground fragrant incense, and bring them inside the veil.
He is to put the incense on the fire before the LORD, so that the cloud of incense covers the mercy seat that is over the testimony, and he will not die.

He is to take some of the blood of the bull and sprinkle it with his finger on the front of the mercy seat, on the east side; and in front of the mercy seat he is to sprinkle some of the blood seven times with his finger.

Then he is to slaughter the goat of the sin offering that is for the people, bring its blood inside the veil, and do with its blood as he did with the blood of the bull: sprinkle it on the mercy seat and in front of the mercy seat.

So he is to make atonement for the holy place because of the uncleannesses of the people of Israel and their transgressions, for all their sins; and he is to do the same for the tent of meeting, which dwells with them in the midst of their uncleannesses.

No one is to be in the tent of meeting from the time he goes in to make atonement in the holy place until he comes out. So he makes atonement for himself, for his household, and for the whole assembly of Israel.

Then he is to go out to the altar that is before the LORD and make atonement on it: he is to take some of the blood of the bull and some of the blood of the goat and put it on the horns of the altar all around.
He is to sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times, and so cleanse it and set it apart as holy from the uncleannesses of the people of Israel.
When he has finished making atonement for the holy place, the tent of meeting, and the altar, he is to present the living goat.

Aaron is to press both his hands on the head of the living goat and confess over it all the iniquities of the people of Israel and all their transgressions, for all their sins, putting them on the head of the goat; and he is to send it away into the wilderness by the hand of a man standing ready.
The goat will carry on itself all their iniquities to a solitary place, and the man is to release the goat in the wilderness.
Then Aaron is to go into the tent of meeting, take off the linen garments he wore when he went into the holy place, and leave them there.

He is to bathe his body in water in a holy place and put on his own garments; then he is to come out and offer his burnt offering and the burnt offering of the people, making atonement for himself and for the people.
He is to turn the fat of the sin offering to smoke on the altar.
The man who releases the goat to Azazel must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and after that he may come into the camp.

The bull of the sin offering and the goat of the sin offering, whose blood was brought in to make atonement in the holy place, are to be taken outside the camp, and their hides, their flesh, and their offal are to be burned with fire.
The man who burns them must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and after that he may come into the camp.

This is to be a perpetual statute for you: in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, you are to afflict yourselves and do no work at all — the native-born and the foreigner who lives among you.
For on this day atonement will be made for you, to cleanse you; you will be clean before the LORD from all your sins.
It is a sabbath of complete rest for you, and you are to afflict yourselves. This is a perpetual statute.
The priest who is anointed and ordained to serve as priest in place of his father is to make atonement, wearing the linen garments, the holy garments.
He is to make atonement for the holy sanctuary; he is to make atonement for the tent of meeting and for the altar; and he is to make atonement for the priests and for all the people of the assembly.
This is to be a perpetual statute for you: atonement is to be made for the people of Israel once a year, for all their sins. And he did just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

leviticus_17.t: Speak to Aaron and his sons and to all the people of Israel and say to them: This is what the LORD has commanded:
Any man of the house of Israel who slaughters an ox or a sheep or a goat inside the camp, or slaughters it outside the camp,

and does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to present it as an offering to the LORD before the tabernacle of the LORD — bloodguilt is to be reckoned to that man: he has shed blood, and that man is to be cut off from among his people.

This is so that the people of Israel will bring the sacrifices they are now sacrificing out in the open field — that they will bring them to the LORD, to the entrance of the tent of meeting, to the priest, and sacrifice them as sacrifices of peace offerings to the LORD.
The priest is to dash the blood on the altar of the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting and turn the fat to smoke as a soothing odour to the LORD.
They are no longer to sacrifice their sacrifices to the goat-demons after which they prostitute themselves. This is to be a perpetual statute for them throughout their generations.
Say to them: Any man of the house of Israel, or of the foreigners living among them, who offers up a burnt offering or a sacrifice,
and does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to offer it to the LORD, that man is to be cut off from his kin.

If any man of the house of Israel, or any foreigner living among them, eats any blood, I will set my face against the person who eats the blood, and I will cut that person off from among their people.
For the life of the flesh is in the blood, and I myself have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for your souls; for it is the blood that makes atonement by the life.
That is why I have said to the people of Israel: No one among you is to eat blood, and no foreigner living among you is to eat blood.
Any man of the people of Israel, or any foreigner living among them, who hunts and catches an animal or a bird that may be eaten must pour out its blood and cover it with earth.

For the life of all flesh is its blood; its blood is its life. So I have said to the people of Israel: You are not to eat the blood of any flesh, for the life of all flesh is its blood. Anyone who eats it is to be cut off.

Anyone who eats an animal that died of itself or one torn by beasts, whether native-born or foreigner, must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening; then he will be clean.
But if he does not wash them and does not bathe his body, he will bear his iniquity.

leviticus_18.t: The LORD spoke to Moses:
Speak to the people of Israel and say to them: I am the LORD your God.
You are not to do as they do in the land of Egypt, where you lived; and you are not to do as they do in the land of Canaan, where I am bringing you; and you are not to walk by their statutes.
You are to do my judgements and keep my statutes, walking in them. I am the LORD your God.
You are to keep my statutes and my judgements; anyone who does them will live by them. I am the LORD.
None of you is to draw near to any close relative to uncover their nakedness. I am the LORD.
You are not to uncover the nakedness of your father, which is the nakedness of your mother. She is your mother; you are not to uncover her nakedness.
You are not to uncover the nakedness of your father's wife; it is your father's nakedness.
You are not to uncover the nakedness of your sister, whether your father's daughter or your mother's daughter, born at home or born elsewhere.
You are not to uncover the nakedness of your son's daughter or your daughter's daughter, for they are your own nakedness.
You are not to uncover the nakedness of the daughter of your father's wife, born to your father; she is your sister.
You are not to uncover the nakedness of your father's sister; she is your father's close relative.
You are not to uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister, for she is your mother's close relative.
You are not to uncover the nakedness of your father's brother by drawing near to his wife; she is your aunt.
You are not to uncover the nakedness of your daughter-in-law; she is your son's wife. You are not to uncover her nakedness.
You are not to uncover the nakedness of your brother's wife; it is your brother's nakedness.
You are not to uncover the nakedness of a woman and her daughter, nor take her son's daughter or her daughter's daughter to uncover her nakedness; they are close relatives. It is depravity.
You are not to take a woman as a rival to her sister, uncovering her nakedness while her sister is still alive.
You are not to draw near to a woman in the menstrual impurity of her uncleanness to uncover her nakedness.
You are not to have intercourse with your neighbour's wife, becoming unclean by her.
You are not to give any of your offspring to be offered to Molech, and you are not to profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.
You are not to lie with a male as one lies with a woman; it is an abomination.
You are not to have intercourse with any animal, becoming unclean by it. And a woman is not to present herself to an animal to mate with it; it is a perversion.
Do not make yourselves unclean by any of these things, for by all of these the nations I am driving out before you have made themselves unclean.
The land became unclean, and I brought its iniquity upon it, and the land vomited out its inhabitants.
But you are to keep my statutes and my judgements and do none of these abominations — neither the native-born nor the foreigner living among you.
For the people of the land who were before you did all these abominations, and the land became unclean.
Then the land will not vomit you out when you make it unclean, as it vomited out the nation that was before you.
For anyone who does any of these abominations — those who do them are to be cut off from among their people.
You are to keep my charge, not doing any of the abominable customs that were done before you, and you are not to make yourselves unclean by them. I am the LORD your God.

leviticus_19.t: The LORD spoke to Moses:
Speak to the whole congregation of the people of Israel and say to them: You are to be holy, for I, the LORD your God, am holy.
Each of you is to revere his mother and his father, and you are to keep my sabbaths. I am the LORD your God.
Do not turn to worthless idols, and do not make gods of cast metal for yourselves. I am the LORD your God.
When you sacrifice a sacrifice of peace offering to the LORD, sacrifice it so that it is accepted for you.
It is to be eaten on the day you sacrifice it and on the next day; whatever remains until the third day must be burned with fire.
If it is eaten at all on the third day, it is tainted and will not be accepted.
Whoever eats it will bear his iniquity, for he has profaned what is holy to the LORD, and that person is to be cut off from his kin.
When you reap the harvest of your land, you are not to reap right to the edge of your field, and you are not to gather the gleanings of your harvest.
You are not to strip your vineyard bare or gather its fallen grapes. Leave them for the poor and for the foreigner. I am the LORD your God.
You are not to steal, you are not to deceive, and you are not to deal falsely with one another.
You are not to swear falsely by my name and so profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.
You are not to oppress your neighbour or rob him. The wages of a hired worker are not to stay with you overnight until morning.
You are not to curse a deaf person or put a stumbling block before a blind person; you are to fear your God. I am the LORD.
You are not to do injustice in judgement. You are not to show partiality to the poor or defer to the great. Judge your neighbour with righteousness.
You are not to go about as a slanderer among your kin. You are not to stand on the blood of your neighbour. I am the LORD.
You are not to hate your brother in your heart. Reprove your neighbour openly, so that you do not incur sin because of him.
You are not to take vengeance or bear a grudge against the members of your people; and you are to love your neighbour as yourself. I am the LORD.
You are to keep my statutes. You are not to breed your livestock with another kind, or sow your field with two kinds of seed, or put on a garment of two kinds of material.

If a man has intercourse with a woman who is a slave-woman designated for another man, and she has not been redeemed and freedom has not been given her, there is to be punishment. They are not to be put to death, because she was not free.
He is to bring his guilt offering to the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting: a ram as a guilt offering.
The priest is to make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering before the LORD, for the sin he has committed, and he will be forgiven the sin he has committed.
When you come into the land and plant any tree for food, you are to treat its fruit as forbidden: for three years it is to be forbidden to you and not eaten.
In the fourth year all its fruit is to be holy, an offering of praise to the LORD.
In the fifth year you may eat its fruit, so that its yield may increase for you. I am the LORD your God.
You are not to eat over the blood. You are not to practise divination or soothsaying.
You are not to round off the edge of your hair at the sides of your head, and you are not to spoil the edge of your beard.
You are not to make gashes in your flesh for the dead, and you are not to put tattoo marks on yourselves. I am the LORD.
Do not profane your daughter by making her a prostitute, or the land will prostitute itself and be filled with depravity.
You are to keep my sabbaths and revere my sanctuary. I am the LORD.
Do not turn to mediums or seek out spiritists, and so be made unclean by them. I am the LORD your God.
You are to rise before the grey-headed and honour the presence of an old person, and you are to fear your God. I am the LORD.
When a foreigner lives with you in your land, you are not to wrong him.
The foreigner living with you is to be to you as one native-born among you, and you are to love him as yourself, for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
You are not to do injustice in judgement, in measures of length, weight, or volume.
You are to have honest balances, honest weights, an honest ephah, and an honest hin. I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
You are to keep all my statutes and all my judgements and do them. I am the LORD.

leviticus_20.t: The LORD spoke to Moses:

Say to the people of Israel: Any man of the people of Israel, or any foreigner living in Israel, who gives any of his offspring to Molech is to be put to death; the people of the land are to stone him with stones.
I myself will set my face against that man and cut him off from among his people, because he has given of his offspring to Molech, to make my sanctuary unclean and to profane my holy name.
And if the people of the land do close their eyes to that man when he gives of his offspring to Molech, and do not put him to death,

then I myself will set my face against that man and against his clan, and I will cut off from among their people both him and all who prostitute themselves after him by prostituting themselves after Molech.
As for the person who turns to mediums and spiritists, prostituting himself after them, I will set my face against that person and cut him off from among his people.
Set yourselves apart as holy and be holy, for I am the LORD your God.
You are to keep my statutes and do them. I am the LORD, who sets you apart as holy.
Anyone who curses his father or his mother is to be put to death. He has cursed his father and his mother; his blood is on him.
If a man commits adultery with another man's wife — commits adultery with the wife of his neighbour — both the adulterer and the adulteress are to be put to death.
A man who lies with his father's wife has uncovered his father's nakedness. Both of them are to be put to death; their blood is on them.
If a man lies with his daughter-in-law, both of them are to be put to death. They have committed a perversion; their blood is on them.
If a man lies with a male as one lies with a woman, both of them have done an abomination. They are to be put to death; their blood is on them.
If a man takes a woman and her mother, it is depravity. He and they are to be burned with fire, so that there is no depravity among you.
A man who has intercourse with an animal is to be put to death, and you are to kill the animal.
If a woman draws near to any animal to mate with it, you are to kill the woman and the animal. They are to be put to death; their blood is on them.

If a man takes his sister, his father's daughter or his mother's daughter, and sees her nakedness and she sees his, it is a disgrace. They are to be cut off before the eyes of the members of their people. He has uncovered his sister's nakedness; he will bear his iniquity.

If a man lies with a woman while she is ailing and uncovers her nakedness, he has laid bare her spring and she has uncovered the spring of her blood; both of them are to be cut off from among their people.
You are not to uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister or your father's sister, for that lays bare one's own close relative; they will bear their iniquity.
A man who lies with his aunt has uncovered his uncle's nakedness. They will bear their sin; they will die childless.
If a man takes his brother's wife, it is impurity. He has uncovered his brother's nakedness; they will be childless.
You are to keep all my statutes and all my judgements and do them, so that the land into which I am bringing you to live does not vomit you out.
You are not to walk by the statutes of the nation I am driving out before you, for they did all these things, and I came to loathe them.

And I said to you: You will take possession of their soil, and I myself will give it to you to possess — a land flowing with milk and honey. I am the LORD your God, who has separated you from the peoples.

You are to separate the clean animal from the unclean and the unclean bird from the clean, and you are not to make yourselves detestable by any animal or bird or anything that crawls on the ground, which I have set apart for you as unclean.
You are to be holy to me, for I, the LORD, am holy, and I have separated you from the peoples to be mine.
A man or a woman who is a medium or a spiritist is to be put to death. They are to be stoned with stones; their blood is on them.

leviticus_21.t: The LORD said to Moses: Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and say to them: A priest is not to make himself unclean for a dead person among his kin,
except for his closest relatives: his mother, his father, his son, his daughter, or his brother,
and for his virgin sister, who is close to him and has not belonged to a husband — for her he may make himself unclean.
He is not to make himself unclean as a husband among his kin, profaning himself.
They are not to shave a bald patch on their heads, or shave off the edges of their beards, or make cuts in their flesh.
They are to be holy to their God and not profane the name of their God, for they are the ones who present the food offerings of the LORD, the food of their God; and they are to be holy.
They are not to take a woman profaned by prostitution, and they are not to take a woman divorced from her husband, for the priest is holy to his God.
You are to set him apart as holy, for he presents the food of your God. He is to be holy to you, for I, the LORD who sets you apart as holy, am holy.
If the daughter of a priest profanes herself by prostituting herself, she is profaning her father; she is to be burned with fire.
The priest who is greatest among his brothers, on whose head the anointing oil has been poured and who has been ordained to wear the garments, is not to let his hair hang loose or tear his garments.
He is not to go near any dead body; he is not to make himself unclean even for his father or his mother.
He is not to go out of the sanctuary or profane the sanctuary of his God, for the consecration of his God's anointing oil is upon him. I am the LORD.
He is to take a wife in her virginity.
He is not to take a widow, a divorced woman, a woman who has been profaned, or a prostitute; he is to take a virgin from his own kin as his wife.
He is not to profane his offspring among his kin, for I am the LORD, who sets him apart as holy.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
Speak to Aaron: None of your offspring throughout their generations who has a blemish is to draw near to present the food of his God.
No man with a blemish is to draw near: no one blind or lame, no one with a disfigured face or a limb too long,
no one with a broken foot or a broken hand,
no hunchback or dwarf, no one with a defect in his eye, an itching disease or scabs, or crushed testicles.
No man of the offspring of Aaron the priest who has a blemish is to come near to present the food offerings of the LORD. He has a blemish; he is not to come near to present the food of his God.
He may eat the food of his God, both from the holiest of the holy things and from the holy things.
But he is not to come to the veil or come near the altar, for he has a blemish; he is not to profane my sanctuaries, for I am the LORD, who sets them apart as holy.
So Moses spoke to Aaron and his sons and to all the people of Israel.

leviticus_22.t: The LORD spoke to Moses:
Speak to Aaron and his sons, that they keep themselves separate from the holy things the people of Israel set apart as holy to me, and not profane my holy name. I am the LORD.

Say to them: Throughout your generations, if any man of your offspring draws near to the holy things that the people of Israel set apart as holy to the LORD while his uncleanness is on him, that person is to be cut off from before me. I am the LORD.

No man of Aaron's offspring who has leprosy or has a discharge may eat of the holy things until he is clean. The same applies to anyone who touches something made unclean by a corpse, or a man who has an emission of semen,
or anyone who touches a swarming creature by which he becomes unclean, or a person by whom he becomes unclean, whatever the uncleanness may be:
The person who touches such a thing will be unclean until evening, and he is not to eat of the holy things unless he has bathed his body in water.
When the sun goes down he will be clean, and afterwards he may eat of the holy things, for they are his food.
He is not to eat an animal that died of itself or one torn by beasts, and so become unclean by it. I am the LORD.
They are to keep my charge, so that they do not bear sin on account of it and die by it, having profaned it. I am the LORD, who sets them apart as holy.
No outsider is to eat a holy thing. A priest's resident or hired worker is not to eat a holy thing.
But if a priest buys a person with his money, that person may eat of it, and those born in his household may eat of his food.
If a priest's daughter is married to a man who is an outsider, she is not to eat of the contribution of the holy things.
But if a priest's daughter becomes a widow or is divorced and has no children, and returns to her father's house as in her youth, she may eat of her father's food; no outsider is to eat of it.
If anyone eats a holy thing inadvertently, he is to add a fifth to it and give the holy thing to the priest.
They are not to profane the holy things that the people of Israel set aside for the LORD,
and so make them bear the iniquity of guilt by eating their holy things; for I am the LORD, who sets them apart as holy.
The LORD spoke to Moses:

Speak to Aaron and his sons and to all the people of Israel and say to them: When any man of the house of Israel, or any foreigner in Israel, presents his offering for any of their vows or freewill offerings that they present to the LORD as a burnt offering,
it must be, for your acceptance, an unblemished male from the cattle, the sheep, or the goats.
You are not to present anything with a blemish in it, for it will not be accepted for you.

When anyone presents a sacrifice of peace offering to the LORD, to fulfil a vow or as a freewill offering, from the herd or from the flock, it must be unblemished to be accepted; there is to be no blemish at all in it.

You are not to present to the LORD an animal that is blind, or injured, or mutilated, or has a running sore, an itch, or scabs; you are not to place any food offering from such animals on the altar to the LORD.
You may offer an ox or a sheep with a limb too long or too short as a freewill offering, but it will not be accepted for a vow.
You are not to present to the LORD an animal whose testicles are bruised, crushed, torn, or cut; and you are not to do this in your land.
You are not to present the food of your God from any such animals obtained from a foreigner, for they are corrupted and blemished; they will not be accepted for you.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
When an ox or a sheep or a goat is born, it is to stay seven days with its mother; from the eighth day onwards it will be accepted as an offering, a food offering to the LORD.
You are not to slaughter an ox or a sheep and its young on the same day.
When you sacrifice a thanksgiving sacrifice to the LORD, sacrifice it so that it is accepted for you.
It is to be eaten on that same day; you are not to leave any of it until morning. I am the LORD.
You are to keep my commandments and do them. I am the LORD.
You are not to profane my holy name, and I will be set apart as holy among the people of Israel. I am the LORD, who sets you apart as holy,
who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be God for you. I am the LORD.

leviticus_23.t: The LORD spoke to Moses:
Speak to the people of Israel and say to them: These are the appointed times of the LORD, which you are to proclaim as holy convocations; these are my appointed times.
Work is to be done for six days, but the seventh day is a sabbath of complete rest, a holy convocation. You are to do no work at all; it is a sabbath to the LORD in all your dwelling places.
These are the appointed times of the LORD, holy convocations, which you are to proclaim at their appointed time.
In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, at twilight, is a passover to the LORD.
On the fifteenth day of that month is the festival of unleavened bread to the LORD; for seven days you are to eat unleavened bread.
On the first day you are to hold a holy convocation; you are to do no occupational work.
For seven days you are to present a food offering to the LORD. On the seventh day there is a holy convocation; you are to do no occupational work.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
Speak to the people of Israel and say to them: When you come into the land I am giving you and reap its harvest, you are to bring the sheaf of the first of your harvest to the priest.
He is to wave the sheaf before the LORD so that it is accepted for you; the priest is to wave it on the day after the sabbath.
On the day you wave the sheaf you are to offer an unblemished year-old lamb as a burnt offering to the LORD,
with its grain offering of two tenths of fine flour mixed with oil, a food offering to the LORD, a soothing odour; and its drink offering of wine, a quarter of a hin.

You are not to eat bread, roasted grain, or fresh grain until that very day, until you have brought the offering of your God. This is a perpetual statute throughout your generations, in all your dwelling places.
You are to count off from the day after the sabbath, from the day you brought the sheaf of the wave offering: seven complete weeks.
You are to count fifty days, up to the day after the seventh week, and then present a new grain offering to the LORD.
From your dwelling places you are to bring two loaves of bread as a wave offering, made of two tenths of fine flour and baked with leaven, as first-fruits to the LORD.

With the bread you are to present seven unblemished year-old lambs, one young bull, and two rams. They will be a burnt offering to the LORD, with their grain offering and their drink offerings, a food offering, a soothing odour to the LORD.
You are to offer one male goat as a sin offering and two year-old lambs as a sacrifice of peace offering.
The priest is to wave them, with the bread of the first-fruits and the two lambs, as a wave offering before the LORD. They will be holy to the LORD, for the priest.
On that very day you are to make a proclamation: you are to hold a holy convocation and do no occupational work. This is a perpetual statute in all your dwelling places, throughout your generations.

When you reap the harvest of your land, you are not to reap right to the edge of your field, and you are not to gather the gleanings of your harvest. Leave them for the poor and for the foreigner. I am the LORD your God.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
Speak to the people of Israel: In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you are to have a day of rest, a memorial of the blowing of trumpets, a holy convocation.
You are to do no occupational work, and you are to present a food offering to the LORD.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
The tenth day of this seventh month is the day of atonement. It is to be a holy convocation for you; you are to afflict yourselves and present a food offering to the LORD.
You are to do no work at all on that very day, for it is a day of atonement, to make atonement for you before the LORD your God.
Anyone who is not afflicted on that very day is to be cut off from his kin.
And I will destroy from among his people anyone who does any work at all on that very day.
You are to do no work at all. This is a perpetual statute throughout your generations, in all your dwelling places.
It is a sabbath of complete rest for you, and you are to afflict yourselves. From the evening of the ninth day of the month, from evening to evening, you are to keep your sabbath.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
Speak to the people of Israel: On the fifteenth day of this seventh month is the festival of booths, seven days to the LORD.
On the first day there is a holy convocation; you are to do no occupational work.

For seven days you are to present a food offering to the LORD. On the eighth day you are to hold a holy convocation and present a food offering to the LORD. It is a solemn assembly; you are to do no occupational work.

These are the appointed times of the LORD, which you are to proclaim as holy convocations, for presenting to the LORD a food offering — burnt offering and grain offering, sacrifice and drink offerings, each on its own day —
these are in addition to the sabbaths of the LORD, and in addition to your gifts, all your vows, and all your freewill offerings that you give to the LORD.

On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you have gathered in the produce of the land, you are to celebrate the festival of the LORD for seven days. The first day is a day of rest, and the eighth day is a day of rest.

On the first day you are to take for yourselves the fruit of a splendid tree, palm fronds, a branch of a leafy tree, and willows of the wadi, and you are to rejoice before the LORD your God for seven days.
You are to celebrate it as a festival to the LORD for seven days in the year. This is a perpetual statute throughout your generations; you are to celebrate it in the seventh month.
You are to live in booths for seven days; every native-born Israelite is to live in booths,
so that your generations may know that I made the people of Israel live in booths when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
So Moses declared the appointed times of the LORD to the people of Israel.

leviticus_24.t: The LORD spoke to Moses:
Command the people of Israel to bring you pure oil of beaten olives for the light, so that a lamp may be kept burning continually.
Outside the veil of the testimony, in the tent of meeting, Aaron is to tend it from evening until morning before the LORD continually. This is a perpetual statute throughout your generations.
He is to arrange the lamps on the pure lampstand before the LORD continually.
You are to take fine flour and bake twelve loaves from it, two tenths of an ephah for each loaf.
You are to set them in two rows, six to a row, on the pure table before the LORD.
You are to put pure frankincense on each row, and it will serve for the bread as a memorial portion, a food offering to the LORD.
Sabbath after sabbath he is to arrange it before the LORD continually, on behalf of the people of Israel, as a covenant of perpetuity.
It will belong to Aaron and his sons, and they are to eat it in a holy place, for it is a holy thing of holy things for him from the food offerings of the LORD — a perpetual prescribed portion.
The son of an Israelite woman, whose father was an Egyptian, went out among the people of Israel, and he and an Israelite man fought in the camp.
The son of the Israelite woman blasphemed the Name and cursed, and they brought him to Moses. His mother's name was Shelomith, daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.
They put him in custody until the decision should be made clear to them by the mouth of the LORD.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
Bring the one who cursed outside the camp; all who heard him are to press their hands on his head, and the whole congregation is to stone him.
And say to the people of Israel: Anyone who curses his God will bear his sin.
Whoever blasphemes the name of the LORD is to be put to death; the whole congregation is to stone him. The foreigner and the native-born alike: when he blasphemes the Name, he is to be put to death.
Anyone who strikes down a human life is to be put to death.
Whoever strikes down an animal is to make it good, life for life.
If anyone inflicts an injury on his neighbour, what he has done is to be done to him:
fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. As he has inflicted an injury on a person, so it is to be inflicted on him.
Whoever strikes down an animal is to make it good, and whoever strikes down a person is to be put to death.
You are to have one law: it will be the same for the foreigner as for the native-born; for I am the LORD your God.
Moses spoke to the people of Israel, and they brought the one who had cursed outside the camp and stoned him with stones. So the people of Israel did just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

leviticus_25.t: The LORD spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai:
Speak to the people of Israel and say to them: When you come into the land I am giving you, the land is to keep a sabbath to the LORD.
For six years you are to sow your field, and for six years prune your vineyard and gather its produce.
But in the seventh year the land is to have a sabbath of complete rest, a sabbath to the LORD. You are not to sow your field or prune your vineyard.
You are not to reap the grain that grows of itself or gather the grapes of your untrimmed vines. It is to be a year of rest for the land.
The sabbath of the land will provide food for you — for yourself, your male and female slaves, your hired worker, and the resident who lives with you,
and for your livestock and the wild animals in your land; all its produce is to be for food.
You are to count off seven weeks of years, seven times seven years, so that the period of the seven weeks of years amounts to forty-nine years.
Then, in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month — on the day of atonement — you are to sound a ram's horn loudly; you are to sound the ram's horn throughout all your land.

You are to set the fiftieth year apart as holy and proclaim a release throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It is to be a jubilee for you: each of you is to return to his holding, and each of you to his clan.
The fiftieth year is to be a jubilee for you. You are not to sow, or reap what grows of itself, or gather from the untrimmed vines.
For it is a jubilee; it is to be holy for you. You are to eat its produce straight from the field.
In this year of jubilee each of you is to return to his holding.
When you sell something to your neighbour, or buy from your neighbour, you are not to wrong one another.
You are to buy from your neighbour according to the number of years since the jubilee, and he is to sell to you according to the number of harvest years remaining.
The more years there are, the more you are to increase the price; the fewer the years, the more you are to reduce it, for what he is selling you is a number of harvests.
You are not to wrong one another; you are to fear your God, for I am the LORD your God.
You are to carry out my statutes and keep my judgements and do them, and you will live on the land in security.
The land will yield its fruit, and you will eat your fill and live on it in security.
And if you say, What are we to eat in the seventh year, since we may not sow or gather in our produce?
then I will command my blessing for you in the sixth year, and it will produce a crop for three years.
You will sow in the eighth year and still eat from the old crop; until the ninth year, until its harvest comes in, you will eat the old crop.
The land is not to be sold beyond reclaim, for the land is mine; you are sojourners and residents with me.
Throughout the land of your holding you are to grant a right of redemption for the land.
If your brother becomes poor and sells some of his holding, his nearest kinsman-redeemer is to come and redeem what his brother has sold.
If a man has no kinsman-redeemer, but his own means suffice and he finds enough for its redemption,
he is to reckon the years since its sale, repay the balance to the man he sold it to, and return to his holding.
But if he cannot find enough to repay him, what he sold is to remain with the buyer until the year of jubilee; in the jubilee it is released, and he returns to his holding.
If a man sells a dwelling house in a walled city, his right of redemption lasts until the end of the year of its sale; his right of redemption is a full year.
If it is not redeemed before a full year is out, the house in the walled city passes in perpetuity to the buyer and his generations; it is not released in the jubilee.
But houses in villages that have no wall around them are to be reckoned with the open farmland: they carry a right of redemption, and they are released in the jubilee.
As for the cities of the Levites, the houses in the cities of their holding: the Levites have a perpetual right of redemption.
Whatever one of the Levites redeems — a house sold, and the city of his holding — is released in the jubilee, for the houses in the cities of the Levites are their holding among the people of Israel.
But the pasture land belonging to their cities is not to be sold, for it is their perpetual holding.
If your brother becomes poor and cannot support himself among you, you are to hold him up as you would a sojourner or a resident, so that he may live with you.
You are not to take interest or increase from him. Fear your God, so that your brother may live with you.
You are not to lend him your silver at interest or give him your food for increase.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be God for you.
If your brother becomes poor among you and sells himself to you, you are not to make him do the labour of a slave.
He is to be with you as a hired worker or a resident; he is to serve with you until the year of jubilee.
Then he is to go out from you, he and his children with him, and return to his clan and to the holding of his fathers.
For they are my servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt; they are not to be sold as slaves are sold.
You are not to rule over him harshly; you are to fear your God.
As for your male and female slaves: you may buy them from the nations around you.
You may also buy from the children of the residents living among you, and from their families born in your land who are with you; they will be your holding.

You may pass them on as an inheritance to your children after you, as a possession to hold; you may keep them in service for ever. But over your brothers, the people of Israel, no one is to rule harshly over his brother.
If a sojourner or resident among you prospers, and your brother becomes poor beside him and sells himself to that sojourner or resident, or to a member of a sojourner's clan,
he retains a right of redemption after he has sold himself; one of his brothers may redeem him.
His uncle or his uncle's son may redeem him, or any close relative from his clan may redeem him; or if he prospers, he may redeem himself.

He is to reckon with his buyer from the year he sold himself to him until the year of jubilee; the price of his sale is to be set by the number of years, reckoned as the days of a hired worker with him.
If many years remain, he is to repay for his redemption a proportionate part of the price of his purchase.
If few years remain until the year of jubilee, he is to reckon accordingly and repay for his redemption in proportion to those years.
He is to be with him as a worker hired year by year, and his employer is not to rule over him harshly in your sight.
If he is not redeemed by any of these means, he is to be released in the year of jubilee, he and his children with him.
For the people of Israel are servants to me; they are my servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.

leviticus_26.t: You are not to make worthless idols for yourselves, or raise up a carved image or a standing pillar, or set a figured stone in your land to bow down on it; for I am the LORD your God.
You are to keep my sabbaths and revere my sanctuary. I am the LORD.
If you walk by my statutes and keep my commandments and do them,
then I will give you your rains in their season, and the land will give its yield, and the trees of the field will give their fruit.
Your threshing will last until the grape harvest, and the grape harvest until the sowing; you will eat your bread to the full and live in security in your land.
I will give peace in the land, and you will lie down with no one to make you afraid; I will rid the land of wild beasts, and no sword will pass through your land.
You will pursue your enemies, and they will fall before you by the sword.
Five of you will pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you will pursue ten thousand; your enemies will fall before you by the sword.
I will turn towards you and make you fruitful and multiply you, and I will establish my covenant with you.
You will still be eating last year's stored grain, and you will have to clear out the old to make room for the new.
I will set my tabernacle among you, and I will not abhor you.
I will walk among you; I will be God for you, and you will be a people for me.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt so that you would no longer be slaves to them; I broke the bars of your yoke and made you walk upright.
But if you do not listen to me and do not carry out all these commandments,
if you reject my statutes and abhor my judgements, so that you do not carry out all my commandments and you break my covenant,

then I in turn will do this to you: I will bring on you sudden terror, wasting disease and fever that consume the eyes and drain away the life; you will sow your seed for nothing, for your enemies will eat it.
I will set my face against you, and you will be struck down before your enemies; those who hate you will rule over you, and you will flee with no one pursuing you.
And if after all this you still do not listen to me, I will go on to discipline you sevenfold for your sins.
I will break the pride of your strength; I will make your heavens like iron and your land like bronze.
Your strength will be spent for nothing; your land will not give its yield, and the trees of the land will not give their fruit.
If you walk contrary to me and are unwilling to listen to me, I will add blows sevenfold, in proportion to your sins.
I will send wild beasts among you; they will bereave you of your children, cut off your livestock, and make you few, and your roads will lie desolate.
If by these things you are not disciplined by me, and you walk contrary to me,
then I in turn will walk contrary to you, and I in turn will strike you sevenfold for your sins.
I will bring a sword upon you that avenges the vengeance of the covenant; you will gather into your cities, and I will send pestilence among you, and you will be given into the hand of an enemy.
When I break your staff of bread, ten women will bake your bread in a single oven and dole it back to you by weight; you will eat and not be satisfied.
If in spite of this you do not listen to me, and you walk contrary to me,
then I will walk contrary to you in fury, and I in turn will discipline you sevenfold for your sins.
You will eat the flesh of your sons, and the flesh of your daughters you will eat.
I will destroy your high places, cut down your incense altars, and pile your corpses on the corpses of your idols; and I will abhor you.
I will make your cities a waste and lay your sanctuaries desolate, and I will not smell your soothing odours.
I myself will lay the land desolate, and your enemies who come to live in it will be appalled at it.
I will scatter you among the nations and draw a sword after you; your land will become a desolation and your cities a waste.
Then the land will make up for its sabbaths, all the days it lies desolate while you are in the land of your enemies; then the land will rest and make up for its sabbaths.
All the days it lies desolate it will rest, because it did not rest during your sabbaths while you lived on it.

As for those of you who are left, I will bring faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies; the sound of a driven leaf will chase them, and they will flee as one flees from a sword and fall with no one pursuing.
They will stumble over one another as though before a sword, with no one pursuing, and you will have no power to stand before your enemies.
You will perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies will consume you.
Those of you who are left will rot away in their iniquity in the lands of their enemies, and also in the iniquities of their fathers along with them they will rot away.
But they will confess their iniquity and the iniquity of their fathers, the unfaithfulness by which they were unfaithful to me, and also that they walked contrary to me —
— I too walked contrary to them and brought them into the land of their enemies — if then their uncircumcised heart is humbled and they make up for their iniquity,
then I will remember my covenant with Jacob, and my covenant with Isaac, and my covenant with Abraham I will remember; and I will remember the land.

The land will be forsaken by them and will make up for its sabbaths while it lies desolate without them; and they will make up for their iniquity, because — yes, because — they rejected my judgements and abhorred my statutes.
And yet even so, while they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them or abhor them so as to make an end of them and break my covenant with them; for I am the LORD their God.
For their sake I will remember the covenant of the ancestors, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations, to be God for them. I am the LORD.
These are the statutes, judgements, and laws that the LORD established between himself and the people of Israel on Mount Sinai, through Moses.

leviticus_27.t: The LORD spoke to Moses:
Speak to the people of Israel and say to them: When anyone makes a special vow to the LORD involving the valuation of persons, this is the scale.
The valuation of a male from twenty to sixty years old is to be fifty shekels of silver, by the shekel of the holy place.
If it is a female, the valuation is thirty shekels.
For ages five to twenty, the valuation is twenty shekels for a male and ten for a female.
From one month to five years, the valuation is five shekels of silver for a male and three shekels of silver for a female.
From sixty years old and up, the valuation is fifteen shekels for a male and ten for a female.
If he is too poor for the valuation, he is to be presented before the priest, and the priest is to value him; the priest is to value him according to what the one making the vow can afford.
If the vow concerns an animal of a kind that may be presented as an offering to the LORD, anything of it given to the LORD becomes holy.
He is not to replace it or exchange it, a good one for a bad or a bad one for a good; and if he does exchange one animal for another, both it and its substitute become holy.
If it is an unclean animal, of a kind that may not be presented as an offering to the LORD, he is to present the animal before the priest,
and the priest is to value it, whether good or bad; as the priest values it, so it will stand.
If he does redeem it, he is to add a fifth to the valuation.
When anyone sets apart his house as holy to the LORD, the priest is to value it, whether good or bad; as the priest values it, so it will stand.
If the one who set it apart wishes to redeem his house, he is to add a fifth of the silver of the valuation to it, and it will be his.
If anyone sets apart to the LORD part of the field of his holding, the valuation is to be according to the seed it takes: a homer of barley seed at fifty shekels of silver.
If he sets apart his field from the year of jubilee, it stands at the full valuation.
If he sets apart his field after the jubilee, the priest is to reckon the price according to the years remaining until the year of jubilee, and that amount is to be deducted from the valuation.
If the one who set the field apart does redeem it, he is to add a fifth of the silver of the valuation to it, and it will stand as his.
But if he does not redeem the field, or if he has sold the field to another man, it can no longer be redeemed.
When the field is released in the jubilee, it becomes holy to the LORD, like a field that has been devoted; it becomes the priest's holding.
If he sets apart to the LORD a field he has bought, which is not part of the field of his holding,
the priest is to reckon for him the amount of the valuation up to the year of jubilee, and he is to pay the valuation that same day as a holy thing to the LORD.
In the year of jubilee the field is to return to the one from whom it was bought, to the one whose holding of the land it is.
Every valuation is to be by the shekel of the holy place: twenty gerahs to the shekel.
But no one is to set apart a firstborn animal, which as a firstling already belongs to the LORD; whether ox or sheep, it is the LORD's.
If it is among the unclean livestock, he is to ransom it at the valuation and add a fifth; if it is not redeemed, it is to be sold at the valuation.

But nothing that a man devotes to the LORD out of all he has — whether a person, livestock, or a field of his holding — may be sold or redeemed. Everything devoted is a holy thing of holy things to the LORD.
No person who has been devoted, from among human beings, may be ransomed; he is to be put to death.
Every tithe of the land, whether from the seed of the land or the fruit of the tree, belongs to the LORD; it is holy to the LORD.
If anyone does redeem part of his tithe, he is to add a fifth to it.
Every tithe of the herd and the flock — all that passes under the shepherd's rod — the tenth is to be holy to the LORD.
He is not to inspect whether it is good or bad, and he is not to exchange it; if he does exchange it, both it and its substitute become holy and cannot be redeemed.
These are the commandments that the LORD commanded Moses for the people of Israel on Mount Sinai.

malachi_1.t: An oracle: the word of the LORD to Israel by the hand of Malachi.
I have loved you, says the LORD. But you say, 'How have you loved us?' Was Esau not Jacob's brother — declares the LORD — and yet I loved Jacob,
but Esau I hated, and I made his hill country a desolation and his inheritance a place for the jackals of the wilderness.

If Edom says, 'We have been shattered, but we will return and rebuild the ruins,' this is what the LORD of hosts says: They may build, but I will tear down; and they will be called the territory of wickedness, the people with whom the LORD is indignant for ever.
Your own eyes will see it, and you will say, 'The LORD is great beyond the border of Israel.'

A son honours his father, and a servant his master. If then I am a father, where is the honour due me? And if I am a master, where is the fear due me? — says the LORD of hosts to you, priests, who despise my name. But you say, 'How have we despised your name?'
You bring defiled food to my altar. But you say, 'How have we defiled you?' By saying that the table of the LORD is despicable.

When you bring a blind animal to sacrifice, is that not evil? When you bring a lame or a sick one, is that not evil? Present it to your governor — will he be pleased with you? Will he show you favour? — says the LORD of hosts.
And now, entreat the face of God, that he may show us favour. This has come from your own hand — will he show favour to any of you? — says the LORD of hosts.
If only one of you would shut the doors, so that you would not light my altar for nothing! I have no delight in you, says the LORD of hosts, and I will accept no offering from your hand.

For from the rising of the sun to its setting my name will be great among the nations, and in every place incense will be brought near to my name, and a pure offering; for my name will be great among the nations, says the LORD of hosts.
But you profane it by saying that the table of the Lord is defiled, and that its fruit, its food, is despicable.

And you say, 'What a weariness this is!' and you sniff at it, says the LORD of hosts. You bring what has been stolen, and the lame and the sick; and this you bring as the offering. Am I to accept that from your hand? — says the LORD.

Cursed be the deceiver who has a sound male in his flock and makes a vow, and then sacrifices a corrupted animal to the Lord. For I am a great king, says the LORD of hosts, and my name is feared among the nations.

malachi_2.t: And now this commandment is for you, priests.

If you will not listen, and if you will not take it to heart to give honour to my name, says the LORD of hosts, then I will send the curse among you and I will curse your blessings — indeed I have already cursed them, because you are not taking it to heart.
I am about to rebuke your offspring, and I will scatter dung on your faces, the dung of your festivals; and you will be carried away with it.
Then you will know that I sent this commandment to you, so that my covenant with Levi might stand, says the LORD of hosts.
My covenant with him was life and peace, and I gave them to him as fear; and he feared me and stood in awe before my name.
True law was in his mouth, and no unrighteousness was found on his lips. He walked with me in peace and in uprightness, and he turned many back from iniquity.
For the lips of a priest should keep knowledge, and people should seek law from his mouth, for he is the messenger of the LORD of hosts.
But you have turned aside from the way. You have made many stumble by your law. You have corrupted the covenant of Levi, says the LORD of hosts.
So I in turn have made you despised and low before all the people, inasmuch as you do not keep my ways but lift up faces in your law.
Do we not all have one Father? Did not one God create us? Why then do we deal treacherously with one another, profaning the covenant of our ancestors?

Judah has dealt treacherously; an abomination has been done in Israel and in Jerusalem. For Judah has profaned the holy place of the LORD, which he loves, and has married the daughter of a foreign god.
May the LORD cut off from the tents of Jacob the man who does this — whoever he may be — and the one who brings an offering to the LORD of hosts.
And this is a second thing you do: you cover the altar of the LORD with tears, with weeping and groaning, because he no longer turns towards the offering or takes it with pleasure from your hand.
But you say, 'Why?' Because the LORD has been a witness between you and the wife of your youth, against whom you have dealt treacherously, though she is your companion and the wife of your covenant.

And did he not make one, with a remnant of spirit belonging to him? And what was the one seeking? Godly offspring. So take heed in your spirit, and let no one deal treacherously against the wife of his youth.
For the one who hates and divorces, says the LORD, the God of Israel, covers his garment with violence, says the LORD of hosts. So take heed in your spirit, and do not deal treacherously.

You have wearied the LORD with your words. But you say, 'How have we wearied him?' By saying, 'Everyone who does evil is good in the eyes of the LORD, and he delights in them,' or, 'Where is the God of judgement?'

malachi_3.t: I am about to send my messenger, and he will clear a way before me. Then suddenly the Lord whom you are seeking will come to his temple, and the messenger of the covenant in whom you delight — he is coming, says the LORD of hosts.
But who can endure the day of his coming? And who can stand when he appears? For he is like a refiner's fire and like the soap of those who wash.

He will sit as one who refines and purifies silver, and he will purify the sons of Levi and purge them like gold and like silver; and they will belong to the LORD, bringing an offering in righteousness.
Then the offering of Judah and Jerusalem will be pleasing to the LORD, as in the days of old and as in former years.

Then I will draw near to you for judgement, and I will be a swift witness against the sorcerers, the adulterers, those who swear falsely, those who defraud the hired labourer of his wages, those who oppress the widow and the fatherless, and those who thrust aside the sojourner — and who do not fear me, says the LORD of hosts.
For I, the LORD, have not changed; and you, sons of Jacob, have not come to an end.
From the days of your ancestors you have turned aside from my statutes and have not kept them. Return to me, and I will return to you, says the LORD of hosts. But you say, 'How are we to return?'
Will a human being rob God? Yet you are robbing me. But you say, 'How have we robbed you?' In the tithe and the contribution.
You are cursed with the curse, and yet you are robbing me — the whole nation of you.

Bring the whole tithe into the storehouse, so that there may be food in my house. Test me in this, says the LORD of hosts: see whether I will not open the floodgates of the heavens for you and pour out blessing for you until there is no sufficiency.
I will rebuke the devourer for you, and it will not destroy the fruit of your ground; and the vine in the field will not fail to bear for you, says the LORD of hosts.
All the nations will call you blessed, for you will be a land of delight, says the LORD of hosts.
Your words have been strong against me, says the LORD. But you say, 'What have we spoken among ourselves against you?'
You have said, 'It is emptiness to serve God. What is the profit in our keeping his charge and walking in mourning before the LORD of hosts?'
And now we call the arrogant blessed. Those who do wickedness are built up; they even test God and escape.
Then those who fear the LORD spoke with one another, and the LORD paid attention and heard; and a book of remembrance was written before him, for those who fear the LORD and esteem his name.
They will be mine, says the LORD of hosts, for the day on which I make a treasured possession; and I will have compassion on them as a man has compassion on his son who serves him.
Then you will return and see the difference between the righteous and the wicked, between one who serves God and one who does not serve him.

malachi_4.t: For the day is coming, burning like a furnace, and all the arrogant and everyone who does wickedness will be stubble; the day that is coming will set them ablaze, says the LORD of hosts, so that it leaves them neither root nor branch.
But for you who fear my name the sun of righteousness will rise, with healing in its wings; and you will go out and skip about like calves from the stall.
And you will tread down the wicked, for they will be ashes under the soles of your feet on the day on which I act, says the LORD of hosts.
Remember the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded him at Horeb for all Israel — statutes and judgements.
I am about to send you Elijah the prophet, before the coming of the day of the LORD, the great and fearsome day.
And he will turn back the hearts of parents to their children and the hearts of children to their parents, so that I do not come and strike the land, devoting it to destruction.

micah_1.t: The word of the LORD that came to Micah of Moresheth in the days of Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.
Hear, O peoples, all of you; pay attention, O earth and all that fills it — and let Lord GOD be a witness against you, my Lord from his holy temple.
For look — the LORD is going out from his place; he will come down and tread on the high places of the earth.
The mountains will melt beneath him and the valleys will be split open, like wax before the fire, like water poured out down a slope.
All this is for the transgression of Jacob and for the sins of the house of Israel. What is the transgression of Jacob? Is it not Samaria? And what are the high places of Judah? Is it not Jerusalem?
And I will make Samaria a heap of ruins in the open field, a place for planting a vineyard; I will pour her stones down into the valley and lay her foundations bare.

All her carved images will be shattered, all her hire will be burned in the fire, and all her idols I will make a waste; for from a prostitute's hire she gathered them, and to a prostitute's hire they shall return.
For this I will lament and wail; I will go barefoot and naked. I will make a lament like the jackals and a mourning like the daughters of the ostrich.
For her wounds are incurable; it has come as far as Judah, it has reached the gate of my people, Jerusalem itself.
In Gath do not tell it; weeping, do not weep. In Beth Leaphrah roll yourself in dust.
Pass on your way, inhabitant of Shaphir, in nakedness and shame. The inhabitant of Zaanan has not come out. The lament of Beth Ezel will take from you its standing place.
For the inhabitant of Maroth waits in anguish for good, because calamity has come down from the LORD to the gate of Jerusalem.
Harness the chariot to the steed, inhabitant of Lachish. She was the beginning of sin for the daughter of Zion, for in you were found the transgressions of Israel.
Therefore you will give parting gifts to Moresheth Gath. The houses of Achzib will be a deceit to the kings of Israel.
Again I will bring the dispossessor upon you, inhabitant of Mareshah. The glory of Israel will come as far as Adullam.
Make yourself bald and shear yourself for the children of your delight; make your baldness as wide as the eagle's, for they have gone from you into exile.

micah_2.t: Woe to those who plan wickedness and work out evil on their beds! In the morning light they do it, because it is in the power of their hand.
They desire fields and seize them, and houses, and carry them off; they oppress a man and his household, a person and his inheritance.
Therefore thus says the LORD: Look, I am planning a calamity against this clan from which you will not remove your necks; and you will not walk haughtily, for it will be an evil time.

On that day one will take up a saying against you and wail a bitter wailing. He will say: We are utterly devastated! He exchanges the portion of my people. How he takes it away from me! He apportions our fields to an apostate.
Therefore you will have no one to cast a measuring line by lot in the assembly of the LORD.
Do not preach! — so they preach — they shall not preach of these things; reproaches will not be turned back.
Is it said, O house of Jacob: Is the spirit of the LORD short? Are these his deeds? Do my words not do good to the one who walks uprightly?
And lately my people have risen as an enemy. You strip the splendid robe from those who pass by in security, turned back from war.
The women of my people you drive out from the house of her delight; from her children you take away my glory for ever.
Arise and go, for this is not the resting place; because of uncleanness it destroys, and the destruction will be grievous.
If a man walking after wind and falsehood lied, 'I will preach to you of wine and strong drink' — he would be the preacher of this people.

I will surely gather all of you, Jacob; I will surely assemble the remnant of Israel. I will put them together like sheep in a fold, like a flock in the midst of its pasture; they will be noisy with people.
The one who breaks through has gone up before them; they have broken through and passed the gate and gone out by it. Their king has passed on before them, and the LORD at their head.

micah_3.t: And I said: Hear now, heads of Jacob and rulers of the house of Israel: Is it not for you to know justice? —
you who hate good and love evil, who tear their skin from off them and their flesh from off their bones;
who have eaten the flesh of my people, stripped their skin from off them, broken their bones in pieces, and chopped them up as into a pot, like meat in the midst of a cauldron.
Then they will cry out to the LORD and he will not answer them. He will hide his face from them at that time, because they have made their deeds evil.

Thus says the LORD concerning the prophets who lead my people astray, who bite with their teeth and proclaim peace; and whoever does not put something into their mouth — against him they consecrate a war.
Therefore it will be night for you, without vision, and darkness for you, without divining. The sun will go down on the prophets, and the day will go dark over them.
The seers will be ashamed and those who divine will be abashed; all of them will cover their upper lip, for there is no answer from God.
But I — I am filled with power, with the spirit of the LORD, and with justice and might, to declare to Jacob his transgression and to Israel his sin.
Hear this now, heads of the house of Jacob and rulers of the house of Israel, who loathe justice and make crooked everything that is straight;
who build Zion with bloodshed and Jerusalem with injustice.
Her heads judge for a bribe, her priests teach for a price, her prophets divine for money; and they lean on the LORD, saying, 'Is not the LORD in our midst? Calamity will not come upon us.'
Therefore, because of you, Zion will be ploughed as a field, Jerusalem will become heaps of ruins, and the mountain of the house, wooded high places.

micah_4.t: And it will be, in the last days, that the mountain of the house of the LORD will be established at the head of the mountains, and it will be lifted up above the hills; and peoples will stream to it.

And many nations will come and say: 'Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD and to the house of the God of Jacob, that he may teach us from his ways and that we may walk in his paths.' For from Zion law will go out, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.

And he will judge between many peoples and decide for mighty nations far away. They will beat their swords into ploughshares and their spears into pruning knives. Nation will not lift up sword against nation, and they will not learn war any more.
And they will sit, each under his own vine and under his own fig tree, and no one will make them afraid; for the mouth of the LORD of hosts has spoken.
For all the peoples walk, each in the name of his god; and we will walk in the name of the LORD our God for ever and ever.
On that day, declares the LORD, I will gather the lame and assemble the outcast, and those to whom I have done harm.
And I will make the lame into a remnant and the one driven far off into a mighty nation; and the LORD will reign over them in Mount Zion from now and for ever.
And you, O tower of the flock, hill of the daughter of Zion — to you it will come; the former dominion will come, the kingship, to the daughter of Jerusalem.
Now, why do you cry aloud? Is there no king in you? Has your counsellor perished, that anguish has seized you like a woman giving birth?

Writhe and burst forth, daughter of Zion, like a woman giving birth; for now you will go out from the town and dwell in the open country, and you will come as far as Babylon. There you will be delivered; there the LORD will redeem you from the hand of your enemies.
And now many nations have gathered against you, those who say, 'Let her be defiled, and let our eyes look on Zion.'
But they do not know the thoughts of the LORD and they do not understand his counsel; for he has gathered them like cut grain to the threshing floor.

Arise and thresh, daughter of Zion, for I will make your horn iron and your hooves bronze, and you will crush many peoples; and I will devote their unjust gain to the LORD, and their wealth to the Lord of all the earth.

micah_5.t: Now you will gash yourself, daughter of a troop. He has set a siege against us. With a rod they strike on the cheek the judge of Israel.
And you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, too little to be among the clans of Judah — from you one will come out for me to be ruler over Israel, and his goings forth are from of old, from ancient days.
Therefore he will give them up until the time when she who is in labour has given birth; and the rest of his brothers will return to the people of Israel.
And he will stand and shepherd by the strength of the LORD, by the majesty of the name of the LORD his God; and they will remain, for now he will be great to the ends of the earth.
And this one will be peace. When Assyria comes into our land and treads on our fortresses, we will raise up against it seven shepherds and eight princes of men.
And they will shepherd the land of Assyria with the sword and the land of Nimrod at its entrances; and he will deliver us from Assyria when it comes into our land and treads on our territory.
And the remnant of Jacob will be in the midst of many peoples like dew from the LORD, like showers on the grass, which does not wait for anyone and does not hope for the children of humankind.

And the remnant of Jacob will be among the nations, in the midst of many peoples, like a lion among the animals of the forest, like a young lion among flocks of sheep, which, when it passes through, tramples and tears, and there is no one to deliver.
May your hand be lifted up over your adversaries, and may all your enemies be cut off.
And it will be on that day, declares the LORD, that I will cut off your horses from your midst and destroy your chariots;
and I will cut off the cities of your land and tear down all your fortresses;
and I will cut off sorceries from your hand, and you will have no soothsayers;
and I will cut off your carved images and your pillars from your midst, and you will no longer bow down to the work of your hands;
and I will pluck up your Asherah poles from your midst, and I will destroy your cities.
And in anger and in rage I will take vengeance on the nations that have not listened.

micah_6.t: Hear now what the LORD is saying: Arise, conduct your case before the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice.
Hear, O mountains, the case of the LORD, and you enduring ones, foundations of the earth; for the LORD has a case with his people, and with Israel he will argue it out.
My people, what have I done to you, and how have I wearied you? Testify against me.
For I brought you up from the land of Egypt, and from a house of slaves I ransomed you; and I sent before you Moses, Aaron and Miriam.
My people, remember now what Balak king of Moab planned and what Balaam son of Beor answered him; from Shittim to Gilgal — so that you may know the righteous acts of the LORD.
With what shall I come before the LORD, and bow myself down to the God on high? Shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves a year old?
Will the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams, with ten thousands of torrents of oil? Shall I give my firstborn for my transgression, the fruit of my body for the sin of my being?
He has told you, O mortal, what is good, and what the LORD is requiring of you: nothing but to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God.
The voice of the LORD calls out to the city — and it is sound wisdom to fear your name — Hear, O rod, and whoever appointed it.
Are there still, in the house of the wicked, treasures of wickedness and a short ephah that is accursed?
Shall I be held innocent with wicked balances and with a bag of deceitful weights?
Her rich are full of violence and her inhabitants speak falsehood, and their tongue is deceit in their mouth.
And I also have made myself sick striking you, making you desolate for your sins.
You will eat and not be satisfied, and your emptiness will be within you; you will carry away and not bring to safety, and what you do bring to safety I will give to the sword.
You will sow and not reap; you will tread the olive and not anoint yourself with oil; and new wine, and not drink wine.

The statutes of Omri are kept, and every deed of the house of Ahab, and you have walked in their schemes — so that I make you a horror and her inhabitants a hissing; and you will bear the reproach of my people.

micah_7.t: Woe is me! For I have become like the gatherings of summer fruit, like the gleanings of the grape harvest: there is no cluster to eat, no early fig that my being craves.
The loyal has perished from the land, and there is no upright one among humankind. All of them lie in wait for blood; each hunts his brother with a net.
Both hands are on the evil, to do it well. The official asks, and the judge is for a bribe, and the great man speaks the craving of his being — he himself — and they weave it together.
The best of them is like a briar, the most upright worse than a thorn hedge. The day of your watchmen, your punishment, has come; now their confusion will come.
Do not believe in a neighbour; do not trust in a close friend. From her who lies in your bosom guard the openings of your mouth.
For a son treats a father with contempt, a daughter rises against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; a man's enemies are the people of his own household.
But I — I will watch for the LORD; I will wait for the God of my salvation. My God will hear me.
Do not rejoice over me, my enemy! Though I have fallen, I will rise. Though I sit in darkness, the LORD is a light to me.
I will bear the indignation of the LORD, for I have sinned against him, until he conducts my case and executes my judgement. He will bring me out to the light; I will look on his righteousness.
And my enemy will see, and shame will cover her — she who says to me, 'Where is the LORD your God?' My eyes will look on her; now she will be a place to be trampled, like the mud of the streets.
A day for building your walls! On that day the boundary will be extended far.
That day — and they will come to you from Assyria and the cities of Egypt, and from Egypt to the River, from sea to sea, and mountain to mountain.
And the earth will become a desolation because of its inhabitants, from the fruit of their deeds.
Shepherd your people with your rod, the flock of your inheritance, dwelling alone, a forest in the midst of a garden land. Let them graze in Bashan and Gilead as in the days of long ago.
As in the days when you came out from the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders.
Nations will see and be ashamed of all their might; they will put a hand over the mouth, their ears will go deaf.

They will lick dust like the serpent, like things that crawl on the ground. They will come trembling out of their strongholds; they will be in dread of the LORD our God, and they will be afraid of you.
Who is a God like you, lifting away iniquity and passing over transgression for the remnant of his inheritance? He does not hold on to his anger for ever, for he delights in steadfast love.
He will again have compassion on us; he will subdue our iniquities. And you will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea.
You will give faithfulness to Jacob, steadfast love to Abraham, which you swore to our ancestors from the days of long ago.

nahum_1.t: An oracle concerning Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.
