The LORD is a jealous and avenging God; avenging is the LORD, and a master of rage; avenging is the LORD toward his adversaries, and he keeps his anger toward his enemies.
The LORD is slow to anger and great in power, yet by no means clearing the guilty. The LORD — his way is in the whirlwind and in the storm, and the cloud is the dust of his feet.
He rebukes the sea and dries it up, and all the rivers he makes dry. Bashan withers, and Carmel, and the blossom of Lebanon withers.
The mountains quake because of him, and the hills melt away. The earth heaves before him, the world and all who dwell in it.
Who can stand before his indignation? And who can endure the burning of his anger? His rage is poured out like fire, and the rocks are torn down by him.
The LORD is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble, and he knows those who take refuge in him.
And with an overflowing flood he will make a complete end of her place, and he will pursue his enemies into darkness.
What are you plotting against the LORD? He is making a complete end; trouble will not rise a second time.
For while they are tangled together like thorns and soaked as with their drink, they are consumed like stubble fully dried.
From you came out one who plots evil against the LORD, a worthless counsellor.
Thus says the LORD: Though they are intact and so many, even so they will be cut down and pass away. Though I afflicted you, I will not afflict you again.
And now I will break his yoke-bar from you, and I will tear your fetters apart.

And the LORD has commanded concerning you: Your name will be sown no more. From the house of your gods I will cut off carved image and cast-metal image. I will make your grave, for you are of no weight.
Look — on the mountains, the feet of one bearing news, proclaiming peace! Keep your festivals, Judah; pay your vows, for never again will a worthless one pass through you. He is cut off, all of him.

nahum_2.t: A scatterer has come up against you. Guard the fortification, watch the road, brace your loins, make your strength very firm.
For the LORD is restoring the majesty of Jacob like the majesty of Israel, for plunderers have laid them waste and destroyed their branches.
The shield of his warriors is dyed red; men of valour are clothed in scarlet. The chariotry is like fire of metal on the day he prepares it, and the cypress spears quiver.
In the streets the chariotry drives madly; they rush about in the open squares. Their appearance is like torches; they run like lightning flashes.
He calls his nobles to mind; they stumble as they go. They hurry to her wall, and the covering is set in place.
The gates of the rivers have been opened, and the palace has melted away.
And it is settled: she was stripped, she was carried off, and her maidservants moan like the sound of doves, beating on their hearts.
And Nineveh is like a pool of water from her earliest days, and they are in flight. "Stop! Stop!" — but no one turns back.
Plunder silver! Plunder gold! There is no end to the store, an abundance of every precious article.
Emptiness and emptiness and devastation! The heart melts, the knees totter, anguish is in every set of loins, and every face of them has grown pale.
Where is the lions' den, the feeding place of the young lions, where the lion walked, and the lioness, and the lion's cub, and no one disturbed them?
The lion tore enough for his cubs and strangled for his lionesses; he filled his holes with prey and his dens with torn flesh.

Look, I am against you — declares the LORD of hosts. I will burn her chariotry in smoke, and the sword will consume your young lions. I will cut off your prey from the earth, and the voice of your messengers will be heard no more.

nahum_3.t: Woe, city of bloodshed! All of her is lies, full of plunder; the prey never leaves.
The crack of a whip, the rattle of a wheel, a galloping horse and a jolting chariot!
A horseman charging, the blade of a sword, the flash of a spear, a multitude of slain, a weight of corpses, and no end to the bodies — they stumble over their bodies.
Because of the many whorings of the prostitute, graceful and lovely, a mistress of sorceries, who sells nations by her whorings and clans by her sorceries —
Look, I am against you — declares the LORD of hosts. I will lift your hem over your face, and I will show the nations your nakedness and the kingdoms your shame.
I will throw filth on you, I will treat you with contempt, and I will make you a spectacle.
And it will be that all who see you will flee from you and say, "Nineveh is devastated! Who will grieve for her?" Where shall I look for comforters for you?
Are you better than No Amon, which sat among the canals, with waters all around her, whose rampart was the sea, her wall from the sea?
Cush was her strength, and Egypt too, without end. Put and the Libyans were among your helpers.
She too went into exile, into captivity. Her children too were dashed in pieces at the head of every street; over her honoured ones they cast lots, and all her great ones were bound in fetters.
You too will become drunk; you will go into hiding. You too will seek a stronghold from the enemy.
All your fortresses are fig trees with first-ripe fruit: if they are shaken, they fall into the mouth of the eater.
Look, your troops in your midst are women. The gates of your land stand wide open to your enemies; fire has consumed your bars.
Draw water for the siege! Strengthen your fortresses! Go into the clay and trample the mortar! Take hold of the brick mould!
There fire will consume you, the sword will cut you off, it will consume you like the young locust. Make yourself as many as the young locust! Make yourself as many as the swarming locust!
You have multiplied your traders beyond the stars of the heavens. The young locust strips the land bare and flies away.

Your courtiers are like the swarming locust, and your officials like a locust of locusts, which settle on the walls on a cold day. The sun rises and it is gone, and no one knows its place — where are they?
Your shepherds slumber, king of Assyria; your nobles lie down. Your people are scattered on the mountains, and there is no one to gather them.
There is no easing of your fracture; your wound is severe. All who hear the report of you clap their hands over you, for over whom has your evil not passed, again and again?

nehemiah_1.t: The words of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah. In the month of Kislev, in the twentieth year, while I was in Susa the citadel,
Hanani, one of my brothers, came with men from Judah; and I asked them about the Jews, the escaped remnant who had survived the captivity, and about Jerusalem.

And they said to me, 'The survivors who have survived the captivity, there in the province, are in great trouble and disgrace; and the wall of Jerusalem is broken down and its gates have been burned with fire.'
And when I heard these words I sat down and wept and mourned for days; and I was fasting and praying before the God of the heavens.
And I said: 'I beg you, LORD, God of the heavens, the great and awesome God, who keeps the covenant and the steadfast love with those who love him and keep his commandments —

let your ear be attentive and your eyes open, to hear the prayer of your servant that I am praying before you today, day and night, for the people of Israel your servants, and confessing the sins of the people of Israel that we have sinned against you. And I and the house of my father have sinned.
We have utterly acted corruptly against you, and we have not kept the commandments and the statutes and the ordinances that you commanded Moses your servant.
Remember now the word that you commanded Moses your servant, saying, "If you act unfaithfully, I will scatter you among the peoples."

"But if you return to me and keep my commandments and do them, then even if your banished ones are at the end of the heavens, from there I will gather them and bring them to the place that I have chosen to make my name dwell there."
And they are your servants and your people, whom you redeemed by your great strength and by your strong hand.

I beg you, Lord, let your ear be attentive to the prayer of your servant and to the prayer of your servants who delight to fear your name; and grant success to your servant today, and give him compassion before this man.' Now I was cupbearer to the king.

nehemiah_2.t: In the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes the king, wine was before him; and I took up the wine and gave it to the king. Now I had never been sad in his presence.
And the king said to me, 'Why is your face sad, when you are not sick? This is nothing but sadness of heart.' And I was very greatly afraid.
And I said to the king, 'Let the king live for ever! Why should my face not be sad, when the city, the house of my ancestors' tombs, lies desolate and its gates have been consumed by fire?'
And the king said to me, 'What is it that you are asking?' And I prayed to the God of the heavens,
and I said to the king, 'If it seems good to the king, and if your servant is good in your sight, send me to Judah, to the city of my ancestors' tombs, that I may build it.'
And the king said to me — the queen consort was sitting beside him — 'How long will your journey be, and when will you return?' And it seemed good to the king, and he sent me; and I gave him a time.
And I said to the king, 'If it seems good to the king, let letters be given to me for the governors of Beyond the River, so that they will let me pass through until I come to Judah;

and a letter to Asaph, keeper of the king's forest, so that he will give me wood to make beams for the gates of the citadel that belongs to the house, and for the wall of the city, and for the house that I shall go into.' And the king gave them to me, according to the good hand of my God upon me.
And I came to the governors of Beyond the River and gave them the king's letters. Now the king had sent army commanders and horsemen with me.
And when Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, heard of it, it displeased them greatly that a man had come to seek good for the people of Israel.
And I came to Jerusalem and was there three days.
And I arose by night, I and a few men with me; and I had told no one what my God was putting into my heart to do for Jerusalem. And there was no animal with me except the one I was riding.
And I went out by night by the Valley Gate, towards the Dragon's Spring and to the Dung Gate; and I was examining the walls of Jerusalem, which were broken down, and its gates consumed by fire.
And I passed on to the Spring Gate and to the King's Pool; and there was no room for the animal to pass under me.
And I went up the wadi by night, examining the wall; and I turned back and came in by the Valley Gate, and returned.
And the officials did not know where I had gone or what I was doing; and I had told nothing so far to the Jews, or the priests, or the nobles, or the officials, or the rest who were doing the work.

And I said to them, 'You see the trouble that we are in, that Jerusalem lies desolate and its gates have been burned with fire. Come, let us build the wall of Jerusalem, and let us be a reproach no longer.'

And I told them of the hand of my God, that it had been good upon me, and also the words of the king that he had spoken to me. And they said, 'Let us arise and build.' And they strengthened their hands for the good work.

And when Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, and Geshem the Arab heard of it, they mocked us and despised us and said, 'What is this thing that you are doing? Are you rebelling against the king?'
And I answered them and said, 'The God of the heavens, he will grant us success; and we his servants will arise and build. But you have no share and no right and no memorial in Jerusalem.'

nehemiah_3.t: Then Eliashib the high priest arose with his brothers the priests, and they built the Sheep Gate. They consecrated it and set up its doors; and as far as the Tower of the Hundred they consecrated it, as far as the Tower of Hananel.
And next to him the men of Jericho built; and next to him Zaccur son of Imri built.
The sons of Hassenaah built the Fish Gate; they laid its beams and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars.
And next to them Meremoth son of Uriah son of Hakkoz repaired; next to them Meshullam son of Berekiah son of Meshezabel repaired; next to them Zadok son of Baana repaired.
And next to them the Tekoites repaired; but their nobles did not put their neck to the work of their lords.
Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah repaired the Jeshanah Gate; they laid its beams and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars.
And next to them Melatiah the Gibeonite and Jadon the Meronothite repaired, the men of Gibeon and Mizpah, up to the seat of the governor of Beyond the River.
Next to him Uzziel son of Harhaiah, of the goldsmiths, repaired; and next to him Hananiah, one of the perfumers, repaired. And they restored Jerusalem as far as the Broad Wall.
And next to them Rephaiah son of Hur, official of half the district of Jerusalem, repaired.
And next to them Jedaiah son of Harumaph repaired, opposite his own house; and next to him Hattush son of Hashabneiah repaired.
Malkijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath-moab repaired a second section, and the Tower of the Ovens.
And next to him Shallum son of Hallohesh, official of half the district of Jerusalem, repaired — he and his daughters.
Hanun and the inhabitants of Zanoah repaired the Valley Gate; they built it and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars, and a thousand cubits of the wall as far as the Dung Gate.
Malkijah son of Rechab, official of the district of Beth-hakkerem, repaired the Dung Gate; he built it and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars.

Shallun son of Col-hozeh, official of the district of Mizpah, repaired the Spring Gate; he built it, roofed it, and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars; and the wall of the Pool of Shelah by the King's Garden, as far as the steps that go down from the City of David.
After him Nehemiah son of Azbuk, official of half the district of Beth-zur, repaired, as far as opposite the tombs of David, as far as the artificial pool, and as far as the house of the mighty men.
After him the Levites repaired: Rehum son of Bani. Next to him Hashabiah, official of half the district of Keilah, repaired for his district.
After him their brothers repaired: Bavvai son of Henadad, official of half the district of Keilah.
And Ezer son of Jeshua, official of Mizpah, repaired next to him a second section, opposite the ascent to the armoury, at the buttress.
After him Baruch son of Zaccai zealously repaired a second section, from the buttress to the entrance of the house of Eliashib the high priest.
After him Meremoth son of Uriah son of Hakkoz repaired a second section, from the entrance of the house of Eliashib to the end of the house of Eliashib.
And after him the priests repaired, the men of the surrounding region.
After him Benjamin and Hasshub repaired, opposite their own house. After him Azariah son of Maaseiah son of Ananiah repaired, beside his own house.
After him Binnui son of Henadad repaired a second section, from the house of Azariah to the buttress and to the corner.
Palal son of Uzai, opposite the buttress and the tower that projects from the king's upper house, which belongs to the court of the guard. After him Pedaiah son of Parosh.
And the temple servants were living on the Ophel, as far as opposite the Water Gate to the east, and the projecting tower.
After him the Tekoites repaired a second section, from opposite the great projecting tower as far as the wall of the Ophel.
Above the Horse Gate the priests repaired, each opposite his own house.
After him Zadok son of Immer repaired, opposite his own house. And after him Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, keeper of the East Gate, repaired.
After him Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph, repaired a second section. After him Meshullam son of Berekiah repaired, opposite his own chamber.
After him Malkijah, of the goldsmiths, repaired as far as the house of the temple servants and the traders, opposite the Muster Gate, and as far as the upper chamber of the corner.
And between the upper chamber of the corner and the Sheep Gate the goldsmiths and the traders repaired.

nehemiah_4.t: And when Sanballat heard that we were building the wall, he burned with anger and was very angry, and he mocked the Jews.

And he said before his brothers and the army of Samaria, 'What are these feeble Jews doing? Will they restore it for themselves? Will they sacrifice? Will they finish in a day? Will they bring the stones back to life out of the heaps of debris, when they are burned?'
And Tobiah the Ammonite was beside him, and he said, 'Even what they are building — if a fox goes up, it will break down their wall of stones.'
Hear, our God, for we have become an object of contempt; turn back their reproach on their own head, and give them up as plunder in a land of captivity.
And do not cover over their iniquity, and let their sin not be wiped out from before you; for they have provoked you to anger before the builders.
So we built the wall, and all of it was joined together to half its height; and the people had a heart to work.

And when Sanballat and Tobiah and the Arabs and the Ammonites and the Ashdodites heard that the repair of the walls of Jerusalem had gone forward, and that the broken places had begun to be closed, they burned with anger exceedingly.
And they all conspired together to come and wage war against Jerusalem, and to make confusion for it.
And we prayed to our God and stationed a guard against them day and night because of them.
And Judah said, 'The strength of the burden-bearers has failed, and the debris is too much; and we are not able to build on the wall.'
And our adversaries said, 'They will not know and they will not see, until we come into their midst and kill them and put an end to the work.'
And when the Jews who lived beside them came, they said to us ten times, 'From all the places where you turn, they will come upon us.'
So I stationed the people at the lowest parts of the site, behind the wall, in the exposed places; and I stationed the people by clans, with their swords, their spears and their bows.

And I looked, and I arose and said to the nobles and the officials and the rest of the people, 'Do not be afraid of them. Remember the Lord, the great and awesome one, and fight for your brothers, your sons and your daughters, your wives and your houses.'
And when our enemies heard that it had been made known to us, and that God had frustrated their purpose, we all returned to the wall, each to his work.
And from that day half of my young men did the work, and half of them held the spears, the shields, the bows and the body armour; and the commanders were behind all the house of Judah,
those who were building on the wall. And those who carried burdens were loaded up: with one hand each did the work, and with the other held a weapon.
And the builders each had his sword girded on his hips as he built; and the one who sounded the ram's horn was beside me.
And I said to the nobles and the officials and the rest of the people, 'The work is great and extensive, and we are spread out on the wall, far from one another.'
In whatever place you hear the sound of the ram's horn, there assemble to us. Our God will fight for us.
So we did the work, and half of them held the spears, from the break of dawn until the stars came out.
Also at that time I said to the people, 'Let each man and his young man spend the night inside Jerusalem, and they will be for us a guard by night and a workforce by day.'
And neither I nor my brothers nor my young men nor the men of the guard who followed me — none of us took off our clothes; each took his weapon even to the water.

nehemiah_5.t: Now there was a great outcry of the people and their wives against their brothers the Jews.
And there were those who were saying, 'Our sons and our daughters — we are many. Let us get grain, that we may eat and live.'
And there were those who were saying, 'We are mortgaging our fields, our vineyards and our houses to get grain in the famine.'
And there were those who were saying, 'We have borrowed money for the king's tribute on our fields and our vineyards.'

And now our flesh is like the flesh of our brothers, our children like their children; and here we are, subduing our sons and our daughters as slaves — and some of our daughters are already subdued — and there is no power in our hand, and our fields and our vineyards belong to others.
And I burned with anger exceedingly when I heard their outcry and these words.

And my heart took counsel within me, and I contended with the nobles and the officials, and said to them, 'You are exacting a loan, each man against his brother.' And I set a great assembly against them.

And I said to them, 'We ourselves have bought back our brothers the Jews who were sold to the nations, as far as we were able; and will you now sell your own brothers, so that they must be sold back to us?' And they were silent and found not a word.
And I said, 'The thing you are doing is not good. Should you not walk in the fear of our God, because of the reproach of the nations, our enemies?'
And I too, and my brothers and my young men, have been lending them money and grain. Let us abandon this loan.
Return to them this very day their fields, their vineyards, their olive trees and their houses; and the hundredth of the money, the grain, the new wine and the fresh oil that you are lending them.
And they said, 'We will return it, and we will require nothing from them. We will do just as you say.' And I summoned the priests and made them swear to act according to this word.

Also I shook out the fold of my garment and said, 'So may God shake out every man who does not carry out this word, from his house and from his property; and so may he be shaken out and empty.' And all the assembly said, 'Amen,' and they praised the LORD. And the people acted according to this word.

Also, from the day I was appointed to be their governor in the land of Judah, from the twentieth year until the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes the king — twelve years — neither I nor my brothers ate the food of the governor.

And the former governors who were before me laid a heavy burden on the people and took from them food and wine, besides forty shekels of silver; and their young men also domineered over the people. But I did not do so, because of the fear of God.
And I also kept hold of the work of this wall, and we acquired no field; and all my young men were assembled there for the work.
And the Jews and the officials, a hundred and fifty men, and those who came to us from the nations around us, were at my table.

And what was prepared for a single day was one ox and six choice sheep, and birds were prepared for me; and every ten days, all kinds of wine in abundance. And with all this I did not ask for the food of the governor, because the service lay heavy on this people.
Remember for me, my God, for good, all that I have done for this people.

nehemiah_6.t: And when Sanballat and Tobiah and Geshem the Arab and the rest of our enemies heard that I had built the wall and that no breach was left in it — though up to that time I had not set up the doors in the gates —
Sanballat and Geshem sent to me, saying, 'Come, let us meet together in Hakkephirim, in the plain of Ono.' But they were planning to do me harm.
And I sent messengers to them, saying, 'I am doing a great work and I am not able to come down. Why should the work cease while I let it drop and come down to you?'
And they sent to me in this way four times, and I answered them in the same way.
And Sanballat sent his young man to me in the same way a fifth time, and an open letter was in his hand.

Written in it: 'It is heard among the nations, and Gashmu says, that you and the Jews are planning to rebel — that is why you are building the wall. And you are to become their king, according to these reports.'

'And you have also appointed prophets to proclaim about you in Jerusalem, saying, "There is a king in Judah!" And now it will be reported to the king according to these words. So now, come, let us take counsel together.'
And I sent to him, saying, 'Nothing has happened according to these words that you are saying; you are inventing them from your own heart.'
For all of them were trying to make us afraid, saying, 'Their hands will drop from the work, and it will not be done.' And now — strengthen my hands.

And I came to the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah son of Mehetabel, and he was shut in; and he said, 'Let us meet at the house of God, inside the temple, and let us close the doors of the temple, for they are coming to kill you — by night they are coming to kill you.'
And I said, 'Should a man like me flee? And who is there like me who would go into the temple and live? I will not go.'
And I recognised that God had not sent him; for he had spoken the prophecy against me, and Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.
He was hired for this purpose: that I might be afraid and act so and sin, and that it might give them a bad name to hold against me, so that they could reproach me.
Remember, my God, Tobiah and Sanballat according to these works of theirs; and also Noadiah the prophetess and the rest of the prophets who were trying to make me afraid.
And the wall was completed on the twenty-fifth of Elul, in fifty-two days.
And when all our enemies heard of it, and all the nations around us were afraid, they fell greatly in their own eyes; and they knew that this work had been done by our God.
Also in those days the nobles of Judah were sending many letters to Tobiah, and Tobiah's letters were coming to them.
For many in Judah were bound by oath to him, because he was son-in-law to Shecaniah son of Arah, and Jehohanan his son had taken the daughter of Meshullam son of Berekiah.
Also they were reporting his good deeds in my presence, and carrying my words out to him. Tobiah sent letters to make me afraid.

nehemiah_7.t: And when the wall had been built and I had set up the doors, the gatekeepers, the singers and the Levites were appointed.
And I put Hanani my brother, and Hananiah the commander of the citadel, in charge of Jerusalem; for he was a faithful man and feared God more than many.

And I said to them, 'The gates of Jerusalem are not to be opened until the sun is hot; and while the gatekeepers are still on duty, let them shut the doors and bolt them. And appoint guards from the inhabitants of Jerusalem, each at his guard post and each opposite his own house.'
Now the city was wide on both sides and large, and the people in it were few, and no houses had been built.

And my God put it into my heart, and I gathered the nobles, the officials and the people to be enrolled by genealogy. And I found the book of the genealogy of those who came up at the first, and I found written in it:

These are the people of the province who came up from the captivity of the exile, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried into exile; and they returned to Jerusalem and to Judah, each to his own city,
those who came with Zerubbabel: Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, Baanah. The number of the men of the people of Israel:
the sons of Parosh, 2,172;
the sons of Shephatiah, 372;
the sons of Arah, 652;
the sons of Pahath-moab, of the sons of Jeshua and Joab, 2,818;
the sons of Elam, 1,254;
the sons of Zattu, 845;
the sons of Zaccai, 760;
the sons of Binnui, 648;
the sons of Bebai, 628;
the sons of Azgad, 2,322;
the sons of Adonikam, 667;
the sons of Bigvai, 2,067;
the sons of Adin, 655;
the sons of Ater, of Hezekiah, 98;
the sons of Hashum, 328;
the sons of Bezai, 324;
the sons of Hariph, 112;
the sons of Gibeon, 95;
the men of Bethlehem and Netophah, 188;
the men of Anathoth, 128;
the men of Beth-azmaveth, 42;
the men of Kiriath-jearim, Kephirah and Beeroth, 743;
the men of Ramah and Geba, 621;
the men of Michmas, 122;
the men of Bethel and Ai, 123;
the men of the other Nebo, 52;
the sons of the other Elam, 1,254;
the sons of Harim, 320;
the sons of Jericho, 345;
the sons of Lod, Hadid and Ono, 721;
the sons of Senaah, 3,930.
The priests: the sons of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua, 973;
the sons of Immer, 1,052;
the sons of Pashhur, 1,247;
the sons of Harim, 1,017.
The Levites: the sons of Jeshua, of Kadmiel, of the sons of Hodevah, 74.
The singers: the sons of Asaph, 148.
The gatekeepers: the sons of Shallum, the sons of Ater, the sons of Talmon, the sons of Akkub, the sons of Hatita, the sons of Shobai, 138.
The temple servants: the sons of Ziha, the sons of Hasupha, the sons of Tabbaoth,
the sons of Keros, the sons of Sia, the sons of Padon,
the sons of Lebanah, the sons of Hagabah, the sons of Shalmai,
the sons of Hanan, the sons of Giddel, the sons of Gahar,
the sons of Reaiah, the sons of Rezin, the sons of Nekoda,
the sons of Gazzam, the sons of Uzza, the sons of Paseah,
the sons of Besai, the sons of Meunim, the sons of Nephushesim,
the sons of Bakbuk, the sons of Hakupha, the sons of Harhur,
the sons of Bazlith, the sons of Mehida, the sons of Harsha,
the sons of Barkos, the sons of Sisera, the sons of Temah,
the sons of Neziah, the sons of Hatipha.
The sons of Solomon's servants: the sons of Sotai, the sons of Sophereth, the sons of Perida,
the sons of Jaala, the sons of Darkon, the sons of Giddel,
the sons of Shephatiah, the sons of Hattil, the sons of Pochereth-hazzebaim, the sons of Amon.
All the temple servants and the sons of Solomon's servants: 392.
And these are those who came up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addon and Immer; and they were not able to declare their ancestral house or their offspring, whether they were of Israel:
the sons of Delaiah, the sons of Tobiah, the sons of Nekoda, 642.
And of the priests: the sons of Hobaiah, the sons of Hakkoz, the sons of Barzillai, who had taken a wife from the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by their name.
These sought their record among those enrolled by genealogy, and it was not found; and they were excluded from the priesthood as defiled.
And the Tirshatha said to them that they were not to eat of the most holy things until a priest should stand for Urim and Thummim.
The whole assembly together: 42,360,
besides their male and female servants, of whom there were 7,337; and they had 200 male and female singers.
Their horses, 736; their mules, 245;
camels, 435; donkeys, 6,720.
And some of the heads of the ancestral houses gave to the work. The Tirshatha gave to the treasury: 1,000 gold darics, 50 basins, 530 priests' garments.
And some of the heads of the ancestral houses gave to the treasury of the work 20,000 gold darics and 2,200 silver minas.
And what the rest of the people gave was 20,000 gold darics, 2,000 silver minas and 67 priests' garments.

And the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, some of the people, the temple servants and all Israel settled in their own cities. And the seventh month arrived, and the people of Israel were in their cities.

nehemiah_8.t: And all the people gathered as one man in the open space before the Water Gate; and they told Ezra the scribe to bring the scroll of the law of Moses, which the LORD had commanded Israel.
And Ezra the priest brought the law before the assembly, both men and women and all who could understand what they heard, on the first day of the seventh month.

And he read aloud from it, in the open space before the Water Gate, from daybreak until midday, in front of the men and the women and those who could understand; and the ears of all the people were toward the scroll of the law.

And Ezra the scribe stood on a high wooden platform that had been made for the purpose; and beside him stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah and Maaseiah on his right hand, and on his left Pedaiah, Mishael, Malkijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah and Meshullam.
And Ezra opened the scroll before the eyes of all the people, for he was above all the people; and as he opened it, all the people stood up.
And Ezra blessed the LORD, the great God; and all the people answered, 'Amen, Amen,' lifting up their hands, and they bowed low and bowed down to the LORD with their faces to the ground.

And Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan and Pelaiah — the Levites — were making the people understand the law, and the people stayed in their place.
And they read aloud from the scroll, from the law of God, explaining it; and they gave the sense, and the people understood the reading.

And Nehemiah — he was the Tirshatha — and Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who were making the people understand, said to all the people, 'This day is holy to the LORD your God. Do not mourn and do not weep.' For all the people were weeping when they heard the words of the law.

And he said to them, 'Go, eat rich food and drink sweet drink, and send portions to those for whom nothing is prepared; for this day is holy to our Lord. And do not be grieved, for the joy of the LORD is your stronghold.'
And the Levites quieted all the people, saying, 'Hush, for this day is holy. Do not be grieved.'
And all the people went to eat and to drink, to send portions and to make great joy, because they had understood the words that had been made known to them.
And on the second day the heads of the ancestral houses of all the people, with the priests and the Levites, gathered to Ezra the scribe, to gain insight into the words of the law.
And they found written in the law that the LORD had commanded by the hand of Moses, that the people of Israel should dwell in booths during the festival in the seventh month,

and that they should make proclamation and send it through all their cities and in Jerusalem, saying, 'Go out to the hill country and bring leaves of olive, leaves of the oil tree, leaves of myrtle, leaves of palm and leaves of leafy trees, to make booths, as it is written.'

And the people went out and brought them, and made themselves booths, each on his own roof, and in their courtyards, and in the courtyards of the house of God, and in the open space of the Water Gate, and in the open space of the Gate of Ephraim.

And all the assembly that had returned from the captivity made booths and lived in the booths; for the people of Israel had not done so since the days of Jeshua son of Nun until that day. And there was very great joy.

And he read aloud from the scroll of the law of God day by day, from the first day to the last day; and they kept the festival seven days, and on the eighth day a solemn assembly, according to the ordinance.

nehemiah_9.t: And on the twenty-fourth day of this month the people of Israel gathered with fasting and in sackcloth, and with earth on them.
And the offspring of Israel separated themselves from all the foreigners; and they stood and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their ancestors.

And they stood up in their place and read aloud from the scroll of the law of the LORD their God a fourth of the day; and a fourth of the day they were confessing and bowing down to the LORD their God.
And Jeshua and Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani and Kenani stood up on the platform of the Levites and cried out with a loud voice to the LORD their God.

And the Levites — Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah and Pethahiah — said, 'Arise, bless the LORD your God from everlasting to everlasting. And let them bless your glorious name, and may it be exalted above all blessing and praise.'

You are he, the LORD, you alone. You made the heavens, the heavens of the heavens and all their host, the earth and all that is on it, the seas and all that is in them; and you preserve them all alive, and the host of the heavens bow down to you.
You are he, the LORD God, who chose Abram and brought him out from Ur of the Chaldeans and made his name Abraham;

and you found his heart faithful before you, and made with him the covenant to give the land of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Jebusite and the Girgashite — to give it to his offspring. And you have fulfilled your words, for you are righteous.
And you saw the affliction of our ancestors in Egypt, and you heard their outcry at the Sea of Reeds.

And you gave signs and wonders against Pharaoh and against all his servants and against all the people of his land, for you knew that they had acted presumptuously against them; and you made a name for yourself, as it is this day.
And you split the sea before them, and they passed through the middle of the sea on dry ground; and their pursuers you threw into the depths like a stone into mighty waters.
And in a pillar of cloud you led them by day, and in a pillar of fire by night, to light up for them the way in which they should walk.
And on Mount Sinai you came down and spoke with them from heaven, and you gave them upright ordinances and laws of faithfulness, good statutes and commandments.
And you made known to them your holy sabbath, and you commanded them commandments and statutes and law by the hand of Moses your servant.

And bread from heaven you gave them for their hunger, and water from a rock you brought out for them for their thirst; and you told them to go in and take possession of the land which you had lifted your hand to give them.
But they and our ancestors acted presumptuously, and stiffened their neck, and did not listen to your commandments.

And they refused to listen, and did not remember your wonders that you had done among them; and they stiffened their neck and appointed a head to return to their servitude in their rebellion. But you are a God of forgivenesses, gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love, and you did not abandon them.
Even when they had made themselves a calf of cast metal and had said, 'This is your god who brought you up from Egypt,' and had committed great blasphemies —

you in your great compassion did not abandon them in the wilderness. The pillar of cloud did not depart from over them by day, to lead them in the way; nor the pillar of fire by night, to light up for them the way in which they should walk.
And you gave your good spirit to instruct them, and you did not withhold your manna from their mouth, and you gave them water for their thirst.
And forty years you sustained them in the wilderness; they lacked nothing. Their clothes did not wear out and their feet did not swell.
And you gave them kingdoms and peoples, and allotted to them every corner; and they took possession of the land of Sihon king of Heshbon, and the land of Og king of Bashan.
And you multiplied their children like the stars of the heavens, and you brought them into the land which you had told their ancestors to go in and take possession of.

And the children went in and took possession of the land, and you brought low before them the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, and gave them into their hand — them and their kings and the peoples of the land — to do with them as they pleased.

And they captured fortified cities and fertile ground, and took possession of houses full of every good thing, hewn cisterns, vineyards, olive trees and fruit trees in abundance. And they ate and were satisfied and grew fat, and luxuriated in your great goodness.
And they were disobedient and rebelled against you, and threw your law behind their back, and killed your prophets who had warned them to bring them back to you; and they committed great blasphemies.

And you gave them into the hand of their adversaries, who caused them distress; and in the time of their distress they cried out to you, and you heard from heaven, and in your great compassion you gave them deliverers, and they delivered them from the hand of their adversaries.

And as soon as they had rest they returned to doing evil before you, and you abandoned them into the hand of their enemies, and they ruled over them; and they returned and cried out to you, and you heard from heaven and rescued them according to your compassion, many times.

And you warned them, to bring them back to your law; but they acted presumptuously and did not listen to your commandments, and against your ordinances they sinned — which, if a person does them, he shall live by them — and they turned a stubborn shoulder and stiffened their neck and did not listen.
And you were patient with them many years, and warned them by your spirit through your prophets; and they did not give ear, and you gave them into the hand of the peoples of the lands.
But in your great compassion you did not make an end of them and did not abandon them, for you are a gracious and compassionate God.

And now, our God — the great, the mighty and the awesome God, who keeps the covenant and the steadfast love — do not let all the hardship seem small before you that has come upon us: upon our kings, our leaders, our priests, our prophets, our ancestors and all your people, from the days of the kings of Assyria until this day.
And you are righteous in all that has come upon us, for you have acted in faithfulness and we have acted wickedly.
And our kings, our leaders, our priests and our ancestors did not do your law, and did not pay attention to your commandments or to your testimonies with which you admonished them.

And they, in their own kingdom and in your great goodness which you gave them, and in the broad and fertile land which you set before them, did not serve you and did not turn back from their evil deeds.
Here we are, slaves today; and the land which you gave to our ancestors to eat its fruit and its good things — here we are, slaves upon it.
And its produce increases for the kings whom you have set over us because of our sins; and they rule over our bodies and over our cattle as they please. And we are in great distress.
And in view of all this we are making a firm agreement and writing it; and on the sealed document are our leaders, our Levites and our priests.

nehemiah_10.t: And on the sealed documents were Nehemiah the Tirshatha son of Hacaliah, and Zedekiah,
Maaziah, Bilgai, Shemaiah. These were the priests.
And the Levites: Jeshua son of Azaniah, Binnui of the sons of Henadad, Kadmiel,
and their brothers: Shebaniah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan,
The heads of the people: Parosh, Pahath-moab, Elam, Zattu, Bani,

And the rest of the people — the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the temple servants, and everyone who had separated himself from the peoples of the lands to the law of God, their wives, their sons and their daughters, everyone who knew and understood —

they held fast to their brothers, their nobles, and entered into a curse and an oath to walk in the law of God, which was given by the hand of Moses the servant of God, and to keep and do all the commandments of the LORD our Lord and his ordinances and his statutes;
and that we will not give our daughters to the peoples of the land, and will not take their daughters for our sons;

and that if the peoples of the land bring wares or any grain on the sabbath day to sell, we will not take it from them on the sabbath or on a holy day; and that we will let go the seventh year and the loan of every hand;
and we established commandments upon ourselves, to lay upon ourselves a third of a shekel a year for the service of the house of our God:

for the bread of the row, the regular grain offering and the regular burnt offering, the sabbaths, the new moons, the appointed times, the holy things and the sin offerings, to make atonement for Israel; and all the work of the house of our God.

And we cast lots concerning the offering of the wood — the priests, the Levites and the people — to bring it to the house of our God, by our ancestral houses, at appointed times, year by year, to burn on the altar of the LORD our God, as it is written in the law.
And to bring the firstfruits of our ground and the firstfruits of all the fruit of every tree, year by year, to the house of the LORD;

and the firstborn of our sons and of our cattle, as it is written in the law; and the firstborn of our herds and our flocks, to bring to the house of our God, to the priests who serve in the house of our God;

and the first of our dough, our contributions, and the fruit of every tree, new wine and fresh oil, we will bring to the priests, to the storerooms of the house of our God; and the tithe of our ground to the Levites — and they, the Levites, are the ones who collect the tithes in all the cities where we labour.

And the priest, the son of Aaron, shall be with the Levites when the Levites collect the tithes; and the Levites shall bring up a tithe of the tithe to the house of our God, to the storerooms of the treasury.

For to the storerooms the people of Israel and the sons of Levi shall bring the contribution of grain, new wine and fresh oil; and there are the articles of the sanctuary, and the priests who serve, and the gatekeepers and the singers. And we will not neglect the house of our God.

nehemiah_11.t: And the leaders of the people lived in Jerusalem; and the rest of the people cast lots to bring one out of ten to live in Jerusalem, the holy city, while nine parts stayed in the other cities.
And the people blessed all the men who volunteered to live in Jerusalem.

And these are the heads of the province who lived in Jerusalem; and in the cities of Judah each lived on his own property, in their own cities — Israel, the priests, the Levites, the temple servants and the sons of Solomon's servants.

And in Jerusalem lived some of the people of Judah and some of the people of Benjamin. Of the people of Judah: Athaiah son of Uzziah son of Zechariah son of Amariah son of Shephatiah son of Mahalalel, of the sons of Perez;
and Maaseiah son of Baruch son of Col-hozeh son of Hazaiah son of Adaiah son of Joiarib son of Zechariah, son of the Shilonite.
All the sons of Perez who lived in Jerusalem: 468 men of strength.
And these are the people of Benjamin: Sallu son of Meshullam son of Joed son of Pedaiah son of Kolaiah son of Maaseiah son of Ithiel son of Jeshaiah;
and after him Gabbai and Sallai: 928.
And Joel son of Zikri was officer over them, and Judah son of Hassenuah was second in command over the city.
Of the priests: Jedaiah son of Joiarib, Jakin;
Seraiah son of Hilkiah son of Meshullam son of Zadok son of Meraioth son of Ahitub, supervisor of the house of God;
and their brothers who did the work of the house, 822; and Adaiah son of Jeroham son of Pelaliah son of Amzi son of Zechariah son of Pashhur son of Malkijah,
and his brothers, heads of ancestral houses, 242; and Amashsai son of Azarel son of Ahzai son of Meshillemoth son of Immer,
and their brothers, mighty men of strength, 128; and officer over them was Zabdiel son of Haggedolim.
And of the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hasshub son of Azrikam son of Hashabiah son of Bunni;
and Shabbethai and Jozabad, of the heads of the Levites, over the outside work of the house of God;

and Mattaniah son of Micah son of Zabdi son of Asaph, the leader who began the thanksgiving at the prayer; and Bakbukiah, second among his brothers; and Abda son of Shammua son of Galal son of Jeduthun.
All the Levites in the holy city: 284.
And the gatekeepers: Akkub, Talmon and their brothers, who kept watch at the gates: 172.
And the rest of Israel — the priests and the Levites — were in all the cities of Judah, each on his own inheritance.
And the temple servants were living on the Ophel; and Ziha and Gishpa were over the temple servants.
And the officer of the Levites in Jerusalem was Uzzi son of Bani son of Hashabiah son of Mattaniah son of Mica, of the sons of Asaph, the singers, for the work of the house of God.
For the king's commandment was upon them, and a firm ordinance was upon the singers, the matter of each day in its day.
And Pethahiah son of Meshezabel, of the sons of Zerah son of Judah, was at the king's side for every matter concerning the people.
And as for the villages with their fields: some of the people of Judah lived in Kiriath-arba and its daughter-towns, in Dibon and its daughter-towns, and in Jekabzeel and its villages,
and in Jeshua, Moladah and Beth-pelet,
and in Hazar-shual, and in Beersheba and its daughter-towns,
and in Ziklag, and in Meconah and its daughter-towns,
and in En-rimmon, Zorah and Jarmuth,
Zanoah, Adullam and their villages, Lachish and its fields, Azekah and its daughter-towns. And they encamped from Beersheba as far as the Valley of Hinnom.
And the people of Benjamin were from Geba: Michmash, Aija, Bethel and its daughter-towns,
Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah,
Hazor, Ramah, Gittaim,
Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat,
Lod and Ono, the Valley of the Craftsmen.
And of the Levites, divisions of Judah belonged to Benjamin.

nehemiah_12.t: And these are the priests and the Levites who came up with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,
Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,
Iddo, Ginnethoi, Abijah,
Mijamin, Maadiah, Bilgah,
Shemaiah, and Joiarib, Jedaiah,
Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, Jedaiah. These were the heads of the priests and their brothers in the days of Jeshua.
And the Levites: Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, Mattaniah — he and his brothers were over the songs of thanksgiving.
And Bakbukiah and Unni, their brothers, stood opposite them in the duties.
And Jeshua fathered Joiakim, and Joiakim fathered Eliashib, and Eliashib, Joiada,
and Joiada fathered Jonathan, and Jonathan fathered Jaddua.
And in the days of Joiakim the priests, heads of the ancestral houses, were: of Seraiah, Meraiah; of Jeremiah, Hananiah;
of Ezra, Meshullam; of Amariah, Jehohanan;
of Malluchi, Jonathan; of Shebaniah, Joseph;
of Harim, Adna; of Meraioth, Helkai;
of Iddo, Zechariah; of Ginnethon, Meshullam;
of Abijah, Zikri; of Miniamin, of Moadiah, Piltai;
of Bilgah, Shammua; of Shemaiah, Jehonathan;
and of Joiarib, Mattenai; of Jedaiah, Uzzi;
of Sallai, Kallai; of Amok, Eber;
of Hilkiah, Hashabiah; of Jedaiah, Nethanel.
The Levites in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan and Jaddua were recorded as heads of ancestral houses; and the priests, until the reign of Darius the Persian.
The sons of Levi, the heads of the ancestral houses, were recorded on the scroll of the annals, up to the days of Johanan son of Eliashib.

And the heads of the Levites were Hashabiah, Sherebiah and Jeshua son of Kadmiel; and their brothers stood opposite them, to praise and to give thanks, by the commandment of David the man of God, division corresponding to division.
Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon and Akkub kept guard as gatekeepers at the storerooms of the gates.
These were in the days of Joiakim son of Jeshua son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor and Ezra the priest and scribe.

And at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem they sought out the Levites from all their places, to bring them to Jerusalem to hold a dedication with joy, with thanksgivings and with song, cymbals, harps and lyres.
And the sons of the singers gathered, from the district around Jerusalem and from the villages of the Netophathites,
and from Beth-gilgal and from the fields of Geba and Azmaveth; for the singers had built themselves villages around Jerusalem.
And the priests and the Levites cleansed themselves, and they cleansed the people and the gates and the wall.
And I brought the leaders of Judah up onto the wall, and appointed two great thanksgiving choirs and processions; and one went to the right on the wall, toward the Dung Gate.
And after them went Hoshaiah and half the leaders of Judah,
and Azariah, Ezra and Meshullam,
Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah and Jeremiah,
and some of the sons of the priests with trumpets: Zechariah son of Jonathan son of Shemaiah son of Mattaniah son of Micaiah son of Zaccur son of Asaph,
and his brothers Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah and Hanani, with the instruments of song of David the man of God; and Ezra the scribe went before them.
And at the Spring Gate, straight ahead of them, they went up the steps of the City of David, at the ascent of the wall, above the house of David, and on to the Water Gate to the east.
And the second thanksgiving choir went in the opposite direction, and I was behind it, with half the people, on the wall, above the Tower of the Ovens and as far as the Broad Wall,
and above the Gate of Ephraim, over the Jeshanah Gate and the Fish Gate, and the Tower of Hananel and the Tower of the Hundred, as far as the Sheep Gate. And they stopped at the Gate of the Guard.
And the two thanksgiving choirs took their stand in the house of God, and I did, and half the officials with me,
and the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah and Hananiah, with trumpets;
and Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malkijah, Elam and Ezer. And the singers made themselves heard, with Izrahiah as officer.

And they offered great sacrifices on that day and rejoiced, for God had made them rejoice with great joy; and the women and the children rejoiced too. And the rejoicing of Jerusalem was heard from far off.

And on that day men were appointed over the chambers for the stores, the contributions, the first fruits and the tithes, to gather into them from the fields of the cities the portions of the law for the priests and the Levites; for the joy of Judah was over the priests and the Levites who stood there.
And they kept the service of their God and the service of the cleansing — as did the singers and the gatekeepers — according to the commandment of David and of Solomon his son.
For in the days of David and Asaph, from of old, there were heads of the singers, and songs of praise and thanksgivings to God.

And all Israel in the days of Zerubbabel and in the days of Nehemiah gave the portions of the singers and the gatekeepers, the matter of each day in its day; and they set apart for the Levites, and the Levites set apart for the sons of Aaron.

nehemiah_13.t: On that day there was read aloud from the scroll of Moses in the hearing of the people; and it was found written in it that no Ammonite or Moabite should enter the assembly of God, for ever,
because they did not meet the people of Israel with food and water, and he hired Balaam against them to curse them; and our God turned the curse into a blessing.
And when they heard the law, they separated all those of mixed descent from Israel.
And before this, Eliashib the priest, who was appointed over the storeroom of the house of our God, being closely allied to Tobiah,

had made him a large room where formerly they used to put the grain offering, the frankincense and the articles, and the tithe of grain, new wine and fresh oil — the portion commanded for the Levites, the singers and the gatekeepers — and the contribution of the priests.
And during all this I was not in Jerusalem, for in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I had gone to the king; and at the end of some days I asked leave of the king,
and I came to Jerusalem, and I saw the evil that Eliashib had done for Tobiah, in making him a room in the courtyards of the house of God.
And it displeased me greatly, and I threw all the goods of Tobiah's household outside, out of the room.
And I gave the order, and they cleansed the storerooms; and I brought back there the articles of the house of God, with the grain offering and the frankincense.
And I learned that the portions of the Levites had not been given, and that the Levites and the singers who did the work had fled, each to his own field.
And I contended with the officials and said, 'Why has the house of God been neglected?' And I gathered them and set them at their place.
And all Judah brought the tithe of grain, new wine and fresh oil to the storerooms.

And I appointed as treasurers over the storerooms Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe and Pedaiah of the Levites; and next to them Hanan son of Zaccur son of Mattaniah, for they were reckoned reliable; and it was their charge to distribute to their brothers.
Remember for me, my God, concerning this; and do not wipe out my acts of loyalty that I have done for the house of my God and for its services.

In those days I saw in Judah men treading winepresses on the sabbath, bringing in the heaps of grain and loading them on donkeys, and also wine, grapes, figs and every kind of load, and bringing them into Jerusalem on the sabbath day; and I protested on the day they sold provisions.
And the Tyrians who lived in it were bringing in fish and every kind of merchandise, and selling on the sabbath to the people of Judah and in Jerusalem.
And I contended with the nobles of Judah and said to them, 'What is this evil thing that you are doing, profaning the sabbath day?'
Did not your ancestors do the same, so that our God brought all this trouble upon us and upon this city? And you are adding to the wrath upon Israel by profaning the sabbath.

And when the gates of Jerusalem grew dark before the sabbath, I gave the order and the doors were shut; and I said they were not to open them until after the sabbath. And I stationed some of my young men at the gates, so that no load should come in on the sabbath day.
And the traders and the sellers of every kind of merchandise spent the night outside Jerusalem, once and twice.
And I warned them and said to them, 'Why are you spending the night in front of the wall? If you do it again, I will stretch out a hand against you.' From that time they did not come on the sabbath.

And I told the Levites to cleanse themselves and come and guard the gates, to keep the sabbath day holy. This also remember for me, my God, and have pity on me according to the greatness of your steadfast love.
Also in those days I saw the Jews who had married women of Ashdod, Ammon and Moab.
And half their children spoke Ashdodite and did not know how to speak Judean, but spoke according to the language of one people or another.

And I contended with them, cursed them, struck some of the men among them and pulled out their hair; and I made them swear by God: 'You shall not give your daughters to their sons, and you shall not take any of their daughters for your sons or for yourselves.'

Did not Solomon king of Israel sin over these? Among the many nations there was no king like him, and he was loved by his God, and God made him king over all Israel; yet even him the foreign women caused to sin.
And are we to hear of you doing all this great evil, acting unfaithfully against our God by marrying foreign women?
And one of the sons of Joiada son of Eliashib the high priest was a son-in-law of Sanballat the Horonite; and I drove him away from me.
Remember them, my God, for the defilements of the priesthood, and of the covenant of the priesthood and of the Levites.
And I cleansed them from everything foreign, and I assigned duties to the priests and the Levites, each in his own work;
and for the offering of the wood at appointed times, and for the firstfruits. Remember for me, my God, for good.

numbers_1.t: The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the tent of meeting, on the first day of the second month of the second year after they came out of the land of Egypt. He said:
Take a census of the whole congregation of the Israelites by their clans and their ancestral houses, listing every male by name, one by one,
from twenty years old and upward, everyone in Israel who goes out with the army. You and Aaron are to enrol them by their divisions.
One man from each tribe is to be with you, each of them the head of his ancestral house.
These are the names of the men who are to stand with you: from Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur;
from Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai;
from Judah, Nahshon son of Amminadab;
from Issachar, Nethanel son of Zuar;
from Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon;
from the sons of Joseph: from Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud; from Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur;
from Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni;
from Dan, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai;
from Asher, Pagiel son of Ocran;
from Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel;
from Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan;
These were the ones called from the congregation, the leaders of their ancestral tribes; they were the heads of the clans of Israel.
Moses and Aaron took these men, who had been designated by name,

and they assembled the whole congregation on the first day of the second month. They registered their descent by their clans and their ancestral houses, listed by name, from twenty years old and upward, one by one.
As the LORD had commanded Moses, so he enrolled them in the wilderness of Sinai.

The descendants of Reuben, Israel's firstborn: their genealogies by their clans and their ancestral houses, listed by name, one by one, every male from twenty years old and upward, everyone who goes out with the army —
Those enrolled of the tribe of Reuben: forty-six thousand five hundred.

The descendants of Simeon: their genealogies by their clans and their ancestral houses, those of them enrolled, listed by name, one by one, every male from twenty years old and upward, everyone who goes out with the army —
Those enrolled of the tribe of Simeon: fifty-nine thousand three hundred.
The descendants of Gad: their genealogies by their clans and their ancestral houses, listed by name, from twenty years old and upward, everyone who goes out with the army —
Those enrolled of the tribe of Gad: forty-five thousand six hundred and fifty.
The descendants of Judah: their genealogies by their clans and their ancestral houses, listed by name, from twenty years old and upward, everyone who goes out with the army —
Those enrolled of the tribe of Judah: seventy-four thousand six hundred.
The descendants of Issachar: their genealogies by their clans and their ancestral houses, listed by name, from twenty years old and upward, everyone who goes out with the army —
Those enrolled of the tribe of Issachar: fifty-four thousand four hundred.
The descendants of Zebulun: their genealogies by their clans and their ancestral houses, listed by name, from twenty years old and upward, everyone who goes out with the army —
Those enrolled of the tribe of Zebulun: fifty-seven thousand four hundred.

The descendants of Joseph — the descendants of Ephraim: their genealogies by their clans and their ancestral houses, listed by name, from twenty years old and upward, everyone who goes out with the army —
Those enrolled of the tribe of Ephraim: forty thousand five hundred.
The descendants of Manasseh: their genealogies by their clans and their ancestral houses, listed by name, from twenty years old and upward, everyone who goes out with the army —
Those enrolled of the tribe of Manasseh: thirty-two thousand two hundred.
The descendants of Benjamin: their genealogies by their clans and their ancestral houses, listed by name, from twenty years old and upward, everyone who goes out with the army —
Those enrolled of the tribe of Benjamin: thirty-five thousand four hundred.
The descendants of Dan: their genealogies by their clans and their ancestral houses, listed by name, from twenty years old and upward, everyone who goes out with the army —
Those enrolled of the tribe of Dan: sixty-two thousand seven hundred.
The descendants of Asher: their genealogies by their clans and their ancestral houses, listed by name, from twenty years old and upward, everyone who goes out with the army —
Those enrolled of the tribe of Asher: forty-one thousand five hundred.
The descendants of Naphtali: their genealogies by their clans and their ancestral houses, listed by name, from twenty years old and upward, everyone who goes out with the army —
Those enrolled of the tribe of Naphtali: fifty-three thousand four hundred.
These are the men enrolled, whom Moses and Aaron enrolled together with the leaders of Israel, twelve men, one for each ancestral house.
So all the Israelites who were enrolled, by their ancestral houses, from twenty years old and upward, everyone in Israel who goes out with the army —
all those enrolled came to six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty.
The Levites, however, were not enrolled by their ancestral tribe along with them.
For the LORD had said to Moses:
'Only the tribe of Levi you are not to enrol; you are not to take their census among the Israelites.

Instead, appoint the Levites over the tabernacle of the testimony, over all its articles and everything that belongs to it. They are to carry the tabernacle and all its articles, they are to serve it, and they are to camp around the tabernacle.
When the tabernacle is to set out, the Levites are to take it down; when the tabernacle is to camp, the Levites are to set it up. Any outsider who comes near is to be put to death.
The Israelites are to camp each in his own camp and each by his own standard, by their divisions.

But the Levites are to camp around the tabernacle of the testimony, so that no wrath falls on the congregation of the Israelites; and the Levites are to keep the charge of the tabernacle of the testimony.
The Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses; so they did.

numbers_2.t: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron:
The Israelites are to camp each by his own standard, under the emblems of their ancestral houses; they are to camp facing the tent of meeting, around it.
Those camping on the east side, toward the sunrise, are to be under the standard of the camp of Judah, by their divisions; the leader of the descendants of Judah is Nahshon son of Amminadab;
His division and those of them enrolled: seventy-four thousand six hundred.
Camping next to them is the tribe of Issachar; the leader of the descendants of Issachar is Nethanel son of Zuar;
His division and those of them enrolled: fifty-four thousand four hundred.
Then the tribe of Zebulun; the leader of the descendants of Zebulun is Eliab son of Helon;
His division and those of them enrolled: fifty-seven thousand four hundred.
All those enrolled in the camp of Judah, by their divisions: one hundred and eighty-six thousand four hundred. They are to set out first.
On the south side is to be the standard of the camp of Reuben, by their divisions; the leader of the descendants of Reuben is Elizur son of Shedeur;
His division and those of them enrolled: forty-six thousand five hundred.
Camping next to them is the tribe of Simeon; the leader of the descendants of Simeon is Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai;
His division and those of them enrolled: fifty-nine thousand three hundred.
Then the tribe of Gad; the leader of the descendants of Gad is Eliasaph son of Reuel;
His division and those of them enrolled: forty-five thousand six hundred and fifty.
All those enrolled in the camp of Reuben, by their divisions: one hundred and fifty-one thousand four hundred and fifty. They are to set out second.

Then the tent of meeting is to set out, with the camp of the Levites in the middle of the camps. They are to set out in the same order in which they camp, each in his own position, by their standards.
On the west side is to be the standard of the camp of Ephraim, by their divisions; the leader of the descendants of Ephraim is Elishama son of Ammihud;
His division and those of them enrolled: forty thousand five hundred.
Next to them is the tribe of Manasseh; the leader of the descendants of Manasseh is Gamaliel son of Pedahzur;
His division and those of them enrolled: thirty-two thousand two hundred.
Then the tribe of Benjamin; the leader of the descendants of Benjamin is Abidan son of Gideoni;
His division and those of them enrolled: thirty-five thousand four hundred.
All those enrolled in the camp of Ephraim, by their divisions: one hundred and eight thousand one hundred. They are to set out third.
On the north side is to be the standard of the camp of Dan, by their divisions; the leader of the descendants of Dan is Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai;
His division and those of them enrolled: sixty-two thousand seven hundred.
Camping next to them is the tribe of Asher; the leader of the descendants of Asher is Pagiel son of Ocran;
His division and those of them enrolled: forty-one thousand five hundred.
Then the tribe of Naphtali; the leader of the descendants of Naphtali is Ahira son of Enan;
His division and those of them enrolled: fifty-three thousand four hundred.
All those enrolled in the camp of Dan: one hundred and fifty-seven thousand six hundred. They are to set out last, by their standards.
These are the Israelites who were enrolled by their ancestral houses. All those enrolled in the camps, by their divisions: six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty.
The Levites, however, were not enrolled among the Israelites, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses. So they camped by their standards, and so they set out, each with his clan, by his ancestral house.

numbers_3.t: These are the generations of Aaron and Moses, from the day the LORD spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai.
These are the names of Aaron's sons: Nadab the firstborn, then Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
These are the names of Aaron's sons, the anointed priests, whom he ordained to serve as priests.

Nadab and Abihu died before the LORD when they presented unauthorised fire before the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai, and they had no sons. So Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests during the lifetime of Aaron their father.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
Bring the tribe of Levi forward and set it before Aaron the priest, and they are to serve him.
They are to keep his charge and the charge of the whole congregation before the tent of meeting, doing the service of the tabernacle.
They are to take care of all the articles of the tent of meeting and keep the charge of the Israelites, doing the service of the tabernacle.
You are to give the Levites to Aaron and his sons; they are wholly given over to him from among the Israelites.
You are to appoint Aaron and his sons, and they are to keep their priesthood; any outsider who comes near is to be put to death.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
As for me, I have taken the Levites from among the Israelites in place of every firstborn, every one that opens the womb among the Israelites. The Levites are to be mine.

For every firstborn is mine. On the day I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt I set apart as holy for myself every firstborn in Israel, from human being to animal. They are to be mine. I am the LORD.
The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai. He said:
Enrol the descendants of Levi by their ancestral houses and their clans. You are to enrol every male from a month old and upward.
So Moses enrolled them at the command of the LORD, as he had been commanded.
These were the sons of Levi by name: Gershon, Kohath and Merari.
These are the names of the sons of Gershon by their clans: Libni and Shimei.
The sons of Kohath by their clans: Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel.
The sons of Merari by their clans: Mahli and Mushi. These are the clans of the Levites by their ancestral houses.
To Gershon belonged the clan of the Libnites and the clan of the Shimeites. These are the Gershonite clans.
Those of them enrolled, counting every male from a month old and upward: seven thousand five hundred.
The Gershonite clans were to camp behind the tabernacle, on the west side.
The leader of the ancestral house of the Gershonites was Eliasaph son of Lael.
The charge of the sons of Gershon at the tent of meeting was the tabernacle and the tent, its covering, and the screen for the entrance of the tent of meeting,
the hangings of the courtyard, the screen for the entrance of the courtyard that surrounds the tabernacle and the altar, and its ropes — all the service they require.
To Kohath belonged the clan of the Amramites, the clan of the Izharites, the clan of the Hebronites and the clan of the Uzzielites. These are the Kohathite clans.
Counting every male from a month old and upward: eight thousand six hundred, who kept the charge of the holy place.
The clans of the sons of Kohath were to camp on the south side of the tabernacle.
The leader of the ancestral house of the Kohathite clans was Elizaphan son of Uzziel.
Their charge was the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the articles of the holy place used in its service, and the screen, and all the service it required.
The chief leader of the Levites was Eleazar son of Aaron the priest; he had oversight of those who kept the charge of the holy place.
To Merari belonged the clan of the Mahlites and the clan of the Mushites. These are the Merarite clans.
Those of them enrolled, counting every male from a month old and upward: six thousand two hundred.
The leader of the ancestral house of the Merarite clans was Zuriel son of Abihail. They were to camp on the north side of the tabernacle.
The appointed charge of the sons of Merari was the frames of the tabernacle, its bars, its pillars and its bases, all its articles and all its service,
and the pillars around the courtyard with their bases, their tent pegs and their ropes.

Those camping in front of the tabernacle on the east side, in front of the tent of meeting toward the sunrise, were Moses and Aaron and his sons, keeping the charge of the sanctuary on behalf of the Israelites. Any outsider who came near was to be put to death.
All the Levites who were enrolled, whom Moses and Aaron enrolled at the command of the LORD by their clans, every male from a month old and upward: twenty-two thousand.
The LORD said to Moses: Enrol every firstborn male among the Israelites from a month old and upward, and take the count of their names.

You are to take the Levites for me — I am the LORD — in place of every firstborn among the Israelites, and the livestock of the Levites in place of every firstborn among the livestock of the Israelites.
So Moses enrolled every firstborn among the Israelites, as the LORD had commanded him.
All the firstborn males, listed by name from a month old and upward, as enrolled, came to twenty-two thousand two hundred and seventy-three.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
Take the Levites in place of every firstborn among the Israelites, and the livestock of the Levites in place of their livestock. The Levites are to be mine. I am the LORD.
And as the redemption price for the two hundred and seventy-three firstborn Israelites who exceed the number of the Levites —
you are to take five shekels for each one, by the sanctuary shekel — the shekel is twenty gerahs.
You are to give the money to Aaron and his sons as the redemption price for those who exceed the number.
So Moses took the redemption money from those who exceeded the number redeemed by the Levites.
From the firstborn of the Israelites he took the money: one thousand three hundred and sixty-five shekels, by the sanctuary shekel.
Moses gave the redemption money to Aaron and his sons at the command of the LORD, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

numbers_4.t: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron:
Take a census of the sons of Kohath from among the Levites, by their clans and their ancestral houses,
from thirty years old and upward to fifty years old, everyone who comes to the service to do the work in the tent of meeting.
This is the service of the sons of Kohath at the tent of meeting: the most holy things.
When the camp is to set out, Aaron and his sons are to come and take down the veil of the screen and cover the ark of the testimony with it.
They are to put a covering of fine leather over it, spread a cloth entirely of violet over that, and put its poles in place.
Over the table of the Presence they are to spread a violet cloth and put on it the dishes, the pans, the bowls and the jars for the drink offering; and the regular bread is to be on it.
They are to spread a scarlet cloth over them, cover it with a covering of fine leather, and put its poles in place.
They are to take a violet cloth and cover the lampstand for the light, with its lamps, its tongs, its firepans and all the oil articles used in its service.
They are to put it and all its articles into a covering of fine leather and place it on the carrying frame.
Over the golden altar they are to spread a violet cloth, cover it with a covering of fine leather, and put its poles in place.
They are to take all the articles of service used in the holy place, put them into a violet cloth, cover them with a covering of fine leather, and place them on the carrying frame.
They are to remove the ashes from the altar and spread a purple cloth over it,

and put on it all the articles used in its service: the firepans, the forks, the shovels and the basins — all the articles of the altar. They are to spread a covering of fine leather over it and put its poles in place.

When Aaron and his sons have finished covering the holy place and all the articles of the holy place, as the camp sets out, then the sons of Kohath are to come and carry them. But they must not touch the holy things, or they will die. These are the load of the sons of Kohath at the tent of meeting.

Eleazar son of Aaron the priest is to have oversight of the oil for the light, the fragrant incense, the regular grain offering and the anointing oil — oversight of the whole tabernacle and everything in it, of the holy place and its articles.
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron:
Do not let the tribe of the Kohathite clans be cut off from among the Levites.
Do this for them, so that they may live and not die when they approach the most holy things: Aaron and his sons are to go in and assign each of them to his service and his load.
They are not to come in and look at the holy things even for a moment, or they will die.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
Take a census of the sons of Gershon as well, by their ancestral houses and their clans.
You are to enrol them from thirty years old and upward to fifty years old, everyone who comes to perform service, to do the service in the tent of meeting.
This is the service of the Gershonite clans, in serving and in carrying:
They are to carry the curtains of the tabernacle, the tent of meeting with its covering and the covering of fine leather that is over it, and the screen for the entrance of the tent of meeting,

the hangings of the courtyard, the screen for the entrance at the courtyard gate that surrounds the tabernacle and the altar, their ropes and all the articles for their service; they are to do everything that has to be done with them.
All the service of the Gershonites is to be at the direction of Aaron and his sons, for all their loads and all their service; you are to assign to them, as their charge, all that they carry.
This is the service of the clans of the Gershonites at the tent of meeting; their charge is under Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
The sons of Merari: you are to enrol them by their clans and their ancestral houses,
from thirty years old and upward to fifty years old. You are to enrol everyone who comes to the service, to do the service of the tent of meeting.
This is the charge of what they carry, for all their service at the tent of meeting: the frames of the tabernacle, its bars, its pillars and its bases,
the pillars around the courtyard with their bases, their tent pegs and their ropes, with all their equipment and all their service. You are to assign by name the articles they are charged to carry.
This is the service of the clans of the sons of Merari, all their service at the tent of meeting, under Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
