Moses, Aaron and the leaders of the congregation enrolled the sons of the Kohathites by their clans and their ancestral houses,
from thirty years old and upward to fifty years old, everyone who comes to the service, for service in the tent of meeting.
Those of them enrolled, by their clans, came to two thousand seven hundred and fifty.
These are the enrolled of the Kohathite clans, everyone who served at the tent of meeting, whom Moses and Aaron enrolled at the command of the LORD, through Moses.
The enrolled of the sons of Gershon, by their clans and their ancestral houses,
from thirty years old and upward to fifty years old, everyone who comes to the service, for service in the tent of meeting.
those of them enrolled, by their clans and ancestral houses, came to two thousand six hundred and thirty.
These are the enrolled of the clans of the sons of Gershon, everyone who served at the tent of meeting, whom Moses and Aaron enrolled at the command of the LORD.
The enrolled of the clans of the sons of Merari, by their clans and their ancestral houses,
from thirty years old and upward to fifty years old, everyone who comes to the service, for service in the tent of meeting.
those of them enrolled, by their clans, came to three thousand two hundred.
These are the enrolled of the clans of the sons of Merari, whom Moses and Aaron enrolled at the command of the LORD, through Moses.
All those enrolled, whom Moses, Aaron and the leaders of Israel enrolled — the Levites, by their clans and their ancestral houses,
from thirty years old and upward to fifty years old, everyone who came to do the work of serving and the work of carrying at the tent of meeting —
those of them enrolled came to eight thousand five hundred and eighty.
At the command of the LORD they were enrolled through Moses, each to his own service and his own load; and those enrolled were as the LORD had commanded Moses.

numbers_5.t: The LORD spoke to Moses:
Command the Israelites to send out of the camp everyone with leprosy, everyone with a discharge, and everyone made unclean by a corpse.
You are to send them out, male and female alike; send them outside the camp, so that they do not make their camps unclean, since I dwell in their midst.
The Israelites did so; they sent them outside the camp. Just as the LORD had spoken to Moses, so the Israelites did.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
Speak to the Israelites: When a man or a woman does any of the sins people commit, acting unfaithfully against the LORD, and that person becomes guilty,
then they are to confess the sin they have committed. He is to repay in full what his guilt amounts to, add a fifth to it, and give it to the person he has wronged.
But if the man has no kinsman to receive the repayment, the guilt payment that is repaid belongs to the LORD, for the priest — apart from the ram of atonement with which atonement is made for him.
Every contribution from all the holy things that the Israelites present to the priest shall be his.
Each person's holy things are his own; but whatever anyone gives to the priest becomes the priest's.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: If any man's wife turns aside and acts unfaithfully against him,

and a man lies with her and there is an emission of semen, and it is hidden from her husband's eyes and she is undetected, and she has been made unclean, and there is no witness against her, and she was not caught —

and a spirit of jealousy comes over him and he is jealous of his wife, and she has been made unclean; or a spirit of jealousy comes over him and he is jealous of his wife, and she has not been made unclean —

then the man is to bring his wife to the priest, and bring her offering with her: a tenth of an ephah of barley flour. He is not to pour oil on it or put frankincense on it, because it is a grain offering of jealousy, a grain offering of remembrance, which brings iniquity to remembrance.
The priest is to bring her forward and set her before the LORD.
The priest is to take holy water in an earthenware vessel, take some of the dust from the floor of the tabernacle, and put it into the water.

The priest is to set the woman before the LORD, unbind the woman's hair, and put in her hands the grain offering of remembrance, which is a grain offering of jealousy; and the priest is to hold the water of bitterness that brings a curse.

The priest is to put her under oath and say to the woman: If no man has lain with you, and if you have not turned aside to uncleanness while under your husband's authority, then be free from this water of bitterness that brings a curse.
But if you have turned aside while under your husband's authority, and if you have been made unclean, and a man other than your husband has lain with you —

then the priest is to put the woman under the oath of the curse, and the priest is to say to the woman: May the LORD make you a curse and an oath among your people, when the LORD makes your thigh fall away and your belly swell;
and this water that brings a curse shall enter your body, to make your belly swell and your thigh fall away. And the woman is to say: Amen, amen.
The priest is to write these curses on a scroll and wipe them off into the water of bitterness.
He is to make the woman drink the water of bitterness that brings a curse, and the water that brings a curse will enter her, causing bitterness.
The priest is to take the grain offering of jealousy from the woman's hand, wave the grain offering before the LORD, and present it at the altar.
The priest is to scoop out from the grain offering its memorial portion and turn it to smoke on the altar, and afterwards he is to make the woman drink the water.

When he has made her drink the water, then if she has been made unclean and has acted unfaithfully against her husband, the water that brings a curse will enter her, causing bitterness: her belly will swell and her thigh will fall away, and the woman will become a curse among her people.
But if the woman has not been made unclean and she is clean, then she is free, and she will conceive children.
This is the law concerning jealousy, when a wife turns aside while under her husband's authority and is made unclean,
or when a spirit of jealousy comes over a man and he is jealous of his wife. He is to set the woman before the LORD, and the priest is to carry out for her all this law.
The man will be free from iniquity, and that woman will bear her iniquity.

numbers_6.t: The LORD spoke to Moses:
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When a man or a woman makes a special vow, the vow of a nazirite, to live as a nazirite to the LORD,
he is to keep away from wine and strong drink. He is not to drink vinegar made from wine or vinegar made from strong drink, or drink any grape infusion, or eat grapes, fresh or dried.
All the days of his consecration he is not to eat anything produced by the grapevine, from the seeds to the skins.

All the days of his vow of consecration no razor is to pass over his head. Until the time is completed for which he lives as a nazirite to the LORD, he is to be holy, letting the locks of his hair grow long.
All the days of his consecration to the LORD he is not to go near a dead body.
He is not to make himself unclean for his father or his mother, his brother or his sister when they die, because the consecration of his God is on his head.
All the days of his consecration he is holy to the LORD.
If someone dies beside him suddenly, all at once, and so makes unclean his consecrated head, then he is to shave his head on the day of his cleansing — on the seventh day he is to shave it.
On the eighth day he is to bring two turtle-doves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
The priest is to offer one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering, and make atonement for him because he sinned in the matter of the corpse; and he is to consecrate his head that day.
He is to live as a nazirite to the LORD for the days of his consecration and bring a year-old male lamb as a guilt offering. The earlier days are void, because his consecration became unclean.
This is the law for the nazirite: on the day the time of his consecration is completed, he is to be brought to the entrance of the tent of meeting.
He is to present his offering to the LORD: one unblemished year-old male lamb as a burnt offering, one unblemished year-old ewe lamb as a sin offering, and one unblemished ram as a peace offering;
and a basket of unleavened bread — fine flour loaves mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers smeared with oil — with their grain offering and their drink offerings.
The priest is to present them before the LORD and offer his sin offering and his burnt offering.
The ram he is to offer as a sacrifice of peace offering to the LORD, together with the basket of unleavened bread; and the priest is to offer its grain offering and its drink offering.
The nazirite is to shave his consecrated head at the entrance of the tent of meeting, take the hair of his consecrated head and put it on the fire under the sacrifice of peace offering.

The priest is to take the boiled shoulder from the ram, one unleavened loaf from the basket and one unleavened wafer, and put them into the hands of the nazirite after he has shaved off his consecration.

The priest is to wave them as a wave offering before the LORD. It is holy, belonging to the priest, along with the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution. After that the nazirite may drink wine.

This is the law for the nazirite who makes a vow: his offering to the LORD for his consecration, apart from whatever else he can afford. He is to do exactly according to the vow he makes, following the law for his consecration.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
Speak to Aaron and his sons and say: This is how you are to bless the Israelites. Say to them:
May the LORD bless you and keep you.
May the LORD make his face shine on you and show you favour.
May the LORD lift up his face towards you and grant you peace.
So they are to put my name on the Israelites, and I will bless them.

numbers_7.t: On the day Moses finished setting up the tabernacle, he anointed it and consecrated it, with all its articles, and the altar with all its articles; he anointed them and consecrated them.
Then the leaders of Israel, the heads of their ancestral houses, presented offerings. These were the leaders of the tribes, the men who had presided over the enrolment.
They brought their offering before the LORD: six covered carts and twelve oxen — one cart for every two leaders and one ox for each — and they presented them in front of the tabernacle.
The LORD said to Moses:
Accept these from them; they are to be used in the service of the tent of meeting. Give them to the Levites, to each according to his service.
So Moses took the carts and the oxen and gave them to the Levites.
Two carts and four oxen he gave to the sons of Gershon, according to their service.
Four carts and eight oxen he gave to the sons of Merari, according to their service, under Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
To the sons of Kohath he gave none, because the service of the holy things fell to them: they carried on the shoulder.
The leaders presented the dedication offerings for the altar on the day it was anointed; the leaders presented their offering before the altar.
The LORD said to Moses: One leader each day, one leader each day, they are to present their offering for the dedication of the altar.
The one who presented his offering on the first day was Nahshon son of Amminadab, of the tribe of Judah.

His offering was one silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels by the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offering: two oxen, five rams, five he-goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Nahshon son of Amminadab.
On the second day Nethanel son of Zuar, the leader of Issachar, presented his offering.

His offering was one silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels by the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offering: two oxen, five rams, five he-goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Nethanel son of Zuar.
On the third day: the leader of the sons of Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon.

His offering was one silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels by the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offering: two oxen, five rams, five he-goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Eliab son of Helon.
On the fourth day: the leader of the sons of Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur.

His offering was one silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels by the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offering: two oxen, five rams, five he-goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Elizur son of Shedeur.
On the fifth day: the leader of the sons of Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.

His offering was one silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels by the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offering: two oxen, five rams, five he-goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
On the sixth day: the leader of the sons of Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel.

His offering was one silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels by the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offering: two oxen, five rams, five he-goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Eliasaph son of Deuel.
On the seventh day: the leader of the sons of Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud.

His offering was one silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels by the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offering: two oxen, five rams, five he-goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Elishama son of Ammihud.
On the eighth day: the leader of the sons of Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.

His offering was one silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels by the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offering: two oxen, five rams, five he-goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
On the ninth day: the leader of the sons of Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni.

His offering was one silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels by the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offering: two oxen, five rams, five he-goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Abidan son of Gideoni.
On the tenth day: the leader of the sons of Dan, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.

His offering was one silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels by the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offering: two oxen, five rams, five he-goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
On the eleventh day: the leader of the sons of Asher, Pagiel son of Ocran.

His offering was one silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels by the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offering: two oxen, five rams, five he-goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Pagiel son of Ocran.
On the twelfth day: the leader of the sons of Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan.

His offering was one silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels by the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offering: two oxen, five rams, five he-goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Ahira son of Enan.
This was the dedication offering for the altar, on the day it was anointed, from the leaders of Israel: twelve silver dishes, twelve silver basins and twelve gold pans.
Each dish weighed a hundred and thirty shekels and each basin seventy; all the silver of the articles came to two thousand four hundred shekels by the sanctuary shekel.
Twelve gold pans full of incense, ten shekels each by the sanctuary shekel; all the gold of the pans came to a hundred and twenty shekels.
All the livestock for the burnt offering: twelve bulls, twelve rams and twelve year-old male lambs, with their grain offering; and twelve male goats for a sin offering.

All the livestock for the sacrifice of peace offering: twenty-four bulls, sixty rams, sixty he-goats and sixty year-old male lambs. This was the dedication offering for the altar after it was anointed.

When Moses went into the tent of meeting to speak with him, he heard the voice speaking to him from above the mercy seat on the ark of the testimony, from between the two cherubim; and he spoke to him.

numbers_8.t: The LORD spoke to Moses:
Speak to Aaron and say to him: When you set up the lamps, the seven lamps are to give light towards the front of the lampstand.
Aaron did so: he set up its lamps towards the front of the lampstand, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
This was how the lampstand was made: hammered work of gold, from its base to its blossom it was hammered work, made according to the pattern the LORD had shown Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
Take the Levites from among the Israelites and cleanse them.
This is what you are to do to cleanse them: sprinkle water of purification from sin on them, have them pass a razor over their whole body, wash their clothes, and so cleanse themselves.
Then they are to take a young bull with its grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil; and you are to take a second young bull for a sin offering.
You are to bring the Levites forward before the tent of meeting and assemble the whole congregation of the Israelites.
You are to bring the Levites before the LORD, and the Israelites are to press their hands on the Levites.
Aaron is to wave the Levites as a wave offering before the LORD, from among the Israelites, and they are to be for doing the service of the LORD.
The Levites are to press their hands on the heads of the bulls; then offer the one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to the LORD, to make atonement for the Levites.
You are to set the Levites before Aaron and his sons and wave them as a wave offering to the LORD.
You are to separate the Levites from among the Israelites, and the Levites will be mine.
After that the Levites are to come and do the service of the tent of meeting. You are to cleanse them and wave them as a wave offering.
For they are wholly given to me from among the Israelites. In place of every firstborn that opens the womb, the firstborn of all the Israelites, I have taken them for myself.
For every firstborn among the Israelites is mine, both human and animal. On the day I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt I set them apart as holy for myself.
And I have taken the Levites in place of every firstborn among the Israelites.

And I have given the Levites as a gift to Aaron and his sons from among the Israelites, to do the service of the Israelites at the tent of meeting and to make atonement for the Israelites, so that no plague will fall on the Israelites when the Israelites come near the holy place.
So Moses, Aaron and the whole congregation of the Israelites did to the Levites everything the LORD had commanded Moses concerning the Levites; that is what the Israelites did to them.
The Levites purified themselves from sin and washed their clothes, and Aaron waved them as a wave offering before the LORD; and Aaron made atonement for them to cleanse them.
After that the Levites came to do their service at the tent of meeting before Aaron and his sons. Just as the LORD had commanded Moses concerning the Levites, so they did to them.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
This is the rule for the Levites: from twenty-five years old and upward a Levite is to come and take part in the work of serving at the tent of meeting;
and from fifty years old he is to retire from the service of the work and serve no longer.
He may assist his brothers at the tent of meeting in keeping the charge, but he is not to do the service. This is how you are to deal with the Levites in their charges.

numbers_9.t: The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the first month of the second year after they came out of the land of Egypt. He said:
Let the Israelites keep the Passover at its appointed time.
On the fourteenth day of this month, at twilight, you are to keep it at its appointed time; you are to keep it according to all its statutes and all its ordinances.
So Moses told the Israelites to keep the Passover.
They kept the Passover in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, at twilight, in the wilderness of Sinai. Just as the LORD had commanded Moses, so the Israelites did.
But there were men who were unclean because of a human corpse and could not keep the Passover on that day, and they came before Moses and Aaron that day.
Those men said to him: We are unclean because of a human corpse. Why should we be kept back from presenting the LORD's offering at its appointed time among the Israelites?
Moses said to them: Wait, and let me hear what the LORD will command concerning you.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
Speak to the Israelites and say: If any of you or of your descendants is unclean because of a corpse or is away on a distant journey, he may still keep a Passover to the LORD.
They are to keep it in the second month, on the fourteenth day, at twilight. They are to eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
They are not to leave any of it until morning, and they are not to break a bone of it. They are to keep it according to every statute of the Passover.

But anyone who is clean and is not away on a journey, and who fails to keep the Passover — that person is to be cut off from his kin, because he did not present the LORD's offering at its appointed time. That man will bear his sin.

When a sojourner is staying with you and would keep a Passover to the LORD, he is to do so according to the statute of the Passover and its ordinance. You are to have one statute, for the sojourner and for the native of the land alike.
On the day the tabernacle was set up, the cloud covered the tabernacle, the tent of the testimony; and in the evening it was over the tabernacle like the appearance of fire, until morning.
So it was continually: the cloud covered it, and by night it had the appearance of fire.
Whenever the cloud was taken up from over the tent, the Israelites would set out after it; and wherever the cloud settled, there the Israelites would camp.
At the command of the LORD the Israelites would set out, and at the command of the LORD they would camp. As long as the cloud settled over the tabernacle they would remain in camp.
When the cloud lingered over the tabernacle for many days, the Israelites kept the charge of the LORD and did not set out.
Sometimes the cloud was over the tabernacle only a few days: at the command of the LORD they would camp, and at the command of the LORD they would set out.
Sometimes the cloud stayed only from evening until morning, and when it was taken up in the morning they set out; or it stayed a day and a night, and when it was taken up they set out.
Or two days, or a month, or longer — whenever the cloud lingered over the tabernacle, settling over it, the Israelites stayed in camp and did not set out; and when it was taken up they set out.
At the command of the LORD they camped, and at the command of the LORD they set out. They kept the charge of the LORD, at the command of the LORD given through Moses.

numbers_10.t: The LORD spoke to Moses:
Make yourself two silver trumpets; make them of hammered work. They are to serve you for summoning the congregation and for setting the camps in motion.
When both are blown, the whole congregation is to gather to you at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
If only one is blown, the leaders, the heads of the thousands of Israel, are to gather to you.
When you sound an alarm, the camps on the east side are to set out.
When you sound an alarm a second time, the camps on the south side are to set out. An alarm is to be sounded for each of their departures.
When the assembly is to be summoned, you are to blow a blast, but not sound an alarm.
The sons of Aaron, the priests, are to blow the trumpets. This is to be a perpetual statute for you throughout your generations.
When you go to war in your land against a foe who presses you, you are to sound an alarm with the trumpets, and you will be remembered before the LORD your God and delivered from your enemies.

On your day of rejoicing, at your appointed times and at the beginnings of your months, you are to blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and over your sacrifices of peace offerings; they will be a memorial for you before your God. I am the LORD your God.
In the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth day of the month, the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle of the testimony.
The Israelites set out on their journeys from the wilderness of Sinai, and the cloud settled in the wilderness of Paran.
They set out for the first time at the command of the LORD given through Moses.
The standard of the camp of the sons of Judah set out first, by their divisions; over its division was Nahshon son of Amminadab.
over the division of the tribe of the sons of Issachar was Nethanel son of Zuar;
over the division of the tribe of the sons of Zebulun was Eliab son of Helon;
Then the tabernacle was taken down, and the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari, who carried the tabernacle, set out.
The standard of the camp of Reuben set out, by their divisions; over its division was Elizur son of Shedeur;
over the division of the tribe of the sons of Simeon was Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai;
over the division of the tribe of the sons of Gad was Eliasaph son of Deuel;
Then the Kohathites set out, carrying the holy things; and the tabernacle was set up before they arrived.
The standard of the camp of the sons of Ephraim set out, by their divisions; over its division was Elishama son of Ammihud;
over the division of the tribe of the sons of Manasseh was Gamaliel son of Pedahzur;
over the division of the tribe of the sons of Benjamin was Abidan son of Gideoni;
The standard of the camp of the sons of Dan set out, the rearguard for all the camps, by their divisions; over its division was Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai;
over the division of the tribe of the sons of Asher was Pagiel son of Ocran;
over the division of the tribe of the sons of Naphtali was Ahira son of Enan;
These were the marching orders of the Israelites by their divisions; and so they set out.

Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses' father-in-law: We are setting out for the place of which the LORD said, 'I will give it to you.' Come with us and we will do good to you, for the LORD has promised good concerning Israel.
He said to him: I will not go; I will go to my own land and to my kindred.
Moses said: Please do not leave us. You know where we should camp in the wilderness, and you can be our eyes.
And if you do go with us, whatever good the LORD does to us, that same good we will do to you.
They set out from the mountain of the LORD, a three days' journey; and the ark of the covenant of the LORD went before them for the three days' journey, to seek out a resting place for them.
And the cloud of the LORD was over them by day, whenever they set out from the camp.
Whenever the ark set out, Moses would say: Rise up, LORD, and let your enemies be scattered, and let those who hate you flee before you.
And when it came to rest, he would say: Return, LORD, to the ten thousands of the thousands of Israel.

numbers_11.t: The people took to complaining of misfortune in the hearing of the LORD; and the LORD heard, and his anger burned, and the fire of the LORD burned among them and consumed the edge of the camp.
The people cried out to Moses; Moses prayed to the LORD, and the fire died down.
That place was named Taberah, because the fire of the LORD had burned among them.
The rabble among them had a craving, and the Israelites too began to weep again and said: Who will give us meat to eat?
We remember the fish we used to eat in Egypt for nothing, and the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions and the garlic.
But now our appetite is dried up. There is nothing at all — nothing but this manna before our eyes.
The manna was like coriander seed, and it looked like bdellium.
The people would go about gathering it, grind it in hand-mills or pound it in a mortar, boil it in a pot and make it into cakes; and it tasted like a rich cake made with oil.
When the dew came down on the camp at night, the manna came down with it.
Moses heard the people weeping, family by family, each at the entrance of his tent. The anger of the LORD burned fiercely, and to Moses it seemed wrong.
Moses said to the LORD: Why have you dealt badly with your servant? Why have I not found favour in your eyes, that you lay the burden of all this people on me?
Did I conceive all this people? Did I give birth to them, that you should say to me, 'Carry them in your bosom, as a nurse carries a nursing child,' to the land you swore to give their fathers?
Where am I to get meat to give to all this people? They weep to me and say, 'Give us meat to eat.'
I am not able to carry all this people by myself; it is too heavy for me.
If this is how you are going to deal with me, then kill me outright, I beg you, if I have found favour in your eyes — and let me not look on my misery.

The LORD said to Moses: Gather seventy men to me from the elders of Israel, men you know to be elders of the people and its officials. Bring them to the tent of meeting and have them take their place there with you.

I will come down and speak with you there, and I will take some of the spirit that is on you and put it on them. They will share with you in carrying the burden of the people, so that you do not carry it alone.

And say to the people: Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, and you will eat meat — because you have wept in the hearing of the LORD, saying, 'Who will give us meat to eat? It was better for us in Egypt.' Now the LORD will give you meat, and you will eat.
You will eat not for one day, nor two days, nor five days, nor ten days, nor twenty days,

but for a whole month, until it comes out of your nostrils and becomes loathsome to you — because you have rejected the LORD who is among you and have wept before him, saying, 'Why did we ever come out of Egypt?'
But Moses said: The people I am among number six hundred thousand on foot, and you say, 'I will give them meat, and they will eat for a whole month.'
Are flocks and herds to be slaughtered for them, and would that be enough for them? Or are all the fish of the sea to be gathered for them, and would that be enough?
The LORD said to Moses: Is the LORD's hand too short? Now you will see whether my word comes about for you or not.
So Moses went out and told the people the words of the LORD. He gathered seventy men from the elders of the people and stationed them around the tent.

Then the LORD came down in the cloud and spoke to him, and took some of the spirit that was on him and put it on the seventy elders. When the spirit rested on them they prophesied — and did not do so again.

But two men had stayed in the camp; the name of one was Eldad and the name of the other Medad. The spirit rested on them — they were among those registered, though they had not gone out to the tent — and they prophesied in the camp.
A young man ran and told Moses: Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp.
Joshua son of Nun, who had been Moses' attendant from his youth, spoke up and said: My lord Moses, stop them!
But Moses said to him: Are you jealous on my account? If only all the LORD's people were prophets, and the LORD would put his spirit on them!
Then Moses withdrew into the camp, he and the elders of Israel.

Then a wind went out from the LORD and drove quails in from the sea and let them fall by the camp, about a day's journey on this side and a day's journey on that side, all around the camp, and about two cubits above the surface of the ground.
The people were up all that day and all that night and all the next day gathering the quail; the one who gathered least gathered ten homers. And they spread them out all around the camp.
The meat was still between their teeth, not yet chewed, when the anger of the LORD burned against the people, and the LORD struck the people with a very severe blow.
That place was named Kibroth-hattaavah, because there they buried the people who had craved.
From Kibroth-hattaavah the people set out for Hazeroth, and they stayed at Hazeroth.

numbers_12.t: Miriam spoke against Moses, and Aaron with her, on account of the Cushite woman he had married — for he had married a Cushite woman.
They said: Has the LORD spoken only through Moses? Has he not spoken through us as well? And the LORD heard it.
Now the man Moses was very humble, more so than anyone else on the face of the earth.
Suddenly the LORD said to Moses, Aaron and Miriam: Go out, the three of you, to the tent of meeting. So the three of them went out.
The LORD came down in a pillar of cloud, stood at the entrance of the tent, and summoned Aaron and Miriam; and the two of them came forward.
And he said: Hear now my words: If there is a prophet among you, I the LORD make myself known to him in a vision, I speak with him in a dream.
Not so with my servant Moses; he is faithful in all my house.
Mouth to mouth I speak with him, plainly and not in riddles; and he beholds the form of the LORD. Why then were you not afraid to speak against my servant, against Moses?
The anger of the LORD burned against them, and he departed.
When the cloud departed from over the tent, there was Miriam, struck with leprosy, white as snow. Aaron turned towards Miriam, and there she was, struck with leprosy.
Aaron said to Moses: Please, my lord, do not lay on us the sin we have committed so foolishly.
Do not let her be like a stillborn child, whose flesh is half eaten away when it comes from its mother's womb.
Moses cried out to the LORD: God, please — heal her, I pray!
The LORD said to Moses: If her father had spat in her face, would she not bear the shame for seven days? Let her be shut outside the camp for seven days, and after that she may be brought back.
So Miriam was shut outside the camp for seven days, and the people did not set out until Miriam was brought back.
After that the people set out from Hazeroth and camped in the wilderness of Paran.

numbers_13.t: The LORD spoke to Moses:
Send men to scout out the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the Israelites. Send one man from each ancestral tribe, each of them a leader among them.
So Moses sent them from the wilderness of Paran at the command of the LORD, all of them men who were heads of the Israelites.
These are their names: from the tribe of Reuben, Shammua son of Zaccur;
from the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Hori;
from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
from the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph;
from the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun;
from the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Raphu;
from the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel son of Sodi;
from the tribe of Joseph, that is, from the tribe of Manasseh, Gaddi son of Susi;
from the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli;
from the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael;
from the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Vophsi;
from the tribe of Gad, Geuel son of Maki;
These are the names of the men Moses sent to scout out the land; and Moses gave Hoshea son of Nun the name Joshua.
Moses sent them to scout out the land of Canaan and said to them: Go up here into the Negev, and go up into the hill country.
See what the land is like, and whether the people who live in it are strong or weak, few or many;
and what the land is like in which they live, whether good or bad; and what the cities are like in which they live, whether they are open camps or fortresses;

and what the land is like, whether it is fertile or poor, and whether there are trees in it or not. Be resolute, and bring back some of the fruit of the land. It was the season of the first ripe grapes.
So they went up and scouted out the land, from the wilderness of Zin as far as Rehob, at Lebo-hamath.
They went up into the Negev and came to Hebron, where Ahiman, Sheshai and Talmai, the descendants of Anak, were. Hebron had been built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.
They came to the Wadi Eshcol and cut down from there a branch with a single cluster of grapes, and carried it on a pole between two of them, along with some pomegranates and figs.
That place was named the Wadi Eshcol, because of the cluster the Israelites cut down there.
They returned from scouting out the land at the end of forty days.

They came to Moses and Aaron and the whole congregation of the Israelites in the wilderness of Paran, at Kadesh. They brought back word to them and to the whole congregation, and showed them the fruit of the land.
They gave him this account: We went to the land you sent us to, and it does flow with milk and honey; and this is its fruit.
But the people who live in the land are strong, and the cities are fortified and very large; and we also saw the descendants of Anak there.
Amalek lives in the land of the Negev; the Hittites, the Jebusites and the Amorites live in the hill country; and the Canaanites live by the sea and along the Jordan.
Then Caleb quieted the people before Moses and said: Let us go straight up and take possession of it, for we are well able to prevail over it.
But the men who had gone up with him said: We cannot go up against the people, for they are stronger than we are.

So they spread among the Israelites a bad report of the land they had scouted out, saying: The land we passed through to scout it out is a land that devours its inhabitants, and all the people we saw in it are men of great size.
And there we saw the Nephilim (the sons of Anak come from the Nephilim), and we seemed to ourselves like grasshoppers, and so we seemed to them.

numbers_14.t: Then the whole congregation lifted up their voice and cried out, and the people wept that night.
All the Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron, and the whole congregation said to them: If only we had died in the land of Egypt! Or in this wilderness — if only we had died!
Why is the LORD bringing us to this land, to fall by the sword? Our wives and our little ones will become plunder. Would it not be better for us to go back to Egypt?
And they said to one another: Let us appoint a leader and go back to Egypt.
Then Moses and Aaron fell on their faces before the whole assembled congregation of the Israelites.
And Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, two of those who had scouted out the land, tore their clothes.
They said to the whole congregation of the Israelites: The land we passed through to scout it out is an exceedingly good land.
If the LORD delights in us, he will bring us into this land and give it to us, a land flowing with milk and honey.
Only do not rebel against the LORD, and do not fear the people of the land, for they are our bread. Their shade has departed from over them, and the LORD is with us. Do not fear them.
But the whole congregation talked of stoning them with stones. Then the glory of the LORD appeared at the tent of meeting to all the Israelites.
The LORD said to Moses: How long will this people spurn me? How long will they refuse to believe in me, after all the signs I have done among them?
I will strike them with pestilence and dispossess them, and make of you a nation greater and mightier than they.
But Moses said to the LORD: Then the Egyptians will hear of it — for you brought this people up by your strength from among them —

and they will tell the inhabitants of this land. They have heard that you, LORD, are among this people; that you, LORD, are seen face to face, that your cloud stands over them, and that you go before them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.
If you put this people to death as one man, then the nations that have heard the report of you will say:
Because the LORD was not able to bring this people into the land he swore to give them, he slaughtered them in the wilderness.
And now, let the power of the Lord be great, as you have spoken, saying:

The LORD is slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love, bearing iniquity and transgression, yet by no means clearing the guilty — visiting the iniquity of fathers upon sons, to the third and the fourth generation.
Forgive the iniquity of this people according to the greatness of your steadfast love, and as you have borne with this people from Egypt until now.
The LORD said: I have forgiven, according to your word.
But as surely as I live, and as surely as all the earth is filled with the glory of the LORD —
none of the men who saw my glory and my signs, which I did in Egypt and in the wilderness, and who have tested me these ten times and have not listened to my voice,
will see the land I swore to give their fathers; none of those who spurned me will see it.
But my servant Caleb — because a different spirit was with him and he followed me fully — I will bring him into the land he went to, and his offspring will take possession of it.
Now the Amalekites and the Canaanites live in the valley. Tomorrow turn and set out for the wilderness by the way of the Sea of Reeds.
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron:
How long must I bear with this evil congregation, which grumbles against me? I have heard the grumblings of the Israelites, which they grumble against me.
Say to them: As surely as I live, declares the LORD, I will do to you exactly what you have spoken in my hearing.
In this wilderness your corpses will fall — all of you who were enrolled, your whole number, from twenty years old and upward, who have grumbled against me.
None of you will come into the land I swore with uplifted hand to settle you in — except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
But your little ones, who you said would become plunder — I will bring them in, and they will know the land you have rejected.
As for you, your corpses will fall in this wilderness.
Your sons will be shepherds in the wilderness for forty years, bearing the consequence of your faithlessness until the last of your corpses lies in the wilderness.
For forty years — one year for each of the forty days you spent scouting out the land, a year for each day — you will bear your iniquities, and you will know my opposition.
I the LORD have spoken: I will surely do this to all this evil congregation that has banded together against me. In this wilderness they will meet their end, and there they will die.
As for the men Moses sent to scout out the land, who came back and made the whole congregation grumble against him by spreading a bad report of the land —
those men, who spread the bad report of the land, died by the plague before the LORD.
But Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh remained alive of the men who went to scout out the land.
Moses told all the Israelites these words, and the people mourned bitterly.
They rose early in the morning and went up to the top of the hill country, saying: Here we are; we will go up to the place the LORD spoke of, for we have sinned.
But Moses said: Why are you transgressing the command of the LORD? It will not succeed.
Do not go up, for the LORD is not among you; otherwise you will be defeated before your enemies.
For the Amalekites and the Canaanites are there before you, and you will fall by the sword; because you have turned back from following the LORD, the LORD will not be with you.
But they presumed to go up to the top of the hill country, though neither the ark of the covenant of the LORD nor Moses left the camp.
Then the Amalekites and the Canaanites who lived in that hill country came down, struck them, and beat them down as far as Hormah.

numbers_15.t: The LORD spoke to Moses:
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you come into the land where you are to settle, which I am giving you,

and you make a food offering to the LORD — a burnt offering or a sacrifice, in fulfilment of a vow, or as a freewill offering, or at your appointed times — to make a soothing odour to the LORD, from the herd or from the flock,
then the one presenting his offering shall present to the LORD a grain offering of a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of oil.
And you are to offer a quarter of a hin of wine as the drink offering with the burnt offering or with the sacrifice, for each lamb.
Or for a ram you are to offer a grain offering of two tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a third of a hin of oil;
and you are to present a third of a hin of wine as the drink offering, a soothing odour to the LORD.
And when you offer a young bull as a burnt offering or a sacrifice, in fulfilment of a vow, or as a peace offering to the LORD,
then he is to present with the young bull a grain offering of three tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with half a hin of oil;
and you are to present half a hin of wine as the drink offering — a food offering, a soothing odour to the LORD.
This is what is to be done for each bull, each ram, or each of the flock, whether a lamb or a goat.
Whatever number you offer, do this for each one, according to their number.
Every native is to do these things in this way, presenting a food offering, a soothing odour to the LORD.
And when a sojourner is staying with you, or anyone else among you throughout your generations, and offers a food offering, a soothing odour to the LORD, he is to do just as you do.
As for the assembly: there is one statute for you and for the sojourner who stays with you, a perpetual statute throughout your generations. You and the sojourner are alike before the LORD.
One law and one ordinance are to apply to you and to the sojourner who stays with you.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you come into the land to which I am bringing you,
then, when you eat the food of the land, you are to present a contribution to the LORD.
From the first of your dough you are to present a loaf as a contribution; present it as you present the contribution from the threshing floor.
From the first of your dough you are to give a contribution to the LORD throughout your generations.
When you go astray and fail to do all these commandments that the LORD has spoken to Moses —
everything the LORD has commanded you through Moses, from the day the LORD gave the command and onward throughout your generations —

then, if it was done inadvertently, without the congregation's knowledge, the whole congregation is to offer one young bull as a burnt offering, a soothing odour to the LORD, with its grain offering and its drink offering according to the ordinance, and one male goat as a sin offering.

The priest is to make atonement for the whole congregation of the Israelites, and they will be forgiven, because it was inadvertent and they have brought their offering, a food offering to the LORD, and their sin offering before the LORD for their inadvertence.
The whole congregation of the Israelites will be forgiven, and the sojourner staying among them, because it happened to all the people inadvertently.
If one person sins inadvertently, that person is to present a year-old female goat as a sin offering.
The priest is to make atonement before the LORD for the person who has gone astray by sinning inadvertently, to make atonement for that person; and he will be forgiven.
For the native among the Israelites and for the sojourner staying among them there is to be one law, for anyone who acts inadvertently.
But the person who acts with a high hand, whether native or sojourner, is reviling the LORD; that person is to be cut off from among his kin.
For he has despised the word of the LORD and broken his commandment; that person is surely to be cut off — his iniquity is upon him.
While the Israelites were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering wood on the sabbath day.
Those who found him gathering wood brought him to Moses and Aaron and the whole congregation.
They put him in custody, because it had not been made clear what should be done to him.
The LORD said to Moses: The man is surely to be put to death. The whole congregation is to stone him with stones outside the camp.
So the whole congregation brought him outside the camp and stoned him with stones, and he died, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD said to Moses:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them to make tassels for themselves on the corners of their garments throughout their generations, and to put a violet cord on the tassel at each corner.
It will serve you as a tassel: you will look at it and remember all the commandments of the LORD and do them, and not go scouting after your own heart and your own eyes, after which you go whoring;
so that you may remember and do all my commandments and be holy to your God.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD your God.

numbers_16.t: Now Korah son of Izhar son of Kohath son of Levi took men, and Dathan and Abiram sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, of the sons of Reuben,
and they rose up before Moses, together with two hundred and fifty men of the Israelites, leaders of the congregation, called to the appointed meeting, men of renown.

They assembled against Moses and Aaron and said to them: You have gone too far! The whole congregation, all of them, are holy, and the LORD is among them. Why then do you exalt yourselves over the assembly of the LORD?
When Moses heard it, he fell on his face.

Then he spoke to Korah and all his company: In the morning the LORD will make known who is his and who is holy, and will bring that person near to himself; the one he chooses he will bring near to himself.
Do this: take censers for yourselves, Korah and all his company,
put fire in them and set incense on them before the LORD tomorrow. The man the LORD chooses is the one who is holy. You have gone too far, sons of Levi!
Moses said to Korah: Now listen, sons of Levi!

Is it too little for you that the God of Israel has separated you from the congregation of Israel, bringing you near to himself to do the service of the tabernacle of the LORD and to stand before the congregation and minister to them?
He has brought you near, and all your brothers the sons of Levi with you; and now you seek the priesthood as well?
So it is against the LORD that you and all your company have banded together. And Aaron — what is he, that you grumble against him?
Moses sent to summon Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, but they said: We will not come up.
Is it too little that you have brought us up from a land flowing with milk and honey to kill us in the wilderness, that you should also set yourself up as a ruler over us?
What is more, you have not brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey, nor given us an inheritance of fields and vineyards. Will you gouge out these men's eyes? We will not come up.
Moses was very angry and said to the LORD: Do not turn towards their grain offering. I have not taken one donkey from them, and I have done harm to none of them.
Moses said to Korah: You and all your company are to present yourselves before the LORD tomorrow — you and they and Aaron.
Each man is to take his censer and put incense on it, and each is to present his censer before the LORD — two hundred and fifty censers — and you and Aaron, each with his censer.
So each man took his censer, put fire in it and set incense on it, and they stood at the entrance of the tent of meeting, with Moses and Aaron.
Korah assembled the whole congregation against them at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD appeared to the whole congregation.
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron:
Separate yourselves from this congregation, and I will consume them in a moment.
They fell on their faces and said: God, God of the spirits of all flesh — one man sins, and will you be angry with the whole congregation?
The LORD spoke to Moses:
Say to the congregation: Get away from around the dwelling of Korah, Dathan and Abiram.
Moses got up and went to Dathan and Abiram, and the elders of Israel followed him.
He said to the congregation: Move away now from the tents of these wicked men, and do not touch anything of theirs, or you will be swept away in all their sins.
So they moved away from around the dwelling of Korah, Dathan and Abiram; and Dathan and Abiram came out and stood at the entrance of their tents, with their wives, their sons and their little ones.
Moses said: By this you will know that the LORD has sent me to do all these works, and that it is not of my own devising:
If these men die a natural death, the fate of all people, and what happens to everyone happens to them, then the LORD has not sent me.

But if the LORD creates something new, and the ground opens its mouth and swallows them and all that belongs to them, and they go down alive to Sheol, then you will know that these men have spurned the LORD.
As he finished speaking all these words, the ground under them split open.
The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and their households, and every person belonging to Korah, and all their property.
They went down alive to Sheol, they and all that belonged to them; the earth closed over them, and they perished from among the assembly.
All the Israelites around them fled at their cry, for they said: The earth may swallow us too!
And fire came out from the LORD and consumed the two hundred and fifty men who were presenting the incense.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
Tell Eleazar son of Aaron the priest to take up the censers from among the burning and scatter the fire far away, for they have become holy —

the censers of these men who sinned at the cost of their lives. They are to be hammered into plates as an overlay for the altar, for they were presented before the LORD and became holy; and they will be a sign to the Israelites.
So Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers that the men who were burned had presented, and they were hammered out as an overlay for the altar,

a reminder to the Israelites that no outsider who is not of Aaron's offspring should come near to burn incense before the LORD, and so not become like Korah and his company — just as the LORD had said to him through Moses.
But the next day the whole congregation of the Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron, saying: You have killed the people of the LORD.
When the congregation assembled against Moses and Aaron, they turned towards the tent of meeting, and there the cloud had covered it, and the glory of the LORD appeared.
Moses and Aaron came to the front of the tent of meeting.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
Get away from this congregation, and I will make an end of them in a moment. And they fell on their faces.

Moses said to Aaron: Take the censer, put fire on it from the altar, set incense on it, and go quickly to the congregation and make atonement for them; for wrath has gone out from before the LORD — the plague has begun.
So Aaron took it, as Moses had said, and ran into the midst of the assembly, where the plague had already begun among the people. He put on the incense and made atonement for the people.
He stood between the dead and the living, and the plague was checked.
Those who died by the plague were fourteen thousand seven hundred, besides those who died over the matter of Korah.
Then Aaron returned to Moses at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and the plague had been checked.

numbers_17.t: Speak to the Israelites and take from them a staff for each ancestral house, from all their leaders according to their ancestral houses — twelve staffs. Write each man's name on his staff.
Write Aaron's name on the staff of Levi, for there is to be one staff for the head of each ancestral house.
Deposit them in the tent of meeting before the testimony, where I meet with you.
And the staff of the man I choose will bud; so I will put an end to the grumblings of the Israelites against me, which they grumble against you.
Moses spoke to the Israelites, and all their leaders gave him a staff, one for each leader, by their ancestral houses — twelve staffs; and Aaron's staff was among their staffs.
Moses deposited the staffs before the LORD in the tent of the testimony.
The next day Moses came into the tent of the testimony, and there the staff of Aaron of the house of Levi had budded: it had put forth buds, produced blossoms, and ripened almonds.
Moses brought out all the staffs from before the LORD to all the Israelites; they looked, and each man took his own staff.
The LORD said to Moses: Put Aaron's staff back before the testimony, to be kept as a sign for the rebels; so you will put an end to their grumblings against me, and they will not die.
Moses did just as the LORD had commanded him; so he did.
The Israelites said to Moses: Look, we are perishing! We are lost, all of us lost!
Anyone at all who comes near to the tabernacle of the LORD will die. Are we all to perish?

numbers_18.t: The LORD said to Aaron: You and your sons and your father's house with you are to bear the iniquity of the sanctuary; and you and your sons with you are to bear the iniquity of your priesthood.

Bring your brothers also, the tribe of Levi, your ancestral tribe, near with you; let them join themselves to you and minister to you, while you and your sons with you are before the tent of the testimony.
They are to keep your charge and the charge of the whole tent; but they must not come near the articles of the holy place or the altar, or they will die — they, and you with them.
They are to join themselves to you and keep the charge of the tent of meeting, for all the service of the tent; and no outsider is to come near you.
You are to keep the charge of the holy place and the charge of the altar, so that wrath does not fall on the Israelites again.
And I myself have taken your brothers the Levites from among the Israelites. They are a gift to you, given over to the LORD, to do the service of the tent of meeting.

You and your sons with you are to keep your priesthood in every matter of the altar and within the veil, and so you are to serve. I give you your priesthood as a service of gift; any outsider who comes near is to be put to death.
The LORD spoke to Aaron: I myself have put you in charge of my contributions. Of all the holy gifts of the Israelites I have given them to you as a portion, and to your sons, as a perpetual due.

This is to be yours from the most holy things, kept back from the fire: every offering of theirs — every grain offering, every sin offering and every guilt offering that they render to me — it is most holy for you and your sons.
You are to eat it in a most holy place; every male may eat it. It is to be holy to you.

This also is yours: the contribution from their gift, from all the wave offerings of the Israelites. I have given them to you and to your sons and daughters with you, as a perpetual due; everyone in your household who is clean may eat it.
All the best of the fresh oil, and all the best of the new wine and the grain — the firstfruits of these, which they give to the LORD — I have given to you.
The firstfruits of everything in their land, which they bring to the LORD, are to be yours; everyone in your household who is clean may eat them.
Every devoted thing in Israel is to be yours.

Every firstborn of the womb, of all flesh, which they present to the LORD, whether human or animal, is to be yours; but you must certainly redeem the firstborn of human beings, and you are to redeem the firstborn of unclean animals.
You are to redeem them from a month old, at your valuation: five shekels of silver by the sanctuary shekel, which is twenty gerahs.

But the firstborn of a cow, a sheep or a goat you are not to redeem; they are holy. You are to dash their blood against the altar and turn their fat to smoke as a food offering, a soothing odour to the LORD.
Their meat is to be yours, like the breast of the wave offering and the right thigh.

All the contributions of the holy gifts that the Israelites present to the LORD I have given to you, and to your sons and daughters with you, as a perpetual due. It is a covenant of salt for ever before the LORD, for you and your offspring with you.
The LORD said to Aaron: You are to have no inheritance in their land, and no share among them. I am your share and your inheritance among the Israelites.
To the sons of Levi I have given every tithe in Israel as an inheritance, in return for the service they perform, the service of the tent of meeting.
The Israelites are no longer to come near the tent of meeting, or they will bear sin and die.

The Levites are to perform the service of the tent of meeting, and they will bear their iniquity. This is a perpetual statute throughout your generations; and among the Israelites they are to inherit no inheritance.

For the tithe of the Israelites, which they present to the LORD as a contribution, I have given to the Levites as an inheritance; that is why I have said of them: Among the Israelites they are to inherit no inheritance.
The LORD spoke to Moses:

Speak to the Levites and say to them: When you take from the Israelites the tithe I have given you from them as your inheritance, you are to present from it a contribution to the LORD, a tithe of the tithe.
Your contribution will be reckoned to you as grain from the threshing floor and as the full yield from the winepress.
In this way you also are to present a contribution to the LORD from all the tithes you receive from the Israelites; and from it you are to give the LORD's contribution to Aaron the priest.
From all the gifts you receive you are to present every contribution of the LORD, from all the best of it — its sacred portion from it.
Say to them: When you present the best of it, it will be reckoned to the Levites as the produce of the threshing floor and the produce of the winepress.
You and your households may eat it anywhere, for it is your wages in return for your service at the tent of meeting.
You will bear no sin in the matter when you present the best of it; but you are not to profane the holy gifts of the Israelites, or you will die.

numbers_19.t: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron:
This is the statute of the law that the LORD has commanded: Tell the Israelites to bring you an unblemished red heifer, one with no defect in it, on which no yoke has been laid.
You shall give her to Eleazar the priest, and he shall take her outside the camp, and someone shall slaughter her in his presence.
Eleazar the priest shall take some of her blood on his finger and sprinkle it seven times toward the front of the tent of meeting.
The heifer shall be burned in his sight — her hide, her flesh, her blood, along with her dung.
The priest shall take cedar wood, hyssop, and scarlet, and throw them into the middle of the burning heifer.
The priest shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water; after that he may come into the camp, but he shall be unclean until evening.
The one who burns her shall wash his clothes in water and bathe his body in water, and he shall be unclean until evening.

A clean man shall gather the ashes of the heifer and deposit them outside the camp in a clean place, and they shall be kept for the congregation of the Israelites, for the water to remove impurity. It is a sin offering.
The one who gathers the ashes of the heifer shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening. This shall be a perpetual statute for the Israelites and for the sojourner who lives among them.
Whoever touches a dead body — the corpse of any human being — shall be unclean for seven days.
He shall purify himself with it on the third day, and on the seventh day he shall be clean. But if he does not purify himself on the third day, he shall not be clean on the seventh.

Anyone who touches a dead body, the corpse of a human being who has died, and does not purify himself, defiles the tabernacle of the LORD, and that person shall be cut off from Israel. Because the water to remove impurity was not dashed on him, he remains unclean; his uncleanness is still on him.
This is the law: when someone dies in a tent, everyone who comes into the tent and everyone who is in it shall be unclean for seven days.
Every open vessel that has no lid corded down on it is unclean.
Anyone who, out in the open field, touches one slain by the sword, or a dead body, or a human bone, or a grave, shall be unclean for seven days.
For the unclean person they shall take some of the dust from the burning of the sin offering, and someone shall put running water on it in a vessel.

A clean person shall take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it on the tent, on all the articles, on the people who were there, and on the one who touched the bone, or the slain, or the dead body, or the grave.

The clean person shall sprinkle on the unclean person on the third day and on the seventh day, and on the seventh day he shall purify him from sin. Then he shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and in the evening he shall be clean.

Anyone who becomes unclean and does not purify himself shall be cut off from among the assembly, because he has defiled the sanctuary of the LORD. The water to remove impurity has not been dashed on him; he is unclean.

This shall be a perpetual statute for them. The one who sprinkles the water to remove impurity shall wash his clothes, and the one who touches the water to remove impurity shall be unclean until evening.
Everything the unclean person touches shall be unclean, and the person who touches that shall be unclean until evening.

numbers_20.t: The Israelites, the whole congregation, came to the wilderness of Zin in the first month, and the people settled at Kadesh. Miriam died there and was buried there.
There was no water for the congregation, and they assembled against Moses and Aaron.
The people quarrelled with Moses and said, "If only we had died when our brothers died before the LORD!"
"Why have you brought the assembly of the LORD into this wilderness, for us and our livestock to die here?"
"Why did you bring us up out of Egypt, to bring us to this evil place? It is no place of grain or figs or vines or pomegranates, and there is no water to drink."
Moses and Aaron went from before the assembly to the entrance of the tent of meeting and fell on their faces, and the glory of the LORD appeared to them.
The LORD spoke to Moses:

"Take the staff, and assemble the congregation, you and Aaron your brother, and speak to the rock before their eyes, and it will give its water. You shall bring water out of the rock for them, and give the congregation and their livestock a drink."
Moses took the staff from before the LORD, as he had commanded him.
Moses and Aaron assembled the assembly in front of the rock, and he said to them, "Listen now, you rebels: are we to bring water out of this rock for you?"
Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with his staff, and water came out in abundance, and the congregation and their livestock drank.
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron, "Because you did not trust me, to treat me as holy before the eyes of the Israelites, therefore you shall not bring this assembly into the land I have given them."
These are the waters of Meribah, where the Israelites quarrelled with the LORD, and he showed himself holy among them.
Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom: "This is what your brother Israel says. You know all the hardship that has come upon us:
"Our ancestors went down to Egypt, and we lived in Egypt many days, and the Egyptians did harm to us and to our ancestors.
"We cried out to the LORD, and he heard our voice and sent an angel and brought us out of Egypt. Now here we are at Kadesh, a city on the edge of your territory.

"Please let us pass through your land. We will not pass through field or vineyard, and we will not drink water from a well. We will go along the King's Highway; we will not turn aside to the right or to the left until we have passed through your territory."
But Edom said to him, "You shall not pass through me, or I will come out against you with the sword."
The Israelites said to him, "We will go up by the highway, and if we drink your water, I and my livestock, I will pay its price. Only let me pass through on foot, nothing more."
But he said, "You shall not pass through." And Edom came out against him with a large force and a strong hand.
So Edom refused to allow Israel to pass through his territory, and Israel turned away from him.
They set out from Kadesh, and the Israelites, the whole congregation, came to Mount Hor.
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron at Mount Hor, on the border of the land of Edom:
"Aaron shall be gathered to his kin, for he shall not enter the land I have given to the Israelites, because you rebelled against my command at the waters of Meribah.
"Take Aaron and Eleazar his son, and bring them up Mount Hor.
"Strip Aaron of his garments and put them on Eleazar his son. Aaron shall be gathered, and he shall die there."
Moses did as the LORD commanded, and they went up Mount Hor before the eyes of the whole congregation.
Moses stripped Aaron of his garments and put them on Eleazar his son, and Aaron died there at the top of the mountain. Then Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain.
When the whole congregation saw that Aaron had died, all the house of Israel wept for Aaron thirty days.

numbers_21.t: The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev, heard that Israel was coming by the way of Atharim, and he fought against Israel and took some of them captive.
Israel made a vow to the LORD and said, "If you will indeed give this people into my hand, I will devote their cities to destruction."
The LORD listened to the voice of Israel and gave the Canaanites up, and Israel devoted them and their cities to destruction; and the place was named Hormah.
They set out from Mount Hor by the way of the Sea of Reeds, to go around the land of Edom, and on the way the people grew impatient.
The people spoke against God and against Moses: "Why did you bring us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? There is no bread and there is no water, and we loathe this worthless bread."
The LORD sent among the people the fiery serpents, and they bit the people, and many of the people of Israel died.
The people came to Moses and said, "We have sinned, for we have spoken against the LORD and against you. Pray to the LORD, that he may take the serpent away from us." And Moses prayed for the people.
The LORD said to Moses, "Make yourself a fiery serpent and put it on a standard, and everyone who is bitten shall see it and live."
So Moses made a bronze serpent and put it on the standard, and whenever the serpent had bitten anyone, he would look at the bronze serpent and live.
The Israelites set out and camped at Oboth.
They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim, in the wilderness facing Moab, toward the sunrise.
From there they set out and camped in the Wadi Zered.
From there they set out and camped beyond the Arnon, which is in the wilderness extending from the territory of the Amorites; for the Arnon is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites.
Therefore it is said in the Book of the Wars of the LORD: Waheb in Suphah, and the wadis, the Arnon,
and the slope of the wadis that extends toward the site of Ar and leans upon the border of Moab.
From there they went to Beer. That is the well of which the LORD said to Moses, "Gather the people, and I will give them water."
Then Israel sang this song: Spring up, O well! Sing to it!
A well — princes dug it, the nobles of the people hollowed it out, with the ruler's staff, with their own staffs. And from the wilderness to Mattanah,
and from Mattanah to Nahaliel, and from Nahaliel to Bamoth,
and from Bamoth to the valley in the region of Moab, at the top of Pisgah, which looks down over the wasteland.
Then Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites:
"Let me pass through your land. We will not turn aside into field or vineyard; we will not drink water from a well. We will go by the King's Highway until we have passed through your territory."
But Sihon would not allow Israel to pass through his territory. He gathered all his people and went out to meet Israel in the wilderness; he came to Jahaz and fought against Israel.
Israel struck him down with the edge of the sword and took possession of his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, as far as the Ammonites; for the border of the Ammonites was strong.
Israel took all these cities and settled in all the cities of the Amorites, in Heshbon and all its dependent villages.
For Heshbon was the city of Sihon king of the Amorites, who had waged war against the former king of Moab and taken all his land from him as far as the Arnon.
Therefore the ballad-makers say: Come to Heshbon! Let it be built, let the city of Sihon be established.
For fire went out from Heshbon, a flame from the town of Sihon; it consumed Ar of Moab, the lords of the high places of the Arnon.
Woe to you, Moab! You have perished, people of Chemosh! He has made his sons fugitives and his daughters captives, to Sihon, king of the Amorites.
And we overthrew them; Heshbon has perished as far as Dibon; we laid waste as far as Nophah, which reaches to Medeba.
So Israel settled in the land of the Amorites.
Moses sent men to spy out Jazer, and they captured its dependent villages, and he dispossessed the Amorites who were there.
Then they turned and went up by the way of Bashan, and Og king of Bashan came out to meet them, he and all his people, for battle at Edrei.
The LORD said to Moses, "Do not fear him, for I have given him into your hand, with all his people and his land. You shall do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon."
So they struck him down, and his sons, and all his people, until no survivor was left to him, and they took possession of his land.

numbers_22.t: The Israelites set out and camped in the plains of Moab, across the Jordan from Jericho.
Balak son of Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amorites.
Moab was terrified of the people, because they were many, and Moab was filled with dread of the Israelites.
Moab said to the elders of Midian, "Now this company will lick up everything around us, as an ox licks up the greenery of the field." Balak son of Zippor was king of Moab at that time.

He sent messengers to Balaam son of Beor, at Pethor by the River, in the land of his kinsmen, to summon him: "A people has come out of Egypt. They have covered the face of the land, and they are settling opposite me.

"Now come, please, and curse this people for me, for they are too mighty for me. Perhaps then I shall be able to strike them and drive them out of the land; for I know that whoever you bless is blessed, and whoever you curse is cursed."
The elders of Moab and the elders of Midian went, with the fees for divination in their hand, and they came to Balaam and spoke Balak's words to him.
He said to them, "Stay here tonight, and I will bring you back word, whatever the LORD speaks to me." So the leaders of Moab stayed with Balaam.
God came to Balaam and said, "Who are these men with you?"
Balaam said to God, "Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, has sent to me:
"'A people has come out of Egypt and covered the face of the land. Now come, put a curse on them for me; perhaps I shall be able to fight against them and drive them out.'"
God said to Balaam, "You shall not go with them. You shall not curse the people, for they are blessed."
Balaam rose in the morning and said to Balak's leaders, "Go back to your own land, for the LORD has refused to let me go with you."
So the leaders of Moab rose and went to Balak and said, "Balaam has refused to come with us."
Balak sent again: leaders more numerous and more honoured than the first.
They came to Balaam and said to him, "This is what Balak son of Zippor says: Please do not let anything hold you back from coming to me,
"for I will honour you richly, and whatever you say to me I will do. Come, please, and put a curse on this people for me."
Balaam answered Balak's servants, "If Balak were to give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go beyond the command of the LORD my God, to do anything small or great."
"Now stay here tonight, you also, so that I may know what more the LORD will say to me."
God came to Balaam at night and said to him, "If the men have come to summon you, get up and go with them; but only the word that I speak to you, that is what you shall do."
Balaam rose in the morning, saddled his donkey, and went with the leaders of Moab.
