But God's anger burned because he was going, and the angel of the LORD stationed himself in the road as an opponent to him. Balaam was riding on his donkey, and his two servants were with him.

The donkey saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with his sword drawn in his hand, and she turned aside from the road and went into the field. So Balaam struck the donkey to turn her back to the road.
Then the angel of the LORD stood in a narrow path between the vineyards, with a wall on one side and a wall on the other.
The donkey saw the angel of the LORD, and she pressed herself against the wall and pressed Balaam's foot against the wall; so he struck her again.
The angel of the LORD went on ahead and stood in a narrow place where there was no way to turn aside, to the right or to the left.
The donkey saw the angel of the LORD, and she lay down under Balaam. Balaam's anger burned, and he struck the donkey with his staff.
Then the LORD opened the donkey's mouth, and she said to Balaam, "What have I done to you, that you have struck me these three times?"
Balaam said to the donkey, "Because you have made a fool of me! If there were a sword in my hand, I would kill you right now."
The donkey said to Balaam, "Am I not your donkey, the one you have ridden all your life until this day? Have I ever been in the habit of doing this to you?" And he said, "No."
Then the LORD uncovered Balaam's eyes, and he saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with his sword drawn in his hand; and he bowed low and prostrated himself on his face.
The angel of the LORD said to him, "Why have you struck your donkey these three times? I myself have come out as an opponent, because the way is perverse before me.
"The donkey saw me and turned aside before me these three times. If she had not turned aside from before me, by now I would surely have killed you and let her live."
Balaam said to the angel of the LORD, "I have sinned, for I did not know that you were standing in the road to meet me. Now, if it is evil in your eyes, I will turn back."
The angel of the LORD said to Balaam, "Go with the men; but only the word that I speak to you, that is what you shall speak." So Balaam went with Balak's leaders.
When Balak heard that Balaam had come, he went out to meet him at the city of Moab, on the border of the Arnon, at the edge of his territory.
Balak said to Balaam, "Did I not send to you urgently to summon you? Why did you not come to me? Am I really not able to honour you?"
Balaam said to Balak, "Here I am, I have come to you. But am I really able to say anything at all? The word that God puts in my mouth, that is what I shall speak."
Balaam went with Balak, and they came to Kiriath-huzoth.
Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep and sent portions to Balaam and to the leaders who were with him.
In the morning Balak took Balaam and brought him up to Bamoth-baal, and from there he saw the outskirts of the people.

numbers_23.t: Balaam said to Balak, "Build me seven altars here, and prepare me seven bulls and seven rams here."
Balak did as Balaam had spoken, and Balak and Balaam offered up a bull and a ram on each altar.
Balaam said to Balak, "Station yourself by your burnt offering while I go. Perhaps the LORD will come to meet me, and whatever word he shows me I will tell you." And he went off to a bare height.
God met Balaam, and Balaam said to him, "I have arranged the seven altars, and I have offered up a bull and a ram on each altar."
The LORD put a word in Balaam's mouth and said, "Return to Balak, and this is what you shall speak."
He returned to him, and there he was, standing by his burnt offering, he and all the leaders of Moab.
Then he lifted up his oracle: From Aram Balak led me, the king of Moab from the mountains of the east: Come, curse Jacob for me, come, denounce Israel.
How shall I put a curse on one whom God has not cursed? How shall I denounce one whom the LORD has not denounced?
For from the top of the rocks I see him, from the hills I observe him. Here is a people that dwells alone and does not reckon itself among the nations.
Who has counted the dust of Jacob, or numbered the fourth part of Israel? Let me die the death of the upright, and let my end be like his.
Balak said to Balaam, "What have you done to me? I took you to put a curse on my enemies, and here you have blessed them outright!"
He answered, "Must I not take care to speak what the LORD puts in my mouth?"
Balak said to him, "Come with me, please, to another place from which you can see them — only the outskirts of them, not the whole — and put a curse on them for me from there."
So he took him to the field of Zophim, to the top of Pisgah, and built seven altars and offered up a bull and a ram on each altar.
He said to Balak, "Station yourself here by your burnt offering, while I go to meet him over there."
The LORD met Balaam and put a word in his mouth and said, "Return to Balak, and this is what you shall speak."
He came to him, and there he was, standing by his burnt offering, with the leaders of Moab. Balak said to him, "What has the LORD spoken?"
Then he lifted up his oracle: Rise, Balak, and hear; give ear to me, son of Zippor.
God is not a man, that he should lie, nor a son of humankind, that he should change his mind. Has he spoken, and will he not do it? Has he said it, and will he not fulfil it?
I have received a charge to bless; he has blessed, and I cannot turn it back.
He has not looked upon misfortune in Jacob, nor seen trouble in Israel. The LORD his God is with him, and the shout of a king is among them.
God is bringing them out of Egypt; he has, as it were, the horns of a wild ox.
For there is no enchantment against Jacob, no divination against Israel. In due time it shall be said of Jacob and of Israel: What God has done!
Here is a people that rises like a lioness, that lifts itself up like a lion. It will not lie down until it devours the prey and drinks the blood of the slain.
Balak said to Balaam, "Then neither put a curse on them at all, nor bless them at all!"
Balaam answered Balak, "Did I not tell you: all that the LORD speaks, that is what I will do?"
Balak said to Balaam, "Come, please, let me take you to another place. Perhaps it will seem right in the eyes of God, and you may put a curse on them for me from there."
So Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor, which looks down over the wasteland.
Balaam said to Balak, "Build me seven altars here, and prepare me seven bulls and seven rams here."
Balak did as Balaam had said, and offered up a bull and a ram on each altar.

numbers_24.t: When Balaam saw that it was good in the eyes of the LORD to bless Israel, he did not go, as he had time after time, to seek omens; instead he set his face toward the wilderness.
Balaam lifted up his eyes and saw Israel encamped tribe by tribe, and the spirit of God came upon him.
Then he lifted up his declaration: The declaration of Balaam son of Beor, the declaration of the man whose eye is opened,
the declaration of one who hears the sayings of God, who sees the vision of the Almighty, falling down, with eyes uncovered:
How good are your tents, Jacob, your dwelling places, Israel!
Like wadis stretched out, like gardens beside a river, like aloes that the LORD has planted, like cedars beside the waters.
Water shall flow from his buckets, and his seed shall be in abundant waters. His king shall be higher than Agag, and his kingdom shall be exalted.
God is bringing him out of Egypt; he has, as it were, the horns of a wild ox. He shall devour the nations, his adversaries, break their bones, and shatter his arrows.
He crouched, he lay down like a lion, like a lioness — who will rouse him? Blessed be those who bless you, and cursed be those who curse you.
Balak's anger burned against Balaam, and he clapped his hands. Balak said to Balaam, "I summoned you to put a curse on my enemies, and here you have blessed them outright, three times now!"
"Now flee to your own place. I said I would honour you richly, but the LORD has withheld you from honour."
Balaam said to Balak, "Did I not also say to the messengers you sent to me:
"'If Balak were to give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go beyond the command of the LORD, to do good or evil out of my own heart. What the LORD speaks, that is what I will speak.'"
"Now I am going to my own people. Come, let me advise you what this people will do to your people in the days to come."
Then he lifted up his declaration: The declaration of Balaam son of Beor, the declaration of the man whose eye is opened,
the declaration of one who hears the sayings of God and knows the knowledge of the Most High, who sees the vision of the Almighty, falling down, with eyes uncovered:
I see him, but not now; I observe him, but not near. A star has marched forth from Jacob, a sceptre has risen from Israel; it shall shatter the corners of Moab and break down all the sons of Sheth.
Edom shall become a possession, and Seir, his enemies, shall become a possession; and Israel shall do valiantly.
One from Jacob shall rule, and shall destroy the survivor from the city.
Then he saw Amalek, and he lifted up his oracle: The first of the nations was Amalek, but his end shall be destruction.
Then he saw the Kenites, and he lifted up his oracle: Enduring is your dwelling, your nest is set in the rock.
Yet Kain shall be for burning. How long until Asshur takes you captive?
Then he lifted up his oracle: Woe! Who shall live when God does this?
And ships from the coast of Kittim — they shall afflict Asshur and afflict Eber, and he too shall come to destruction.
Then Balaam rose and went, and returned to his place; and Balak also went his way.

numbers_25.t: Israel settled at Shittim, and the people began to whore with the daughters of Moab.
They invited the people to the sacrifices of their gods, and the people ate and bowed down to their gods.
So Israel joined itself to Baal of Peor, and the anger of the LORD burned against Israel.
The LORD said to Moses, "Take all the heads of the people and impale them before the LORD in the sun, so that the burning anger of the LORD may turn away from Israel."
Moses said to the judges of Israel, "Each of you kill the men of yours who have joined themselves to Baal of Peor."

Then a man of the Israelites came and brought the Midianite woman to his brothers, before the eyes of Moses and of the whole congregation of the Israelites, while they were weeping at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
When Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose from among the congregation and took a spear in his hand.
He went after the Israelite man into the chamber and pierced the two of them through — the Israelite man and the woman, into her belly. Then the plague was held back from the Israelites.
Those who died by the plague were twenty-four thousand.

"Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, has turned back my wrath from the Israelites by being zealous with my own zeal among them, so that I did not make an end of the Israelites in my zeal."
"Therefore say: I am giving him my covenant of peace.
"It shall be for him and for his offspring after him a covenant of perpetual priesthood, because he was zealous for his God and made atonement for the Israelites."
The name of the Israelite man who was struck down, who was struck down with the Midianite woman, was Zimri son of Salu, a leader of an ancestral house among the Simeonites.
The name of the woman who was struck down, the Midianite, was Cozbi daughter of Zur. He was head of the tribes of an ancestral house in Midian.
"Be hostile to the Midianites and strike them down,

"for they are hostile to you with the deceits by which they deceived you in the matter of Peor, and in the matter of Cozbi daughter of the leader of Midian, their sister, who was struck down on the day of the plague in the matter of Peor."

numbers_26.t: After the plague, the LORD said to Moses and to Eleazar son of Aaron the priest:
"Take a census of the whole congregation of the Israelites, from twenty years old and upward, by their ancestral houses — everyone in Israel who goes out with the army."
So Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke with them in the plains of Moab, at the Jordan across from Jericho:
"From twenty years old and upward" — as the LORD had commanded Moses and the Israelites who came out of the land of Egypt.
Reuben, Israel's firstborn. The descendants of Reuben: through Hanoch, the Hanochite clan; through Pallu, the Palluite clan;
through Hezron, the Hezronite clan; through Carmi, the Carmite clan.
These are the Reubenite clans; those enrolled of them were forty-three thousand seven hundred and thirty.
The descendants of Pallu: Eliab.

The descendants of Eliab: Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These are the Dathan and Abiram, called from the congregation, who contended against Moses and against Aaron in Korah's company, when they contended against the LORD,
and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and Korah, when that company died, when the fire consumed two hundred and fifty men; and they became a warning sign.
But the sons of Korah did not die.
The descendants of Simeon by their clans: through Nemuel, the Nemuelite clan; through Jamin, the Jaminite clan; through Jachin, the Jachinite clan;
through Zerah, the Zerahite clan; through Shaul, the Shaulite clan.
These are the Simeonite clans: twenty-two thousand two hundred.
The descendants of Gad by their clans: through Zephon, the Zephonite clan; through Haggi, the Haggite clan; through Shuni, the Shunite clan;
through Ozni, the Oznite clan; through Eri, the Erite clan;
through Arod, the Arodite clan; through Areli, the Arelite clan.
These are the clans of Gad's descendants, according to those enrolled of them: forty thousand five hundred.
The descendants of Judah: Er and Onan. Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.
The descendants of Judah by their clans were: through Shelah, the Shelanite clan; through Perez, the Perezite clan; through Zerah, the Zerahite clan.
The descendants of Perez were: through Hezron, the Hezronite clan; through Hamul, the Hamulite clan.
These are the clans of Judah, according to those enrolled of them: seventy-six thousand five hundred.
The descendants of Issachar by their clans: through Tola, the Tolaite clan; through Puvah, the Punite clan;
through Jashub, the Jashubite clan; through Shimron, the Shimronite clan.
These are the clans of Issachar, according to those enrolled of them: sixty-four thousand three hundred.
The descendants of Zebulun by their clans: through Sered, the Seredite clan; through Elon, the Elonite clan; through Jahleel, the Jahleelite clan.
These are the Zebulunite clans, according to those enrolled of them: sixty thousand five hundred.
The descendants of Joseph by their clans: Manasseh and Ephraim.
The descendants of Manasseh: through Machir, the Machirite clan; and Machir fathered Gilead; through Gilead, the Gileadite clan.
These are the descendants of Gilead: through Iezer, the Iezerite clan; through Helek, the Helekite clan;
and Asriel, the Asrielite clan; and Shechem, the Shechemite clan;
and Shemida, the Shemidaite clan; and Hepher, the Hepherite clan.
Zelophehad son of Hepher had no sons, only daughters; and the names of Zelophehad's daughters were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
These are the clans of Manasseh; those enrolled of them were fifty-two thousand seven hundred.
These are the descendants of Ephraim by their clans: through Shuthelah, the Shuthelahite clan; through Becher, the Becherite clan; through Tahan, the Tahanite clan.
And these are the descendants of Shuthelah: through Eran, the Eranite clan.
These are the clans of Ephraim's descendants, according to those enrolled of them: thirty-two thousand five hundred. These are the descendants of Joseph by their clans.
The descendants of Benjamin by their clans: through Bela, the Belaite clan; through Ashbel, the Ashbelite clan; through Ahiram, the Ahiramite clan;
through Shephupham, the Shuphamite clan; through Hupham, the Huphamite clan.
The descendants of Bela were Ard and Naaman: the Ardite clan; through Naaman, the Naamanite clan.
These are the descendants of Benjamin by their clans; those enrolled of them were forty-five thousand six hundred.
These are the descendants of Dan by their clans: through Shuham, the Shuhamite clan. These are the clans of Dan by their clans.
All the Shuhamite clans, according to those enrolled of them: sixty-four thousand four hundred.
The descendants of Asher by their clans: through Imnah, the Imnite clan; through Ishvi, the Ishvite clan; through Beriah, the Beriite clan.
Of the descendants of Beriah: through Heber, the Heberite clan; through Malchiel, the Malchielite clan.
And the name of Asher's daughter was Serah.
These are the clans of Asher's descendants, according to those enrolled of them: fifty-three thousand four hundred.
The descendants of Naphtali by their clans: through Jahzeel, the Jahzeelite clan; through Guni, the Gunite clan;
through Jezer, the Jezerite clan; through Shillem, the Shillemite clan.
These are the clans of Naphtali by their clans; those enrolled of them were forty-five thousand four hundred.
These are those enrolled of the Israelites: six hundred and one thousand, seven hundred and thirty.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"To these the land shall be divided as an inheritance, by the number of names.
"To the large tribe you shall give a large inheritance, and to the small a small inheritance; each shall be given its inheritance according to those enrolled of it.
"But the land shall be divided by lot; they shall inherit according to the names of their ancestral tribes.
"Its inheritance shall be divided according to the lot, between the large and the small."
And these are those enrolled of the Levites by their clans: through Gershon, the Gershonite clan; through Kohath, the Kohathite clan; through Merari, the Merarite clan.
These are the clans of Levi: the Libnite clan, the Hebronite clan, the Mahlite clan, the Mushite clan, the Korahite clan. And Kohath fathered Amram.
The name of Amram's wife was Jochebed, daughter of Levi, who was born to Levi in Egypt; and she bore to Amram Aaron and Moses, and Miriam their sister.
To Aaron were born Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
Nadab and Abihu died when they presented unauthorised fire before the LORD.

Those enrolled of them were twenty-three thousand, every male from a month old and upward; for they were not enrolled among the Israelites, because no inheritance was given to them among the Israelites.
These are those enrolled by Moses and Eleazar the priest, who enrolled the Israelites in the plains of Moab at the Jordan across from Jericho.
Among these there was not one man from those enrolled by Moses and Aaron the priest, who enrolled the Israelites in the wilderness of Sinai.
For the LORD had said of them, "They shall surely die in the wilderness." And not one of them was left except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

numbers_27.t: Then the daughters of Zelophehad drew near — Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, of the clans of Manasseh son of Joseph. These are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
They stood before Moses, before Eleazar the priest, before the leaders and the whole congregation, at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and said:
"Our father died in the wilderness. He was not among the company that gathered against the LORD in Korah's company; he died for his own sin, and he had no sons.
"Why should our father's name be taken away from his clan because he had no son? Give us a possession among our father's brothers."
So Moses brought their case before the LORD.
The LORD said to Moses:
"The daughters of Zelophehad speak rightly. You shall surely give them a possession as an inheritance among their father's brothers, and you shall transfer their father's inheritance to them.
"And you shall say to the Israelites: If a man dies and has no son, you shall transfer his inheritance to his daughter.
"If he has no daughter, you shall give his inheritance to his brothers.
"If he has no brothers, you shall give his inheritance to his father's brothers.

"And if his father has no brothers, you shall give his inheritance to the nearest relative in his clan, and he shall take possession of it. This shall be a statute of judgement for the Israelites, as the LORD commanded Moses."
The LORD said to Moses, "Go up this mountain of the Abarim and see the land I have given to the Israelites."
"When you have seen it, you also shall be gathered to your kin, as Aaron your brother was gathered,

"since you rebelled against my command in the wilderness of Zin, in the strife of the congregation, to treat me as holy at the waters before their eyes. Those are the waters of Meribath-kadesh in the wilderness of Zin."
Moses spoke to the LORD:
"Let the LORD, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation,
"who will go out before them and come in before them, who will lead them out and bring them in, so that the congregation of the LORD may not be like sheep that have no shepherd."
The LORD said to Moses, "Take Joshua son of Nun, a man in whom is the Spirit, and lay your hand on him.
"You shall make him stand before Eleazar the priest and before the whole congregation, and commission him before their eyes.
"You shall put some of your majesty on him, so that the whole congregation of the Israelites may obey.

"He shall stand before Eleazar the priest, who shall enquire for him by the judgement of the Urim before the LORD. At his word they shall go out and at his word they shall come in — he and all the Israelites with him, the whole congregation."
Moses did as the LORD commanded him. He took Joshua and made him stand before Eleazar the priest and before the whole congregation,
and he laid his hands on him and commissioned him, as the LORD had spoken by the hand of Moses.

numbers_28.t: The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Command the Israelites and say to them: You shall take care to present to me at its appointed time my offering, my food, for my food offerings, my soothing odour."
"And say to them: This is the food offering that you shall present to the LORD: two unblemished year-old male lambs a day, as a continual burnt offering.
"You shall offer the one lamb in the morning and the second lamb at twilight,
"and a tenth of an ephah of fine flour for a grain offering, mixed with a quarter of a hin of beaten oil.
"It is a continual burnt offering, the one instituted at Mount Sinai, a soothing odour, a food offering to the LORD.
"Its drink offering shall be a quarter of a hin for the one lamb; in the holy place pour out a drink offering of strong drink to the LORD.
"You shall offer the second lamb at twilight; you shall offer it with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning, a food offering, a soothing odour to the LORD.
"On the sabbath day: two unblemished year-old male lambs, and two tenths of an ephah of fine flour for a grain offering mixed with oil, and its drink offering.
"This is the burnt offering for each sabbath, in addition to the continual burnt offering and its drink offering.
"At the beginnings of your months you shall present a burnt offering to the LORD: two young bulls, one ram, and seven unblemished year-old male lambs;
"and three tenths of an ephah of fine flour for a grain offering mixed with oil, for the one bull; and two tenths of an ephah of fine flour for a grain offering mixed with oil, for the one ram;
"and a tenth of an ephah of fine flour for a grain offering mixed with oil, for each lamb. It is a burnt offering, a soothing odour, a food offering to the LORD.
"Their drink offerings: half a hin of wine for the bull, a third of a hin for the ram, and a quarter of a hin for the lamb. This is the burnt offering for each month, through the months of the year.
"And one male goat as a sin offering to the LORD; it shall be offered in addition to the continual burnt offering and its drink offering.
"In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, is a Passover to the LORD.
"On the fifteenth day of this month is a festival; for seven days unleavened bread shall be eaten.
"On the first day there shall be a holy convocation; you shall do no occupational work.
"You shall present a food offering, a burnt offering to the LORD: two young bulls, one ram, and seven year-old male lambs — they shall be unblemished for you;
"and their grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths of an ephah for the bull and two tenths for the ram you shall offer.
"A tenth of an ephah you shall offer for each lamb, for the seven lambs.
"And one male goat as a sin offering, to make atonement for you.
"You shall offer these in addition to the morning burnt offering, which is the continual burnt offering.
"In this way you shall offer daily, for seven days, the food of a food offering, a soothing odour to the LORD; it shall be offered in addition to the continual burnt offering and its drink offering.
"On the seventh day you shall have a holy convocation; you shall do no occupational work.
"On the day of the firstfruits, when you present a new grain offering to the LORD at your Weeks, you shall have a holy convocation; you shall do no occupational work.
"You shall present a burnt offering as a soothing odour to the LORD: two young bulls, one ram, and seven year-old male lambs;
"and their grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths of an ephah for the one bull, two tenths for the one ram,
"a tenth of an ephah for each lamb, for the seven lambs;
"one male goat, to make atonement for you.
"You shall offer them in addition to the continual burnt offering and its grain offering — they shall be unblemished for you — with their drink offerings."

numbers_29.t: "In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you shall have a holy convocation; you shall do no occupational work. It shall be for you a day of a loud blast.
"You shall offer a burnt offering as a soothing odour to the LORD: one young bull, one ram, and seven unblemished year-old male lambs;
"and their grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths of an ephah for the bull, two tenths for the ram,
"and one tenth of an ephah for each lamb, for the seven lambs;
"and one male goat as a sin offering, to make atonement for you;

"in addition to the new-moon burnt offering and its grain offering, and the continual burnt offering and its grain offering, with their drink offerings according to their ordinance, a soothing odour, a food offering to the LORD.
"On the tenth day of this seventh month you shall have a holy convocation, and you shall afflict yourselves; you shall do no work at all.
"You shall present a burnt offering to the LORD, a soothing odour: one young bull, one ram, seven year-old male lambs — they shall be unblemished for you;
"and their grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths of an ephah for the bull, two tenths for the one ram,
"a tenth of an ephah for each lamb, for the seven lambs;
"one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the sin offering of atonement and the continual burnt offering with its grain offering and their drink offerings.
"On the fifteenth day of the seventh month you shall have a holy convocation; you shall do no occupational work. You shall celebrate a festival to the LORD for seven days.
"You shall present a burnt offering, a food offering, a soothing odour to the LORD: thirteen young bulls, two rams, fourteen year-old male lambs — they shall be unblemished;
"and their grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths of an ephah for each of the thirteen bulls, two tenths for each of the two rams;
"and a tenth of an ephah for each lamb, for the fourteen lambs;
"and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the continual burnt offering, its grain offering and its drink offering.
"On the second day: twelve young bulls, two rams, fourteen unblemished year-old male lambs;
"with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams and the lambs, by their number, according to the ordinance;
"and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the continual burnt offering and its grain offering, and their drink offerings.
"On the third day: eleven young bulls, two rams, fourteen unblemished year-old male lambs;
"with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams and the lambs, by their number, according to the ordinance;
"and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the continual burnt offering and its grain offering and its drink offering.
"On the fourth day: ten young bulls, two rams, fourteen unblemished year-old male lambs;
"with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams and the lambs, by their number, according to the ordinance;
"and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the continual burnt offering, its grain offering and its drink offering.
"On the fifth day: nine young bulls, two rams, fourteen unblemished year-old male lambs;
"with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams and the lambs, by their number, according to the ordinance;
"and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the continual burnt offering and its grain offering and its drink offering.
"On the sixth day: eight young bulls, two rams, fourteen unblemished year-old male lambs;
"with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams and the lambs, by their number, according to the ordinance;
"and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the continual burnt offering, its grain offering and its drink offerings.
"On the seventh day: seven young bulls, two rams, fourteen unblemished year-old male lambs;
"with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams and the lambs, by their number, according to their ordinance;
"and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the continual burnt offering, its grain offering and its drink offering.
"On the eighth day you shall have a solemn assembly; you shall do no occupational work.
"You shall present a burnt offering, a food offering, a soothing odour to the LORD: one young bull, one ram, seven unblemished year-old male lambs;
"with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bull, the ram and the lambs, by their number, according to the ordinance;
"and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the continual burnt offering and its grain offering and its drink offering.
"These you shall offer to the LORD at your appointed times, apart from your vows and freewill offerings — your burnt offerings, your grain offerings, your drink offerings and your peace offerings."
So Moses told the Israelites everything that the LORD had commanded Moses.

numbers_30.t: Moses spoke to the heads of the tribes of the Israelites: "This is the word that the LORD has commanded.
"When a man vows a vow to the LORD or swears an oath to bind an obligation on himself, he shall not break his word; he shall do according to all that goes out of his mouth.
"When a woman vows a vow to the LORD and binds an obligation on herself in her father's house in her youth,

"and her father hears of her vow and the obligation she has bound on herself, and her father says nothing to her — then all her vows shall stand, and every obligation she has bound on herself shall stand.
"But if her father forbids her on the day he hears of it, none of her vows or the obligations she has bound on herself shall stand; and the LORD will forgive her, because her father forbade her.
"If she does marry while her vows are upon her, or the rash utterance of her lips by which she has bound herself,
"and her husband hears of it on the day he hears and says nothing to her — then her vows shall stand, and the obligations by which she has bound herself shall stand.
"But if on the day her husband hears of it he forbids her and annuls the vow that is upon her and the rash utterance of her lips by which she has bound herself, then the LORD will forgive her.
"But the vow of a widow or a divorced woman — everything by which she has bound herself shall stand against her.
"If she vowed in her husband's house, or bound an obligation on herself by an oath,
"and her husband heard of it and said nothing to her and did not forbid her — then all her vows shall stand, and every obligation she bound on herself shall stand.

"But if her husband annuls them on the day he hears of it, nothing that has gone out of her lips, whether her vows or the obligation on herself, shall stand; her husband has annulled them, and the LORD will forgive her.
"Every vow and every binding oath to afflict herself, her husband may confirm or her husband may annul.

"But if her husband says nothing at all to her from day to day, then he has confirmed all her vows or all the obligations that are upon her; he has confirmed them, because he said nothing to her on the day he heard.
"But if he annuls them after he has heard, then he shall bear her iniquity.
These are the statutes that the LORD commanded Moses, between a man and his wife, and between a father and his daughter in her youth in her father's house.

numbers_31.t: The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Avenge the Israelites on the Midianites; afterward you shall be gathered to your kin."
So Moses spoke to the people: "Equip men from among you for the army, and let them go against Midian, to execute the LORD's vengeance on Midian.
"A thousand from each tribe, from all the tribes of Israel, you shall send out to the army."
So there were handed over from the thousands of Israel a thousand from each tribe: twelve thousand armed for the army.
Moses sent them out, a thousand from each tribe, to the army — them and Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest, with the articles of the holy place and the trumpets for the blast in his hand.
They waged war against Midian, as the LORD had commanded Moses, and killed every male.
They killed the kings of Midian along with the rest of their slain: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, the five kings of Midian; and they killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword.
The Israelites took the women of Midian captive with their little ones, and they plundered all their cattle, all their livestock, and all their wealth.
They burned with fire all their cities where they lived and all their encampments.
They took all the spoil and all the booty, both people and livestock.
They brought the captives, the booty and the spoil to Moses, to Eleazar the priest, and to the congregation of the Israelites, at the camp in the plains of Moab, at the Jordan across from Jericho.
Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the leaders of the congregation went out to meet them outside the camp.
But Moses was angry with the officers of the force, the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, who were coming in from the campaign.
Moses said to them, "Have you let every female live?"
"These were the ones who, by Balaam's word, led the Israelites to act unfaithfully against the LORD in the matter of Peor, and the plague came upon the congregation of the LORD.
"Now then, kill every male among the little ones, and kill every woman who has known a man by lying with a male.
"But all the young among the women who have not known lying with a male, keep alive for yourselves.

"And you, camp outside the camp for seven days. Everyone who has killed a person and everyone who has touched a slain one shall purify himself on the third day and on the seventh day, you and your captives.
"And every garment, every article of hide, everything made of goats' hair, and every article of wood you shall purify.
Eleazar the priest said to the men of the army who had gone into the battle, "This is the statute of the law that the LORD commanded Moses.
"Only the gold and the silver, the bronze, the iron, the tin and the lead —

"everything that can go into the fire you shall pass through the fire, and it shall be clean; nevertheless it must also be purified with the water to remove impurity. And everything that cannot go into the fire you shall pass through the water.
"You shall wash your clothes on the seventh day and be clean, and afterward you may come into the camp."
The LORD said to Moses:
"Take the sum of the booty that was taken, both people and livestock — you and Eleazar the priest and the heads of the ancestral houses of the congregation.
"You shall divide the booty in half between the fighting men who went out to the army and the whole congregation.
"You shall raise a levy for the LORD from the men of war who went out to the army: one out of every five hundred, from the people, the cattle, the donkeys and the sheep.
"You shall take it from their half and give it to Eleazar the priest as a contribution to the LORD.

"From the Israelites' half you shall take one drawn out of every fifty, from the people, the cattle, the donkeys, the sheep, from all the livestock, and give them to the Levites who keep the charge of the tabernacle of the LORD."
Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The booty, beyond the plunder the men of the army had taken for themselves, came to: 675,000 sheep,
72,000 cattle,
61,000 donkeys,
and 32,000 people — the women who had not known lying with a male.
The half that was the portion of those who went out with the army came to: 337,500 sheep,
and the levy for the LORD from the sheep was 675;
the cattle were 36,000, and their levy for the LORD was 72;
the donkeys were 30,500, and their levy for the LORD was 61;
and the people were 16,000, and their levy for the LORD was 32 persons.
Moses gave the levy, the LORD's contribution, to Eleazar the priest, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
As for the Israelites' half, which Moses had divided off from the men who went to war —
the congregation's half was 337,500 sheep,
36,000 cattle,
30,500 donkeys,
and 16,000 people.

Moses took from the Israelites' half the one drawn out of every fifty, from the people and from the livestock, and gave them to the Levites who keep the charge of the tabernacle of the LORD, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then the officers who were over the thousands of the army drew near to Moses — the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds —
and said to Moses, "Your servants have taken the sum of the men of war who were in our charge, and not one of us is missing.
"So we have presented the LORD's offering — each of us what he found, articles of gold: armlets, bracelets, signet rings, earrings and necklaces — to make atonement for ourselves before the LORD."
Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold from them, all of it worked articles.
All the gold of the contribution that they raised for the LORD came to 16,750 shekels, from the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds.
The men of the army had each taken plunder for himself.
Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold from the commanders of thousands and of hundreds and brought it into the tent of meeting, as a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD.

numbers_32.t: The descendants of Reuben and the descendants of Gad had a great deal of livestock, very numerous. When they saw the land of Jazer and the land of Gilead, the place was indeed a place for livestock.
So the descendants of Gad and the descendants of Reuben came and said to Moses, to Eleazar the priest, and to the leaders of the congregation:
"Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo and Beon —
"the land that the LORD struck down before the congregation of Israel — it is a land for livestock, and your servants have livestock."
They said, "If we have found favour in your eyes, let this land be given to your servants as a possession; do not make us cross the Jordan."
But Moses said to the descendants of Gad and the descendants of Reuben, "Shall your brothers go to battle while you sit here?"
"Why do you turn the hearts of the Israelites away from crossing into the land that the LORD has given them?
"This is what your fathers did when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to see the land.
"They went up as far as the Wadi Eshcol and saw the land, and they turned the hearts of the Israelites away, so that they would not go into the land that the LORD had given them.
"The anger of the LORD burned on that day, and he swore an oath:
"'Surely the men who came up from Egypt, from twenty years old and upward, shall not see the land that I swore to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob — because they have not followed me fully.'"
"except Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and Joshua son of Nun, for they followed the LORD fully.
"So the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he made them wander in the wilderness for forty years, until the whole generation that had done evil in the eyes of the LORD was finished.
"And here you have risen up in place of your fathers, a brood of sinful men, to add still more to the burning anger of the LORD against Israel.
"For if you turn back from following him, he will once more leave them in the wilderness, and you will have destroyed this entire people."
Then they drew near to him and said, "We will build sheepfolds here for our livestock and cities for our little ones,

"and we ourselves will arm and go in haste ahead of the Israelites until we have brought them to their place. Our little ones shall live in the fortified cities, because of the inhabitants of the land.
"We will not return to our houses until the Israelites have each inherited their inheritance.
"For we will not inherit with them on the far side of the Jordan and beyond, because our inheritance has come to us on this side of the Jordan, to the east."
Moses said to them, "If you do this thing — if you arm yourselves before the LORD for the battle,
"and every armed man among you crosses the Jordan before the LORD until he has dispossessed his enemies before him,

"and the land is subdued before the LORD, and afterward you return — then you shall be clear of obligation before the LORD and before Israel, and this land shall be yours as a possession before the LORD.
"But if you do not do so, then you have sinned against the LORD; and know that your sin will find you out.
"Build cities for your little ones and folds for your sheep, and do what has gone out of your mouth."
The descendants of Gad and the descendants of Reuben said to Moses, "Your servants will do just as my lord commands.
"Our little ones, our wives, our livestock and all our cattle shall stay there, in the cities of Gilead.
"But your servants will cross over, every man armed for the army, before the LORD to the battle, just as my lord says."
So Moses gave orders concerning them to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua son of Nun, and to the heads of the ancestral houses of the tribes of the Israelites.

Moses said to them, "If the descendants of Gad and the descendants of Reuben cross the Jordan with you, every man armed for battle before the LORD, and the land is subdued before you, then you shall give them the land of Gilead as a possession.
"But if they do not cross over armed with you, then they shall receive their possession among you in the land of Canaan."
The descendants of Gad and the descendants of Reuben answered, "What the LORD has spoken to your servants, that is what we will do.
"We ourselves will cross over armed before the LORD into the land of Canaan, and the possession of our inheritance shall remain ours on this side of the Jordan."

So Moses gave them — the descendants of Gad, the descendants of Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph — the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan: the land with its cities within their borders, the cities of the land round about.
The descendants of Gad built Dibon, Ataroth and Aroer,
Atroth-shophan, Jazer and Jogbehah,
Beth-nimrah and Beth-haran — fortified cities and sheepfolds.
The descendants of Reuben built Heshbon, Elealeh and Kiriathaim,
and Nebo and Baal-meon — their names being changed — and Sibmah; and they gave names to the cities they built.
The descendants of Machir son of Manasseh went to Gilead and captured it, and dispossessed the Amorites who were there.
So Moses gave Gilead to Machir son of Manasseh, and he settled in it.
Jair son of Manasseh went and captured their tent-villages, and he called them Havvoth-jair.
And Nobah went and captured Kenath and its dependent villages, and called it Nobah, after his own name.

numbers_33.t: These are the stages of the Israelites, who came out of the land of Egypt by their divisions, by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
Moses wrote down their points of departure stage by stage, at the command of the LORD; and these are their stages, by their points of departure.
They set out from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month. On the day after the Passover the Israelites went out with a high hand, before the eyes of all Egypt,
while the Egyptians were burying those whom the LORD had struck down among them, every firstborn; and on their gods the LORD had executed judgements.
The Israelites set out from Rameses and camped at Succoth.
They set out from Succoth and camped at Etham, on the edge of the wilderness.
They set out from Etham, turned back to Pi-hahiroth, which faces Baal-zephon, and camped before Migdol.
They set out from before Hahiroth, passed through the middle of the sea into the wilderness, went a three days' journey in the wilderness of Etham, and camped at Marah.
They set out from Marah and came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there.
They set out from Elim and camped by the Sea of Reeds.
They set out from the Sea of Reeds and camped in the wilderness of Sin.
They set out from the wilderness of Sin and camped at Dophkah.
They set out from Dophkah and camped at Alush.
They set out from Alush and camped at Rephidim, where there was no water for the people to drink.
They set out from Rephidim and camped in the wilderness of Sinai.
They set out from the wilderness of Sinai and camped at Kibroth-hattaavah.
They set out from Kibroth-hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth.
They set out from Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.
They set out from Rithmah and camped at Rimmon-perez.
They set out from Rimmon-perez and camped at Libnah.
They set out from Libnah and camped at Rissah.
They set out from Rissah and camped at Kehelathah.
They set out from Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shepher.
They set out from Mount Shepher and camped at Haradah.
They set out from Haradah and camped at Makheloth.
They set out from Makheloth and camped at Tahath.
They set out from Tahath and camped at Terah.
They set out from Terah and camped at Mithkah.
They set out from Mithkah and camped at Hashmonah.
They set out from Hashmonah and camped at Moseroth.
They set out from Moseroth and camped at Bene-jaakan.
They set out from Bene-jaakan and camped at Hor-haggidgad.
They set out from Hor-haggidgad and camped at Jotbathah.
They set out from Jotbathah and camped at Abronah.
They set out from Abronah and camped at Ezion-geber.
They set out from Ezion-geber and camped in the wilderness of Zin, that is, Kadesh.
They set out from Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor, on the border of the land of Edom.

Aaron the priest went up Mount Hor at the command of the LORD and died there, in the fortieth year after the Israelites came out of the land of Egypt, in the fifth month, on the first day of the month.
Aaron was a hundred and twenty-three years old when he died on Mount Hor.
And the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev in the land of Canaan, heard that the Israelites were coming.
They set out from Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah.
They set out from Zalmonah and camped at Punon.
They set out from Punon and camped at Oboth.
They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim, on the border of Moab.
They set out from Iyim and camped at Dibon-gad.
They set out from Dibon-gad and camped at Almon-diblathaim.
They set out from Almon-diblathaim and camped in the mountains of the Abarim, before Nebo.
They set out from the mountains of the Abarim and camped in the plains of Moab, at the Jordan across from Jericho.
They camped by the Jordan from Beth-jeshimoth as far as Abel-shittim, in the plains of Moab.
The LORD spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab, at the Jordan across from Jericho:
"Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
"you shall dispossess all the inhabitants of the land before you, destroy all their figured stones and all their cast-metal images, and demolish all their high places.
"You shall take possession of the land and settle in it, for I have given you the land to possess.

"You shall apportion the land by lot according to your clans: to the large you shall give a large inheritance, and to the small a small one. Wherever the lot falls for anyone, that shall be his. You shall inherit by your ancestral tribes.

"But if you do not dispossess the inhabitants of the land before you, then those of them you leave shall be thorns in your eyes and pricks in your sides, and they shall be hostile to you in the land where you live.
"And it shall be that as I intended to do to them, I will do to you."

numbers_34.t: The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Command the Israelites and say to them: When you come into the land of Canaan, this is the land that shall fall to you as an inheritance, the land of Canaan with its borders:
"Your southern side shall run from the wilderness of Zin along the edge of Edom; your southern border shall begin at the end of the Salt Sea, on the east.
"The border shall turn south of the Ascent of Akrabbim, pass on toward Zin, and end south of Kadesh-barnea; then it shall go out to Hazar-addar and pass on toward Azmon.
"The border shall turn from Azmon toward the Wadi of Egypt, and end at the sea.
"For the western border, the Great Sea shall be your border; this shall be your western border.
"This shall be your northern border: from the Great Sea you shall mark out a line to Mount Hor.
"From Mount Hor you shall mark out a line to Lebo-hamath, and the border shall end at Zedad.
"The border shall go out to Ziphron and end at Hazar-enan. This shall be your northern border.
"For your eastern border you shall mark out a line from Hazar-enan to Shepham.
"The border shall go down from Shepham to Riblah, east of Ain; then it shall go down and reach the slope of the Sea of Kinnereth on the east.
"The border shall go down to the Jordan and end at the Salt Sea. This shall be your land with its borders all round."
Moses commanded the Israelites: "This is the land you shall inherit by lot, which the LORD has commanded to be given to the nine tribes and the half-tribe.
For the tribe of the Reubenites by their ancestral house and the tribe of the Gadites by their ancestral house have taken theirs, and the half-tribe of Manasseh has taken its inheritance.
The two tribes and the half-tribe have taken their inheritance across the Jordan from Jericho, eastward toward the sunrise.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"These are the names of the men who shall apportion the land to you as an inheritance: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.
"And you shall take one leader from each tribe to apportion the land as an inheritance.
"These are the names of the men: of the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
"of the tribe of Simeon, Shemuel son of Ammihud;
"of the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad son of Chislon;
"of the tribe of Dan, a leader: Bukki son of Jogli;
"of the descendants of Joseph: of the tribe of Manasseh, a leader: Hanniel son of Ephod;
"of the tribe of Ephraim, a leader: Kemuel son of Shiphtan;
"of the tribe of Zebulun, a leader: Elizaphan son of Parnach;
"of the tribe of Issachar, a leader: Paltiel son of Azzan;
"of the tribe of Asher, a leader: Ahihud son of Shelomi;
"of the tribe of Naphtali, a leader: Pedahel son of Ammihud."
These are the ones whom the LORD commanded to apportion the inheritance to the Israelites in the land of Canaan.

numbers_35.t: The LORD spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab, at the Jordan across from Jericho:
"Command the Israelites to give the Levites, out of the inheritance they possess, cities to live in; and you shall give the Levites pasture land around those cities.
"The cities shall be theirs to live in, and their pasture lands shall be for their cattle, their property, and all their animals.
"The pasture lands of the cities that you give the Levites shall extend from the city wall outward a thousand cubits all round.

"You shall measure outside the city: the east side two thousand cubits, the south side two thousand cubits, the west side two thousand cubits, and the north side two thousand cubits, with the city in the middle. This shall be theirs, the pasture lands of the cities.
"The cities you give the Levites shall be the six cities of refuge, which you shall give for the killer to flee to, and in addition to them forty-two cities.
"All the cities you give the Levites shall be forty-eight cities, with their pasture lands.

"The cities you give from the possession of the Israelites shall be taken in proportion: from the large, more; from the small, fewer. Each tribe shall give some of its cities to the Levites according to the inheritance it receives."
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
"you shall provide yourselves cities to be cities of refuge for you, and a killer who has struck a person down unintentionally shall flee there.
"The cities shall be a refuge for you from the avenger, so that the killer shall not die until he has stood before the congregation for judgement.
"The cities you give shall be six cities of refuge for you.
"Three cities you shall give on the far side of the Jordan and three cities in the land of Canaan; they shall be cities of refuge.
"These six cities shall be a refuge for the Israelites, for the sojourner and for the resident alien among them, so that anyone who strikes a person down unintentionally may flee there.
"But if he struck him with an iron instrument so that he died, he is a killer; the killer shall surely be put to death.
"If he struck him with a hand-held stone by which a person may die, so that he died, he is a killer; the killer shall surely be put to death.
"Or if he struck him with a hand-held wooden instrument by which a person may die, so that he died, he is a killer; the killer shall surely be put to death.
"The avenger of blood shall himself put the killer to death; when he meets him, he shall put him to death.
"If he pushed him in hatred, or threw something at him while lying in wait, so that he died,
"or struck him with his hand in enmity so that he died, the one who struck him shall surely be put to death; he is a killer. The avenger of blood shall put the killer to death when he meets him.
"But if he pushed him suddenly, without enmity, or threw any object at him without lying in wait,
"or with any stone by which a person may die, without seeing him, and he dropped it on him so that he died — while he was not his enemy and was not seeking to harm him —
"then the congregation shall judge between the one who struck and the avenger of blood, according to these rules.

"The congregation shall deliver the killer from the hand of the avenger of blood, and the congregation shall return him to his city of refuge where he had fled; and he shall live in it until the death of the high priest who was anointed with the holy oil.
"But if the killer ever goes beyond the border of the city of refuge to which he fled,
"and the avenger of blood finds him outside the border of his city of refuge, and the avenger of blood kills the killer, there is no blood-guilt for him.
"For he must stay in his city of refuge until the death of the high priest; and after the death of the high priest the killer may return to the land of his possession.
"These shall be a statute of judgement for you throughout your generations, in all your dwelling places.
"Anyone who strikes a person down shall be killed on the testimony of witnesses; but no one shall be put to death on the testimony of a single witness.
"You shall not take a ransom for the life of a killer who is guilty and deserves to die; he shall surely be put to death.
"And you shall not take a ransom for one who has fled to his city of refuge, allowing him to return and live in the land before the death of the priest.
"You shall not pollute the land where you are, for blood pollutes the land; and no atonement can be made for the land, for the blood shed in it, except by the blood of the one who shed it.
"You shall not make unclean the land where you live, in the midst of which I dwell; for I, the LORD, dwell in the midst of the Israelites."

numbers_36.t: The heads of the ancestral houses of the clan of the descendants of Gilead son of Machir son of Manasseh, from the clans of the descendants of Joseph, drew near and spoke before Moses and before the leaders, the heads of the ancestral houses of the Israelites.

They said, "The LORD commanded my lord to give the land as an inheritance by lot to the Israelites, and my lord was commanded by the LORD to give the inheritance of Zelophehad our brother to his daughters.

"But if they become wives to men from another of the tribes of the Israelites, their inheritance will be withdrawn from the inheritance of our fathers and added to the inheritance of the tribe they marry into; and it will be withdrawn from the lot of our inheritance.

"And when the jubilee comes for the Israelites, their inheritance will be added to the inheritance of the tribe they marry into, and their inheritance will be withdrawn from the inheritance of our fathers' tribe."
So Moses commanded the Israelites at the command of the LORD: "The tribe of Joseph's descendants speaks rightly.
"This is the word that the LORD has commanded concerning the daughters of Zelophehad: Let them marry whomever is good in their eyes — only, they must marry within the clan of their father's tribe.
"An inheritance of the Israelites shall not pass round from tribe to tribe; each of the Israelites shall cling to the inheritance of his fathers' tribe.

"Every daughter who possesses an inheritance from the tribes of the Israelites shall marry one of the clan of her father's tribe, so that each of the Israelites may possess the inheritance of his fathers.
"An inheritance shall not pass round from one tribe to another, for the tribes of the Israelites shall each cling to its own inheritance."
The daughters of Zelophehad did just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah and Noah, the daughters of Zelophehad, married the sons of their uncles.
They married within the clans of the descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, and their inheritance remained with the tribe of their father's clan.
These are the commandments and the judgements that the LORD commanded by the hand of Moses to the Israelites in the plains of Moab, at the Jordan across from Jericho.

obadiah_1.t: The vision of Obadiah. This is what Lord GOD says concerning Edom: We have heard a report from the LORD, and an envoy has been sent among the nations: "Rise up, and let us rise against her for battle!"
Look, I have made you small among the nations; you are utterly despised.
The presumption of your heart has deceived you, you who dwell in the clefts of the rock, whose dwelling is set high, who say in your heart, "Who will bring me down to the ground?"
If you set yourself high like the eagle, and if your nest is placed among the stars, from there I will bring you down — declares the LORD.
If thieves came to you, if plunderers by night — how you have been destroyed! — would they not steal only as much as they wanted? If grape-gatherers came to you, would they not leave gleanings?
How Esau has been ransacked, his hidden treasures hunted out!

They have driven you to the border, all the men of your covenant; they have deceived you, they have overpowered you, the men of your peace. Your bread — they set a snare beneath you. There is no understanding in him.
On that day — declares the LORD — will I not destroy the wise out of Edom, and understanding from the mountain of Esau?
Your warriors will be dismayed, Teman, so that everyone will be cut off from the mountain of Esau by slaughter.
Because of the violence done to your brother Jacob, shame will cover you, and you will be cut off for ever.
On the day you stood aloof, on the day strangers carried off his wealth and foreigners entered his gates and cast lots over Jerusalem — you too were like one of them.
Do not look on your brother's day, the day of his misfortune; do not rejoice over the people of Judah on the day they perish; do not talk big on the day of distress.
Do not enter the gate of my people on the day of their disaster; do not look, you too, on his calamity on the day of his disaster; do not reach out for his wealth on the day of his disaster.
Do not stand at the parting of the ways to cut off his fugitives; do not hand over his survivors on the day of distress.
For the day of the LORD is near upon all the nations. As you have done, it will be done to you; your recompense will come back on your own head.
For as you have drunk on my holy mountain, all the nations will drink continually; they will drink and swallow, and they will be as though they had never been.
But on Mount Zion there will be deliverance, and it will be a holy place, and the house of Jacob will take possession of their own possessions.

The house of Jacob will be a fire, the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau stubble; they will burn among them and consume them, and there will be no survivor left to the house of Esau — for the LORD has spoken.

Those of the Negev will take possession of the mountain of Esau, and those of the Shephelah of the Philistines; they will take possession of the region of Ephraim and the region of Samaria, and Benjamin of the Gilead.

And the exiles of this rampart, the people of Israel, who are among the Canaanites as far as Zarephath, and the exiles of Jerusalem who are in Sepharad, will take possession of the cities of the Negev.
And deliverers will go up on Mount Zion to judge the mountain of Esau, and the kingship will belong to the LORD.

proverbs_1.t: The proverbs of Solomon son of David, king of Israel:
To know wisdom and discipline, to understand sayings of understanding;
to receive the discipline that gives insight, righteousness, justice, and equity;
to give shrewdness to the naive, knowledge and discretion to the young —
Let the wise listen and gain in learning, and let the discerning acquire guidance —
to understand a proverb and a figure, the words of the wise and their riddles.
The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge; fools despise wisdom and discipline.
Listen, my son, to your father's discipline, and do not reject your mother's law.
For they are a wreath of favour for your head and a necklace for your neck.
My son, if sinners entice you, do not consent.
If they say, "Come with us, let us lie in wait for blood, let us lurk for the innocent without cause;
let us swallow them alive, like Sheol, and whole, like those who go down to the pit;
we shall find all kinds of precious wealth, we shall fill our houses with plunder;
throw in your lot with us; we shall all share one purse" —
My son, do not walk in the way with them; hold your foot back from their path.
For their feet run to evil, and they hurry to shed blood.
For the net is spread in vain in the sight of any winged thing.
And they lie in wait for their own blood; they lurk for their own lives.
Such are the ways of everyone greedy for unjust gain: it takes the life of those who hold it.
Wisdom cries aloud in the street; in the open squares she raises her voice.
At the head of the noisy streets she calls out; at the entrances of the gates in the city she speaks her sayings:
"How long, you naive ones, will you love being naive? And mockers delight in mockery, and dullards hate knowledge.
If you turn back at my reproof, see, I will pour out my spirit to you; I will make my words known to you.
Because I called and you refused, I stretched out my hand and no one paid attention,
and you let all my counsel go, and you did not want my reproof —
I also will laugh at your calamity; I will mock when what you dread comes,
when what you dread comes like a devastation and your calamity arrives like a storm-wind, when trouble and distress come upon you.
Then they will call me and I will not answer; they will search hard for me and will not find me,
because they hated knowledge and did not choose the fear of the LORD.
They did not want my counsel; they spurned all my reproof.
So they will eat from the fruit of their way and have their fill of their own schemes.
For the turning away of the naive will kill them, and the complacency of dullards will destroy them.
But whoever listens to me will dwell in security and be at ease, without dread of harm."

proverbs_2.t: My son, if you receive my sayings and store up my commandments within you,
making your ear attend to wisdom, turning your heart towards discernment;
if indeed you call out for understanding and raise your voice for discernment;
if you seek her like silver and search for her like hidden treasure,
then you will understand the fear of the LORD and find the knowledge of God.
For the LORD gives wisdom; from his mouth come knowledge and discernment.
He stores up sound sense for the upright, a shield for those who walk in integrity,
guarding the paths of justice and preserving the way of his godly ones.
Then you will understand righteousness and justice and equity, every good course.
For wisdom will come into your heart, and knowledge will be pleasant to you;
discretion will watch over you; discernment will preserve you,
to deliver you from the way of evil, from anyone who speaks perversity,
those who leave the paths of uprightness to walk in the ways of darkness,
those who are glad to do evil and exult in the perversity of evil,
whose paths are twisted and who are crooked in their tracks —
to deliver you from the forbidden woman, from the adulteress who makes her sayings smooth,
who leaves the companion of her youth and has forgotten the covenant of her God;
for her house sinks down to death, and her tracks lead to the shades.
None who go in to her return, nor do they reach the paths of life.
So you will walk in the way of the good and keep to the paths of the righteous.
For the upright will dwell in the land, and the blameless will remain in it;
but the wicked will be cut off from the land, and the treacherous will be torn away from it.

proverbs_3.t: My son, do not forget my law, and let your heart keep my commandments;
for they will add to you length of days, years of life, and peace.
Do not let steadfast love and faithfulness leave you; bind them on your neck, write them on the tablet of your heart.
and you will find favour and good repute in the eyes of God and of people.
Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and do not lean on your own understanding.
In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight.
Do not be wise in your own eyes; fear the LORD and turn away from evil.
It will be healing to your body and refreshment to your bones.
Honour the LORD with your wealth and with the first of all your produce,
and your storehouses will be filled with plenty, and your vats will burst with new wine.
My son, do not reject the discipline of the LORD, and do not loathe his reproof;
for the LORD reproves the one he loves, as a father does the son he delights in.
How blessed is the person who finds wisdom, the person who obtains discernment!
For the profit from her is better than profit from silver, and her gain better than fine gold.
She is more precious than corals, and nothing you delight in compares with her.
Length of days is in her right hand; in her left hand are wealth and honour.
Her ways are ways of kindness, and all her pathways are peace.
She is a tree of life to those who take hold of her, and those who hold her fast are called blessed.
The LORD founded the earth by wisdom; he established the heavens by discernment;
by his knowledge the deeps were split open, and the clouds drip down dew.
My son, do not let them slip from your sight; keep sound sense and discretion,
and they will be life to you and an ornament at your neck.
Then you will walk your way in security, and your foot will not stumble.
If you lie down, you will not be afraid; you will lie down and your sleep will be pleasant.
Do not be afraid of sudden terror, or of the devastation of the wicked when it comes,
for the LORD will be your confidence and will keep your foot from being caught.
Do not withhold good from those it belongs to when it is in your power to do it.
Do not say to your neighbour, "Go and come back, and tomorrow I will give it" — when you have it with you.
Do not devise harm against your neighbour when he lives beside you in security.
Do not contend with anyone without cause, if he has done you no evil.
Do not envy a violent person, and do not choose any of his ways.
For the crooked person is an abomination to the LORD, but his confidence is with the upright.
The curse of the LORD is on the house of the wicked, but he blesses the dwelling of the righteous.
Though he mocks the mockers, he gives favour to the humble.
The wise will inherit honour, but dullards get disgrace for their portion.

proverbs_4.t: Listen, children, to a father's discipline, and pay attention, so as to know understanding;
for I give you good learning; do not abandon my law.
For I was a son to my father, tender, and the only one in my mother's sight.
And he taught me and said to me: "Let your heart hold fast to my words; keep my commandments and live.
Acquire wisdom, acquire understanding; do not forget and do not turn aside from the sayings of my mouth.
Do not abandon her, and she will keep you; love her, and she will guard you.
The beginning of wisdom is this: acquire wisdom, and with all you acquire, acquire understanding.
Prize her, and she will exalt you; she will honour you when you embrace her.
She will set a wreath of favour on your head; she will bestow on you a crown of beauty."
Listen, my son, and receive my sayings, and the years of your life will be many.
I have taught you in the way of wisdom; I have led you in tracks of uprightness.
When you walk, your step will not be hindered; and if you run, you will not stumble.
Take hold of discipline, do not let go; keep her, for she is your life.
Do not go on the path of the wicked, and do not walk in the way of the evil.
Avoid it, do not pass along it; turn away from it and go on.
For they cannot sleep unless they do harm; their sleep is snatched away unless they make someone stumble.
For they eat the bread of wickedness and drink the wine of violence.
But the path of the righteous is like the light of dawn, shining brighter and brighter until the day is full.
The way of the wicked is like deep darkness; they do not know what they stumble over.
My son, pay attention to my words; incline your ear to my sayings.
Do not let them slip from your sight; keep them in the midst of your heart.
For they are life to those who find them and health to the whole body.
Above all that you guard, guard your heart, for from it flow the sources of life.
Put crookedness of mouth away from yourself, and put deviousness of lips far from you.
Let your eyes look straight ahead, and your gaze be fixed straight before you.
Make level the track of your foot, and all your ways will be secure.
Do not turn aside to the right or to the left; turn your foot away from evil.

proverbs_5.t: My son, pay attention to my wisdom; incline your ear to my discernment,
so that you may preserve discretion and your lips may keep knowledge.
For the lips of the strange woman drip honey, and her mouth is smoother than oil;
but in the end she is bitter as wormwood, sharp as a two-edged sword.
Her feet go down to death; her steps take hold of Sheol.
She does not make the path of life level; her tracks wander, and she does not know it.
And now, children, listen to me, and do not turn away from the sayings of my mouth.
Keep your way far from her, and do not go near the entrance of her house,
lest you give your vigour to others and your years to someone cruel;
lest strangers have their fill of your strength, and your labours end up in a foreigner's house;
and you groan at your end, when your flesh and your body waste away,
and you say, "How I hated discipline, and my heart spurned reproof!
and I did not listen to the voice of my instructors, and did not incline my ear to my teachers.
I came to almost every calamity in the midst of the assembly and the congregation."
Drink water from your own cistern, running water from your own well.
Should your springs overflow into the street, your channels of water into the open squares?
Let them be yours, yours alone, and not for strangers along with you.
Let your spring be blessed, and rejoice in the wife of your youth,
a loving doe, a graceful mountain goat. Let her breasts satisfy you at all times; be intoxicated always by her love.
And why should you go astray, my son, with a strange woman and embrace the bosom of a foreign woman?
For a man's ways are before the eyes of the LORD, and he weighs out all his tracks.
The wicked man's own iniquities will seize him, and he will be held fast by the cords of his sin.
He will die for lack of discipline, and in his great folly he will go astray.

proverbs_6.t: My son, if you have stood surety for your neighbour, if you have struck hands for a stranger,
you have been ensnared by the sayings of your mouth, you have been caught by the sayings of your mouth.
Do this, then, my son, and deliver yourself, for you have come into your neighbour's hand: go, humble yourself, and press your neighbour hard.
Do not give sleep to your eyes or slumber to your eyelids.
Deliver yourself like a gazelle from a hunter's hand, like a bird from the hand of a fowler.
Go to the ant, sluggard; consider her ways and become wise.
which has no commander, no officer and no ruler,
yet she prepares her bread in the summer and gathers her food at the harvest.
How long, sluggard, will you lie there? When will you rise from your sleep?
A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest —
and your poverty will come like a traveller, your want like an armed man.
A worthless person, a man of wickedness, goes about with a crooked mouth,
winking with his eyes, shuffling his feet, pointing with his fingers,
with perversity in his heart, devising evil all the time, sending out contentions.
Therefore his disaster will come suddenly; in an instant he will be broken, and there will be no healing.
There are six things the LORD hates, seven that are an abomination to him:
haughty eyes, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood,
a heart that devises plans of wickedness, feet that hurry to run to evil,
a false witness who breathes out lies, and one who sends out contentions between brothers.
Keep your father's commandment, my son, and do not forsake your mother's law.
Bind them on your heart continually; tie them around your neck.
When you walk about, it will guide you; when you lie down, it will watch over you; and when you awake, it will speak with you.
For the commandment is a lamp and the law a light, and the reproofs of discipline are a way of life,
to keep you from the evil woman, from the smooth tongue of the foreign woman.
Do not desire her beauty in your heart, and do not let her capture you with her eyelids.
For a prostitute brings a man down to a loaf of bread, but another man's wife hunts down a precious life.
Can a man scoop fire into his lap and his clothes not be burned?
Or can a man walk on burning coals and his feet not be scorched?
So is the one who goes in to his neighbour's wife: no one who touches her will go unpunished.
People do not despise a thief if he steals to fill his appetite when he is hungry;
yet if he is found out he must repay sevenfold; he will give all the wealth of his house.
Whoever commits adultery with a woman lacks sense; the one who does it destroys himself.
He will find a wound and disgrace, and his reproach will not be wiped away.
For jealousy rouses a man's rage, and he will not spare on the day of vengeance.
He will not accept any ransom, and he will not consent, however great a bribe you offer.

proverbs_7.t: My son, keep my sayings, and store up my commandments within you.
Keep my commandments and live, and keep my law like the pupil of your eye.
Bind them on your fingers; write them on the tablet of your heart.
Say to wisdom, "You are my sister," and call understanding your kinswoman,
to keep you from the strange woman, from the foreign woman who makes her sayings smooth.
For at the window of my house, through my lattice, I looked down,
and I saw among the naive, I noticed among the young men a youth lacking sense,
passing along the street beside her corner, and he strode along the way to her house,
at twilight, at the evening of the day, in the depth of night and darkness.
And there was a woman coming to meet him, dressed as a prostitute and guarded of heart.
She is boisterous and rebellious; her feet will not stay at home.
Now in the street, now in the open squares, and beside every corner she lies in wait.
She takes hold of him and kisses him; with a bold face she says to him:
"Sacrifices of peace offerings were due from me; today I have paid my vows.
That is why I came out to meet you, to seek your face — and I have found you.
I have spread coverings on my couch, coloured fabrics, linen of Egypt.
I have sprinkled my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.
Come, let us drink our fill of love until morning; let us take our delight in love.
For the man is not at home; he has gone on a long journey.
He took the bag of silver with him; he will come home at the full moon."
She turns him aside with her great persuasiveness; with the smoothness of her lips she drives him on.
He goes after her at once, like an ox going to the slaughter, like a stag caught fast in a fetter —
until an arrow pierces its liver; as a bird hurries into a trap, and does not know that it will cost him his life.
And now, children, listen to me, and pay attention to the sayings of my mouth.
Do not let your heart turn aside to her ways; do not stray into her pathways.
For many are those she has struck down, and numerous are all those she has killed.
Her house is the way to Sheol, going down to the chambers of death.

proverbs_8.t: Does not wisdom call out, and discernment raise her voice?
At the top of the heights, beside the way, at the crossroads she takes her stand.
Beside the gates, at the mouth of the town, at the entrance of the doorways, she cries aloud:
"To you, O people, I call, and my voice goes out to the children of humankind.
You naive, learn shrewdness; you dullards, learn sense.
Listen, for I will speak noble things, and what my lips open with will be equity.
For my mouth will utter truth, and wickedness is an abomination to my lips.
All the sayings of my mouth are in righteousness; there is nothing twisted or crooked in them.
They are all plain to the one who discerns, and upright to those who find knowledge.
Take my discipline and not silver, knowledge rather than choice gold.
For wisdom is better than corals, and nothing you may delight in compares with her.
I, wisdom, dwell with shrewdness, and I find knowledge and discretion.
The fear of the LORD is to hate evil. Pride and arrogance, the way of evil, and a mouth of perversity — I hate them.
Counsel is mine, and sound sense; I am understanding; strength is mine.
