By me kings reign, and rulers decree righteousness;
by me princes rule, and nobles, all who judge with righteousness.
I love those who love me, and those who search hard for me find me.
Wealth and honour are with me, enduring wealth and righteousness.
My fruit is better than fine gold, even than pure gold, and my yield better than choice silver.
I walk in the path of righteousness, in the midst of the pathways of justice,
to give substance as an inheritance to those who love me, and to fill their treasuries.
The LORD brought me forth at the beginning of his way, before his works, from of old.
From long ago I was set in place, from the beginning, from the earliest times of the earth.
When there were no deeps I was brought forth, when there were no springs heavy with water.
Before the mountains were sunk into place, before the hills, I was brought forth —
while he had not yet made the earth and its open places, nor the first of the dusts of the world.
When he established the heavens, I was there; when he marked out a circle on the face of the deep,
when he made firm the clouds above, when the springs of the deep grew strong,
when he set the sea its limit, so that the waters should not overstep his command, when he marked out the foundations of the earth —
then I was beside him, a master craftsman, and I was his delight day by day, playing before him always,
playing in the world of his earth, and my delight was in the children of humankind.
And now, children, listen to me: how blessed are those who keep my ways!
Listen to discipline and be wise, and do not neglect it.
How blessed is the person who listens to me, watching at my doors day after day, keeping watch at the posts of my doorways!
For whoever finds me finds life and obtains favour from the LORD;
but whoever misses me does violence to himself; all who hate me love death."

proverbs_9.t: Wisdom has built her house; she has hewn out her seven pillars.
She has butchered her meat, she has mixed her wine, and she has set her table.
She has sent out her young women; she calls from the high points of the town:
"Whoever is naive, let him turn in here!" To the one who lacks sense she says:
"Come, eat of my bread and drink of the wine I have mixed.
Leave naivety behind and live; walk straight on in the way of understanding."
Whoever admonishes a mocker takes disgrace for himself, and whoever reproves a wicked person gets a defect of his own.
Do not reprove a mocker, or he will hate you; reprove a wise person, and he will love you.
Give to a wise person, and he will be wiser still; teach a righteous person, and he will gain in learning.
The start of wisdom is the fear of the LORD, and the knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.
For by me your days will increase, and years of life will be added to you.
If you are wise, you are wise for yourself; and if you mock, you alone will bear it.
The woman Dullness is boisterous — all naivety, and she knows nothing at all.
And she sits at the doorway of her house, on a seat at the high points of the town,
to call to those who pass by on the road, who are making their paths straight:
"Whoever is naive, let him turn in here!" And to the one who lacks sense she says:
"Stolen water is sweet, and bread eaten in secret is delightful."
And he does not know that the shades are there, that her guests are in the depths of Sheol.

proverbs_10.t: The proverbs of Solomon. A wise son makes a father glad, and a dull son is his mother's grief.
Treasures of wickedness do not profit, but righteousness delivers from death.
The LORD does not let the righteous go hungry, but he thrusts aside the craving of the wicked.
A slack hand makes a person poor, but the hand of the diligent makes rich.
A son who gathers in summer acts with insight; a son who sleeps through harvest acts shamefully.
Blessings are on the head of the righteous, but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.
The memory of the righteous is a blessing, but the name of the wicked will rot.
The wise of heart accepts commandments, but a babbling fool will be ruined.
Whoever walks in integrity walks in security, but whoever makes his ways crooked will be found out.
Whoever winks an eye causes pain, but a babbling fool will be ruined.
The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life, but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.
Hatred stirs up contentions, but love covers over all transgressions.
On the lips of the discerning wisdom is found, but a rod is for the back of one who lacks sense.
The wise store up knowledge, but the mouth of a fool is ruin close at hand.
The wealth of the rich is their fortified town; the ruin of the poor is their poverty.
The wage of the righteous leads to life; the yield of the wicked leads to sin.
Whoever keeps discipline is a path to life, but whoever abandons reproof leads others astray.
Whoever conceals hatred has lying lips, and whoever spreads slander is a dullard.
Where words are many, transgression does not cease, but whoever restrains his lips acts with insight.
The tongue of the righteous is choice silver; the heart of the wicked is worth little.
The lips of the righteous feed many, but fools die for lack of sense.
The blessing of the LORD makes rich, and he adds no sorrow with it.
Doing depravity is sport to a dullard, and wisdom is sport to a person of discernment.
What the wicked dreads will come upon him, but the desire of the righteous will be granted.
When the storm-wind passes, the wicked is no more, but the righteous is a foundation that lasts.
Like vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes, so is the sluggard to those who send him.
The fear of the LORD adds days, but the years of the wicked will be cut short.
The expectation of the righteous is joy, but the hope of the wicked will perish.
The way of the LORD is a stronghold to the blameless, but ruin to those who do wickedness.
The righteous will never be shaken, but the wicked will not dwell in the land.
The mouth of the righteous bears wisdom as its fruit, but a perverse tongue will be cut off.
The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable, but the mouth of the wicked is perversity.

proverbs_11.t: Scales of deceit are an abomination to the LORD, but an accurate weight is his delight.
When insolence comes, disgrace comes; but with the modest is wisdom.
The integrity of the upright guides them, but the distortion of the treacherous destroys them.
Wealth does not profit in the day of fury, but righteousness delivers from death.
The righteousness of the blameless makes his way straight, but by his own wickedness the wicked falls.
The righteousness of the upright delivers them, but the treacherous are caught by their own craving.
At the death of a wicked person hope is lost, and the expectation founded on strength perishes.
The righteous is drawn out of distress, and the wicked comes in his place.
With his mouth the godless ruins his neighbour, but by knowledge the righteous are delivered.
When the righteous prosper, a town rejoices, and when the wicked perish there is a shout of joy.
By the blessing of the upright a town is exalted, but by the mouth of the wicked it is torn down.
Whoever despises his neighbour lacks sense, but a person of discernment keeps quiet.
Whoever goes about as a talebearer reveals a confidence, but one faithful in spirit conceals a matter.
Where there is no guidance a people falls, but deliverance is in a multitude of counsellors.
Whoever stands surety for a stranger will surely suffer for it, but one who hates striking hands is secure.
A gracious woman lays hold of honour, and the ruthless lay hold of wealth.
A loyal person does himself good, but a cruel one troubles his own body.
The wicked earns a wage of falsehood, but one who sows righteousness earns a true wage.
Righteousness truly leads to life, and whoever pursues evil goes to his own death.
Those perverse of heart are an abomination to the LORD, but those blameless in their way are his delight.
Be assured of it: the evil will not go unpunished, but the offspring of the righteous will be delivered.
A gold ring in a pig's snout — that is a beautiful woman who turns aside from discretion.
The desire of the righteous is only good; the hope of the wicked is fury.
There is one who scatters and gains still more, and one who withholds what is due, only to come to want.
A generous person will be enriched, and whoever gives water will himself be watered.
The people curse whoever withholds grain, but a blessing is on the head of the one who sells it.
Whoever earnestly seeks good seeks favour, but whoever searches out evil — it will come upon him.
Whoever trusts in his wealth will fall, but the righteous will flourish like green leaves.
Whoever troubles his household will inherit wind, and a fool will be servant to the wise of heart.
The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and the wise wins people over.
See, the righteous is repaid on the earth — how much more the wicked and the sinner!

proverbs_12.t: Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge, but whoever hates reproof is a brute.
A good person obtains favour from the LORD, but a man of schemes he condemns.
No one is established by wickedness, but the root of the righteous will not be moved.
A capable wife is her husband's crown, but one who acts shamefully is like rot in his bones.
The plans of the righteous are justice; the counsel of the wicked is deceit.
The words of the wicked lie in wait for blood, but the mouth of the upright delivers them.
The wicked are overthrown and are no more, but the house of the righteous will stand.
A person is praised according to his insight, but one perverted of heart will be held in contempt.
Better to be lightly esteemed and have a servant than to honour oneself and lack food.
The righteous knows the needs of his animal, but the compassion of the wicked is cruel.
Whoever works his ground will have plenty of food, but whoever pursues worthless things lacks sense.
The wicked covets the stronghold of evil men, but the root of the righteous yields fruit.
In the transgression of the lips is an evil snare, but the righteous comes out of trouble.
From the fruit of his mouth a person is filled with good, and what a person's hands have dealt out returns to him.
The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, but whoever listens to counsel is wise.
A fool's vexation is known the same day, but whoever conceals an insult is shrewd.
Whoever breathes out faithfulness declares what is right, but a false witness declares deceit.
There is one whose rash speech is like sword thrusts, but the tongue of the wise is healing.
Truthful lips are established for ever, but a lying tongue lasts only a moment.
Deceit is in the heart of those who devise evil, but those who counsel peace have joy.
No trouble befalls the righteous, but the wicked are full of distress.
Lying lips are an abomination to the LORD, but those who act in faithfulness are his delight.
A shrewd person conceals knowledge, but the heart of dullards proclaims folly.
The hand of the diligent will rule, but slackness ends in forced labour.
Anxiety in a person's heart weighs it down, but a good word makes it glad.
The righteous is a guide to his neighbour, but the way of the wicked leads them astray.
The slack man does not roast what he has hunted, but a diligent person's wealth is precious.
In the path of righteousness is life, and along that pathway there is no death.

proverbs_13.t: A wise son heeds a father's discipline, but a mocker does not listen to a rebuke.
From the fruit of his mouth a person eats good, but the appetite of the treacherous is violence.
Whoever guards his mouth keeps his life; whoever opens his lips wide comes to ruin.
The sluggard's appetite craves and gets nothing, but the appetite of the diligent is well fed.
The righteous hates a lying word, but the wicked acts odiously and comes to shame.
Righteousness guards the one whose way is blameless, but wickedness overthrows the sinner.
There is one who pretends to be rich and has nothing, and one who pretends to be poor and has great wealth.
A person's wealth is the ransom of his life, but a poor person hears no threat.
The light of the righteous shines brightly, but the lamp of the wicked will be put out.
Insolence brings nothing but contention, but with those who take counsel is wisdom.
Wealth got from nothing dwindles, but whoever gathers little by little increases it.
Expectation drawn out makes the heart sick, but a desire fulfilled is a tree of life.
Whoever despises a word will be held in pledge to it, but whoever fears a commandment will be rewarded.
The law of the wise is a fountain of life, turning one aside from the snares of death.
Good insight gives favour, but the way of the treacherous is their ruin.
Every shrewd person acts with knowledge, but a dullard spreads out his folly.
A wicked messenger falls into trouble, but a faithful envoy brings healing.
Poverty and disgrace come to whoever lets discipline go, but whoever keeps reproof will be honoured.
A desire fulfilled is pleasant to a person, but turning away from evil is an abomination to dullards.
Whoever walks with the wise becomes wise, but the companion of dullards will be harmed.
Calamity pursues sinners, but the righteous are repaid with good.
A good person leaves an inheritance to his children's children, but the wealth of a sinner is stored up for the righteous.
Much food is in the fallow ground of the poor, but some is swept away for want of justice.
Whoever withholds his rod hates his son, but whoever loves him is diligent to discipline him.
The righteous eats to the satisfying of his appetite, but the belly of the wicked goes empty.

proverbs_14.t: The wisest of women builds her house, but folly tears it down with her own hands.
Whoever walks in his uprightness fears the LORD, but whoever is crooked in his ways despises him.
In the mouth of a fool is a rod of pride, but the lips of the wise preserve them.
Where there are no cattle the manger is clean, but much produce comes by the strength of an ox.
A faithful witness does not lie, but a false witness breathes out lies.
A mocker seeks wisdom and finds none, but knowledge comes easily to the discerning.
Get away from a dull person, for you will not find lips of knowledge there.
The wisdom of the shrewd is to understand his own way, but the folly of dullards is deceit.
Fools scoff at the guilt offering, but among the upright there is favour.
The heart knows its own bitterness, and a stranger does not share its joy.
The house of the wicked will be destroyed, but the tent of the upright will flourish.
There is a way that seems right to a person, but its end is the ways of death.
Even in laughter a heart may ache, and the end of that joy is grief.
The backslidden of heart will have his fill of his own ways, and a good man of what is his own.
A naive person believes every word, but a shrewd one considers his step.
A wise person fears and turns away from evil, but a dullard rages on, sure of himself.
One quick to anger does folly, and a man of schemes is hated.
The naive inherit folly, but the shrewd are crowned with knowledge.
The evil bow before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.
Even by his neighbour the poor is hated, but the rich have many friends.
Whoever despises his neighbour sins, but how blessed is the one who shows favour to the humble!
Do those who devise evil not go astray? But loyalty and faithfulness belong to those who devise good.
In all hard labour there is profit, but mere talk leads only to want.
The crown of the wise is their wealth; the folly of dullards is folly.
A truthful witness delivers lives, but one who breathes out lies brings deceit.
In the fear of the LORD is strong confidence, and for his children there will be a refuge.
The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, turning one aside from the snares of death.
In a multitude of people is a king's glory, but without a people a ruler is ruined.
One slow to anger has great discernment, but one short of temper exalts folly.
A tranquil heart is the life of the body, but jealousy is rot in the bones.
Whoever oppresses the poor reproaches his Maker, but whoever shows favour to the needy honours him.
In his own evil the wicked is thrust down, but the righteous finds refuge even in his death.
In the heart of the discerning wisdom rests, and even among dullards it makes itself known.
Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin is a disgrace to any people.
A king's favour goes to a servant who acts with insight, but his fury to one who acts shamefully.

proverbs_15.t: A soft answer turns away rage, but a hurtful word stirs up anger.
The tongue of the wise commends knowledge, but the mouth of dullards pours out folly.
In every place are the eyes of the LORD, watching the evil and the good.
A healing tongue is a tree of life, but distortion in it breaks the spirit.
A fool spurns his father's discipline, but whoever keeps reproof is shrewd.
In the house of the righteous is great store, but the income of the wicked brings trouble.
The lips of the wise scatter knowledge, but the heart of dullards is not so.
The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to the LORD, but the prayer of the upright is his delight.
The way of the wicked is an abomination to the LORD, but he loves whoever pursues righteousness.
Harsh discipline awaits whoever forsakes the path; whoever hates reproof will die.
Sheol and Abaddon are before the LORD — how much more the hearts of the children of humankind!
A mocker does not love being reproved; he will not go to the wise.
A joyful heart brightens the face, but by sorrow of heart the spirit is stricken.
A discerning heart seeks knowledge, but the mouth of dullards grazes on folly.
All the days of the afflicted are wretched, but a cheerful heart has a feast continually.
Better a little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure and turmoil with it.
Better a dish of vegetables where there is love than a fattened ox and hatred with it.
A hot-tempered man stirs up strife, but one slow to anger quiets a dispute.
The way of the sluggard is like a thorn hedge, but the path of the upright is a raised road.
A wise son makes a father glad, but a dullard despises his mother.
Folly is a joy to one who lacks sense, but a person of discernment walks straight ahead.
Plans are frustrated where there is no counsel, but with many counsellors they stand.
A person has joy in the answer of his mouth, and a word in its time — how good it is!
The path of life leads upward for the one with insight, so that he turns aside from Sheol beneath.
The LORD tears down the house of the proud, but he sets firm the boundary of a widow.
The plans of an evil person are an abomination to the LORD, but sayings of kindness are pure.
Whoever takes unjust gain troubles his own house, but whoever hates bribes will live.
The heart of the righteous considers how to answer, but the mouth of the wicked pours out evils.
The LORD is far from the wicked, but he hears the prayer of the righteous.
The light of the eyes makes the heart glad; good news puts fat on the bones.
An ear that hears life-giving reproof will lodge among the wise.
Whoever lets discipline go rejects himself, but whoever heeds reproof acquires sense.
The fear of the LORD is the discipline of wisdom, and humility comes before honour.

proverbs_16.t: The arrangements of the heart belong to a person, but from the LORD comes the answer of the tongue.
All a person's ways are pure in his own eyes, but the LORD weighs the spirits.
Roll your works onto the LORD, and your plans will be established.
The LORD has made everything for its purpose, and even the wicked for a day of calamity.
Everyone haughty of heart is an abomination to the LORD; be assured of it, he will not go unpunished.
By loyalty and faithfulness iniquity is atoned for, and by the fear of the LORD one turns away from evil.
When the LORD is pleased with a person's ways, he makes even his enemies be at peace with him.
Better a little with righteousness than great gains without justice.
A person's heart plans his way, but the LORD directs his steps.
An oracle is on a king's lips; in judgement his mouth does not break faith.
An honest balance and scales are the LORD's; all the weights in the bag are his work.
Doing wickedness is an abomination to kings, for by righteousness a throne is established.
Righteous lips are a king's delight, and he loves whoever speaks what is upright.
A king's rage is a messenger of death, but a wise person will appease it.
In the light of a king's face is life, and his favour is like a cloud of spring rain.
To acquire wisdom — how much better than fine gold! And to acquire understanding is better than silver.
The highway of the upright is to turn away from evil; whoever guards his way keeps his life.
Pride comes before a breaking, and haughtiness of spirit before a stumbling.
Better to be lowly of spirit with the humble than to divide plunder with the proud.
Whoever gives attention to a word will find good, and how blessed is the one who trusts in the LORD!
The wise of heart will be called discerning, and sweetness of speech increases learning.
Insight is a fountain of life to whoever has it, but the discipline of fools is folly.
The heart of the wise gives insight to his mouth and increases the learning on his lips.
Sayings of kindness are a honeycomb: sweet to the person and healing to the bones.
There is a way that seems right to a person, but its end is the ways of death.
A labourer's appetite labours for him, for his mouth presses him on.
A worthless person digs up evil, and on his lips is a scorching fire.
A perverse person sends out strife, and a slanderer separates close companions.
A violent man entices his neighbour and leads him in a way that is not good.
Whoever shuts his eyes is devising perversity; whoever purses his lips has accomplished evil.
Grey hair is a crown of splendour; it is found in the way of righteousness.
Better one slow to anger than a warrior, and one who rules his own spirit than one who captures a city.
The lot is cast into the lap, but every decision it gives is from the LORD.

proverbs_17.t: Better a dry morsel with quietness than a house full of feasting with strife.
A servant who acts with insight will rule over a son who acts shamefully, and will share the inheritance among the brothers.
A crucible is for silver and a furnace for gold, but the LORD tests hearts.
An evildoer pays attention to wicked lips; a liar gives ear to a destroying tongue.
Whoever mocks the poor reproaches his Maker; whoever is glad at calamity will not go unpunished.
The crown of the old is their children's children, and the splendour of children is their parents.
Fine speech is not fitting for a boor — how much less lying speech for a noble!
A bribe is a charm in the eyes of the one who gives it; wherever he turns, he prospers.
Whoever covers over a transgression seeks love, but whoever repeats a matter separates close companions.
A rebuke goes deeper into one who understands than a hundred blows into a dullard.
An evil person seeks only rebellion, and a cruel messenger will be sent against him.
Better to meet a bear robbed of her cubs than a dullard in his folly.
Whoever returns evil for good — evil will not depart from his house.
Starting a quarrel is like letting out water; abandon the dispute before it breaks out.
Whoever justifies the wicked and whoever condemns the righteous — both alike are an abomination to the LORD.
Why should there be a price in a dullard's hand to buy wisdom, when he has no sense?
A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.
A person who lacks sense strikes hands, giving a pledge before his neighbour.
Whoever loves transgression loves contention; whoever builds his gateway high seeks a breaking.
One twisted of heart does not find good, and one perverted in his tongue falls into trouble.
Whoever begets a dullard begets grief for himself, and the father of a boor has no joy.
A joyful heart is good medicine, but a stricken spirit dries up the bones.
A wicked person takes a bribe from the fold of a garment to turn aside the paths of judgement.
Wisdom is right before the face of one who understands, but the eyes of a dullard are at the ends of the earth.
A dull son is a vexation to his father and bitterness to the one who bore him.
To fine the righteous is not good, nor to strike nobles for their uprightness.
Whoever restrains his sayings knows knowledge, and one precious of spirit is a person of discernment.
Even a fool who keeps silent is reckoned wise; one who shuts his lips is reckoned discerning.

proverbs_18.t: Whoever separates himself seeks his own desire; he bursts out against all sound sense.
A dullard takes no delight in discernment, only in laying bare his own heart.
When a wicked person comes, contempt comes too, and with disgrace comes reproach.
The words of a person's mouth are deep waters; the fountain of wisdom is a flowing stream.
To show partiality to the wicked is not good, nor to turn the righteous aside in judgement.
A dullard's lips get him into strife, and his mouth calls out for a beating.
A dullard's mouth is his ruin, and his lips are a snare to his life.
The words of a slanderer are like delicacies; they go down into the chambers of the belly.
One who is slack in his work is brother to a destroyer.
The name of the LORD is a strong tower; the righteous runs into it and is set on high.
The wealth of the rich is their fortified town, and like a high wall — in their own imagination.
Before a breaking a person's heart is haughty, but humility comes before honour.
Whoever answers before he has listened — it is folly for him, and ignominy.
A person's spirit will sustain him in sickness, but a stricken spirit — who can bear it?
A discerning heart acquires knowledge, and the ear of the wise seeks knowledge.
A person's gift makes room for him and brings him before the great.
The first to state his case seems right, until his neighbour comes and examines him.
The lot puts an end to contentions and separates powerful opponents.
A brother wronged is harder to win than a fortified town, and contentions are like the bar of a fortress.
From the fruit of his mouth a person's belly is filled; with the produce of his lips he is filled.
Death and life are in the power of the tongue, and those who love it will eat its fruit.
Whoever finds a wife finds a good thing and obtains favour from the LORD.
A poor person speaks in supplications, but a rich one answers roughly.
A person with many companions may come to ruin, but there is a friend who clings closer than a brother.

proverbs_19.t: Better a poor person who walks in his integrity than one perverse of speech who is a dullard.
A person without knowledge is not good, and one who hurries with his feet misses the way.
A person's folly subverts his way, and then his heart rages against the LORD.
Wealth adds many friends, but a poor person is separated even from his friend.
A false witness will not go unpunished, and whoever breathes out lies will not escape.
Many entreat the favour of a noble, and everyone is a friend to one who gives gifts.
All a poor person's brothers hate him — how much more do his friends keep far from him! He pursues sayings; they are his.
Whoever acquires sense loves himself; whoever keeps discernment will find good.
A false witness will not go unpunished, and whoever breathes out lies will perish.
Luxury is not fitting for a dullard — how much less for a servant to rule over princes!
A person's insight makes him slow to anger, and it is his splendour to pass over a transgression.
A king's rage is like the roar of a young lion, but his favour is like dew on grass.
A dull son is his father's ruin, and a wife's contentions are a continual dripping.
House and wealth are an inheritance from parents, but a prudent wife is from the LORD.
Laziness makes deep sleep fall, and a slack person will go hungry.
Whoever keeps a commandment keeps his life; whoever despises his ways will die.
Whoever shows favour to the poor lends to the LORD, and he will repay him what is due.
Discipline your son, for there is hope, but do not set your desire on putting him to death.
A man of great rage bears the penalty; for if you rescue him, you will have to do it again.
Listen to counsel and accept discipline, so that you may be wise in the end.
Many are the plans in a person's heart, but it is the counsel of the LORD that will stand.
What is desired in a person is steadfast love, and better a poor person than a liar.
The fear of the LORD leads to life; one rests satisfied, untouched by harm.
A sluggard buries his hand in the dish; he will not even bring it back to his mouth.
Strike a mocker and the naive will learn shrewdness; reprove one who is discerning and he will understand knowledge.
Whoever assaults a father and drives out a mother is a son who brings shame and disgrace.
Cease, my son, to listen to discipline, and you will stray from the sayings of knowledge.
A worthless witness mocks justice, and the mouth of the wicked swallows wickedness down.
Judgements are prepared for mockers, and blows for the backs of dullards.

proverbs_20.t: Wine is a mocker, strong drink is a brawler, and no one who staggers under it is wise.
A king's terror is like the roar of a young lion; whoever enrages him forfeits his own life.
It is an honour for a person to keep clear of strife, but every fool bursts out.
After winter the sluggard does not plough; he asks at harvest and there is nothing.
Counsel in a person's heart is deep waters, but a person of discernment draws it out.
Many a person proclaims his own loyalty, but a faithful person — who can find one?
The righteous goes about in his integrity — how blessed are his children after him!
A king seated on the throne of judgement winnows all evil with his eyes.
Who can say, "I have kept my heart pure; I am pure from my sin"?
Two kinds of weight and two kinds of measure — both alike are an abomination to the LORD.
Even a youth is known by his deeds, whether what he does is pure and upright.
An ear that hears and an eye that sees — the LORD has made both alike.
Do not love sleep, or you will become poor; open your eyes and you will have plenty of food.
"Bad, bad," says the buyer; and when he goes away, then he boasts.
There is gold, and corals in abundance, but lips of knowledge are a precious thing.
Take the garment of one who has stood surety for a stranger, and hold it in pledge for a foreign woman.
Bread got by falsehood is sweet to a person, but afterwards his mouth is filled with gravel.
Plans are established by counsel; and wage war by guidance.
Whoever goes about as a talebearer uncovers confidences; so do not get involved with one whose lips are always open.
Whoever curses his father or his mother — his lamp will be put out in deep darkness.
An inheritance gained hastily at first — its end will not be blessed.
Do not say, "I will repay evil"; wait for the LORD, and he will deliver you.
Two kinds of weight are an abomination to the LORD, and deceitful scales are not good.
A man's steps are from the LORD; how then can a person understand his own way?
It is a snare for a person to declare something holy rashly and only after the vows to reconsider.
A wise king winnows the wicked and drives the threshing wheel over them.
The breath of a human being is the lamp of the LORD, searching all the chambers of the belly.
Loyalty and faithfulness preserve a king, and he upholds his throne by loyalty.
The splendour of young men is their strength, and the honour of the old is grey hair.
Wounds that bruise scour away evil, and blows reach the chambers of the belly.

proverbs_21.t: A king's heart is a channel of water in the LORD's hand; he turns it wherever he desires.
Every way of a person is upright in his own eyes, but the LORD weighs hearts.
To do righteousness and justice is chosen by the LORD above sacrifice.
Haughty eyes and an arrogant heart — the tillage of the wicked is sin.
The plans of the diligent lead only to advantage, but everyone who is hasty comes only to want.
Getting treasures by a lying tongue is a driven vapour — and a seeking of death.
The violence of the wicked will drag them away, because they refuse to do justice.
The way of a guilty person is crooked, but the pure — his work is upright.
Better to live on a corner of the roof than share a house with a contentious wife.
The appetite of a wicked person craves evil; his neighbour finds no favour in his eyes.
When a mocker is punished, the naive becomes wise; and when a wise person is instructed, he takes in knowledge.
The Righteous One considers the house of the wicked and brings the wicked down to calamity.
Whoever shuts his ear to the cry of the poor will himself call out and not be answered.
A gift given in secret subdues anger, and a bribe in the bosom, strong rage.
Doing justice is a joy to the righteous, but ruin to those who do wickedness.
A person who wanders from the way of insight will come to rest in the assembly of the shades.
Whoever loves pleasure will come to want; whoever loves wine and oil will not grow rich.
The wicked becomes a ransom for the righteous, and the treacherous take the place of the upright.
Better to live in a wilderness land than with a contentious and vexing wife.
Desirable treasure and oil are in the dwelling of the wise, but a dullard swallows them up.
Whoever pursues righteousness and loyalty finds life, righteousness, and honour.
A wise person scales a city of warriors and brings down the stronghold it trusted in.
Whoever guards his mouth and his tongue keeps himself out of trouble.
Proud, arrogant — "Mocker" is his name, one who acts in an overflow of insolence.
The desire of a sluggard kills him, because his hands refuse to work.
All day long he craves and craves, but the righteous gives and does not hold back.
The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination — how much more when he brings it with depravity!
A false witness will perish, but one who listens will speak on and be heard.
A wicked person puts on a bold face, but an upright one considers his way.
There is no wisdom, no discernment, and no counsel that can stand against the LORD.
A horse is prepared for the day of battle, but the deliverance belongs to the LORD.

proverbs_22.t: A good name is to be chosen above great wealth, and favour above silver and gold.
The rich and the poor meet together; the LORD is the maker of them all.
A shrewd person sees trouble and hides himself, but the naive pass on and are punished.
The reward of humility, the fear of the LORD, is wealth and honour and life.
Thorns and snares are in the way of the perverse; whoever guards himself keeps far from them.
Train a youth in the way he should go, and even when he is old he will not turn from it.
The rich rules over the poor, and the borrower is servant to the lender.
Whoever sows unrighteousness will reap trouble, and the rod of his fury will come to an end.
The generous will be blessed, for he gives of his bread to the poor.
Drive out a mocker and strife goes out with him; dispute and disgrace cease.
Whoever loves purity of heart and has grace on his lips will have the king as his friend.
The eyes of the LORD preserve knowledge, but he overturns the words of the treacherous.
The sluggard says, "There is a lion outside! I shall be murdered in the open squares!"
The mouth of the strange woman is a deep pit; one cursed by the LORD falls into it.
Folly is bound up in the heart of a youth; the rod of discipline drives it far from him.
Whoever oppresses the poor to increase his own wealth, and whoever gives to the rich, come only to want.
The Words of the Wise Incline your ear and hear the words of the wise, and set your heart to my knowledge;
for it is pleasant if you keep them within you and they are ready together on your lips.
so that your trust may be in the LORD, I have made it known to you today — to you.
Have I not written thirty of them for you, with counsels and knowledge,
to make known to you the truth of sayings of faithfulness, so that you may bring back sayings of faithfulness to those who send you?
Do not rob the poor because he is poor, and do not crush the afflicted at the gate,
for the LORD will conduct their case and will rob of life those who rob them.
Do not make friends with a hot-tempered man, and do not go about with a man of rages,
lest you learn his ways and take a snare for yourself.
Do not be among those who strike hands, among those who stand surety for debts.
If you have nothing to pay with, why should your bed be taken from under you?
Do not move an ancient boundary that your ancestors set.
Do you see a person skilled in his work? He will take his stand before kings; he will not stand before obscure men.

proverbs_23.t: When you sit down to eat with a ruler, consider carefully what is before you,
and put a knife to your throat if you are a man of large appetite.
Do not crave his dainties, for it is deceptive food.
Do not wear yourself out to grow rich; have the sense to stop.
Will you set your eyes on it, and it is gone? For it surely makes itself wings and flies off to the heavens like an eagle.
Do not eat the food of the stingy, and do not crave his dainties,
for as he calculates within himself, so is he. "Eat and drink," he says to you, but his heart is not with you.
The morsel you have eaten you will vomit up, and you will have wasted your pleasant words.
Do not speak in the ears of a dullard, for he will despise the insight of your words.
Do not move an ancient boundary, and do not enter the fields of the fatherless,
for their Redeemer is strong; he will conduct their case against you.
Bring your heart to discipline and your ears to sayings of knowledge.
Do not withhold discipline from a youth; if you strike him with the rod he will not die.
You strike him with the rod and deliver his life from Sheol.
My son, if your heart is wise, my own heart will rejoice;
and my inmost self will exult when your lips speak what is upright.
Do not let your heart envy sinners, but be in the fear of the LORD all day long;
for surely there is a future, and your hope will not be cut off.
Listen, my son, and be wise, and guide your heart in the way.
Do not be among those who drink wine deep, among those who gorge themselves on meat;
for the deep drinker and the glutton will become poor, and drowsiness clothes a man in rags.
Listen to your father who begot you, and do not despise your mother when she is old.
Buy truth and do not sell it — wisdom, discipline, and understanding.
The father of a righteous son will greatly rejoice, and whoever begets a wise son will rejoice in him.
Let your father and your mother rejoice, and let her who bore you be glad.
Give me your heart, my son, and let your eyes keep to my ways.
For a prostitute is a deep pit, and a foreign woman a narrow well.
She also lies in wait like a robber and multiplies the treacherous among people.
Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has contentions? Who has complaint? Who has wounds for nothing? Who has bloodshot eyes?
Those who linger over wine, who go looking for mixed wine.
Do not look at wine when it is red, when it sparkles in the cup, when it goes down smoothly.
In the end it bites like a snake and stings like a viper.
Your eyes will see strange things, and your heart will speak perversity.
You will be like one lying down in the heart of the sea, like one lying at the top of a mast.
"They struck me — I felt nothing; they beat me — I did not know it. When shall I wake? I will look for another."

proverbs_24.t: Do not envy evil people, and do not desire to be with them,
for their heart plots violence, and their lips speak trouble.
By wisdom a house is built, and by discernment it is established;
and by knowledge the rooms are filled with all precious and pleasant wealth.
A wise man is strong, and a person of knowledge increases strength.
For by guidance you will wage war, and deliverance lies in a multitude of counsellors.
Wisdom is too high for a fool; at the gate he does not open his mouth.
Whoever plans to do evil will be called a master of schemes.
The scheming of folly is sin, and a mocker is an abomination to people.
If you go slack in the day of trouble, your strength is small.
Deliver those being taken to death, and hold back those staggering to the slaughter.
If you say, "But we did not know this" — does not the one who weighs hearts perceive it? Does not the one who guards your life know? And he will repay each person according to his work.
Eat honey, my son, for it is good, and honey from the comb is sweet to your taste.
So know wisdom for yourself: if you find it, then there is a future, and your hope will not be cut off.
Do not lie in wait, wicked one, against the dwelling of the righteous; do not devastate his resting place,
for the righteous falls seven times and rises again, but the wicked stumble into calamity.
When your enemy falls, do not rejoice, and when he stumbles, do not let your heart be glad,
lest the LORD see it and it be evil in his eyes, and he turn his anger away from him.
Do not fret over evildoers; do not envy the wicked,
for the evil person has no future; the lamp of the wicked will be put out.
Fear the LORD, my son, and the king; do not get involved with those who change,
for their calamity will arise suddenly, and who knows the ruin that comes from them both?
These also are of the wise. To show partiality in judgement is not good.
Whoever says to the wicked, "You are righteous" — peoples will curse him and nations denounce him.
But for those who reprove, it will go well, and a rich blessing will come upon them.
Whoever gives a straight answer kisses the lips.
Get your work ready outside and make it ready for yourself in the field; afterwards build your house.
Do not be a witness without cause against your neighbour, and do not deceive with your lips.
Do not say, "As he has done to me, so I will do to him; I will repay him according to what he has done."
I passed by the field of a lazy person and by the vineyard of one who lacks sense,
and there it was, all grown over with thorns; its surface was covered with nettles, and its stone wall was broken down.
And I looked and set my heart to it; I saw, and I received instruction.
A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest —
and your poverty will come walking in, and your want like an armed man.

proverbs_25.t: These also are proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.
It is the glory of God to conceal a matter, and the glory of kings to search out a matter.
The heavens for height and the earth for depth, and the heart of kings — beyond searching out.
Remove the dross from silver, and a vessel comes out for the smith.
Remove the wicked from before a king, and his throne is established in righteousness.
Do not put yourself forward before a king, and do not stand in the place of the great;
for it is better that he say to you, "Come up here," than that you be put lower before a noble whom your own eyes have seen.
Do not rush out to litigate, for what will you do in the end when your neighbour puts you to shame?
Argue your case with your neighbour himself, and do not reveal another's confidence;
lest whoever hears it shame you, and the ill report of you never be undone.
Apples of gold in settings of silver: so is a word spoken at the right time.
A gold ring, an ornament of fine gold: so is a wise reprover to a listening ear.
Like the cold of snow in the day of harvest is a faithful envoy to those who send him: he restores the life of his masters.
Clouds and wind but no rain: so is a person who boasts of a gift he never gives.
By patience a ruler is persuaded, and a soft tongue breaks a bone.
Have you found honey? Eat only your fill, or you will have too much and vomit it up.
Let your foot be seldom in your neighbour's house, or he will have too much of you and hate you.
A war-club, a sword, a sharpened arrow: so is one who testifies against his neighbour as a false witness.
A broken tooth, a foot that slips: so is trust in a treacherous person in the day of trouble.
Taking off a garment on a cold day, vinegar poured on soda: so is singing songs to a heavy heart.
If your enemy is hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he is thirsty, give him water to drink.
for you will be heaping burning coals on his head, and the LORD will reward you.
The north wind brings forth rain, and a secretive tongue, angry faces.
Better to live on a corner of the roof than share a house with a contentious wife.
Cool water to a weary person: so is good news from a distant land.
A muddied spring, a ruined fountain: so is a righteous person who gives way before the wicked.
To eat much honey is not good, nor is it glorious to search out one's own glory.
A city broken into, left without a wall: so is a person with no control over his spirit.

proverbs_26.t: Like snow in summer and rain at harvest, so honour is not fitting for a dullard.
Like a bird in its flitting, like a swallow in flight, so a curse without cause does not come home.
A whip for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a rod for the back of dullards.
Do not answer a dullard according to his folly, or you will become like him yourself.
Answer a dullard according to his folly, or he will be wise in his own eyes.
Cutting off one's own feet, drinking violence: so is sending a message by the hand of a dullard.
The legs of a lame person hang limp: so is a proverb in the mouth of dullards.
Like binding a stone into a sling, so is giving honour to a dullard.
A thorn that comes up in a drunkard's hand: so is a proverb in the mouth of dullards.
Like an archer who wounds at random: so is one who hires a dullard or hires any passer-by.
Like a dog returning to its vomit, so is a dullard who repeats his folly.
Do you see a person wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a dullard than for him.
The sluggard says, "There is a lion in the road! A lion in the open squares!"
A door turns on its hinge, and a sluggard on his bed.
A sluggard buries his hand in the dish; he is too weary to bring it back to his mouth.
A sluggard is wiser in his own eyes than seven who can answer with discernment.
Taking a passing dog by the ears: so is one who meddles in a quarrel not his own.
Like a madman shooting firebrands, arrows and death,
so is a person who deceives his neighbour and says, "I was only joking!"
Without wood a fire goes out, and without a slanderer strife falls quiet.
Charcoal to burning coals and wood to fire: so is a contentious person for kindling strife.
The words of a slanderer are like delicacies; they go down into the chambers of the belly.
A glaze of silver dross over earthenware: so are fervent lips and an evil heart.
With his lips a hater disguises himself, and within himself he stores up deceit.
When he makes his voice gracious, do not trust him, for seven abominations are in his heart.
Hatred may cover itself with deception, but his wickedness will be revealed in the assembly.
Whoever digs a pit will fall into it, and whoever rolls a stone — it will come back on him.
A lying tongue hates those it crushes, and a flattering mouth works ruin.

proverbs_27.t: Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day will bring forth.
Let a stranger praise you, and not your own mouth; an outsider, and not your own lips.
A stone is heavy and sand is a burden, but a fool's provocation is heavier than both.
Rage is cruel and anger a flood, but who can stand before jealousy?
Better open reproof than hidden love.
The wounds of a friend are faithful, but the kisses of an enemy are profuse.
A full appetite tramples on honeycomb, but to a hungry appetite every bitter thing is sweet.
Like a bird straying from its nest, so is a person straying from his place.
Oil and perfume make the heart glad, and so does the sweetness of a friend's counsel.
Do not forsake your own friend or your father's friend, and do not go to your brother's house in the day of your calamity. Better a neighbour near by than a brother far off.
Be wise, my son, and make my heart glad, so that I may answer whoever taunts me.
A shrewd person sees trouble and hides himself; the naive pass on and are punished.
Take the garment of one who has stood surety for a stranger, and hold it in pledge for a foreign woman.
Whoever blesses his neighbour with a loud voice, rising early in the morning — it is reckoned to him as a curse.
A continual dripping on a day of steady rain and a contentious wife are alike.
To restrain her is to restrain the wind, or to grasp oil with the right hand.
Iron sharpens iron, and one person sharpens the face of another.
Whoever tends a fig tree will eat its fruit, and whoever guards his master will be honoured.
As water reflects face to face, so one person's heart reflects another.
Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied, and the eyes of a person are never satisfied.
A crucible for silver and a furnace for gold, and a person is tested by the praise he receives.
Though you pound a fool in a mortar, among the grain with a pestle, his folly will not leave him.
Know well the condition of your flock; set your heart on your herds.
For wealth does not last for ever, nor a crown to all generations.
The grass is gone and new growth appears, and the mountain vegetation is gathered in.
The lambs are for your clothing, and the goats the price of a field.
and enough goats' milk for your food, for the food of your household, and sustenance for your servant girls.

proverbs_28.t: The wicked flee with no one pursuing, but the righteous are as confident as a young lion.
When a land transgresses, its rulers are many, but under a person of understanding and knowledge order lasts.
A poor man who oppresses the poor is a driving rain that leaves no food.
Those who forsake law praise the wicked, but those who keep law contend against them.
Evil people do not understand justice, but those who seek the LORD understand it fully.
Better a poor person who walks in his integrity than one whose ways are perverse, though he is rich.
Whoever keeps law is a son of understanding, but whoever keeps company with gluttons shames his father.
Whoever increases his wealth by interest and usury gathers it for one who shows favour to the poor.
Whoever turns his ear from hearing law — even his prayer is an abomination.
Whoever leads the upright astray into an evil way will fall into his own pit, but the blameless will inherit good.
A rich person is wise in his own eyes, but a poor one with understanding sees through him.
When the righteous triumph there is great glory, but when the wicked arise, people go into hiding.
Whoever conceals his transgressions will not prosper, but whoever confesses and forsakes them will be shown mercy.
How blessed is the person who is always in fear, but whoever hardens his heart will fall into calamity.
A roaring lion, a charging bear: so is a wicked ruler over a poor people.
A ruler who lacks discernment is great in extortion, but whoever hates unjust gain will prolong his days.
A person burdened by the blood of another will flee to the pit; let no one support him.
Whoever walks blameless will be delivered, but whoever is crooked in his ways will fall suddenly.
Whoever tills his ground will have plenty of food, but whoever pursues empty things will have his fill of poverty.
A faithful person will abound in blessings, but whoever hastens to grow rich will not go unpunished.
To show partiality is not good, and for a piece of bread a man will transgress.
A stingy person hastens after wealth and does not know that poverty will come upon him.
Whoever reproves a person will in the end find more favour than one who flatters with his tongue.
Whoever robs his father or his mother and says, "It is no transgression," is a companion to a destroyer.
The greedy stir up strife, but whoever relies on the LORD will prosper.
Whoever trusts in his own heart is a dullard, but whoever walks in wisdom will escape.
Whoever gives to the poor will have no lack, but whoever hides his eyes will have many curses.
When the wicked arise, people hide themselves, but when they perish, the righteous increase.

proverbs_29.t: Whoever hardens his neck after many reproofs will suddenly be broken beyond healing.
When the righteous increase, the people rejoice, but when the wicked rule, a people groans.
Whoever loves wisdom makes his father glad, but whoever keeps company with prostitutes destroys his wealth.
A king by justice establishes a land, but one who exacts levies tears it down.
A man who flatters his neighbour spreads a net for his own footsteps.
In the transgression of an evil person is a snare, but the righteous sings out and rejoices.
The righteous knows the cause of the poor; the wicked does not understand knowledge.
Scoffing men set a town ablaze, but the wise turn away anger.
When a wise person goes to law with a fool, the fool rages and laughs, and there is no quiet.
Bloodthirsty men hate the blameless, and the upright seek his life.
A dullard lets out all his temper, but a wise person holds it back.
If a ruler listens to falsehood, all his officials become wicked.
The poor and the oppressor meet together; the LORD gives light to the eyes of them both.
A king who judges the poor with truth — his throne will be established for ever.
The rod and reproof give wisdom, but a youth left to himself shames his mother.
When the wicked increase, transgression increases, but the righteous will look on their downfall.
Discipline your son and he will give you rest; he will give delight to you.
Where there is no vision, the people run wild, but how blessed is the one who keeps law!
A servant is not disciplined by words alone, for he understands and yet does not answer.
Do you see a person hasty in his words? There is more hope for a dullard than for him.
Whoever pampers a servant from his youth will find him an heir in the end.
An angry person stirs up strife, and a hot-tempered one abounds in transgression.
A person's pride will bring him low, but the lowly in spirit will attain honour.
Whoever shares with a thief hates his own life; he hears the adjuration and does not tell.
Fear of others lays a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD will be set on high.
Many seek the face of a ruler, but a person's justice comes from the LORD.
An unjust person is an abomination to the righteous, and one whose way is upright is an abomination to the wicked.

proverbs_30.t: The words of Agur son of Jakeh. The oracle. The declaration of the man to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ukal.
For I am more brutish than anyone, and I have not the understanding of a human being.
And I have not learned wisdom, nor do I know the knowledge of the Holy One.

Who has gone up to the heavens and come down? Who has gathered the wind in his fists? Who has wrapped the waters in a cloak? Who has set up all the ends of the earth? What is his name, and what is his son's name, if you know?
All the speech of God is refined; he is a shield to those who take refuge in him.
Do not add to his words, or he will reprove you and you will be proved a liar.
Two things I ask of you; do not withhold them from me before I die:
Put falseness and lying words far from me; give me neither poverty nor wealth; feed me with the food that is my portion,
lest I be full and deny you, and say, "Who is the LORD?"; and lest I become poor and steal, and profane the name of my God.
Do not slander a servant to his master, or he will curse you and you will be held guilty.
There is a generation that curses its father and does not bless its mother;
there is a generation pure in its own eyes and not washed from its filth;
there is a generation — how haughty its eyes, how lifted up its eyelids;
there is a generation whose teeth are swords and whose jaws are knives, devouring the afflicted from the earth and the needy from among the living.
The leech has two daughters: "Give! Give!" There are three things that are never satisfied, four that never say "Enough":
Sheol, and a barren womb; land never satisfied with water, and fire, which never says "Enough".
The eye that mocks a father and despises obedience to a mother — the ravens of the valley will pluck it out, and the young eagles will eat it.
Three things there are that are too wonderful for me, and four that I do not know:
the way of an eagle in the heavens, the way of a snake on a rock, the way of a ship in the heart of the sea, and the way of a man with a young woman.
Such is the way of an adulterous woman: she eats and wipes her mouth and says, "I have done nothing wrong."
Under three things the earth quakes, and under four it cannot bear up:
a servant when he becomes king, and a boor when he is filled with food;
a hated woman when she is married, and a servant girl when she dispossesses her mistress.
Four things there are that are small on the earth, yet they are exceedingly wise:
the ants, a people without strength, yet they prepare their food in the summer;
rock badgers, a people without power, yet they make their home in the rock;
locusts have no king, yet they all go out in ranks;
the lizard you can catch in your hands, yet it is in the palaces of a king.
Three things there are that are stately in their stride, and four that are stately in their walk:
the lion, mightiest among the animals, which turns back before nothing;
a strutting cock, or a he-goat, and a king with his army about him.
If you have been foolish in exalting yourself, or if you have plotted evil — put your hand to your mouth!
For pressing milk brings forth butter, and pressing the nose brings forth blood, and pressing anger brings forth strife.

proverbs_31.t: The words of Lemuel the king. An oracle, with which his mother instructed him.
What, my son? What, son of my womb? What, son of my vows?
Do not give your strength to women, or your ways to those who destroy kings.
It is not for kings, Lemuel, not for kings to drink wine, nor for rulers to crave strong drink;
lest he drink and forget what has been decreed, and pervert the cause of all the afflicted.
Give strong drink to one who is perishing, and wine to those who are bitter in spirit;
let him drink and forget his poverty, and remember his trouble no more.
Open your mouth for the speechless, for the cause of all who are passing away.
Open your mouth, judge with righteousness, and plead the cause of the afflicted and the needy.
A capable wife — who can find one? Her worth is far beyond corals.
The heart of her husband trusts in her, and he lacks nothing of value.
She does him good and not evil all the days of her life.
She seeks out wool and flax and works with willing hands.
She is like a merchant's ships; from far off she brings her food.
She rises while it is still night and gives food to her household, and a portion to her servant girls.
She considers a field and buys it; from the fruit of her hands she plants a vineyard.
She girds her loins with strength and makes her arms strong.
She perceives that her trading is good; her lamp does not go out at night.
She stretches out her hands to the distaff, and her palms grasp the spindle.
She opens her palm to the afflicted and stretches out her hands to the needy.
She does not fear the snow for her household, for all her household is clothed in scarlet.
She makes coverings for herself; her clothing is fine linen and purple.
Her husband is known in the gates, when he sits with the elders of the land.
She makes linen garments and sells them, and supplies belts to the merchants.
Strength and honour are her clothing, and she laughs at the days to come.
She opens her mouth with wisdom, and the law of kindness is on her tongue.
She watches over the ways of her household and does not eat the bread of idleness.
Her children rise up and call her blessed; her husband also, and he praises her:
"Many daughters have done capably, but you have surpassed them all."
Favour is deceptive and beauty is vapour; a woman who fears the LORD — she will be praised.
Give her of the fruit of her hands, and let her works praise her in the gates.

psalms_1.t: How blessed is the person who has not walked in the counsel of the wicked, and has not stood in the way of sinners, and has not sat in the seat of mockers;
but his delight is in the law of the LORD, and over his law he murmurs day and night.
He is like a tree planted by streams of water, which gives its fruit in its time, and its leaf does not wither; and everything he does prospers.
Not so the wicked; they are like chaff that the wind drives away.
Therefore the wicked will not stand in the judgement, nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous.
For the LORD knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked perishes.

psalms_2.t: Why are the nations in tumult, and the peoples murmuring a vain thing?
The kings of the earth take their stand, and rulers take counsel together against the LORD and against his anointed:
'Let us tear off their bonds, and throw their cords off from us.'
He who sits in the heavens laughs; the Lord mocks them.
Then he speaks to them in his anger, and in his fury he terrifies them:
'But I have installed my king on Zion, my holy mountain.'
Let me tell of the decree of the LORD. He said to me: 'You are my son; today I have begotten you.
Ask of me, and I will make the nations your inheritance, and the ends of the earth your possession.
You will break them with a rod of iron; you will shatter them like a potter's vessel.'
And now, kings, act prudently; be disciplined, judges of the earth.
Serve the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling.
Kiss the son, or he will be angry and you will perish in the way, for his anger burns in a little while. How blessed are all who take refuge in him.

psalms_3.t: A psalm of David, when he fled from Absalom his son.
LORD, how many are my foes! Many are rising against me.
Many are saying of my being, 'There is no salvation for him in God.' Selah
But you, LORD, are a shield around me, my glory, and the one who lifts my head.
I call aloud to the LORD, and he answered me from his holy mountain. Selah
I lay down and slept; I awoke, for the LORD sustains me.
I will not fear ten thousands of people who have set themselves against me all around.
Arise, LORD! Save me, my God! For you have struck all my enemies on the jaw; you have broken the teeth of the wicked.
Salvation belongs to the LORD; your blessing be on your people. Selah

psalms_4.t: For the choir director, with stringed instruments. A psalm of David.
When I call, answer me, God of my righteousness! In distress you made room for me; be gracious to me and hear my prayer.
Sons of man, how long will my glory be turned to disgrace? How long will you love a vain thing and seek falsehood? Selah
Know that the LORD has set apart the loyal one for himself; the LORD hears when I call to him.
Tremble, and do not sin. Speak in your heart upon your bed, and be silent. Selah
Offer sacrifices of righteousness, and trust in the LORD.
Many are saying, 'Who will show us good?' Lift up the light of your face upon us, LORD!
You have put gladness in my heart more than when their grain and new wine abound.
In peace I will both lie down and sleep, for you alone, LORD, make me dwell in security.

psalms_5.t: For the choir director, to nehiloth. A psalm of David.
Give ear to my sayings, LORD; consider my murmuring.
Attend to the sound of my cry for help, my King and my God, for it is to you that I pray.
LORD, in the morning you hear my voice; in the morning I lay out my case before you, and I watch.
For you are not a God who delights in wickedness; evil does not stay with you.
Boasters do not take their stand before your eyes; you hate all who do wrong.
You destroy those who speak falsehood; the LORD abhors a man of bloodshed and deceit.
But I, through the abundance of your steadfast love, will come into your house; I will bow down toward your holy temple in fear of you.
LORD, lead me in your righteousness because of those who watch me; make your way straight before me.
For there is nothing reliable in his mouth; their inward part is destruction; their throat is an open grave; with their tongue they speak smooth words.
Hold them guilty, God! Let them fall by their own schemes. For the abundance of their transgressions banish them, for they have rebelled against you.
But let all who take refuge in you be glad; let them shout for joy forever; and may you shelter them, and let those who love your name exult in you.
For you bless the righteous, LORD; like a body-shield you surround him with good pleasure.

psalms_6.t: For the choir director, with stringed instruments, upon the sheminith. A psalm of David.
LORD, do not reprove me in your anger, and do not discipline me in your wrath.
Be gracious to me, LORD, for I am withered; heal me, LORD, for my bones are dismayed.
And my being is greatly dismayed; and you, LORD — how long?
Return, LORD! Rescue my being! Save me for the sake of your steadfast love.
For in death there is no remembrance of you; in Sheol, who gives you thanks?
I am weary with my groaning; every night I make my bed swim; with my tears I dissolve my couch.
My eye has wasted away from vexation; it has grown weak because of all my adversaries.
Turn away from me, all you who do wrong, for the LORD has heard the sound of my weeping.
The LORD has heard my supplication; the LORD accepts my prayer.
Let all my enemies be ashamed and greatly dismayed; let them turn back and be ashamed in a moment.

psalms_7.t: A shiggaion of David, which he sang to the LORD concerning the words of Cush, a Benjaminite.
LORD my God, in you I have taken refuge. Save me from all my pursuers and deliver me,
or he will tear my being like a lion, tearing it apart with no one to deliver.
LORD my God, if I have done this, if there is injustice in my hands,
if I have repaid evil to the one at peace with me, or plundered my adversary without cause —
let an enemy pursue my being and overtake it, and let him trample my life to the earth, and lay my glory in the dust. Selah
Arise, LORD, in your anger! Raise yourself against the rages of my adversaries, and awake for me — you have commanded judgement.
Let the congregation of peoples surround you, and over it return on high.
The LORD gives judgement to the peoples. Judge me, LORD, according to my righteousness and according to the integrity that is in me.
Let the evil of the wicked come to an end, and establish the righteous — you who test hearts and kidneys, righteous God.
My shield is with God, the saviour of the upright in heart.
God is a righteous judge, and a God who is indignant every day.
If a man does not turn back, he sharpens his sword; he has bent his bow and made it ready.
And for him he has prepared instruments of death; he makes his arrows into flaming shafts.
Look — he is in labour with wrongdoing; he has conceived trouble and given birth to a lie.
He dug a pit and hollowed it out, and he has fallen into the ditch he was making.
His trouble returns on his own head, and his violence comes down on his own skull.
I will give thanks to the LORD according to his righteousness, and I will sing praise to the name of the LORD Most High.

psalms_8.t: For the choir director, upon the gittith. A psalm of David.
LORD our Lord, how magnificent is your name in all the earth, you who have set your splendour above the heavens!
Out of the mouth of children and infants you have established strength, because of your adversaries, to put an end to enemy and avenger.
When I see your heavens, the work of your fingers, the moon and the stars that you have established —
what is a human being that you remember him, and a son of humankind that you attend to him?
You have made him a little lower than the heavenly beings, and you crown him with glory and majesty.
You make him rule over the works of your hands; you have put everything under his feet:
flocks and cattle, all of them, and also the animals of the field,
the birds of the heavens and the fish of the sea, whatever passes along the paths of the seas.
LORD our Lord, how magnificent is your name in all the earth!

psalms_9.t: For the choir director, upon muth-labben. A psalm of David.
I will give thanks to the LORD with all my heart; I will recount all your wonders.
I will be glad and exult in you; I will make music to your name, Most High.
When my enemies turn back, they stumble and perish before you.
For you have upheld my judgement and my cause; you have sat on a throne, judging righteously.
You have rebuked nations, you have destroyed the wicked; you have wiped out their name forever and ever.
The enemy has come to an end in perpetual ruins; you have uprooted cities; their very memory has perished.
But the LORD sits forever; he has established his throne for judgement.
And he himself will judge the world in righteousness; he will give judgement to the peoples in uprightness.
Let the LORD be a high refuge for the oppressed, a high refuge in times of distress.
Those who know your name will trust in you, for you have not forsaken those who seek you, LORD.
Make music to the LORD who dwells in Zion; declare his deeds among the peoples.
For he who seeks out bloodshed has remembered them; he has not forgotten the cry of distress of the humble.
Be gracious to me, LORD! See my affliction at the hands of those who hate me, you who lift me up from the gates of death,
so that I may recount all your praises in the gates of the daughter of Zion, and rejoice in your salvation.
The nations have sunk into the ditch they made; in the net they hid, their own foot has been caught.
The LORD has made himself known; he has done judgement. By the work of his own hands the wicked is snared. Higgaion. Selah
The wicked will return to Sheol, all the nations that forget God.
For the needy will not be forgotten in perpetuity; the hope of the afflicted will not perish forever.
Arise, LORD! Let no human being prevail; let the nations be judged before your face.
Set terror over them, LORD; let the nations know that they are only human beings. Selah

psalms_10.t: Why, LORD, do you stand at a distance? Why do you hide in times of distress?
In his pride the wicked hotly pursues the afflicted; let them be caught in the schemes they have devised.
For the wicked has boasted over what his being craves, and the greedy one has cursed and spurned the LORD.
The wicked, in the haughtiness of his face, does not seek; 'There is no God' — that is all his thoughts.
His ways endure at all times. Your judgements are on high, far out of his sight; as for all his adversaries, he snorts at them.
He says in his heart, 'I shall not be shaken; from generation to generation I will never be in trouble.'
His mouth is full of cursing and deceit and oppression; under his tongue are trouble and wrongdoing.
He sits in ambush near the villages; in the hiding places he kills the innocent; his eyes lie in wait for the hapless.
He lies in wait in the hiding place like a lion in its lair; he lies in wait to seize the afflicted; he seizes the afflicted, dragging him off in his net.
He is crushed, he sinks down, and the hapless fall into his powerful grip.
He says in his heart, 'God has forgotten; he has hidden his face; he will never see.'
Arise, LORD! God, lift up your hand! Do not forget the humble.
Why has the wicked spurned God? He has said in his heart, 'You will not call it to account.'
You have seen — for you yourself observe trouble and vexation, to take it into your hand. The hapless commits himself to you; to the fatherless you have been a helper.
Break the arm of the wicked and the evil one; seek out his wickedness until you find none.
The LORD is king forever and ever; the nations have perished from his land.
You have heard the desire of the humble, LORD; you establish their heart, you make your ear attend,
to give judgement for the fatherless and the oppressed, so that a human being from the earth may terrify no more.

psalms_11.t: For the choir director. Of David.
In the LORD I have taken refuge. How can you say to my being, 'Flee to your mountain, bird!'?
For look — the wicked bend a bow; they have set their arrow on the string, to shoot from the dark at the upright in heart.
If the foundations are torn down, what can the righteous do?
The LORD is in his holy temple; the LORD — his throne is in the heavens. His eyes see; his eyelids test the children of humankind.
The LORD tests the righteous; but the wicked and the one who loves violence his being hates.
He will rain snares on the wicked; fire and sulphur and a scorching wind are the portion of their cup.
For the LORD is righteous; he loves righteous deeds. The upright will see his face.

psalms_12.t: For the choir director, upon the sheminith. A psalm of David.
Save, LORD, for the loyal one has come to an end; the faithful have vanished from among the children of humankind.
They speak emptiness, each with his neighbour; with flattering lips and a double heart they speak.
May the LORD cut off all flattering lips, the tongue that speaks great things —
those who say, 'By our tongue we will prevail; our lips are our own — who is master over us?'
'Because of the devastation of the afflicted, because of the groaning of the needy, now I will arise,' says the LORD; 'I will set in safety the one who pants for it.'
The speech of the LORD is pure speech, silver refined in a crucible on the ground, purged sevenfold.
You, LORD, will keep them; you will guard him from this generation forever.
The wicked walk about on every side, when vileness is exalted among the children of humankind.

psalms_13.t: For the choir director. A psalm of David.
How long, LORD? Will you forget me in perpetuity? How long will you hide your face from me?
How long must I hold counsel within my being, with sorrow in my heart by day? How long will my enemy be exalted over me?
Look at me, answer me, LORD my God! Give light to my eyes, or I will sleep the sleep of death,
or my enemy will say, 'I have prevailed over him,' and my foes will rejoice when I am shaken.
But I have trusted in your steadfast love; let my heart rejoice in your salvation.
I will sing to the LORD, for he has dealt bountifully with me.

psalms_14.t: For the choir director. Of David.
The fool has said in his heart, 'There is no God.' They act corruptly, they make their deeds abominable; there is no one who does good.
The LORD looked down from the heavens on the children of humankind, to see whether there is anyone acting prudently, anyone seeking God.
They have all turned aside; together they are tainted; there is no one who does good, not even one.
Do they not know, all the workers of wrongdoing, who devour my people as they eat bread? They do not call on the LORD.
There they were in dread, for God is with the righteous generation.
You would put to shame the counsel of the afflicted, but the LORD is his refuge.
Who will grant from Zion the salvation of Israel? When the LORD restores the fortunes of his people, let Jacob rejoice and Israel be glad.

psalms_15.t: LORD, who may sojourn in your tent? Who may dwell on your holy mountain?
The one who walks blameless and does righteousness, and speaks truth in his heart;
he does not go about slandering with his tongue, he does not do evil to his neighbour, and he does not take up a reproach against his kinsman;
in his eyes a rejected man is despised, but those who fear the LORD he honours; he has sworn to his own hurt and does not change;
he does not lend his money at interest, and he does not take a bribe against the innocent. The one who does these things will never be shaken.

psalms_16.t: Keep me, God, for I have taken refuge in you.
I said to the LORD, 'You are Lord; I have no good apart from you.'
As for the holy ones who are in the land, they are the magnificent ones in whom is all my delight.
Their sorrows increase — they have hurried after another god; I will not pour out their drink offerings of blood, and I will not take their names on my lips.
The LORD is the portion of my inheritance and my cup; you hold my lot.
The boundary lines have fallen for me in pleasant places; indeed, my inheritance is beautiful to me.
I will bless the LORD, who has counselled me; indeed, by night my kidneys instruct me.
I have set the LORD before me continually; because he is at my right hand, I will not be shaken.
Therefore my heart is glad and my glory rejoices; my flesh also dwells in security.
For you will not forsake my being to Sheol; you will not let your loyal one see decay.
You will make known to me the path of life; fullness of gladness is in your presence, pleasant things at your right hand in perpetuity.

psalms_17.t: Hear a righteous cause, LORD! Attend to my cry of entreaty! Give ear to my prayer — from lips without deceit.
Let my vindication come from your presence; let your eyes see what is upright.
You have tested my heart, you have visited by night, you have refined me — you will find nothing. I have resolved that my mouth will not transgress.
As for what people do — by the word of your lips I have kept from the paths of the violent man.
My steps have held to your tracks; my footsteps have not slipped.
I call on you, for you answer me, God; incline your ear to me, hear my speech.
Show the wonder of your acts of steadfast love, saviour of those who take refuge at your right hand from those who rise against them.
Keep me like the pupil of the eye; hide me in the shadow of your wings,
from the wicked who have assailed me, my deadly enemies who surround me.
They have closed up their fat hearts; with their mouth they speak in pride.
They have now surrounded our steps; they set their eyes to bring us down to the ground.
He is like a lion that longs to tear, like a young lion crouching in hiding places.
Arise, LORD! Confront him, bring him down! Bring my being to safety from the wicked by your sword,

from men by your hand, LORD, from men of this world whose portion is in this life, whose belly you fill with your treasure; they are satisfied with sons, and they leave their abundance to their children.
As for me, in righteousness I will see your face; I will be satisfied, when I awake, with your form.

psalms_18.t: For the choir director. Of the servant of the LORD, of David, who spoke to the LORD the words of this song on the day the LORD delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.
And he said: I love you, LORD, my strength.
The LORD is my rock and my fortress and the one who brings me to safety; my God is my Rock, in whom I take refuge, my shield and the horn of my salvation, my high refuge.
I call on the LORD, who is to be praised, and I am saved from my enemies.
The cords of death encompassed me, and the torrents of worthlessness overwhelmed me.
The cords of Sheol surrounded me; the traps of death confronted me.
In my distress I called on the LORD, and to my God I cried for help; he heard my voice from his temple, and my cry for help came before him, into his ears.
Then the earth shook and quaked, and the foundations of the mountains trembled; they shook back and forth, because he was angry.
Smoke went up from his nostrils, and fire from his mouth consumed; coals burned out from him.
He stretched out the heavens and came down, and thick darkness was under his feet.
He rode on a cherub and flew; he soared on the wings of the wind.
He made darkness his secret place, his shelter around him, a darkness of waters, thick clouds of the skies.
From the brightness before him his thick clouds passed on, hail and coals of fire.
The LORD thundered in the heavens, and the Most High gave forth his voice: hail and coals of fire.
He sent out his arrows and scattered them; he shot many lightning flashes and routed them.
