Let the house of Aaron say: 'His steadfast love is for ever.'
Let those who fear the LORD say: 'His steadfast love is for ever.'
From the narrow place I called on the LORD; the LORD answered me in a broad place.
The LORD is for me; I will not be afraid. What can anyone do to me?
The LORD is for me among my helpers, and I will look in triumph on those who hate me.
It is better to take refuge in the LORD than to trust in humankind.
It is better to take refuge in the LORD than to trust in nobles.
All nations surrounded me; in the name of the LORD I fended them off.
They surrounded me, they surrounded me on every side; in the name of the LORD I fended them off.
They surrounded me like bees; they were extinguished like a fire of thorns; in the name of the LORD I fended them off.
You pushed me hard, to make me fall, but the LORD helped me.
My strength and my might is the LORD, and he has become my salvation.
The sound of a shout of joy and salvation is in the tents of the righteous: 'The right hand of the LORD does valiantly!'
The right hand of the LORD is lifted high; the right hand of the LORD does valiantly!
I will not die, but live, and I will recount the works of the LORD.
The LORD has disciplined me severely, but he has not given me over to death.
Open to me the gates of righteousness; I will enter through them and give thanks to the LORD.
This is the gate of the LORD; the righteous will enter through it.
I will give you thanks, for you answered me, and you have become my salvation.
The stone the builders rejected has become the head of the corner.
This has come from the LORD; it is wonderful in our eyes.
This is the day the LORD has made; let us be glad and rejoice in it.
We beg you, LORD, save us now! We beg you, LORD, grant success now!
Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the LORD; we bless you from the house of the LORD.
The LORD is God, and he has given us light. Bind the festival sacrifice with cords, up to the horns of the altar.
You are my God, and I will give you thanks; my God, I will exalt you.
Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good; his steadfast love is for ever.

psalms_119.t: How blessed are those whose way is blameless, who walk in the law of the LORD.
How blessed are those who observe his testimonies, who seek him with all their heart.
They also do no injustice; they walk in his ways.
You have commanded your precepts, to be kept diligently.
If only my ways were steadfast, to keep your statutes!
Then I will not be ashamed when I look to all your commandments.
I will give you thanks with an upright heart, when I learn your righteous judgements.
I will keep your statutes; do not utterly forsake me.
How can a young man keep his path pure? By keeping it according to your word.
With all my heart I have sought you; do not let me stray from your commandments.
In my heart I have stored up your speech, so that I will not sin against you.
Blessed are you, LORD; teach me your statutes.
With my lips I have recounted all the judgements of your mouth.
In the way of your testimonies I have exulted, as over all wealth.
On your precepts I will meditate, and look to your paths.
In your statutes I will delight myself; I will not forget your word.
Deal bountifully with your servant, that I may live and keep your word.
Uncover my eyes, that I may look at wonders out of your law.
I am a sojourner on the earth; do not hide your commandments from me.
My being is crushed with longing for your judgements at all times.
You rebuke the arrogant, the accursed, who stray from your commandments.
Roll away from me reproach and contempt, for I have observed your testimonies.
Even officials sat and spoke against me; your servant meditates on your statutes.
Your testimonies also are my delight, my counsellors.
My being clings to the dust; give me life according to your word.
I recounted my ways and you answered me; teach me your statutes.
Make me understand the way of your precepts, and I will meditate on your wonders.
My being weeps from grief; raise me up according to your word.
Remove from me the way of falsehood, and grant me your law in favour.
I have chosen the way of faithfulness; I have set your judgements before me.
I have clung to your testimonies; LORD, do not put me to shame.
I will run the way of your commandments, for you enlarge my heart.
Teach me, LORD, the way of your statutes, and I will observe it to the end.
Make me understand, that I may observe your law and keep it with all my heart.
Lead me in the pathway of your commandments, for in it I delight.
Incline my heart to your testimonies, and not to unjust gain.
Turn my eyes away from looking at worthlessness; in your ways give me life.
Fulfil for your servant your speech, which is for the fear of you.
Take away my reproach, which I dread, for your judgements are good.
See, I have longed for your precepts; in your righteousness give me life.
Let your acts of steadfast love come to me, LORD, your deliverance according to your speech,
and I will have an answer for the one who taunts me, for I have trusted in your word.
And do not take the word of faithfulness utterly from my mouth, for I have hoped for your judgements.
And I will keep your law continually, for ever and ever.
And I will walk about in a broad place, for I have sought your precepts.
And I will speak of your testimonies before kings and will not be ashamed.
And I will delight myself in your commandments, which I love.
And I will lift up my hands to your commandments, which I love, and I will meditate on your statutes.
Remember the word to your servant, on which you have made me hope.
This is my comfort in my affliction, that your speech has given me life.
The arrogant have utterly mocked me; I have not turned aside from your law.
I remember your judgements from of old, LORD, and I comfort myself.
Burning indignation has seized me because of the wicked, who forsake your law.
Your statutes have been songs to me in the house of my sojourning.
I have remembered your name in the night, LORD, and I have kept your law.
This has been mine: that I have observed your precepts.
My portion is the LORD; I have said I will keep your words.
I have entreated your face with all my heart; be gracious to me according to your speech.
I have thought about my ways and turned my feet back to your testimonies.
I have hurried and not delayed to keep your commandments.
The cords of the wicked have surrounded me; I have not forgotten your law.
At midnight I rise to give you thanks for your righteous judgements.
I am a companion of all who fear you and of those who keep your precepts.
Your steadfast love, LORD, fills the earth; teach me your statutes.
You have dealt well with your servant, LORD, according to your word.
Teach me good discernment and knowledge, for I have believed in your commandments.
Before I was afflicted I went astray, but now I keep your speech.
You are good and you do good; teach me your statutes.
The arrogant have smeared me with falsehood; I, with all my heart, observe your precepts.
Their heart is gross as fat; I delight in your law.
It was good for me that I was afflicted, so that I might learn your statutes.
The law of your mouth is better to me than thousands in gold and silver.
Your hands made me and established me; make me understand, that I may learn your commandments.
Those who fear you will see me and rejoice, for I have hoped for your word.
I know, LORD, that your judgements are righteous, and that in faithfulness you have afflicted me.
Let your steadfast love comfort me, according to your speech to your servant.
Let your compassion come to me, that I may live, for your law is my delight.
Let the arrogant be ashamed, for they have wronged me with falsehood; I will meditate on your precepts.
Let those who fear you turn to me, and those who know your testimonies.
Let my heart be blameless in your statutes, so that I will not be ashamed.
My being is spent with longing for your deliverance; I have hoped for your word.
My eyes are spent looking for your speech, saying, 'When will you comfort me?'
For I have become like a wineskin in smoke; I have not forgotten your statutes.
How many are the days of your servant? When will you execute judgement on those who harass me?
The arrogant have dug pits for me, which are not according to your law.
All your commandments are trustworthy; they harass me with falsehood — help me!
They have almost made an end of me on the earth, but I have not forsaken your precepts.
According to your steadfast love give me life, and I will keep the testimony of your mouth.
For ever, LORD, your word stands firm in the heavens.
Your constancy is to all generations; you established the earth, and it stands.
By your judgements they stand this day, for all things are your servants.
If your law had not been my delight, I would have perished in my affliction.
I will never forget your precepts, for by them you have given me life.
I am yours; save me, for I have sought your precepts.
The wicked have waited for me, to destroy me; I will consider your testimonies carefully.
To all perfection I have seen an end; your commandment is exceedingly broad.
How I love your law! All day long it is my meditation.
Your commandments make me wiser than my enemies, for they are mine for ever.
I have more insight than all my teachers, for your testimonies are my meditation.
I gain more understanding than elders, for I have observed your precepts.
I have held my feet back from every evil path, so that I may keep your word.
I have not turned aside from your judgements, for you yourself have taught me.
How sweet your speech is to my palate, sweeter than honey to my mouth!
From your precepts I gain understanding; therefore I hate every path of falsehood.
Your word is a lamp for my foot, and a light for my pathway.
I have sworn and confirmed it, to keep your righteous judgements.
I have been utterly afflicted; LORD, give me life according to your word.
Accept, please, the freewill offerings of my mouth, LORD, and teach me your judgements.
My life is continually in my hand, and I have not forgotten your law.
The wicked have set a snare for me, but I have not gone astray from your precepts.
I have taken your testimonies as my inheritance for ever, for they are the joy of my heart.
I have inclined my heart to do your statutes, for ever, to the end.
I hate the half-hearted, but I love your law.
You are my hiding place and my shield; I have hoped for your word.
Turn away from me, evildoers, that I may observe the commandments of my God.
Sustain me according to your speech, that I may live, and do not put me to shame in my hope.
Uphold me, that I may be saved, and I will have regard for your statutes continually.
You reject all who stray from your statutes, for their deceitfulness is falsehood.
You put an end to all the wicked of the earth like dross; therefore I love your testimonies.
My flesh trembles from dread of you, and I am afraid of your judgements.
I have done judgement and righteousness; do not abandon me to my oppressors.
Stand surety for your servant for good; do not let the arrogant oppress me.
My eyes are spent looking for your salvation and for your righteous speech.
Deal with your servant according to your steadfast love, and teach me your statutes.
I am your servant; make me understand, that I may know your testimonies.
It is time for the LORD to act; they have broken your law.
Therefore I love your commandments more than gold, more than pure gold.
Therefore I hold all your precepts to be right in everything; I hate every path of falsehood.
Your testimonies are wonders; therefore my being observes them.
The unfolding of your words gives light; it gives understanding to the simple.
I opened my mouth wide and panted, for I longed for your commandments.
Turn to me and be gracious to me, as is the judgement for those who love your name.
Direct my footsteps by your speech, and let no wickedness have power over me.
Ransom me from human oppression, and I will keep your precepts.
Make your face shine on your servant, and teach me your statutes.
Streams of water run down from my eyes, because they do not keep your law.
You are righteous, LORD, and your judgements are upright.
You have commanded your testimonies in righteousness and in great faithfulness.
My zeal has consumed me, for my foes have forgotten your words.
Your speech is thoroughly refined, and your servant loves it.
I am small and despised; I have not forgotten your precepts.
Your righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and your law is truth.
Distress and anguish have found me; your commandments are my delight.
Your testimonies are righteous for ever; make me understand, that I may live.
I have called with all my heart; answer me, LORD; I will observe your statutes.
I have called on you; save me, that I may keep your testimonies.
I rose early in the twilight and cried for help; I have hoped for your word.
My eyes anticipated the night watches, to meditate on your speech.
Hear my voice according to your steadfast love; LORD, according to your judgements give me life.
Those who pursue wickedness have drawn near; they are far from your law.
You are near, LORD, and all your commandments are truth.
Long ago I learned from your testimonies that you founded them for ever.
See my affliction and rescue me, for I have not forgotten your law.
Plead my cause and redeem me; according to your speech give me life.
Salvation is far from the wicked, for they have not sought your statutes.
Your compassion is great, LORD; according to your judgements give me life.
Many are those who harass me, and my foes; I have not turned aside from your testimonies.
I saw the treacherous and felt disgust, because they did not keep your speech.
See that I love your precepts; LORD, according to your steadfast love give me life.
The sum of your word is truth, and every one of your righteous judgements is for ever.
Officials have harassed me without cause, but my heart is in dread at your word.
I exult over your speech, like one who finds great plunder.
I hate and abhor falsehood; I love your law.
Seven times a day I praise you for your righteous judgements.
Great peace belongs to those who love your law, and nothing makes them stumble.
I have waited for your salvation, LORD, and I have done your commandments.
My being has kept your testimonies, and I love them exceedingly.
I have kept your precepts and your testimonies, for all my ways are before you.
Let my cry of entreaty come before you, LORD; according to your word make me understand.
Let my supplication come before you; according to your speech deliver me.
Let my lips pour out praise, for you teach me your statutes.
Let my tongue sing of your speech, for all your commandments are righteous.
Let your hand be ready to help me, for I have chosen your precepts.
I have longed for your salvation, LORD, and your law is my delight.
Let my being live, and it will praise you, and let your judgements help me.
I have gone astray like a lost sheep; seek your servant, for I have not forgotten your commandments.

psalms_120.t: To the LORD in my distress I called, and he answered me.
LORD, deliver my life from lying lips, from a deceitful tongue.
What will he give you, and what more will he do to you, you deceitful tongue?
A warrior's sharpened arrows, with burning coals of broom wood.
Woe to me, that I sojourn in Meshech, that I dwell among the tents of Kedar!
Long has my being dwelt with those who hate peace.
I am peace; but when I speak, they are for war.

psalms_121.t: I lift up my eyes to the mountains: from where will my help come?
My help is from the LORD, maker of the heavens and the earth.
He will not let your foot slip; he who guards you will not slumber.
Look, he who guards Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.
The LORD is your guardian; the LORD is your shade at your right hand.
By day the sun will not strike you, nor the moon by night.
The LORD will guard you from all harm; he will guard your being.
The LORD will guard your going out and your coming in, from now and for ever.

psalms_122.t: A song of ascents. Of David.
I rejoiced when they said to me, 'Let us go to the house of the LORD.'
Our feet have been standing in your gates, Jerusalem.
Jerusalem, built as a city joined firmly together,
where the tribes went up, the tribes of the LORD, as a testimony to Israel, to give thanks to the name of the LORD.
For there the thrones stood for judgement, the thrones of the house of David.
Ask for the peace of Jerusalem: may those who love you be at ease.
May peace be within your rampart, ease within your fortresses.
For the sake of my brothers and my friends I will say, 'Peace be within you.'
For the sake of the house of the LORD our God I will seek your good.

psalms_123.t: To you I have lifted up my eyes, you who are enthroned in the heavens.
Look — as the eyes of slaves are to their master's hand, as the eyes of a female slave to her mistress's hand, so our eyes are to the LORD our God, until he shows us favour.
Show us favour, LORD, show us favour, for we have had more than enough of contempt.
Long has our being been surfeited with the mockery of the complacent, with the contempt of the arrogant.

psalms_124.t: A song of ascents. Of David.
If it had not been the LORD who was for us — let Israel say it —
if it had not been the LORD who was for us when people rose up against us,
then they would have swallowed us alive, when their anger burned against us;
then the waters would have overflowed us, a torrent would have passed over us;
then they would have passed over us — the raging waters.
Blessed be the LORD, who has not given us as prey to their teeth.
We have escaped like a bird from the fowlers' snare; the snare was broken, and we escaped.
Our help is in the name of the LORD, maker of the heavens and the earth.

psalms_125.t: Those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion, which cannot be shaken but remains for ever.
As the mountains are around Jerusalem, so the LORD is around his people, from now and for ever.
For the sceptre of wickedness will not rest on the allotted portion of the righteous, so that the righteous may not stretch out their hands to do injustice.
Do good, LORD, to the good, and to the upright in their hearts.
But those who turn aside to their crooked ways — the LORD will lead them away with those who do wickedness. Peace be on Israel.

psalms_126.t: When the LORD restored the fortunes of Zion, we were like those who dream.
Then our mouth was filled with laughter, and our tongue with a shout of joy. Then they said among the nations, 'The LORD has done great things for these people.'
The LORD has done great things for us; we were joyful.
Restore our fortunes, LORD, like stream-beds in the Negev.
Those who sow with tears will reap with a shout of joy.
He who goes out weeping, carrying the bag of seed, will surely come home with a shout of joy, carrying his sheaves.

psalms_127.t: A song of ascents. Of Solomon.
Unless the LORD builds a house, its builders toil on it in vain. Unless the LORD watches over a city, the watchman keeps awake in vain.
It is in vain for you who rise early, who sit down late, who eat the bread of toil — for he gives to his beloved even in sleep.
Look, sons are an inheritance from the LORD; the fruit of the womb is a reward.
Like arrows in a warrior's hand, so are the sons of one's youth.
How blessed is the man who has filled his quiver with them! They will not be ashamed when they speak with enemies in the gate.

psalms_128.t: How blessed is everyone who fears the LORD, who walks in his ways.
You will surely eat the product of your hands; how blessed you are, and it will be well with you.
Your wife will be like a fruitful vine within your house; your children like olive shoots all around your table.
Look, so will a man be blessed who fears the LORD.
May the LORD bless you from Zion; may you look on the good of Jerusalem all the days of your life.
And may you see your children's children. Peace be on Israel.

psalms_129.t: Long have they oppressed me from my youth — let Israel say it —
long have they oppressed me from my youth, yet they have not prevailed against me.
Plowmen have plowed on my back; they have made their furrows long.
The LORD is righteous; he has cut the cords of the wicked.
Let them be ashamed and turned back, all who hate Zion.
Let them be like grass on the roofs, which withers before it is pulled up;
with which a reaper does not fill his hand, nor the one who binds sheaves his bosom.
And those who pass by do not say, 'The blessing of the LORD be on you; we bless you in the name of the LORD.'

psalms_130.t: Out of the depths I have called on you, LORD.
Lord, hear my voice; let your ears be attentive to the sound of my supplications.
If you kept a record of iniquities, LORD, Lord, who could stand?
But with you there is forgiveness, so that you may be feared.
I have waited for the LORD; my being has waited, and for his word I have hoped.
My being waits for the Lord more than watchmen for the morning, more than watchmen for the morning.
Hope in the LORD, Israel, for with the LORD is steadfast love, and with him is abundant ransom.
And he will ransom Israel from all its iniquities.

psalms_131.t: A song of ascents. Of David.
LORD, my heart has not been lofty, nor have my eyes been raised, and I have not walked among things too great and too wonderful for me.
Surely I have stilled and quieted my being, like a weaned child on its mother; my being within me is like a weaned child.
Hope in the LORD, Israel, from now and for ever.

psalms_132.t: Remember, LORD, in David's favour all his hardships,
how he swore to the LORD, and vowed to the Mighty One of Jacob:
'I will not enter the tent of my house, or go up onto the couch of my bed,
'I will not give sleep to my eyes, or slumber to my eyelids,
'until I find a place for the LORD, a dwelling place for the Mighty One of Jacob.'
Look, we heard of it in Ephrathah; we found it in the fields of Jaar.
Let us go to his dwelling place; let us bow down at his footstool.
Arise, LORD, to your resting place, you and the ark of your strength.
Let your priests be clothed with righteousness, and let your loyal ones shout for joy.
For the sake of David your servant, do not turn away the face of your anointed.
The LORD swore to David in faithfulness — he will not turn back from it: 'One of the fruit of your body I will set on a throne for you.
'If your sons keep my covenant and the testimonies I will teach them, their sons also, for ever, will sit on a throne for you.'
For the LORD has chosen Zion; he has desired it for his dwelling.
'This is my resting place for ever; here I will dwell, for I have desired it.
I will richly bless her provision; I will satisfy her needy with food.
'And I will clothe her priests with salvation, and her loyal ones will surely shout for joy.
'There I will make a horn sprout for David; I have prepared a lamp for my anointed.
'I will clothe his enemies with shame, but on him his crown will shine.'

psalms_133.t: A song of ascents. Of David.
Look, how good and how pleasant it is when brothers dwell together!
It is like the good oil on the head, running down on the beard, the beard of Aaron, running down on the collar of his robes;
like the dew of Hermon running down on the mountains of Zion. For there the LORD commanded the blessing, life for ever.

psalms_134.t: Look, bless the LORD, all you servants of the LORD, who stand in the house of the LORD by night.
Lift up your hands toward the sanctuary and bless the LORD.
May the LORD bless you from Zion, maker of the heavens and the earth.

psalms_135.t: Hallelujah. Praise the name of the LORD; praise him, you servants of the LORD,
who stand in the house of the LORD, in the courts of the house of our God.
Praise the LORD, for the LORD is good; make music to his name, for it is pleasant.
For the LORD has chosen Jacob for himself, Israel as his own possession.
For I know that the LORD is great, and our Lord is above all gods.
All that the LORD desires he does, in the heavens and on the earth, in the seas and all the deeps.
He brings up clouds from the end of the earth; he makes lightning for the rain; he brings out wind from his storehouses.
who struck down the firstborn of Egypt, both human and beast;
he sent signs and wonders into your midst, Egypt, against Pharaoh and all his servants;
who struck down many nations and killed mighty kings —
Sihon king of the Amorites, and Og king of Bashan, and all the kingdoms of Canaan;
and he gave their land as an inheritance, an inheritance to Israel his people.
LORD, your name is for ever; LORD, your reputation to all generations.
For the LORD will vindicate his people and have compassion on his servants.
The idols of the nations are silver and gold, the work of human hands.
They have a mouth, but do not speak; eyes, but do not see;
ears, but do not give ear; and there is no breath at all in their mouth.
Those who make them will become like them, and everyone who trusts in them.
House of Israel, bless the LORD; house of Aaron, bless the LORD;
house of Levi, bless the LORD; you who fear the LORD, bless the LORD.
Blessed be the LORD from Zion, he who dwells in Jerusalem. Hallelujah.

psalms_136.t: Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good; for his steadfast love is for ever.
Give thanks to the God of gods, for his steadfast love is for ever.
Give thanks to the Lord of lords, for his steadfast love is for ever.
To him who alone does great wonders, for his steadfast love is for ever;
to him who made the heavens by understanding, for his steadfast love is for ever;
to him who spread out the earth on the waters, for his steadfast love is for ever;
to him who made the great lights, for his steadfast love is for ever;
the sun for dominion by day, for his steadfast love is for ever;
the moon and stars for dominion by night, for his steadfast love is for ever;
to him who struck Egypt through their firstborn, for his steadfast love is for ever;
and brought Israel out from among them, for his steadfast love is for ever;
with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, for his steadfast love is for ever;
to him who cut the Sea of Reeds in two, for his steadfast love is for ever;
and made Israel pass through the middle of it, for his steadfast love is for ever;
and shook Pharaoh and his army off into the Sea of Reeds, for his steadfast love is for ever;
to him who led his people through the wilderness, for his steadfast love is for ever;
to him who struck down great kings, for his steadfast love is for ever;
and killed mighty kings, for his steadfast love is for ever;
Sihon king of the Amorites, for his steadfast love is for ever;
and Og king of Bashan, for his steadfast love is for ever;
and gave their land as an inheritance, for his steadfast love is for ever;
an inheritance to Israel his servant, for his steadfast love is for ever;
who remembered us in our low condition, for his steadfast love is for ever;
and tore us free from our foes, for his steadfast love is for ever;
who gives food to all flesh, for his steadfast love is for ever.
Give thanks to the God of the heavens, for his steadfast love is for ever.

psalms_137.t: By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat and wept when we remembered Zion.
On the poplars there we hung up our lyres.
For there our captors asked us for words of a song, and our mockers for gladness: 'Sing us one of the songs of Zion!'
How can we sing the song of the LORD on foreign ground?
If I forget you, Jerusalem, let my right hand forget its skill.
Let my tongue cleave to my palate if I do not remember you, if I do not set Jerusalem above my highest joy.
Remember, LORD, against the sons of Edom the day of Jerusalem — those who said, 'Lay it bare, lay it bare, down to its foundation!'
Daughter of Babylon, you who are to be destroyed, how blessed is the one who repays you what you dealt out to us!
How blessed is the one who seizes your infants and smashes them against the rock!

psalms_138.t: I will give you thanks with all my heart; before the gods I will make music to you.
I will bow down toward your holy temple and give thanks to your name for your steadfast love and your faithfulness; for you have made your speech great above all your name.
On the day I called, you answered me; you made me bold, with strength in my being.
All the kings of the earth will give you thanks, LORD, when they hear the sayings of your mouth,
and they will sing of the ways of the LORD, for great is the glory of the LORD.
For the LORD is exalted, yet he sees the lowly, and the proud he knows from afar.
Though I walk in the midst of trouble, you give me life; against the anger of my enemies you stretch out your hand, and your right hand saves me.
The LORD will accomplish what concerns me; LORD, your steadfast love is for ever — do not abandon the works of your hands.

psalms_139.t: For the choir director. Of David. A psalm.
LORD, you have examined me and known me.
You know when I sit down and when I rise up; you understand my thought from afar.
My travelling and my lying down you sift out, and you are intimately acquainted with all my ways.
For before a word is on my tongue, look, LORD, you know all of it.
Behind and before you have enclosed me, and you have laid your hand on me.
Such knowledge is too wonderful for me; it is set too high — I cannot reach it.
Where can I go from your spirit, and where can I flee from your presence?
If I ascend to the heavens, you are there; if I make my bed in Sheol, there you are.
If I take the wings of the dawn and dwell at the far end of the sea,
even there your hand will lead me, and your right hand will hold me fast.
And I said, 'Surely darkness will crush me, and the light around me will be night' —
even the darkness is not dark to you, and night shines like the day; darkness and light are the same.
For you created my kidneys; you wove me together in my mother's womb.
I will give you thanks, because I am fearsomely and wonderfully made; your works are wonders, and my being knows it well.
My frame was not hidden from you when I was made in the secret place, embroidered in the depths of the earth.
Your eyes saw my unformed substance, and in your scroll all of them were written — the days that were formed, and one of them was for it.
And to me, how precious are your thoughts, God! How vast is their sum!
If I would count them, they are more than the sand; I awake, and I am still with you.
If only you would kill the wicked, God! You men of blood, depart from me —
who speak of you with wicked intent, your enemies take your name in vain.
Do I not hate those who hate you, LORD, and loathe those who rise against you?
With perfect hatred I hate them; they have become my enemies.
Examine me, God, and know my heart; test me and know my disquieting thoughts.
And see whether there is any hurtful way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way.

psalms_140.t: For the choir director. A psalm of David.
Rescue me, LORD, from the evil man; preserve me from the man of violence —
those who plan evil things in their heart, who stir up wars all day long.
They sharpen their tongue like a serpent; the venom of a viper is under their lips. Selah.
Keep me, LORD, from the hands of the wicked; preserve me from the man of violence, those who plan to trip up my footsteps.
The proud have hidden a trap for me, and cords; they have spread a net beside the path; they have set snares for me. Selah.
I said to the LORD, 'You are my God'; give ear, LORD, to the sound of my supplications.
GOD the Lord, the strength of my salvation, you covered my head in the day of battle.
Do not grant, LORD, the desires of the wicked; do not promote his plot, or they will be exalted. Selah.
As for the head of those who surround me, let the mischief of their lips cover them.
Let burning coals fall on them; let them be cast into the fire, into pits, never to rise.
Let the slanderer not be established in the land; let evil hunt down the man of violence with blow after blow.
I know that the LORD will maintain the cause of the poor, the justice of the needy.
Surely the righteous will give thanks to your name; the upright will dwell in your presence.

psalms_141.t: LORD, I call on you; hurry to me; give ear to my voice when I call to you.
Let my prayer be set before you as incense, the lifting of my hands as the evening offering.
Set a guard over my mouth, LORD; keep watch over the door of my lips.
Do not turn my heart to anything evil, to busy myself with wicked deeds alongside men who do wickedness; and let me not eat of their delicacies.
Let a righteous man strike me — it is steadfast love; let him rebuke me — it is oil for the head; let my head not refuse it. For my prayer is still against their evil deeds.
Their judges have been thrown down from the sides of a rock, and they will hear my sayings, for they are pleasant.
As when one plows and breaks open the earth, our bones have been scattered at the mouth of Sheol.
For my eyes are toward you, GOD the Lord; in you I take refuge — do not pour out my life.
Keep me from the jaws of the trap they have laid for me, and from the snares of those who do wickedness.
Let the wicked fall into their own nets, all together, while I pass by.

psalms_142.t: A maskil of David, when he was in the cave. A prayer.
With my voice I cry out to the LORD; with my voice I plead for favour from the LORD.
I pour out my complaint before him; I tell my trouble before him.
When my spirit faints away within me, you know my pathway. In the path where I walk they have hidden a trap for me.
Look to the right and see — there is no one who recognises me; every place of escape is lost to me; no one cares for my life.
I cry out to you, LORD; I say, 'You are my refuge, my portion in the land of the living.'
Attend to my cry of entreaty, for I have been brought very low. Deliver me from those who harass me, for they are stronger than I am.
Bring me out of prison, that I may give thanks to your name. The righteous will surround me, for you will deal bountifully with me.

psalms_143.t: LORD, hear my prayer; give ear to my supplications; in your constancy answer me, in your righteousness.
And do not enter into judgement with your servant, for no one living is righteous before you.
For an enemy has pursued my life; he has crushed my life to the ground; he has made me dwell in dark places, like those long dead.
And my spirit faints away within me; inside me my heart is appalled.
I have remembered the days of old; I have meditated on all your deeds; I muse on the work of your hands.
I have spread out my hands to you; my throat thirsts for you like a parched land. Selah.
Hurry, answer me, LORD; my spirit is spent. Do not hide your face from me, or I will be like those who go down to the pit.
Make me hear your steadfast love in the morning, for in you I have trusted. Make known to me the way I should go, for to you I lift up my being.
Deliver me from my enemies, LORD; to you I have fled for cover.
Teach me to do your will, for you are my God. May your good spirit lead me on level ground.
For the sake of your name, LORD, give me life; in your righteousness bring me out of trouble.
And in your steadfast love cut off my enemies and destroy all who oppress my life, for I am your servant.

psalms_144.t: Blessed be the LORD my Rock, who trains my hands for war, my fingers for battle;
my steadfast love and my stronghold, my high refuge and my deliverer, my shield, in whom I take refuge, who subdues my people under me.
LORD, what is humankind, that you take knowledge of them, a child of humanity, that you regard them?
Humankind is like a breath; their days are like a passing shadow.
LORD, bend down your heavens and come down; touch the mountains, and they will smoke.
Flash lightning and scatter them; send your arrows and rout them.
Stretch out your hands from on high; set me free and deliver me from the great waters, from the hand of foreigners,
whose mouth speaks falsehood, and whose right hand is a right hand of deception.
God, I will sing a new song to you; on a ten-stringed harp I will make music to you,
who gives deliverance to kings, who sets David his servant free from the evil sword.
Set me free and deliver me from the hand of foreigners, whose mouth speaks falsehood, and whose right hand is a right hand of deception —
so that our sons may be like plants full-grown in their youth, our daughters like corner pillars, carved for the structure of a palace;
our granaries full, providing every kind of store; our flocks bringing forth thousands, ten thousands in our fields;
our cattle heavy with young; no loss and no miscarrying, and no outcry in our streets.
How blessed is the people for whom it is so! How blessed is the people whose God is the LORD!

psalms_145.t: A praise. Of David.
I will exalt you, my God the King, and bless your name for ever and ever.
Every day I will bless you, and praise your name for ever and ever.
Great is the LORD and greatly to be praised, and his greatness is unsearchable.
One generation to another will extol your works, and declare your mighty deeds.
On the majesty of the glory of your splendour, and on the story of your wonders, I will meditate.
And they will tell of the might of your fearsome deeds, and I will recount your greatness.
They will pour out the remembrance of your abundant goodness, and shout for joy at your righteousness.
Gracious and compassionate is the LORD, slow to anger and great in steadfast love.
The LORD is good to all, and his compassion is over all his works.
All your works will give you thanks, LORD, and your loyal ones will bless you.
They will tell of the glory of your kingdom, and speak of your might,
to make known to the children of humankind his mighty deeds and the glorious majesty of his kingdom.
Your kingdom is a kingdom of all ages, and your dominion endures through all generations.
The LORD sustains all who fall and raises up all who are bent down.
The eyes of all look to you, and you give them their food in its time.
You open your hand and satisfy the desire of every living thing.
The LORD is righteous in all his ways and loyal in all his works.
The LORD is near to all who call on him, to all who call on him in truth.
He brings about the desire of those who fear him; he hears their cry for help and saves them.
The LORD guards all who love him, but all the wicked he will destroy.
My mouth will speak the praise of the LORD, and all flesh will bless his holy name for ever and ever.

psalms_146.t: Hallelujah. Praise the LORD, my being.
I will praise the LORD as long as I live; I will make music to my God while I still am.
Do not trust in nobles, in a mortal, in whom there is no deliverance.
His breath goes out, he returns to his ground; on that very day his plans perish.
How blessed is the one whose help is the God of Jacob, whose hope is in the LORD his God,
who made the heavens and the earth, the sea and all that is in them, who keeps faithfulness for ever,
who does justice for the oppressed, who gives food to the hungry. The LORD sets prisoners free;
The LORD opens the eyes of the blind; the LORD raises up those who are bent down; the LORD loves the righteous.
The LORD watches over sojourners; he upholds the fatherless and the widow, but the way of the wicked he makes crooked.
The LORD will reign for ever, your God, Zion, to all generations. Hallelujah.

psalms_147.t: Hallelujah. For it is good to make music to our God; it is pleasant, and praise is fitting.
The LORD is the builder of Jerusalem; he gathers the banished of Israel.
who heals the broken-hearted and binds up their wounds,
who counts the number of the stars and calls them all by name.
Great is our Lord and abundant in power; his understanding is beyond number.
The LORD relieves the humble; he brings the wicked low to the ground.
Sing to the LORD with thanksgiving; make music to our God with the lyre,
who covers the heavens with clouds, who prepares rain for the earth, who makes grass sprout on the mountains.
who gives the beast its food, and the young ravens that cry out.
He does not delight in the strength of the horse; he takes no pleasure in a man's legs.
The LORD takes pleasure in those who fear him, in those who hope for his steadfast love.
Extol the LORD, Jerusalem; praise your God, Zion.
For he has strengthened the bars of your gates; he has blessed your children within you.
who makes peace in your territory; with the finest of wheat he satisfies you.
who sends his speech to the earth; his word runs very swiftly.
who gives snow like wool; he scatters frost like ashes.
who throws down his ice like crumbs — who can stand before his cold?
He sends his word and melts them; he makes his wind blow, and the waters flow.
He declares his words to Jacob, his statutes and his judgements to Israel.
He has not done so for any nation; as for his judgements, they do not know them. Hallelujah.

psalms_148.t: Hallelujah. Praise the LORD from the heavens; praise him in the heights.
Praise him, all his angels; praise him, all his hosts.
Praise him, sun and moon; praise him, all you stars of light.
Praise him, highest heavens, and you waters above the heavens.
Let them praise the name of the LORD, for he commanded and they were created.
He established them for ever and ever; he gave a statute that will not pass away.
Praise the LORD from the earth, you sea creatures and all the deeps,
fire and hail, snow and mist, stormy wind that does his word,
mountains and all hills, fruit trees and all cedars,
wild animals and all livestock, creeping things and winged birds,
kings of the earth and all peoples, officials and all judges of the earth,
young men and virgins alike, old people together with the young.
Let them praise the name of the LORD, for his name alone is exalted; his splendour is above earth and heavens.
And he has raised up a horn for his people, praise for all his loyal ones, for the Israelites, a people near to him. Hallelujah.

psalms_149.t: Hallelujah. Sing to the LORD a new song, his praise in the assembly of the loyal.
Let Israel rejoice in its maker; let the children of Zion be glad in their king.
Let them praise his name with dancing; with tambourine and lyre let them make music to him.
For the LORD takes pleasure in his people; he adorns the humble with salvation.
Let the loyal exult in honour; let them shout for joy on their beds.
The high praises of God in their throat, and a two-edged sword in their hand,
to execute vengeance on the nations, punishments on the peoples,
to bind their kings with fetters and their nobles with shackles of iron,
to execute on them the judgement that is written — that is honour for all his loyal ones. Hallelujah.

psalms_150.t: Hallelujah. Praise God in his sanctuary; praise him in the vault of his strength.
Praise him for his mighty deeds; praise him according to his abundant greatness.
Praise him with the blast of the ram's horn; praise him with harp and lyre.
Praise him with tambourine and dancing; praise him with strings and pipe.
Praise him with sounding cymbals; praise him with shouting cymbals.
Let everything that breathes praise the LORD. Hallelujah.

ruth_1.t: In the days when the judges judged, there was a famine in the land. A man went from Bethlehem in Judah to live as a foreigner in the country of Moab — he, his wife, and his two sons.
The man's name was Elimelech, his wife's name was Naomi, and his two sons were named Mahlon and Kilion — Ephrathites from Bethlehem in Judah. They came to the country of Moab and stayed there.
Then Elimelech, Naomi's husband, died, and she was left, she and her two sons.
They took Moabite wives for themselves; the name of one was Orpah, and the name of the second was Ruth. They lived there about ten years.
Then the two of them also died — Mahlon and Kilion — and the woman was left without her two children and without her husband.
Then she set out, she and her daughters-in-law, to return from the country of Moab, for she had heard in the country of Moab that the LORD had visited his people to give them bread.
She went out from the place where she had been, and her two daughters-in-law with her, and they set out on the road to return to the land of Judah.
But Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, "Go, each of you return to her mother's house. May the LORD deal with you in steadfast love, as you have dealt with the dead and with me.
May the LORD grant that you find rest, each of you in the house of her husband." Then she kissed them, and they raised their voice and wept.
And they said to her, "No — we will return with you, to your people."
But Naomi said, "Go back, my daughters. Why would you go with me? Do I still have sons in my womb, that they could become your husbands?
Go back, my daughters, go, for I am too old to belong to a husband. Even if I said, 'I have hope' — even if I belonged to a husband tonight and even bore sons —

— would you wait, then, until they grew up? Would you, then, refrain from having husbands? No, my daughters, for it is far more bitter for me than for you, because the hand of the LORD has gone out against me."
Then they raised their voice and wept again. Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth clung to her.
And she said, "Look, your sister-in-law has gone back to her people and to her gods. Go back after your sister-in-law."
But Ruth said, "Do not press me to leave you, to turn back from following you. For where you go, I will go, and where you lodge, I will lodge. Your people will be my people, and your God my God.
Where you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. May the LORD do so to me, and more also, if anything but death separates me from you."
When Naomi saw that she was determined to go with her, she stopped speaking to her about it.
So the two of them went on until they came to Bethlehem. When they came to Bethlehem, the whole town was stirred over them, and the women said, "Is this Naomi?"
But she said to them, "Do not call me Naomi. Call me Mara, for the Almighty has made my life very bitter.
I went out full, and the LORD has brought me back empty. Why do you call me Naomi, when the LORD has testified against me and the Almighty has brought harm on me?"
So Naomi returned, and with her Ruth the Moabite, her daughter-in-law, who had returned from the country of Moab. And they came to Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest.

ruth_2.t: Now Naomi had a kinsman on her husband's side, a man of great standing, from the clan of Elimelech, and his name was Boaz.
And Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi, "Let me go to the field and glean among the ears of grain behind anyone in whose eyes I find favour." And she said to her, "Go, my daughter."
So she went out and came and gleaned in the field behind the harvesters. As it happened, she came upon the portion of the field belonging to Boaz, who was from the clan of Elimelech.
And there was Boaz, coming from Bethlehem. He said to the harvesters, "The LORD be with you," and they said to him, "May the LORD bless you."
Then Boaz said to his young man who was set over the harvesters, "Whose young woman is this?"
The young man who was set over the harvesters answered, "She is a Moabite young woman, the one who came back with Naomi from the country of Moab.

She said, 'Let me glean and gather among the sheaves behind the harvesters.' So she came, and she has been on her feet from early morning until now; she has been sitting in the shelter only a little."
Then Boaz said to Ruth, "Listen, my daughter. Do not go to glean in another field, and do not go on from this one; stay close here with my young women.

Keep your eyes on the field they are harvesting, and go behind them. Have I not ordered the young men not to touch you? And when you are thirsty, go to the jars and drink from what the young men have drawn."
Then she fell on her face and bowed to the ground and said to him, "Why have I found favour in your eyes, that you should take notice of me, when I am a foreigner?"

Boaz answered her, "I have been told in full all that you have done for your mother-in-law since the death of your husband — how you left your father and your mother and the land of your birth and went to a people you did not know before.
May the LORD repay what you have done, and may your wages be full from the LORD, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to take refuge."
And she said, "May I find favour in your eyes, my lord, for you have comforted me and have spoken to the heart of your maidservant — though I am not the equal of one of your maidservants."

At mealtime Boaz said to her, "Come over here and eat some of the bread, and dip your piece in the sour wine." So she sat beside the harvesters, and he held out roasted grain to her, and she ate and was satisfied and had some left over.
When she rose to glean, Boaz ordered his young men, "Let her glean even among the sheaves, and do not humiliate her.
And you are also to pull out some for her from the bundles and leave it, and let her glean it, and do not rebuke her."
So she gleaned in the field until evening, and she beat out what she had gleaned, and it came to about an ephah of barley.
She lifted it and came into the town, and her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned. She also brought out and gave her what she had left over after she had eaten her fill.

Her mother-in-law said to her, "Where did you glean today, and where did you work? Blessed be the one who took notice of you." So she told her mother-in-law whom she had worked with and said, "The name of the man I worked with today is Boaz."

And Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, "Blessed be he by the LORD, who has not forsaken his steadfast love toward the living and toward the dead." And Naomi said to her, "The man is a near relative of ours; he is one of our kinsman-redeemers."
And Ruth the Moabite said, "He even said to me, 'Stay close with my young men until they have finished all my harvest.'"
And Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, "It is good, my daughter, that you go out with his young women, so that no one sets upon you in another field."
So she stayed close with the young women of Boaz, gleaning until the barley harvest and the wheat harvest were finished; and she lived with her mother-in-law.

ruth_3.t: Then Naomi her mother-in-law said to her, "My daughter, should I not seek a resting place for you, so that it may go well for you?
And now, is not Boaz our kinsman, with whose young women you have been? Look — tonight he is winnowing barley at the threshing floor.
So wash, anoint yourself, put on your garments, and go down to the threshing floor. Do not make yourself known to the man until he has finished eating and drinking.
And when he lies down, take note of the place where he lies; then go and uncover his feet and lie down, and he will tell you what to do."
And she said to her, "All that you say to me I will do."
So she went down to the threshing floor and did all that her mother-in-law had commanded her.
Boaz ate and drank, and his heart was merry, and he went to lie down at the end of the heap of grain. Then she came quietly, uncovered his feet, and lay down.
In the middle of the night the man was startled and turned over — and there was a woman lying at his feet.
And he said, "Who are you?" And she said, "I am Ruth, your slave woman. Spread your wing over your slave woman, for you are a kinsman-redeemer."
And he said, "Blessed be you by the LORD, my daughter. You have made this last act of steadfast love better than the first, in not going after the young men, whether poor or rich.
And now, my daughter, do not be afraid. All that you say I will do for you, for the whole gate of my people knows that you are a woman of ability.
And now, though it is true that I am a kinsman-redeemer, there is also a kinsman-redeemer nearer than I.
Stay the night, and in the morning, if he will redeem you, good — let him redeem. But if he is not willing to redeem you, then I myself will redeem you, as the LORD lives. Lie down until morning."
So she lay at his feet until morning, and she rose before anyone could recognise another. And he said, "Let it not be known that the woman came to the threshing floor."
And he said, "Bring the shawl you are wearing and hold it out." So she held it, and he measured out six measures of barley and set it on her; and he went into the town.
When she came to her mother-in-law, she said, "Who are you, my daughter?" And she told her all that the man had done for her.
And she said, "He gave me these six measures of barley, for he said to me, 'Do not go empty-handed to your mother-in-law.'"
And she said, "Sit still, my daughter, until you know how the matter falls out, for the man will not rest unless he settles the matter today."

ruth_4.t: Boaz went up to the gate and sat down there. And there was the kinsman-redeemer of whom Boaz had spoken, passing by. He said, "Turn aside, sit down here, So-and-so." So he turned aside and sat down.
Then he took ten men from the elders of the town and said, "Sit down here." And they sat down.
Then he said to the kinsman-redeemer, "Naomi, who has come back from the country of Moab, is selling the portion of the field that belonged to our brother Elimelech.

And I thought I would disclose it to you and say: Acquire it in the presence of those sitting here and of the elders of my people. If you will redeem it, redeem it; and if you will not redeem it, tell me, so that I may know, for there is no one but you to redeem, and I come after you." And he said, "I will redeem it."
Then Boaz said, "On the day you acquire the field from Naomi's hand, you also acquire Ruth the Moabite, the wife of the dead man, to raise up the name of the dead over his inheritance."
And the kinsman-redeemer said, "I am not able to redeem it for myself, or I would ruin my own inheritance. Take over my right of redemption for yourself, for I am not able to redeem."

Now this was the custom formerly in Israel concerning redemption and exchange, to confirm any matter: a man would draw off his sandal and give it to the other party. This was the manner of attestation in Israel.
So the kinsman-redeemer said to Boaz, "Acquire it for yourself," and he drew off his sandal.
Then Boaz said to the elders and all the people, "You are witnesses today that I have acquired all that belonged to Elimelech and all that belonged to Kilion and Mahlon, from the hand of Naomi.

And Ruth the Moabite, the wife of Mahlon, I have also acquired as my wife, to raise up the name of the dead over his inheritance, so that the name of the dead may not be cut off from among his brothers and from the gate of his place. You are witnesses today."

And all the people who were at the gate, and the elders, said, "We are witnesses. May the LORD make the woman coming into your house like Rachel and like Leah, the two of whom built the house of Israel. Act with ability in Ephrathah, and make a name in Bethlehem.
And may your house be like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah, through the offspring that the LORD gives you from this young woman."
So Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife, and he went in to her; and the LORD gave her conception, and she bore a son.
Then the women said to Naomi, "Blessed be the LORD, who has not left you today without a kinsman-redeemer. May his name be proclaimed in Israel.
He will be a restorer of life to you and a sustainer of your old age, for your daughter-in-law who loves you has borne him — she who is better to you than seven sons."
Then Naomi took the child and laid him in her lap, and she became his nurse.
And the women of the neighbourhood gave him a name, saying, "A son has been born to Naomi." And they called his name Obed. He was the father of Jesse, the father of David.
Now these are the generations of Perez. Perez fathered Hezron,
Hezron fathered Ram, Ram fathered Amminadab,
Amminadab fathered Nahshon, Nahshon fathered Salmon,
Salmon fathered Boaz, Boaz fathered Obed,
Obed fathered Jesse, and Jesse fathered David.

song of songs_1.t: The song of songs, which is Solomon's.
Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth, for your lovemaking is better than wine.
Your oils are good to smell; your name is oil poured out. That is why the young women love you.
Draw me after you — let us run. The king has brought me into his chambers. Let us rejoice and be glad in you; let us call your lovemaking to mind more than wine. Rightly do they love you.
I am black and lovely, daughters of Jerusalem, like the tents of Kedar, like the curtains of Solomon.
Do not stare at me because I am dark, because the sun has looked on me. My mother's sons were angry with me; they made me keeper of the vineyards — my own vineyard I have not kept.
Tell me, you whom my being loves, where you graze, where you make your flock lie down at noon. Why should I be like one veiled beside the flocks of your friends?
If you do not know, most beautiful among women, go out in the tracks of the flock and pasture your young goats beside the shepherds' dwellings.
To a mare among Pharaoh's chariots I liken you, my companion.
Your cheeks are beautiful with strings of ornament, your neck with beads.
Strings of gold we will make for you, with studs of silver.
While the king was at his table, my nard gave forth its fragrance.
A bag of myrrh is my beloved to me, lodging between my breasts.
A cluster of henna is my beloved to me, in the vineyards of En Gedi.
Here you are, beautiful, my companion; here you are, beautiful. Your eyes are doves.
Here you are, beautiful, my beloved, and pleasant. Our bed, too, is verdant.
The beams of our houses are cedars, our rafters cypresses.

song of songs_2.t: I am a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valleys.
Like a lily among the thorns, so is my companion among the daughters.
Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest, so is my beloved among the sons. In his shade I delighted to sit, and his fruit was sweet to my palate.
He has brought me to the house of wine, and his banner over me is love.
Sustain me with raisin cakes, refresh me with apples, for I am weak with love.
His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me.
I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles or by the does of the field: do not awaken or arouse love until it pleases.
The sound of my beloved! Here he comes, leaping over the mountains, bounding over the hills.
My beloved is like a gazelle or the fawn of the deer. Here he is, standing behind our wall, gazing in at the windows, peering through the lattices.
My beloved answered and said to me: Arise, my companion, my beautiful one, and come away.
For the winter has passed; the rain has passed away and gone.
The blossoms have appeared in the land; the time of singing has arrived, and the sound of the turtle-dove has been heard in our land.
The fig tree has ripened its early figs, and the vines in blossom have given fragrance. Arise, my companion, my beautiful one, and come away.
My dove, in the clefts of the rock, in the hiding place of the cliff, let me see your form, let me hear your voice; for your voice is sweet and your form is lovely.
Seize for us the foxes, the little foxes that ruin vineyards — and our vineyards are in blossom.
My beloved is mine and I am his, who grazes among the lilies.
Until the day breathes and the shadows flee, turn, my beloved; be like a gazelle or the fawn of the deer on the mountains of Bether.

song of songs_3.t: On my bed in the nights I sought him whom my being loves; I sought him and did not find him.
Let me arise now and go about in the city, in the streets and in the open places; let me seek him whom my being loves. I sought him and did not find him.
The watchmen who go about in the city found me: Him whom my being loves — have you seen him?
Scarcely had I passed from them when I found him whom my being loves. I grasped him and would not let him go until I had brought him to my mother's house, to the room of her who conceived me.
I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles or by the does of the field: do not awaken or arouse love until it pleases.
Who is this coming up from the wilderness like columns of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with every scent-powder of the trader?
Here is his couch, Solomon's: sixty warriors are around it, of the warriors of Israel,
all of them grasping a sword, trained for war, each with his sword on his thigh against dread in the nights.
A litter King Solomon made for himself from the wood of Lebanon.
Its pillars he made of silver, its back of gold, its seat of purple; its inside was fitted out with love, by the daughters of Jerusalem.
Come out and look, daughters of Zion, at King Solomon, at the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding, on the day of the rejoicing of his heart.

song of songs_4.t: Here you are, beautiful, my companion; here you are, beautiful. Your eyes are doves behind your veil. Your hair is like a flock of goats that have come down from Mount Gilead.
Your teeth are like a flock of shorn ewes that have come up from the washing, all of them bearing twins, and not one among them bereaved.
Like a thread of scarlet are your lips, and your mouth is lovely. Like a slice of pomegranate is your temple behind your veil.
Your neck is like the tower of David, built in courses; a thousand shields hang on it, all the bucklers of the warriors.
Your two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle, that graze among the lilies.
Until the day breathes and the shadows flee, I will go to the mountain of myrrh and to the hill of frankincense.
All of you is beautiful, my companion, and there is no blemish in you.
With me from Lebanon, bride, with me from Lebanon you shall come. You shall look down from the top of Amana, from the top of Senir and Hermon, from the dens of lions, from the mountains of leopards.
You have taken my heart, my sister, bride; you have taken my heart with one glance of your eyes, with one bead of your necklace.
How beautiful is your lovemaking, my sister, bride! How much better is your lovemaking than wine, and the fragrance of your oils than any spice!
Your lips drip flowing honey, bride; honey and milk are under your tongue, and the fragrance of your garments is like the fragrance of Lebanon.
A locked garden is my sister, bride, a locked spring, a sealed fountain.
Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates with choice fruit, henna with nard,
nard and saffron, cane and cinnamon, with all the trees of frankincense, myrrh and aloes, with all the choicest spices —
a spring of gardens, a well of living water, and streams from Lebanon.
Awake, north wind, and come, south wind; breathe upon my garden, let its spices flow. Let my beloved come to his garden and eat its choice fruit.

song of songs_5.t: I have come to my garden, my sister, bride; I have gathered my myrrh with my spice, I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey, I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, companions; drink and be drunk, lovers.

I was sleeping, but my heart was awake. The sound of my beloved, knocking: Open to me, my sister, my companion, my dove, my perfect one; for my head is filled with dew, my locks with the drops of the night.
I have taken off my tunic — how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet — how shall I soil them?
My beloved put his hand in through the opening, and my inward parts stirred for him.
I arose to open to my beloved, and my hands dripped myrrh, my fingers flowing myrrh, on the handles of the bolt.
I opened to my beloved, but my beloved had turned away and gone. My being went out when he spoke. I sought him and did not find him; I called him and he did not answer me.
The watchmen who go about in the city found me; they struck me, they bruised me. They lifted my shawl from me, the watchmen of the walls.
I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem: if you find my beloved, what will you tell him? That I am weak with love.
How is your beloved more than another, most beautiful among women? How is your beloved more than another, that you adjure us so?
My beloved is dazzling and ruddy, conspicuous among ten thousand.
His head is gold, pure gold; his locks are curls, black as the raven.
His eyes are like doves beside channels of water, washing in milk, mounted like jewels.
His cheeks are like a bed of spice, towers of aromatic herbs. His lips are lilies, dripping flowing myrrh.
His hands are rods of gold set with beryl. His body is a plate of ivory covered with sapphires.
His legs are pillars of marble, founded on bases of pure gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, choice as the cedars.
His mouth is sweetness, and all of him is desirable. This is my beloved and this is my companion, daughters of Jerusalem.

song of songs_6.t: Where has your beloved gone, most beautiful among women? Where has your beloved turned, that we may seek him with you?
My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spice, to graze in the gardens and to gather lilies.
I am my beloved's and my beloved is mine, who grazes among the lilies.
You are beautiful, my companion, as Tirzah, lovely as Jerusalem, majestic as the bannered hosts.
Turn your eyes away from before me, for they have overwhelmed me. Your hair is like a flock of goats that have come down from Gilead.
Your teeth are like a flock of ewes that have come up from the washing, all of them bearing twins, and not one among them bereaved.
Like a slice of pomegranate is your temple behind your veil.
There are sixty queens and eighty concubines and young women without number.
One is she, my dove, my perfect one; one is she to her mother, pure is she to the one who bore her. Daughters saw her and called her blessed; queens and concubines, and they praised her.
Who is this who looks down like the dawn, beautiful as the full moon, pure as the sun, majestic as the bannered hosts?
To the nut garden I went down, to look at the green shoots of the wadi, to see whether the vine had budded, whether the pomegranates had bloomed.
I did not know — my being set me among the chariots of my princely people.
Turn, turn, Shulammite; turn, turn, that we may look at you. Why will you look at the Shulammite, as at the dance of the two camps?

song of songs_7.t: How beautiful are your feet in sandals, daughter of a noble! The curves of your thighs are like jewels, the work of a master craftsman's hands.
Your navel is a rounded bowl — may it not lack mixed wine. Your belly is a heap of wheat, fenced about with lilies.
Your two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle.
Your neck is like the tower of ivory. Your eyes are pools in Heshbon by the gate of Bath-rabbim. Your nose is like the tower of Lebanon, looking towards Damascus.
Your head upon you is like Carmel, and the hair of your head like purple. A king is bound in the tresses.
How beautiful you are and how lovely, O love, among the delights!
This stature of yours is like a palm tree, and your breasts like clusters.
I said: Let me climb the palm tree, let me take hold of its fruit-stalks. Let your breasts be like the clusters of the vine, and the fragrance of your nose like apples,
and your mouth like the best wine, going down smoothly for my beloved, gliding over the lips of sleepers.
I am my beloved's, and his desire is towards me.
Come, my beloved, let us go out to the field; let us pass the night in the villages.
Let us rise early to the vineyards; let us see whether the vine has budded, whether the blossom has opened, whether the pomegranates have bloomed. There I will give you my lovemaking.
The mandrakes have given fragrance, and over our doorways are all choice things, new as well as old, which I have stored up for you, my beloved.

song of songs_8.t: Who would make you like a brother to me, one who nursed at my mother's breasts? Then, finding you outside, I would kiss you, and no one would despise me.
I would lead you, I would bring you to my mother's house — she would teach me. I would give you spiced wine to drink, the juice of my pomegranate.
His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me.
I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem: why would you awaken, why arouse love, until it pleases?
Who is this coming up from the wilderness, leaning on her beloved? Under the apple tree I roused you. There your mother was in labour with you; there she was in labour, she bore you.
Set me as a seal upon your heart, as a seal upon your arm; for love is strong as death, jealousy is hard as Sheol. Its flashes are flashes of fire, a flame of the LORD.
Many waters cannot extinguish love, and rivers cannot sweep it away. If a man gave all the wealth of his house for love, they would utterly despise him.
We have a little sister, and she has no breasts. What shall we do for our sister on the day she is spoken for?
If she is a wall, we will build on her a battlement of silver; and if she is a door, we will enclose her with a board of cedar.
I am a wall, and my breasts are like the towers. Then I became in his eyes like one who finds peace.
Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon. He gave the vineyard to keepers; each would bring for its fruit a thousand of silver.
My own vineyard is before me. The thousand is yours, Solomon, and two hundred for those who keep its fruit.
You who dwell in the gardens — friends are listening for your voice. Let me hear it.
Hasten, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or the fawn of the deer on the mountains of spices.

zechariah_1.t: In the eighth month, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah son of Berekiah son of Iddo the prophet:
The LORD was very angry with your fathers.
And you shall say to them: Thus says the LORD of hosts: Return to me, declares the LORD of hosts, and I will return to you, says the LORD of hosts.

Do not be like your fathers, to whom the former prophets proclaimed, saying, "Thus says the LORD of hosts: Turn back, please, from your evil ways and your evil deeds." But they did not listen and did not pay attention to me, declares the LORD.
Your fathers — where are they? And the prophets, do they live for ever?

But my words and my statutes, which I commanded my servants the prophets — did they not overtake your fathers? And they turned back and said, "Just as the LORD of hosts planned to do to us, according to our ways and according to our deeds, so he has done with us."
On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month — that is the month of Shebat — in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah son of Berekiah son of Iddo the prophet:
I saw in the night, and there was a man riding on a red horse. He was standing among the myrtles in the hollow, and behind him were horses: red, sorrel and white.
And I said, "What are these, my lord?" And the angel who was speaking with me said to me, "I will show you what these are."
And the man who was standing among the myrtles answered and said, "These are the ones whom the LORD has sent to go about on the earth."
And they answered the angel of the LORD who was standing among the myrtles and said, "We have gone about on the earth, and all the earth is at rest and undisturbed."
And the angel of the LORD answered and said, "LORD of hosts, how long will you have no compassion on Jerusalem and on the cities of Judah, with which you have been indignant these seventy years?"
And the LORD answered the angel who was speaking with me with good words, comforting words.
And the angel who was speaking with me said to me: Proclaim, saying, "Thus says the LORD of hosts: I am jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with great jealousy,
and with great anger I am angry with the nations that are at ease; for I was angry a little, and they helped make it worse.
Therefore thus says the LORD: I have returned to Jerusalem with compassion. My house will be rebuilt in it, declares the LORD of hosts, and a measuring-line will be stretched out over Jerusalem.
Proclaim again, saying: Thus says the LORD of hosts: My cities will again overflow with good, and the LORD will again comfort Zion and will again choose Jerusalem.
And I lifted up my eyes and saw, and there were four horns.
And I said to the angel who was speaking with me, "What are these?" And he said to me, "These are the horns that scattered Judah, Israel and Jerusalem."
And the LORD showed me four craftsmen.

And I said, "What are these coming to do?" And he said, "These are the horns that scattered Judah, so that no one lifted his head; and these have come to terrify them, to throw down the horns of the nations that lifted a horn against the land of Judah to scatter it."

zechariah_2.t: And I lifted up my eyes and saw, and there was a man with a measuring cord in his hand.
And I said, "Where are you going?" And he said to me, "To measure Jerusalem, to see how great its breadth is and how great its length."
And there was the angel who was speaking with me, going out; and another angel was going out to meet him.
And he said to him, "Run, speak to this young man: Jerusalem will remain as open regions, because of the multitude of people and livestock in her midst."
"And I myself will be for her, declares the LORD, a wall of fire all around, and I will be for glory in her midst."
Alas, alas! Flee from the land of the north, declares the LORD, for I have spread you out like the four winds of the heavens, declares the LORD.
Alas, Zion! Escape, you who dwell with the daughter of Babylon.
For thus says the LORD of hosts — after glory he sent me to the nations who plundered you — for whoever touches you touches the pupil of his eye.
For look, I am brandishing my hand over them, and they will become plunder for their own slaves; and you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me.
Shout for joy and rejoice, daughter of Zion, for look, I am coming, and I will dwell in your midst, declares the LORD.
And many nations will join themselves to the LORD on that day, and they will become a people for me; and I will dwell in your midst, and you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me to you.
And the LORD will take Judah as his portion for an inheritance on the holy ground, and he will again choose Jerusalem.
Hush, all flesh, before the LORD, for he has roused himself from his holy dwelling.

zechariah_3.t: And he showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the LORD, with the accuser standing at his right hand to accuse him.
And the LORD said to the accuser, "May the LORD rebuke you, accuser! And may the LORD rebuke you, he who has chosen Jerusalem! Is this not a brand snatched from the fire?"
And Joshua was clothed in filthy garments as he stood before the angel.
And he answered and said to those standing before him, "Remove the filthy garments from him." And he said to him, "See, I have taken your iniquity away from you, and I will clothe you in robes."
And I said, "Let them put a clean turban on his head." And they put the clean turban on his head and clothed him in garments, and the angel of the LORD was standing by.
And the angel of the LORD admonished Joshua, saying:
Thus says the LORD of hosts: If you walk in my ways and if you keep my charge, then you also will govern my house and guard my courts, and I will give you access among these who are standing here.
Hear, please, Joshua the high priest, you and your companions who sit before you — for they are men who are a sign — for look, I am bringing my servant, the Branch.

For here is the stone that I have set before Joshua — on one stone are seven eyes. Look, I am engraving its engraving, declares the LORD of hosts, and I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day.
On that day, declares the LORD of hosts, each of you will invite his neighbour to sit under a vine and under a fig tree.

zechariah_4.t: And the angel who was speaking with me returned and roused me, like a man who is roused from his sleep.
And he said to me, "What are you seeing?" And I said, "I see a lampstand, all of it gold, with a bowl on its top and its seven lamps on it — seven and seven pipes for the lamps that are on its top."
And two olive trees are by it, one at the right of the bowl and one at its left.
And I answered and said to the angel who was speaking with me, "What are these, my lord?"
And the angel who was speaking with me answered and said to me, "Do you not know what these are?" And I said, "No, my lord."
And he answered and said to me: This is the word of the LORD to Zerubbabel: Not by strength and not by power, but by my spirit, says the LORD of hosts.
Who are you, great mountain? Before Zerubbabel you will become level ground! And he will bring out the top stone with shouts of "Favour, favour to it!"
And the word of the LORD came to me:
The hands of Zerubbabel have founded this house, and his hands will finish it; and you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me to you.
For who has despised the day of small things? They will rejoice and see the tin stone in the hand of Zerubbabel. These seven are the eyes of the LORD; they rove about in all the earth.
And I answered and said to him, "What are these two olive trees, at the right of the lampstand and at its left?"
And I answered a second time and said to him, "What are these two clusters of the olive trees beside the two golden pipes, which are pouring out the gold from upon them?"
And he said to me, "Do you not know what these are?" And I said, "No, my lord."
And he said, "These are the two sons of the fresh oil, who stand by the Lord of all the earth."

zechariah_5.t: And I turned and lifted up my eyes and saw, and there was a flying scroll.
And he said to me, "What are you seeing?" And I said, "I am seeing a flying scroll; its length is twenty cubits and its breadth ten cubits."

And he said to me: "This is the curse that goes forth over the face of all the land; for everyone who steals has been purged away on this side according to it, and everyone who swears has been purged away on this side according to it."

"I have sent it forth, declares the LORD of hosts, and it will go into the house of the thief and into the house of the one who swears falsely by my name; and it will lodge in the midst of his house and destroy it, both its timbers and its stones."
And the angel who was speaking with me went out and said to me, "Lift up your eyes, please, and see what this is that goes forth."
And I said, "What is it?" And he said, "This is the ephah that goes forth." And he said, "This is their appearance in all the land."
And there was a round cover of lead being lifted, and there was one woman sitting in the midst of the ephah.
And he said, "This is Wickedness." And he threw her into the midst of the ephah and threw the weight of lead onto its mouth.

And I lifted up my eyes and saw, and there were two women going forth, and wind was in their wings; and they had wings like the wings of the stork. And they lifted up the ephah between the earth and the heavens.
And I said to the angel who was speaking with me, "Where are they taking the ephah?"
And he said to me, "To build a house for it in the land of Shinar; and when it is prepared, it will be set down there on its own stand."

zechariah_6.t: And I turned and lifted up my eyes and saw, and there were four chariots coming out from between the two mountains; and the mountains were mountains of bronze.
With the first chariot were red horses, and with the second chariot black horses,
and with the third chariot white horses, and with the fourth chariot dappled, strong horses.
And I answered and said to the angel who was speaking with me, "What are these, my lord?"
And the angel answered and said to me, "These are the four winds of the heavens, going forth from presenting themselves before the Lord of all the earth."
The chariot with the black horses is going out to the land of the north, and the white have gone out after them, and the dappled have gone out to the land of the south.
