And the strong ones have gone out and have sought to go, to go about on the earth. And he said, "Go, go about on the earth." And they went about on the earth.
And he called out to me and spoke to me: "See, those going out to the land of the north have caused my spirit to rest in the land of the north."
And the word of the LORD came to me:
Take from the exiles — from Heldai, from Tobiah and from Jedaiah — and go yourself on that day; go to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah, who have come from Babylon.
And you shall take silver and gold and make a crown, and set it on the head of Joshua son of Jehozadak the high priest.
And you shall say to him: Thus says the LORD of hosts: Here is a man — his name is the Branch — and from where he is he will sprout, and he will build the temple of the LORD.

And he himself will build the temple of the LORD, and he himself will bear majesty, and he will sit and rule on his throne; and there will be a priest on his throne, and a counsel of peace will be between the two of them.
And the crown will be for Helem, for Tobiah, for Jedaiah and for Hen son of Zephaniah, as a memorial in the temple of the LORD.

And those who are far off will come and build in the temple of the LORD, and you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me to you. And this will be, if you diligently listen to the voice of the LORD your God —

zechariah_7.t: And in the fourth year of Darius the king, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah on the fourth day of the ninth month, in Kislev.
And Bethel had sent Sharezer and Regem-melech and his men to entreat the face of the LORD,
to say to the priests of the house of the LORD of hosts, and to the prophets: "Shall I weep in the fifth month, consecrating myself, as I have done these many years?"
And the word of the LORD of hosts came to me:
Say to all the people of the land and to the priests: When you fasted and mourned in the fifth and in the seventh month these seventy years, was it really for me that you fasted?
And when you eat and when you drink, is it not you who are the eaters and you who are the drinkers?

Are these not the words that the LORD proclaimed by the hand of the former prophets, when Jerusalem was inhabited and at ease, with her cities around her, and the Negev and the Shephelah were inhabited?
And the word of the LORD came to Zechariah:
Thus says the LORD of hosts: Judge with a judgement of faithfulness, and do loyalty and compassion, each with his brother.
And do not oppress the widow and the fatherless, the sojourner and the poor; and do not plan harm against one another in your heart.
But they refused to pay attention; they turned a stubborn shoulder and made their ears too heavy to hear.
And they made their heart flint, so as not to hear the law and the words that the LORD of hosts had sent by his spirit through the former prophets. And there was great anger from the LORD of hosts.
And it was: just as he called and they did not listen, so they called and I did not listen, says the LORD of hosts.

And I stormed them away over all the nations that they had not known, and the land was left desolate behind them, with no one passing through and no one returning; and they made a land of desire into a waste.

zechariah_8.t: And the word of the LORD of hosts came:
Thus says the LORD of hosts: I am jealous for Zion with great jealousy, and with great rage I am jealous for her.
Thus says the LORD: I have returned to Zion and will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem; and Jerusalem will be called the City of Faithfulness, and the mountain of the LORD of hosts, the Holy Mountain.
Thus says the LORD of hosts: Old men and old women will again sit in the open squares of Jerusalem, each with his staff in his hand for the abundance of his days.
And the open squares of the city will be filled with boys and girls playing in her open squares.
Thus says the LORD of hosts: If it is too difficult in the eyes of the remnant of this people in those days, will it also be too difficult in my eyes? declares the LORD of hosts.
Thus says the LORD of hosts: Look, I am saving my people from the land of the east and from the land of the setting of the sun.
And I will bring them and they will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem; and they will become a people for me, and I myself will become God for them, in faithfulness and in righteousness.

Thus says the LORD of hosts: Let your hands be strong, you who in these days are hearing these words from the mouth of the prophets who spoke from the day the house of the LORD of hosts was founded, the temple, to be rebuilt.

For before those days there was no wage for a person and no wage for the animal, and for the one going out and the one coming in there was no peace from the adversary; and I set every person each against his neighbour.
But now I am not as in the former days toward the remnant of this people, declares the LORD of hosts.

For there will be a sowing of peace: the vine will give its fruit, the land will give its produce, and the heavens will give their dew; and I will give the remnant of this people all these things as an inheritance.
And it will be that, just as you were a curse among the nations, house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will save you and you will be a blessing. Do not be afraid; let your hands be strong.
For thus says the LORD of hosts: Just as I planned to do harm to you when your fathers provoked me to anger, says the LORD of hosts, and I did not relent —
so I have turned back and planned in these days to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. Do not be afraid.
These are the things that you shall do: Speak truth, each with his neighbour; judge with faithfulness and a judgement of peace in your gates.
And do not plan in your heart harm against one another, and do not love a false oath; for all these are things that I hate, declares the LORD.
And the word of the LORD of hosts came to me:

Thus says the LORD of hosts: The fast of the fourth month, the fast of the fifth, the fast of the seventh and the fast of the tenth will become joy and gladness for the house of Judah, and good appointed times. So love faithfulness and peace.
Thus says the LORD of hosts: Peoples will yet come, and the inhabitants of many cities;
and the inhabitants of one city will go to another, saying, "Let us go at once to entreat the face of the LORD and to seek the LORD of hosts." "I will go, I too."
And many peoples and mighty nations will come to seek the LORD of hosts in Jerusalem and to entreat the face of the LORD.

Thus says the LORD of hosts: In those days, ten men from all the tongues of the nations will take hold — they will take hold of the skirt of a Jewish man and say, "Let us go with you, for we have heard that God is with you."

zechariah_9.t: An oracle. The word of the LORD: It is against the land of Hadrach, and Damascus is its resting place; for to the LORD belongs the eye of humankind and all the tribes of Israel.
and also Hamath, which borders on it; Tyre and Sidon, for she is very wise.
And Tyre built a fortification for herself and heaped up silver like dust and gold like the mud of the streets.
Look, the Lord will dispossess her and strike her wealth into the sea, and she will be consumed by fire.
Ashkelon will see and be afraid, and Gaza, and she will writhe greatly, and Ekron, for her object of confidence has been shamed. A king will perish from Gaza, and Ashkelon will not be inhabited.
And a mixed people will dwell in Ashdod, and I will cut off the pride of the Philistines.
And I will remove his blood from his mouth and his detestable things from between his teeth; and he too will be left for our God, and he will be like a chief in Judah, and Ekron like a Jebusite.
And I will encamp at my house as a guard against anyone passing through or returning, and no oppressor will pass over them again, for now I have seen with my own eyes.

Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion! Shout aloud, daughter of Jerusalem! Look, your king comes to you: righteous and having salvation is he, poor and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.

And I will cut off chariotry from Ephraim and the horse from Jerusalem, and the battle bow will be cut off; and he will speak peace to the nations, and his dominion will be from sea to sea and from the River to the ends of the earth.
As for you also — by the blood of your covenant I have set your prisoners free from the pit in which there is no water.
Return to the stronghold, prisoners of the hope! Today too I declare: I will restore double to you.
For I have bent Judah for myself as a bow; I have filled it with Ephraim. And I will rouse your sons, Zion, against your sons, Greece, and make you like the sword of a warrior.
And the LORD will appear over them, and his arrow will go forth like the lightning; and Lord GOD will blow the horn and go in the storm winds of the south.
The LORD of hosts will shield them, and they will devour and subdue the sling-stones; and they will drink and be in an uproar as with wine, and be full like the basin, like the corners of the altar.
And the LORD their God will save them on that day as the flock of his people; for they are stones of a crown, glittering over his ground.
For how great is his goodness, and how great his beauty! Grain will make the young men flourish, and new wine the virgins.

zechariah_10.t: Ask rain from the LORD at the time of the spring rain — the LORD who makes the thunder-clouds; and he gives them showers of rain, to each one vegetation in the field.

For the teraphim speak wickedness and the diviners see falsehood; they speak dreams of emptiness and comfort with futility. Therefore the people have set out like a flock; they are afflicted, for there is no shepherd.

My anger has burned against the shepherds, and I will visit punishment upon the leaders; for the LORD of hosts has visited his flock, the house of Judah, and will make them like his horse of majesty in the battle.
From him a cornerstone, from him a tent peg, from him the bow of war, from him every ruler will come forth together.
And they will be like warriors, treading down in the mud of the streets in the battle; and they will fight, for the LORD is with them, and they will put to shame the riders of horses.

And I will make the house of Judah strong, and the house of Joseph I will save, and I will restore them, for I have had compassion on them; and they will be as though I had not rejected them, for I am the LORD their God and I will answer them.
And Ephraim will be like a warrior, and their heart will be glad as with wine; their children will see and be glad, their heart will rejoice in the LORD.
I will whistle for them and gather them, for I have redeemed them; and they will multiply as they once multiplied.
And I will sow them among the peoples, and in distant places they will remember me; and they will live with their children and return.
And I will bring them back from the land of Egypt, and from Assyria I will gather them; and I will bring them to the land of Gilead and Lebanon, and there will not be room enough for them.

And he will pass through the sea of trouble and strike the waves in the sea, and all the depths of the Nile will dry up; the pride of Assyria will be brought down, and the sceptre of Egypt will depart.
And I will make them strong in the LORD, and in his name they will go about, declares the LORD.

zechariah_11.t: Open your doors, Lebanon, and let fire consume your cedars!
Wail, cypress, for the cedar has fallen, for the majestic ones have been devastated! Wail, oaks of Bashan, for the impenetrable forest has come down!
The sound of the wailing of the shepherds, for their splendour has been devastated! The sound of the roaring of young lions, for the thicket of the Jordan has been devastated!
Thus says the LORD my God: Shepherd the flock of slaughter,
whose buyers kill them and are not held guilty, and whose sellers say, "Blessed be the LORD, for I have grown rich!" and their own shepherds have no compassion on them.

For I will no longer have compassion on the inhabitants of the land, declares the LORD. Look, I am delivering up each person into the hand of his neighbour and into the hand of his king; and they will crush the land, and I will not rescue it from their hand.
And I shepherded the flock of slaughter — the afflicted of the flock, that is. And I took for myself two staffs: one I called Pleasantness, and one I called Bonds. And I shepherded the flock.
And I annihilated the three shepherds in one month. My being grew short with them, and their being also loathed me.
And I said: I will not shepherd you. The one that is dying, let it die; the one that is being destroyed, let it be destroyed; and those that survive, let them devour each the flesh of her neighbour.
And I took my staff Pleasantness and cut it up, to break my covenant that I had made with all the peoples.
And it was broken on that day. And so the afflicted of the flock, who were watching me, knew that it was the word of the LORD.
And I said to them: "If it is good in your eyes, give me my wages; and if not, refrain." And they weighed out my wages, thirty pieces of silver.

And the LORD said to me: "Throw it to the potter — the magnificent price at which I was valued by them!" And I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them into the house of the LORD, to the potter.
And I cut up my second staff, Bonds, to break the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.
And the LORD said to me: "Take for yourself again the equipment of a foolish shepherd."

For look, I am raising up a shepherd in the land: those that are being destroyed he will not visit, the young he will not seek, and the maimed he will not heal; the one that stands firm he will not sustain; and he will eat the flesh of the fat one and tear off their hooves.
Woe to my worthless shepherd, who abandons the flock! A sword against his arm and against his right eye! Let his arm wither utterly, and let his right eye grow completely dim.

zechariah_12.t: An oracle. The word of the LORD concerning Israel — declares the LORD, who stretched out the heavens and founded the earth and formed the spirit of a human within him:
Look, I am making Jerusalem a bowl of reeling for all the peoples all around; and it will be against Judah too, in the siege against Jerusalem.
And it will be on that day that I will make Jerusalem a stone of burden for all the peoples; all who lift it will surely injure themselves, and all the nations of the earth will gather against her.

On that day, declares the LORD, I will strike every horse with bewilderment and its rider with madness; but over the house of Judah I will open my eyes, and every horse of the peoples I will strike with blindness.
And the chiefs of Judah will say in their heart: "The inhabitants of Jerusalem are strength for me, by the LORD of hosts their God."

On that day I will make the chiefs of Judah like a pot of fire among wood and like a torch of fire among cut grain, and they will consume all the peoples all around, on the right and on the left; and Jerusalem will remain again in her place, in Jerusalem.
And the LORD will save the tents of Judah first, so that the splendour of the house of David and the splendour of the inhabitants of Jerusalem may not be exalted above Judah.

On that day the LORD will shield the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and the one among them who stumbles will be like David on that day, and the house of David like God, like the angel of the LORD before them.
And it will be on that day that I will seek to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem.

And I will pour out on the house of David and on the inhabitants of Jerusalem a spirit of favour and supplications; and they will look to me, the one whom they pierced through, and they will mourn over him as one mourns over an only son, and grieve bitterly over him as one grieves over a firstborn.
On that day the mourning in Jerusalem will be great, like the mourning of Hadad-rimmon in the plain of Megiddo.
And the land will mourn, clan by clan, each apart: the clan of the house of David apart, and their wives apart; the clan of the house of Nathan apart, and their wives apart;
the clan of the house of Levi apart, and their wives apart; the clan of the Shimeites apart, and their wives apart;
all the clans that remain, clan by clan, each apart, and their wives apart.

zechariah_13.t: On that day a fountain will be opened for the house of David and for the inhabitants of Jerusalem, for sin and for impurity.

And it will be on that day, declares the LORD of hosts, that I will cut off the names of the idols from the land, and they will not be remembered again; and I will also make the prophets and the spirit of uncleanness pass from the land.

And when anyone still prophesies, his father and his mother who begot him will say to him, "You shall not live, for you have spoken falsehood in the name of the LORD." And his father and his mother who begot him will pierce him through when he prophesies.
And on that day the prophets will be ashamed, each of his vision when he prophesies; and they will not wear a hairy cloak in order to deceive.
And he will say, "I am not a prophet; I am a man who tills the ground, for someone sold me in my youth."
And someone will say to him, "What are these wounds on your chest?" And he will say, "Those with which I was wounded in the house of my friends."

Sword, awake against my shepherd, and against the man who is my companion, declares the LORD of hosts. Strike the shepherd, and let the flock be scattered; and I will turn my hand against the little ones.
And it will be in all the land, declares the LORD, that two parts in it will be cut off and perish, and a third will be left in it.

And I will bring the third into the fire and refine them as silver is refined, and test them as gold is tested. They will call on my name and I will answer them. I will say, "They are my people"; and they will say, "The LORD is my God."

zechariah_14.t: Look, a day is coming for the LORD, and your plunder will be divided in your midst.

And I will gather all the nations to Jerusalem for the battle; and the city will be captured, the houses plundered and the women raped; and half the city will go out into exile, but the rest of the people will not be cut off from the city.
And the LORD will go forth and fight against those nations, as on the day he fights, on a day of battle.

And his feet will stand on that day on the Mount of Olives, which is before Jerusalem on the east; and the Mount of Olives will be split in half, from east to west, a very great valley; and half the mountain will move northward and half of it southward.

And you will flee by the valley of my mountains, for the valley of the mountains will reach to Azal; and you will flee as you fled from the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah. And the LORD my God will come, all the holy ones with him.
And it will be on that day that there will be no light; the splendid ones will congeal.
And there will be one day — it is known to the LORD — neither day nor night; and at the time of evening there will be light.
And on that day living waters will go out from Jerusalem, half of them to the eastern sea and half of them to the western sea; in summer and in winter it will be so.
And the LORD will become king over all the earth. On that day the LORD will be one, and his name one.

All the land will be changed like the Arabah, from Geba to Rimmon south of Jerusalem; and she will rise and remain in her place, from the Gate of Benjamin to the place of the First Gate, to the Corner Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel to the king's winepresses.
And people will dwell in her, and there will be no more devoting to destruction; and Jerusalem will remain in security.

And this will be the plague with which the LORD will strike all the peoples that waged war against Jerusalem: their flesh will rot while they are standing on their feet, and their eyes will rot in their sockets, and their tongue will rot in their mouth.
And on that day a great panic from the LORD will be among them; each will take hold of the hand of his neighbour, and his hand will go up against the hand of his neighbour.
And Judah too will fight at Jerusalem; and the wealth of all the surrounding nations will be gathered — gold and silver and garments in very great abundance.
And so will be the plague of the horse, the mule, the camel and the donkey, and of all the livestock that will be in those camps — like this plague.
And everyone who remains of all the nations that came against Jerusalem will go up year by year to bow down to the King, the LORD of hosts, and to keep the festival of booths.
And whoever does not go up, from the clans of the earth, to Jerusalem to bow down to the King, the LORD of hosts — on them there will be no rain.

And if the clan of Egypt does not go up and does not come, then there will be no rain on them; there will be the plague with which the LORD strikes the nations that do not go up to keep the festival of booths.
This will be the punishment for the sin of Egypt and the punishment for the sin of all the nations that do not go up to keep the festival of booths.
On that day there will be on the bells of the horses: "Holy to the LORD." And the pots in the house of the LORD will be like the basins before the altar.

And every pot in Jerusalem and in Judah will be holy to the LORD of hosts; and all who sacrifice will come and take some of them and boil in them; and there will no longer be a Canaanite in the house of the LORD of hosts on that day.

zephaniah_1.t: The word of the LORD that came to Zephaniah son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, son of Hezekiah, in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah.
I will utterly sweep away everything from the face of the ground — declares the LORD.

I will make an end of human and animal; I will make an end of the birds of the heavens and the fish of the sea, and the stumbling-blocks along with the wicked; and I will cut humankind off from the face of the ground — declares the LORD.
I will stretch out my hand against Judah and against all the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and I will cut off from this place the remnant of Baal, the name of the idol-priests along with the priests —
and those who bow down on the rooftops to the host of the heavens; and those who bow down and swear to the LORD and who also swear by Milcom;
and those who turn back from following the LORD, who have not sought the LORD and have not enquired of him.
Hush before Lord GOD! For the day of the LORD is near; for the LORD has prepared a sacrifice, he has consecrated those he has invited.
And it will be, on the day of the LORD's sacrifice, that I will punish the princes and the sons of the king and all who dress in foreign clothing.
And on that day I will punish everyone who leaps over the threshold, those who fill their masters' house with violence and deceit.
And on that day — declares the LORD — there will be the sound of a cry from the Fish Gate, and a wailing from the Second District, and a great crashing from the hills.
Wail, you who live in the Mortar, for all the trading people are destroyed; all who weigh out silver are cut off.
And at that time I will search Jerusalem with lamps, and punish the men who are settling like wine on its dregs, who say in their heart, "The LORD will do neither good nor harm."
Their wealth will become plunder, and their houses a desolation; they will build houses and not live in them, and plant vineyards and not drink their wine.
The great day of the LORD is near, near and hurrying fast. The sound of the day of the LORD is bitter; there the warrior cries out.
That day is a day of fury, a day of trouble and distress, a day of devastation and desolation, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and thick darkness,
a day of trumpet and battle-cry against the fortified cities and against the high corner-towers.
And I will bring distress on humankind, and they will walk like the blind, because they have sinned against the LORD. Their blood will be poured out like dust, and their bowels like dung.

Neither their silver nor their gold will be able to deliver them on the day of the LORD's fury. In the fire of his jealousy the whole earth will be consumed, for he will make a complete destruction, and a terrible one, of all the inhabitants of the earth.

zephaniah_2.t: Gather yourselves together, gather, O nation that has no shame —
before the decree gives birth — the day passes like chaff — before the burning anger of the LORD comes upon you, before the day of the LORD's anger comes upon you.
Seek the LORD, all you humble of the land, who have kept his ordinance. Seek righteousness, seek humility; perhaps you will be hidden on the day of the LORD's anger.
For Gaza will be abandoned, and Ashkelon a desolation; Ashdod — at noon they will drive her out, and Ekron will be uprooted.
Woe to the inhabitants of the sea-coast, the nation of the Kerethites! The word of the LORD is against you, Canaan, land of the Philistines: "I will destroy you, until no one lives there."
And the sea-coast will become pastures, meadows for shepherds and folds for sheep.

And the coast will belong to the remnant of the house of Judah; they will graze on it; in the houses of Ashkelon they will lie down in the evening; for the LORD their God will attend to them and restore their fortunes.
I have heard the reproach of Moab and the revilings of the Ammonites, with which they reproached my people and made themselves great against their territory.

Therefore, as I live — declares the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel — Moab will become like Sodom, and the Ammonites like Gomorrah: a patch of nettles and a salt-pit, a waste for ever. The remnant of my people will plunder them, and the rest of my nation will take possession of them.
This will be theirs in return for their pride, because they reproached and made themselves great against the people of the LORD of hosts.
The LORD will be terrible against them, for he will shrivel all the gods of the earth; and they will bow down to him, each from their own place — all the coastlands of the nations.
You also, Cushites — they are the slain of my sword.
And he will stretch out his hand against the north and destroy Assyria; he will make Nineveh a waste, a dry place like the wilderness.

Herds will lie down in her midst, every kind of animal; both the desert owl and the hedgehog will lodge on her column-tops; a voice will sing in the window, desolation on the threshold, for the cedar-work has been laid bare.

This is the jubilant city that lived in security, that said in her heart, "I am, and there is no one besides me." How she has become a waste, a lair for animals! Everyone who passes by her hisses and shakes a fist.

zephaniah_3.t: Woe to the filthy and defiled one, the city that oppresses!
She has not listened to any voice, she has not accepted discipline; she has not trusted in the LORD, she has not drawn near to her God.
Her princes in her midst are roaring lions; her judges are evening wolves that leave nothing to gnaw by morning.
Her prophets are reckless, treacherous men; her priests have profaned what is holy, they have done violence to law.
The LORD is righteous in her midst; he does no injustice. Morning by morning he brings his justice to light; it does not fail. But the unjust one knows no shame.
I have cut off nations; their corner-towers lie desolate. I have laid waste their streets, so that no one passes through. Their cities are destroyed, with no one in them, with no inhabitant.
I said, "Surely you will fear me, you will accept discipline, and her dwelling will not be cut off — all that I appointed for her." But they rose early and corrupted all their deeds.

"Therefore wait for me — declares the LORD — for the day I rise up as prey; for my judgement is to gather nations, for me to assemble kingdoms, to pour out on them my indignation, all my burning anger. For in the fire of my jealousy the whole earth will be consumed."
For then I will give the peoples a purified lip, so that all of them call on the name of the LORD and serve him shoulder to shoulder.
From beyond the rivers of Cush my suppliants, the daughter of my scattered ones, will bring my offering.

On that day you will not be ashamed of all the deeds by which you transgressed against me; for then I will remove from your midst those who exult in your pride, and you will never again be haughty on my holy mountain.
And I will leave in your midst an afflicted and poor people, and they will take refuge in the name of the LORD.
The remnant of Israel will do no injustice and will not speak falsehood, and no deceitful tongue will be found in their mouth; for they will graze and lie down, and no one will make them afraid.
Shout for joy, daughter of Zion; shout aloud, Israel; rejoice and exult with your whole heart, daughter of Jerusalem!
The LORD has removed the judgements against you; he has cleared away your enemy. The king of Israel, the LORD, is in your midst; you will never again fear evil.
On that day it will be said to Jerusalem: "Do not fear, Zion; do not let your hands go slack."
The LORD your God is in your midst, a warrior who saves. He will rejoice over you with joy; he will be silent in his love; he will be glad over you with a shout of joy.
Those grieved at being kept from the appointed feast I will gather; they were from among you — a burden upon her, a reproach.
Here I am, dealing with all who afflicted you at that time. I will save the lame, and gather the outcast; and I will make them a praise and a name in all the earth where their shame had been.

At that time I will bring you in, at the time when I gather you; for I will make you a name and a praise among all the peoples of the earth, when I restore your fortunes before your eyes, says the LORD.

1 corinthians_1.t: Paul, called to be an apostle of Christ Jesus through God's will, and Sosthenes our brother,
to God's community in Corinth - people made holy in Christ Jesus, called to be holy - together with everyone everywhere who calls on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, their Lord and ours:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I always thank my God about you, for the grace of God given to you in Christ Jesus,
because in him you were made rich in everything - in all speech and all knowledge,
just as the testimony about Christ was confirmed among you,
so that you are not lacking in any gift while you wait for our Lord Jesus Christ to be revealed -
who will also keep you firm to the end, beyond accusation on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
God is faithful - the one through whom you were called into partnership with his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.

I appeal to you, brothers and sisters, through the name of our Lord Jesus Christ: all say the same thing, and let there be no splits among you; be knit together in the same mind and the same judgment.
For it has been made clear to me about you, my brothers and sisters, by Chloe's people, that there are quarrels among you.
What I mean is this: each of you is saying, 'I belong to Paul,' 'I to Apollos,' 'I to Cephas,' 'I to Christ.'
Has Christ been carved up? Paul wasn't crucified for you, was he? Or were you baptised into Paul's name?
I thank God that I baptised none of you except Crispus and Gaius,
so no one can say you were baptised into my name.
I did baptise Stephanas' household too. Beyond that, I don't know whether I baptised anyone else.
For Christ did not send me to baptise but to announce the good news - and not with clever speech, so the cross of Christ is not emptied out.
For the message of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is God's power.
For it is written: 'I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and the intelligence of the intelligent I will set aside.'
Where is the wise one? Where is the scribe? Where is the debater of this age? Hasn't God made the world's wisdom foolish?
For since, in God's wisdom, the world did not come to know God through its wisdom, God was pleased to save those who trust through the foolishness of what is preached.
Jews ask for signs and Greeks look for wisdom,
but we proclaim a crucified Christ - an offence to Jews, foolishness to the nations,
but to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ - God's power and God's wisdom.
Because God's foolish thing is wiser than human beings, and God's weak thing is stronger than human beings.
Look at your calling, brothers and sisters: not many of you were wise according to the flesh, not many powerful, not many well-born.
But God chose the world's foolish things to shame the wise, and God chose the world's weak things to shame the strong,
and God chose the world's low-born and despised things - things that are not - to nullify the things that are,
so that no flesh may boast in God's presence.
It is from him that you are in Christ Jesus, who became wisdom for us from God - and rightness and holiness and release,
so that, as it is written, 'Let the one who boasts boast in the Lord.'

1 corinthians_2.t: And when I came to you, brothers and sisters, I did not come announcing God's mystery to you with any superiority of speech or wisdom.
For I decided to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ - and him crucified.
And I came to you in weakness, in fear, and in a great deal of trembling,
and my speech and my preaching were not in persuasive words of wisdom but in a demonstration of Spirit and power,
so that your trust would not rest in human wisdom but in God's power.
Yet we do speak wisdom among the mature - but not the wisdom of this age, nor of this age's rulers, who are being brought to nothing.
No - we speak God's wisdom in a mystery, wisdom that has been hidden, which God marked out beforehand, before the ages, for our glory.
None of the rulers of this age has known it - for if they had known, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.
But as it is written: 'What eye has not seen and ear has not heard, and what has not come up into a human heart - what God has prepared for those who love him.'
But God has revealed them to us through the Spirit; for the Spirit searches everything, even the depths of God.
For which person knows a person's own matters except that person's spirit within them? In the same way, no one has known God's matters except the Spirit of God.
And we did not receive the spirit of the world, but the Spirit that is from God, so we can know the things God has freely given us.
And we speak these things not in words taught by human wisdom but in words taught by the Spirit, explaining spiritual things to spiritual people.
A merely natural person does not accept the things of God's Spirit, because they are foolishness to him and he cannot know them, since they are examined spiritually.
But the spiritual person examines everything, while he himself is examined by no one.
'For who has known the Lord's mind, who will instruct him?' But we have the mind of Christ.

1 corinthians_3.t: And I, brothers and sisters, could not speak to you as spiritual people but as people of flesh, as infants in Christ.
I gave you milk to drink, not solid food - you weren't ready yet. In fact you still aren't ready,
because you are still fleshly. When there is jealousy and quarrelling among you, aren't you fleshly? Aren't you walking the way people ordinarily do?
For when one says, 'I belong to Paul,' and another, 'I to Apollos,' aren't you merely human?
So what is Apollos? And what is Paul? Ones who serve, through whom you came to trust - and to each of them as the Lord gave.
I planted, Apollos watered - but God kept making it grow.
So neither the one who plants is anything nor the one who waters, but God, who makes it grow.
The one who plants and the one who waters are one, and each will receive his own wage according to his own labour.
For we are God's co-workers; you are God's field, God's building.
According to God's grace given to me, like a skilled master builder I laid a foundation, and someone else is building on it. But let each one watch how he builds.
For no one can lay another foundation than the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ.
If anyone builds on this foundation with gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, straw -
each one's work will become visible. The Day will show it, because it is revealed in fire; and the fire itself will test what sort of work each has done.
If anyone's work that he built survives, he will receive a wage.
If anyone's work burns up, he will suffer loss; he himself will be saved, but like someone coming through fire.
Don't you know that you are God's temple, and that God's Spirit lives in you?
If anyone destroys God's temple, God will destroy that person - for God's temple is holy, and that is what you are.
Let no one deceive himself. If anyone among you thinks he is wise in this age, let him become foolish so that he may become wise.
For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God. For it is written: 'He is the one who catches the wise in their own craftiness' -
and again: 'The Lord knows that the reasonings of the wise are empty.'
So let no one boast in people. For everything is yours -
whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas, whether the world or life or death, whether things present or things to come - all of it is yours,
and you are Christ's, and Christ is God's.

1 corinthians_4.t: This is how a person should regard us: as Christ's assistants and stewards of God's mysteries.
Now what is looked for in stewards is that a person be found faithful.
For me it counts for very little to be examined by you, or by any human court. In fact I don't even examine myself.
For I am aware of nothing against myself - but that is not what acquits me. The one who examines me is the Lord.

So do not judge anything before the time, until the Lord comes - the one who will bring to light what is hidden in darkness and make visible the intentions of hearts. And then each will get his praise from God.

Brothers and sisters, I have applied these things to myself and Apollos for your sake, so that through us you may learn 'nothing beyond what is written', and so that none of you will be puffed up in favour of one against another.
For who makes you different? What do you have that you did not receive? And if you did receive it, why do you boast as though you had not?
Already you are full! Already you have grown rich! You have begun to reign without us - and I wish you really did reign, so that we could reign with you!
For I think God has put us apostles on display at the end of the line, like people condemned to death - because we have become a spectacle to the world, to angels and to people.
We are fools for Christ's sake, but you are sensible in Christ; we are weak, but you are strong; you are honoured, but we are dishonoured.
Right up to this hour we go hungry and thirsty, we are poorly clothed and beaten and homeless,
and we work hard with our own hands. When we are abused, we bless; when we are persecuted, we endure;
when we are slandered, we speak kindly. We have become like the scourings of the world, the scrapings of everything, right up to now.
I am not writing this to shame you, but to warn you as my beloved children.
For even if you had ten thousand guardians in Christ, you do not have many fathers; for in Christ Jesus I fathered you through the good news.
So I appeal to you: become imitators of me.
That is why I sent Timothy to you, who is my beloved and faithful child in the Lord. He will remind you of my ways in Christ Jesus, just as I teach everywhere in every community.
Some have become puffed up, as though I were not coming to you.
But I will come to you soon, if the Lord wills, and I will find out not the talk of these puffed-up people but their power.
For the kingdom of God is not in talk but in power.
What do you want? Am I to come to you with a rod, or with love and a spirit of gentleness?

1 corinthians_5.t: It is actually reported that there is sexual immorality among you - and immorality of a kind not even found among the nations: someone has his father's wife.
And you are puffed up! Shouldn't you rather have gone into mourning, so that the man who did this deed would be removed from among you?
For my part - absent in body but present in spirit - I have already passed judgment, as if present, on the man who did this,
in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ: when you are gathered together, and my spirit with the power of our Lord Jesus,
to hand this man over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that the spirit may be saved on the day of the Lord.
Your boasting is not good. Don't you know that a little yeast leavens the whole batch of dough?
Clean out the old yeast so that you may be a new batch, since you are unleavened. For our Passover lamb, Christ, has been sacrificed.
So let us keep the festival, not with old yeast, nor with the yeast of malice and evil, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
I wrote to you in my letter not to mix with sexually immoral people -
not meaning the immoral of this world generally, or the greedy and the swindlers or idolaters, since in that case you would have to leave the world.

But now I am writing to you not to mix with anyone who is called a brother if he is sexually immoral, or greedy, or an idolater, or abusive, or a drunkard, or a swindler - with such a person, do not even eat.
For what business is it of mine to judge outsiders? Isn't it those inside that you are to judge -
while God judges those outside? 'Remove the evil one from among yourselves.'

1 corinthians_6.t: Does one of you, when he has a matter against another, dare to go to law before the unjust and not before God's people?
Or don't you know that God's people will judge the world? And if the world is judged among you, are you unworthy of the smallest cases?
Don't you know that we will judge angels? How much more, then, everyday matters!
So when you have cases about everyday matters, do you seat as judges those the community counts as nothing?
I say this to shame you. Is there really no one wise among you who will be able to decide between one brother and another?
Instead, brother goes to law against brother - and that before unbelievers!
Actually, it is already a total defeat for you that you have lawsuits with one another. Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be defrauded?
But you yourselves wrong and defraud - and you do it to brothers and sisters.
Or don't you know that wrongdoers will not inherit God's kingdom? Do not be misled: not the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor men who lie with men -
nor thieves, nor the greedy; no drunkards, no abusers, no swindlers will inherit God's kingdom.
And some of you were these things. But you were washed, you were made holy, you were justified, in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and in the Spirit of our God.
'Everything is permitted me' - but not everything is beneficial. 'Everything is permitted me' - but I will not be brought under anything's authority.
'Food is for the stomach and the stomach for food' - and God will bring both to nothing. But the body is not for sexual immorality; it is for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.
And God both raised the Lord and will raise us up through his power.
Don't you know that your bodies are parts of Christ? So shall I take Christ's parts and make them a prostitute's parts? Absolutely not.
Or don't you know that whoever is joined to a prostitute is one body with her? For it says, 'The two will become one flesh.'
But whoever is joined to the Lord is one spirit with him.
Flee sexual immorality. Every other sin a person commits is outside the body, but the one who is sexually immoral sins against his own body.
Or don't you know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God - and that you are not your own?
You were bought at a price. So glorify God in your body - and in your spirit, which are God's.

1 corinthians_7.t: Now, about the things you wrote to me: 'It is good for a man not to touch a woman.'
But because of sexual immorality, let each man have his own wife and each woman have her own husband.
Let the husband give his wife what he owes her, and likewise the wife her husband.
The wife does not have authority over her own body; her husband does. And likewise the husband does not have authority over his own body; his wife does.

Do not defraud one another, except perhaps by agreement for a set time, so you may be free for fasting and prayer - and then be together again, so that Satan does not test you through your lack of self-control.
I say this as a concession, not as a command.
I wish all people were as I myself am. But each has his own gift from God, one of this kind, another of that.
To the unmarried and to the widows I say: it is good for them if they remain as I am.
But if they do not have self-control, let them marry - for it is better to marry than to burn.
To the married I give this instruction - not I, but the Lord: a wife is not to separate from her husband.
But if she does separate, she is to remain unmarried or be reconciled to her husband. And a husband is not to divorce his wife.
To the rest I say - I, not the Lord: if any brother has an unbelieving wife and she is content to live with him, he is not to divorce her.
And if a woman has an unbelieving husband and he is content to live with her, she is not to divorce her husband.

For the unbelieving husband has been made holy through his wife, and the unbelieving wife has been made holy through the brother. Otherwise your children would be unclean - but as it is, they are holy.
But if the unbelieving partner separates, let them separate. The brother or the sister is not enslaved in such cases; God has called you in peace.
For how do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife?
Only, let each person walk as the Lord has assigned, as God has called each one. This is what I lay down in all the communities.
Was anyone called already circumcised? He should not undo it. Was anyone called uncircumcised? He should not be circumcised.
Circumcision is nothing and uncircumcision is nothing; keeping God's commands is what matters.
Let each remain in the calling in which he was called.
Were you called as a slave? Do not let it trouble you - but if you are able to gain your freedom, take the opportunity.
For the one called in the Lord as a slave is the Lord's freed person; likewise the one called as a free person is Christ's slave.
You were bought at a price; do not become slaves of people.
Brothers and sisters, let each remain with God in whatever condition he was called.
Now about virgins: I have no command from the Lord, but I give an opinion as one who has been shown mercy by the Lord to be trustworthy.
So I think this is good, because of the present pressure - that it is good for a person to stay as he is.
Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek release. Are you free of a wife? Do not seek a wife.
But if you do marry, you have not sinned; and if a virgin marries, she has not sinned. But such people will have distress in the flesh, and I am trying to spare you.
This I say, brothers and sisters: the time has been shortened. From now on, let even those who have wives be as though they had none,
and those who weep as though not weeping, and those who rejoice as though not rejoicing, and those who buy as though not possessing,
and those who use the world as though not using it up. For the present shape of this world is passing away.
I want you to be free from anxieties. The unmarried man is anxious about the Lord's matters, how to please the Lord;
but the married man is anxious about the world's matters, how to please his wife,

and he is divided. And the unmarried woman, or the virgin, is anxious about the Lord's matters, so that she may be holy in body and in spirit; but the married woman is anxious about the world's matters, how to please her husband.
I say this for your own benefit - not to throw a noose over you, but for what is fitting and for undistracted devotion to the Lord.
If anyone thinks he is behaving improperly toward his betrothed - if she is past her prime, and it has to be so - let him do what he wants; he is not sinning: let them marry.
But whoever stands firm in his heart, under no compulsion, having authority over his own will, and has decided this in his own heart - to keep his own virgin - he will do well.
So the one who gives his own virgin in marriage does well, and the one who does not will do better.
A wife is bound for as long as her husband lives. But if her husband falls asleep, she is free to marry whomever she wishes - only in the Lord.
But in my opinion she is happier if she stays as she is - and I think I too have God's Spirit.

1 corinthians_8.t: Now about food sacrificed to idols. We know that 'we all have knowledge'. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.
If anyone thinks he knows something, he does not yet know as he ought to know.
But if anyone loves God, this person is known by him.
So, about eating food sacrificed to idols: we know that 'an idol is nothing in the world' and that 'there is no God but one'.
For even if there are so-called gods, whether in heaven or on earth - as indeed there are many gods and many lords -
yet for us there is one God, the Father, from whom all things are and for whom we exist; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things are and through whom we exist.
But not everyone has this knowledge. Some, being until now accustomed to the idol, eat food as though it really were sacrificed to an idol, and their conscience, being weak, is stained.
Food will not present us to God: we are no worse off if we do not eat, and no better off if we do.
But watch that this right of yours does not somehow become a stumbling-block to the weak.
For if someone sees you, the one who has knowledge, reclining at table in an idol's temple, will not his conscience, weak as it is, be built up to eat food sacrificed to idols?
So the weak person is destroyed by your knowledge - the brother for whom Christ died.
And sinning like this against brothers and sisters, and striking their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.
So if food trips up my brother, I will never eat meat again, so that I do not trip up my brother.

1 corinthians_9.t: Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus Christ our Lord? Are you not my work in the Lord?
If I am not an apostle to others, at least I am to you — you are the seal on my apostleship in the Lord.
Here is my defence to those who put me on trial:
Do we not have the right to eat and drink?
Do we not have the right to take a believing wife along with us, as the other apostles do, and the Lord's brothers, and Cephas?
Or are Barnabas and I the only ones with no right to stop working for a living?
Who ever serves as a soldier at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat its fruit? Or who shepherds a flock and does not drink from the flock's milk?
Am I saying this only on human authority? Doesn't the law say the same?
In the law of Moses it is written: Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain. Is it oxen God is concerned about?
Isn't he saying it entirely for our sake? Yes, it was written for us, because the one who ploughs ought to plough in hope, and the one who threshes should thresh in hope of a share.
If we sowed spiritual things among you, is it too much if we reap material things from you?
If others share this right over you, don't we all the more? But we did not use this right. We put up with everything rather than put any obstacle in the way of the good news of Christ.
Don't you know that those who work in the temple eat what comes from the temple, and those who attend at the altar share in what is on the altar?
In the same way the Lord commanded that those who announce the good news should live from the good news.
But I have used none of these rights. And I am not writing this so that it will be done for me. I would rather die than — no one is going to empty out my boast.
If I announce the good news, that is no boast of mine — I am under compulsion. It would go badly for me if I did not announce it.
If I do this willingly, I have a wage coming. If unwillingly, I have simply been entrusted with a job to manage.
So what is my wage? Just this: that when I announce the good news I can offer it free of charge, and so not make full use of my right in the good news.
Free as I am from everyone, I made myself a slave to everyone, to win over as many as possible.
To the Jews I became like a Jew, to win Jews. To those under the law I became like one under the law — though I am not myself under the law — to win those under the law.
To those outside the law I became like one outside the law — not being outside God's law, but inside the law of Christ — to win those outside the law.
To the weak I became weak, to win the weak. I have become all things to all people, so that by every means I might save some.
I do all of this because of the good news, so that I may share in it.
Don't you know that in a race all the runners run, but only one gets the prize? Run in such a way as to take it.
Every competitor goes into strict training. They do it for a wreath that withers; we do it for one that does not.
So I do not run aimlessly, and I do not box like a man punching the air.
I bruise my own body and lead it as a slave, so that after preaching to others I am not myself found to fail the test.

1 corinthians_10.t: I do not want you to be unaware, brothers and sisters, that our ancestors were all under the cloud and all passed through the sea,
and all were baptised into Moses in the cloud and in the sea,
and all ate the same spiritual food,
and all drank the same spiritual drink; for they drank from the spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ.
But God was not pleased with most of them; their bodies were scattered across the desert.
These things happened as patterns for us, so that we would not crave what is evil, as they craved.
Do not become idol-worshippers, as some of them were. As it is written: The people sat down to eat and drink, and got up to play.
And let us not commit sexual immorality, as some of them did — and twenty-three thousand fell in a single day.
And let us not put Christ to the test, as some of them did — and they were destroyed by snakes.
And do not grumble, as some of them grumbled — and they were destroyed by the destroyer.
These things happened to them as patterns, and they were written down as a warning for us, on whom the ends of the ages have arrived.
So then, whoever thinks he is standing had better watch out that he does not fall.

No trial has taken hold of you except what is common to human beings. God is trustworthy: he will not let you be tried beyond what you can bear, but with the trial he will make the way out too, so that you are able to endure it.
So then, my dear friends, run from idol-worship.
I am speaking to you as sensible people; judge for yourselves what I am saying.
The cup of blessing that we bless — is it not a sharing in the blood of Christ? The bread that we break — is it not a sharing in the body of Christ?
Because there is one loaf, we who are many are one body — for we all share in the one loaf.
Look at Israel according to the flesh: are those who eat the sacrifices not partners with the altar?
So what am I saying? That food sacrificed to an idol is anything, or that an idol is anything?
No — what they sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God, and I do not want you to become partners with demons.
You cannot drink the Lord's cup and the cup of demons. You cannot share the Lord's table and the table of demons.
Or are we trying to provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he is?
Everything is permitted for me — but not everything is good for anyone. Everything is permitted for me — but not everything builds up.
No one should look for his own good, but for the good of the other person.
Eat anything sold in the meat market without raising questions of conscience,
for the earth is the Lord's, and everything in it.
If an unbeliever invites you over and you want to go, eat whatever is set in front of you without raising questions of conscience.
But if someone says to you, This has been offered in sacrifice, then do not eat it — for the sake of the one who told you, and for conscience; for the earth is the Lord's, and everything in it.
By conscience I mean the other person's, not your own. For why should my freedom be judged by someone else's conscience?
If I take part with thanks, why am I slandered over something I give thanks for?
So whether you eat or drink or do anything else, do it all for God's glory.
Give no offence to Jews or Greeks or to God's community,
just as I try to please everyone in everything, not looking for my own advantage but for that of the many, so that they may be saved.

1 corinthians_11.t: Follow my example, as I follow Christ's.
I praise you for remembering me in everything and for holding on to the traditions just as I passed them to you.
But I want you to know that the head of every man is Christ, and the head of a woman is the man, and the head of Christ is God.
Any man who prays or prophesies with something down over his head shames his head.
And any woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered shames her head — it is one and the same thing as having it shaved.
If a woman will not cover her head, she may as well have her hair cut off. And if it is a disgrace for a woman to have her hair cut off or shaved, then let her cover her head.
A man ought not to cover his head, since he is the image and glory of God; the woman is the glory of the man.
For the man did not come from the woman, but the woman from the man;
and the man was not created for the woman's sake, but the woman for the man's.
This is why the woman ought to have a symbol of authority on her head — because of the angels.
Even so, in the Lord woman is not independent of man, nor man of woman.
For just as the woman came from the man, so also the man comes through the woman — and everything comes from God.
Judge for yourselves: is it fitting for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?
Doesn't nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair it is a dishonour to him,
but if a woman has long hair it is her glory? For her hair has been given to her in place of a covering.
If anyone wants to argue about this — we have no such practice, and neither do God's communities.
In giving this instruction I have no praise for you, because your meetings do more harm than good.
First of all, I hear that when you meet as a community there are divisions among you, and I partly believe it.
There have to be factions among you, I suppose, so that those who are genuine become obvious.
So when you gather in one place, it is not the Lord's supper that you eat.
Each of you goes ahead with your own supper, so one is hungry and another is drunk.
Don't you have homes to eat and drink in? Or do you despise God's community and humiliate those who have nothing? What am I to say to you? Am I to praise you? In this I do not.
For what I received from the Lord I also passed on to you: that the Lord Jesus, on the night he was handed over, took bread,
and when he had given thanks he broke it and said, Take, eat; this is my body, which is broken for you. Do this in memory of me.
In the same way he took the cup after supper, saying, This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Do this, whenever you drink it, in memory of me.
For every time you eat this bread and drink this cup, you announce the Lord's death until he comes.
So whoever eats the bread or drinks the Lord's cup in an unworthy manner will be answerable for the body and blood of the Lord.
Let each person examine himself, and then eat from the bread and drink from the cup.
For whoever eats and drinks without discerning the body eats and drinks judgement on himself.
That is why many among you are weak and ill, and quite a number have died.
If we discerned ourselves, we would not be judged.
But when we are judged by the Lord, we are being trained, so that we will not be condemned along with the world.
So, my brothers and sisters, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.
If anyone is hungry, let him eat at home, so that your meetings do not bring judgement on you. I will give directions about the rest when I come.

1 corinthians_12.t: Now about spiritual matters, brothers and sisters: I do not want you to be uninformed.
You know that when you were pagans you were somehow drawn away to idols that could not speak.
So I want you to understand that no one speaking by God's Spirit says, Jesus is cursed, and no one can say, Jesus is Lord, except by the Holy Spirit.
There are different kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit.
There are different kinds of service, but the same Lord.
There are different kinds of activity, but the same God, who activates all of them in everyone.
To each person the Spirit's showing is given for the common good.
To one, a word of wisdom is given through the Spirit; to another, a word of knowledge according to the same Spirit;
to another, faith by the same Spirit; to another, gifts of healing by the one Spirit;
to another, workings of power; to another, prophecy; to another, distinguishing between spirits; to another, kinds of tongues; to another, interpretation of tongues.
All of these are the work of one and the same Spirit, who distributes them to each person individually, as he chooses.
For just as the body is one and has many parts, and all the parts of the body, many as they are, are one body — so it is with Christ.
For we were all baptised by one Spirit into one body — Jews or Greeks, slaves or free — and we were all given the one Spirit to drink.
For the body is not a single part but many.
If the foot were to say, Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body — that would not make it any less part of the body.
And if the ear were to say, Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body — that would not make it any less part of the body.
If the whole body were an eye, where would the hearing be? If the whole were hearing, where would the sense of smell be?
But in fact God arranged the parts, each one of them, in the body just as he wanted.
If they were all one part, where would the body be?
As it is, there are many parts but one body.
The eye cannot say to the hand, I do not need you — nor again the head to the feet, I do not need you.
On the contrary, the parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable,
and the parts of the body we think less honourable we surround with greater honour, and our unpresentable parts are treated with greater modesty,
while our presentable parts need none of this. But God combined the body, giving greater honour to the part that lacked it,
so that there would be no division in the body, but the parts would have the same care for one another.
If one part suffers, every part suffers with it; if one part is honoured, every part rejoices with it.
You are Christ's body, and individually parts of it.
And God has placed in the community first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then powerful deeds, then gifts of healing, acts of help, acts of guidance, kinds of tongues.
Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Do all work powerful deeds?
Do all have gifts of healing? Do all speak in tongues? Do all interpret?
But be eager for the greater gifts. And now I will show you a way beyond all comparison.

1 corinthians_13.t: If I speak in the tongues of human beings and of angels but do not have love, I have become a booming gong or a clashing cymbal.
If I have prophecy and know all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have all the faith needed to move mountains but do not have love, I am nothing.
If I give away everything I own, and if I hand over my body so that I may boast, but do not have love, I gain nothing.
Love waits without anger; love is kind. Love is not jealous, does not brag, is not inflated with itself,
does not behave disgracefully, does not look for its own interests, is not provoked, keeps no account of wrong,
does not rejoice at wrongdoing but rejoices along with the truth,
puts up with everything, trusts in everything, hopes for everything, endures everything.
Love never falls. But prophecies will be brought to an end; tongues will stop; knowledge will be brought to an end.
For we know in part and we prophesy in part,
but when the complete comes, the partial will be brought to an end.
When I was a child, I spoke like a child, I thought like a child, I reasoned like a child. When I became a man, I put an end to childish things.
For now we see through a mirror, in a riddle; then, face to face. Now I know in part; then I will know fully, just as I have been fully known.
So now these three remain: faith, hope, love. And the greatest of these is love.

1 corinthians_14.t: Pursue love. Be eager for the things of the Spirit, and above all that you may prophesy.
Anyone who speaks in a tongue is not speaking to people but to God, since no one understands; he is speaking mysteries by the Spirit.
But the one who prophesies speaks to people, building them up, urging them on and consoling them.
The one who speaks in a tongue builds himself up; the one who prophesies builds up the community.

I would like all of you to speak in tongues, but even more that you would prophesy. The one who prophesies is greater than the one who speaks in tongues — unless he interprets, so that the community may be built up.
As it is, brothers and sisters, if I come to you speaking in tongues, what good will I do you, unless I bring you some revelation or knowledge or prophecy or teaching?
Even lifeless instruments that make a sound — a flute, say, or a lyre — if they do not give distinct notes, how will anyone know what is being played?
And if the trumpet gives an uncertain call, who will get ready for battle?
It is the same with you: unless you produce speech that is clear, how will anyone know what is being said? You will be talking into the air.
There are, no doubt, any number of kinds of language in the world, and none of them is without meaning.
So if I do not know what a language means, I will be a foreigner to the speaker, and the speaker a foreigner to me.
So with you: since you are eager for spirits, seek to overflow with what builds up the community.
So the one who speaks in a tongue should pray for the power to interpret.
For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit is praying but my mind is unproductive.
So what am I to do? I will pray with my spirit, and I will pray with my mind as well. I will sing with my spirit, and I will sing with my mind as well.
Otherwise, if you are blessing God with your spirit, how will the person who is in the position of an outsider say the Amen to your thanksgiving, when he does not know what you are saying?
You may be giving thanks well enough, but the other person is not built up.
I thank God that I speak in tongues more than all of you.
But in the assembly I would rather speak five words with my mind, to instruct others as well, than ten thousand words in a tongue.
Brothers and sisters, do not be children in your thinking. Be infants when it comes to evil, but in your thinking be grown up.
In the law it is written: By people of strange tongues and by the lips of foreigners I will speak to this people, and even so they will not listen to me, says the Lord.
So then, tongues are a sign not for believers but for unbelievers; prophecy is not for unbelievers but for believers.
So if the whole community comes together in one place and everyone is speaking in tongues, and outsiders or unbelievers come in, will they not say you are out of your minds?
But if everyone prophesies and an unbeliever or an outsider comes in, he is convicted by all, examined by all,
and the secrets of his heart become plain, and so he falls on his face and worships God, declaring that God is really among you.
So what should happen, brothers and sisters? When you come together, each of you has a psalm, a teaching, a revelation, a tongue, an interpretation. Let everything be for building up.
If anyone speaks in a tongue, let it be two, or at most three, and one at a time — and someone must interpret.
If there is no interpreter, he should keep silent in the assembly and speak to himself and to God.
Let two or three prophets speak, and let the others weigh what is said.
And if a revelation comes to someone else sitting there, the first speaker should stop.
For you can all prophesy one by one, so that everyone may learn and everyone be encouraged.
And the spirits of prophets are subject to prophets.
For God is not a God of disorder but of peace. As in all the assemblies of God's people,
women should keep silent in the assemblies. They are not permitted to speak; they are to be in submission, as the law also says.
If they want to learn something, they should ask their own husbands at home; for it is shameful for a woman to speak in the assembly.
Or did the word of God originate with you? Or are you the only ones it has reached?
If anyone thinks he is a prophet or a spiritual person, he should recognise that what I am writing to you is the Lord's command.
If anyone does not recognise this, he is not recognised.
So, my brothers and sisters, be eager to prophesy, and do not stop anyone speaking in tongues.
But let everything be done properly and in order.

1 corinthians_15.t: Now I want to remind you, brothers and sisters, of the good news I announced to you, which you received, in which you stand,
and through which you are being saved — if you hold on to the message I announced to you. Otherwise you came to trust for nothing.
For I passed on to you as of first importance what I also received: that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures,
and that he was buried, and that he has been raised on the third day according to the scriptures,
and that he appeared to Cephas, then to the Twelve.
Then he appeared to more than five hundred brothers and sisters at once, most of whom are still alive, though some have died.
Then he appeared to James, then to all the apostles.
And last of all he appeared to me too, as to one born at the wrong time.
For I am the least of the apostles, not fit to be called an apostle, because I persecuted God's community.
But by God's grace I am what I am, and his grace toward me was not wasted. On the contrary, I worked harder than all of them — not I, though, but God's grace with me.
So whether it was I or they, this is what we announce, and this is what you came to trust.
Now if Christ is proclaimed as raised from the dead, how can some of you say there is no resurrection of the dead?
If there is no resurrection of the dead, then Christ has not been raised either.
And if Christ has not been raised, then our proclamation is empty, and your trust is empty too.
What is more, we are found to be false witnesses about God, because we testified against God that he raised Christ — whom he did not raise, if in fact the dead are not raised.
For if the dead are not raised, then Christ has not been raised either.
And if Christ has not been raised, your trust is futile; you are still in your sins.
It would follow, too, that those who have died in Christ are lost.
If our hope in Christ is for this life only, we are the most pitiable of all people.
But in fact Christ has been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have died.
For since death came through a human being, the resurrection of the dead comes through a human being as well.
For as in Adam all die, so also in Christ all will be made alive.
But each in his own order: Christ the firstfruits, then, at his coming, those who belong to Christ.
Then comes the end, when he hands the kingdom over to God the Father, after he has brought every ruler and every authority and power to an end.
For he must reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet.
The last enemy to be brought to an end is death.
For he has put everything under his feet. But when it says that everything has been put under him, it is obvious that this does not include the one who put everything under him.
And when everything has been put under him, then the Son himself will also be put under the one who put everything under him, so that God may be all in all.
Otherwise, what will those people do who are baptised for the dead? If the dead are not raised at all, why are they baptised for them?
And why do we put ourselves in danger every hour?
I die every day — as surely as I boast about you, brothers and sisters, in Christ Jesus our Lord.
If I fought wild animals at Ephesus on merely human terms, what did I gain? If the dead are not raised, then let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.
Do not be deceived: bad company ruins good character.
Sober up, as you should, and stop sinning. Some of you are ignorant of God — I say this to your shame.
But someone will ask: How are the dead raised? What kind of body do they come with?
You fool! What you sow does not come to life unless it dies.
And what you sow is not the body that is going to be — it is a bare seed, of wheat perhaps, or something else.
But God gives it a body as he chose, and to each kind of seed its own body.
Not all flesh is the same flesh: there is one kind for human beings, another for animals, another for birds, another for fish.
There are heavenly bodies and earthly bodies; but the splendour of the heavenly is one thing and the splendour of the earthly is another.
The sun has one kind of splendour, the moon another, the stars another — and star differs from star in splendour.
So it is with the resurrection of the dead. What is sown is perishable; what is raised is imperishable.
It is sown in dishonour, raised in glory; sown in weakness, raised in power.
It is sown a natural body, raised a spiritual body. If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual one.
So it is written: The first human, Adam, became a living soul; the last Adam became a life-giving Spirit.
But the spiritual did not come first; the natural did, and then the spiritual.
The first human was from the earth, made of dust; the second human is the Lord from heaven.
As the man of dust was, so are those made of dust; and as the heavenly man is, so are those who are heavenly.
And just as we have borne the image of the man of dust, we will also bear the image of the heavenly one.
I tell you this, brothers and sisters: flesh and blood cannot inherit God's kingdom, and what decays does not inherit what does not decay.
Look — I am telling you a mystery: we will not all sleep, but we will all be changed,
in an instant, in the blink of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed.
For this perishable thing must put on imperishability, and this mortal thing must put on immortality.
And when this perishable thing has put on imperishability and this mortal thing has put on immortality, then the saying that is written will come true: Death has been swallowed up in victory.
Where, death, is your victory? Where, death, is your sting?
The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.
But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
So then, my dear brothers and sisters, stand firm, immovable, always overflowing in the Lord's work, since you know that your labour in the Lord is not empty.

1 corinthians_16.t: Now about the collection for God's people: do what I directed the communities in Galatia to do.
On the first day of every week, each of you should set something aside at home, saving up whatever you can afford, so that no collections have to be made when I come.
When I arrive, I will send those you approve, with letters, to carry your gift to Jerusalem.
And if it seems worth my going too, they will travel with me.
I will come to you after I pass through Macedonia — for I am going through Macedonia —
and I may well stay with you, perhaps even spend the winter, so that you can send me on my way wherever I go.
I do not want to see you just in passing this time; I hope to stay with you for a while, if the Lord permits.
I will stay on in Ephesus until Pentecost,
because a wide door has opened for me, one with real work in it — and there are many opponents.
If Timothy comes, see that he has nothing to fear among you, because he is doing the Lord's work, just as I am.
So no one should look down on him. Send him on his way in peace, so that he can come back to me — I am waiting for him with the brothers.
About our brother Apollos: I strongly urged him to visit you with the brothers, but he was quite unwilling to come now. He will come when he has the opportunity.
Keep alert. Stand firm in the faith. Show yourselves men. Be strong.
Let everything you do be done in love.
I urge you, brothers and sisters — you know the household of Stephanas, that they were the firstfruits of Achaia and set themselves to serve God's people —
— that you in turn put yourselves under people like this, and under everyone who works and labours with them.
I am glad that Stephanas, Fortunatus and Achaicus have arrived, because they have made up for your absence.
They refreshed my spirit, and yours. So give recognition to people like this.
The communities in Asia greet you. Aquila and Prisca greet you warmly in the Lord, together with the community that meets in their house.
All the brothers and sisters greet you. Greet one another with a holy kiss.
This greeting is in my own hand — Paul.
If anyone has no love for the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be accursed. Marana tha.
The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
My love is with all of you in Christ Jesus. Amen.

1 john_1.t: What was from the beginning, what we have heard, what we have seen with our own eyes, what we looked at and our hands handled — concerning the word of life —
and the life was made visible, and we have seen it and we testify and we announce to you the eternal life that was with the Father and was made visible to us —
what we have seen and heard we announce to you too, so that you also may have a share with us. And our share is with the Father and with his Son Jesus Christ.
And we are writing these things so that our joy may be complete.
And this is the message we have heard from him and announce to you: that God is light, and in him there is no darkness at all.
If we say we have a share with him and we are walking in the dark, we are lying and we are not doing the truth.
But if we walk in the light, as he himself is in the light, we have a share with one another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanses us from every sin.
If we say we have no sin, we are leading ourselves astray, and the truth is not in us.
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just — so that he forgives us the sins and cleanses us from all wrongdoing.
If we say we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.

1 john_2.t: My little children, I am writing these things to you so that you may not sin. And if anyone does sin, we have an advocate with the Father: Jesus Christ, the Just One.
and he himself is the propitiation for our sins — and not for ours only, but also for the whole world's.
And by this we know that we have come to know him: if we keep his commands.
The one who says 'I have come to know him' and does not keep his commands is a liar, and the truth is not in this one.
But whoever keeps his word — in this one the love of God has truly been brought to completion. By this we know that we are in him.
