The one who says he remains in him ought himself to walk just as that one walked.
Beloved, I am not writing you a new command but an old command, which you have had from the beginning. The old command is the word you heard from the beginning.
Again, a new command I am writing to you — which is true in him and in you — because the darkness is passing away and the true light is already shining.
The one who says he is in the light and hates his brother or sister is in the darkness still, right up to now.
The one who loves his brother or sister remains in the light, and there is no cause of stumbling in him.
But the one who hates his brother or sister is in the darkness, and walks in the darkness, and does not know where he is going, because the darkness blinded his eyes.
I am writing to you, little children, because your sins have been forgiven you on account of his name.
I am writing to you, fathers, because you have come to know the one who is from the beginning. I am writing to you, young men, because you have conquered the evil one.

I wrote to you, children, because you have come to know the Father. I wrote to you, fathers, because you have come to know the one who is from the beginning. I wrote to you, young men, because you are strong and the word of God remains in you and you have conquered the evil one.
Do not love the world, nor the things in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him.
because everything in the world — the craving of the flesh and the craving of the eyes and the boasting about one's living — is not from the Father but is from the world.
And the world is passing away, and its craving with it — but the one who does the will of God remains forever.
Children, it is the last hour — and just as you heard that antichrist is coming, so now many antichrists have come. From this we know that it is the last hour.
They went out from us, but they were not of us. For if they had been of us, they would have remained with us — but so that it might be shown that none of them are of us.
And you have an anointing from the Holy One, and you all know.
I did not write to you because you do not know the truth, but because you do know it, and because no lie is of the truth.
Who is the liar if not the one who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This one is the antichrist — the one who denies the Father and the Son.
Everyone who denies the Son does not have the Father either. The one who confesses the Son has the Father also.
As for you — let what you heard from the beginning remain in you. If what you heard from the beginning remains in you, you too will remain in the Son and in the Father.
And this is the promise that he himself promised us: the eternal life.
I have written these things to you about those who are leading you astray.

And as for you — the anointing you received from him remains in you, and you have no need for anyone to teach you. But as his anointing teaches you about everything, and is true and is not a lie — and just as it taught you — remain in him.
And now, little children, remain in him — so that if he is made visible we may have boldness and not be shamed away from him at his coming.
If you know that he is just, you know too that everyone who does what is right has been born from him.

1 john_3.t: See what kind of love the Father has given us — that we should be called children of God. And we are. This is why the world does not know us: because it did not know him.
Beloved, now we are children of God, and what we will be has not yet been made visible. But we know that if he is made visible we will be like him, because we will see him just as he is.
And everyone who has this hope set on him purifies himself, just as that one is pure.
Everyone who does sin also does lawlessness — and sin is lawlessness.
And you know that that one was made visible to take away our sins — and in him there is no sin.
Everyone who remains in him does not sin. Everyone who sins has not seen him nor come to know him.
Little children, let no one lead you astray. The one who does what is right is righteous, just as that one is righteous.
The one who does sin is from the devil, because the devil has been sinning from the beginning. For this the Son of God was made visible: to undo the works of the devil.
Everyone who has been born from God does not do sin, because his seed remains in him — and he cannot sin, because he has been born from God.
By this the children of God and the children of the devil are visible: everyone who does not do what is right is not from God — nor is the one who does not love his brother or sister.
because this is the message you heard from the beginning: that we should love one another —
not as Cain, who was from the evil one and butchered his brother. And why did he butcher him? Because his own works were evil and his brother's were right.
And do not be surprised, my brothers and sisters, if the world hates you.
We know that we have crossed over out of death into life, because we love the brothers and sisters. The one who does not love remains in death.
Everyone who hates his brother or sister is a murderer — and you know that no murderer has eternal life remaining in him.
By this we have come to know love: that that one laid down his life for us. And we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers and sisters.
But whoever has the world's livelihood and sees his brother or sister in need and shuts his guts against him — how does the love of God remain in him?
My little children, let us not love with word or with the tongue, but in deed and truth.
And by this we will know that we are from the truth, and we will persuade our heart before him —
for if our heart condemns us, God is greater than our heart and knows everything.
Beloved, if our heart does not condemn us, we have boldness toward God,
and whatever we ask we receive from him, because we keep his commands and do what pleases him.
And this is his command: that we trust the name of his Son Jesus Christ and love one another, just as he gave us command.
And the one who keeps his commands remains in him, and he in him. And by this we know that he remains in us: from the Spirit he gave us.

1 john_4.t: Beloved, do not trust every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God — because many false prophets have gone out into the world.
By this you know the Spirit of God: every spirit that confesses Jesus Christ having come in flesh is from God.

And every spirit that does not confess Jesus Christ having come in flesh is not from God. And this is the spirit of the antichrist, which you have heard is coming — and now it is already in the world.
You are from God, little children, and you have conquered them — because greater is the one in you than the one in the world.
They are from the world. This is why they speak from the world, and the world listens to them.
We are from God. The one who knows God listens to us; whoever is not from God does not listen to us. From this we know the spirit of truth and the spirit of deception.
Beloved, let us love one another, because love is from God, and everyone who loves has been born from God and knows God.
The one who does not love did not know God, because God is love.
By this the love of God was made visible among us: that God has sent his only Son into the world, so that we might live through him.
In this is love: not that we have loved God, but that he loved us and sent his Son as the atonement for our sins.
Beloved, if God loved us like this, we too ought to love one another.
No one has ever yet gazed on God. If we love one another, God remains in us and his love has been brought to completion in us.
By this we know that we remain in him and he in us: because he has given us of his Spirit.
And we have gazed and we testify that the Father has sent the Son as Saviour of the world.
Whoever confesses that Jesus Christ is the Son of God — God remains in him, and he in God.
And we have come to know and have trusted the love that God has among us. God is love, and the one who remains in love remains in God, and God remains in him.
By this love has been brought to completion with us: so that we may have boldness on the day of judgement — because just as that one is, so also are we in this world.
There is no fear in love; rather, complete love throws fear outside — because fear has punishment in it, and the one who fears has not been brought to completion in love.
We love him because he first loved us.
If anyone says 'I love God' and hates his brother or sister, he is a liar. For the one who does not love his brother or sister whom he has seen cannot love God whom he has not seen.
And this is the command we have from him: that the one who loves God love his brother or sister also.

1 john_5.t: Everyone who trusts that Jesus is the Christ has been born from God — and everyone who loves the one who fathered loves the one fathered from him.
By this we know that we love the children of God: whenever we love God and do his commands.
For this is the love of God: that we keep his commands. And his commands are not heavy.
because everything born from God conquers the world. And this is the conquest that conquered the world: our trust.
And who is the one who conquers the world except the one who trusts that Jesus is the Son of God?
This is the one who came through water and blood: Jesus Christ — not in the water only, but in the water and in the blood. And the Spirit is the one testifying, because the Spirit is the truth.
For there are three that testify:
the Spirit and the water and the blood — and the three converge on the one.
If we accept the testimony of people, the testimony of God is greater — because this is the testimony of God: that he has testified about his Son.
The one who trusts into the Son of God has the testimony in himself. The one who does not trust God has made him a liar, because he has not trusted the testimony that God has testified about his Son.
And this is the testimony: that God gave us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.
The one who has the Son has the life. The one who does not have the Son of God does not have the life.
These things I have written to you who trust into the name of the Son of God, so that you may know that you have eternal life.
And this is the boldness we have toward him: that if we ask anything according to his will, he hears us.
And if we know that he hears us in whatever we ask, we know that we have the requests we have asked from him.

If anyone sees his brother or sister sinning a sin not toward death, he will ask, and he will give him life — to those sinning not toward death. There is a sin toward death; I do not say that he should make request about that one.
All wrongdoing is sin — and there is sin not toward death.
We know that everyone who has been born from God does not sin; rather, the one born from God keeps him, and the evil one does not touch him.
We know that we are from God, and the whole world lies in the evil one.

And we know that the Son of God has come and has given us understanding, so that we may know the True One. And we are in the True One, in his Son Jesus Christ. This one is the true God and eternal life.
Little children, guard yourselves from the idols. Amen.

1 peter_1.t: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to those chosen and living as resident foreigners in the dispersion — Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia —
chosen according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, by the Spirit's setting-apart, for obedience and for the sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ: may grace and peace be multiplied to you.
Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who in his great mercy gave us new birth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
into an inheritance that cannot decay, cannot be defiled and cannot fade, kept in the heavens for you,
you who are being garrisoned by God's power through trust for a rescue ready to be revealed at the last moment.
In this you rejoice, though for a little while now, if it must be, you have been grieved by trials of every kind,

so that the tested genuineness of your trust — worth far more than gold, which perishes though it is assayed by fire — may be found to result in praise and glory and honour at the revealing of Jesus Christ.
You love him without having seen him; and though you do not see him now, you trust him, and you rejoice with a joy beyond words and full of glory,
as you receive the outcome of your trust, the rescue of your lives.
About this rescue the prophets searched and searched — the ones who prophesied about the grace meant for you —
searching to find what person or what time the Spirit of Christ in them was pointing to, when it testified in advance to the sufferings meant for Christ and the glories after them.

It was revealed to them that they were not serving themselves but you, in the things now announced to you through those who brought you the good news by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven — things angels long to stoop and look into.
So then, with the belt of your mind fastened, sober, set your hope completely on the grace being brought to you at the revealing of Jesus Christ.
As children of obedience, do not be shaped by the cravings you had before, in your ignorance,
but as the one who called you is holy, you yourselves become holy in your whole way of life,
since it is written: 'You shall be holy, because I am holy.'
And if you call on him as Father — the one who judges impartially according to each person's work — then live out the time of your residence here as foreigners in fear.
You know that it was not with perishable things, silver or gold, that you were ransomed out of the futile way of life handed down from your fathers,
but with precious blood, as of a lamb without blemish or spot — the blood of Christ,
foreknown before the foundation of the world, but revealed at the end of the times for your sake —
you who through him trust in God, who raised him from the dead and gave him glory, so that your trust and hope are in God.
Now that you have purified your lives by obedience to the truth, for sincere brotherly love, love one another intensely from a clean heart —
born again, not from perishable seed but from imperishable, through the word of God, living and remaining.
For 'all flesh is like grass, and all its glory like the flower of the grass. The grass withered and the flower fell off,
but the word of the Lord remains for ever.' And this is the word that was announced as good news to you.

1 peter_2.t: So strip off all malice and all deceit, hypocrisies, envies and every kind of slander,
and like newborn infants long for the pure milk of the word, so that by it you may grow up into rescue,
if indeed you have tasted that the Lord is good.
As you come to him — a living stone, rejected by people but chosen and precious in God's sight —
you yourselves, like living stones, are being built into a spiritual house, for a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
For it stands in Scripture: 'Look, I am laying in Zion a chosen and precious cornerstone, and the one who trusts on him will never be put to shame.'
So the honour is yours, who trust; but for those who do not trust, 'the stone the builders rejected — this one became the head of the corner',
and 'a stone to strike against and a rock to trip over'. They strike against it because they disobey the word — which is also what they were appointed to.

But you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for his possession, so that you may announce the excellences of the one who called you out of darkness into his marvellous light —
you who once were not a people, but now are God's people; who had not received mercy, but now have received mercy.
Beloved, I urge you as foreigners and resident aliens to keep away from the cravings of the flesh, which are on campaign against your life.
Keep your way of life among the nations good, so that where they speak against you as wrongdoers, they may see your good works and glorify God on the day he visits.
Submit to every human institution for the Lord's sake: whether to a king as the one holding power,
or to governors as those sent by him to punish wrongdoers and praise those who do good.
Because this is God's will: that by doing good you should muzzle the ignorance of foolish people.
Live as free people — not using your freedom as a cover for malice, but as God's servants.
Honour everyone. Love the brotherhood. Fear God. Honour the emperor.
Household slaves, submit to your masters with all fear — not only to the good and reasonable ones, but also to the crooked.
Because this is a gracious thing: if, because of an awareness of God, someone bears up under griefs while suffering unjustly.
What credit is it if you endure a beating for doing wrong? But if you endure while doing good and suffering for it, this is a gracious thing before God.
This is what you were called to, because Christ also suffered for you, leaving you a copy to trace, so that you would follow in his footsteps.
'He committed no sin, and no deceit was found in his mouth.'
When he was insulted he did not insult back; suffering, he did not threaten, but handed himself over to the one who judges justly.
He himself carried up our sins in his body onto the tree, so that we might be done with sins and live for rightness. By his welt you were healed.
You were straying like sheep, but now you have turned back to the shepherd and overseer of your lives.

1 peter_3.t: In the same way, wives, submit to your own husbands, so that even if some of them disobey the word they may be won without a word, through their wives' way of life,
when they see your pure way of life, lived in fear.
Let your adornment not be the outward kind — braided hair, gold jewellery, fine clothes —
but the hidden person of the heart, in the imperishable quality of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is of great value before God.
This is how the holy women who hoped in God used to adorn themselves long ago, submitting to their own husbands —
as Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him lord. You became her children when you do good and are not frightened by any terror.

Husbands, in the same way, live with your wives with understanding, as with a weaker vessel — the female one — assigning her honour as a fellow heir of the grace of life, so that your prayers are not cut off.
Finally, all of you: be of one mind, sympathetic, loving as brothers and sisters, tender-hearted, humble-minded.
Do not pay back evil for evil, or insult for insult; on the contrary, bless — because this is what you were called to, so that you may inherit a blessing.
For 'whoever wants to love life and see good days must keep his tongue from evil and his lips from speaking deceit;
he must turn away from evil and do good, seek peace and pursue it.
Because the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous and his ears are turned to their plea, but the face of the Lord is against those who do evil.'
And who will harm you if you become zealots for what is good?
But even if you should suffer for the sake of rightness, you are blessed. Do not be afraid of what they fear, and do not be shaken.
but set apart Christ as Lord in your hearts, always ready to make a defence to anyone who asks you for an account of the hope in you —
but with gentleness and reverence, keeping a good conscience, so that when you are spoken against, those who abuse your good way of life in Christ may be put to shame.
Because it is better to suffer for doing good, if that should be God's will, than for doing evil.
Because Christ also suffered for sins once for all, a righteous one for unrighteous ones, to bring you to God — put to death in the flesh, made alive in the spirit.
In which he also went and made proclamation to the spirits in prison,
those who disobeyed long ago, when God's patience was waiting in the days of Noah while the ark was being built. In it a few — that is, eight lives — were brought safely through water.
And baptism, which corresponds to that, now saves you too — not a removal of dirt from the flesh, but a pledge to God from a good conscience — through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,
who is at God's right hand, having gone into heaven, with angels and authorities and powers made subject to him.

1 peter_4.t: So then, since Christ suffered in the flesh, arm yourselves with the same intention — because whoever has suffered in the flesh has finished with sin —
so as to live out the time that is left in the flesh no longer by human cravings but by God's will.
The time that has gone by is enough for having done what the nations want — walking in debauchery, cravings, drunkenness, revels, drinking parties and lawless idolatries.
They are taken aback that you do not run with them into the same flood of dissipation, and they abuse you for it —
and they will give an account to the one who is ready to judge the living and the dead.
This is why the good news was announced even to the dead: so that, though judged in the flesh as people are, they might live in the spirit as God does.
The end of all things has drawn near. So be clear-headed and sober for prayer.
Above all, keep your love for one another at full stretch, because love covers a multitude of sins.
Be hospitable to one another without grumbling.
As each has received a gift, use it to serve one another, as good managers of God's varied grace:

if anyone speaks, as speaking God's oracles; if anyone serves, as out of the strength God supplies — so that in everything God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom belong the glory and the power for ever and ever. Amen.
Beloved, do not find the burning among you strange — it is happening to test you — as though something strange were happening to you.
Instead, rejoice to the extent that you share in Christ's sufferings, so that at the revealing of his glory you may also rejoice and be overjoyed.
If you are insulted for the name of Christ, you are blessed, because the Spirit of glory — the Spirit of God — rests on you: on their side he is blasphemed, but on your side he is glorified.
None of you should suffer as a murderer or a thief or a wrongdoer or as a meddler in other people's affairs.
But if anyone suffers as a Christian, he should not be ashamed; he should glorify God in this name.
Because it is time for the judgement to begin at the household of God — and if it begins with us, what will be the end for those who disobey God's good news?
And 'if the righteous person is scarcely rescued, where will the ungodly and the sinner appear?'
So then, those who suffer according to God's will should entrust their lives to a faithful Creator while doing good.

1 peter_5.t: So I urge the elders among you — I who am a fellow elder and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and a sharer in the glory about to be revealed:
shepherd the flock of God that is among you, overseeing it not under compulsion but willingly, as God would have it; not for shameful gain but eagerly;
not lording it over those in your charge, but becoming patterns for the flock.
And when the chief shepherd is revealed, you will receive the unfading crown of glory.

In the same way, you who are younger, submit to the elders. And all of you, tie humility round yourselves toward one another, because 'God sets himself against the arrogant, but to the lowly he gives grace.'
So be brought low under God's mighty hand, so that he may lift you up at the right time,
throwing all your anxiety onto him, because he cares about you.
Be sober, stay awake. Your opponent in court, the slanderer, prowls about like a roaring lion, looking for someone to swallow.
Stand against him, firm in your trust, knowing that the same kinds of suffering are being completed in your brotherhood throughout the world.
And the God of all grace, who called you into his eternal glory in Christ, will himself restore, steady, strengthen and settle you after you have suffered a little while.
To him belong the glory and the power for ever and ever. Amen.
Through Silvanus, whom I regard as a faithful brother, I have written to you briefly, urging you and testifying that this is the true grace of God. Stand in it.
She who is in Babylon, chosen together with you, greets you, and so does Mark, my son.
Greet one another with a kiss of love. Peace to all of you who are in Christ Jesus. Amen.

1 thessalonians_1.t: Paul, Silvanus and Timothy, to the assembly of the Thessalonians in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ: grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
We always thank God for all of you, mentioning you unceasingly in our prayers
remembering before our God and Father your work that comes from trust, your labour that comes from love, and your endurance that comes from hope in our Lord Jesus Christ.
We know, brothers and sisters loved by God, that he has chosen you;

because our good news did not come to you in word only, but also in power and in the Holy Spirit and with much full assurance — just as you know what kind of people we proved to be among you for your sake.
And you became imitators of us and of the Lord, receiving the word in much affliction with the joy of the Holy Spirit,
so that you became a pattern for all the believers in Macedonia and in Achaia.
For the word of the Lord has rung out from you, not only in Macedonia and Achaia; your trust toward God has gone out in every place, so that we have no need to say anything.
For they themselves report about us what kind of welcome we had among you, and how you turned to God from idols, to serve a living and true God
and to wait for his Son from the heavens, whom he raised from the dead — Jesus, who rescues us from the coming anger.

1 thessalonians_2.t: You yourselves know, brothers and sisters, that our coming to you was not empty.
On the contrary, though we had already suffered and been outrageously treated in Philippi — as you know — we found boldness in our God to speak God's good news to you in the face of great opposition.
For our appeal did not come from error or from impurity, nor was it made with deceit;
but just as we have been approved by God to be entrusted with the good news, so we speak — not to please people but to please God, who tests our hearts.
For we never came with flattering speech, as you know, nor with a pretext for greed — God is witness —
nor were we seeking glory from people, either from you or from others.
though as Christ's apostles we could have made our weight felt. Instead we were gentle among you — like a nurse cherishing her own children.
So, yearning for you, we were glad to share with you not only God's good news but our own selves, because you had become dear to us.
For you remember, brothers and sisters, our labour and hardship: working night and day so as not to burden any of you, we proclaimed to you the good news of God.
You are witnesses, and so is God, of how devoutly and justly and blamelessly we behaved toward you believers,
just as you know how we treated each one of you as a father treats his own children —
appealing to you and encouraging you and urging you — so that you would walk worthily of the God who calls you into his own kingdom and glory.

And because of this we also thank God constantly: that when you received the word of God's message from us, you accepted it not as a human word but as what it truly is — the word of God, which is also at work in you who trust.
For you, brothers and sisters, became imitators of God's assemblies in Judea that are in Christ Jesus, because you suffered the same things from your own countrymen as they did from the Jews
who killed both the Lord Jesus and the prophets, and drove us out, and do not please God, and are hostile to all people —
hindering us from speaking to the nations so that they may be saved, and so always filling up the measure of their sins. But God's anger has come upon them at last.
But we, brothers and sisters, having been orphaned from you for a short time — in person, not in heart — made all the more eager efforts to see you face to face, with great longing.
For we wanted to come to you — I, Paul, more than once — and Satan blocked our way.
For what is our hope or joy or crown of boasting? Is it not you, before our Lord Jesus at his coming?
Yes, you are our glory and joy.

1 thessalonians_3.t: So when we could bear it no longer, we were content to be left behind in Athens alone,
and we sent Timothy — our brother and God's servant and our co-worker in the good news of Christ — to strengthen you and encourage you concerning your faith,
so that no one would be shaken by these afflictions. For you yourselves know that we are appointed for this.
In fact, when we were with you we kept telling you in advance that we were going to be afflicted — and so it turned out, as you know.
That is why, when I could bear it no longer, I sent to find out about your faith — in case the tempter had tempted you and our labour had come to nothing.
But now that Timothy has come to us from you and brought us the good news of your faith and love — and that you always remember us kindly, longing to see us just as we long to see you —
for this reason, brothers and sisters, in all our distress and affliction we were encouraged about you through your faith,
because now we live, if you are standing firm in the Lord.
For what thanks can we give back to God for you, for all the joy we rejoice with because of you before our God,
praying night and day more than abundantly to see your face and to supply what is lacking in your faith?
Now may our God and Father himself, and our Lord Jesus, direct our way to you.
And may the Lord make you increase and overflow in love for one another and for everyone, just as we do for you,
so that he may strengthen your hearts to be blameless in holiness before our God and Father at the coming of our Lord Jesus with all his saints.

1 thessalonians_4.t: Finally then, brothers and sisters, we ask and urge you in the Lord Jesus that, as you received from us how you ought to walk and please God — as indeed you are walking — you would do so all the more.
For you know what instructions we gave you through the Lord Jesus.
For this is God's will: your holiness — that you keep away from sexual immorality;
that each of you know how to control his own body in holiness and honour,
not in the passion of lust, like the nations that do not know God;
that no one overstep and take advantage of his brother in this matter, because the Lord is the avenger in all these things, just as we told you before and testified solemnly.
For God did not call us to impurity but in holiness.
So then, whoever rejects this is not rejecting a human being but God, who also gives his Holy Spirit to you.
Now about brotherly love, you have no need for anyone to write to you, for you yourselves are taught by God to love one another;
and in fact you are doing it toward all the brothers and sisters throughout Macedonia. But we urge you, brothers and sisters, to do so all the more,
and to make it your ambition to live quietly, to mind your own affairs and to work with your own hands, just as we instructed you,
so that you may walk decently toward those outside and be dependent on no one.
We do not want you to be uninformed, brothers and sisters, about those who are sleeping, so that you may not grieve as the rest do, who have no hope.
For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, so also, through Jesus, God will bring with him those who have fallen asleep.
For this we tell you by a word of the Lord: we who are alive, who are left until the coming of the Lord, will certainly not go ahead of those who have fallen asleep.
For the Lord himself, with a shouted command, with an archangel's voice and with God's trumpet, will come down from heaven, and the dead in Christ will rise first.
Then we who are alive, who are left, will be snatched up together with them in clouds to meet the Lord in the air — and so we will always be with the Lord.
So encourage one another with these words.

1 thessalonians_5.t: Now about the times and the seasons, brothers and sisters, you have no need for anything to be written to you,
for you yourselves know accurately that the day of the Lord comes like a thief in the night.
When people are saying 'Peace and security,' then sudden destruction comes upon them, like labour pains on a pregnant woman, and they will certainly not escape.
But you, brothers and sisters, are not in darkness, so that the day should overtake you like a thief.
For you are all sons of light and sons of the day. We are not of the night or of darkness.
So then, let us not sleep as the rest do, but let us stay awake and be sober.
For those who sleep sleep at night, and those who get drunk are drunk at night.
But since we belong to the day, let us be sober, putting on the breastplate of trust and love, and for a helmet the hope of deliverance.
For God did not appoint us for anger, but for obtaining deliverance through our Lord Jesus Christ,
who died for us, so that whether we are awake or asleep we may live together with him.
So encourage one another and build each other up, just as you are doing.
We ask you, brothers and sisters, to recognise those who labour among you and lead you in the Lord and warn you,
and to regard them very highly in love because of their work. Be at peace among yourselves.
We urge you, brothers and sisters: warn the disorderly, comfort the discouraged, hold on to the weak, be patient toward everyone.
See that no one repays anyone evil for evil, but always pursue what is good for one another and for everyone.
Rejoice always.
Pray without stopping.
Give thanks in everything, for this is God's will in Christ Jesus for you.
Do not put out the Spirit's fire.
Do not treat prophecies with contempt.
Test everything; hold on to what is good.
Keep away from every form of evil.
May the God of peace himself make you holy through and through, and may your whole spirit and soul and body be kept blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
The one who calls you is faithful; he will also do it.
Brothers and sisters, pray for us too.
Greet all the brothers and sisters with a holy kiss.
I put you under oath by the Lord to have this letter read to all God's people, the brothers and sisters.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen. [To the Thessalonians, first letter, written from Athens.]

1 timothy_1.t: Paul, an apostle of the Lord Christ Jesus by the command of God our Saviour and of the Lord Christ Jesus our hope,
To Timothy, my true child in faith: grace, mercy, and peace from God our Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
Just as I urged you to stay on in Ephesus when I was setting out for Macedonia, so that you might charge certain people not to teach a different doctrine,
or to give their attention to myths and endless genealogies. These produce speculations rather than God's stewardship, which is in faith.
The aim of this charge is love — out of a clean heart, a good conscience, and unhypocritical trust.
Some have missed the mark on these and turned aside to empty talk,
wanting to be teachers of the law, though they understand neither what they say nor the things they so confidently insist on.
Now we know that the law is good, if a person uses it lawfully —

knowing this: that law is not laid down for a righteous person, but for the lawless and unruly, the ungodly and sinful, the unholy and profane, for those who kill their fathers and mothers, for murderers,
the sexually immoral, men who lie with men, slave-traders, liars, perjurers — and whatever else stands opposed to the healthy teaching,
in accord with the gospel of the glory of the blessed God, which I myself was entrusted with.
I am grateful to the one who gave me strength, Christ Jesus our Lord, because he considered me trustworthy and appointed me to service —
though I was formerly a blasphemer, a persecutor, and a violent man. But I was shown mercy, because I acted in ignorance, in unbelief.
and the grace of our Lord overflowed beyond measure, with the trust and love that are in Christ Jesus.
Trustworthy is the saying, and worthy of full acceptance: that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners — of whom I am first.
But this is why I was shown mercy: so that in me, as the first, Christ Jesus might display the whole of his patience, as a sketch for those about to trust in him for eternal life.
Now to the King of the ages — imperishable, invisible, the only wise God — be honour and glory forever and ever. Amen.
This is the charge I entrust to you, my child Timothy, in accord with the prophecies once made over you — so that by them you may fight the good fight,
holding on to faith and a good conscience. Some have thrown these away and have made shipwreck of the faith —
among them Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I handed over to Satan so that they may be taught not to blaspheme.

1 timothy_2.t: First of all, then, I urge that requests, prayers, appeals, and thanksgivings be made for all people,
for kings and all who hold high position — so that we may lead a quiet and peaceful life in all godliness and dignity.
This is good, and acceptable before God our Saviour,
who wants all people to be saved and to come to a full knowledge of truth.
For there is one God, and one mediator between God and people — a human being, Christ Jesus,
who gave himself as a ransom for all — the testimony given at its own proper times.
For this I was appointed a herald and an apostle — I am telling the truth in Christ, I am not lying — a teacher of the nations, in trust and truth.
So I want the men in every place to pray, lifting up holy hands, without anger or argument;
and likewise the women, to adorn themselves in orderly dress, with modesty and self-control — not with braided hair and gold or pearls or expensive clothing,
but with good works — which is what suits women who profess reverence for God.
A woman is to learn in quietness, in all submission.
I do not permit a woman to teach, or to have authority over a man, but to be in quietness.
For Adam was formed first, then Eve.
And Adam was not deceived; but the woman, thoroughly deceived, came into transgression.
But she will be saved through childbearing — if they remain in trust and love and holiness, with self-control.

1 timothy_3.t: Trustworthy is the saying: if anyone aspires to oversight, he desires a good work.
So the overseer must be beyond reproach: the husband of one wife, clear-headed, self-controlled, orderly, hospitable, able to teach,
not a drunkard, not violent, not greedy for shameful gain, but gentle, not quarrelsome, not a lover of money,
managing his own household well, keeping his children in submission with all dignity —
for if someone does not know how to manage his own household, how will he care for God's community?
not newly planted, so that he does not become puffed up and fall into the devil's judgement.
He must also have a good reputation with those outside, so that he does not fall into disgrace and the devil's trap.
Those who serve, likewise, are to be dignified: not two-tongued, not given to much wine, not greedy for shameful gain,
holding the mystery of the faith with a clean conscience.
And these too must first be tested; then let them serve, being beyond accusation.
Their wives likewise are to be dignified: not slanderers, clear-headed, trustworthy in everything.
Those who serve are to be husbands of one wife, managing their children and their own households well.
For those who have served well gain a good standing for themselves, and great boldness in the faith that is in Christ Jesus.
I am writing these things to you, hoping to come to you soon —
but if I am delayed, so that you may know how one must behave in God's household, which is the community of the living God, a pillar and buttress of the truth.
And by common confession, great is the mystery of godliness: who was revealed in flesh, vindicated in spirit, seen by angels, proclaimed among the nations, trusted in the world, taken up in glory.

1 timothy_4.t: But the Spirit says explicitly that in later times some will stand away from the faith, giving their attention to deceiving spirits and to teachings of demons,
through the hypocrisy of liars whose own conscience has been branded,
forbidding marriage and requiring abstinence from foods that God created to be received with thanksgiving by those who trust and have come to know the truth.
For every creation of God is good, and nothing is to be thrown away if it is received with thanksgiving —
for it is made holy through God's word and prayer.
By setting these things before the brothers and sisters you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus, nourished on the words of the faith and of the good teaching you have followed.
Have nothing to do with profane, old-wives' myths. Train yourself for godliness instead.
For bodily training is of limited use, but godliness is useful for everything, holding a promise of life both now and to come.
Trustworthy is the saying, and worthy of full acceptance.
For to this end we labour and struggle, because we have set our hope on the living God, who is the Saviour of all people — especially of those who trust.
Charge these things, and teach them.
Let no one look down on your youth. Instead become a pattern for those who trust — in speech, in conduct, in love, in spirit, in trust, in purity.
Until I come, attend to the public reading, to the exhortation, to the teaching.
Do not neglect the gift in you, which was given to you through prophecy with the laying on of the hands of the elders.
Practise these things; be immersed in them, so that your progress may be plain to everyone.
Watch yourself and the teaching. Stay with them — for by doing this you will save both yourself and those who hear you.

1 timothy_5.t: Do not sharply rebuke an older man, but appeal to him as a father — younger men as brothers,
older women as mothers, younger women as sisters — in all purity.
Honour widows who are really widows.
But if a widow has children or grandchildren, let them first learn to show godliness toward their own household and to make a return to their parents — for this is good and acceptable before God.
The one who is really a widow, left all alone, has set her hope on God and stays at her requests and prayers night and day;
but the one who lives for pleasure is dead while she lives.
Charge these things too, so that they may be beyond reproach.
If anyone does not provide for their own — and especially for their household — they have denied the faith and are worse than someone who does not trust.
Let a widow be enrolled only if she is not less than sixty years old, the wife of one husband,

attested by good works: if she raised children, if she showed hospitality to strangers, if she washed the feet of God's people, if she came to the aid of the afflicted, if she pursued every good work.
But refuse younger widows. For when their desires pull them away from Christ, they want to marry,
and so they incur judgement, because they have set aside their first pledge.
And at the same time they learn to be idle, going round from house to house — and not only idle, but gossips and busybodies, saying what they should not.
So I want younger women to marry, to bear children, to manage a household, to give the adversary no occasion for abuse;
for some have already turned aside after Satan.
If any believing man or woman has widows, let that person help them, so that the community is not burdened and can help those who are really widows.
Elders who preside well are to be considered worthy of double honour — especially those who labour in speaking and teaching.
For the Scripture says, "You shall not muzzle an ox while it treads out the grain," and, "The worker is worthy of his wages."
Do not accept an accusation against an elder except on the word of two or three witnesses.
Those who go on sinning, reprove in front of everyone, so that the rest may have fear as well.
I solemnly charge you before God and the Lord Christ Jesus and the chosen angels: keep these things without prejudging, and do nothing out of favouritism.
Do not lay hands on anyone hastily, and do not share in the sins of others. Keep yourself pure.
Stop drinking only water; use a little wine because of your stomach and your frequent illnesses.
The sins of some people are obvious, going ahead of them to judgement; the sins of others follow after.
In the same way, good works are obvious too — and those that are not cannot stay hidden.

1 timothy_6.t: All who are under the yoke as slaves are to consider their own masters worthy of all honour, so that the name of God and the teaching are not blasphemed.

And those who have believing masters must not look down on them because they are brothers; they should serve them all the more, because those who benefit from their good service are trusting and beloved. Teach and urge these things.
If anyone teaches a different doctrine and does not come over to healthy words — those of our Lord Jesus Christ — and to the teaching that accords with godliness,
he is puffed up, understanding nothing, but sick over controversies and word-battles. Out of these come envy, strife, slanders, evil suspicions,
constant frictions among people whose minds are ruined and who have been robbed of the truth, supposing that godliness is a means of gain. Keep away from such people.
But godliness with contentment is a great means of gain.
For we brought nothing into the world, and it is clear that we can carry nothing out.
But if we have food and covering, we will be content with these.
Those who want to be rich fall into temptation and a trap and many senseless and harmful desires, which plunge people into ruin and destruction.
For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil. Some, reaching for it, have been led away from the faith and have pierced themselves through with many pains.
But you, person of God, flee these things. Pursue rightness, godliness, trust, love, endurance, gentleness.
Fight the good fight of the faith. Take hold of eternal life, to which you were called and about which you made the good confession before many witnesses.
I charge you before God, who gives life to all things, and before Christ Jesus, who under Pontius Pilate testified to the good confession,
to keep the command spotless and beyond reproach until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ,
which he will display at his own proper times — the blessed and only Sovereign, the King of those who reign and Lord of those who rule,
who alone has immortality, living in unapproachable light, whom no one has ever seen or is able to see. To him be honour and eternal power. Amen.

Charge those who are rich in the present age not to be arrogant, and not to set their hope on the uncertainty of wealth but on God, the living one, who richly supplies us with everything for our enjoyment.
to do good, to be rich in good works, to be generous, ready to share,
storing up for themselves a good foundation for what is coming, so that they may take hold of the life that is really life.
Timothy, guard the deposit. Turn away from the profane empty talk and the contradictions of what is falsely called knowledge —
which some have professed, and so have missed the mark concerning the faith. Grace be with you. Amen. [To Timothy, the first, written from Laodicea, which is the chief city of Phrygia Pacatiana.]

2 corinthians_1.t: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through God's will, and Timothy our brother — to God's community in Corinth, together with all God's holy people throughout the whole of Achaia:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ — the Father of mercies and the God of all comfort,
who comforts us in all our pressure, so that we are able to comfort those in any kind of pressure, through the comfort we ourselves are comforted with by God.
Because just as the sufferings of Christ overflow into us, so also through Christ our comfort overflows.
If we are under pressure, it is for your comfort and rescue; if we are comforted, it is for your comfort — comfort that does its work as you endure the same sufferings we also suffer.
And our hope for you is unshaken, because we know that as you share in the sufferings, so you also share in the comfort.

Brothers and sisters, we don't want you left in the dark about the pressure that came on us in Asia: we were weighed down beyond all measure, past our strength, so much that we despaired even of living.
In fact, we had the death sentence inside ourselves — so that we would not put our confidence in ourselves but in the God who raises the dead.
He rescued us from so deadly a peril, and he will rescue us. On him we have set our hope, that he will rescue us again,
as you also join in helping us by your prayer — so that thanks may be given for us by many, on behalf of the gift given to us through many people.

This is our boast: the testimony of our conscience that we conducted ourselves in the world — and above all toward you — in God's singleness of heart and sincerity, not in fleshly wisdom but in God's grace.
We aren't writing you anything other than what you read and in fact understand — and I hope you will go on understanding to the end,
just as you have understood us in part — that we are your boast, as you will also be ours, on the day of our Lord Jesus.
It was with this confidence that I intended to come to you first, so that you might have a second gift of grace —
to pass by way of you into Macedonia, then come back to you from Macedonia and be sent on by you to Judea.
So when I intended this, was I being casual about it? Or do I make my plans the way the flesh makes plans, so that with me 'Yes, yes' and 'No, no' come out of the same mouth?
But God is faithful: our word to you is not Yes and No.
Because God's Son, Jesus Christ, the one proclaimed among you by us — by me and Silvanus and Timothy — was not Yes and No; in him it has become Yes.
For however many promises God has made, in him they are Yes. And so through him we say the Amen, to God's glory.
It is God who makes us stand firm with you in Christ, and who anointed us,
who also sealed us and gave us the Spirit in our hearts as the down payment.
I call God as witness against my own life: it was to spare you that I did not come again to Corinth.
Not that we lord it over your faith — we are fellow workers for your joy, because it is by faith that you stand.

2 corinthians_2.t: So I decided this for myself: not to come to you again in grief.
Because if I am the one who grieves you, then who is left to cheer me — except the very person I grieved?
And I wrote this very thing so that when I came I would not be grieved by the people who ought to make me glad — trusting you all, that my joy is the joy of all of you.
Because I wrote to you out of great pressure and anguish of heart, through many tears — not so that you would be grieved, but so that you would know the love I have for you in overflowing measure.
And if someone has caused grief, he has not grieved me but — not to overstate it — all of you, in part.
For such a person, this rebuke by the majority is enough.
So now you should do the opposite: forgive him and comfort him, or he may be swallowed up by too much grief.
So I urge you to confirm your love for him publicly.
This is in fact why I wrote: to find out whether you would stand the test — whether you are obedient in everything.
Anyone you forgive, I forgive too. And what I have forgiven — if I have forgiven anything — I forgave for your sake in the presence of Christ,
so that we would not be outmanoeuvred by Satan — we are not ignorant of his designs.
When I came to Troas for the good news of Christ, and a door was opened for me in the Lord,
I still had no relief in my spirit, because I did not find Titus my brother there. So I said goodbye to them and went on to Macedonia.
But thanks be to God, who always leads us in his triumphal procession in Christ and through us makes the aroma of knowing him perceptible everywhere.
Because we are the fragrance of Christ to God, among those being rescued and among those perishing:
to the one, a stench from death leading to death; to the other, a fragrance from life leading to life. And who is adequate for this?
We are not like so many, hawking God's word for profit. No — we speak in Christ from sincerity, from God, and in God's sight.

2 corinthians_3.t: Are we starting to recommend ourselves again? Or do we need — as some do — letters of recommendation to you, or from you?
You yourselves are our letter, written on our hearts, known and read by everyone.
It is clear that you are a letter from Christ, delivered by us — written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on stone tablets but on tablets that are hearts of flesh.
This is the kind of confidence we have toward God through Christ.
Not that we are adequate in ourselves to count anything as coming from us — our adequacy comes from God,
who made us adequate as servants of a new covenant — not of letter but of Spirit; because the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.

Now if the ministry that brought death — carved in letters on stones — came with such glory that the sons of Israel could not look straight at Moses' face because of the glory of his face, a glory being brought to nothing,
how will the ministry of the Spirit not come with far more glory?
Because if the ministry of condemnation had glory, the ministry of rightness overflows with far more glory.
In fact, what was glorified has not been glorified at all in this case, because of the glory that surpasses it.
Because if what is being brought to nothing came through glory, how much more does what remains exist in glory.
So, having this kind of hope, we speak with great openness —
and not like Moses, who used to put a veil over his face so that the sons of Israel would not gaze at the end of what was being brought to nothing.
But their minds were hardened. To this very day the same veil remains over the reading of the old covenant — it is not lifted, because it is in Christ that it is brought to nothing.
But to this day, whenever Moses is read, a veil lies over their heart.
But whenever someone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.
Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.
And all of us, with unveiled face, beholding the Lord's glory as in a mirror, are being transformed into the same image, from glory to glory — just as from the Lord who is the Spirit.

2 corinthians_4.t: That is why, since we have this ministry — since we were shown mercy — we do not lose heart.

Instead we have renounced the hidden things people are ashamed of. We don't operate by cunning or adulterate God's word; by the open display of the truth we commend ourselves to every human conscience in God's sight.
And even if our good news is veiled, it is veiled among those who are perishing —
among whom the god of this age blinded the minds of those who do not trust, so that the light of the good news of the glory of Christ — who is the image of God — would not dawn on them.
Because we do not proclaim ourselves — we proclaim Jesus Christ as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for Jesus' sake.
Because the God who said 'Light will shine out of darkness' is the one who has shone in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of God's glory in the face of Jesus Christ.
But we hold this treasure in clay pots, so that the extraordinary power belongs to God and does not come from us.
Pressed on every side but not crushed; at a loss but not at a dead loss;
pursued but not abandoned; knocked down but not destroyed;
always carrying around in the body the dying of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be made visible in our body.
Because we who are alive are always being handed over to death for Jesus' sake, so that the life of Jesus may also be made visible in our mortal flesh.
So death is at work in us, but life in you.
But we have the same spirit of trust as in what is written — 'I trusted, therefore I spoke' — and we too trust, and therefore we speak,
knowing that the one who raised the Lord Jesus will also raise us with Jesus and present us with you.
Because it is all for your sake, so that grace, as it reaches more and more people, may make thanksgiving overflow to God's glory.
That is why we do not lose heart. Even if our outer person is wasting away, our inner person is being renewed day by day.
Because this momentary lightness of our pressure is producing for us an eternal weight of glory beyond all measure and beyond all comparison —
as we fix our attention not on what is seen but on what is not seen; because what is seen is temporary, but what is not seen is eternal.

2 corinthians_5.t: Because we know that if our earthly house — this tent — is torn down, we have a building from God: a house not made by hands, eternal, in the heavens.
In fact we groan in this one, longing to put on our dwelling from heaven over it —
if in fact, once we have put it on, we will not be found naked.
Because we who are in this tent groan under the weight — not that we want to be stripped, but to be further clothed, so that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life.
And the one who prepared us for this very thing is God, who gave us the Spirit as the down payment.
So we are always confident, knowing that while we are at home in the body we are away from home, away from the Lord —
because we walk by trust, not by sight —
and we are confident, and would much rather leave home from the body and be at home with the Lord.
So whether at home or away from home, we make it our ambition to please him.

Because all of us must be made visible before the judgement seat of Christ, so that each may be paid back for what was done through the body, according to what he practised, whether good or worthless.
So, knowing the fear of the Lord, we try to persuade people. To God we are already visible, and I hope we are visible to your consciences too.
We are not recommending ourselves to you again; we are giving you an occasion to boast about us, so that you have something to say to those who boast in appearances and not in the heart.
Because if we were out of our minds, it was for God; if we are in our right mind, it is for you.
Because the love of Christ holds us together, once we have reached this judgement: that one died on behalf of all, and therefore all died.
And he died on behalf of all, so that those who live might no longer live for themselves but for the one who died and was raised on their behalf.
So from now on we regard no one according to the flesh. Even if we once knew Christ according to the flesh, we know him that way no longer.
So if anyone is in Christ — new creation. The old things have passed; look, they have become new.
And all of it is from God, who reconciled us to himself through Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation:
that God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, not counting their trespasses against them, and placing in us the word of reconciliation.
So we are ambassadors on Christ's behalf, as though God were making his appeal through us. We beg you on Christ's behalf: be reconciled to God.
The one who did not know sin, he made to be sin on our behalf, so that in him we might become God's rightness.

2 corinthians_6.t: Working together with him, then, we also urge you not to receive God's grace for nothing.
Because he says: 'At an acceptable time I heard you, and on a day of rescue I helped you.' Look — now is the well-accepted time; look — now is the day of rescue.
We give no one any cause to stumble, so that no fault can be found with the ministry.
Instead, in everything we commend ourselves as God's servants: in great endurance, in pressures, in hardships, in tight places,
in beatings, in prisons, in riots, in labours, in sleepless nights, in times without food,
in purity, in knowledge, in patience, in kindness, in the Holy Spirit, in love without pretence,
in the word of truth, in God's power; through the weapons of rightness for the right hand and the left,
through glory and dishonour, through slander and praise; treated as deceivers, and true;
as unknown, and well known; as dying — and look, we live; as disciplined, and not put to death;
as grieved but always rejoicing; as poor but making many rich; as having nothing and possessing everything.
Our mouth is open to you, Corinthians; our heart is wide open.
You are not cramped by us; you are cramped in your own affections.
In fair exchange — I am speaking as to children — open wide yourselves too.
Do not become unevenly yoked with those who do not trust. For what partnership do rightness and lawlessness have? Or what fellowship has light with darkness?
What agreement does Christ have with Beliar? Or what share has one who trusts with one who does not?

What agreement has God's temple with idols? Because we are the temple of the living God, just as God said: 'I will live among them and walk among them; I will be their God and they will be my people.'
'So come out from among them and be separated,' says the Lord, 'and touch nothing unclean; and I will welcome you,'
'and I will be a Father to you, and you will be sons and daughters to me,' says the Lord Almighty.

2 corinthians_7.t: So, dear friends, since we have these promises, let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of flesh and spirit, completing holiness in the fear of God.
Make room for us. We wronged no one, we ruined no one, we took advantage of no one.
I am not saying this to condemn you — I said before that you are in our hearts, to die together and to live together.
I speak to you with great openness; I boast about you a great deal. I am filled with comfort; I am overflowing with joy in all our pressure.
In fact, when we came into Macedonia our flesh had no relief at all; we were under pressure from every side — fights outside, fears inside.
But God, who comforts the downcast, comforted us by the arrival of Titus —
and not only by his arrival, but by the comfort he had received from you, as he reported to us your longing, your mourning, your zeal for me — so that I rejoiced all the more.
Because even if I grieved you with the letter, I do not regret it. Even if I did regret it — I see that that letter grieved you, if only for an hour —
now I rejoice — not that you were grieved, but that you were grieved into a change of mind. You were grieved in a way that answers to God, so that you suffered no loss from us in anything.
Because grief that answers to God produces a change of mind that leads to rescue and leaves no regret; but the world's grief produces death.

Look at what this very thing — being grieved in a way that answers to God — produced in you: what earnestness, what defence, what indignation, what fear, what longing, what zeal, what punishment! In every way you proved yourselves clean in the matter.
So even though I wrote to you, it was not for the sake of the one who did wrong, nor for the sake of the one wronged, but so that your earnestness for us might be made plain to you before God.
That is why we have been comforted. And beyond our own comfort, we rejoiced even more at the joy of Titus, because his spirit has been refreshed by all of you.
Because if I had boasted to him at all about you, I was not put to shame. On the contrary — just as everything we said to you was true, so our boasting to Titus turned out to be the truth as well.
And his affection for you is all the greater as he remembers the obedience of you all — how you welcomed him with fear and trembling.
I rejoice that in everything I have confidence in you.

2 corinthians_8.t: Brothers and sisters, we want you to know the grace of God that has been given among the communities of Macedonia:
that in a severe test of pressure, the overflow of their joy and their rock-bottom poverty overflowed into the wealth of their single-hearted generosity.
Because according to their means — I testify to it — and beyond their means, of their own accord,
they begged us urgently for the favour of sharing in this service to God's people —
and not as we had hoped: they gave themselves first to the Lord, and then to us, through God's will.
So we urged Titus that, just as he had made a start, he should also complete this act of grace among you.

But just as you overflow in everything — in trust, in speech, in knowledge, in all earnestness, and in the love that comes from us and is among you — see that you overflow in this act of grace as well.
I am not saying this as a command; I am testing the genuineness of your love against the earnestness of others.
Because you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ — that for your sake he became poor, being rich, so that you by his poverty might become rich.
And I give my opinion in this, because it is to your advantage: you were the ones who last year made a start not only on the doing but on the wanting.
So now finish the doing as well, so that just as there was readiness in the wanting, so there may be a completing out of what you have.
Because if the readiness is there, it is acceptable according to what someone has, not according to what he does not have.
This is not so that others get relief and you get pressure, but a matter of equality:
at the present time your surplus goes to their lack, so that their surplus may in turn go to your lack — so that there may be equality,
as it is written: 'The one with much had nothing over, and the one with little had no lack.'
But thanks be to God, who put the same earnestness for you into Titus' heart,
because he welcomed our appeal, and being all the more earnest he is going out to you of his own accord.
And we are sending with him the brother whose praise in the good news runs through all the communities —

and not only that: he was also appointed by the communities as our travelling companion in this act of grace that we are administering, for the glory of the Lord himself and to show our own readiness.
We are avoiding this: that anyone should find fault with us over this generous sum we are administering.
Because we are taking thought for what is good, not only in the Lord's sight but in the sight of people.
And we are sending with them our brother, whom we have often tested in many things and found earnest — and now much more earnest because of his great confidence in you.
As for Titus — he is my partner and fellow worker for you. As for our brothers — they are emissaries of the communities, the glory of Christ.
So give them the proof of your love and of our boasting about you — in full view of the communities.

2 corinthians_9.t: Now about the service to God's people — it is superfluous for me to write to you,
because I know your readiness, which I boast about on your behalf to the Macedonians — that Achaia has been ready since last year — and your zeal has stirred up most of them.
But I have sent the brothers so that our boasting about you would not prove hollow in this matter — so that, as I kept saying, you would be ready;
in case some Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, and we — not to say you — would be humiliated in this confident undertaking.

So I thought it necessary to urge the brothers to go on ahead to you and arrange in advance your previously promised blessing, so that it would be ready as a blessing and not as something squeezed out of you.
This is the point: the one who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and the one who sows on blessings will also reap on blessings.
Each should give as he has decided in his heart, not grudgingly or under compulsion — because God loves a cheerful giver.
And God is able to make every grace overflow to you, so that having enough of everything at all times, you may overflow into every good work —
as it is written: 'He scattered, he gave to the poor; his rightness stands forever.'
And the one who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your seed, and will increase the harvest of your rightness.
You will be made rich in every way for every kind of single-hearted generosity, which produces thanksgiving to God through us;
because the administration of this service is not only filling up what God's people lack — it is also overflowing through many thanksgivings to God.

Through the proof this service gives, they glorify God for your obedience to the confession of the good news of Christ, and for the single-hearted generosity of your sharing with them and with everyone,
while they also pray for you and long for you, because of the surpassing grace of God on you.
Thanks be to God for his indescribable gift.

2 corinthians_10.t: I myself, Paul, appeal to you by the meekness and gentleness of Christ — I who am humble when face to face with you, but bold toward you when away.
I beg you not to make me bold when I am present, with the confidence I reckon I will dare to use against certain people who reckon that we walk according to the flesh.
Because though we walk in the flesh, we do not wage war according to the flesh.
The weapons of our campaign are not fleshly but powerful — by God — for the demolition of strongholds, demolishing arguments
We demolish arguments and every height raised up against the knowledge of God, and we take every thought captive into obedience to Christ,
and we are ready to punish every disobedience, once your obedience is complete.
You are looking at what is in front of your faces. If anyone is convinced he belongs to Christ, let him reckon this again about himself: that just as he belongs to Christ, so do we.
Because even if I boast somewhat too much about our authority — which the Lord gave for building you up and not for tearing you down — I will not be put to shame.
— so that I may not seem to be frightening you off with my letters.
Because, someone says, 'His letters are weighty and strong, but his bodily presence is weak and his speech contemptible.'
Let such a person reckon this: what we are in word through letters when absent, that is what we will be in action when present.

We would not dare to class or compare ourselves with certain people who commend themselves. But when they measure themselves by themselves and compare themselves with themselves, they do not understand.
We will not boast beyond measure, but according to the measure of the field God assigned us as our measure — to reach even as far as you.
We are not overextending ourselves, as if we had not reached you — we did in fact get all the way to you with the good news of Christ.
We do not boast beyond measure in other people's labours; but we hope that as your trust grows, we will be enlarged among you, according to our own field, and abundantly so —
so as to bring the good news to the regions beyond you — not to boast in another's field about work already done.
'Let the one who boasts, boast in the Lord.'
Because it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one the Lord commends.

2 corinthians_11.t: I wish you would put up with a little foolishness from me. Do bear with me!
Because I am jealous over you with God's own jealousy: I betrothed you to one husband, to present you to Christ as a pure virgin.
But I am afraid that, just as the serpent deceived Eve by his cunning, your minds may be corrupted away from the singleness and purity that belong to Christ.

Because if someone comes and proclaims another Jesus — one we did not proclaim — or you receive a different spirit which you did not receive, or a different good news which you did not accept, you put up with it well enough.
Because I reckon I am in no way inferior to the super-apostles.
Even if I am untrained in speech, I am not in knowledge — in fact we have made this plain to you in every way, in all things.
Or did I commit a sin by humbling myself so that you might be exalted — because I announced God's good news to you free of charge?
I robbed other communities, taking wages from them to serve you.

And when I was with you and in need, I was a dead weight on no one; the brothers who came from Macedonia filled up my lack. I kept myself from being a burden to you in every way, and I will keep on doing so.
The truth of Christ is in me: this boast of mine will not be silenced in the regions of Achaia.
Why? Because I don't love you? God knows.
And what I am doing I will keep on doing, so as to cut away the pretext of those who want a pretext — so that in the thing they boast about, they may be found to be just like us.
Because such people are false apostles, deceitful workers, disguising themselves as apostles of Christ.
And no wonder — Satan himself disguises himself as an angel of light.
So it is no great thing if his servants also disguise themselves as servants of rightness. Their end will match their works.
I say again: let no one think me a fool. But if you do, then accept me as a fool, so that I too may boast a little.
What I am saying, I am not saying according to the Lord — I am speaking as in foolishness, in this confident boasting.
Since many boast according to the flesh, I too will boast.
Because you gladly put up with fools, being so wise yourselves!
You put up with it if someone enslaves you, if someone devours you, if someone takes you in, if someone puts on airs, if someone slaps you in the face.
I say this to my shame — as though we had been too weak for that! But whatever anyone else dares — I am speaking in foolishness — I dare too.
Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they Abraham's seed? So am I.
Are they servants of Christ? — I am talking like a madman — I am more: in far greater labours, in far more imprisonments, in beatings beyond measure, in death after death.
Five times I received from Jews the forty minus one.
Three times I was beaten with rods, once I was stoned, three times I was shipwrecked; I spent a night and a day in the open sea.

On journeys often: dangers from rivers, dangers from bandits, dangers from my own people, dangers from the nations, dangers in the city, dangers in the wilderness, dangers at sea, dangers among false brothers;
in labour and hardship, in sleepless nights often, in hunger and thirst, often without food, in cold and without clothing.
And apart from everything else, there is the daily pressure on me: my anxiety for all the communities.
Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is made to stumble, and I do not burn?
If I must boast, I will boast of the things that show my weakness.
The God and Father of the Lord Jesus, who is blessed forever, knows that I am not lying.
In Damascus the governor under King Aretas was guarding the city of the Damascenes in order to seize me,
and I was lowered in a basket through a window in the wall, and escaped his hands.

2 corinthians_12.t: Boasting is necessary. It does no good, but I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord.
I know a person in Christ who fourteen years ago — whether in the body I do not know, or outside the body I do not know, God knows — was caught up to the third heaven.
And I know that this person — whether in the body or apart from the body I do not know, God knows —
was caught up into paradise and heard unspeakable words, which no human being is permitted to utter.
On behalf of such a person I will boast; but on my own behalf I will not boast — except in my weaknesses.
Because if I did want to boast, I would not be a fool — I would be speaking the truth. But I hold back, so that no one will credit me with more than what he sees in me or hears from me,

and because of the extraordinary character of the revelations. So, to keep me from being lifted up, a thorn in the flesh was given to me, a messenger of Satan to beat me — to keep me from being lifted up.
Three times I appealed to the Lord about this, that it would leave me.

And he has said to me, 'My grace is enough for you, because power is brought to completion in weakness.' So I will boast all the more gladly in my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may pitch its tent over me.
That is why I take pleasure in weaknesses, in insults, in hardships, in persecutions and tight places, for Christ's sake; because whenever I am weak, then I am strong.
I have become a fool. You forced me to it — I ought to have been commended by you. Because I fell short of the super-apostles in nothing, even if I am nothing.
The signs of an apostle were performed among you with all endurance — signs and wonders and acts of power.
Because in what way were you worse off than the rest of the communities — except that I myself was not a dead weight on you? Forgive me this wrong!

Look — this is the third time I am ready to come to you, and I will not be a dead weight, because I am not looking for what is yours but for you. Children ought not to store up for their parents, but parents for their children.
And I will most gladly spend, and be spent out, for your lives. If I love you more, am I to be loved less?
Let it stand: I did not burden you. But — being the crafty one — I took you in by deceit!
Did I take advantage of you through anyone I sent to you?
I urged Titus to go, and I sent the brother with him. Titus didn't take advantage of you, did he? Didn't we walk in the same spirit? In the same footsteps?
You have been thinking all along that we are defending ourselves to you. We speak in God's sight, in Christ — and all of it, dear friends, is for building you up.

Because I am afraid that when I come I may not find you as I want, and you may not find me as you want — that there may be strife, jealousy, outbursts of anger, rivalries, slander, whispering, arrogance, disorder;

and that when I come again my God may humble me before you, and I may mourn over many who sinned before and have not changed their minds about the uncleanness and sexual immorality and unrestraint they practised.

2 corinthians_13.t: This is the third time I am coming to you. 'Every matter shall be established on the word of two witnesses, or three.'
I said it before, and I say it in advance now — as when I was present the second time, and now absent — to those who sinned before and to all the rest: if I come again, I will not spare anyone.
— since you are looking for proof that Christ speaks in me. He is not weak toward you; he is powerful among you.
Because he was indeed crucified out of weakness, but he lives by God's power. And we too are weak in him, but we will live with him by God's power toward you.
Test yourselves, to see whether you are in the faith; examine yourselves. Or do you not recognise about yourselves that Jesus Christ is in you? — unless you fail the test.
And I hope you will realise that we do not fail the test.
And we pray to God that you do nothing wrong — not so that we may appear to have passed the test, but so that you may do what is good, even if we should look like failures.
Because we can do nothing against the truth — only for the truth.
Because we rejoice whenever we are weak and you are strong. And this is what we pray for: your restoration.
This is why I am writing these things while absent — so that when I am present I will not have to be severe, using the authority the Lord gave me for building up and not for tearing down.
Finally, brothers and sisters: rejoice; be put back in order; be comforted; think the same thing; live in peace. And the God of love and peace will be with you.
Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the holy ones greet you.

The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with all of you. Amen. [Second to the Corinthians, written from Philippi in Macedonia by Titus and Luke.]
