2 john_1.t: The elder — to the chosen lady and to her children, whom I love in truth; and not I alone, but also all who have come to know the truth,
because of the truth that remains in us — and it will be with us forever.
Grace, mercy, peace will be with us from God the Father and from Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, in truth and love.
I rejoiced greatly because I have found some of your children walking in truth, just as we received command from the Father.
And now I ask you, lady — not as though writing you a new command, but the one we have had from the beginning — that we love one another.
And this is love: that we walk according to his commands. This is the command, just as you heard from the beginning — that you walk in it.
because many deceivers have gone out into the world — those who do not confess Jesus Christ coming in flesh. This one is the deceiver and the antichrist.
Watch yourselves, so that you do not lose what we worked for, but receive a full wage.
Everyone who runs ahead and does not remain in the teaching of Christ does not have God. The one who remains in the teaching — this one has both the Father and the Son.
If anyone comes to you and does not bring this teaching, do not take him into a house, and do not say 'welcome' to him.
For the one who says 'welcome' to him shares in his evil works.
Having many things to write to you, I did not want to with paper and ink — but I hope to come to you and to speak mouth to mouth, so that your joy may be complete.
The children of your chosen sister greet you.

2 peter_1.t: Simeon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ, to those who have been allotted a trust of equal value with ours, in the rightness of our God and Saviour Jesus Christ:
May grace and peace be multiplied to you in the full knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord.
His divine power has granted us everything we need for life and godliness, through the full knowledge of the one who called us by his own glory and excellence.

Through these he has granted us the precious and very great promises, so that through them you may become sharers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through craving.
For this very reason, bring all your effort to bear and supply, alongside your trust, excellence; and alongside the excellence, knowledge;
and alongside the knowledge, self-control; and alongside the self-control, endurance; and alongside the endurance, godliness;
and alongside the godliness, brotherly love; and alongside the brotherly love, love.
Because if these things are yours and are increasing, they will keep you from being idle or unfruitful in the full knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Whoever does not have these things is blind, short-sighted, having taken on forgetfulness of the cleansing from his old sins.
So all the more, brothers and sisters, make every effort to make your calling and choosing secure; because if you do these things you will never stumble.
For in this way the entrance into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ will be richly supplied to you.
So I will always be ready to remind you of these things, even though you know them and are established in the truth you now have.
And I think it right, as long as I am in this tent, to stir you up by way of a reminder,
since I know that the laying aside of my tent is coming soon, just as our Lord Jesus Christ made clear to me.
And I will make every effort to see that after my departure you will be able to call these things to mind at any time.
For we did not follow cleverly devised myths when we made known to you the power and arrival of our Lord Jesus Christ; we had been eyewitnesses of his majesty.
For he received honour and glory from God the Father when a voice like this was carried to him by the Majestic Glory: 'This is my Son, my beloved, in whom I have taken delight.'
And we ourselves heard this voice carried from heaven, when we were with him on the holy mountain.
And we have the prophetic word made more certain, and you do well to pay attention to it as to a lamp shining in a murky place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts —
knowing this above all: that no prophecy of Scripture comes about from anyone's own untying of it.
Because prophecy was never carried along by a human being's will; rather, people carried along by the Holy Spirit spoke from God.

2 peter_2.t: But there were also false prophets among the people, just as there will be false teachers among you — people who will smuggle in destructive divisions and even deny the Master who bought them, bringing swift destruction on themselves.
And many will follow their debaucheries, and because of them the way of truth will be blasphemed;
and in their greed they will exploit you with fabricated words. Their judgement, pronounced long ago, is not idle, and their destruction is not asleep.
For if God did not spare angels when they sinned, but cast them into Tartarus and handed them over to chains of deep gloom, kept for judgement;
and if he did not spare the ancient world but preserved Noah, a herald of rightness, with seven others, when he brought a flood on a world of the ungodly;
and if he condemned the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah, reducing them to ashes by an overturning, setting them as an example of what is coming for the ungodly;
and if he rescued righteous Lot, worn down by the way of life of lawless people in their debauchery —
for that righteous man, living among them, tormented his righteous soul day after day by what he saw and heard of their lawless deeds —
then the Lord knows how to rescue the godly out of a trial and to keep the unrighteous under punishment until the day of judgement —
and above all those who go after the flesh in a craving that defiles, and who despise authority. Bold, self-willed, they do not tremble when they blaspheme glorious ones,
whereas angels, who are greater in strength and power, do not bring a blasphemous judgement against them before the Lord.
But these people — like irrational animals, creatures of instinct born to be caught and destroyed, blaspheming what they do not understand — will also be destroyed in their own destruction,
wronged as the wage for wrongdoing. They count it a pleasure to revel in the daytime; stains and blemishes, they revel in their deceptions while they feast with you.
Their eyes are full of an adulteress and never stop sinning. They bait unsteady souls. Their heart is trained in greed. Children of a curse!
Leaving the straight road, they were led astray. They followed the road of Balaam son of Bosor, who loved the wage of wrongdoing
but was rebuked for his own lawbreaking: a mute beast of burden spoke with a human voice and stopped the prophet's madness.
These people are springs without water, mists driven by a squall; the gloom of darkness has been kept for them.
For uttering swollen, empty words, they use the cravings of the flesh and debaucheries to bait people who are only just escaping from those who live in error.
They promise them freedom while they themselves are slaves of corruption — because whatever overpowers a person, to that he has been enslaved.

Because if, having escaped the pollutions of the world through the full knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, they are again entangled in them and overpowered, the last state has become worse for them than the first.
It would have been better for them not to have known the way of rightness than, having known it, to turn back from the holy command handed on to them.
What the true proverb says has happened to them: 'A dog returning to its own vomit', and 'a washed sow returning to wallow in mud'.

2 peter_3.t: This is now the second letter I am writing to you, beloved. In both of them I am stirring up your sincere mind by way of a reminder,
so that you will remember the words spoken beforehand by the holy prophets, and the command of the Lord and Saviour given through your apostles.
Know this above all: that in the last days mockers will come with their mockery, following their own cravings
and saying, 'Where is the promise of his arrival? Since the fathers fell asleep, everything goes on just as it has from the beginning of creation.'
In holding this they overlook the fact that heavens existed long ago and an earth was formed out of water and through water by the word of God,
and by these the world of that time was flooded with water and destroyed.
But by the same word the present heavens and earth have been stored up for fire, kept for the day of judgement and destruction of ungodly people.
But do not let this one thing escape you, beloved: that with the Lord one day is like a thousand years and a thousand years like one day.
The Lord is not slow about his promise, as some reckon slowness; he is patient toward you, not wanting anyone to be destroyed but for all to make room for a change of mind.
The day of the Lord will come like a thief. On that day the heavens will pass away with a roar, the elements will be dissolved as they burn, and the earth and the works in it will be exposed.
Since all these things are being dissolved in this way, what sort of people ought you to be, in holy ways of living and godliness,
expecting and hurrying on the arrival of the day of God, because of which the heavens will be dissolved in flames and the elements melt as they burn?
But according to his promise we are expecting new heavens and a new earth, in which rightness lives.
So then, beloved, since you are expecting these things, make every effort to be found by him without spot or blemish, at peace.
And regard the patience of our Lord as rescue — just as our beloved brother Paul also wrote to you, according to the wisdom given to him,

as he does in all his letters when he speaks in them about these matters. In them there are some things hard to understand, which the untaught and unsteady twist — as they do the rest of the Scriptures — to their own destruction.
So you, beloved, knowing this in advance, be on your guard, so that you are not carried off by the error of lawless people and fall from your own steadiness.
Instead, grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ. To him be the glory both now and to the day of eternity. Amen.

2 thessalonians_1.t: Paul, Silvanus and Timothy, to the assembly of the Thessalonians in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ:
grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
We ought always to thank God for you, brothers and sisters, as is fitting, because your trust is growing beyond measure and the love every one of you has for one another is increasing.
So we ourselves boast about you among God's assemblies, about your endurance and trust in all your persecutions and in the afflictions you are bearing.
This is evidence of God's just judgement, so that you may be counted worthy of God's kingdom, for which you are also suffering.
since it is just in God's sight to repay affliction to those who afflict you,
and relief to you who are afflicted, together with us, at the revealing of the Lord Jesus from heaven with the angels of his power,
in flaming fire, as he deals out justice to those who do not know God and to those who do not obey the good news of our Lord Jesus Christ.
They will pay the penalty of eternal ruin, away from the presence of the Lord and from the glory of his strength,
when he comes on that day to be glorified in his holy ones and to be marvelled at among all who believed — because our testimony to you was believed.
With this in view we always pray for you, that our God may count you worthy of his call and fulfil every good desire and work of trust with power,
so that the name of our Lord Jesus may be glorified in you, and you in him, according to the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.

2 thessalonians_2.t: Now about the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our being gathered to him, we ask you, brothers and sisters,
not to be quickly shaken out of your mind or alarmed — not by a spirit, or by a word, or by a letter supposedly from us — as though the day of the Lord had already come.
Let no one deceive you in any way. For that day will not come unless the rebellion comes first and the man of lawlessness is revealed, the son of destruction,
who opposes and exalts himself over everything called god or object of worship, so that he sits in God's temple, displaying himself as being God.
Do you not remember that when I was still with you I used to tell you these things?
And now you know what is restraining him, so that he may be revealed at his own time.
For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work — only until the one now restraining is out of the way.
And then the lawless one will be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus will do away with by the breath of his mouth and abolish by the appearing of his coming.
The coming of the lawless one is by Satan's working, with all power and signs and wonders of falsehood,
and with every deception of wrongdoing for those who are perishing, because they did not receive the love of the truth so as to be saved.
And for this reason God sends them a strong delusion, so that they believe the lie,
so that all may be judged who did not believe the truth but took pleasure in wrongdoing.
But we ought always to thank God for you, brothers and sisters loved by the Lord, because God chose you as firstfruits for deliverance, in the holiness the Spirit gives and in trust in the truth,
to which he called you through our good news, so that you may obtain the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So then, brothers and sisters, stand firm and hold to the traditions you were taught, whether by word or by our letter.
Now may our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God our Father — who loved us and gave us eternal encouragement and good hope in grace —
encourage your hearts and strengthen you in every good work and word.

2 thessalonians_3.t: Finally, brothers and sisters, pray for us, that the word of the Lord may run and be glorified, just as it is with you,
and that we may be rescued from perverse and evil people — for not everyone has faith.
But the Lord is faithful; he will strengthen you and guard you from the evil one.
And we are confident in the Lord about you, that you are doing and will do what we instruct.
May the Lord direct your hearts into God's love and into the endurance of Christ.

We instruct you, brothers and sisters, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to keep away from every brother or sister who walks in a disorderly way and not according to the tradition they received from us.
For you yourselves know how you must imitate us, because we were not disorderly among you,
nor did we eat anyone's bread as a gift; instead, with labour and hardship, working night and day, we kept from burdening any of you.
Not that we do not have the right, but so that we might give you ourselves as a pattern to imitate.
For even when we were with you, we used to instruct you: if anyone is not willing to work, neither let him eat.
For we hear that some among you are walking in a disorderly way, doing no work but being busybodies.
We instruct and urge such people in the Lord Jesus Christ to work quietly and eat their own bread.
And you, brothers and sisters, do not grow weary in doing good.
If anyone does not obey our word in this letter, take note of that person and do not associate with him, so that he may be put to shame.
Yet do not regard him as an enemy, but warn him as a brother.
Now may the Lord of peace himself give you peace at all times, in every way. The Lord be with all of you.
The greeting is in my own hand — Paul's. This is the sign in every letter; this is how I write.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you. Amen. [To the Thessalonians, second letter, written from Athens.]

2 timothy_1.t: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through God's will, according to the promise of life that is in Christ Jesus,
To Timothy, my beloved child: grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
I am grateful to God, whom I serve as my forebears did, with a clean conscience, as I remember you constantly in my requests night and day,
longing to see you — remembering your tears — so that I may be filled with joy.
I have been reminded of the unhypocritical trust in you, which lived first in your grandmother Lois and in your mother Eunice — and I am persuaded that it lives in you too.
For this reason I remind you to fan into flame the gift of God that is in you through the laying on of my hands;
for God did not give us a spirit of cowardice, but of power and love and sound judgement.
So do not be ashamed of the testimony about our Lord, or of me, his prisoner. Instead share in suffering for the gospel, according to God's power —
the God who saved us and called us with a holy calling — not according to our works but according to his own purpose and grace, given to us in Christ Jesus before eternal times,
and now made visible through the appearing of our Saviour Christ Jesus, who abolished death and brought life and incorruptibility to light through the gospel.
For this I was appointed a herald and an apostle and a teacher of the nations.
This is why I suffer these things. But I am not ashamed, for I know the one I have trusted, and I am persuaded that he is able to guard what has been entrusted to me until that day.
Hold to the pattern of healthy words you heard from me, in the trust and love that are in Christ Jesus.
Guard the good deposit through the Holy Spirit who lives in us.
You know this: that everyone in Asia turned away from me — among them Phygelus and Hermogenes.
May the Lord grant mercy to the household of Onesiphorus, because he often refreshed me and was not ashamed of my chain.
On the contrary, when he came to Rome he searched hard for me and found me.
May the Lord grant him to find mercy from the Lord on that day. And you know better than I do how much he served in Ephesus.

2 timothy_2.t: So you, my child, be strengthened in the grace that is in Christ Jesus.
And what you heard from me through many witnesses, entrust to trustworthy people who will be competent to teach others as well.
Share in suffering as a good soldier of Christ Jesus.
No one serving as a soldier gets entangled in the affairs of ordinary life, so that he may please the one who enlisted him.
And if someone competes as an athlete, he is not crowned unless he competes according to the rules.
The farmer who works hard must be the first to share in the crops.
Think about what I am saying — the Lord will give you insight in everything.
Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, from David's seed — according to my gospel,
for which I suffer hardship to the point of chains, like a criminal. But God's word is not chained.
So I endure everything for the sake of the chosen, so that they too may obtain the salvation that is in Christ Jesus, with eternal glory.
Trustworthy is the saying: for if we died with him, we will also live with him;
if we endure, we will also reign with him; if we deny him, he will also deny us;
if we are unfaithful, he remains faithful — for he cannot deny himself.
Keep reminding them of these things, solemnly charging them before God not to fight over words — which does no good and only ruins those who listen.
Be eager to present yourself to God as one approved: a worker with no need to be ashamed, cutting the word of truth straight.
Keep away from profane empty talk, for they will only advance further into ungodliness,
and their word will spread like gangrene. Among them are Hymenaeus and Philetus,
who have missed the mark concerning the truth, saying that the resurrection has already happened, and they are overturning the faith of some.
Nevertheless God's firm foundation stands, bearing this seal: "The Lord knew those who are his," and, "Let everyone who names the name of the Lord stand away from unrighteousness."
In a large house there are vessels not only of gold and silver but also of wood and clay — some for honour, some for dishonour.
So if anyone cleanses himself from these things, he will be a vessel for honour — made holy, useful to the master, prepared for every good work.
Flee the desires of youth. Pursue rightness, trust, love, and peace, along with those who call on the Lord out of a clean heart.
Refuse foolish and uninstructed debates — you know they breed fights.
And the Lord's servant must not fight, but be gentle to everyone, able to teach, patient under wrong,
correcting opponents with gentleness. Perhaps God will grant them a change of mind leading to a full knowledge of truth,
and they may come back to their senses, out of the devil's trap, having been captured alive by him to do his will.

2 timothy_3.t: Know this: that in the last days difficult times will set in.
For people will be lovers of themselves, lovers of money, boastful, arrogant, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, ungrateful, unholy,
unloving, unforgiving, slanderers, without self-control, savage, hating what is good,
treacherous, reckless, puffed up, lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God,
holding a form of godliness but denying its power. Turn away from these people.
For some of them are the ones who slip into households and take captive weak women loaded down with sins, driven along by all kinds of desires,
always learning and never able to come to a full knowledge of truth.
In the same way that Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, these also oppose the truth — people with ruined minds, who fail the test regarding the faith.
But they will not get much further, for their folly will be plain to everyone — as theirs also became.
But you have followed my teaching closely — my way of life, my purpose, my trust, my patience, my love, my endurance,
my persecutions, my sufferings — the sort of things that happened to me in Antioch, in Iconium, in Lystra. What persecutions I endured! And the Lord rescued me out of them all.
And indeed everyone who wants to live in a godly way in Christ Jesus will be persecuted.
But evil people and impostors will advance from bad to worse, deceiving and being deceived.
You, though — remain in what you learned and were convinced of, knowing from whom you learned it,
and that from infancy you have known the sacred writings, which are able to make you wise for salvation through trust in Christ Jesus.
All Scripture is God-breathed and useful for teaching, for reproof, for setting straight, for training in rightness,
so that the person of God may be complete, fully equipped for every good work.

2 timothy_4.t: I solemnly charge you before God and the Lord Christ Jesus, who is about to judge the living and the dead — and by his appearing and his kingdom:
proclaim the word; be ready in season and out of season; reprove, rebuke, urge — with all patience and teaching.
For a time will come when they will not put up with healthy teaching. Instead, to suit their own desires, they will heap up teachers for themselves, with itching ears,
and they will turn their hearing away from the truth and be turned aside to myths.
But you — be clear-headed in everything, endure hardship, do the work of an evangelist, carry out your service in full.
For I am already being poured out as a drink offering, and the time of my departure is here.
I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.
From now on the crown of rightness is laid up for me, which the Lord will give me on that day — the righteous judge — and not only to me but to all who have loved his appearing.
Do your best to come to me soon.
For Demas deserted me, having loved the present age, and went to Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia, Titus to Dalmatia.
Only Luke is with me. Get Mark and bring him with you, for he is useful to me for service.
I sent Tychicus to Ephesus.
When you come, bring the cloak I left with Carpus in Troas — and the scrolls, especially the parchments.
Alexander the coppersmith did me much harm. The Lord will repay him according to his works.
Be on guard against him yourself, for he strongly opposed our words.
At my first defence no one stood with me; everyone deserted me. May it not be counted against them.
But the Lord stood by me and gave me strength, so that through me the proclamation might be carried out in full and all the nations might hear — and I was rescued out of the lion's mouth.
The Lord will rescue me from every evil work and will bring me safely into his heavenly kingdom. To him be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
Greet Prisca and Aquila, and the household of Onesiphorus.
Erastus stayed in Corinth; I left Trophimus ill at Miletus.
Do your best to come before winter. Eubulus greets you, and Pudens and Linus and Claudia and all the brothers and sisters.
The Lord be with your spirit. Grace be with you all.

3 john_1.t: The elder — to Gaius the beloved, whom I love in truth.
Beloved, in all things I pray that you may go well and be in health, just as your soul goes well.
For I rejoiced greatly when brothers came and testified to your truth, just as you walk in truth.
I have no greater joy than these things: to hear that my children are walking in the truth.
Beloved, you are doing a faithful thing in whatever you work for the brothers — and for strangers at that —
who testified to your love before an assembly. You will do well to send them on their way worthily of God.
for they went out on behalf of the Name, taking nothing from the gentiles.
So we ought to take such people in, so that we may become co-workers with the truth.
I wrote something to the community, but Diotrephes, who loves to be first among them, does not receive us.

This is why, if I come, I will bring up his works — the ones he is doing, babbling against us with evil words. And not satisfied with these, he does not receive the brothers himself, and he stops those who want to, and throws them out of the community.
Beloved, do not imitate the bad but the good. The one who does good is from God; the one who does bad has not seen God.
Demetrius has been testified to by everyone — and by the truth itself. And we also testify, and you know that our testimony is true.
I had many things to write to you, but I do not want to write to you with ink and pen.
But I hope to see you soon, and we will speak mouth to mouth.
Peace to you. The friends greet you. Greet the friends by name.

acts_1.t: The first account I made, Theophilus, was about everything Jesus began to do and to teach,
up to the day he was taken up, after he had given orders through the Holy Spirit to the apostles he had chosen.
After his suffering he presented himself alive to them with many proofs, appearing to them over forty days and speaking about the kingdom of God.
While he was with them he ordered them not to leave Jerusalem, but to wait for what the Father had promised — "which you heard from me;
because John baptised with water, but you will be baptised in the Holy Spirit not many days from now."
So when they had come together they asked him, "Lord, is this the time when you are restoring the kingdom to Israel?"
He said to them, "It is not for you to know times or seasons that the Father has set by his own authority,
but you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria and to the end of the earth."
When he had said this, while they watched, he was lifted up, and a cloud took him from their sight.
As they were staring into the sky while he went, suddenly two men in white clothing stood beside them,
and they said, "Men of Galilee, why are you standing here looking into the sky? This Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way you saw him go into heaven."
Then they went back to Jerusalem from the hill called Olive Grove, which is near Jerusalem, a Sabbath day's walk away.

When they came in, they went up to the upstairs room where they were staying: Peter and John and James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James son of Alphaeus and Simon the Zealot and Judas son of James.
All of these were devoting themselves with one mind to prayer, together with women and Mary the mother of Jesus and with his brothers.
In those days Peter stood up among the brothers and sisters — the group of people gathered was about a hundred and twenty — and said,
"Brothers, the scripture had to be fulfilled which the Holy Spirit spoke beforehand through David's mouth about Judas, who became the guide for those who arrested Jesus.
He was counted among us and was allotted a share in this service."
(This man bought a field with the payment for his wrongdoing, and falling headlong he burst open in the middle and all his insides poured out.
It became known to everyone living in Jerusalem, so that the field was called in their own language Hakeldama, that is, Field of Blood.)
"For it is written in the book of Psalms: 'Let his home be deserted, and let there be no one living in it,' and, 'Let another take his position of oversight.'
So one of the men who accompanied us the whole time the Lord Jesus went in and out among us —
beginning from John's baptism until the day he was taken up from us — must become a witness with us of his resurrection."
So they put forward two: Joseph called Barsabbas, who was also known as Justus, and Matthias.
Then they prayed, "Lord, you know everyone's heart. Show which of these two you have chosen
to take the place in this service and mission that Judas left when he went to his own place."
They cast lots for them, and the lot fell to Matthias, and he was counted with the eleven apostles.

acts_2.t: When the day of Pentecost was being fulfilled, they were all together in the same place.
Suddenly a sound came from the sky like a violent wind rushing through, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting.
Tongues like fire appeared to them, dividing up, and one rested on each of them.
They were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other languages, as the Spirit gave them to speak out.
Now there were Jews living in Jerusalem, devout men from every nation under heaven.
When this sound came, the crowd gathered and was bewildered, because each one heard them speaking in his own language.
They were astonished and amazed, and said to each other, "Look, aren't all these people who are speaking Galileans?
So how is it that each of us hears them in our own native language?
Parthians and Medes and Elamites, and residents of Mesopotamia, Judea and Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia,
Phrygia and Pamphylia, Egypt and the parts of Libya near Cyrene, and visitors from Rome,
Jews and converts, Cretans and Arabs — we hear them telling the great things God has done in our own languages!"
They were all astonished and at a loss, saying to one another, "What does this mean?"
But others sneered and said, "They're full of new wine."
Then Peter stood up with the eleven, raised his voice and addressed them: "Men of Judea and all of you living in Jerusalem, let this be known to you, and pay attention to my words.
These people are not drunk, as you suppose — it is only nine in the morning —
but this is what was said through the prophet Joel:

'And it will be in the last days, God says, that I will pour out from my Spirit on all flesh, and your sons and your daughters will prophesy, and your young men will see visions, and your old men will dream dreams.
And even on my male servants and my female servants in those days I will pour out from my Spirit, and they will prophesy.
And I will give wonders in the sky above and signs on the earth below — blood and fire and a mist of smoke.
The sun will be turned to darkness and the moon to blood before the great and glorious day of the Lord comes.
And it will be that everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.'
"Men of Israel, listen to these words. Jesus of Nazareth was a man attested to you by God with acts of power and wonders and signs that God did through him among you, as you yourselves know —
this man, handed over by God's settled purpose and foreknowledge, you killed by nailing him up through the hand of lawless men.
God raised him up, freeing him from the pains of death, because it was not possible for him to be held by it.
For David says about him: 'I kept the Lord before me always, because he is at my right hand so that I will not be shaken.
That is why my heart was glad and my tongue rejoiced; and my flesh too will rest in hope,
because you will not abandon my life to the grave, nor let your holy one see decay.
You have made known to me the ways of life; you will fill me with gladness in your presence.'
"Brothers, I can say to you plainly about the patriarch David that he died and was buried, and his tomb is here among us to this day.
So being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn an oath to him to seat one of his descendants on his throne,
he saw ahead and spoke about the resurrection of the Christ, that he was not abandoned to the grave and his flesh did not see decay.
God raised this Jesus up, and we are all witnesses of it.
So, lifted up to God's right hand and having received from the Father the promised Holy Spirit, he has poured out this that you now see and hear.
For David did not go up into the heavens, but he himself says: 'The Lord said to my Lord, "Sit at my right hand,
until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet."'
So let the whole house of Israel know for certain that God has made him both Lord and Christ — this Jesus whom you crucified."
When they heard this they were cut to the heart, and said to Peter and the rest of the apostles, "Brothers, what should we do?"
Peter said to them, "Change your minds, and let each of you be baptised in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
The promise is for you and for your children and for all who are far off, as many as the Lord our God calls to himself."
He testified with many other words and urged them, "Be saved from this crooked generation."
So those who welcomed his message were baptised, and about three thousand people were added that day.
They devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and to the shared life, to the breaking of the bread and to the prayers.
Awe came over everyone, and many wonders and signs were happening through the apostles.
All the believers were together and had everything in common,
and they would sell their property and possessions and distribute the proceeds to everyone, as anyone had need.
Day by day they kept meeting with one mind in the temple, and breaking bread from house to house they shared their food with glad and simple hearts,
praising God and enjoying the goodwill of all the people. And the Lord added to their number day by day those who were being saved.

acts_3.t: Peter and John were going up to the temple at the hour of prayer, the ninth hour.
A man lame from birth was being carried in; they used to put him every day at the temple gate called Beautiful, to ask for handouts from those going into the temple.
When he saw Peter and John about to go into the temple he asked for something.
Peter looked straight at him, with John, and said, "Look at us."
He paid attention to them, expecting to get something from them.
But Peter said, "Silver and gold I do not have, but what I do have I give you: in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, get up and walk."
He took him by the right hand and raised him up, and at once his feet and ankles were made firm.
He jumped up, stood, and began to walk; and he went into the temple with them, walking and leaping and praising God.
All the people saw him walking and praising God,
and they recognised him as the one who used to sit begging at the Beautiful Gate of the temple, and they were filled with amazement and astonishment at what had happened to him.
While he was holding on to Peter and John, all the people ran together to them in the colonnade called Solomon's, utterly astonished.
When Peter saw it he answered the people: "Men of Israel, why are you amazed at this? Why do you stare at us as if by our own power or godliness we had made him walk?
The God of Abraham and of Isaac and of Jacob, the God of our ancestors, has glorified his servant Jesus — whom you handed over and disowned in front of Pilate, when he had decided to release him.
You disowned the holy and righteous one and asked for a murderer to be granted to you,
and you killed the pioneer of life, whom God raised from the dead. We are witnesses of this.
And by trust in his name, his name has made strong this man whom you see and know; and the trust that comes through him has given him this complete health in front of you all.
And now, brothers, I know that you acted in ignorance, as your rulers did too.
But this is how God fulfilled what he foretold through the mouth of all the prophets, that his Christ would suffer.
So change your minds and turn back, so that your sins may be wiped out,
so that times of relief may come from the Lord's presence, and he may send the Christ appointed for you, Jesus,
whom heaven must receive until the time when everything is restored, which God spoke about long ago through the mouth of his holy prophets.
Moses said, 'The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers. Listen to him in everything he says to you.
And it will be that everyone who does not listen to that prophet will be utterly destroyed from among the people.'
And all the prophets from Samuel onwards, as many as have spoken, also announced these days.
You are the children of the prophets and of the covenant God made with your ancestors, when he said to Abraham, 'And in your offspring all the families of the earth will be blessed.'
God raised up his servant and sent him to you first, to bless you by turning each of you from your wickedness."

acts_4.t: While they were speaking to the people, the priests and the captain of the temple and the Sadducees came up to them,
annoyed because they were teaching the people and announcing in Jesus the resurrection from the dead —
and they arrested them and put them in custody until the next day, since it was already evening.
But many who heard the message trusted, and the number of the men came to about five thousand.
The next day their rulers and elders and scribes gathered in Jerusalem,
with Annas the high priest and Caiaphas and John and Alexander, and all who were of the high-priestly family.
They stood them in the middle and questioned them: "By what power or in what name did you do this?"
Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them, "Rulers of the people and elders,
if we are being examined today about a good deed done to a sick man, and how this man has been made well,

let it be known to all of you and to all the people of Israel that it is by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead — by him this man stands here in front of you healthy.
This is the stone that was rejected by you, the builders, which has become the cornerstone.
And there is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among people by which we must be saved."
When they saw Peter's and John's boldness, and grasped that they were uneducated and ordinary men, they were amazed; and they recognised them as having been with Jesus.
And seeing the man who had been healed standing there with them, they had nothing to say against it.
So they ordered them to leave the council, and conferred with each other,
saying, "What are we to do with these men? For it is obvious to everyone living in Jerusalem that a remarkable sign has happened through them, and we cannot deny it.
But so that it spreads no further among the people, let us warn them with threats to speak no more to anyone in this name."
So they called them in and ordered them not to speak or teach at all in the name of Jesus.
But Peter and John answered them, "Whether it is right in God's sight to listen to you rather than to God — you decide.
We cannot stop speaking about what we have seen and heard."
After threatening them further they let them go, finding no way to punish them, because of the people — for everyone was glorifying God over what had happened.
For the man on whom this sign of healing had happened was over forty years old.
When they were released they went to their own people and reported everything the chief priests and elders had said to them.
When they heard it they raised their voice to God with one mind and said, "Master, you are the God who made the heaven and the earth and the sea and everything in them,
who said through the Holy Spirit, by the mouth of our ancestor David your servant: 'Why did the nations rage and the peoples plot in vain?
The kings of the earth took their stand, and the rulers were gathered together against the Lord and against his Christ.'
For truly in this city Herod and Pontius Pilate, with the nations and the peoples of Israel, were gathered together against your holy servant Jesus, whom you anointed,
to do whatever your hand and your plan had decided beforehand should happen.
And now, Lord, look at their threats, and give your servants the ability to speak your word with complete boldness,
while you stretch out your hand to heal, and signs and wonders happen through the name of your holy servant Jesus."
When they had prayed, the place where they were gathered was shaken, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke God's word with boldness.
The whole group of those who trusted was one heart and one soul, and no one said any of his possessions was his own, but they had everything in common.
And with great power the apostles were giving their testimony to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus, and great favour was on them all.
There was not a needy person among them, because all who were owners of land or houses would sell them and bring the proceeds of what was sold
and lay it at the apostles' feet; and it was distributed to each as anyone had need.
Joseph, whom the apostles called Barnabas — which means son of encouragement — a Levite, a Cypriot by birth,
sold a field he owned, brought the money and laid it at the apostles' feet.

acts_5.t: But a man named Ananias, with his wife Sapphira, sold a piece of property,
and he kept back part of the price for himself, with his wife's knowledge, and brought a portion and laid it at the apostles' feet.
But Peter said, "Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit and keep back part of the price of the land?
While it stayed unsold, wasn't it yours? And after it was sold, wasn't it at your disposal? Why did you set this thing in your heart? You did not lie to people but to God."
When Ananias heard these words he fell down and stopped breathing. And great fear came on everyone who heard about it.
The younger men got up, wrapped him, carried him out and buried him.
About three hours later his wife came in, not knowing what had happened.
Peter said to her, "Tell me, did you sell the land for this much?" She said, "Yes, for that much."
Peter said to her, "Why did you agree together to test the Spirit of the Lord? Look, the feet of the men who buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out."
She fell down at his feet at once and stopped breathing. The young men came in, found her dead, carried her out and buried her beside her husband.
And great fear came on the whole community and on everyone who heard about these things.
Many signs and wonders were happening among the people through the apostles' hands. And they were all together with one mind in Solomon's colonnade,
None of the others dared to join them, but the people spoke highly of them.
More than that, crowds of men and women who trusted the Lord were being added,
so that they would even carry the sick out into the streets and put them on cots and mats, so that when Peter came by at least his shadow might fall on some of them.
Crowds also came together from the towns around Jerusalem, bringing the sick and those troubled by unclean spirits, and they were all healed.
Then the high priest rose up, and all those with him — that is, the party of the Sadducees — and they were filled with jealousy,
and they arrested the apostles and put them in the public prison.
But during the night an angel of the Lord opened the prison doors, led them out and said,
"Go and stand in the temple and tell the people all the words of this life."

When they heard this they went into the temple at daybreak and began teaching. Meanwhile the high priest and those with him arrived, called the council together — the whole senate of the sons of Israel — and sent to the jail to have them brought.
But when the officers got there they did not find them in the prison. They went back and reported,
"We found the jail locked up completely securely and the guards standing at the doors, but when we opened it we found no one inside."
When the captain of the temple and the chief priests heard this they were baffled about them, wondering what this would come to.
Then someone came and reported to them, "Look — the men you put in prison are standing in the temple teaching the people."
So the captain went with the officers and brought them, but not by force, because they were afraid the people would stone them.
They brought them and stood them before the council, and the high priest questioned them,
"We gave you strict orders not to teach in this name, and look, you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching, and you intend to bring this man's blood on us."
Peter and the apostles answered, "We must obey God rather than people.
The God of our ancestors raised Jesus, whom you laid hands on and killed by hanging him on a tree.
God exalted him at his right hand as leader and saviour, to give Israel a change of mind and forgiveness of sins.
And we are witnesses of these things, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey him."
When they heard this they were furious and wanted to kill them.
But a Pharisee named Gamaliel stood up in the council, a teacher of the law honoured by all the people, and ordered the men to be put outside for a short time,
and said to them, "Men of Israel, be careful what you are about to do to these men.

For before these days Theudas rose up, claiming to be somebody, and a number of men, about four hundred, joined him. He was killed, and all who were persuaded by him were dispersed and came to nothing.
After him Judas the Galilean rose up in the days of the census and drew people away after him. He too was destroyed, and all who were persuaded by him were scattered.
So now I tell you: keep away from these men and leave them alone. If this plan or this work is of human origin it will be destroyed,
but if it is from God you will not be able to destroy them — or you may even be found fighting against God." And they were persuaded by him.
They were persuaded by him, and they called in the apostles, had them beaten, ordered them not to speak in the name of Jesus, and released them.
So they left the council rejoicing, because they had been counted worthy to be dishonoured for the Name.
And every day, in the temple and from house to house, they did not stop teaching and announcing the good news that the Christ is Jesus.

acts_6.t: In those days, as the disciples were increasing in number, the Greek-speakers complained against the Hebrews, because their widows were being overlooked in the daily distribution.
So the twelve called the whole body of disciples together and said, "It is not right for us to leave the word of God to serve tables.
So brothers and sisters, pick out from among you seven men who are well spoken of, full of the Spirit and wisdom, whom we will appoint to this need;
and we will devote ourselves to prayer and to the service of the word."

The proposal pleased the whole group, and they chose Stephen, a man full of trust and of the Holy Spirit, and Philip and Prochorus and Nicanor and Timon and Parmenas and Nicolaus, a convert from Antioch.
They set these men before the apostles, who prayed and laid their hands on them.
And the word of God kept growing, and the number of disciples in Jerusalem increased greatly, and a large group of the priests were becoming obedient to the faith.
Stephen, full of grace and power, was doing great wonders and signs among the people.
But some from what is called the Synagogue of the Freedmen — Cyrenians and Alexandrians and people from Cilicia and Asia — stood up and argued with Stephen,
and they could not stand up against the wisdom and the Spirit with which he spoke.
Then they secretly put men up to say, "We have heard him speaking blasphemous words against Moses and God."
They stirred up the people and the elders and the scribes, and came on him, seized him and brought him to the council.
They put forward false witnesses who said, "This man never stops speaking words against this holy place and the law.
For we have heard him say that this Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place and change the customs Moses handed down to us."
Everyone sitting in the council looked closely at him and saw his face like the face of an angel.

acts_7.t: The high priest said, "Is this so?"
He said, "Brothers and fathers, listen. The God of glory appeared to our ancestor Abraham while he was in Mesopotamia, before he settled in Haran,
and said to him, 'Go out from your land and from your relatives, and come to the land I will show you.'
Then he went out from the land of the Chaldeans and settled in Haran. And from there, after his father died, God moved him into this land where you are now living.
He gave him no inheritance in it, not even a foot's length of ground, but promised to give it to him as a possession and to his offspring after him — though he had no child.
God spoke like this: that his offspring would be foreigners in a land belonging to others, and they would enslave them and mistreat them for four hundred years.
'And I will judge the nation they serve as slaves,' God said, 'and after that they will come out and worship me in this place.'
And he gave him the covenant of circumcision; and so Abraham fathered Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day, and Isaac fathered Jacob, and Jacob the twelve patriarchs.
The patriarchs were jealous of Joseph and sold him into Egypt. But God was with him,
and rescued him out of all his troubles, and gave him favour and wisdom before Pharaoh king of Egypt, who made him ruler over Egypt and over his whole household.
Then a famine came over the whole of Egypt and Canaan, and great distress, and our ancestors could not find food.
When Jacob heard there was grain in Egypt he sent our ancestors there the first time.
On the second visit Joseph made himself known to his brothers, and Joseph's family became known to Pharaoh.
Joseph sent and called for his father Jacob and all his relatives, seventy-five people in all.
So Jacob went down into Egypt, and he died, and our ancestors did too,
and they were carried back to Shechem and laid in the tomb that Abraham had bought for a sum of silver from the sons of Hamor in Shechem.
As the time of the promise God had made to Abraham drew near, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt,
until another king rose over Egypt who did not know Joseph.
He dealt craftily with our people and mistreated our ancestors, making them abandon their infants so they would not survive.
At that time Moses was born, and he was beautiful before God. He was brought up three months in his father's house,
and when he was exposed, Pharaoh's daughter took him up and brought him up as her own son.
Moses was educated in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and he was powerful in his words and deeds.
When he was forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the sons of Israel.
Seeing one of them being wronged, he defended him and got justice for the man being oppressed by striking down the Egyptian.
He assumed his brothers would understand that God was giving them deliverance through his hand — but they did not understand.
The next day he appeared to some of them while they were fighting, and tried to reconcile them into peace, saying, 'Men, you are brothers. Why are you wronging each other?'
But the man who was wronging his neighbour pushed him away and said, 'Who appointed you ruler and judge over us?
You don't want to kill me the way you killed the Egyptian yesterday, do you?'
At this word Moses fled and became a foreigner in the land of Midian, where he fathered two sons.
When forty years had passed, an angel appeared to him in the wilderness of Mount Sinai in a flame of fire in a bush.
When Moses saw it he was amazed at the sight; and as he came near to look, the voice of the Lord came:
'I am the God of your ancestors, the God of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob.' Moses trembled and did not dare to look.
The Lord said to him, 'Take off the sandal from your feet, because the place where you are standing is holy ground.
I have surely seen the mistreatment of my people in Egypt, and I have heard their groaning, and I have come down to rescue them. So now, come, I will send you to Egypt.'
This Moses, whom they rejected when they said, 'Who appointed you ruler and judge?' — this man God sent as both ruler and deliverer, by the hand of the angel who appeared to him in the bush.
This man led them out, doing wonders and signs in the land of Egypt and at the Red Sea and in the wilderness for forty years.
This is the Moses who said to the sons of Israel, 'God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers.'
This is the one who was in the assembly in the wilderness with the angel who spoke to him on Mount Sinai, and with our ancestors; he received living words to give to us.
Our ancestors were unwilling to obey him. They pushed him away, and in their hearts they turned back to Egypt,
saying to Aaron, 'Make us gods who will go ahead of us; as for this Moses who brought us out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.'
In those days they made a calf and brought a sacrifice to the idol, and they celebrated over the works of their hands.

So God turned and handed them over to worship the army of the sky, as it is written in the book of the prophets: 'Did you bring me slaughtered animals and sacrifices for forty years in the wilderness, house of Israel?
You took up the tent of Moloch and the star of your god Rephan, the figures you made to worship. And I will deport you beyond Babylon.'
Our ancestors had the tent of testimony in the wilderness, just as the one who spoke to Moses instructed him to make it, according to the pattern he had seen.
Our ancestors in their turn brought it in with Joshua when they took possession from the nations that God drove out before them, until the days of David.
David found favour before God and asked to find a dwelling place for the house of Jacob.
But Solomon built him a house.
Yet the Most High does not live in things made by hands, as the prophet says:
'Heaven is my throne, and the earth a footstool for my feet. What kind of house will you build for me, says the Lord, or what is the place of my rest?
Did not my hand make all these things?'
"You stiff-necked people, uncircumcised in hearts and ears! You are always resisting the Holy Spirit. As your ancestors did, so do you.
Which of the prophets did your ancestors not persecute? They killed those who announced beforehand the coming of the Righteous One, and now you have become his betrayers and murderers —
you who received the law by the direction of angels, and did not keep it."
When they heard this they were furious in their hearts and ground their teeth at him.
But he, full of the Holy Spirit, looked intently into the sky and saw God's glory and Jesus standing at God's right hand,
and he said, "Look, I see the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at God's right hand."
But they shouted out with a loud voice, covered their ears, and rushed at him with one mind.
They threw him out of the city and began stoning him. And the witnesses laid their clothes at the feet of a young man called Saul.
And they went on stoning Stephen as he called out and said, "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit."
Then he knelt down and cried out with a loud voice, "Lord, do not hold this sin against them." When he had said this, he fell asleep.

acts_8.t: And Saul approved of his killing. On that day a great persecution broke out against the community in Jerusalem, and they were all scattered through the regions of Judea and Samaria, except the apostles.
Devout men buried Stephen and made loud lamentation over him.
But Saul was ravaging the community, going into house after house, dragging off men and women, and handing them over to prison.
So those who had been scattered went about announcing the good news of the word.
Philip went down to the city of Samaria and proclaimed the Christ to them.
The crowds paid attention with one mind to what Philip said, as they heard him and saw the signs he was doing.
For many who had unclean spirits — crying out with a loud voice — came out of them, and many paralysed and lame people were healed.
And there was great joy in that city.
Now a man named Simon had been in the city practising magic and astonishing the people of Samaria, saying he was someone great.
Everyone from the least to the greatest paid attention to him and said, "This man is the power of God that is called Great."
They paid attention to him because he had astonished them with his magic for a long time.
But when they trusted Philip as he announced the good news about the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptised, both men and women.
Simon himself also trusted, and after he was baptised he stayed close to Philip; and seeing signs and great acts of power happening, he was astonished.
When the apostles in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them.
They went down and prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Spirit —
because it had not yet fallen on any of them; they had only been baptised into the name of the Lord Jesus.
Then they laid their hands on them, and they were receiving the Holy Spirit.
When Simon saw that the Spirit was given through the apostles' laying on of hands, he brought them money,
saying, "Give me this authority too, so that whoever I lay my hands on may receive the Holy Spirit."
But Peter said to him, "May your silver go to destruction with you, because you thought you could get God's gift with money.
You have no part or share in this matter, because your heart is not straight before God.
So change your mind about this wickedness of yours and beg the Lord — if perhaps the intention of your heart may be forgiven you.
For I see you are in the gall of bitterness and the bond of injustice."
Simon answered, "You beg the Lord for me, so that none of what you have said comes on me."
So when they had testified and spoken the word of the Lord, they went back to Jerusalem, announcing the good news to many Samaritan villages.
An angel of the Lord spoke to Philip: "Get up and go south, to the road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza." (This is a desert road.)
So he got up and went. And there was an Ethiopian man, a eunuch, a court official of Candace queen of the Ethiopians, who was in charge of all her treasury; he had come to Jerusalem to worship,
and he was on his way back, sitting in his chariot and reading the prophet Isaiah.
The Spirit said to Philip, "Go up and join this chariot."
Philip ran up and heard him reading the prophet Isaiah, and said, "Do you actually understand what you are reading?"
He said, "How could I, unless someone guides me?" And he invited Philip to come up and sit with him.
The passage of scripture he was reading was this: 'Like a sheep he was led to slaughter, and like a lamb silent before the one who shears it, so he does not open his mouth.
In his humiliation justice was taken from him. Who will tell of his generation? For his life is taken from the earth.'
The eunuch answered Philip, "Please tell me, who is the prophet saying this about? Himself, or someone else?"
Philip opened his mouth and, starting from this scripture, announced the good news of Jesus to him.
As they were going along the road they came to some water, and the eunuch said, "Look, water! What is to stop me being baptised?"
[Philip said, "If you trust with your whole heart, it is permitted." And he answered, "I trust that Jesus Christ is the Son of God."]
He ordered the chariot to stop, and both of them went down into the water, Philip and the eunuch, and he baptised him.
When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord snatched Philip away, and the eunuch did not see him any more; he went on his way rejoicing.
But Philip was found at Azotus, and as he passed through he announced the good news to all the towns until he came to Caesarea.

acts_9.t: But Saul, still breathing out threat and murder against the Lord's disciples, went to the high priest
and asked him for letters to the synagogues in Damascus, so that if he found any who belonged to the Way, men or women, he could bring them bound to Jerusalem.
As he travelled, he was approaching Damascus, and suddenly a light from the sky flashed around him.
He fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to him, "Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?"
He said, "Who are you, Lord?" And the Lord said, "I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting. [It is hard for you to kick against the goads.]"
["Trembling and astonished he said, 'Lord, what do you want me to do?' And the Lord said to him,] "But get up and go into the city, and you will be told what you must do."
The men travelling with him stood speechless, hearing the voice but seeing no one.
Saul got up from the ground, and though his eyes were open he could see nothing. They led him by the hand and brought him into Damascus.
And for three days he could not see, and he did not eat or drink.
There was a disciple in Damascus named Ananias, and the Lord said to him in a vision, "Ananias." He said, "Here I am, Lord."
The Lord said to him, "Get up and go to the street called Straight, and look in the house of Judas for a man from Tarsus named Saul — for he is praying,
and he has seen in a vision a man named Ananias coming in and laying hands on him so that he can see again."
But Ananias answered, "Lord, I have heard from many about this man, how much harm he has done to your holy people in Jerusalem.
And here he has authority from the chief priests to bind everyone who calls on your name."
But the Lord said to him, "Go, because this man is a chosen instrument of mine, to carry my name before the nations and kings and the sons of Israel.
For I will show him how much he must suffer for my name."

So Ananias went and entered the house, laid his hands on him and said, "Brother Saul, the Lord has sent me — Jesus, who appeared to you on the road you were travelling — so that you can see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit."
At once something like scales fell from his eyes, and he could see again; and he got up and was baptised,
and after taking food he regained his strength. He was with the disciples in Damascus for some days,
and at once he was proclaiming Jesus in the synagogues — that he is the Son of God.
Everyone who heard was astonished and said, "Isn't this the man who destroyed those in Jerusalem who call on this name? And hadn't he come here for this — to bring them bound to the chief priests?"
But Saul grew stronger and confounded the Jews living in Damascus by proving that this man is the Christ.
After many days had passed, the Jews there plotted to kill him,
but their plot became known to Saul. They were watching the gates day and night to kill him,
so his disciples took him at night and let him down through the wall, lowering him in a basket.
When he arrived in Jerusalem he tried to join the disciples, and they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple.

But Barnabas took hold of him and brought him to the apostles, and told them how he had seen the Lord on the road, and that he had spoken to him, and how in Damascus he had spoken boldly in the name of Jesus.
So he was with them, going in and out in Jerusalem, and speaking boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus,
speaking and debating with the Greek-speakers; but they were trying to kill him.
When the brothers and sisters found out, they took him down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.

So the community throughout the whole of Judea and Galilee and Samaria had peace and was being built up; and living in the fear of the Lord and in the encouragement of the Holy Spirit, it kept increasing.
As Peter travelled through all those places, he came down also to the holy people living in Lydda.
There he found a man named Aeneas, who had been lying on a mat for eight years, paralysed.
Peter said to him, "Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you. Get up and make your own bed." And at once he got up.
And all who lived in Lydda and Sharon saw him, and they turned to the Lord.
In Joppa there was a disciple named Tabitha, which translated means Dorcas. She was full of good works and acts of mercy that she kept doing.
In those days she got ill and died. They washed her and laid her in an upstairs room.
Lydda was near Joppa, so when the disciples heard Peter was there they sent two men to him, urging him, "Don't delay in coming to us."

Peter got up and went with them. When he arrived they took him up to the upstairs room, and all the widows stood beside him, weeping and showing the tunics and coats Dorcas used to make while she was with them.
Peter put them all outside, knelt down and prayed. Then he turned to the body and said, "Tabitha, get up." She opened her eyes, and when she saw Peter she sat up.
He gave her his hand and raised her up; then he called the holy people and the widows and presented her alive.
It became known throughout Joppa, and many trusted in the Lord.
And he stayed on in Joppa for many days with a man named Simon, a tanner.

acts_10.t: There was a man in Caesarea named Cornelius, a centurion of the cohort called the Italian.
He was devout, and he feared God together with his whole household; he gave many gifts of mercy to the people and prayed to God constantly.
About three in the afternoon he saw plainly in a vision an angel of God come in to him and say, 'Cornelius.'
He stared at him, terrified, and said, 'What is it, sir?' The angel said to him, 'Your prayers and your gifts of mercy have gone up as a memorial before God.'
Now send men to Joppa and fetch a certain Simon who is called Peter.
He is a guest of a certain Simon, a tanner, whose house is by the sea. He will tell you what you must do.
When the angel who spoke to him had gone, he called two of his household slaves and a devout soldier from those who attended him,
explained the whole thing to them, and sent them to Joppa.
The next day, while they were on the road and getting near the city, Peter went up on the roof to pray, about noon.
He became hungry and wanted something to eat. While they were getting it ready, a trance came over him,
and he sees heaven opened and something coming down like a great sheet, let down to the ground by its four corners.
In it were all the four-footed animals and reptiles of the earth and birds of the sky.
And a voice came to him: 'Get up, Peter, kill and eat.'
But Peter said, 'By no means, Lord. I have never eaten anything common or unclean.'
And the voice came to him a second time: 'What God has made clean, you must not call common.'
This happened three times, and at once the thing was taken up into the sky.
While Peter was at a loss within himself about what the vision he had seen might mean, look: the men sent by Cornelius had asked their way to Simon's house and were standing at the gate.
They called out and asked whether Simon called Peter was a guest there.
While Peter was still turning the vision over, the Spirit said to him, 'Look, three men are looking for you.
Get up, go down, and go with them without hesitating at all, because I have sent them.'
Peter went down to the men and said, 'Look, I am the one you are looking for. What is the reason you are here?'
They said, 'Cornelius, a centurion, a just man who fears God, well spoken of by the whole nation of the Jews, was instructed by a holy angel to send for you to his house and to hear words from you.'
So he invited them in and gave them lodging. The next day he got up and went off with them, and some of the brothers and sisters from Joppa went with him.
The following day he came into Caesarea. Cornelius was expecting them and had called together his relatives and his close friends.
As Peter was coming in, Cornelius met him, fell at his feet and bowed low.
But Peter raised him up, saying, 'Stand up. I am a man myself.'
Talking with him, he went in and found many people gathered.
He said to them, 'You know that it is taboo for a Jewish man to associate with a foreigner or to approach one. And to me God has shown that I am to call no human being common or unclean.
That is why I came without objection when I was sent for. So I ask: why did you send for me?'
Cornelius said, 'Four days ago, at this very hour, I was fasting and praying at three in the afternoon in my house, and look: a man stood in front of me in shining clothing
and says, 'Cornelius, your prayer has been heard and your gifts of mercy have been remembered before God.
So send to Joppa and summon Simon who is called Peter. He is a guest in the house of Simon the tanner, by the sea.'
So I sent to you at once, and you were good to come. So now we are all here before God to hear everything the Lord has commanded you.'
Peter opened his mouth and said, 'I truly understand that God is not one to take the face into account,
but in every nation the one who fears him and works rightness is acceptable to him.
The word he sent to the sons of Israel, announcing the good news of peace through Jesus Christ — this one is Lord of all —
you know the thing that happened throughout Judea, beginning from Galilee after the baptism John proclaimed:
Jesus of Nazareth — how God anointed him with the Holy Spirit and with power, and he went about doing good and healing all who were being tyrannised by the devil, because God was with him.
And we are witnesses of everything he did both in the country of the Jews and in Jerusalem — whom they also killed by hanging him on a tree.
God raised him on the third day and granted him to be made visible —
not to all the people, but to witnesses chosen beforehand by God, to us, who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead.
And he ordered us to proclaim to the people and to testify that this is the one marked out by God as judge of living and dead.
To him all the prophets testify, that everyone who believes in him receives release from sins through his name.
While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell on everyone who was listening to the message.
The believers from the circumcision who had come with Peter were astonished that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on the nations,
for they heard them speaking in tongues and magnifying God. Then Peter answered:
'Can anyone withhold the water to keep these people from being baptised — people who received the Holy Spirit just as we did?'
So he ordered that they be baptised in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked him to stay on for some days.

acts_11.t: The apostles and the brothers and sisters throughout Judea heard that the nations too had received the word of God.
When Peter came up to Jerusalem, those of the circumcision took issue with him,
saying, 'You went in to men who have a foreskin, and you ate with them.'
So Peter began and set it out for them in order:
'I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision: something coming down like a great sheet, let down from the sky by its four corners, and it came right to me.
I looked closely into it and saw the four-footed animals of the earth, the wild beasts, the reptiles and the birds of the sky.
And I heard a voice saying to me, 'Get up, Peter, kill and eat.'
But I said, 'By no means, Lord. Nothing common or unclean has ever entered my mouth.'
But the voice answered from heaven a second time: 'What God has made clean, you must not call common.'
This happened three times, and then the whole thing was pulled back up into the sky.
And right then three men stood at the house where we were, sent to me from Caesarea.
The Spirit told me to go with them without making any distinction. These six brothers came with me too, and we went into the man's house.
He reported to us how he had seen the angel standing in his house and saying, 'Send to Joppa and fetch Simon who is called Peter.
He will speak words to you by which you will be saved, you and your whole household.'
As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell on them just as it did on us at the beginning.
And I remembered the word of the Lord, how he said, 'John baptised with water, but you will be baptised in the Holy Spirit.'
So if God gave them the same gift he gave us when we believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I to be able to stand in God's way?'
When they heard this they went quiet, and they gave glory to God, saying, 'So God has given a change of mind that leads to life to the nations as well.'
Now those who had been scattered by the persecution that arose over Stephen travelled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus and Antioch, speaking the message to nobody except Jews.
But some of them, men of Cyprus and Cyrene, came to Antioch and began speaking to the Greek-speaking Jews as well, announcing the good news of the Lord Jesus.
The hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number believed and turned to the Lord.
News about them reached the ears of the community in Jerusalem, and they sent Barnabas out as far as Antioch.
When he arrived and saw the grace of God he was glad, and he encouraged them all to stay with the Lord with the purpose of their heart,
for he was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and of trust. And a sizeable crowd was added to the Lord.
He went off to Tarsus to hunt for Saul,

and when he found him he brought him to Antioch. For a whole year they met together in the community and taught a sizeable crowd, and it was in Antioch that the disciples were first publicly styled Christians.
In those days prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.
One of them named Agabus stood up and indicated through the Spirit that a great famine was about to come over the whole inhabited world — which did happen, under Claudius Caesar.
The disciples decided, each according to what he could afford, to send help to the brothers and sisters living in Judea.
And they did it, sending it to the elders by the hand of Barnabas and Saul.

acts_12.t: About that time Herod the king laid hands on some who belonged to the community, to do them harm.
He killed James, John's brother, with a sword.
And when he saw that it pleased the Jews, he went on to seize Peter as well. These were the days of unleavened bread.
He arrested him and put him in prison, handing him over to four squads of four soldiers to guard him, intending to bring him out to the people after the Passover.
So Peter was kept in the prison, but prayer was being made intensely to God for him by the community.
On the night before Herod was going to bring him out, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, and guards in front of the door were watching the prison.
And look: an angel of the Lord stood there, and light shone in the cell. He struck Peter's side and woke him up, saying, 'Get up, quickly.' And the chains fell off his hands.
The angel said to him, 'Get dressed and put on your sandals.' He did. And he says to him, 'Throw your cloak round you and follow me.'
He went out and followed, and he did not know that what was happening through the angel was real; he thought he was seeing a vision.

They passed the first guard and the second and came to the iron gate that leads into the city, and it opened for them of its own accord. They went out and walked down one street, and immediately the angel left him.
Then Peter came to himself and said, 'Now I know truly that the Lord sent his angel and rescued me from Herod's hand and from everything the people of the Jews were expecting.'
Realising this, he went to the house of Mary the mother of John who is called Mark, where a good many had gathered and were praying.
When he knocked at the door of the gateway, a servant girl named Rhoda came to answer.
She recognised Peter's voice and, out of sheer joy, did not open the gate but ran in and announced that Peter was standing at the gateway.
They said to her, 'You are out of your mind.' But she kept insisting it was so. And they kept saying, 'It is his angel.'
Peter kept on knocking. When they opened, they saw him and were astounded.

He motioned to them with his hand to be quiet and told them how the Lord had brought him out of the prison. He said, 'Report this to James and to the brothers.' Then he left and went to another place.
When day came there was no small commotion among the soldiers about what had become of Peter.
Herod searched for him and did not find him. He interrogated the guards and ordered them led away, and he went down from Judea to Caesarea and stayed there.

Herod was furious with the people of Tyre and Sidon. They came to him with one accord, and after winning over Blastus, the king's chamberlain, they asked for peace, because their country was fed from the king's.
On an appointed day Herod put on royal clothing, sat on the platform and made a public speech to them.
The assembled people kept shouting, 'The voice of a god and not of a man!'
At once an angel of the Lord struck him down, because he did not give the glory to God, and he was eaten by worms and died.
But the word of God kept growing and multiplying.
And Barnabas and Saul returned to Jerusalem, having completed their service, taking with them John who was called Mark.

acts_13.t: In the community at Antioch there were prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon called Niger, Lucius the Cyrenian, Manaen who had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.
While they were serving the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, 'Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.'
Then, after fasting and praying and laying their hands on them, they let them go.
So they, sent out by the Holy Spirit, went down to Seleucia and from there sailed for Cyprus.
When they reached Salamis they announced the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews. They also had John as their assistant.
They went through the whole island as far as Paphos, and they found a man who was a magician, a false prophet, a Jew, whose name was Bar-Jesus.
He was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus, an intelligent man. He called for Barnabas and Saul and wanted to hear the word of God.
But Elymas the magician — that is how his name is translated — opposed them, trying to turn the proconsul away from the faith.
But Saul, who is also Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, stared at him
and said, 'You who are full of every kind of deceit and every kind of fraud, son of the devil, enemy of all rightness — will you not stop twisting the straight ways of the Lord?

And now, look: the hand of the Lord is on you, and you will be blind, not seeing the sun for a time.' Immediately mist and darkness fell on him, and he went about looking for people to lead him by the hand.
Then the proconsul, seeing what had happened, believed, astonished at the teaching of the Lord.
Paul and his companions put to sea from Paphos and came to Perga in Pamphylia. John left them and went back to Jerusalem.
