because a friend of mine has arrived from a journey and I have nothing to set before him.
And the man inside answers: Do not bother me. The door is already locked, and my children are in bed with me. I cannot get up and give you anything.
I tell you, even if he will not get up and give him anything because he is his friend, still because of his shamelessness he will get up and give him whatever he needs.
And I tell you: ask, and it will be given to you; look, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks receives, and the one who looks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened.
Which father among you, if his son asks for [bread, will hand him a stone; or if he asks for] a fish, will hand him a snake instead of a fish?
Or if he asks for an egg, will he hand him a scorpion?
So if you, who are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will the Father from heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him.
He was driving out a demon, and it was mute. When the demon had gone out, the mute man spoke, and the crowds were amazed.
But some of them said: He drives out the demons by Beelzeboul, the ruler of the demons.
Others, testing him, were looking for a sign from heaven from him.
But he knew what they were thinking and said to them: Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and a house falls on a house.
And if Satan is divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? Because you say I drive out the demons by Beelzeboul.
And if I drive out the demons by Beelzeboul, by whom do your own sons drive them out? So they will be your judges.
But if I drive out the demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has arrived upon you.
When a strong man, fully armed, guards his own courtyard, his possessions are safe.
But when someone stronger than he is attacks and defeats him, he takes away the armour he had trusted in and hands out the spoils.
Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.
When the unclean spirit goes out of a person, it travels through waterless places looking for rest, and when it finds none it says: I will go back to my house, where I came out of.
And when it comes, it finds the house unoccupied, swept and put in order.
Then it goes and takes seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they go in and settle there. And that person ends up worse off than before.
As he was saying this, a woman in the crowd raised her voice and said to him: Blessed is the womb that carried you and the breasts you nursed at.
But he said: Rather, blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it.
As the crowds were packing in around him he began to say: This generation is an evil generation. It looks for a sign, and no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah.
For just as Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so also the Son of Man will be to this generation.

The queen of the south will be raised at the judgement with the men of this generation and will condemn them, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon's wisdom, and look, something greater than Solomon is here.
The men of Nineveh will stand up at the judgement with this generation and will condemn it, because they changed their minds at Jonah's proclamation, and look, something greater than Jonah is here.
No one lights a lamp and puts it in a cellar or under a basket, but on a lampstand, so that those who come in can see the light.
Your eye is the lamp of the body. When your eye is single, your whole body is full of light too; but when it is evil, your body is dark as well.
So watch out that the light in you is not darkness.
So if your whole body is full of light, with no part of it dark, it will be wholly full of light, as when a lamp lights you with its flash.
While he was speaking, a Pharisee asked him to have a meal with him. So he went in and reclined at table.
The Pharisee saw it and was surprised that he had not first washed before the meal.
But the Lord said to him: Now you Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and the dish, but inside you are full of greed and evil.
You fools, did not the one who made the outside make the inside too?
But give what is inside as charity, and look, everything is clean for you.
But how terrible for you Pharisees, because you tithe the mint and the rue and every herb, and you pass by justice and the love of God. These you should have done, without leaving those aside.
How terrible for you Pharisees, because you love the front seat in the synagogues and the greetings in the marketplaces.
How terrible for you, because you are like unmarked graves, and the people who walk over them do not know it.
One of the lawyers answered him: Teacher, when you say these things you insult us too.
But he said: How terrible for you lawyers too, because you load people with loads that are hard to carry, and you yourselves do not touch the loads with one of your fingers.
How terrible for you, because you build the tombs of the prophets, and it was your fathers who killed them.
So you are witnesses, and you approve of your fathers' works: they killed them, and you build.
That is why the wisdom of God said: I will send them prophets and apostles, and some of them they will kill and persecute,
so that the blood of all the prophets poured out since the foundation of the world may be required from this generation,
from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who was killed between the altar and the house. Yes, I tell you, it will be required from this generation.
How terrible for you lawyers, because you took away the key of knowledge. You did not go in yourselves, and you stopped those who were going in.
When he had gone out from there, the scribes and the Pharisees began to press him hard and to interrogate him about many things,
lying in wait for him, trying to catch something out of his mouth so that they could accuse him.

luke_12.t: Meanwhile, when the crowd had gathered in their tens of thousands, so that they were trampling one another, he began to say to his disciples first: Watch yourselves against the yeast of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
There is nothing covered up that will not be uncovered, and nothing hidden that will not be known.
So whatever you have said in the dark will be heard in the light, and what you whispered into an ear in the inner rooms will be proclaimed from the rooftops.
And I tell you, my friends: do not be afraid of those who kill the body and after that have nothing more they can do.
But I will show you whom to fear: fear the one who, after killing, has authority to throw into Gehenna. Yes, I tell you, fear that one.
Are not five sparrows sold for two small coins? And not one of them is forgotten before God.
But even the hairs of your head have all been counted. Do not be afraid. You are worth more than many sparrows.
And I tell you, everyone who acknowledges me before people, the Son of Man will also acknowledge before the angels of God.
But the one who denies me before people will be denied before the angels of God.
And everyone who says a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but the one who slanders the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
When they bring you before the synagogues and the rulers and the authorities, do not worry about how or what you will say in your defence, or what you will say,
for the Holy Spirit will teach you in that very hour what you must say.
Someone in the crowd said to him: Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.
But he said to him: Man, who appointed me a judge or an arbitrator over you?
And he said to them: Watch out and guard yourselves against every kind of greed, because a person's life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions.
And he told them a parable: The land of a certain rich man produced well.
And he reasoned to himself: What shall I do, because I have nowhere to gather my crops?
And he said: This is what I will do. I will pull down my barns and build bigger ones, and I will gather all my grain and my goods there,
and I will say to my soul: Soul, you have many good things stored up for many years. Rest, eat, drink, enjoy yourself.
But God said to him: Fool, this night they are demanding your soul back from you. And the things you prepared, whose will they be?
That is how it is for the one who stores up treasure for himself and is not rich toward God.
And he said to his disciples: This is why I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear.
For life is more than food, and the body more than clothing.
Think about the ravens: they do not sow or reap, they have no storeroom or barn, and God feeds them. How much more you are worth than the birds.
And which of you by worrying can add a single hour to his span of life?
So if you cannot do even the smallest thing, why worry about the rest?
Think about the lilies, how they grow: they do not labour or spin. But I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was dressed like one of them.
And if that is how God clothes the grass, which is in the field today and thrown into the oven tomorrow, how much more you, you of little trust.
And you, do not go looking for what you will eat and what you will drink, and do not be unsettled.
For all the nations of the world chase after these things, and your Father knows that you need them.
Rather, look for his kingdom, and these things will be added to you.
Do not be afraid, little flock, because your Father was pleased to give you the kingdom.
Sell your possessions and give to charity. Make yourselves purses that do not wear out, an inexhaustible treasure in the heavens, where no thief comes near and no moth destroys.
For where your treasure is, there your heart will be too.
Have your waists belted and your lamps lit,
and be like people waiting for their master to come home from the wedding feast, so that when he comes and knocks they can open for him at once.
Blessed are those slaves whom the master finds awake when he comes. I tell you the truth, he will belt himself up and have them recline, and he will come and serve them.
Even if he comes in the second watch, or comes in the third and finds them like that, those slaves are blessed.
But know this: if the householder had known what hour the thief was coming, he would not have let his house be broken into.
You too be ready, because the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not expect.
Peter said: Lord, are you telling this parable for us, or for everyone?
And the lord said: Who then is the trustworthy manager, the sensible one, whom the master will put in charge of his household of attendants to give them their ration at the right time?
Blessed is that slave whom his master finds doing so when he comes.
Truly I tell you, he will put him in charge of all his property.
But if that slave says in his heart: My master is taking a long time coming, and starts to beat the slave boys and slave girls and to eat and drink and get drunk,
the master of that slave will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not know, and will cut him in two and put his portion with the unfaithful.
That slave who knew his master's will and did not get ready or act on it will be beaten with many blows.

But the one who did not know, and did things deserving a beating, will be beaten with few. From everyone who has been given much, much will be required; and from the one they have entrusted much to, they will ask all the more.
I came to throw fire on the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled.
But I have a baptism to be baptised with, and how constrained I am until it is completed.
Do you think I came to give peace on the earth? No, I tell you, but division.
For from now on five in one household will be divided, three against two and two against three.

They will be divided: father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.
And he also said to the crowds: When you see a cloud rising in the west, you say at once that a downpour is coming, and so it happens.
And when a south wind is blowing, you say there will be scorching heat, and it happens.
Hypocrites. You know how to interpret the face of the earth and the sky, but how is it you do not know how to interpret this present time?
And why do you not judge for yourselves what is right?

For as you are going with your opponent before a magistrate, make an effort on the road to be rid of him, so that he does not drag you off to the judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.
I tell you, you will certainly not get out of there until you have paid back even the last lepton.

luke_13.t: At that very time some people were there telling him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
And he answered them: Do you think that those Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans, because they suffered this?
No, I tell you. But unless you change your minds, you will all be destroyed in the same way.
Or those eighteen the tower in Siloam fell on and killed: do you think they were in greater debt than everyone else living in Jerusalem?
No, I tell you. But unless you change your minds, you will all be destroyed in the same way.
And he told this parable: Someone had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came looking for fruit on it and did not find any.
So he said to the vine-worker: Look, for three years I have been coming to look for fruit on this fig tree and I do not find any. Cut it down. Why should it use up the ground as well?
But he answered him: Sir, leave it this year too, until I dig round it and put manure on it.
And if it bears fruit next year, well and good. If not, you can cut it down.
He was teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbath.
And there was a woman there who had had a spirit of weakness for eighteen years. She was bent double and could not straighten up at all.
When Jesus saw her he called her over and said to her: Woman, you have been released from your weakness.
And he put his hands on her, and immediately she was straightened up and began praising God.

But the synagogue leader was indignant that Jesus had healed on the sabbath, and he said to the crowd: There are six days on which work must be done. So come and be healed on those, and not on the sabbath day.
But the Lord answered him: Hypocrites. Does not each of you untie his ox or his donkey from the manger on the sabbath and lead it off to give it a drink?
And this woman, a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan bound for eighteen years, was it not necessary for her to be untied from this bond on the sabbath day?
As he said this, all his opponents were put to shame, and the whole crowd was rejoicing at all the splendid things that were happening through him.
So he said: What is the kingdom of God like, and what shall I compare it to?
It is like a mustard seed that a man took and threw into his own garden, and it grew and became a tree, and the birds of the sky nested in its branches.
And again he said: What shall I compare the kingdom of God to?
It is like yeast that a woman took and hid in three measures of flour, until the whole batch was leavened.
And he went on through towns and villages, teaching and making his way to Jerusalem.
Someone said to him: Lord, are only a few being saved? And he said to them:
Struggle to get in through the narrow door, because many, I tell you, will try to get in and will not be able to.
Once the householder has got up and shut the door, you will start standing outside and knocking at the door, saying: Lord, open for us. And he will answer you: I do not know where you are from.
Then you will start saying: We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets.
And he will say: I tell you, I do not know where you are from. Get away from me, all you workers of injustice.
There will be weeping and grinding of teeth there, when you see Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, and yourselves thrown outside.
And people will come from east and west and from north and south and recline at table in the kingdom of God.
And look, there are last who will be first, and there are first who will be last.
At that very hour some Pharisees came and said to him: Get out and go away from here, because Herod wants to kill you.
And he said to them: Go and tell that fox: Look, I am driving out demons and completing healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I complete my mission.
But I must go on today and tomorrow and the next day, because it is not acceptable for a prophet to be destroyed outside Jerusalem.
Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those sent to you, how often I wanted to gather your children together as a bird gathers her brood under her wings, and you did not want it.
Look, your house is left to you. And I tell you the truth, you will not see me until the time comes when you say: Blessed is the one coming in the name of the Lord.

luke_14.t: One sabbath he went into the house of one of the leading Pharisees to eat bread, and they were watching him closely.
And there in front of him was a man with dropsy.
And Jesus said to the lawyers and Pharisees: Is it permitted to heal on the sabbath, or not?
But they stayed silent. So he took hold of him, healed him and sent him away.
And he said to them: Which of you, if a son or an ox falls into a well, will not pull him out at once on the sabbath day?
And they could not give any answer to that.
And he told a parable to the guests, when he noticed how they were picking out the places of honour. He said to them:
When you are invited by someone to a wedding, do not recline in the place of honour, in case someone more distinguished than you has been invited by him,
and the one who invited you both comes and says to you: Give this man your place. And then you will start, in shame, to take the last place.

But when you are invited, go and recline in the last place, so that when the one who invited you comes he will say to you: Friend, move up higher. Then you will have honour in front of everyone reclining with you.
For everyone who lifts himself up will be brought low, and the one who lowers himself will be lifted up.

And he also said to the man who had invited him: When you put on a lunch or a dinner, do not call your friends or your brothers or your relatives or rich neighbours, in case they invite you back in return and you are repaid.
But when you put on a reception, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, the blind.
And you will be blessed, because they have nothing to repay you with. For you will be repaid at the resurrection of the just.
One of those reclining with him heard this and said to him: Blessed is whoever will eat bread in the kingdom of God.
But he said to him: A man was giving a great dinner and invited many.
And at dinner time he sent his slave to say to those who had been invited: Come, because it is ready now.
And they all alike began to excuse themselves. The first said to him: I have bought a field and I have to go out and look at it. Please accept my excuses.
And another said: I have bought five pairs of oxen and I am going to test them. Please accept my excuses.
And another said: I have married a woman, and that is why I cannot come.

And the slave came and reported this to his master. Then the householder was angry and said to his slave: Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the town and bring in the poor and crippled and blind and lame here.
And the slave said: Sir, what you ordered has been done, and there is still room.
And the master said to the slave: Go out to the roads and the hedges and compel them to come in, so that my house may be filled.
For I tell you, not one of those men who were invited will taste my dinner. [For many are called, but few are chosen.]
Large crowds were travelling with him, and he turned and said to them:
If anyone comes to me and does not hate his own father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, and his own life as well, he cannot be my disciple.
And whoever does not carry his own cross and come after me cannot be my disciple.
For which of you, wanting to build a tower, does not first sit down and calculate the cost, to see whether he has enough to complete it?
Otherwise, when he has laid a foundation and cannot finish, everyone watching will start to mock him,
saying: This man started to build and could not finish.
Or what king, going out to engage another king in war, will not sit down first and consider whether he is able with ten thousand to meet the one coming against him with twenty thousand?
And if not, while the other is still far off he sends a delegation and asks for terms of peace.
So then, none of you who does not say goodbye to all his own possessions can be my disciple.
So salt is good; but if even the salt goes flat, what will it be seasoned with?
It is no use for the soil or for the manure heap. They throw it out. Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.

luke_15.t: All the tax collectors and the sinners were coming near him to listen to him.
And the Pharisees and the scribes were grumbling among themselves and saying: This man welcomes sinners and eats with them.
So he told them this parable:
Which man among you, if he has a hundred sheep and loses one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the one that is lost until he finds it?
And when he has found it he puts it on his shoulders, rejoicing,
and he comes home and calls his friends and neighbours together and says to them: Celebrate with me, because I found my lost sheep.
I tell you that in the same way there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who changes his mind than over ninety-nine just people who have no need to change their minds.
Or what woman, if she has ten drachmas and loses one drachma, does not light a lamp and sweep the house and search carefully until she finds it?
And when she has found it she calls her women friends and neighbours together and says: Celebrate with me, because I found the drachma I lost.
In the same way, I tell you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner who changes his mind.
And he said: A man had two sons.
And the younger of them said to his father: Father, give me the share of the property that falls to me. So he divided his living between them.
And not many days later the younger son gathered everything together and left for a distant country, and there he scattered his property, living without restraint.
When he had spent everything, a severe famine came over that country, and he began to be in need.
So he went and attached himself to one of the citizens of that country, and the man sent him into his fields to feed pigs.
And he was longing to fill his belly with the pods the pigs were eating, and no one was giving him anything.
But he came to himself and said: How many of my father's hired workers have more than enough bread, and here I am dying of hunger.
I will get up and go to my father and say to him: Father, I have sinned against heaven and in front of you.
I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired workers.
So he got up and went to his own father. But while he was still a long way off, his father saw him and was moved with compassion, and ran and fell on his neck and kissed him.
And the son said to him: Father, I have sinned against heaven and in front of you. I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired workers.
But the father said to his slaves: Quick, bring out the best robe and put it on him, and put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet.
And bring the fattened calf, kill it, and let us eat and celebrate,
because this son of mine was dead and has come back to life, he was lost and has been found. And they began to celebrate.
But his elder son was out in the field. And as he came near the house he heard music and dancing,
and he called one of the young slaves over and asked what all this might be.
He said to him: Your brother has come, and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has got him back safe and sound.
But he was angry and refused to go in. So his father came out and was pleading with him.
But he answered his father: Look, all these years I have been slaving for you and I never disobeyed an order of yours, and you never gave me a young goat so that I could celebrate with my friends.
But when this son of yours came, the one who ate up your living with prostitutes, you killed the fattened calf for him.
But he said to him: Child, you are always with me, and everything that is mine is yours.
But we had to celebrate and be glad, because this brother of yours was dead and has come alive, and was lost and has been found.

luke_16.t: He also said to his disciples: There was a rich man who had a manager, and this man was accused to him of squandering his property.
So he called him and said to him: What is this I hear about you? Hand over the account of your management, because you cannot be manager any longer.
And the manager said to himself: What shall I do, since my master is taking the management away from me? I am not strong enough to dig, and I am ashamed to beg.
I know what I will do, so that when I am removed from the management, people will welcome me into their houses.
So he called each one of his master's debtors and said to the first: How much do you owe my master?
He said: A hundred baths of olive oil. And he said to him: Take your bill, sit down quickly and write fifty.
Then he said to another: And you, how much do you owe? He said: A hundred kors of wheat. He said to him: Take your bill and write eighty.
And the master commended the manager of injustice, because he had acted shrewdly. For the children of this age are shrewder toward their own generation than the children of light.
And I tell you, make friends for yourselves out of the mammon of injustice, so that when it gives out they may welcome you into the eternal tents.
The one who is trustworthy in the smallest thing is trustworthy in much too, and the one who is unjust in the smallest thing is unjust in much too.
So if you have not proved trustworthy with the unjust mammon, who will entrust you with the true wealth?
And if you have not proved trustworthy with what belongs to someone else, who will give you what is your own?
No household slave can serve two masters. Either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will hold to one and think nothing of the other. You cannot serve God and mammon.
The Pharisees, who were lovers of money, heard all this and were sneering at him.
And he said to them: You are the ones who justify yourselves in front of people, but God knows your hearts. Because what is exalted among people is a disgusting thing before God.
The law and the prophets were until John. From then on the kingdom of God is announced as good news, and everyone is forcing his way into it.
But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one stroke of a letter of the law to fall.
Everyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery, and the one who marries a woman divorced from her husband commits adultery.
There was a rich man, and he used to dress in purple and fine linen, enjoying himself in splendour every day.
And a poor man named Lazarus had been laid at his gateway, covered in sores,
and longing to be filled with what fell from the rich man's table. Even the dogs came and licked his sores.
And it happened that the poor man died and was carried away by the angels to Abraham's side. And the rich man also died and was buried.
And in Hades he lifted up his eyes, being in torment, and saw Abraham far off and Lazarus at his side.
And he called out: Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, because I am in agony in this flame.
But Abraham said: Child, remember that you received your good things in your life, and Lazarus likewise the bad things. But now he is comforted here, and you are in agony.
And besides all this, a great chasm has been fixed between us and you, so that those who want to cross from here to you cannot, and no one crosses from there to us.
And he said: Then I ask you, father, to send him to my father's house,
because I have five brothers, so that he can warn them, so that they do not also come to this place of torment.
But Abraham said: They have Moses and the prophets. Let them listen to them.
But he said: No, father Abraham. But if someone goes to them from the dead, they will change their minds.
But he said to him: If they do not listen to Moses and the prophets, they will not be persuaded even if someone rises from the dead.

luke_17.t: He said to his disciples, "It is impossible for the traps not to come — but misery to the one they come through.
It would pay him better to have a millstone hung round his neck and be thrown into the sea, than to trip up one of these little ones.
Watch yourselves. If your brother sins against you, confront him; and if he changes his mind, release him.
And if he sins against you seven times a day, and seven times turns back to you saying 'I am changing my mind' — you will release him."
And the apostles said to the Lord, "Add faith to us."
And the Lord said, "If you have faith like a mustard seed, you would say to this mulberry tree, 'Be uprooted and planted in the sea,' and it would obey you."
"Which of you, with a slave ploughing or shepherding, will say to him when he comes in from the field, 'Come at once and take your place at table'?
Will he not rather say to him, 'Get my dinner ready, and tie up your clothes and serve me while I eat and drink — and after that you can eat and drink'?
Does he thank the slave because he did what he was told? I think not.
So with you: when you have done everything you were told, say, 'We are useless slaves. We have done what we owed.'"
And it happened that as he was travelling to Jerusalem, he was passing through the middle of Samaria and Galilee.
And as he was entering a village, ten men with a skin disease met him. They stood at a distance,
and they raised their voices, saying, "Jesus, Master, have mercy on us."
And when he saw them he said, "Go and show yourselves to the priests." And it happened that as they went, they were made clean.
One of them, seeing that he had been healed, turned back, glorifying God at the top of his voice.
And he fell on his face at his feet, thanking him. And he was a Samaritan.
Jesus answered, "Were not the ten made clean? Where are the nine?
Were none found to turn back and give glory to God except this foreigner?"
And he said to him, "Get up and go. Your faith has saved you."
When the Pharisees asked him when the kingdom of God was coming, he answered them, "The kingdom of God is not coming with things to watch for,
nor will they say, 'Look, here!' or 'Look, there!' For look — the kingdom of God is among you."
And he said to the disciples, "Days will come when you will long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, and you will not see it.
And they will say to you, 'Look, there!' 'Look, here!' Do not go off, do not chase after them.
For as the lightning flashes and lights up the sky from one end to the other, so will the Son of Man be in his day.
But first he must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.
And as it was in the days of Noah, so it will be in the days of the Son of Man.
They were eating, drinking, marrying, being given in marriage — up to the day Noah went into the ark, and the flood came and destroyed them all.
It was the same in the days of Lot: they were eating, drinking, buying, selling, planting, building.
But on the day Lot left Sodom, fire and sulphur rained from the sky and destroyed them all.
It will be like that on the day the Son of Man is revealed.
On that day, whoever is on the roof, with his belongings in the house, must not go down to get them; and the one in the field, likewise, must not turn back for what is behind.
Remember Lot's wife.
Whoever tries to secure his life will lose it, and whoever loses it will keep it alive.
I tell you, on that night there will be two on one bed: one will be taken and the other left.
There will be two women grinding together: one will be taken and the other left."
[Two will be in the field: one will be taken and the other left.]
And they answered him, "Where, Lord?" And he said to them, "Where the body is, there the vultures will gather."

luke_18.t: He told them a parable about the need to pray always and not lose heart.
He said: "In a certain city there was a judge who did not fear God and had no regard for anyone.
And there was a widow in that city, and she kept coming to him and saying, 'Give me justice against my opponent.'
And for a while he refused. But afterwards he said to himself, 'Even if I do not fear God or have regard for anyone,
still, because this widow keeps bothering me, I will give her justice, so she does not wear me out by coming for ever.'"
And the Lord said, "Listen to what the unjust judge says.
And will God not give justice to his chosen ones, who cry out to him day and night? Will he be slow with them?
I tell you, he will give them justice, and quickly. But when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?"
He also told this parable to some who were confident that they themselves were righteous and looked down on everyone else.
"Two men went up to the temple to pray, one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
The Pharisee stood and prayed this, to himself: 'God, I thank you that I am not like the rest of humanity — greedy, unjust, adulterers — or even like this tax collector.
I fast twice a week; I tithe on everything I acquire.'
But the tax collector, standing far off, would not even lift his eyes to heaven, but beat his chest and said, 'God, be merciful to me, the sinner.'
I tell you, this man went down to his house justified, rather than the other. For everyone who lifts himself up will be brought low, and the one who brings himself low will be lifted up."
They were bringing him even their babies, so that he might touch them; but when the disciples saw it, they rebuked them.
But Jesus called them to him and said, "Let the children come to me, and do not stop them; for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
I tell you the truth: whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child will never enter it."
And a certain ruler questioned him: "Good teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?"
And Jesus said to him, "Why do you call me good? No one is good except one — God.
You know the commandments: do not commit adultery, do not murder, do not steal, do not give false testimony, honour your father and your mother."
And he said, "I have kept all these since I was young."
When Jesus heard this he said to him, "One thing you still lack. Sell everything you have and distribute it to the poor, and you will have treasure in the heavens; and come, follow me."
But when he heard this he became deeply grieved, for he was extremely rich.
Jesus looked at him, deeply grieved as he was, and said, "How hard it is for those who have money to go into the kingdom of God!
It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God."
Those who heard it said, "Then who can be saved?"
And he said, "What is impossible for people is possible for God."
And Peter said, "Look, we have left what was ours and followed you."
And he said to them, "I tell you the truth: there is no one who has left house or wife or brothers or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God
who will not receive back many times as much in this present time, and in the age to come, eternal life."
He took the twelve aside and said to them, "Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and everything written through the prophets about the Son of Man will be completed.
For he will be handed over to the nations, and mocked and insulted and spat on;
and after they have flogged him they will kill him, and on the third day he will rise."
And they understood none of this. This saying was hidden from them, and they did not grasp what was being said.
And it happened that as he came near Jericho, a blind man was sitting by the road begging.
Hearing a crowd going past, he asked what this might be.
And they told him that Jesus the Nazorean was going by.
And he shouted, "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!"
Those going ahead rebuked him, telling him to be quiet; but he shouted all the more, "Son of David, have mercy on me!"
Jesus stopped and ordered him to be brought to him. When he came near, he asked him,
"What do you want me to do for you?" And he said, "Lord, let me see again."
And Jesus said to him, "See again. Your faith has saved you."
And immediately he saw again, and he followed him, glorifying God. And all the people, seeing it, gave praise to God.

luke_19.t: He entered Jericho and was going through it.
And there was a man called by the name Zacchaeus. He was a chief tax collector, and he was rich.
And he was trying to see who Jesus was, and he could not because of the crowd, since he was short.
So he ran on ahead and climbed a sycamore-fig tree to see him, because he was about to pass that way.
And when Jesus came to the place he looked up and saw him and said to him, "Zacchaeus, hurry down; today I must stay at your house."
And he hurried down and welcomed him, rejoicing.
And when they all saw it they grumbled, saying, "He has gone in to stay with a sinful man."
But Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, "Look, Lord — half of what I own I give to the poor; and if I have extorted anything from anyone, I pay back four times over."
And Jesus said to him, "Today salvation has come to this house, since he too is a son of Abraham.
For the Son of Man came to seek and to save what was lost."
While they were listening to this, he went on to tell a parable, because he was near Jerusalem and they thought that the kingdom of God was about to appear at once.
So he said: "A man of noble birth travelled to a distant country to receive a kingdom for himself and then return.
He called ten of his slaves and gave them ten minas and said to them, 'Do business with these until I come.'
But his citizens hated him, and sent a delegation after him saying, 'We do not want this man to reign over us.'
And it happened that when he came back, having received the kingdom, he ordered these slaves to whom he had given the money to be called to him, so that he might know what business each had done.
The first came forward and said, 'Lord, your mina has made ten more minas.'
And he said to him, 'Well done, good slave! Because you were trustworthy in a very small thing, take authority over ten cities.'
And the second came, saying, 'Your mina, lord, has made five minas.'
And he said to this one too, 'And you — be over five cities.'
And the other came, saying, 'Lord, here is your mina, which I kept put away in a cloth.
For I was afraid of you, because you are a harsh man: you take up what you did not put down, and you reap what you did not sow.'
He said to him, 'Out of your own mouth I judge you, wicked slave. You knew that I am a harsh man, taking up what I did not put down and reaping what I did not sow.
So why did you not put my money in the bank? Then when I came I would have collected it with interest.'
And he said to those standing by, 'Take the mina from him and give it to the one who has the ten minas.'
And they said to him, 'Lord, he has ten minas!'
'I tell you, to everyone who has, more will be given; but from the one who has not, even what he has will be taken away.
But as for these enemies of mine, who did not want me to reign over them — bring them here and slaughter them in front of me.'"
And when he had said this, he went on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.
And it happened that when he came near Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount called Olivet, he sent two of his disciples,
saying, "Go into the village opposite, and as you enter it you will find a colt tied, which no one has ever sat on. Untie it and bring it.
And if anyone asks you, 'Why are you untying it?' say this: 'Its Lord has need of it.'"
So those who were sent went off and found it just as he had told them.
And as they were untying the colt, its owners said to them, "Why are you untying the colt?"
And they said, "Its Lord has need of it."
And they brought it to Jesus, and they threw their cloaks over the colt and set Jesus on it.
And as he went, they were spreading their cloaks on the road.
And as he came near, at the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole crowd of the disciples began to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice for all the powerful acts they had seen,
saying, "Blessed is the one who comes, the king, in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest!"
And some of the Pharisees in the crowd said to him, "Teacher, rebuke your disciples."
And he answered, "I tell you, if these are silent, the stones will cry out."
And as he came near and saw the city, he wept over it,
saying, "If only you had known, on this day of yours, the things that make for peace! But now they are hidden from your eyes.
For days will come upon you when your enemies will throw up a barricade against you and encircle you and press you in on every side,
and they will level you to the ground, you and your children within you, and they will not leave one stone on another in you — because you did not recognise the time of your visitation."
And he went into the temple and began to drive out those who were selling,
saying to them, "It is written: 'And my house shall be a house of prayer' — but you have made it a bandits' cave."
And he was teaching daily in the temple. But the chief priests and the scribes and the leading men of the people were seeking to destroy him,
and they could not find what to do, for all the people hung on his words.

luke_20.t: And it happened on one of those days, while he was teaching the people in the temple and announcing the good news, that the chief priests and the scribes came up with the elders
and said to him, "Tell us: by what authority are you doing these things? Or who is it who gave you this authority?"
He answered them, "I will ask you a question too. Tell me:
was John's baptism from heaven or from people?"
And they reasoned among themselves, saying, "If we say 'From heaven,' he will say, 'Why then did you not believe him?'
But if we say 'From people,' all the people will stone us, for they are convinced that John was a prophet."
And they answered that they did not know where it was from.
And Jesus said to them, "Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things."
And he began to tell the people this parable: "A man planted a vineyard and leased it out to farmers and went abroad for a long time.
And at the season he sent a slave to the farmers, so that they would give him some of the fruit of the vineyard. But the farmers beat him and sent him away empty-handed.
And he sent yet another slave; and that one too they beat and dishonoured and sent away empty-handed.
And he sent yet a third; and this one too they wounded and threw out.
And the lord of the vineyard said, 'What shall I do? I will send my beloved son. Perhaps they will respect him.'
But when the farmers saw him, they reasoned with one another, saying, 'This is the heir. Let us kill him, so the inheritance becomes ours.'
And they threw him out of the vineyard and killed him. So what will the lord of the vineyard do to them?
He will come and destroy those farmers and give the vineyard to others." When they heard it they said, "May it never be!"
But he looked straight at them and said, "Then what does this mean that is written: 'The stone the builders rejected — this one became the head of the corner'?
Everyone who falls on that stone will be shattered; and the one it falls on, it will crush to dust."
And the scribes and chief priests tried to lay hands on him at that very hour, but they were afraid of the people; for they knew that he had told this parable against them.
So they watched him and sent in spies who pretended to be righteous, so as to catch him in a word and hand him over to the rule and authority of the governor.
And they questioned him: "Teacher, we know that you speak and teach rightly, and show no partiality, but teach the way of God in truth.
Is it permitted for us to pay tribute to Caesar or not?"
But he saw through their trickery and said to them, "Why are you testing me?
"Show me a denarius. Whose image and inscription does it have?" And they said, "Caesar's."
And he said to them, "Then give back to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's."
And they could not catch him in a word in front of the people, and, amazed at his answer, they fell silent.
Some of the Sadducees came up — those who say there is no resurrection — and questioned him,
saying, "Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if someone's brother dies having a wife, and he is childless, his brother should take the wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
Now there were seven brothers. The first took a wife and died childless.
And the second took the wife, and he died childless.
And the third took her, and likewise all seven left no children and died.
Last of all, the woman died too.
So the woman — in the resurrection, whose wife does she become? For the seven had her as wife."
And Jesus said to them, "The sons of this age marry and are given in marriage;
but those counted worthy to attain that age, and the resurrection from the dead, neither marry nor are given in marriage.
For they cannot die any more, since they are like angels, and they are sons of God, being sons of the resurrection.
And that the dead are raised, even Moses disclosed at the bush, where he calls the Lord 'the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob.'
He is not God of the dead but of the living; for to him all are alive."
Some of the scribes answered, "Teacher, you have spoken well."
For they no longer dared to ask him anything.
And he said to them, "How is it that they say the Christ is David's son?
For David himself says in the book of Psalms: 'The Lord said to my Lord, "Sit at my right hand
until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet."'
So David calls him Lord — then how is he his son?"
While all the people were listening, he said to his disciples,
"Beware of the scribes, who like to walk about in long robes and love greetings in the marketplaces and the front seats in the synagogues and the places of honour at dinners,
who devour widows' houses and for a pretext pray at length. These will receive a heavier judgement."

luke_21.t: He looked up and saw the rich putting their gifts into the treasury.
And he saw a needy widow putting in two small coins there.
And he said, "Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all of them.
For all these put in gifts to God out of their surplus, but she out of her lack put in all the living she had."
And while some were speaking about the temple, that it was adorned with fine stones and votive offerings, he said,
"As for these things you are looking at — days will come when not one stone will be left on another here that will not be thrown down."
And they questioned him: "Teacher, when then will these things be? And what will be the sign when these things are about to happen?"
And he said, "Watch that you are not led astray. For many will come in my name, saying 'I am he' and 'The time has drawn near.' Do not go after them.
And when you hear of wars and uprisings, do not be terrified. These things must happen first, but the end will not come at once."
Then he said to them, "Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
There will be great earthquakes, and in place after place famines and plagues; and there will be terrors and great signs from heaven.
But before all this, they will lay their hands on you and persecute you, handing you over to synagogues and prisons, dragging you before kings and governors for the sake of my name.
It will turn out for you as an opportunity to testify.
So settle it in your hearts not to prepare your defence in advance,
for I will give you a mouth and wisdom that none of your opponents will be able to withstand or contradict.
You will be handed over even by parents and brothers and relatives and friends, and they will put some of you to death.
And you will be hated by everyone because of my name.
And not a hair of your head will perish.
By your endurance you will gain your lives.
"But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that her desolation has drawn near.
Then those in Judea must flee to the mountains, and those inside the city must get out, and those in the countryside must not go into it.
For these are days of vengeance, for all that is written to be fulfilled.
Misery for those who are pregnant and those nursing in those days! For there will be great distress on the land and wrath against this people,
and they will fall by the mouth of the sword and be taken captive into all the nations. And Jerusalem will be trampled by the nations, until the times of the nations are fulfilled.
"And there will be signs in sun and moon and stars, and on the earth distress of nations in bewilderment at the roaring of the sea and the surge,
people fainting from fear and from expectation of what is coming on the inhabited world; for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
And then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.
But when these things begin to happen, straighten up and lift your heads, because your redemption is drawing near."
And he told them a parable: "Look at the fig tree, and all the trees.
When they have already budded, you see it for yourselves and know that summer is already near.
So also you: when you see these things happening, know that the kingdom of God is near.
Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all this has happened.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
"Watch yourselves, or your hearts will be weighed down with dissipation and drunkenness and the worries of daily life, and that day will come upon you suddenly
like a trap. For it will come upon all who sit on the face of the whole earth.
But stay awake at every moment, praying that you may have strength to escape all these things that are about to happen, and to stand before the Son of Man."
By day he was teaching in the temple, and at night he would go out and spend the night on the mount called Olivet.
And all the people would come to him early in the morning in the temple to hear him.

luke_22.t: The festival of Unleavened Bread, called Passover, was drawing near,
and the chief priests and the scribes were looking for a way to do away with him, for they were afraid of the people.
And Satan entered into Judas, called Iscariot, who was of the number of the twelve.
And he went off and talked with the chief priests and the temple officers about how he might hand him over to them.
And they were glad, and agreed to give him money.
And he consented, and began looking for a good moment to hand him over to them away from the crowd.
And the day of Unleavened Bread came, on which the Passover lamb had to be sacrificed.
And he sent Peter and John, saying, "Go and prepare the Passover for us, so we may eat it."
And they said to him, "Where do you want us to prepare it?"
And he said to them, "Look: as you go into the city, a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him into the house he enters,
and say to the master of the house, 'The Teacher says to you: Where is the guest room where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?'
And he will show you a large upstairs room, furnished. Prepare it there."
And they went off and found it just as he had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
And when the hour came, he took his place at table, and the apostles with him.
And he said to them, "With desire I have desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.
For I tell you, I will not eat it again until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God."
And he took a cup, gave thanks, and said, "Take this and divide it among yourselves.
For I tell you, from now on I will not drink of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes."
And he took bread, gave thanks, broke it and gave it to them, saying, "This is my body, [given for you. Do this in remembrance of me."
And the cup likewise, after supper, saying, "This cup is the new covenant in my blood, poured out for you.]
"But look — the hand of the one handing me over is with me on the table.
For the Son of Man goes as it has been determined; but misery to that man through whom he is handed over."
And they began to argue among themselves about which of them it might be who was going to do this.
And there was also a quarrel among them about which of them seemed to be the greatest.
And he said to them, "The kings of the nations lord it over them, and those who exercise authority over them are called 'Benefactors'.
But not so with you. Rather, the greatest among you must become like the youngest, and the one who leads like the one who serves.
For who is greater, the one at table or the one who serves? Is it not the one at table? But I am among you as one who serves.
You are the ones who have stayed with me through my trials.
And I confer on you a kingdom, just as my Father conferred one on me,
so that you may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
"Simon, Simon — look, Satan asked to have you all, to sift you like wheat.
But I have prayed for you, that your faith may not fail. And you, when you have turned back, strengthen your brothers."
And he said to him, "Lord, I am ready to go with you both to prison and to death."
And he said, "I tell you, Peter, the cock will not crow today until you have three times denied knowing me."
And he said to them, "When I sent you out without purse or bag or sandals, did you lack anything?" And they said, "Nothing."
And he said to them, "But now, whoever has a purse must take it, and a bag likewise; and whoever has none must sell his cloak and buy a sword.
For I tell you, this that is written must be completed in me: 'And he was counted with the lawless.' For what concerns me has its end."
And they said, "Lord, look — here are two swords." And he said to them, "It is enough."
And he went out and made his way, as was his custom, to the Mount of Olives; and the disciples also followed him.
And when he came to the place he said to them, "Pray that you do not come into testing."
And he withdrew from them about a stone's throw, and knelt down and prayed,
saying, "Father, if you are willing, take this cup away from me. But let not my will be done, but yours."
And an angel from heaven appeared to him, strengthening him.
And being in anguish he prayed more intently; and his sweat became like clots of blood falling to the ground.
And he got up from prayer and came to the disciples and found them sleeping from grief,
and he said to them, "Why are you sleeping? Get up and pray, so that you do not come into testing."
While he was still speaking, a crowd came — and the man called Judas, one of the twelve, was leading them. And he came up to Jesus to kiss him.
But Jesus said to him, "Judas, are you handing over the Son of Man with a kiss?"
When those around him saw what was about to happen, they said, "Lord, shall we strike with the sword?"
And one of them struck the slave of the high priest and took off his right ear.
But Jesus answered, "Let it go this far." And he touched the ear and healed him.
And Jesus said to the chief priests and temple officers and elders who had come out against him, "Have you come out with swords and clubs, as against a bandit?
Day after day I was with you in the temple, and you did not stretch out your hands against me. But this is your hour, and the authority of darkness."
They seized him and led him away and brought him into the house of the high priest. And Peter was following at a distance.
When they had lit a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat down together, Peter sat among them.
And a slave girl saw him sitting in the firelight and stared at him and said, "This man was with him too."
But he denied it, saying, "I do not know him, woman."
And a little later someone else saw him and said, "You are one of them too." But Peter said, "Man, I am not."
And about an hour later, someone else insisted, "In truth this man was with him too — for he is a Galilean."
But Peter said, "Man, I do not know what you are talking about." And immediately, while he was still speaking, a cock crowed.
And the Lord turned and looked straight at Peter. And Peter remembered the word of the Lord, how he had said to him, "Before a cock crows today, you will deny me three times."
And he went outside and wept bitterly.
And the men who were holding him were mocking him and beating him.
And they blindfolded him and kept asking him, "Prophesy! Who is it that hit you?"
And they said many other insulting things against him.
And when day came, the council of elders of the people gathered — both chief priests and scribes — and they led him away into their council chamber,
saying, "If you are the Christ, tell us." And he said to them, "If I tell you, you will not believe;
and if I ask you, you will not answer.
But from now on the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God."
And they all said, "Are you then the Son of God?" And he said to them, "You say that I am."
And they said, "Why do we still need testimony? We ourselves have heard it from his own mouth."

luke_23.t: And the whole assembly of them stood up and led him to Pilate.
And they began to accuse him, saying, "We found this man subverting our nation and forbidding the payment of tribute to Caesar, and saying that he himself is Christ, a king."
And Pilate questioned him: "Are you the king of the Jews?" And he answered him, "You say so."
And Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowds, "I find no ground for a charge in this man."
But they insisted, saying, "He stirs up the people, teaching throughout the whole of Judea — starting from Galilee and coming as far as here."
When Pilate heard this, he asked whether the man was a Galilean;
and when he learned that he was under Herod's jurisdiction, he sent him up to Herod, who was himself in Jerusalem in those days.
When Herod saw Jesus he was very glad, for he had been wanting to see him for a long time, because he had heard a great deal about him, and he was hoping to see some sign done by him.
And he questioned him at some length, but he answered him nothing.
And the chief priests and the scribes stood there, vehemently accusing him.
And Herod, with his soldiers, treated him with contempt and mocked him; and he put a splendid robe on him and sent him back to Pilate.
And Herod and Pilate became friends with each other that very day; for before that they had been at enmity with each other.
And Pilate called together the chief priests and the rulers and the people,
said to them, "You brought me this man as one who turns the people away. And look — I have examined him in front of you, and I have found no grounds in this man for the charges you bring against him.
Nor did Herod — for he sent him back to us. And look, he has done nothing deserving death.
So I will have him flogged and release him."
[Now he was obliged to release one man to them at the festival.]
But they all cried out together, "Take this man away! Release Barabbas to us!"
He was a man who had been thrown into prison for a certain uprising that had happened in the city, and for murder.
Pilate addressed them again, wanting to release Jesus.
But they kept shouting back, "Crucify him! Crucify him!"
And a third time he said to them, "Why? What evil has this man done? I have found no ground for death in him. So I will have him flogged and release him."
But they pressed him with loud shouts, demanding that he be crucified; and their shouts prevailed.
And Pilate decided that their demand should be granted.
He released the man who had been thrown into prison for insurrection and murder, the one they asked for; but Jesus he handed over to their will.
And as they led him away, they seized a certain Simon of Cyrene, coming in from the country, and put the cross on him, to carry it behind Jesus.
And a great crowd of the people followed him, and women who were beating their breasts and lamenting for him.
But Jesus turned to them and said, "Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for me; weep instead for yourselves and for your children.
For look, days are coming when they will say, 'Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that never bore, and the breasts that never nursed.'
Then they will begin to say to the mountains, 'Fall on us,' and to the hills, 'Cover us.'
For if they do these things when the wood is green, what will happen when it is dry?"
And two others, criminals, were being led away with him to be executed.
And when they came to the place called The Skull, there they crucified him, and the criminals — one on the right and one on the left.
And Jesus was saying, "Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing." And they cast lots, dividing up his clothes.
And the people stood watching. But the rulers kept sneering, saying, "He saved others. Let him save himself, if this is the Christ of God, the chosen one."
And the soldiers also mocked him, coming up and offering him sour wine,
and saying, "If you are the king of the Jews, save yourself."
And there was also an inscription over him, written in Greek and Latin and Hebrew letters: THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.
And one of the criminals hanging there was blaspheming him, saying, "Are you not the Christ? Save yourself — and us!"
But the other rebuked him and said, "Do you not even fear God, since you are under the same sentence?
And we justly, for we are getting back what our deeds deserve. But this man has done nothing out of place."
And he said, "Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom."
And Jesus said to him, "Truly I tell you, today you will be with me in paradise."
And it was already about the sixth hour, and darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour,
as the sun failed. And the curtain of the sanctuary was torn down the middle.
And Jesus cried out with a loud voice and said, "Father, into your hands I entrust my spirit." And having said this, he breathed his last.
And when the centurion saw what had happened, he glorified God and said, "Truly this man was righteous."
And all the crowds who had gathered for this spectacle, when they saw what had happened, went home beating their breasts.
And all those who knew him stood at a distance, and the women who had followed him from Galilee, watching these things.
And there was a man named Joseph, a member of the council, and a good and righteous man —
he had not agreed with their decision and action — from Arimathea, a city of the Jews, and he was waiting for the kingdom of God.
This man went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
And he took it down, wrapped it in a linen cloth, and laid him in a tomb cut in rock, where no one had yet been laid.
And it was the day of Preparation, and the sabbath was beginning to dawn.
And the women who had come with him from Galilee followed after, and they saw the tomb and how his body was laid.
And they went back and prepared spices and perfumed oils. And on the sabbath they rested, according to the commandment.

luke_24.t: But on the first day of the week, at deep dawn, they came to the tomb, bringing the spices they had prepared; and some others were with them.
And they found the stone rolled away from the tomb.
And when they went in they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.
And it happened that while they were at a loss about this, look — two men stood by them in dazzling clothing.
And as they became terrified and bowed their faces to the ground, the men said to them, "Why do you seek the living among the dead?
He is not here — he has been raised. Remember how he spoke to you while he was still in Galilee,
saying that the Son of Man must be handed over into the hands of sinful men and be crucified, and on the third day rise."
And they remembered his words.
And they returned from the tomb and reported all this to the eleven and to all the rest.
It was Mary Magdalene and Joanna and Mary the mother of James, and the rest of the women with them; they were telling these things to the apostles,
and these words seemed to them like nonsense, and they did not believe them.
But Peter got up and ran to the tomb, and stooping down he sees only the linen wrappings; and he went away home, wondering at what had happened.
And look — two of them were going, that same day, to a village sixty stadia from Jerusalem, whose name was Emmaus.
and they were talking with each other about all these things that had happened.
And it happened that while they were talking and debating, Jesus himself came near and went with them —
but their eyes were held from recognising him.
And he said to them, "What are these words you are exchanging with each other as you walk?" And they stopped, looking gloomy.
And one of them, named Cleopas, answered him, "Are you the only visitor in Jerusalem who does not know the things that have happened there in these days?"
And he said to them, "What things?" And they said to him, "The things about Jesus the Nazarene, who was a man, a prophet powerful in deed and word before God and all the people,
and how our chief priests and rulers handed him over to a sentence of death and crucified him.
But we were hoping that he was the one about to redeem Israel. And besides all this, it is now the third day since these things happened.
But also some women of our group astonished us: they were at the tomb early,
and when they did not find his body they came saying that they had even seen a vision of angels, who said he was alive.
And some of those with us went off to the tomb and found it just as the women had said; but him they did not see."
And he said to them, "O foolish ones, and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets spoke!
Was it not necessary for the Christ to suffer these things and enter into his glory?"
And beginning from Moses and from all the prophets, he interpreted to them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself.
And they came near the village where they were going, and he made as if to go further on.
And they pressed him hard, saying, "Stay with us, because it is toward evening and the day has already declined." And he went in to stay with them.
And it happened that when he had taken his place at table with them, he took the bread and blessed it, and having broken it he was giving it to them.
And their eyes were opened, and they recognised him — and he became invisible to them.
And they said to each other, "Were not our hearts burning within us as he spoke to us on the road, as he opened the scriptures to us?"
And they got up that very hour and went back to Jerusalem, and found the eleven and those with them gathered together,
who were saying, "The Lord has really been raised, and he has appeared to Simon!"
And they were describing what had happened on the road, and how he was made known to them in the breaking of the bread.
And while they were saying these things, he himself stood in their midst, and says to them, "Peace to you."
But they were terrified and frightened, and thought they were seeing a spirit.
And he said to them, "Why are you troubled? And why do doubts rise in your hearts?
See my hands and my feet — that it is I myself. Handle me and see, because a spirit does not have flesh and bones, as you see I have."
And having said this, he showed them his hands and his feet.
And while they still could not believe it, for joy, and were wondering, he said to them, "Do you have anything here to eat?"
And they gave him a piece of grilled fish [and some honeycomb];
and he took it and ate it in front of them.
And he said to them, "These are my words which I spoke to you while I was still with you: that everything written about me in the law of Moses and the prophets and the psalms must be fulfilled."
Then he opened their minds to understand the scriptures,
and said to them, "Thus it is written: that the Christ is to suffer and rise from the dead on the third day,
and that a change of mind, for the release of sins, is to be proclaimed in his name to all the nations, beginning from Jerusalem.
You are witnesses of these things.
And look — I am sending out the promise of my Father upon you. But you, stay in the city until you are clothed with power from on high."
And he led them out as far as Bethany, and lifting up his hands he blessed them.
And it happened that while he was blessing them, he was parted from them and carried up into heaven.
And they worshipped him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy,
and they were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God. [Amen]

matthew_1.t: The book of the origin of Jesus Christ, son of David, son of Abraham.
Abraham was the father of Isaac; Isaac the father of Jacob; Jacob the father of Judah and his brothers;
Judah was the father of Perez and Zerah by Tamar; Perez the father of Hezron; Hezron the father of Ram;
Ram was the father of Amminadab; Amminadab the father of Nahshon; Nahshon the father of Salmon;
Salmon was the father of Boaz by Rahab; Boaz the father of Obed by Ruth; Obed the father of Jesse;
Jesse was the father of David the king; and David was the father of Solomon by the wife of Uriah;
Solomon was the father of Rehoboam; Rehoboam the father of Abijah; Abijah the father of Asaph;
Asaph was the father of Jehoshaphat; Jehoshaphat the father of Joram; Joram the father of Uzziah;
Uzziah was the father of Jotham; Jotham the father of Ahaz; Ahaz the father of Hezekiah;
Hezekiah was the father of Manasseh; Manasseh the father of Amos; Amos the father of Josiah;
Josiah was the father of Jechoniah and his brothers, at the deportation to Babylon.
After the deportation to Babylon, Jechoniah was the father of Shealtiel; Shealtiel the father of Zerubbabel;
Zerubbabel was the father of Abiud; Abiud the father of Eliakim; Eliakim the father of Azor;
Azor was the father of Zadok; Zadok the father of Achim; Achim the father of Eliud;
Eliud was the father of Eleazar; Eleazar the father of Matthan; Matthan the father of Jacob;
and Jacob was the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary — from whom was born Jesus, the one called Christ.

So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; and from David to the deportation to Babylon, fourteen generations; and from the deportation to Babylon to the Christ, fourteen generations.
The origin of Jesus Christ was like this. His mother Mary had been pledged in marriage to Joseph, and before they came together she was found to be pregnant — from the Holy Spirit.
Joseph her husband was a man who did what was right, and he did not want to make a public example of her, so he decided to divorce her quietly.

But while he was turning this over, look — a messenger of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, "Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife, because what has been conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.
She will give birth to a son, and you are to call his name Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins."
All this happened so that what the Lord had spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled:
"Look, the virgin will be pregnant and will give birth to a son, and they will call his name Immanuel" — which translated is "God with us".
Joseph woke from sleep and did as the messenger of the Lord had instructed him: he took his wife,
and he did not have relations with her until she gave birth to a son; and he called his name Jesus.

matthew_2.t: After Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea, in the days of Herod the king — look, magi from the east arrived in Jerusalem,
saying, "Where is the one born king of the Jews? For we saw his star at its rising, and we have come to bow down to him."
When Herod the king heard it he was shaken, and all Jerusalem with him,
and he gathered all the chief priests and teachers of the law of the people and kept asking them where the Christ was to be born.
They said to him, "In Bethlehem of Judea, because this is how it stands written through the prophet:
'And you, Bethlehem, land of Judah, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah; for out of you will come a ruler who will shepherd my people Israel.'"
Then Herod called the magi secretly and got from them the exact time the star had appeared,
and he sent them to Bethlehem and said, "Go and search carefully for the child; and when you find him, report back to me, so that I too may come and bow down to him."
They listened to the king and went. And look — the star they had seen at its rising went ahead of them until it came and stood over the place where the child was.
When they saw the star they were overjoyed — enormously.
They went into the house and saw the child with Mary his mother, and they fell down and bowed to him; and they opened their treasure-boxes and offered him gifts — gold and frankincense and myrrh.
And having been warned in a dream not to go back to Herod, they withdrew to their own country by another road.

When they had withdrawn — look, a messenger of the Lord appears to Joseph in a dream, saying, "Get up, take the child and his mother and flee to Egypt, and stay there until I tell you; because Herod is about to look for the child, to destroy him."
So he got up and took the child and his mother by night and withdrew to Egypt,
and stayed there until the death of Herod — so that what the Lord had spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled: "Out of Egypt I called my son."

Then Herod, seeing that he had been outwitted by the magi, was enraged, and he sent and killed all the boys in Bethlehem and in all its districts, from two years old and under, according to the time he had ascertained from the magi.
Then what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled:
"A voice was heard in Ramah, wailing and loud lamentation — Rachel weeping for her children, and she would not be comforted, because they are no more."
When Herod had died — look, a messenger of the Lord appears in a dream to Joseph in Egypt,
saying, "Get up, take the child and his mother and go to the land of Israel; because those who were seeking the child's life have died."
So he got up and took the child and his mother and went into the land of Israel.
But hearing that Archelaus was reigning over Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go there; and having been warned in a dream, he withdrew to the region of Galilee,
and he came and settled in a town called Nazareth — so that what was spoken through the prophets might be fulfilled: that he will be called a Nazorean.

matthew_3.t: In those days John the Baptist arrives, proclaiming in the wilderness of Judea
and saying, "Change your minds, because the kingdom of heaven has come near."
This is the one spoken of through Isaiah the prophet, who said: "A voice of one crying in the wilderness — 'Prepare the road of the Lord, make his paths straight.'"
John himself had his clothing from camel hair and a leather belt around his waist; and his food was locusts and wild honey.
Then Jerusalem and all Judea and the whole region around the Jordan were going out to him,
and they were being baptised by him in the river Jordan, confessing their sins openly.
But seeing many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his baptism, he said to them, "Offspring of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the anger that is coming?
So produce fruit worthy of the change of mind.
And do not presume to say among yourselves, 'We have Abraham as our father.' Because I tell you, God is able to raise up children for Abraham out of these stones.
And already the axe is laid at the root of the trees; so every tree not producing good fruit is cut down and thrown into fire.
"I baptise you in water, into a change of mind; but the one coming after me is stronger than I am, and I am not fit to carry his sandals. He will baptise you in the Holy Spirit — and fire.
His winnowing-fork is in his hand, and he will clear his threshing-floor right through and gather his wheat into the barn — but the chaff he will burn up with fire that cannot be put out."
Then Jesus arrives from Galilee at the Jordan, to John, to be baptised by him.
But John tried to stop him, saying, "I am the one who needs to be baptised by you, and you come to me?"
Jesus answered him, "Let it be for now; because this is how it is fitting for us to fulfil all rightness." Then he lets him.
And when Jesus had been baptised he came up from the water at once. And look — the heavens were opened to him, and he saw the Spirit of God coming down like a dove and coming on him.
And look — a voice out of the heavens, saying, "This is my son, the beloved; in him I was well pleased."

matthew_4.t: Then Jesus was led up into the wilderness by the Spirit, to be tested by the slanderer.
And after fasting forty days and forty nights, he was hungry.
And the tester came and said to him, "If you are the son of God, tell these stones to become loaves."
But he answered, "It stands written: 'A person will not live on bread alone, but on every word coming out through the mouth of God.'"
Then the slanderer takes him into the holy city and stood him on the parapet of the temple

and says to him, "If you are the son of God, throw yourself down; because it stands written: 'He will give his messengers orders about you, and they will lift you on their hands, so that you never strike your foot against a stone.'"
Jesus said to him, "Again, it stands written: 'You shall not put the Lord your God to the test.'"
Again the slanderer takes him to a very high mountain and shows him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory,
and said to him, "All these I will give you, if you fall down and bow to me."
Then Jesus says to him, "Get away behind me, Satan! Because it stands written: 'You shall bow to the Lord your God, and him only shall you serve.'"
Then the slanderer leaves him; and look — messengers came and were serving him.
When Jesus heard that John had been handed over, he withdrew into Galilee.
And leaving Nazara he came and settled in Capernaum by the sea, in the districts of Zebulun and Naphtali —
so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled:
"Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, the road of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations —
the people sitting in darkness saw a great light; and on those sitting in the country and shadow of death, a light rose on them."
From then on Jesus began to proclaim and to say, "Change your minds, because the kingdom of heaven has come near."
Walking beside the sea of Galilee he saw two brothers — Simon, the one called Peter, and Andrew his brother — casting a net into the sea; for they were fishermen.
And he says to them, "Come after me, and I will make you fishers of people."
And at once they left the nets and followed him.
And going on from there he saw two other brothers — James the son of Zebedee and John his brother — in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them.
And at once they left the boat and their father and followed him.
And he went round the whole of Galilee, teaching in their synagogues and proclaiming the good news of the kingdom and healing every disease and every weakness among the people.
