And the report of him went out into all of Syria; and they brought him everyone who was ill, gripped by various diseases and torments, and demon-possessed and moonstruck and paralysed; and he healed them.
And large crowds followed him from Galilee and the Ten Towns and Jerusalem and Judea and beyond the Jordan.

matthew_5.t: Seeing the crowds he went up onto the mountain; and when he had sat down his learners came to him.
And he opened his mouth and began to teach them, saying:
How fortunate are the poor in spirit — because the kingdom of heaven is theirs.
How fortunate are those who mourn — because they will be comforted.
How fortunate are the gentle — because they will inherit the earth.
How fortunate are those hungering and thirsting for rightness — because they will be filled.
How fortunate are the merciful — because they will be shown mercy.
How fortunate are the pure in heart — because they will see God.
How fortunate are the peacemakers — because they will be called sons of God.
How fortunate are those who have been persecuted for the sake of rightness — because the kingdom of heaven is theirs.
You are fortunate when they insult you and persecute you and say every kind of evil thing against you, lying, because of me.
Rejoice and be glad, because your reward is great in the heavens; for that is how they persecuted the prophets before you.
You are the salt of the earth. But if the salt is made foolish, what will it be salted with? It is no longer good for anything except to be thrown outside and trampled by people.
You are the light of the world. A city cannot be hidden when it sits on a hill;
nor do people light a lamp and put it under the basket, but on the lampstand, and it shines for everyone in the house.
In the same way, let your light shine in front of people, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father in the heavens.
Do not think that I came to tear down the law or the prophets. I did not come to tear down but to fill full.
I tell you the truth: until heaven and earth pass away, not one iota, not one stroke, will pass from the law until everything has happened.

So whoever breaks one of the least of these commands and teaches people to do the same will be called least in the kingdom of heaven; but whoever does them and teaches them, this one will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
Because I tell you that unless your rightness exceeds that of the teachers of the law and the Pharisees, you will certainly not enter the kingdom of heaven.
You heard that it was said to the ancients: "You shall not murder"; and whoever murders will be liable to judgement.

But I say to you that everyone who is angry with his brother or sister [without cause] will be liable to judgement; and whoever says to his brother or sister, "Empty-head!" will be liable to the council; and whoever says, "Idiot!" will be liable to the Gehenna of fire.
So if you are bringing your gift to the altar and there you remember that your brother or sister has something against you,
leave your gift there in front of the altar and go — first be reconciled to your brother or sister, and then come and bring your gift.

Come to terms with the one bringing a case against you, quickly, while you are with him on the road — or the accuser may hand you over to the judge, and the judge to the officer, and you will be thrown into prison.
I tell you the truth: you will certainly not come out from there until you have paid back the last penny.
You heard that it was said to the ancients: "You shall not commit adultery."
But I say to you that everyone who looks at a woman in order to want her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
And if your right eye trips you up, tear it out and throw it away from you; because it is better for you that one of your parts be destroyed than that your whole body be thrown into Gehenna.
And if your right hand trips you up, cut it off and throw it away from you; because it is better for you that one of your parts be destroyed than that your whole body go off into Gehenna.
And it was said: "Whoever divorces his wife, let him give her a certificate of separation."
But I say to you that everyone who divorces his wife — apart from a matter of sexual immorality — makes her commit adultery; and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
Again, you heard that it was said to the ancients: "You shall not break an oath, but you shall pay to the Lord what you have sworn."
But I say to you: do not swear at all — not by heaven, because it is God's throne,
nor by the earth, because it is the footstool of his feet; nor towards Jerusalem, because it is the city of the great king;
nor are you to swear by your head, because you cannot make one hair white or black.
Let your word be "Yes, yes" — "No, no"; anything beyond these is from the evil one.
You heard that it was said: "An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth."
But I say to you: do not stand against the one who is evil. Instead, whoever slaps you on your right cheek, turn the other to him as well;
and to the one wanting to take you to court and take your tunic, let him have your cloak as well;
and whoever presses you into service for one mile, go with him two.
Give to the one who asks you, and do not turn away from the one wanting to borrow from you.
You heard that it was said: "You shall love your neighbour and hate your enemy."
But I say to you: love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who abuse you and persecute you —
so that you may become sons of your Father in the heavens; because he raises his sun on the evil and the good, and rains on the right and the wrong.
Because if you love those who love you, what wage do you have? Do not the tax collectors do the same?
And if you greet only your brothers and sisters, what more are you doing? Do not the gentiles do the same?
So you are to be complete, as your heavenly Father is complete.

matthew_6.t: Take care not to practise your rightness in front of people, to be seen by them; otherwise you have no wage with your Father in the heavens.

So when you give to the poor, do not sound a trumpet in front of you, the way the play-actors do in the synagogues and in the streets so that people will praise them. I tell you the truth: they have their wage in full.
But when you give to the poor, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,
so that your giving may be in secret. And your Father, who sees in secret, will pay you back.

And when you pray, you are not to be like the play-actors; because they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and on the street corners, so as to be visible to people. I tell you the truth: they have their wage in full.
But you, when you pray, go into your storeroom and shut your door and pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will pay you back.
And when you pray, do not babble on like the gentiles, because they think they will be heard for their many words.
So do not be like them; because God your Father knows what you need before you ask him.
So this is how you are to pray: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name;
let your kingdom come; let your will happen, as in heaven, so also on earth.
Give us today our daily bread;
and let go of our debts for us, as we ourselves have let go of our debtors;
and do not bring us into testing, but rescue us from evil. [Because yours is the kingdom and the power and the glory, into the ages. Amen.]
Because if you let go of people's missteps for them, your heavenly Father will also let go of yours;
but if you do not let go of people's missteps for them, neither will your Father let go of your missteps.
And when you fast, do not become gloomy-faced like the play-actors; because they disfigure their faces so that people will see them fasting. I tell you the truth: they have their wage in full.
But you, when you fast, put oil on your head and wash your face,
so that you do not appear to people to be fasting, but to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will pay you back.
Do not store up treasures for yourselves on the earth, where moth and eating destroy and where thieves dig through and steal;
but store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor eating destroys and where thieves do not dig through or steal.
Because where your treasure is, there your heart will be too.
The lamp of the body is the eye. So if your eye is healthy, your whole body will be full of light;
but if your eye is bad, your whole body will be full of darkness. So if the light in you is darkness — how great that darkness is.
Nobody can serve two masters as a slave; because either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will hold to one and think nothing of the other. You cannot serve God and mammon as slaves.

That is why I tell you: do not be anxious about your life — what you will eat or what you will drink — or about your body, what you will wear. Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothing?
Look at the birds of the sky: they do not sow or reap or gather into barns, and your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not worth more than they are?
And which of you by being anxious can add one forearm's length to his span?
And why are you anxious about clothing? Learn from the lilies of the field, how they grow: they do not labour or spin;
but I tell you that not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.
And if God clothes the grass of the field like this — here today and thrown into the oven tomorrow — will he not much more clothe you, you of little trust?
So do not be anxious, saying, "What will we eat?" or "What will we drink?" or "What will we wear?"
Because the gentiles chase after all these things; and your heavenly Father knows that you need all of them.
But seek first the kingdom of God and his rightness, and all these things will be added for you.
So do not be anxious about tomorrow, because tomorrow will be anxious about itself. Enough for the day is its own trouble.

matthew_7.t: Do not judge, so that you are not judged;
because with the judgement you judge, you will be judged; and with the measure you measure out, it will be measured to you.
And why do you look at the splinter in your brother's eye, but do not notice the beam in your own eye?
Or how will you say to your brother, "Let me get the splinter out of your eye" — and look, the beam is in your own eye?
Play-actor! First get the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly enough to get the splinter out of your brother's eye.
Do not give what is holy to the dogs, and do not throw your pearls in front of the pigs — or they will trample them with their feet, and turn and tear you to pieces.
Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
Because everyone who asks receives, and the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened.
Or which of you is the sort of person who, when his son asks him for bread, will hand him a stone?
Or if he asks for a fish, will he hand him a snake?
So if you, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in the heavens give good things to those who ask him!
So everything you want people to do for you, do the same for them; because this is the law and the prophets.
Go in through the narrow gate; because wide is the gate and broad is the road leading away into destruction, and many are the ones going in through it.
How narrow is the gate and how pressed the road leading away into life — and few are the ones finding it.
Watch out for the false prophets, who come to you in sheep's clothing but inside are ravenous wolves.
You will recognise them by their fruits. People do not gather grapes from thorn bushes, or figs from thistles, do they?
In the same way, every good tree produces good fruit, but the rotten tree produces bad fruit.
A good tree cannot produce bad fruit, nor a rotten tree produce good fruit.
Every tree not producing good fruit is cut down and thrown into fire.
So then, you will recognise them by their fruits.
Not everyone who says to me, "Lord, Lord," will go into the kingdom of heaven, but the one doing the will of my Father in the heavens.
Many will say to me on that day, "Lord, Lord — did we not prophesy in your name, and cast out demons in your name, and do many acts of power in your name?"
And then I will declare to them: "I never knew you. Go away from me, you who work lawlessness."
So everyone who hears these words of mine and does them will be like a sensible man who built his house on the rock.
And the rain came down and the rivers came and the winds blew and fell against that house, and it did not fall — because it had been founded on the rock.
And everyone who hears these words of mine and does not do them will be like a foolish man who built his house on the sand.
And the rain came down and the rivers came and the winds blew and struck against that house, and it fell — and its fall was great.
And it happened, when Jesus had finished these words, that the crowds were astounded at his teaching;
because he was teaching them like someone who has authority — and not like their teachers of the law.

matthew_8.t: When he came down from the mountain, large crowds followed him.
And look — a man with a skin disease came and bowed to him, saying, "Sir, if you are willing, you can make me clean."
And he stretched out his hand and touched him, saying, "I am willing — be clean." And at once his skin disease was cleansed.
And Jesus says to him, "See that you tell nobody; but go, show yourself to the priest and offer the gift that Moses commanded — as a testimony to them."
When he had entered Capernaum, a centurion came to him, appealing to him
and saying, "Sir, my boy is laid up at home, paralysed, in terrible torment."
And he says to him, "Am I to come and heal him?"
And the centurion answered, "Sir, I am not fit for you to come in under my roof; but only say the word, and my boy will be healed.
Because I too am a man placed under authority, with soldiers under me; and I say to this one, 'Go,' and he goes; and to another, 'Come,' and he comes; and to my slave, 'Do this,' and he does it."
Hearing this Jesus was amazed, and said to those following, "I tell you the truth: I have not found trust like this from anyone in Israel.
And I tell you that many will come from east and west and recline at table with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven,
but the sons of the kingdom will be thrown out into the outer darkness; there there will be weeping and grinding of teeth."
And Jesus said to the centurion, "Go; let it happen for you as you trusted." And the boy was healed in that hour.
And Jesus came into Peter's house and saw his mother-in-law laid up with a fever;
and he touched her hand, and the fever left her; and she got up and began to serve him.
When evening came they brought him many who were possessed by demons; and he drove out the spirits with a word, and healed everyone who was ill —
so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled: "He himself took our weaknesses and carried our diseases."
Seeing a crowd around him, Jesus gave orders to go off to the other side.
And one scribe came and said to him, "Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go."
And Jesus says to him, "The foxes have dens and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head."
And another of the disciples said to him, "Lord, let me first go and bury my father."
But Jesus says to him, "Follow me, and leave the dead to bury their own dead."
And when he got into the boat, his disciples followed him.
And look — a great shaking happened in the sea, so that the boat was being covered by the waves; but he was sleeping.
And the disciples came and woke him, saying, "Lord, save us — we are perishing!"
And he says to them, "Why are you cowards, you of little trust?" Then he got up and rebuked the winds and the sea, and there was a great calm.
And the people were amazed, saying, "What sort of being is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him?"
And when he came to the other side, to the region of the Gadarenes, two demon-possessed men met him, coming out of the tombs — so violent that nobody was strong enough to pass by along that road.
And look — they screamed, saying, "What have we to do with you, son of God? Have you come here to torment us before the time?"
Now there was a herd of many pigs feeding, some distance from them.
And the demons appealed to him, saying, "If you drive us out, send us into the herd of pigs."
And he said to them, "Go." And they came out and went off into the pigs; and look — the whole herd rushed down the cliff into the sea and died in the waters.
And the herdsmen fled, and went off into the city and reported everything, including what had happened to the demon-possessed men.
And look — the whole city came out to meet Jesus; and when they saw him they appealed to him to move on from their district.

matthew_9.t: And he got into a boat and crossed over and came to his own town.
And look — they were bringing him a paralysed man laid on a bed. And seeing their trust, Jesus said to the paralysed man, "Take heart, child; your sins are released."
And look — some of the scribes said among themselves, "This man is speaking blasphemy."
And seeing their thoughts, Jesus said, "Why are you thinking evil things in your hearts?
Because which is easier — to say, 'Your sins are released,' or to say, 'Get up and walk'?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on the earth to release sins" — then he says to the paralysed man, "Get up, pick up your bed and go to your house."
And he got up and went off to his house.
Seeing it, the crowds were afraid, and they gave glory to God, who had given such authority to people.
And as Jesus was passing on from there he saw a man sitting at the tax booth, called Matthew, and he says to him, "Follow me." And he stood up and followed him.
And it happened, as he was reclining at table in the house — look, many tax collectors and sinners came and were reclining with Jesus and his disciples.
And seeing it, the Pharisees said to his disciples, "Why does your teacher eat with the tax collectors and sinners?"
But hearing it he said to them, "Those who are strong have no need of a doctor — but those who are ill do.
But go and learn what this means: 'I want mercy and not sacrifice.' Because I did not come to call the right but sinners — to a change of mind."
Then John's disciples come to him, saying, "Why do we and the Pharisees fast a great deal, but your disciples do not fast?"
And Jesus said to them, "Can the sons of the bridal chamber mourn while the bridegroom is with them? But days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast.
Nobody puts a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment; because the patch pulls away from the garment, and a worse tear happens.
Nor do they put new wine into old skins; otherwise the skins burst, and the wine is spilled and the skins are destroyed. Instead they put new wine into fresh skins, and both are preserved together.
While he was saying these things to them — look, a ruler came and bowed to him, saying, "My daughter has just died; but come and lay your hand on her, and she will live."
And Jesus got up and followed him — and so did his disciples.
And look — a woman who had been bleeding for twelve years came up behind him and touched the tassel of his cloak;
because she was saying to herself, "If I only touch his cloak, I will be saved."
But Jesus turned, and seeing her he said, "Take heart, daughter; your trust has saved you." And the woman was saved from that hour.
And Jesus came into the ruler's house and saw the flute-players and the crowd making a commotion,
and he said, "Get out — because the girl did not die, she is sleeping." And they laughed at him.
But when the crowd had been put out, he went in and took hold of her hand, and the girl was raised.
And this report went out into that whole region.
And as Jesus was passing on from there, two blind men followed him, shouting and saying, "Have mercy on us, son of David!"
And when he came into the house, the blind men came to him, and Jesus says to them, "Do you trust that I am able to do this?" They say to him, "Yes, Lord."
Then he touched their eyes, saying, "According to your trust let it happen to you."
And their eyes were opened. And Jesus warned them sternly, saying, "See that nobody knows."
But they went out and spread the news about him through that whole region.
As they were going out — look, they brought him a man who could not speak, possessed by a demon.
And when the demon had been driven out, the man who had not been able to speak spoke. And the crowds were amazed, saying, "Nothing like this has ever appeared in Israel."
But the Pharisees were saying, "He drives out the demons by the ruler of the demons."
And Jesus went round all the towns and the villages, teaching in their synagogues and proclaiming the good news of the kingdom and healing every disease and every weakness.
Seeing the crowds, he was moved with compassion for them, because they were harassed and thrown down like sheep that have no shepherd.
Then he says to his disciples, "The harvest is large, but the workers are few;
so ask the Lord of the harvest to throw out workers into his harvest."

matthew_10.t: He called his twelve disciples to him and gave them authority over unclean spirits, to drive them out, and to heal every disease and every sickness.
These are the names of the twelve apostles: first, Simon (the one called Peter) and Andrew his brother; James son of Zebedee and John his brother;
Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James son of Alphaeus, and Lebbaeus who was surnamed Thaddaeus;
Simon the Cananaean, and Judas Iscariot — the one who also handed him over.
These twelve Jesus sent out, instructing them: 'Do not go off on a road of the nations, and do not enter a town of Samaritans.
Go instead to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
As you go, proclaim: 'The kingdom of heaven has come near.'
Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse those with skin disease, drive out demons. You received without payment; give without payment.
Do not acquire gold or silver or copper for your belts,
no bag for the road, no second tunic, no sandals, no staff — for the worker deserves his food.
Whatever town or village you enter, find out who in it is worthy, and stay there until you leave.
As you enter the house, greet it.
If the house is worthy, let your peace come on it; if it is not worthy, let your peace return to you.
And if anyone will not welcome you or listen to your words, as you leave that house or town, shake the dust off your feet.
I tell you the truth: it will be more bearable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgement than for that town.
Look — I am sending you out like sheep among wolves. So be shrewd as snakes and unmixed as doves.
Be on guard against people: they will hand you over to councils and flog you in their synagogues,
and you will be brought before governors and kings because of me, as a testimony to them and to the nations.
When they hand you over, do not worry about how or what you are to say; it will be given to you in that hour what to say.
For it is not you speaking, but the Spirit of your Father speaking in you.
Brother will hand over brother to death, and a father his child; children will rise against parents and put them to death.
You will be hated by everyone because of my name; but the one who endures to the end — this one will be saved.
When they persecute you in one town, flee to the next. I tell you the truth: you will not have gone through the towns of Israel before the Son of Man comes.
A disciple is not above the teacher, nor a slave above his master.
It is enough for the disciple to become like his teacher, and the slave like his master. If they called the head of the house Beelzeboul, how much more the members of his household!
So do not be afraid of them. Nothing is covered that will not be uncovered, and nothing hidden that will not be known.
What I tell you in the dark, say in the light; and what you hear in your ear, proclaim from the rooftops.
Do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Fear instead the one who can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.
Aren't two sparrows sold for a penny? And not one of them will fall to the ground apart from your Father.
As for you — even the hairs of your head are all numbered.
So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.
So everyone who acknowledges me before people, I too will acknowledge before my Father in the heavens;
But whoever disowns me before people, I too will disown before my Father in the heavens.
Do not think I came to bring peace on the earth. I did not come to bring peace, but a sword.
For I came to divide a man against his father, a daughter against her mother, a bride against her mother-in-law;
and a person's enemies will be the members of his own household.
Whoever loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me; and whoever loves son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me;
and whoever does not take up his cross and follow behind me is not worthy of me.
Whoever finds his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life for my sake will find it.
Whoever welcomes you welcomes me, and whoever welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me.
Whoever welcomes a prophet because he is a prophet will receive a prophet's wage, and whoever welcomes an upright person because he is upright will receive an upright person's wage.
And whoever gives even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones because he is a disciple — I tell you the truth, he will certainly not lose his wage.

matthew_11.t: When Jesus had finished instructing his twelve disciples, he moved on from there to teach and proclaim in their towns.
When John heard in prison what the Christ was doing, he sent word through his disciples
and asked him, 'Are you the one who is coming, or should we expect someone else?'
Jesus answered them: 'Go and report to John what you hear and see:
the blind see again, the lame walk, those with skin disease are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor have good news announced to them.
And blessed is anyone who is not tripped up by me.
As they were leaving, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: 'What did you go out into the wilderness to look at? A reed shaken by the wind?
Then what did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft clothes? Look — those who wear soft clothes are in kings' houses.
Then what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
This is the one about whom it is written: 'Look, I am sending my messenger ahead of you, who will prepare your way before you.'
I tell you the truth: among those born of women no one greater than John the Baptist has arisen; yet the lesser one in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.
From the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffers violence, and violent people are seizing it.
For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John.
And if you are willing to accept it, he is Elijah, the one who is to come.
Whoever has ears, let them hear.
To what shall I compare this generation? It is like children sitting in the marketplaces who call out to the others,
'We played the flute for you and you did not dance; we sang a lament and you did not beat your breasts.'
For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, 'He has a demon.'
The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, 'Look — a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners.' And wisdom was vindicated by her works.
Then he began to reproach the towns in which most of his acts of power had happened, because they did not change their minds:
Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! Because if the acts of power that happened in you had happened in Tyre and Sidon, they would have changed their minds long ago, in sackcloth and ashes.
But I tell you: it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgement than for you.
And you, Capernaum — will you be lifted up to heaven? You will go down to Hades. Because if the acts of power that happened in you had happened in Sodom, it would have remained to this day.
But I tell you that it will be more bearable for the land of Sodom on the day of judgement than for you.
At that time Jesus responded: 'I acknowledge you publicly, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you hid these things from the wise and the clever and revealed them to infants.
Yes, Father, because this is how it pleased you.

Everything has been handed over to me by my Father; and no one fully knows the Son except the Father, and no one fully knows the Father except the Son and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal him.
Come to me, all who are labouring and loaded down, and I will give you rest.
Take my yoke on you and learn from me, because I am gentle and lowly in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.
For my yoke is kind and my load is light.

matthew_12.t: At that time Jesus went through the grainfields on the sabbath. His disciples were hungry and began to pluck heads of grain and eat them.
When the Pharisees saw it they said to him, 'Look — your disciples are doing what is not permitted on a sabbath.'
He said to them, 'Have you not read what David did when he and those with him were hungry?
How he entered the house of God and they ate the bread of the Presence, which was not permitted for him to eat, nor for those with him, but only for the priests?
Or have you not read in the law that on the sabbaths the priests in the temple profane the sabbath and are not guilty?
But I tell you that something greater than the temple is here.
If you had known what this means — 'I want mercy and not sacrifice' — you would not have condemned the guiltless.
For the Son of Man is lord even of the sabbath.
He moved on from there and went into their synagogue.
And there was a man there with a withered hand. They questioned him: 'Is it permitted to heal on the sabbaths?' — so that they could bring a charge against him.
He said to them, 'Which one of you who has a single sheep, if it falls into a pit on the sabbath, will not take hold of it and lift it out?
How much more valuable is a person than a sheep! So it is permitted to do good on the sabbaths.
Then he says to the man, 'Stretch out your hand.' He stretched it out, and it was restored, healthy as the other.
The Pharisees went out and took counsel against him — how they might destroy him.
Knowing this, Jesus withdrew from there. Large crowds followed him, and he healed them all,
and he warned them sharply not to make him known,
so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled:
'Look — my servant, whom I chose; my beloved, in whom my soul was well pleased. I will put my Spirit on him, and he will announce judgement to the nations.
He will not quarrel or shout, and no one will hear his voice in the streets.
A bruised reed he will not break, and a smouldering wick he will not put out, until he brings judgement through to victory.
And in his name the nations will hope.
Then a man possessed by a demon, blind and mute, was brought to him, and he healed him, so that the mute man could both speak and see.
All the crowds were beside themselves and said, 'This isn't the Son of David, is it?'
But when the Pharisees heard it they said, 'This man does not drive out the demons except by Beelzeboul, the ruler of the demons.'
Knowing their thoughts, he said to them: 'Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and no city or house divided against itself will stand.
And if the Adversary drives out the Adversary, he is divided against himself; so how will his kingdom stand?
And if I drive out the demons by Beelzeboul, by whom do your sons drive them out? For that reason they will be your judges.
But if I drive out the demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has arrived upon you.
Or how can anyone enter the strong man's house and seize his goods unless he first ties up the strong man? Then he will plunder his house.
Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.
For this reason I tell you: every sin and slander will be released for people, but the slander of the Spirit will not be released.

And whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man, it will be released for him; but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit, it will not be released for him — not in this present age, nor in the one to come.
Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree rotten and its fruit rotten; for the tree is known by its fruit.
Offspring of vipers! How can you speak good things when you are evil? For the mouth speaks out of the overflow of the heart.
The good person brings good things out of the good treasure of the heart, and the evil person brings evil things out of the evil treasure.
I tell you that people will give an account on the day of judgement for every idle word they speak.
For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.
Then some of the teachers of the law and Pharisees answered him: 'Teacher, we want to see a sign from you.'
He answered them: 'An evil and adulterous generation hunts for a sign, and no sign will be given it except the sign of Jonah the prophet.
For just as Jonah was in the belly of the sea-monster three days and three nights, so the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth three days and three nights.
Ninevite men will rise at the judgement with this generation and condemn it, because they changed their minds at Jonah's proclamation — and look, something greater than Jonah is here.

A queen of the south will be raised at the judgement with this generation and will condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon's wisdom — and look, something greater than Solomon is here.
When the unclean spirit goes out of a person, it passes through waterless places looking for rest and does not find it.
Then it says, 'I will return to my house, which I left.' And when it comes it finds it standing idle, swept and put in order.

Then it goes and takes with it seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they go in and settle there; and that person's last state becomes worse than the first. So it will be for this evil generation too.
While he was still speaking to the crowds, his mother and his brothers were standing outside, wanting to speak with him.
Someone said to him, 'Look — your mother and your brothers are standing outside, wanting to speak with you.'
He answered the one who told him, 'Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?'
And stretching out his hand towards his disciples he said, 'Look — my mother and my brothers.'
For whoever does the will of my Father in the heavens — this one is my brother and sister and mother.

matthew_13.t: That day Jesus went out of the house and sat down beside the sea.
Large crowds gathered to him, so he got into a boat and sat there, and the whole crowd stood on the shore.
And he spoke to them at length in parables: 'Look — the sower went out to sow.
And as he sowed, some fell along the path, and the birds came and ate it up.
Other seed fell on rocky ground where it did not have much soil, and it sprang up at once because the soil was not deep.
But when the sun rose it was scorched, and because it had no root it withered.
Other seed fell among the thorns, and the thorns came up and choked it.
And other seed fell on the good soil and produced fruit — one a hundred, another sixty, another thirty.
Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear.
The disciples came and said to him, 'Why do you speak to them in parables?'
He answered them: 'Because it has been given to you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it has not been given.
For whoever has, more will be given to him and he will have in abundance; but whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.
This is why I speak to them in parables: because seeing they do not see, and hearing they do not hear and do not understand.
And in them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled, which says: 'You will hear and hear, and never understand; and you will look and look, and never see.

For this people's heart has grown fat; they have heard heavily with their ears, and they have shut their eyes — so that they might not see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their heart and turn, and I would heal them.'
But blessed are your eyes, because they see, and your ears, because they hear.
I tell you the truth: many prophets and upright people longed to see what you see and did not see it, and to hear what you hear and did not hear it.
So listen to the parable of the sower:
When anyone hears the word of the kingdom and does not understand it, the evil one comes and snatches away what was sown in his heart. This is the one sown along the path.
The one sown on rocky ground is the person who hears the word and immediately receives it with joy,
but he has no root in himself and lasts only a season; when trouble or persecution comes because of the word, he is immediately tripped up.
The one sown among the thorns is the person who hears the word, but the worry of this age and the deceit of wealth choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
But the one sown on the good soil is the person who hears the word and understands it, who then bears fruit and produces — one a hundred, another sixty, another thirty.
He put another parable before them: 'The kingdom of heaven has become like a man who sowed good seed in his field.
But while people were sleeping, his enemy came and sowed darnel among the wheat, and went away.
When the blade sprouted and produced fruit, then the darnel appeared as well.
The householder's slaves came and said to him, 'Master, didn't you sow good seed in your field? Where then did the darnel come from?'
He said to them, 'An enemy — a person — did this.' The slaves say to him, 'Do you want us to go and gather them?'
He says, 'No — in gathering the darnel you might uproot the wheat along with it.
Let both grow together until the harvest; and at harvest time I will tell the reapers: gather the darnel first and tie it in bundles to burn it, but bring the wheat into my barn.'
He put another parable before them: 'The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed which a man took and sowed in his field.
It is the smallest of all the seeds, but when it has grown it is the largest of the garden plants and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the sky come and nest in its branches.'
He told them another parable: 'The kingdom of heaven is like yeast which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour until the whole batch was leavened.'
Jesus said all these things to the crowds in parables, and he said nothing to them without a parable,
so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled: 'I will open my mouth in parables; I will pour out things hidden from the foundation of the world.'
Then he left the crowds and went into the house. His disciples came to him and said, 'Explain to us the parable of the darnel in the field.'
He answered them: 'The one sowing the good seed is the Son of Man.
The field is the world; the good seed are the children of the kingdom; the darnel are the children of the evil one;
the enemy who sowed them is the accuser; the harvest is the completion of the age; and the reapers are angels.
So just as the darnel is gathered and burned with fire, so it will be at the completion of this age.
The Son of Man will send out his angels, and they will gather out of his kingdom everything that trips people up, and those who do lawlessness,
and will throw them into the furnace of fire. There will be weeping there, and grinding of teeth.
Then the upright will shine out like the sun in their Father's kingdom. Whoever has ears, let them hear.
The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field, which a man found and hid; and in his joy he goes and sells everything he has and buys that field.
Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant looking for fine pearls.
When he found one very valuable pearl, he went away and sold everything he had and bought it.
Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a dragnet thrown into the sea, gathering from every kind;
when it was full they hauled it up on the shore, and they sat down and collected the good into containers, but the rotten they threw outside.
So it will be at the completion of the age: the angels will go out and separate the evil from among the upright,
and will throw them into the furnace of fire. There will be weeping there, and grinding of teeth.
Jesus says to them, 'Have you understood all these things?' They say to him, 'Yes.'
He said to them: 'For this reason every teacher of the law who has been trained as a disciple for the kingdom of heaven is like a householder who brings out of his treasure things new and old.'
When Jesus had finished these parables, he moved on from there,
and coming to his home town he taught them in their synagogue, so that they were astounded and said, 'Where did this man get this wisdom and these acts of power?
Isn't this the carpenter's son? Isn't his mother called Mary, and his brothers James and Joseph and Simon and Judas?
And aren't his sisters all here with us? So where did this man get all this?'
And they were tripped up by him. But Jesus said to them, 'A prophet is not without honour except in his home town and in his own household.'
And he did not do many acts of power there, because of their lack of trust.

matthew_14.t: At that time Herod the tetrarch heard the report about Jesus
and said to his attendants, 'This is John the Baptist. He has been raised from the dead, and that is why these powers are at work in him.'
For Herod had seized John, tied him up and put him away in prison, because of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip.
For John kept telling him, 'It is not permitted for you to have her.'
And though he wanted to kill him, he feared the crowd, because they held him to be a prophet.
But when Herod's birthday came, the daughter of Herodias danced in front of them and pleased Herod,
so he promised on oath to give her whatever she asked.
Prompted by her mother, she says, 'Give me the head of John the Baptist here, on a platter.'
The king was grieved, but because of the oaths and those reclining at table with him, he ordered it to be given,
and he sent and had John beheaded in the prison.
His head was brought on a platter and given to the girl, and she brought it to her mother.
His disciples came and took the corpse and buried him; then they went and reported it to Jesus.
When Jesus heard it he withdrew from there by boat to a deserted place by himself. But when the crowds heard, they followed him on foot from the towns.
When he came out he saw a large crowd, and he was moved with compassion for them and healed their sick.
When evening came the disciples came to him and said, 'The place is deserted and the hour has already passed. Send the crowds away so they can go into the villages and buy food for themselves.'
But Jesus said to them, 'They do not need to go away. You give them something to eat.'
They say to him, 'We have nothing here except five loaves and two fish.'
He said, 'Bring them here to me.'

He ordered the crowds to recline on the grass, and taking the five loaves and the two fish he looked up to heaven, spoke a blessing, and broke the loaves and gave them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the crowds.
They all ate and were filled, and they took up what was left over of the broken pieces — twelve baskets full.
Those eating were about five thousand men, besides women and children.
At once he made the disciples get into the boat and go ahead of him to the other side, while he released the crowds.
After releasing the crowds he went up the mountain by himself to pray. When evening came he was there alone,
but the boat was already many stadia away from the land, battered by the waves, because the wind was against them.
In the fourth watch of the night he came to them, walking on the sea.
When the disciples saw him walking on the sea they were terrified and said, 'It is a phantom!' — and they cried out in fear.
But at once Jesus spoke to them: 'Take courage — I am. Do not be afraid.'
Peter answered him, 'Lord, if it is you, order me to come to you on the waters.'
He said, 'Come.' And Peter got down from the boat and walked on the waters and came towards Jesus.
But seeing the strong wind he was afraid, and beginning to sink he cried out, 'Lord, save me!'
At once Jesus stretched out his hand, took hold of him, and says to him, 'You of little trust — why did you doubt?'
And when they got into the boat the wind dropped.
Those in the boat bowed down before him and said, 'Truly you are God's Son.'
And crossing over, they came to land at Gennesaret.
When the men of that place recognised him, they sent word into all the surrounding region and brought him everyone who was ill,
and they begged him to let them just touch the fringe of his cloak; and all who touched it were brought safely through.

matthew_15.t: Then Pharisees and teachers of the law from Jerusalem come to Jesus and say,
'Why do your disciples step over the tradition of the elders? For they do not wash their hands when they eat bread.'
He answered them, 'And why do you step over the command of God because of your tradition?
For God said: 'Honour your father and your mother', and 'Whoever speaks evil of father or mother must certainly die.'
But you say: whoever tells his father or mother, 'Whatever help you might have had from me is a gift to God' —
then he need not honour his father or his mother. And so you have made the word of God void because of your tradition.
Hypocrites! Isaiah prophesied well about you when he said:
'This people honours me with their lips, but their heart is far away from me;
and they revere me in vain, teaching as teachings the commands of people.'
He called the crowd to him and said to them, 'Listen and understand.
It is not what goes into the mouth that makes a person common; it is what comes out of the mouth that makes a person common.'
Then the disciples came and say to him, 'Do you know that the Pharisees were tripped up when they heard that saying?'
He answered: 'Every plant that my heavenly Father did not plant will be pulled up by the roots.
Leave them. They are blind guides of the blind. And if a blind person guides a blind person, both will fall into a pit.'
Peter answered him, 'Explain this parable to us.'
He said, 'Are you still without understanding too?
Do you not grasp that everything going into the mouth passes into the belly and is expelled into the latrine?
But what comes out of the mouth comes out of the heart, and those things make a person common.
For out of the heart come evil thoughts — murders, adulteries, sexual immoralities, thefts, false testimonies, slanders.
These are the things that make a person common; but eating with unwashed hands does not make a person common.'
Jesus left there and withdrew to the region of Tyre and Sidon.
And a Canaanite woman from that territory came out and kept crying to him, 'Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David! My daughter is badly possessed by a demon.'
But he did not answer her a word. And his disciples came and asked him, 'Send her away, because she keeps crying out behind us.'
He answered, 'I was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.'
But she came and bowed down before him, saying, 'Lord, help me.'
He answered, 'It is not right to take the children's bread and throw it to the little dogs.'
She said, 'Yes, Lord — and yet the little dogs do eat the crumbs that fall from their masters' table.'
Then Jesus answered her, 'Woman, your trust is great. Let it happen for you as you want.' And her daughter was healed from that hour.
Jesus moved on from there and went along the Sea of Galilee, and he went up the mountain and sat there.
Large crowds came to him bringing with them the lame, the blind, the crippled, the mute, and many others, and they put them down at his feet; and he healed them,
so that the crowd was amazed to see the mute speaking, the crippled made whole, the lame walking and the blind seeing. And they glorified the God of Israel.

Jesus called his disciples to him and said, 'I am moved with compassion for the crowd, because they have already stayed with me three days and have nothing to eat. And I do not want to send them away hungry, in case they collapse on the way.'
The disciples say to him, 'Where in a deserted place could we get enough loaves to fill such a crowd?'
Jesus says to them, 'How many loaves do you have?' They said, 'Seven — and a few small fish.'
And he instructed the crowd to sit down on the ground,
and he took the seven loaves and the fish, gave thanks, broke them and kept giving them to his disciples, and the disciples gave them to the crowds.
They all ate and were filled, and they took up what was left over of the broken pieces — seven hampers full.
Those eating were four thousand men, besides women and children.
And after releasing the crowds he got into the boat and went to the region of Magadan.

matthew_16.t: The Pharisees and Sadducees came and, to test him, asked him to show them a sign from heaven.
He answered them: 'When evening comes you say, "Fair weather — the sky is red."
And in the morning, "Storm today — the sky is red and lowering." You know how to judge the face of the sky, but you cannot judge the signs of the times.
An evil and adulterous generation hunts for a sign, and no sign will be given it except the sign of Jonah.' And he left them and went away.
When the disciples came to the other side, they had forgotten to take bread.
Jesus said to them, 'Watch out, and be on guard against the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.'
They were reasoning among themselves and saying, 'It is because we took no bread.'
Knowing this, Jesus said to them, 'Why are you reasoning among yourselves, you of little trust, that you have no bread?
Do you not yet grasp it, or remember the five loaves of the five thousand, and how many baskets you took up?
Or the seven loaves of the four thousand, and how many hampers you took up?
How do you not grasp that I was not speaking to you about bread? But be on guard against the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.'
Then they understood that he had not told them to be on guard against the yeast of bread, but against the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
When Jesus came into the region of Caesarea Philippi he asked his disciples, 'Who do people say the Son of Man is?'
They said, 'Some say John the Baptist; others Elijah; others Jeremiah or one of the prophets.'
He says to them, 'But you — who do you say that I am?'
Simon Peter answered, 'You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.'
Jesus answered him, 'Blessed are you, Simon son of Jonah, because flesh and blood did not reveal this to you, but my Father in the heavens.
And I tell you: you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not overpower it.
I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven; and whatever you bind on earth will have been bound in the heavens, and whatever you loose on earth will have been loosed in the heavens.
Then he ordered the disciples to tell no one that he was the Christ.

From that time Jesus Christ began to show his disciples that he must go to Jerusalem and suffer many things from the elders and chief priests and teachers of the law, and be killed, and on the third day be raised.
Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him: 'Mercy on you, Lord! This will never happen to you.'
But he turned and said to Peter, 'Get behind me, Adversary. You are a trap to me, because you are not minding the things of God but the things of people.'
Then Jesus said to his disciples, 'If anyone wants to come after me, let him disown himself and take up his cross and follow me.
For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life for my sake will find it.
For what will it profit a person to gain the whole world and forfeit his life? Or what will a person give in exchange for his life?
For the Son of Man is about to come in his Father's glory with his angels, and then he will repay each one according to what he has done.
I tell you the truth: there are some standing here who will certainly not taste death until they see the Son of Man coming in his kingdom.

matthew_17.t: Six days later Jesus takes Peter and James and John his brother and leads them up a high mountain by themselves.
And he was transformed in front of them: his face shone like the sun, and his clothes became white as the light.
And Moses and Elijah appeared to them, talking with him.
Peter answered and said to Jesus, 'Lord, it is good for us to be here. If you want, I will make three shelters here — one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.'
While he was still speaking, a bright cloud overshadowed them, and a voice out of the cloud said: 'This is my Son, the beloved, in whom I was well pleased. Listen to him.'
When the disciples heard it they fell on their faces and were terrified.
Jesus came and touched them and said, 'Get up, and do not be afraid.'
And lifting their eyes they saw no one except Jesus alone.
As they were coming down the mountain, Jesus commanded them: 'Tell no one the vision until the Son of Man has been raised from the dead.'
And the disciples asked him, 'Why then do the teachers of the law say that Elijah must come first?'
He answered them, 'Elijah does come first, and he will restore all things.
But I tell you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognise him but did to him whatever they wanted. So too the Son of Man is about to suffer at their hands.'
Then the disciples understood that he had spoken to them about John the Baptist.
When they came to the crowd, a man came to him, kneeling before him
and saying, 'Lord, have mercy on my son, because he is moonstruck and suffers badly: he often falls into the fire, and often into the water.
I brought him to your disciples, and they could not heal him.'
Jesus answered, 'You untrusting and twisted generation — how long will I be with you? How long will I put up with you? Bring him here to me.'
And Jesus rebuked it, and the demon came out of him, and the boy was healed from that hour.
Then the disciples came to Jesus privately and said, 'Why could we not drive it out?'

He says to them, 'Because of your little trust. For I tell you the truth: if you have trust like a mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, "Move from here to there", and it will move — and nothing will be impossible for you.'
[But this kind does not go out except by prayer and fasting.]
As they were gathering in Galilee, Jesus said to them, 'The Son of Man is about to be handed over into human hands,
and they will kill him, and on the third day he will be raised.' And they were deeply grieved.
When they came to Capernaum, the collectors of the two-drachma tax came to Peter and said, 'Doesn't your teacher pay the two drachmas?'
He says, 'Yes.' And when he came into the house, Jesus spoke first: 'What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth take duties or poll-tax — from their own sons, or from others?'
When he said, 'From others', Jesus said to him, 'Then the sons are free.
But so that we do not trip them up, go to the sea, throw in a hook, and take the first fish that comes up. Open its mouth and you will find a stater. Take it and give it to them for me and you.'

matthew_18.t: At that hour the disciples came to Jesus and said, 'Who then is greatest in the kingdom of heaven?'
He called a child to him and stood it in the middle of them
and said, 'I tell you the truth: unless you turn and become like children, you will certainly not enter the kingdom of heaven.
So whoever lowers himself like this child — this one is the greater in the kingdom of heaven.
And whoever welcomes one child like this in my name welcomes me.
But whoever trips up one of these little ones who trust in me — it would be better for him to have a donkey's millstone hung round his neck and to be drowned in the open sea.
Woe to the world because of the things that trip people up. It is necessary that the trip-ups come, but woe to that person through whom the trip-up comes.

If your hand or your foot trips you up, cut it off and throw it away from you. It is better for you to enter life maimed or lame than to have two hands or two feet and be thrown into the eternal fire.
And if your eye trips you up, take it out and throw it away from you. It is better for you to enter life one-eyed than to have two eyes and be thrown into the Gehenna of fire.
See that you do not look down on one of these little ones. For I tell you that their angels in the heavens continually see the face of my Father in the heavens.
[For the Son of Man came to save what was lost.]
What do you think? If a man has a hundred sheep and one of them goes astray, will he not leave the ninety-nine on the mountains and go looking for the one that has gone astray?
And if he happens to find it, I tell you the truth: he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine that were not led astray.
In the same way, it is not the will before your Father in the heavens that one of these little ones should be lost.
If your brother sins against you, go and put it to him between you and him alone. If he listens to you, you have gained your brother.
But if he does not listen, take one or two others with you, so that by the mouth of two or three witnesses every matter may be established.
If he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the community. And if he refuses to listen even to the community, let him be to you as the outsider and the tax collector.
I tell you the truth: whatever you bind on earth will have been bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will have been loosed in heaven.
Again I tell you the truth: if two of you agree on earth about any matter they ask for, it will come about for them from my Father in the heavens.
For where two or three have been gathered in my name, there I am in the middle of them.
Then Peter came and said to him, 'Lord, how many times will my brother sin against me and I forgive him? As many as seven times?'
Jesus says to him, 'I do not say to you as many as seven times, but as many as seventy-seven times.'
For this reason the kingdom of heaven has become like a king who wanted to settle accounts with his slaves.
When he had begun the settlement, one debtor of ten thousand talents was brought to him.
Since he did not have the means to repay, the master ordered him to be sold, and his wife and his children and everything he had, and repayment to be made.
So the slave fell down and was bowing before him, saying, 'Be patient with me, and I will repay you everything.'
The master of that slave was moved with compassion, released him, and cancelled the loan for him.
But that slave went out and found one of his fellow slaves who owed him a hundred denarii, and he seized him and was throttling him, saying, 'Pay back whatever you owe.'
So his fellow slave fell at his feet and begged him, 'Be patient with me, and I will repay you.'
But he was unwilling; instead he went off and threw him into prison until he should repay what was owed.
When his fellow slaves saw what had happened they were deeply grieved, and they went and reported to their master everything that had happened.
Then his master called him in and says to him, 'Evil slave! I cancelled that whole debt for you because you begged me.
Should you not also have had mercy on your fellow slave, as I also had mercy on you?'
And his master was angry and handed him over to the torturers until he should repay everything that was owed him.
So my heavenly Father will do to you too, unless each of you releases his brother from your hearts.

matthew_19.t: When Jesus had finished saying these things, he left Galilee and went into the territory of Judea across the Jordan.
Large crowds followed him, and he healed them there.
Some Pharisees came up to test him. They asked, "Is a man allowed to divorce his wife for any reason at all?"
He answered, "Haven't you read that the one who created them from the beginning made them male and female,
and said, 'This is why a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two will become one flesh'?
so they are no longer two but one flesh. What God has yoked together, then, let no one separate."
They said to him, "Then why did Moses command a man to give her a certificate of divorce and send her away?"
He said to them, "Moses allowed you to divorce your wives because your hearts are hard. It was not like that from the beginning.
And I tell you: whoever divorces his wife — except on the ground of sexual immorality — and marries another commits adultery. And the man who marries a divorced woman commits adultery."
His disciples said to him, "If that is how it stands between a man and his wife, it is better not to marry."
He said to them, "Not everyone can make room for this saying, only those to whom it has been given.

For there are eunuchs who were born that way from their mother's womb; there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by others; and there are eunuchs who have made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. Let the one who can make room for this make room for it."
Then children were brought to him so that he could lay his hands on them and pray, and the disciples scolded them.
But Jesus said, "Let the children be, and do not stop them coming to me — the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these."
And he laid his hands on them and went on from there.
And look — a man came up to him and said, "Good teacher, what good thing must I do to have eternal life?"
He said to him, "Why do you ask me about what is good? There is one who is good. But if you want to enter life, keep the commandments."
"Which ones?" he asked. Jesus said, "You shall not murder, you shall not commit adultery, you shall not steal, you shall not give false testimony,
honour your father and mother, and you shall love your neighbour as yourself."
The young man said to him, "I have kept all these. What am I still missing?"
Jesus said to him, "If you want to be complete, go, sell what belongs to you and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow me."
When the young man heard this he went away grieving, because he had many possessions.
Jesus said to his disciples, "I tell you the truth: it will be hard for a rich person to enter the kingdom of heaven.
Again I tell you: it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God."
When the disciples heard it they were astounded, and said, "Then who can be saved?"
Jesus looked straight at them and said, "With people this is impossible, but with God everything is possible."
Then Peter answered him, "Look — we have left everything and followed you. So what will there be for us?"

Jesus said to them, "I tell you the truth: at the renewal of all things, when the Son of Man sits on the throne of his glory, you who have followed me will also sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
And everyone who has left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or fields for the sake of my name will receive a hundred times as much, and will inherit eternal life.
But many who are first will be last, and the last first.

matthew_20.t: For the kingdom of heaven is like a landowner who went out at daybreak to hire workers for his vineyard.
He agreed with the workers on a denarius for the day and sent them into his vineyard.
About nine in the morning he went out and saw others standing idle in the marketplace,
and he said to them, "You go into the vineyard too, and I will give you whatever is right."
And they went. He went out again about noon and about three in the afternoon and did the same.
About five he went out and found others standing there, and he said to them, "Why have you been standing here idle all day?"
They said to him, "Because no one hired us." He said to them, "You go into the vineyard too, and you will get whatever is right."
When evening came, the owner of the vineyard said to his foreman, "Call the workers and pay them their wage, beginning with the last and going to the first."
Those hired about five came and each received a denarius.
When the first came, they assumed they would get more; and they too each received a denarius.
When they got it, they began to grumble against the landowner,
saying, "These last ones worked one hour, and you have made them equal to us — and we bore the day's burden and the scorching heat!"
But he answered one of them, "Friend, I am doing you no wrong. Didn't you agree with me on a denarius?
Take what is yours and go. I choose to give this last man the same as you.
Am I not allowed to do what I want with what is mine? Or is your eye evil because I am good?"
So the last will be first, and the first last. For many are called, but few are chosen.
As Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he took the twelve disciples aside on the road and said to them,
"Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the teachers of the law. They will condemn him to death,
and they will hand him over to the nations to be mocked and flogged and crucified — and on the third day he will be raised."
Then the mother of Zebedee's sons came to him with her sons, kneeling down and asking something of him.
He said to her, "What do you want?" She said to him, "Say that these two sons of mine may sit, one at your right and one at your left, in your kingdom."
Jesus answered, "You do not know what you are asking. Can you drink the cup I am about to drink, and be baptised with the baptism I am baptised with?" They said to him, "We can."

He said to them, "You will drink my cup and be baptised with the baptism I am baptised with. But to sit at my right and at my left is not mine to give; it is for those for whom it has been prepared by my Father."
When the ten heard it, they were indignant at the two brothers.
Jesus called them to him and said, "You know that the rulers of the nations lord it over them, and their great ones throw their weight about over them.
It will not be like that among you. Whoever wants to become great among you must be the one who serves you,
and whoever wants to be first among you must be your slave —
just as the Son of Man did not come to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many."
As they were leaving Jericho, a large crowd followed him.
And look — two blind men were sitting by the road. When they heard that Jesus was passing by, they shouted, "Have mercy on us, Lord Jesus, Son of David!"
The crowd told them off and ordered them to be quiet, but they shouted all the louder, "Have mercy on us, Lord, Son of David!"
Jesus stopped, called them and said, "What do you want me to do for you?"
They said to him, "Lord, that our eyes may be opened."
Moved with compassion, Jesus touched their eyes, and at once they could see again, and they followed him.

matthew_21.t: When they came near Jerusalem and reached Bethphage at the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent two disciples,
telling them, "Go into the village ahead of you. You will find a donkey tied up there straight away, and a colt with her. Untie them and bring them to me.
And if anyone says anything to you, say, 'The Lord needs them' — and he will send them at once."
This happened so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled:
"Say to the daughter of Zion: Look, your king comes to you, gentle, and mounted on a donkey, and on a colt, the foal of a beast of burden."
The disciples went and did as Jesus had instructed them.
They brought the donkey and the colt, put their cloaks on them, and he sat on them.
Most of the crowd spread their own cloaks on the road, and others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.
The crowds going ahead of him and those following kept shouting, "Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!"
When he entered Jerusalem, the whole city was shaken, and said, "Who is this?"
And the crowds said, "This is the prophet Jesus, from Nazareth in Galilee."
Jesus went into the temple of God and drove out everyone selling and buying in the temple. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves,
and he said to them, "It is written, 'My house will be called a house of prayer' — but you are making it a bandits' cave."
The blind and the lame came to him in the temple, and he healed them.
But when the chief priests and the teachers of the law saw the wonderful things he did, and the children shouting in the temple, "Hosanna to the Son of David!", they were indignant
and said to him, "Do you hear what they are saying?" Jesus said to them, "Yes. Have you never read, 'Out of the mouths of infants and nursing babies you have prepared praise'?"
And he left them, went out of the city to Bethany, and spent the night there.
Early in the morning, as he was returning to the city, he was hungry.
He saw a fig tree by the road and went to it, and found nothing on it but leaves. He said to it, "May no fruit ever come from you again." And the fig tree withered on the spot.
When the disciples saw it they were amazed. "How did the fig tree wither so quickly?" they said.

Jesus answered them, "I tell you the truth: if you have trust and are not divided in yourselves, you will not only do what was done to the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, 'Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,' it will happen.
And whatever you ask for in prayer, trusting, you will receive."

When he came into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came to him while he was teaching, and said, "By what authority are you doing these things? And who gave you this authority?"
Jesus answered them, "I will ask you one question too. If you answer me, I will also tell you by what authority I do these things.
Where did John's baptism come from? From heaven or from human beings?" They talked it over among themselves: "If we say 'From heaven,' he will say to us, 'Then why didn't you trust him?'
But if we say 'From human beings,' we are afraid of the crowd — they all hold John to be a prophet."
So they answered Jesus, "We don't know." And he said to them, "Then neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.
What do you think? A man had two children. He went to the first and said, 'Child, go and work in the vineyard today.'
He answered, 'I don't want to' — but later he changed his mind and went.
The father went to the other son and said the same thing. He answered, 'I will, sir' — and did not go.

Which of the two did the father's will?" They said to him, "The first." Jesus said to them, "I tell you the truth: the tax collectors and the prostitutes are going into the kingdom of God ahead of you.

For John came to you in the way of rightness, and you did not trust him — but the tax collectors and the prostitutes trusted him. And even when you saw it, you did not change your minds afterwards and trust him.
Listen to another parable. There was a landowner who planted a vineyard, put a fence round it, dug a winepress in it and built a tower. Then he leased it to tenant farmers and went abroad.
When the time for the fruit came near, he sent his slaves to the tenants to collect his fruit.
The tenants seized his slaves: one they beat, one they killed, one they stoned.
Again he sent other slaves, more than the first, and they did the same to them.
Finally he sent his son to them, saying, 'They will respect my son.'
But when the tenants saw the son, they said among themselves, 'This is the heir. Come on — let us kill him and have his inheritance.'
So they took him, threw him out of the vineyard and killed him.
So when the owner of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those tenants?"
They said to him, "He will bring those wretches to a wretched end, and lease the vineyard to other tenants who will give him the fruit at the proper times."
Jesus said to them, "Have you never read in the scriptures: 'The stone the builders rejected has become the head of the corner; this came from the Lord, and it is wonderful in our eyes'?
This is why I tell you: the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a nation that produces its fruit.
And the one who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces; and anyone it falls on it will crush to dust.
When the chief priests and the Pharisees heard his parables, they knew he was speaking about them.
They wanted to arrest him, but they were afraid of the crowds, because the crowds held him to be a prophet.

matthew_22.t: Jesus answered them again in parables:
"The kingdom of heaven is like a king who gave a wedding feast for his son.
He sent his slaves to call those who had been invited to the wedding, and they refused to come.

Again he sent other slaves, saying, 'Tell those who have been invited: Look, I have prepared my dinner, my oxen and fattened cattle have been slaughtered, and everything is ready. Come to the wedding.'
But they took no notice and went off, one to his own field, another to his business.
And the rest seized his slaves, outraged them and killed them.
The king was enraged. He sent his troops, destroyed those murderers and burned their city.
Then he said to his slaves, 'The wedding is ready, but those invited were not worthy.
So go out to where the roads leave the city, and invite everyone you find to the wedding.'
Those slaves went out into the roads and gathered everyone they found, bad and good alike — and the wedding hall was filled with guests.
But when the king came in to look at the guests, he saw a man there who was not wearing wedding clothes,
and he said to him, 'Friend, how did you get in here without wedding clothes?' The man was speechless.
Then the king said to the attendants, 'Tie him hand and foot and throw him out into the darkness outside. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth there.'
For many are called, but few are chosen."
Then the Pharisees went and made a plan to trap him in what he said.

They sent their disciples to him along with the Herodians, saying, "Teacher, we know that you are truthful, that you teach the way of God in truth, and that no one sways you, because you do not look at people's faces.
So tell us what you think: is it lawful to pay the poll tax to Caesar, or not?"
But Jesus knew their malice and said, "Why are you testing me, you play-actors?
Show me the coin used for the tax." They brought him a denarius.
He said to them, "Whose image is this, and whose inscription?"
They said to him, "Caesar's." Then he said to them, "Then give back to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's."
When they heard this they were amazed, and they left him and went away.
That same day some Sadducees — who say there is no resurrection — came to him and questioned him,
saying, "Teacher, Moses said, 'If a man dies without children, his brother is to marry the widow as next of kin and raise up offspring for his brother.'
Now there were seven brothers among us. The first married and died, and having no offspring he left his wife to his brother.
The same with the second and the third, down to the seventh.
Last of all the woman died.
So in the resurrection, whose wife will she be, out of the seven? All of them had her."
Jesus answered them, "You are being led astray, because you do not know the scriptures or the power of God.
For in the resurrection people neither marry nor are given in marriage; they are like the angels of God in heaven.
And about the resurrection of the dead — have you not read what was said to you by God:
'I am the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob'? He is not God of the dead but of the living."
When the crowds heard it, they were astounded at his teaching.
When the Pharisees heard that he had silenced the Sadducees, they gathered together in one place.
And one of them, an expert in the law, put him to the test with a question:
"Teacher, which commandment in the law is the great one?"
Jesus said to him, "You shall love the Lord your God with your whole heart and with your whole soul and with your whole mind.
This is the great and first commandment.
And a second is like it: 'You shall love your neighbour as yourself.'
On these two commandments the whole law hangs, and the prophets."
While the Pharisees were gathered, Jesus questioned them:
"What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is he?" They said to him, "David's."
He said to them, "Then how is it that David, in the Spirit, calls him Lord, saying:
'The Lord said to my lord: Sit at my right hand until I put your enemies under your feet'?
So if David calls him Lord, how is he his son?"
No one could answer him a word, and from that day on no one dared to question him any more.

matthew_23.t: Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to his disciples:
"The teachers of the law and the Pharisees sit in the seat of Moses.
So do and keep everything they tell you — but do not do what they do, because they say and do not do.
They tie up heavy loads, hard to carry, and lay them on people's shoulders — and they themselves are not willing to lift a finger to move them.
They do everything they do to be seen by others. They make their phylacteries broad and their tassels long.
They love the place of honour at dinners and the front seats in the synagogues,
and greetings in the marketplaces, and being called 'Rabbi' by people.
But you are not to be called 'Rabbi,' because you have one teacher, and you are all brothers and sisters.
And do not call anyone on earth your father, because you have one Father, the heavenly one.
And do not be called instructors, because you have one instructor, the Christ.
The greatest among you will be the one who serves you.
Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
But woe to you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, play-actors! You shut the kingdom of heaven in people's faces. You do not go in yourselves, and you do not let those who are going in enter.
[Woe to you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, play-actors! You devour widows' houses and for a show you pray at length. For this you will receive a heavier judgement.]
Woe to you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, play-actors! You cross sea and dry land to make a single convert, and when he becomes one you make him twice as much a son of Gehenna as yourselves.
Woe to you, blind guides, who say, 'If anyone swears by the sanctuary, it is nothing; but if anyone swears by the gold of the sanctuary, he is bound by it.'
You fools and blind! Which is greater, the gold, or the sanctuary that makes the gold holy?
And, 'If anyone swears by the altar, it is nothing; but if anyone swears by the offering on it, he is bound by it.'
You blind! Which is greater, the offering, or the altar that makes the offering holy?
So the one who swears by the altar swears by it and by everything on it,
and the one who swears by the sanctuary swears by it and by the one who dwells in it,
and the one who swears by heaven swears by the throne of God and by the one who sits on it.
