Woe to you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, play-actors! You tithe mint and dill and cumin, and you have left aside the weightier matters of the law: justice and mercy and faithfulness. These you should have done, without leaving the others aside.
Blind guides! You strain out the gnat and swallow the camel.
Woe to you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, play-actors! You clean the outside of the cup and the dish, but inside they are full of what you have seized and of self-indulgence.
Blind Pharisee! First clean the inside of the cup and the dish, so that the outside may become clean too.
Woe to you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, play-actors! You are like whitewashed tombs, which look beautiful on the outside but inside are full of dead men's bones and every kind of uncleanness.
So you too look right to people on the outside, but inside you are full of play-acting and lawlessness.
Woe to you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, play-actors! You build the tombs of the prophets and decorate the monuments of the righteous,
and you say, 'If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we would not have shared with them in the blood of the prophets.'
So you testify against yourselves that you are the sons of those who murdered the prophets.
Go on, then — fill up the measure of your fathers.
Snakes! Brood of vipers! How are you going to escape the judgement of Gehenna?
This is why I am sending you prophets and wise men and teachers of the law. Some of them you will kill and crucify, and some of them you will flog in your synagogues and hound from town to town,
so that on you may come all the righteous blood shed on the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Barachiah, whom you murdered between the sanctuary and the altar.
I tell you the truth: all these things will come upon this generation.

Jerusalem, Jerusalem, killing the prophets and stoning those sent to her — how often I wanted to gather your children together, the way a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you were not willing.
Look — your house is left to you deserted.
For I tell you: you will not see me from now on until you say, 'Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord.'"

matthew_24.t: Jesus left the temple and was going away when his disciples came up to show him the temple buildings.
He answered them, "You see all these, don't you? I tell you the truth: not one stone will be left here on another that will not be thrown down."

As he was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to him privately and said, "Tell us, when will these things happen? And what will be the sign of your coming and of the completion of the age?"
Jesus answered them, "Watch out that no one leads you astray.
For many will come using my name and saying, 'I am the Christ,' and will lead many astray.
You will hear of wars and rumours of wars. See that you are not alarmed — this must happen, but the end is not yet.
For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be famines and plagues and earthquakes in place after place.
All these are the beginning of the birth pains.
Then they will hand you over to be afflicted and will kill you, and you will be hated by all the nations because of my name.
And then many will be tripped up, and will hand one another over and hate one another.
And many false prophets will arise and will lead many astray.
And because lawlessness will be multiplied, the love of most people will grow cold.
But the one who endures to the end — that person will be saved.
And this good news of the kingdom will be proclaimed in the whole inhabited world as a testimony to all the nations — and then the end will come.
So when you see the desolating abomination, spoken of through the prophet Daniel, standing in a holy place — let the reader understand —
then those in Judea must flee to the mountains.
The one on the roof must not go down to take anything out of his house,
and the one in the field must not turn back to get his cloak.
Woe to those who are pregnant and those nursing babies in those days!
Pray that your flight may not be in winter or on a sabbath.
For there will be great distress then, such as has not happened from the beginning of the world until now, and never will.
And if those days had not been cut short, no flesh would be saved; but for the sake of the chosen ones those days will be cut short.
Then if anyone says to you, 'Look, here is the Christ,' or 'Here!' — do not trust it.
For false christs and false prophets will arise and will give great signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if possible, even the chosen ones.
Look — I have told you beforehand.
So if they say to you, 'Look, he is in the wilderness,' do not go out; 'Look, he is in the inner rooms,' do not trust it.
For as the lightning comes from the east and shines as far as the west, so will the coming of the Son of Man be.
Wherever the corpse is, there the vultures will gather.
Immediately after the distress of those days the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light, and the stars will fall from the sky, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

And then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in the sky, and then all the tribes of the earth will beat their breasts, and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of the sky with power and great glory.
And he will send his angels with a great trumpet blast, and they will gather his chosen ones from the four winds, from one end of the heavens to the other.
Learn the parable from the fig tree: as soon as its branch becomes tender and it puts out leaves, you know that summer is near.
So also you: when you see all these things, know that he is near, at the doors.
I tell you the truth: this generation will certainly not pass away until all these things happen.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will certainly not pass away.
But about that day and hour no one knows — not even the angels of the heavens, nor the Son — only my Father.
For as the days of Noah were, so will the coming of the Son of Man be.
For as in those days before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, right up to the day Noah went into the ark,
and they did not know until the flood came and took them all away — so will the coming of the Son of Man be.
Then two men will be in the field: one is taken and one is left.
Two women will be grinding at the mill: one is taken and one is left.
So keep awake, because you do not know on what day your Lord is coming.
But know this: if the householder had known in which watch of the night the thief was coming, he would have stayed awake and would not have let his house be broken into.
So you too must be ready, because the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not expect.
Who then is the faithful and sensible slave, whom his master put in charge of his household to give them their food at the right time?
Blessed is that slave whom his master finds doing so when he comes.
I tell you the truth: he will put him in charge of all he owns.
But if that wicked slave says in his heart, 'My master is taking his time,'
and starts beating his fellow slaves, and eating and drinking with drunkards,
the master of that slave will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not know,
and will cut him in two and put his portion with the play-actors. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth there.

matthew_25.t: Then the kingdom of heaven will be like ten young women who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.
Five of them were foolish and five were sensible.
For the foolish ones took their lamps and did not take oil with them,
but the sensible ones took oil in flasks along with their lamps.
While the bridegroom was delayed, they all became drowsy and fell asleep.
In the middle of the night there was a shout: "Look, the bridegroom! Come out to meet him!"
Then all those young women got up and trimmed their lamps.
And the foolish ones said to the sensible ones, "Give us some of your oil — our lamps are going out."
But the sensible ones answered, "There may not be enough for us and for you. Go instead to those who sell it and buy some for yourselves."
While they were away buying it, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready went in with him to the wedding — and the door was shut.
Later the other young women came too, saying, "Lord, lord, open to us!"
But he answered, "I tell you the truth: I do not know you."
So keep awake, because you do not know the day or the hour in which the Son of Man is coming.
For it is like a man going abroad, who called his own slaves and handed his property over to them.
To one he gave five talents, to another two, to another one — to each according to his own ability. Then he went away. At once
the man who had received the five talents went and traded with them, and made another five.
In the same way the one with the two made another two.
But the one who had received the one talent went off, dug in the ground and hid his master's silver.
After a long time the master of those slaves came and settled accounts with them.
The one who had received five talents came and brought another five, saying, "Master, you handed over five talents to me. Look — I have made another five on top of them."
His master said to him, "Well done, good and faithful slave. You were faithful over a little; I will put you in charge of much. Come into your master's joy."
The one with the two talents came and said, "Master, you handed over two talents to me. Look — I have made another two on top of them."
His master said to him, "Well done, good and faithful slave. You were faithful over a little; I will put you in charge of much. Come into your master's joy."
Then the one who had received the one talent came and said, "Master, I knew you are a hard man, reaping where you did not sow and gathering where you did not scatter,
and I was afraid, so I went and hid your talent in the ground. Here — you have what is yours."
His master answered him, "You wicked and shrinking slave! You knew that I reap where I did not sow and gather where I did not scatter?
Then you should have put my silver with the bankers, and when I came I would have got back what was mine with interest.
So take the talent from him and give it to the one who has the ten talents.
For to everyone who has, more will be given, and he will have plenty; but from the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away.
And throw the useless slave out into the darkness outside. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth there."
When the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then he will sit on the throne of his glory.
All the nations will be gathered before him, and he will separate them from one another as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats,
and he will put the sheep on his right and the goats on his left.
Then the king will say to those on his right, "Come, you who are blessed by my Father. Inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.
For I was hungry and you gave me something to eat; I was thirsty and you gave me a drink; I was a stranger and you took me in;
naked and you clothed me; I was ill and you looked after me; I was in prison and you came to me."
Then the righteous will answer him, "Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you a drink?
And when did we see you a stranger and take you in, or naked and clothe you?
And when did we see you ill or in prison and come to you?"
And the king will answer them, "I tell you the truth: whatever you did for one of the least of these my brothers, you did for me."
Then he will say to those on his left, "Go away from me, you who are cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.
For I was hungry and you gave me nothing to eat; I was thirsty and you gave me nothing to drink;
I was a stranger and you did not take me in; naked and you did not clothe me; ill and in prison and you did not look after me."
Then they too will answer, "Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or ill or in prison, and did not serve you?"
Then he will answer them, "I tell you the truth: whatever you did not do for one of these least ones, you did not do for me."
And these will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.

matthew_26.t: When Jesus had finished all these words, he said to his disciples,
"You know that after two days the Passover comes, and the Son of Man is handed over to be crucified."
Then the chief priests and the teachers of the law and the elders of the people gathered in the courtyard of the high priest, the one called Caiaphas,
and they made a plan to seize Jesus by trickery and kill him.
But they said, "Not during the festival, or there will be a riot among the people."
While Jesus was in Bethany at the house of Simon the leper,
a woman came to him with an alabaster jar of very costly perfume, and poured it on his head as he reclined at table.
When the disciples saw it they were indignant. "Why this waste?" they said.
"This could have been sold for a great deal and given to the poor."
But Jesus knew, and said to them, "Why are you making trouble for the woman? She has done a beautiful thing for me.
For you always have the poor with you, but you do not always have me.
When she poured this perfume on my body, she did it to prepare me for burial.
I tell you the truth: wherever this good news is proclaimed in the whole world, what she has done will also be told, in memory of her."
Then one of the twelve, the one called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests
and said, "What are you willing to give me if I hand him over to you?" And they weighed out thirty pieces of silver for him.
And from then on he was looking for a good opportunity to hand him over.
On the first day of Unleavened Bread the disciples came to Jesus and said to him, "Where do you want us to prepare for you to eat the Passover?"
He said, "Go into the city to a certain man and say to him, 'The teacher says: My time is near. I am keeping the Passover at your house with my disciples.'"
The disciples did as Jesus had instructed them and prepared the Passover.
When evening came, he reclined at table with the twelve disciples.
And while they were eating he said, "I tell you the truth: one of you will hand me over."
They were deeply distressed, and each one began to say to him, "Surely it isn't me, Lord?"
He answered, "The one who dipped his hand in the bowl with me — he will hand me over.
The Son of Man goes as it is written about him — but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is handed over. It would have been better for that man if he had not been born."
Judas, the one handing him over, answered, "Surely it isn't me, Rabbi?" He said to him, "You said it."
While they were eating, Jesus took bread, blessed it and broke it, and gave it to the disciples and said, "Take, eat. This is my body."
And he took a cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying, "Drink from it, all of you,
for this is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many for the release of sins.
And I tell you, I will not drink from this fruit of the vine from now on, until the day when I drink it new with you in my Father's kingdom."
And when they had sung the hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
Then Jesus said to them, "All of you will be tripped up because of me tonight. For it is written: 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.'
But after I am raised, I will go ahead of you to Galilee."
Peter answered him, "Even if everyone is tripped up because of you, I never will be."
Jesus said to him, "I tell you the truth: tonight, before the cock crows, you will disown me three times."
Peter said to him, "Even if I have to die with you, I will never disown you." And all the disciples said the same.
Then Jesus came with them to a place called Gethsemane, and he said to the disciples, "Sit here while I go over there and pray."
He took Peter and the two sons of Zebedee with him, and he began to be grieved and in anguish.
Then he said to them, "My soul is overwhelmed with grief, to the point of death. Stay here and keep awake with me."
He went on a little further, fell on his face and prayed, "My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me. But not as I want — as you want."
He came to the disciples and found them sleeping, and he said to Peter, "So you could not keep awake with me for one hour?
Keep awake and pray that you do not come into testing. The spirit is eager, but the flesh is weak."
Again, a second time, he went away and prayed, "My Father, if this cup cannot pass unless I drink it, let your will be done."
He came again and found them sleeping, because their eyes were heavy.
So he left them and went away again and prayed a third time, saying the same words again.
Then he came to the disciples and said to them, "Go on sleeping now and take your rest. Look — the hour has come near, and the Son of Man is handed over into the hands of sinners.
Get up, let us go. Look — the one handing me over has come near."
While he was still speaking — look — Judas, one of the twelve, arrived, and with him a large crowd with swords and clubs, from the chief priests and elders of the people.
The one handing him over had given them a signal: "The one I kiss — that is him. Seize him."
He went straight up to Jesus and said, "Greetings, Rabbi" — and kissed him.
Jesus said to him, "Friend, do what you came for." Then they came forward, laid hands on Jesus and seized him.
And look — one of those with Jesus reached out his hand, drew his sword, struck the high priest's slave and cut off his ear.
Then Jesus said to him, "Put your sword back in its place. For all who take up the sword will die by the sword.
Or do you think I cannot call on my Father, and he would put more than twelve legions of angels at my side this minute?
How then would the scriptures be fulfilled, that say it must happen this way?"
At that hour Jesus said to the crowds, "Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest me, as though I were a bandit? Day after day I sat teaching in the temple, and you did not seize me.
But all this has happened so that the writings of the prophets might be fulfilled." Then all the disciples left him and fled.
Those who had seized Jesus took him away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the teachers of the law and the elders had gathered.
Peter followed him at a distance, as far as the high priest's courtyard. He went inside and sat with the attendants, to see how it would end.
The chief priests and the elders and the whole council were looking for false testimony against Jesus, so that they could put him to death,
but they found none, though many false witnesses came forward. At last two came forward
and said, "This man said, 'I can destroy the sanctuary of God and build it in three days.'"
The high priest stood up and said to him, "Have you no answer? What is it these men are testifying against you?"
But Jesus stayed silent. And the high priest said to him, "I put you on oath by the living God: tell us whether you are the Christ, the Son of God."
Jesus said to him, "You said it. But I tell you: from now on you will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of the Power and coming on the clouds of the sky."
Then the high priest tore his clothes and said, "He has blasphemed! Why do we still need witnesses? Look, you have now heard the blasphemy.
What do you think?" They answered, "He deserves death."
Then they spat in his face and beat him with their fists; and others struck him with open hands,
saying, "Prophesy to us, Christ! Who was it that hit you?"
Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard, and a servant girl came up to him and said, "You were with Jesus the Galilean too."
But he denied it in front of them all: "I don't know what you are talking about."
When he went out to the gateway, another girl saw him and said to those there, "This man was with Jesus the Nazorean."
And again he denied it, with an oath: "I do not know the man."
A little later the bystanders came up and said to Peter, "You really are one of them — your accent gives you away."
Then he began to curse and to swear, "I do not know the man!" And at once the cock crowed.
And Peter remembered what Jesus had said to him: "Before the cock crows you will disown me three times." And he went outside and wept bitterly.

matthew_27.t: When morning came, all the chief priests and the elders of the people made their plan against Jesus, to put him to death.
They bound him, led him away and handed him over to Pontius Pilate the governor.
Then Judas, the one who had handed him over, saw that Jesus had been condemned. He changed his mind and brought the thirty pieces of silver back to the chief priests and the elders,
saying, "I have sinned — I handed over innocent blood." They said, "What is that to us? You see to it."
He threw the silver into the sanctuary, left, and went off and hanged himself.
The chief priests took the silver and said, "It is not lawful to put this into the treasury, since it is blood money."
So they made a plan, and with the money they bought the potter's field as a burial place for foreigners.
That is why that field has been called the Field of Blood to this day.

Then what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled: "And they took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of the one whose price had been set, on whom a price was set by the sons of Israel,
and they gave them for the potter's field, as the Lord instructed me."
Jesus was made to stand before the governor, and the governor questioned him: "Are you the king of the Jews?" Jesus said to him, "You say so."
And when he was accused by the chief priests and the elders, he answered nothing.
Then Pilate said to him, "Don't you hear how much they are testifying against you?"
And he did not answer him a single word, so that the governor was greatly amazed.
At the festival the governor was in the habit of releasing to the crowd one prisoner, whichever one they wanted.
At that time they had a notorious prisoner called Jesus Barabbas.
So when they had gathered, Pilate said to them, "Which one do you want me to release to you? Jesus Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?"
For he knew they had handed him over out of envy.
While he was sitting on the judgement seat, his wife sent word to him: "Have nothing to do with that righteous man. I have suffered a great deal today in a dream because of him."
But the chief priests and the elders persuaded the crowds to ask for Barabbas and to have Jesus destroyed.
The governor answered them, "Which of the two do you want me to release to you?" They said, "Barabbas."
Pilate said to them, "Then what shall I do with Jesus who is called Christ?" They all said, "Let him be crucified."
The governor said, "Why — what evil has he done?" But they shouted all the more, "Let him be crucified."

When Pilate saw that he was getting nowhere and that a riot was starting instead, he took water and washed his hands in front of the crowd, saying, "I am innocent of this righteous man's blood. You see to it."
And all the people answered, "His blood be on us and on our children."
Then he released Barabbas to them; and he had Jesus flogged and handed him over to be crucified.
Then the governor's soldiers took Jesus into the praetorium and gathered the whole cohort round him.
They stripped him and put a scarlet military cloak on him,
and they twisted together a crown out of thorns and put it on his head, and a reed in his right hand. They knelt in front of him and mocked him: "Hail, king of the Jews!"
And they spat on him, took the reed and struck him on the head.
When they had finished mocking him, they took the cloak off him, put his own clothes back on him and led him away to be crucified.
As they were going out, they found a man from Cyrene named Simon, and they pressed him into service to carry his cross.
And when they came to a place called Golgotha (which means Place of a Skull),
they gave him wine to drink mixed with gall; and when he tasted it, he would not drink it.

When they had crucified him, they divided his clothes among them by casting lots, so that what was spoken by the prophet might be fulfilled: "They divided my garments among themselves, and for my clothing they cast lots."
And they sat down and kept watch over him there.
And above his head they put the written charge against him: "This is Jesus, the king of the Jews."
Then two bandits were crucified with him, one on the right and one on the left.
Those who passed by insulted him, shaking their heads
and saying, "You who destroy the sanctuary and build it in three days, save yourself! If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross."
In the same way the chief priests, with the teachers of the law and the elders and the Pharisees, mocked him and said,
"He saved others; he cannot save himself. He is the king of Israel — let him come down now from the cross, and we will trust him.
He trusted in God — let God rescue him now, if he wants him. For he said, 'I am God's son.'"
The bandits crucified with him taunted him in the same way.
From about noon until three in the afternoon, darkness came over the whole land.
About three in the afternoon Jesus cried out in a loud voice, "Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?" — that is, "My God, my God, why have you abandoned me?"
Some of those standing there heard it and said, "This man is calling Elijah."
At once one of them ran, took a sponge, filled it with sour wine, put it on a reed and gave it to him to drink.
But the rest said, "Leave him. Let us see whether Elijah comes to save him."
And Jesus cried out again in a loud voice and let go of his spirit.
And look — the curtain of the sanctuary was torn in two from top to bottom, and the earth shook and the rocks were split,
and the tombs were opened, and many bodies of the holy ones who had fallen asleep were raised.
And coming out of the tombs after his rising, they went into the holy city and appeared to many.
When the centurion and those with him who were guarding Jesus saw the earthquake and what had happened, they were terrified and said, "Truly this was God's son."
Many women were there, watching from a distance. They had followed Jesus from Galilee, serving him.
Among them were Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of Zebedee's sons.
When evening came, a rich man from Arimathea named Joseph arrived, who had himself been made a disciple of Jesus.
He went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus. Then Pilate ordered it to be given to him.
Joseph took the body, wrapped it in a clean linen cloth,
and put it in his own new tomb, which he had cut in the rock. He rolled a great stone across the doorway of the tomb and went away.
Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were there, sitting opposite the grave.
The next day — the day after the Preparation — the chief priests and the Pharisees gathered before Pilate
and said, "Sir, we remember that while he was still alive that deceiver said, 'After three days I am raised.'

So give the order for the grave to be made secure until the third day, in case his disciples come and steal him and tell the people, 'He has been raised from the dead.' Then the last deception would be worse than the first."
Pilate said to them, "You have a guard. Go and make it as secure as you know how."
So they went and made the grave secure, sealing the stone and posting the guard.

matthew_28.t: After the sabbath, as the first day of the week was growing light, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to look at the grave.
And look — there was a great earthquake, for an angel of the Lord came down from heaven, came and rolled the stone away, and sat on it.
His appearance was like lightning and his clothing white as snow.
The guards shook with fear of him and became like dead men.
The angel said to the women, "You — do not be afraid. For I know that you are looking for Jesus, the crucified one.
He is not here — he has been raised, just as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay.
And go quickly and tell his disciples that he has been raised from the dead. And look — he is going ahead of you to Galilee; there you will see him. Look, I have told you."
So they left the tomb quickly, with fear and great joy, and ran to tell his disciples.
And as they were going to tell his disciples — look — Jesus met them and said, "Greetings." They came up, took hold of his feet and knelt before him.
Then Jesus said to them, "Do not be afraid. Go and tell my brothers to go to Galilee, and there they will see me."
While they were going, some of the guard went into the city and reported to the chief priests everything that had happened.
They met with the elders, made a plan, and gave a large sum of silver to the soldiers,
telling them, "Say, 'His disciples came at night and stole him while we were asleep.'
And if this reaches the governor, we will persuade him and keep you out of trouble."
So they took the silver and did as they were instructed. And this story has been spread among Jews to this day.
The eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had arranged to meet them.
And when they saw him they knelt before him — but they doubted.
Jesus came to them and spoke to them: "All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me.
So go and make disciples of all the nations, baptising them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
teaching them to keep everything I have commanded you. And look — I am with you all the days, to the completion of the age." Amen

mark_1.t: The beginning of the good news of Jesus Christ, Son of God.
As it is written in Isaiah the prophet: "Look, I am sending my messenger ahead of you, who will prepare your road" —
a voice shouting in the wilderness: "Prepare the Lord's road, make his paths straight."
John came, baptising in the wilderness and proclaiming a baptism of a change of mind for the forgiveness of sins.
And the whole Judean countryside and all the people of Jerusalem were going out to him, and they were being baptised by him in the Jordan river, confessing their sins.
And John was dressed in camel hair with a leather belt around his waist, and he ate locusts and wild honey.
And he proclaimed, "The one stronger than me is coming after me, and I am not fit to stoop down and untie the strap of his sandals."
"I baptised you with water, but he will baptise you with the Holy Spirit."
And it happened in those days that Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee and was baptised by John in the Jordan.
And at once, coming up out of the water, he saw the heavens being torn open and the Spirit coming down into him like a dove.
And a voice came from the heavens: "You are my Son, the beloved; in you I am well pleased."
And at once the Spirit drives him out into the wilderness.
And he was there in the wilderness forty days, being tested by Satan; and he was with the wild animals, and the angels were serving him.
And after John was handed over, Jesus came into Galilee proclaiming the good news of the kingdom of God,
and saying, "The time has been filled up and the kingdom of God is at hand. Change your minds, and trust in the good news."
And passing alongside the Sea of Galilee he saw Simon and Simon's brother Andrew casting a net in the sea — for they were fishermen.
And Jesus said to them, "Come after me, and I will make you become fishers of people."
And at once they left their nets and followed him.
And going on a little from there he saw James son of Zebedee and his brother John, and they were in the boat mending the nets.
And at once he called them. And they left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired men and went off after him.
And they go into Capernaum. And at once, on the sabbath, he went into the synagogue and was teaching.
And they were astonished at his teaching, for he was teaching them as one who has authority, and not like the teachers of the law.
And at once there was in their synagogue a man in an unclean spirit, and he screamed out,
saying, "What do you want with us, Jesus the Nazarene? Did you come to destroy us? I know who you are — the holy one of God."
And Jesus rebuked it, saying, "Be silent, and come out of him."
And the unclean spirit convulsed him and shouted with a loud voice and came out of him.
And they were all amazed, so that they argued with each other, saying, "What is this? A new teaching — with authority! And he gives orders to the unclean spirits, and they obey him."
And the report about him went out at once everywhere, into the whole region around Galilee.
And at once they came out of the synagogue and went into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.
Now Simon's mother-in-law was lying down with a fever, and at once they tell him about her.
And he came and raised her up, taking hold of her hand; and the fever left her at once, and she was serving them.
When evening came, when the sun had set, they were bringing to him all who were ill and those possessed by demons.
And the whole city was gathered together at the door.
And he healed many who were ill with various diseases, and he drove out many demons, and he would not let the demons speak, because they knew him.
And very early, while it was still night, he got up and went out and went off to a deserted place, and there he was praying.
And Simon and those with him hunted him down,
and they found him and they say to him, "Everyone is looking for you."
And he says to them, "Let's go somewhere else, to the neighbouring towns, so that I can proclaim there too — that is what I came out for."
And he went proclaiming in their synagogues throughout the whole of Galilee, and driving out the demons.
And a man with a skin disease comes to him, begging him and kneeling to him and saying to him, "If you want to, you can make me clean."
And moved with compassion, he stretched out his hand and touched him and says to him, "I want to. Be clean."
And at once, when he had said it, the skin disease left him, and he was made clean.
And he snorted at him and at once threw him out,
and he says to him, "See that you say nothing to anyone; but go, show yourself to the priest and offer for your cleansing what Moses commanded, as evidence to them."

But he went out and began to proclaim it freely and to spread the word, so that Jesus could no longer go openly into a town, but was outside in deserted places. And they kept coming to him from everywhere.

mark_2.t: And he went into Capernaum again after some days, and it was heard that he was at home.
And at once many were gathered, so that there was no longer room, not even at the door, and he was speaking the word to them.
And they come, bringing to him a paralysed man carried by four.
And when they could not bring him to Jesus because of the crowd, they took off the roof where he was and dug through it and lower the mat the paralysed man was lying on.
And when Jesus saw their trust he says to the paralysed man, "Child, your sins are forgiven."
Now some of the teachers of the law were sitting there and reasoning in their hearts:
"Why does this man talk like this? He is blaspheming! Who can forgive sins except one — God?"
And at once Jesus, knowing in his spirit that they were reasoning like this among themselves, says to them, "Why are you reasoning these things in your hearts?
Which is easier — to say to the paralysed man, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, 'Get up and pick up your mat and walk'?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority to forgive sins on the earth" — he says to the paralysed man,
"I say to you: get up, pick up your mat, and go to your house."
And he got up and at once picked up the mat and went out in front of everyone, so that they were all beside themselves and glorified God, saying, "We have never seen anything like this."
And he went out again beside the sea, and the whole crowd was coming to him, and he was teaching them.
And passing by he saw Levi son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth, and he says to him, "Follow me." And he got up and followed him.
And it happens that he is reclining at table in his house, and many tax collectors and sinners were reclining with Jesus and his disciples — for there were many, and they were following him.

And the teachers of the law of the Pharisees, when they saw that he was eating with sinners and tax collectors, were saying to his disciples, "Why does he eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?"
And Jesus heard it and says to them, "Those who are strong have no need of a doctor, but those who are ill do. I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners."
Now John's disciples and the Pharisees were fasting, and they come and say to him, "Why do John's disciples and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but your disciples do not fast?"
And Jesus said to them, "The wedding guests can't fast while the bridegroom is with them, can they? As long as they have the bridegroom with them they cannot fast.
But days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast, on that day.
No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth onto an old coat. If he does, the new patch pulls away from the old and a worse tear happens.
And no one puts new wine into old wineskins. If he does, the wine will burst the skins, and the wine is lost and so are the skins. No — new wine into new wineskins.
And it happened that he was going through the grainfields on the sabbath, and his disciples began to make their way, picking the heads of grain.
And the Pharisees were saying to him, "Look, why are they doing on the sabbath what is not permitted?"
And he says to them, "Have you never read what David did when he was in need and hungry, he and those with him —

how he went into the house of God, in the time of Abiathar the high priest, and ate the bread of the presence, which no one is permitted to eat except the priests, and gave it also to those with him?"
And he was saying to them, "The sabbath came into being for the sake of people, and not people for the sake of the sabbath.
So the Son of Man is lord even of the sabbath."

mark_3.t: And he went into the synagogue again, and there was a man there with a withered hand.
And they were watching him closely, to see whether he would heal him on the sabbath, so that they could accuse him.
And he says to the man with the withered hand, "Get up into the middle."
And he says to them, "Is it permitted on the sabbath to do good or to do harm, to save a life or to kill?" But they were silent.
And looking around at them with anger, deeply grieved at the hardness of their hearts, he says to the man, "Stretch out your hand." And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored.
And the Pharisees went out and at once began plotting with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him.
And Jesus withdrew with his disciples to the sea, and a great crowd from Galilee followed, and from Judea
and from Jerusalem and from Idumea and from beyond the Jordan and around Tyre and Sidon — a great crowd, hearing all he was doing, came to him.
And he told his disciples that a small boat should stay ready for him because of the crowd, so that they would not crush him.
For he healed many, so that all who had diseases were falling on him to touch him.
And the unclean spirits, whenever they saw him, were falling down before him and screaming, saying, "You are the Son of God."
And he rebuked them sharply, so that they would not make him known.
And he goes up onto the mountain and calls to himself those he wanted, and they went off to him.
And he made twelve, whom he also named apostles, so that they would be with him and so that he could send them out to proclaim,
and to have authority to heal diseases and to drive out the demons.
And he made the twelve, and he put on Simon the name Peter,
and James son of Zebedee and John the brother of James, and he put on them the name Boanerges, which is "sons of thunder";
and Andrew and Philip and Bartholomew and Matthew and Thomas and James son of Alphaeus and Thaddaeus and Simon the Cananaean,
and Judas Iscariot, who also handed him over.
And he comes home, and the crowd gathers again, so that they could not even eat bread.
And when his family heard, they went out to seize him; for they were saying, "He is out of his mind."
And the teachers of the law who had come down from Jerusalem were saying, "He has Beelzebul," and, "By the ruler of the demons he drives out the demons."
And he called them to him and was speaking to them in parables: "How can Satan drive out Satan?
And if a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
And if a household is divided against itself, that household will not be able to stand.
And if Satan has risen against himself and is divided, he cannot stand — he is finished.
But no one can go into the strong man's house and plunder his goods unless he first ties up the strong man; and then he will plunder his house.
I tell you the truth: everything will be forgiven the children of men — the sins and the blasphemies, whatever they blaspheme.
But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit never has forgiveness, but is guilty of an eternal sin" —
because they were saying, "He has an unclean spirit."
And his mother and his brothers come, and standing outside they sent to him, calling him.
And a crowd was sitting around him, and they say to him, "Look, your mother and your brothers and your sisters are outside asking for you."
And he answered them and says, "Who is my mother — and my brothers?"
And looking around at those sitting in a circle around him, he says, "Look — my mother and my brothers.
Whoever does the will of God — this person is my brother and sister and mother."

mark_4.t: And again he began to teach beside the sea. And a very great crowd gathers to him, so that he got into a boat and sat in it on the sea, and the whole crowd was on the land facing the sea.
And he was teaching them many things in parables, and he was saying to them in his teaching:
"Listen! Look — the sower went out to sow.
And it happened, as he sowed, that some fell along the road, and the birds came and ate it up.
And other seed fell on the rocky ground, where it did not have much soil, and at once it sprang up, because it had no depth of soil.
And when the sun rose it was scorched, and because it had no root it was withered.
And other seed fell among the thorns, and the thorns came up and choked it, and it gave no fruit.
And other seeds fell into the good soil, and they were giving fruit, coming up and growing, and it bore thirty and sixty and a hundred.
And he was saying, "Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear."
And when he was alone, those around him with the twelve were asking him about the parables.
And he was saying to them, "To you has been given the knowing of the mystery of the kingdom of God; but to those outside, everything comes in parables,
so that 'seeing they may see and not perceive, and hearing they may hear and not understand, in case they turn back and it be forgiven them.'"
And he says to them, "Don't you understand this parable? Then how will you know all the parables?
The sower sows the word.
These are the ones along the road, where the word is sown: and when they hear, at once Satan comes and takes away the word that has been sown in them.
And these are the ones sown on the rocky ground in the same way: when they hear the word, at once they receive it with joy,
and they have no root in themselves but last only a short time. Then, when pressure or persecution comes because of the word, at once they are tripped up.
And others are the ones sown among the thorns. These are the ones who heard the word,
and the worries of this age and the deceit of wealth and the desires for everything else come in and choke the word, and it becomes fruitless.
And those are the ones sown on the good soil, who hear the word and take it in and bear fruit — thirty and sixty and a hundred."
And he was saying to them, "Does the lamp come in to be put under the basket or under the bed? Isn't it to be put on the lampstand?
For nothing is hidden except to be made visible, and nothing was concealed except to come into the open.
If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear."
And he was saying to them, "Watch what you hear. By the measure you measure it will be measured to you, and more will be added to you who hear.
For whoever has, it will be given to him; and whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken from him."
And he was saying, "The kingdom of God is like this: as if a person throws the seed on the ground,
and sleeps and rises, night and day, and the seed sprouts and grows long — how, he does not know.
By itself the earth bears fruit: first a blade, then a head, then full grain in the head.
But when the crop allows, at once he sends the sickle, because the harvest has arrived."
And he was saying, "How shall we compare the kingdom of God, or in what parable shall we put it?
It is like a mustard seed, which when it is sown on the ground is smaller than all the seeds on the earth.
And when it is sown it comes up and becomes greater than all the garden plants and makes large branches, so that the birds of the sky can nest in its shade."
And with many parables like these he was speaking the word to them, as they were able to hear it.
And he was not speaking to them without a parable; but privately he was explaining everything to his own disciples.
And he says to them on that day, when evening had come, "Let's go across to the other side."
And they left the crowd and take him along, just as he was, in the boat; and other boats were with him.
And a great windstorm comes, and the waves were breaking into the boat, so that the boat was already being swamped.
And he was in the stern, asleep on the cushion. And they wake him and say to him, "Teacher, don't you care that we are being destroyed?"
And he woke up and rebuked the wind and said to the sea, "Be quiet! Be muzzled!" And the wind dropped, and there was a great calm.
And he said to them, "Why are you cowardly? Do you still have no trust?"
And they were terrified with a great fear and were saying to one another, "Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?"

mark_5.t: And they came to the other side of the sea, into the region of the Gerasenes.
And when he had come out of the boat, at once a man in an unclean spirit met him out of the tombs —
a man who had his dwelling among the graves. And no one could bind him any more, not even with a chain,
because he had often been bound with shackles and chains, and the chains had been torn apart by him and the shackles smashed, and no one was strong enough to subdue him.
And all the time, night and day, he was in the tombs and in the hills, screaming and cutting himself with stones.
And seeing Jesus from a distance he ran and bowed down before him,
and screaming with a loud voice he says, "What do you want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I put you under oath by God — don't torture me!"
For he was saying to him, "Come out of the man, unclean spirit!"
And he was asking him, "What is your name?" And he says to him, "My name is Legion, because we are many."
And he was begging him urgently not to send them out of the region.
Now there was there, near the hillside, a large herd of pigs feeding.
And they begged him, saying, "Send us into the pigs, so that we can go into them."

And at once Jesus permitted them. And the unclean spirits came out and went into the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea — about two thousand — and they were drowning in the sea.
And those feeding them fled and reported it in the town and in the countryside. And they came to see what it was that had happened.
And they come to Jesus and see the man who had been possessed by demons sitting, clothed and in his right mind — the one who had had the legion — and they were afraid.
And those who had seen it described to them what had happened to the man possessed by demons, and about the pigs.
And they began to beg him to go away from their district.
And as he was getting into the boat, the man who had been possessed by demons was begging him to be with him.
And he did not let him, but says to him, "Go to your house, to your own people, and report to them how much the Lord has done for you, and that he had mercy on you."
And he went away and began to proclaim in the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him; and everyone was amazed.
And when Jesus had crossed over again in the boat to the other side, a large crowd gathered to him, and he was beside the sea.
And look — one of the synagogue rulers comes, named Jairus; and seeing him he falls at his feet
and begs him urgently, saying, "My little daughter is at the point of death. Come and lay your hands on her, so that she may be saved and live."
And he went off with him. And a large crowd was following him and pressing in on him.
And there was a woman who had had a flow of blood for twelve years,
and had suffered much under many doctors and had spent everything she had and had gained nothing, but had rather got worse.
She heard about Jesus, came up behind him in the crowd, and touched his cloak;
for she was saying, "If I touch even his clothes, I will be saved."
And at once the source of her blood dried up, and she knew in her body that she was healed of her affliction.
And at once Jesus, recognising in himself that power had gone out of him, turned around in the crowd and was saying, "Who touched my clothes?"
And his disciples were saying to him, "You see the crowd crushing you, and you say, 'Who touched me?'"
And he was looking around to see the woman who had done it.
And the woman, afraid and trembling, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell down before him and told him the whole truth.
And he said to her, "Daughter, your trust has saved you. Go in peace, and be well from your affliction."
While he was still speaking, they come from the synagogue ruler's house, saying, "Your daughter has died. Why bother the teacher any more?"
But Jesus, overhearing the word being spoken, at once says to the synagogue ruler, "Do not be afraid; only trust."
And he did not let anyone follow along with him except Peter and James and John the brother of James.
And they come to the house of the synagogue ruler, and he sees a commotion and people weeping and wailing loudly,
and he went in and says to them, "Why are you making a commotion and weeping? The child has not died — she is sleeping."
And they were laughing at him. But he threw them all out and takes the child's father and mother and those with him and goes in where the child was.
And taking hold of the child's hand he says to her, "Talitha koum," which translated is, "Little girl, I say to you, get up."
And at once the girl got up and was walking around — for she was twelve years old. And at once they were beside themselves with great amazement.
And he ordered them strictly that no one should know this, and he said to give her something to eat.

mark_6.t: And he went out from there and comes to his home town, and his disciples follow him.

And when the sabbath came he began to teach in the synagogue, and many who heard him were astonished, saying, "Where did this man get these things? And what is this wisdom given to him, that such deeds of power happen through his hands?
Isn't this the carpenter, the son of Mary and brother of James and Joses and Judas and Simon? And aren't his sisters here with us?" And they were tripped up over him.
And Jesus was saying to them, "A prophet is not without honour except in his home town and among his relatives and in his own household."
And he was not able to do any deed of power there, except that he laid his hands on a few sick people and healed them.
And he was amazed at their lack of trust. And he was going around the villages in a circuit, teaching.
And he calls the twelve to him and began to send them out two by two, and he was giving them authority over the unclean spirits.
And he ordered them to take nothing for the road except a staff only — no bread, no bag, no copper in the belt —
but to wear sandals, and "do not put on two tunics."
And he was saying to them, "Wherever you go into a house, stay there until you leave that place.

And any place that will not receive you or listen to you — as you leave there, shake off the dust under your feet as evidence to them." [I tell you the truth: it will be more bearable for Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgement than for that town.]
And they went out and proclaimed that people should change their minds,
and they were driving out many demons and anointing many sick people with oil and healing them.
And King Herod heard, for his name had become known, and they were saying, "John the Baptist has been raised from the dead, and that is why these powers are at work in him."
But others were saying, "He is Elijah"; and others were saying, "He is a prophet, like one of the prophets."
But when Herod heard he was saying, "John, whom I beheaded — this man has been raised."
For Herod himself had sent and seized John and bound him in prison, because of Herodias his brother Philip's wife, since he had married her.
For John was saying to Herod, "It is not permitted for you to have your brother's wife."
And Herodias had it in for him and was wanting to kill him — and could not,
for Herod was afraid of John, knowing him to be a righteous and holy man, and he was protecting him. And when he heard him he was very perplexed, and he was listening to him gladly.
And an opportune day came, when Herod on his birthday made a banquet for his officials and the commanders and the leading men of Galilee.
And when the daughter of Herodias herself came in and danced, she pleased Herod and those reclining with him. And the king said to the girl, "Ask me for whatever you want, and I will give it to you."
And he swore to her many times, "Whatever you ask me I will give you, up to half my kingdom."
And she went out and said to her mother, "What should I ask for?" And she said, "The head of John the Baptist."
And she came in at once, with haste, to the king and asked, saying, "I want you to give me right now, on a platter, the head of John the Baptist."
And the king became deeply grieved, but because of the oaths and those reclining with him he did not want to refuse her.
And at once the king sent an executioner and ordered him to bring his head. And he went off and beheaded him in the prison
and brought his head on a platter and gave it to the girl, and the girl gave it to her mother.
And when his disciples heard, they came and took his corpse and laid it in a tomb.
And the apostles gather to Jesus and reported to him everything — all they had done and all they had taught.
And he says to them, "Come away by yourselves to a deserted place and rest a little." For there were many coming and going, and they had no time even to eat.
And they went off in the boat to a deserted place by themselves.
And people saw them going, and many recognised them, and they ran together there on foot from all the towns and got there ahead of them.
And he came out and saw a large crowd, and he was moved with compassion for them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. And he began to teach them many things.
And when it was already late, his disciples came to him and were saying, "The place is deserted and it is already late.
Send them away, so that they can go into the surrounding countryside and villages and buy themselves something to eat."
But he answered and said to them, "You give them something to eat." And they say to him, "Should we go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread and give it to them to eat?"
And he says to them, "How many loaves do you have? Go and see." And when they knew, they say, "Five, and two fish."
And he ordered them to make everyone recline, group by group, on the green grass.
And they reclined in rows, in groups of a hundred and of fifty.
And he took the five loaves and the two fish, looked up to heaven, blessed and broke the loaves and was giving them to his disciples to set before them; and he divided the two fish among them all.
And they all ate and were filled,
and they took up twelve baskets full of broken pieces, and of the fish.
And those who ate the loaves were about five thousand men.
And at once he made his disciples get into the boat and go ahead to the other side, to Bethsaida, while he himself dismisses the crowd.
And after saying goodbye to them he went off to the mountain to pray.
And when evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea and he was alone on the land.
And seeing them tormented as they rowed — for the wind was against them — about the fourth watch of the night he comes to them, walking on the sea. And he was meaning to pass by them.
But when they saw him walking on the sea, they thought it was a ghost, and they screamed out;
for they all saw him and were shaken. But at once he spoke with them and says to them, "Take heart — it is I. Do not be afraid."
And he went up to them into the boat, and the wind dropped. And they were completely and utterly beside themselves,
for they had not understood about the loaves, but their heart was hardened.
And when they had crossed over to the land, they came to Gennesaret and moored there.
And when they came out of the boat, people recognised him at once,
and they ran around that whole region and began to carry the sick about on their mats to wherever they heard he was.

And wherever he went — into villages or towns or the countryside — they were putting the sick in the marketplaces and begging him that they might touch even the edge of his cloak; and as many as touched him were made well.

mark_7.t: And the Pharisees gather to him, and some of the teachers of the law who had come from Jerusalem.
And they saw that some of his disciples were eating their bread with defiled — that is, unwashed — hands.
For the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash their hands with a fist, holding to the tradition of the elders;

and when they come from the marketplace they do not eat unless they wash. And there are many other things they have received to hold to — washings of cups and jugs and copper vessels and dining couches.
And the Pharisees and the teachers of the law question him: "Why do your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders, but eat their bread with defiled hands?"
And he answered and said to them, "Isaiah prophesied well about you hypocrites, as it is written: 'This people honours me with their lips, but their heart is far away from me.
And they worship me in vain, teaching as teachings the commandments of people.'
You leave behind the commandment of God and hold to the tradition of people — washings of jugs and cups, and you do many other things like this.
And he was saying to them, "How nicely you set aside the commandment of God, so that you can establish your tradition!
For Moses said, 'Honour your father and your mother,' and, 'Whoever speaks evil of father or mother must certainly die.'
But you say, 'If a person says to his father or his mother, "Whatever you would have gained from me is Korban"' — that is, a gift —
then you no longer let him do anything for his father or his mother,
cancelling the word of God by your tradition, which you have handed down. And you do many things like this."
And he called the crowd to him again and was saying to them, "Listen to me, all of you, and understand.
There is nothing outside a person that can defile them by going into them; but the things that come out of a person — those are what defile a person."
[If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.]
And when he had gone into a house away from the crowd, his disciples were questioning him about the parable.
And he says to them, "Are you also without understanding? Don't you see that nothing that goes into a person from outside can defile them,
because it does not go into their heart but into the stomach, and goes out into the latrine?" (By saying this he made all foods clean.)
And he was saying, "What comes out of a person, that is what defiles a person.
For from inside, out of people's hearts, come the evil reasonings: sexual immorality, thefts, murders,
adulteries, greed, wickednesses, deceit, indecency, an evil eye, slander, arrogance, foolishness.
All these evil things come out from inside and defile a person."
And he got up from there and went off into the region of Tyre and Sidon. And he went into a house and did not want anyone to know — and he was not able to escape notice.
But at once a woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit heard about him, and she came and fell at his feet.
The woman was a Greek, Syrophoenician by race, and she was asking him to drive the demon out of her daughter.
And he was saying to her, "Let the children be fed full first; for it is not good to take the children's bread and throw it to the little dogs."
But she answered and says to him, "Yes, sir — and the little dogs under the table eat from the children's crumbs."
And he said to her, "Because of this word, go — the demon has gone out of your daughter."
And she went away to her house and found the child lying on the bed, and the demon gone.
And he went out again from the region of Tyre and came through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee, through the middle of the region of the Decapolis.
And they bring him a man who was deaf and could hardly speak, and they beg him to lay his hand on him.
And he took him aside from the crowd privately, put his fingers into his ears, and spat and touched his tongue,
and looking up to heaven he groaned and says to him, "Ephphatha," that is, "Be opened."
And at once his hearing was opened, and the bond of his tongue was loosened, and he was speaking properly.
And he ordered them to tell no one; but the more he ordered them, the more abundantly they proclaimed it.
And they were utterly astonished, saying, "He has done everything well. He even makes the deaf hear and the speechless speak."

mark_8.t: In those days, when there was again a large crowd and they had nothing to eat, he called the disciples to him and says to them,
"I am moved with compassion for the crowd, because they have already stayed with me three days and have nothing to eat.
And if I send them away to their homes hungry, they will collapse on the road — and some of them have come from a long way."
And his disciples answered him, "Where will anyone be able to get enough bread to feed these people here in a deserted place?"
And he was asking them, "How many loaves do you have?" And they said, "Seven."

And he orders the crowd to recline on the ground, and taking the seven loaves and giving thanks he broke them and was giving them to his disciples to set before them, and they set them before the crowd.
And they had a few small fish; and blessing them he said that these too should be set before them.
And they ate and were filled, and they took up seven large baskets of leftover pieces.
And there were about four thousand. And he sent them away.
And at once he got into the boat with his disciples and came into the district of Dalmanutha.
And the Pharisees came out and began to argue with him, looking for a sign from heaven from him, testing him.
And groaning deeply in his spirit he says, "Why does this generation look for a sign? I tell you the truth: no sign will be given to this generation."
And he left them, got into the boat again, and went off to the other side.
And they forgot to take bread, and they had only one loaf with them in the boat.
And he was warning them, saying, "Watch out — look out for the yeast of the Pharisees and the yeast of Herod."
And they were reasoning with one another, saying, "It is because we have no bread."
And knowing it, he says to them, "Why are you reasoning that you have no bread? Do you still not perceive or understand? Do you have your heart hardened?
Having eyes, do you not see? And having ears, do you not hear? And do you not remember?
When I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many baskets full of pieces did you take up?" They say to him, "Twelve."
"And when I broke the seven for the four thousand, how many large baskets full of pieces did you take up?" And they say to him, "Seven."
And he was saying to them, "Do you still not understand?"
And they come to Bethsaida. And they bring him a blind man and beg him to touch him.
And taking hold of the blind man's hand he brought him outside the village, and spitting into his eyes and laying his hands on him he was asking him, "Do you see anything?"
And he looked up and was saying, "I see people — because I see them like trees, walking."
Then he laid his hands on his eyes again, and he saw clearly and was restored, and he was seeing everything sharply.
And he sent him to his house, saying, "Do not even go into the village."
And Jesus went out, and his disciples, to the villages of Caesarea Philippi. And on the road he was asking his disciples, saying to them, "Who do people say that I am?"
And they told him, saying, "John the Baptist; and others, Elijah; and others, that you are one of the prophets."
And he was asking them, "But you — who do you say that I am?" Peter answered and says to him, "You are the Christ."
And he rebuked them, that they should tell no one about him.
And he began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected by the elders and the chief priests and the teachers of the law, and be killed, and after three days rise.
And he was speaking the word openly. And Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him.
But he turned around and, seeing his disciples, rebuked Peter and says, "Get behind me, Satan — because you are not minding the things of God but the things of people."
And he called the crowd to him with his disciples and said to them, "If anyone wants to follow after me, let him say no to himself and take up his cross and follow me.
For whoever wants to save his life will lose it; but whoever loses his life for my sake and the good news will save it.
For what does it benefit a person to gain the whole world and forfeit his life?
For what could a person give in exchange for his life?
For whoever is ashamed of me and my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when he comes in the glory of his Father with the holy angels."

mark_9.t: And he was saying to them, "I tell you the truth: there are some standing here who will not taste death until they see the kingdom of God come in power."
And six days later Jesus took Peter and James and John along and brought them up a high mountain by themselves, alone. And he was transformed in front of them,
and his clothes became dazzling, intensely white, like snow — the way no cloth-bleacher on earth could whiten them.
And Elijah appeared to them along with Moses, and they were talking with Jesus.
And Peter responds and says to Jesus, "Rabbi, it is good that we are here — let us make three shelters, one for you and one for Moses and one for Elijah."
— he did not know what to say, because they had become terrified.
And a cloud came, overshadowing them, and a voice came out of the cloud: "This is my son, the beloved. Listen to him."
And all at once, looking around, they no longer saw anyone — only Jesus with them.
And as they were coming down from the mountain he gave them strict orders to tell no one what they had seen, until the Son of Man should rise from the dead.
And they held on to that saying among themselves, arguing about what rising from the dead means.
And they were asking him, "Why do the scribes say that Elijah has to come first?"
And he said to them, "Elijah does come first and restores everything. And how is it written of the Son of Man that he should suffer much and be treated as nothing?"
"But I tell you, Elijah has in fact come, and they did to him whatever they wanted, just as it is written of him."
And when they came to the disciples they saw a large crowd around them and scribes arguing with them.
And at once the whole crowd, when they saw him, were completely astonished, and they ran up and greeted him.
And he asked them, "What are you arguing about with them?"
And one of the crowd answered him, "Teacher, I brought my son to you. He has a spirit that cannot speak."
"And wherever it takes hold of him it throws him down, and he foams and grinds his teeth and goes stiff. And I told your disciples to drive it out, and they were not strong enough."
And he answered them, "You generation without trust — how long will I be with you? How long will I put up with you? Bring him to me."
And they brought him to him. And when the spirit saw him it at once convulsed him, and he fell on the ground and rolled about, foaming.
And he asked his father, "How long has this been happening to him?" And he said, "From childhood."
"And it has often thrown him into fire and into water to destroy him. But if you can do anything, have compassion on us and help us."
And Jesus said to him, "'If you can' — everything is possible for the one who trusts."
At once the child's father cried out, in tears: "I trust — help my lack of trust!"
When Jesus saw that a crowd was rushing together he rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it, "Spirit that cannot speak and cannot hear, I command you: come out of him, and never enter him again."
And it cried out and convulsed him violently and came out, and the boy became like a corpse, so that most of them said he had died.
But Jesus took him by the hand and raised him, and he got up.
And when he had gone into a house his disciples asked him privately, "Why were we not able to drive it out?"
And he said to them, "This kind cannot come out by anything except prayer [and fasting]."
And they left there and were passing through Galilee, and he did not want anyone to know,

because he was teaching his disciples. And he was telling them, "The Son of Man is being handed over into human hands, and they will kill him, and once he has been killed, after three days he will rise."
But they did not understand what he said, and they were afraid to ask him.
And they came to Capernaum. And once he was in the house he asked them, "What were you discussing on the road?"
But they kept quiet, because on the road they had argued with one another about who was greatest.
And he sat down and called the twelve and says to them, "If anyone wants to be first, he shall be last of all and the one who serves all."
And he took a child and stood it in the middle of them, and he put his arms around it and said to them,
"Whoever welcomes one child like this in my name welcomes me; and whoever welcomes me is not welcoming me but the one who sent me."
John said to him, "Teacher, we saw someone driving out demons in your name, and he does not follow us, and we tried to stop him, because he was not following us."
But Jesus said, "Do not stop him. No one who does an act of power in my name will be able to speak evil of me straight afterwards."
"For whoever is not against us is for us."
"For whoever gives you a cup of water to drink on the ground that you belong to the Christ — I tell you the truth, he will certainly not lose his reward."
"And whoever trips up one of these little ones who trust in me — it would be better for him if a millstone the size a donkey turns were hung round his neck and he had been thrown into the sea."
"And if your hand trips you up, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life maimed than to have your two hands and go off into Gehenna, into the fire that is never put out —"
["where their worm does not die and the fire is not put out."]
"And if your foot trips you up, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life lame than to have your two feet and be thrown into Gehenna —"
["where their worm does not die and the fire is not put out."]
"And if your eye trips you up, throw it out. It is better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into Gehenna,
where their worm does not die and the fire is not put out."
"For everyone will be salted with fire."
"Salt is good. But if the salt loses its saltiness, what will you season it with? Have salt among yourselves, and be at peace with one another."

mark_10.t: And he got up and left there and comes into the territory of Judea and across the Jordan, and crowds gather to him again, and as he was used to doing he was teaching them again.
And Pharisees came up and were asking him whether it is permitted for a man to divorce a wife — testing him.
And he answered them, "What did Moses command you?"
And they said, "Moses permitted a man to write a certificate of separation and send her away."
And Jesus said to them, "He wrote you this command because of your hard-heartedness."
"But from the beginning of creation, 'God made them male and female.'"
"'For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife,'"
"'and the two will become one flesh.' So they are no longer two, but one flesh."
"So what God has yoked together, let no person separate."
And in the house the disciples were asking him about this again.
And he says to them, "Whoever divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery against her."
"And if she divorces her husband and marries another, she commits adultery."
And they were bringing children to him so that he might touch them, and the disciples rebuked them.
But when Jesus saw it he was angry and said to them, "Let the children come to me. Do not stop them. The kingdom of God belongs to people like these."
"I tell you the truth: whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child will never enter it."
And he took them in his arms and blessed them warmly, laying his hands on them.
And as he was setting out on the road, one man ran up and knelt in front of him and was asking him, "Good teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?"
And Jesus said to him, "Why do you call me good? No one is good except one — God."
"You know the commandments: do not murder, do not commit adultery, do not steal, do not give false testimony, do not defraud, honour your father and mother."
And he said to him, "Teacher, I have kept all these from my youth."
And Jesus looked straight at him and loved him and said to him, "One thing you lack. Go, sell whatever you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. And come, follow me."
But his face fell at the word and he went away grieving, because he had many possessions.
And Jesus looked around and says to his disciples, "How hard it will be for those who have money to enter the kingdom of God!"
And the disciples were astounded at his words. But Jesus responds again and says to them, "Children, how hard it is to enter the kingdom of God!"
"It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God."
And they were completely amazed, saying to one another, "Then who can be saved?"
Jesus looked straight at them and says, "With people it is impossible, but not with God. Everything is possible with God."
Peter began to say to him, "Look, we have left everything and have followed you."
Jesus said, "I tell you the truth: there is no one who has left house or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or fields for my sake and for the gospel's sake

who will not receive a hundred times as much now, in this present time — houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and fields, along with persecutions — and in the age that is coming, eternal life."
"But many who are first will be last, and the last first."

They were on the road going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was walking ahead of them, and they were astounded, and those following were afraid. And he took the twelve aside again and began to tell them what was about to happen to him:
"Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes, and they will condemn him to death and hand him over to the nations,
and they will mock him and spit on him and flog him and kill him, and after three days he will rise."
And James and John, the two sons of Zebedee, come up to him, saying to him, "Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we ask you."
And he said to them, "What do you want me to do for you?"
And they said to him, "Grant us to sit one at your right and one at your left in your glory."
But Jesus said to them, "You do not know what you are asking. Can you drink the cup I drink, or be baptised with the baptism I am baptised with?"
And they said to him, "We can." And Jesus said to them, "The cup I drink you will drink, and the baptism I am baptised with you will be baptised with.
But to sit at my right or at my left is not mine to give — it is for those for whom it has been prepared."
And when the ten heard, they began to be angry at James and John.
And Jesus called them to himself and says to them, "You know that those who are supposed to rule the nations lord it over them, and their great ones throw their weight around on them.
It is not like that among you. Whoever wants to become great among you shall be the one who serves you,
and whoever wants to be first among you shall be slave of all.
For even the Son of Man did not come to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many."
And they come to Jericho. And as he was leaving Jericho with his disciples and a sizeable crowd, the son of Timaeus — Bartimaeus, the blind beggar — was sitting beside the road.
And when he heard that it was Jesus the Nazarene he began to cry out and say, "Son of David, Jesus, have mercy on me!"
And many were telling him off, that he should be quiet. But he was crying out all the more, "Son of David, have mercy on me!"
And Jesus stopped and said, "Call him." And they call the blind man, saying to him, "Take heart — get up, he is calling you."
And he threw off his cloak, jumped up, and came to Jesus.
And Jesus answered him, "What do you want me to do for you?" And the blind man said to him, "Rabbouni, that I might see again."
And Jesus said to him, "Go. Your trust has saved you." And at once he saw again, and he was following him on the road.

mark_11.t: And when they come near to Jerusalem, to Bethphage and Bethany, at the Mount of Olives, he sends two of his disciples
and says to them, "Go into the village opposite you, and as soon as you go into it you will find a colt tied up, one no one has ever sat on. Untie it and bring it."
"And if anyone says to you, 'Why are you doing this?' say, 'The Lord needs it, and he is sending it back here at once.'"
And they went off and found a colt tied at a door, outside on the street, and they untie it.
And some of the people standing there were saying to them, "What are you doing, untying the colt?"
And they said to them what Jesus had said, and they let them go.
And they bring the colt to Jesus and throw their cloaks over it, and he sat on it.
And many spread their cloaks on the road, and others cut leafy branches out of the fields and spread them on the road.
And those going ahead and those following were shouting, "Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord!
Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David! Hosanna in the highest!"
And he went into Jerusalem, into the temple, and looked round at everything; and since it was already late he went out to Bethany with the twelve.
And the next day, when they had come out from Bethany, he was hungry.

And seeing a fig tree in the distance that had leaves, he went to see whether he would find anything on it. And when he came to it he found nothing but leaves — because it was not the season for figs.
