And he responded and said to it, "May no one ever eat fruit from you again." And his disciples were listening.

And they come to Jerusalem. And he went into the temple and began to throw out those selling and those buying in the temple, and he overturned the tables of the money-changers and the seats of those selling doves,
and he would not let anyone carry a vessel through the temple.
And he was teaching them and saying, "Is it not written, 'My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations'? But you have made it a bandits' cave."
And the chief priests and the scribes heard, and they were looking for a way to destroy him — because they were afraid of him, since the whole crowd was astounded at his teaching.
And whenever evening came, they would go out of the city.
And passing by early in the morning they saw the fig tree withered from the roots.
And Peter remembered and says to him, "Rabbi, look — the fig tree you cursed has withered."
And Jesus answered and says to them, "Have trust in God."
"I tell you the truth: whoever says to this mountain, 'Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,' and does not waver in his heart but trusts that what he says is happening — it will be his.
"For this reason I tell you: whatever you pray for and ask for, trust that you received it, and it will be yours.
"And whenever you stand praying, release whatever you have against anyone, so that your Father in the heavens may also release you your trespasses."
["But if you do not release, neither will your Father in the heavens release your trespasses."]
And they come to Jerusalem again. And as he was walking in the temple the chief priests and the scribes and the elders come to him
and were saying to him, "By what authority are you doing these things? Or who gave you this authority to do them?"
And Jesus said to them, "I will ask you one question. Answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.
The baptism of John — was it from heaven or from people? Answer me."
And they were arguing with one another, saying, "If we say 'From heaven', he will say, 'Then why did you not trust him?'
But if we say 'From people' — " They were afraid of the crowd, because everyone held that John really had been a prophet.
And they answered Jesus, "We do not know." And Jesus says to them, "Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things."

mark_12.t: And he began to speak to them in parables. "A man planted a vineyard and put a fence around it and dug out a wine-vat and built a tower, and he leased it to farmers and went away abroad.
And at the season he sent a slave to the farmers, to receive from the farmers some of the fruit of the vineyard.
And they took him and beat him and sent him away empty-handed.
And again he sent another slave to them; and that one they hit on the head and dishonoured.
And he sent another; and that one they killed — and many others, beating some and killing others.
He still had one, a beloved son. He sent him to them last of all, saying, 'They will respect my son.'
But those farmers said to one another, 'This is the heir. Come on, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.'
And they took him and killed him and threw him out of the vineyard.
"What will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the farmers and give the vineyard to others.
Have you not read this scripture: 'The stone the builders rejected — this one became the head of the corner;
this came from the Lord, and it is marvellous in our eyes'?"
And they were looking to seize him — and they were afraid of the crowd, because they knew he had told the parable against them. And they left him and went away.
And they send some of the Pharisees and the Herodians to him, to trap him in a word.

And they came and say to him, "Teacher, we know that you are truthful and that no one's opinion concerns you — you do not look at people's faces, but you teach the way of God in accordance with truth. Is it permitted to pay the poll tax to Caesar or not?"
Should we pay, or should we not?' But he saw through their pretence and said to them, 'Why are you testing me? Bring me a denarius so I can look at it.'
And they brought one. And he says to them, "Whose image is this, and whose inscription?" And they said to him, "Caesar's."
And Jesus said to them, "Give back to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's." And they were amazed at him.
And Sadducees come to him — the ones who say there is no resurrection — and they were asking him,
"Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if someone's brother dies and leaves a wife behind and does not leave a child, his brother should take the wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
There were seven brothers. And the first took a wife, and when he died he left no offspring.
And the second took her and died, leaving no offspring behind. And the third likewise.
And the seven left no offspring. Last of all the woman also died.
In the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife will she be? For the seven had her as wife."
Jesus said to them, "Is this not why you are going astray — because you do not know the scriptures or the power of God?
For when they rise from the dead they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but they are like the angels in the heavens.
But about the dead being raised — have you not read in the book of Moses, at the bush, how God spoke to him, saying, 'I am the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob'?
He is not God of the dead but of the living. You are going far astray."
And one of the scribes came up, having heard them arguing and seeing that he had answered them well, and asked him, "Which commandment is first of all?"
Jesus answered, "The first is: 'Hear, Israel — the Lord our God is one Lord;
and you shall love the Lord your God out of your whole heart and out of your whole soul and out of your whole mind and out of your whole strength.'
The second is this: 'You shall love your neighbour as yourself.' There is no other commandment greater than these."
And the scribe said to him, "Well said, teacher. You have spoken the truth, that he is one and there is no other besides him,

and to love him out of the whole heart and out of the whole understanding and out of the whole strength, and to love the neighbour as oneself, is far more than all the whole burnt offerings and sacrifices."
And Jesus, seeing that he had answered with intelligence, said to him, "You are not far from the kingdom of God." And no one dared to question him any more.
And Jesus responded, teaching in the temple, "How do the scribes say that the Christ is son of David?
David himself said, in the Holy Spirit, 'The Lord said to my lord: Sit at my right until I put your enemies under your feet.'
David himself calls him lord — so how is he his son?" And the large crowd was listening to him with pleasure.
And in his teaching he was saying, "Watch out for the scribes, who like to walk about in long robes and to be greeted in the marketplaces
and to have the front seats in the synagogues and the top places at dinners —
the ones who devour widows' houses and pray at length for show. These will receive a heavier judgement."
And he sat down opposite the treasury and was watching how the crowd throws copper into the treasury. And many rich people were throwing in a lot.
And one poor widow came and threw in two small coins, which make a quadrans.
And he called his disciples and said to them, "I tell you the truth: this poor widow has thrown in more than all those throwing into the treasury.
For they all threw in out of their surplus, but she out of her lack threw in everything she had — her whole life."

mark_13.t: And as he was going out of the temple one of his disciples says to him, "Teacher, look — what stones and what buildings!"
And Jesus said to him, "Do you see these great buildings? Not one stone will be left here on another that will not be thrown down."
And as he was sitting on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew were asking him privately,
"Tell us, when will these things be, and what is the sign when all these things are about to be brought to completion?"
And Jesus began to say to them, "Watch out that no one leads you astray.
Many will come on my name, saying, 'I am,' and they will lead many astray.
And when you hear of wars and reports of wars, do not be alarmed. It has to happen, but the end is not yet.
For nation will rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom. There will be earthquakes in place after place; there will be famines. These things are the beginning of birth-pangs.
But watch out for yourselves. They will hand you over to councils, and you will be beaten in synagogues, and you will stand before governors and kings for my sake, as a testimony to them.
And the gospel must first be proclaimed to all the nations.

And when they lead you away and hand you over, do not worry beforehand about what you will say; but whatever is given you in that hour, say that. For you are not the ones speaking, but the Holy Spirit.
And brother will hand over brother to death, and a father his child, and children will rise up against parents and put them to death.
And you will be hated by everyone because of my name. But the one who endures to the end — this one will be saved.
But when you see the desolating abomination standing where it should not — let the reader understand — then let those in Judea flee to the mountains.
Let the one on the roof not come down or go inside to take anything out of his house,
and let the one in the field not turn back to get his cloak.
And how terrible for those who are pregnant and those nursing in those days.
Pray that it does not happen in winter.
For those days will be a tribulation such as has not happened from the beginning of the creation that God created until now, and never will.
And if the Lord had not cut short the days, no flesh would be saved. But for the sake of the chosen, whom he chose, he cut short the days.
And then, if anyone says to you, 'Look, here is the Christ,' or 'Look, there,' do not trust it.
For false christs and false prophets will arise and will give signs and wonders to lead astray, if possible, the chosen.
But you, watch out. I have told you everything beforehand.
But in those days, after that tribulation, the sun will be darkened and the moon will not give its light,
and the stars will be falling out of the sky, and the powers in the heavens will be shaken.
And then they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory.
And then he will send out the angels and gather his chosen from the four winds, from the end of the earth to the end of heaven.
Learn the parable from the fig tree. Whenever its branch has already become tender and puts out leaves, you know that summer is near.
So also you, whenever you see these things happening, know that it is near, at the doors.
I tell you the truth: this generation will certainly not pass away until all these things have happened.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will certainly not pass away.
But about that day or the hour no one knows — not the angels in heaven, nor the Son — except the Father.
Watch out. Stay awake. You do not know when the time is.
It is like a man away from home who left his house and gave his slaves the authority, each with his own work, and commanded the doorkeeper to stay awake.
So stay awake — for you do not know when the master of the house is coming, whether late, or at midnight, or at cockcrow, or early —
so that he does not come suddenly and find you sleeping.
And what I say to you I say to everyone: stay awake.

mark_14.t: It was two days before the Passover and the Festival of Unleavened Bread, and the chief priests and the scribes were looking for a way to seize him by trickery and kill him.
For they were saying, "Not during the festival — there might be a riot of the people."

And while he was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, as he was reclining at table, a woman came with an alabaster jar of ointment — pure nard, very costly. She broke the jar and poured it over his head.
And some were indignant, saying to one another, "Why has this waste of the ointment happened?
This ointment could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii and given to the poor." And they were furious with her.
But Jesus said, "Leave her alone. Why are you making trouble for her? She has done a good work for me.
For you always have the poor with you, and whenever you want you can do good for them; but you do not always have me.
She did what she had. She anointed my body beforehand for burial.
I tell you the truth: wherever the gospel is proclaimed in the whole world, what she did will also be spoken of, in memory of her."
And Judas Iscariot, the one of the twelve, went off to the chief priests to hand him over to them.
And when they heard they were glad, and they promised to give him silver. And he was looking for a good opportunity to hand him over.
And on the first day of Unleavened Bread, when they were sacrificing the Passover lamb, his disciples say to him, "Where do you want us to go and prepare for you to eat the Passover?"
And he sends two of his disciples and says to them, "Go into the city, and a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him.
And wherever he goes in, say to the householder, 'The teacher says: Where is my guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?'
And he will show you a large upstairs room, furnished and ready. Prepare for us there."
And the disciples went out and came into the city and found it just as he had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
And when evening came he comes with the twelve.
And as they were reclining and eating, Jesus said, "I tell you the truth: one of you will hand me over — one eating with me."
They began to be grieved and to say to him one by one, "Surely not me?"
And he said to them, "One of the twelve — the one dipping into the one bowl with me.
For the Son of Man goes as it is written of him, but how terrible for that man through whom the Son of Man is handed over. It would have been good for him if that man had not been born."
And as they were eating he took bread, blessed it, broke it and gave it to them, and said, "Take[, eat]. This is my body."
And he took a cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, and they all drank from it.
And he said to them, "This is my blood of the covenant, poured out for many.
I tell you the truth: I will certainly not drink again from the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God."
And when they had sung the hymn they went out to the Mount of Olives.
And Jesus says to them, "You will all be tripped up, because it is written: 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.'
But after I am raised I will go ahead of you into Galilee."
But Peter said to him, "Even if they are all tripped up, I will not be."
And Jesus says to him, "I tell you the truth: today, this very night, before the cock crows twice, you will deny me three times."
But he kept saying all the more insistently, "If I have to die with you, I will never deny you." And they were all saying the same.
And they come to a place whose name was Gethsemane, and he says to his disciples, "Sit here while I pray."
And he takes Peter and James and John along with him, and he began to be utterly shaken and distressed.
And he says to them, "My soul is deeply grieved, to the point of death. Stay here and stay awake."
And he went forward a little and was falling on the ground and praying that if it were possible the hour might pass from him.
And he was saying, "Abba, Father — everything is possible for you. Take this cup away from me. But not what I want, but what you want."
And he comes and finds them sleeping, and says to Peter, "Simon, are you sleeping? Were you not strong enough to stay awake one hour?
Stay awake and pray that you do not come into testing. The spirit is willing but the flesh is weak."
And he went away again and prayed, saying the same words.
And he came again and found them sleeping, for their eyes were weighed down, and they did not know what to answer him.
And he comes the third time and says to them, "Sleep on now and take your rest. Enough. The hour has come. Look — the Son of Man is being handed over into the hands of sinners.
Get up, let us go. Look — the one handing me over has come near."
And at once, while he was still speaking, Judas arrives — one of the twelve — and with him a crowd with swords and clubs, from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.
The one handing him over had given them a signal, saying, "The one I kiss is him. Seize him and lead him away under guard."
And he came and at once went up to him and says, "Rabbi," and kissed him warmly.
And they laid hands on him and seized him.
But one of those standing by drew his sword and struck the high priest's slave and cut off his ear.
And Jesus responded and said to them, "Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest me as though I were a bandit?
Day after day I was with you in the temple teaching, and you did not seize me. But — so that the scriptures may be fulfilled."
And they all left him and fled.
And a certain young man was following him, with a linen cloth thrown over his bare body, and they seize him.
But he left the linen cloth behind and fled naked.
And they led Jesus away to the high priest, and all the chief priests and the elders and the scribes come together.
And Peter followed him at a distance, right into the courtyard of the high priest, and he was sitting with the attendants and warming himself at the fire.
And the chief priests and the whole council were looking for testimony against Jesus in order to put him to death, and they were not finding any.
For many were giving false testimony against him, and the testimonies did not agree.
And some stood up and were giving false testimony against him, saying,
"We heard him saying, 'I will destroy this sanctuary made with hands, and in three days I will build another, not made with hands.'"
And not even so did their testimony agree.
And the high priest stood up in the middle and questioned Jesus, "Do you answer nothing? What is it these men are testifying against you?"
But he was silent and answered nothing. Again the high priest questioned him and says to him, "Are you the Christ, the son of the Blessed One?"
And Jesus said, "I am. And you will see the Son of Man seated at the right of the Power and coming with the clouds of heaven."
And the high priest tore his clothes and says, "Why do we still need witnesses?
You heard the blasphemy. What do you think?" And they all condemned him as deserving death.
And some began to spit at him and to cover his face and to hit him with their fists and to say to him, "Prophesy!" And the attendants took him with slaps.
And while Peter was below in the courtyard, one of the high priest's servant girls comes,
and seeing Peter warming himself she looked straight at him and says, "You too were with the Nazarene, Jesus."
But he denied it, saying, "I neither know nor understand what you are saying." And he went outside into the forecourt. And a cock crowed.
And the servant girl saw him and began again to say to those standing there, "This man is one of them."
But he denied it again. And after a little while those standing there were saying to Peter again, "You really are one of them — you are a Galilean too[, and your speech matches]."
But he began to curse and to swear, "I do not know this man you are talking about."
And at once a cock crowed a second time. And Peter remembered the word Jesus had said to him: "Before a cock crows twice, you will deny me three times." And he broke down and wept.

mark_15.t: And at once, early in the morning, the chief priests held a council with the elders and scribes — the whole council — and they bound Jesus and led him away and handed him over to Pilate.
And Pilate questioned him, "Are you the king of the Jews?" And he answered him, "You say so."
And the chief priests were accusing him of many things.
And Pilate questioned him again, "Do you answer nothing? Look how many things they are accusing you of."
But Jesus answered nothing more, so that Pilate was amazed.
At the festival he used to release for them one prisoner, whomever they asked for.
And there was a man called Barabbas, imprisoned with the rebels who had committed murder in the uprising.
And the crowd came up and began to ask him to do as he usually did for them.
And Pilate answered them, "Do you want me to release for you the king of the Jews?"
For he knew that the chief priests had handed him over out of envy.
But the chief priests stirred up the crowd, so that he should release Barabbas for them instead.
And Pilate answered them again, "What then do you want me to do with the one you call the king of the Jews?"
And they shouted again, "Crucify him!"
And Pilate said to them, "Why? What evil has he done?" But they shouted all the more, "Crucify him!"
And Pilate, wanting to satisfy the crowd, released Barabbas for them, and he had Jesus flogged and handed him over to be crucified.
And the soldiers led him away inside the courtyard — that is, the praetorium — and they call together the whole cohort.
And they dress him in purple, and they twist together a crown of thorns and put it on him.
And they began to salute him: "Hail, king of the Jews!"
And they were striking his head with a reed and spitting at him, and they were kneeling down and bowing before him.
And when they had mocked him they stripped the purple off him and put his own clothes on him. And they lead him out to crucify him.
And they conscript a passer-by, Simon of Cyrene, coming in from the countryside — the father of Alexander and Rufus — to carry his cross.
And they bring him to the place Golgotha — which translated means Place of a Skull.
And they were giving him wine drugged with myrrh, but he did not take it.
And they crucify him, and they divide his clothes among themselves, casting lots for them to see who should take what.
It was the third hour, and they crucified him.
And the inscription of the charge against him was written up: The King of the Jews.
And with him they crucify two bandits, one at his right and one at his left.
[And the scripture was fulfilled that says, "And he was counted with the lawless."]
And those passing by were insulting him, shaking their heads and saying, "Aha! You who would destroy the sanctuary and build it in three days —
save yourself and come down from the cross!"
In the same way the chief priests, along with the scribes, were mocking him among themselves and saying, "He saved others; he cannot save himself.
Let the Christ, the king of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and trust." And those crucified with him were reviling him.
And when the sixth hour came, darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.
And at the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, "Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?" — which translated is, "My God, my God, why have you abandoned me?"
And some of those standing by heard it and were saying, "Look — he is calling Elijah."
And someone ran and filled a sponge with sour wine, put it on a reed and gave him a drink, saying, "Leave him. Let us see whether Elijah comes to take him down."
But Jesus let out a loud cry and breathed out his life.
And the curtain of the sanctuary was torn in two, from top to bottom.
And when the centurion standing opposite him saw that he breathed out his life like this, he said, "Truly this man was the Son of God."
And there were also women watching from a distance, among them Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome —
women who used to follow him and serve him when he was in Galilee, and many others who had come up with him to Jerusalem.
And when evening had already come, since it was the day of preparation — that is, the day before the sabbath —
Joseph of Arimathea came, a respected member of the council, who was himself also waiting for the kingdom of God, and he dared to go in to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
And Pilate was surprised that he had already died, and he called the centurion and asked him whether he had been dead for some time.
And when he learned it from the centurion he granted the corpse to Joseph.
And he bought a linen cloth, took him down, wrapped him in the linen cloth and laid him in a tomb that had been cut out of rock, and he rolled a stone against the door of the tomb.
And Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses were watching where he was laid.

mark_16.t: And when the sabbath had passed, Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of James and Salome bought spices, so that they could come and anoint him.
And very early on the first day of the week they come to the tomb, just after the sun had risen.
And they were saying to one another, "Who will roll the stone away from the door of the tomb for us?"
And they looked up and see that the stone has been rolled back — for it was extremely large.
And they went into the tomb and saw a young man sitting on the right, dressed in a white robe, and they were utterly shaken.
And he says to them, "Do not be shaken. You are looking for Jesus the Nazarene, the crucified one. He was raised. He is not here. Look — the place where they laid him.
But go, tell his disciples and Peter that he is going ahead of you into Galilee. There you will see him, just as he told you."

And they went out and fled from the tomb — trembling and bewilderment had hold of them. And they said nothing to anyone. They were afraid, for — [[And they briefly reported all they had been told to those around Peter. And after this Jesus himself sent out through them, from east to west, the holy and imperishable proclamation of eternal salvation. Amen.]]
[[And when he had risen, early on the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had driven out seven demons.
She went and reported to those who had been with him, who were mourning and weeping.
And when they heard that he was alive and had been seen by her, they did not believe it.
After this he appeared in a different form to two of them as they were walking, on their way into the country.
And they went and reported to the rest; they did not believe them either.
Later he appeared to the eleven themselves as they were reclining at table, and he rebuked their unbelief and hard-heartedness, because they had not believed those who had seen him risen.
And he said to them, "Go into all the world and proclaim the gospel to the whole creation.
The one who believes and is baptised will be saved; the one who does not believe will be condemned.
And these signs will accompany those who believe: in my name they will drive out demons, they will speak in new tongues,
and they will pick up snakes; and if they drink anything deadly it will certainly not harm them; they will lay hands on the sick and they will be well."
So then the Lord Jesus, after speaking to them, was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right of God.
And they went out and proclaimed everywhere, while the Lord worked with them and confirmed the word through the accompanying signs.]]

philippians_1.t: Paul and Timothy, servants of Christ Jesus, to all God's people in Christ Jesus who are in Philippi, together with the overseers and deacons:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I thank my God every time I remember you,
always, in every prayer of mine for all of you, making my prayer with joy
because of your partnership in the good news from the first day until now.
I am confident of this very thing: that the one who began a good work among you will bring it to completion by the day of Christ Jesus.
It is right for me to think this about all of you, because I hold you in my heart — you who all share with me in the grace, both in my chains and in the defence and confirmation of the good news.
God is my witness how I long for all of you with the deep affection of Christ Jesus.
And this is my prayer: that your love may overflow more and more in knowledge and every kind of discernment,
so that you can test what really matters, and be sincere and blameless for the day of Christ,
filled with the fruit of rightness that comes through Jesus Christ, to the glory and praise of God.
I want you to know, brothers and sisters, that what has happened to me has actually served to advance the good news,
so that it has become clear throughout the whole praetorium, and to everyone else, that my chains are for Christ.
and most of the brothers and sisters, made confident in the Lord by my chains, now dare all the more to speak God's word without fear.
Some, it is true, proclaim Christ out of envy and rivalry; others out of goodwill.
The one group acts out of love, knowing that I am put here for the defence of the gospel.
The other group proclaims Christ out of rivalry, not sincerely, supposing they can stir up trouble for me in my chains.
So what? Only this: in every way, whether from pretence or from truth, Christ is announced — and in that I rejoice. Yes, and I will go on rejoicing.
for I know that this will turn out for my deliverance through your prayer and the supply of the Spirit of Jesus Christ,

in keeping with my eager expectation and hope that I will be put to shame in nothing, but that with full boldness, now as always, Christ will be made great in my body, whether through life or through death.
For to me, living is Christ and dying is gain.
But if I go on living in the flesh, that means fruitful labour for me — and I do not know which I will choose.
I am hemmed in between the two. I have the desire to cast off and be with Christ, which is far better by much;
but to stay on in the flesh is more necessary for your sake.
Convinced of this, I know that I will remain and stay alongside all of you, for your advance and joy in the faith,
so that your boast may overflow in Christ Jesus on account of me, through my coming to you again.

Only conduct yourselves in a manner worthy of the good news of Christ, so that whether I come and see you or am absent, I may hear about you — that you are standing firm in one spirit, with one soul contending side by side for the faith of the good news,
and not frightened in anything by those who oppose you. This is a sign to them of destruction, but of your deliverance — and this from God.
For it has been given to you as a gift, on Christ's behalf, not only to believe in him but also to suffer for him,
having the same struggle you saw in me and now hear that I have.

philippians_2.t: So if there is any encouragement in Christ, any comfort from love, any sharing in the Spirit, any deep affection and mercy,
then complete my joy: think the same way, have the same love, be joined in soul, set your minds on the one thing.
Do nothing out of rivalry or empty conceit, but in humility consider one another as surpassing yourselves,
each of you looking not to your own interests but also to those of others.
Think this way among yourselves — the way that was also in Christ Jesus,
who, existing in the form of God, did not regard equality with God as something to be grasped,
but emptied himself by taking the form of a slave, coming to be in the likeness of human beings, and being found in appearance as a human
He humbled himself, becoming obedient as far as death — and death on a cross.
Therefore God also raised him to the highest place and gave him as a gift the name that is above every name,
so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bend — in heaven and on earth and under the earth —
and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
So then, my beloved, just as you have always obeyed — not only when I was present but now much more in my absence — work out your own salvation with fear and trembling,
for God is the one at work among you, producing both the willing and the working, for the sake of his good pleasure.
Do everything without grumbling and arguing,
so that you may be blameless and unmixed, children of God without fault in the middle of a crooked and twisted generation, among whom you shine like lights in the world,
holding out the word of life — so that on the day of Christ I may have a boast, that I did not run for nothing or labour for nothing.
But even if I am being poured out as a drink offering on the sacrifice and priestly service of your faith, I rejoice — and I rejoice together with all of you.
In the same way you also should rejoice and rejoice together with me.
I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon, so that I too may be encouraged when I learn how you are.
I have no one else of like soul who will genuinely care about your situation.
For they all seek their own interests, not those of Jesus Christ.
But you know his proven worth: that like a child with a father he served as a slave with me for the good news.
So I hope to send him as soon as I see how things go with me,
and I am confident in the Lord that I myself will come soon.
Still, I thought it necessary to send you Epaphroditus — my brother, co-worker and fellow soldier, and your envoy and minister to my need.
For he was longing for all of you and was distressed because you heard he had been ill.
He was indeed ill, close to death; but God had mercy on him — and not on him only but on me too, so that I would not have grief on top of grief.
So I am sending him all the more eagerly, so that when you see him again you may rejoice and I may be less grieved.
So welcome him in the Lord with all joy, and hold people like him in honour,
because for the work of Christ he came near to death, gambling with his own life, to make up what was lacking in your service to me.

philippians_3.t: Finally, my brothers and sisters, rejoice in the Lord. Writing the same things to you is no trouble to me, and it is a safeguard for you.
Watch out for the dogs, watch out for the evil workers, watch out for the mutilation.
For we are the circumcision — we who serve by the Spirit of God and boast in Christ Jesus and put no confidence in the flesh,
though I myself have grounds for confidence in the flesh as well. If anyone else thinks he has grounds for confidence in the flesh, I have more:
circumcised on the eighth day, from the people of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew born of Hebrews; as to the law, a Pharisee;
as to zeal, a persecutor of the community; as to the rightness that is in the law, blameless.
But whatever was gain to me, these things I have come to count as loss because of Christ.
More than that, I count everything as loss because of the surpassing worth of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord. For his sake I have lost all things, and I count them as rubbish, so that I may gain Christ
and be found in him, not having a rightness of my own that comes from law, but the one that comes through faith in Christ — the rightness from God that rests on trust,
so as to know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the sharing of his sufferings, being formed together with his death,
if somehow I may arrive at the resurrection out from the dead.
Not that I have already received it, or have already been brought to completion; but I pursue it, to see if I may take hold of that for which I was taken hold of by Christ Jesus.
Brothers and sisters, I do not reckon myself to have taken hold of it. But one thing: forgetting what is behind and stretching out toward what is ahead,
I press on toward the mark, for the prize of God's upward call in Christ Jesus.
So all of us who are mature should think this way; and if you think differently about anything, God will reveal that to you as well.
Only, as for what we have already reached — let us walk in line by the same rule and think the same way.
Join in imitating me, brothers and sisters, and watch those who walk as you have us for a pattern.
For many walk — I have often told you about them, and now I tell you weeping — as enemies of the cross of Christ.
Their end is destruction, their god is the belly, and their glory is in their shame; they think about earthly things.
For our citizenship exists in the heavens, and from there we eagerly await a Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ,
who will refashion the body of our lowliness so that it becomes formed like the body of his glory, by the working of his power to subject all things to himself.

philippians_4.t: So then, my brothers and sisters — loved and longed for, my joy and crown — stand firm in the Lord in this way, beloved.
I urge Euodia and I urge Syntyche to think the same way in the Lord.
Yes, and I ask you too, true companion: help these women, who contended alongside me in the good news, together with Clement and the rest of my co-workers, whose names are in the book of life.
Rejoice in the Lord always. I will say it again: rejoice.
Let your reasonableness be known to everyone. The Lord is near.
Do not be anxious about anything, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God;
and the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will stand guard over your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.

Finally, brothers and sisters: whatever is true, whatever is honourable, whatever is just, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever is well spoken of — if there is any excellence and anything praiseworthy — take these into account.
What you learned and received and heard and saw in me — do these things, and the God of peace will be with you.
I rejoiced greatly in the Lord that now at last you have made your concern for me bloom again. You were indeed concerned, but you had no opportunity.
I do not say this because I am in need; for I have learned to be content in whatever circumstances I am in.
I know how to be brought low, and I know how to have more than enough. In any and every situation I have been initiated into being well fed and going hungry, having plenty and going without.
I am strong enough for all these things in the one who empowers me.
Still, you did well to share with me in my hardship.
You Philippians know too that at the beginning of the good news, when I left Macedonia, no community entered into partnership with me in the matter of giving and receiving except you alone;
for even in Thessalonica you sent for my need more than once.
Not that I am seeking the gift; I am seeking the fruit that accumulates to your account.
I have been paid in full and have more than enough. I am fully supplied, having received from Epaphroditus what came from you — a fragrant aroma, an acceptable sacrifice, pleasing to God.
And my God will fill every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
To our God and Father be the glory for ever and ever. Amen.
Greet every one of God's people in Christ Jesus. The brothers and sisters with me greet you.
All God's people greet you, especially those from Caesar's household.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen. [To the Philippians, written from Rome by Epaphroditus.]

philemon_1.t: Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy our brother, to Philemon our beloved fellow worker,
and to Apphia our sister, and to Archippus our fellow soldier, and to the community that meets in your house:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I always thank my God, mentioning you in my prayers,
hearing of your love and of the trust that you have toward the Lord Jesus and for all God's people —
and I pray that the sharing of your trust may become effective in a full knowledge of every good thing that is in us, toward Christ.
For I had much joy and encouragement from your love, brother, because the hearts of God's people have been given rest through you.
So although I have plenty of boldness in Christ to order you to do what is fitting,
I would rather appeal on the basis of love — being what I am: Paul, an old man, and now a prisoner of Christ Jesus as well.
I appeal to you about my own child, whose father I became in my chains — Onesimus,
who once was useless to you but now is useful to you and to me.
I am sending him back to you — he is my own heart.
I wanted to keep him with me, so that he might serve me on your behalf while I am in chains for the gospel;
but I did not want to do anything without your consent, so that your good deed would not be forced but voluntary.
Perhaps this is why he was separated from you for a while — so that you might have him back forever,
no longer as a slave, but more than a slave: a beloved brother — most of all to me, and how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord.
So if you consider me a partner, welcome him as you would welcome me.
And if he wronged you in any way, or owes you anything, charge it to me.
I, Paul, am writing this with my own hand: I will repay it — not to mention that you owe me your very self besides.
Yes, brother — let me have some use of you in the Lord. Give my heart rest in Christ.
Confident of your obedience, I write to you, knowing that you will do even more than I say.
At the same time, get a guest room ready for me — for I hope that through your prayers I will be given back to you.
Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, greets you,
as do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke — my fellow workers.
The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.

revelation_1.t: An unveiling of Jesus Christ, which God gave him to show his servants what has to happen soon — and he signalled it by sending it through his messenger to his servant John,
who testified to the word of God and to the testimony of Jesus Christ — everything he saw.
Blessed is the one who reads aloud, and blessed are those who hear the words of the prophecy and keep what is written in it — because the time is near.
John, to the seven communities in Asia: grace to you and peace from the One who is and who was and who is coming, and from the seven spirits before his throne,
and from Jesus Christ, the faithful witness, the firstborn from the dead and the ruler of the kings of the earth. To the one who loves us and released us from our sins by his blood
and made us a kingdom, priests to his God and Father — to him be the glory and the power forever and ever. Amen.
Look — he is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see him, including those who pierced him; and all the tribes of the earth will beat their breasts on account of him. Yes. Amen.
I am the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end, says the Lord God — the One who is and who was and who is coming, the Almighty.
I, John, your brother and partner in the persecution and the kingdom and the endurance that are in Jesus, was on the island called Patmos because of the word of God and the testimony of Jesus Christ.
I was in the Spirit on the Lord's day, and I heard behind me a loud voice like a trumpet
saying: What you see, write in a scroll and send it to the seven communities — to Ephesus and Smyrna and Pergamum and Thyatira and Sardis and Philadelphia and Laodicea.
I turned to see the voice that was speaking with me, and when I turned I saw seven gold lampstands,
and in the middle of the lampstands someone like a son of man, dressed in a robe down to his feet and belted across the chest with a gold sash.
His head and his hair were white like wool, white as snow, and his eyes like a flame of fire,
and his feet like burnished bronze refined in a furnace, and his voice like the sound of rushing water,
and holding seven stars in his right hand, and a sharp two-edged sword coming out of his mouth, and his face like the sun shining at full strength.
When I saw him I fell at his feet like a dead man. He laid his right hand on me and said: Do not be afraid. I am the first and the last,
and the living one. I was dead, and look — I am alive forever and ever. And I hold the keys of death and of Hades.
So write what you saw, and what is, and what is going to happen after this —
As for the mystery of the seven stars you saw in my right hand and the seven gold lampstands: the seven stars are the angels of the seven communities, and the seven lampstands are seven communities.

revelation_2.t: To the messenger of the community in Ephesus write: This is what the one who holds the seven stars in his right hand says, the one who walks among the seven gold lampstands.
I know your works and your labour and your endurance, and that you cannot bear people who are evil. You tested those who call themselves apostles and are not, and you found them false.
You have endured, and you have carried the load for the sake of my name, and you have not grown weary.
But I have this against you: you have let go of your first love.

So remember where you have fallen from, and change your mind, and do the works you did at first. If not, I am coming to you and I will move your lampstand out of its place — unless you change your mind.
But you do have this: you hate what the Nicolaitans do, which I also hate.
Whoever has an ear, listen to what the Spirit is saying to the communities. To the one who conquers I will give the right to eat from the tree of life, which is in the paradise of my God.
And to the messenger of the community in Smyrna write: This is what the first and the last says, who was dead and came to life:
I know your affliction and your poverty — but you are rich — and the slander from those who say they are Jews and are not, but are a synagogue of Satan.

Do not fear what you are about to suffer. Look — the devil is about to throw some of you into prison so that you may be tested, and you will have affliction for ten days. Be faithful to the point of death, and I will give you the crown of life.
Whoever has an ear, listen to what the Spirit is saying to the communities. The one who conquers will certainly not be harmed by the second death.
And to the messenger of the community in Pergamum write: This is what the one who has the sharp two-edged sword says:

I know where you live — where Satan's throne is. And you hold on to my name, and you did not deny your trust in me, even in the days of Antipas my faithful witness, who was killed among you, where Satan lives.

But I have a few things against you: you have people there who hold to the teaching of Balaam, who taught Balak to put a trap in front of the sons of Israel — to eat food sacrificed to idols and to commit sexual immorality.
In the same way you also have people who hold to the teaching of the Nicolaitans.
So change your mind. If not, I am coming to you quickly, and I will make war against them with the sword of my mouth.

Whoever has an ear, listen to what the Spirit is saying to the communities. To the one who conquers I will give some of the hidden manna, and I will give him a white stone, and on the stone a new name written that no one knows except the one receiving it.
And to the messenger of the community in Thyatira write: This is what the Son of God says, the one whose eyes are like a flame of fire and whose feet are like burnished bronze:
I know your works — your love and trust and service and endurance — and that your recent works are greater than the first ones.
But I have this against you: you tolerate the woman Jezebel, who calls herself a prophet and teaches and misleads my servants into sexual immorality and eating food sacrificed to idols.
I gave her time to change her mind, and she does not want to change her mind about her immorality.
Look — I am throwing her onto a bed, and those who commit adultery with her into great affliction, unless they change their minds about what she does.
And I will kill her children with death, and all the communities will know that I am the one who searches minds and hearts, and I will give to each of you according to your works.
But to the rest of you in Thyatira — all who do not hold this teaching, who have not known what they call the deep things of Satan — I say this: I am not putting any other burden on you.
Only hold on to what you have until I come.
And the one who conquers and keeps my works to the end — I will give him authority over the nations,
and he will shepherd them with an iron rod, as clay pots are shattered —
as I also have received from my Father. And I will give him the morning star.
Whoever has an ear, listen to what the Spirit is saying to the communities.

revelation_3.t: And to the messenger of the community in Sardis write: This is what the one who has the seven spirits of God and the seven stars says: I know your works — that you have a name for being alive, and you are dead.
Wake up, and strengthen what remains, which was about to die — because I have not found your works completed in the sight of my God.
So remember what you received and heard, and keep it, and change your mind. If you do not wake up, I will come like a thief, and you will not know at what hour I will come to you.
But you have a few names in Sardis who have not defiled their clothes, and they will walk with me in white, because they are worthy.

The one who conquers will be dressed like this, in white clothes, and I will certainly not wipe his name out of the book of life, and I will acknowledge his name before my Father and before his angels.
Whoever has an ear, listen to what the Spirit is saying to the communities.

And to the messenger of the community in Philadelphia write: This is what the holy one says, the true one, the one who has the key of David — who opens and no one will shut, and shuts and no one opens:
I know your works. Look — I have put in front of you an open door that no one is able to shut, because you have a little power, and you kept my word and did not deny my name.

Look — I am handing over some from the synagogue of Satan, those who say they are Jews and are not but are lying. Look, I will make them come and bow down before your feet, and know that I have loved you.
Because you kept the word of my endurance, I will also keep you from the hour of testing that is coming on the whole inhabited world, to test those who live on the earth.
I am coming quickly. Hold on to what you have, so that no one takes your crown.

The one who conquers — I will make him a pillar in the sanctuary of my God, and he will never go outside again. And I will write on him the name of my God, and the name of the city of my God, the new Jerusalem that comes down out of heaven from my God, and my own new name.
Whoever has an ear, listen to what the Spirit is saying to the communities.
And to the messenger of the community in Laodicea write: This is what the Amen says, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of God's creation:
I know your works — that you are neither cold nor hot. I wish you were cold or hot!
So because you are lukewarm — neither hot nor cold — I am about to vomit you out of my mouth.
because you say: I am rich, I have grown rich, I need nothing — and you do not know that you are the wretched one, the pitiable one, poor and blind and naked.

I advise you to buy from me gold refined by fire so that you may be rich, and white clothes to wear so that the shame of your nakedness is not exposed, and ointment to rub on your eyes so that you can see.
I rebuke and discipline everyone I love. So be earnest, and change your mind.
Look — I am standing at the door and knocking. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in to him and eat with him, and he with me.
The one who conquers — I will give him the right to sit with me on my throne, just as I also conquered and sat down with my Father on his throne.
Whoever has an ear, listen to what the Spirit is saying to the communities.

revelation_4.t: After this I looked, and there was a door standing open in heaven. And the first voice I had heard, like a trumpet speaking with me, said: Come up here, and I will show you what has to happen after this.
At once I was in the Spirit, and there was a throne standing in heaven, and someone seated on the throne.
And the one seated looked like jasper and carnelian, and a rainbow around the throne looked like emerald.
Around the throne were twenty-four thrones, and on the thrones I saw twenty-four elders seated, dressed in white clothes, with gold crowns on their heads.
Out of the throne come flashes of lightning and rumblings and thunder. And seven torches of fire burn before the throne, which are the seven spirits of God.
And in front of the throne there was something like a sea of glass, like crystal. And in the middle of the throne and around the throne, four living creatures full of eyes in front and behind.
The first living creature was like a lion, the second living creature like an ox, the third living creature had a face like a human face, and the fourth living creature was like a flying eagle.

And the four living creatures, each one of them, had six wings, and they are full of eyes all around and inside. And day and night they never stop saying: Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, who was and who is and who is coming.
And whenever the living creatures give glory and honour and thanks to the one seated on the throne, who lives forever and ever,
the twenty-four elders fall down before the one seated on the throne and worship the one who lives forever and ever, and they throw their crowns down in front of the throne, saying:
You are worthy, our Lord and God, the holy one, to receive the glory and the honour and the power — because you created all things, and by your will they existed and were created.

revelation_5.t: And I saw on the right hand of the one seated on the throne a scroll written on the inside and on the back, sealed with seven seals.
And I saw a strong angel proclaiming with a loud voice: Who is worthy to open the scroll and break its seals?
And no one in heaven or on earth or under the earth was able to open the scroll or to look at it.
And I wept a great deal, because no one was found worthy to open the scroll or to read it or to look at it.
And one of the elders says to me: Do not weep. Look — the Lion from the tribe of Judah, the root of David, has conquered, so that he can open the scroll and its seven seals.

And I saw, in the middle of the throne and of the four living creatures and in the middle of the elders, a little lamb standing as though it had been slaughtered, with seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven spirits of God sent out into all the earth.
And he came and took the scroll out of the right hand of the one seated on the throne.

And when he took the scroll, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fell down before the Lamb, each holding a harp and gold bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of God's holy people.

And they sing a new song: You are worthy to take the scroll and to open its seals, because you were slaughtered, and by your blood you bought people for God from every tribe and language and people and nation,
and you made them a kingdom and priests for our God, and they will reign on the earth.

And I looked, and I heard the sound of many angels around the throne and the living creatures and the elders. And their number was tens of thousands times tens of thousands, and thousands times thousands,
saying with a loud voice: Worthy is the Lamb who was slaughtered to receive the power and wealth and wisdom and strength and honour and glory and blessing.

And every created thing in heaven and on the earth and under the earth and on the sea, and everything in them, I heard saying: To the one seated on the throne and to the Lamb be the blessing and the honour and the glory and the might forever and ever.
And the four living creatures said: Amen. And the elders fell down and worshipped.

revelation_6.t: And I watched as the Lamb opened one of the seven seals, and I heard one of the four living creatures say, with a voice like thunder: Come!
And I looked, and there was a white horse, and its rider held a bow. And a crown was given to him, and he went out conquering and to conquer.
And when he opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature say: Come!
And another horse went out, fiery red. And to its rider it was given to take peace from the earth, so that people would slaughter one another. And a great sword was given to him.
And when he opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature say: Come! And I looked, and there was a black horse, and its rider held a pair of scales in his hand.

And I heard what sounded like a voice among the four living creatures saying: A quart of wheat for a day's wage, and three quarts of barley for a day's wage — and do not damage the olive oil and the wine.
And when he opened the fourth seal, I heard the voice of the fourth living creature say: Come!

And I looked, and there was a pale green horse, and its rider — his name was Death, and Hades was following with him. And authority was given to them over a quarter of the earth, to kill by sword and famine and death and by the wild animals of the earth.
And when he opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of those who had been slaughtered because of the word of God and because of the testimony they had given.
And they cried out with a loud voice: How long, Sovereign Lord, holy and true, until you judge and avenge our blood on those who live on the earth?

And a white robe was given to each of them, and they were told to rest a little longer, until the number of their fellow slaves and their brothers and sisters who were about to be killed, as they had been, was complete.
And I watched as he opened the sixth seal, and there was a great earthquake, and the sun turned black like sackcloth made of hair, and the whole moon became like blood,
and the stars of the sky fell to the earth like a fig tree dropping its late figs when it is shaken by a strong wind,
and the sky was split apart like a scroll being rolled up, and every mountain and island was moved out of its place.
And the kings of the earth and the great men and the commanders and the rich and the strong, and every slave and every free person, hid themselves in the caves and among the rocks of the mountains,
and they say to the mountains and the rocks: Fall on us, and hide us from the face of the one seated on the throne and from the anger of the Lamb —
because the great day of their anger has come, and who is able to stand?

revelation_7.t: After this I saw four angels standing at the four corners of the earth, holding back the four winds of the earth so that no wind would blow on the earth or on the sea or on any tree.

And I saw another angel coming up from where the sun rises, holding the seal of the living God. And he called out with a loud voice to the four angels who had been given power to damage the earth and the sea,
saying: Do not damage the earth or the sea or the trees until we have sealed the servants of our God on their foreheads.
And I heard the number of those who were sealed: a hundred and forty-four thousand, sealed from every tribe of the sons of Israel.
From the tribe of Judah twelve thousand sealed, from the tribe of Reuben twelve thousand, from the tribe of Gad twelve thousand,
from the tribe of Asher twelve thousand, from the tribe of Naphtali twelve thousand, from the tribe of Manasseh twelve thousand,
from the tribe of Simeon twelve thousand, from the tribe of Levi twelve thousand, from the tribe of Issachar twelve thousand,
from the tribe of Zebulun twelve thousand, from the tribe of Joseph twelve thousand, from the tribe of Benjamin twelve thousand sealed.

After this I looked, and there was a huge crowd that no one could count, from every nation and tribe and people and language, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, dressed in white robes with palm branches in their hands.
And they cry out with a loud voice: Salvation belongs to our God, who is seated on the throne, and to the Lamb.
And all the angels were standing around the throne and the elders and the four living creatures, and they fell on their faces before the throne and worshipped God,
saying: Amen. The blessing and the glory and the wisdom and the thanksgiving and the honour and the power and the strength belong to our God forever and ever. Amen.
And one of the elders spoke up and said to me: These people dressed in the white robes — who are they, and where did they come from?
And I said to him: My lord, you know. And he said to me: These are the ones coming out of the great affliction, and they washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.
That is why they are before the throne of God, and they serve him day and night in his sanctuary, and the one seated on the throne will shelter them with his presence.
They will not be hungry any more, or thirsty any more; the sun will not beat down on them, nor any scorching heat,
because the Lamb at the centre of the throne will shepherd them and guide them to springs of living water, and God will wipe away every tear from their eyes.

revelation_8.t: And when he opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven for about half an hour.
And I saw the seven angels who stand before God, and seven trumpets were given to them.

And another angel came and stood at the altar, holding a gold censer. And he was given a great deal of incense to offer with the prayers of all God's holy people on the gold altar in front of the throne.
And the smoke of the incense went up with the prayers of God's holy people, from the angel's hand, before God.
And the angel took the censer and filled it with fire from the altar and threw it on the earth. And there were thunder and rumblings and lightning and an earthquake.
And the seven angels holding the seven trumpets got ready to blow them.

And the first angel blew his trumpet, and there came hail and fire mixed with blood, and it was thrown on the earth. A third of the earth was burnt up, and a third of the trees were burnt up, and all the green grass was burnt up.
And the second angel blew his trumpet, and something like a great mountain burning with fire was thrown into the sea. And a third of the sea became blood,
and a third of the creatures in the sea that had life died, and a third of the ships were destroyed.
And the third angel blew his trumpet, and a great star fell from the sky, burning like a torch, and it fell on a third of the rivers and on the springs of water.
And the name of the star is called Wormwood. And a third of the waters turned to wormwood, and many people died from the waters, because they had been made bitter.

And the fourth angel blew his trumpet, and a third of the sun was struck, and a third of the moon, and a third of the stars, so that a third of them went dark — and the day lost a third of its light, and the night too.

And I looked, and I heard a single eagle flying high overhead, saying with a loud voice: Woe, woe, woe to those who live on the earth, because of the remaining trumpet blasts of the three angels who are about to sound them.

revelation_9.t: And the fifth angel blew his trumpet, and I saw a star that had fallen from the sky to the earth, and the key to the shaft of the abyss was given to him.
And he opened the shaft of the abyss, and smoke went up out of the shaft like the smoke of a huge furnace, and the sun and the air were darkened by the smoke from the shaft.
And out of the smoke locusts came onto the earth, and they were given power like the power that scorpions of the earth have.
And they were told not to damage the grass of the earth or any green plant or any tree, but only the people who do not have God's seal on their foreheads.
And they were not allowed to kill them, only to torture them for five months. And their torture was like the torture of a scorpion when it strikes a person.
And in those days people will look for death and will certainly not find it. They will long to die, and death runs away from them.
And the locusts looked like horses prepared for battle. On their heads were what looked like crowns of gold, and their faces were like human faces,
and they had hair like women's hair, and their teeth were like lions' teeth,
and they had chest armour like iron breastplates, and the sound of their wings was like the sound of many horses and chariots charging into battle.
And they have tails like scorpions, and stings; and in their tails is their power to damage people for five months.
They have a king over them — the angel of the abyss. His name in Hebrew is Abaddon, and in Greek he has the name Apollyon.
The first woe has passed. Look — two more woes are still coming after this.
And the sixth angel blew his trumpet, and I heard one voice from the four horns of the gold altar that is before God,
saying to the sixth angel, the one holding the trumpet: Release the four angels bound at the great river Euphrates.
And the four angels were released — the ones prepared for the hour and the day and the month and the year — to kill a third of humanity.
And the number of the mounted troops was two hundred million; I heard their number.

And this is how I saw the horses in the vision, and those riding them: they had breastplates of fire red and dark blue and sulphur yellow, and the heads of the horses were like lions' heads, and out of their mouths came fire and smoke and sulphur.
By these three plagues a third of humanity was killed — by the fire and the smoke and the sulphur coming out of their mouths.
For the power of the horses is in their mouths and in their tails; for their tails are like snakes, with heads, and with them they do damage.

And the rest of humanity, the ones not killed by these plagues, did not change their minds about the works of their hands. They would not stop worshipping the demons and the idols of gold and silver and bronze and stone and wood, which cannot see or hear or walk.
And they did not change their minds about their murders or their drugs or their sexual immorality or their thefts.

revelation_10.t: And I saw another strong angel coming down out of heaven, wrapped in a cloud, with the rainbow over his head, and his face like the sun, and his feet like pillars of fire.
And he was holding in his hand a little scroll, opened. And he set his right foot on the sea and his left on the land,
and he shouted with a loud voice, like a lion roaring. And when he shouted, the seven thunders spoke with their own voices.
And when the seven thunders spoke, I was about to write; and I heard a voice from heaven saying to me: Seal up what the seven thunders said, and do not write it.
And the angel I had seen standing on the sea and on the land raised his right hand to heaven
and swore by the one who lives forever and ever, who created heaven and what is in it and the earth and what is in it and the sea and what is in it: There will be no more delay.
But in the days when the seventh angel is about to sound his trumpet, the mystery of God will be completed, as he announced to his servants the prophets.
And the voice I had heard from heaven spoke with me again and said: Go, take the scroll that is open in the hand of the angel standing on the sea and on the land.
And I went to the angel and asked him to give me the little scroll. And he says to me: Take it and eat it up. It will make your stomach bitter, but in your mouth it will be sweet as honey.
And I took the little scroll from the angel's hand and ate it up, and in my mouth it was sweet as honey — and when I had eaten it, my stomach turned bitter.
And they say to me: You must prophesy again about many peoples and nations and languages and kings.

revelation_11.t: And I was given a measuring rod like a staff, and I was told: Get up and measure the sanctuary of God and the altar, and those worshipping in it.
But leave out the courtyard outside the sanctuary; do not measure it, because it has been given to the nations, and they will trample the holy city for forty-two months.
And I will give my two witnesses authority, and they will prophesy for 1,260 days, dressed in sackcloth.
These are the two olive trees and the two lampstands that stand before the Lord of the earth.
And if anyone wants to harm them, fire comes out of their mouth and consumes their enemies. And if anyone should want to harm them, that is how he must be killed.

These have the authority to shut the sky so that no rain falls during the days of their prophesying, and they have authority over the waters to turn them into blood, and to strike the earth with every kind of plague as often as they want.
And when they have finished their testimony, the beast that comes up out of the abyss will make war with them and will conquer them and kill them.
And their corpse will lie on the main street of the great city — the city that is called, spiritually, Sodom and Egypt — where their Lord was also crucified.
And for three and a half days, people from the peoples and tribes and languages and nations look at their corpses, and they do not allow their corpses to be put in a tomb.
And those who live on the earth celebrate over them and are glad, and they will send each other gifts, because these two prophets tortured those who live on the earth.
And after the three and a half days, a breath of life from God entered them, and they stood up on their feet, and great fear fell on those watching them.
And they heard a loud voice from heaven saying to them: Come up here. And they went up to heaven in the cloud, and their enemies watched them.
And at that hour there was a great earthquake, and a tenth of the city fell, and seven thousand people were killed in the earthquake. And the rest were terrified and gave glory to the God of heaven.
The second woe has passed. Look — the third woe is coming quickly.
And the seventh angel blew his trumpet, and there were loud voices in heaven saying: The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of his Christ, and he will reign forever and ever.
And the twenty-four elders who sit on their thrones before God fell on their faces and worshipped God,
saying: We thank you, Lord God Almighty, the One who is and who was, because you have taken your great power and begun to reign.

and the nations were angry, and your anger came, and the time for the dead to be judged, and to give the reward to your servants the prophets and to God's holy people and to those who fear your name, small and great, and to destroy those destroying the earth.
And the sanctuary of God in heaven was opened, and the ark of his covenant was seen in his sanctuary. And there came flashes of lightning and rumblings and thunder and an earthquake and heavy hail.

revelation_12.t: Then a great sign appeared in the sky: a woman clothed with the sun, the moon under her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars.
She was pregnant, and she cries out in labour, in agony to give birth.
Then another sign appeared in the sky: a great fiery-red dragon with seven heads and ten horns, and seven royal crowns on his heads.

His tail drags a third of the stars of the sky, and he threw them to the earth. And the dragon has stood before the woman who is about to give birth, so that when she gives birth he can devour her child.
And she bore a son, a male, who is going to shepherd all the nations with an iron rod. And her child was snatched away to God and to his throne.
And the woman fled into the wilderness, where she has there a place prepared from God, so that there they would feed her one thousand two hundred and sixty days.
And there came war in heaven. Michael and his angels — to make war with the dragon; and the dragon made war, and his angels,
and he was not strong enough, nor was a place found for them any longer in heaven.

And the great dragon was thrown down — the ancient serpent, the one called Devil and the Satan, the one deceiving the whole inhabited world — he was thrown down to the earth, and his angels were thrown down with him.

And I heard a loud voice in heaven saying: 'Now has come the rescue and the power and the kingdom of our God, and the authority of his Christ, because the accuser of our brothers and sisters was thrown down — the one accusing them before our God day and night.'
And they themselves conquered him through the blood of the Lamb and through the word of their testimony, and they did not love their life as far as death.
Because of this, be glad, you heavens and all who tent in them. Woe to those who inhabit the earth and the sea, because the devil went down to you having great rage, knowing that he has little time.
And when the dragon saw that he had been thrown to the earth, he pursued the woman who bore the male.

And the woman was given the two wings of the great eagle, so that she could fly into the wilderness into her place, where she is fed there a time and times and half a time, from the face of the serpent.
And the serpent threw water like a river out of his mouth after the woman, so that he might make her river-carried — swept away in the flood.
And the earth helped the woman: the earth opened its mouth and swallowed the river which the dragon threw out of his mouth.
And the dragon was enraged at the woman, and went off to make war with the rest of her seed — those who keep the commandments of God and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.
And he stood on the sand of the sea.

revelation_13.t: And I saw a beast coming up out of the sea, having ten horns and seven heads, and on its horns ten royal crowns, and on its heads names of blasphemy.
And the beast I saw was like a leopard, and its feet like a bear's, and its mouth like a lion's mouth. And the dragon gave it his power and his throne and great authority.
And I saw one of its heads as though slaughtered to death, and the wound of its death was healed. And there was wonder in whole the earth after the beast,
and they worshipped the dragon because he gave the authority to the beast, and they worshipped the beast, saying: 'Who is like the beast? And who is able to make war with it?'
And it was given a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies, and it was given authority to make war forty-two months.
And it opened its mouth in blasphemies toward God — to blaspheme his name and his tent, those who tent in heaven.
And it was given power to make war with God's holy ones and to conquer them, and it was given authority over every tribe and people and language and nation.
And all who inhabit the earth will worship it — everyone whose name has not been written from the founding of the world in the book of life of the Lamb who was slaughtered.
If anyone has an ear, let them hear.
If anyone gathers into captivity, into captivity he goes. If anyone by sword to be killed — he must by sword be killed. Here is the endurance and the trust of God's holy ones.
And I saw another beast coming up out of the earth. It had two horns like a lamb, and it spoke like a dragon.
And it does all the authority of the first beast in its presence, and it makes the earth and those who inhabit it worship the first beast, the one whose wound of its death was healed.
And it does great signs, even making fire come down out of the sky to the earth before people.

And it deceives my own, those who inhabit the earth, through the signs which were given to it to do before the beast — telling those who inhabit the earth to make an image for the beast who has the wound from the sword and lived.

And it was given power to give breath to the image of the beast, so that the image of the beast could even speak, and could bring it about that all who do not worship the image of the beast are killed.
And it makes all — the small and the great, the rich and the poor, the free and the slaves — that they should give them a mark on their right hand or on their forehead,
and so that no one can buy or sell except the one who has the mark — the name of the beast or the number of its name.
Here is the wisdom. Let the one who has the mind calculate the number of the beast, for it is a number of a human, and its number is six hundred and sixty-six.

revelation_14.t: Then I looked, and there was the Lamb standing on Mount Zion, and with him a number, one hundred and forty-four thousand, having his name and his Father's name written on their foreheads.
And I heard a sound out of heaven like the sound of many waters and like the sound of great thunder; and the sound I heard was like harpists harping on their harps.

And they sing what is like a new song before the throne and before the four living creatures and the elders; and no one could learn the song except the hundred and forty-four thousand, the ones purchased from the earth.

These are the ones who were not defiled with women, for they are virgins. These are the ones who follow the Lamb wherever he goes. These were purchased from among humanity, a firstfruit to God and to the Lamb,
And no falsehood was found in their mouth; they are without blemish.
Then I saw another angel flying in mid-heaven, having an eternal good news to announce upon those who sit on the earth — upon every nation and tribe and language and people.
He said in a loud voice: 'Fear God and give him glory, because the hour of his judgement has come. And worship the one who made the heaven and the earth and the sea and the springs of waters.'
And another angel, a second, followed, saying: 'Fell, fell Babylon the great — she who made all the nations drink from the wine of the rage of her sexual immorality.'
And another angel, a third, followed them, saying in a loud voice: 'If anyone worships the beast and its image and receives a mark on their forehead or on their hand,
they too will drink of the wine of the rage of God, mixed unmixed in the cup of his wrath, and they will be tormented in fire and sulphur before the holy angels and before the Lamb.'
And the smoke of their torment goes up forever and ever, and they have no rest day and night — those who worship the beast and its image, and anyone who receives the mark of its name.
Here is the endurance of God's holy ones, here — those who keep the commandments of God and their faith in Jesus.

Then I heard a voice out of heaven saying to me: 'Write: Blessed the dead who die in the Lord from now on.' 'Yes,' says the Spirit, 'so that they will rest from their labours, for their works follow with them.'
Then I looked, and there was a white cloud, and on the cloud one sitting like a son of man, having on his head a golden wreath and in his hand a sharp sickle.

And another angel came out of the sanctuary, crying in a loud voice to the one sitting on the cloud: 'Send your sickle and reap, because the hour to reap came for you, because the harvest of the earth was dried.'
And the one sitting on the cloud threw his sickle upon the earth, and the earth was reaped.
And another angel came out of the sanctuary that is in heaven, having, he too, a sharp sickle.

And another angel came out from the altar — the one who has authority over the fire — and he called in a loud voice to the one who had the sharp sickle: 'Send your sharp sickle and gather the clusters of the vine of the earth, because its grapes reached their peak.'
And the angel threw his sickle into the earth and gathered the vine of the earth, and threw it into the winepress of the rage of God, the great one.
And the winepress was trodden outside the city, and blood came out of the winepress as far as the bridles of the horses, from one thousand six hundred stadia.

revelation_15.t: Then I saw another sign in heaven, great and marvellous: seven angels having seven plagues, the last ones, because in them the rage of God was completed.
And I saw what was like a glassy sea mixed with fire, and those conquering out of the beast and out of its image and out of the number of its name, standing on the glassy sea, having harps of God.
