And they sing the song of Moses the servant of God and the song of the Lamb: 'Great and marvellous are your works, Lord God the Almighty. Right and true are your ways, King of the nations.'
Who will not fear you, Lord, and glorify your name? Because you alone are holy; because all the nations will come and will worship before you; because your righteous acts were made visible.
And after this I looked, and the sanctuary of the tent of the witness in heaven was opened.
And the seven angels having the seven plagues came out of the sanctuary, clothed in clean bright linen and girded around the chest with golden sashes.
And one of the four living creatures gave the seven angels seven golden bowls full of the rage of God, who lives into the ages of the ages.
And the sanctuary was filled with smoke from the glory of God and from his power, and no one could enter the sanctuary until the seven plagues of the seven angels were completed.

revelation_16.t: Then I heard a loud voice out of the sanctuary saying to the seven angels: 'Go and pour out the seven bowls of the rage of God into the earth.'
So the first went off and poured out his bowl into the earth, and a bad and evil sore came upon the people who had the mark of the beast and worshipped its image.
And the second angel poured out his bowl into the sea, and it became blood as of a dead person, and every soul of life died — the things in the sea.
And the third angel poured out his bowl into the rivers and into the springs of the waters, and it became blood.
And I heard the angel of the waters saying: 'Right are you, Lord — the one being and the one was and the holy one — because you judged these things,
because they poured out the blood of God's holy ones and prophets, and you have given them blood to drink. They are worthy.'
And I heard another out of the altar saying: 'Yes, Lord God the Almighty, true and right are your judgements.'
And the fourth angel poured out his bowl upon the sun, and it was given to it to scorch people with fire.
And people were scorched a great scorching, and they blasphemed the name of God who has the authority over these plagues, and they did not change their mind to give him glory.
And the fifth angel poured out his bowl upon the throne of the beast, and its kingdom became darkened, and they were chewing their tongues from the pain,
and they blasphemed the God of heaven because of their pains and their sores, and they did not change their mind about their works.
And the sixth angel poured out his bowl upon the great river Euphrates, and its water was dried up, so that the way might be prepared for the kings from the rising of the sun.
And I saw out of the mouth of the dragon and out of the mouth of the beast and out of the mouth of the false prophet three unclean spirits like frogs.
for they are spirits of demons doing signs, which go out to the kings of the earth and of the whole inhabited world, to gather them to the war of that great day of God the Almighty.
'Look, I come as a thief. Blessed the one who keeps watch and keeps his garments, so that he does not walk naked and they see his shame.'
And he gathered them into the place called in Hebrew Harmagedon.
And the seventh angel poured out his bowl upon the air, and a loud voice came out of the sanctuary of heaven, from the throne, saying: 'It has come to be.'
And there came lightnings and voices and thunders, and there came a great earthquake, such as had not come to be from when the humans came to be upon the earth — so great an earthquake, so great.
And the great city came to be into three parts, and the cities of the nations fell. And Babylon the great was remembered before God, to be given the cup of the wine of the rage of his wrath.
And every island fled, and the mountains were not found.
And great hail, about a talent in weight, comes down out of the sky upon people. And they blasphemed God because of the plague of the hail, because its plague is exceedingly great.

revelation_17.t: Then one of the seven angels who had the seven bowls came and spoke with me, saying to me: 'Come, I will show you the judgement of the great prostitute who sits on the many waters,'
with whom the kings of the earth committed sexual immorality, and from the wine of her sexual immorality those who inhabit the earth were made drunk.
And he carried me away in spirit into a wilderness. And I saw a woman sitting on a scarlet beast, full of names of blasphemy, having seven heads and ten horns.
And the woman was clothed in purple and scarlet, gilded with gold and precious stone and pearls, having a golden cup in her hand full of abominations and the unclean things of her sexual immorality.
And on her forehead a name written: Mystery, Babylon the great, the mother of the prostitutes and of the abominations of the earth.
And I saw the woman drunk from the blood of God's holy ones and from the blood of the witnesses of Jesus. And when I saw her I marvelled a great marvel.
And the angel said to me: 'Why did you marvel? I will tell you the mystery of the woman and of the beast that carries her, the one having the seven heads and the ten horns.'

The beast you saw was and is not, and is about to come up out of the abyss and goes off into destruction. And those who inhabit the earth will marvel — whose name has not been written upon the book of life from the founding of the world — when they see the beast, that it was and is not and will be present.
Here is the mind that has wisdom. The seven heads are seven mountains, where the woman sits on them — and they are seven kings.
The five fell, and the one is, the other has not yet come; and when he comes, he must remain a little.
And the beast which was and is not — it is itself an eighth and is of the seven, and goes off into destruction.
And the ten horns you saw are ten kings, who have not yet received a kingdom, but who receive authority as kings for one hour with the beast.
These have one mind, and they give their power and their authority to the beast.
These will make war with the Lamb, and the Lamb will conquer them, because he is Lord of lords and King of kings — and those with him are called and chosen and faithful.
And he says to me: 'The waters you saw, where the prostitute sits, are peoples and crowds and nations and languages.'
And the ten horns you saw, and the beast — these will hate the prostitute and will make her desolate and naked, and will eat her flesh and burn her up with fire.
For God gave it into their hearts to do his mind — to be of one mind and to give their kingdom to the beast — until the words of God will be completed.
And the woman you saw is the great city that has a kingdom over the kings of the earth.

revelation_18.t: After this I saw another angel coming down out of heaven, having great authority, and the earth was lit up from his glory.

And he cried out with a strong voice, great, saying: 'Fell, fell Babylon the great! And she became a dwelling of demons, and a guard-house of every unclean spirit, and a guard-house of every unclean bird, and a guard-house of every unclean and hated beast,'

because from the wine of the rage of her sexual immorality all the nations have drunk, and the kings of the earth committed sexual immorality with her, and the merchants of the earth grew rich from the power of her luxury.
And I heard another voice out of heaven saying: 'Come out of her, my people, so that you do not share together in her sins, and so that you do not receive from her plagues;'
because her sins were glued together as far as heaven, and God remembered her wrongs.
Give back to her as she also gave back, and double to her the double things according to her works. In the cup which she mixed, mix for her double.
As much as she glorified herself and lived in luxury, so much give her torment and grief, because in her heart she says: 'I sit a queen, and I am not a widow, and I will certainly not see grief.'
Because of this in one day her plagues will come — death and grief and famine — and she will be burned up with fire, because strong is the Lord God who judged her.
And the kings of the earth who committed sexual immorality and lived in luxury with her will weep and beat themselves over her, when they see the smoke of her burning,
standing far off because of the fear of her torment, saying: 'Woe, woe, the great city, Babylon the strong city! Because in one hour your judgement came.'
And the merchants of the earth weep and grieve over her, because no one buys their cargo any longer —

cargo of gold and silver and precious stone and pearls, of fine linen and purple and silk and scarlet; every citron wood and every ivory vessel and every vessel of most precious wood, and of bronze and iron and marble;
and cinnamon and spice and incense and ointment and frankincense, and wine and oil and fine flour and wheat, and cattle and sheep, and of horses and of carriages and of bodies — and souls of humans.
And the fruit of the desire of your soul went away from you, and all the fat things and the bright things perished from you, and they will certainly not find them any longer.
The merchants of these things, who grew rich from her, will stand far off because of the fear of her torment, weeping and grieving,
and saying: 'Woe, woe, the great city, clothed in fine linen and purple and scarlet, and gilded with gold and precious stone and pearl!'
because in one hour so much wealth was made desolate. And every shipmaster and everyone sailing to a place, and the crowd, and sailors and as many as work the sea, stood far off
and they were crying out as they saw the smoke of her burning, saying: 'What is like the great city?'

And they threw dust on their heads and were crying out, weeping and grieving and saying: 'Woe, woe, the great city, in which all who had the ships in the sea grew rich from her costliness! Because in one hour she was made desolate.'
Be glad over her, heaven, and the holy ones and the apostles and the prophets, because God judged your judgement out of her.
And one strong angel lifted a stone like a great millstone and threw it into the sea, saying: 'So with violence will Babylon the great city be thrown, and will certainly not be found any longer.'

And the sound of harpers and musicians and flute-players and trumpeters will certainly not be heard in you any longer; and every craftsman of every craft will certainly not be found in you any longer; and the sound of a millstone will certainly not be heard in you any longer;

and the light of a lamp will certainly not shine in you any longer; and the voice of a bridegroom and a bride will certainly not be heard in you any longer — because your merchants were the great ones of the earth, because by your sorcery all the nations were deceived.
And in her was found the blood of prophets and of God's holy ones, and of all those slaughtered on the earth.

revelation_19.t: After this I heard what was like the great voice of a numerous crowd in heaven, saying: 'Hallelujah! The salvation and the glory and the honour and the power to the Lord of our God,'
because true and right are his judgements: because he judged the great prostitute who was corrupting the earth with her sexual immorality, and he avenged the blood of his servants out of her hand.
And a second time they have said: 'Hallelujah! And her smoke goes up into the ages of the ages.'
And the twenty-four elders and the four living creatures fell and worshipped God who sits on the throne, saying: 'Amen. Hallelujah.'
And a voice came out from the throne saying: 'Praise our God, all his servants and you who fear him, the small and the great.'
And I heard what was like the voice of a numerous crowd, and like the voice of many waters, and like the voice of strong thunders, saying: 'Hallelujah! Because the Lord our God the Almighty reigned.'
Let us rejoice and exult and give the glory to him, because the wedding of the Lamb came, and his wife prepared herself.
And it was given to her that she should be clothed in fine linen, bright and clean — for the fine linen is the righteous acts of God's holy ones.
And he says to me: 'Write: Blessed those who are called to the supper of the wedding of the Lamb.' And he says to me: 'These are the true words of God.'

And I fell before his feet to worship him, and he says to me: 'See — no! I am your fellow servant, and of your brothers and sisters, those having, having the testimony of Jesus. Worship God! For the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of the prophecy.'
And I saw heaven opened, and look — a white horse, and the one sitting on it called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he judges and makes war;
and his eyes as a flame of fire, and on his head many royal crowns, having names written and a name written which no one knows except himself,
and clothed with a garment dipped in blood; and his name has been called the Word of God.
and the armies in heaven were following him on white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and clean.

And out of his mouth goes a sharp two-edged sword, so that with it he might strike the nations. And he himself will shepherd them with an iron rod, and he himself treads the winepress of the wine of the rage and the wrath of God the Almighty.
And he has on the garment and on his thigh a name written: King of kings and Lord of lords.
And I saw one angel standing in the sun, and he cried out in a loud voice, saying to all the birds flying in mid-heaven: 'Come, be gathered to the great supper of God,'

so that you may eat fleshes of kings and fleshes of commanders and fleshes of strong ones, and fleshes of horses and of those sitting on them, and fleshes of all — both free and slaves, both small and great.
And I saw the beast and the kings of the earth and their armies gathered to make the war with the one sitting on the horse and with his army.

And the beast was seized, and with it the false prophet who did the signs before it, by which he deceived those who received the mark of the beast and those worshipping its image. Alive, the two were thrown into the lake of the fire that burns with sulphur.
And the rest were killed by the sword of the one sitting on the horse, the sword that came out of his mouth. And all the birds were filled from their fleshes.

revelation_20.t: And I saw an angel coming down out of heaven, having the key of the abyss and a great chain upon his hand.
And he seized the dragon — the ancient serpent, who is Devil and the Satan, the one deceiving the whole inhabited world — and bound him a thousand years,

and he threw him into the abyss and shut and sealed above him, so that he would not deceive the nations any longer until the thousand years were completed. After these things he must be loosed a little time.

And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgement was given to them — and the souls of those beheaded because of the testimony of Jesus and because of the word of God, and whoever did not worship the beast nor its image and did not receive the mark upon the forehead and upon their hand. And they came to life and reigned with the Christ the thousand years.
But the rest of the dead did not come to life until the thousand years were completed. This is the first resurrection.

Blessed and holy the one who has a part in the first resurrection. Over these the second death does not have authority, but they will be priests of God and of the Christ, and they will reign with him the thousand years.
And when the thousand years are completed, the Satan will be loosed out of his prison,
and he will go out to deceive the nations in the four corners of the earth — the Gog and the Magog — to gather them to the war, of whom their number is as the sand of the sea.
And they went up upon the breadth of the earth and encircled the camp of God's holy ones and the beloved city. And fire came down from God out of heaven and devoured them.
And the devil who deceives them was thrown into the lake of the fire and sulphur, where also the beast and the false prophet are, and they will be tormented day and night into the ages of the ages.
And I saw a great white throne and the one sitting upon it, from whose face the earth and heaven fled, and a place was not found for them.

And I saw the dead, the great and the small, standing before the throne, and books were opened. And another book was opened, which is the book of life. And the dead were judged out of the things written in the books, according to their works.
And the sea gave up the dead who were in it, and the Death and the Hades gave up the dead who were in them, and they were judged each according to their works.
And the Death and the Hades were thrown into the lake of the fire. This is the second death — the lake of the fire.
And if anyone was not found written in the book of life, they were thrown into the lake of the fire.

revelation_21.t: And I saw a new heaven and a new earth. For the first heaven and the first earth went away, and the sea is not any longer.
And I, John, saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.

And I heard a loud voice out of the throne saying: 'Look — the tent of God with the humans! And he will tent with them, and they themselves will be his peoples, and he himself, God with them, will be their God.'
And God will wipe away every tear out of their eyes, and the death will not be any longer, nor grief nor crying, nor will pain not be any longer — because the first things went away.
And the one sitting on the throne said: 'Look — I make all things new.' And he says to me: 'Write, because these words are faithful and true.'
And he said to me: 'They have come to be. I am the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end. To the one thirsting I will give out of the spring of the water of life freely.'
The one conquering will inherit these things, and I will be God to them, and they themselves will be the son to me.

But to the cowardly and unbelieving and sinful and detestable, and murderers and the sexually immoral and sorcerers and idolaters and all the false ones — their part is in the lake burning with fire and sulphur, which is the second death.
And there came to me one of the seven angels having the seven bowls full of the seven last plagues, and he spoke with me saying: 'Come, I will show you the bride, the wife of the Lamb.'
And he carried me away in spirit onto a great and high mountain, and showed me the great city, the holy Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God,
having the glory of God. Its radiance was like a most precious stone, as a jasper stone, crystal-clear;
having a great and high wall, having twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names inscribed, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the sons of Israel;
from the east three gates, and from the north three gates, and from the south three gates, and from the west three gates.
And the wall of the city having twelve foundations, and on them twelve names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.
And the one speaking with me had a measure, a golden reed, so that he might measure the city and its gates and its wall.
And the city lies four-square, and its length is as much as also its breadth. And he measured the city with the reed at twelve thousand stadia; its length and breadth and height are equal.
And he measured its wall, a hundred and forty-four cubits, a measure of a human, which is of an angel.
And the structure of its wall was jasper, and the city pure gold, like clear glass.
And the foundations of the wall of the city adorned with every precious stone: the first foundation jasper, the second sapphire, the third chalcedony, the fourth emerald,
the fifth sardonyx, the sixth carnelian, the seventh chrysolite, the eighth beryl, the ninth topaz, the tenth chrysoprase, the eleventh jacinth, the twelfth amethyst.
And the twelve gates twelve pearls; each one of the gates was of one pearl. And the street of the city pure gold, like transparent glass.
And a sanctuary I did not see in it; for the Lord God the Almighty is its sanctuary — and the Lamb.
And the city has no need of the sun nor of the moon to shine in it; for the glory of God lit it, and its lamp is the Lamb.
And the nations of the saved will walk through its light, and the kings of the earth bring their glory and their honour into it.
And its gates will certainly not be shut by day; for night will not be there.
And they will bring the glory and the honour of the nations into it.
And there will certainly not enter into it anything common, nor the one doing an abomination and a falsehood — except those written in the book of life of the Lamb.

revelation_22.t: And he showed me a clean river of water of life, bright as crystal, going out from the throne of God and of the Lamb.

In the middle of its street and of the river, on this side and on that, a tree of life producing twelve fruits, yielding its fruit each single month; and the leaves of the tree for the healing of the nations.
And every curse will not be any longer, and the throne of God and of the Lamb will be in it, and his servants will serve him,
and they will see his face, and his name on their foreheads.
And night will not be any longer, and they have no need of the light of a lamp and the light of the sun, because the Lord God will shine upon them. And they will reign into the ages of the ages.
And he said to me: 'These words are faithful and true. And the Lord, the God of the spirits of the prophets, sent his angel to show his servants the things which must come to be quickly.'
'And look, I come quickly. Blessed the one who keeps the words of the prophecy of this book.'
And I, John, am the one hearing and seeing these things. And when I heard and saw, I fell to worship before the feet of the angel showing me these things.
And he says to me: 'See — no! For I am your fellow servant, and of your brothers and sisters the prophets, and of those keeping the words of this book. Worship God!'
And he says to me: 'Do not seal the words of the prophecy of this book, because, for the time is near.'
The one doing wrong, let him do wrong still; and the filthy one, let him be filthy still; and the right one, let him do rightness still; and the holy one, let him be made holy still.
'Look, I come quickly, and my wage is with me, to give back to each as their work is.'
'I am the Alpha and the Omega, the first and the last, the beginning and the end.'
Blessed those who wash their robes, so that their authority will be over the tree of life, and by the gates they may enter into the city.
Outside: the dogs and the sorcerers and the sexually immoral and the murderers and the idolaters, and everyone loving and doing falsehood.
'I, Jesus, sent my angel to testify these things to you upon the communities. I am the root and the offspring of David, the bright morning star.'
And the Spirit and the bride say: 'Come.' And let the one hearing say: 'Come.' And let the one thirsting come; let the one willing take the water of life freely.
'I testify, I myself, to everyone hearing the words of the prophecy of this book: if anyone adds upon them, God will add upon them the plagues written in this book.'
'And if anyone takes away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God will take away their part from the tree of life and out of the holy city, from the things written in this book.'
The one testifying these things says: 'Yes, I come quickly.' Amen. Yes — come, Lord Jesus.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ with all of the you. Amen.

romans_1.t: Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus, called as an apostle, set apart for God's good news —
which he promised beforehand through his prophets in holy writings,
about his Son, who came from David's seed as far as the flesh goes,
and who was declared to be Son of God in power, according to a spirit of holiness, from the resurrection of the dead — Jesus Christ our Lord.
Through him we received grace and a sending out for the obedience of faith among all the nations, for the sake of his name —
and you are among them, called ones belonging to Jesus Christ —
to all in Rome who are loved by God, called as his holy people: grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your trust is being announced all over the world.
God is my witness — the God I serve in my spirit in the good news of his Son — how unceasingly I make mention of you,
always in my prayers asking whether somehow, now at last, I may be given a clear road by God's will to come to you.
I long to see you, so that I may share some spiritual gift with you to make you firm —
or rather, that we may be encouraged together while I am among you, each by the other's trust, yours and mine.

I don't want you to be unaware, brothers and sisters, that I often planned to come to you — and was prevented until now — so that I might have some fruit among you too, as among the rest of the nations.
I am in debt to Greeks and to barbarians, to the wise and to the unthinking.
So, for my part, I am eager to announce the good news to you in Rome as well.
I am not ashamed of the good news, because it is God's power for rescue to everyone who trusts — to the Jew first and also to the Greek.
For in it God's rightness is revealed, from trust to trust, as it is written: 'The one who is right from trust will live.'
For God's anger is being revealed from heaven against every irreverence and unrightness of people who hold the truth down in unrightness —
because what can be known of God is plain among them; God made it plain to them.
Ever since the creation of the world his unseeable things — his everlasting power and divinity — have been clearly seen, understood through the things he made, so that they are without defence.
For though they knew God, they did not honour him as God or thank him; instead they became futile in their reasonings, and their uncomprehending heart was darkened.
Claiming to be wise, they were made fools;
and they exchanged the glory of the imperishable God for a likeness of an image of perishable humanity — and of birds and four-footed animals and creeping things.
So God handed them over, in the desires of their hearts, to uncleanness — to the dishonouring of their bodies among themselves.
They exchanged the truth of God for the lie, and revered and served what was created rather than the Creator — who is blessed for ever. Amen.
Because of this, God handed them over to passions of dishonour: their females exchanged the natural use for the one contrary to nature,

and likewise the males too, leaving the natural use of the female, were inflamed in their craving for one another — males with males working out the indecency, and receiving back in themselves the payment their straying required.
And since they did not think it worth approving to keep God in their knowledge, God handed them over to an unapproved mind, to do what is not fitting —
filled with every kind of unrightness, sexual immorality, wickedness, greed, malice; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, spite; whisperers,
slanderers, God-haters, insolent, arrogant, boasters, inventors of evils, disobedient to parents,
senseless, promise-breaking, heartless, unforgiving, merciless.
They recognise God's just decree — that those who practise such things deserve death — and they not only do them but applaud those who practise them.

romans_2.t: So you have no defence, whoever you are who judge. In judging someone else you condemn yourself, because you the judge practise the same things.
We know that God's judgement is according to truth against those who practise such things.
Do you reckon this, you who judge those who practise such things and do them yourself — that you will escape God's judgement?
Or do you look down on the wealth of his kindness and forbearance and patience, not knowing that God's kindness is leading you to a change of mind?
But by your hardness and unchanged heart you are storing up anger for yourself on a day of anger, when God's just judgement is revealed —
He will pay back to each according to his works:
to those who by endurance in good work seek glory and honour and imperishability — eternal life;
but to those who act out of rivalry, and disobey the truth while obeying unrightness — anger and fury.
Trouble and constriction on every human being who works out evil — the Jew first and also the Greek;
but glory and honour and peace to everyone who works the good — the Jew first and also the Greek.
For God shows no favouritism.
All who sinned outside law will also perish outside law, and all who sinned under law will be judged through law.
For it is not the hearers of law who are right before God; the doers of law will be justified.
For whenever nations that do not have law do by nature the things of the law, these, not having law, are a law to themselves.
They show the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience testifying with them, and their reasonings among one another accusing or even defending them —
on a day when God judges the hidden things of people through Christ Jesus, according to my good news.
But if you call yourself a Jew and rest on law and boast in God
and know the will and approve the things that matter, being instructed out of the law,
and are convinced that you yourself are a guide of the blind, a light for those in darkness,
a corrector of the foolish, a teacher of infants, having in the law the outline of knowledge and of truth —
you then who teach someone else — do you not teach yourself? You who proclaim not to steal, do you steal?
You who say not to commit adultery, do you commit adultery? You who detest idols, do you rob temples?
You who boast in law — through breaking the law do you dishonour God?
For 'the name of God is blasphemed among the nations because of you', as it is written.
Circumcision is of benefit if you practise law; but if you are a law-breaker, your circumcision has become foreskin.
So if the foreskin keeps the just requirements of the law, will not his foreskin be reckoned as circumcision?
And the one uncircumcised by birth, by completing the law, will judge you who — with letter and circumcision — are a law-breaker.
For the Jew is not the one who is so in the open, nor is circumcision the one in the open, in flesh;
but the Jew is the one hidden, and circumcision is of the heart, in spirit not in letter — whose praise comes not from people but from God.

romans_3.t: What then is the advantage of the Jew, or what is the benefit of circumcision?
Much, in every way. First of all, they were entrusted with the sayings of God.
For what if some were unfaithful? Their unfaithfulness will not cancel God's faithfulness, will it?
Absolutely not. Let God be true and every person a liar, as it is written: 'So that you may be justified in your words and will win when you are judged.'
But if our unrightness demonstrates God's rightness, what shall we say? Is God unjust to bring the anger? (I am speaking in human terms.)
Absolutely not — since then how will God judge the world?
But if God's truth abounded to his glory by my lie, why am I still judged as a sinner?
And why not say — as we are slandered as saying, and as some claim we say — 'Let us do the evil things so that the good may come'? Their judgement is deserved.
What then? Are we better off? Not at all. For we have already charged that all, both Jews and Greeks, are under sin,
as it is written: 'There is no one right, not even one;
there is no one who understands, there is no one who seeks out God.
All turned away, together they became useless; there is no one doing kindness, there is not so much as one.
Their throat is an opened grave; with their tongues they kept deceiving; venom of asps is under their lips;
their mouth is full of cursing and bitterness.
Their feet are swift to pour out blood;
ruin and misery are in their ways,
and the way of peace they did not know.
There is no fear of God before their eyes.'
Now we know that whatever the law says, it says to those under the law, so that every mouth may be stopped and the whole world become answerable to God —
because by works of the law no flesh will be justified before him; for through law comes recognition of sin.
But now, apart from law, God's rightness has been made visible — testified to by the law and the prophets —
God's rightness through faith in Jesus Christ, to all and on all who trust. For there is no distinction:
for all sinned and are falling short of the glory of God,
being justified freely by his grace, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus —
whom God set forth as a propitiation through trust, in his blood, as a demonstration of his rightness — because of the passing over of the sins committed beforehand, in the forbearance of God —
toward the demonstration of his rightness at the present time — that he himself is right and the justifier of the one who has faith in Jesus.
Where then is the boasting? It was shut out. Through what kind of law? Of works? No — but through a law of trust.
For we reckon that a person is justified by trust, apart from works of the law.
Or is God the God of Jews only? Not of the nations too? Yes, of the nations too,
since God is one — the one who will justify circumcision out of trust and foreskin through the trust.
Do we then put law out of work through trust? Absolutely not — we establish law.

romans_4.t: What then shall we say that Abraham, our forefather according to the flesh, has found?
For if Abraham was justified by works, he has something to boast about — but not before God.
For what does the scripture say? 'Abraham trusted God, and it was reckoned to him for rightness.'
Now to the one who works, the wage is not reckoned as a gift but as what is owed;
but to the one who does not work but trusts on the one who justifies the irreverent, his trust is reckoned for rightness.
just as David also speaks the blessing of the person to whom God reckons rightness apart from works:
'Blessed are those whose lawless acts were forgiven and whose sins were covered over;
blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will certainly not reckon.'
Is this blessing then on the circumcision, or on the foreskin too? For we say: 'To Abraham trust was reckoned for rightness.'
How then was it reckoned? While he was in circumcision or in foreskin? Not in circumcision but in foreskin.

And he received a sign — circumcision, a seal of the rightness of the trust he had while uncircumcised — so that he might be father of all who trust while uncircumcised, so that rightness might be reckoned to them too,
and father of circumcision — not for those who are merely of circumcision, but also for those who walk in line with the footsteps of the trust our father Abraham had while uncircumcised.
For the promise to Abraham or to his seed — that he would be heir of the world — did not come through law but through the rightness of trust.
For if those of law are heirs, trust has been emptied and the promise put out of work.
For the law works out anger; but where there is no law, neither is there transgression.

That is why it is out of trust — so that it may be according to grace, and the promise firm for all the seed, not only for those of the law but also for those of Abraham's trust, who is father of us all,
as it is written: 'I have made you father of many nations.' He is our father before the God he trusted — the God who makes the dead alive and calls the things that are not as being.
Against hope, upon hope he trusted, so that he became father of many nations, according to what was said: 'So will your seed be.'
And not weakening in trust, he did not consider his own body, already dead — being about a hundred years old — or the deadness of Sarah's womb.
Toward God's promise he was not divided by unbelief; instead he was strengthened in trust, giving glory to God,
fully convinced that what God has promised he is also able to do.
That is why it was also reckoned to him for rightness.
But it was not written for his sake alone that it was reckoned to him,
but for ours too, to whom it is going to be reckoned — to those who trust on the one who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead,
who was handed over because of our trespasses and was raised because of our justification.

romans_5.t: So, having been justified out of trust, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ,
through whom we have also had our access by trust into this grace in which we stand; and we boast on the hope of God's glory.
And not only that — we also boast in our afflictions, knowing that affliction works out endurance,
and endurance, testedness; and testedness, hope;
and hope does not put us to shame, because God's love has been poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit given to us.
For while we were still weak, at the right time Christ died for the irreverent.
For someone will scarcely die for a righteous person — though for the good person someone might perhaps even dare to die.
But God demonstrates his own love toward us in this: that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.
How much more, then, having now been justified by his blood, will we be rescued through him from the anger.
For if, while we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, how much more, having been reconciled, will we be rescued by his life.
And not only that, but boasting in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received the reconciliation.
Because of this: just as through one person sin entered into the world, and through sin death, and so death spread to all people, because all sinned —
For until law, sin was in the world; but sin is not put on the account where there is no law.
Yet death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those who did not sin in the likeness of Adam's transgression — who is a pattern of the one to come.

But the gift is not like the trespass. For if by the trespass of the one the many died, how much more did God's grace and the gift in grace — the grace of the one person Jesus Christ — overflow to the many.
And the gift is not like what came through the one who sinned: for the judgement from one led to condemnation, but the free gift from many trespasses led to a verdict in our favour.
For if by the trespass of the one, death reigned through that one, how much more will those who receive the overflow of grace and of the gift of rightness reign in life through the one, Jesus Christ.
So then: as through one trespass it came to all people, to condemnation, so also through one act of rightness it came to all people, to a justification that is life.
For as through the disobedience of the one person the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the one the many will be made right.
And law slipped in alongside, so that the trespass might increase; but where sin increased, grace overflowed all the more —
so that, just as sin reigned in death, so also grace might reign through rightness, to eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

romans_6.t: What then shall we say? Are we to stay on in sin so that grace may increase?
Absolutely not. We who died to sin — how can we still live in it?
Or are you unaware that all of us who were baptised into Christ Jesus were baptised into his death?
So we were buried with him through baptism into death, so that just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, so we too might walk in newness of life.
For if we have grown together with the likeness of his death, we shall certainly also be of the resurrection.
knowing this: that our old humanity was crucified with him, so that the body of sin might be put out of work, so that we no longer serve sin as slaves.
For the one who has died has been freed from sin.
And if we died with Christ, we trust that we shall also live with him,
knowing that Christ, having been raised from the dead, dies no more; death no longer rules over him.
For the death he died, he died to sin once for all; but the life he lives, he lives to God.
So you too: reckon yourselves dead to sin but alive to God in Christ Jesus our Lord.
So do not let sin reign in your mortal body, so that you obey its desires;
and do not go on presenting your limbs to sin as weapons of unrightness, but present yourselves to God as those alive from the dead, and your limbs to God as weapons of rightness.
For sin will not rule over you, because you are not under law but under grace.
What then? Are we to sin because we are not under law but under grace? Absolutely not.
Do you not know that when you present yourselves to someone as slaves for obedience, you are slaves of the one you obey — whether of sin, leading to death, or of obedience, leading to rightness?
But thanks be to God that, though you were slaves of sin, you obeyed from the heart the pattern of teaching to which you were handed over.
And having been set free from sin, you were enslaved to rightness.

I am speaking in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh. For just as you presented your limbs as slaves to uncleanness and to lawlessness, leading to lawlessness, so now present your limbs as slaves to rightness, leading to holiness.
For when you were slaves of sin, you were free with regard to rightness.
So what fruit did you have then, in the things you are now ashamed of? For the end of those things is death.
But now, set free from sin and enslaved to God, you have your fruit leading to holiness — and the end, eternal life.
For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.

romans_7.t: Or are you unaware, brothers and sisters — I am speaking to people who know law — that the law rules over a person for as long as he lives?
For the married woman is bound by law to her husband while he lives; but if the husband dies, she is discharged from the law of the husband.

So then, while the husband lives she will be called an adulteress if she becomes another man's; but if the husband dies she is free from the law, so that she is not an adulteress by becoming another man's.
So, my brothers and sisters, you also were put to death to the law through the body of Christ, so that you might become another's — the one raised from the dead — so that we might bear fruit for God.
For when we were in the flesh, the passions of sins that came through the law were at work in our limbs, to bear fruit for death.
But now we have been discharged from the law, having died to what held us down, so that we serve as slaves in newness of spirit and not in oldness of letter.
What then shall we say? Is the law sin? Absolutely not. But I would not have known sin except through law; for I would not have known desire if the law had not said, 'You shall not desire.'
But sin, taking a base of operations through the commandment, worked out in me every kind of desire; for apart from law sin is dead.
I was once alive apart from law; but when the commandment came, sin came back to life,
and I died, and the commandment that was for life — this one was found to be death for me.
For sin, taking a base of operations through the commandment, deceived me and through it killed me.
So the law is holy, and the commandment holy and right and good.

Did the good then become death to me? Absolutely not — but sin did, so that it might show itself as sin, working out death in me through the good, so that sin might become sinful beyond all measure through the commandment.
For we know that the law is spiritual; but I am fleshly, sold under sin.
For what I work out I do not know; for what I want, this I do not practise, but what I hate, this I do.
But if I do what I do not want, I agree with the law that it is good.
But as it is, it is no longer I who work it out, but sin living in me.
For I know that good does not live in me — that is, in my flesh. For the willing lies ready to hand for me, but the working out of the good does not.
For I do not do the good I want, but the evil I do not want — this I practise.
But if I do what I do not want, it is no longer I who work it out but sin living in me.
So I find the law: that when I want to do the good, evil is what lies ready to hand for me.
For I delight together with the law of God, as far as the inner person goes,
but I see a different law in my limbs, warring against the law of my mind and taking me captive in the law of sin that is in my limbs.
Wretched person that I am! Who will rescue me from the body of this death?
But thanks be to God, through Jesus Christ our Lord! So then, I myself with my mind serve God's law as a slave, but with my flesh, sin's law.

romans_8.t: So now there is no condemnation for those in Christ Jesus who do not walk according to flesh but according to spirit.
For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus set you free from the law of sin and of death.
For what the law could not do, weak as it was through the flesh — God, sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and concerning sin, condemned sin in the flesh,
so that the just requirement of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not according to flesh but according to spirit.
For those who are according to flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh, but those according to spirit on the things of the spirit.
For the mindset of the flesh is death, but the mindset of the spirit is life and peace;
because the mindset of the flesh is hostility toward God: it does not submit to God's law, nor can it;
and those who are in flesh cannot please God.
But you are not in flesh but in spirit, if indeed God's Spirit lives in you. And if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, this person is not his.
But if Christ is in you, the body is dead because of sin, but the Spirit is life because of rightness.
And if the Spirit of the one who raised Jesus from the dead lives in you, the one who raised Christ from the dead will also make your mortal bodies alive through his Spirit living in you.
So then, brothers and sisters, we are debtors — not to the flesh, to live according to flesh.
For if you live according to flesh, you are going to die; but if by the Spirit you put to death the practices of the body, you will live.
For all who are led by God's Spirit — these are sons of God.
For you did not receive a spirit of slavery leading back into fear, but you received a spirit of adoption as heirs, in which we cry, 'Abba! Father!'
The Spirit itself testifies together with our spirit that we are God's children.
And if children, then heirs — heirs of God and co-heirs with Christ — if indeed we suffer together with him so that we may also be glorified together with him.
For I reckon that the sufferings of the present time are not worth setting against the glory about to be revealed to us.
For creation's straining expectation awaits the revealing of the sons of God.
For creation was subjected to futility — not willingly, but because of the one who subjected it — in hope
that creation itself will also be set free from the slavery of decay into the freedom of the glory of God's children.
For we know that the whole creation groans together and is in labour together until now.
And not only that — we ourselves, having the firstfruit of the Spirit, we ourselves also groan within ourselves, awaiting adoption as heirs: the redemption of our body.
For in hope we were rescued. But hope that is seen is not hope; for who hopes for what he sees?
But if we hope for what we do not see, we await it through endurance.
In the same way the Spirit also takes hold with us in our weakness; for we do not know what to pray as we ought, but the Spirit itself pleads on our behalf with groans that go unspoken.
And the one who searches the hearts knows what the Spirit's mindset is, because it pleads on behalf of the holy ones according to God.
And we know that for those who love God, God works all things together for good — for those who are called according to purpose.
because those he knew beforehand he also marked out beforehand as sharing the form of his Son's image, so that he might be firstborn among many brothers.
And those he marked out beforehand, these he also called; and those he called, these he also justified; and those he justified, these he also glorified.
What then shall we say to these things? If God is for us, who is against us?
He who did not spare his own Son but handed him over for us all — how will he not also, together with him, freely give us everything?
Who will bring a charge against God's chosen? God is the one who justifies.
Who is the one who condemns? Christ Jesus is the one who died — rather, who was raised from the dead — who is also at God's right hand, who also pleads on our behalf.
Who will separate us from the love of Christ? Affliction, or constriction, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or danger, or sword?
As it is written: 'For your sake we are being put to death all day long; we were reckoned as sheep for slaughter.'
But in all these things we more than conquer through the one who loved us.
For I have been persuaded that neither death nor life, nor angels nor rulers, nor things present nor things to come, nor powers,
nor height nor depth, nor any other created thing, will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

romans_9.t: I am telling the truth in Christ, I am not lying, my conscience testifying with me in the Holy Spirit —
that I have great grief and unceasing pain in my heart.
For I could pray that I myself were cursed and cut off from the Christ for the sake of my brothers and sisters, my own kin according to the flesh —
who are Israelites: theirs is the adoption as heirs, the glory, the covenants, the giving of the law, the worship, and the promises;
theirs are the fathers, and from them, according to the flesh, came the Christ, who is over all, God blessed forever. Amen.
It is not as though God's word has failed. For not all who are from Israel are Israel,
nor are they all children because they are Abraham's seed; rather: through Isaac your seed will be named.
That is: it is not the children of the flesh who are God's children, but the children of the promise who are counted as seed.
For this is the word of promise: At this season I will come, and Sarah will have a son.
And not only that — there is also Rebecca, who conceived by one man, our father Isaac.
For when they had not yet been born and had done nothing good or worthless, so that God's purpose according to choice might stand —
not from works but from the one who calls — it was said to her: The greater will be a slave to the lesser.
as it is written: Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated.
What then shall we say? Is there injustice with God? Absolutely not.
For he says to Moses: I will have mercy on whomever I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whomever I have compassion.
So then it does not depend on the one who wills or the one who runs, but on God who shows mercy.
For the scripture says to Pharaoh: For this very purpose I raised you up, so that I might display my power in you, and so that my name might be proclaimed in all the earth.
So then he has mercy on whom he wills, and he hardens whom he wills.
You will say to me then: Why does he still find fault? For who has resisted his will?
Human being — who are you, on the contrary, to answer back to God? Will what is moulded say to the one who moulded it: Why did you make me like this?
Or does the potter not have authority over the clay, to make out of the same lump one vessel for honour and another for dishonour?
And what if God, willing to display his wrath and to make known his power, bore with great patience vessels of wrath prepared for destruction —
and did so in order to make known the riches of his glory upon vessels of mercy, which he prepared beforehand for glory?
even us, whom he called, not only from among Jews but also from among the nations —
as he also says in Hosea: I will call the one who is not my people my people, and the one not loved, loved.
And it will be that in the place where it was said to them: You are not my people — there they will be called sons of the living God.
And Isaiah cries out over Israel: Though the number of the sons of Israel be like the sand of the sea, the remnant will be saved.
For the Lord will carry out his word on the earth, completing it and cutting it short.
And as Isaiah said beforehand: If the Lord of hosts had not left us seed, we would have become like Sodom and been made like Gomorrah.
What then shall we say? That nations who were not pursuing rightness took hold of rightness — the rightness that is from trust;
but Israel, pursuing a law of rightness, did not arrive at that law.
Why? Because it was not from trust but as though from works of the law. They stumbled over the stone of stumbling,
as it is written: Look, I am placing in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence, and the one who trusts in him will not be put to shame.

romans_10.t: Brothers and sisters, my heart's good will and my plea to God on their behalf is for their rescue.
For I testify about them that they have a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge.
For being ignorant of God's rightness and seeking to establish their own, they did not submit to God's rightness.
For Christ is the end of the law, for rightness to everyone who trusts.
For Moses writes about the rightness that comes from the law: The person who does these things will live by them.
But the rightness that comes from trust speaks this way: Do not say in your heart: Who will go up into heaven? — that is, to bring Christ down;
or: Who will go down into the abyss? — that is, to bring Christ up from the dead.
But what does it say? The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart — that is, the word of trust that we proclaim;
that if you confess with your mouth the word that Jesus is Lord, and trust in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be rescued.
For with the heart a person trusts, leading to rightness, and with the mouth confession is made, leading to rescue.
For the scripture says: Everyone who trusts in him will not be put to shame.
For there is no distinction between Jew and Greek: the same Lord is Lord of all, rich toward all who call on him.
For everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be rescued.
How then are they to call on one they have not trusted? And how are they to trust one they have not heard? And how are they to hear without someone proclaiming?
And how are they to proclaim unless they are sent? As it is written: How beautiful are the feet of those who announce good news of peace, who announce good news of good things.
But not all obeyed the good news. For Isaiah says: Lord, who has trusted our report?
So trust comes from hearing, and hearing comes through the word of Christ.
But I say: Have they not heard? On the contrary: Their sound went out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the inhabited world.
But I say: Did Israel not understand? First Moses says: I will make you jealous over what is not a nation; over a nation without understanding I will make you angry.
And Isaiah dares to say: I was found by those who were not seeking me; I became visible to those who were not asking for me.
But to Israel he says: All day long I stretched out my hands to a people who disobey and contradict.

romans_11.t: So I say: Has God pushed away his people? Absolutely not. For I too am an Israelite, from Abraham's seed, of the tribe of Benjamin.
God has not pushed away his people, whom he knew beforehand. Or do you not know what the scripture says in the passage about Elijah — how he appeals to God against Israel?
Lord, they have killed your prophets, they have torn down your altars, and I alone am left, and they are seeking my life.
But what does the divine answer say to him? I have left for myself seven thousand men who have not bent a knee to Baal.
So in the same way, at the present time too, a remnant has come into being according to a choice of grace.
And if by grace, then no longer from works — otherwise grace is no longer grace. And if from works, it is no longer grace — otherwise the work is no longer work.
What then? What Israel is seeking, it did not obtain; the chosen obtained it, and the rest were hardened —
as it is written: God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that do not see and ears that do not hear, right up to this present day.
And David says: Let their table become a snare and a trap, a stumbling block and a payback for them;
let their eyes be darkened so that they cannot see, and bend their backs continually.
So I say: Did they stumble so as to fall for good? Absolutely not. Rather, by their trespass rescue has come to the nations, to make Israel jealous.
And if their trespass means riches for the world, and their loss riches for the nations, how much more their fullness!
Now I am speaking to you, the nations. Inasmuch as I am an apostle to the nations, I make much of my service —
if somehow I might make my own flesh jealous and rescue some of them.
For if their setting aside means the world's reconciliation, what will their acceptance mean but life from the dead?
If the firstfruit is holy, so is the whole lump; and if the root is holy, so are the branches.
But if some of the branches were broken off, and you, being a wild olive shoot, were grafted in among them and became a sharer in the root and the richness of the olive tree,
do not boast over the branches. And if you do boast — you do not carry the root; the root carries you.
You will say then: Branches were broken off so that I might be grafted in.
True enough. They were broken off by their lack of trust, and you stand by trust. Do not think high things — be afraid.
For if God did not spare the natural branches, neither will he spare you.
So look at God's kindness and severity: severity toward those who fell, but God's kindness toward you, if you remain in that kindness — otherwise you too will be cut off.
And they too, if they do not remain in their lack of trust, will be grafted in; for God is able to graft them in again.
For if you were cut from what is by nature a wild olive and grafted, contrary to nature, into a cultivated olive, how much more will these, the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree?

For I do not want you to be ignorant of this mystery, brothers and sisters, so that you will not be wise in your own estimation: a hardening has come upon part of Israel until the fullness of the nations comes in,
and in this way all Israel will be rescued, as it is written: The deliverer will come out of Zion; he will turn ungodliness away from Jacob;
and this is my covenant with them, when I take away their sins.
As regards the good news, they are enemies for your sake; as regards the choice, they are loved for the sake of the fathers.
For God's gifts and calling are not taken back.
For just as you were once disobedient to God but have now received mercy through their disobedience,
so also these have now disobeyed, so that by the mercy shown to you they too might now receive mercy.
For God shut them all up into disobedience, so that he might have mercy on them all.
O the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable his judgements, and how untraceable his ways!
For who has known the Lord's mind? Or who has been his counsellor?
Or who has given to him first, and will be repaid?
For from him and through him and to him are all things. To him be the glory forever. Amen.

romans_12.t: So I appeal to you, brothers and sisters, through God's compassion: present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God — your spiritual worship.
And do not be shaped by this age; instead be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you may test and discern what God's will is — what is good and pleasing and complete.

For through the grace given to me I say to every one of you: do not think of yourself more highly than you ought to think, but think so as to think soberly, each according to the measure of trust God has apportioned.
For just as we have many parts in one body, and all the parts do not have the same function,
so we, though many, are one body in Christ, and individually parts belonging to one another.
We have different gifts according to the grace given to us. If prophecy, then in proportion to trust;
if service, then in serving; the one who teaches, in teaching;
the one who encourages, in encouragement; the one who shares, with singleness of heart; the one who leads, with diligence; the one who shows mercy, with cheerfulness.
Love without pretence. Hate what is evil; hold fast to what is good.
Be devoted to one another in family affection; outdo one another in showing honour.
Do not be lazy in diligence; be aglow in the Spirit; serve the Lord as slaves.
Rejoice in hope; endure under pressure; persist in prayer.
Share in the needs of God's people; pursue hospitality.
Bless those who persecute you; bless and do not curse.
Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep.
Think the same way toward one another. Do not set your mind on high things, but go along with the lowly. Do not be wise in your own estimation.
Repay no one evil for evil. Take thought for what is good in the sight of all people.
If possible, so far as it depends on you, be at peace with all people.
Do not take revenge for yourselves, loved ones; instead leave room for the wrath. For it is written: Vengeance is mine, I will repay, says the Lord.
Rather: If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink. For in doing this you will heap coals of fire on his head.
Do not be conquered by evil; conquer evil with good.

romans_13.t: Let every person be subject to the governing authorities. For there is no authority except from God, and those that exist have been ordered under God.
So the one who sets himself against the authority has resisted God's ordering, and those who resist will bring judgement on themselves.
For rulers are not a terror to good work but to bad. Do you want to have no fear of the authority? Do what is good, and you will have praise from it —

for it is one who serves God, for you, for good. But if you do what is bad, be afraid — it does not carry the sword for nothing. For it is one who serves God, an avenger bringing wrath on the one who does what is bad.
So it is necessary to be subject, not only because of the wrath but also because of conscience.
This is also why you pay taxes: they are God's public officers, attending to this very thing.
Pay everyone what is owed: tax to whom tax is owed, duty to whom duty, fear to whom fear, honour to whom honour.
Owe no one anything, except to love one another; for the one who loves the other has fulfilled the law.

For the commandments — do not commit adultery, do not murder, do not steal, do not give false testimony, do not covet — and any other commandment, are summed up in this word: love your neighbour as yourself.
Love does no evil to the neighbour. So love is the fulfilling of law.
And do this, knowing the time — that the hour has already come for you to be raised from sleep. For our rescue is nearer now than when we first trusted.
The night has advanced, and the day has drawn near. So let us put off the works of darkness and put on the weapons of light.
Let us walk properly, as in daylight: not in carousing and drunkenness, not in bed-taking and shamelessness, not in strife and jealousy.
Instead, put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the flesh, to gratify its desires.

romans_14.t: Welcome the one who is weak in trust, but not for disputes over opinions.
One person trusts that he may eat anything; the one who is weak eats vegetables.
The one who eats must not despise the one who does not eat, and the one who does not eat must not judge the one who eats — for God has welcomed him.
Who are you to judge someone else's household slave? He stands or falls to his own master. And he will stand, for the Lord is able to make him stand.
One person judges one day above another; another judges every day alike. Let each be fully convinced in his own mind.

The one who observes the day observes it to the Lord; and the one who does not observe the day does not observe it to the Lord. And the one who eats, eats to the Lord, for he gives thanks to God; and the one who does not eat, to the Lord does not eat, and gives thanks to God.
For none of us lives to himself, and none dies to himself.
For if we live, we live to the Lord; and if we die, we die to the Lord. So whether we live or die, we belong to the Lord.
For this is why Christ died and rose and lived: so that he might be Lord of both the dead and the living.
But you — why do you judge your brother or sister? Or you — why do you despise your brother or sister? For we will all stand before God's judgement seat.
For it is written: As I live, says the Lord, every knee will bend to me, and every tongue will confess to God.
So then each of us will give an account of himself to God.
So let us stop judging one another; instead decide this: not to put a stumbling block or a trap in a brother or sister's way.
I know, and am persuaded in the Lord Jesus, that nothing is defiled in itself — except that to the one who reckons something to be defiled, to that person it is defiled.
For if your brother or sister is grieved because of food, you are no longer walking according to love. Do not destroy with your food the one for whom Christ died.
So do not let what is good for you be spoken of as evil.
For the kingdom of God is not eating and drinking, but rightness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit.
For the one who serves Christ as a slave in this is pleasing to God and approved by people.
So then let us pursue what makes for peace and for building one another up.
Do not tear down God's work for the sake of food. All things are clean, but it is evil for the person who eats and in doing so trips someone.
It is good not to eat meat or drink wine or do anything by which your brother or sister trips.
The trust you have — have it to yourself before God. Happy is the one who does not condemn himself in what he approves.
But the one who is divided is condemned if he eats, because it is not from trust; and everything that is not from trust is sin.

romans_15.t: We who are strong ought to bear the weaknesses of those without strength, and not to please ourselves.
Let each of us please the neighbour, for good, toward building up.
For Christ did not please himself, but as it is written: The insults of those who insult you fell on me.
For whatever was written before was written for our instruction, so that through endurance and through the encouragement of the scriptures we might have hope.
May the God of endurance and encouragement give you to think the same way among one another, according to Christ Jesus,
so that with one accord, with one mouth, you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So welcome one another, just as Christ also welcomed you, to God's glory.
For I say that Christ has become one who serves the circumcision, on behalf of God's truth, to confirm the promises given to the fathers,
and that the nations might glorify God for his mercy, as it is written: For this reason I will confess you among the nations, and I will sing to your name.
And again it says: Rejoice, nations, with his people.
And again: Praise the Lord, all you nations, and let all the peoples praise him.
And again Isaiah says: The root of Jesse will come, the one who rises to rule the nations; in him the nations will hope.
May the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in trusting, so that you may overflow in hope, by the power of the Holy Spirit.
I myself am persuaded about you, my brothers and sisters, that you yourselves are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, and able to instruct one another.
But I have written to you rather boldly on some points, as a way of reminding you again, because of the grace given to me by God,
to be a public servant of Christ Jesus to the nations, serving the good news of God as a priest, so that the offering of the nations might be acceptable, made holy in the Holy Spirit.
So I have my boast in Christ Jesus, in what concerns God.
For I will not dare to speak of anything except what Christ has worked through me, for the obedience of the nations, by word and by deed,
by the power of signs and wonders, by the power of God's Spirit — so that from Jerusalem and around as far as Illyricum I have completed the good news of Christ.
In this way I make it my ambition to announce the good news not where Christ has already been named, so that I would not build on someone else's foundation,
but as it is written: Those to whom nothing was announced about him will see, and those who have not heard will understand.
This is why I was so often hindered from coming to you.
But now, having no more room in these regions, and having longed for many years to come to you,
whenever I travel to Spain I will come to you. For I hope to see you as I pass through, and to be sent on my way there by you, once I have first had my fill of your company, at least in part.
But now I am travelling to Jerusalem, serving God's people.
For Macedonia and Achaia were pleased to make some contribution for the poor among God's people in Jerusalem.
They were pleased to do it, and they are in their debt. For if the nations shared in their spiritual things, they owe it to serve them in material things.
So when I have completed this and sealed this fruit over to them, I will go off through you to Spain.
And I know that when I come to you, I will come in the fullness of Christ's blessing.
I appeal to you, brothers and sisters, through our Lord Jesus Christ and through the love of the Spirit: struggle alongside me in your prayers to God on my behalf,
that I may be rescued from those in Judea who refuse to be persuaded, and that my service for Jerusalem may be acceptable to God's people,
so that I may come to you with joy, through God's will, and be refreshed together with you.
May the God of peace be with all of you. Amen.

romans_16.t: I commend to you Phoebe, our sister, who is also one who serves the community in Cenchreae,
so that you may welcome her in the Lord in a manner worthy of God's people, and stand by her in whatever matter she may need from you. For she herself has been a patron of many, and of me myself.
Greet Prisca and Aquila, my coworkers in Christ Jesus,
who risked their own necks for my life — to whom not only I give thanks, but also all the communities of the nations —
and greet the community that meets in their house. Greet my loved one Epaenetus, who is the firstfruit of Asia for Christ.
Greet Mary, who has worked hard for you.
Greet Andronicus and Junia, my kin and my fellow prisoners, who are well known to the apostles, and who were in Christ before me.
Greet Ampliatus, my loved one in the Lord.
Greet Urbanus, our coworker in Christ, and my loved one Stachys.
Greet Apelles, who is approved in Christ. Greet those who belong to the household of Aristobulus.
Greet Herodion, my kinsman. Greet those of the household of Narcissus who are in the Lord.
Greet Tryphaena and Tryphosa, who work hard in the Lord. Greet the beloved Persis, who has worked very hard in the Lord.
Greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother — and mine.
Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers and sisters with them.
Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas, and all God's people with them.
Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the communities of Christ greet you.
I appeal to you, brothers and sisters, to watch out for those who create divisions and traps contrary to the teaching you learned, and turn away from them.
For such people do not serve our Lord Christ as slaves but their own belly, and by smooth talk and flattery they deceive the hearts of the innocent.
For your obedience has reached everyone, so I rejoice over you. But I want you to be wise about what is good, and innocent about what is evil.
And the God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
Timothy, my coworker, greets you, and so do Lucius and Jason and Sosipater, my kin.
I, Tertius, who wrote this letter down, greet you in the Lord.
Gaius, host to me and to the whole community, greets you. Erastus, the city treasurer, greets you, and so does Quartus the brother.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you. Amen.
[Now to the one who is able to strengthen you, according to my gospel and the proclamation of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of a mystery kept silent for long ages]
[but now brought to light and made known through the prophetic writings, by the command of the eternal God, for the obedience of trust among all the nations —]
[to the only wise God, through Jesus Christ, to whom be the glory for ever. Amen.] [To the Romans, written from Corinth by Phoebe, who serves the assembly at Cenchreae.]

titus_1.t: Paul, a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the trust of God's chosen and the full knowledge of the truth that accords with godliness,
resting on the hope of eternal life, which the God who does not lie promised before eternal times,
and at his own proper times he made his word visible in the proclamation with which I was entrusted, by the command of God our Saviour —
To Titus, my true child according to a shared trust: grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Saviour.
I left you behind in Crete for this reason: so that you might set right what was left undone and appoint elders in each city, as I directed you —
if anyone is beyond accusation, a one-woman man, with children who are trustworthy, not open to a charge of wild living or insubordination.
For the overseer must be beyond accusation, as God's household manager: not self-willed, not quick-tempered, not a drunkard, not violent, not greedy for shameful gain,
but hospitable, a lover of good, self-controlled, upright, holy, disciplined,
holding firmly to the trustworthy word as it was taught, so that he may be able both to urge with the healthy teaching and to refute those who contradict it.
For there are many who are insubordinate — empty talkers and deceivers of minds — especially those from the circumcision.
They must be silenced. They are overturning whole households, teaching what they should not, for the sake of shameful gain.
One of them — their own prophet — said: "Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, lazy bellies."
This testimony is true. For that reason, reprove them sharply, so that they may be healthy in the faith,
not giving their attention to Jewish myths and to commands of people who turn away from the truth.
To the clean, everything is clean; but to those who are defiled and do not trust, nothing is clean — their mind and their conscience are both defiled.
They profess to know God, but by their works they deny him — detestable, disobedient, and failing the test for any good work.

titus_2.t: But you — speak what fits healthy teaching.
Older men are to be clear-headed, dignified, self-controlled, healthy in trust, in love, in endurance.
Older women likewise are to be reverent in their bearing, not slanderers, not enslaved to much wine, teachers of what is good —
so that they may bring the young women to their senses — to love their husbands, to love their children,
self-controlled, pure, working at home, good, submitting to their own husbands — so that God's word may not be blasphemed.
Likewise, urge the younger men to be self-controlled,
showing yourself in every way a pattern of good works — with integrity in your teaching, dignity,
a healthy word beyond condemnation, so that the opponent may be put to shame, with nothing bad to say about us.
Slaves are to submit to their own masters in everything, to be well-pleasing, not talking back,
not pilfering, but showing all good faithfulness — so that in everything they may adorn the teaching of God our Saviour.
For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all people,
training us to renounce ungodliness and worldly desires, and to live with self-control, uprightly, and in godliness in the present age,
as we wait for the blessed hope — the appearing of the glory of our great God and Saviour Jesus Christ,
who gave himself for us to ransom us from all lawlessness and to cleanse for himself a people of his own possession, eager for good works.
Speak these things; urge and reprove with all authority. Let no one look down on you.

titus_3.t: Remind them to submit to rulers and authorities, to obey, to be ready for every good work,
to speak evil of no one, to be peaceable, gentle, showing all courtesy toward all people.
For we ourselves were once senseless, disobedient, led astray, enslaved to all kinds of desires and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hated and hating one another.
But when the kindness and the love for humanity of God our Saviour appeared,
he saved us — not on the basis of works done in rightness that we ourselves did, but according to his mercy — through a washing of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit,
which he poured out on us richly through Jesus Christ our Saviour,
so that, having been justified by his grace, we might become heirs according to the hope of eternal life.
Trustworthy is the saying, and I want you to insist on these things, so that those who have trusted God may be careful to devote themselves to good works. These things are good and useful for people.
But avoid foolish debates and genealogies and quarrels and fights about the law, for they are useless and empty.
Have nothing more to do with a person who causes division, after a first and second warning,
knowing that such a person is twisted and is sinning, self-condemned.
When I send Artemas to you, or Tychicus, do your best to come to me at Nicopolis — I have decided to spend the winter there.
Send Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their way with care, so that they lack nothing.
And let our own people also learn to devote themselves to good works, to meet pressing needs, so that they may not be unfruitful.
All who are with me greet you. Greet those who love us in trust. Grace be with you all.
